I also used a little garlic powder along with the salt and pepper on the chicken breasts. It was so delicious.  Served with garlic mashed potatoes and veggies.  Comfort food at its best.

This one is terrific!  I thought I had fixed chicken in a crockpot every way there was to fix it, but then I saw this recipe.  DH and I agreed that it may be the best I've ever tried.  We will definitely be making this again.  It reminded me of Thanksgiving flavors.  I used Campbell's Cream of Mushroom with Roasted Garlic Soup and added another cup of stuffing.  Otherwise, everthing was the same.  Yum.  Thank you very much.

I would give it 10 stars if I could! I have tried similar recipes, but this recipe is stellar. No comparison. I served it with garlic mashed potatoes, yum! A definite keeper. Thanks so much for posting.
Very good, Chicken was very tender. My stuffing was pretty moistened by the soup mixture, so no crunchy top, but it was still delicious.

OK, I won't bring down the rating for this recipe since everyone seems to love it.  But this was a disaster.  It is not necessarily the fault of the recipe, but I made this in my 6-qt crockpot which runs very hot.  I followed the recipe exactly, did not change anything.  When I got home from work, the entire recipe was stuck to the bottom.  And the stuffing was black.  I did not consider this edible.  My husband insisted on sampling it.  I scraped a spoonful for him and he said that it was ok, just overdone.  So I tried some, and it was extremely salty.  Of course, the liquid had reduced so much that I guess that shouldn't be surprising.  I had only cooked it for 6 hours.  So just be careful, if you have a hot crockpot, you may need to cook it much less.  I may attempt this again, but only if I will be around to keep an eye on it.
wonderful meal.  the chicken was so moist and tender.  i have a husband that loves anything with "cream of.." soup on it and this one is so easy and flavorful.  thank you!
I am trying to like chicken. I have never been a big fan until now. This was so tasty! I added an additional cup of stuffing. I also cooked on high for 3 1/2 hours. Turned out wonderful!
Family loved it!

The kids loved this! I will certainly make again.  It's very quick and easy to assemble and on those days when there are 10+ things going on after school and work, this is a great chicken dish to have waiting at home.  Served this with steamed broccoli, dinner was on the table in 10 mins.  It's a beautiful thing!  :)

I must be in the minority here because we really didn't care for this.  I had to use an entire bag of stuffing mix (2 cups would never have been enough) and it still had way too much liquid and the stuffing was very soggy. It was also very salty.  I really wanted to like this and I'm sorry I couldn't give it a higher rating.  I think I'll stick to an oven version of this recipe I have.

This was absolutely scrummy!  I followed the recipe exactly although I used normal cheddar cheese as thats all I had.
There are some leftovers in the freezer ready for another day!LOL But this is defo a keeper.Thanks

I made this last night.   My husband is not a fan of chicken or stuffing, but I wanted to see if he would at least try this.  He raved about it.  I was shocked.  He even took leftovers to work to eat at lunch today.  My two daughters, one who is picky, didn't want any of it, until I convinced her to try it.  Then she ate the whole plate.  My other daughter only ate the chicken because she doesn't care for stuffing...but don't go by her, she's a typical teenager! It was delicious.  There was a lot of liquid, soup and such, compared to the stuffing I think I may add a bit more stuffing next time.  Also I didn't have the 6-8 hrs. to cook this, so I took the suggestion of another reviewer and used frozen chicken and cooked it on high for 3.5 hrs.  I think that may be why my swiss cheese melted into my soup.  It gave the soup a cheesey delicious flavor though.  Next time I will use thawed chicken and use the 6-8 hrs on low and see what is different. My crockpot is round and it is quite big but I still had to stack a little of the chicken on top of each other, that may be another reason why things slid off into the soup. Anyway, if I can get a non-chicken eater and my picky wickys to eat this and like it, I will definitely make it again.
This was very good.  I didn't have any swiss so used shredded cheddar instead.  Turned out very well and had plenty for leftovers too.
An easy meal with ingredients usually on hand... thanks for the good meal.

I have been wanting to try this recipe and the other day I thought to myself, Self.. you need to make this!  But I had already ran out of time for the crock pot, SO I cooked it in the oven instead ( after pan cooking the chicken in chicken broth to almost doneness ). I used two boxed stuffings and just mixed the seasoning packets with the milk/soup/broth combo.  I cut each breast in half, layed them flat, put slices of swiss over them, covered them with the breadcrumbs, then poured the liquid mixture over it all and popped that bad boy in the oven.  Oh my goodness!  The swiss cheese is something I would have never thought of and it gave it the most delicious flavor. Thank You Thank You Lusil for this wonderful recipe.  Next Time I am going to plan ahead to make it in the crock pot... but this is wonderful from the oven as well!!!!!
This was awesome! And it sure did make my house smell good.  Thank you!

This was delicious and very easy to put together.  We both enjoyed it very much.  The chicken breasts were very tender, the sauce was delicious and the stuffing was the crowning touch that pulled it all together.  I served it with mashed potatoes and steamed carrots and a side of Bergy's cranberry chutney for a totally delicious meal that spelled comfort from the moment I walked in the door.  I didn't take a photo as there is already a lovely photo of the dish.  Thanks so much for a great recipe I know I will make again, and again, and again....
Because of all of the high reviews I had high hopes for this recipe.  I have a recipe for this dish that cooks in the oven.  It is not as watery and the stuffing has a better flavor.

Simple ingredients, quick prep time and no fuss clean up makes this a five star recipe any day of the week.  

This is high on my list to make on a day when I'm craving the ultimate kind of comfort food.
This is a very good recipe if you like chicken and stuffing!  I made my own stuffing with wheat bread toasted and buttered and added some poultry seasoning to the dish.  It is somewhat runny.

Definately a keeper.  The whole family loved it, even my very picky 3 year old.  Added 2 more cups of stuffing though, because I love stuffing.  Will definately make again, maybe with fresh mushrooms in with the stuffing.
SO yummy!  Next time I will double the stuffing as there was plenty of gravy but not enough stuffing for my tastes.  Otherwise - wouldn't change a thing!

Yummy.  Perfect comfort food.  Great for warming up on a cold winter day. I used three cups of stuffing and it worked out nicely.  Go easy on the salt, the stuffing makes it salty enough.  Delicious.  Will make this one again.
After reading the reviews I chose to double the stuffing, which I chose to use stove top, I omitted the salt and pepper and I use provolone chese.  Thank you for posting this.  Excellant!

Wow!  This was wonderful!  I loved the gravy made by the soups mixed with milk; the chicken was fall-off-the-bones-delicious (the swiss cheese was a nice touch); and the stuffing was loved by all (even me, and I am not usually a big stuffing fan).  What can I say that has not been said by all the other reviewers, except that we loved this!!!
The flavor is very good, but presentation didnt hold up very well. Very mushy, but still tasted great.

So good and easy!  I used about 3 cups of stuffing instead of 2 and I also substituted 1/2 cup cooking sherry instead of milk and it added a great flavor.  Next time I might also add a little sour cream to the mix.  This recipe will be added to my regular rotation!

I used mozzarella instead of swiss (was out) and it was still delicious. Extremely easy assembly and added onion to stuff mix as suggested. Would use about 4C stuff next time. A definite easy OAM meal for me so THANKS so much.
This is an awesome recipe!!!!!!! This dish is always a hit in our house. Like everyone else I serve with mashed potatos and perhaps a dinner roll or two.

This is a great crockpot dish. I also used frozen chicken breast. I would be careful about the amount of salt used because of the salt in the soups. I actually had to cook mine about 11 hours on low and it turned out just fine.  Yummy stuff.

This was much better tasting than it looked ;-)  I did not use the cheese, and cut the butter back to 3 TBS....next time I think I will add more stuffing.  I might have made a mistake by letting it cook in the crock pot about 9 hours until my husband got home from work, instead of the recommended 6hrs.  Served with mashed potatoes and it was very tasty!

This is a great recipe!  My son loved it...said it was a keeper!  He couldn't stop eating it!  I also had to make myself stop eating it!  We juist cut up the chicken and mixed it all up!  Great comfort food!

This is a wonderful comfort food made easy with the crockpot. The only thing I would change, is to use the whole bag of stuffing (the small bag) on top because I really love stuffing.  Smells delicious and tastes even better.
total comfort food.  thanks!

Thank you for sharing this recipe! My family gobbles it up whenever I make it. I usually throw in frozen chicken and it cooks up beautifully. Last time I used smoked gouda cheese and it really added a nice twist to the dish! Yum Yum!

My DH and DD loved this recipe and my DH doesn't even really like chicken, but raved about this.  Chicken cooks extremely tender and the herbs from the stuffing flavor everything great!! Thanks for an easy, fast, and tasty meal.
This was really good. I doubled it for my family size and it was gone in a flash. Definitely will be repeating it and soon!

I came home and opened up the lid and saw what looked to be burnt stuffing, so I removed the stuffing off the top and after a small taste realized that it was not burnt, just dark in color..who knows??  But this dish was soooo yummy.  The chicken literally fell apart and I had to use a spoon to scoop the chicken and tasty gravy over some homemade garlic mashed potatoes...perfect after the very long day we had.  Thanks Anne!

This recipe is definitely comfort food!  I would have given it the full 5 8's, but the stuffing turned into complete mush...tasty mush, but not the texture I was hoping for.  I am going to try this recipe again because the chicken came out perfectly tender and delicious without being dry or overly cooked, but I will use less broth in the bottom of the crockpot.  Nice dish to come home to after a long day.  Thanks for posting.
used 4 whole boneless chicken breasts and sliced into 8 thinner breasts, used 6 slices swiss, 1/2 cup chicken broth and 3 cups stuffing mix...THANK YOU
Good, simple recipe. Will likely make again.
Great, quick and easy!  This dish is great for the working family.  My friends are even calling for the recipe.  Easy! Thanks!

This recipe was good, chicken turned out very moist. I used Stove Top stuffing, Campbells cream soups & mozzerella instead of swiss. I thought it was a little salty, my husband & 3yr old son gave it a thumbs up.
This was very easy, and great. I used a box of generic chicken stuffing mix, and it still turned out wonderful. An easy set it and forget it dinner.
This was great.  It was very saucy so we made mashed potatoes to go with it.  The sauce was very good on top of the potatoes.
i use mozzarella cheese instead of swiss !!! YUM

This dish rocks! The only thing I changed was to add thinly sliced onion and freash mushrooms to the top of the sauce before I added the bread crumbs. Next time I think I will add some capers also.
Thanks!
I was looking for an easy wholesome meal for mother's day and this was it! My kids and my husband went bonkers for this beautiful casserole. Thank you so much for the recipe, it goes in my favorites!

I think I seasoned my chicken too well because I found it to be really salty.  I love salt so for me to say it was salty I know it had too much for the others.  But I ate it the next day and it was fine, not too salty at all.  what the heck?  The chicken had a great flavor and was so tender.  Will make again but will sub low sodium for the soups and less salt on my chicken.  I'm new to crock pot cooking so I'm sure any complaints or faults are operator error and not the recipe!  Thanks for sharing!

I was in the mood for something homey and comforting. This was a great selection. The chicken was incredibly tender and I loved the flavor of the gravy and stuffing. I used the low-fat versions of the cream soups and thought that worked out well. I put this together in 10 minutes, so there is essentially no prep time. Thanks for sharing a wonderful recipe.

This was so tasty! I used two cans of cream of mushroom soup, added 1/2 cup of white wine and 2 T of sour cream instead of the milk.
Thanks for a great recipe!
cooked as directed except used box of stovetop mix. chicken was OK, but stuffing was way too brown. very disappointed.

This have very good flavor, pretty rich.  I used extra stuffing and extra cheese and it was great, not dry at all, but I made sure everything was covered by the soup. I've made it for company and been asked for the recipe.

Comfort food at its best; and so easy!!  I didn't have the PF herb stuffing, but did have bread cubes.  I wanted to try this recipe without having to run out to the store, so I let them out to get somewhat hard and stale.  Added tarragon, rosemary, sage, poultry seasoning, parsely and onion powder and used this instead. Otherwise, made as posted except used three chicken breasts and just 1 can cream of mushroom.  Because I used the bread cubes, the stuffing was a bit "mushy", but the flavor was delicious! Served it with peas and carrots. This tasted like a Thanksgiving meal without any of the hard work! Thanks for a wonderful recipe.

Delish! It was very easy to put together and the outcome was pure comfort. Nothing fancy, just that good ol' comfort food taste. I used provolone cheese, since I don't care for swiss. It was great. Thanks!
A wonderful meal-very tasty and easy to prepare.The only item I added to it was a one-half onion sauteed in butter and this was added to the soups. Thank you for this recipe.

excellent. Moist and flavorfull my whole family asked for seconds.
I did leave out the butter and it was just fine.
thanks!

My family loved this! I used 2 cans of Cream of Chicken Soup for the mushroom haters in my house and used the entire bag of stuffing plus a cup of seasoned croutons as we are stuffing lovers in my house. After it was cooked I removed the chicken and diced it then stirred the entire thing together like a casserole. I served peas on the side but some mixed them right in with the chicken and stuffing. Everyone, including my twin granddaughters loved this!

Very nice.  I used stovetop stuffing mix, but next time I'll do my own with just some sage and rosemary.  Found it to be a little too salty with the stuffing mix.  Planning on leaving out the butter for this reason as well.
My DH made this and we loved it.  Did use 3 cups stuffing and cut the butter to 1/4th cup as some others have suggested.

Excellent! This is a keeper! I could tell early on that this was going to be really good. It smelled just like my Grandmother's chicken and dressing. It tasted so rich, just like Grandma's without all the work. Very easy to put together too. I didn't use Pepperidge Farm stuffing. I bought a box of generic stuffing and it worked just fine and was less than half the price.
this was awesome very tender juicy flavorfull everything in one pot what more could you ask for i too put the chicken in frozen thanks for sharing

This was very tasty but, alas, it didn't come out anything like Wildflour's lovely picture.  The  stuffing disappeared entirely!  The strange thing is that I used 3 cups of stuffing instead of 2... so, where did it all go?

When I try this recipe again, I will try it with less liquid and see what happens.  Incidentally, we didn't add any of the butter, which cut down significantly on the fat and calories, and we used the leftovers (with added water to thin them down) over noodles to make a wonderful casserole dish.

This was a really easy meal.  Next time I will leave out the swiss cheese and cut the butter in half.  The stuffing was a little soggy but we liked it anyway.  The gravy would have been smoother without the swiss cheese--which we really didn't taste. DH said it was worth "tweeking".  We also couldn't imagine serving it without cranberry sauce.

I will probably make this again. The flavor was great and it was SO easy! Next time I think I will melt the butter in a big bowl, then add the stuffing mix and stir and then put that on top in the crockpot.

This was so good, my whole family enjoyed it! I did modify it as I have a son who is allergic to milk. I didn't use the cheese or the cream soups, instead I used turkey gravy. Next time I'm going to try it exactly as written and fix DS something else! Thanks for posting!

This is such a fabulous comfort food dish! I followed the stuffing directions on the box, sauteeing onions and celery in the butter, and then mixing the broth, veggies, and stuffing, which made it taste so delicious. We also used Havarti cheese instead of Swiss, and it came out quite tasty. This is now one of my husband's favorite dishes.

This made for an easy Sunday night dinner.  I was concerned about saltiness after reading other reviews so I seasoned the chicken with only pepper and used low sodium chicken broth.  I also used 2 slices of provolone cheese for 5 breasts.  I was pleasantly surprised by the stuffing.  I expected goo on the bottom and raw on the top.  There was a little of that but not to either extreme.  I just mixed it all up and it ended up just about perfect.  Served with mashed potatoes, rolls, and acorn squash.
My husband and I loved this meal. We had tasty leftovers for the next 2 days.

This was excellent!!Very easy to throw together.
I changed one thing..I sprayed the crockpot with cooking spray 1st. 
We enjoyed this after a long day at work.  We walked into the house to that great familiar smell of chicken and stuffing.
Thank you for a great recipe!
WOW was this a winner! We used half the butter and added a drained, 8 oz can of mushrooms. Didn't miss the butter and could probably add another 4 oz of mushrooms. A really great meal!

Yum! My kids loved this!! I added an extra cup of stuffing and next time I will add a total of 4 cups. The next day my kids were asking me to make it again. I will soon.  
So easy too! I put it all in before leaving for work and came home to a house that smelled like Thanksgiving dinner. Might try with turkey breasts next time.

My family really liked this - I used 1/4 cup butter drizzle and the rest of the can of chicken broth and used 4 cups of stuffing. Next time I will omit butter and 4 cups of stuffing seemed just right. I made in the crockpot on high for 3 hours and it turned out great.

This was an absolute hit at my house!  I made this with carrots & mashed potatoes.  Also, makes a great gravy to go over potatoes.  This was a meal that hubby & our 3 yr old enjoyed. Thanks for sharing!
This was really good.. I used more stuffing and it was watery but good.. Next time I think I may use less liquid or more stuffin I too didnt use the butter
Very good and easy. Way too much butter, I will omit next time. Thank you for sharing.
Yum! This is an easy version of a dish I grew up on. Great comfort food. Thanks!

This was so delicious!  I used chicken thighs instead of breasts.  The taste reminded me exactly of Thanksgiving, and although there weren't any mashed potatoes in the dish, it tasted like it.  Thank you very much!

Wow, is this amazing stuff.  Sunday dinner doesn't get any easier.  I've made it several times and my family absolutely loves it.  I eliminated the Swiss cheese - not a big fan of Swiss cheese - and I also don't melt the butter first, I just dot it on top of the stuffing.  It melts as it cooks.  Thanks for posting this!  PS - I served this to my in-laws for Christmas dinner and it went over fabulously!

WOW, this is great easy comfort food. I used 5 frozen boneless chicken breats, added and extra 1/4 cup of broth, 4 cups stuffing and cheddar cheese since I am not a swiss cheese fan. Oh, and I used cream of chicken with herbs and cream of celery. Cooked on low 6 hours. chicken was perfectly cooked. Stuffing was not soggy and the gravy was excellent. Great for leftovers.
a complete meal and tastes great
Very good.  I served this with mashed potatoes and cranberries.  Delicious meal.  I cooked on low for 6 hours and it was done perfectly.  Thanks for a really good chicken dinner....Stephanie

We thought this was pretty good. Even my crockpot hating hubby thought it was ok, but the chicken was a little bland. I think I'll try marinading the chicken before hand and see how that goes. Other wise, it was great!

My DH and I both liked this but 2 cups of stuffing definitely was not enough.  It was really gooey (although delicious).  I will be making this again but with twice as much stuffing.  And probably I will add some more poultry seasoning, celery, onions, & mushrooms chopped up in the stuffing.  This recipe contains a lot of salt so we won't be able to have it very often.

I made this recipe because of the great rating but as I pulled it out of the crockpot I was very sceptical on if it was going to be good. To my surprise, this was pretty darn good! I also upped the quantity of the stuffing to 3 cups like others suggested. And I used the Healthy Request soups to make it a little lower in fat & sodium.
This was absolutely wonderful!  What a tasty and comforting meal to come home to.  We will be making this often... thanks for posting.

Not giving stars because I didn't follow the recipe exactly, but this just didn't turn out for us.  I read the reviews and added more stuffing.  As it cooked I got worried because the stuffing was just dry and getting dryer, so I added a little more butter and a little more broth thinking I just added too much stuffing.  In the end, I ended up with dry chicken and stuffing with the consistency of mashed potatoes.  I wouldn't say there was gravy.  It honestly didn't taste horrible, but it looked horrible and the texture just wasn't right.  If I made it again I would try making it exactly like the directions said to make a more honest opinion.
This is so good. I am standing and eating the stuffing out of the crock pot right now. I left out the cheese and butter. I poured chicken stock on top of the stuffing instead. So good. Yummy.
Wonderful!! Made exactly as is and it came out perfect.  Such comfort food and so easy to make - what could be better than that?  Thanks!!!

Made this twice now...I used an oval crockpot and I had enough chicken that I had to stack a few pieces on top of the bottom layer...I put in one and a half cups of broth...I didn't realize that I was out of cream of chicken soup so I used two cans of cream of mushroom soup...I wanted a lot of stuffing so I used an entire bag of the recommended stuffing...I put it in a bowl, added two small cans of mushrooms (with the liquid) and added a quarter cup of water...I then added the melted butter and mixed it up before I put it in the crockpot...Apparently you can't hurt this recipe...It was excellent...

I just started using a crocpot again after over 30 years.  My husband never liked food cooked in them. It's a big hit now. This is the third recipe I've used in the crockpot and we love it. It was delicious. The chicken was so tender. This one will be a favorite in our house
sooo good I normaly do not leave reviews  but this was really good. I even eat the left overs for lunch which i normally dont do thanks

like this needs another review, but I want to add my TIP!
I have a new crockpot, digital...I think they are more powerful than the older ones as this dish was cooked on low and done in 3 hours!  I had to turn it off and let sit on warm until dinner.  VERY good...used prov cheese and was terrific!

This was amazing.  The best part was that I used a whole chicken!  I rubbed my chicken with salt/black pepper/garlic powder/paparika.  I then stuffed the chicken with the stuffing mix and used toothpicks to close the cavity of the chicken.  Cooked it in my crock pot for 8 hours.  Fantastic!!  Kids loved it and asked to make it again :) using a whole chicken 0)
This was fantastic...I doubled the recipe and fed 10 people! This is sure to become a staple in my house! Thanks

I didn't care for the flavor and there was way too much gravy that looked alot like vomit in the bottom of the pot. I followed the recipe exactly and the chicken was very rubbery. Not my favorite, I won't be making this again.
This recipe is a winner!  My family loved it (including my 2 year old).  Best of all it was super easy to make.
This turned out really well, will keep this in rotation! Served over Mashed potatoes with a hint of garlic.

I couldn't eat this myself due to some dietary restrictions but everyone in my house (4 others) liked it.  Half *loved* it and the other two thought it was just so-so and would have preferred to have the stuffing separate from the kitchen.  For ME, who was responsible for making it, it was a God send because I could do it in the morning, in no time flat!  All I had to do was prepare green beans when I got home and supper was ready in 15 minutes!  Thanks for a great recipe when you're short on time!

Great meal for very little effort.  We are renovating our kitchen so crockpot meals are perfect.  I served the meal with a side of honey-glazed carrots.  I think my family will ask for this...even after the new kitchen is in!
This was a nice "comfort food" recipe and I will definitely make it again.  I used 3 cups of stuffing, but next time I will use 4 cups because we like our stuffing on the dry side.

Awesome recipe with plenty of room to add ingredients.  I added chopped onions, celery, and carrots.  Next time that i make this I plan to add more carrots and green beans.  The whole family loved it.  Thanks!

This is a fantastic recipe. I made this dish for my son and family, and they loved it. My son said this was the best chicken dish he has had in a long time. I used a whole cut-up chicken since that is what I had on hand. I skinned the pieces, and salted and peppered them before placing them in the crock pot. I also substitued American cheese slices for the Swiss cheese and used a box of Stove Top Stuffing mix. Also, after reading some of the reviews, I did not use the milk but used all of the chicken broth in its place, and I just placed a few pads of butter on top of the stuffing mix to melt into the stuffing as it cooked. Thanks for posting this recipe. It is definately a keeper.

This tasted great, and I'm giving it 5 stars because of that.  I have to admit, it didn't look too good - most likely because I let it cook for about 8 hrs on low instead of the 6 that the recipe suggested.  The extra cooking time pretty much disintigrated the Stove Top stuffing that I used.  Even though it looked like mush on top, the taste was wonderful and the family loved it.  I'll be making it again, but only on a day when I'll be home a little earlier.
Great and easy to make!  I followed the instructions exactly.  It tasted wonderful and was nice to come home to dinner ready!
I've made this several times as it is a favourite! I added a layer of potatoes over the chicken, plus an extra 1/2 C. of broth the last time I made it, and it turned out great!
I'm not much of a cook but my mother recently had surgery and could not cook so I put this together and it was a big hit. I left out the swiss cheese and added more stuffing it was great
This was such a tasty meal!  I think the swiss cheese really adds a unique flavor and makes this whole dish!  Really Great!  I will absolutely make this again!
This was delicious! I did as another chef did and cooked it in the oven instead of crock pot as cooking this was a last minute decision. I will definitely make this again!

Super great, easy recipe.  My husband LOVED this.  I used a pkg of low sodium stove top stuffing (came out to be three cups) and it was great.  The only thing I would do differently is spray my crockpot with non stick spray first because it wasn't fun to scrub off!!! :) Oh... and i only used 1/4 cup of margarine on top. Thanks!

This rates 10* with my family.  They said this is the best recipe I've gotten off of here and they would like it every couple of weeks! Super easy to put together in the CP.  I used a whole can of sodium free broth and subbed stove top stuffing because that is what was in my pantry.  Thanks Anne for a fabulous keeper!
Absolutely delicious and so easy.  I made this for my BF and now he makes it once a week for himself!  Sometimes he uses boneless pork chops which sounds good too.

This is just great.  It's quick easy and taste great but it is rather bland.  So do spice it up with extra seasonings. I used herbed cream of chicken and I put some garlic powder in the broth.  Next time I may also use poultry seasoning.
I made this with provolone cheese because it's what I had. This was amazingly easy and amazingly delicious.
Excellent dish! So easy and tastes soooooo good. I followed the recipe exactly and I'm glad I did. Thanks for sharing Anne!

Very good!  The first chicken crock pot recipe that I have truly liked.  I doubled the stuffing, and will probably add even just a little more next time. I used cheddar cheese, had no swiss.  I will for sure use swiss next time.  This is a keeper!
This was excellent. i did follow the directions to a tee. Easy to make smells fantastic and taste great
This was a delicious "comfort food" dish! ...and so easy!  I'll definitely be making this again!  Yum!
I loved it about SS didn't like the cheese.  Next time I 'll leave the cheese out.  Great meal thanks for posting.

Comfort food that is so easy and DELICIOUS! I have made this many times now and all have been great but my fav changes are to sprinkle poultry seasoning and pepper on the chicken, omit the cheese, and use cornbread instead of the bread stuffing mix. To my crumbled cornbread, I add chopped onion, celery, bell pepper, mushrooms, parsley, sage-just like you would make your stuffing but I bet Stove Top Cornbread mix would be great, too. I also like to add veggies like baby carrots, peas, green beans, kernel corn for all-in-one meal. This is also great w/ pork chops and you can add some sour cream to change it up a bit. In my crock pot I love to use the liners and my chicken is fully cooked in 3 hours on low. And of course, serve w/ cranberry sauce! Thank you, Anne, for a great recipe!!!

This is definately 5 star!!! I made this last night with a few changes. First I didn't have swiss cheese so I used mozzerella cheese. I couldn't find the pepperidge farb herb stuffing so I used pepperidge farm cornbread stuffing. Oh and I used 5 chicken breasts instead of four just because of our family size, and used 3 cups of stuffing. It turned out awesome!! I also did as someone else mentioned and used some poultry seasoning on the chicken. 
My son who is 2 now is extremely picky. I made this with mashed potatoes and gave him his taters and chicken and he ate ALL of his supper....which is VERY rare for him!!
It's gone under favorites now and we will definately have this again!!

Made this & DH & Mom both loved it. It was so easy to throw together & then come back later & dinner is ready. Make some egg noodles, rice or mashed potates and steamed veggies & you have a real "comfort food" meal.  Thanks for posting I have made this several times, just never got around to rating.

So delicious and so easy!!! My DH gave it 10 stars!!!  My picky eater DD (4) also had no problem cleaning her plate completely.  I added some fresh mushrooms, but I only had a few...Next time I will add more!  I also didn't have the chicken broth..but I just added about 3/4 cups of water with poultry seasoning, and some chopped onion.  Keeper!

We loved this! I turned this into a OAMC Dinner Kit! I bagged the chicken by itself, then in a large freezer bag I combined the soups, milk and broth. In a quart size freezer bag I placed the swiss cheese. Doing the same with the stuffing. I then placed all of those baggies into a large freezer bag arranged them so they would lie flat; printed the recipe and tossed it in the freezer! Came out beautifully! Once thawed I followed your instructions. Thanks for posting!

I dont know if I did it wrong - quite possibly - but I found the texture really quite gloopy. Maybe I used too much stuffing. I think I would make this in the oven instead of the crock pot. That way the surfae area (I have a very large crock pot) would be smaller and then the stuffing would just be a crunchy topping.

This was very very good and really easy. The only changes I made was to use water instead of broth (I was out of chicken broth), added some garlic powder when seasoning the chicken, and I used herb cream cheese instead of swiss.  I think it would have been better had I used broth, but it was tasty and easy, and freezes well!

Wonderful recipe!  My DH and I loved it!  He loved having the leftovers the next night as well.  I couldn't believe how easy it was.  I will be making this again and again! edit 9/22/08 My Dh made this again, but wanted to make more than our crock pot would hold.  He used a 13 x 9 pan and used the same recipe order and baked it tightly covered for 2 1/2 hrs @ 350 degrees.  It was still very good!

This was delicious! Even my husband and kids like it and they don't like cream of mushroom soup. I did leave out the cheese (I didn't have any Swiss on hand and didn't want to sub the first time trying a recipe), but it was great even without it! Thanks for sharing!

I used boneless thighs and tossed this in the crock pot right before we left for the game.  It literally took me longer to locate the slower cooker lid, which is always hiding someplace clever, than it did to prepare this meal.  We arrived home, dished it up and OMG!!  Fabulous!  Juicy and tender with fantastic flavor.  Perfect for workdays.
This was soooooo goooood!!!! Not for the health concious though :) Very yummy comfort food. Mmmmm Mmmmm good!
Easy and very tasty recipe...will definitely make this again...I also used boneless thighs, as mentioned in a review.
It was very good and the kids really liked it. I just found that the stuffing came out way too "mushy" for my taste. Not sure how to remedy that.  Thanks for posting!
This recipe is fantastic, I made as directed. My entire family loved it.

it was 3pm and i was wanting some chicken and stuffing. being pregnany and super lazy this recipe was exactly what i was looking for. this turned out really good and talk about tasty! this one would get 5*s from us w/ a few adjustments. i used frozen chicken breasts, just put them in the pot right out of the freezer. i used Recipe #57287 instead of the canned soup, just dumped it in hot on top of the frozen chicken, broth, and cheese. I used cheddar/jack cheese as we didn't have any swiss and couldn't even tell it was in there so next time i'll probably leave it out all together.  I used my own dried bread cubes and next time i'll double up the stuffing as others did so there will be more of it.  it was also a bit salty for us, next time i won't use any extra salt at all. i cooked it 3 hrs on high in my old crock pot and it came out great. i have to say i'd be hesitant about cooking it for 6 hrs on low, mainly because it seems like the stuffing would turn to mush. but i usually forget to put the crock pot on till later anyway so the 3hr cook time was perfect for us. i'm tempted to try this sometime w/ biscuits on top instead of the stuffing, hummm.... but this will definitely be a regular in this house, thanks for a keeper! :)
yummy and super easy...even my two year old gobbled it up :)

I realized I have never reviewed this, even though I have made it many times.  May not need a review with so many 4 and 5 stars, but it gets another 5 star from me.  I use frozen boneless, skinless breasts, I  use sharp cheddar and Velveta for extra smoothness with the cheese.  Some thyme and parsley in the broth....100% comfort meal.  I don't measure the stuffing mix, just cover the chicken and broth mix, and it turns out great.  Love it!

We really enjoyed this recipe...I have not been feeling so good, and have had not much of an appetite, this was a good thing to make and tasted wonderful...I too did not have any swiss cheese so subbed with morzerella and provolone blend.
that was good but nest time i will do it in the oven son the stuffing can get crisp .. thanks
This recipe would be a great subsitute for Thanksgiving if you are only cooking for two.  It's easy and tastes wonderful.  I used lower fat and sodium soups.

This was definitely a winner in our home. So simple to throw together. I baked mine (as another poster suggested) due to time. But I look forward to making it in the crock too. This will be a regular in our home.
Thanks for posting!

Good for throwing something together quickly.  I would suggest one of two things:  either omit the salt on the chicken breasts or purchase low-sodium/healthy request soups and broth.  I like salty, but this was too much for me.  Very easy recipe.  Thanks.

This is calorie laden, but ohhhhhh so good! Excellent. 

I wanted to add a few more things as I eat the leftovers of this wonderful meal. It is very salty, I would not salt the chicken, and I believe that reduced sodium soups would be much better. Also, I used baby swiss slices which I don't think add so much to the flavor as it does the texture of the gravy. I also used about a half bag of the PF cubed stuffing. I don't like stuffing, at all and this stuff is the bomb! I served it with cranberry sauce and green beans. I jokingly called a poor man's Thanksgiving.
blahhhhhh
I'm sorry to only give this 3 stars, but it  did not really come out that good, the stuffing was real soggy and the taste was so,so.
Was not a fan. Found it more of a mushy mess.  My kids wouldn't touch it.

I have made this dish three times in the last 2 months and my family really seems to enjoy it. Because of sons allergies I use a "homemade cream soup"  and omit the cheese. It looks like a mushy mess but all ask for it over and over again. Thanks for the great recipie.

Okay, 2 cans of soup makes this too mushy, is this correct?  After reading some of the reviews, I noticed a lot of people adding extra stuffing.  The reviews are misleading because of people altering the original recipe.  I did forget the milk(this would have made it worse).  This tasted good, but my hubby did not like the texture of the dressing.

Wow! Can't get any easier than this. I altered this a little bit, I used a box of Pepperidge Farm Stuffing box with the seasonings instead of the recomended.  This meal tasted great, everyone loved it. Thanks for posting.

This is such an easy dinner! I big hit in my house. I did follow another reviewer's suggesting about adding more stuffing. I used 3 cups, and plan on using atleast 4 cups of stuffing next time, and maybe 1/2 an onion.
Made this tonight......It turned out a little overdone after cooking for 6 hours on low. The chicken was very tender and tasty, though :)

This was great - I threw everything into the crock pot on my way to work and it was ready when I walked through the door.  I set the table, tossed together a quick salad, and dinner was served.  I had Chicken Stovetop Stuffing on hand, so I used that (the whole box) instead of the Peppridge Farm Herb Stuffing.  I couldn't figure out where to add the milk, so I didn't use any.  Other than that, I followed the recipe.  It turned out great - the chicken was falling apart tender and the stuffing and gravy were delicious.  This is a great crock pot recipe - simple & tasty.

This recipe was awesome! The chicken reminded me of rotisserie chicken from the store! I did make a few changes...used only one can of "cream of" soup, didn't use any milk, skipped the cheese (still very rich and creamy without) and used cornbread stuffing. Oh and I also cut up about 3 potatoes and threw them in. It turned out GREAT! Thanks for the keeper Anne!

Easiest dish to make.  Was leary of the amount of sodium so I didn't add any salt.  I also used low sodium soups.  Didn't use the cheese.  Didn't add any broth or milk. There was plenty of sauce just from the chicken and soup.  I also used frozen chicken breast.  Couldn't have been any easier.
this was really good! I used cornbread and chicken stuffing mixed together, and I didnt use cheese. My kids loved it too!! Super moist and great flavor!!

This is delicious and easy to make. I did change it up. I only used the cream of mushroom, 2 cups of chicken broth and nearly twice as much stuffing, no cheese and half the butter. It was kind of salty, so I may omit that next time I make it. The chicken was fantastic and everyone loved it.

This is our favorite "new" recipe! Comfort food! Unfortunately I changed it so much it is really different but you get the same type results.  I use 6 small boneless chicken breast in crockpot, 3 to 4 98% fat free condensed cans cream of chicken soup over top of chicken and then sprinkle one package of low sodium chicken flavored stuffing on top.  No broth, no butter, no milk, no cheese.  FANTASTIC! I only changed it because I wanted less fat. Thanks for a great recipe for me to tweak to our liking!  I like to use frozen chicken breasts and cook on high for two hours and then low for two hours.

There is a similar recipe on the cream of chicken and mushroom label.  So instead of using both soups, you could just use the one.  Also, the first time I made this (in the oven..), my husband was expecting STUFFING, so the second time I made it, I used Stove Top.  We just love the taste that the swiss cheese and the different soup brings.  Most people know of the cream of mushroom/stuffing bake recipe.  The cheese and different soup makes it MUCH better!!  Great recipe!!!
My family and I love it! I also made it with a turkey breast. I had to double up on the soup and broth for the turkey and skip the cheese.

I made this last week and almost the whole family LOVED it (the exception being my three year-old son who doesn't like to try anything). The changes I made were to use Pepperidge Farm Cornbread Stuffing instead of the Herb Stuffing and provolone cheese instead of the swiss cheese since I figured the swiss would be too sharp a taste for my kids. I also used vegetable broth instead of the chicken broth since I was out of chicken broth. I'll definitely be making this one again. It's a keeper!!

I have made this several times and forgot to review it. It's a great recipe. Delicious, and so easy! The first time I did add the swiss cheese, but for some reason I couldn't even tell that the cheese was in there when it was done cooking. So the other times I made it, I just left out the cheese.

I've made the oven version of this many times, but this was my first time making it in the crockpot.  I used 3 chicken breasts, a box of stovetop stuffing since I didn't have any Pep Farm on hand, and only a couple tablespoons of butter.  It turned out GREAT and was even better left over the next day.  I will definitely be making this again . Thanks!

We liked this.  I did make changes according to what I had on hand.  
I used a pint-sized jar of home canned chicken breasts and the broth from this can.  I added a bit of water and chicken bouillon.  Was out of Swiss cheese.  Used sharp cheddar.  (was good, but probably would be better with the Swiss).  Used Recipe #25653 Condensed Cream of Soup Mix recipe for the 2 cans of soup.  (Heated 'til thickened.)  Used remaining ingredients.  Cooked in crockpot for much shorter time.  Easy, yummy, whole family actually ate it - yeah!

I have made this recipe twice now and I must say it's pretty good.  Both times I've used the low fat soup and low sodium chicken broth.  I have also substituted the Pepperidge Farm Cornbread stuffing in place of the herb.  Like others have stated, my dressing for the most part dissolves but it still tastes great!

Like some other reviewers said, I used extra stuffing mix. One of the times I made this, I forgot the cheese and butter -- it was still delicious. I found it quite salty, so put just pepper on the chicken and used mostly low-sodium soups. Another substitution that went over well was using cream of potato soup in place of the cream of mushroom. Also, I added some chopped onion, carrot and some frozen peas to the soup mixture. Overall, excellent meal that comes out perfect even with changes or adding what you have on hand.

LOVE THIS!  I put in frozen chicken breasts like another reviewer but had it on high for 1 1/2 hr and then put to low to finish and the chicken just fell apart.  Such a simple recipe with such great flavor.

Ok. I'm reviewing this according to my family's taste. I had gall bladder surgery and couldn't eat a bite. I used Stove-top chicken stuffing and cheddar. Those are the things I had on hand. My kids and parents thought it was wonderful. I will be making again just so I can taste. Thanks for an easy meal to make for the family on a hectic day!

Very Good. Quick and simple yet has great flavor. I did not have cream of mushroom so I used cream of celery and it worked out fine. I also added some diced celery. Will defenitely be making again. Thank you anne for posting.

I over cooked it and everyone still cleaned their plates.  The chicken was dry was all. If we would have ate when planned it would have been perfect.. but still an awesome dish that I will make again.
I have made this several times, keep forgrtting to review it. It is so delocious and easy to prepare. DH loves it. Thank you Anne for posting the recipe.

Great combination...great taste.  Left out the cheese and didn't miss it at all.  I used low sodium broth and one of the cans of soup was reduced sodium but it was still a bit salty...that's a personal preference and I can adjust next time.  Will definitely make again.  The chicken was so tender!  Will definitely make this one again.  Thanks for posting!

So delicious and easy.....I have made this 3 times...the last time I completely mixed the soup and stuffing together about 30 minutes before serving...actually, my old crock was cooking so slow that I decided to finish cooking in the oven...I poured everything into a casserole dish.....the soup and stuffing completely mixed together......the stuffing turned out even more flavorful and was very mosit.....my family liked this better than leaving the stuffing on top....next time, I plan on mixing soup and stuffing together before adding to my crock pot......thank you for posting!

This was delicious. I did make a couple changes. I have a 3 qt. crock pot. I layered about four quartered baby red potatoes on the bottom of the crock, then added a couple handfuls of baby carrots on top of the potatoes.  I then followed the recipe as shown except I used Muenster cheese and Stove Top cornbread stuffing. All this filled my crock pot to the top.  For the soups I used Healthy Request & low sodium broth to cut down sodium and fat.  Everything came out wonderfully. Very tasty. I'll certainly make this recipe again and again
WOW!!!  Delish!!!
This recipe is great!!! I make at least once a month. My girls love this on cold,raw days. This is comfort food at it's best. I use what ever cheese I have on hand and it always comes out yummy!!
This was so easy to make and the entire family loved it! I did accidently put to much stuffing in mine and some of it was dry, but that was my fault and we still liked it. So thanks for posting!

This dish was very nice. I only changed one thing about this recipe and that was that instead of using cream of chicken and mushroom soups I used all cream of celery. It came out quite tasty however I think it would be a better dish for the regular oven because the chicken had a mushy texture. Its already a very fast and easy dish, I don't see how using your regular oven would make much of a difference, besides improving texture.

Our family loves this recipe, but NOT the fat. We make it healthier by using fat free cream of chicken soup and substituting 1/2 chicken broth for the melted butter. It's delicious and we can eat it without feeling guilty.

Oh Johnny! This is such a tasty dish- sooo rich and comforting. I've made it chicken breasts and it's always been amazing. However, I LOVE this recipe with DRUMSTICKS! If you want to try it with drumsicks make sure you take the skin off before you start cooking. I put them standing up in the crockpot so when they're done everyone can easily grab a drumstick and spoon the sauce overtop.
So easy and SO good!  The best crockpot recipe I have tried so far!
This recipe is amazing.  It is specially requested atleast once a month in my house
Very good and easy! The only thing I would recommend is adding a lot more stuffing as 2 cups just isn't enough! Great easy meal!
Delicious! I used cream of chicken with herbs & the whole bag of stuffing. I did leave out the cheese because DH doesn't like it.

I've made this 4 or 5 times already and my family loves it! I used butter flavored Pam instead of the real butter to save on calories. I serve leftovers over jasmine rice, so yummy. You can use frozen chicken breasts but allow about 1.5 hrs addl cooking time on HIGH. Thanks so much for this keeper!
My family and I really enjoyed this recipe. I will make it again soon. The next time I may add potatoes and veggies for a complete meal. My DH says I can make this every week.

Comfort food at it's best.  Made as directed using boneless, skinless chicken thighs.  So easy to put together and delish.  The swiss cheese gave the gravy a nice rich flavor.  This is like Thanksgiving in a crockpot.  Served with steamed peas, mashed potatoes and dinner rolls.  Next time I am tempted add cranberry sauce.  DH loved this!  Thanks for sharing.

My family loved this. I found that it didnt have enough gravy but i did use more stuffing, so i might double the cannned soup part next time. 2 cups a stuffing just wasnt enough. my husband loves the stuff:) I added corn too, made a real nice touch. Thank you!

I only gave this 3 stars because my DS didn't like it at all and I thought it was way too salty. I didn't follow the recipe exactly, I used 2 cans of cream of chicken soup because that's all I had, but I don't think that would have made much of a difference for the salty taste. Sorry!
What a wonderful easy recipe for the fall.....mmmmmm!!!  This was so easy to put together!! We all loved this with pillsbury flaky biscuts on the side.  My DH said the gravy was very good!
I used all chicken soup and split chicken breast with skin and bone because that is what I had.  I used Pep. Farm cornbread stuffing and added onion powder, sage and pepper.  Very good. 4.5 stars

I've made this twice now, and the first time, I hated it. But it just looks so good in the pics, I had to try it again. It was incredible! I loved it. The only change I made was the stuffing-I can't find the PepFarm stuffing anywhere. Last time we used Stove Top, this time the cheap-o Target brand. It was delightful.

Made it first time week ago and my family LOVED it.  It was so easy and SO GOOD.  Gave it to all my friends and they loved it also.  I don't like dried pepperidge farm stuffing so I used the soft fresh bread crumbs and it came out wonderful.  Just a hint if you use the fresh breadcrumbs use 4 to 5 cups as opposed to 2 of the dry.  Try it - you won't be sorry - really comfort food.
The stuffing was so good that I'd recommend using the whole box instead of 2 cups.

I'm not going to give this any stars because so many people loved it and I don't want to bring the rating down.  I really liked the flavor of the chicken, but the stuffing was mushy.  I will probably make again, but won't put any stuffing in - maybe add a few potatoes.
made this many times and my family loves it! I also throw my chicken in frozen, add more stuffing and use chicken broth instead of butter.  I true keeper.

This was good and easy to make, however a bit on the rich side for me . I think it might have been the swiss cheese, so ill leave that out next time. I shredded my chicken breast with a fork once they were cooked. I agree with a previous review, the stuffing was a bit mushier than I prefer. The 4 stars are for how easy it was, but I think I will make a few adjustments. Thanks!

This was WONDERFUL! I thought the cans of soup would make the gravy taste like... soup. It did not! It was a wonderful magical blend of the seasoning in the dressing and the broth and soup. ONE big change I made that we loved, boneless pork chops instead of chicken. the most tender chops ever! Make sure you use boneless, or you will have to be dodging bones all thru the meal. Another change I made was to leave out the cheese. I did not miss it Also, I put an entire bag of stuffing on top, same amount of butter, yummy .We served this with mashed potatoes on a cold Sunday afternoon.
A note on Pepperidge Farm stuffing, some of the bags in my store seemed crushed, and some were in cubes. We liked the sage and onion!

A real winner. Made exactly as stated w/ only one substitution no butter on hand so melted 1/4 cup Smart Balance spread. Worked just fine. I used perhaps a bit more cheese, my slices were approx 4x4 so I used two per breast and overlapped them a bit. Plugged her in at 10am and we ate at 5:30. The chicken was VERY tender. Wonderful on a rainy night. Next time I will add the 3rd cup of stuffing as others have suggested. Thanks for a great and so simple meal. Update: I made this again using Pepperidge Farm stuffing and it came out very mushy. Previously I had used a crouton like stuffing from Mrs. Cubison which held together nicely. The PF was too crushed to begin with for such a long cooking time. Update: Made again for the third time. This time I used healthy request soups and reduced fat swiss cheese. The result was great!

WOW!  This was a HUGE hit with my hubby and 4 year old!  So easy - and really yummy! I put the b/s chicken breast in partially frozen...cooked on high for 3 hours and they were PERFECT! Juicy and very tasty! I didnt have two cans of "cream of" soup so I used 1 can of cream of mushroom - and a jar of chicken gravy - and I added about a 1/2 cup of chopped up onion on top of the stuffing.  oh..and white american cheese because that's what we had. Again... totally delish and I was told to keep this recipe!
Very nice! I used 1/2 butter and more dressing and subbed salt for garlic salt.

Followed the recipe as written but used chedder cheese as we are not fans of swiss and that is what we had in the house.  
Chicken was moist and very tender.  I would add more stuffing next time as I only had a small box of cornbread stuffing.  I would probably go for the light version of the soups as well to decrease the salt content.  But overall, this was an easy recipe and the flavor was great.  I would definately make this again.

This was about as tasty as it gets!  We all really liked it.  Our one very tiny, VERY TINY, complaint that there wasn't enough stuffing.  I think I will add more than the 2 cups next time to see if that helps.  Swiss cheese gave it just a great flavor.  I can't wait to make it again.  It's a keeper!

Our family really liked this, especially the kids (ages 1 and 3) who gobbled it up with mashed potatoes. I made it exactly as written, except I used shredded Swiss (had some that needed to be used up). I think next time I will stir canned mushrooms, diced celery and browned pork sausage in with the stuffing mix. (We just prefer stuffing that way.) Also, I think you could add more stuffing mix, if you desired, and it wouldn't hurt it. Super easy, kid friendly meal! Thanks for sharing!

I made this almost exactly as written. I had to use bone in chicken as this was all I had and I baked it in the oven because I got a late start and it wouldn't have been done in time for dinner in a crock pot! The chicken was SUPER tender and falling off the bone almost! I baked it covered in a casserole dish in the oven for about an hour and left the cover off and cooked for another 15 minutes to brown up the stuffing. This was great! Very easy and tasted wonderful with mashed potatoes and asparagus. The gravy tasted very homemade and not like "canned soup"! I can't wait to make this in the crock pot. I love using my crock pot and coming home to a cooked meal! Thanks for posting Anne!

Loved this recipe.  I used Mrs. Cubbison's stuffing mix and provolone cheese as those are what I had on hand.  It came out perfect.  I will definately be making this over and over again.  Thanks for sharing!

i only used 3 chicken breasts (for the size of our family) and one can of soup (cream of chicken) instead of 2 cans. I used grated cheddar on instead of swiss since that's what we have..turned out really well, maybe a bit too much liquid for some tastes since the stuffing became borderline mushy close to the chicken, but we all liked it and hubby declared it a "leftovers won't be wasted" meal...although there were no leftovers! Next time i might put fresh sliced mushrooms on over the chicken since i'll never use 2 cans of soup, or other veggies instead of making a side dish of them.
the recipe is great! i used provolone and stove top sage stuffing and it worked out fine. definitely a keeper!
Very easy and very flavorful
I followed directions without changing.  Stuffing was too mushy for our tastes. Might be better if placed in oven and baked.  May try again.

Great recipe!  I used Asiago cheese (because it's what I had) and added a can of french style green beans before  topping it with stuffing.  Next time I'm going to try it using Fat Free Soups.   Thanks for a great recipe!

We thought this was a very good Chicken and Dressing.  Only thing I would suggest is one might use the lower sodium soups.  It tends to be a little salty tasting.  Will make again soon.  Thanks for posting this recipe.
Chicken & stuffing is one of my DH favorite meals...and this one makes it easy on me.  He loved it & said it was a definite have again.

This definitely wasn't what I was expecting, but in a good way. First off, I used pork chops. I figured they would stay a bit more solid, but they wound up being so tender that they fell to pieces as I was trying to get them out. I also thought the stuffing on top would get crunchy but it wound up being soft. I loved it so much because it reminded me of a cheesy chicken (or pork, I guess) corn chowder (I added corn, too). It was great! I think next time, I will try it with chicken and pray that it turns out the same consistency! Thanks for posting! 5 stars all the way!
We love this!  Great to come home to.  Usually have everything on hand.  I use a whole bag of Stove-top stuffing and have used mozzarella cheese.
Comfort food at its finest and SO easy to make! Delicious! I usually serve this over brown rice.
Made this based off other good reviews. Did not work out very well for my husband and I. The cheese made everything greasy and oily. Did not like very much. Will not be making again.

I just can't give this one a great rating. It did taste very good, but that was thanks to Kraft's StoveTop stuffing, not the recipe. I used 2 very large chicken breasts, a box of Stove Top mix, omitted the cheese and used half the butter. Otherwise followed the recipe. It cooked in half the time listed in my 6 qt. crockpot. The stuffing was a goopy wet mess. Flavor was great, but like I said...

Prepared as directed except I used mozzarella cheese (its what I had on hand) and Stove Top stuffing.  I found it to be too salty/rich and the stuffing didn't hold up very well.  It was tasty, but I probably won't make this again.

I've made this in the crock pot and in the oven, and I must say that the oven method, to me, was so much better!  I changed a few minor things:  I used 1/2 c. of broth instead of a cup, and I didn't add milk to the soups for fear of watery gravy, and I added about an extra cup of stuffing!  Otherwise, I followed the recipe as written.  I covered a 9 x 13 pan with foil, baked at 375 for one hour, removed the foil and baked for an additional ten minutes to allow the stuffing to brown.  Just right!
super easy to make...  in crock pot now!  Can't wait to taste it!

The chicken was very moist and flavourful. The stuffing was great.
I added 2 extra cups of stuffing and found it was too much. Therefore, only 1 extra cup would be perfect (3 total).
My kids devoured it.

This recipe as posted is very salty.  I would defintely suggest using reduced sodium chicken broth and reduced sodium (healthy request) soup.  It also doesn't hold up well.  The stuffing turns into a soggy mushy mess. The overall flavor is good and it is very easy to toss together.  It is much better prepared in the oven.  Because the texture of the stuffing wasn't very appetizing, I put everything in the fridge.  When the chicken cooled off I sliced it up and I bought some cranberry sauce.  I made chicken, stuffing and cranberry sandwhiches.  It felt like the day after Thanksgiving!

Made this as written and we all liked it very much. It was easy to make and just made a veggie as a side to round out the meal. Will be adding this to our menu to make again. I will probably try and cut back on some of the butter next time.

No comfort food is as good as Thanksgiving! This hits the spot. I left out the cheese and used boneless chicken thighs. Also used the entire bag of stuffing bc we all love it. We did have it with cranberry sauce but the whole time I was wanting some green beans so next time I will put a bag of frozen green beans underneath the chicken layer with a little cranberry sauce to sweeten them. Thanksgiving in a pot! No measuring required!

Everyone loved this simple dinner including my picky 10 year old.  I had turkey cutlets thawed so I used them instead of chicken and I used a box of Stove Top stuffing that I had in the cabinet AND I used provolone cheese instead of Swiss just because I like it better.  It turned out great for a fall day...my kids said it was like a Thanksgiving preview.  Will definitely go into my crock pot rotation.

I added onions and baby carrots under the boneless chicken- chicken breasts were frozen- and I added about 1/4 cup of white wine to the stock, reducing the soup to just one can. I used Pepperidge Farm sage stuffing mix, but as the other testers stated, I would add more dry stuffing mix on the top next time, to soak up more of the juices on top. I cooked it on high for 4 hours.Tasted wonderful, chicken  was falling apart tender and no dryness from being frozen. I added mashed potatoes on the side, and it was a great tasting, roast chicken dinner that was so easy. I love that you can use frozen boneless chicken and it turns out great! Sometimes I forget to thaw the chicken overnight in the fridge, and I am left in the morning scrambling before work, with out the main ingredient for my slowcooker easy dinner! This solves the problem and it's really good!  Great cold weather dinner too!
I followed the recipe as written. It was absolutely delicious!!! Even better the next day as leftovers. I only wished there would have been more stuffing so I'll add more next time around.

Made this almost as written; I used a stove top style cornbread stuffing mix (the entire package after reading reviews about there not being enough), only had mushroom soup so I used 2 cans of that, no cheese or broth (just added water and milk.)  This was really salty, but had excellent flavor.  Even used reduced sodium soup.  Perhaps this was becuase of the stuffing I used.  Nevertheless, this was a good dish.  I want to tweak it and see if I can get the sodium down.  Thanks!

I tired this recipe because it sounded pretty good and got great reviews. I have to say that I was very dissapointed.
