Based on some of the previous comments stating that the muffins were dry and tart, I decided to replace the cup of cranberries with a cup of canned whole cranberry sauce, and the muffins turned out fantastic! They were not at all dry, nor were they tart. They were moist, sweet, but not overly so, and had a wonderful balance between orange and cranberry, both flavours came through perfect.

I would definitely make these muffins again, they were delicious!!! A very nice treat.

I just made a batch of these this morning.  They are very very good.  In response to those who find them dry, I would say that they are right if you are comparing them to cake muffins.  so i that is what you prefer, these are not the muffins for you.  But, if you are a fan of denser muffins, then you should give these a try.  Also, INMHO, the muufin batter is adequately sweet.  The tartness is all in the cranberries.  Next time I''ll cut them in hslf do that the tartness is less concentrated in certain spots.  The only thing I changed this time was to use melted butter in place of oil.

I used craisens and sprinkled top with Wiltons Sparkling White Sugar Sprinkles instead of fresh cranberrys and regular sugar (sugar on tops of muffins) and they turned out absolutly fantastic!! I love them. Now the real test is with my husband. He doesn't like sweets but he loves these muffins! Thanks food.com for another great recipe

These were great! I did increase the BP to two teaspoons like other reviewers. I also used the zest of one whole orange. Based on the reviews of being tart I chopped the cranberries coarsely and stirred them into the sugar and let them sit for a couple of minutes before adding the rest of the dry ingredients. This worked well, they were sweet and tart but not too tart! Will be making these again in the future.

Very easy to make and turned out great. I used craisins but I wasn't crazy about they texture since they're so much denser than the muffins, which were nice and fluffy. I'll definitely be making these again, but I want to try fresh cranberries and see how they are. I like that they're relatively guilt-free, and my wife and especially my daughter loved them.

I made these several times then tried a variation. I substituted clean lemon fruit (no sements pith or peel) for the cranberries and topped them with grand marnier and honey. They were pretty much the best muffins I have ever had and they look so beautiful. They were also good with lime and lemon fruit. Enjoy!

Very excellent!  Of, course I made a few very minor changes.  Used Craisins instead of fresh cranberries because that's what I had.  Squeezed 1/3 c. fresh orange juice, added it to a small sauce pan, and with occasional stirring, let the juice be absorbed by the Craisins for about 5 minutes on low medium heat.  Had to cut the salt in half because I used salted butter. Also increased the Baking powder to reflect the 2 cups of flour.  Added a teaspoon of ginger too. Sprinkled raw sugar on the top of the muffins prior to putting in the oven but was contemplating making a glaze of powdered sugar, butter, and orange juice which I may try sometime in the future.  Naw.  Would go counter to my life philosophy of KISS.
The recipe I've been looking for!! I followed the directions exactly,
These muffins are amazing. I have made them over and over and have given out this recipes many time.

Gotta give it 5 stars as my husband said "these are damn good muffins!" That must mean 5 stars, lol. OK, they ARE very good! I like the tartness. I chopped fresh whole cranberries, I used 2 tsp baking powder as others suggested. I didn't have fresh orange zest, only had dried orange peel (Penzey's spices) so I added that to the liquid and let it hydrate. Wonderful muffin, not too heavy with sugar or oil.

Made this muffins today - really great!  Love the flavour of cranberry & orange.  Only adjustment I did was as other reviewers suggested, used 2 tsp baking powder, otherwise made exactly as stated.  Delicious, will definately be making again. Only 4 pts on WW!
Very yummy.  Would make this recipe again.

I just made this recipe last night.  I really needed to go grocery shopping so I made a couple mods to make use of what I had avaliable in the pantry.  I used 1C dried "Craisins" and cooked them in orange juice over Med heat for about 5 minutes to plump them and then drained them.  I did not have the orange zest available, so I ommited that ingredient.  Also, I was out of eggs and had a huge bag of ground flaxseed, so I ommited the eggs and substituted 1 Tbl of ground flax seed and 3 Tbl. of water for the one egg.  These muffins turned out EXCELLENT!  I find that the Craisins plumped in OJ really gave it what it needed without the orange zest available.   I am very happy to have found this recipe and they turned out just great!  This is going to be a keeper for sure!  Thanks for the recipe!  :)

I made these for my husband and son and they loved them. I substituted applesauce for the oil and added a teaspoon of orange extract to the batter, which added the perfect balance. I made the batter the night before and baked them first thing in the morning.
Yummy and moist muffins :)

I used flax in place of egg and added a little soy milk, and did some in mini-loaves.  M said they were among the top 5 yummiest muffins he's had.  I chopped the cranberries and mixed them with sugar first. I put in just over 1 1/4 c. sugar when doubling the recipe, plus topping

I never ever write reviews but I felt compelled to this time. I am terrible at baking, my muffins and cookies and breads always come out dry or too underdone and with very little flavor. This recipe was super simple to follow and the results were delicious! I followed the advice of other reviewers by increasing the baking powder from 1 tsp to 2, and as I did not have cranberries, I reconstituted 3/4 cup of craisins in 1 cup of orange juice, then used 3/4 cup of that OJ as called for in the recipe. It definitely helps to drain the plumped up craisins and add them to the dry ingredients before adding the wet ingredients - the flour coating prevents them from all falling to the bottom of the muffins. I sprinkled brown sugar on the tops before baking, but I think the molasses made them a bit too crispy, so I'll stick with white sugar next time.
I  made this recipe as written. The muffins were dry and not very sweet. I will try again.

Recipe turned out amazing! Fast and Easy Morning Goodness!!!!

I substituted Granulated sugar for Baking Coconut Sugar, they turned out slightly browner since the coconut sugar has that effect on everything! But turned out just as Good! Thanks!
Good muffins!  Needed to use up some oranges, so I juiced them, rehydrated my cranberries and these turned out good. DDIL really liked them as did DGS#2.
Wonderful recipe, simple, fast and very tasty, thank you.

Thanks for the great muffin recipe.  I was looking for a corn muffin recipe, so I just replaced 1/2 cup of the white flour with corn meal.  I also have some toasted mixed nuts that I added.  This recipe is super even without the modifications.  So much that my friends here in Taiwan really like this one.

Perfect. I had been using the recipe on the back of the Ocean Spray fresh cranberries bag, this recipe is almost identical.Doubled the baking powder as suggested, they rose up perfectly. I didn't have any zest (which is fabulous btw, and worth the effort). I reduced the sugar slightly & added a few extra cranberries. These are my DD's favorite,  They freeze beautifully, just pull out and pop in the microwave for a few seconds for a quick breakfast (topped with cream chesse). Thanks for sharing, this one is a keeper.

I just made these and they turned out delicous!! I used the tip from another reviewer with using dried cranberries and it worked wonderfully.  I did think they could use another level of flavor, so that is why they were only given 4 stars, but this is definitely a keeper!! Maybe a pinch of cinnamon for some depth? I will be using this one again!

Great recipe! I made a few changes: I placed the cranberries in a cup and added orange juice until the berries were completely covered. I added: Agave sugar (1/4 tsp) & orange extract (1/4 tsp) to the berries & orange juice. I left the mixture in the refrigerator overnight. I didn't use the orange juice used to soak the cranberries, but I will the next time I make these muffins.  I used 1/4 cup brown sugar & 1/4 cup of cane sugar. I substituted 1/4 cup sour cream instead of vegetable oil. **I used 2 tsp of baking powder as recommended by the previous reviews**.
This is an excellent recipe. Not only do they taste delicious, are moist and fluffy, but they are as pretty as the picture shows!

Loved these! I used 2 cups cranberries chopped in half and 'marinated' them in 1/4 cup of the OJ with an added 1/4 of sugar (so total sugar upped to 1 cup). I didn't have fresh orange peel, just dried - I uses 2 tsp of that. Also I used unsalted butter instead of oil. Great result and even better the next day!

I made this with those little "Cuties" mandarin oranges that were about to turn, and rehydrated craisins.  I had 3/4 c orange juice, and 1/4 c heavy cream to bind everything together then placed in a bundt pan.  Yummmmmmy.

I must add a 5 star review to all the other 5 star reviews that this recipe has received.  I made loaves instead of muffins but it did not change the deliciousness nor texture.  Great balance of flavors, not difficult to make at all.  Thanks for posting, I will use this recipe again!!

I checked the written recipe again just now because something has to be wrong. I read reviews of recipes. I'm an experienced cook (and baker) and after a lot of prep (chopping cranberries, zesting and juicing oranges) these taste horrible! I cannot taste any orange at all and the cranberries are as bitter as if I ate them plain. I'm more than disappointed since this flavor combination is my child's favorite and these were going to be breakfast. I have dogs who love my baking but the bitterness overrules, these are going in the trash.
Excellent!  The whole batch was gone in 1 day in my house.  The kids loved them. I added peanut butter mini chips - perfect.

I made this as is, and it was perfect. I did not see a need to increase the baking powder, since there is also baking soda in the recipe. We are in Massachusetts, and well, cranberries ARE tart, ha ha. This is quick and easy to throw together, the ratios and measurements are easy to remember, and my family eats them up! Make it as is (easy) before tinkering...

I've made these with regular all-purpose flour and they are terrific, but I have a story to tell. The second time I started making them, I noticed I had some Gold Medal Better for Bread flour leftover from some other recipe. I thought "Meh, flour is flour, why not." The result wasn't a batter, but more of a cookie dough. I used a cookie scoop to portion into the greased muffin cups and baked according to direction. The dough conformed to the muffin cups, while baking. The result was a more solid and just as moist muffin with crispy, sweet peaks, not smooth like with a wet batter. I've made them this way, ever since.
i vegan-ized these by using ground flax instead of an egg, turned out great!  thanks <3

Great recipe! I did make a couple alterations after seeing other reviews. Like others, I used 2 tsp of baking powder instead of 1, and reconstituted 3/4 cup of Craisins in a cup of orange juice on the stove rather than using fresh cranberries.

I also added a really simple glaze after baking (1 cup icing sugar + 3 tablespoons of orange juice, whisked together and then drizzled over the warm muffins.)  I initially glazed half the batch and left the other half as is, but once I'd tried both, I went back and added glaze to the rest as well. My only quibble with the original recipe is that it was a little dry for my taste (and a little less sweet than I prefer), but the glaze improved it on both fronts. With it this recipe is 5 stars :)

Just made it. Used a stick of butter instead of oil and soaked the cranberries in orange juice and used 2 tsp of baking powder instead of one.  IT IS DELICIOUS! The best cranberry muffin!!!! Moist and just the right sweetness.

These are great! I made these and the only differences: I used self-rising flour (I got some by accident at the grocery store and decided to use it here) and I used dried cranberries that I soaked in a little brandy then microwaved for 1 1/2 minutes to rehydrate, then drain remaining brandy and use cranberries. I see people saying they were dry? Mine were not. When mixing the dry with the wet ingredients, really do it carefully and don't overmix. (I still saw a tiny bit of flour in places after I mixed them together.) With this type of dough, over mixing it will cause it to be too dry.

I love this recipe for its simplicity, but I just had to jazz it up. I started by simmering 1 cup of cranberries in the 3/4 cup of orange juice that I freshly squeezed, doubled the amount of orange zest, added cardamom, added 1 tbsp of fresh grated ginger and 1/2 cup of flax milk. I did need to add another 1/3 cup of flour to balance out the added liquid, but man on man were they good.

Seconding many of the reviews, these turned out incredibly after a few changes: Up the BP to 2 tsp, let the cranberries sit in an extra 1/4 c sugar while you're prepping everything else, and add 1 tsp vanilla extract. With these changes the muffins turned out super moist, flavorful, sweet/tart. Love this recipe!
Gorgeous orange color with cranberry gems. These were very good. Next time I will put more sugar on top because the cranberries were pretty tart.

I think the recipe is great! I read the reviews and tips and decided to try it before trying alternatives and I am glad I did. The only thing I recommend is an old trick...replace oil with equal amount of applesauce. Reduces calories and fat significantly.

This recipe just didn't work out well for me. I don't mind that they aren't that sweet but that could definitely be an issue for some. If you have lactose intolerant friends then go with this recipe. I think I prefer recipes with milk and butter. These cooked faster than the written time, scorched in some places. And, no, I'm not an inexperienced baker. So meh on the recipe over all.

These are great! I used half whole wheat flour and half AP. I live in a really dry climate and when I started mixing, I knew they would be too dry, so I added a little more liquid. The second time I made them, I added a 1/4 cup of cooked quinoa and they were brilliant! These were plenty sweet for me and I didn't sprinkle them with sugar.

I tweaked the recipe with recommendations from prior bakers, but I have another one to solve the problem of too tart cranberries. Craisins! To rehydrate them, put the cup of craisins in a microwave safe bowl with a teaspoon of water. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap, and put a few slts in the top for release of steam. Microwave on high for 30 seconds, then set aside to cool. Drain the craisins, and put in a paper towel lined bowl to dry them.

I really liked these, but would have liked more orange flavor. I think next time, instead of vanilla extract, I'll use orange extract. I used Craisins and rehydrated them in orange juice, as I really love the combination of orange and cranberry flavors. I like how moist these muffins came out and that they aren't overly sweet like the cranberry orange muffins you get from a mix. I doubled the recipe, wanting 24 muffins, but wound up with 41, which is not a problem, except for my waistline. :P Thank you for the wonderful recipe!

Delicious . I used butter instead of oil and turbinado sugar instead refined sugar. I read other posts that mentioned that the cranberries were too tart, so I added 2 tbsp of brown sugar to the freshly washed fresh cranberries and that helped with that. When I ate one still warm and fresh out the oven, the cranberries were tart but...... once they cooled they were ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!!!!! The tartness was very mild and the muffin perfect. Next time I make these I will add more fresh cranberries.

Reduced sugar and rehydrated dried cranberries to half a cup each in order to reduce carb count a little. Also followed Chef Wahoo's baking powder adjustment. Muffins had a super nice flavour and while they were still around 30g carbs, they were worth it - big hit for sure - would recommend!

I doubled the cranberries and tripled the orange and made 9 instead of 12 muffins per recipe as I like a large muffin top. As others have said I also doubled the baking soda. I really like these but you do need to adjust to taste as I love the tartness of cranberries and other on here seem to find them to tart. I you want a sweeter cranberry soak them in sugar for 10-15 minutes before hand.
I had to keep them in longer because of our altitude. I've made them twice, once with apple juice and once with tangerines. Delicious both times. I can hardly wait to add green chile.

Absolutely thankful I found this recipe. Muffins turned out moist cake-like texture. I let the dried cranberries soak for 1 hr in warmed OJ. Pressed most of juice from berries, added a little more juice and blended w/dry ingreds. I also added 1 addtl tsp of bkg soda. Definitely a baker's and a crowd pleaser.

Made these again this morning for the 4th time! Delicious! I used fresh squeezed clementines/zest (it's what I had) instead of orange juice/zest - amazing! I also used half the sugar in the recipe and still came out sweet enough for our tastes. Definitely going into the recipe box!

These were good but not great. Needs more sugar I think, and I used dried cranberries, didn't love it like that... maybe soaking them like other commenter said would work. Mine were also dry BUT I have read that making a moist muffin has a LOT of other dependant things... so I won't blame the recipe (I didn't over stir, read that buttermilk makes more moist)
I used fresh crans, avocado oil and added 1/2 c of white choc chips. Doubled the zest as well. The bomb!
First time so I made the muffins per recipe extra backing soda, with dried cranberries and OJ. They were moist. Very good.
i just baked a batch of these muffins..... They were delish!
my muffins came out dry i made 6 large ones and baked them 20 min help please

Fantastic with 2nd Attempt. Our "perfect" cranberry Orange muffins were achieved using some ideas from other reviewer posts (Thank You so much!) plus an additional tweak of mine. First batch was very dry and over baked. Recipe Changes from the original recipe: Chopped cranberries - added 1/4 cup sugar; let them sit while preparing the rest of the recipe. 2 teaspoons baking powder 2-3 teaspoons Orange rind Orange Pineapple banana juice replaces Orange juice Coconut oil replaces vegetable oil. (I used Nutiva organic cold pressed), My oven has always run hot; I always reduce my cooking/ baking temperature by 25 degrees from whatever a recipe calls for. I used a dark coated muffin pan; so in theory, the first batch should have been fine at 350. However the first batch of muffins was 'parched'. I found that baking at 300 for 18 minutes resulted In baked through muffins that retained their moisture. Hoping this will help anyone else who may have had a similiar experience.

March muffins...no fresh cranberries. I used a can of whole canned cranberries. I make banana nut muffins every week, but thought these sounded good so I thought I'd try. Using the canned berries the batter was very loose...I thought too loose so I used an extra 1/2 cup of flour and added an extra 1/2 teaspoon of baking powder. The muffins were in the over at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes. The orange flavor was nicely prominent, less so with the cranberries. Given that I was flying by the seat of pants without fresh berries I opted not to add nuts because I hadn't made the recipe before. (I know the recipe didn't call for nuts) However, without fresh berries I felt the muffins would have benefited by adding nuts because of the mouth feel. The other thing I'm not successful with is adding the sugar to the top - I know what it SHOULD look like, but it just melts into the batter - maybe I have to let the muffins set up a bit and add the sugar later during the baking time. I actually was very happy with the results, but would like to try again with fresh berries.

ohhhh my GOSH! These are now my fav muffins! This is my 3rd dozen in as many weeks, and I've eaten nearly everyone of them. I guess I better slow down or It's going to show on my waistline! I'm using frozen cranberries and they taste delish. I actually put more than the recipe calls for -like 1 1/2 cups I also bought the crystals to go on top...I mix 1/4 c. of the sugar & zest of 1/2 orange! It is YUMMY gotta run! I'm almost ready to put them in the oven!!! Oh yeah! It smells soooo good in our house for the entire day!
For those who prefer to use dried cranberries/craisins: Use about 1/2 to 2/3 c. of craisins and let them plump up a bit in the orange juice called for in the recipe. They are available year-around.
I used Bob's gluten free flour mixture and they came out perfectly. With a few tweaks. And remember, never, ever overmix muffin batter!

1. Substituted oil for butter. 2. Doubled amount of baking powder. 3. Used WHOLE FRESH cranberry. Did not soak it. Added a little bit more berries, I love them. 4. Added zest of 1 whole orange and still barely can taste it. 1 tsp is too little. 5. Started at 400F, then lowered to 350. Checked twice. LOVE IT!
I'm not sure why but there wasn't much flavor.

I changed it: instead of oil I used one stick melted butter. The batter came out like cookie dough so I added about 1/4 cup skim milk. Finally, I made a thin glaze to drizzle over the top of the baked muffins using more orange juice and powdered sugar mixed together. It helped because these muffins were not sweet enough. Next time I'd use more cranberries and maybe orange flavoring. Or, I'd make a cream cheese frosting. Yum! I was expecting a tarter, sweeter muffin but there are tweaks you can easily make to get that! P.S. these are dessert not breakfast so that is why I wanted them sweeter.
This is an excellent recipe. However, I did find the orange flavor was very subtle and, to compensate for this, I add a generous amount of orange rind, probably 3 tsp. or more.

I happened upon this recipe today and decided since I had all the ingredients on hand, I would try it.  I don't usually have soup this time of year too much but the recipe appealed to me. I'm glad I did.  I really enjoyed this for dinner tonight.  Very easy to do.  I made it while running back and forth watching the Portugal/Holland Soccer game.  I followed the directions except I added garlic and a little basil. And I liked that it was good for phase 1 of the SB Diet.  I have done that diet and it is wonderful.  Thanks, Tara for a great recipe and Good Luck on your diet.

This recipe was so easy to make, and it tastes great, especially the next day when the flavors have really blended.  Next time I'll use a little more broth, to make it more soupy - but it's fine just as it is.
Easy to fix, great tasting with good flavor.

Very easy and comforting soup.  I sauteed my onions with the ground beef and added garlic, also.  My tomatoes were petite diced with garlic and olive oil.  (I don't like big chunks of stewed tomato.)  I added a second can of beef broth, as there just didn't seem to be enough liquid, and adjusted the seasoning amounts in accordance with the added liquid.  I also added about 1/2 cup of tomato juice to enhance the flavor.  There weren't any red kidney beans in my pantry...so I used white beans.  Hubby had 2 bowls of this soup with some crusty multi-grain dinner rolls.  I plan on taking the leftovers for my lunch.  This is a simple, but tasty soup.

This was very easy and inexpensive since I was looking to use up these ingredients. I found it a little bland - but I think that the ingredients made my thoughts turn to chili .... 

I added garlic salt and some cayene pepper and that brightened it right up. 

Additionally ( since it made a lot ) I added some frozen mixed veggies on day 3 and morphed it into vegetable soup - very good as well. 

An excellent soup and a really good base for a lot of other things, minestrone, veggie, chili etc. 

Thanks for a great recipe.

Excellent recipe! This is a soup that looks and tastes like you've spent all day preparing it. The only change that I made was to add a can of black eyed peas instead of the kidney beans. Thanks for sharing!

This was a very easy recipe to make.  I always follow recipes exactly as written, and did so with this one as well, but found it a bit bland for our taste and added extra pepper and some salt.  Being cabbage lovers, I put in more than the recipe called for and I also had to add two more cans of broth.  This is a great soup and I definitey plan to make it again.  Thanks Tara.

This is a delicious soup. I really love kidney beans so I couldn't resist trying this recipe. I'm glad I did. I added a little sugar because my family likes some sweetness when tomatoes are involved. I will definitely make this again. Thanks a lot for sharing!

This soup made a delicious and filling lunch that we really enjoyed.  We'll make this again and I think that I will brown the onions with the beef for extra flavor and maybe add some extra broth or even tomato sauce because it was sooo thick (more like a stew than a soup).  This goes together quickly and would be great for a week night meal if pre-shredded cabbage were used (I shredded my own this time).  Thanks for a great low-carb meal!

This is a great soup!  I made it WW friendly by using 8oz Cooked lean ground beef and sub the thyme and bay leaf with 1 T worscheshire (sp) sauce and 2 T splenda (personal preference) this is 3 pts for 1 cup and is a core recipe!  Thanks for sharing!!!!
simple, easy, fun (for some reason I love chopping cabbage), and good! I added celery and garlic, and spiced it up some more with cumin, chili powder, and salt.

this was very good.  I didn't have he thyme or bay leaf, so i left them out, used a can of italian diced tomatoes since i couldn't find stewed - used up some purple cabbage from my CSA that otherwise would have gone bad.  Simple, easy, and tasty.  Thanks for posting

This is the same recipe I use from Sandra Woodruff's Good Carb Cookbook, except she uses 12 oz. of lean ground beef. I added a chopped clove of garlic and canellini beans instead of red kidney beans, and some boullion granules and extra water because we like our soup to be more liquidy. I've made this simple soup many times and it's always good.
Love this soup. When I make it I add chopped up baby carrots (which I pre-cook in the microwave for a few minutes) and a can of Rotel tomatoes to spice it up a bit.

Yummy!  This are so good and easy to put together.  I was looking for a healthier waffle and was very happy to find these.  I think I like these better than the regular ones I've made (which surprised me a little!).  Thanks so much for posting!
I found these a little on the bland side. "like Eggo waffles"? Not quite. The addition of 3/4 tsp. salt and a couple Tbsp. syrup to the batter made them closer to Eggos and more flavorful.

These waffles are delicious!  I was afraid that using all whole wheat flour would make them very dense, but they had great texture and wonderful flavor.  I used 4-1/2 Tbsp. of Ener-G egg replacer mixed in with the dry ingredients, then added an extra 3/4 c. soy milk to make up for the egg volume, and used a whole teaspoon of salt. I forgot to add the oil, but no matter - they were delicious anyway, and I probably won't even bother with it in the future. The recipe made 12 waffles for me.  I served them with unsweetened homemade applesauce and mixed berries.  My family was delighted - thanks for the great recipe Kelly!

I LOVED these waffles. The big difference is that I added 1/4 cup mini choc chips to the batter & it was wonderful! I use applesauce for the oil, Eggbeaters, skim milk & Splenda. They were great! I baked them for about 7 min to get them crunchy, the way I like them. Thanks so much!!!

These make a hearty, but light waffle that should please everyone. I used half wheat/white and added some vanilla. Thanks for posting, kelly!

Roxygirl

These were amazing!  I added one tbsp of cinnamon and one tbsp of vanilla to the recipe.  I used your idea of making extra, underbaking them and freezing them.  I tried them in the toaster for lunch and they were still perfect!  I will definitely be making these again.  Thanks for posting your recipe!

These were great! They are so filling and taste great. I used apple sauce in place of the oil and skim milk and splenda. I also added a bit of vanilla and cinnamon - so tasty! They were easy to make and everyone loved them - can't wait to make them again! Thanks for posting!
these were pretty good, but still a bit bland, IMO.  Will add a bit of vanilla next time.
These are the best for my daughter's breatfast. I've been making them and freezing them for a few months now. I also like to add cinnamon. She likes it when I spread a little applesauce on top.

1/4 cup honey in place of the sugar makes a softer waffle, but just as tasty and sugar-free. I enjoyed this recipe.

Second day:
I used 1/2 cup pumpkin puree in place of the oil and 1/4 cup honey in place of the sugar. It was lovely. Softer waffle again. This is a very versatile recipe.

Great waffles. Nice and healthy and great for the kids in the morning. I made them as directed, and I also made more to freeze. They froze well also, just make sure to let them cool completely before bagging. Thanks for posting.

Perfection!  My only sub was to use half sugar/half Splenda.  Remarkably light waffles for whole wheat.  For those who find whole wheat too heavy, try other brands.  There IS a big difference.  I use Prairie Gold by Wheat Montana (from Wal-mart) and it is a wonderful whole wheat.  Please don't confuse stone ground whole wheat with all whole wheat flours.

Very good for using whole wheat.  I used one egg and 1/2 c. egg whites, used splenda for the sugar. I used 1 c. of canned pumpkin in place of oil and 2 tsp. of pumpkin pie spice. wanted to make them as healthy and tastey as possible.  My husband liked them so much, he was eating them with nothing on them!  I would like to try this with applesauce in place of the oil and double the vanilla next time I make these. I will also add some fibersure to the recipe to see if I can't slip in some added fiber. I used approx. 2/3 c. of batter per waffle for my iron and bake them about 3-4 min. each.  Pretty easy to make too. I liked them even better the next day warmed in the toaster, which made them a little crispy on the outside. Thank you Kelly for a really good waffle recipe.

These were great -  they hit the spot for my waffle craving.  I substituted Splenda for the sugar and Egg Beaters for the eggs.  Served them w/ fresh blueberries and maple syrup.  Reheated leftovers in the toaster the next day.

Delicious!  Easy to make, very tasty and so much healthier than usual.  Try these topped with chopped strawberries.  I subbed buttermilk for regular milk and consequently added 1 teaspoon baking soda and reduced the baking powder to 2 tbsp.  Worked just fine. Will use again. Thanks!
These were wonderful.  We added fresh blueberries and they turned out delicious.
I used half whole wheat flour and half white flour. These baked up in the waffle iron fluffy and delicious. We topped with strawberries and fat-free cool whip, delicious.
These were pretty good. My husband I found that they blended better with fruit topping than regular maple syrup. Overall they were tasty and healthy, so that is always a plus. Thanks for posting.

Beautiful Waffles! I used 1 1/4c white flour, 3/4c wheat flour, 1/2c oat bran & 4 egg whites. I whipped up the egg whites first and cut the oil to 1/4c. These were great topped with fresh strawberries. It was wonderful to serve something healthier than bisquick! Thank you!

Can it be correct that this recipe requires 3 tablespoons baking powder?  I could taste it in the waffle and had to add more flour, oil, and milk to make it edible.  I have never seen any recipe w/ this much baking powder.  Is it a misprint?     
Other than this, it was a good recipe for my new waffle maker.

These were great waffles.  I added 1/4 cup of ground flax and some cinnamon.  Also, beat the egg whites separately and added at the very end.  Substituted brown sugar for white sugar.  My kids loved them.

This really is a great recipe!  Very versatile and provides a nice hearty crisp, there is nothing wimpy about this waffle.  Think another reviewer compared its consistency to that of an Eggo which is quite accurate.  I've added a number of extras to this recipe...mashed banana, applesauce, flax seed, oatbran, you name it....it still tastes wonderful.
These didn't get cripy at all, they were soggy. Used regular waffle maker. I must have done something wrong.

Taste great. It is not heavy at all, even though it was made with 100% whole wheat. I was looking for a crispy Belgian Waffle recipe, but it didn't turn out to be crispy for me for some reason. I will try again.

I was worried about heaviness, so I made it using 1 cup whole wheat flour and 3/4 cup white flour. The other 1/4 cup was wheat germ. It turned out really good! Next time I'll try just whole wheat and wheat germ. Maybe some flax meal too. Thanks!

I guess it must depend on your waffle maker, but these came out great on our Belgian Waffle Maker.  There was nothing "Eggo"-like about them.  They do taste "healthier" (i.e. less taste & more dry) than regular waffles, but it wasn't that significant.  I added a pinch of minature chocolate chips to each batch and that made them perfect! I also subbed 1/4 cup of ww flour with 2 Tbsp. each wheat germ & flax seed.  This made 6 large Belgian Waffles.  My 2 young sons LOVED them as did I!
Delicious! I am always ISO healthy waffles and these are pretty close. I took the suggestion of the last reviewer and subbed some wheat germ and flax. I'll be making these again. Thanks! :)
Made enough for about 4 people. I'd say double or quadruple it if you want enough. It was really good though. I subbed some flour for flax meal just to add some omegas and it turned out great!
My husband substituted egg whites and one egg, honey for the sugar, and light olive oil, and they were still *amazingly* good!  Thanks Bella!

I did not really like the outcome the first time I tried this recipe with 1/2 applesauce and 1/2 oil. The second time I used all applesauce, a tablespoon of oatmeal and wheat bran, and pumpkin pie spice and it improved greatly. They came out nice and crispy, just how I like them!

Perfect. I had gotten used to whole wheat just not tasting good, and relied on my family being hungry enough to eat anything. These waffles are actually TASTY. ?!?! And easy - other recipes had me whipping egg whites to get them fluffy. Thank you so much for posting!
Yum! I actually thought it was very fluffy for a 100% whole wheat waffle. I used applesauce instead of oil; the rest as written.

These are great.  I used whole wheat pastry flour.  I also separated the eggs and whipped the egg whites before folding them into the rest of the mixture.  Those changes made a very fluffy, light waffle, which is awesome for whole wheat.  Great results!  Next time I will add 1 teaspoon of cinnamon.  Will also try subbing oil with applesauce or pumpkin.  Thanks!

Fabulous! I didn't have high hopes for a whole wheat waffle recipe, but these were delicious and had a wonderful, light texture. I love that these were fast and easy to make and that I didn't have to separate eggs and whip egg whites. I used whole wheat pastry flour and ended up with 24 small Belgian waffles.

Very tasty. My first try at Belgian on 2-waffle maker -- lots of excess batter for me, so hoping refrigerating it works & will make more tomorrow. I liked plain with butter the best.  UPDATE: I halved the recipe (using 2 eggs) and it didn't seem to come out quite right, so next time I might try halving it using 1 egg.
Perfect waffles. Tasty and healthy, thanks for the great recipe!

I was pleasantly surprised at how good these turned out.  I did use white whole wheat flour (got it at King Arthur Flour) which gives results closer to white flour than ordinary whole wheat flour.  Still, I was expecting a heavy and grainy result, but instead got fluffy regular waffles.  Now, these are NOT as light as Belgian waffles made with white flour; they are more like the kind in the freezer section.  But, since I'm trying to go whole grain these days, I'm saying this recipe is a keeper.  Try it, you'll like it.

This will be my new go-to waffle recipe--I had these this morning and really liked how they turned out. They are not as dense as the description made them sound--I would call them "hearty" but not dense (I found them to be pretty airy actually, probably because they use more baking powder than my normal recipe). I was also pleased that they were so light given the use of only whole wheat flour. I cut the recipe by four, and it made 3 waffles; I also used melted butter instead of the oil, which might have helped it crisp up so much. Served with caramelized cinnamon apples--perfect fall breakfast!

WONDERFUL! For 2 adults, half a recipe is enough. I used 2 eggs for half recipe and would use 4 for a full one. We like the egg taste. Beat the eggs for 1 minute before adding the rest. Mix dry ingredients together before gradually adding to eggs and alternate with milk. They were very fluffy, crispy and much better than any batter mix of the market.

I was feeling lazy this morning and wanted a recipe using whole grain flour that didn't require me to separate and beat the yolks and whites separately. I used Bob's Red Mill Whole Wheat Pastry Flour in place of regular whole wheat flour. The amount of baking powder seemed off, and because I was almost out I only used one tablespoon of baking powder. My waffles came out light and fluffy with a great taste. Whole wheat flours vary immensely from brand to brand and depending on the density of the flour you might need to use all three tablespoons. of baking powder. I mentioned Bob's Red Mill Whole Wheat Pastry Flour by name because I've had great success in substituting it for white flour in most recipes ( I wouldn't use it in cakes where a fine crumb is desired). When using whole wheat flours it is important to let the batter sit for 10-15 minutes so the flour can absorb the liquid. Resist the urge to add more flour at first if the batter seems thin, it will get thicker with time.
These were great! Light and fluffy with good flavor.  Worked well with my waffle maker.  Thanks!
Excellent whole wheat waffle recipe.  Definitely the best I have had.  The whole family loved it.  I added mini chocolate chips for my kids & husband as a special treat.

LOVED IT--To me it was fluffy, yet dense at the same time,  Very filling  I used 2/3 cup of batter per waffle for my waffle maker.  I also halved the recipe (with 2 eggs).  They didn't come out as pretty as some of the pictures still, but rarely anything I make does :).  Delicious!  I have a few extra waffles and I am really hoping that they are going to freeze and reheat well,

We have a favorite whole-wheat waffle recipe but I needed one that made just a couple more.  This was excellent!  My only complaint is that mine didn't get crisp at all.  <br/><br/>We have a Belgian waffle maker and this made 7 or 8 (I lost count as my kids kept grabbing the ones I made!).

Excellent, healthy waffle recipe. I love that it's made with whole wheat flour. I also like that it doesn't have that much sugar. Once you put some pure maple syrup over them, it's plenty sweet enough! Thank you for posting.

Wonderful waffles, the first recipe I tried in my new Belgian waffle maker.  I made 5 servings with 1 egg for a trial batch.  They were not too dense and had some crunch, may cook them longer next time.  I subbed stevia for the sugar, light margarine melted for the oil and added a bit of multi grain hot cereal for crunch, more fiber and nutrients.  I am going to try subbing apple sauce or pumpkin for the oil as suggested in other comments.  Thanks for posting and for all the hints in the comments!

Surprisingly light and delicious! I tried this recipe with a new Belgian waffle maker and was delighted at the results. I used butter instead of oil and cooked them for 4-1/2 minutes each. I did not cook to a crisp As I like a sweet bread texture, and they were good in hand without syrup right off the grill. Healthy high fiber addition to any meal. Froze a few for on the go snack. Highly recommended.

I did this recipe for a diabetic. I used Organic Agave in place of the sugar. I only used 1. 1/4 cups of milk as the Agave is liquid. I used pure vanilla extract. With Agave, you use exact amount as sugar. This made very fluffy waffles and made 5- 8 inch circumference waffles.
These are awesome! First time using whole wheat flour for my family and they approve! Yay! So glad I found your recipe. I used 2 cups almond milk and 1/4 cup of coconut palm sugar.
Way too much baking powder. I think it should be 3 tsp. instead of 3 Tbsp. Also, they would be better with melted butter.
That much baking powder is inedible. Perhaps 3 teaspoons would work. My husband wanted to surprise us with breakfast. Shame for him to go to so much effort only to throw them away.
I used the 3 TSP baking powder recommended and beat the egg whites before adding them and my family said they were great. . . usually complain about whole wheat flour recipes!
You need to update this recipe. It should be 3 teaspoons, not 3 tablespoons of baking powder. I made a whole bunch of these waffles and they are disgusting. I’ll have to throw them all away now.
I’ve been making this weekly for the past couple of years and it NEVER disappoints!!! My kids devour them in seconds. Perfect as written.
Great taste delicious ??

Excellent as written! Kids absolutely loved them. I ended up doing 1 cup wheat flour, 3/4 cup unbleached white flour, and 1/4 oat flour...just for fun. I also increased the vanilla...because we LOVE it:) Thanks for the recipe!

This is a fantastic recipe as is, but I'm always looking to tweak to make things at least a 'bit' more healthy. I used unsweetened vanilla almond milk instead of regular milk. I used Truvia instead of the sugar, and I subbed apple sauce for the vegetable oil (sometimes I use combination of apple sauce and oil). Whether you tweak this or make this 'as is' the recipe is fantastic. For me, the recipe made 5 large Belgian waffles. Also, wait a bit before making the waffles. On AllRecipes.com, for one of their pancake recipes, they say waiting "allows the baking powder to form bubbles that will your pancakes fluffier and more tender."

Sue this was incredible. The chicken browned beautifuly, and left lots of great golden bits in the pan. I did need more oil for the onion, garlic stage. The smells were divine. I used Sultana raisins and let the whole thing simmer about 10 minutes so that the raisins got nice and plump. I then added the yogurt (1/2 of a small container)directly into the pan and it made the sauce nice and creamy(we don't like it on the side). Added some of the cilantro in the pan, but did use some to top off on the plate. Served with Basmati rice. The cilantro really makes a big difference here, I would not omit it, and fresh is the way to go. Thanks, BH who hates curry dishes, had two portions!

Absolutely delicious. I was hesitant on making it due to my non-curry loving husband but followed the recipe exactly except for using 1/2 the amount of curry and it turned out beautifully. It was thoroughly enjoyed by all. This is definately a keeper and I will be sure to make this again soon. Thanks Sue.

this recipe is wonderful!
i serve this up to my friends all the time and they always go back for third helpings!
thank you!
Very tasty, will definitely become a regular in our household.
Delicious basic curry.  I too stirred about a 1/2 cup of yogurt directly into the pan rather than serving it on the side, which resulted in a creamy sauce.  Thank you Sue for sharing the recipe.

if i could, i would give this dish a thousand stars!!! i am a cook at a restaurant, and i made this recipe x 3 for a lunch special.  it sold so fast i had to make a second batch x 3, and that sold out too!!! the best meal i have had in a while!!!

Good stuff!  Made per recipe, but used a cajun mix for my cayenne pepper (the mix contains mostly cayenne and a few other spices).  I also was out of yogurt and tomato paste, so I used sour cream and tomato sauce.  The chicken came out very tender and tasted great - with just the right amount of "kick" to it.  I'm not a huge fan of curry, but I had the craving.  This will be the recipe that I turn to if/when that craving comes around again!
Incredible! I added a can of drained chick peas  when I add the chicken stock and really enjoyed it!!!
This was really good. My wife gave it a big thumbs up also.

I've made this twice and both times I didn t' have any yogurt on hand, so we did without.  The results are still great.  The cilantro is a must.  The second time I made it, we were out of raisins so my wife handed me a bag of dried mangos and said to try it.  I chopped up an equal amount of the mangos and I think it turned out better than with the raisins!  Served it with jasmine rice.

Oh my!  This is much better than I expected- not that I doubted you!  Better than restaurant chicken curry so fast?  It made my day.  I'm even thinking about making it again tomorrow.  I used E.V.O.O. instead of canola oil, didn't add the raisins and I stirred the yogurt in before serving instead of adding it on top.  Thank you, thank you, thank you!

This was great!!! Delicious!!! Cooking curries always take a while. But this was quick and simple with ingredients that you could get hold of easily. Thanks to the flour coating you do not have to worry about thickening the sauce when the dish simmers(saves time), AND it makes the chicken a wonderful golden brown when fried. The chicken was succulent and the spices were a great combination. I just upped the curry a bit to fit our taste. The fresh coriander/cilantro is a MUST. It does all the difference!!! I had to use soy yoghurt (provamel) because my boyfriend is lactose intolerant (cannot eat any milk products). This dish is doubly great since there is no butter and I was able to stir the yoghurt in afterwards so it did  not clot/clash, like it always does if it even simmers. It worked great!!!  My boyfriend was so glad that he finally could have a creamy indian curry. I will definitely cook it again but I am thinking about adding some vegs, bell pepper &/or mushrooms etc. for variety and vitamins next time.

Yum, yum -- wanted to try this recipe because there was no "toasting" of the spices so the whole house did not smell of curry. It was quick, the instructions excellent and the taste divine -- had only 1 chicken breast so made up the difference with boneless chicken thighs
This curry was delicious.  Easy and quick to prepare.

This is THE BEST quick chicken curry recipe. It was so good we almost ended up eating the chicken pieces after browning alone! LOL. I didn't have any raisins so I omitted those. I also doubled the curry spice and the cayenne pepper, hubby and I love spicy-hot! I LOVE cilantro which I ended up using a lot of. Everything else was left the same. The results? DELICIOUS and very versatile. Thank you so much.
I think I would add more curry powder myself, but the overall taste was very good.

I loved this for a fast curry fix!  The chicken was nice and tender, and dredging it before cooking made a nice thick sauce.  I did add about 3 x the curry powder and 2x the cayenne.  Once the curry was finished I added a tbsp of splenda to mellow out the sauce.  Thank you Sue L this is going right in my cookbook!

This recipe was a WINNER in our household - even for my 77 yr old dad who doesn't care to try "new" foods. 
Since I'm not an experienced cook, this was not a fast dish for me.  It took close to an hour from kitchen counter to table (just cutting up, coating and cooking the chicken took over 30 minutes...).  No speeding ticket here but some happy faces at the dinner table!;)THANK YOU for posting!

This was wonderful, very quick and easy to make and the flour coating on the chicken made for a rich, thick sauce.  I used chopped chicken thighs and doubled the recipe without any problems.  The sweetness of the raisins complimented the spicy curry.   This is definitely a keeper, thanks for posting!
Loved all the flavors of this recipe.  I used chicken thighs and it took me longer than 20 minutes, but it turned out delicious. I will make this again.
Love this recipe! Have made it many times. I like to add aparagus for something different.
great and easy. my husband loves curry chicken and this is the first time i have made it for him. he loved it thanks to you.

This was GREAT!  I was in the mood for Thai food and just really enjoyed this chicken.  As another suggested, I added the yogurt to the sauce after removing it from the heat.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly.  I served this with Thai Coconut Rice Recipe #63446 and Asparagus With Lemon and Mint Recipe #126827.  It was such a wonderful meal.  Thanks so much, I'll be making this again!
Delicious and quick - will definitely cook this again!

I was skeptical about this dish, but it really is a delicious Indian curry that only takes 20 minutes!  My husband even loved it and he is incredibly picky.  The plain yogurt really makes the dish - don't omit it!  I love the way it brings out the raisins and spices.

I loved this curry... so simple and quick...the sweetness of the raisins mixed with the heat of the curry (which is not to bland, not to hot, but just right i might add ) was wonderful... i will definately be making this again and again
Best cuury I've ever had hands down, So tasty, spiced just right, and the golden  raisins were brilliant!
We enjoyed this curry dish, it had good flavors and was easy to make.

I enjoyed this recipe's quickness and ease.  Since I am a huge curry fan, I ended up tripling the curry and I used thighs instead of breasts (since that's all I had).  But, a very good recipe and something I will make again with a few minor changes.  Thanks!

This was excellent!  First time cooking curry and I am so glad I picked this recipe.  It was easy to prepare and very tasty.  Did cut down on the cayenne to begin with but will continue to add more as the kids adjust to the heat.   The family loved it.  Even my picky young daughter enjoyed it.
Both my DH and I have really enjoyed this recipe! I left out the raisins, but did everything else just like the recipe said. This makes a super-easy, fast, and delicious dinner.
This was wonderful. The whole family (and the boyfriend) liked it. I added more veggies (green bell pepper and mushroms) and threw in the yogurt while it was still cooking. Yum!
This method is brilliant!  One of the best innovations I've come across in ages (i.e., shaking the chicken in the spiced flour).  It looks pretty with some red bell pepper and green beans thrown in.

A flavorful recipe, but both my husband and I found it too spicy/hot. It was a brand new bottle of curry powder so maybe that was a factor. We just finished eating this and I had to rate it right away.  This is absolutely amazing.  I had a curry craving for a while and this quelched it! His complements for my cooking generally don't exceed a "pretty good" and for this meal he hasn't stopped raving.  A million thanks!

Excellent recipe and so easy too.  I also mixed the yogurt and cilantro into sauce at end instead of serving on the side.  Very flavorable and the raisins are so good (I might add a tad more next time because I like the contrast so much.) I will be making this for company in a few weeks. Thanks!

Delicious.  I have made this several times now.  I used about 3 small chicken breasts in this recipe, & enough curry to coat the surface of the chicken in the pan.  I omitted the raisins and yogurt and it still tasted good. I agree that cilantro is a must in this recipe, and could even be increased to about 1/3 cup.
This was a little spicier than I had thought it would be.  When I make it again I will mix the yogurt in the end like other reviewers suggested.

I never wrote a review but this one went right into my regular dinner menu, we eat it all the time, at least once every two weeks and even my step-mom who is african and grew up on traditional curry loved it!

Yum! I didn't have golden raisins, so I used regular ones, and I didn't have any cilantro so I just left that out completely. This was still very good, and so quick. I would love to add some vegetables and serve it over rice. We will make this again!

I was hoping for a spicier curry, but as far as easy goes, this is spectacular. Added extra cayenne and curry powder. I did add a little cinnamon and some peas and let the broth boil longer to let the raisins get tender. Put yogurt in the sauce and mixed it in with the rice at the end. I will definitely make this again but hope to find something to add some kick for next time.
I didn't know how I would feel about Curry, but I LOVE this recipe!!!!!!!!  I have two girls 6 and 2 and they along with my husband ate this up like it was the next best thing!!

Wonderful one pot wonder!  Only change I made was I used chicken thighs because I think they are better for curries and much tender.  The sauce was yummy and for the small amount of curry it gave lots of flavour.  Thank you Sue L

Quick and easy and full of flavour, great dish that even the DM (mention curry and she runs a mile, so we tell her it is buttered chicken), well she ate the lot up and was looking for seconds and even the DH says he'll have that one again (high praise indeed)  Thank you Sue L, made as a recipenap for Swapp #22 November 2008.

I have to agree w/ everyone else. My Indian hubby enjoyed. I do have curry powder on hand but lowered the amt - curry powder is not typically used by Indian households. I added a dash of cumin powder and tomatoes into the sauce. Delicious.

Awesome curry recipe!  I made it without the yogurt and cilantro, didn't have any on hand...but it was still so good!  I have tried several curry recipes, and the others all turned out badly, you should definitely try this one, can't go wrong.
Wow this was delicious!! One of the best curry recipes I have stumbled across :) I had never tried dalloping yogurt on anything, and decided to give it a go this time... oh man it was wonderful!

This is one of the best meals I have ever made!!!  I used only 1/4 the onions and 1/2 the garlic due to family taste.  The raisins are hidden no one could figure out what they were, but they balance out the spicy very well.  We LOVED this meal!

Great flavor and extremely quick, just as advertised.  My sensitive taste-bud spouse suggested that some mild-mouthed folks might want to go lighter on the onion and for those that are not having to watch fat/calories whole yogurt on this dish is a wonderful upgrade. (P.S.  Just the dry mixture ingredients make a great fast-fry coating if you are using cubed breast meat, it's hard to keep oneself from snitching pieces of chicken (already fully cooked)

OK, so I didn't make this in a hurry. All I had were chicken thighs on the bone so I slow cooked them in a deep pan on the stove. I doubled the sauce and boiled it down till it became thick. The indian flavors were intense and wonderful. I also served this with Afghanistan potatoes # 214966 (I combined countries and flavors). They worked well together.

This was really great.  My husband, who does not like curry and was not looking forward to this meal (I could tell), ended up saying it was very good.
