Served with basmati rice - it was a great meal.  :-)  Thanks for a keeper!

My DS wanted Curry for his B'day so this was my first time to make it and it was excellent. I added extra broth and tomato paste, as we like lots of sauce. I served it wih jasmine rice, Recipe #8948, and Recipe #60449. My DS says it was 2star spicy -just the way he likes it. It took more than 20 mins, but any time dinner takes less than an hour is great!

This is my new favorite Chicken Curry recipe. I added a bit of heavy cream to the sauce (didn't have any yogurt), used olive oil instead of canola, and left out the tomato paste. We tend to like ours with a little more sauce so I added extra broth for that, and the cream thickened it nicely. My goodness I can't wait to make it again. Thanks so much for posting this wonderful recipe!! The flour mixture on the chicken really really made a difference in the taste.
Great, quick curry. Served it with rice and veggies. It's good for you, too.

This recipe is AMAZING! It tastes just like what you would get in a restaurant.  I subbed olive oil for canola, and used just a drizzle instead of the full amount.  I also used red pepper flakes instead of cayenne becasue I was out. Finally, I actually added the yogurt at the end and mixed it in instead of using it for garnish.  Sooo delicious, and leftovers were even better!

really good! i found it a bit too hot but used only 2 chicken breasts.  the flavour was really nice. definately would make again with the right measurements of chicken! very fast. (didn't use raisins b/c didn't have any)
Excellent and easy, what more can you ask for?  Make exact as directed with the exception that I add a little more than a dallop of yogurt.  We will make this again.
easy....and delicious

It was a good thing I had to feed the family.  I could have stood over the pan and ate the whole meal myself.  This ROCKED Sue:) I have wanted to try this for a long time but hesitant b/c of the curry with my family. They loved it. My 4 and 2 y.o. ate it. This says alot.  I decreased the cayenne pepper, added more garlic and followed Nat Da Brat's recommendations. You should definitely put the yogurt and some of the cilantro in the sauce. I love the sweetness of the raisins.  This was awesome. I will double the sauce next time. Try it!
good recipe, but you don't need all that salt. I would cut it in half for sure. The chicken came out really tender. Will do this one again.
Mmmm, Mmmm, Good!!!  What a great recipe and I must say this is one of the best combination of ingredients I've tasted from a curry dish.  Thanks so much!!!

I doubled this recipe to take to a potluck dinner with guests from Bangladesh in attendance (ah, the nerve!), and they all said it was good.  I liked it too.  I used 3T of curry powder, and just 3C of rice (to fit my casserole dish).

Love this recipe, quick and easy way to get used to making curry.  After making it twice, I started throwing the curry together without checking with the recipe and instinctive measurements with great results.  I do tend to forget to add the raisins when I'm not reading off the recipe when I make it though, as those were a new curry ingredient for me.  Got to start remembering them, because they bring a lovely, mellow sweetness to the curry.
Awesome dish! Easy and delicious. My new favorite!

thanks for a great recipe.  I made this tonight & had to double the recipe as everyone in the family commented on how great it smelled as it cooked.  I will definitely make this again.  I may add spinach to get some greens in the diet.
This was delicious!  It was easy as far as curries go, and it had lots of great flavors.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!

A lifesaver!  I planned to make my usual curry chicken, which takes 1.5 hours.  I had a busy day and got delayed in starting the meal.  Jumped on 'zaar and found this VERY reasonable facsimilie.  I just made few adjustments for personal preferences and voila...only 20 minutes later we had a mouthwatering dinner. Thanks for this great dish!

Great recipe!  I am Indian and have always found it difficult to cook Indian food, but this recipe was easy to understand and I had most of the ingredients in my kitchen cupboard!  I omitted the raisins and substituted 1 cup of water for the chicken broth.  Like the other reviewers, I added the yogurt and cilantro directly into the pan.  This dish was delicious.  Thank you!  :)

Outstanding recipe! Me, my wife, and our two teenagers all loved it. I however used pork instead of chicken. I too added the yogurt to the pan but omitted the cilantro altogether. I didn't have any and I'm not the fan of it that many seem to be. Thanks for sharing.
Really delicious!  Using the full amount of cayenne made a VERY spicy curry.  I may cut back next time.
We loved it! I added some green pepper, and potatoes to the dish to make it more hearty for my family. Thanks for the recipe!

my boyfriends son wanted to try makin curry. we had never made and sure i haven't tried it before. served over orzo.  everyone loved! asked the kids if this was something they would eat again if i made it and i got 100% yes!! quick meal that the kids can get involved in. simple, and about all things i usually have on hand except for golden grapes. oh, i totally nixed the yogurt as my man doesn't like it and also nixed cilantro as the kids and i are not that bigga fans of the stuff. thanks a ton Sue!!
I found this very easy to make and so yummy

Very delicious. I used a bouillon cube in water in place of the broth, and omitted the salt, it worked out beautifully. I also didnt have any cilantro, so i tossed in some coriander seeds with the onion, it gave it a great spiciness.

We really liked this recipe. It's super easy and super tasty! :) I followed the recipe with the exception of using veg. broth instead of chicken broth. My BIL and DH (both South Asian) really enjoyed this dish as did I! I love that it's quick and authentic-tasting! Will most definitely make again!
We liked this one.  The raisins are a nice touch.  Don't leave out the garnish, the yogurt and cilantro really make it.

This was honestly the best chicken curry recipe I have encountered. The only variance for my dish was the lack of raisins. Everything else was the same, and the result was fabulous. Thank you for sharing!

This is a VERY good recipe with JUST the right amount of HEAT. I added carrots and potatoes and omitted the raisins. This recipe NEEDS the sweetness though so I added some sugar and it was perfect.So if you dont like raisins its ok just add some sugar or some type of sweetener to balance the strength of the curry powder. I used McCormick brand Curry powder. I try to stay away from the 99cent spices as they just don't taste as good. The stickiness and texture comes out perfect with the chicken broth (you may need to add water to cook the carrots and potatoes until soft) I highly recommend that you use jasmine rice. If your not good at making rice do this. Add 1 cup rice and 2 cups of water to a pot. Dont rinse it. Turn on the flame, and wait for it to boil, wait 5 minutes, cover and lower the heat to low. By the time the curry is done the rice will be PERFECT! Thanks Sue!

I made this for supper this evening.  I'd never made a curry before but I had all the ingredients except raisins (and I don't like raisins anyway) and I needed a fast supper.  I also didn't have the yogurt but I did stir about 1/4 cup of heavy cream into the sauce before serving.  That gave it a great creamy taste.  I asked my husband to rate it, though I knew it would probably be a 4 in his book since only Mexican food gets a 5 star rating from him.  You could have knocked me over with a feather.  He gave it a 5.  

This is definitely a keeper.

My first attempt at making a curry dish at home and it was so simple.  I agree with another reviewer the recipe needs the sweetness of the raisins.  I also added a small bit of brown sugar to balance out the heat.  Will repeat often.
Very tastey. Very fast. What more could you want?

Wonderful! I made this for my 80 year old mother, who was quite the cook back in her day, and we both loved it! Back in the '60's mom used to copy Julia Childs recipes from her show in shorthand so she knows good, easy recipes when she tastes them. Make sure you use a good quality curry powder. It makes a huge difference.

This is absolutely one of the best recipes I've found on recipezaar!! My family asks for it every single week. We skip the raisins, because no one in my family likes them. I serve this over coconut jasmine rice, and top with toasted coconut. Of course, I have to double the recipe to feed everyone, so it takes a little longer than 20 minutes, but it is SO worth the wait!! Just fantastic!

little tip, turn the heat down on the chicken before adding the curry powder or it starts smoking and you do NOT want to breathe that. i used sour cream instead of yogurt as that's what i had and omitted the raisins and cilantro because i don't like them. doubled the curry powder since mine was really mild. turned out very tasty! next time i think i'll add some mushrooms and broccoli.

This was so good. The only change was tomato sauce for the tomato paste. The raisins add just the right amount of sweetness.  I served it over rice and the sauce was very tasty. I loved the addition of the yogurt. It really was very fast. Thank you for posting.

I chose this recipe as one of my first forays into actual cooking and I'm so glad I did! Not only is it pretty easy and very tasty but it's also fairly idiot proof. The only thing I discovered is that coating the chicken was easier dredging than in a bag since when the bag got wet (from the chicken) the flour mix stuck to it.

loved it! my 2 year old twin daughters ate this! i added mushrooms and colored bell peppers and i substituted sour cream for yogurt. i also stirred a little in the sauce for a creamier effect, very tasty!
Absolutely fantastic!!  Followed the recipe exactly (minus the raisins).  Great spicy flavor.  Will definitely be hanging on to this in my "keeper" file :)
Wonderful!  I doubled the recipe and served it with rice and loved it!
I love it!  There is some spice to it.  I made 10 servings and left out the raisins.  I will be making chicken curry again.

Oh my, this is dee-licious! I am always skeptical with trying dishes with curry, as they never  come out to my expectations, but this was amazing! I added some cumin to the chicken, and added the requested amount of curry and then some when everything was simmering. I also added mushrooms to the mix. I served it over mixed greens and a side of Basmati rice, and it is so juicy and flavorful. I will definitely make this again. Thanks for a keeper!
Pretty tasty and very aromatic. I think I'll play around with the ingredients but this recipe def. was easy to follow and was quick which was awesome! Thanks for posting

That was AMAZING!!!! - I followed the recipe exactly except I made it a bit lower in fat and Sugar:  I used 1/4 cup sultana raisins instead of 1/3. I also used cooking spray instead of the oil. Lastly, as recommended by the others, I added the coriander and yogurt during the simmering phase along with some Mushrooms. SOOOO GOOD - Going to be in my cookbook for sure!

Definitely a 5-star recipe. Next time I make this, I will probably skip the salt in the flour due to the saltiness of the chicken base I used for my broth. Bought madras (hot) curry powder and it was soooo good. Did not use the raisins - I just don't like fruit in meat dishes; did not use the cilantro because I forgot to buy it; and forgot to add a dollop of yogurt and it was still superb! I served it over white rice cooked in coconut milk. Perfect!
Loved this recipe!  I used dark raisins instead of golden, but followed the recipe exactly otherwise.  It was delicious!  I will be adding this to the regular dinner rotation.
I have made this recipe several times now, and it's always a favorite! We skip the raisins and add lots of veggies like mushrooms, extra onions, corn or broccoli. Thanks for posting!!

I've made this recipe 3 times, and both my husband and I love it! I also put the cilantro and yogurt directly into the sauce as others have mentioned. A perfect amount of spiciness when paired with rice. I made this along with sugar snap peas cooked in a bit of oil with garlic, ginger, salt and pepper.

Super easy!  I cut the cayenne down to 1/8 tsp for my kids, who fear spicy food, and added a cup of frozen peas as a veggie.  The tomato paste & raisins made it a little sweet, which probably would be offset if I had included more cayenne.  Everyone asked for seconds!  Will make again.

This was awesome! I used skinless boneless chicken thighs instead of breasts. I omitted the cilantro and raisins, and I just used a pinch of cayenne to keep the heat down. I also stirred the yogurt into the curry when it was done. And as others suggested, doubling the curry powder did make it great.

This was so delicious!  My hubby said it's better than restaurant Indian food.  Even my kids loved it.  I made a 3-4 times the amount of sauce for a triple batch of chicken: 3 lbs chicken breast (this was a LOT of chicken w/ 3Tbs curry powder, next time I'd do half chicken and half beans and add a head of cooked cauliflower right into the sauce at the end since the sauce seems to beg for some creamy soft cauliflower), 6 oz can of tomato paste, 4 cups of chicken broth, 3 onions, 5 Tbs minced garlic (we love garlic), no cayenne pepper, 2/3 c. regular raisins, wish I had more cilantro since it added a nice bright flavor, the plain nonfat yogurt added a delicious creaminess to it and everyone reached for more yogurt to mix-in.  Flouring the chicken in the plastic bag was really worth the extra step, the chicken stayed very moist with slight breading-like interesting texture (used white whole wheat flour).  Delicious!  Did take me an hour to make but I made a huge batch, for us it's enough for 2 full meals which is just perfect.  Served with brown jasmine rice from Trader Joe's and peas.  Thanks for the awesome recipe!
For as easy as it was to prepare, this was a pretty good curry.  I mean, it's not going to replace my proper "take forever to make" curry recipe, but as the name suggests, it was good in a hurry :)
Excellent and easy.  Has a wonderful flavor all its own, not a typical curry. Raisins give it a nice hint of sweet amid the spice.  My wife loved it.  Definite keeper.

What a Fabulous Dish!  I made this last night, and my boyfriend said it's the best dish I've ever cooked for him!  He couldn't stop complimenting the dinner!  I did double the cayenne pepper and curry powder as previously suggested, and also added the yougurt and cilantro to the simmering pan versus serving them as a garnish.  Thanks so much for a keeper!

Very nice. I used garam masala instead of curry powder. Right amount of spiciness, and all. I left out the golden raisins and yogurt because I didn't have them, but it was still excellent. I gave it four stars instead of five, because the children didn't care for it. It must be a grown-up food in our house.

The quality of this curry was excellent for the amount of time involved! A lot of reviewers said that it wasn't spicy enough, and to double the curry. Because of this, I added an extra half of a tablespoon or curry powder, and it was VERY spicy! I think it would have been fine to use just the one tablespoon. I think it might have a lot to do with the type of curry powder used. I used an imported indian curry called, "Karahi Chicken Masala". So, my advice to anyone making this is to try the recipe as is first, and then adjust the heat to your own preference the next time. I didn't have raisins or tomato paste on hand, but I did have a 15 oz. can of stewed tomatoes, which I think worked out nicely. I also stirred in the yogurt at the very end. I am definitely adding this recipe to my cookbook. Thanks so much!!

Having never cooked Indian food before I was nervous that I would ruin this. I didn't, and the end product was delicious! Based on other reviews I stirred in the yogurt and cilantro at the end. So glad I don't have to go out for curry any more!

I hurt myself every time I make this... I just cannot stop eating it! I leave the raisins out (not a fan of savory food with fruit), double the curry AND the cayenne (we like it HOT, can you tell?). Served over saffron rice. Look out, it's addicting!

This was so simple - I almost didn't make it. BOY AM I GLAD I DID! Incredible!!!  I don't care for onions so I minced them.  It changed the texture a smidgen but it was excellent.  I added the cilantro while cooking, and put in 1/3 C. coconut milk at the end, that I had leftover from another curry. Don't care for the yogurt so skipped. Easy to add and take away stuff.  I made a little extra sauce - NEXT TIME I WILL DOUBLE THE SAUCE AND ADD SOME DICED POTATOES AND MUSHROOMS.  I'm freezing a batch in a zip-lock bag, and suspect it will reheat nicely!
My family LOVED this!  Next time, I'm going to add more curry, but all-in-all, this one is a keeper!  Thanks for posting!
This was great  with the doubled curry powder and yogurt mixed in. However, I found that it took about an hour to make...not 20 minutes so beware.

UM WOW!!!!! So, I decided to make this tonight, and I did make a few changes - I doubled the recipe and doubled the cayenne, as well as doubling the curry powder - but used 1/2 tbsp of Garam Masala. Instead of doubling the chicken, I added green beans, eggplant, cauliflower and red and orange peppers. It'll be served over long grain rice. I say 'it will' because my boyfriend ran out to grab a movie quick, and it was ready so fast, I'm waiting for him to get home so I can officially eat it! In the meantime, I'll just pick away here.. although the pan is getting less and less full.. hahaha.
I also omitted the cilantro and the raisin's, and haven't yet stirred in the yogurt, but I plan on doing that. THIS IS AMAZING! I am so excited, because it is VERY close in taste to one of my favourite, super huge crave attack dishes at my neighbourhood chinese food place.. sad for them, I won't have to break the bank as much! Woo!
You obviously don't need another positive review, but I've gotta leave one! This recipe was so easy and tasted amazing. The husband LOVED it. Thank you!

It was nice over white rice but .... it was way TOO bland. I usually don't eat curry from outside because it is too spicy but this recipe has the complete opposite problem. I had to add extra salt, curry, adobo, crushed pepper, and sazon to fix it up but once I did it was nice. I used chicken legs instead of breasts and I used regular raisins instead of golden because that's all I had. It is a good basic recipe, you JUST have to make it your own.

Delicious!  After reading through several recipes for chicken curry, I decided to try this one based on what I already had in the pantry.  The modifications I made were to omit the raisins, and to double the cayenne and curry powder as other reviewers suggested.  Additionally, I didn't have yogurt on hand so I substituted sour cream and it worked just fine.  DH and I ate this dish served over rice and both agree that it was a success.  Thanks for such a great recipe!

I made this recipe on a whim -- and it is the BEST!!!  Like many others, I doubled the curry and the cayenne (we like it hot).  The raisons were a delight and the touch of yogurt was wonderful.  My husband and I tried to get the perfect bite of cilantro, rice, chicken, and yogurt...mmmmmmmnombnombnomb.

This went over well with my family. I had to increase servings to 6 and went by the recipe... I love spicey food and this was at about my limit so I am surprised at those who doubled the cayenne and curry powder. I didn't have any chicken stock so I had to use a chicken flavored ramen noodle sachet. I used garlic powder as I had no fresh. I omited the raisins as I have diabetic to serve but put in shredded carrot. I cooked my chicken pieces in batches and they turned out wonderful! Very tender and moist, melt in your mouth. Served with basmati rice and a yogurt raita made with chopped cucumber and cilantro.

This was an excellent recipe. So fast to prepare and so delicious. I did tune the recipe a bit: instead of 1/2 teaspoons I did add 2 teaspoons of cayenne pepper and I also did add 1 teaspoon of ginger powder to the flour mixture. I also doubled the amount of curry. This makes it hot. The yogurt and hottenes of the sauce mix well together.
This is a very good recipe when you want to get nice and delicius dinner after you have got back home after a long work day. I did serve this with very simple salad: tomato, green salad, cucumber.
This was great!!! I did double the pepper and the curry powder. I left out the raisins but I think next time I will add sliced almonds.
Easy and scrumptious.  I listened to the last reviewer and omitted the raisins and sprinkled with toasted, sliced almonds - wonderful.

I had never tried Indian food before, but my husband loves it. I made this for dinner the other night and we both thought it was delicious! The only change i made was to omit the raisins. I made some basmati rice and homemade naan to go with it. Was surprised by how hot it was, but still enjoyed it. He's already asking me to make it again.

Since I originally posted almost a year ago, my husband asks me to make this on a weekly basis. I've played around with the amount of cayenne pepper, and usually cut it almost in half. I've also been to quite a few Indian restaurants since making this that first time, and so far this is tastier than any restaurant curry I've had.

Absolutely fantastic. I added a little bit more cayenne pepper than necessary, so two of us had to eat it with a bit of yoghurt, but my spice-loving friend went wild for it. (My pansy roommate couldn't handle it, though.) I had my doubts when I added the chicken back to the pan (it smelled overwhelmingly of tomato paste), but the flavors all melded together perfectly. Perfect with the yoghurt and cilantro on top.
Very good thanks!  Added broccoli to the onions and garlic part...

This was nearly perfect. I wasn't sure about the raisins and I added them anyway because, hey, I like raisins. They were okay, but this would fare just as well without them. Other than that, this was exactly the recipe I was looking for! I didn't double the cayenne and curry like a lot of reviewers did, but I did put in 50% more than was called for and it was still very spicy.
New to Indian food...tried this (left out raisins).  I'm a believer now.  DH and DS raved about it.  Served with basmati rice and homemade naan.  Thanks!
Delicious! I also put a tsp of ginger in the flour mixture, and I added two tsps of ground cumin with the curry. Very easy, and very tasty!

This is tastier than a lot of the Indian restaurant curries I have had.  I left out the raisins and yogurt and did not use the whole amount of taste paste, due to personal preferences, but that didn't matter.  This dish was still delish!!
Tasty

Definitely a 5 star recipe is what my husband and I both said.  I won't worry about making more complicated ones than this ever again.  Notes-- I used raisins and sliced almonds, both good additions.  I doubled the sauce for a kilo of thighs, less after they were cleaned and chopped. I didn't use all of the tomato sauce in the doubled recipe and I'm glad.  I did put in a couple of TBLSP of coconut powder. I used half a container of very light creme fraiche in place of the yogurt and only a small amount of coriander, mixed in.  Restaurant quality, maybe better than I've had in a restaurant and certainly cheaper.  Keeper for sure.
We love this. I DO NOT like raisins, but they really add to this dish. This is one of the very few dishes that I don't "tweak" as I make it.

This is a fantastic recipe! I have never had curry chicken before but I was feeling adventurous the other day and decided to try it. I'm so glad I did!

I, like many others omitted the raisins and yogurt. I also doubled the cayenne pepper and curry because I really wanted some kick. The only disappointment was using minute rice. I will have to search for a more complementary side dish.

It was excellent , I made it for myself & my 2 sons & we all really enjoyed it even Daniel ( my younger son ) who can be quite critical . It was also really easy to make , but I`m very slow in the kitchen so it did take longer than 20 minutes with all the prep
Loved it! Not made in the authentic Indian way but it was certainly pretty quick!

Wow, this is really good.  I wasn't sure about a curry dish but its so good.  I made just as written except used regular raisins (what I had on hand).  We loved it, it was just the right amount of heat.  Thank you for introducing me to a new flavor.

I tried it and it was delicious!! I made it exactly as is.  I love the amount heat and will increase the amount of curry next time.  I didn't top with yogurt or cilantro - personal taste. But it's definitely a keeper! Thanks for posting!

Thank you Sue for adding such a great recipe. My husband is the curry making king in our house and he loved this one. He was surprised that I knew how to make such a great curry - he has no idea how quick it was to make! ;)

Terrific.  Not the best I have ever had, but the best takes a very long time, and for a quicky - this is just fabulous!  Made it up in about 20 minutes.  Used all hot curry, next time will mix 1/2 sweet curry and 1/2 hot.  Also added fresh mushrooms, which was a lovely addition.  Would highly recommend for anyone who enjoys curry.  This is simple, fast and really very good.  Thanks!  :]

This was the first Indian food I have ever made. It came out pretty good. If I were to make it again I would greatly increase the cayenne pepper, since I like spicy food. Also, there are different types of curry and I would like to try a more spicy one next time. I used dried apricots instead of raisins and they tasted great. Instead of rice I put the chicken over rice noodles.

Wow, what an awesome recipe! Comes together quickly and easily, and really does taste as good, if not better than anything we've had in a number of Indian restaurants! I also love how the ingredients are surprisingly basic and simple to prepare -- I've spent a lot more time on curries in the past.

I served this yummy curry with jasmine rice made with cumin seeds (cooked easily with the help of my rice cooker), some peas (from frozen), and some Trader Joe's naan. Husband ate so much that he looked like he would explode!

This recipe has immediately been elevated into our rotation of favorite go-to meals. Next time I will probably use about half the amount of cayenne and/or swap in ancho chili powder instead, because it was a bit too spicy for me to enjoy as much as I would like (though my husband thought the spiciness was perfect.)

Thanks for sharing such a mind-blowing recipe!

This is certainly not the typical curry that I am used to but this is still great! I've never cooked curry before as it's very time consuming but after reading all the reviews here, I just have to give this recipe a try. DH who can't stand the smell of curry is also a fan of this dish and that is a major WOW! Thank you very much, Sue!

This is a decent curry, especially for how quick and easy it is to make.  It is better to double the amount of curry powder though, and even then the flavors aren't as strong as in your usual curry.  Ultimately, I'm going to stick with my favorite curry recipes even though the cooking times are longer, but this recipe is a great option for people who are strapped for time.

Awesome! I haven't done much Indian cooking, but my husband and I love eating it in restaurants. Well, this recipe rocks! Have prepared it several times now, with and without the raisins. Fab and oh so easy!  When I have time I make Naan (from threeovens recipe #456790) to scoop our curry into - if not, just serve over rice cooked in chicken broth. Thanks for posting!

Lovely! This was hot enough for us :) Had to use sultanas as I didn't have raisins, but it was beautiful. I cooked it for a lot longer than 20 mins and just kept adding water to stop the sauce getting to thick. Will be making again :)

We always enjoy a good curry and this was no exception, thank you Sue!!!!   Did omit the raisins since I dont care for them, but otherwise as recipe.  Very good, thank you! Made for I Recommend tag game

I loved this recipe! The only alteration I would offer to this though, is to add 2 TBSP of sour cream instead of yogurt (yogurt will give a different texture), as well as add a little more salt. Thanks again!

Thank you Sue for sharing this wonderful recipe.  I feel like you gave up some trade secrets on this one - and we love the name!  I was hesitant to add so much curry and to add it after the chicken was cooked but it made the difference.  Excellent instructions and a guaranteed winner if the recipe is followed.  Thanks!

I LOVE THIS. i cooked it for my boyfriend about 6 months ago for the first time, since he loves curry and hadnt had any in about 2 years, he loved it.... i made a few changes:

I like to add pineapple cut into squares when i return the chicken to the pan.
I use cream instead of yogurt.
I omit the risins
sometimes i add zucchini.

i like it creamy so i add a bit more cream. i cook this about 2-3 times per month :)
This is delicious. I made it tonight as written. Served  over rice and it was a winner. The two of us polished it off with no problem. Thanks for a great recipe

This was so good, I had never had curry before and wanted to try something new. After reading a few other recipes this one looked pretty easy to do. I changed a few things, added sour cream, double the curry power and did not use golden raisin. It came out amazing! Thank you for the simple and easy recipe!!

I made this last week it was delicious. My brother loved it even though he is a picky eater. I put the four and curry powder in with the broth not with the chicken, but still good. It was a little too spicy. But who am i kidding i am only twelve. Still it was good.
Awesome and super easy. I substituted red curry paste for the tomato sauce...nice zing

This was fantastic. My bf loves curry, myself not a huge fan. But this recipe was quick, easy, not many ingredients and soooooooo good. I omitted the raisins (but will probably add them next time), I used green onion instead of cilantro, used sour cream on top instead of yogurt and added uncooked shrimp to the pan for the last 10 mins of cooking. They were fantastic. Overall a great dish that I will make again and again.
Chicken curry in a hurry was Merry :)<br/>Just loved  the way it's..<br/>I had it with chappathi. Thanks for such a food recipe.

My family loved it.  Wonderfully simple receipe, I didnt add raisins.  But next time i will add cashews and make raita instead of using plain yogart.  I love indian food and I have to say this is better then 85% of most indian resturants

i love this recipe its so simple takes ingredients everyone has in their pantry i find that i add 2 cups of chicken stock and if i make it for just me and my partner add half a tablespoon of extra curry powder for extra kick.i teamed this recipe with a naan bread i also found on this site.definately one to keep as you can alter it to everyones tastes
Really good, I followed some other reviews and added a little extra cayenne and curry powder, my family was very happy.
Quick and easy!

I followed the recipe exactly, but this did not taste like any Indian curry I've ever eaten. I've had both Vindaloo and Masala, which I love. I don't know what this was supposed to be, but I didn't like it.

Soooooo good. We loved this. Made as written. It takes a lot more than 7 minutes to prep but well worth it. The golden raisins were a sweet tidbit in a savory sauce. The entire family inhaled it. Served over rice. We will make again and again. Thanks for posting Sue! Enjoy! ChefDLH

Delicious!  I get a craving for curry once in awhile and this fit the bill!  The only change I made was to use regular raisins instead of the golden because that's what I had and I chopped them up really fine so my family wouldn't know they were in there.  I definitely think you need the taste of the raisins in it, they add so much.  I made naan bread to go with this.
Fantastic recipe!  I omitted the raisins, substituted coconut yogurt for plain, and sriracha for cayenne, then added a sweet potato, that I microwaved, and cubed.  Took it to another level...

Like jentastic, I didn't have any raisins on hand, so I had to leave them out. Nor did I have yogurt, so once again I followed jentastics review and used sour cream instead. I served it over rice.  DH and I were the only ones who liked this. Guess my crew just isn't fans of Indian food.

Fantastic! I was really happy with how easy this recipe was without taking away any flavor. I substituted vanilla yogurt because I had it on hand and it worked just fine. Next time I make it I'll probably add bell peppers and potatoes to add even more to the already amazing dish. I did not put the raisins for I'm not a fan.

Hi, thanks for the nice recipe.  i made some changes: didn't use, flour to thicken the curry instead used some fresh onions and ginger and garlic this helped thicken the curry very well.  I cook all my food in pure-clay pots, since they're very healthy, i did this one in a pure clay pot too and it came out great.  google pure-clay cookware to find them.
Quick, easy and tasty!

5 stars for several reasons 
The flavor was great. Warm but refreshing. I feel like all the ingredients compliment each other very nicely. 
And it comes together so quick. A weeknight hearty meal in about 20 minutes and lunch for tomorrow. I used the amount of pepper for my taste but other than that followed it to a T. Great recipe a definite keeper.

If I could give this 10 stars, I would. It was GREAT! I didn't measure my chicken or flour, but I guess it was about 1.5 lbs. of floured chicken tender bite size pieces. I used seasoned salt instead of the cayenne and salt, but did add a touch of cayenne (hubby isn't happy if he has steam coming out his ears) but otherwise stuck pretty closely to the recipe. I used Penzy's curry powder which was quite fresh, so the spices were wonderful. The raisins are a tasty sweet addition to the other spicy flavors (you could probably use dark raisins instead of the golden ones.) I added about 1/2 red bell pepper to the onion, and that made it pretty much a one-dish meal (if you count peppers as a vege.) A side of rice and sliced tomato was all it took to complete the plate. Yum, yum, yum - don't bother with any other recipe for chicken curry. This is the best.

Very good for homemade Indian food! It was just a tad spicy for our tastes, but the flavor was definitely there. I think I will only add half the cayenne next time. I also omitted the raisins-not a big fan. The yogurt complimented perfectly, however, I don't think the cilantro made a big difference, so I probably won't bother with it next time. Adding it to our Favorites Cookbook. :)

Amazing !! calculation to serve different number ! we are having free residential home from youth with impairment nearly 84 beneficiaries are there at our campus, struggling from log time for recipes calculation your geniuskitchen.com gave simple solution, Thanks to the Team and God Bless Help us to feed good by more south Indian recipes

This recipe makes a dandy sauce! I made it up to use in Little Bee's Taco Casserole, and it worked great!  Very simple to put together, and, even better, with ingredients I keep on hand all the time anyway! I did double the recipe, so, have enough left over for another night!
Thanks for sharing, JQ ... Good recipe!
This is excellent.  My kids don't like chunks of tomato in their salsa.  Two thumbs up for this one, Thanks
I love recipes that use "normal" pantry items - and this one qualifies! It enabled me to make Bergy's Leftover Beef Enchiladas (recipe #11827) without driving 15 kms to the store. Thanx QT!

This is an excellent sauce.  I made it yesterday to use in another recipe (Taco Stuffed Pasta Shells)and was delighted with the results!  I think I will be using this taco sauce from now on!  Why buy it if it is so cheap, easy and tasty to make at home!  Thanks!

Great stuff! Even though I'm loathe to admit it being from southern Arizona (neighbor to Mexico), I love Taco Bell, and their hot sauce is a prime reason why.  This is a really great approximation of it!  Worked really well as the taco sauce for Bergy's Leftover Beef Enchiladas #11827, and I'll make it again. Thanks!
This is a good recipe because the ingredients are so simple and most likely on hand. The flavor is good as well.

Since I don't make tacos very often, it seemed so wasteful to have to open a new bottle of taco sauce every time I needed it. Now I can make my own at a fraction of the cost, plus I happened to have every ingredient called for in the recipe on hand! And the taste was great, hot or cold.

Wow! Excellent flavor and SO cheap to make. Used this for recipe#72614 Taco Casserole by KITTENCAL.
Thanks for a great keeper!

Very easy to make. I used this in recipe 72614, and was very pleased with the results. For personal preference I skipped the cumin and garlic salt but otherwise made it as written. Thanks for the recipe.

So easy and so cheap to make! My 14 yr. old made this and we all loved it.
Thanks for posting this.

I love this sauce, I love Taco Bell sauce but not the food so much so it is nice to be able to make this at home and as far as I am concerned this is a very close match. It has a nice kick to it. I am making enchiladas tonight, I doubled this recipe to use as the sauce.
I used chopped onion and garlic and table salt and I have a shaker full of crushed red peppers and I put that in there to taste. It added a lot to my taco. I really liked it and will always use it.
This worked just fine and made Taco Bell mild sauce that was much cheaper than purchasing a jar of sauce! Thanks.

OK I read the reviews, and whoever was complaining about the sugar may have gotten "tomato sauce" confused with "tomato ketchup" - because ketchup is totally loaded with sugar, especially if you go with Heinz. HOWEVER... the ingredients on my tomato sauce (Muir Glen organic) are just tomatoes, water, and salt - no sugar, no HFCS - and even Hunts doesn't have as much sugar as Heinz. The amount of sugar added to this recipe is just 1/4 TEASPOON - negligible at best - but you can always add an equal amount of Kosher salt to cut the sweet edge of that sugar and still get the rounded palette flavor.

That said, we are a household with Celiac and food allergies to accommodate, so processed sauces are hazardous to our health. This is one of the easiest sauces with best taste that I've found for tacos and enchiladas - and having lived all over the SW and in TX, I'm pretty picky about what's passable for Mexican cuisine. That said, I made the following modifications:

Instead of garlic powder, I used fresh garlic with garlic oil.
Instead of dried minced onion, I used onion powder to get the deeper flavor.
I added salt to taste to balance out the sweetness.

original review:WOW! This is the closest thing to "real" bread that I have had in 10 years!  Thank you Gluten Free GIrl for posting this GREAT find.

The people who make guar gum or xanthan gum recommend it be dissolved in the oil/wet mixture before being added to the recipe. It needs the oil or fat to be properly dissolved. Although recipes do work doing it the way that the author wrote, it works much better if done the other way and have a better texture. The guar gum also should not be used in recipes with a high acid content as the acid tends to neutralize it. The xanthan gum does a better job of combining starches. See Bob's Red Mill site if you are interested in recommended proportions for different recipes.
Although the rice and tapioca flours are 'safe' flours with a more neutral taste, I tend to prefer working with combinations of other flours for about a third the flour amount for the increased vitamins and proteins that they offer. Changing the starches can have an effect on the recipe if you are inexperienced in working with these flours.

The funky taste was still there. The third batch we we switched to white distilled vinegar, and it was still gross. So we figured it had to be one of the flours. So my husband started smelling them and found it was the tapioca. I don't know if our flour is bad or if that is just how it tastes. I've never noticed it taste bad like that in any of the other recipes I've used it in. Other than that the bread is delicious. It is soft on the inside and has a crisp and slightly chewy crust. I can only say that I am in heaven as I eat a meatball sandwich with my own gluten free turkey/chicken meatballs and this bread, nobody in my big Italian family would ever know it was gluten free OR that the meatballs were gluten free (used one of my fallen french bread recipes for gluten free bread crumbs, mixed with Italian seasoning and baked in the oven for 10 minutes).<br/><br/>Now, the only sub I made (I hate it when people substitute and then say the recipe doesn't work!) was that I used 1 cup of super fine brown rice flour and 1 cup of super fine white rice flour. Everything else was the same. I did not use the egg replacer, not sure why that is in there? <br/><br/>I baked it in my regular oven in a french bread pan (I have a triple pan, I only used 2 of them and I lined it with parchment paper). I baked it for 40 minutes. After 20 minutes, I tented it with Aluminum, as I don't like a dark crust. PERFECT!!! <br/><br/>Thanks GlutenFreeGirl!<br/><br/>I did leave the door ajar and didn't take it out for 5 minutes in case it fell, which it did not. I slide it about 20 minutes after it came out and it is to die for.
Thank you very much for this recipe! My daughter is allergic to gluten. In Poland we have no shops with gluten free products so I have to prepare it by myself . And finally I found great recipe!:)

I have made this bread many times, and everyone always loves it.  I tried making it using spices and asiago cheese,  then sprinkling a generous amount of asiagio cheese on the top before baking, took it to a party, and everyone gobbled it up.  <br/>One more thing,  I always put a pan of water on the bottom shelf of the oven before I preheat.<br/>And I spray the inside of the oven with water 3 or 4 times while it is baking.  <br/>My husband says it is the best french bread he has ever tasted.
This bread recipe is a winner at our house! My husband said that this makes the best sandwich bread (cut horizontally) that he's had in years. He's very picky so this is high praise!
WOOOOW! Love it! I made it so I could use it for GF bread pudding, but it almost didn't make it to the second recipe. It's so good!
I have made this bread many times! hands down the best ever! I cook mine in small loaf pans they come out perfect each time.
This turned out perfectly..had to cook a bit longer but still fantastic!! Tip: put parchment paper on the baguette pan and it will be less of a mess than the cornmeal! It's my go to GF bread!
I went gf in 1/17. I have yet to find a 'bread'
Made this bread loved it.I forgot the egg replacer It came out any way the best
This is by far the best tasting GF bread I have ever tasted, and so easy. I did not have egg substitute so omitted it and used sweet rice flour.
Is this recipe too wet to use a perforated french bread pan? I have horrid visions of the bread dripping through the tiny holes in the pan all over my oven!
This is the best GF bread recipe I've tried. Fabulous!! A++ Lorie
The is the best GF bread I have made
This was a great recipe. The bread was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Stayed that way for days!
I baked in my cloche (received 15 yrs ago as a wedding gift and never used until now!) and here's the beautiful result. The crust is wonderful and has a nice hollow sound when tapped.
Question not good at cooking this I will try as have to follow a FODMAP diet any tips lol ??

I like this gluten free French bread even better than regular French bread. I followed the recipe exactly except that I used 2 whole eggs instead of 3 egg whites. Somebody on here suggested to use brown rice flour instead of white, but it wouldn't rise, so I'm sticking with white. I baked it 45 minutes at 375 because I have a convection oven and you are supposed to reduce the temperature by 25 degrees.
Delicious! Not time consuming and so much better than expensive store bought non gluten.
I have tried to make this recipe 3 times now, and my dough will not rise. What am i doing wrong
Tastes great, with an equally wonderful aroma. Follow the recipe.

This is very delicious! I have done it twice. First time, I made it, I followed the directions to the letter. It was flavorful. Next time, I modified it - Step 8, placed 2 cups wine, carrots, and water. Then I simmered it for 1 hour. I used a can of Italian tomatoes with garlic. Take note garlic is not included in the recipe, neither is parsley. They are both optional, but we prefer it that way.  After simmering for a long time, there is no need to thicken the sauce in our opinion, but then again, that is a matter of taste. The hoisin sauce made the sauce thicker and richer and we loved it. Thanks Evelyn for this lovely recipe.
very good!  great flavor, the hoisin sauce is a great touch

Thanks for the suggestions Evelyn. I followed the recipe, but used left over teriyaki marinaded fondue meat. This was easy, and I had all the ingredients on hand. I was tempted to add broth, but didn't. After simmering with the carrots, there was plenty of liquid. I served in a bowl, with bread.

This is super-delicious, eve! I love the flavor from the red wine although I don't drink RW (FYI, I used Cab Sauv from Australia). And the hoisin sauce imparts a slightly sweet taste to the sauce, which works perfectly with the flavor or the RW (slightly dry). Didn't change a thing to the recipe, except to scaled to down to 1 serving i.e. 265g beef which is just enough for the 2 of us. Although I used 1 full cup of RW for 1/6 of the recipe! Thanks for the great recipe.
This was fabulous! Very rich tasting. I added a little more garlic as we love it. Served with the egg noodles as suggested and a side salad. YUM!

This is very delicious.  I made it yesterday during a blizzard and it made the whole house smell wonderful.  The hoisin sauce adds a slight sweetness that is very appealing.  The only things I did differently were that I floured the meat with Wondra before browning, added button mushrooms and sliced celery,and lots of garlic.  I had frozen pearl onions I was going to add also but forgot about them.  This is a keeper.  Thanks Evelyn.  I've made a number of your recipes and they're all terrific.

This stew is very easy to prepare and smells great while cooking. The flavors blend beautifully and taste even better the next day. This was served with crusty bread and got rave reviews. Delicious recipe, thank you for sharing Evelyn!

Delicious!  Meat was so tender and the flavor was excellent. I confess I skipped adding the cornstarch--the sauce as it was was thin but delicious and I decided to forego extra starch.  Everyone loved it.

A delicious stew, which I'm sure must taste good the next day but we never got to find out..all gone! Had to make a few improvisations (bare pantry), but it still tasted great...I halved the recipe (though still used the same amount of hoisin sauce), substituted 3 tablespoons of tomato paste for the tinned tomato, water and 2 tablespoons of balsamic vinegar for the red wine, and added 1/2 dozen chopped mushrooms. Oh, and I used fresh herbs rather than dried, added them just before the end. I also found the cornstarch unnecessary as the sauce reduced nicely within the cooking time. Served this over some creamy mashed potato for scrumptious comfort food...thanks Evelyn!
This was a wonderful stew!!!  I added some potatoes to this as well as a red pepper - wonderful!  The meat is tender and the flavour is awesome!  Easy to prepare and very good.

Excellent Flavour! I made a half recipe and served it over mashed Yukon Gold potatoes. I also added red pepper flakes and omitted the thyme and used a very flavourful Merlot. I think the wine you choose makes a big difference. I will be making this again! Many thanks Evelyn!

The combo of hoisin sauce and wine in this dish made it outstanding and didn't seem to overpower the vegetables either.  My BF made it for supper last night and he used less oil and a meat substitute for the chuck roast (making it vegetarian and lower in fat too).  Never would have thought to put hoisin sauce in a stew but it was great.  I've found that commercial hoisin sauces can be either too bitter or too sweet and I haven't yet found my favorite either, so all I can say is try to find one you like first.  Thanks very much for this recipe.

Very nice stew!  I made this exactly as written, using a Galena Cellars Country Red for the wine.  We had it over Yukon gold mashed potatoes with some biscuits.  It was a very comforting meal on this cold, blustery April day!  Thanks for the recipe Ev, it's a keeper :)
I made this recently and the flavour was wonderful.  The hoison sauce made all the difference....will definitely make again !

Excellent! A gourmet stew with deep dark layers of elegant flavors. I made the recipe as directed using leftover Shiraz Cabernet and Tuscan (Antinori) red wine. I doubled the garlic and subbed 2 celery stalks for 2 of the carrots. I served the stew over mashed potatoes. I made the full recipe for just the two of us, expecting to freeze some, but at the rate it is disappearing - we will be fighting over the leftovers tomorrow! Great recipe Ev, goes right into my cookbook of "Special Tricks".

Made this quite some time ago, and forgot to review - I loved it, although DH did not like the sweet taste....however, you have to expect that with the hoisin sauce.  I thought it was simple, delicious comfort food with a delightfully different twist.
My stew is still cooking but I tasted the sauce and I am amazed. It is just a little bit sweet and full meal. I am very happy for that I made that dish.
this was really great and it made the kitchen smell wonderful while it was cooking!  I didn't change a thing.  Thanks a lot!
Made this for Sunday dinner...turned out very good...I put in a little quick tapioca the last hour to thicken and it turned out perfect.
This is a keeper.  Followed the recipe exactly and won't change a thing.  This was the first time I  used Hoisin sauce in a stew, and I am glad I did.

Wonderful! I added 1 1/2 cups of Cabernet right at the beginning as well as 3 additional cloves of garlic. My kids loved it as much as we did. This is a great "fix it and forget it" meal as well as a great choice for company. Thanks for a keeper!

Wow, this was incredible.  First let me say that my husband does not like beef stew and the only reason I decided to try this is the hoisin, which he loves (oh, and the 22 5 star reviews were also in infulence).  He thought this was wonderful and definately wants it again and often.  He even said it was guest worthy, which one does not usually say of a stew.  I only used 2 1/2 1bs. of stew meat (already cut up) which worked out just fine because we love lots of sauce.  I used a fabulous bottle of 2001 BV costal cabernet, which was also wonderful.  I followed your directions completely except that after adding the carrots I cooked for an hour because the carrots took that long to get the way we like them.  I also added a couple of handfuls of frozen peas at the end.  In my mind I think mashed potatoes should go with beef stew, so I made potatoes and egg noodles.  I must add that the flavor was way more enhanced by the noodles and I won't make potatoes with it again.  Like other reviewers I did not need to add the cornstarch it was perfect without it.  Thanks so much for sharing what is a new family favorite.
Menfolk loved it!  Served on buttered egg noodles, and added button mushrooms.

Yes. No, I mean YES! I started nibbling at the edge of the pot while cooking in order to refrain from actually eating the stew all up before my poor, hungry husband came home. CHANGES:  Since I didn't want to go to the store, I used what I had on hand which included a smaller package of stew meat (so I halved the recipe) and dried rather than fresh parsley. Yummmmmmm and THANKS!

This was very satisfying. I seared the meat and carmelized the onions and then put everything into the crockpot for the day. I had to use a lot more than 1 tbs of cornstarch to thicken the sauce, but I think it was because of the low heat I used. I think next time (and there will be a next time) I will use a better wine. Like some of the other reviewers, I too added garlic and mushrooms. Thanks for sharing this.

Extremely sweet!  My husband gave it a 4, my kids wouldn't eat anything but the carrots. It doesn't taste bad, it's just over poweringly sweet.  I think, and husband agrees, that the sauce would be better used in a side dish, not as the main part of a meal - a little goes a long way.  I followed directions exactly except reduced oil to 1T.  Served with noodles. I like sweetness but this was just too much for us.

Wow.  I really loved this.  Strangely, the sauce wasn't thin for me.  I made only about a half of the recipe, which seems like it would be enough for maybe four people.  I ate enough for probably two people.  The hoison sauce wasn't too sweet, but I did season with a lot of salt and pepper at the end.   I thought the flavor was very good, with lots of depth.  Next time I will use more tomatoes and throw in some mushrooms.  Overall, I'm impressed.  We served this over mashed potatoes!  Thanks.

WOW--what a wonderful blend of flavors!! I halved the recipe for the two of us, but used the full can of tomatoes.  I added cubed potatoes at the same time as the carrots.  Did not need to thicken as the sauce was perfect.  The rich, deep flavor of this stew was delicious!!  Next time I will serve it over mashed potatoes or noodles - - to soak up that wonderful sauce.  I look forward to serving this special "stew" to company on a cold, wintery evening!!
This was fab, I followed the recipe and added some new potatoes near the end of cooking time. I served this with cabbage, Will be making again thank you for sharing
YUM.  I will make this again and again and again.  Perfect for cold days, thanks for posting this fabulous recipe.

Soooo good!The hoisin sauce really added a depth and sweetness that my family loved(my  5 yr old daughter ate every bite, so that is saying something!!).I added some mushrooms towards the end and it was just perfect.Thanks for the great recipe!!!

Great recipe & smelled wonderful. Mine looked as good as the picture. I served it with mash potaoes. I did not need to thicken the sauce. I used stewing beef & had no problem. Thank you Evelyn I will be making this again.

As everyone has said, this is fantastic!  I used half the beef, added diced potatoes and crimini mushrooms (to make up for the beef I left out, weight-wise) in the last 45 minutes - great!  Did not need the cornstarch, thanks for that suggestion, everyone.  The hardest part is waiting until it's cooked.  The aroma of this is to die for - and wait until you taste it!  Thanks so much, Evelyn, it's absolutely the best, another one of your great recipes.
This stew smelled absolutely wonderful.  Although my husband loved it, I won't be making it again.  It tasted good, it was just too rich for me.
This is a wonderful stew. The Flavour is so rich but absolutely delightful - I served with oven baked potatoes - my own recipe and we couldn't get enough!
Delicious flavor.  Easy to make but you have to hang around to get through the directions.  Had it with basmati rice.  Will make again.

A very good and different way to have stew.  I used 1 lb. stew meat so I halved the other ingredients.  I did substitute 1/2 chicken broth and 1/2 red grape juice for the wine.  Don't know how much difference it made in the taste from wine, but it was not super sweet like some others have said and was very delicious.  Will definitely be making this again.
divine over garlic mashed potatoes, the flavor is unlike any beef stew you will ever come across. takes awhile but it's worth it. 5 stars.

Prepared this for dinner tonight, just half the recipe since I had on hand about half the amount of meat called for. Hubby and son loved it! (Me, too.) We had it over noodles with a dollop of sour cream.
Scrumptious! I love it when a recipe is a hit with all of us! Thanks for sharing this Evelyn.

Can't even remember the last recipe I rated on here but I ran right to the computer after eating this!  This is the kind of wonderful dish that makes you think of reasons to invite family and friends over just so you can make it again and impress everyone.
Made it almost exactly as stated except I added celery.  So glad my hubby asked for stew tonight and I stumbled upon this :0)

Made this over the weekend and our house smelled delicious! Only changes: I simmered it much longer and then, because we had last-minute company, added 4 c. water to stretch it out. Everyone raved over it. I'll be making this again soon!

LOVELY -  This is very quick to make, and the flavor is terrific!  The hoisin sauce makes a huge difference. I used home-made hoisin sauce, which was lovely.  I did double up on the garlic (never can have too much!).

A wonderfully easy recipe ideal for when the days are getting shorter.We invited friends over and served this with the noodles as suggested.  It was a winner!! I substituted 1 cup of red wine vinegar for the red wine, and even managed to track down the hoisin sauce.  The dried herbs make a real difference to the delicate flavour of this dish, and I added a tablespoon of tomato paste. This is one of our family favourites, and it is great to find a recipe that can be left simmering on the stove.  The carrots add a sweetness, and when I served the dish I was pleased to see that they had not desintigrated into nothing, as they were added at a later stage.  Also nice to serve some hot French bread to enjoy the flavourful gravy.  Ten out of ten Evelyn!!

I just didnt find this stew that tasty....it has alot of great reviews so I was a little upset about not liking it. I used an expensive bottle of wine and wished I hadnt of now. Also had to really hunt for the hoisin sauce..went to 3 diffrent stores. 
 I am more of a southern stew kind of person...this was just really not for me.

This was really, really, REALLY good.  I followed directions, with the exception of my adding 4-5 medium potatoes (cubed) and subbing 1-2 c. beef bullion (when I ran out of wine!).  This will be my "go to" stew recpe from now on.  So refreshing to have a recipe for stew that isn't so darn salty!  One word:  YUM!

What can you say about perfection!!! This was wonderful....I would highly recommend this to anyone.....this felt very upscale....I would not hesitate to serve to company.  The flavour is so deep & mellow.  Thank you so much Evelyn for a wonderful recipe....I have never used hoisin sauce before...it was magical.....

I have just finished preparing this recipe and have not even served it yet - but I have done the spoon tasting.  What a flavor!  This is probably way more information that you want to hear -but I am from south Texas and my mom was an awful cook (Sorry, Mom!)  We had stew at least once a week and it was white, the meat was tough and stingy and it was just plain awful.  Consequently, I do not make stew often, if at all.  Today, I had some meat that needed to be cooked right away and I found your recipe.  I had no carrots and I had no Hoisin Sauce -but I had peas, mushrooms and oyster flavored sauce. I followed the recipe with those ingredients and then cooked it with dumplings.  I am just getting ready to serve it and all I can say, is priliminary tasting is a solid ""A"".  What a wonderful dish!  Thank you so much for bringing a dish back to me that should have been wonderful but wasn't - but now is.  Post more please!!

This is a terrific stew!  We served it over mashed red potatoes and it looked beautiful.  Definitely something I would serve to company, and stew isn't something I would usually even consider being in that category.  I think it would be even better with thick-cut mushrooms...yum!  I was about 1/4 cup short on the wine, but it still tasted great to me!  Baby carrots did the trick for me - no cutting and they look better - IMHO.  The parsley at the end is what makes this dish look so pretty, so don't leave that out.  My husband took leftovers to work for lunch the next day and he enjoyed it even more.  Thanks for sharing your wonderful recipe!

LOVED IT!! The hoisin sauce brings a wonderful asian element to beef stew. My husband found it a bit sweet, which is why we rated it a four star.  But that's just a personal preference. We did remove the beef while sauting the onions, as I was afraid of overbrowning the beef. Our beef was very tender!!  Loved the sauce, alot of depth and flavour with a perfect texture.  We also added a drained can of mushrooms near the end. A perfect meal on a cold winter day!! Thank you for posting this recipe!
I'm not a big fan of stew, but my husband is and we both agreed that this is an outstanding recipe -- especially good over the egg noodles as suggested for a winter dinner!

This was wounderful! This stew is hearty and full of flavor. The only thing I changed was that I added celery and I added the veggies with the rest of the ingredients because I wanted the carrots to be soft. I think the next time I make this I would cut the Hoisin sauce down maybe to half. It was great the first few bites but then It became too sweet for us. Other than that this was really good! Definately different from your every day, ordinary  beef stew. Thank You for posting!

Really great stew!  Although not notated, this recipe was originally published by Bon Apetit magazine.  I first found it on the Epicurious website.  After reading the reviews on their site, I learned that many hoisin sauces list sugar as their number one ingredient.  This probably leads to the excessive sweetness that some reviewers notate.  Before buying your hoisin sauce, look at the label carefully!

I thought the sauce was very good.  I think it would work well with brisket too. My youngest son didn't like it much but my older one gave it a 5 and his friend liked it too.  DH said it was good but for stew he prefers a traditional brown sauce variety. Thanks for posting.
Soooo Yummy! My DH thought said this was the best stew he ever had! Only changes I made was cooking longer (wanted the meat to be more tender), added some beef stock and then added peas at the end.

This was delicious, the whole family loved it!!! (an impromptu guest who 'wasn't really hungry' and usually doesn't eat red meat couldn't stop eating it either). I didn't have any hoisin so threw in a combination of mushroom soy sauce, regular soy sauce and some other kind of Thai sauce I had in the house, 'twas really great. I'll try and find hoisin for next time :-)

Can I give this 100 stars or more please...thanks Ev this was fantastic, amazing, delicious, awesome the whole family loved it...half way through cooking when I sampled I wanted to leave my review but waited for the whole family to try and it was unanimous...I added some potatoes cut up small to it and served it with crusy bread...wow!!!  Thanks so so so so so much for this it will definitely become a family favorite...thanks...Anne - Grecorican

Purely delicious!  My husband and I loved this stew, but unfortunately the kids didn't eat it.  I used 1 tablespoon less olive oil while sauteeing the onions and an extra clove of garlic.  Like another reviewer suggested, I added the carrots and all of the wine in Step 8.  I cooked the stew for 45 minutes at this point with the lid on.  Then I cooked the stew with the lid off for between 15-30 minutes until the carrots were close to done.  I did need to thicken the liquid with the cornstarch mixture followed by finishing cooking until carrots were completely cooked.  I can't wait to make this recipe again!
It was very good.  We added potatoes.  Next time I'll cook the meat a little longer, since it was a little more chewy than I like in stew.
O.K., this review is probably completely pointless as I'm the 85th reviewer and it's so obvious that this is an amazing recipe but here goes: We loved, loved, loved this! This was delicious.
Wow, wow wow!!  This has become perhaps the best dish I have ever made!  So tangy, complex, savory and the meat just falls apart!  I served it with mashed potatoes :-)  THANKS!!!

I was very skeptical about this recipe once I started cooking.  It smelled really strong and I had doubts about using all four cups of onions since I'm not a fan.  When I was finished the sauce looked really thick and dark and I was worried it would taste horrible.  But my husband tried it and loved it so much he ate two huge bowls.  I loved it as well.  It has a rich, sweet flavor. I crumbled up some Jiffy cornbread in it to cut the sweetness but it tastes great by itself.  I am a newly-wed with little to no cooking experience.  But I can honestly say that this dish is the best I've tried so far.
The sauce on this was to die for.  Next time I wouldn't cook for as long as I found the meat was overcooked.  I also didn't have to add the cornstarch it was thick enough.  This is a keeper for sure.

Not sure what I think about this. I guess the taste was sweet and unexpected for me. It is good. It took me a lot of time to cook however. I started it at 11am and was done at 4pm. Could have been the big chucks of stew meat. Would I make it again? Not likely. My boyfriend loved it and thought it was the best stew ever. I'm sure he'll be asking me to make it again :)

This was soooo yummy!  I've tried other recipes and nothing else compares to this.  This one is far and away the best and it's the only beef stew for me!  It was easy to make and my family just loved it.  The only change I made was to add peas and not use parsley for finish.  I've already made it twice.  Once over rice and the other over buttered egg noodles.  I like the noodles better, but that's the beauty of this recipe.  Served over rice, noodles or potatoes - it's just outstanding!
WONDERFUL!!  I usually don't care for stew, but this was great.  I added mushrooms, but I followed the rest of the recipe to the letter.  Thank you
This is an excellent hearty stew.  I think I might decrease the cooking time a bit next time because mine was very thick but the taste was wonderful.

Very good!  Followed the recipe as far as ingredients..but cooked in a crock pot for about 6-7 hours.  I added the carrots after about 2 hours because I like them nice and tender. I found I did not need cornstarch because removing the lid and turning on high for the last 45 minutes was sufficient to thicken it nicely.  The meat was very very tender.  The only change I might make next time is to go a little heavier on the garlic (we love garlic).  1 clove was almost too subtle for us, but that's just a personal preference.

We opted to serve it over plain mashed potatoes and let it stand on it's own...which it did admirably!
My picky british wife said to give it 10 out of 10 (a rating like that from her usually requires mushrooms)!

What a delicious recipe. My home smelled wonderful as this was cooking. Our Councilman rang the doorbell to let us know what was going on in our Ward, the first thing he said as I opened up the door was "something really smells good in here". I added mushrooms and celery. Next time I am going to put a few potatoes in also. Thanks Evelyn for a wonderful recipe.

OMGOODNESS was this AWESOME! The flavors in this beef stew deserve more than 5 stars. It was easy to pull together and tasty on top. Everyone went back for seconds. I did add more garlic and potatoes. I definitely will make this stew again!
I liked this recipe a lot, it was just a tad sweet for our taste. I will surely try it again, but maybe cut back on the hoisin a bit, but otherwise excellent!

This was awesome - my new stew recipe. I started it out on the stove and after the first hour I transferred to the crockpot. Added the baby carrots sliced in half and red baby potatoes , cut in four pcs. I added the last cup of wine and let it cook on low for the next 4 hours while I ran errands.
Awesome! The potatoes thickened the sauce and all I finished it with was the fresh parsley and some sourdough bread.
Thanks for a keeper!
Very good and not hard to make.  I enjoyed it but my husband did think it was too sweet for his taste.

This stew was amazing.  I made the recipe as stated except I added more carrots (family preference) and added approximately 2 Tbs of cocoa.  I served it over fontina mashed potatoes.  The cheese in the potatoes paired amazingly well with the sweetness in the stew.  We loved it.  Thanks so much.

Really great "fancy" stew!  I added the carrots  right after the onions in order to ensure their tenderness.  It is very rich - my teenagers weren't too thrilled with it, but hubby and I were in heaven!  I also added some frozen peas near the end, personal preference.  I think next time we might use 1/2 the hoisin as it was quite sweet - but could be just the brand of sauce that we had.  We served it over buttered noodles as suggested.  Thanks!
We love this stew.  It has become one of our favorite cold-weather comfort foods.  I have also shared the recipe with friends who say they have received raves on it, too.  Thanks for submitting it.
Great recipe!  I added peas just for color.  Yummy!
Great dish!  I never would have thought to serve stew over noodles but it was great, we loved it.  Thanks Evelyn!

I loved this stew - I added a couple of diced potatoes, some mushrooms and a parsnip along with the carrots.  I also simmered the meat with a couple of beef soup bones to flavor the broth and it was one of the best stews I've ever made.  The hoisin sauce definitley made this stew. Give it a try - you won't be sorry.

We enjoyed this so much.  The beef was nice and tender and the sauce had a surprise sweetness which enhanced the flavor of the stew.  I used baby carrots which helped ease the prep work and served with the suggested side of buttered egg noodles.  Next time I make this, I will reduce the amount of the hoisin sauce.  Thank you so much, Evelyn!

I made this today during a Colorado blizzard.  It smelled wonderful while it was cooking but that was nothing compared to how wonderful it tasted when it was done.  We followed the recipe almost exactly as written except we used a mixture of 1/4 Cup Hoisin Sauce and 1/4 Cup of Water instead of the full 1/2 Cup Hoisin Sauce.  We cooked the stew on low for several hours all afternoon and the meat just fell apart it was so tender.  We served the stew over mashed potatoes and just loved, loved, loved the gravy.  Thanks very much for a wonderful recipe.  We will make this again and again!!!

Great recipe. I added some diced potatoes at the beginning.  Cooked in a slow cooker on low for 8.5 hours.  I added carrots and some quinoa and cooked on high for an hour.  The carrots could have done with a little more cooking but I didn't have time to let it sit longer.  Good flavor!

I was overwhelmed by the flavor when I first made this.  So I added 2 cups of beef stock and increased the cornstarch by 1 Tbsp.  Also added cubed potatoes near the end of the cooking time.  I believe this is one dish that improves when the flavors are allowed to meld, so good to prepare a day ahead.
My family loved it! I have been wanting a stew and this sounded really good and different, so I made it.  Great recipe Evelyn!

I absolutely loved this--it was delicious and slightly sweet--wonderful on a cold winter night.  However my dh did not care for it. *sigh*  It seems he does not care for a lot of stews unless they are curry. Don't hesitate to try this recipe tho--what does he know ;-)?

Delightful! I used the crockpot and it took me awhile to get the gravy thickened, I could not stop going back and forth to the crockpot to keep sampling the gravy. Great flavor! Served over egg noodles and with recipe#90151

Couldn't pass up this recipe.  I made it along with some good biscuits and it hit the spot, with all the cold weather we have been having.  Sure did give me comfort!  Thank you Evelyn for a great recipe!  Wiggie
I loved this stew. The only change I made was to the amount of hoisin sauce - I cut it down to 1/4 cup. This gave the right amount of sweetness for hubby and me. It was delicious.

This was very good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as far as the ingredients but I put everything in the crock pot and cooked it for 6 hours. It was so moist. It also smelled so good when I came home from work. Everyone really enjoyed it.
I made this for dinner tonight.   The only change I made was to add potatoes, celery and peas.   We loved it!  Thanks for the recipe

Very good!  I did make a few changes, as follows:  I dredged the meat with flour, salt and pepper before browning.  Used 2 chopped onions, and at least 2-3 cloves garlic.  Instead of 1 lb carrots, I probably used about 1/2 cup.  I also added about 1/2 chopped celery, a diced potato, 8 oz. fresh mushrooms and peas.  I was afraid this may be overly sweet with the hoisin sauce, but that wasn't the case at all.
So good, this is going in my permanent file!
My husband and mother both loved this dish.  It's on the sweet side, very different from usual stew recipes.  It's a nice change of pace.  Excellent cold weather comfort food.

This was a little too sweet for my tastes, but it was a nice change of pace from the usual stews.  Made it in the crockpot and my boyfriend really enjoyed it.  The recommended amount of cornstarch wasn't enough to thicken it, so I added more.
It took a lot of work and the end result was okay....it was quite bland and we ended up dumping on a lot more salt and pepper.  I gave the rest to my hub for lunches, as I refused to eat it.

This was different, but I liked it. I don't know if this recipe will replace my normal beef stew, but I'll definitely make it again. I added garlic and some hot pepper flakes--personal preference. It had a lovely colour  and it was very nice served with mash potatoes.

This stew has a very nice flavor, i didn't have any wine so i used low sodium beef broth, and i did add a couple more cloves of garlic, (i can't help it, garlic is so good).  I also froze half of this for another night. I can't wait to make this with wine, i bet it's even better! Thank you evelyn for this recipe.

Added some carrots and potatoes after cooking the onions.  Only 1 cup of wine and 1 cup of water.  No constarch.  Cooked it on a cast iron dutch oven that lets no heat escape.  After browning the meat and onions, I added the liquid and stuck in a preheated 300 oven for 4 1/2 hours and it came fork tender with an incredible flavor.  Highly recommend this cooking method.

What more can be said about this winner of a recipe.  We couldn't stop eating it.  My DH said he can't wait till we have it again.  I made plenty of potatoes and poured the gravy over them.  I highly recommend making this luscious stew!
This recipe was perfect we used gravy roast pieces for this dish.The only thing i added was 1 teaspoon chopped ginger. I will be checking out more recipes from Evelyn.

this was a hit w/ the fam. my husband couldn't figure out what the new secret ingredient was but he assumed it had a slight bbq flavor. so i let him think that and didn't mention the hoisin sauce. kids loved it so this will definately go into their favorites file. i on the other hand still prefer the traditional beef stew. but overall this was a great recipe.

This went over big at my house.  I rolled the meat in  flour before adding to the pot to saute.  Also, I used pearl onions in place of the chopped,  and threw in some fresh mushrooms and lg. chunks of celery about 10 minutes after the carrots. The combo of ingredients made for a great flavored stew and one that will be repeated here when the mood strikes for stew again. We loved it's richness and flavors!  Had along with mashed potatoes and sauteed garlic green beans on the side.

I've made a similar version of this recipe for years and it was great -- that is, until I found this recipe that added red wine!  The wine does wonders for the flavour, I can hardly believe how much better it is this way.  Thanks!
The slow-cooking really bought out all the flavours of this dish. We used veal and homemade hoisin sauce, but otherwise exactly as the recipe entails. My hubby raved about this!!

I really enjoyed this beef stew, which I modified to suit the ingredients we had on hand. I used white wine rather than red, and just 1 c rather than 2 because if it were too "winy", my son would balk. I also added 2 lbs of halved gold new potatoes along with the carrots, and used one 28-oz can whole peeled tomatoes so my son could easily avoid them. This was a great one-pot meal that went well with crusty bread, and it's terrific as leftovers too. Thank you!

Very good!  Deep and rich and perfect comfort food.  I was not sweet at all to me.  I followed the directions but added about a 1/4 cup of brown sugar and some worchecisizer (sp LOL) sauce.  I also doebled the cornstarch with a can of beef broth! My son loves it too!
Tasty! I added pearl onions and cooked it for seven hours on simmer. The meat fell apart and the gravy was really nice. I served it on mashed potatoes with peas.

Ev, this was great, thank you.  I wanted it to slow cook as I had to go and get the girls from school so ended up cooking in the oven on about 125C for a couple of hours.  I'm also not keen on carrots so instead used some diced sweet potato and about 1/2 hour before serving threw in some frozen peas and didn't end up thickening it.  Served in some Aldi brand yorkshire puddings which were frozen and just needed heating up in the oven.  Great recipe for a cold night.

OMG this was absolutely delicious. The combination of flavours worked so well with just enough of the wine flavouring coming through. I had things to do during the day so I browned the meat after lightly flouring it and then threw everything bar 1 cup of wine and the garlic (and the finishing ingredients) into the crock pot on high and let it be for most the day. About an hour or so prior to serving I threw in the other cup of wine and the garlic with the carrots etc. This got raves from my guests and is definately something I'd cook again and again. Who would have thought stew could be so stylish!
I made this last night and received rave reviews from my daughter.  She said if her tummy would let her she would eat the whole thing!  Guess I will be making this one again.
Great stew!! Definately will make this recipe again. I served this with mashed potatoes. I used about 1/3 cup hoisin sauce which was perfect for our tastes. Thanks for sharing this great recipe.
Perfection!
Has a bit of a sweet flavor that I didn't care for.
The family really liked this one and I changed it up the next night for leftovers and served it with dumplings.  I will definitely use this one again.  thanks
Delicious.  Used half the hoisin sauce and added more garlic and veggies.  Wonderful stew.
Delicious! Very rich flavour. Even the kids loved it.
