This was just what I was looking for!  It was easy to prepare and very delicious.  I did put 1/4 cup red wine in the sauce, and I baked it for 15 minutes more than recipe called for.  My husband says this recipe is a keeper.

Amazing recipe!  I used whole wheat noodles.  It took a little longer to prep than the recipe stated, but it wasn't hard to make at all.  Definitely use a large dish because this is a huge batch.  You can probably feed a minimum of a dozen people with it.

Great Recipe!  I did end up adding equal parts eggplant and zucchini.  I seasoned them and pre-roasted them in the oven.  I also added green onions to the recipe. I also put in a little extra effort making sure that the spinach was as well drained as possible... The result was that this casserole stood up well and was not runny at all! No carrots as I'm not a big fan. I followed the baking instructions on the back of the lasagna box  and covered it with sprayed foil to prevent sticking, and baked it in the oven for about an hour. It came out a little watery at the bottom, so next time I'm going to make sure I dry the spinach and mushrooms thoroughly! Another thing I would do differently next time is I would lightly salt the veggies. I would use fresh sauteed spinach vs. the frozen/thawed kind... frozen spinach retained a lot of water. It was borderline impossible to dry, tasted funky, and was VERY stemmy(I hate spinach stems, Ill spend one hour de-stemming fresh spinach, Im crazy like that). It kind of over-powered the ricotta, which where I used the skim kind it was a little bland to begin with. All in all a great recipe and I will make it again!

This was amazing. I definitely messed with the recipe a little, just because I was so afraid it would be soggy. This added an hour to my prep, but I felt it was worth it. I roasted the sliced zuchini and the carrots with olive oil and salt before layering them. I also sauteed the mushrooms to remove excess water and add flavor. I added salt and pepper and a little parsley and basil to the cheese mixture and used some of the mozzarella as well. I think next time I will add asiago to the cheesy nonsense on top, but overall, this is the best veggie lasagna I have ever had. It was a huge hit at my New Year's Eve dinner party and I will definitely be trotting it out often in the future.
Made this for the first time tonight and it was a huge success! Will most definitely be making again!!!
This is absolutely amazing ... I used carrot "chips" and full fat ricotta and fresh shredded full fat mozzarella ! It was incredible and my husband loved it !

I was told by my husband and daughter last night that this was officially THE best meal I have ever made!! I have to agree, it was amazing!! This was a great recipe! I did follow Birdinhand's suggestions and I browned a small onion and then added the mushrooms to the saute pan and saute'ed them with the onions, as well. I added the minced garlic to the sauce along with the oregano. Then I remembered that the flavor I associate with "lasagna" is fennel, and I added about a half teaspoon of ground fennel to the sauce, too. Oh, did that make the difference! My box of whole wheat pasta had 8 lasagna noodles and I used them all, so I had a couple of noodles going perpendicular to the rest at the bottom of my casserole dish. I had two cups of zucchini, so I cut back the spinach to one 10 oz box and kept the sauce to one quart since zucchini is so juicy. I do not like a sloppy lasagna. I also ended up with about a cup of carrots when I grated two of them, and used it all. I also used all of my two packages of mozzarella, which was four cups. I probably used about a cup of grated parm, too. I probably don't need to point this out by now, but just in case this is the first of its reviews you are reading, this recipe is very flexible! Throw in whatever vegetables you like, but don't let them be too wet. Make sure they will cook through in the baking, or prepare them by sauteing them first.
Alittle prep time involved but the lasagne is delicious! The shredded carrots add a nice texture. My family loved this!
Delicious... I am transitioning to a more vegetarian food plan and had to try this. Delicious. I followed the recipe exactly except I used oven ready noodles. It was so good.. thank you for sharing.

I did not cook the lasagna noodles, added a bit of salt to the sauce & ricotta layers, cooked a bag of fresh spinach and everything turned out perfectly. I added salt to the sauce & ricotta layers. Excellent flavor for a veggie lasagna. This was delicious, I used fresh spinach i washed it and shook it but that was it. I used a jar of tom pasta sauce and added in extra cup of grated carrot and a tin of diced tomatoes.

Keep tweaking the recipe, it will be great.

This was the first time that I made egg rolls & it was easier than I imagined. I enjoyed the recipe and will make these again. Next time I will buy two packages of egg roll wrappers as I had a lot of the "stuffing left over since I only had 1 package. Thanks for sharing. Great, easy recipe.

I was very pleasantly surprised with the ease of making these egg rolls -- and the excellent taste that resulted. This was my maiden voyage in this area of endeavor and I had a head full of dreadful consequences -- none of which materialized. I added about half a can of chopped Chinese vegetables -- and this turned out very well. Also, I recommend these be rolled as tightly as possible -- this makes for greater ease in both cooking and eating. Excellent addition to my new Chinese Cookbook. Bonnie, thanks for posting this.

These are AWESOME! I too added sesame oil and ginger to the mix of ground beef and cabbage.  I get asked to make these at all the events I have.  If you are wondering if it is worth the time and the effort...it is!! However I liked them best dipped in sweet and sour dipping sauce.
I loved this recipe, they were fabulous and surprisingly, very easy to make!

I can't believe I forgot to review these!  We made these a month or so ago and loved it!  I couldn't find a "package" of shredded cabbage, so I got head and shredded it myself, same w/ the carrots.  Weights or volume would have been great in this recipe!  Instead of the ground beef, we used chicken.  YUMMY.  I think next time I will add a bit of green onion tops, soy sauce, ginger and sesame oil like some of the other reviewers.  And there will be a next time....tomorrow!!  We froze the leftovers and they made handy lunches for awhile!

My first attempt at making egg rolls.  Although they didn't look the greatest the taste was amazing.  My family devoured them and requested them for all our "chinese nights".  Very good flavor and simple ingredients. thank you for a winner....Stephanie

My famiy and I love egg rolls.  This was a wonderful recipes and we will be adding this to our Chinese night menus.  The first time we made them, we hardly had any left for dinner.  I made them earlier in the afternoon to avoid the dinner time frenzy and DH, DS, DD and even myself could hardly keep our fingers off them.  They were even good cold out of the fridge!  At dinner time I just put them on a cookie sheet and plopped them in a 400 degree oven for about 10 minutes, using a thermometer we brought them back up to 160.  They were fabulous!!  Thanks.

The filling for the inside of these was good but I had problems getting the wraps tight enough. They kept ballooning out when I put them in the deep fryer & 1 popped open leaving a mess in the oil. This was my 1st attempt making egg rolls & I must say I suck at it. I think they would have tasted better if I had wrapped them tight enough because they were also greasy all thru the roll.
 I'm keeping the recipe just in case I want to attempt this again because I know the filling was good. I used ground chicken instead of ground beef.

My boyfriend had a terrible day at work yesterday so I made him a themed dinner to cheer huim up - Chinese!  This recipe along with fried rice and sesame chicken - amazing!  These were so simple to make and tasted better than some we have had at restaurants.  Wow, that's all I can say.

Thank thanks this recipe was great? I made them tonight my family loved them, I served them with rice and sweet and sour pork, Ill try to post the recipe for the sweet and sor pork soon. The egg rolls tasted great with it.
We had these with dinner last night and they were EXCELLANT. I will make these again soon.

These are really good. I used the preshredded coleslaw mix and added a little powdered ginger to the meat.
Next time I think I will use ground pork instead. I also pan fried mine in Canola oil rather than deep frying, so they were flatter, but still tasty.

This is about how I make mine. The only thing I do is add water chestnuts, soy sauce to the ground beef mixture plus lots of red pepper flakes. Other than that follow the recipe to the T! Love them!!!!

I know you don't need another raving review, but you're gonna get one.  These egg rolls lived up to their name.  I boiled the cabbage first, throwing the shredded carrot in the pan just a couple minutes before draining.  I added ginger along with the spices & made sweet & sour sauce for dipping.  The recipe states 2 teaspoons of filling but my egg roll wrappers must have been huge cause I ended up using 2 Tablespoons each & still had enough filling for 40 egg rolls.  I fried them on the stove instead of digging out the deep fryer.  We'll be making this recipe again & again.  Thanks for sharing, Bonnie!

This was my first time ever making egg rolls.  I made the recipe like it says except I added soy sauce to the meat and it turned out really good.  I could use a little practice on my wrapping but otherwise they were really good.  I love egg rolls and thanks to this recipe I can now make my own.  thanks for the recipe.

Loved this recipe.  I did however make some "adjustments" to fit it into a busy weeknight.  First I used ground pork instead of beef.  I also cheated and used a bagged coleslaw mix instead of the cabbage and carrots.  You do definately need to "over season" the meat but it turns out perfectly when mixed with the other ingredients.  My family says they were way better than take out!

These were Awesome!!, a little putzee, but fun to make. I used bottles sweet & sour sauce for dipping. They were very good reheated in microwave, altough they lost the crunch, it did not deter from the awesome flavor. Great to make ahead and reheat for the party hors'derves.

These were GREAT!  I added some chopped celery and chopped onion and added some sesame seed oil to give more flavor. I also used about 1 Tbs. of minced garlic along with the garlic powder when browning the ground beef.  We enjoyed these dipped in recipe#116960 
Thanks for sharing the recipe! :)
These were very good, and you are very right about all the seasoning.  I believe I under-seasoned them.  Will probably make again with shrimp or chicken next time.  Thanks!
You will never buy a another egg roll from the chinese retaurant again.  I make these without the ground beef.   I just microwave the cabbage and carrots for a 2 minutes and then season and roll.

Thank you.  I'm a Chicago transplant, and I miss the food so much.  There was a Chinatown hole in the wall named Guey Yee that I grew up on.  Have never found an egg roll to compare, but this put me on the right track.  Added 2T peanut butter to the filling mixture, and whoop, there it is!

Awesome recipe! I used Jimmy Dean reduced fat pork sausage. I browned the meat w/ a little chopped onion & garlic. I didn't measure any of the spices, I just added a little here and there until everything tasted the way I wanted it. I did add a frozen bag of sliced green beans to the recipe. I let the meat and vegetables sit for about 20 minutes. With the egg roll wrappers I used I didn't need an egg to seal the wrap I just dabbed a little bit of water. Came out great! Thanks for the recipe!
There were wonderful. We used duck sauce to dip. Made these for dinner guests who proclaimed they were the best egg rolls - ever!
These were really fun to make.  Enjoyed them very much!

These are soooo good.  They're better than even the best restaraunt eggrolls I've ever had.  I think it's because they're so fresh.  I've done these with gd. beef and pork sausage.  We've played with the recipe and added cilantro, fresh ginger, cucumber, etc. but I still love the basic cabbage/carrot mixture best.  Thanks Bonnie for  a fantastic recipe!

There used to be this wonderful chinese resturant where I grew up, they had the best egg rolls. The place closed a few years back. Since then, I have never had egg rolls that even came close to theirs, until now! These are out of this world. After fixing these, you'll never order egg rolls again. They also freeze well. Thanks for such a great recipe!!!
yum!  even the kids liked these, amazing!

Me and my boyfriend gobbled these down. I had trouble rolling them so they came out more like pockets, but were still delicious. Also, I found that for some strange reason, if you let them sit maybe 10 minutes or so after frying they taste much better. So give them plenty of time to cool and they are amazing. So easy with such simple ingredients that create such huge flavor!

These were delicious and I had plenty left to freeze for later. The only problem I had was with the carrots. They were too hard, even after soaking them with the beef for the 15 minutes, and they poked holes in some of the egg roll wrappers. I think I'll just leave them out next time. Also, I had a lot of leftover filling so I think next time I'll only use 3/4 lb of ground beef.

My son, who does not like restaurant egg rolls, loved these! I used chicken thighs instead of ground beef and 'overspiced' the mixture as suggested. Then I mixed all the ingredients together while the chicken was still hot and let it sit. This sufficiently softened the cabbage and carrots. Easy and delicious! Thanks for posting!
Awesome the only problem is that it didn't occur  to me that you don't stack them together before you fry them duh anyways 5 stars

I made this for my aunt for her birthday! they came out fantastic. you were soooo right about "over" seasoning. the next time I make them, I'm definately using more garlic, but they were DELICIOUS. My aunt loved them, and she had never eaten egg rolls before!

I have always felt intimidated about making egg rolls because I thought it would be difficult. I was WRONG. These were easy and tasted pretty good. Of couse nothing is a substitute for authentice Chinese egg rolls, but these at home goodies stack up pretty well. The only changes that I made were adding ground ginger powder along with the salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Also, for health reasons, I opted to bake these at 425 degrees for 15ish minutes after I sprayed them with Pam. 
My preference would NOT be Grey Poupon Dijon. It was gross. I did like soy sauce and honey mustard as dipping sauces.
With soy sauce added, and using ground pork, these are sensational!  I used Chinese Duck Sauce to dip them in.  Yum Mmmmm!
I really liked these eggrolls because of the simplicity.  My husband did use a little chunk of ginger while cooking the meat (we used ground pork instead).  Thank you so much for posting!

I LOVE THESE!!!!! WOW! 
My family and I all agree that these are some of the best egg rolls we have ever had. I pan fried a couple of pork chops then minced them very fine in place of the ground beef and added a small amount of 5 spice powder.
These were really great. I didn't use the pre-packaged cabbage or carrots so I had the portions off a little and we ended up with more veggie than beef. But they were still very tasty. Thanks!!

I'm currently in egg roll heaven.  We wanted chinese night without having to go out, so I scoured Zaar for some recipes.  The perfect egg roll has always eluded me, I almost gave up and bought some frozen ones, and I found this.  I was so impressed with these!  The trick to overseasoning was right...I used some jarred minced garlic AND powder on the ground beef, then dumped it over a  bag of coleslaw mix (carrots, red and white cabbage).  I microwaved it for 5 minutes to soften it all, and let cool for about 20 minutes as I was preparing other things.  I thought I had used plenty of seasoning, then tasted and added even more, along with the tiniest pinch of chinese 5 spice, since we like the flavor. My 5 year old helped me with the egg wash, and we fried in peanut oil.  Fantastic, and the leftovers froze well, and reheated in te oven beautifully.  And it was EASY!  Thanks so much for this recipe!
These ROCK!!!!!!!

You were right, I was skeptical... I seasoned the meat until it nearly triggered my gag reflex but these turned out awesome... I added a cup or two of bean sprouts and they went quick. Thanks, excellent recipe...

As an update I made them substituting mild spicy pork sausage instead of ground beef and of course backed down the spices. They were terrific...!

Thanks again.

Great recipe! I didn't put enough seasoning in the filling. I tasted one after I made it and could hardly taste any flavor in the meat mixture, so thankfully I hadn't rolled all of them up. I added more seasoning to the mixture and cooked them up. They were delicious
So easy to make and tastes wonderful!  My 4 year old daughter was very excited to help with this recipe as well.

These were very easy and very tasty.  I went with pork instead of beef but otherwise followed the recipe.  I do wish there were amounts listed on the spices since I'm so bad at adjusting according to my own taste.  Next time, I will add even more seasoning.  Still, they were very good!  This made 19 regular size egg rolls for me.
i made this for the first time tonight and they turned out wonderfully. i added curry powder and substituted fresh crushed garlic. i'll definately be using this recipe again. 5 stars.

I came across this recipe recently and gave them a try tonight and found them wonderful, Only change I made was use a pound of ground pork since that is what I had on hand and while meat was browning I added a few dashes of Worchestershire sauce.along with some finely chopped green onion. Also I found along with my famikly that LACHOY Sweet & Sour sauce as the dipping sauce, we found it was much better than Dijon mustard. :)

I think this could use a lot more spices....I even added ginger and Chinese 5 Spice, and I still didn't get the egg-roll I was hoping for. My huband loved it though! I also bought sweet and sour dipping sauce, and szchesuan sauce to have some more variety.

These were very easy to make and very flavorful but I wish it had a little something else to them just not sure what.  My family ate them just fine even my 5 year old.  I dipped mine in honey mustard which was good.  I'm sure I'll make them again at some point! Thanks for sharing

It was much better than a previous egg roll recipe I tried, but I really didn't like having no guide on how much salt & garlic to use.  If I could flavor things well on my own, I wouldn't need recipes.

These are yummy!  I found out the hard way that you have to fry them as you roll them.  I tried rolling all of mine and then frying them in batches (I doubled the recipe for a party).  The rolls got soggy and fell apart on me, but that was my error, the recipe is great!

These are BOMB-DIGGITY!!!! My ex mother in law who was Japanese used to make homemade egg rolls with ground beef but I couldn't remember her recipe so searching online found this recipe that I could use as a guideline along with what I could remember from her. I added green onions, shredded ginger root, and broccoli cut into small pieces (tops only; dime-sized) with the cabbage. Opted to use the angel hair prepared cabbage and shredded my own carrots since they were not cooked prior to frying.

I served these for Christmas Brunch yesterday.  They are so delicious & full of flavour!!  Everyone was gushing with compliments. I followed the recipe exactly & then added a sprinkling of freshly ground pepper before baking.  I'm pretty certain I'm going to be asked to make these again & again.

Served this with steaks and French Bread. They were delicious! I fellowed the recipe exactly the way it was written and had no problem. They were GREAT! I added freshly ground pepper before baking also. Its a keeper for sure in my book! Thank you for sharing your recipe.
My in-laws were in town from North Carolina, and I wanted to impress them with a good breakfast. This did it! Great subtle taste, but definately have a home-feel cooked flavor.

I haven't made these yet, but I'm a nut for not dirtying dishes if I don't have to! So I thought of this shortcut. Why put the potatoes in the pot to mix with all the ingredients?  Just put them from the colander into the baking dish and toss with the other ingredients before baking! Saves on messy pot. Just a thought,  Lee

Doubled recipe and made it with Christmas breakfast.  It was okay, but I don't think I would make it again.  Just a preference, but our family likes things that are a little more special and not so everyday ingredients for holiday meals. Thanks for the recipe.

Fantastic potato recipe.  I use it instead of french fries with my burger meals.  I reduced the salt and added some crushed red pepper for a little zing.  My boys love these....easy, tasty, and satisfying!!
My whole family loves these potatoes!  I had some like this during a beach trip once and was so happy to find the recipe on here!
awesome recipe. I only added about 1 to 1 1/2 tsp of the seasoning salt. It was plenty! 2 tsp would have been too much! I also overboiled the potatoes....accidently but they still came out lovely!
I skipped the onion and paprika but these were still delish and perfectly cooked!

This review is long overdue!  I actually was sure I had submitted one a couple months ago, but it doesn't seem to be showing up.  I've made these potatoes a few times and they always turn out so well.  They can be served with a variety of dishes -- and also any meal or occasion.  I love being able to finish them off in the oven.

definitely a keeper - i prefer this method over baking the potatoes in the oven or frying them on the stove.  boiling them first gives them a much better texture, and then baking them crisps up the skin.  delicious.

Made exactly as directed but I did them ahead up until the baking part.  I put them in the refrigerator overnight and baked them in the morning.  Everyone loved these potatoes!  Served with ham, french toast and fruit salad.
Great tasting, easy recipe. I will replace the nutmeg with cinnamon next time as I prefer the later.
Terrific recipe! I left out the mushrooms and used Italian Sweet Sausage with casings removed, but did everything else with the recipe. DEEEEEELISH! Thanks for posting!!

When I told DH we were having stuffed squash for dinner, it was all he could do not to order pizza.  However, he ended up eating half of it!  Even my finicky 2 year old loved it, although my notional 5 year old was less enthusiastic.  It did take a while to do all the chopping (I did it by hand) but the recipe was very, very easy otherwise and well worth they time.
These were great.  I used Jimmy Dean sausage and bread cubes instead of crumbs.  Made a nice main course for a Fall women's luncheon for 114.  Would also be a nice addition to ghe Thanksgiving table.

My dad is overflowing with vegetables this year because of the warm fall, so he convinced me to take a couple of acorn squash home with me.  I am so glad that I did and that I decided to try out this recipe!  mmmmm was it delicious!  The apples, sausage, and squash go so well together.  The only modifications that I made were using 1/2 lb turkey sausage and bread cubes rather than 1 lb pork sausage and bread crumbs.  Oh, and I didn't have quite a cup of bread cubes, so I actually used some crumbled ramen noodles.  It gave the stuffing a little crunch.  This recipe is a keeper!  Thanks Kaarin!
As a tradition, my family votes on for the best dish on the Thanksgiving table.  This came is second. This is a wonderful way to serve acorn squash.

I absolutely loved this! Half of my family loved it and half didn't like it at all. Kids! My boys didn't care for it at all but what do they know? My 4 yr old daughter cleaned her plate. This was awesome! Thanks!
Delicious made with turkey sausage.

Loved this! Let's see... I cut out the celery (because I didn't have any and don't really prefer that taste), used crushed croutons instead of breadcrumbs (had no bread) and decreased the whole recipe to make just one squash. The flavor of the mushrooms sinking into the squash, mmmmmm.... So good!!

This is my new favorite recipe! I didn't have any sage or celery rib, and I used fresh garlic instead of garlic salt. I used chicken italian sausage. The mix of ingredients were so tasty together, and made for great leftovers. I will repeat this recipe often!

This was great--even with the changes I had to make! I needed to use pantry ingredients, and so had no sausage, no onion, no celery, no mushroom... So I used ground beef with breakfast sausage spices (Recipe #214213) and dried cherries and raisins instead of the apple, with onion powder and celery seed. I think it would be even better as written! Definitely a keeper! Thanks!  Update:  I made this again, as written (except for the mushrooms) and it was fantastic!!!!  Definitely 5 stars!
We really enjoyed this. I halved the recipe but used the full pound of sausage (I used Italian turkey sausage) Instead of acorn squash I used an ambercup. Great autumn treat.

I followed the recipe as close as possible. Use gala apples. I might try to take the squash out of the shell after it is cooked, put it in a dish, then put the stuffing over it and put it back in the oven so it would be less messy.
Made this for thanksgiving, it looks great on the table and it's delicious too.

I thought this was just wonderful. Instead of the sage and garlic salt I coated the raw squash with a little butter, molasses and brown sugar after poking lots of hole in the squash so the flavor would soak in. It gave the dish a sweet rich flavor.
LOVED this recipe!! I did alter it a bit and it was SO delish!!! I omitted the mushrooms and instead added 1/4 c toasted chopped pecans and 1/4 c dried cranberries.  I will make this dish often!!!
I decided to try this recipe because I'd never had acorn squash before.  I don't think I would like the texture of the squash by itself, but combined with the stuffing it was pretty good.
I love roasted acorn squash as a side dish, and this is a really good way to do it as a main course. I used maple flavored sausage and all the flavors went together wonderfully.
This is a great fall meal. We made it with regular pork sausage the first time and the last two times, we've used chicken apple sausage and really liked the combo with the apples already in the mix.
Very good.  I used chicken sausage with apple.  Good and filling, I think you could probably experiment and find other seasoned sausages that would work with this.

This is a really great and filling recipe. Only problem I had was that I had way more stuffing than I could fit in my squash so I think next time I would only make half of the stuffing or else fill more squash

My husband found a sale on Squash, so I had to come up with some new ways to prepare it.  This recipe is sure to be a family favorite.  A very nice mix of flavors, and use other ingredients that I usually keep on hand.   A winner!

We enjoyed this dish very much.  We thought the stuffing was excellent, though maybe not as ideal of a pairing with acorn squash.  We plan to use the stuffing with either chicken or duck because I think it would be a very nice compliment.  Thanks for an enjoyable dinner.

DH, not an avid veggie eater, scarfed this down and asked if there was more.  I used turkey breakfast sausage.  Simple to make, good for you and delicious...five stars from us.  It might also be fun to cut the top off of the squash like a jack-o-lantern and stuff it that way.  I have another stuffed acorn squash recipe that does it this way.

This dish is so good it is ridiculous! And just as good for leftovers too. I am sooo very glad I stumbled upon it. Thank you for posting! UPDATE - Instead of pork sausage I used Recipe #100408 instead and topped it with a round slice of provolone. Healthier and just as tasty!!
Yum!  I veganized it by using Gimme Lean Sausage & egg replacer.  Very yummy and healthy!

This recipe is a winner! I'm notorious for changing things up a bit, so instead of parsley I added some rosemary and thyme. I also added some slivered almonds that I had leftover from another recipe, which added a nice extra layer of texture, and put some swiss cheese on top.  Worked so well with this recipe! Thank you, I will definitely be making this again!

Really nice, balanced recipe - subtly sweet, reflecting nicely the squash. We used some fantastic, spicy farmer's market chorizo, farro (soaked, not cooked) in place of the bread crumbs, and a duck egg instead of a chicken egg. The chorizo probably made the dish and the farro was a sweet/nutty/chewy addition (wild rice would also make a nice substitution). Without the chorizo it might have been under-spiced. We were able to stuff three squash with the filling we made.
Fun! I've never said that about a recipe before, but is was a fun and delicious meal.  Next time I might try turkey sausage to keep the calories down.  Well done Kaarin

We thought this was recipe was really good. Total comfort food for a cold, rainy night. I used Italian sausage and followed the recipe all the way. I think next time I'll add some dried cranberries and pecans. Thanks for posting this delicious Fall recipe.
This was great!  I would love to make this for Thanksgiving or Christmas.  Such simple ingredients but tasted (and looked) like it came from a fancy restaurant!  Definitely will make again.

Absolutely fantastic!  I made this gltuen/dairy free by using Smart Balance in place of the butter and made bread crumbs out of a toasted gluten free roll.  It was absolutely delicious.  I will most definitely be making this again.  Thanks for sharing!

Made this last night and both my husband and I thought that the flavors were absolutely wonderful. The sausage paired with the apple and herbs blended really well and made for a filling and tasty main dish. I did change it a bit from the main recipe to give a little bit more flavor, instead of parsley we used fresh rosemary and thyme from our garden. I also added chopped carrot to the vegetables which gave it nice texture and flavor. I also only cooked the acorn squash for 45 minutes the first time and a full 20 minutes the last time with the stuffing. The squash was perfectly done- not overcooked. The only thing that we might change is that it was not as moist as we would like (we like our stuffing more dense and moist than dry) but other than that, a wonderful recipe!

Made it tonight using a Kuri squash, because it's what I had.  Used a locally made Chicken Italian sausage, skipped the garlic and mushrooms and used  apple, celery, onion, chopped pecans and dried cherries, and crushed herb Pepperidge bread stuffing mix for the crumbs.  Also poked holes in the squash and used the butter, brown sugar, molasses another reviewer mentioned.  Clearly this is a recipe that is very forgiving, --so easy to make it the way you want it.  It was fabulous and not a lot of work.  And, you can make it ahead, baking the squash and mixing the stuffing, then fill the squash when ready and bake for 30 minutes (longer if ingredients are cold).  Definitely going into our winter rotation.  Thanks Kaarin and reviewers whose ideas I stole!

I made this for dinner tonight and it was delicious.  I followed the recipe with only one exception - I used fresh sage since I did not have dried.   We thought it was a fantastic blend of flavors. This was the best acorn squash recipe I have ever made and will definitely be making this again.  Thank you
Filling and delicious.  We baked the seeds for a healthy treat tomorrow too.

Wonderful recipe. I used half spicy and half regular Italian sausage, which adds a nice kick to the dish. I also added water to my dish when baking the squash. This cut down on the initial cooking time and kept the squash quite moist.

I made this the other night for dinner and omg this is delicious.  The sage butter brushed on the squash add so much to the dish.  My kids weren't sure about it at first, but warmed up to it in the end.  The sausage mixture is so good.  Thank you for sharing this recipe with us, its so good.
What a delicious recipe! My husband and young children also loved it. I didn't have mushrooms, but I added zucchini and minced fresh garlic. I will definitely be making this again!

Apparently I am the only one who does it this way but my sausage is home ground and very, very lean! I just mix up all the stuffing without any sauteing or browning and mound it in the cut squash. It bakes in about an hour and the juices bake right into the squash.
I tweaked this kind of a lot for my husband's and my tastes, and actually ended up posting my version Recipe #508813 with credit to Kaarin, of course! Thanks so much for a really amazing recipe!

Delicious recipe!  I too made a few substitutions (I used cranberry turkey sausage to add some more of the "fall" flavor) and used honeycrisp apples instead of macintosh. So good!!  The stuffing was a little dry, but I think that's because turkey sausage doesn't give much in the way of drippings.  When mixed with the acorn squash it wasn't an issue though.  I used the extra stuffing to make tiny meatloaf cupcakes.  Thanks for the recipe!
Made this tonight, it smells as good as it looks!! There are going to be no leftovers!! :-)

I made this for dinner tonight using veggie sausage, fresh sage and Parmesan cheese  because that is what I had on hand.  It ended up being just DH  for dinner so I oly used one acorn squash.  Instead of stuffing the squash I scooped it out and added it to the stuffing mixture before putting it all in an 8" square baking dish. I covered it with foil and baked for twenty minutes.  We both really enjoyed this.

I made this for tonight's dinner and it was delicious! I used hot Italian sausage, fresh sage and made my own bread crumbs, leaving them a little more like actual stuffing. This dinner was fantastic for this time of year and since it's raining outside, it seemed like the perfect comfort food.

This came out great! I used chicken sausage instead (a mix of sweet blueberry and garlic and herb). Omitted the mushrooms since the DH is not a fan, and used farro instead of the breadcrumbs (very happy I did this, it added great texture). Topped with a little grated sharp white cheddar and served with crusty garlic bread. This was a hit! Now that I've made it, I will change the following next time: 1) use chorizo or hot sausage -- a little spice would bring this to another level, 2) increase the apple amount -- i was scared it would be too sweet, so I was conservative with the apples but I shouldn't have been. The sweetness is definitely needed to offset the plain flavor of the squash, 3) add some fresh thyme/rosemary and a little nutmeg, and maybe even throw in some dried cranberries for extra "oomph". Can't wait to try it again with these changes!

I followed the recipe to the letter and it was yummy. Then I modified it and it turned out yummier. Got rid of the breadcrumbs and used olive oil versus melted butter. Made a crisscross pattern with knife on squash to allow greater penetration of the oil. Sauteed the vegetables with olive oil. Used fresh spinach and one dried fig for sweetness.
This recipe is absolutely delicious and filling. I used spicey chicken sausage in place of pork, and quinoa instead of bread crumbs, just to make it a bit healthier. I will be making this again!

I made this dish tonight after returning from farmers market with a variety of squash. I followed the base of this recipe substituting out the sausage for veggie sausage and then i replace the bread crumbs with cooked quinoa. I felt an egg would weigh down the fluffiness of the quinoa so i left that out. This was SOOO good. I was hesitant on using too much apple so i only used one small one. It was fine but could of used a second apple. Luckily for me, i had a jar of homemade applesauce and paired it on the side. Perfect
Made this and it was delicious!! Was a huge hit with my husband as well. I used seasoned panko crumbs and it added a really nice flavor! Also added some kale in for a bit of extra greens!
I added a second egg because the sausage mixture seemed a bit dry. Also left out the mushrooms. It was delicious!

Thanks Kaarin! just finished it for dinner!! Very yummy! I pre-cooked the squash in the morning and flipped them upside down until 5 when I prepped the rest. I had organic ground pork, so there wasn't a need to drain the pork - not a lot of drippings. Used some basil in the stuffing as well! Will make again! Suzanne

Used ground beef instead of pork. Macintosh apples were not at my store so used Granny Smith. Spiced it up with oregano, red pepper, garlic and cayenne. Salt and pepper of course. Then thought it needed a little more sweetness so added a little brown sugar. Was absolutely delisous. Don’t be afraid to alter the basic recipe to your taste. I’ll. Make it again for company. Oh I also topped it with a little Ragu more for presentation than anything else but it added just the right flavor to the dish.
Absolutely delicious! Wonderful combination of flavors.

I really enjoyed this fall recipe. Like others, I baked the squash 40 minutes, then the final 20 minutes with stuffing. I added carrots, but beyond that stuck to the recipe. My husband added sirracha ketchup because his taste buds are fried, but I thought it had a great sweet flavor as is. Great dish to mix up the regular routine in our house.

Knock your socks off good! My husband doesn't like squash, and I'm not a big fan of acorn squash, and we both thought it was terrific. Very filling, too. I especially like that unlike similar recipes, it binds with egg instead of cheese.

Thank you for the quickie recipe! I added in browned hamburger and 1 Table spoon of white vinegar because I like beef in my borscht and a bit more bite. We got beets at the local farmer's market and I roasted them...then just chopped them and added them later with the cabbage. Thanks again!

This was the best borscht recipe I've tried so far!  Our daughters are adopted from Russia and we're trying to incorporate Russian cuisine into our meals occasionally.  I used vegetarian broth and added some salt/pepper.  It was delicious!
We eat this all the time at my house.  My husband loves it.  It tastse just like the borscht at Moscow on the Hill, a Russian restaraunt in our area where I first tasted borscht.
This was a great and simple recipe.  My family loved it so much we didn't have any leftovers.  Next time I am definitely doubling the recipe.
Delicious and easy, thank you!!  I really liked it with lemon and sour cream.  I used vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian....

I have never had borscht before so I can't compare it to anything but this was quite good.  I love how healthy it is.  I might even skip the sour cream next time.  We found it to be very light...too light for a main course.  We added some tofu "meatballs" and it gave it much more heft which made it filling enough for us.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Sometimes simple is the best and this borscht is a good example. I cheated a bit and used bagged shredded carrot and cabbage and used plain yogurt rather than sour cream. Made for ZWT4
Fantastic! Easy to make, nutritious and delicious! Its great with or without sour cream and dill.

Definitely better the next day! I love borscht and this is the first time I've made it myself. I really like the borscht I've had at restaurants better. But this stuff is pretty good. I added bay leaves, oregano, thyme, and some dill while everything was cooking. I also added cilantro finish it off. I also added a sprinkle of sea salt and some pepper. Otherwise, I think this would be very bland as is. Really good and easy to prepare, but I am going to still look for a better recipe.

I love this recipe for its simplicity, great taste, and the fact that it's pretty much impossible to screw up.  I don't worry much about measuring how much veg I put in it, I just keep stirring until it all cooks down (which takes longer than specified below, usually 40m to really get the cabbage tender, though that's probably because I put a lot more in).  I make this often and from scratch with beef bullion instead of canned...makes my whole house smell amazing!  Also fabulous with a heavy pumpernickel bread & butter.

This was delicious.  I was impressed at how hearty it was w/o meat.  I did modify the ingredients to match what I had.  I did not have cabbage, but I added chopped cauliflower and grated potato.  I also added oregano, bay leaves and dill as embuggy suggested.  I didn't have any sour cream, but I added a teaspoon of cream cheese to each serving.  I'm excited to try the leftovers tomorrow!  Thanks again.

I made this borscht during this past winter and wow, was it ever delicious. I wanted to make some easy recipes to celebrate my Polish/Russian heritage and this was a great way to start. It was easy and saved well. I used red onion and red cabbage to really intensify the color of the borscht. I served this with some sour cream I blended with lemon juice and fresh dill, as well as potato pancakes. Thanks for the fabulous recipe.

I found this soup kind of bland and I was eating it the next day. I added a bay leaf and a little bit of dried marjoram as I didnt have any oregano like another reviewer suggested. I used part of a huge red cabbage and homemade beef stock, and olive oil in replacement of butter to be dairy free. I dont expect I will make this again and if I want a Borscht I will look for another recipe.

How is it possible for vegetables and no seasonings to taste so good? It's like magic! So yummy. Even my very hesitant boyfriend loved it! Only one question; was I supposed to peel the beets? I did, and it seemed to work out.

I have to say this was a great recipe... we just got back from Russia after adopting our precious daughter and this tastes just like the Borscht we had there.  I did add some fresh dill and i think that it really compliments it well.
Thanks for a great recipe...
Made this for our Khazak exchange student who was craving a taste of home. She loved it-- said it was similar to what her mom made. Thanks for posting!

WOW! yum! So incredibly easy and so amazing in taste! It's a nice rich flavor while still being relatively light!

I actually made some homemade bone broth just prior to making this recipe, and my bones were meaty, so I chopped up the meat and threw it in the dish. I don't think the flavor changed much from doing this. It's really a fantastic dish as is.

oh--I did add salt and pepper to taste; that's the only other change.

We found this to be a great non-meat borscht. I followed the recipe and directions, but because I bought a low-sodium beef broth, I did add a little salt and pepper to taste. Also, my DH added a little dill to his (as that is how his mother always made it). Do the reviewer who found it bland - if you used homemade beef stock/broth, you probably did need to add a little salt & some seasonings. I don't think it's really fair to rate a recipe when you don't actually use the ingredients that are indicated. That's like rating a movie that you didn't actually watch based on the previews you have seen...
Excellent dish! This was my first attempt at borscht and it's a hit!

Delicious!!  I've made this 4-5 times now, following the recipe plus adding herbs (dill, thyme, oregano, cilantro -- fresh are best, but dried are great too) along with salt and pepper.  My DH and ultra-picky kids love it.  I've also taken it to a couple of "soup parties" where it has been a big hit.  Thanks so much for posting!
This is delicious, and makes good leftovers.  It's filling, has a whole ton of vegetables in it, and using a food processor for the shredding/chopping made it pretty quick too.

Absolutely wonderful! A bit time consuming to make if you're grating everything by hand, but well worth the effort. However, the beef broth is what makes it, so don't use a cheap brand! Trust me, it makes a huge difference on the end product.

When life gives you beets, make borscht!  We got a ton of beets in our CSA this year and I generally don't like beets, I think they literally taste like dirt.  But I ventured out on a limb and tried this recipe.  I am so glad I did!  For being so simple, this is a great soup.  Like a beety french onion soup.  Thanks for sharing!

Overall a great recipe! I quadrupled it even though it was a 1st time attempt.  It turned out great & I love how all the veggies are shredded...somehow it tastes better!  I did find it a tad on the bland side so added some salt, pepper, and vinegar.  Anything more I think would be too overpowering.  Thanks for posting!

I have never liked borscht and didn't think my family would either, but we decided to try this recipe while studying about Russia.  Many tears were shed by my children who did not want to eat this.  My DH took one taste and poured his in the trash (when the kids weren't looking).  We are still not fans of borscht.  This may be a good recipe for it but it didn't win any of us over to beet & cabbage soup.

So I have only had this soup once before at a Russian restaurant and I have to say that your version was even better! I love beets and cabbage so I guess it comes as no surprised that I loved this too. Super easy. Super budget friendly. I used non dairy sour cream. Hubby care for it but I personally think this is 5 stars all the way. Thanks for posting.
Delicious!! Will be making this often!! Thanks!

This soup was so easy to make, and a fantastic way to use beets.  I made it with red cabbage, just to intensify the purple veggie content.  Too bad my DH doesn't like beets, but that just means more for me!

I have never had borscht before. I like all the ingredients, so I of course liked the soup. I thought it was a little bland.  I will probably try a meat based borscht recipe next time, but this wasn't bad.

I've made this recipe several times and I've tweaked it slightly every time. As others have stated, I use red cabbage. I find it to be a versatile recipe that my family - yes, even my kids- enjoys immensely.

Simple to fix and great for folks who juice and are vegans, or anyone who just wants to get healthy and cleanse a bit. If it's bland to your taste, play with the herbs and spices a bit for enhancement. I added pinches of this and that and it came out fine. My 'this&that' were a tad of garlic, a teaspoon of balsamic and a bit of paprika. Came out great. Thank you for posting this....

Add a little potatoes and fry the vegetables a little and simmer in tomato paste with water. Then add the vegetables to the broth with the cooked potatoes and add the cabbage. 5 minutes - can be turned off. Eat better with sour cream
For a real treat, sprinkle with red wine vinegar (in place of the lemon juice) and some dill seed just before eating.
Nice and easy to prepare.  Mine only took about 2 hours to cook,  but my crock pot is very hot.  Wasn't too spicy for my toddler.  next time I'll skip the cornstarch.

This has to be one of the easiest recipe's in the world.  When I put in the whole seasoning packet I thought for sure it was going to be a complete flop.  But was I ever wrong!!!!  Its easy to prepare, and taste wonderful!!!!

If you like HOT and SPICY food this is GREAT!!!  I made my own taco seasoning and used medium salsa, but next time I will use my homemade salsa for even better flavor.  I also cooked it on high for 4 hours.  This is definately a keeper!  Thanks for posting.

This was excellent and easy.  I had most of a 1.25 oz. packet of taco seasoning.  When I checked the supermarket shelves, I found Taco seasoning varied from 1 oz. to 1.25 oz.  Used mild salsa.  Great!

Delicious!  I found that even when I doubled the cornstarch the sauce needed more thickening, but perhaps I just like more of a gravy.  I served over rice and also put a bit of shreded cheese on top.  I think next time I will serve with corn bread on the side, for a bit more of a "mexican" hint without being obvious.  Also, it got our mouths watering for enchiladas, so I shreded the extra chicken and we'll be having enchiladas with the leftover chicken and sauce as a base.  Thanks for the tasty recipe!  Now to go look for enchilada recipes... ;-)
Outstanding recipe. So easy to make and the whole family scarfed it down.

Quick, easy and tasty .My kind of
meal.Thank you for sharing.

I tried this recipe when I was looking for something to make so I wouldn't have to go to the store!  The family really liked it and it will be a keeper.  The only thing I will change next time is to either cut back on the corn starch a little or add some more liquid - it got pretty thick but other than that the flavor was really good..
This was easy to prepare and tasty with just a few simple staples. I shredded the chicken, thickened,  and served it inside tortillas with sour cream and cheese... great!

This was just spicy enough. We really loved the flavor of this one. It couldn't be easier. I didn't change a thing, this is too good to mess with! Thanks for sharing, I will make this again and again.

This was delicious!  Since it was a hot, humid day I decided to use the crockpot and came across this recipe.  I followed it exactly except I found I didn't need to add the corn starch to thicken it at the end.  The sauce was delicious served over plain white rice.  This is definitely a keeper and I'll be making it again.  Thanks for sharing!
This was really good, and I think I will shred it and try with tortillas next time. Thanks for the suggestion, Missyb33!!
This is really easy and amazing!  I cooked this for 4 hours on high.  It tasted so good!  My son gobbled it up like it was going to be his last meal...this will definitely be made again in my house!
This is a great crockpot recipe, so quick and easy with little mess.  I served with rice and sprinkled green onions on top  before serving.

I left this recipe ou for my husband to make with I was at the University. The flavours blended so well together and it was a fantastic crockpot recipe that we will be sure to make again. We served this with Mexican Rice recipe#25517. Thanks for posting!
I love this recipe it is very tasting and it is ready when I get home from work.

This is delicious.  Easy to make - throw together in the morning and it's ready afer a long day of work or play!  Served it over rice and it was just great.  Had to use mild salsa because of the kiddies.  Everyone in the family loves this one!
My family wasn't thrilled with this, but it is very easy and a good recipie

I have had this recipe as a favorite for years. I use 1 jar of salsa and omit the cornstarch due to an allergy. It makes a lot of sauce which I love. When I give friends this recipe they dont even think it needs cornstarch. I serve this over rice and it is delicious.

Delicious, easy to prepare, relatively inexpensive & a big hit. We shredded it & made quesadillas, pouring the sauce over the top of the quesadillas. Next time I'll definitely make sure to use the reduced sodium seasoning as this was a bit salty since I used the regular. Wonderful recipe!

Very easy to mke and a definate hit with DH and kids. After removing the chicken, I transfered the remaining sauce into a saucepan and added the cornstarch and sour cream to thicken. This made the sauce nice and cramy-thick. I served it with my own version of Mexican rice and topped it with cheese. Thank you for posting such an easy and enjoyable dish.
Not much I can add after all the terrific reviews this has received except to say I agree!!  I used bone in breasts and (Zaar recipe) homemade taco seasoning.  Made for a terrific dinner.

A good meal, and so easy!  We had this with beans, rice, and corn.  My chicken breasts were frozen when I put them in the crockpot, but by the time we ate dinner they were so tender they were falling apart.  This is a recipe I know I'll use often- a great thing to throw in the crockpot before work, and I always have these ingredients on hand.  Thanks for sharing!

This was great and so easy to make! This is a keeper. We added some shredded cheese and put the sour cream on last.
Very tasty! Love to make new recipes in the crockpot.
Thanks
This recipe is awesome and so easy! I have even used frozen chicken breasts and it turns out just as great.
Tasty and quick.

Made a hit with my DH. I halved the recipe for just the 2 of us. The chicken was so tender and tasty.I served it over rice with mexican spirls #15988 as a side.We will be eating chicken more often. Thank U for the recipe...

Everyone liked it! I didn't give the kids the sauce (there's green "things" in it). The chicken was very moist. Next time, I will just use 1/2 packet of the taco seasoning- personal preference. Thanks for another night I only have to make 1 dinner to please the family!

Delicious!  I shredded our chicken and served it with tortillas, lettuce and tomato.  It was a little spicy for the kids (but I loved it as is), so I will halve the taco seasoning next time. I plan to make a double batch as well and freeze it for other meals.  Thanks!

so, so, so, good!!
i am so impressed by this recipe, its so simple. great recipe..

To die for  and so quick and easy.  Used chicken thighs, bone in and did for 8 hours.  Served with Mexican rice # 25517 as suggested by Pamela in Winnipeg and was fabulous.  Also used homemade salsa, wonderful salsa #9572 these combinations were just amazing!!  Thanks so much

It doesn't get much easier than this!  I used Newman's Own Tequila Lime Salsa, and I cooked it on high for 4 hours and on low for 1.  Instead of thickening with the cornstarch, I shredded it for tacos.  Served it with some calabacitas, spanish rice, and sangria.  Yum!
This was easy, quick, and tasty. Next time I will not be adding the cornstarch because I thought the sauce became to thick. I will be making this again for sure!

This was MUCH better than i ever expected!  I was looking for a low calorie chicken dish and this one was perfect.  I made it twice since i liked it so much.  The second time i only used half of the sour cream and found that it was just as good.  My boyfriend added extra to his. Also, i really enjoyed the sauce so i doubled the amount of salsa the second time around.  Thanks!!!
This recipe was so easy and so good!  As in another comment, I shredded the chicken and made tacos.  I also did not add the cornstarch because I didnt feel it needed it.  Thanks for the great post!

This was soo yummy, even my BF who swears he hates sour cream in ANYTHING gobbled this up. We had it over rice, but it would taste good with anything, pasta, in a tortilla, i'd even pile in on a bun and make a sour cream salsa chicken sandwich! So delicous, so easy and so good for you too

Sooo good, even though I forgot to start in the crockpot!  Here's how I did it in 20 min:  rubbed taco seasoning on chicken, sauteed in 2tbs olive oil.  When chicken was almost cooked, topped with salsa and covered for 5 more min.  Removed chicken, turned down to low heat and add water/cornstarch mixture.  Cooled slightly then added sour cream.  Topped each thigh with sauce...YUM!  Thanks for a great recipe!
I used a 16 oz. jar of salsa and didn't need to thicken-I also added a drained can of black beans and served over rice-great!!

I made these for dinner the other night and they were very good.  The chicken was extremely tender (almost falling apart!) and it was so easy to make.  My only "complaint" is that the sauce didn't get very thick - even though I used cornstartch and water to thicken it.  It still tasted very good, but wish the sauce would have been more like a gravy.

I have made this soo many times!  I add 1 can of cream of mushroom soup at the beginning.  Otherwise, I make it the same!  Served with rice.  

Yummy thanks for sharing!
It was really good. A little salty so I think I would use less of the taco seasoning or do as one of the other reviewers said and use a low sodium kind. It was spicy also. Delish!

This was a good, easy recipe. I shredded my chicken and made tacos out of it. I did not add the sour cream into the chicken mixture, but just put it on our tacos. I think it would be better served over rice, so that is what I plan on doing next time. Thanks!
We cooked about a pound of boneless skinless chicken on low for just under 5 hours and it was perfectly tender and falling apart.  Nice, easy Mex fare.

This was a big hit with my family.  Not too spicy and not too mild.  I doubled the recipe and shredded the leftovers for enchiladas the next day.  This will go in my "keepers" recipe box to be enjoyed again.

I made this yesterday, Putting it all in the crock pot was super easy,I had it on high for 4 hours, but I only had 3 chicken breasts,the edges of my sauce got a little burnt but thats probably from my own error, and it didnt effect the taste at all! I didnt add the sour cream or cornstarch water mix because I was in a rush to have dinner before heading out, but the main point is that tasted fantastic! Everyones plate was clean and the chicken was beautifully tender, Will definitley make this again!
We all loved it here!  Great easy to put together dinner that you can stick in the crockpot and leave and come back to a great meal, ready and waiting.  My kinda meal!  Ida

This is a really good recipe! It tastes really good, I have one child who hates anything even slightly spicy- but she gobbled it up, We couldn't believe our eyes! This will definitely be made again in our home.

I like this because it is really low fat, easy and delicious.  I've made it twice and the second time I added 2 tsp. of liquid smoke so it tasted like the tomatoes in the salsa had been roasted.  
Thank you!
This was very good.   I even used fat free sour cream.  My boys ate it on a tortilla and I liked it plain.  We will be making it again!
This was surprisingly good. I used a tomatillo salsa which is green and it worked really well and the flavor was nice. The chicken was a little tuff or I would have given it five stars.

Excellent!  Everything you could ask for. It was flavorful without being too spicy for the kids, creamy without being heavy, tender, juicy, and a real family pleaser! I used 99% fat free boneless skinless chicken breast tenders that were frozen. I cooked it on low for 7 hours and it was the most perfect chicken I've ever had in a crock pot! I've found that the texture can be gummy sometimes, but these tenders were perfect. A delicious, healthy meal that I feel good feeding my family. Thanks for posting!

Since I'm a working mom with two very active children, I'm always looking for crock pot recipe's. This turned out very good. Served this with some spanish rice then off to soccer practice! This is great for those busy week nights because it's very easy to put together before I go to work. Yes, this does work even if the chicken is still frozen before you put it in the corck pot!

My family really enjoyed this.  It wasnt quite as hot as i like, i might add something to fire it up a little.. but my daughter was able to indulge in it without burning her tongue off.. she really like it
Quick and easy for a working mom like me.

DH enjoyed this, I thought it was ok.  But the kiddos didn't like it.  Which surprised me because they like all the ingredients.  It was simple to make, and would be good for a busy day.  I guess DH gets the leftovers all to himself.
My boyfriend and I love this!!  Super easy, few ingredients, and yummy!!
Really good, and so easy! Flavors are great and I love how the cornstarch is used to make a nice thick sauce. Will use the extra chicken tomorrow for tacos. Thanks!
sooooooooooooooo yummy and very easy to make!!!!!!! Hubby loves it!! Thanks!
This is one of my "go to" recipes.  I use 1/2 cup sour cream, but otherwise my recipe is exactly the same.  Thanks for posting!

This is delicious. A bit spicy, so I added a brick of 1/3 less fat cream cheese and 1/4 c. brown sugar, and then 1/4 c. sour cream for that tangy touch. I did not add the corn starch. My daughter who is a gourmet cook was visiting and she dubed it as "awesome." It's definitely one I'll do again and will take to church dinners.

This is excellent! Low fat, low calories, low carb, high taste and flavor, plus EASY! I followed the simple recipe, then at the end I added a can of black beans and a cup of corn when thickening the sauce. I also shredded the chicken and we ate it rolled into tortillas. Thank you!

The flavours were good in this dish, though it took a while for the sauce to thicken in the crockpot. It would have been much faster in a small saucepan. Also, the chicken was quite dry - maybe a fattier cut would have worked better.
This was simple and tasty.  Thanks!
This is absolutely delicious. My sauce was too thick but that's because I forgot the water. I also used thighs but I'm sure it would be just as wonderful with breasts. And so easy.

This recipe has been a family favorite for 15+ years.  It is very versatile, meaning you can serve it over rice, or as chicken tacos.  We like it with black beans and rice, but sometimes fat free refried beans for something different.  

If you leave out the sour cream and serve the sour cream on the side, it's just as good.
Super good.  I think this is the first cookie where my husband and little boy ate up every single one of them... even with a box of Chips Ahoy in the cupboard.  Thanks!

These are the best snickerdoodles I have made. They are very soft and moist; GREAT with a cup of tea or cocoa. My daughters loved them. They are quite easy to make, dont take much time but the result is a DELICIOUS cookie!

These taste like the cookies my grandmother baked for me 45 years ago when I was very young. I've always searched for the recipe thinking it was a sugar cookie. Grandma never called it a snickerdoodle! Thanks for the memory!
Wonderful, soft & chewy cookies, just the way I love them!  Took some to the office & everyone gobbled them up!
They didn't last long at my house!!  These soft cookies have an 'old fashioned' taste and I'll probably be making them again and again.

I thought these were great. I love love love a soft cookie. The dough was so soft I wasn't sure about them but they came out great. Very tasty!!! I would say though that the prep time in total is off. Bake time is fine but they take a lot longer start to finish than stated.

Juju Bee, these cookies are delicious! I haven't had snickerdoodles in many years and for some reason this caught my eye. I'm glad it did. I used 1/2 c oil and 1/2 c unsalted butter, and for the flour I used 2 c whole wheat pastry and 3/4 c oat flours. Using a half-ounce cookie scoop, my yield was 53 2-inch cookies, which took 9 minutes to bake because of their smaller size. My 8 y.o. son loves them and had fun helping me roll the dough in the cinnamon sugar. Thanks for posting this recipe.

Everyone that tried these loved them. Perfect recipe that needed no modifications. Awhile back, I had made a box mix of these very cookies but these are by FAR superior! Thanks for this great recipe and for introducing my family to a REAL snickerdoodle!

I needed to bring cookies to a potluck at work, but didn't have any yummy ingredients at home, but this cookie did the trick! Had all the ingredients on hand and everyone raved about them. Very soft and chewy and delicious. Thanks for the recipe JuJu Bee! I need to make some for home now!

These are very tasty cookies.  the recipe made about 54 cookies for me but I made them smaller (about a rounded teaspon size) Also I used a lot more cinnamon sugar mixture.  I took about 1/2 cup of sugar and 3 teaspoons of cinnamon and had some left over.

We are a soft cookie family. I made the recipe exactly as posted. A great cookie! Will be making them again, as I always have the ingredients on hand and they are easy to make. Make up the dough the evening before and bake them the next day. Thanks for a really good soft cookie.

Goody, goody! I made crispy cookies by flattening the dough balls flat with a fork and baking few extra minutes. They crack in oven and that makes nice cinnamon stripes on top. Must try them as soft balls, next time.

FANTASTIC!  I love this cookie recipe.  None of my basic cookie recipes gave me the soft sugar cookie my mom used to make.  Now this one DOES. Soft, chewy, yummy cookies that everyone loves.  Thanks for posting!

***** I prepared everything the night before so I could get up early & pop them in the oven. My husband and out of town guests woke up wondering what smells so good? Soooo guess what we had for breakfast? Right, your delicious Snickerdoodle! This was not the plan, this was going to be a snack for later! I tried to be a little good, along with coffee & cookies I did put out a fruit salad & juice. We all thought these cookies are sooo good. I have chilled the dough before, when making other cookies butI never chilled the cookie sheets. Thats what must have helped keep them puffy and and rounded, which I loved. I'm going to do that with other cookies that you don't want to flatten out. Thank you Juju Bee for sharing your Grandma's great recipe. — Jul 29, 2005
Absolutely wonderful, what more can I say?

Delicious!  My husband has always been bragging about how his friend's mom makes the best snickerdoodle cookies because they turn out so soft.  Well...he said these cookies were just like hers!  We were both VERY pleased!  I doubt they will last long in our house!!

Yes, these are soft and delicious.  However, I must be snickerdoodle impaired b/c it took me until the very last bit of dough to figure this recipe out.  The cookies MUST be measured into heaping teaspoon or tablespoons (depending on preference) to turn out.  My first few rounds of dough turned out still doughy in the middle.  But, once I reduced the size of the cookies they were excellent.  They even cracked on the top.  So, don't make the same mistake I did.  Make the cookies small!  I also had to adjust the temp to 360 degrees for my tempermental oven.  These cookies are incredibly soft and the dough is amazing once I figured it out! Thanks!
We took these to a party and then ate the rest for breakfast. Easy and delicious!

These turned out absolutely delightful!  My mom and I tried this recipe, and she wanted them less tender (I prefer them soft), but even crispy they still taste fabulous, especially dipped in tea.  Definitely worth making (and are simple to do!

This is my favorite cookie recipe of the year so far! These were delicious with a wonderful texture, and the cooking time was just right (prep time was much longer than 10 minutes though). I was able to make 72 cookies from the recipe. Thank you for posting this!

My son decided that this is now his favorite cookie, surpassing the classic chocolate chip!  Then my fiance (who doesn't eat very many sweets) came in and said, "I don't know what kind of cookie that is, but it is GOOD!" The recipe is simple to understand and the cookies came out perfect! Thanks!
Loved them!!

These were the best Snickerdoodles I've had! They kept getting stolen off the cooling rack so I'm not sure how many this makes. They were soft & chewy in the middle and lightly crisp on the out. Followed the recipe exactly and they turned out great! Thanks so much for sharing this!

PERFECT! I love this soft cookie. This is the first snickerdoodle recipe I've made that the cookies actually turn out soft. I omitted the cream of tartar without any adverse effect. Thanks for sharing a great recipe!!

These cookies are sooo yummy! They were so easy to make! I followed the recipe exactly. Thank you Juju Bee for sharing this wonderful recipe! My husband and 3 boys LOVED them! I will add this recipe to my favorites list & make them often!!

These were excellent and super easy to make! I made a batch and brought them to work - they were gone in 10 minutes.  I made a double batch and brought them the next day - gone in 30 minutes!  I will definitely make these again.
These cookies are very good. I followed the recipe  just as you had it. I took them to work and they were gone in no time! Thanks for the great recipe!
My husband couldn't keep his hands off these.  Not exactly a dieter's dream, but if you're looking for a good cookie recipe, who cares?
These are delicious!  I love the soft and thin quality of them...  Thanks for the recipe!
These were delicious! I haven't made Snickerdoodles in so long. I made them for my son's sleepover, and the boys really enjoyed them, as did I! Thanks.

This is my first batch of snicker doodle cookies and came out great. This is a great recipe.  Thanks,
Brewhead

OMG!!!These cookies are fantastic! I have been looking for a cookie recipe like this for a long time. Its like a sugar cookie and the cinnamon gives a nice spice taste. Couldnt stop eatting them and they are still soft next day! Thanks!

This cookies are very soft and tasty!
 I've added 1 cup of chocolate chips white almonds and nuts! And a 1/5 cup of whisky.
 Awesome!!! Thanks!
These are AMAZINGLY good...soft and the texture is lovely! My whole family adores them.
OUTSTANDING!!!  The recipe was incredibly simple and the cookies were excruciatingly delicious. I HIGHLY HIGHLY recommend this recipe!  I wish I could give it 6 stars!

This recipe shows 24 for the servings amount, but no where does it say that a serving is two cookies. It makes about 48 cookies when using the default ingredient amounts, and making one inch round balls.<br/><br/>After refrigerating the mixed dough I divide the dough into 4 even size pieces. I scoop up very rounded teaspoons full  (about one and a half teaspoons) of the dough which then comes pretty close to making the one inch size balls that the recipe recommends. Each quarter section of dough should yield 12 balls. Adjust your scoop size as you go along if necessary. I place these balls on dinner plates, 24 per plate and re-refrigerate for 15 minutes. I do not refrigerate the cookie trays. I then bake 1 plate at a time using two cookie trays 11.5"  x 15.5" (12 cookies per tray). Half way through the baking (at 5 minutes) I switch the trays to the opposite rack in the oven and turn them around for even baking.

I must've read 300 or so of the reviews about these cookies and I have to agree with most of them. These things iz good!! It is a simple drop dough that comes together really fast, and bakes off just as easily. I made a double batch of the dough right before I went to bed, and portioned out a couple dozen balls with a #40 (3/4 oz.) Portion scoop. The next morning, I preheated the oven while showering. I was able to bake off 2 dozen cookies and get them cool enough for my wife to take to work, and still had time to sit down and drink a full cup of coffee. Total morning time invested? An hour!! I didn't run across any of the problems I read about in the reviews, though I did change the creaming method just a bit. First, I took the butter and clarified it on the stovetop till I had a nice brown butter. It makes the cookies even better, I think! Anyway, I creamed the cooled down butter with the sugar, salt, and 1 Tbsp of bourbon vanilla extract per batch. Using a hand mixer, I creamed the mixture on high speed for 1 minute. Using COLD eggs, I mixed them in one at a time on low speeds till just incorporated. I did it this way because I wanted to limit the amount of air that got mixed in during the creaming process, and using cold eggs sets the butter back up faster, which stops the emulsification of egg yolk and fat. This is key if you want those cookies that you had when you were a kid! At this point, I took the dry ingredients and sifted them into the creamed mixture all at once. I folded it all together with a wooden spoon till it just comes together. I only use this method with these cookies and a shortbread recipe my grandmother gave me. I used whole wheat pastry flour which weighs 4 1/2 oz. per cup. A.P. flour weighs a little more and bread flour a little more again. Sugar weighs 8 oz. per cup, 1 pound per pint. I did use the baking soda, though!! But rather than go buy creme of tartar for this and maybe an Italian merengue or two, I used what I had. Apple cider vinegar! It took me a couple times making them to get it right. It seems to work at 1 Tbsp per batch. For those who like a bit fluffier, chewy cookie, you can add 2 tsp cornstarch. This helps prevent some of the collapse when they cool and helps the outside with the crispness! Using a 3/4 oz. portion scoop, I got 51 cookies out of a double batch. I don't press them down, I just roll em and place on a parchment paper lined sheet pan. Bake for 11 minutes and check. The edges should start to brown slightly. If they aren't yet, another minute always finishes them off for me. I store the doughballs in the freezer for up to a month. After that the baking soda can start degrading. On a whim, I sprinkled the sugar mixture in the bottom of a small pyrex baking dish. I took the dough and pressed a cookie "shell" in the bottom of it and halfway up the side. Cover and place in the fridge to chill. I made a filling out of apples, a little fresh oj, and some of its zest, some brown sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and cardamom, and some sultana raisins lightly pickled in champagne vinegar and honey. I sauteed this for about 8 minutes or so, until I could add some roux and a bit of cornstarch slurry, and it was really, really thick. As it bakes it will release more moisture, which will thin it out somewhat. I put the COLD filling in the pyrex and put one cookie ball for every serving in the dish on top. I sprinkle liberally with sugar mixture and put in a 350ºF. oven, on the middle shelf. I set a timer for 15 minutes and checked it. I moved it to the top shelf because the bottom cookie was cooking a bit faster than the top. It was done at the 20 minute mark. Snickerdoodle apple cobbler. Yep.

People love these cookies. Here are some extra precautions you can take to make sure they turn out right. 1. Make sure your butter and eggs are at room temperature before you start. 2. REALLY cream the butter and sugar together before you add the vanilla and eggs. It should have a light, almost whipped, consistency and only a little granulation left. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well between eggs. Add vanilla to the butter/sugar/egg mixture and mix well again. 3. When you add the flour/dry mixture to the wet, mix until JUST combined. Do not over-mix at this step. 4. Chill dough in the fridge for at least an hour before baking. If you're in a hurry, you can chill for 10-15 minutes, then roll the dough into one inch balls, coat in the cinnamon-sugar mixture, and then chill again in the fridge for 15-20 minutes. 5. Use silicone baking mats if you have them. If not, double up on the baking sheets/pans. This will help the bottoms not brown too quickly. Either way, cool baking sheets in the fridge for 10-15 minutes right before adding the cookie dough balls, flattening just a little bit with your palm, and baking. 6. Recipe says bake at 350 degrees which is ok if you're SURE your oven doesn't run hot. If when you bake cookies the bottoms sometimes come out too dark, bake at 325 instead. 7. Cookie bottoms should be just barely browned but the edges should be firm when you remove them from the oven.
