Excellent chocolate cake!  I used Sue L's Chocolate Buttercream Frosting #44126,and that went really well with it!  We were invited for Christmas dinner at some friends, and decided to bring this (among other things) for dessert.  I decorated it for the occasion, and it went over big with everyone.  It was delicious and moist, and just the perfect chocolate cake.  I decided not to make it in layers, but to bake it in a 9 x 13 cake pan (more like a sheetcake).  I baked it about 12 minutes longer than instructed for the round layer cakes.  I iced it right in the pan, making it easier to transport.  Thank you for posting it, ms_bold.

I made this cake using all the frostings as Sue B used and it turned out FABULOUS.  A friend returned home from the Navy and I made this for her for her birthday and she loved it, along with everyone else!

I also made this cake with all the same frostings listed.  I have reviewed those frostings as well.  I was using a hand mixer (didn't have the counter space at the time to get out the big dog) and the batter seemed a less incorporated than I would have liked.  I don't like to beat a cake mix to death, so I didn't.  I left it like that.  I used two 8 inch dark nonstick springform pans coated lightly with release/flour spray.  I cooked them at the same time in my oven on the same shelf, rotating them front to back midway during cook time. The one that was in front last required 2 more minutes of cooktime and was the one that had the most loft.  I cut that loft off since I was making a layer cake anyway and I also cut each cake into layers to end up with four layers. The cake tolerated the cutting very nicely as well as setting the layers and frosting with the sticky buttercream frosting.  It turned out beautifully and I took it to share at a Superbowl get together.  It created quite an interest and some people asked for the recipe.  It was very moist and hard to stop eating it.  I'm not a huge fan of triple chocolate cakes because they are usually too rich, but a narrow sliver of this is perfect.  Loved it, and thank you so much for rescuing this one!  
-Caryn
No doubt this is one of the best chocolate cakes there is around! Dense, moist and so deliciously chocolaty! Easy no-beat recipe,low in saturated fats. Any frosting would complement the cake.

What can I say that hasn't been said already?  This cake is one of the best recipes out there.  I made this for DH's birthday and used recipe #80118 for the frosting.  I did not change or alter the recipe.  I couldn't find my 9" round cake pans so I used a 9" X 13" cake pan.  I had to cook the cake an additional 12 minutes but it did not change the flavour.  The important thing is DH loved it and so did the rest of the family.
Wow is all I can say.  I made a heart shaped cake yesterday and it was divine!  Took longer to bake because I used one 6" deep pan.  The only chocolate cake recipe I will ever need!
Fabulous!  The only way I can see to improve this recipe is to use unsalted butter or ghee in place of the bottled oil.
This is an amazingly moist and flavorful chocolate cake.  Thanks for sharing!
I made this chocolate cake for my little boy's birthday and it went down a storm! I followed one of the reviewers and used the frosting suggested. It was lovely! Thank you so much.

I have made this 4 times now all with in about a month's time. Each time it is perfect. The only thing that is bothering me is that each time I've mixed the cocoa powder and boiling water it has given me a different consistency...but no matter what the cake is awesome each time. Thanks!

OMG, DS had a B-day the other day and I  made this for his cake.  I have always thought chocolate cake to be dry and crumbly.  NOT SO.  This cake is so moist and delicious.  I loved it and my kids couldn't get enough of it.  The best part about the whole thing is I always have the ingredients on hand so we can whip this up at any time.  Thank you for posting and converting me to chocolate cake....STephanie

WOWSERS! I can't believe a homemade cake is this good!
Made it for my hubby's b'day and he ate 1/4 of it in one sitting. It is extremelly decandent and moist. Thanks for posting the recipe and to the others who suggested the frosting recipe in their reviews.(31809) Both were excellant.
Brenda-ohio

Yummy!!
I was afraid they wouldn't rise because the batter was so thin, but they were perfect. Although next time I will fill the muffin tins fuller, because they don't grow hugely like some cupcakes. 
The flavor was wonderful. just the perfect amount of chocolate and not too heavy. 
I frosted with kitten kal's white fluffy frosting. Wonderful combination!

This cake is delicious-- I made it on a whim today for no other reason than my husband and I felt like eating cake. We topped it with Chocolate Buttercream Frosting [recipe=44126]44126[/recipe]. I baked it in a 9x13" pan and it took about 50 min to bake at 350F in my oven. Yum!

This is a great cake... the only thing I did was change the temperature from 350 degrees to 325 degrees F.  This keeps my cakes from getting that dome on top and they are flat when they are baked.  Of course, I had to bake this cake for 45 minutes, but it was perfectly flat when I turned it out onto the cooling rack.  I use the toothpick method to make sure it is done... do not leave it in until the cake pulls from the sides as it will be dry.  Everyone was right about the taste of the cake!  Thanks for sharing.

This recipe was SO good! It was so rich, moist, chocolaty, and just delicious! Really easy to make. This will definitely be my new go to cake recipe. I topped it with peanut butter frosting from this site...Yum!

I DOUBLED this recipe and poured it into 2 11 inch cake pans for a big wedding shower; it was a HIT! I used a chocolate frosing fililng #44126 and then used a white (it's more bridal, right?!?) frosting on the outside, #80118. THANKS!
Made for hubby's birthday. Easy, moist, chocolatey. Very good. Will make again.Thanks.

This is the chocolate cake recipe I've been looking for. Rich, dark and perfectly moist. This is the taste you hope for when you see the big slices of cake in restaurants or magazine ads. This is my chocolate cake recipe from now on. Thanks.

This was my first scratch cake.  I can't believe I waited so long to try it.  It was moist, perfect and fool proof.  My daughter's 16th birthday was a hit thanks to Sue B!  This cake baked up nicely in a Wilton character pan.  I saved so much $$$ not having to buy a cake.  In these times, every penny counts!

Wow, I HATE giving out low star reviews but for whatever reason, there was WAY to much liquid in this cake. Before I even added the oil, water or milk, it was the consistency of a a cake mix so I was wondering why I should add more liquid. After 45 minutes, the cake still wasn't solid. I could see the oil boiling on the top! Eeek! I finally pulled it out of the oven, it was in a silicone dinousar mold because it was going to be a birthday cake. I turned it over to get it out and it collapsed in an oily mess. I'm going to try to freeze what came out and turn it into a trifle but I don't know if that will workl. Sorry :(

Great for high altitudes!  Perfectly moist, held together just fine, incredibly easy to make and basically a one-bowl recipe.  This is the only chocolate cake recipe I use now, period.  It is so delicious I even like it without frosting.
I made this for my DH and he is loving it! Every night he has a piece with a glass of milk and is happy. Thanks!

I'm a novice baker and almost always use a box mix because frankly, every cake I've ever made from scratch, didn't taste any better than a box. This recipe is better than a box! Very moist and very delicious. I did make two subs but I am unsure if they made any difference. I only had 1/2 cup of white sugar so I used light brown sugar to make up the difference. I also used cake flour. My layers were done after only 25 minutes. I made a great birthday cake for a chocoholic loved one and he raved over this cake. I frosted with Recipe #44126 . Terrific recipe.
my cake turned out weird. It didn't rise very much, it wasn't moist or chocolatey, the edges were really crisy, and it fell apart really easily, not sweet enough.

This is NOT a cake recipe it is a pancake recipe. I had no problem baking it and the flavor is great but it is not a cake. The texture is chewy and full of air pockets. It rises and falls in the oven just like a pancake does, good thing I used my 3 inch deep pans. Itâ€™s the oil that turns it into a pancake texture. Use margarine instead of oil for a more cake like outcome. One thing is for sure I now have a wonderful buttermilk chocolate pancake recipe!
Gud cake nuthing dat great though zaar has better recipes that i wud look upto .This cake is not very sweet so a sweeter icing wud fit the perfect sweeth tooths like me !!

This is the perfect chocolate cake recipe!  Moist throughout, very chocolate-y, tastes better than a bakery cake.  I followed the directions exactly, using a good quality cocoa, and it came out perfect.  I made into cupcakes which I then made into a Barbie cake and covered with a marshmallow fondant.  Even days later, they were moist and delicious.  I had a few leftover that I froze and thawed a week later - still tasted just as fresh.  I plan on making this recipe for every birthday that comes along.

This is a fantastic chocolate cake.  It's very moist, dense but tender, and deeply chocolate.  As some other reviewers noted, it gets more moist as it sits so is best made a day ahead of serving.  I spread a thick layer of white chocolate ganache betwen the layers, and covered the ganache with a raspberry filling.  The tart raspberries paired well with the sweet ganache.  I covered the top of the cake with a thick layer of bittersweet chocolate ganache, and frosted the sides with a rich chocolate buttercream.  Because this cake isn't as sweet as some, you can lather on the frostings and fillings.  My layers were done in 29 minutes.  I dusted the pans with cocoa instead of flour.  To enhance the chocolate flavour, I added 1 tbsp. of instant espresso to the boiling water.

I think the cake was pretty plain, I actually prefer box mixes.  There were clumps in the cake that tasted like waxed paper, even though I didn't use any..still don't know what that was about!  I'm going to keep looking for a recipe, but thanks for posting.
Perfect! Thanks for sharing
This was good, but not as chocolatey as I hoped it would be. But it was moist and easy to make.
Best chocolate cake i've ever had, honest! easy to make too!!! you won't regret this one.

I made this rich, chocolately cake for my son's 13th birthday. I am so glad I chose this recipe! The recipe calls for ingredients I generally have on hand. The recipe instructions are straightfoward enough that a rookie baker can make it with great success. I turned the cake into a 4 layer cake by slicing each round horizontally. I filled AND iced the cake with the chocolate butter cream recipe mentioned above. Thanks for sharing this delightful recipe! I will be sure to use it again.  ~~~update~~~ Here we are, on my son's 15th birthday and this cake is STILL the one he requests every year.  Thank you, again, for the best chocolate cake ever.

Excellent recipe!  I had everything on hand except the buttermilk.  Made that by adding 1 T. lemon juice to 1 c. milk.  This cake will definitely replace my old stand by recipe. Topped it with recipe #44126.  Love this cake!  Thanks ms_bold for posting here!

Delicious! I halved the recipe since I only needed one 9" round cake. I used 2 oz. unsweetened chocolate squares plus 1 Tbsp. Hershey's cocoa, reduced the oil a tiny bit since I used chocolate squares and it turned out perfectly. Baked for 35 min at 350.

My son made this cake for a youth fair and won first prize! It's such a moist, delicious cake, and the directions are easy to follow, even for a beginner. He greased the pans and then coated with cocoa powder instead of flour, and skipped the parchment paper. Thanks ms bold for adopting!

My nephew said this was the best chocolate cake he every had.  This chocolate cake is moist and full of flavor without being overly sugary like a lot of box cake mixes.  I have made it several times and it works great as 2 rounds and also as a 13"x9"  or 12" round cake.   I found that I didn't need to use the parchment paper.  It slides out with just cooking spray/flour applied to the pan(s).  Thanks for a great recipe!
Great recipe! It's probably one of the best scratch cakes I've made.
A yummy cake--we also used a chocolate icing which made for a great cake.  I have made other cakes that were moister but this one definitely had a wonderful chocolate flavor and we enjoyed it.

I thought I had better write a review, as I have made this cake so many times and I have been caught up in the busy nanna syndrome, making things for party's and just never seemed to have time. But I am making time today, as I feel to not take time and review this cake is a sin. This cake is amazing my grandsons will have nothing else. Mum bought a very very large cake for the party as we were having a lot of guests but GS said ok, but I still want my nana's cake. I didn't have the heart to tell him it wasn't mine but yours. It comes out perfect every time. And the frosting is perfect for this cake. Any one who is thinking about making  it please do as you will definitely not be disappointed. thank you for a marvelous recipe and helping to keep my grandchildren very happy.

So good it's ridiculous. The first time I mixed this cake together I watched the eggs and buttermilk blending with the canola oil and just figured that the cake was doomed: it was so weird looking. I finished it and through it in the oven anyhow. My doubt goes to show what I know about baking. 

I've made this cake 3 times and it's not only helped morale at work for a whole 8 hours but won me points with the in-laws. I can't thank you enough.

This is an exceptional cake! Rich, dark flavor and is so moist! Mine took about 5 minutes longer to bake, I think my oven is a little off. I made this for my next-door neighbor's birthday. I used Lion's custard powder to fill it and it was a beautiful sight. I invited several of my neighbors over and they went crazy over it. Wonderful cake, a keeper for sure. Thanks so much for posting!
The perfect chocolate cake, dark and wonderful.
This is the moistest cake ever! I used coconut oil and baked it in a rectangle glass pan for about 35 minutes.  It turned out great.  Thanks for sharing.

I have made this cake several time now, and it is quite good.  However, unlike the description, I would not consider it a "dense" cake. It is more dense than a box mix by a little, but not as dense as several other home made cake recipes I have tried over the years.  It is very moist, and makes a HUGE cake.  In fact, I now cut the recipe back to 2/3 of the original volume most of the time.  I have also found it takes longer than 30 min to bake.  Thanks for a good base recipe.

Needed a cake to impress the boyfriend and his family for his birthday, and this definitely did the trick.  Preparation was easy and the cake rose to perfection for a dual layer cake in exactly 30 minutes.  Flavor was good (not too sweet), cake was moist, and it turned out perfectly.
Terrific!!!!  Made into cupcakes with Recipe# 130623 and they were fantastic!

Not quite as chocolatey as I expected, but a fantastic chocolate cake! Next time I'll throw in some mini choco chips (just me though)  My Fiance requested a 1 layer square chocolate cake for his friend's "leaving for a new job" lunch. So I made this in a 13x9, and baked about 40 minutes -perfecto! Frosted with chocolate whipped cream frosting (tastes like ice cream with your cake) He came home and actually used the word "phenomenal"!! His boss tried to steal the left overs and sneak home lol But I managed to get a piece. Used strong coffee for the water - that was my only alteration. For those who said the batter is thin - it's normal. I make several cupcake recipes this consistency. I had no troubles with rising and falling. All went great!
This cake was great! I used almond milk and vinegar instead of buttermilk, and whole wheat flour, plus I added some chocolate chips. Easy to make and really moist, I will be making this again.
Delicious chocolate cake, and so easy to make. I'll be making this again, thank you!

I made this for my daughter's birthday. Absolutely loved it. Very moist and rich flavor. I used Kittencals Chocolate frosting with the cake. The combination was delicious.  I liked the suggestion of adding mini-cholocate chips. Will try that next time.  Can never get enough chocolate!
Not sure what I did wrong. The flavor wasn't as chocolatey as  I thought it would be. I baked in 2 nine inch layers.  They didn't rise at all and the texture was a little chewy.

Very good!  My 9-year old and I made this for his birthday.  We used regular milk as we didn't have buttermilk on hand and somehow we forgot the vanilla....but it still turned out fantastic!  Will definitely be using this one again, it is a keeper, and seemingly fail proof!

This recipe created a cake light, moist and fluffy exactly what I was looking for to create a special cake for my mother in law.  I love that I didn't have to cream the butter etc and I just used a whisk for the whole lot. I reduced the sugar a quarter and the runniness worried me but it cooked perfectly. I changed the amounts to make 3 layers and they were quite thick. The centre of this cake rises so I sliced the tops off to make even layers. I'll be using this recipe again, it was a huge hit and got great comments. I won't need another chocolate cake recipe. Thanks for posting

This cake was so delicious!  Very moist and the perfect amount of chocolatey-ness.  The batter seemed on the thin side as I was pouring it into the pans, so I originally thought something was wrong.  However, it turned out fabulous!  Thank you for sharing!

This is absolutely the best chocolate cake I have ever had. I just started baking a few months ago and this was the first chocolate cake I have ever made (from scratch) in my life and it was super easy and delicious. I have gotten nothing but great reviews on how delicious it is.
Kaitie-Pie made this cake for my 32nd birthday. and boyyyy was it yummy! she got the baking powder/ baking soda mixed up and it still turned out great! :)

Oh my goodness, it's my cake recipe! I'm so happy to see all these reviews, and so happy so many people are enjoying it. I developed this recipe years ago for a woman (Sue B.) on the old Fine Cooking discussion boards. She had a recipe she kind of liked, but it had problems. I took it and reworked it for her, thus, Sue B.'s Chocolate Cake.

This is the first cake I have ever baked from scratch, and it was marvelous! I cut the recipe in half to have a smaller, 3-person 2-layer cake that was more manageable. I also substituted 2% milk with a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar for the buttermilk. The end result was a dense, moist cake that wasn't too sweet and also wasn't too chocolate-y for me (but I'm not a huge chocolate fan). With chocolate icing, raspberry jam between the two layers, and raspberries on top, it was literally the perfect cake. I will make this again.
My family thouhgt this recipe was ok.

Delicious cookies!  My daughter and I made these together this afternoon.  I found the directions to be very accurate - even down to the number of cookies.  I used a small meatball scooper to measure and came up with exactly 72 cookies.  They hold their shape well while baking - not much spreading at all. The raisins stayed moist and plump - I liked the unique method of pre-soaking them.  On a personal note, I am so happy that Merrie shared this recipe online- I am part of the family mentioned in the description, but since I live very far away,  I don't often get a chance to taste her yummy dishes.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This is a great recipe. The cookies came out just crisp enough to be really delicious. Not too soft, not too crisp.
My wife considers herself to be an Oatmeal Cookie connoisseur and she raved about the cookies. She even took some to her work place and everyone there enjoyed the cookies.
Thanks for posting this recipe.
YUM!  My fiance is very particular about oatmeal raisin cookies and he loved them!  They have such a good flavor.  I think I may add a few more raisins next time.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Yes, this is a great cookie recipe.  I originally found the recipe in the "Colorado Cache Cookbook" published 1978.

The cookies are wonderful...I agree, the secret is in the 'egg-raisin-soak process'.
I have discarded my favorite oatmeal cookie recipe and added this one to my file!
Thanks for sharing!!!!!

I don't usually like cookies, I'm more interested in the dough...but these are more than great, they are awesome!!!  I have had to make these 4 times since I got the recipe a week ago, and 3 of the 4 times I had to double the batch.  I did add some nutmeg (1 tsp.) to the spices and a little less than 1/4 cup milk to the egg mix.  Now I have neighborhood kids coming over just to see if I have baked any more of these wonderful little things.  What an awesome recipe!!!
Great oatmeal cookies! Better than my mother's recipe(don't tell her). Thanks for sharing.

I halved the recipe and these cookies tasted great. The texture was just a lttle too soft for me but that could well have been my fault for not giving them a couple more minutes in the oven. Presoaking the fruit is a wonderful idea, good for bread and butter puddings too.

These cookies turned out great! Wow, soaking the raisins makes all the difference. Two of my kids (raisin haters) cringed when they saw the cookies and I pleaded with them to give them a try. They were absolutley amazed. They gobbled them up. The directions were perfect and easy to follow. Thank you, Thank you! I too will throw way my other oatmeal cookie recipes. This is the one!
I made these cookies the other day and thought they were delicious.  I have made oatmeal cookies for years and these were a little different.  We really liked them.

These cookies are incredibly good.  I thought at least with the oatmeal and raisins they'd have something healthy in there, but I'm just afraid they're better than that.  Like Goldilocks, these turned out "just right"; not too soft, not too crisp, perfect, petite, and YES! even dainty. (If you can imagine a dainty oatmeal cookie, this would be the one.) From now on, this will be my oatmeal cookie of choice!
Awesome.  A nice mix of oatmeal and cookie dough texture!  A good amount of raisins too.  They stay chewy, which is the most important part of all! Thanks
These cookies were perfect in every way except for being just a tad salty.  Next time I will reduce the salt by one-half.

My family is not fond of oatmeal raisin cookies, but these disappeared in no time.  My husband loved the texture, not too hard or soft, just right.  One of the best things about Recipe-zaar is that when my friend wanted this recipe, I just told her where I got it and she didn't have to wait for me to get it to her.

Excellent, I used only .5 tsp of salt, and omitted the pecans, everything turned out perfect.used parchment on the pan (easy cleanup), In my oven 10 min. was max need to watch or can easily be over done.  Thanks for the recipe.
This is the exact same recipe that I use!  I got it from the Colorado Cache Cookbook.  It is THE best oatmeal cookies!

EXCELLENT cookies! I had some raisins lurking in my cupboard that I wanted to use up before they ended up tossed and this was the perfect recipe for them! I knew these raisins were just starting to dry out a bit, so the fact that you soak them first, made this recipe even more attractive to me. It worked like a charm! These cookies were moist, flavourful and very delicious. I rolled mine in balls and cooked for the 10 mins. as I prefer softer cookies, and they came out just as I like,(they even came out very nicely shaped), they were sooo good just out of the oven,enjoyed by myself,my two little ones, and the little boy I babysit.... and they were STILL soft the next day! My husband came in while they were still on the cooling rack and immediately inhaled 3 of them in about 2 seconds flat! So, needless to say these cookies were enjoyed in this house and will definitely be a keeper recipe! Thanks for sharing this Merrie!:)
I'm already making these delicious cookies again(my family requested), this time a double batch! I'm telling you if you love oatmeal raisin cookies you'll love these

Made these and they are wonderful.  Fat content, cholesterol & sodium content is just what the doctor ordered.  Found the batter a little hard to work with after dry ingredients added so used my fingers and it worked out fine.  Thanks again
These were good cookies.  I forgot to add the nuts.  I didn't have any raisins on hand so I added Craisins instead...still yummy!

WOW, these are the best oatmeal cookies I've ever had!!!Of course,I'm a little biased :0)Thanks for posting this mom,I really miss having these,and everyone at the office coulden't stop raving about them!!!!Your the best,keep posting my childhood favorites and I'll get a raise in no time.

I halved the recipe and used 2 eggs. I also cut the salt down as someone mentioned. I left out the nuts as DH doesn't like them in cookies. They came out perfect in 10 min. I also used the small cookie scoop and got about 36 cookies, didn't have time to count them as they were getting eaten as fast as they came out the oven.Next time I will make the whole recipe.

This is the best Oatmeal cookie recipe I have ever baked.  Every person who ate these thought they were the greatest and wanted the recipe.

No one would have guessed (had I not told them) I substituted SPLENDA for the sugar.  Soaking the raisen seems to give a natural sweetness to the cookies of their own.

Thanks for sharing the family recipe Merrie!  Can't even remember how I got to your recipe today but used it for a 4th of July get-together where every single one got eaten.  They stay soft&chewy for so long!

I just made a batch of these cookies.  Instead of raisins I used chopped dried strawberries and only 1/2 tsp of salt.  The kids love them. Thanks for sharing the soaking secret, it really does make a huge difference.  : ) Tiffany
These cookies were wonderful.  I brought them to work and everyone raved about them.  Highly recommended and so easy to make.

I made these last night and WOW!  We love them.  I added 2 tablespoons of rum to the egg mixture and soaked the raisins but that's the only thing I changed in this recipe.  Thanks so much - they're the best oatmeal cookies yet.

Made these in the wee hours of yesterday morning when I couldn't sleep. I followed the recipe exactly using 2 sticks of butter rather than 1/2 margerine. They were clightly crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside. I had never soaked the raisins when making cookies before and I think that made all the differance. My kids and husband thought they were the best cookies I have ever made and needless to say they are over 1/2 gone within a day. These will be definately be made again
this is really a good recipe. quite different from the norm. I made these and cheated with a few butterscotch chips, about a cup and the cookies were wonderful. next time i will try wheat germ

I too like a chewy cookie and these are wonderful.  I used 2 sticks of butter and the 2 cups of oatmeal (to heck with "healthy", ha, ha.)  Everyone loved these cookies and I will make them again and again.  Thanks so much, Roxygirl in Colorado.
My family loved these cookies. I did bake these for 8-10 minutes (started checking at 8 minutes). Nice flavor.
Another 5 stars! I made these to give for Christmas along with chocolate chip and molasses cookies. Yummy and easy to make. Thanks Merrie!
Yummy!

Very good oatmeal recipe.  The hint about soaking the raisins is total genius!  My husband loved these.  I'm going to cut back a bit on the cinnamon and use half as much.  That's just a personal preference. Other than that, a great cookie!
Very very yummy.  I personally thought it was a bit salty... personal preference.  Other than that, VERY YUMMY!  Thank you for posting!
Well with so many good review this recipe had to be good, so I tried it and it come as everyone had said before me: "just fantastic". Thank you for sharing it.

Wow! I just discovered my favorite oatmeal cookie recipe - and I don't even care for raisins!  In fact, I've passed over this recipe for a long time because of the raisins. Today, I decided to make the recipe for DH.  I cut the recipe to make 2/3 batch, and I got 30 large cookies (golf ball size dough before baking).  I used dark brown sugar, because that's what I had on hand.  I soaked the raisins in the egg/vanilla mixtures about an hour and 20 minutes (I got distracted), and to my surprise, I really enjoyed the raisins in this recipe - these cookies were so crispy/tender and flavorful.  DH better hurry home because there may not be any left for him!
This is definately the BEST oatmeal raisen cookies I've ever had. Made it 3 times and lots of praise from it. This will definately be the OATMEAL RAISEN RECIPE ill use from now on!

Oatmeal cookies are my very favorite,so I was certainly glad I picked this recipe to try,it was a hard decision,as there are so many good sounding ones on recipezaar,but I don't think I could have done any better than these,I made them exactly as the recipe called for,and the were Wonderful!!!
Thanks SOOOOOO much,Darlene

The name of the recipe says it all. I haven't made oatmeal/raisin cookies in a long time because the outcome just wasn't worth the effort. These cookies are easy and great! It must be the secret step of soaking the raisins in the egg and vanilla. Sometimes I substitute chopped walnuts for the pecans. Don't even think of halving the recipe - they are gone in a heartbeat!

Good cookie! Normally I'm not a great fan of cooked raisins (I find them bitter and tough), but the method of soaking them in the egg and vanilla beforehand made them tender and tasty in the cookie. I made these a bit larger than the suggested heaping tsp and mine were baked at about 12 minutes- and still have nicely chewy centers. Thanks for posting!

THESE ARE VERY GOOD!!  I just finished making a batch and these are very good raisin oatmeal cookies.  they feel like they are going to be crisp but when you bite into them they turn out to be decadent and chewy.  DELICIOUS.  I cheated and used 2 sticks of margarine (all i had on hand) and they turned out fine.  mine took 10 minutes and came out beautiful golden brown.  Love the taste texture and look of these cookies.  thank you roxygirl for this great recipe. =)

This recipe is fantastic!!  I brought some of them into work--they were gone almost immediately!  I have been told by my coworkers that they now expect cookies every weekend that I work!  I always add extra vanilla to my cookie recipes, but otherwise I followed the recipe exactly and it was very easy to make.  I don't usually make oatmeal cookies--I usually prefer chocolate chip, but this recipe changed my mind--I now have a new favorite!  Thank you so much for the great recipe!

sweet recipe!! since it was just for my parents, i halved it but then added some molasses (2 tbsp.)to make em a bit darker and they turned out really well- sorta gingerbreadie haha. i didnt have any pecans so i just used some more raisins. also, i only needed to bake 12 of them for 8 minutes though. thanks again!

These were awesome!  My DH and his buddies loved them.  Soaking the raisins really added something. They are sooooo moist!  I did put icing on them as my DH loves Iced Oatmeal Cookies. Finally found a good oatmeal cookie recipe! Soaking the raisins is key in order to plump them up. I've soaked them in boiling water before but never like this. Worked perfectly. This is how my go-to recipe!

I cooked this for friends and family on Christams Eve and it went down a storm. I modified it slightly with less flour and only had one tin of chickpeas but it was fabulously flavoursome and I shall definitely cook it again for an informal supper in winter or summer. Thank you for a wonderful recipe.

This was a delicious recipe.  One change I made was to use less onion (about 3/4 of a medium yellow onion), as I thought more might overpower the dish.  Other than that, the only change was to use one can of chickpeas rather than two, because my crockpot was getting a bit full.
YUM!!  This was great.  I served it with rice cooked with currants and it was fabulous.  Recieved many compliments, and I will definately be making it again.  Thanks!
Can't beat the flavor of this recipe.  I set my rice cooker to be done at the same time and had a hassle free dinner ready and waiting.  Freezes well too.  Thanks for posting it!
Delicious! Thank you for this awesome recipe... It works great with my new crock pot!

This was a great & very simple recipe. I did not have fresh ginger, so I used ground ginger which was fine. The juice was rich & fruity & you were right French Tart, it was very simple in the crockpot. The chickpeas made it a real one pot meal too. I did not have the special Moroccan seasoning, but like the ginger, it was great with the alternatives offered. A real firm family favourite already! I recommend this recipe 100%. Thanks for sharing it with us French Tart.......Love your user name!!!

This was TERRIFIC, yes, TRUE!
Hubby even RAVED about it too!
DEFINATE keeper this is for me!
Nothing but empty plates did I see!
--- I used 4 VERY large chicken breasts with 3 tablespoons flour...onion powder (didnt have fresh) and ground ginger as well
Hubby LOVES chick peas, so used two 400g cans as well as two 400g cans of chopped tomatoes with grilled veggies in it....THANKS!!
GREAT recipe! Hope more people try it!!!

We have made this over and over again ever since my friend made it for us. UI have given the recipe out each time I've shared it with others (upon demand!)  great- srong but not overpowering flavors.Unusual but appeals to many.
Smelled wonderful as soon as I walked through the door..I had left the stew cooking in my slow cooker all day.  It was so easy and tastes great!

This is to die for!!  Used Chicken thighs, bone in for this and also added about 1/2 cup of Kalamata Olives and topped with preserved limes and coriander when serving, just wonderful.   The perfect accompaniment was spiced couscous #24336 the flavours together were amazing

We have made this recipe twice. For a brighter, cleaner flavor: Omit the flour. Instead of tomato paste and 3 TBS honey, use 3 TBS ketchup and 1 TBS honey. The recipe needs chemical heat. Add to the tomatoes 1 TSP sambal oelek (chili paste) or Tabasco or any hot pepper sauce. Add to the tomatoes the grated zest of one lemon. The cooking time in the recipe is vastly too long. Using chunks of boneless chicken breast, it will be ready in one hour. The result with these changes was the best tagine we have ever eaten, anywhere, anytime

Also: the quantities in this recipe will feed at least eight very hungry people.

yummy!  I did it wrong too.  I put in 1 can of chicken broth but cut the rest of the ingredients in half.  It was a little salty b/c I was too heavy-handed with the salt.  I was amazed that the chicken was so moist after 8 hrs on LOW in the crockpot. I also didn't have the special seasoning but the subs worked great! Next time, I will make the full recipe of sauce, still use 1 can of chickpeas, and put more than 2 chicken breasts in (I put the breasts in whole and frozen).  I served with couscous.  Pita or flatbread would DEFINITELY be good too!  Thanks!  DH said I can put this in the rotation...

I bought a tagine in Spain last week and this was my first recipe cooked after seasoning it. It came out beautifully. I left out the flour to make a 'clearer' sauce and subbed a can of haricot beans as I didn't have chickpeas. Served it in the tagine with a bowl of couscous and bread to mop up the sauce. It was wolfed back!

I tried this the other night as a friend has a tagine she got from North Africa - it was the most delicious thing I have ever cooked. I changed nothing other than using the alternative recommended spices - it fed a whole group of us with left overs too!I am now going to try more tagine recipes as this was very easy & a really tasty one, plus we all like spicy food in my flat!

Five stars, no question! I also served it along with Spiced Couscous, they go perfectly together! I had only two people over so I put a little less of everything. It was easy to put together but after less than an hour of cooking in the tajine (a traditional clay tajine I got from my mom!), the spicy mixture started overflowing through the slit between the top & bottom parts of the tajine and leaking down on the stovetop... Other than this minor problem I had no issues. I used regular flour and I managed to find ras el hanout (great combo!). My flatmate can't stand tomatoes so I left them out along with the tomato paste and put a little tabasco sauce instead, and the end result was perfect. My guests were impressed, this is a real winner!

This is a very easy recipe, and it is truly delicious.

I would highly recommend it!
My husband and I love this.  We just serve it with a side of plain couscous.  Thanks for sharing.

FRENCH TART, "thank you"! This is one of the BEST adaptable recipes I have discovered in RECIPEZAAR! As it was available, substituted pan-fried Italian sausage(cut in 1-inch lengths)and apples for the meat and fruit ... now for some belly-dancing lessons!
Everyone loved this dish except me...It's the first time I've tried Moroccan food and the spices are a bit much for me. But the family enjoyed it. Thank you

What a simple yet absolutely delicious recipe!  Thank you so much for sharing it.  Morrocan food uses many of the same ingredients as North Indian cooking in the Moghul style so I wanted to clarify one thing,  I think this recipe might be calling for "Chilli" powder, (note the extra "l"), which is the hot stuff (aka Cayenne powder) instead of Chili powder which is used to make Chili soup, a southwestern dish and usually contains oregano which is NOT used in Moroccan cooking. Most Morrocan dishes use chilli powder (the hot kind) and this recipe calls for 1 tsp of it which should be enough for the stoutest taste buds!  We like things a bit tamer and opted for 1/2 tsp which seemed plenty hot to us!  Also, all the spices can be found cheaply in an East Indian grocery store.  Anyway, thanks for the great recipe!!
Very flavorful, not spicy like expected but somewhat sweet tasting.  Great with couscous.  Definitely a dish that most people would enjoy.

We loved this.  I halved the chick peas &  tomatoes, used 5 thigh cutlets & added some Morocan Spice Mix & a teaspoon of harissa to give it some heat.   A HUGE hit.  Served it with the fruity couscous as others have recommended.   Lovely, thank you.

We loved the tagine and so our guests. I followed the instractions. Just added some pitted green olives for salteness. I cooked it for 5 hours on 10 hours settings. Thanks for good recepie. Will make it again for sure.

I made this to use the lovely Ras El Hanout received in the Spice Swap exactly as written including the saffron using the crock pot directions: my first Moroccan dish and it's wonderful.  Spicy but not hot and everyone in the family loved it!
Will definitely be making this again.  Now to find preserved lemons "by mail."

This is a fantastic combination of flavours!  I used boneless chicken thighs and they were delicious.  Also served with mashed potato, which is a great accompaniment.  I served this to fussy family members and they were raving about this dish!
YESS.  This is delicious!!  Thank you, Karen!!!  Now I want my own tagine, lol.  Large or individual sizes...??

I have made this receipe several times in the crock pot and it always turns out delicious! Even my kids (ages 6 and 7) gobble it up. I don't keep gingerroot on hand but have found ground ginger works well - otherwise I don't change a thing. This recipe makes a large serving (not a bad thing!) but for our family of 4, I've found cutting the ingredients in half is still enough to give us leftovers, especially if served over couscous. Thanks for the recipe!

We made this recipe in the crockpot and loved it, will definitely make again. 
We made the following changes: divided the recipe by 1/2, used 1/2 tsp of black pepper and 1/4 tsp of salt, increased the garlic to 3 gloves (for half the recipe), minced the ginger and omitted the optional carrots. Nice and balanced flavors.

I LOVED this as I was making it until I added the honey.  Its odd because I would have thought honey would go well with the other ingredients.  I still gave this recipe five stars because it is so delicious and I believe that others will enjoy.  I'm not a fan of chickpeas so I subbed pinto beans. At the end, I added more coriander and turmeric than the recipe called for and I added jamaican allspice and cardamon.  Thanks for sharing! It's a keeper!

Perfect, I served this for Rosh Hashannah and it was a winner all the way around.  Perfect blend of spices and so simple!  This is on my regular menu.  Don't leave out the cayenne pepper either.  If it is light enough for my six year old your can handle it.  Very light and subtle.

This was a hit! my family and guests loved it. but I agree with the other reviews, it definitely tastes better with some heat! I used Indonesian sambal chili paste. I served it with couscous and pita. There was a total of 9 people at dinner that night and It took me 2 days to finish the leftovers! I highly recommend it.

Very tasty.  Smelled amazing while cooking.  A bit more complicated than what I expected, but I would make this again.  I used the cornflour.  Had to sub dried ginger for fresh.  My only complaint is that I think I left this cook too long because the chicken was a little dry.  Next time, I will keep an eye.  This also freezes well.

This was an excellent recipe! I left out the canned tomatoes for dietary reasons (but kept the tomato paste)and only used one extra large onion instead of 2 large. The spices were incredible and gave a multi-dimensional flavor in every bite. I only used about 3/4 teaspoon of cayenne and it came out perfect... exactly as you described French Tart, "fragrant and fruity". I used my slow cooker for 3 hours on high and everything was great. Served it with couscous and whole wheat baguette. Thanks for a great meal! ***UPDATE:  The leftovers were even better!  I recommend letting this sit and settle overnight.  The flavors meld together wonderfully.

Yep - I agree with everyone else that this was yummy.  I didn't use the apricots (DW believes that fruit in savoury dishes is contraversial!) and used preserved lemon instead (I guess sour fruit must be OK?).  Absolute winner in the slow cooker!

Outstanding.  I thought I already rated this but must have missed.  I made it on the stove over the holidays and my husband who is Algerian and I loved it.  I put about 4 servings in the freezer.  We had it last night and my daughter who is picky was gobbling it up as well.  I used leg quarters instead of breast.  Will definitely make again for my family and anyone who I want to impress.  Thanks French Tart!!!

French Tart, you've done it again, another wonderful recipe.  You never disappoint.  If I sound like I am gushing over you, I'm not, I am gushing over your recipes.  They are delicious.  My family loved this dish.  They are not used to eating cooked apricots, but I think the flavor does get infused into the dish even if you do not eat the cooked apricots.  Yummy.  I followed the recipe exactly, but I used boned in chicken thights.  I also substituted paprika for the cayenne pepper because we have young children who do not like spicy food.  Yummy, the whole house smelled wonderful when I brought my kids home from swimming practice.  This is going into our regular rotation.  Thank you.

Delicious! facinating flavors. I didin't have the  ras el hanout spice mix, so I used the other spices, let it cook in my crock pot on high for about three hours and then on low to keep it warm. I didn't cut up the chicken, but just put whole thighs. I think I'll cut up the meat next time. I also made some Roti, Chapati to eat with it. I've never done a Moraccan dish before. Thanks for the recipe!

My husband and I loved this dish.  I have made it twice in 2 weeks.  I used a cut up whole chicken both times.  I browned the chix before putting it in the crock pot.  The first time I made it, I only used one can of chick peas--the second, two cans.  I think one can is plenty.  I didn't have the Ras El Hanout Spice Mix so I just used the substitution spices though I am excited to try the authentic spice mixture next time.  The dish was delicious served over couscous.  Thanks French Tart for a wonderful recipe that will definitely become part of my regular rotation!

I didn't have all the ingredients, but I made a variation of this that was just incredible! I used chicken legs and sultanas instead of apricots!  I did have ras el hanout and this was the first time I'd used it.  What an incredible collection of flavours.  A truly wonderful dish, unique but comfortingly familiar! I served it with plain couscous! Excellent, will make again I am sure!

Simply amazing. My boyfriend made this for me one night, and he did actually add golden raisins along with the apricots. He also made it using boneless, skinless chicken breasts which we both felt were not the best choice. It needed a *meatier* taste - I think bone-in, skinless thighs would work amazingly with this. We had it with plain couscous and West Indian hot pepper sauce on the side (all we had on hand) to give it some added heat. However, over all this is a totally filling, beautiful combination of flavours and textures.  I should add that I read the review below in which a member mentions that they feel the cooking time is too long, especially for chicken breast meat.  Perhaps their crock pot had a higher temperature setting, because I have our second attempt at this in the crock pot as I type, and it has definitely taken at least three hours to achieve fully cooked chicken, and I think the chickpeas need longer to soften a bit more.  But that's just my opinion. ;-)  Overall, this dish is a stunning combination of flavours and textures, and is totally satisfying and filling.  A great dish!

This was quite a nice tagine.  The chicken was so tender, and the apricots were juicy.  I made it exactly as stated, with the optional preserved lemons.  Next time I'll try it with chicken thighs.  Yum!  Thanks French Tart!

Wow!! Amazing combination of flavours and textures.  Great.  I forgot to put the apricots, but it was still fantastic.  I used fresh tomatoes and pepper flakes instead of the cayenne.  Next time I am going to add a diced potatoe.  Thanks for posting, I am still enjoying it.

Have made this several times now and it's become a firm favourite. I usually freeze some in individual portions and microwave up for a quick tasty meal when I'm in a hurry. Usually serve it with chunks of homemade garlic and rosemary foccacia also lazily stored in that freezer!

This is one of the best dishes I have ever made, and indeed one of the best I have ever eaten. I used French Tart's ras el hanout recipe. I used a lot of whole spices and ground them the day I made the spice mix. So good and worth the effort, but playing with spices is my idea of fun. I didn't alter the recipe at all, and won't next time, which is unusual for me. That's how good it is! I intend to check out French Tart's many other recipes. Next on the menu: Her Fragrant Moroccan Beef, Date, Honey and Prune Tagine.
This was terrific, I couldn't find dried Apricots so I used Apricot preserves - it made it a little sweeter but it was delicious. I also used less cayenne because I was afriad it would be too spicy.
Delicious - thanks for posting! Will me making this often. Cheers :-)
My family didn't care for this at all.  I think it was because of the apricots in the recipe.  It just didn't hit our taste buds in a happy way.
Wow!  I made this for my hubby's birthday and it is fabulous.  We had it with rice and Arabic Salad (Recipe #90140).  It was a great meal.  I can't tell you how much I appreciate this recipe.

This was perfect!  I used another recipe for ras-el-hanout and substituted chickpea flour for the wheat flour/corn flower because of an allergy, and it was absolutely delicious.  Next time, I think I'll add fewer apricots and toss in a handful of raisins and/or craisins for a little more variety.

This was so tasty. Wonderful flavors and hearty. I can't wait to make it again. I also browned the chicken before adding to the crock pot as per your directions when using chicken with the bone in. My family enjoyed this meal a lot. I served it with rice and pita bread. Thanks!

French tart this is devine thankyou so much for sharing,i was unable to get the ras el hanout here in Australia but made your recipe205185 i also made Recipe #176181 to go with it.
Perfect thankyou
really great recipe!  i followed drumfishs' revisions and thought it was absolutely wonderful! I will definitely be making again and soon! Thanks for posting!
This was delicious. Very European taste.  The picture alone sold me to try it.  Like someone said the leftovers were even better. My husband and son loved it too.

It took an extra helping for me to get use to and appreciate the taste - it was very new to me :) But this, hands down, is quite the amazing dish! The blend of heat and sweet are perfect!  I prepared it as stated, with the substitute spices.  I will say that it took me quite a bit longer to prep it, but it was WELL worth it!  I used boneless breasts, cut in large chunks.  Cooked on high for 3 hours...next time I might try bone-in legs to see if it could possibly be any better!!  This is a DEFINITE "keeper".   Thanks so much for sharing!!  You MUST try this one...you won't regret it!!

This dish is so incredibly delicious!  I used the substitute spices, and want to try it next time with the spice blend and preserved lemons.  I can't imagine that it could be any tastier.  I wish I could find more crock pot meals that are this interesting, healthy, and delicious.

I made this dish for my monthly supper club this week - was delicious and everybody loved it! Was so easy in the crock pot. It is the PERFECT crock pot meal after a busy day at work - will be making it this week. thanks for the posting.

Great flavours!  Will definately make this again and again.  My crockpot must run a bit hot as the chicken & apricots were to my mind overcooked.  No-one else seemed to notice.  Next time I'd reduce the time by an hour.
