Forgive me but this was called "Chicken, Chickpeas & Rice" as he likes all three.  Was a hit!  Thanks French Tart
I made the recipe as written, using the carrots but not the preserved lemons. I did not have the Ras-el-Hanout so I used the other spices listed. I will make this again for sure. Thanks!
This was great...easy to make, healthy, and flavorful.   Whole family loved it!  Thanks!

I only have one complaint about this recipe and that is the ingredients are not listed in the order they are used which I found a bit disorienting. 

The aroma was wonderful as this was cooking and the flavour lived up to the fragrance.  I served it with couscous and everyone enjoyed it.

This is FANTASTIC! Not too sweet, not too spicy -- just perfect! My somewhat picky SO loved it, too, so it's going to be appearing on our table quite often. Thank you for posting this. I cooked this with 2 bone-in chicken breast halves and 6 bone-in skin-on thighs, browned and with the skin removed after browning. Absolutely delightul.
Heavenly!  We made it in a tagine and it was divine!  :o)  Thank you for posting!
Loved it!  Very easy with impressive results!

Very good.  I used bone in, skin on chicken breasts.  I made my own spice mix by French Tart in addition to using the TAGINE mix from Williams Sonoma.  I added golden raisins.  I used only 1 can of chick peas and that was more than enough.  It took about 1 to 1 1/2 hours in my new Emile Henry Tagine (olive green colour).  Served over Tyler Florence's great couscous recipe.  The chicken was very very tender.  Had it the second night and was even better.  The sauce had more taste.  Also added lemon zest.

Linda

this was pretty good. i think next time (and yes there will be a next time) i will use chicken on the bone... but it's still really yummy with the chicken breast. i'm even considering buying a bigger crock pot so i can make more and lots of it!!
This is delicious! Tastes like pure comfort food.

This recipe is a perfect example of why I love Recipezaar.  How else could someone in the Midwest have an authentic Moroccan tagine on an ordinary Monday night?  I felt transported to another place.  This is such a special recipe, and I plan to entertain with it soon.  I made it exactly as stated (in my crockpot), and I used carrots and served it over basmati rice with some sweet mango chutney.  (My house has smelled positively delicious all afternoon.)  Thanks for a great recipe that I'll use many more times. :-)

Excellent, excellent, excellent!. When I tasted it at first I thought it was a little too sweet for my liking and I found it a tiny bit bland.  I added a little curry and wow!  Pure delight!  I also found that the next day was even better.  I guess after all the flavors married.  What a great make-ahead stew.  This was my first time cooking with fruit so now I'm on to other fruity ingredients.  Thanks for posting and introducing me to the fruity flavors!

This was wonderful. I really like sweet fruity dishes like this and it worked well in the crock pot even though I reduced it to 2 servings. Hubby and I are whimps when it comes to eating spicy hot foods so we didn't do the harissa. Thanks for the recipe.

Thanks for another winner FT, well 3 winners in fact as I also made recipe#209887 & recipe#205185 and the meal was outstanding. I had a whole chicken so I just skinned, boned and cut into 8 pieces. I don't have a tagine nor a slow cook so I used a heavy duty dutch oven and started the onions and garlic on the stove top then threw everything else in brought it to the boil put the lid on and popped it in the oven for a couple of hours on 250f. So easy. Served with pita bread and couscous.

Update: April 09 - made for friends Saturday night in our new crock pot.  Chicken thighs were on hand this time so I used them.  One thing about this recipe is I don't think you can go wrong it's so easy. If you have access to good spices I really recommend making the Ras El Hanout spice mix.  I'm fortuate to be able to get organic spices in bulk so making up a batch is fairly cheap.  I went with couscous and corn tortillas as DH is currently off wheat, but with this dish anything would work.  Thanks again FT.

A great recipe to make again.  I didn't add the lemon or the harissa but I did add the carrots and I also added zucchini.  
I left out the ginger, coriander, and saffron because I didn't have any.   
I added more chicken broth because I wanted more sauce because I was serving it over cous cous.

Mmmmm!  Making this lead me to making the Ras El Hanout and preserved lemons.  Since I still have a while to go until the lemons are done, I made the tagine without and it was delicious.  I'm definitely making it again when the lemons are ready.  Thanks for sharing.

This receipe was delicious and I would recommend trying it! The only change I made was adding cannellini beans 10mins before the end, in place of chickpeas as I had run out, they were delicious though.  I did find the dish was too sweet in flavour with the honey & apricots, so next time I would only add 1tbsp of honey, I will also try adding the preserved lemon next time!
Wow, I'm so glad i tried this. My crock pot is tiny so i simmered it in a huge pot with a lid for 1 1/2 hrs.
This is the best recipe I have yet made in my crock pot and was well worth the work it took to find ras el hanoub.  Highly recommended!
I omitted the flour and I didn't put apricots as I didn't have any. I also used a cut up whole chicken. It reminded me of a restaurant style Indian curry. I'll make this again.
Very good recipe! It did not all fit in my tagine, however, and I had to transfer it to my largest skillet and finish it in my crockpot. It was a lot of food!

This is a stunningly good dish--interesting to foodies, yet gentle enough on the palate that even my most food conservative friends and family enjoy it.
Take the time to make a batch of the "Ras al Hanoud" spice mixture before hand--it is the magic secret--and it is wonderfulin a lot of other dishes too.

Awesome, awesome recipe! I used chicken thighs instead of breasts because I think thighs stand up better to long cooking times. Next time, I'll cut the amount of chicken in half and add a few more apricots. Other than that, the flavors were really, really good. I loved it and even my picky weekend gourmet chef dh said to put this one in the rotation. Thank you for the recipe, French Tart!

This is absolutely fabulous! The flavors were amazing--I just can't say enough good things about this recipe! I'd been wanting to try one of French Tart's recipes--and I finally got around to it!  I cut the entire recipe in half and took drumfish's suggestion re:ketchup and used the substitution for the ras el hanout (can't get it here in North Carolina). Also, I used boneless, skinless chicken breasts and made the entire dish the night before, stuck it in the fridge, and turned my crockpot to low when I went to work.  I think that the low crockpot setting, plus sitting overnight made the chicken perfectly moist and flavorful--no dry chicken here!  It was so good!!  The only unfortunate part was that bf wasn't a fan--so it won't make it into my dinner rotation as much as I would like it to...but I do believe I will keep this recipe on hand for company and dinner parties.  Thanks SOOO much!!

awesomely tasty and easy crockpot recipe.  My family loved this one.  I halved this recipe and got enough food for 6 hearty portions.  Used twice the apricots and threw in a chopped bell pepper for the heck of it.  Even better reheated the next day.  I didn't add any chemical heat since my nine year old was eating this but instead put Sriracha sauce on my own portion and it was divine.

This was amazing! A fragrant and tasty combination of flavors that my family loved.  Followed the recipe exactly but left out the cilantro at the end (personal preference).  Cooked several hours in the crock pot - served over rice.

This is my first review ever and I just had to put in my two cents! First of all It was fabulous! I made one adjustment and added golden raisins instead of apricots (family doesn't like them) and ran out of honey but still turned out amazing! This is definately a keeper!! Note: I cut this in half and it still fed 4 adults with leftovers.

This recipe ROCKS.  It has so many layers of flavor and is a superb 'guests coming over' meal as well as just a good one to prepare at the beginning of the week and eat all week.  I definitely recommend adding some harissa (or thai chili garlic paste) to cut the sweetness.  As the chef recommends, maybe best to let your guests add their own to their taste.  Highly recommended recipe, from a highly picky eater.

This was a good recipe, but not a favorite.  I used only 4oz. of apricots (and chopped them) and still found it a bit sweet.  As far as appearances, it doesn't look very appetizing -- mine was a very uniform yellow color.  If I made it again, I would have to add the carrots and larger chunks of tomato to give it more color.  My boyfriend also commented that the chicken seemed a bit dry.  I think I would try low heat for four hours instead of high heat for three hours.

Yummy!  We've made it as is, and also a vegetarian version, substituting a cup or two of almonds for the chicken.  It works quite well, although the chicken really adds a depth of flavour.  We were lucky enough to bring back loads of Ras el Hanout from Morocco, but we also add an extro tsp of ultra hot paprika.  We usually serve it with couscous.  Delicious!  Thanks for posting.

This was another great dish, I made it as written with the addtion of some golden raisins. My hand may have been a bit heavy with the spices but we don't shy away from bold flavours.  I will definitely make again, and as written. I highly recommend this recipe to anyone wanting to try something new.  Thanks again French Tart!

This was easy to put together & incredibly good, even the picky eaters went back for more!
Thanks for sharing, definitely one I'll make again :)
This was really good, and a great way to use up dried apricots. I threw some more in there than the recipe called for because I like them so much. I'll definitely make this again!

Over the summer I had Moroccan chicken tagine in a very fancy, very expensive restaurant in California and I've been trying to replicate it ever since. This came incredibly close to that original dish was aaaaaabsolutely delicious. I cooked it on the "low and slow" setting for 8 hrs instead of on high for 3. A few alterations though: I used chicken thighs, which I browned quickly in a pan before adding, instead of breasts. Personally I just loooove chicken thighs. I wasn't able to find ras el hanout, but the substitute spice mix worked wonderfully anyway. I also made a few changes as per the suggestions of drumfish. I omitted the flour, used ketchup and honey, and added lemon zest. My only suggestion is I may omit the chickpeas altogether next time since they were still quite hard even after 8 hours, and clashed a bit with the rest of the dish texturally. I served this with some couscous doctored with cumin and turmeric and some warm pita bread. And the leftovers the next day were even better, if that's possible. A-MAZING!

Served to family members (some that i was going out on limb serving an international dish) and they all loved it. Don't forget to lightly brown the chicken before putting in the crock pot (seasoned with mit mita), not too much...High setting for about 2 hrs and low for about 3 hrs with boneless skinless chicken thighs and it was still moist. I keep everything in the recipe except 1,1/2 cans of chickpeas. Added a little ketchup, a little extra tumeric, chopped the apricots, 2 carrots, 1 bell pepper, and 1 sweet potato made for a really nice balance of flavors, was worried about a strong apricot flavor and was not the case at all, in fact could have added a few more apricots, also added 2 dried lemons instead of preserved lemon, served with cous cous and naan. used canned garbanzo beans and they were soft for me. Very very good...curry/stew/chili feel but at whole different level. Thanks for this recipe.

French Tart,  This is the first recipe I have successfully cooked in a crock pot.  I am totally impressed by this recipe and just love it.  It will be a family favourite.  Thank you so much for posting this recipe. Do you have any more fabulous recipes for the crock pot hidden away.  A five PLUS for this one. :-)

This was a good meal, I must admit I am always disapointed with apricot recipes, I love them but always expect so much better but I believe this is just me who thought this, With the leftovers I made pies out of them in the piemaker and are so delish and handy to chuck in the oven anytime! TY French Tart

An easy and good recipe. I substituted chicken thighs for the breasts. I had Ras El Hanout that I had ordered from tagines.com a while ago. I did not use a crock pot as I wanted to use my tagine. Unfortunately as soon as I assembled everything in my large fry pan I realized there was no way it was going in the tagine! This recipe easily feeds 8 with rice and naan bread. I added the flour before the chicken stock to cook off the flour taste for a minute then added everything in the order that the recipe calls for. (I drained the tomatoes and chick peas) Then I transfered it to my dutch oven all at once. I cooked it covered, low and slow at 225 degrees for about 3 hours in my oven. Came out wonderful. Next time I make it my DH requested a little heat in it, so as suggested by other posters I will try it with some cayenne.
DELICIOUS! I didn't have the ras el hanout spice mix so just used the other spices mentioned (including the cayenne pepper) and it ended up being such a unique and tasty mix of sweet, spicy, and hot!

FANTASTIC! I really enjoyed this recipe it was delicious. I ate it tonight for the 2nd night in a row and I have enough left for tomorrow night. Thank you for sharing this recipe I can't wait to cook it for friends.

Very tasty and great flavor combos! I halved the recipe and used the optional spices if I didn't make the recommended blend.  I did cook in the slow cooker 4 hours on high and it was way too long for the chicken.  I figured it probably would be but wanted to try the recipe "as is" the first time.  It will be made again and I will just tweek the cooking times or maybe cook on my low setting.  Thanks for sharing FT!

Excellent! I have never been asked by so many people to share a recipe of something I have cooked. Thank you! One tip - at the end I took all the chicken and apricots etc out and reduced the juices on the stove to about 1/2 and it really increased the intensity of the flavor.

You can choose from several different kinds of ras el hanout at Cost Plus World Market for less than $2. The flavor is really spectacular and far more interesting than the 4 spices listed, if you have any Cost Plus markets in your area. I used bone-in thighs and crushed tomatoes, plus extra garlic.

Loved how this made the house smell; little disappointed in the results.  I adore dried apricots, but they were lost in the other flavors.  Chicken breasts too dry, I'll try this once more with thigh meat.

I'm not sure what I did wrong, but it turned out a bit bland, despite the spice mix. The chickpeas were the most prominent thing in the dish, and the carrots and apricots got really mushy through the long cooking time. Also, this recipe made enough to feed an army, so I wish I had halved or even quartered it when I first made it to make sure I liked it. We got sick of eating the leftovers and I ended up throwing about half of it away. Maybe it would have been better if we cut back on the chickpeas and chicken but left the more flavorful ingredients the same.
Wow, this was great!  Flavors sang & textures were good.  I'll bet it's even better with boneless thighs.  That's what I'll try next time, otherwise no changes.  It was a big hit at dinner!

This recipe was easy to follow and absolutely DELICIOUS! I cooked it in the Crockpot and it came out perfectly. Being a vegetarian, I replaced the chicken with chunks of frozen and thawed tofu (freezing it gives it a hearty, toothsome texture). It worked perfectly with the flavors in the dish. Yum! Will definitely make this dish again. And it's so healthy!!

An excellent recipe, which is both easy to follow and faithful to the original. It fed four greedy people one day, then I added another can of chickpeas to feed five for lunch the next day! I added all the suggested options, and even the veg-hater seemed to enjoy it. AND it is really healthy!! I may try making my own ras el hanout next time, though the mix I bought is lovely. If you like spicy, don't forget to put harissa on the table!

Based on the previous reviews, I was expecting thisdinner to be spectacular but was left disappointed. My guests "liked" it but didn't rave over it. I followed the recipe to a exactly except used skinless, boneless chicken thighs, but like other reviews found it a bit soupy and bland. I will keep searching for that elusive Moroccan chicken dish!

This is a STUNNING and EASY intro to Tagines and middle eastern flavor.  This inspired me to make up the ras el hanout spice mix (a couple ingredients are still missing -- but it's close) and I can't wait to try making preserved lemons.  My variations: our veg house means no chicken, but I used Quorn naked chick'n cutlets instead (briefly cooking on stovetop before throwing into the slow cooker); I omitted the flour, like other reviewers -- it doesn't need it; I agree that chemical heat is a plus -- I added some red chili flakes leftover from pizza nite (about a tsp for the entire slow cooker).  The dried apricots are not absolutely essential (I didn't have any one time), but they add so much flavor and have a great consistency, that you might want to track some down (check the farmer's market).  Don't feel overwhelmed by the list of ingredients -- just open the cans and toss them in the slow cooker (and add in the Quorn cutlets), sprinkle with spices, stir and walk away for a few hours (I agree that you don't need the hours, especially if you drop the meat, but the flavors blend nicely with the time involved).  The flavor here is addictive, intoxicating -- so yummy!  Add a dark leafy green (kale, chard, spinach, etc) in the final stage of cooking and serve with rice, bread, pasta, couscous, or any grain for a tasty, balanced meal.

Well, I really liked it, but my husband didn't. He said it was a texture thing.. Next time I will cook the chckpeas longer before hand b/c after 3 1/2 hrs in crockpot they were still hard. Other than that it was pretty good!

Really liked it, was very impressed when my 5 yr old said she "loved" it; a very rare thing for her to say. Couldn't find Ras-el-Hanout but I note that you've said its readily available in France so will definately look out for it during our hols in Aug. Sweet, mild and flavoursome, made for ZWT6

I'd like to give 4 1/2 stars, but Zaar won't let me give halves!  I made this in a crock pot, and that may be why I ended up with 4 instead of 5 stars.  Something about the texture was just a bit off.  Also, I think I'd prefer sultanas to the apricots.  Loved the ability to add heat with the harissa on the side...have a non-heat tolerating eater and I love heat! I loved the mix of seasonings!  Loved the consistency and color of the sauce.  Overall, this was a delicious dinner, I just think I'll prepare it in a dutch oven next time instead of the crock pot. Personal preference.  Thanks for sharing a delightfully different dinner.

Loved how easy it was and how perfectly cooked the chicken came out--not dry, just perfect.  I used canned chickpeas to get around the chickpea problem from the previous poster.   (Dried ones are often iffy in final quality.)   I stirred some (1 tsp.) of the pickle in it, but not much because that stuff is really hot and strong.  Worried about DH not liking it.  So I set some on the side for me.  This is kinda a bland dish (which was great for him); good to spice it up with the pickle for me.  I went back and made the Ras El Hanout mentioned in the introduction and then served the whole thing over mashed potatoes.   I used 2 tsp. of the spice mix since I'd already put in the other spices when originally cooked.  This time, it was much better for me but overly spiced for my husband.   ZWT6

Delicious!  I loved the combination of fruity, sweet, and spicy flavors in this, made even better by the ease of crockpot preparation!  I used Recipe #262189 for the ras el hanout.  I'll have to try this with preserved lemons next time when I have the time to plan in advance for them.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe!  Made for ZWT6.

Great flavor, and I especially loved that we could add heat to taste. I loved the flavor of the apricots and the sweetness from the honey. I needed to cook it 7 hours on low because I went to work, but I would suggest following the directions for the best results. Thank you French Tart. Made for ZWT 6. by an Unruly Under the Influence.

This is one sensational tagine. I used tinned chickpeas and followed the recipe, using boneless chicken thighs and a dutch oven on the stovetop. What a heavenly smell it gave my kitchen. The preserved lemon and harissa are the perfect finishing touches. Thanks so very much for posting.
This is an awesome recipe!  The flavor is wonderful :)  I served this with basmati rice and steamed cauliflower.  Leftovers are great!

This was so good, that I paid myself twenty dollars plus a tip for this entree and asked to see the dessert menu. I do not own a crock pot so I cooked this in my oven at 275 for 2 hours then turned it up to 400 for another 30 minutes to kill any bacteria. I used the exact ingredients listed and it was plenty spicy for me.

Yum! So sweet and flavorful, and low in fat! What a pleasant surprise in my crock-pot. :)
We were out of dried apricots, so I used some dried mangoes that we had on hand, and it was wonderful over rice.

I used Recipe #392583 for the chickpeas and then cooked them again for the three hours stated.  Loved all the spices, just used half a recipe for 2 thighs and half the cayenne.  Will make more next time.

This recipe was delicious. Because I enjoy heartier, rich foods (and wanted to add some extra nutrients to it) I changed it up a little bit :)
So... Instead of chicken breast, I used ~ 3lbs of chicken legs and thighs (bone in- but the meat falls right off the bone and you can fish the bones out). I added 2 zucchinis cut into thick strips, 2 carrots cut width-wise, additional 1/3-1/2 cup chicken stock, 2 oz more dried apricots, one potato cut in medium chunks (next time I may use a yam), and about 1/3 tsp more of each spice (if you dont want it too spicy, leave out the additional cayenne pepper). I adjusted the cooking time too. Cooked on high for 3 hours, then on low for 4 hours. I wanted the meat to be super tender and melt in your mouth, and the cooking time on the recipe just didnt do that. I served it over rice, and it was fabulous! If you want, you could add a creamy dollop of spiced sour cream :)

I made this with chicken thighs, and followed the recipe. So yummy, really really liked it! My husband said it was the best chicken dish we have made so far in our slow cooker. I love chick peas so will make again, and we tried couscous for the first time as well !
Very flavourful and super easy to make.
great recipe.  Made as directed wish I had remember to buy the bread to go with it.

This turned out really well and made in the crockpot was super easy to put together. We are going to a Moroccan-themed dinner next week and have been trying many dishes to figure out what we'll bring. This is it! Thanks so much.

I bought a crock pot specifically for this recipe, and I was not at all disappointed! I've never cooked anything exotic before, so I was a little nervous, but the recipe turned out fabulous. It reminded me a lot of the aloo chole or channa masala I get at Indian restaurants. In fact, I think I may even omit the chicken and put in potatoes instead next time. The only issue I did have was that the dried apricot were a little too prominent -- but maybe I put too many in or didn't cut them up enough or something. I might even try having a heavier hand on the spices next time, too. It certainly wasn't flavorless, but I wouldn't mind giving it an extra kick. All in all, it was a really great dish, and I'm so glad I tried it!

This was a wonderful meal. I cooked mine in the oven and served it with basamati rice, pita bread, and chutney to compliment the flavor. As I sat eating it I pictured eating this in France and somehow it made it all the more delightful!! I had plenty of leftovers so I took some to my elderly mother and she LOVED it she said it had an addictive flavor and I totally agree. I can't wait to make it again and I thank you again for an amazing recipe:)

This wonderful dish is good anytime of the year. I made the tagine on the stove top and slowly simmered it for three hours. I was afraid the boneless/skinless chicken breasts would be dried out but they were moist and so tender I could cut it with my spoon. Served with plain couscous. Thanks for another great recipe.

This is the best thing I have ever made in the slow cooker!  Has helped to restore my faith that there is a way to have a tasty and nutritious meal waiting for my family after work.  So many other recipes turn out bland, but not this one!  I used bone in thighs, prepared the sauce mixture and precooked dried chick peas the night before. I made the Ras-El-Hanout, but upped the amount slightly as we like spicy food, some of my dried spices were a little old, and as mentioned above - we have had bad luck with bland food coming out of the slow cooker before. Nestled the chicken in the sauce mixture to marinate overnight in the fridge.  Cooked for 6 hours on low and then kept it warm until we were ready to eat. Yum!

I have recently been given a Tagine and have loved trying different Morrocan Recipes.
This has by far been the very best recipe to date. I and my family just love it and I look forward to making it for friends in the future.
Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe, my husband loves it to pieces and can't get enough :)

Made this last night. We enjoyed it but it wasn't 5 stars. I thought it came out a bit too soupy. Next time i will only add 1 can of diced tomatoes. Also I will cut back to 2 tablespoons for the honey. We don't like tons of heat so I cut the Cayenne back to 1/2 tsp, which could account why it was too sweet for us.
Thank you for a great recipe.

I have had this recipe in my cookbook forever and my husband finally made it yesterday. It was absolutely amazing! We made a few mods based on our tastes and what we had on hand - we used 2lbs of cut up boneless skinless chicken thighs (browned first), one large onion, 2 tbsp flour, 1 can each of drained chickpeas and diced tomatoes, 1tbsp honey, and about 2 cups of homemade stock. We forgot the saffron but will remember the next time. The apricots were large so we tore them in half but it wasn't really necessary. Cooked on high for just under 3.5 hrs. The chicken was tender, the sauce perfect - not too runny or too thick. No extra salt needed. He served it with mixed veg couscous and the meal was simply sublime. Oh, and I just realized he forgot the cilantro! We didn't miss it though, it's great as is. Thank you for a terrific recipe, French Tart.

This was a good dish. My family liked it although DS isn't so sure he likes chickpeas...lol.  Anyway, we thought it was flavorful and turned out good.  I will make again, as DH kept eating and eating and eating!!!  Thank you for sharing one of your family's favorites with us.

I am giving this 5 stars I loved it!  The flavor was to die for even though my better half did not care for it...the ras el hanout spice makes it pop and of course the saffron...I bought the spice on amazon and it was fabulous and not that expensive...

Yes, stunningly good! I cooked half the quantity, but used 3/4 of the spice recommended for the full quantity. I mixed the spices (the mix including the cayenne) and grated fresh ginger together with orange juice and finely grated rind rather than lemon juice, added a handful of black olives  and some ground sea salt and replaced half the apricots with sultanas, mixed in a splosh of olive oil, rubbed this mix into the chicken and left to chill and marinade overnight. Then I fried off the onion, half a leek and the garlic in olive oil for a few minutes before adding the chicken so that the spices just got into song. I had no honey so added some dark brown sugar - about half a tablespoonful. Only used 2/3 can chickpeas. Then cooked on high for 30 minutes, followed by low for two and a half hours. Can't think why some people don't rate this at all - I'm definitely in the 5 star camp and will cook full amount next time so we get some left-overs. Sensational!

A tasty, exotic dish. I did not add the cayenne pepper and would do so next time, since this sweet dish would've been even better with a little heat. I was concerned about the large dried apricots, but they actually come apart after cooking if you smash them with your fork and are a delicious addition. I served this dish one night over rice, and the next night over pasta. It's better over rice. Thank you for posting.
This was a great recipe! My husband and son both loved it!

My husband thought this was very yummy. I did change it up a little to make it vegan. I didn't use chicken or chicken stock, and I doubled up on the garbanzos. I served it over rice. He loved it for his no meat days!!
Yum, another awesome recipe from French Tart. Keep them coming!
delicious!  no significant changes made, and the leftovers tasted even better, reheated!  thank you, french tart!

I have had limited experience with Moroccan food so when our homeschool group planned a Moorish Feast as part of our history study, I knew I needed to be sure I had a recipe I could count on. When a I saw a French Tart recipe, I knew I was good. Made my own El Ras Hanout mix and drained my cans of chickpeas. Despite using the 2 Tablespoons of cornflour in the recipe, I still did a little cornstarch slurry to thicken it towards the end of cooking. Not a problem. The dish received rave reviews. The fact that it was a crock pot recipe took it over the top. Good for transport. Thanks, Frenchie.

What a wonderful dish! I made it as described except I added 2 chicken breasts and 1 large local sweet onion because that's what I had on hand. I also used the saffron & skipped the optional cayenne. It was so good I was happy that we had last minute company over to enjoy it too. Will definitely make again, thanks so much French Tart! I served with garlic butter couscous (2 cups dry   4 cups water).

This was the first time trying anything like this before. I really loved it, but my husband said "it wasn't his thing." Owell, I froze it in portions and it was even better out of the freezer warmed up! I did make a mistake and instead of looking for the Harissa at the Specialty store i bought a jar of Tagine...well maybe next time i will try this with the Harissa. Thanks for posting!

This adapted splendidly to a vegetarian version. I used 2 cups of textured soy protein (chicken-like) chunks, which I had rehydrated in tamarind soup base. I used dates rather than apricots (because I had the dates on hand). I was quite pleased with the result, and there was no problem about leftovers (gg). A beauty of tagine-type cooking is that one can generally substitute root vegetables, TSP or Quorn for the meat and still have a terrific result. And yes, it DOES work well in a Crock-Pot or in a high-domed chicken fryer. This is a really fine starter recipe, because it's easy and can be done well without special hardware.

OMG! What a wonderul smell this made in the house and the taste is devine. Both kids and friends alike enjoyed. Served with cous cous and homemade naan (tried the mpst rated nan recipe). Will definitely make again. Super easy and over the top in flavor!

Wonderful recipe!

The wonderful aromas from this cooking had my wife circling the kitchen long before it was done. I served with couscous and the wonderful glistening color made it a delight for the eyes. I used chicken thighs rather than breast, which I think adds a little more chicken flavor. (Most supermarket battery-raised chicken is pretty flavorless compared to what we used to be able to buy).

Tomorrow, I'll try my hand at some khobz to go along with it.

This was really good and simple. I think I cooked it for around four hours on high and it was great. The spices really came out the next day. I served with couscous and I will definitely be making this again, and then I'll try freezing it, it didn't last long enough to freeze this time :)
Loved this!  We made it as written (without the optional carrots) and it was delicious!  Next time we're going to use chicken thighs instead of breasts, but otherwise we'll leave it alone.

I made this recipe tonight and can say that it surely didn't disappoint! it came together quickly, despite the lengthy ingredient list, and was full of flavor! I made small adjustments, due to not having everything on hand. Like I only used one can of garbanzo beans, instead of two. And I only had one can of Italian stewed tomatoes, and one small can of tomato sauce, instead of the two cans of chopped, stewed tomatoes. And reduced the cayenne to 1/4 tsp. But those were not significant changes. I cooked this in the crockpot on high for 3 hrs, and when our family walked in the door from our son's basketball game, it was done beautifully!!! All I needed was to spend 15 minutes making a quick pot of couscous (using chicken broth to make it, and stirring in some golden raisins, slivered almonds and a few tablespoons of butter at the end to make it delicious!) and a warm, hearty and delicious dinner was on the table, with everyone enjoying it! I used all the spices called for, and topped the dish with fresh chopped cilantro, but did not make the other spice mixture. Perhaps next time. Thank you so much French Tart for contributing this flavorful and special meal, that's easy enough for a weeknight post-game dinner! This is good enough to serve for company too!
**One side note is that I'd say this makes enough to serve 10-12 people, not 6! So the nutritional values look high as is. But dividing it in half, they're more reasonable. 5 of us ate tonight, and we didn't get through half of it! It makes a lot! Which is great, because we'll have enough for a second night!

As a grad student, I did not have time to "pre-cook" everything.  It all went straight into the slow cooker on low for the 7-9 hour range.  It was wonderful.  Good to know I can just throw it all together and not worry about it.  Have made this several times this way now, and thought it would be good for others to know it works fine without pre-cooking.

This is my boyfriend's favourite. I use only about half the apricots because I find them too sweet and I don't like fruit much. Also I only use maybe a tablespoon of honey because once again it can get too sweet. I also put in a sprinkle of Vegeta to really make it pop. It's absolutely DELICIOUS! I serve it with rice and use chicken thighs, cook on high for about 6-8 hours, can't over cook it with thighs. YUM!
Absolutely beautiful, thank you for the recipe! It had great flavour, and the chicken and vegies were lovely and tender.

You know I wasn't wild about this recipe at first, but the leftovers tasted great.  I kept the pot in the fridge and put it back on very low heat in the morning, and by the second day the flavors really picked up.  I followed the recipe exactly, but I forgot to buy dried apricots unfortunately...  That seemed like a big mistake, because the dish could have really used them.

Absolutely fantastic. Enjoyed every bite. Served it with rice and naan. Can't wait for leftovers tomorrow. Followed the recipe exactly. If you are a heat lover, I recommend adding some cayenne tableside. Thanks for sharing.

This recipe was amazing! I messed up and did not precook the chicken breasts but it still came out juicy and delicious. I made couscous with it and it was perfect. My husband didn't even add anything to it which it rare! I should also add, I am not a huge chicken breast fan, but it was juicy and good. This makes servings for 10-12 not 6.

This was great and froze very well!  I served it over cous cous and it made some lovely lunches and dinners!  I did make some changes though...  I added golden raisens and used the ketchup suggestion by drumfish (Instead of tomato paste and 3 TBS honey, use 3 TBS ketchup and 1 TBS honey), 10-12 boneless skinless chicken thighs, ground ginger, and only 1 can of chick peas.  I also used the spice mixture listed instead of ras el hanout and left out the tumeric (my taste).  Turned out great in the crock pot and is definitely a keeper!  Thanks!!!

First time I've ever been asked for a recipe! Great with larger couscous ... I didn't bother adding the corn flour/corn starch.  The juices get soaked up by the couscous.  I threw in additions to the couscous after cooking it in chicken broth: some sliced almonds, peas, raisins.  FANTASTIC!!  Even better the next day. Freezes very well.
Smelled and tasted great when I put it in the crock pot. Came out wattery and bland. Definitely would not make again.

was pretty good, not what i expected. DEFINITELY reduce the chickpeas to one can instead of two, and instead of all apricots, put some prunes in as well. We served it over toasted almond and raisin cinnamon couscous. a little too tomato-y for our taste but still delicious and hearty

This recipe was amazing!  Perfect meal after a long Winter's day.  My husband said I "knocked it out of the park!"  I made it with lamb this time, but I will try chicken for the next. I used 4 tsp of this Ras el Hanout recipe. http://allrecipes.com/recipe/ras-el-hanout/  I may also increase the flour as it was a bit soupy.  Other than that, I wouldn't change a thing! Delicious!

Excellent flavors and oh-so-easy to prepare makes this dish a 5  star winner. I improvised and used 4tsp of Garam Masala in place of the Mas mix, works perfectly. I used only one can of chickpeas because I'm not a huge fan, added the cayenne because I am a fan. Also I did add the apricots which lose their sweetness into the dish, very good taste. I will use thighs next time so the chicken is moist, breasts tend to dry out. I served over couscous cooked in chicken broth with golden raisins and topped all with chopped cilantro; some warm Naan and an arugula salad with cucumbers. Fantastic!

One of the best crock pot dishes I've encountered.  It's exciting to finally get a full-flavored dish out of this thing (my first).  A few modifications: I was light on onions, so I only used 3/4 of one.  Also, found out I only had one can of chickpeas, so that's what I went with.  I used a pre-made Moroccan spice blend I had on hand, and nearly doubled the volume (7.5 tsp).  That gave the base sauce a great flavor profile before I even added it to the crock pot.  Also used boneless skinless chicken thighs and cubed and browned them before adding them in.  I found I needed to add about another cup of water to the crock before I started cooking it to make sure the apricots (which I sliced) and carrots were submerged.  Cooked on high for about 2 hours. Added some sliced almonds just before serving on  abed of whole wheat couscous.  Will make again!

I made it with one tablespoon of honey and chopped up the apricots based on some other reviewers.  I was nervous about the chicken breasts drying out too much but they were nice and tender (I cut them into large chunks).  This made enough for an eight person ladies' luncheon plus leftovers for everyone.  This will go into my freezer cooking rotation.  Delicious!
This was decent. Do not plan to make often but it was okay. Sorry, I don't have a much better review of the dish.
excellent recipe.  Good seasoning.  Pertty easy.

Quite delicious!  Followed recipe exactly but think I cooked it in the crockpot too long. The chicken breast meat dried. Plan to make it for a vegetarian friend using veg stock instead of chicken stock and turnips/parsnips instead of chicken. Simply outstanding flavors!

Made this for holiday dinner tonight.  Actually made it yesterday and served it tonight.  A BIG hit!!  Even my husband, who thinks all chicken tastes the same, had seconds and commented on it.  Two notes: the recipe doesn't state whether to use the liquid from the canned tomatoes.  I drained one can and used the liquid from the second can.  Also, I would use more apricots.  With only six, they got lost.  AND, I forgot the cilantro at the end!  :-(     Definitely a keeper!
Just excellent. I don't like too many crock pot recipes but this is another keeper from French Tart.<br/>Thanks,<br/>Jan

This came out perfect and quite tasty.  It was so simple to do in the crock pot.  I served it over buttered rice.  Just a wonderful blend of flavors, hint of sweetness and heat.  In my cookbook to stay.

This is wonderful. I used my tagine because I love it so much and could not have been more pleased with the results. It's like sitting to table on a rooftop terrace in Marakesh. The flavors meld exquisitely and offer pure satisfaction. Thank you Karen, I still miss you.
Simply marvelous! salt is NOT needed. Thank you for sharing!

Awesome!!!!<br/>The only reason this took some time was because I prepared the ras el hanout spice mix. Take the time to make this and you won't regret it! The only changes made was that I left out the cardamom and substituted dried dates for the apricots. Absolute winner! Thank you French Tart!!

Made it for dinner in my cheap slow cooker from Goodwill. Deeeee-licious! Had my 21 yr old nephew over for dinner, and he liked it, too. I used chicken thighs, on the bone, didn't brown them, just skinned them and tossed them in. I don't like coriander so I used celery seed instead. Didn't have garbanzo beans so just cooked a normal American medley of beans as a side (kidney, pinto, white, black, etc.) Served with couscous, yellow rice, and sweet, buttered Hawaiian rolls it was quite a good plate.

This was my dinner tonight and it was delicious!!!  Everyone loved it including my 2 yr. old granddaughter.  I made a half of a recipe, but just halved the chicken, tomatoes, chicken peas, honey and broth.  I used the full amount of spices and it had a nice flavor that wasn't too spicy. I also added the carrots. We enjoyed it with rice, would have made couscous but we had that the other night. Next time. Thank you for tasty chicken dish.

Very good flavorful dish! I cooked the onions and garlic, took off the heat and then dumped everything else in. I drained most of the juice out of the chickpea cans. I put in tupperware for the night until about 10:00 am and then threw into the crock on low. 7 hours was plenty of time for this. We'll do this again :) Thank you!

This is quite possibly the most delicious dish I have ever made in my entire life. And I cook a LOT of really good stuff! I followed the recipe to the exact letter, and the only change I made was using coconut flour instead of regular flour (if you don't have coconut flour you can just put a few TBSP of unsweetened shredded coconut in the food processor until it turns into powder), and i also added 1/4 cup of shredded coconut to the crock pot. It just seemed like it would be a good addition based on the rest of the ingredients and spices and it sure was! Subtle, but definitely there. And for the ras el hanout - I didn't have any on hand, but I also didn't just use the four spices listed in the recipe (since true ras el hanout can have up to 50 spices in it!). Instead I found a more elaborate recipe for it on Epicurious' website - just Google "ras el hanout Epicurious" and it'll be the first link. Absolutely awesome. And I added a few threads of saffron to it as well as some tumeric powder. Served it over a bed of quinoa & brown rice and it was OUT OF THIS WORLD.
This was a nice change of pace and satisfying on a cool fall evening.  Thank you for sharing this recipes.
This was very good. I used rabbit stew meat, no cayenne pepper. I didn't have any apricots; thought about raisins but didn't. Will try apricots another time.

I didn't have honey so I substituted molasses . I didn't have dried apricots so I used prunes.  I had two pounds of chicken breast . I used one can of tomatoes and one can of chick peas drained. I followed the recipe for everything else.  It wasn't too sweet, it was amazing! I served it over plain quinoa. Delicious!

This is my 2nd time making this dish and it is fantastic!  I added a little extra chicken broth the 2nd time as I wanted a little more juice.  The combination of spices is phenomenal as are the chickpeas and tomatoes.  I am so glad to find a healthy crockpot recipe as so many crockpot recipes are not.  The smell of this cooking was amazing!  I can't wait for leftovers tomorrow!  
Thanks for an awesome recipe!!!!
In a Tagine you do not sear the meat or chicken, the idea is to let it absorb all the spices as you cook it slowly... Searing or browning is piece of European nonsense.,

This was great! The first Tagine I have ever been confident enough to make---it was a hit with the husband and friends. I made it exactly as described. Even the toddler ate the chicken and chickpeas out of it (he said the apricots were gross though--to be fair they were a bit mushy by the end, but so tasty!). We served it over brown Basmati rice. I think this would go well with yogurt as well. Great flavors! This served 3 adults and one toddler and we had left overs.

I adjusted this recipe to suit the fact I only had one can of tomatoes (I added about 3 tabs of tomato purée instead) - used ras el hanout as well as the spices as we like plenty of heat and taste - I also included the carrot and dissected a whole chicken and threw in some thighs and I cooked it over the job but goodness the end result was absolutely fantastic... The men in the house dived in for 'thirds' - this is most definitely going into my online recipe software!! Thanks !!

Loved this . Substituted coconut oil for olive oil, chickpea flour for flour and prunes for apricots.did not brown meat.followed link to ras el hanout which was easy to make and a great addition. Second time added carrots celery and parsley and added preserved lemon at time I served. Accompanied with socca since it is gluten free.

I had excellent results by lightly browning the chopped chicken with the olive oil, onions and garlic. I added every thing else in the order the recipe states, Then put it all in the crock pot on high for 2 1/2 hours. (I also prepared just half the recipe because my crock pot isn't large enough for the whole recipe and it all worked really really well.)
This was awesome! My honey & I thoroughly loved it and will be making it again!
So so so delicious....i was impressed and surprised!!!

This was so awesome!! Only complaint is that my carrots were not soft after 3 hrs in crockpot (I was kind of surprised). Next time I’ll sauté the carrots beforehand. Also looking forward to trying in instant pot.

Crazy good! I was cooking for four so used one can of chickpeas and tomatoes, and cut the broth down to one cup. Used a pound and a half of boneless chicken thighs, cut up. Sauteed chicken in pan after removing vegetables and spices to add some color and flavor. Used full amount of spices and added a bit of red pepper flakes for hit. Didn't have preserved lemon so added a third cup of pitted green olives. Cooked on low for six hours and served over cauliflower rice. Delish!

This is a great recipe. That said, I have found that skinless chicken breast tend to be dry after hours in a slow cooker. My change to the recipe was to take half the spice ingredients, two tablespoons of EVO , and 4 ounces of beer and marinade the cut chicken breasts for 3 hours while the other ingredients were simmering. I sautéed the chicken breasts and added them to the mix at the end of the cooking process. The spices work well together, and linger on the palette, enticing you to take another bite!
This recipe is so delicious!  I thought I was eating at an authentic Mexican restaurant. Thank you for the great recipe!

This was ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!! We LOVED it!! I totally should have doubled the recipe because this went so fast! Because I have picky eaters who won't touch something if they see a veggie, after I sauted the seasonings in butter, I placed it all in a small blender I have and blended everything before I added the chicken, tomato sauce and broth. We were all raving about how delicious this was! My picky eaters devoured it (never realizing there were veggies)!! It was very VERY easy to make! Definately adding to our recipe list! Simply outstanding!! Wish we could give more than 5 stars! I can't believe no one reviewed this yet!! Thank you JT'sMom so much for posting this delicious mixture!!

I made Enchiladas for our friends using this shredded chicken.  Let me tell you...everyone LOVED it and asked for the recipe.  I'm going to make up another batch to freeze so all I have to do is heat it up for my next "fix" of this.  Great recipe, JT's Mom...thanks for sharing.
My husband loved this chicken!  I made extra & froze it use for quick week night dinners.

YUM!! This recipe was very delicious!! The flavor was just wonderful.  I didn't have any tomato sauce on hand so I searched around and found Recipe #90954 to use in this recipe. This is a fantastic recipe! Even my husband (who normally doesn't like Mexican food) couldn't stop raving! Made this about 2 weeks ago for chicken quesadillas. We LOVED it! Super tasty and tender. I would say it's very close to restaurant quality, if not better.

Simi Valley, CA

I made this chicken last night and used it to make soft tacos and it was VERY good. The flavor was great. It was very easy to make, I just let it simmer on the stove top for a few hours until it was dinner time.  I will be making this again very soon. Everyone loved it. Thanks!

I made my taco filling last night and I really have to admit that I didn't follow the recipe to the letter ingredient wise but I LOVE the method of this recipe.

I loved how moist and tender the meat was without being soggy.

I'll also try it with the veggies minus the cumin:) 
Thanks for such a great recipe and method of preparation!
Very simple recipe, yet yummy.  I followed exactly, except  I added  1 more clove of garlic, and added 2 tbs. of pico de gallo  to the tomato sauce.

Excellent and Easy!! Increased the amounts of veggies, garlic and tomato sauce and added some regular chili powder and chipotle chili powder! It was wonderful! Next time I will make a double batch and freeze half for quick dinners. Thanks!

Delicious! I just made this recipe for my boyfriend and myself for dinner tonight and we had to force ourselves to stop 
eating. This recipe is definitely a stand-out and very authentic-tasting. It's incredibly easy to make and virtually impossible to mess up. It's easy to adjust the amounts of ingredients to your own tastes. 
I didn't have a jar of tomato sauce on hand, so instead I chopped up a medium/large tomato and heated it in a small sauce pan along with some olive oil, salt, and a dash of ground chili pepper. I also used a bit more cilantro, a bit more garlic, as well as some green chili pepper in addition to the bell pepper. 
I will definitely be making this recipe again. My boyfriend is still raving about it 2 hours after dinner, and has already requested that I make it again. We both love Mexican food, and because we live in Japan, authentic Mexican is hard to come by. I can't wait to make this dish for my friends! Thank you, JT's Mom!
Loved it!!

Wow, this was absolutely incredible.  I made this for chicken burritos and served with guacamole.

I made this a couple times now. Everyone asks me for the recipe and I'm very happy that it was shared! Thanks so much:) !

I put this together yesterday and reserved 2 cups to make chicken enchiladas tonight, with my home made tomatillo sauce.  Froze the rest of it in 2 cup batches. I made this last weekend and really liked it.  I doubled the recipe and I think I will use the second half when I make Chicken Tortilla Soup sometime soon. This was exactly the kind of chicken recipe that I was looking for!  It does taste like the chicken they serve in the chimichangas at my favorite mexican restaurant! Thank you for posting this EXCELLENT recipe! It is so authentic and flavorful! I have used this as filling for enchiladas, quesadillas, and tacos. It was terrific!

Wonderfully flavorful, but not overpowering.  Because I chose to boil 2 whole chickens, it was a rather time consuming project, but the end results were worth it. Will def. be using again.
Excellent chicken!  I used this chicken to make Oven-Fried Chimichangas (#28148) and served with Mexican Rice (#117892).  I will absolutely use this recipe again, probably in many different dishes!

I made enchiladas using recipe #109685 (on recipezaar) and this chicken. Thanks to this recipe my mexican food cravings were satisfied.

Used this delicious filling in the baked chimichangas recipe #28148. They were a big hit! Using small tortillas would make nice appetizers.

This is so good.  I made this for tacos last night and we loved them.  I didn't have the problem of it being too much liquid, as a matter of fact, I had to add more as it all cooked down.  These are delicious and I plan on making for DD's graduation as she has requested mexican for her party. Thank you for sharing.

Cooked the chicken this morning before going to church, came home and finished it up and used in Recipe #129926.  Very tasty.  Had some leftover so it's in the fridge now. I just made this and it is absolutely the best shredded chicken I have ever had!  I had everything but the tomato, so I added extra sauce at the end for flavor and it turned out wonderful.  I will definitely be making this one often in my home!

This is delicious, simple and pretty to look at.  Thanks for sharing!

Hands down the best recipe I've made from this website.  I took the advice of another reviewer and pureed the veggies to "hide" them from my picky eaters.  May add 1/2 a jalapeno next time too for a little heat.

Great recipe!  VERY tasty!

I served the meat in corn tortillas with a little cheddar on top and my husband loved them.   Simple, but definitely a hit.  This recipe is a keeper!  Thank you!

AWESOME!!! I didn't have a fresh tomato so used petite diced in the can and was so delish I couldn't stop eating before I could get it inside tacos! Super good!  Have made this twice and 2nd time I was out of tomatos so I threw in my homemade salsa and it was perfect also.  I skipped the green peppers too but still wonderful. Only problem is my 18 year old son can't seem to get enough!

There is no need for all of the salt listed for this recipe.  I make this chicken on a regular basis with no salt, using real spices.  There is over 11,000 mg of sodium for the 10 servings this recipe makes.

A miracle happened with my adaptation of this recipe.  <br/>I had four day old cooked chicken I did not want to throw out, but afraid to eat as was.  I wanted to cook it again, long and slow to rescue it for another meal.<br/>So, I came across this recipe, doubting it would resuscitate the chicken to a much enjoyed state, but unwilling to throw out the chicken.<br/>Here's what happened:  I had fresh tomatoes, Ancho peppers and Salsa peppers (hot) from the garden (last gasp of Summer).  I chopped those along with the garlic and onion in recipe. I was too lazy to chop cilantro (which I love but had).<br/>I threw all this into a heavy cast iron skillet along with the cumin, marjoram, pepper and chicken.  (Did not add any butter, water, broth, salt or tomato sauce.)  Put burner on low, covered skillet, poured a glass of wine and watched TV news, let it cook down about an hour.<br/>Located some flour tortillas, rubbed a few with drop of olive oil both sides, toasted in another cast iron skillet set on low burner, toasting both sides.  When crisp, put a sprinkle of Mexican blend cheese on top to melt, served up the chicken mixture, crisp tortilla on top (!), heated some canned green enchilada sauce to go over tortilla, garnished with sour cream and some raw, chopped onion.<br/>OMG  This was the lazy person's chimichanga!<br/>Bonus was low fat, inexpensive, and absolutely delicious.

We love this recipe, I have made it several times and I wouldn't change a thing!  When I make this I also make Mexican Rice, Recipe #117892 for a side and make enchiladas with the filling.  Along with all the toppings cheese, salsa, guacamole, sour cream mmmmmmm!  One excellent meal!  Thank you!
Turned out great in the slow cooker, just put everything in and cooked for 7 hours best, I used split breast on the bone I'm not sure if that added to the flavor but it was perfect!

This was awesome and super simple. I used canned, diced tomatoes with green chilies in them (which I drained most of the liquid from) but otherwise followed the directions as written. Really, really great. Will make again.

This recipe is absolutely delicious!! I am kind of picky about my tastes, which is pretty basic (i am a lover of kid friendly type foods). This is an astounding recipe. It is so multi-use. I used it in enchiladas. Perfecto!

This recipe is terrible!  Make tacos like this and you'll bust your butt making bland tacos.  The two stage cooking method is ridiculous.  So is the high salt content.  And who ever made "authentic" Mexican chicken filling without chili powder?  Keep searching... The best shredded chicken is from a crock pot. This is very tasty, and the chicken stays nice and moist. I double or triple the recipe and freeze the shredded chicken in quart-size freezer bags (about 2 cups per bag).  Then I have cooked chicken on hand any time I want to make tacos, burritos, enchiladas, etc.
This is a great recipe. I followed the instructions except the marjoram. I used this for enchiladas, a lentil recipe I have and chicken chili. Very versatile.

Absolutely delicious and so flavorful.  This is my go-to recipe for shredded chicken, thanks so much for sharing this recipe! I've always had a difficult time attempting to get my breast meat tender and flavorful.  The cooking technique perfect as well as the flavor that the spices bring out!
Easy and delicious recipe. Will use again and again!

Excellent! I did the crockpot adaptation of this recipe. Forgot the cilantro and got it after I made it...never needed it. A local place makes it nearly identical except they add a little potato and carrot... Makes a lot, be prepared to use or freeze some. It freezes well.

I used my crockpot for this recipe - first on high and then low overnight. To save time, I bought fresh pre-made pico de gallo (tomato, onion, peppers, cilantro, lime juice, etc -no preservatives just fresh produce/ingredients), I used Knorr chicken bouillon (2 cubes instead of broth), leftover homemade tomato based marinara sauce, frozen crushed garlic cubes (2), and 6 chicken breasts (otherwise they would've spoiled in the fridge), and cumin as called in the recipe. I didn't have any marjoram. I put everything in the crock pot, massaged it all together by hand, turned it on and walked away. WARNING: The aromatic sensations are irresistible!!!! Also I used fresh chopped tomato not canned so I didn't have quite enough liquid and a small layer at the top of the rice was not quite cooked so next time I will add a bit more water. Some have said it's mushy but I don't think so. It's fork tender is what it is. I have made meatballs in the oven many a times but the meatballs tend to be not so tender or moist when done in the oven so following this recipe by placing in the sauce for hours is a better way to go. It leaves the meatballs nice and moist and tender, not dried out as in the oven. Now what I might do next time is brown in some oil for a couple of minutes on each side then place in the sauce for a couple of hours. I think if you brown all sides of the meatballs you'll seal off the meatballs from having the sauce flavor from penetrating them and will get less flavor so maybe just brown on one side and flip over and brown on another but not on all four sides. Just enough to brown and put in sauce. If you don't brown all sides then the unbrowned sides will have a chance to absorb the sauce flavor. If you brown every inch you'll not be able to allow the meatballs to absorb the sauce flavor and also might not be as tender inside anyway.

I made these today, but I didn't do as directed.  First of all I would never put raw meat in my sauce or gravy, I fried mine first or you could broil them (or they will fall apart). I never heard of cooking any type of spaghetti sauce (gravy) 3 hours unless it was a Sicilian sauce and then they have to add sugar to account for the bitterness of such a long cook!  Italian tomato sauces were made to cook up fast, few ingredients, and definately no oregano while cooking, add it at the end if you must have it.  Basil and parsley taste so much better. Italian meatballs, Jersey style,, Two lbs chuck meat, (90%) 1 medium onion minced, 2 eggs, 1 TB garlic (juiced), 1/2 cup minced parsley, 12inches of hard stale banquet (stick of French Bread) 1 TB sea salt, ! TB ground black pepper, Start by soaking the stale banquet in warm water (two qt pot break up in several pieces) add meat to a lg bowl (6 qt) add eggs, onion, garlic, parsley, salt & pepper everything except the bread, mix by hand until all ingredients are combined an set aside, drain water from pot that the stale bread is in, with cupped hands scoop a hand full of soaked bread an squeeze with cupped hands until water is not dripping from hands, when all the bread is drained of water, break up with fingers until all the bread is consistency of wet bread crumbs, now add to meat  an with hands combine until evenly mixed, now form the meat balls with cupped hands an set aside 1/4 lb ea, in large fry pan 12 or larger pour 1 cup of EVO an heat on med high until you see small bubbles forming , raise heat to high an add meatballs from the middle out forming a circular pattern, make sure all are touching, do not cover, foaming EVO should almost cover the meatballs, after 2 or 3 minutes on high lower to med high, inspect meatballs an when med dark brown turn each meatball with two forks an repeat cooking process, when meatballs are done they will have a rich brown crust all over, remove from fry pan an ina large flat pan put several paper towels an place the cooked meatballs inside to drain for minute or so, then in a bowl big enough to hold all the meatballs line with paper towels an place meatballs inside an cover with a suitable cloth, until ready to serve or add to sauce .

This is the "authentic Italian" meatball I was looking for, the kind I eat at an Italian restaurant. I was a chef in the New Orleans area for 10 years. I've always browned off the meatballs before putting them in the sauce, but dropping them straight in the sauce, to me, is so much better! So juicy and full of flavor. By dropping them in raw, the meat seems to pull in the sauce as they cook, absorbing the sauce. The flavor of the meatballs releases in the sauce. A marriage of flavors. The texture is superb, a great ratio of ingredients. It makes an unbelievable gravy! Is it safe to put raw meat into a pot with sauce?

Of course it is. Why wouldn't it be? Just curios about the question itself. Remember, you kill harmful bacteria by heating it. Bacteria that is harmful to you can be killed INSTANTLY at 165 degrees; however that same bacteria can be killed at even less temperatures (as low as 130 degrees). The only difference being time. If cooked in a sauce, for 3 hours, even if that sauce is only 130 to 140 degrees...you will have an entirely safe meatball. The sauce is HOT, even if simmering. I'd be more concerned with the excess fat without draining all of that 80% to 85% ground beef.
