Sooo very good!  I kept to the original recipe and used a food processor to chop the cauliflower and mix in the cheese, bacon etc.  Turned out very rich and creamy - will make again!
Loved it!
So Perfect... didn't change anything...just added a little more cheddar cheese..so so good! Thank you for sharing!
Tastes just like loaded potatoes!
Sorry to disagree, but I found this too rich and creamy. I would much rather make standard cauliflower and shredded cheese.
Tried this last night for the first time.<br/>Everyone loved it!
This dish was so crazy good just as is! Thanks for the recipe

FANTASTIC recipe!!  The folks who wrote that it was too creamy, etc., must have either overcooked the cauliflower, run it through a food processor, or both.  If one simply undercooks the cauliflower over steam (or in the microwave), chops it manually into medium sized pieces, and follows the recipe instructions, the outcome is wonderfully satisfying and delicious.  This was great as a side with some broiled salmon last evening!  Thanks so much for posting it for all of us to enjoy.

Excellent recipe! I changed it up slightly: I used a fresh cauliflower that I cut up and steamed until just tender (10 min); subbed chopped cooked turkey bacon, used half lite sour cream and half 2% Greek yogurt, and instead of green onions, I used chives from my garden.  Highly recommended :)
Officially my new favorite recipe! This recipe proves eating healthy doesn't have to feel like a punishment! :)

Yummmm! Definately a keeper and easily gluten free. The califlower I got was small so I added some left over steamed carrots-turnips-beets and all was chopped about 1 inch square to maintain some crunch. I steamed the fresh califlower 15 minutes. Used Jennie O turkey bacon. My husbands testimony..."tell them I ate it before I ate my meatloaf." Very colorful, it would be a great pot luck dish.
Made this for my boyfriend and now he asks for it all the time. Perfect side dish! I used frozen cauliflower and left it in big pieces. Doesn't resemble mashed potatoes but is still amazing!!

This was easy to make (I used the steaming the frozen cauliflower method, and using a hand potato masher to break down my cauliflower). I followed the recipe as written. Made three GENEROUS portions. I thought it tasted more like loaded rice than loaded potato, but who cares! It was still very yummy.

LOVED THIS!  It was amazingly delicious and really, very easy to make.  I used fresh cauliflower that I steamed before baking.  I made this to go along with a spinach stuffed chicken and steamed baby carrots for a rather healthy and low carb dinner.  I used the measurements listed and got enough to make 6 side dish portions.  Will be making this time and again I am sure.  Thank you Helping Hands.
delicious!

I made this last night to go with our Valentine's dinner of lobster & steak. I steamed a whole head of cauliflower, drained and mashed with a potato masher, added 2 tlbs. of butter, about 3 tlbs. of ranch dressing, cuz i was out of sour cream, 3 green onions chopped,6 slices of chopped cooked bacon & the bottom shakes of shredded & cubed cheddar cheese & pepper.   I didn't bake it, cuz it was getting late.The outcome was delish, my hubby said he could live without real mashed potatoes for this & that says alot cuz he is a meat & potato kinda man! Thanks for sharing, will be making this again soon!

I thought it tasted good, but was more work than I'd want for an ordinary side dish--having to pre-cook the bacon and cauliflower then having to bake everything after mixing it all together & layer it uses too many dishes.  Might be good if asked to bring a side for something, but I wouldn't want to go through all this for a regular dinner night.

This was delicious! I did follow some other's suggestions and due to being on a very low carb diet, exchanged the sour cream for cream cheese. Otherwise, followed the directions.  I used a potato masher and it had more of a creamy, cheesy rice consistency.  Even my picky kids thought it was good.  This is a must have recipe when watching your carbs.  I'm making it a second time for this week!  Thanks Helping Hands

This was super good and really did not even taste like cauliflower.  I steamed fresh cauliflower to use in this recipe. I also used half the amount of sour cream and substituted the other half with low fat cream cheese.  Low carb and delicious too!
This is darn fine eats.... I modified slightly because I know what my family likes. I am sure it would be good made exactly as stated, as well.
So very delicious!  I used frozen cauliflower,  low fat sour cream, and only one green onion.  It came perfect!  I will definitely make this again!

This dish is now a staple on my table. I use a medium sized head of cauliflower, full-fat cheese and sour cream and add two ounces of cream cheese too. This is the perfect pot-luck dish. Low-carb and a palate powerhouse.

WOW! This was amazing - I also increased the cauliflower and used frozen cauliflower that we steamed first, fat free sour cream, low fat cheese but extra bacon because it's bacon. All the guys kept saying was it was so good it tastes like a twice baked potato. We will make this again, possibly for my next pot luck!
The family loved it! I used up the cheddar and jack cheese I had and added ricotta because I needed to use it up. Best low carb cauliflower recipe I've ever had.

This was sooooo yummy!  My kids and hubby all loved it.  Definitely a keeper!
Thank u.  :)
Family loves this! I had fresh cauliflower so I used it and chopped it with a pat of butter. Only one serving was left and that took willpower it was that good~

Wow!!!  AWESOME!!!

I didn't have green onions, so I used dried chives. Still awesome! !!
Amazing. I make this for every potluck.
first cauliflower substitution recipe I like.

Great recipe, I use natural yoghurt instead of sour cream and add a teaspoon of chilli flakes to liven it up. I also mix breadcrumbs with the cheese for a crunchy golden topping, its a favourite in our house

This was even better than expected!  I cored and sliced a head of fresh cauliflower, then braised the cauliflower over medium heat in a covered pan with 2 T. butter, 1 tsp. salt, and about 1/4 cup chicken stock.  It took about 15 minutes on medium for the cauliflower to become tender.  Then I removed the lid, raised the heat to high and continued cooking a couple more minutes to allow the liquid evaporate.  Then I stirred and mashed it into smaller pieces.  (You may recognize the method from Chef John's cauliflower potato mash) Didn't need to use any more salt in the sour cream mixture, used almost 1/2 tsp. pepper.  I used pre-shredded casserole cheese blend and baked it in a 7 x 11 pan.  Thanks for a great recipe, I will be making this one a lot!

This is AWESOME! I roasted the cauliflower in the oven, gave it great flavor! I did sub half of the sour cream with cream cheese, otherwise, made it as is. It was the only side dish at Easter that was gone! I will be making this again and again!
I made these for dinner tonight. I didn't make any changes and made the recipe as written. I didn't eat any but my family seemed to enjoy them. They gave them 4 stars.

My husband's doctor wants him to cut down on carbs, but that's tough for a "meat and potatoes" guy. This recipe sure went a long way to getting him to foget his troubles! My 21-year-old stepson ate about HALF of this on the first night. They were very happy with it and I was glad that it was so easy to make!

This was my first time making this and loved it. I doubled the recipe, however I used a 50/50 cream cheese and sour cream ratio yum! But didn't use 2 cups of creamy mixture when doubling. Only made up about 1 1/4 cup creamy ingredients which was more than enough! I was worried it would be too heavy as there was that much creamy but the oven dries it out slightly to the right level :)
how many calories and net carbs please?
Great! I used garlic instead of chives. It’s was a huge hit with my family, they want me to make more. I made a double batch and it wasn’t enough! Great recipe !!!!
Outstanding recipe! I used lite sour cream and added 1/4 tsp cayenne. My Foodie wife said she would serve this dish to anyone!
This was yummy! I subbed plain Greek yogurt for the sour cream and garlic for the onions as I can't eat onions. Both my boys ate it!
This was an ok way to use cauliflower and get the kids to eat it, buy only I was willing to touch the left overs. Better the second day anyway.
These are my kind of potatoes. The balance of spices is perfect and the lemon and herb finish it off nicely. Served with grilled organic beef sausages and Recipe #449610. Thanks so much for posting.
Yummy! I enjoyed all the spices and the potatoes browned up nicely. Thanks for something a little different!

Loved this potato dish!  The mustard seeds, along with the other spices, really made this dish stand out and the lemon juice and cilantro really added a freshness to the overall flavor.  I served this dish along with recipe#277765 and some Naan bread.  We invited a friend over for dinner and he raved about both dishes.  Made for Fall PAC, October, 2011.

The only change I made in this recipe was to leave the potato peels on, 'cause we do like that very nutritional part, & your recipe definitely makes for a very nice tasting side dish, what with the combo of spices used! Definitely something I'd make again! Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Tagged & made in Please Review My Recipe]

Zipptiy doo dah!! We LOVED these potatoes. I'm usually not a big fan of potatoes, but since I was making your chicken balti, I thought I'd give these a try. What fun when biting down and having some of the seeds pop in the mouth. The finish of fresh lemon juice and chopped fresh cilantro was brilliant. Thanks for a great treat.

I love these potatoes.  They're easy to make, and the spice mixture is just right.  I used lime juice instead of lemon juice, and thought that addition along with the cilantro really brought everything together.  I served this with beef vindaloo, and it was one of the best meals we've had in a while- thanks for posting!  [Made & Reviewed for PRMR]
Incredible Dessert.  Rich, nutty and deliciouso!  Wiggie
Great stuff!! Thanks for sharing! This is a definite keeper - & easy, too!!

I thought about not giving a review on these brownies at all, they were the worst brownies we have ever tried. the texture was rubbery,the taste awful.
I made them just as the recipe states,but left out the walnuts. the cook time says 35 minutes,it was more like 15 minutes.
we wach tried one then threw them away.
Flavor good, texture AWFUL. Needs baking powder?

I personally have never been pleased with Woodruff so I haven't personally tried this particular brownie.  However try using a fruit puree instead of the apple sauce such as prunes or apple blueberry or the like.  Also Woodruff recommends if the texture leaves a lot to be desired add a tablespoon or two of Lecithin granules.  Since you are removing the fats you need to whip the daylights out of those whites and fold them in very very gently because the air you would get from adding the fat isn't there.  Just some hints for anyone who really wants to try this.
This must be missing an ingredient, like baking powder.  They were horrible.
Definitely terrible.  I think they need baking soda or baking powder!

I liked this recipe.  I made a couple of changes though.  Instead of the applesauce, I used fat-free plain yogurt.  I then needed to add about 1/2 cup water.  From reading the other reviews, I decided to add 1/8 teaspoon of baking soda.  The texture is fudgy and tastes very chocolaty!

The first time I've made them, and they taste delicious! I used all the suggestions from Steph82. But I think the batter fell, beause they still felt ever so slightly rubbery. Next time I wil put 1/4 teaspoon of baking powder to make it fluffier, and I will substitute the 1/2 cup of water with skim milk to add further richness. Excellent substitutions, Steph82!
This was exceptional....It really does need baking powder and i added a mashed banana...thank you for the reviews

Wow!  Impressively delicious and this absolutely couldn't be easier.  I will probably never again do all that advance prep and frying/sauteing when making a recipe of this kind.  Why eat all those fat grams and calories?  I was short on mozzarella so I added about 6 ounces of goat cheese and really enjoyed the tang it imparted.  I'll probably make it the same way next time.  Great recipe.  A definite keeper.

This was incredibly easy to make & was very good, as well.  All of us enjoyed this for supper with noodles & a tossed salad.  I used some frozen chicken tenderloins and grated mozzerella, otherwise followed the recipe to a "T", baking for 40 minutes.  Jacking my own review, I will add that dd liked this meal, although when she was a toddler & was served eggplant parmesan, her response was "If it's got plant in it, I don't like it!"

I made this a couple weeks ago and forgot to review it :)   it is absolutely delicious and so so so easy!!  My recipe that I do takes a long process and is pretty high in fat and also delicious but I really didn't miss all that fat when eating this recipe. I lowered the fat content even more by using reduced fat cheese and it was still great.  My husband really loved it too!! thanks so much for this recipe!!

Just made this tonight and it was awesome!  I think next time, I'll try adding a few black olives into the mix and a little garlic, but it's great just the way it is.  Tastes great, wasn't extraordinarily difficult to make.  Overall, an excellent recipe!

This has become my default dinner. Period. If I'm too tired or clueless to think about dinner (24/7/52, almost), this is what he's goin' get, 'cause it is sooo easy and sooo good. For the two of us I make it in a square pan with two sliced medium chicken breast halves. There is still one little piece left over, which I cherish cold the next day. I sprinkle a little oregano and basil over regular breadcrumbs to make them Italian. Thanks so much for this gem.

I just made this tonight.  It was delicious.  I skipped the breadcrumbs (to cut the carbs), added fresh garlic (between the chicken & the eggplant) and used less cheese (trying to eat a little healthier).  This sounds like I made a dull recipe but it still turned out super yummy so the fully recipe I am sure would be even more delicious.  I did put the eggplant between two paper towels and added a little salt to take out the water (still not sure why the water is bad, my mom always said to do this) then patted (hard) with regular towel.  Thank you GrandmalsCooking for this great recipe that I know will be one of our regular meals!!!  Served this to friends who loved it as well.

I put 1/2 of it in my freezer for one of my 'too rushed' nights!  This was very tasty!  I'd say it is essential to slice the eggplant relatively thinly (1/4") and do peel it.  I was a little careless and a thick, unpeeled piece of eggplant is just hard to eat!  I added salt, pepper, and lots of garlic cloves between chicken & eggplant layers, and used olive pasta sauce.  YUM!
Yum! I made my own bread crumbs with some Italian Seasoning. My 15-month old even ate it. Thanks for posting.

Hey this was WONDERFUL!  Very quick and easy!  The only alterations I will make for next time is to season up the chicken with some salt and garlic seasoning other then that this was wonderful.  I served it over a small bed of pasta!  It was very yummy and filling.  This was my husbands first time ever having eggplant and he loved it so much! (to add though, this meal didn't taste as wonderful re-heated the next day) But the 1st time around, this is WONDERFUL

I must say, I was skeptical about this recipe at first, but it was easy and delicious and will be a regular meal at our home!!! I used boneless chicken tenders, and classico cabernet marinara sauce.  I added 3 cloves of garlic, and added italian seasoning on top. I also sprinkled garlic and onion powder on the chicken before smothering it with the eggplant....very, very good, highly recommend.

This was absolutely delicious and it couldn't have been easier!!! My husband and I both loved it!!! The only modification I made was I added some more herbs to the bread crumbs plus a dash of red pepper flakes. This is a keeper!!!

This was incredibly good! I actually made it because I needed a recipe to use up some chicken from the night before and an eggplant that had been sitting on the counter for several days with no purpose. The chicken was already cooked and I only had about 3/4 of a pound, but I kept everything else the same and it was delicious. My husband and I loved it. The bread crumbs gave it such a neat texture. Thanks for posting!
This was tasty and very easy to prepare.  The kids didn't even realize there was eggplant!  I made a triple batch so we'll see how the freezer version turns out.  Thanks for the recipe!

Easy! Tasty!

I used two zucchini instead of one eggplant (what I had available, since I don't like eggplant -- I made thick diagonal slices, and I did NOT "drain" the zucchini so no waiting there), grated mozzarella instead of slices (leftover from pizza), and canned crushed tomatoes (with basil, oregano, and garlic to taste) instead of jarred marinara sauce. Sliced chicken (mine was still slightly frozen) worked out well. This was easy to pull together, fast to assemble, and tasted great!

Excellent and easy. Friends and family loved it. Used a nice garlic and herb marinara sauce. One large eggplant works better for me. Also bought 1-1/2 lbs of chicken strips. Fresh mozarella and parmesan (not the stuff in the green cardboard tube)really helps. Served it with green salad and fresh italian garlic bread...no need for pasta.

This was great, I added red bell pepper but it was still pretty crunchy so next time I would probably just use onion instead.  I choped and eggplant into cubes to make it easier to eat.  I also seasoned the chicken and eggplant with cajun seasoning, onion powder italian seasoning and minced garlic.  I only had cheddar cheese and panko breadcrumbs but it was fine.  I would like to try it with the mozzarella slices sometime, but I was looking to make it healthier.
While it was easy, you could not taste the eggplant at all which for me was a sad waste of eggplant :(
Really good and really easy! I added squash and mushrooms and chicken.  Wonderful!!

This was delicious.  We served it with General Tso's Chicken and they went well together.  The 1/2 cup of butter was plenty for us, in fact we could have used a little less.  The 1/4 cup of soy sauce was also plenty for us -- and next time I would even cut back on that a little bit as well.  We did really enjoy this and thank you for posting this recipe!
Dianne

My first fried rice attempt was a total success - thanks! I skipped the celery and added onion powder for extra taste. Used a can of peas instead and worked well for me. Started with 1/4 C soy sauce but then added more to probably the 1/2 C mark. Was EASY and delicious with Hawaiian Chicken #116908. Will never use store-bought dry mix again. Thanks for posting!

This was an excellent recipe. It was my first attempt to make fried rice, but won't be my last. I used between 1/4 and 1/2 cup of soy sauce. I also forgot the celery. It still turned out to be the perfect rice for our chinese meal. I can't wait to make it again.

I found this to be an easy to prepare fried rice that went well with Vietnamese Spring Rolls that my wife made.  I will, in the future, back off or even eliminate the celery or, perhaps better yet, chop it even finer (I had about 1/8" x 1/8" x 1/8" pieces this time). I think some chopped sugar pea pods would also go rather well with this dish.  This dish will be welcome to return to my table.
Excellent recipe.  It is so easy to make and tastes so great, I would go even as far as it tastes even better than some chinese restaurant fried rice.

Mona,
  This was indeed VERY easy and it went together so well,I have tried other recipes but they did not mix well.I loved this recipe,Everyting went so smooth and easy I was done and eating it before I knew it,will definitely make this often.Thanks,Darlene Summers

Easy, tasty recipe!  I cut it in half cause I only had 1 1/2 cups of rice.  Used 1 egg instead of 1 1/2.  Only had a few slices of onion so I added a couple diced garlic cloves.  Used canned peas (recommend sticking with the frozen - canned too mushy). Also added diced precooked bacon. This recipe is very adaptable as far as ingredients.  It's a definite keeper.  Thanks Mona.
Easy! Quick! Tasty! Used frozen mixed vegies and 1/4 cup soy sauce.

This is a really great recipe. Not exactly like something from a Chinese restaurant, but regardless my family consumed it. Even my very picky brother, and that alone says how good it is. It had a wonderful flavor, something I will make again. Thanks!

I guess I forgot to rate this the last time I made this, but that is ok because I am rating it now! The first time I made this was August 15th 2002 (I printed it out the day I made it.) My brother loves it, and this time I actually had all of the ingredients (last time we didn't have celery or peas- but even that way was good tasting). I will continue using this recipe when we need fried rice because it is very easy and tastes great. Thank you for sharing!
EASIEST FRIED RICE EVER!!!!  Everyone liked it.  Will be using this recipe for sure from now on!

This fried rice recipe was simple to make and had a good flavor. I left out the celery, but otherwise followed the recipe.  I felt there was something missing in flavor, but couldn't put my finger on it.  I will make this again.
I made this last night and served it with General Tso's Chicken (by Mean Chef), and all I can say is DELICIOUS!!!!  Thanks Mona!

I love this recipe!  It was so easy.  

Over the years I've tried to make fried rice and it's always flopped.

This came out perfectly and I will make it often.

I added some diced chicken breast.
we had this with general tso's chicken. it was better than take-out.....

This is uindeed an easy Fried Rice recipe that has great flavor. I cut the oleo bck to 1 tbsp and the egg back to one. Didn't have any celery but added mushrooms. Used left over cooked carrots. It was very tasty thanks Mona
This was super easy and it was good. I left out the peas and eggs because I'm not a fan of them but overall good recipe.
I, too have never been able to fry rice but I got it this time.  Thanks for the recipe.  I cut it down for 2 people and still have enough for us to eat again.  Be posting a picture soon.

GREAT RECIPE MONA!!! I did not have celery on hand-so did not put that,, and i didn't want so much butter-so used little olive oil instead. I have never made good fried rice--but thanks to you, i am doing great with it now!!!!!! Thanks again!!!!!!!!!

This was really good and the first fried rice I've made that looks like Chinese restaurant fried rice.  I prepared as written, throwing in about 1 1/2 cups of leftover pork roast.  I'll definitely make this again but will tweak the seasonings as the flavor was a bit bland.  Great instructions and visually perfect....just needs a little bit more flavor!  Thanks for the recipe Mona :)
Really good stuff.
Probably the best fried rice i've tried making (and I've tried a lot!!) Doesn't taste anything like restaurant but good nonetheless.

I made a version of this tonight with brown rice, a little olive oil and Bragg's Liquid Aminos (which is gluten free). Instead of chopping carrots I used frozen mixed petite peas and cubed carrots. Yum! I will definitely be making this again!

Absolutely super delicious and so EASY to make....I'll definately make this again and again.....
P.S.  I used brown rice....very tasty.....

Delicious!  I left out the veggies & only used 2 eggs, & it still turned out wonderful!

I also substituted oleo for margarine, & used pre-cooked frozen rice that I got on sale.  This is definatly a keeper, & will be a regular at my house :D

Mine didn't turn out the prettiest, but tasted great, even better after sitting and the flavors melded more.  Decided pretty last minute to make this with Chinese Chicken Balls so needed to make fresh rice and cooled it quickly in freezer, left out the peas (preference), used slightly less than 1/2 cup of margarine, diced all the veggies, used 2 eggs and just enough soy to have a slight flavor.

This rice was good, but WAY too much butter, and I used 4 cups of rice to 1/2 cup butter.  I will try it again with maybe 1/4 cup butter and a little bit of oil.  Overall a good recipe, just needs a little tweeking to get to fit my taste buds.

My family really enjoyed this rice. This was my first attempt to make fried rice and it turned out great and I thought it was quite simple to make! I put the extra (1/2 cup) of soy sauce in it which made it come out darker and not quite as pretty but it was so yummy!!! I look forward to making this recipe again!!
DH & I loved it.  My 6 yr old ate it after I suggested mixing Ranch dressing in it.  My 3 yr old nibbled.  Guess we'll just make it for us and fix something else for them - which we rarely do.

Great easy recipe!  i only had fresh broccoli, carrots and onion and it tasted great!  I used a small amount of butter and soy sauce and i couldn't believe how tasty is came out.  Thank you for sharing your recipe!!
Tonya

Wonderful recipe.  I added chopped up peppers and 1/2 bag of frozen mixed veggies.  2 breasts of chicken so I increased soy sauce more.  Next time, I'll add the chicken before the adding the rice.  Still, even my three year old loved it!  I've made this OVER AND OVER since the first time and love it every time.  Have tried with ham instead of chicken and a variety of veggies.  My favorite is a $1 bag of frozen veggies w/peas and carrots.

loved this recipe!!  i omitted the eggs.  i added garlic, serrano peppers, and green onions.  i used about 1/4 cup soy sauce, but next time i will gradually add to taste. so easy and very yummy!  i will be making this often.  thanks, mona!!
Easy recipe and one that I will use over and over again. Thank you.

Great recipe, THANKS! I used 2 Tbsp olive oil instead of oleo and reduced the soy sauce to about 2TBS or 1/8 cup to just give it a hint of flavor. Wonderful, the family loved it and asked for it at dinnertime 3 days straight! We're going to treasure this recipe! Thanks again.

Loved it! I never have any leftover cold rice when I want to make Fried Rice, so I bought the new Birds Eye Frozen Microwave SteamFresh bag of Long Grain White Rice.  I let it thaw on the counter for about 30 minutes, then added it (some grains were still frozen) to the hot pan.  It worked great!!!  I also added about 1/2 tablespoon of Sesame Seeds right at the end because my favorite Japanese restaurant always adds them to their fried rice and they taste so good in it!  Thanks for the great recipe!!
Was asy to make with ingredients I normally have on hand.And the whole family liked it. Only 4 stars because it did not taste like take- out fried rice, but good none the less.

Very easy and tasty, with ingredients I have on hand too.  My whole family loved it, but it was too oily for us.  Next time (and there will be a next time) I will use a little less and it will be perfect.
Very nice fried rice.  Served it with teriyaki marinated chicken and my Japanese Steakhouse Shrimp Sauce.  Loved it!  Made for Zaar Cookbooks Tag.

YUM!  My husband and I do not like vegetables in our rice, so I added only the eggs to the rice.  I only used about 1/4 cup of butter, since I was only mixing the butter with the rice and eggs.  I will definitely add onions next time, i just didn't have any on hand.  Great rice...I served with bourbon chicken, Recipe #45809.

AWESOME!!! I used 1/2 c of mix veggies(thats what i had on hand)
YUM!!! Thanks for posting :)
Very good!
This was so great!  I actually used some veg-all (gasp!) because we are not exactly vegetable eaters and it was still amazing.  Bravo!!!

This came out good....my husband enjoyed it so that was nice!  I didn't have onion, so just used a little onion powder.  I also cut up celery to put in rice.  I also used a little sesame oil to saute in.  Thanks for posting....I will make again!
This recipe makes great fried rice! I use much less oil, just adding as I need it.

We *really* liked this. My three year old could not stop eating the stuff!  I just added a bit of seasame seed oil for flavor and let out the celery.
I'll be making this again! Thank you for posting!

This is a really nice fried rice recipe. I used frozen mixed vegetables, a splash of seasame oil and cooked diced bacon. I used less butter, about 4 T. and 2(- or +) oz of soy sauce. Turned out great. I served this with jerked chicken and everyone loved it. Thanks for a great recipe. It's a keeper and so easy1

Very good and Very easy! I love to make this the day after we have had pan fried (not breaded) pork chops. I always make sure to have a couple chops left over that I can finely dice and add to the fried rice. I don't use as much butter or soy sauce though and last time realized too late that I didn't have any celery but it still came out great! Thanks for sharing , it has become a family favorite!!!
This really was easy and very tasty also. The whole family enjoyed it. I served it with "bourbon chicken Recipe #45809" and it made for a very satisfying meal. Thanks for the great recipe!

Just what I was hoping to find - I, too have had bad experiences with fried rice in the past.  This turned out quite well, I did cut the butter in half, and then added two Tbsp. olive oil for cooking the eggs. I didn't have any peas or celery, but it still tasted as close as I've ever come to restaurant flavor.  Next time I think I'll use chives at the end, too.  Thanks so much!

Sorry, we were not crazy about this, I used butter instead of oleo, which is a substitute.  I didn't like the taste of the butter in it and I only used 2 Tablespoons, tasted like buttered soy rice, just my opinion.

My family LOVES this recipe! Even my mom, who is very picky, loves this more than any take out Chinese food. The only thing I do different is I add sauteed shrimp. This is diffidently on the regular menu.

Delicious! I had some left-over white rice and I didn't know what to do with it. I followed the directions almost  exactly ( I used butter instead of oleo) . And the rice cooker, set on the warm setting, kept this dish ( made in a pan) warm while the rest of dinner cooked. This recipe goes in the make again book.

EVERYONE loved this recipe.....after I tweaked it a little. But basically it is a really easy dish to make. I used less carrots and celery and only 2 eggs. I put more than 1 cup of frozen peas, probably 2 cups, we love peas! We had about 3 cups of leftover rice that was a week old and it was perfect for this. Added to cookbook.

Made this with Recipe #328562 (Baked Chicken Teriyaki).  I left out the celery since I didn't have any and I substituted butter for the oleo.  This was quite possibly one of the most delicious fried rice recipes I've ever made, and oh so easy!  Was a wonderful compliment to the baked teriyaki chicken.  I will definitely make this again!  Thanks for sharing!

When I first made this recipe, I didn't realize it said 1/2 to 1 CUP oleo, I assumed it was Tablespoons! Well anyways, I only used about 1 Tbsp. canola oil to cook the veggies in to make it low-fat. (Cooking in a non-stick pan so the eggs wouldn't stick.) I also skipped the celery. It was very good and I will probably make this again. The second time I made it with garlic and basil and parmesan.  Frankly, the bread texture and flavor was excellent both times and the bread was still tasty to eat several days later.  

Excellent!

Thoroughly enjoyed this recipe!  Found that I needed to use a bit more flour (probably about 1/2 cup) to be able to work w/ it.  Decided to bake it on a pizza stone, so divided the dough in half, and so the bake time was about 20-22 minutes at 400 degrees.  Will definitely make it again!

i am new to breadmaking and have had some trouble in the past, but this was a definite success! so easy to make and dee-lish! the more garlic the better, and the next time i make this i will even put some in the dough for extra punch. the flavors really intensify with all the olive oil (they sell flavor infused olive oil at the market and i'm thinking of trying that too). this tastes just like authentic italian focaccia. A+++++

This was so perfect and tasted really great! I did use fresh rosemary in place of the dried, and used 5 cloves of garlic, yummy. I think next time I might snip a little sun-dried tomatoes on top even though its perfect just the way it is. Thanks for posting evelyn/athens....

LOVED IT!!  I made it into 6 round loafs and split them for sandwiches.  I also kneaded the garlic and fresh rosemary into the dough instead of on top.  Also I swapped one cup of white flour for whole wheat flour.  They were YUMMY!
Made this bread at least twice already and realized I forgot to review!  I Love this bread.  So EASY and comes out perfect every time!  Very good directions and thank-you for this great bread recipe.
Delicious!!! I converted it to the bread machine and it worked great!

What a great bread.  The texture of the bread was great.  I wanted it a bit thicker so used a baking pan slightly smaller than 15.5x10.5"  I used 1 cup whole wheat bread flour, 1 cup whole wheat flour and the rest all purpose flour.  The dough is easy to work with and the topping was great and added delicious flavor.  Thanks!!
We like focacia. This is a great bread, but next time I would use 1 teaspoon of salt instead of 1/2 teaspoon. Grilled it the second day, still great!

I chose this recipe for my very first attempt at bread making and it was a delicious success. I used about a half cup of parmesan in the dough. I also forgot to sprinkle sea salt, something I won't miss next time. The one thing I would change in this recipe is not to sprinkle garlic over the dough before baking. The garlic burns while the bread cooks and I had to scrape it off the bread to avoid the nasty bitter taste of burnt garlic. Thanks for a wonderful recipe, Evelyn.
OK, I'm hooked. . .  this is really good stuff!   Made meal of this an a salad!  Thanks for sharing

Super delicious bread, made the dough exactly as written but let it rise three times, twice in the bowl once after it was shaped in the pan.  I then cooked it on the BBQ.  I threw a couple of cloves of fresh garlic in the blender with about 1/4 c. of olive oil and some parm. cheese blended it until the garlic was in little pieces then brushed it over the fresh, hot, cooked bread and then sprinkled on more cheese.  It was so good.  Thanks for this great recipe the dough was beautiful and easy to work with.
easy and very yummy

This was my first recipe to try off of Recipezaar.  It was wonderful.  I have made focaccia once before in the past, and it was not good.  This was great!  Very easy, and the texture and taste was wonderful.  My husband and I enjoyed it with a warm cup of soup.  I will keep this recipe on hand to have again.  Thank you!

ONE BOWL!!! No stand mixer or bread machine!!  The chorus is singing "Hallelujah" on this one! The topping possibilities are endless.  I used some garlic olive oil, and some roasted garlic cloves pressed into the dough right before baking, along with the rosemary.  The company I made it for raved!!
Thanks!

Focaccia's exterior was crusty and the interior was chewy. I made mine smaller, 5 loaves to be exact, just so I could vary the toppings. My home smelled so good while the focaccia loaves were baking in the oven. Next time I need to remember that the 3 tbsps of olive oil were of divided use. I made a mistake and poured all 3 tbsps into the dough. 
Thank you for this recipe.

Delicious, especially if you like a slightly salty bread.  Make sure the pan really is well-oiled, I had a little trouble with the bread sticking and will oil the pan more generously next time I make this!

Can't believe that I forgot to review this!!! I made it a long while back and it is SCRUMPTIOUS!! The only bad thing was that the garlic burned a bit, so next time I'll probably just mix into the dough. I used four tablespoons of crushed garlic that comes in a jar and delish! While I was preparing the dough, I mixed the olive oil and garlic and let it sit to kind of meld the flavors. Thanks again for a great recipe!

This is excellent for chicken-mozzarella paninis or just as a snack by itself maybe with some hummus or eggplant dip. A friend made this for a wine-tasting party and I've been hooked ever since. It's easier to put together than you think and it smells wonderful while baking!

Thank you so much Evelyn for sharing this wonderful and easy recipe. Baking bread is my new passion.  So far I'v tried a few recipes and the results were ok, but this one is the winner. I've divided it into three, the 1st section baked at 375 as per recipe. The 2nd I used to make a dozen pizza roll ups with tomato sauce and kalamata olives. The 3rd I used to make a dozen cinnamon rolls, which I baked at 400. From one dough I ended up with a baking feast, needless to say they all tasted fantastic, I particularly like the light texture which this recipe provides with very little effort and time. This will be my favourite dough for now. Thank you again

My family really liked this bread, especially my youngest son, he didn't want to eat anything else but the bread, lol. I haven't had alot of experience using yeast, so i was a little nervous at first, but your instructions were great, i had no trouble making this bread at all, in fact it was pretty easy, i'm deffinitly going to be  making this bread often. The only thing i did a little different, was to mix the olive oil, garlic, and fresh rosemary together, and then rub all over dough, right before baking. Thank you for the recipe evelyn.

Made this last night for dinner party/poker night. Was not as complicated as it seemed to make at all, was really fun actually getting my hands in there.

Made it exactly as the recipe stated, next time at Step 7 I will mix the olive oil and garlic together because it would have been easier then me trying to 'sprinkle' minced garlic over it :-)

AMAZING!!!
This was so good. It was fluffy and good, not completely dense and heavy. I will make this again, it was so easy.

This was so simple - my entire family loved it, including my 12 year old DS.  I loved that you didn't have to knead the dough.  Mine turned out a little 'fluffier' than some of the pictures, but it was perfect for sandwiches.  This may be because I used bread flour instead of all-purpose flour?  I served it with "recipe#220645".  We also ate some plain, as it makes a huge loaf - perfect both ways!  Next time I will put the garlic in the dough, it burned on the top and kept falling off.

This was the perfect focaccia recipe. I added 1 tsp of italian spices (dried basil,oregano & parsley) in with the dry ingredients. I mixed 2 cloves of garlic into the dough after the first rise to prevent the burn other reviewers noted. I also subbed fresh rosemary for the dried. The results were excellent, crispy on the outside soft and chewy inside. I froze the leftovers, which tasted just as good as the fresh when warmed in the oven after thawing.  I can't wait to make this again!

I'm sorry I didn't rate sooner but I must THANK you because this focaccia was AWESOME!!! I used your wonderful focaccia recipe for my French school project, in which I had to make a Monegasque recipe. During my research, I found that they have a type of focaccia called "Fougasse aux herbes". It's a focaccia made with herbes d'Provence so I used your focaccia recipe and tweaked it a bit by adding the needed herbs and eliminating the garlic. The result....GREAT! It was a total hit at my school and people were literally fighting over the bread to get a piece. I had to cut it in very small pieces so I could save some for my family to try out. They also loved it! It was soft, tasty and although I made it the night before the event which was the following day in the afternoon, it was soft and tasted like recently made. I'm truly wordless! Thanks again!!!!!

PS: I forgot to mention that I actually WON 1st place for the 11th grade "category" since it was a "culinary" event at my school there were actually judges (French teachers) who rated your presentation (talking, material, recipe, etc.)! THANKS!!!!!
Excellent recipe! Easiest bread I have ever made.  I took the advice of one of the other reviewers and added 1/2 cup parmesan cheese to the dough.  The sea salt really makes this flavorful!
Absolutely amazing recipe.  I've made this several times and it comes out wonderfully every time.  Everyone in my house loves it.  The perfect belnd of herbs and salt.

Once again, a great recipe from Evelyn!  Very quick and easy to prepare - my family of men LOVED it.  
I know that if evelyn/athens posts a recipe, it will be wonderful!  Thanks for sharing!

What a terrific bread!  I made this the other night to accompany spaghetti and was delighted to see my kids try to stuff the spaghetti into the bread!  Usually nothing gets in between the fork and their mouths when it's spaghetti, LOL!  Preparation was a snap, ingredients are those always on hand in my pantry.  My daughter asked if we can try this focaccia as a pizza base.  I think I want to have it the next time I make my Syrian feast.  Great recipe!  Thanks so much for sharing it!
good, but it did not rock my world or remind me of focaccia the way I have always had it in Italian bakeries.  thanks though.

This is the perfect bread! Very easy. I've increased the garlic from the first time I made this we are up to 4 cloves now! I minced the garlic and I add it to the olive oil and let it sit while I make the bread. Thanks for sharing evelyn. ETA: Ive made this bread more times than I can count, its just soo good and easy to make. I had a chance to snap a photo  Now we feel like the lucky ones having this recipe!!

I just finished making this bread, and I really love it. I started simmering sloppy joes (Recipe #15344) earlier today and realized I had no rolls to serve them on. I found this foccacia recipe to quickly make some good rolls. One tip: I had a packet of Good Seasonings Garlic & Herb salad dressing mix on hand. I stirred this in to the warm water and yeast instead of the sugar (the first ingredient in this packet is sugar, so my yeast still had lots of good stuff to eat). I shaped the dough into flat rolls, topped with just oil and sea salt. Really great!

Loved this bread. It was a huge hit at dinner despite the fact that I'd left out the salt!
Will make this again and again. I cut up what was left over from the meal into generous chunks and froze them. I now just pull out a piece and pop it in the microwave for a minute whenever I need something tasty to go with a stews or just to eat on it's own. Yummm

This was excellent! I had focaccia at a restaurant a few weeks ago, and wanted to try making it. The was so much better than what i bought! I will never buy it again! I just made a half batch and put it in a circle cake pan. I also used an mixture of italian herbs, instead of just rosemary. It turned out golden with a perfect fluffy center. 
Thank you!
This is delicious. I made the dough in my bread machine and that worked like a charm. Made for ZWT4's trip to Italy!

Prep was really simple and easy to follow. Made the dough in our KitchenAid. Mine turned out more like a loaf than some of the other pictures but the flavor was still wonderful. Thank you very much for sharing this recipe. ~Buddha

Love this recipe - very easy to make and tastes great!  Dimpi mentioned that the garlic burns in the oven, so in order to avoid that, I sliced the garlic cloves into the olive oil and heated it for a few minutes, then drizzled the dough with the oil before baking - no burned garlic, but we still got the garlicky flavour.  I'll certainly be making this again!

This recipe was amazing! After a depressing streak of bread failures, I didn't trust the dough when it mixed up smooth and elastic right from the start!

I made the dough with my Kitchenaid (using the dough hook), and then let the dough rise per the instructions. I actually rolled the dough flat and cooked it on a pizza stone with fresh mozzarella, basil and plum tomatoes on top. This would make a perfect pizza crust.

AMAZING! Delicious, soft and chewy on the inside. I used 4 cloves garlic, 1 tablespoon dried rosemary, 1 teaspoon sea salt (though I think 1.5 would have been perfect), only drizzled 4 teaspoons oil onto the loaf (2T really would have been too much), and baked in a 9x13. The loaf was perfect! Fantastic recipe, a definite keeper and crowd pleaser.

Evelyn/Athens, thank you so much for this focaccia recipe. I am good at making bread but I could never make focaccia , they always come out densed and hard. But your recipe is perfect. The crust is crispy and the crumb is light, chewy and tender. I could eat the whole pan myself. The dough is a dream to work with too. Note: I think if you spread the dough out thinner, it would make a wonderful pizza crust. Also,  I would not put the garlic on top because it is bitter when it is burned.  I will try  the garlic inside the dough or sprinkle it on the last 15 minutes of baking the next time. Keeper  Recipe!!!

I love trying new bread recipes, and this was a fairly good one.  The only thing I didn't like was the flavor - even though it had a perfect, fluffy texture, the taste seemed a bit bland.  I will make it again with more rosemary, kosher salt, and perhaps additional herbs.  :)  Also will add the garlic later during cook time - it got bitter when it burned a bit from being on top.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Delicious! I made this once years ago and never got a chance to review it. I finally made it again with dinner tonight and boy was it amazing! I put on lots of garlic for the last 15 minutes of cooking so it wouldn't burn. SO good. Thank you for a great recipe!

Very good focaccia recipe. I took the advice of some of the other reviewers and didn't add the garlic to the top because I didn't want to deal with burning.
I used the dough cycle of my bread machine for the majority of this and then finished it up by cooking it in the oven. My bread was done in less than 30 minutes.
FABULOUS!!! I have made this twice and it was excellent both times. Served with chicken ceasar salad and then another time at a girls lunch with chicken salad. THANK YOU for the recipe!

We enjoyed this recipe and I"m looking forward to trying it again.  Next time, I think I might try mixing some rosemary and garlic into the dough rather than just sprinkling it on top.  Thanks for sharing!!!

This was my first attempt at making a yeast bread..It was a very good recipe and made my whole place smell like rosemary & garlic! I did not use as much flour as the recipe called for..more like 3 cups. I also folded in the salt, rosemary and garlic before the 2nd rise. I was afraid the garlic would burn. It turned out really great! I will def. make again!
We make lots of bread and this is still one of our favorites!

Delicious!!!  I topped mine with garlic, onions, kosher salt and parsley.  The garlic did burn, so next time I'll have to add it to the top with less cooking time left.  I picked it off and compensated with garlic powder and it was still out of this world good!  Next time I want to try some sliced tomatoes on top as well!
I have made many focaccia breads, but this one is over the top.  It is now in my regular bread rotation.  Thanks for posting.

Don't wonder if you see that this recipe got so many wonderful reviews!
This is the best focaccia I ever prepared.
Thanks a lot Evelyn for posting such great recipes.
You are always a star and you will get more and more stars!

We followed recipe, & it came out way too thick for focaccia and lacked flavor. Was more like white bread. Nothing like focaccia in Italy. At the end, I thought it was ok but husband and son (bread-a-holics) didn't like it at all.

Almost perfect - it could stand a little more salt.  I might double the amount next time I make this.  Otherwise, the texture and consistency were just what I'd hoped for.  Thanks for the great recipe, I think it's my new go-to focaccia!

I have made this bread countless times since I ound the recipe and absolutely love it. All my friends have taken a copy of the recipe and my chef son uses it too. Thanks you Evelyn for sharing it with us.
What an easy and delicious recipe!  The focaccia was so light and flavorful!  Thank you for sharing!

Have been making this one for years, and have passed on to several others - including those who said they can't make bread....  can also be cut into squares for dipping into seasoned olive oil and vinegar for an appetizer. Sure to impress !  Love Evelyn and have followed her for years.
This is a wonderful Focaccia recipe! Easy and delicious! A favorite at home and at parties!
This was yummy and very easy. Took longer than I expected, though - a little over 3 hours start to finish. Made for Fall Bake Along Challenge #1 2013.
I finally made this - much better than any we have purchased and was fairly easy to make.  Thanks for the great recipe.

I made a half-recipe, and baked it in a quarter-sheet pan.  Delicious!  I mixed the minced garlic into the dough. I mixed the rosemary with a little oil, and scattered it over the dough after dimpling it, also sprinkled it with grated parmesan.  The top browned nicely, but I had to flip it over and broil the bottom to get it brown and crispy.  It was done in about 20 minutes.  Tasted  great with our spaghetti dinner!  Will definitely make this again.
Great recipe,lovely flavours & easy to follow. The family loved it they didn't even let it cool down a little ate in straight out the oven! Thanks!
So easy! Everyone raves when I make it.  I just let the dough rise in the baking sheet with a little extra olive oil in the pan! You can cut the pieces small and use them as croutons.
I am sorry to say, but I was very disappointed with this recipe. It was too chewy and not Focaccia like in texture at all

As one reviewer suggested, I tried this as a pizza dough (without the rosemary & garlic) and it's fantastic: crispy/chewy and easy to roll out, which is just the way we like it. Thanks Evelyn for yet another great recipe.

Not a bad recipe at all. I accidentally used bread flour because i wasn't paying enough attention when shopping! Will be making again very soon but shall add some more salt i think as it was quite bland.

The first time I made this it stuck terribly to my pan, even with a generous amount of olive oil, but the part I was able to eat was so yummy, I've made it two more times. Parchment paper made all the difference. I heated my olive oil, garlic, and rosemary and a bit of salt in the microwave oven, and brushed the infused oil on top, but avoided placing the bits of garlic, for fear of burning them into bitter bits. I added additional olive oil to the garlic I left off and used it for dipping. I've added caramelized onions to the top after it baked once and that was so good! Love this recipe! Thank you!
This was wonderful.  I loved them!!!! I will make these very often.
Great & easy way to use up over ripe bananas! Kids loved it (so did I)! :)

This is the new favorite salad at our house, and so easy to make.  I was skeptical about a salad with raw kale, as I've only ever considered kale a cooked green.  The combination of the lemon juice, sweel mangos, and pepitas makes for a great salad.  The kale holds up well without wilting and can even be served the next day (if there's any left).  We've gone from a household that never had kale and mangos on hand, to eating this salad at least twice a week.

This is definitely a "keeper" recipe; however, we use cleaned and spun drained bagged baby spinach instead of kale and we don't go through the whole trimming process. Without reservation, I offer a 5 star rating!
I made it as is and it was GREAT!!
looks great.i'll  try it.

The flavors in this dish are wonderful- the mix of mango, greens, and pumpkin seeds with the dressing. I will definitely be making this again. I think I might wilt the kale next time by blanching or in a saute pan to tenderize it just a bit. Then cool it back down. It is a little bit tougher to chew than your typical salad and I LOVE my kale done that way. But otherwise the flavors were fantastic. [Made for Zaar Cookbook Tag]

This salad is amazing! I used the black kale, squeezed a half lemon,sea salt and evoo over; massaged it for 2 min. and added the mango and lots of honey and freshly ground pepper. That's it! Unbelievable how good this is!!!

Update: The next morning for breakfast I toasted bread, used a little mayo, sprinkled it with chipotle pwdr and lawry's seasoning salt, heated up and added a morning star sausage pattie and put on top a nice dollop of the salad on top....SO SCRUMPTIOUS! and healthy :)

May '12 I too saw Aarti makes this recipe and have wanted to make it ever since its debut.
I used baby kale (no need to massage it), fresh pineapple and toasted almond slices.
It was very good and the dressing is perfect with the sweetness of the fruit. UPDATE: Aug. '12 I used regular kale this time & mango as suggested. The kale is best when cut into thin ribbons. WOW, this is amazing! I didn't use the pepitas, so feel free to omit, it's still yummy. So good and perfect with chicken dishes.

This was my first time eating Kale and based on this recipe it is going to be a long and happy relationship.
I don't know if what I had was baby kale or not but I massaged it anyway. I do enjoy a 'hands on' approach. :) I used pineapple and pepitas as that is what I had on hand and was really happy with the results. I'm thrilled to have such a healthy salad in my repertoire. I asked DH what he thought and he said 'pretty good'. I almost fell on the floor as there are very few greens he likes. That alone would be worth the 5 stars.
Thanks so much for posting a recipe we will enjoy again and again!

This is a fantastic salad.  I did not change any ingredients, but I had read somewhere to massage it 5-6 minutes--so I did that.  My kale was not young, so I was a little worried about it.  Delicious!
This was awesome!  I didn't have pepitas but I can image it would add a great crunch.  My new favorite salad.
Fantastic!! Super easy and delicious. I also added thinly sliced fennel to my version but otherwise prepared as directed. Will definitely make this again.
I love  this healthy salad!!  This turns bitter raw kale into something I look forward to snacking on!  Turned me into loving pepitas as well :)

Kale is one of my go to greens these days for it's healthful benefits. I use it in salads, but not as one. Massaging it does break it down and is more palatable. I think my lemon was a tad big, as I found the dressing to be a tad tart, so next time I will cut back a bit. Took it to a potluck and everyone enjoyed it. :)
This won over a dinner party of 6 people. Everyone loved it! This was super-easy (I omitted the pepitas and seeds as we didn't have them) and I will definitely make again! Thanks!

I made this last night and was pleasantly surprised. I typically am not attracted to fruit in my salad and wasn't sure about the honey as part of the dressing. The result was delicious! Not too sweet and different than the usual salad line-up.

I did make a few adjustments: I massaged the kale with the juice of one whole lemon and added an extra half later with the dressing. I used two ripe peaches as my fruit and I added cooked quinoa to give it some more bite and variation. Give it a try!

I decided to make this for my daughter after dinner one night as a healthy snack/dessert.  She loved it!  She also had it again the day after with her breakfast.  I think I might try some over a bowl of corn flakes!  Delicious!

This turned out to be a great late night snack for me.  Without the ice, this is much lighter than a smoothie yet rich and filling.  I ended up sprinkling a bit of cardamom in which really enhanced the banana flavor and added to its Asian flavor.  Looking forward to pouring a bit onto my oatmeal tomorrow morning.
I made this just as posted and thought it was great! My kids have been asking for more all day! I love kid snacks that don't need sugar. This is a good one, thanks!

This was a real delight.  As a kid I often liked to drink milk with a banana anyway.  I used 3/4 cup low-fat milk and added 6 ice cubes.  Incredibly healthy snack or dessert, and I can see it would be just perfect on top of cereal.  I can see adding cardamom, cinnamon or nutmeg too, and maybe a little sugar or artificial sweetener according to preference.

Amis, thanks so much for posting this little gem of a recipe.  I used to make this a lot and drink it before racing out the door in the morning.  You’ve reminded me to make it again!  Amazing how easily recipes can drop out of your routine and thereby out of your life!  I make mine with soy milk and add about ½ tablespoon of wheatgerm, which adds a little texture and heaps more nutrition!  I find I really don’t need the vanilla at all.  A nice touch, but I don’t need it.  Here’s me being heroic in the name of ‘healthiness’ and it’s probably not even bad for you!  Great starter drink and it would taste wonderful on cereal!
This was so yummy! I love bananas, so I had to try this one and I thought it was so tasty. I poured it on granola and Oh MY!!! delicous!

YEAH! A 'smoothie' that is low cal and low fat and healthy and TASTES GOOD! 

Thankx Amis

I'm am not a huge fan of bananas, but this was great. Like Toni, I made this for a late night snack....but I didn't have any left over for my cereal, because I just drank it right down.  I think I will have another one today!
I did add ice cubes. It was light and good. Had it for a quick breakfast!Was on the thin side I do like my drinks a bit thicker! I`m sure this would be great over hot or cold cereal!

This is perfect.  My doc keeps telling me to drink DAIRY to lose weight (soy milk smoothies don't count apparently) and accordingto the new food pyramid we're supposed to consume more fruits & veggies.  Mission accomoplished with this recipe & there's VANILLA in it, too!!  MmmmMMM.
Sorry, this just wasn’t my thing.
This was kind of dissapointing, would be better with sugar added, just personal preference. The texture is not really what I thought it would be..Kittencal
First of all this is a great snack and for my breakfast this went really well with Oatmeal Crisp-Vanilla Yogurt!

I first had "banana juice" in the Dominican Republic and have been looking for something similar ever since.  This is pretty close!  I made it with two bananas and one cup of milk to make it a little thicker.  I bet it would be good with chocolate syrup added or with ice cream instead of milk, too.  Thanks for posting.

This always reminds me of a snack my mom would make for me growing up.  I always blend mine w/ milk, and omit the vanilla (personal preference).  Every time I buy bananas I have to make this.  Thanks for sharing!

I loved this!  I just finished my glass, and it was wonderful!  I was low on regular milk, so I used 1/2 cup vanilla soy milk (so I didn't need to add any extra vanilla), and then the other 1/2 regular milk.  My banana was huge, so it made the drink rather thick which I really enjoyed.  My mom had a sip, and her reaction was "what? only banana and milk? tastes so nice!"  I have no excuse not to grab a quick breakfast from now on!

I run a dayhome and almost everyday the same kid shows up with a bottle of store bought banana milk so today I thought I would make this for him, real banana for a change....the kid didnt like it and wouldnt drink it.  But we arent going to count him at all because the other three kids were screaming for more, 6 banana's later they were satified but they are asking for it for breakfast tomorrow, out to the store tonight.  Thanks for something healthy, real and tastly...gonna go pour that other "stuff" down the sink.

Made this to go with our lazy Saturday brunch today. Pretty good stuff! I like how it's an easy way to get some fruit in my kids' diet. They drank it okay, although I wouldn't say it's a fast favorite or anything. Neat idea though and we enjoyed it.
Well, the nearly-two-year-old just pounded this down. What an easy, healthy snack! Thank you for the wonderful idea!  PS - This doesn't serve well in a sippy cup.  The banana seeds clog it up!
This was very good with my corn flakes. My little girl liked drinking it as well. Thank you for the recipe.

I made this exactly as posted with skim milk, a very ripe banana and the vanilla. It was sweet and tasty. I think I will try it with either ice next time or a frozen banana but it was great just the way it's posted. thanks for sharing a delightful treat.

My 9 yr old daughter thinks this is awsome.  She definely whats me to make it again.  Perfect way to get a little extra fruit into a childs diet.  Super simple to throw together with a magic bullet blender.

Excellent! I omitted the vanilla, used soymilk, six cubes of ice and a tablespoon of flaxmeal to make this delicious drink. I shared with my toddler, and he loved it! The ice thickened the banana milk and moved it into smoothie staus. This is now in regular rotation at our house. My toddler can't get enough of it!
My husband loved this Banana Milk, so did I. It was fresh and refreshing. I just added a little honey to it.

Good stuff! Rather stupid for anyone to be disappointed with the flavor or texture. It's called MILK, it's going to be runny/watery so don't expect it to be thick like a smoothie. And use RIPE bananas (brown/spotted bananas) for full flavor. There really is no need for vanilla or honey or sugar. It's great as is!
i've made this with just the milk and banana many times and it's so surprising how delicious and simple it is!!! excellent snack, desert, or as part of a breakfast.
A nice light drink that I enjoyed for an afternoon snack.  I used skim milk and didn't add the vanilla (personal preference).  I also added a little bit of honey as I wanted it to be sweeter.

I was looking around Youtube and came across a Korean Banana Milk commercial. I looked up "Banana Milk" and this page came up so I decided to try it and I LOVED it. This along with frozen banana ice cream is my current favorite snack. :) If you love bananas, you'll love banana milk.

I made this as written and then we sampled it. Although we thought it was good as written, we decided to add some coconut extract and some ice cubes (since it is scorching hot today) and it was a really nice and refreshing drink. The kids enjoyed it very much. Thx Amis!

Yum! I froze the banana after chopping it up so the drink would be cold without having to put ice in it. I can see this being great in cereal, I drank it as a side to some peanut butter oatmeal granola bars I'd made. Perfect complement!

This is good, DD (toddler) likes it also. I used spring water and a halal vanilla paste from the health food store in a lesser amount as I find it stronger. I do prefer this without the vanilla although that is the reason I tried this recipe. I always make banana milk with a bit more banana per preference to 1 cup water.

I just made it and it took few minutes. Soooo delicious! Good idea adding vanilla. I also like that this drink is somewhat filling, with banana and milk. It would be a great drink for growing kids. I'll be making this again all the time. Healthy and delicious!
Very easy, and great.
Definitely new, definitely sweet- my kids liked it! So sweet and healthy and great for a homeschooling project. Tasted yummy- Added cinnamon sugar and honey as a dessert drink.

I just made this and it's delicious!
I used almond milk (It's all I had - plus I feel like the bit of nutty flavor lends well to the banana) and I used a frozen banana I had.

Perfect use for frozen bananas (I can never seem to use them fresh quick enough), I would also imagine it would be a good hangover cure with a bit of honey ;)

This recipe was wonderful. I like the fact that it doesn't add extra sugar, because the banana's natural sugars sweeten the drink perfectly. I also like the hint of vanilla in the drink. It doesn't overpower the banana taste, which is something that I definitely was afraid of. I'll definitely be making this when I have extra bananas lying around.
I made this for breakfast and it was delicious!
When I had this it reminded me of New Orleans.  Can't wait to have it again

I liked the entire recipe! I am sorry that you submitted 2 servings though. The rules state to submit 4 servings. I used the entire tomato. I like the seeds. I know it looks better without but it was a wonderful sauce with them also. I used minced garlic in a jar. My favorite breakfast is hash browns and eggs and....that wonderful sauce and shrimp just improves the meal.

This was such a satisfying lunch (the meal I made it for).  The sauce is perfection and tasted great with the egg and hash browns.  The instructions were very clear and well-written.  Thanks for a tasty meal.

I couldn't believe how fabulous this recipe was, especially when you consider how few ingredients went into it! This was my first time eating a dish like this before (with the egg on top). It definitely was like something out of a restaurant. Thanks Paula, for broadening my culinary horizons!
Roxygirl

We loved this!  The combination of flavors was wonderful.  I generously added hot sauce, and we loved the kick it gave the dish.  It was colorful and appealing to the eye, and the textural contrast between the crispy potato and the soft egg was delightful.  Thanks for sharing!

This was very good pie.  The cheesecake and pumpkin flavors went very well together.  I made this for Thanksgiving in place of a traditional pumpkin pie, and they went quick.  My only suggestion is to add a little more cinnamon and flavoring, and perhaps sugar, to the pumpkin mixture.  It needs just a little, tiny bit of oomph.

This is my most favorite pumpkin pie.  It is a tradition in my house that my dad and I make this together every year the day before Thanksgiving.  
Just a note about the directions - I always mix the milk and the pudding together and then add the pumpkin and spices.  I have found that this makes sure the pudding is completely mixed together.

I was going to post this recipe, but I see someone has long since beaten me to it!  :)  This is my favorite pumpkin pie recipe (the traditional pie gets tiring). I've made at least one at Thanksgiving for the last several years. I like to use French vanilla pudding in mine, and have tried the cheesecake pudding once, but didn't like it as well. The French vanilla gives the pumpkin mixture an even richer taste.  And no baking involved (you're busy enough with everything else).   You will definitely enjoy this recipe.!  :)

This is THE BEST pumpkin pie!!  I've been using this recipe for years and much prefer it to the regular pumpkin pie.  Like Elmolvsu said though I also mix the milk and pudding together first to make sure the pudding is mixed well.  Great recipe!!

YUMMMY! I used the french vanilla pudding as suggested and subsituted low fat milk, cool whip and cream cheese- noone seemed to notice and my guests loved it.  I omitted the ginger and added some pumpkin pie spice and nutmeg instead, thanks for a great pumkin pie, I'll be making this again.

This pie is fabulous. The blend of spices was absolutely perfect.  I made this as "healthy" as I could by substituting 2 sugar free vanilla puddings, Neufchatel cheese, fat free whipped topping, Splenda, and low-fat milk. I even found a "low-carb" graham cracker crust.  It set up perfectly and was almost guilt free!  Thank you for posting.

Delicious! I've been wanting to try this recipe for quite some time now and I'm so glad I did. What a yummy, creamy dessert! I used pumpkin pie spice instead of the spices listed but besides that I followed the recipe exactly. This is a very rich pie, sure to compliment your Thanksgiving meal. Thanks for sharing this delicious recipe!
Kristen

I came on to post this recipe, but will review it instead.  :)  I make this every holiday season and it is always a favorite.  I am always surprised at how good it tastes each year!  The cream cheese layer just makes the pie.

This was some pretty awesome pie and so easy to make!  I was surprised at how high the pumpkin layer was...you could probably half that part and get away with it, but why would you?...it's soooo tasty! I used French Vanilla Cool Whip, otherwise, followed recipe exact.  I used a whisk for all mixing, but a hand mixer may have been a bit easier and quicker.  I tried to eat some before it chilled for the full 4 hours and it was a little soft, so I would suggest waiting...it's worth it!  Thanks for sharing this recipe...I'll be making it again and again.
This was a hugh hit at our Thanksgiving.  I love the cream cheese and pumpkin combination.  No need for the extra cool whip.  Thanks for posting.

I made this for a Thanksgiving dinner I went to and, 3 days later, I made it AGAIN (and I'll probably make it for Christmas dinner too).  This was a very easy recipe to make.  I made it as written except I forgot to take the whipped cream topping to the dinner so we had the low cal version (tee hee).  This was a delicious ending to our holiday meal!  Thank you for sharing this recipe!!!
This is now the "must have" pumpkin pie at our house. It is easy, has no exotic ingredients, and it looks like you slaved over it. Thanks!

This is our favorite Pumpkin Pie! I had misplaced my recipe and was glad to find that you had posted it here.  We have this every year at Thanksgiving and Christmas. The pie is easy to make and looks like you put a lot more effort in to it than you actually do to make it.  Just the right blend of flavors.  The pudding mix in the pumpkin makes it "set up" to a nice custard consistency and adding the cream cheese to the cool whip thickens it enough so that it supports the pumpkin layer and tastes GREAT !!!
Made this for Thankgiving and it was a HUGE hit!  Everyone loved it and we'll be making another for Christmas!

Oh boy, what a treat! It dosen't get any better than this if you are a pumpkin lover like myself! I doubled the cream cheese layer but I don't know why I even bothered. The pumpkin mousse layer is what makes this pie so dreamy! I had admired this recipe for years in magazines during the holiday season and I have no idea why I waited so long to make it! I could eat the top layer by itself by the bowlfuls! Thanks Sackville Girl! Awesome recipe! BTW, I'm thinking that this pie in frozen state would be awesome for summertime!
i love pumpkin pie anyway and this just made it better.  thanks so much for posting it, it gave me an idea for thanksgiving.

Yummy Yummy! My step son loves pumpkin pie and cheesecake. What a great way to have both!! I made 2 of these... didn't have any left. But we did have regular pumpking left. I sent it home with SIL. I have since made 2 more and they are gone. Time to make another. This is so easy and the best part is NO BAKING!! THank You!!

My family loved this pie.  It is very easy to make and went together very quickly (my kind of recipe).  It is a nice change from the "traditional" pumpkin pie.  I will definitely be making this one again.  Thank you for posting this recipe.  It is a keeper!!

Great Recipe! I love how easy this pie comes together. The cream cheese in the whipped cream really gives a nice subtle cheesecake cake taste to the pie. I could not get the cream cheese to become smooth, so the whipped cream layer had visible cream cheese specks. It did not hamper the taste of the pie at all. Very creamy. Not as spicy as traditional pumpkin pie and has a much creamier texture - so people  who are not fans of traditional pumpkin pie would love this recipe. Thanks Sackville!
Great easy recipe to add to the Thanksgiving table!  Thanks for the recipe!

Everyone loved this and fought over taking home the leftovers! Pretty sweet so doesn't need much extra Cool Whip on top. Very easy and super good recipe.
Thanks!

This is so yummy. I could eat a million infinity five hundred and could eat the whole pie twice a day! I measured everything. I whisked(electric whisk)it(the cool whip mixture) and put it in the pie shell all by myself. I wisked the pumpkin part too but had help putting it on the white creamy part. Thank you Chef! UPDATE: I made this for my family for Thanksgiving and used fresh pumpkin - it did not hold together well.... and I will stick with the can next time.... still yummy!

I love watching my 4 year old son in the kitchen and he just loves this pie and is so proud each time he makes it. I do not like pumpkin pies because of all the spices and I really like this recipe because the spices are not so strong. We had this for Thanksgiving 2006.

I gave this 5 stars. I got the recipe from Kraft and it was a hit last thanksgiving. I wanted to make something different then plain old pumpkin pie and everyone loved it. Very yummy and easy. Thanks for posting christine (internetnut)

This was a big hit at our holiday party.  Even the people who don't like pumpkin enjoyed this thoroughly.  It was easy to make and a welcome twist on the traditional pumpkin pie.  I was out of cloves but it didn't adversely impact the flavor of the pie.

Very good pie.  I baked my own crust using 1 cup graham crackers, 1/2 cup pecans, 3 tbsp white sugar, 1/2 tsp cinnammon, 1/4 cup butter and a pinch pumpkin spice. Placed it in the oven at 350 for 8 mins and let it cool. Also, followed the advice of others and mixed the pudding with the milk first, then added the pumpkin and spices.  To the pumpkin layer, I did add another pinch of pumpkin spice. Thank you loads for the posting. I will be making it again.
Sounds delicious. I love my pumpkin pie at the holidays. This is a nice twist. Will make it for Thanksgiving. Thanks!

Ridiculously Easy to make! My DH said it was definitely "excellent". I used a Nilla wafer pie crust and it was really tasty. For sure let it set for at least 4 hours - I thought 1 hour would be fine but it was just too soft to cut and serve. Will certainly be making this again!
This is DH's absolute FAVORITE! I also use the French vanilla pudding and it makes it so much more Yummy! I make it every Thanksgiving! Thank you people at Kraft.

Well yum!  We did a little pre-Thanksgiving test tonight and it was a hit.  DH is the big pumpkin pie lover around here and he hasn't tried it yet, but the kids and I loved it.  I'll probably still do the traditional pumpkin pie for Thursday but I'm making another one of these too.

This was sooo good. I made my own graham cracker crust as I like it very moist and sweet. Also, I thought that I had ground ginger, but didn't, so I added 1/2 t of pumpkin pie spice. The taste was pumpkin pie..but more subtle. Thanks so much for a great recipe!

Great Pie everyone loved it. Very easy to make. I did make Tigerlilly #2 crust with the graham crackers and Pecans. WOW. Used French Vanilla pudding and mixed the pudding first then the pumpkin and increased the spices a little.(personal preference) This is a keeper. Will make again.

I made this last night to take to our friends' house for dinner.  I wasn't able to let it chill the entire 4 hours, so it wasn't completely set (my fault!), but despite that it got rave reviews!!  The spices give it a real kick and several people commented that they really liked that.  It has a lighter texture than pumpkin pie and the cream cheese and graham cracker crust added make a yummy combination!  Also, it was simple enough that my 3 year old could help and was very easy to mix up.  Thank you so much!!  We'll make this again!
Saw this in Kraft too. I made it for Christmas and everyone liked it, tasted just like a baked pie! Yummy!

I made this for my family about 15 years ago for Thanksgiving dinner.  I have had to make it every year since them, the entire family loves this pumpkin pie and it is so very easy to make.  I have to make a minimum of 5 every year now !!  You will love it !!
Clearly this is perfection. I've made this for the past few years and now have my whole office using it. It's flawless!
This is awesome, I made it once and everyone just loved it!

The best! We are not traditional pumpkin pie eaters in my house. However, this one always goes qucikly! I needed to find the recipe for this year(Thanksgving Morning...LOL) and sure enough it was here on Zaar. Thanks!
What a wonderful quick and easy pie to make.  The only change I will make next time is to cut the cloves back by half ( just a personal preferance).  Comes together quick and is so tasty.

Wanted to share this but way too late! I have shared this recipe with family and friends over the years. I have to make it every year for Thanksgiving, or i'm not invited! Even people who don't like pumpkin pie will love this!
Wonderful! My daughter's first pumpkin pie and we all loved it. Thank you for this recipe!
This was really easy and fun to put together. This made a nice weeknight dessert that we will definately be making again! Thanks for posting!
Yum!!

I am a pumpkin pie fanatic so I was very excited to try this recipe!  This was pretty good.  I thought it was a nice change, next time I may use a little less clove.  Thanks :)

This pie was okay, I was a little disappointed.  It didn't set up that great and had a bit too much spice.  There was alot of filling leftover so I made a tiny pie with homemade crust.  I think with a few changes I will still make again.
As far as double layer pumpkin pies, this is a good recipe, but for me it just tastes too "instant" I guess that is the best way to explain it.
my family loved it. i will make it again!!!!! thanks for the recipe!

This pie was delicious! While it is an "instant" pie so to speak, it certainly didn't taste like one. The only change I would make is in the directions - use a fork, not a whisk. Too hard to get the good stuff out of the whisk, LOL! Don't change a thing, the pie is perfect just as written.

I do not like regular pumpkin pie. This one I love! The extras in the double layer part just as a different taste which makes this perfect. When I bring this recipe to a carry-in, it always disappears.

My mom has made these since I was little. They are the dessert of choice every Thanksgiving, they have all but replaced traditional pumpkin pie. It has a sort of cheesecake-y flavor. My mom has always used pumpkin pie spice instead of the spices listed- using each individual spice overpowers the other flavors. This year I am making 2 of these, and we have always used generic ingredients, unless name-brand is on sale for cheaper. Give it a try, chances are your family will love this pie too!
A family favorite! We have been making this for years!

I made this pie today for the first time and overall it was good, though I will try to improve the pumpkin layer next time... maybe with a different flavor of pudding mix to start with.  My can of pumpkin seemed really 'wet', making the filling very soft.  I was able to slice it though not as neatly as I would have liked.
