I'd like to share this on our Facebook Page, Pumpkin Hill, East Berlin, if there is a share. It's delicious

This is a luscious salad, so easy to make, so pretty on the plate. I can't thank you enough for this, Dancer^! Just my style--nice and easy.  I did leave the peel on the apples and used sliced boneless pork loin.  DH and DS loved them.  Thanks for posting.

Delicious! I made these a few months ago and forgot to post a review. "When your memory goes, forget it." Sorry about that. I browned the chops Ghee (it has a very high smoke point) in a cast iron skillet. I removed them and kept them warm as I did steps 6 through 10 in the same skillet. I'm always looking for recipes my kids will eat and this one is definitely high on their list!  They loved the apples and they've always liked pork chops.  I'll definitely make this one again.

For some reason my previous review is not showing up, so I am resubmitting.  These pork chops were so moist and tender you could cut them with a fork.  My husband loved them.  I didn't care for the apples.
This was a very tender and tasty recipe. I enjoyed the sweetness of the apples cooked under them also. I used Granny Smith apples  and did not peel them. Thanks for another good recipe.

My kids were a bit skeptical about the apples combined with the pork at first, but after one tentative bite they ended up cleaning their plates. ;) It was simple to prepare and very moist and tender; we will be using this recipe again (especially in the fall...such an 'autumn' flavor). Thanks!

This has found it's way into our regular meal rotation.  We all LOVE it (even my super picky 2 year old!)  The chops come out moist and juicy.  Just don't make the mistake of forgetting to cover it while it's baking!

Very, very good! Finally a meal where there were no leftovers; considering I have two picky eaters, THAT is a miracle. I only made a few changes for us.  I used the four pork chops (Omaha Steaks brand), but only two apples and cut the sugar and cinammon in half accordingly.  I also put the apples and cinnamon in the microwave for two minutes on high to pre-cook and soften, then placed the pork chops on top, covered with foil and shortened my cooking time to 40 minutes at 375 degrees.  I forgot to 'spray' coat the pan, but it didn't seem to make a difference; the pork chops didn't stick so clean up was easy.  I served this with mashed potatoes and gravy (turkey gravy package made with leftover porkchop drippings from frying), and frozen mixed peas and carrots.  The whole meal was around an hour prep and cook time to table and serving.  Thanks for a new addition to the family meal planner!

This is a regular meal now in our family. We all love it - and I have a lot of trouble finding things that we all like. I have yet to have it turn out any way other than perfect, which is saying a lot.

One word- WOW!
I had a family pack of pork chops and used half of them to make another recipe that I've already reviewed for dinner last night. This recipe was for dinner tonight. (yes, pork chops two nights in a row).
Anyway, was spooning these into a bowl and decided to take a nibble. OMG!  The nibble ended with the disappearance of an entire pork chop. These tasted absolutely amazing. The meat was so moist and tender. I loved every mouthful and won't change a thing the next time I make this. Thanks!

This recipe was a huge hit in my house.  My grandmother loved the apples and my 7 year old son had more than one.  The meat was so tender when it was served that you didn't need a knife.  The apples give it a great flavor and at to the visual appeal of the dish.I will definately be making this recipe again.

This recipe absolutely deserves five stars.  It was SIMPLE, yet delivered on flavor.  The combination of the savory pork and sweet apples is fantastic.  I halved the recipe with no problems.  I will make this again.  Thank you Ladypit for a keeper.
YUM! My picky 2 year old son gobbled this up! I will add this to my regular winter recipes. Stuffing was a good side dish. It's not just for Thanksgiving!

Yummy! My family loved this meal (no leftovers in sight).  The pork was very tender and, as noted by another reviewer, is easy to cut with a fork.  The baked apples (golden delicious)were wonderful.  The only regret/complaint I had was that I didn't make more!  Thanks for sharing!

This was really tasty! I cut amounts down to 2 chops (boneless, thick cut) and used 1 large Jonagold apple, sliced thin and the peel left on. Baked for just an hour; any longer and the chops would've been way overcooked. Made enough for 3 servings for me, served with Simple Cranberry and Toasted Walnut Stuffing. Made a most excellent meal! Thanks for the recipe ladypit!

Wonderful flavor and very easy!  Hubby and I just wished there were more apples!  Used 2 large granny smith apples, 3 thick cut boneless pork chops (which I salted and peppered before browning)and subbed Splenda brown sugar for regular.  Thanks for the awesome recipe, ladypit!

Outstanding recipe.  I used 5 apples and just eye-balled the brown sugar and cinnamon.  I also fixed a package of stove top dressing and spread that on top before baking.  Smelled delicious and tasted wonderful.  DH said this is a keeper.

Good.  I sliced my apples very thin- next time I'll leave them a little thicker, because they got a little soggy. Verrrry good. I used splenda blend brown sugar and apple pie spice instead of cinnamon, and I only baked it for an hour. I also put the sugar and spices in a baggie and tossed the apples rather than sprinkling the sugar over them - other than that I left everything as is. Hubby and I both give it 5 stars and will definatly make it again. Thanks for posting.

Super bon !

Thanks a lot, we loved your easy recipe.

I really liked this recipe, but my husband thought it was a little odd to mix apples with pork chops. I only ended up baking these for 1/2 an hour and they were done (the chops were bone in). Thanks ladypit for a great fall/winter recipe!
WOW! I made this tonight and it was awesome. My husband said "THIS is what we're having for Thanksgiving!" Thanks!
I recently tried this for my husband and myself and it was excellent.  So easy and so good.
This was a very good homecooked type meal. Loved the apple, cinnamon, brown sugar flavor.

My family loved this recipe!  I used Granny Smith apples and made it pretty much exactly as stated except for using cooking spray to brown chops and a bit more cinnamon because we really love cinnamon.  Served it with brown rice and green beans and enjoyed every single bite.  I can't wait till fall and the fresh apple crop.

This smells HEAVENLY! My kitchen smelled like a holiday feast was all in one pan in my oven! This is SO easy and delicious! I seasoned the pork chops with seasoned salt and ground rosemary before browning in butter flavored nonstick spray. I decided to use 2 apples, and 1 large vidalia onion. I sliced the onion thin and put it on the bottom, then sprinkled it with a little of the brown sugar. I topped it with the thin apple slices and sprinkled them with the remaining brown sugar and all of the cinnamon. Added just a hint of freshly ground nutmeg too. I baked the dish covered with foil at 375 for 45 minutes, and entire dish was melt in your mouth tender. I served with steamed broccoli, corn in butter sauce, and stuffing. This will become a regular in my rotation. Thanks for posting!

Quick and easy to make.   I too only cooked for an hour and the pork chops just fell apart and were very tender.  Topped with the apples was delicious! I put the sugar, cinnamon and cut apples in a bag and shook to coat them which worked well. Definately a recipe to save.

This was wonderful!  I took a box of Pork StoveTop stuffing, prepared it, and spooned it over the pork before covering and baking, and it was delicious.   A quick and easy recipe to prepare -- loved it!

Made this last night and it was terrific!  I only cooked it for 1 hour and that was plenty.  Next time I will caramelize some onions on the stove first and mix them in with the apples.  I would also take the foil off a few minutes early.  Also - be sure to brown the pork chops well.  I also sprinkled them with a little salt and pepper first.  I will definitely be making this again!
These were spectacular! The apples cooked nicely and the pork was oh-so-tender. Thank you for the great recipe!
Really Good!

I needed to make pork chops that were not tough, and boy this fit that bill perfectly.  I cut the recipe to just 2 pork chops, used 3 apples, but should have used 2.  I used a bit more cinnamon than called for, since I really love cinnamon.  We enjoyed it, great fall meal.
So simple and yet so yummy!  I cut it down to serve just 2 of us and used Splenda Brown Sugar and added a bit of nutmeg too.  Delightful!

Very delicious!
I'm not a pork chop fan because they are usually so dry, but this recipe made them quite moist and the cinnamon........mmmmmm the house smelled so good!

Delicious!  My husband raved and we couldn't stop eating!  I used bone-in pork chops and cooked them for about an hour.  Also, I used another reviewer's suggestion and put seasoned salt and rosemary on the pork chops before browning.  The smell in the house was amazing and the pork chops were tender. I thought this was pretty good and my husband thought it was okay.  I will make it again because it is easy and great for me...I'm following Weight Watchers.  I seasoned the chops with salt, pepper & a little garlic powder before browning.  I also subbed less canola oil for the butter.  Thanks for this good weeknight meal!

Good Basic and Easy Recipe... I added a drizzle of maple syrup on the pork chops and some walnuts with the apple and cinnamon...  due to I made  a similar recipe before that called to it, I think the walnut add nicely to it:)

This was good. DH said it was a keeper and by BIL seemed to like it too - his plate was clean! Even my 11 month old liked it. The flavor was fantastic!  This was such an easy dinner.  Followed directions according to recipe.  My pork chops were boneless and thin.  DH is VERRY picky and does not like anything new   He Loved this one.    Thank you for sharing!

The flavors in this dish were excellent!  I forgot to grease the pan but didn't need to due to the juices from the pork & apples. This would also be a good one to try in the crockpot - thanks for such a tasty & simple recipe!

EXCELLENT!! Not only does it taste amazing but my house smells wonderful too (always a bonus!). I added 1/4 cup apple juice at the bottom of the baking dish rather then greasing it. Delish!!  The entire family -all 7 of us- enjoyed this.  Will be making again but cutting down on the cook time to 1 hour.  The chops were a touch dry, that's where those yummy apples are perfect!

Keep the cooking time closer to around 45 minutes. The 1 to 1 1 /2 hours will give you dry, tough chops.

I got mixed responses to this recipe - the girls loved it, the boys hated it. I wanted to address the issue of cooking time, after reading so many reviews that insisted the stated time was wrong, or would ruin the chops. I did cook these less than the stated time, but only because it was late and I was starving. I did brine my chops (I almost always do - 3 T salt in 1 1/2 qt. water for almost an hour), but I am not sure how effective it was this time... my son did it for me and I discovered that the salt didn't all dissolve. I followed the recipe exactly to the point of putting it in the oven. I cooked the dish for 30 min. At that point, the meat temp was 184F, or "overcooked". Usually you would cook pork to 145F and let rest to about 155F. They were not dry and tasted good. That said, there was plenty of liquid and moisture in the covered pan for a proper oven braise, and 1 1/2 hours would have been perfect for that. The texture would be completely different, but tasty. I would like to try that if I made this again (but will likely not given that half my family didn't like it). I used Empire apples, which had a good flavor and moisture content. One of my personal complaints was that I would like to taste some seasoning on the meat. The common complaint from the non-eaters was that the apples tasted more like pork than apple.
I put all kinds of vegies under the chops along with the apples and a slice of lemon on top of the chop. Yummm

This is a keeper! Made only minor changes.
I seasoned my pork chops with sage, onion powder, no salt seasoning and pepper. In place of the sugar I used splenda.
Both the apples and pork were tender enough to cut with a fork and the family raved about it well after dinner. I will be making this again. Thanks for sharing.

Just made this for the first time. Took the advise of others and seasoned chops with garlic salt, pepper and dried rosemary. I used thick boneless pork chops and cooked for the 1 1/2 hours and it was awesome!!! Best pork chops I have ever had and husband loved them too! Served them with cheddar au gratin potatoes and the meal was a hit!

Quite surprised how good this is, given the simplicity of the recipe! I used 3 pork chops but otherwise kept the proportions the same (still used 4 apples, etc). I seasoned my chops with a little pepper, garlic powder, and paprika before browning, and cooked for 1 hour (thick bone-in chops, but fairly small otherwise). I suspect they could have come out of the oven earlier, but they came out beautifully anyway - tender and moist. I used granny smith apples - I thought their natural tartness worked well with the sugar, and they kept their shape fairly well. There was also plenty of liquid in the pan at the end.

This was a great choice for us! All four of us -- I have one child who doesn't care for meat dishes -- really enjoyed it. My pork tenderloins were more than 1" thick and were not fully thawed when placed in the skillet. I sprinkled garlic powder and a little pepper on the pork chops when browning them. They were ready in about 75 minutes. There was plenty of sweet sauce in the pot for dipping the luscious bites of pork chop and apple into. My husband's comment -- "foodgasm." My four-year-old son couldn't eat enough of the apples. I served this with scalloped potatoes (http://southern.food.com/recipe/scalloped-potatoes-85629). They paired well together and made for a meal that will definitely go into regular rotation in our home. Thank you so much for posting the recipe!!

Just made this recipe with apples from my Dad's trees.  Amazing!  I used Smithfield Pork Chops and only 1 tablespoon of butter.  In the oven for an hour and ten minutes.  Even my son ate the chops!  I did use onion powder, garlic powder, and black pepper per some of the other reviews while the chops were in the pan browning.  Will make again!  I have a new favorite!
Loved this recipe and used it on boneless pork ribs, Added rosemary and garlic salt to meat and followed the directions for the rest of the dish (apples). The family couldn't get enough of it!

I have never had pork chops and apples before... but I had some gorgeous apples and some chops so I decided to give it a try. First of all, the aroma of this cooking is to DIE for. I wish I could find a pork chop/baked apple candle. I followed the recipe as directed, except I sprinkled the chops with a dusting of season salt before baking. There were no left-overs and the baking dish was scraped clean. Loved this.

I used bone in Pork Chops about 1 inch thick.  The apples turned to mush and the Pork Chops were soooooooo dry.  I have been cooking for 52 years and should have known that the Pork Chops will cook in 20 minutes in the oven.  The next time I try this recipe, I will slice the apples a lot thicker and check them after 30 minutes to make sure they are done.  I know the Pork Chops will be done.
This recipe is awesome!! Spread the warm apples over the pork chops!! Yum!!!

Wow! What a great recipe. Easy to make and delicious.  I used 1" boneless chops and Fiji apples.  The only change I made is to cut the recipe in half everything else was followed and it was wonderful. This is a keeper.

This worked out really well.  It's just the two of us so I used two Braeburn apples and a few Tbs of brown sugar.  Baked for the full 90 min.  Tender, fall-apart and juicy ¾" bone in chops.  This is my new pork chop recipe and my picky eater husband gives this five stars.  I'm so glad to finally find a recipe which doesn't produce dry and tough pork chops!  It's basically fool proof.

OK. Brined my chops first (1/2 in thick, 4hrs in brine of 2T kosher salt to 2&1/2 C water) then followed the recipe. I used a large cast iron frying pan to fry chops and used the same pan to bake them. Seasoned chops with fresh rosemary, sage, and garlic salt. Thick sliced the apples. Baked 1 hr. Chops were very tender, apples were cooked very soft. All in all, pretty good. Would make again.

Good, but IMO the chops were overcooked--dry and not that tasty.  Maybe I just have a very hot oven, I will try cooking for 30 min. next time, also adding more seasonings as others have mentioned.  The apples were perfect though. :)

I made this with garlic, paprika and a bit of black pepper.  Medium sweetness apples.  Next time I will try macintosh because I love sweet apples and these were just not sweet enough.  Brined the meat in salt water with a cap full of vinegar for 4 hours. Then followed the directions.  Only cooked half an hour using a thin, bone in pork chop at 350 preheated (metal pan with metal lid) and that is the most tender meat ever.  Need to work on the seasonings though, maybe oregano.  Will play around a little but this is a great base recipe!  Had to eat mine with apple sauce to get my sweet on.
It was ok I cooked 8 small boneless pork chops @350 for 45 minutes I seasoned my chop with onion powder garlic powder seasoning salt everything else I followed the recipe it was ok

ok, my husband hates pork chops. really. i make them occasionally because i like them and i need variety. i made these and he actually said "these are good" . you must understand this is a compliment above all measure. great recipe!!!

So delicious. I didn't veer from the recipe except I used my ovenproof skillet to brown my chops then removed them and put the granny smith apple slices right on the cooked butter and pork bits. I then sprinkled the apples with the brown sugar cinnamon mixture reserving about 2 tspns. Placed the pork chops on the apples and sprinkled the remaining sugar mixture on top of the chops. My house smelled heavenly and my husband and I agreed they were the best pork chops we ever had. Yummmmm.

I actually cheated and used prepared apple pie filling with sliced apples not chopped. I put that on top of the pork chops after they were Browned in a cast iron skillet and also used that to bake them.
I would like to try this.Can I use saccerin instead of brown sugar?

This was delicious! I had 2 very thick pork chops that I didn’t want to dry out during cooking. Using the apples and covering with foil provided a (steamed) delicious meal. Will make again. Thank you for the recipe??
Turned out great! So happy I found this recipe. Served with real mashed potatoes and homemade gravy made with some frying pan drippings, beef bouillon, water and milk.
First time making pork....I wanted a fall recipe and this was perfect! Made mashed potatoes on the side.
For anyone on carb restrictions, substitute the brown sugar with Splenda brown sugar or any other brown sugar substitute according to the recommendations.
very good! Will make again and again!!!!
whoops, made this for thanksgiving dinner and everyone loved it. all of my guests demanded the recipe. definitely a winner and a keeper for all holiday.easy to make and delicious!!!!!
This sounds wonderful.  If you feel daring...replace the water with a can of Mountain Dew.  It is great!!!

I made this as a side for my Christmas dinner and it was a hit.  No leftovers to be had.  Later in the evening the kids were looking for some "dumplings" to snack on only to be disappointed.  As a result, I have been ordered to make this recipe again in the very near future!  Thanks for a great recipe.

WOW! I have had my sights set on this recipe for ages and I finally found the time to make it. I know it is classfied as a 'holiday' treat but I could not resist. I was blown away when I tasted the first bite of sugary dough and creamy sweet potatoes. DH said it was one of the best things I have ever made. I can't wait to try it again! I can also see this recipe being good with apples instead of sweet potatoes.
Wow these are awesome and everyone loves them. (even the ones who dont like sweet potatoes) this can be a side dish or a dessert. thanks. Recipe was very easy to follow.

I made this for Thanksgiving for something different. They were delicious but very very sweet.  I would do them again and adjust the sugar in the sauce.  Everyone really enjoyed them, though.  Thanks for a great way to serve a Holiday staple!

I made this for Thanksgiving and got rave reviews from my guests along with several requests for the recipe.  So delicious and sweet it could easily have been used as a dessert.  We had leftovers which were just as delicious reheated.
Very tasty. They were a big hit.The recipe says it's OK for to overlap the dumplings in the pan. I think they would come out crispy on all sides if they were not overlapped.
I've been looking forward to trying this recipe, and I finally got my chance tonight. Let me tell you, these were even BETTER than I was expecting them to be! And so easy too! Wonderful recipe!!!

I was looking for a different way to fix sweet potatoes for Thanksgiving, and came across this recipe.  WOW!  Was it a hit with my family!  I'll do this one again, and won't just save it for the holidays.
Very easy to prepare and yummy. Had for thanksgiving and my son just gobbled them up. Thanks for warning about them floating in the pan.

Guess I'm the odd man out; I always hate to be the first to say a recipe was less than perfect when it already has a bunch of rave reviews, but these could have worked better and dear family didn't complain exactly but they weren't singing this dish's praises either. On the upside they were easy and made very little mess in my kitchen. However, I know I used the right size pan so now I wonder if the biscuits I used were too big (though the recipe does specify to use the big ones and said it was okay if they overlap). I have to disagree about that as the dumplings didn't cook where they overlapped and I had a lot of overlap. I cooked for 25 minutes and then ended up flipping over the ones that were most done and setting them on top so they would cook on the bottom (10 minutes), pulled them out, spread everything else out and cooked for another 15 minutes. I did make one major change: I halved the sugar in the sauce (1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup granulated, 1/4 cup splenda) as some of the other reviews had mentioned this being very sweet and I was afraid it would be overpoweringly so. I'm glad I did as I don't think we could have eaten this at full sweetness; it's almost hard to believe that it's a side dish rather than a dessert. The consensus on the filling was that it was rather blah and tasted like it needed something (didn't see how it would convert any sweet potatoe haters; it's really just sweet potatoes and you can really taste them, certainly didn't change DH's mind). I used 1 can buttermilk  biscuits and 1 can butter flavored, both were good with the sauce cooked in, but the butter flavored was slightly better. I think if we try these again, I would actually forget about the sweet potatoes, fill the dumplings with pumpkin pie filling and serve them with vanilla ice-cream as a dessert. Thanks for posting. It was worth a try and definately has potential.

OH MY GOSH,  these are Awesome!  So easy, little mess and absolutely a hit with the entire family!  I think next time I will half the biscuits and make them smaller.  That is the only thing I would change.

I am a fairly new cook and was looking for something was easy and tasty and found this.  Well I fix them for Sunday dinner, and it was a hit, but my little brother and I agreed that you should add sugar and cinnamon and some vanilla to the can sweet potatoes.  Also next time I may have too bake them at 30 minutes, instead of 45.  My mother kept saying it felt like she was eating dessert during dinner...but the rest of us agree it was good with dinner.

My daughter Kaylee reviewed this since it was made for her special dinner at her request.  "I wish I could give it 10 stars. The cinnamon makes it really sweet and yummy". I did add some cinnamon and butter to the sweet potato mixture.  I used less sugar in the topping.  We actually had this as dessert.  I could not imagine having this as a side dish.

This was so very good! I would split the biscuits next time and make them smaller.I add sugar and cinnamon into the potatoes and instead of water I used the liquid from the drained can of sweet potatoes. At first I was planing on useing them as a side dish, but after sneeking one I held them back for a desert. So So good and my DH says he hates Sweet potatos but he loved these.!
These were the talk Christmas dinner! Everyone raved! Thank you!
It's was delicious! But I didn't mash up the Sweet potatoes. Just cut a piece to fit flatten biscuit. Also added pecans on top! It was a hit!
This is a wonderful recipe!!! I substituted apples for the sweet potatoes. This made a great dessert. I have also used sweet potatoes.

Wow!!! This recipe is absolutely DELICIOUS!!! It's definitely a dessert item but you don't need ice cream with it - you can really be satisfied with the dumpling alone. As far as the amount of sugar goes you just have to adjust to taste like you would any seasoning but that's no reason to ax the recipe entirely. I can't wait to take this to my mom's house and share it with the family tomorrow (Thanksgiving) in addition to putting some on my own table. As soon as I took a bite of the first one I melted. YUM! This really is a WONDERFUL TREAT! Let me say that I used fresh sweet potato, boiled, mashed and added cinnamon and brown sugar then blended until thick but smooth. They were all different sizes and didn't come out looking perfect - I cut some of the biscuits in half because I wanted to play with sizes and see what I liked. I used a glass baking dish that was shallow so when they were done they had a crisp top with a dumpling bottom - I simply flipped them over in the remaining liquid and let them sit and they fell right into place. Delicious!!! Thanks a million!!!
Absolutely wonderful!  Best treat I've had in a while.  I've been thinking about fixing these for a while now.  Boy did I miss out by not fixing them sooner.  Thanks for the lovely lovely treat.
Wonderful, I have made this for my family, inlaws and the kids school functions. Everyone is always begging for the recipe. They can't get enough of it.

Made these for dinner tonight in hopes of making something new for Thanksgiving dinner, They are wonderful, and pretty to boot. Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe. And oh yeah, They made the cut for Thanksgiving Dinner..

I made the recipe in a 9" square pan—I made half the dumplings but did not halve the sauce. They cooked in about 33 minutes. Mine were more crescent-shaped than round, which worked just fine. I took a number of suggestions from other reviewers and it turned out well. I was careful not to overlap the dumplings, used butter-flavored biscuits, halved the sugar in the sauce, substituted as much of the potatoes' packing fluid for water as I had, and added some cinnamon and sugar and vanilla to the filling. I will continue to use all of these tweaks when I make it in the future. My family loved them, but it was suggested that they would work better for breakfast than a dinner side. I think they work fine either way.
This was amazing! Perfect. I omitted the greens peppers.and the seasoning salt. And I served it over wide egg noodles. As always I use low sodium soy sauce. So delicious...

YUM! We enjoyed this recipe. Tips were very tender and the flavor was wonderful. I added some freshly sliced mushrooms after making the gravy part. I did had alittle whipping cream to the gravy to make a richer flavor.  I served this over Recipe #259339    Was a delicious dinner :)
Thanks for sharing the recipe!
This made quite a lot and was really good. I didn't use the soy sauce because our family doesn't like it, but even without it, it was very good.
Very good.  I loved it.  My husband thought it was okay but then again, beef tips are not his thing. I think next time I would season the flour before tossing with the beef.  Great recipe!
Kim, these tips are TOPS! Wife and I looking for a quick, tasty dish and found it here. Thanks for sharing-- it will be on our repeat list for sure.
I threw in some mushrooms and we were chowing down in no time.  Very good din din!  Dave
I took the suggestion to also add mushrooms, other than that followed the recipe. We really enjoyed this, DH had two servings, it had great flavor.  Even better the next day.  I served it over rice.

I have tried a lot of different beef tips recipes, and this is the first I've really enjoyed. I subbed half of the water for beef broth because I didn't have any seasoning salt, and didn't thicken the sauce out of personal preference, but made the same otherwise. Oh so good, definitely comfort food that I'm hanging onto! Thanks so much Kim D.
Wow......so yummy!  Fixed this for dinner and it was a hit!  We will make this again!  Thanks for the recipe! :-)

This is by far the best beef tips and rice recipe I have ever had.  It reminds me of my grandmothers beef tips and rice.  I did put some fresh parsley in it and used low sodium soy sauce.  It was even better the next day.  Kudos to the chef!
This was ok.  I might try it again if I had stewing beef and wanted an alternative to making beef stew.  This is a lot more work than beef stew though.

We loved this. I didn't coat the steak with flour, I just threw it in the pan. I cooked it with the onions, peppers and garlic and then drained the broth. I then followed the rest of the recipe as written. I made rice and egg noodles as hubby doesn't like rice. I loved it with rice and everyone else liked it with egg noodles. I only cooked mine for thirty minutes and it was so tender. Will be making again.

Made this for my husband. I used green and red peppers and added mushrooms. I left out the seasoned salt. I also added about 3 Tbs of sour cream to make a richer gravy.  My husband said it was delicious; something that you'd get from a restaurant. The beef was nice and tender. I will certainly make this for him again.

I made this for my Grandchildren, but added some of my own ingred.  I added a very LARGE Tablespoon + of Chile sauce and 2 heaping Tablespoons of Mayo and some A-1 sauce to taste.  The boys LOVED it over rice.  Of course we are from Louisiana & Mississippi; anything with rice is good.  But it is a great dish to feed to a large bunch of growing kids.  It has lots of flavor that stays with them for a few hours.  I am not a measurer of ingredients, so I just added what I thought it needed.  I don't think you could over do anything in this dish.
I loved this recipe...I wanted a little mushroom taste so I added a can of cream of mushroom in place of the 4 cups of water. It thickened it up. I only cooked 30 min. Put it over rice....delicious

Oh wow this was fantastic!  I cut back a tiny bit on the soy and Lea and Perrins just for taste.  I used beef stew meat so I upped the cooking time and kept adding water as the sauce was cooking down.  Added some carrots to the mix and mushrooms would have gone great too.  Oh we are gluten free so we didn't use any flour and just thickened with arrowroot starch.  Served over cauliflower rice, delicious!

This is a very good and very easy recipe. The meat came out really tender and the flavor of the gravy was very good. It's just as good as leftovers when you put it over some fresh halved dinner rolls.

well, since I'm the one reviewing(and not my husband), I will grade it on my own opinion. Simply stated.. I HATED IT. The soy sauce to me is what made it disgusting. Not much flavor either. I made it exactly as written except I added a little red wine to it. Nothing can help this recipe except for it to be scrapped and rewritten. To me, it was a HUGE waste of $15.00 worth of beef. Hubby didn't dislike it as much as I do, but he wouldn't care if I never made it again. Good thing, too.
This was so simple to make and tasted amazing!
This recipe is perfect exactly as written! I did take out the bell peppers the second time around (I love they hate peppers.) I subbed the water with beer. Oh my word my guy tore it in half!!
Sub water for beef broth. Gives it a better taste and more flavor..
Amazing! Made just as listed and the flavor was wonderful. Will definately make again

Had all the ingredients except the green bell pepper so I substituted some small pieces of red b pepper I had saved. It was very good but I believe the green b pepper would have been the difference between 4 or 5 stars. Will make this again for sure!
Amazingggg! I used 3 cups of water instead of 4, perfect. Glad i found the recipe

This recipe is amazing! The BOMB dot com!! All of THAT! I don't cook because most recipes are a disaster or the serving size is too big or it takes too long. I'm cooking for one and I don't want to slave over a hot stove all day for one. Sometimes, its just not worth it. But this recipe was easy to reduce, prepare, and cook! AND DEVOUR! Satisfied my craving for beef tips and rice!!! Locked in my recipe memory. Now to find a man to cook for. LOL!
We will definitely make this again! Thank you!
This is the best potato soup I have ever made.  It was even a hit with my husband, who usually doesn't like soups.  I will definitely make this again.

This was excellent cheese soup Christmas Carol! almost like mine (#71245) but a little different. I doubled the recipe, and used turkey broth that I had frozen in my freezer in place of the chicken broth, left out the carrots and used half Velveeta cheese and half grated cheddar cheese, I cooked the potatoes seperately in fear of becoming too soft....I topped/sprinkled the soup with with grated 5 year old very aged cheese before serving, and chopped green onions also. We enjoyed this soup very much with my homemade bread rolls. Thank you so much for sharing...Kittencal:)

I made this soup for ds who had just had his wisom teeth out & the whole family enjoyed it.  I doubled the recipe to feed four, but it ended up leaving lots of leftovers (not a bad thing, but the recipe as written probably would've fed all of us).  The potatoes came out just right, not too mushy, & the cheese flavor was subtle enough not to overpower the soup.  DS thanks you, Carol, & so do I.
Great Soup!  The best I have ever tasted. The flavor was wonderful.  Very good directions.  Thanks for posting.

Delicious!  Made for my DH  he loves potato soup. I used whipping cream for a richer flavor in place of the milk and I forgot to add the white vinegar since I don't usually use vinegar in potato soup. It was still good. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Really easy, tasty recipe! Loved the flavor and used all the toppings. Will be making again. Thanks for posting Carol.
I made this before and couldn't find the recipe. It's wonderful! My husband and I both love it.
this was really a good potato soup, I added cauliflower to mine and I did add the cheese, but would have been fantastic even without the cheese. will make again and again, thanks!

I can't tell you if it's anything like Ruby Tuesday's, but I can tell you it's delicious.  A definite make-again recipe.  I found this recipe courtesy of Top Secret Recipes and Todd Wilbur.  Thanks for posting Christmas Carol!

Very nice flavor with the spices under the skin.  I used sweet paprika, but next time I'll try the hot paprika for a little more "kick".  I wasn't sure I'd like the combination of onions and plantains, but it worked well.  The onions seemed to pick up some sweetness from browning, the wine, and from the plantains.  Thanks for sharing this recipe, toni.

Excellent flavor and a very good combination of flavors.  I found the dish to be too dry--added stock and wine and still wished I had a bit more liquid at the end.  It is important not to slice the plantains too thin or they become too hard after baking.

MMMMM! I made this today and it was very good. My plantains were hit or miss though. Some pieces were nice and sweet, others were a bit dry. I think next time, I will use more oil when frying the plantains. The seasoning on the chicken, however, was perfect! I will do this again. Thanks!

Outstanding, outstanding! I was running out of time tonight, and had just gotten some organic chicken thighs and legs from our local store. When I rubbed the Hungarian hot paprika, cumin, and S&P right into the chicken and browned it in the oil. I moved the chicken off to the side a bit, and added the plantains to brown in the browned bits. Terrific! I put the chicken in the pot/with plantains and added a bit of wine with the onions and reduced until it was a juicy bit of delicious topping. We will be making this again, and soon. Thanks, Toni!

I used leg quarters, which required longer baking time, one hour.  The chicken was truly scrumptious.  I basted with the chicken broth while the chicken cooked and I made the plantains separate. The chicken is very flavorful and I imagine it is even better baking on the onions and plantains, however I had the satisfy the onionphobes in my family and leave them out!

This was AMAZING!  I served it with roasted garlic mashed potatoes and it was a definite hit.  I forgot to add the chicken broth or wine so my chicken was  a bit dry, but the onions, plantains and potatoes mixed all together were SO good that I didn't even care.
Yummy!  I used these ingredients, added a can of Rotel (diced tomatoes and green chiles, spicy!), and baked the chicken breasts in foil packets.

Oh my gosh, these are delicious!!  They taste like an ooey gooey chocolate chip cookie.  I used colorful M&M's instead of the kissables because that is what I had on hand.  I also baked them in a 9x13 Pyrex dish instead of a jelly-roll pan.  I cooked them for about 24 minutes, and they were still a little gooey in the middle, but that's the way we like them.  My sons devoured them and were asking for more.  Believe me I will be making these again and again!!  Thanks Nikki for the great recipe!  Made for My 3 Chefs, 2009.
This is the first Pie Crust I have ever tryed to to make. Very Easy!!! It turned out GREAT. I did not change nothing. Thank You
I was a little skeptical when I read the recipe but gave it a try and am so glad I did.  This is really good and easy and turned out really flaky.  It's great when you just want 1 crust.  Thanks!

This is a perfect crust for people who don't like to make them.  There is almost no possibility of messing it up.
It is actually quiet nice as a "pot pie" crust.  I made two, one for the top and one for the bottom.  It isn't too sweet.  It is easy to get to the thickness desired.
I made it into the little pans like you get a store bought pot-pie in and it made five bottoms and three tops, so it would have made four complete pot-pie crusts but I did roll it between plastic wrap to get it thin.
This crust is great for pies and pot pies.
The climate may make a difference in the amount of liquid needed.

Great and easy peasy pie crust to make!!  I teamed it with Lennie's Old-fashioned Banana Cream Pie #14979.  Wanted to make the whole thing from scratch and not buy a pie crust.  Glad I did that now.  Well worth it.  Nice and crumbly and tasty!  Next time, I might add half a teaspoon of vanilla extract to the milk before mixing it all together.  Fail proof!

This is too easy and too good to be true! It whipped together in no time and tastes great! Thanks LAURIE I now have no excuse when makimg a pie that needs 1 crust! I made it with Miss Annies Amish Rhubarb pie and it worked beautifully! The flavor is wonderful and the ingredients are all pantry staples. What a time saving spectacular recipe! Everyone try this...you will not regret it!

I used this crust and made the "Yummy, Crunchy, Caramel Apple Pie" # 31128 for a local contest over the fourth of July and won first place! I cooked the crust for about 10 minutes before filling. It couldn't have been easier and it tasted wonderful with the pie!Excellent!!
Any time I make a pie i use this crust because it is the easiest and is the best tasting. Why try any other crust ever again?

Super easy but a bit crumbly- probably my own fault, not adding enough liquid?  Not quite enough to make a high fluted rim like I like, but still a recipe I will come back to when I am in a hurry (which is more often than I care to admit)  Thanks Laurie!

I don't know where I might have gone wrong, but it was too salty, I didn't notice it being sugary. It was too flaky, broke apart too easily. Sorry for this review. I will definetly try again to see how it fairs.
Was a bit too sweet for me and I also had problems with it being too crumbly. Very easy and quick to make. Hope to try again, thanks!

Just today I came across an old favorite recipe of mine that I thought I had lost forever.  It's a cranberry walnut pie.  Now, mind you, I have never made my own crust for anything -  I must admit I buy them (Oh the shame!) and I had none in the house.  Then I remembered I had your recipe saved in my cookbook and I gave it a spin - WOW!  I will never buy pie crusts again!  I love how it is sweet and yet a little salty all at the same time.  When I was mixing it up it didn't ball up for me so I added another teaspoon or so of milk and it came right together.  Perfect!
I made this crust for a broccoli quiche.  It was really good - light and flaky.  And it really was so easy to do!  Definitely using this recipe again and again and again!  THANKS

I needed a pie crust, was feeling lazy (and I'm not too good at rolling out crusts to begin with).  This turned out to be perfect.  It had a good flavor and was actually tender and flaky.  In future, I'll use this if I'm lazy all the time instead of a frozen crust.
Even I couldn't mess this up! Thank you so much for a simple and lovely pie crust. Used this for Lemon Fluff Pie by JanetC-KY.

This was very good. I did sub 1/2 the flour with wheat flour and was very happy with the result. Was so happy to get rid of the rolling and the freezing, etc. ;) I blind baked it for 15 minutes before I added the filling. Thank you for this wonderful addition to my make often (as in whenever I make pies) file. :) Fay

Good, but the dough was kind of crumbly and it ended up tasting a bit too oily.  I wonder how melted butter or shortening would work?  I will probably make it again and try one of these, as I really like the idea of a no-roll pie crust.

EZ as pie! Makes pie EZ! 
I will make this crust for lots of my pies! I made "Yummy Crunchy Caramel Apple Pie ~ recipe #31128" and we loved it! 
It looks a bit 'different', because it is...!...but it bakes up wonderfully, and stayed crunchy to the last piece! :)

This is the recipe that my mother let me use to learn how to make pie crust when I was just learning my way around the kitchen.  Probably 40 years ago!!!  We called it "pat in the pan" pie crust.  It is so flaky and light. It is the only recipe I use.  I must say that I have graduated to rolling it out between wax paper, and it rolls out beautifully.  For me, pie is all about the crust anyway, and this is delicious!!!

This isn't the "best" pastry I've made but its certainly the easiest! My main issue is that the no-roll method makes it difficult to maintain the thickness of the pastry. BUT, I'll definitely use it when I'm pressed for time or feeling lazy. Thanx Laurie!

I have not attempted to make a pie crust from scratch in many years because I am so clumsy with a rolling pin.  This one is perfect.  I even made a mistake and it still turned out delicious.  I accidentally added too much oil, so I added a little extra flour.  It was a nice flaky crust.  For my personal taste, next time I will cut the salt in half.  I posted my picture of it, even though it looks a little rough, but remember it is a real pie crust made by the woman who never could make a good crust!

I am a failure at making my own pie crust but this one worked!  I made a lemon meringue pie and prebaked the crust for 10 minutes at 400º and it worked perfectly!  So nice and flaky.  I now have a recipe for all of my berry and one crust pies!  Thank you so much for posting this keeper!!

Even though I hate rolling out pastry dough, I still prefer my mother's tried-and-true recipe.  This is very easy and quick.  I used this with for a rhubarb pie.  We all thought the crust was a little greasy.  I'm not sure if I did something wrong.  I followed the recipe exactly.  When time is short, I will use this; but I don't think I will make it my all-time recipe.  Thanks for an easy crust when time is a factor.

I can't make a real pie crust right now...My kitchen's too small, I don't have a rolling pin, and honestly I don't enjoy the process. This is a great alternative to the traditional method.  I used it for recipe #54170, Chocolate Chip Toll House Pie, it worked out great.  Thanks for posting!
Worked great! I pre-baked at 400 degrees for about 12 min and filled with a lemon custard. So easy...Thanks!

I have made this twice.  The first time is was so flakey that it fell apart, but taste good.  Today I left out the sugar, and used 1/3 cup of oil and added more milk.  It held up better and I left the sugar out because it was a meat pie.
Wonderful!

I made this crust tonight so I could use it for  Recipe #71250. Since the type of oil wasn't specific, I used 1/2 cup of walnut oil and the result was a quick and easy crust with a nutty flavor. Mmm! This recipe is perfect for me. I hate all the hoops you have to jump through for other crusts. This is great! Thanks so much for sharing, you've made my life so much easier!!!

This was the easiest pie crust ever!  However, 425 seemed to be a bit too hot.  I had set the timer for 15 mins, normally would be checking periodically, but forgot about it... and the edges burned.  Next time I'll try at 400 with a tbsp or 2 less of oil, as others have suggested.  Thanks for the superb time-saver recipe!
This is my favorite crust now!  Thank you for posting such a quick and easy recipe.  Just don't use olive oil like my mom did once....eeeewwwww!!

I used this crust with 
Black Bottom Strawberry Cream Pie #163938..absolutely delicious! My family loved it..the slightly sweet and crumbly crust was a perfect compliment to the strawberry filling. Thanks Laurie!  Hazeleyes

WOW!!  I didn't even know you could do this.  I used this crust for Banana Cream Pie.  It was soo good and sooo easy.  Even my daughter who doesn't like pie crust loved it.  It was flaky and sweet and yummy.  I even ate the thicker pieces and I don't usually do that!  Thanks.

Delicious!!!! Totally flaky, used wholemeal flour and it turned out fine. My only problem with it is that it's kinda crumbly, which I found hard to make a lid with, but as simply a crust, it's perfect!

This worked perfect for what I needed it for. I used it as the base for Raspberry Almond Bars Recipe #167825 and it matched so well! In the descripition I put this recipes as a reccomindtion.
Thanks for the recipe LizAnn!

I try to cut out transfats (crisco) in my cooking as much as I can by using oil or butter in place.  I liked this recipe because of that.  I was skeptical about pressing the crust into the pie pan, but it worked.  It held up fine when I cut the pie and tThe best part is that it tasted great!  Thanks for posting.  Pam

Wow! Where has this recipe been all my life? My family loves my cream pies, but I don't make them often because I don't want to make a crust! This is the perfect solution! It was so flaky, easy, and had a really great flavor. We thought it was a little salty so I will reduce the salt to 1/2 tsp. But it was still delish! :D I used this for looneytunesfan's Strawberry Lover's Pie Recipe #169204. Awesome! Thanks for posting!

I used this crust to make recipe #52356, Strawberry pie. It was so nice to have a homemade crust without all the rolling out mess! The crust was a bit too salty for our taste, so next time I'll reduce the salt a bit, but other than that it was perfect! Thanks for sharing this easy and delicious recipe!
Thank you!!  Pie crusts have been a mystery to me, but this was so easy!!  :)  I left out the sugar as I was making a souffle & it turned out quite well!!
This pie crust is great!  Will be my all time now. Thank you

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this yet! I have been using this recipe for my pecan pie for a few years now. It is so easy to throw together, and is perfectly flakey and good. Thanks so much for posting!
I wanted a recipe that did not use butter.  This fit the bill well!

As if this recipe needs more reviews, but I did use 100% whole wheat and it turned out great.  If you leave out the sugar it makes a great crust for pot pies or tomato pie...never new a pie crust could be this easy, it makes me want to throw away my rolling pin...well, maybe I'll keep it around for cookies. LOL  Thanks for sharing, will use this often!
I didn't care much for this crust, it was falling apart and too salty for the lemon meringue pie i made.

Thank you so much for this recipe. I have always thought that making pie crust is difficult and have therefore never dared to attempt making one, but with this recipe, I actually got to make pie!! Soooo easy, too. I only added 2tbsp of sugar because I wanted to use this crust to make Tarte a Bouillie (Tarte a Bouillie (French Custard Pie)) which is a sweet custard. Love this crust and custard combo. Thank you again for posting.

I tried this with a pumpkin pie.  It was SO easy!  I've tried making rolled out crusts and was never successful.  With this, it doesn't look as pretty, but who cares!  It's going to get eaten anyways.  When I make the pumpkin pie for Thanksgiving, I'll add 1 more T of sugar (I use Sucanat).  I used whole wheat flour, so maybe that's what made it need more sugar.  Will definitely save this one.

Awesome crust.  Very tender, went a little heavier on the sugar (2 Tbsp), and it was perfect.  Such a timesaver.  Stood up really well to an apple pie with struesel topping that generated a lot of juice.  I'll be using this a lot.  Thanks for sharing.
My first pie crust ever! Super easy and not intimidating at all. Will definitely make again. Did find it to be a bit salty so I think I will use 1/2 tsp of salt next time. Thanks so much!

I thought this was so easy and the taste was pretty good.  It was nice to have a homemade crust come together so easily without all the rolling and chilling. However, we did miss the buttery flavor and flaky texture of a traditional pie crust.  I used this for my Thanksgiving pumpkin pie and I did not pre-bake this crust, which really turned out nicely after having baked for a little over an hour.  It had nice color and was a little dense and crumbly when eaten. Overall, I would make this again when I'm in a pinch or would like a homemade crust without doing a lot of work.  Thanks!

I made a ches pie with this crust. It was very good. Quick and easy. I never make crust but that will all change now. I wonder how this would taste with a fruit filling. It seems perfect for a cream pie.
I did use about 1/2 the amount of salt and increased the sugar.

This crust gets lots of points for using oil rather than shortening, lard, or butter. Texture is somewhere between flaky and crumbly, not at al tough like some other oil pastries I've sampled. Very easy, especialy since it's mixed in the pie plate. I found the crust too thick for my tastes, and would probably reduce the ingredients by about 25%. Would also reduce the salt. I prebaked the crust for a cream pie without any problems. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I refuse to make anything that I have to roll out so I usually buy ready made crusts, but I hate doing that because there's always transfats in them. This crust turned out beautiful, light, flaky and tasty! It would be appropriate for all kinds of pies. Thank you so much! I will make pies much more often now.
Great recipe!! So easy to throw together when the store bought ones you pull out of the freezer are damaged beyond repair! I rolled it out and cut it into thin strips as a topping for apple pie.
Great tasting pie crust that is very easy! Thanks!

I loved this crust. I used part whole grain flour and part white. I decreased the oil by 2 T. and increased the milk by the same amount. So easy to mix and I love the firm, crunchy texture. I baked it for 15 minutes before adding my sweet potato filling, and later thought the crust edges were getting too brown, but they were fine. I might reduce the first baking to just 10 minutes next time. What's also great is that  you don't have to use pie weights or beans to blind bake this. Just prick the crust and it doesn't puff up. Great recipe.
great pie crust easy to put together

WOW! This was so easy to make! I loved that I didn't not even have to dirty any bowls!!I made the recipe just as it is written, and it was wonderful! I'll definitely be making this again and again! Thanks!

The first time I tried this, it turned out too dry.  This time, it turned out wonderful!  I think I just didn't add enough oil the first time. It's a gorgeous crust, perfect golden brown and looks very flaky and crispy. I'm using it for "Forget your Diet Luscious Chocolate Cream Pie" #64028. Very easy way to make a quick pie crust.

Oh I am so glad to have found this recipe!  This is a cinch to put together, and it is already in the pan.  I used this as a pre-baked pie shell for my Recipe #24591 and it worked beautifully well.  We were unable to eat the pie for 24 hours after it was prepared and the crust's crispiness held up to the task!  I will be making this again, Laurie!!  Thank you so much for this recipe!

I would give this 5 stars for ease and taste.  I did't like the constancy of the crust after it was baked, although it looked beautiful.  It was just a little to crumbly when I slice and served the strawberry pie.  This will not replace the recipe I've used in the past, but I will probably use it again when I am in a hurry.  Thanks for sharing.
Thanks for a recipe for an easy pie crust!  I will be using this again and again.  Mine didn't turn out oily at all...just right! Thanks Laurie!
Very good and easy. I ran out of regular oil so used olive oil to make up the difference. Used the crust with recipe #33454, Spinach, Tomato and Feta Quiche.

Not too bad of a crust and I have never seen anything easier to make. Now I'll be making more pot pies for dinner. A QUICK TIP: to make this even easier, take a piece of Saran Wrap and place it on top of the dough pressing through the plastic wrap to even it out and work it up the sides of the pie plate. When you're done simply throw away the plastic wrap and no messy hands to clean up, plus it presses even faster against the plastic.  I used to hate to have to go to all the work of making a crust, chilling, rolling, etc this recipe makes things a snap.

I've only got one good arm these days so don't have the ability to roll out pie crust.  What a lifesaver this recipe is!  Even if I had the use of both arms, I'd still use this... no shortening (and so no trans fat) makes it that much better!  Picture I  submitted is of this pie crust and Nestle' Toll House Walnut Pie (Aka Black Cat Pie) -- (recipe #19677)

Of course, nothing's going to be quite as perfect and flaky as your grandma's hand-rolled crust, but this one is sooo much easier and quicker (and still tasty) ... well, you'll find it hard to get motivated to roll pastry when you know you can whip up one of these in seconds.  :)  This is now a stand-by for me.  Thanks!
You cannot mess this up!  It tastes fantastic.  Thank you for a great recipe I'll use over and over.
This was so easy and worked well to make a blueberry pie.  Thanks for the recipe.

wow. this turned out great. light and flaky. i was scared it would be soggy bc i poured a warm mixture in it and immediately loosely covered it and put it in the fridge.  also it didn't form a ball so i smashed it down with my hands.  i baked it for about 15 minutes.

I love it! It doesn't get much easier than this -- and it turned out yummy and flaky. I used it for a crumb topped apple pie.  I used olive oil and it worked great.  This is going into my keeper file.  Thank you.
Wow!  I had my concerns about how this would turn out when I was making this, but it was awesome!  Will DEFINITELY make this over and over again!
This is so easy and I will never use another crust!
WOW!! Nice and easy. Will use again..and again!!  Thanks!!

Very good!! I doubled it, and used it as the top and bottom crust of a pot pie.  Turned out just right, and was very easy.

Was a bit crumbly for me.  But it worked for my deep dish pie, so hands down SUCCESSFUL!!!  Very flaky and nice.  My friend's 80 year old dad even liked it and he's a pie "expert" (years of experience).  :)
awesome and easy to put together. super simple to work with and tasty i used it for a lemon pie and they were fantastic together, thanks.

Absolutely wonderful. Its flakey and a tiny bit crumbly....yummy! I used this crust as a base for South African Melktert or Milk Tart Recipe #173067. Worked so well together. I loved it. The quantity of liquid really does depend on the climate I think so keep that in mind. I didnt really need all the oil when making this one today.

This is now a weekly addition to our house.  My kids love the Yummy Crunchy Carmel Apple Pie (#31128)and this is the only crust I'm using.
Thanks!!!

A great quick and easy pie crust.  When using it for fruit pies, I do not bake it first.  I usually make 1-1/2 batches when I want to make a crumb topping on a pie.  I use one batch for the bottom crust, then add extra sugar (1-2 T) and crumble on top before baking.  It makes the perfect crumb topping.

This pie crust was very easy. I used it to make a pie from the leftover filling I had from my apple-pear turnnover recipe. I also used the advice of the previous chef and made some extra to create a crumble topping. I wasn't thrilled by the texture of the dough, I think that next time I would use a little less flour maybe. Mine was just too...doughy. Thank you very much though for giving me something new to try.

This was a great, and easy pie crust recipe. I made this crust to use with Aroostook's crab quiche recipe #89565 and it came out awesome! Will be making and freezing this for many more uses. Thanks for posting!!!!

I was all set to make a chocolate pudding pie tonight... I thought I had a graham cracker crust on hand, but I was mistaken!  It was just a spare empty foil pie pan. But it was still tasty, and I think it would be an ideal crust for a pot pie (or other savoury pie).

This dough was too oily for my liking and it did not form a ball.It was more like breadcrumbs.I had to adjust the ingredients in order to make it into a dough.Once I fixed it up it was better but I would not use this recipe as it is.

I liked this crust, it tasted just fine, but it didn't hold up very well. I used it for a strawberry pie and it completely fell apart when I tried to get the slices out of the pie plate. I didn't really like that you couldn't do a pretty edge with it either (well not without a lot of patience). This would be a great recipe if you're short on time and you want something that tastes good... otherwise I would stick with a traditional roll out crust.
This was so easy. Everyone who ate it loved it. Thanks!
This was a great substitute when I didn't have time to roll out a crust for recipe #14569!  Wonderful; so easy and flaky!
This was quick and easy. Only complaint that I heard was it was too flaky.
This was so easy and tasty!!! I made a sweet potato pie with this crust. hmmm~
This was my first time making a pie crust...it turned out great!  Very easy, good for a beginner like me.  :)  Made with Dutch Apple Pie #43990.

Where has this pie crust been all my life?  Could not be easier and came out perfect and flaky.  I think it took 20 minutes from start to finish!  Much cheaper than store-bought and so easy there's no reason not to make your own.

This is great! It is so easy to put together and the taste is outstanding. I also like the fact that the crust does not shrink when you bake it in the oven. Delicious! I will use this all the time for all the one crust pies I make. I made it with Bev's "Recipe#24591", an awesome strawberry pie, btw. Thanks for sharing. Update: I use this pie crust all the time for one-crust pies. I just recently made Karen's "Recipe#34185" using this terrific pie crust.
This pie crust is great! It tastes amazing and was really easy to make. I used it with a berry crumble pie from this site and it turned out perfect!

Easy to make. I thought the oil taste was a little overwhelming, but could easily be remedied by adding some vanilla or substituting with butter. I used this with the Granny's Banana Cream Pie recipe, and it was a hit with my family. Thanks for posting!

I hate making pie crusts!!! until I found this recipe! I normally wouldn't make a pie if I had to make the crust myself until I found this recipe theres very little clean up which was awesome! This ones a keeper for sure!

This pie crust is excellent with chess pie.  It tastes amazing!

This crust was really good!  I must say I was skeptical at first because I've always rolled my pie crusts.  This crust had a great flavor and was flakey too.  I used this recipe for Recipe #100480 and we loved it.  Thanks Laurie for posting.  I will be using this recipe again!

I'm so sorry, but.........................
THIS IS THE AWESOMEST CRUST RECIPE I'VE EVER TASTED - FOR TASTE AND EASINESS!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This is my new pot pie crust recipe!

I did roll out 2 separate batches for the tops of my pies and found out the dough does not roll so well. Still fabulous. Thanks so much for posting!!

This was the prettiest pie crust I've ever made.  It went together quickly and easily and had such little clean-up.  I did feel that it was a bit salty, even though I used a scant tsp.    In the future, we'll add more sugar for fruit pies, but it's fine as is for a pot pie.

I have to say, that I was skeptical about a crust that did not have to be rolled.  Since my husband has been diagnosed with high cholesterol, I decided to try this as a healthier alternative to traditional.  This was great!! Thank you so much for posting such a wonderful recipe.
So easy! thank you for sharing this and helping me out in a bind. I loved not having to blend in shortening or roll out the dough. Thanks!

This is WONDERFUL!! This is the first crust I ever made and is THE BEST!!

oh man! so good!

This is one EASY and SUPER TASTY  Piecrust, and I am sure I will never roll crust again.

This was great for my chicken pot pie recipe.  But I don't think it would go well with a "sweet" pie, like fruit, or pudding.  But for meat, etc...it's good.

This was pretty good.  I made it for a french silk pie and found it to be a little too salty.  It was also quite crumbly and hard to get out of the pan without the whole rim going to pieces.  That could be my fault though, being that I used whole wheat pastry flour.  All in all, it wasn't bad.  In fact, I just may have to try again with less salt, more sugar, and white flour.

I have used this recipe for better than 20 years and found it to be the easiest and best pie crust in the world.  There are no shaping or serving problems.  My edges are always beautiful and professional looking.  It works great for any pie that I might want to make.  I recommend it to everyone.

Wow! What a GREAT recipe.  Thank you Laurie for posting it.  This pie crust takes all the stress out of baking homemade pies!  I love mixing the crust right in the pie pan.  The texture was excellent.  No need to ever roll out another crust!
This was a tasty crust, but not very pretty because the edges were not rolled looking or fluted.  Great for an everyday crust.
Perfect recipe!

It has been over 30 years since I made my one and only pie - using a store bought crust.  Wanted to make a buttermilk pie and had no need for two shells, and no room in the freezer for the second.  Found this recipe and thought I'd give it a try.  This could not possibly be any better.  It was wonderful.  Now my family thinks I can cook...LOL.
Ok, a little dry for me.  Maybe I will add less flour next time.  But SUPER easy to make!

Let me be the 100th person to say "Great recipe!"  I've never made a pie crust before, and this couldn't have been easier.  I was worried about so much oil, but it just worked perfectly.  I added a bit more sugar, and left out some flour.

Yet another review saying how great this was. Since so many people mentioned it was too salty, I used about 3/4 tsp. of salt. Since I don't have a rolling pin (and I never liked using them, anyway), this will be my new "go to" crust recipe. Thanks for delivering me from "prepared crust purgatory"!! :-)
Absolutely perfect for sweet pies. So easy, so fast, so wonderful. This is a wonderful thing!
Excellent!  I used whole wheat flour to make it healthier, and it was fantastic.  It goes very well with pumpkin pie.  Thanks for the recipe!
Not a bad pie crust and super easy to fix. I loved the fact no rolling pin. Very easy to handle, used it for a Strawberry Pie.

Very easy and tastes great too. I found it a bit salty the first time so I cut the salt in half the second time. It worked out well. This crust is extremely flaky so expect it to fall apart when you slice the pie but the taste and simplicity make up for the appearance.

Perfection! I made this using EVOO and it turned out great. Really easy too! Used it for an Old Fashioned Custard Pie - Recipe #260656. Thanks for posting a recipe that will become a "regular" in my house.
This recipe couln't be easier!  I will definitely use this recipe again...and again..and again!!

Yeah, this is really good and easy. All they payoff of a homemade crust with half the work. Thanks for the recipe.

this was great! like melanie2590, i also made the crust with 1/2 butter and 1/2 oil. everyone raved about how great it was! used this for Recipe #375024. i will def make this again!
thanks for posting.

My husband and I both loved it. I'm due to have my baby any day now, and being on my feet for too long isn't an option, so this crust was a DREAM. I made an apple pie with a crumb topping. Best.  Pie Crust.  EVER.  I increased the sugar to 1 tbsp and added a pinch of cinnamon for dessert pies.
I was so nervous to try this crust...but OMG! So EASY and SO good! Next time I will cut hte salt in half though...thanks for sharing!

Excellent and easy crust!  Gives the crumbly homemade crust texture I always want but don't want to put the time of rolling into!  Wonder how it would turn out with 1/2c of melted butter instead of oil...maybe  I'll try that next time!

I AM SO EXCITED! I had stopped making pies because my crusts never turned out right, and my husband hates the store bought crusts. We loved this crust! I am going to use this from now on! Thank you so much for such an easy and delicious pie crust recipe!
Thanks for a fantastic recipe!  So easy & a million times more tasty than shop bought ones! Used it for my wild blackberry pie and it was perfect!!! Time for more experimenting!
Quick and easy to make. A bit too rich for my liking for a dessert crust, so if I use this recipe again it will be for something savory. Also found it to be very crumbly. Good recipe in a pinch.

This continues to be my "go to" recipe for crust.  It is absolutely the easiest, flakiest crust I have found.  The flavor is very good, and yes, I would use the freshest oil you can find.

Made this just because it was mentioned in connection with a quiche recipe I was making! This couldn't be easier & DEFINITELY does make for a tasty crust! A keeper, for sure, with me!
Love this recipe. I used walnut oil (SO good for you) and then made a buttermilk pie in it (#56). One of our favorites!
