We made this for my daughter's first birthday party (minus the eggs), and all the kids loved it, as did the adults!  We used a full pound of mac, as some others had mentioned, but if you do, you need to be sure to stir it at least every twenty minutes, otherwise you will have a hard-to-clean crock, and not-so-creamy mac.  Today we used slightly less and stirred it frequently, and it turned out great!  Also, we used white pepper so you wouldn't see it.  Definitely NOT a fix-it & forget-it, but worth the effort!
This was just too creamy for us and the soup gave it a processed flavor.  I would not make this again.

According to my kids....THIS IS THE BEST MAC N' CHEESE they've ever had.  It was moist and so creamy and not dried out at all.  I did double the recipe, cause my kids just love mac n'cheese, but I only added 3 eggs, and it still came out wonderful!!  Thanks for sharing this recipe....this is a definite keeper for every holiday.

I made this for Thanksgiving and it was very good.  It is easy to make and I made it as written (with the omission of the eggs).  I didnt find it bland at all.  Thank You!  I will use this again soon I am sure.

This came out amazing!!!! I made three changes, but nothing major. I used 3 beaten eggs and low fat sour cream and 1% milk. I mixed up the cheese mix in a sauce pan, cooked the macoroni and then dumped everything into a ziplock bag and stuck it in the fridge with directions. My daughter put it all into the crock pot when she got home from school and by the time I was home from work (3 hours later) dinner was ready. It tasted identical to and had the same consistency as my Nanas homemade mac and cheese. Don't forget to put the stewed tomatoes on the side. This recipe is a winner! One last note, I couldn't find my dried mustard so I left it out. edit 1/08 I made this in the oven at 350 for 35 min (til lightly browned) and it was awesome too! I boiled the macaroni a bit longer.

I made this just as directed, but the sauce came out rather dry and congealed. I checked it every half hour in the crockpot and it was nice and creamy, but at the 2-hour mark I opened up the crockpot lid and the sauce was very thick and was separating even though I had the temp on low. Once I added some extra hot milk and stirred it into the finished dish, the taste was good, however.

Very good macaroni and cheese. I made this for a work function and it was gone in minutes. I made this twice, the first time I followed the directions exactly but I did omit the eggs. The second time, I made a few changes. I sprayed my crock pot with Pam, then added all ingredients (except noodles) directly to the crock pot. Next I boiled one full pound of elbow noodles for 6  minutes, drained them, and added to crock pot. As I stirred the hot noodles, the cheese and butter melted. I  used 1% milk, low fat sour cream, and again omitted the eggs. The result was just as good as the first batch. This is a wonderful quick recipe. I would also recommend using a crock pot liner (if available) for quick clean-up.

I made this for a party of 40 ppl and adjusted the amounts to suit the recipe, but it was amazing and rich and was practically gone!  I would definitely make this everyday (if it weren't for the calories!)
This was really creamy and cheesy. Making in the crockpot gives it a more creamy texture. Will make again.

This Mac and Cheese is so wonderful!  I have made it three times, and I find that when I use a whole box of elbows(about 3 and a half cups) leave out the eggs as recommended and not melt the cheese in a sauce pan, instead add the soup and other ingredients to the crock pot, then the cooked elbows and then the cheese and butter on top, stir it up and cook it for 2.5 hours it is perfect for us! This is a great recipe, thanks for sharing!
I make this for family reunions.  There is never any leftovers.  I do add the eggs.

This was pretty good, though I had to make a few changes. I made sure to use very sharp cheddar cheese, and ended up using about twice the amount of milke listed as it was soaked up fast. I also didn't have a can of cream of cheddar soup, but I did have a can of ceam of onion and it gave it a nice little zing. Also I added a little garlic poweder and cayenne pepper for extra heat. Was very good.

OK, Im anothe one that is going to make a whole new recipe from this, so here it is....used whole box of shells, 3 cups cheddar, 1 egg, twice the milk.....boiled shells 3 min............next time i will add 2 cans of soup..............this was wonderful..............
Very yummy! I skipped the eggs and next time will half the mustard.

It was very good...hard to find a good mac and cheese recipe that turns out not dried out!
I did use FRESH grated cheese as the bagged stuff gets gummy when you melt it with butter. I also used an extra 3/4 c cheese on the top the last half hour to keep the moisture in and make it look like a casserole. Great flavors!

there is absolutely no need for dirtying another pot! I boiled the noodles for about 5 minutes, then just mixed everything cold in the crock pot (a double batch), threw it in the fridge overnight and heated it in the morning for a lunch potluck. we haven't eaten yet but I stole a bite and it's AMAZING. gooey, stringy, creamy perfection and not sticking to the pot at all thanks to the butter. I added a chunk of shredded gruyere with the cheddar for a little fondue-y taste, used skim milk, lite sour cream and the stick "ICBINT for baking" (losing the caloric battle with all that cheese, but every little bit helps!), and I also omitted the eggs (because I forgot to buy them). definitely never use bagged shredded cheese in recipes like this - they coat it with an anti-caking agent to prevent sticking together but it also prevents nice creamy melting. this is superb though; try it!
Turns out great every time. I've even baked it in a glass dish at 350 until it's hot and bubbling.

Excellent recipe. I made it for a work function and everyone is requesting the link to this recipe. I didn't add the eggs either, I sprinkled a little cheese on the top and I cooked the macaroni a little less. Since I doubled the recipe, the directions said to boil the macaroni six minutes, but I only boiled them 3 since I knew that this would be sitting in a crockpot for a while. I mixed it in the morning before work and plugged it in when I got there. It was perfect and hot at the right time.

After reading a lot of reviews & using some common "cook" sense here's how this turned out suberb!  While the noodles were cooking (6 min), I sprayed the pot lightly with Pam (just in case, like 1 reviewer suggested), turned my 3-qt Crock Pot on High & melted the butter (not margarine) & sharp cheese (I grated 16 oz wedge of sharp hoop cheese & reserved a little for the top later).  Was not completely melted when other ingredients were added, but it did not matter- was all melted in the end.  Turned the pot to Low.   Whisked all the other ingredients in a separate bowl first before adding them to the pot.  In this order: 1 beaten egg, sour cream, spices (used white pepper), soup, 1% milk.  Added the noodles last. (compromised on the amount: a little more than the recipe calls for, but not quite the whole box. I think it would be fine to if you want to stretch it a little farther.  It was plenty cheesy!)  Was definitely ready to eat in 1 1/2 hours.  Stirred it often.  Sprinkled rest of cheese on top for last 20-30 min.  Next time, I will try 2 eggs & reduced fat sour cream.  Will never substitute the hoop cheese!

Better the next day.

Used 2 eggs and a pound of pasta...cooked pasta 5 minutes.. set crockpot on low for 2 hours and 1/2 hour on warm.  Turned out good
this is a huge hit.  I save even more time ... I do NOT cook the macaroni before, I put it in straight from the box... 2 1/2 hours later it is awesome!

This is the best Mac I have made/had!  My hubby begs me to make it all the time.  :)  I have been making this for 4 years now.  In Paula's cookbook, it says to bake it so I have always baked it (plus my hubby likes it crunchy on top) but maybe I will try it in the crock pot next time.

I omitted the eggs and will do so again. I will make this again. I decided at the last minute to follow another suggestion to not pre-cook the macaroni. That might be okay, except I used small shells instead of elbow and I think they were too delicate. They  almost disappeared into the sauce. Don't get me wrong, there wasn't a bite leftover, but I wouldn't do it again. Next time I will use elbow slightly pre-cooked as the recipe says. The flavor was great.

A colleague brought this to our Christmas luncheon.  It was great!  His wife did use the eggs and put in the crockpot so he could have it ready by our luncheon.  We all begged for the recipe and he shared yours with us.  When I make it, I probably will omit the three eggs, but I definitely will be making it!

This is the closest tasting to Stouffers mac-n-cheese yet! I did add 2 beaten eggs, a generous dash of onion powder and cayenne pepper to the mixture. From the reveiws I decided to only cook the pasta 4 minutes which worked out perfectly for us. The only thing I missed was the crunchy brown edges, but I soon got over that when I tasted it. For the ease of preperation I can miss the browned edges! I also must mention I did not melt the cheese, just stirred it in and it melted and blended perfectly and saved a step!

I made this for a company pot luck - everyone loved it!  I then made it for a dinner party - again all good reviews.  I've forwarded more people than I can count to this recipe link to follow.  I did as you said and left out the eggs.  And definitely no need to melt the cheese in advance - just dump it all in the crockpot and viola!
Made this for an event and everyone wanted the recipe.  Took others advice and omitted the eggs (no curdling), added onion and garlic powders, cayenne pepper, paprika and nutmeg.  Delish!
This is a great recipe!  I added my own spin to it by using pepperjack cheese instead for some spice.  Amazing!
My kids are very picky when it comes to Mac n Cheese and they all loved this recipe.  As recommended I omitted the eggs.  This is a keeper!

This is a great recipe for the crockpot!  I made this recipe to take to a potluck.  I par-cooked the noodles for 5 minutes, drained and cooled them, and then mixed all of the ingredients (minus eggs) in my cold crock and put it in the fridge overnight.  Took it to work the next day and plugged it in-- 2/5 hours later, a party success!  I decided to leave the eggs out because i was not cooking it right away.  It was very creamy, and the noodles did not get mushy.  I miss the crunchy topping that baked macs get, and I think the next time I'll add some paprika or extra pepper for a kick.

Made a version of this recipe last night to bring to clean-up in park today. This was one of the dishes made to feed our volunteers.
Made recipe for 8 (it made more than that) with the following changes...3 jars of Old English Sharp Cheese, 3 (10 1/2 oz) cans condensed cheddar cheese soup. Used all the other ingredients except eggs. Added a little garlic and onion powder. It was an immediate hit and there was nothing left. Have to make it again in 2 weeks for another clean-up.
Best mac and cheese ever.

I always make baked mac and cheese in the oven but saw this recipe and figured the crock pot would be a great idea for a party.  Made it for the kids, (since so many were picky eater and would not enjoy the adult food), on Halloween.  Let me tell you, the adults put a big dent in this dish.  There was nothing left at the end of the night and I always make enough to have plenty of leftovers.  It was easy, creamy and delicious.  My daughter said "oh Mom, this is just like the mac and cheese in Disney".  I also omitted the egg and used a mexican blend of cheeses (without the taco seasoning) and some provolone.  Will definitely make this one again.
This was great and an awesome way to have a warm dish at a family potluck! DIdn't use the eggs, but maybe I will next time.  I'm curious to know the difference. Thanks!

This is a very easy way to make macaroni and cheese. I made this recipe last minute and EVERYONE loved it. This is a keeper!!!! We loved it!! I read prev reviews and didn't use the eggs, and prob will never use the eggs. This recipe is perfect without them.

I tried this recipe for the first time today. It was GREAT. I doubled the recipe...use 2 eggs, 1 tsp of Gouldens Spicy mustard  instead of dry mustard and about a  1/2 cup of pepper jack cheese.. I will make this again and again..It was a big hit..
I'm made this recipe several times for my family and they LOVE it!  I've never left out the eggs, but I am going to try it this time.  I like to add rotel tomatoes to it to add spice.  Great Recipe!

I admit when I watched Paula Deen make this on her show, I thought it looked terrible. However, the base seemed good. So I decided to give it a whirl. First, I used corkscrew pasta. The sauce clung to the ridges so nicely.
I used 8 oz. of smoked cheddar with about 3 oz of parmisagna cheese and instead of dry mustard, I used a tablespoon of Dijon mustard along with a 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder.
After cooking the pasta, I tossed it into the slow cooker with 1/2 cup of half and half, 1/2 cup of chicken stock and about 1/8 cup of 2% milk. Stirred it well with the pasta, then while stirring, added the three beaten eggs to temper them a little better than Paula did on the show.
I also chose to melt the butter and cheese on the stove top along with the can of cheese soup, sour cream, salt, pepper, mustard and garlic powder. I added the cheese mixture to the pasta mixture in the slow cooker as the final step. It was AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS!!!!!!!!!!! Very smooth and creamy and the smokey cheddar cheese was a nice touch. Try it!! :o)

I had my son's high school swim team over for a team dinner, 25 hungry boys, and made this recipe.  They loved it and it was the first thing gone!!  I tripled this recipe and did not use the eggs.  The boys said this was the best mac and cheese they've ever had!!  I would definitely recommend this recipe and plan to make it again and again!!!

Ok I am a stay at home dad(not sure how long this will last) trying to learn to cook. I have it all together and in the crockpot! Wow I am cooking something :) I used the eggs becuase guys just like cracking and breaking stuff. It looks good and I'll let you know how it turns out.
Loved this- Made it for a big crowd and doubled it. I did not use the eggs at all and halved the butter and it was great!

I make this recipe all the time for my family.  it is the best mac n cz as far as my family is concerned.  I make it exactly as the recipe states.  I usaully have to triple recipe because it is gone so fast.  If I don't make it for the get together everyone is very disappointed.  Get recipe!

We loved this recipe!  First time I made with half as many eggs as recipe called for and 2nd  time left them out completely.  It had a much nicer consistency without the eggs!  This is definitely a recipe to keep!

YUM!  I should have known this would be good since it was from Paula Deen, but I didn't expect my husband to love it.  My husband is not a mac and cheese kind of guy, so that is a huge compliment.  Normally, I make just enough for me.  I took this to a party, and thought I was going to give out most of the leftovers to the guests...wrong!  My husband made it a point to tell me this was some amazing mac and cheese, and to make sure and bring some home for him.  I doubled it, and used a 16 ounce block of sharp cheddar and 8 ounce block of colby/jack.  I thought I had more milk, so I had to use a mix of milk and evaporated milk.  I added all the cheese sauce ingredients into the Crockpot, turned it on low for about an hour, and stirred to make sure it was all melted and creamy.  I don't like how eggs change the texture of mac and cheese, so I left them out.   After the sauce was nice and melted, I added the cooked whole wheat noodles (cooked about 5 minutes), and added a bit more evaporated milk.  I stirred it all up and cooked it about 2 hours until it was done.   People were stand-offish when they saw mac and cheese in a Crockpot, but they weren't once they tasted it.  I cut lots of the fat with  reduced fat cheeses, skim milks, and fat free sour cream but no one knew by the taste. It was so creamy and so good!  All of the guests agreed this was a great recipe, and all of them wanted some leftovers to take home.  My husband monitored to make sure they didn't take too much :)

great recipe...i used 3 different cheeses, did add the eggs (all you have to do is temper them :), they really do add a richness and stability to the recipe) and baked in the oven in a buttered casserole until bubbly; 350 for about 30 min...thanks for posting :)

Good, but it wasn't really silky like I expected.  I added a lot more milk to it as it was cooking too.  Not sure what I did wrong, I tried to stick to the recipe until it looked like it was burning on low... thus the additions of milk.  It may be that my crockpot cooks higher than some and I may try and use the keep warm setting next time.  It was good though, so don't get me wrong!  Didn't use eggs.
Had this mac and cheese at a friends house and they added chopped jalapenos this dish.  What a wonderful kick. Will be making this dish for Easter!
I like this mac & cheese with 4 eggs and 3 cups sharp cheddar. Want to try doubling all quantities because the mac & cheese gets eaten so quickly.
I love this recipe.. I skip the eggs as well and sometimes it doesnt even make it in the slow cooker.. its sooo delish!

I couldn't find the recipe I previously used with great success for a company pot luck, so I tried this one. After draining the pasta, I immediately knew I was going to have to double the recipe and jimmy the recipe a bit, since I didn't have double of everything. So, I made another 2 cups pasta, for a total of 4.5 cups uncooked. I used 5 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese, the same 1 can of soup, 1 stick of butter, 8 ounces sour cream, 2 eggs and double the seasoning. It came out so yummy and not grainy at all, but the pasta held their shape perfectly. I cooked the pasta for 6 minutes each time. I cooked on low for 2.5 hours as it wasn't quite hot enough for my taste at 2 hours. I won second place at the pot luck out of 20  dishes, and only lost to a yummy chocolate dessert. Will definitely make again!

I made this for a tailgating party at work.  I didn't use eggs or dry mustard.  I would have added some whole milk to make it creamier.  I also may have left out the evaporated milk and swapped it out completely for whole milk.  It was still very good and a BIG hit among my coworkers.  I just forwarded one of them the recipe.

Wow, we loved this!! I didn't have high hopes because a lot of mac n cheese recipes turn out grainy or not creamy at all. The main thing I have to have in a mac n cheese dish is creaminess. When you bake it, things seem to separate and the cheese settles on top while the noodles are by themselves, so I never bake it. This was sooo creamy and so cheesy. I even used packaged shredded cheese cuz it was all I had which usually causes separation, but it was still creamy! Mine was done in just a little over an hour, and we were hungry so we didn't wait to see what the difference would be if it was in there longer. Also, for anyone wondering, I've made this in 2 different sized crock pots. The 2qt one I have, it filled to the top and made it slightly more difficult to stir but was fine. In the 4qt one, it came up pretty much half way and was easier to stir.

Wow! Great Mac and cheese. I omitted eggs and will add 3 cups pasta next time. Creamy and delish just be patient when melting cheese with butter (yeah I used the preshredded bag kind) and don't stir too much while melting. This will be my go to potluck dish. Definitely not for the diet crowd but sooo good!

Wow! This was fabulous!!!!! Took it to a Christmas potluck and everyone raved about it. They even admitted things like "This was better than my recipe and I always thought mine was the best" type of thing.

It is definitely one I will use again. I doubled the recipe, and there was only enough leftover to have a tiny bit with my lunch today! It was totally devoured!

This recipe is fantastic. We just finished dinner and I had to rate this 5 stars.  I am seriously considering having a 3rd helping when I finish typing this.  The only modifications I made were to use 2 eggs instead of 3 and I added a bit of swiss cheese since I had it on hand from another recipe.  I freshly grated both cheeses.  Delish!!!
This was so yummy!! It will become a staple in our house.  Thank you so much!

I won't be giving up my regular macaroni recipe, but this was SO handy to have ready when we got back from swimming tonight.  Three minutes after walking in the door, the kids were eating.  Two out of the 3 really liked it, and the third (who believes only in Velveeta) was willing to eat it if it meant she got a cupcake.  Made according to the recipe except I couldn't find ground mustard in the cabinet so I used brown mustard.  You could definitely taste the mustard, so keep that in mind.  Not all of the shredded cheddar melted nicely, so I will consider using a chunk of velveeta next time, but most of it melted just fine.  I also didn't have time to do it all on the stove top, so I started it melting in the microwave, then just stirred it all together and called it good.  I used 3 cups of macaroni, so I had one serving leftover.  It wasn't as creamy as I was hoping, but it really didn't take any more time to put together than a box of mac and cheese, and yet was so much more real, so I'll keep it in mind.  I also liked how it was a crock pot meal, but it didn't take all day to cook it.  I frequently don't figure out dinner until mid afternoon, so this really worked for me.

I have a new slow cooker mac and cheese now! I used 1% milk, light sour cream, 2 cups extra sharp cheddar and a 4 oz chunk of 2% Velveta and it was nice and creamy.  Also skipped the eggs. Followed the technique, but love the idea of melting the cheese and butter in the crockpot then mixing in everything else.  Made a good sized batch, had dinner tonight for 3 of us, enough for at least lunch tomorrow.  Thanks for posting, a keeper for sure.

I LOVE this recipe.  I made this for my husband's family who was visiting from out of town and they raved about it.  I followed a few of the other posters' suggestions. I used 2 1/2 cups of uncooked large elbow macaroni, cooked it al dente and put it to the side.  I also shredded my own cheese (2 1/2 cups of sharp chedder and 1/2 cup of pepper jack) because someone mentioned the pre-shredded cheese doesn't stick together well when melted.   While that was melting, I blended only 2 eggs, sour cream, soup and the spices together in a medium sized bowl.  I added this to the butter and cheese mixture when it was half way melted (i was impatient), stirred it in well, then added the pasta.  Mixed it all well and put the crock pot on LOW, stirred frequently and was done 80-90 mins later.

I make this all the time!  I omit the eggs also and I've also tried it with different grated cheeses such as Jack.  When I use Jack cheese, I add some extra seasonings and once the macaroni is cooked, I mix in some crispy bacon,  yum!
Fabulous! It was so cheesy. Everyone loved it. Next time i will definitely use the sharp cheddar, though.

Wonderful recipe! I made this Sunday for Father's Day with my family and everybody loved it. I did as you said and omitted the eggs. I also did not have any dry mustard so I used garlic powder instead. While my elbow macaroni was boiling, I mixed all the ingredients in the crock pot instead of on the stove top and it all came out perfect! Thank you so much for sharing!!

I discovered this recipe a couple years ago when my obsession with all things Paula Deen began...This is my fav mac & cheese recipe. I've taken this to multiple pot lucks and its always a hit and people are begging for more. I don't use the crockpot. I usually just put in the oven for about an hour on 350 and its amazing!!!
Very cheesy! In my crockpot it was done to perfection in 2.5 hours.

This dish is absolutely delish and so easy to prepare.  I brought it to my niece's birthday party and the crock pot was cleaned out in no time.  Everyone wanted the recipe because of the taste and ease of preparing.  The only changes I did was to use a full box of macaroni, use 4 cups preshredded sharp cheddar cheese and no eggs.  Needless to say - I will be making this dish many times in the future.
This tasted very delicious but had a weird fluffy texture (from the eggs?).  I might try it without the eggs next time.

I followed a fellow reviewer's advice and didn't use a second pot to melt the butter and cheese together.  I just boiled the noodles for five minutes and then threw all ingredients in the crock pot together.  I too omitted the eggs - I've made it both ways and I can't tell the difference, so I don't think they're necessary at all.  It turned out perfectly and my boyfriend practically begs me to make this recipe now - I've made it three times, and each time it was wonderful.  I used a mixture of extra sharp, sharp, and medium sharp cheddar cheese because I like the strong, distinct, cheesy taste.
It was ok, but LOTS of calories (what do I expect from a cheese dish?).  Taste was good and creamy.  Enjoyed by my family.  I made it in the oven since I did not have time to crock-pot it.

I took this to a meeting (about 18 people there), I made a quadruple batch (yes, that's 4 TIMES the recipe! lol) and it was all gone except one scoopful. So I'd say that was a success.

For the quad batch, I only used 3 eggs (instead of 12! what the recipe would call for), and 3 cups of milk, instead of 4, 3 cans of cheese instead of 4 and no dry mustard.

I also used pre-shredded-in-the-bag cheddar cheese, although I think fresh definitely would have been a little better. And I didn't use all cheddar, I used probably 4-5 cups of cheddar and then 3-4 cups of mixed cheeses (like a fiesta blend.)

It was very good, but not perfect (in my mind), I might have to adjust ingredients a little for next time, but will definitely save as a favorite, until I find that "perfect" mac and cheese! (No complaints from the 18 other people who ate it...lol)
I'm entering a Southern theme cook off at work & hoping this will be the winning dish! :)

I have been using this recipe for a few years.  I do not add the eggs but follow the rest of the instructions as given.  I hate that the recipe calls for using the condensed cheddar cheese soup because I would prefer making mac and cheese from scratch but this is so yummy it's one of my  exceptions!  Turns out cheesy and creamy every time.  Perfect for get togethers because of using the slow cooker.

I made this for our Octoberfest party.  Everyone seemed to like it, but I'm gonna review based on my own tastes!  I found this to be really boring mac-n-cheese.  Granted, I had colby-jack cheese on hand, so I used that instead of cheddar.  (Maybe that was a critical mistake.)  But, people really liked it with the tangy pulled pork I made (a balancing factor?).  Like others, I only used 2 pots, my crock and a pan to boil noodles, so very easy dish to make.  I think this mac-n-cheese would be great for little palates, who don't like their food too spiced.  Thank you for posting the recipe.
I used rotini noodles and added a little extra cheese. I also didnt realize tha I was out of eggs! so those were omitted.

Amazingly simple and delicious. My husband raved about how great this dish turned out. This is the Only way to prepare Mac and cheese. Paula Deen always hits one out of the park when it comes to cooking southern style. As easy and delicious as her recipe for greens, which by the way I served with the Mac and cheese.

Making this for the 2nd time now.  DH loves it (so do I).  Definitely not for the calorie-conscious, but so good!   I omit the eggs and use a good quality cheddar block, cut into pieces.  Comes out so creamy and cheesy. Using a crockpot liner this time to cut down on post-meal scouring! :)

I hate eating healthy, though we have been trying to do so, per the doctor. (Just TRY to eat a little healthier!)  This was a snow day treat....oh yeah!! I omitted the eggs and used 2% milk. I also had a 7-quart Crock pot, so I doubled the recipes and we have plenty of leftovers to snack on later. It was pretty awesome! Husband loved it. Still, as most things with PD, it was sooooo heavy that I know we can't have this very often. If more recipes could taste like this, without a Surgeon General warning (butter, cheese, Yum! Wait....Bad, Bad! No, good...it tastes so GOOD! ugh!) I would be a happy woman.

No need for an extra pot!  I have made this several time now, and every time I dump all ingredients (except pasta) into the crock pot and stir well.  Then add the pasta a little at a time and mix well to coat.  It comes out beautifully every time!  I have also dressed it up a bit by adding chunks of cooked ham, fried onion bits, chopped mushrooms, and a few dashes of hot sauce. My husband loves it, and it was a hit at a office pot luck.  thanks for posting!

This is good...not to die for.  I had 2, 2 year olds that loved it but I wasn't over the moon.  Made it as written but next time will leave out the eggs and see how that works...I wonder if they made it temperamental?  Anyway, thanks for the recipe GiddyUpGo and Paula...

I did not like this mac n cheese (I would have given it 3 stars).  I thought it needed something more. BUT I took this to a pot luck and people RAVED about it.  Actually when I was taking my crock pot home, somebody stopped me and said..."that's the mac n cheese I heard about."  (the 4 stars)  I personally think it would have been better with a velveeta cheese instead of the sharp cheddar.  Also, I didn't add the eggs but followed the rest to a T.
Made this for Easter dinner! Our family just loved! Will be making it again!

This is really the best tasting Mac n Cheese out there as far as taste.  It's something I make only occasionally though as it's really pretty decadent from a calorie, cholesterol, sodium, ungodly saturated fat perspective.  Tastes splendid though.  A-
My absolute favorite Mac & Cheese! I have made it several times and it gets rave reviews from everyone that tastes it!! and it is SO incredibly easy.

The recipe is great and easy to add your own twist to! I have been looking for the right recipe to make my mac and cheese creamy and this one does just that. I used 2 beaten eggs, added Prego's new "creamy cheddar cheese sauce" instead of the canned cheese soup, put 4 cups of shells because there was plenty of room for more noodles. I also added some frozen broccoli and kielbasa sausage and topped it with campbell's crunchy onions. Came out great!!

I made it without the eggs because it just sounds like they could mess with the texture.  I left out the mustard because I ran out and it still tasted great - though I did add a dash of nutmeg.   I doubled the recipe for an office potluck and it got great reviews.  I cooked my noodles 4 minutes because I don't like my pasta too soft.  I also diced up and fried up a pack of bacon and reserved about 2-3 tablespoons of the bacon fat.  I then incorporated the bacon into the mac and cheese just before serving.  I toasted a cup of Italian style bread crumbs in bacon fat on the stove and sprinkled it on top of the mac and cheese before serving for some crunchy texture since it's coming out of the crock pot.  I also threw in some garlic and onion powder just because we like the taste.  Great recipe with a great base!  This was the first pot to be finished in our potluck and everyone raved about it :)

I've made this many times and it's wonderful! I always use 1 less egg and more cheese, once it's done in the crock pot pour it into a baking dish, layer Sharp cheddar cheese on top (shred your own, never buy pre-shredded cheese!) and put in the oven under the broiler to make it crust. Viola! It's done.
substituted cream of chicken for the cheddar soup....was delicious!
Do u need sour cream?

I used 2 eggs instead of three, I took the note of another review and while cooking the pasta I melted the butter in the crockpot on high. After butter was melted, added the cheese, the other stuff that I had mixed in a bowl, added pasta. Stirred every 20-30 minutes, it was done probably in 1 1/2 hours, and it was soooo good. I'm taking left overs to work tomorrow.

Needed a side dish for my son for a Marching Band picnic on Memorial Day.  Made the recipe (doubled) as written (without eggs) and it was perfect!  It's not your baked-type mac and cheese - it is creamy and good!  I made it with shredded Velveeta because that's what the boy loves - and he just brought home the scraped, empty crock pot!  Thank you for this recipe!

Changed it up a bit.  Used 1lb uncooked macaroni.  Boiled for 6 minutes and slightly rinsed.  Put butter and 2 -8ounce blocks of cheddar cheese (put in food processor to shred) and melted.  Sprayed crockpot with Pam and set on high.  Once warm mixed 2 cans cheddar cheese soup, about 2/3 cup sour cream and cup milk.  Whisked together real good then added cheese mixture and whisked again.  Added salt and pepper then cooked macaroni.  Turned crockpot on low. It's not done yet but I can't stop sampling it.  It's so creamy and cheesy.  Good luck
Oh my lord is this good. FYi just go ahead and double, even triple, the recipe. It is to die for.

Just like someone else said "no need to dirty up a 2nd pot".  I put all ingredients (except eggs) into the crock pot and in the end added the hot noodles, which in turn melted the butter and cheese almost immediately. I also sprayed some pam into the crock pot prior to adding the ingredients, to avoid a sticky mess in the end.  I made this recipe several times and have found that cheddar cheese is the best cheese to use (gives it a great taste and the golden color), do not include the eggs as it can come out as little curds in the midst and gives it a "blah" taste and like I said before, no reason to dirty a pan if you can literally all throw it together in the Crockpot.
I always have to double the recipe as everyone wants seconds and there is just not enough for all to go around (I got big eaters).  I just have another double batch in my crockpot as I type this to bring to a Volunteer appreciation event at for a Community Theatre.  I brought this dish once before to the Theatre and now whenever we have a pot-luck kind of function I am automatically put down for the Mac N Cheese, without even being asked :) 
This is a simple, quick recipe that will reward you with a rich and flavorful comfort dish that is oh so yummy!

Finally! I found a recipe for slow cooker macaroni and cheese that my entire family enjoys. Not a single complaint from 6 of my kids and my husband. They were dying for leftovers, but unfortunately there wasn't enough to go around the next day despite my doubling of the recipe. I did double this, but left out the eggs, and also only used 3.5 cups of cheese instead of the 5 that doubling would have required, i think it would have been way too cheesy? Not sure. Still giving it 5 stars with my alterations because I can't wait to make it again!

This recipe was a hit!  I did make a few important modifications, though:

1) I did not use eggs.  I like creamy, rather than fluffy
2) I did not use dry mustard.  Instead, I added a can of chopped/roasted green chiles
3) I used 1% milk, not whole - mainly because it's what I had in my fridge
4) I used a blend of cheese: mild cheddar (sharp makes it less creamy), jack and shredded parmesan.  I'm convinced, the more variety of cheeses you use, the better it tastes (don't use pre-shredded cheese - the coating they put on it makes melting difficult)

Otherwise, I followed everything else and took a double-batch to an office party.  It was gone within 10 minutes.  My partner, who got a small taste the night before, was bummed that I had none left over to bring home.  Guess I'm making more this weekend! :o)

Love. I followed the advice from the reviews and omitted the eggs as we like a more creamy and less stiff mac and cheese. I also  like to add some tips: 
1. Creamette pasta brand has a "OVEN READY ELBOWS" so you dont have to boil. I added EVERYTHING at once with no other pots or pans to the crock pot. Wonderful if you can find it in your grocery its worth it and makes this even easier. 
2. I used a block of white cheddar just to change it up. OMG so good! 
3. Fancy it up and use this as a base for Lobster Mac and Cheese (a restrauant fav but usu expensive). I layer the prepared crock pot mac & cheese with cut up cooked lobster  in a casserole dish. Added butter crumb crust to top (mashed Ritz crackers layer or herbed bread crumb mix dotted with butter chunks) and finished off with a sprinkle of cheese and baked until top was browned and bubble. Husband LOVED it!

I totally wanted this recipe to work out better than it did! I gave it 3 stars because my son liked it. I only used 2 eggs and I used a larger elbow macaroni which I think hurt it because even though I only boiled it for 6 min, it was falling apart after the dish was complete. It was also curdling and I don't know if it was from the eggs because I noticed a lot of reviewers omitted them for that reason? I'm determined so I WILL try again, but to me...this one was kind of a bust.
I only added one egg do to other reviews and this was very good and I would make again for sure

I made this today for a pot luck lunch at work and it was amazing.  But as one reviewer already said, no need to dirty any additional dishes.  I only cooked the noodles for 3 and a half minutes and then put them and all the other ingredients in the crockpot cold then stuck it in the fridge last night.  Took it to work this morning and plugged it in on low for 3 and half hours.  Perfectly gooey and creamy!  I did change it up a bit.  I tripled the recipe and used four cups of sharp cheddar, two cups of Gruyere and one and half cups of American.  I also used Dijon mustard instead of mustard powder.  And no egg.  Finally I sprinkled some paprika on top.  Once it was heated and all the cheese was melted I made sure to stir it every hour or so to assure all the ingredients were thoroughly mixed.  I have been getting rave reviews all afternoon.  Would definitely make this again.
I followed the recipe as suggested (no eggs) and everyone loved it and it went pretty fast. There wasn't much leftover. Will make again.
Easier than most Mac and cheese recipes, and people always love it. Plus, unlike most Mac and cheese recipes, this one is good reheated the next day.

LOVED this recipe! I made this for a Thanksgiving kid's side dish. Even the fussy picky kid eaters had seconds. I used the Cheddar and Philly shredded cheese with a cup or so of sharp white cheddar. No eggs in this one either. Glad I doubled the recipe, it was gone.

This is my favorite Macaroni and cheese recipe ever! When I make it I always double the recipe and I like to add to it a little bit to make it my own.

I usually make the cheese with 2 parts cheddar and 1 part pepper jack, it gives it a little kick. I also boil the noodles in water seasoned well with bacon salt and I add a pound of cooked and crumbled Wright brand bacon. 

This is a huge hit with any pot luck or party I take it too, usually the first dish to disappear!
I am NOT a good cook. So that being said, I tried this recipe, and it came out perfectly. It was SO delicious! It was super easy and fast to make.

This stuff is INCREDIBLE. I've made it at family gatherings and it's a hit. However, I think the use of whole milk and sour cream is just unnecessary - 2% milk and Greek yogurt instead of sour cream do a lot to reduce the fat (and in the case of the Greek yogurt, adds a nice punch of protein). Be careful to use unsalted butter; the cream of cheddar soup is usually enough salt for the entire dish - season to your own taste, of course. I've never used the eggs and it comes out creamy and delicious. You can also use ditalini instead of elbow noodles and it works really well. I'm making this tonight and I'm going to try just throwing it all in the crockpot because melting the cheese and butter in the saucepan is kind of a pain in the butt and seems redundant, dish-wise.

DOUBLE THIS RECIPE. I doubled this recipe as it was given (no eggs) because I was having friends over. We were 5 people and there was BARELY enough for all 5 of us with it doubled. We aren't piggies, either! I have tried about 5 other mac and cheese recipes, most in the crockpot, some baked, but LET ME TELL YOU, this recipe is THE BEST I have tried. It is super creamy and the cheese doesn't get lumpy and chewy like other recipes i have tried. I am trying it tomorrow again but I am stirring in cooked hamburger meat. A++++
I made this according to the recipe and was extremely disappointed. It was very bland and mealy. Not sure if it was the cheese or the eggs, but I won't be making it again.

This went over so well in my household I was asked to make it again 4 days later. I added hame to the mix though. Word to the wise though. Don't put it on high and push through the cooking process the sauce will break leaving you with a not ideal consistency, though still tasty.
I found this recipe about 4 yrs ago and it has become our family's favorite holiday side dish! I make two 8 qt crockpots for the crowd and never any leftovers! No eggs!

This mac and cheese is simply amazing. It comes out perfect every time I make it and I am no chef. The only thing I have done differently is take out the eggs. It is fine with the eggs in there but I feel that it has a smoother texture without them.

Ok guys and girls, I'm making this for Thanksgiving...and read every single review. And I am confused...isn't it the sour cream that has made people's dishes curdle? Not the eggs. Eggs are meant to be cooked....sour cream is not. I have tried cooking other things with sour cream before and it has curdled. I traditionally make a baked Mac and cheese but it's so much work and I'm looking for something easier and still delicious. I think I would like the eggs in it bc I like a bit of the crumbly rather than creamy texture to my Mac.... But can I just leave out the sour cream is my real question? I'm afraid to use it and have it curdle...
Question: where in the process does the cheese soup come in? On the stove with the butter? Or just mixed into the slow cooker with everything else?

Excellent! Quadrupled the batch for thanksgiving dinner. (We had 50 people) not a noodle was left. Everyone was raving about how they liked it. I added a couple other cheeses to the mix on top of the cheddar. It was really good!

I was excited to try this recipe. The texture was perfect. I omitted the eggs too. However, I think the dried mustard made it taste weird. I will make this recipe again but I will omit the mustard next time.

Our family loves this recipe. I usually make it once a week. I omit the eggs and dried mustard. You can add hot dogs or ground beef for the meat lovers. If you don't have time for the crock pot you can whip it all up on the stove. Today will actually be the first time I make it in the crock pot.

Huge hit for Christmas dinner. I won't cook the macaroni for the full 6 min next time. Probably will try 4 minutes instead. I used half 1% milk and half heavy whipping cream. It was a double batch and it worked out fine using the time in the recipe. The packaged, grated cheese turned out creamy with cooking. I omitted the eggs and the dry mustard. Can't wait to make it again!

I made this yesterday in my crock pot...really loved this at first but I think the eggs turned the smooth sauce into a cottage mixture. I did add some milk to re-gain the sauce with little luck. I will try again and omit eggs.
Oh my goodness! Sooo good! I added some about Half of cup of half and half and half a cup of milk instead of the one cup of milk. Also added a packet of Velveeta cheese sauce! Big hit in my house!
This recipe is amazing, and always a hit! The only thing I changed is replacing the can of bland soup with a jar of Tostino's con queso. It gives it a tiny kick that my family loves.

Fantastic homemade Mac and cheese!! I made this recipe twice. The first time I added 2 egg yolks instead of whole eggs. I made the sauce in a saucepan and tempered the yolk. The egg is to thicken the sauce and add richness. I cooked the par boiled noodles and added them to the sauce and cooked on low for 20 minutes until pasta was cooked. It turned out good. The second time I made it I omitted the egg altogether but still made the sauce in a large saucepan. I reduced the sour cream to 1/4 cup and reduced the mustard powder to half the amount also. I did not par boil the elbow macaroni but I did increase the milk by about 1/2 cup and added some garlic powder. Oh and I added probably an extra cup of cheese! Buttered the cold crock pot and mixed the dry macaroni and sauce and cooked on low for 3 hours. WOW!!! Amazing! Tip: place a clean dish towel or double layer of paper towel under the crockpot lid to keep the moisture/water from dripping back down into the Mac and cheese. Oh and do not use pre shredded cheese! Shred a brick of cheese. The flour and starch that is coated on the ore shredded stuff can make the dish grainy.

This is my go-to Mac recipe. I've made several times with slight tweaks along the way. Here are some slight modifications I've made and love the final recipe. No eggs needed, fiesta nacho cheese soup instead of cheddar soup gives a little more flavor, probably very similar to tostitos dip mentioned by others, real Bacon chopped up because what doesn't taste better with bacon, add a little of the grease, I replaced some of the butter with it, and I used a variety of the shredded cheeses, like Mexican or jalapeño jack, along with the cheddar. Also, I only cooked the pasta separately, many times the night before, and then throw it all in crackpot. No need to cook anything else separately. It all yummifies by itself with a little time. Mmmmm.

I always double the recipe for a potluck. I use more cheeses too, mostly sharp cheddar but also fresh shredded parmesan, mild cheddar, and colby. I omit the eggs as well. This last time I added a quarter cup of real bacon pieces, dry parsley, and garlic. I always season it with the dry mustard, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt. Be sure not to over boil the noodles, they'll turn to mush if you do. I've used small and large elbow noodles, you could also use penne or shells to change it up. Everyone always raves about this - it's easy and amazing!

I never made mac and cheese from scratch before , usually made it from a box or package. I followed this recipe just as it said {omitted the eggs because every one said to} -tripled the recipe . Brought it to my son's Kentucky Derby Party and hoped that it would get eaten . It was gone in 2 hours and everyone one wanted to know who made it, even my kids{ young adults} were shocked that I made it. This is not a low calorie recipe and I told every one at the party , if some one had a heart attack -I was going to be the blame .
The best ever!!!

We made this last weekend for my niece's graduation open house. We made TWO triple recipes and both were gone within 2 hours! We did a few things differently for the second crockpot; we drained the macaroni after cooking and added the butter to the cooked macaroni after we put it in the crockpot. Then we added the grated cheddar cheeses, the soup, the milk and the sour cream. No need to melt the cheese with the butter; there was no discernible difference between the first batch and the second. We also left out the salt... do not need any salt with the cheese and soup adding more than enough. We also did not use the eggs. People really liked this as it disappeared so quickly!

I tripled this recipe for a 4th of July party. I cooked the pasta for 4 minutes, drained and rinsed it just a bit. I put the pasta into the crock and mixed the butter with the pasta until it was all melted. I omitted the eggs, mustard and additional salt. I suggest a taste test after all ingredients are melted together before adding any salt. I put the rest of the ingredients including a mixture of shredded sharp cheddar and fresh parmesan right into the crock. 2 1/2 hours later I had perfect mac n cheese! Not a morsel left at the end of the party!! Three people asked for my recipe.

This is absolutely the very best way to make macaroni and cheese. I boiled the pasta for only 5 minutes, I did not include the eggs - and I used almost a whole stick of butter. This turned out perfectly! The beauty of it is that it will never get "dried out" like it does when you bake it. After the cook time is over, just put it on warm - wonderful! If I could give this 10 stars, I would! I have never posted a review on Food - this is my first - but I just have to tell everyone how fabulous this is - this is how I will make macaroni and cheese forevermore! (TIP: Buy a block of sharp cheddar from the deli - and grate your own - the pre-grated in the bags is TERRIBLE!)
WOW! This mac and cheese is so good!! I followed the recipe, except did omit the eggs. It turned out so creamy and delicious, my kids loved it!! A definite keeper.
This can also be cooked in oven for about an hour,if you don't pour hot cheese directly on sour cream an mix mixture it won't look like cottage cheese mixture.
Made it for my daughter's birthday party and turned out amazing. I had never made Mac and cheese before. Doubled the recipe and everything was gone. Everybody was asking for the recipe!

I'm a new mom of a 2 month old and needed an easy mac and cheese for a family picnic that would please a bunch of kids. This was perfect! I shredded the cheese the night before to make it quicker. I did leave out the eggs so I'm not sure what the difference in that is. I also forgot the sour cream. It was still so delicious. All the kids in my family lived it!!!! It's was creamy and delicious! I received multiple recipe requests.

My family and church love it! I omit the eggs and also sometimes skip the salt, pepper, and mustard. Also, you don't have to melt the cheese and butter separately, or pre-cook the noodles. I've just thrown all the ingredients into the crock pot and cook it on high for about 2 hours, stirring frequently, and it turns out great! I definitely love this recipe!!!!!
Always perfect and never have leftovers - they scrape the crock pot for every last spoonful. I’ve been making it for at least 5 years - wonderful.

I skip the eggs (they curdle) and the melting the cheese and butter together. Dump it all in a crock pot and cook for two hours on low or or mix and put in a casserole dish and bake at 350 for an hour. Either way, this is my go to mac n cheese!

I've made this from Paula's original recipe. I thought the eggs made it dry. I created a hybrid recipe - part Paula's, part Mom's. Instead of the cream of cheddar, I use cream of mushroom and skim milk. I also found it reheats creamier than using eggs.

I want to make this for Thanksgiving based off of everyones reviews. I would need to transport it for about 2 hours to the dinner. Any recommendations on the best way to reheat it? I was thinking about just keeping it in the crockpot and then adding a little more milk when turning it back on.... PLEASE HELP!!!!

No need to dirty more pots and bowls. I boiled the macaroni for about 7 minutes, while that was boiling I added all the ingredients to the crock pot. All different cheeses I had pieces of in the fridge, I can evaporated milk, some water (1/2 cup) about one cup regular milk, dry mustard powder, pepper, frozen broccoli, ham chunks, drained macaroni, put in on top of every thing in the crock pot, stirred it all together cocked for 2 1/2 hours on low (covered). Great one pot meal, vegetables, meat and starch all in the same pot. Been making it like this for years but usually put it in the oven as I had never thought to use crock pot prior to seeing the above recipe. It came out amazing and I only had to rinse one pot. Love it!

I made this for the kid’s Christmas dinner, but we adults ate most of it. Other than omitting the eggs as recommended, I followed the directions exactly. After making multiple Mac and cheese recipes from complicated six cheese Mac and cheese to a million different crockpot varieties that included anything between cheddar to extra sharp, I finally found our “go to” Mac and cheese recipe. And it’s simple to beat!
Amazing dish! I omitted the eggs and use a sharp and medium chedddar cheese blend. I also used gluten free elbow macaroni noodles. So easy and a family favorite.

I followed the recipe exactly. It tasted wonderful, however the texture of the cheese became kind of grainy. I used whole milk, the eggs, everything exactly as listed. Does anyone know what I could have done wrong? In fact at about the 2 hour mark I noticed the texture and I added another can of cheddar soup. Again, it tasted great and dinner wasn't ruined, but it should look creamy. I'd appreciate any feedback.
Great recipe but I couldn’t get the cheese to melt. It would become goey but not liquid. But in the end it turns out ok

We absolutely love this recipe! It's quick to throw together and consistently turns out delicious. I use a can Fiesta Nacho Cheese instead of the condensed cheddar cheese soup and throw in some cayenne pepper for more flavor and a little kick. I wisk everything together very well in the crockpot before adding the noodles and it always turns out super creamy!
I have been searching for a homemade Mac and cheese that my picky 9 yr old would. I too omitted the eggs. It was delish my child gave it 10 thumbs up!!!!!!
Just double the recipe. Trust me. I dumped in all of the ingredients then added the cooked noodles. After it was done I added some cut up bacon. Omg. THE BEST!!!!

A hearty vegan dish!  I doubled the quinoa to make it thicker and waited longer to add it to the stew base.  I also used a full teaspoon of chili powder.  Quite a delicious combination of flavors.  I'm thinking I'll use the leftovers to stuff peppers.

What a great vegetarian dish! I substituted vegetables on hand (brussels sprouts, halved) for those I didn't care for (bell pepper, celery) or unavailable (zucchini). I also made mistakes, like adding the cooked quinoa too soon. I didn't have coriander in my spice rack. Despite all these changes, the dish came out great! I really recommend this.
Nice stewy lunch. Very tomatoey. I increased spices, probably not necessary. Quite good with fresh biscuits crumbled over it. Took 2 min in a pressure cooker. Can't beat that!

Why cook the quinoa separately? It takes roughly the same time to cook as the stew, once you've added the stock (a little less, actually). If you add it raw at that point it'll pick up the flavor of the veggies and it will turn out more tasty.
My coworker made this Peruvian Quinoa chili it was delicious!!

I was making a different recipe and heavily tweaking it, so I was googling around, and lo and behold I found this recipe. More or less what I made, and it's delicious. I used 1 zucchini, 4 small carrots, 3 stalks celery, 5 plum tomatoes pulsed in food processor, 1 tbl cumin (plus more), 1 tbs dried oregano, 1 Serrano pepper, dash of cayenne, 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1/2 tsp sea salt and some pepper. I threw in spinach at the end. I added 1/2 cup quinoa and used 33 oz of chicken broth. I simmered partially covered for 25 mins then threw in some spinach. I pulsed 1 cup of cilantro and 6 scallions in a food processor and added that in. A squeeze of lime and I was done!

This was okay, I made it as written. We didn't like the texture of the apples, or the chewy skin of them. We also thought there was too much pepper for the delicate flavor of the apples. And I didn't understand why I needed to stir the flour until smooth for 2-3 minutes in the pan, so I added the broth/juice to it and made a roux. I don't think this will be made by us again.

Tried these this morning and they were very good. My DW says this recipe is a keeper.  I had 2 eggs, my DW had 1. Her comment: "The one egg satisified me without leaving me overstuffed."  This will become a 'several times a month' recipe'. Substitutions used: frozen turkey sauage links (thawed and diced them) and canned mushrooms. Omitted the salt and red pepper flakes.
When was the last time I had Green Goddess Dressing--  It was very good.  I also choose to leave out the anchovies.  Instead of minced fresh tarragon I used 1/2 tsp dried.  This recipe is a keeper.

I liked this. I used Kraft light mayonnaise that was WAY TOO sweet so I had to add a lot of salt to make it work. I also used more yogurt (6oz) and only 6oz of mayo to use it more as a dip for crudite. VERY nice if you don't do dairy!! :)

This was a wonderful way to use leftover chicken.  It prepares and cooks up quickly and alongside spanish rice makes a terrific meal.  We loved the consistency of the sauce; but next time would add either a can of green enchilada sauce or another can of diced chilies.  We needed to kick up the spice just a bit.  Thanks for posting.

Hi,I just made this recipe yesterday and it was the best! I could not stop eating. I made it almost as  
is but before I poured the sauce I spooned a small amount of corn,black bean  
and roasted pepper salsa 
over it. It will be a great 
new staple in our menu.
Thank you!!!
These were wonderful! They were easy to make, tasted great and were very creamy. Followed recipe exactly and it came out perfect. Thanks Deb!
Simply describes the preparation but not the taste. I searched several recipe sites and tried several different versions.  These were the best. Thanks for the recipe

I agree with the other reviewers:  This is the best creamy enchilada recipe I've ever made!  It is rich and filling.  DH, who can usually eat two beef or chicken enchiladas, could only eat one of these.  The flavor is mild but absolutely scrumptious!  Thank you so much!
OMG Delicious,So easy to make, creamy and great flavor. I made them just like the recipe stated. These freeze very well. Thank you Deb for this tasty recipe!

I used only a cup of cheese, and added a little bit of scallion cream cheese because I didn't have quite enough sour cream.  I also added a half of a diced red pepper in with the onions that I had on hand.  These were delicious and pretty easy!

These were good chicken enchiladas.  I love the creamy sauce!  I did make a few changes.  I added 1 tsp. cumin and 1 1/2 tsp. chili powder to the chicken & onion mixture as well as a little salt & pepper.  They were very yummy!  Thank you!
Perfect! These are my favorite enchiladas. I left out onions, and they were still great.

Wonderful enchiladas!!
I love it that there is not canned soup in them. These are so creamy and cheesy. I added a diced red bell pepper to the chicken and onions for color. My new favorite!
Thank you, thank you, thank you for a great creamy enchilada and no disgusting cream of anything soup.  Nothing turns me off worse than that.  Great one Deb.
I have made these several times now. great recipe and one of my husbands favorite dishes. Thanks for sharing it with us!

This recipe is incredible! I used 3/4 lb of chicken because there are just the 2 of us, but I made the sauce to the full amount and it ended up being the perfect amnt. I am making them again this evening and am making chicken in the crockpot instead of in the skillet. That way it will shred and be delicious!
I've made chicken enchiladas with cream soups many times. None of them had the wonderful flavor of this recipe. They are simply delicious. A new family favorite!
They worked out great in the crockpot.  A bit of work to make these but they are worth it.

Fabulous!
These came out incredibly tender, juicy and flavorful. You wouldn't believe how it perks up jarred spaghetti sauce.
I used freshly minced garlic in place of the garlic powder and used smoked mozzarella. The hardest part about this dish was waiting the two hours for them to simmer in the sauce, but I'm glad I resisted the urge to pull them out sooner. Will most definitely make this again!
Thanks!   :)
I have made this several times and we love it! After browning I threw them into the crock pot and let them simmer for 4 hours. They were so tender that they cut with a fork. Thanks Holly!

We all loved these to pieces...though no pieces were left. ;o) Picked up some already thinly-sliced round steaks, used 5 cloves of fresh garlic instead of powdered, mixed that with a little very finely sliced celery, and used a jar of artichoke marinara sauce.  Major yummage! They went together very easily, particularly since I threaded a toothpick in each instead of using string. Thank you, Holly!

I browned the meat first and then put it in the crockpot, based on another review, for 4 hours on high.  It could've been the quality of my meat (it was round steak), but it was tough.  The taste was good, but I was disappointed that even though I cooked the meat that long, it still wasn't tender.  I have wanted to make Braciola, so thank you HollyGolightly for the recipe.

I used the very thin cut round steak and pounded it a little to get it even thinner.  I also used two toothpicks to hold each one together. I cooked them in my electric fry pan.  Very good recipe.
Thanks

We really enjoyed this.  I used Gouda cheese, which is what I had on hand. I used the Crockpot method, so all of the cheese melted away into the sauce.  (That's ok though, because I used the leftover sauce in a couple of other dishes like #213935.) The meat was tender and tasty.  Thank you for posting this!

Easy and yummy!  I was bad and bought the premade Braciole from my local butcher, I followed the rest of your directions - the butcher had only put parmesan and parsley in the middle, so I opened each one up and put a slice of cheese in the middle. The DH was in heaven.  He actually had the leftovers for breakfast this morning.

This was good and fork tender. I followed the recipe other then I used fresh garlic instead of garlic powder. I cooked mine on the stove for 2.5 hours and it was so tender. It smelled awesome as it was cooking.

Excellent flavors with this dish.  I used my homemade sauce, the cheese ozzed out into the sauce which made it even better.  Have lots of meat left so will just add more sauce for another meal.  Served with spaghetti, salad and hot Italian bread.
Wow -- Excellent.  My 2 kids could only say YUMMMMM.
This is a basic recipe in my opinion but a good start.
This cake is super!!  It's not really hard to make and everyone who tried it loved it!!!  I have made it three times in the last two weeks because my hubby loves it!!!

recipe looked harder than it is !! It's a great combination of a cheese cake and a carrot cake. I served this up to company, and everyone loved it. I did make a change on the topping, as I thought the frosting might be a little rich on cheesecake. I beat 2 8oz. cream cheese with 1 c. white sugar, then folded in an 8 oz. container of Cool Whip.  It made a nice creamy topping that wasn't too sweet.
Very nice recipe Meagan!
I made this for a friend's birthday and it was wonderful.  Very easy to make and has a wonderful taste.  I will definitely be making this again.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I ate this cheesecake at the Cheesecake Factory and thought it was just so unique and tasty that I had to try to make it for myself.  So for our Pioneer Girls Bake-Off competition I dared to whip it up and it's actually much easier than it appears! So I ended up making a 2nd one (oh darn, I had to eat the first myself!) and this time tweaked the recipe a bit:
1) I added only about 1 TBSP of chopped pineapple, as I thought that maybe it was too wet.
2) After baking for 60 minutes, I reduced the temperature to 300 and added approx. 20 minutes of baking time (I have an electric oven and I certainly didn't want to have a runny middle again!)
3) I made my own glaze of 3 oz. cream cheese, 1 1/2 c. powdered sugar, a dash of milk and just a bit of vanilla.  Then I topped it with chopped walnuts.

Also to note-- this cheesecake is not supposed to have a crust, as the carrot cake actually serves in that function so don't worry that it has no graham crackers.  And alone the cheesecake is quite good, not too sweet and very mild; but with the glaze... whoa watch out for sweetness!  Everyone at the contest was wowed by the idea of it and although I'm not an expert cook and haven't even made a cheesecake in maybe 10 years, I still won first place!
