Followed instructions " to the t". Cake came out so good! Looking good, testing great! Thank you for the recipe. Will definitely continue baking it. One change made- didn't have walnuts so substituted for almonds. Taste great anyway.
The moistest and most amazing dessert ever...!!!! Where has this been all my life!!!??????
make this exactly like the recipe except I did cook on 300 for hour and 15 minutes came out perfect delicious
For the cheesecake, is the 1 t. vanilla in the ingredient list, or 2 t. vanilla in the directions correct? Please note that the word spoonsful is correct, not spoonfuls.
Sounds so good! All these recipes I want to hurry and make them.
This cake was amazing!! Everyone loved it! I made the recipe as is and it was a hit!

Oh my gosh this is good!  I had a little trouble getting the sauce to thicken. I think it may be from eyeballing the amount of chicken broth.  I bought two cans of 10 1/2 ounces each and used one can plus about half. The consistency was good and the sauce started to thicken, but didn't quite set.  When I baked it for 20 minutes, it was runny still but that didn't take away from the taste so I still rate this 5 stars!  I used light sour cream, multigrain tortillas, and ended up using a little more cheese.  Will definately make this again.  I also added garlic salt, and pepper to the sauce for added flavor. Thanks Deb for this great recipe.
DEB!  Thank you sooooo much for this recipe!  I made this for my Once a Month Cooking and OH MY!!  The sauce is to die for! :)  I am in love with this recipe!  How delicious!  Thank you so much!

Thank you soo much for this recipe.  We loved it- easy to make, and tastes so much better with out the canned soup.  We have tried a few different enchilada recipes and by far this is the best one.  Thanks a million!

Delicious!!!  I realized I had no chicken broth once I got started.  All I had was some Campbells Soup at Hand's in chicken noodle.  So I strained those and used that liquid.  Still turned out great!!!

This was nice for a quick and easy dinner, but I guess my family is one of the few who didn't really care for it.  We thought it was kind of plain, with a strong sourcream taste.  The addition of some spices and tomatoes to the chicken to give it a little more flavor would be nice. Thank you for sharing the recipe.
My family really enjoyed the flavor of these enchiladas.  The bonus for me was such a simple recipe, and ingredients that I typically have on hand.  Thanks for sharing!
Thank you for not including soup.  There are too many recipes with soup in it any more.

I used 6 tortillas, much less cheese, and seasoned the chicken with cumin and pepper.  The sauce was excellent, creamy and nicely seasoned from the green chiles.  Next time I try this recipe, I will reduce the sour cream a little or sub a reduced-fat sout cream.  I also think this would be really good with some black beans and red or yellow bell peppers added to the filling to boost the nutrition.
This recipe was WONDERFUL!! I made these and froze them for when we had a new baby. I defrosted completely and cooked as directed. They were great. A new fav! Thanks.
Loved these!  I cooked ahead and froze them, had them for dinner about a week later.  They were great, thanks for sharing!

This is really a great recipe. I LOVE that fact that there's no soup in it. The roux made it really great. The only think I changed was I added about 1 Tbls. of diced jalapeno peppers from a jar. It really added some great extra flavor and a just a TINY bit of kick. I'm already thinking about ways to alter it to make it into my own cream of chicken tortilla SOUP, LOL!

I have been looking for "this" recipe for years. Thank you for posting!  Since I prefer corn to flour tortillas, I made  four of each, then placed one of each (flour/corn) in each of four small casseroles.  One casserole eaten and it was delicious; three frozen.

This was wonderful! Very easy to put together and very tasty!  I followed the recipe except that I used two cans of chopped green chilies and a package of ChiChi's fiesta seasoning.  I also took the advice of another reviewer and after the chicken cubes were cooked, put into the food processer.  It was so filling!!

These are truly fantastic!  I doubled the recipe and cooked the chicken breasts ahead of time in the crockpot.  This also produced a wonderful broth, which I was able to use for the sauce.  I sauteed the shredded chicken with the onion, but next time I might even just add the onion to the crockpot.  Preparing the chicken (and resulting broth) in the crockpot made this a snap to put together at the end of the day.  Plus, by doubling the recipe, I was able to freeze a pan of them for later!  This has quickly become one of my family's favorites.

These were okay.... I fixed them for super tonight and my husband and I both ate them but they weren't really anything we could brag about.... Maybe trying some of the others advice and adding seasoning to the chicken mixture and the sauce would make a difference next time.... Thanks for sharing though....

These were great.  I agree with some of the other reviewers that the chicken could use some spicing or tomatoes or salsa or something, but the sauce was wonderful!  I will definitely make these again, since I'm always on the lookout for great freezer compatible dishes.
I liked the broth/sour cream sauce and added spices to chicken. Kids liked it.

My family and I simply love this. To the chicken mixture I add sweet red pepper either cut into strips or chopped and I add about 1 tsp (heaping or not) cumin as well. For the cheese I used Black Diamond Bistro shredded cheese, the mexican blend. The only other change I made was to use 2 cans of green chilies. I found it took away the "heavy" sour cream taste. Thanks for the great recipe.

These were very good, however I added a lot of chili powder and cumin to the chicken and sauce. I didn't have Mexican cheese and used sharp cheddar  Much easier than other recipes I have and they taste just as good.  I did freeze a batch and they didn't look very good, but they tasted great!

There was a small Mexican restaurant that used to make this and they were my favorite.  They didn't make it through Hurrican Ivan so I've been trying to find something similar. This hit the mark. We've made this several times and each time it's delish. The first time we made exactly as the recipe and it was wonderful.  Although we've only managed to make 4 enchiladas.  The second time we added a second can of green chilies and it was even better.  Last night we made it and I realized I didn't have any chilies and so I added a couple slices of jalepenos and it was still good. Thank you for a fantasic recipe for a favorite of mine.

Good, but I modified it for my convenience. I made a 9x9 pan for supper (6 tortillas) and froze a 9x6 pan (5 tortillas) for later. I used a batch of homemade cream soup instead of the white sauce, then added just 8 oz. of chicken broth. Added more flavor by liberally sprinkling cooked chicken mixture with cumin and chili powder. Turned out to be flavorful and just saucy enough.

A very easy recipe to put together for a quick meal.  I was drawn to the recipe because there was no canned cream soup in it...   My BF loves sour cream and I had some chicken breasts in the refrigerator that needed to be cooked up so this looked really good.  However, I thought there was something missing in the chicken filling.  To me, it was just kind of flat... I couldn't put my finger on it.  The sour cream sauce was good... but a bit rich for us.  All in all, we liked it but might try experimenting with spicing up the chicken filling a bit more next time.  Thanks for sharing!

This is an awesome recipe. Everytime my family and I go home to visit my mom talks me into making these (I'm from a family of 10 so I have to triple the recipe). I use salt pepper and season salt to season the chicken, no green chilis for me. We also used cheddar and jack cheese. The one thing I would suggest is to triple the sauce on this recipe because it doesn't make much sauce. Well, not enough for me anyway. I do make this recipe alot though because it is a fave for me.

these were pretty good! i baked my chicken first and sauteed the onions and combined them after and then made them as written and it turned out very tasty! i used a can of rotel chiles and tomatoes drained instead to make it a little more mild beause 4 oz of chiles is kind of too hot for my taste.

This was amazing!!  I surprised my DH with it and he loved it.  I found it very easy to make, and the only substitution I made was using olive oil instead of vegetable oil to cook the chicken.  Will definitely make this recipe again.  Thanks Deb!

Tried this last night and my husband was thrilled, i added a fresh jalapeno to the chicken to add a little spice and then topped them with fresh salasa right before serving! this is a great recipe and easy to make.
Thanks again!

All I can say about this recipe is WOW! I made it for a Mexican Themed Party and it was really easy to make. I doubled the recipe, used onion powder instead of onions, and used some pre-cooked shredded chicken I had frozen plus the diced chicken. I also used freshly roasted green chilies that I diced really finely. I had one LITTLE tiny problem.... I made it the morning of the party and put it in a disposable tin pan with a layer of foil between the pan and the plastic lid. When I got to the party and put it in the oven..... Well, I forgot to take the plastic lid off! It's great to know those things just melt down into a hard plastic square and don't burst into flames! Good thing there was a foil lining too or I might have ruined this FABULOUS dish that everyone loved!

I made this today. My family really liked it. I liked it because it did not use condensed soup. (which I love) I need to watch my sodium intake, so this was a plus. I also used my own chicken stock. I will add more seasonings the next time I make this.(Probably garlic powder and cumin as someone else did). I did put a tiny bit of chili powder this time. The recipe was good, but for my family we want a tad bit more seasoning. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

I gave it 5 stars for the sour cream sauce...sooooo yummy!  I mades some changes with the chicken filling though.  I added salsa, a little bit of chicken broth, cumin, oregano, and garlic powder to give it a little more flavor.  I also used corn tortillas instead of flour, as thats what I prefer.  Thanks for the recipe!
This was simple, delicious and satisfying!  I used low fat sour cream to cut the fat content a bit, and used whole wheat flour.

These were wonderful! I did add some cumin, a few hunks of fresh tomatoes (using what is left from the garden) and chili powder to the chicken mixture. I also used pepper jack cheese, and added that to the chicken mix before wrapping them in the tortillas. DBF thought that browning the butter and flour mixture would make it taste better, and he was right! When it was golden brown, we added the chicken broth, sour cream and chilies. I know this sounds like we changed a lot, but really, we didn't. This will be one of my favorite mexican dishes from now on, and we will serve it to company anytime. Fantastic! I wish I could give it 10 stars! Thanks so much for posting this recipe!

Very good, I like the fact that no "cream of" soup is in this dish. I tossed some chicken breasts with salsa in the crockpot the day before to make this dish even easier to assemble.  I used corn tortillas, and a mixture of pepper jack and colby cheese. After tasting the sauce, I added a bit of cumin and chili powder, next time I will add more green chilies.  I was pleasantly surprized on how good this dish is.  I ate way too much (thanks alot).  This is a definate repeater for us!
I loved all the flavors going on in this dish.  Great taste, and an easy recipe with just the right amount of everything.  Loved it Deb's!
This is the best chicken enchilada recipe I've ever tried!  Whole family loved it and the kids have even asked me to make it again. Thank you for posting it.

This was a wonderful recipe. Rich and creamy, easy to prepare. Served with MexiCorn and a salad.
Thanks for a keeper, Deb.
Okay, this was work but worth the effort.  The only thing I did different was leave out the green chilies (since I can not buy them here).  I doubled the recipe and now have one in the freezer!
best chicken enchiladas ever!
Good, but the sour cream over powered the taste.
The overall taste was very good. The sour cream sauce was a nice touch to these enchilladas. Very easy and quick to put together. This recipe is a definite keeper.

Thank you! It is a complete pleasure to see recipes WITHOUT canned cream of crap soup or powdered onion soup! 
Thanks!!!
A++++ yummy

Good stuff!!  Probably didn't add a whole onion with chicken, but I added a can of rotel and some pace in the white sauce in the end.  So it probably evened out.  Otherwise made as written.  I wanted just a little more heat.  It was just a tad spicy, just the way I like it.  I think that it was better than many restaurants.  It was also very fast to prepare.  I cooked it about 25 minutes.  Will be making again soon.

This was ok.  I definitely should have added some spices to both the chicken mixture, and the sour cream mixture... it was too bland for my taste!  I was also hoping for more of the green chili taste to come through.  Next time I will buy some green enchilada sauce and incorporate that into it.  DH and DSS said these were okay, but not like the green enchiladas I usually make.

I loved these! They are super mild and creamy. I do think next time I will add a pinch of spice such as cumin to the sauce at least. My hubby just gobbled them up! It's a real keeper!! I wanted to add that I used 10" tortillas and got six HUGE enchiladas that easily filled a 9x13 pan. I also used about 3/4 cup sour cream because it was all I had in my container. I KNOW I will make these again, and again. Oh, I had already boiled my chicken breasts, so I just cooked up my onions and mixed them together. I will always do that. I hate messing with cutting up raw chicken.YUK.
1/22/08 
Made them again tonight and added about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of chunky mild salsa and it made a huge taste improvement. It definitely added more flavor.

We really enjoyed this and it was easy to put together. I did find the flavor to be a bit bland, but the rest of the family had no complaints. It is good that there was no cream soup! (Sometimes I try to limit such things.) I served it with a packaged green salad kit (Mexican/taco style, not sure of the name) which went well. Next time I might try using a "regular" chicken broth (I used Swanson's Natural Goodness, which is what I always buy, but it is lower sodium - might have contributed to my sense of "blandness").

Made these last night and they are the BOMB! I made 1/2 times more sauce and added that to the chicken before filling the tortillas.  I filled an 8x8 pan and had for dinner and filled another 8x8 and it's in the freezer for dinner another night.  Dd (age 6) loved them and dh was still talking about them when we went to bed. Thank you!

These were great!  Made as directed but used leftover chicken and everone loved it!  
They are very mild but good.  The chicken I used was chicken cooked in crockpot with a can of rotel & a packet of taco seasoning, then shredded so that added some flavor.  If you want spicy, serve with jalapeno slices on top.  Thanks!  This is a great recipe!
This was great.  I used thigh meat instead of breast, more favorful and cheaper.

These are a really good mild enchilada. I loved all the extra sour cream sauce to top over the enchilada & mexican rice that I served with it. Next time I'm going to make these vegetarian with vegetable broth & black beans. I think the sour cream sauce will really go great with it.

Oh my!  My husband LOVES these!!  He requests them every week!  i cook my chicken in a crock pot for about 8 hours first-- then shred it.  My husband likes them made with a little bit of jalapenos.  I also add a little bit of chicken broth to the bottom of the greased dish-- prevents the bottom of the enchilada from getting "tough".  I also add a bit more cheese since we like them cheesey!!  Fantastic recipe-- thanks fro sharing!!

These were wonderful and I was told by several people I should have doubled the recipe!  I made it exactly as written except I made 1 1/2 the amount of sauce.  I was blessed to find monterey jack in slices so it was ultra easy to prepare with one slice per enchilada and then covered the top of the enchiladas with a layer of slices. Awesome!! Thank you so much for sharing!
We loved these and will definately make again!  Thank you for sharing.

These were simple and delicious. I took the advice of earlier reviews and added cumin and chili powder to the chicken and the sauce. Personally I think it would benefit from more green chilies too, maybe even some freshly roasted hatch chilies from the farmers market!

Thanks, we loved it.  My husband said, "This is even better than the Mexican casserole".  The same Mexican casserole that he couldn't get enough of last week...  Like another reviewer, I only used 4 tortillas.  I  seasoned the chicken with dried cilantro, salt & pepper before cooking.  To top it off we added several dashes of Tabasco Chipotle sauce, yum, it hit the spot.

My DH just raved about this dish.  It is so tasty :)  I did add a little cumin and chili powder as suggested by a couple of reviewers.  Also used a large can of green chile's. This will definitely go into our favorite recipe file.

Awesome recipe.  I'd be giving it 5 stars except that I think the other reviewers hit the nail on the head.  This would be relatively bland and creamy if you failed to add the cumin, cilantro, and a clove or so of garlic to the recipe.  Definitely a keeper with the modifications.  Thanks for sharing!
This recipe is great!  I did add the spices as suggested by the other reviewers and it turned out excellent.  My family raved about these enchiladas! Thank you for sharing!

Wow! This was really incredible...better than a mexican restaurant!  I did tweak it abit.  Added garlic, hot and spicy taco seasoning mix to the chicken while cooking.  Added a can of diced tomatoes with zesty chilies...a few jalapenos (we like things spicy!) some leftover corn we had, red pepper flakes, cumin.  In the white sauce I sprinkled a little chipotle seasoning...this was incredible.  I only used 1 can of the chilies would probably use 2 next time.  There were no leftovers...I will be making this again this weekend for our DD's recital...thank you sooo much for one of the best recipes I've made on Zaar!  Try this ....you won't be sorry!!!

Very nice! Instead of the roux and chicken broth I substituted a can of green enchilada sauce, mixed in the sour cream & green chilies and covered the enchiladas.  It was tangy and lovely, and we topped it with pickled sliced jalapenos for some spice.
Great recipe!

Well, I don't know if I can fairly rate the recipe as is,but I think it is worth 5 stars. I substituted 1 lb. ground turkey for the chicken and stirred in a 14oz. can of enchilada sauce in with the turkey and onion mixture. Delicious.
These are VERY good. Will make them again and again. Thanks for the recipe.
Fantastic! They are very filling, i could probably make a meal out of a half of one.
These were the best chicken enchiladas I have ever made.  Thanks for the recipe.  We both enjoyed them very much.

Excellent Dish.  I made this tonight for the first time and was worried that the sauce would taste like flour....because I have made enchiladas that didn't turn out well in the past.  These were very good.  My husband added a little salsa to his....but other than that - followed the recipe exactly and was a big hit.  Thank you for a great meal.
This is an awesome recipe!! My husband LOVES it and so do my 2 boys.  They ask for it.  Simply delicious and easy to make!!!!

This is the greatest enchilada recipe!! I am so glad I found a good recipe that doesn't use condensed soup! So delicious and very easy to make, everyone enjoyed it! Definitely a keeper and will make often!

Theses were great. Instead of adding chopped green chilies I added about 1/2 c of mild green enchilada sauce to my creamy topping mixture. This made a nice smooth creamy topping with wonderful flavor. This recipe puts the chicken enchiladas to shame at my favorite restaurant, and it is soooo inexpensive to make.

Very, very, nice.  I chose this because it did not have any canned soup in the recipe.  My husband gave this a 10.5.  This was the lst. time anything had gone higher than a 10!  One thing I had to change was the cooking method because of starving family.  I zapped them in the micro. for several mins.  This worked out so well, I will use this method again.  Thank you!

YUM.  My daughter even ate the Onions!   had extra meat and onions left over and she was starving so  I so I rolled two taco's & placed in the toaster oven at 350 for about 5 min until crisp.  I put the sauce over the top.  AWESOME.  Like a Chimi but not fried!

These are great comfort food!  We got back from the pool this afternoon and were all starving.  I whipped these up quickly, as I had all of the ingredients on hand.  I had made a chicken the night before, so we just used up the shredded chicken.  Only real differences were that I added salsa to the chicken mixture, and then used low fat sour cream.  I also used homemade chicken stock (from yesterday's crock pot chicken!) and left the green chilies out.  No major differences here, and boy were they yummy!!  I will definately be keeping this recipe and probably next time add it to my freezer rotation!  Thanks for the great recipe!
This is abosolutely my favorite enchilada recipe.  I do season the chicken with some additional spices prior to adding to the tortillas, but LOVE the sauce and so easy to make.

Oh my gosh, that was good! I'm not much of a cook (trying to learn!), but this made me look so good! Since I wasn't able to dice the chicken quite as small as I wanted, I cut into small pieces, cooked it (no onions - someone in our house won't eat them), and then put it into my food processor for just a few pulses to make it perfect for filling. Followed the rest exactly, and it was absolutely heaven, and I'm usually not a huge fan of chicken. The sauce is to die for! Thank you for sharing this delicious and easy recipe!  ***Update*** Still a fabulous recipe, even with reduced fat sour cream and cheese, whole wheat tortillas and using canned chicken breast, making it a little healthier. Sticking to one enchilada per serving but with low-fat refried beans still made this filling but somewhat diet friendly. Very, very yum. I keep coming back to this recipe.

yum, yum, yum!  much better than the ones with canned soup.  i added some garlic to the chicken, just because i like it, and some cumin and chili powder like someone else suggested.  i also used a can of tomatoes with green chilies just because that's what i had.  i also made homemade wheat flour tortillas for these and substituted 1/3 of the sour cream for plain yogurt in attempts to make healthier.  thanks for a great recipe!

I added in some Mexican rice with the chicken for added flavor and it came out really delicious!  I also added some cumin and chili powder for more flavor.  Very yummy!  Thank you for sharing your recipe with us!
Awesome recipe.  Tastes like going out for Mexican.  Thanks!

Resubmitting my review and giving it another star!! While I still think it needs "spicing up", it is way, way tastier reheated the next day. Go figure, but the creamy white sauce kind of melds together and is very, very good. Thanks Deb, for a very good enchiladas recipe. Pretty easy on the pocketbook, too.

Super delicious!!! I've made this four times now and my family wouldn't argue if I made it once a week!  I used a rotisserie chicken that I pulled apart and the texture was heavenly.  Added some lime juice, cumin, salt and pepper, and the sauteed onion to the meat and followed the rest exactly.  Panicked a little the first time because I thought it was going to be a soupy mess when I poured the sauce over top.  Thankfully, it was not too wet at all once it badked.  The textures and flavors were perfect and it definitely reheats extremely well.  Broiled about 3-4 minutes at the end to brown the cheese a bit.  This is my favorite Recipezaar venture to date.  Thanks for posting this.

Instead of 1 can of green chilies I added 1 can Rotel tomatoes with green chilies.  Gave it just enough flavor to really tickle our tastebuds!  We REALLY loved this casserole!  Thanks for sharing it with us!

This receipe is wonderful!  I have made it several times and saved it on my computer, which crashed and it took me awhile to find it again. I am printing it out for sure!  Best chicken enchiladas I've ever had.  Husband & Kids agree!

I was very skeptical when my husband decided to make this dish. However, first bite...was not impressed (must've been the sour cream taste?!) But by second bite I was hooked and wished that we had made more :) Thank you for sharing such a great recipe that we will making again and again!!! Since first trying this recipe, we have turned many of our friends onto this style of enchiladas, as we tend to make these when we have company.  And then they ask for the recipe every single time! A little change I started doing to the dish, was adding refried beans inside along with the chicken, I felt it added a little something. I also started cooking the chicken in taco or fajita seasoning, whatever I had on hand. I really enjoyed the flavor a whole lot more! My girlfriend still thanks me for finding this recipe, they love it as much as we do!!

I followed the recipe, howver I used corn tortillas and low fat cream cheese. OH My was this fantastic!!  all I can say is YummY...everyone loved it ans the leftovers were gone the next day. keeper recipe.

This was so easy and delicious!!  I think next time I might add a little bit of spice to the chicken, or add green peppers. But overall it was wonderful, love the fact that there is no cream of anything in it!!!!
My family really enjoyed these enchiladas!  It was a perfect weekday meal very quick and easy!  Will be making them again!!
Wow, great enchilada recipe.  Everyone said it was the best homemade enchiladas they had had.  Sadly, no leftovers for lunch today!  Good recipe to double and freeze one portion.

Made this yesterday - it was very easy, and had wonderful taste!  Used the Shredded Chicken... (recipe #169500) for the chicken filling, and used Flour Tortillas (recipe #65491) and Corn Tortillas (Recipe #50820).  Did half the dish with the flour tortillas, and half with the corn tortillas, and both were great!  This sauce was fantastic on both - used light sour cream, and light/low sodium chicken broth, and you wouldn't know I used anything light!!  Definitely a keeper!!

If I could give this recipe a 10, I would. It was so tasty!! And, it was simple enough that my husband was  able to make it. (He doesn't cook very often.) We used grilled chicken strips and low fat sour cream. We loved that it had no soup for its ingredients. Thank you, thank you, thanks you. This will go in my personal favorites cookbook!

YUM!  I made this a few months ago for the first time, and forgot to write a review... Sorry!  It was very easy to put together, but the results were impressive!  The only thing I did different was to use wheat tortillas, and they worked great!  Thanks for the great recipe!

Giving this 5 stars, based on the reviews of 3 dinner companions (and me)! Personally, I would prefer this to be a bit saucier, but it is terrific as is. I used 2 cans of chicken breast because I was in a hurry, skipped the sauteeing with onion part and just sprinkled some onion powder, cumin and chili powder on the meat. Also, I used whole wheat tortillas. Otherwise, made exactly as written. Absolutely delicious. Next time will make 2 batches and throw one in the freezer! Thanks so much for sharing!

This recipe turned out excellent!  The secret to this recipe is the sour cream sauce. 

The best sour cream chicken enchiladas I have had were at El Fenix here in Fort Worth.  This recipe comes closer than I expected.  I took the liberty of doctoring the chicken by cooking it in a pressure cooker and adding 1 tsp. of cumin, 1/2 tsp. cayenne pepper, and 1 tsp. of chili powder with the onion and oil.  Although my chicken turned out okay, I feel it could be improved.

This recipe is so valuable for the sauce alone.  I will keep checking to see what improvements others have made.  What a great recipe to play with!
These were good, but I didn't have the chiles, so the sauce was a bit bland, but still tasted very good.  Very rich.

yum! i had made Recipe #4957 and doubled that recipe so i could have a couple nights of tacos and then make the enchiladas, it turned out so good. i was kind of worried that the sauce would be bland but it was really good. i followed the directions exactly, aside from starting with the pre cooked chicken. i did saute the onions and a couple cloves of garlic a bit then added the chicken to heat through before assembling the enchiladas. we will make this again for sure! thanks for sharing the recipe. :)
Great recipe! I wish it would have told me to shred the chicken finely- the family said the diced chicken was hard to chew. I also chopped a bell pepper and sprinkled it on top for color and flavor.

I think this was a great base recipe, but I doctored up the flavour quite a bit because it seemed a bit bland to me...added some mexican spices and garlic to the chicken, and ended up adding cheese to the sauce.  I also made a vegetarian version at the same time with some veggie ground round (TVP) and it was great.  Thanks!!
Five stars all the way.  We loved these and will make this dish many times over.  I served this with spanish rice and refried beans with tortilla chips.  Thank y ou for a simple chicken dish.

This was a wonderful dish! The only changes I made were that I used milk instead of chicken broth for the sauce. I also added some hot sauce and other spices to the sauce to give it more zest. We loved this recipe though and will definitely make it again! :)

OMG!!! This was soooooo good!!! Not only did my picky three year old LOVE it so did my husband who doesn't exactly care for Mexican food!  I did add chili powder, a teeny bit of red pepper flakes, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to the chicken though.  Still this is something I will make again and again and again!
These came out perfect!! Thanks for the recipe!

These were DELISH! I was worried about them not having enough salt, but they came out perfect with the combo of ingredients.  I bought a deli rotisserie chicken, making this super easy.  Then I just added the chopped onion to the roux with the chilies.  They came together in under 20 minutes, making this a great meal to throw together after work. Thanks!

I was looking for a recipe for sour cream chicken enchiladas; and, since I was away from home (and my recipe file), I looked on Recipezaar, and found this one.  Although it looks similar to a fav one I have, it seemed to lack something, in the finished product.  I appreciated the lack of "cream" soups; however, my family thought it tasted gummy and plain (even though I spiced up the chicken, with some cumin and chili powder, as some reviewers suggested).  Looks like most people enjoyed it more than we did; but thanks, anyway, for the help away from home.

With the addition of cumin and chili powder we ate these right up.  My DS's all loved it, and that's unusual in my family!  We will have this often and it's headed to my favorites so I know where it is!  Thanks

This was REALLY GOOD!! I used corn tortillas and mixed cheddar and jack cheeses. The chicken I used was previously cooked and shredded. I added some chili verde inside the tortillas with the chicken, and more to the sauce for a bump in flavor. An excellent alternative to using "Cream Of..." soup. Leftovers were great!!

This was my first time making enchiladas and let me tell you, it was much easier than I had andicipated. I put refried beans in side the tortilla with the chicken. These were so good that my boy friend would not let me share the leftovers with anyone!
These were great and easy to make. Thanks so much!

We loved your Enchiladas!  I liked how easy the recipe went together.  The cream sauce is yummy.  Only change I made was to add some taco seasoning and cilantro while frying up the chicken and onion mixture.   Thanks, Deb, for posting.
Fabulous! Everyone loves these! I would not change a single thing.
I love this recipe. I have made it several times. If someone is looking for enchiladas with something other then the traditional red sauce that is mild but flavorful I recommend this.

These were fantastic.  For kosher reasons we had to make these vegetarian style.  We substituted the chicken for yellow rice, green peppers, and onions but we kept the rest the same.  The recipe was great I loved the sauce but my DH wasn't as fond of it.  But he still loved the dish as a whole.

WILL MAKE AGAIN!!
We absolutely love this recipe! I made it for my in-laws using pepper jack cheese. It was a hit! Thanks for posting!!

Delicious!  I cooked the chicken in my crockpot with a can of rotel and a packet of taco seasoning on low for about 5 or 6 hours so the chicken shredded and fell apart easily.  I doubled the recipe and was able to get 1 9x13 dish (which fed my dinner party of 6) and then another 9x9 to freeze for later.  I also used both flour and corn tortillas.  I think that I like the corn better.  I would have been able to get 2 9x13 dishes had I added a pound of chicken.  Another reviewer was right.  This does taste like the sour cream enchillads at El Fenix.  I've been ordering those my entire life.  It's my favorite dish.  I will for sure be making these again.  I'm going to try low fat sour cream to see if I can get the same flavor.
I used jalapenos and chiles in adobo sauce instead of green chiles.  This was an excellent dish. I will definitely make these again.
We loved them!

This was an excellent recipe.  I followed someone else's advice and added 1 tsp of cumin and 1 1/2 tsp of chili powder as well as salt and pepper to the cooking chicken and onion mixture.  After the chicken/onion mixture was done cooking, I drained off the liquid and added 1/2 a block of cream cheese and 1/2 cup of sour cream to it before filling the tortillas with it, just for American flair (if you've ever had Carlos O'Kelleys Chicken Enchiladas de Poblano, you know where I was going with this).  These were absolutely amazing.  Thank you for the great recipe!

I liked these and found them easy to prepare.  However, my husband thought they needed a little something.  Maybe the addition of seasonings other than the salt/pepper I used on the chicken would have been helpful.  I also tend to like a little of the creamy stuff inside the enchiladas.

Finally a real creamy sour cream enchillada done right. I use jalepenos rather than chiles. The sour cream sauce can absorb into the tortillas over night, so if you cannot eat all of this at once, rather than baking it, it's best to simply microwave a tortilla open face with the chicken, onion, jalepenos, and cheese for 1.5 minutes. Then roll into enchillada and top with sour cream sauce. That way you are not left with subpar leftovers.

These are just like the ones at Teds Cafe Escondido in OKC where folks travel in from out of state and wait 2 hrs to get in.  

PS. Rating this recipe down because it's bland is silly. As with any recipe you spice to taste. If you're a spice person, you know to add more when making something.

This was really good the first time I made it, so I made another one to freeze. When I cooked it a few weeks later, it had lost some of it's flavor and was almost mushy so I think I will stick to making it the day we plan on eating it.

Wonderful!!!  I have never made enchiladas and my boyfriend has been bugging me to make some.  I spent about a week looking for a recipe.  This recipe is so easy to make!  I did make some minor changes.  I saw another review that added chili powder and cumin.  That added a lot of flavor to the chicken.  I also boiled the chicken and put it in a food processor to shred it. Then I put it in a pan with the onion.  The only complaint was that I had put too much onion in it.  I would also suggest adding salt to the sauce.  This will definitely be something I make again!!!

Excellent!  The only change made was to add a pinch of salt to the sauce.  I used green chilies that I had frozen last summer.  I don't know if canned chilies have salt added or not.  I think I will season the chicken next time I make them.  Thanks for an easy, delicious recipe!

Absolutely great.  It was my first introduction to real enchiladas, so I thank Anacoana25 very much!  I've made these a number of times, and now I do a few things different than the recipe.  1)  Corn tortillas instead of flour.  2) Up the roux mix and leave out the sour cream :)   Guess you'd have to change the name eh?
These were yummy and SO SO easy! Thanks for the great post!

My family LOVES these! I use homemade tortillas when I make them and also once i cook the chicken i put it in my food processor and chop it up to make it more like a shredded chicken type enchilada that you would get at a restaurant. I also put some of the sauce inside the tortilla with the chicken and the cheese. They come out awesome every time! Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

I love this recipe! It is so easy and quick to make and everything is on hand in the kitchen except for the tortillas. I stretched it out a little bit and used 10 tortillas and served it with salsa on the side, came out perfect! I will definitely be making this again. Thanks.

Not only have I made this several times, but my three daughters have also made it.  They are 13, 10, and 7, and once a week they pick a receipe and make it.  It is SUPER easy even for them.  When I am cooking the chicken, I usually throw a can of enchilada sauce into the pan, it gives some added falvor without adding any work.  It is a TREMENDOUS recipe for adults and kids alike.  Great job!

These were great! I had some friends over for a Mexican themed meal and this was very good. After reading some of the other reviews I decided to spice up the chicken a bit - I added a couple shakes of taco seasoning and some red pepper flakes. I also only used half an onion. These were delicious, and served with some yellow rice (I used Zatarain's boxed yellow rice for time/convenience) this recipe is yummy. Thanks for posting!

YAY! I love this recipe. I've made it twice for my family and friends now. Thank you so much. I looked up a bunch of different recipes for these type of enchiladas and this seemed like it would be the best. I was right, it was the best. I found that the flavor when you bit into the enchiladas was lacking a bit but I remedied this by adding some of the sour cream sauce to the chicken and onions.

Yummy.  My whole family enjoyed this recipe.  I froze 1/2 of it to enjoy later.  Easy to make.
Catherine
This is so very simple, yet delicious.  This was a big hit at dinner last night, and will be made again!
Good basic chicken enchiladas. Thanks for sharing!

Three words:  TO DIE FOR!
I can't believe anything so easy to make could taste this good!  I also added the tsp. of cumin and a tsp. of chili powder for a little extra spice, but I also made it without too.  Either way, they were both so yummy! Thank you for sharing such a awesome recipe!

these are getting 3 stars from me and 5 from DH. i used corn tortillas, as we try to avoid white flour in our home... i added chili powder and garlic powder to the chicken and onion mix but found the chicken a bit bland still. also, the sauce is kind of bland. ...i think i would've put even more sour cream in if i would've known how bland it would be. they just tasted like something was missing to me, but i couldn't quite put my finger on it.
DH loved them, however. he likes things a bit simpler than i do.
This was a little bland for my tastes. May recommend adding some spices to both the chicken and the sauce.

This was such an easy and delicious dinner. I followed the recipe with a few exceptions. I added some Amazing Taste fajita seasoning to the chicken and onion mixture. I also eliminated the green chilies as I thought that would deter my kids from eating it. My 5 year old, who is the pickiest of us all, ate her entire enchilada plus a quarter of another one.
This was a huge hit! Thanks for sharing.

This was yummy.  I only made a couple of changes as per some other reviews.  I sauteed the onions in olive oil to soften, then added chicken tenders and a can of stewed tomatoes with some homemade chicken broth.  After the chicken had poached, I shredded it and added about 1/2 of a can of refried beans.  I forgot to add the cheese, so just sprinkled it on top.  I followed the rest of the recipe as written.  All of my non-vegetarian family loved it!  Thanks!

very quick and easy recipe.  I was in search of something new and this hit the spot.  I did not have everything on hand so I did alter it a bit.  I was out of chicken broth so I substituted beef broth for it and I didn't have any Mexican blend cheese so I used colby Jack.  I also did not add chilies as my kids don't like them.  Even with all the substitutions I would give it a 5 star.  I can't wait to try it following the recipe exactly!  thanks for posting it.

This is a very yummy recipe,Deb! I made this and froze individual portions for my DH and his friend to take on a photography trip to the Southwest and froze the rest for us when he got back. The sauce is to-die-for good and is what makes this dish, in my opinion! I used whole wheat with green onion tortillas. Thanks for posting this- it's a keeper!
My whole family loves this recipe! I always use any left over chicken in this instead of cooking some. Great recipe!
Great recipe.  I have to freeze meals for my husband to take with him since he lives out of state.  These came out perfect and are great for freezing.  We love them and can't wait to make them again.

This recipe should of been in the top 100 for 2008!  
Excellent taste, easy to assemble, great for leftovers and the fact there is no soup in the recipe drastically cut down on the sodium content.  This is a recipe that can be great on its own or for the cretive cook, one can alter to make it even more spectacular.  A true blue ribbon winner!

Loved this recipe!  I added a tiny bit of cumin to the chicken while it was cooking...this is a great dish, one I will make again, and again, and....well, you get the picture.  My husband and 4 kids devoured it!

Awesome! After reading the other reviews, I sauteed the onions first in butter, then the chicken with an extra can of chilis, diced tomatoes, 1/2 frozen corn, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder (will add 3 tsp next time), 1 tsp garlic salt, and 1/2 tsp oregano. Delicious!!! Thank you, Deb!

As I always do the first time I try a new recipe I follow it to a t! This was wonderful, made it for my son's 28th birthday.  I love the fact that there isn't any cream soup in it, I've made a chicken enchilda before with the soup and this is so much better.  I would probably add some chiles next time just to give it more heat.  I wasn't sure that everyone would have enjoyed that so made it just like it was.  Will be making this again for sure.

I made these for Cinco de Mayo and they were wonderful. I added a tablespoon of miced cilantro, 1/2 tsp cumin and 1/2 tsp of chili powder  to the sauce. I will be using this recipe from now on. SO good. Thank you for posting.
Really nice flavor! I may add the cumin and chili powder next time for a change, but we will definitely be making these again. Thanks!
Fabulous!

I tweaked this a bit and loved it. The sauce I made a little differently. I added 1/2 packet of taco seasoning to it once it was thick and bubbly and then added the sour cream and about 8 diced pickled jalepenos and a can of drained,diced tomatoes with onions and green peppers. Oh yum is that sauce good :) I used 2 bouillon cubes in 15 oz of water since I was out of chicken broth as well. For the Chicken I used Rotisserie chicken (BBQ) seasoned with garlic/herb Mrs.Dash and a little cajun seasoning. I shredded it up in the food processor after it was warmed in the saute pan with the onion and oil. Topped the tortillas with meat mixture and mild cheddar cheese (what I had on hand) and rolled and poured sauce over the rolled enchiladas and topped everything off with the remaining cheese. Yum! I love this sauce...TY for a base idea to get me started.

I'm sorry, but these were nasty. I know how to make a roux, etc., and the sauce seemed promising when I put it in the oven. But when the dish came out, the sauce got "funny" after only a couple minutes. I refrigerated leftovers and heated some up for lunch today and -- disgusting, couldn't even eat it. The sauce itself needs to have cheese melted in to give it a better consistency; I will not be making these again. Sorry.

I have not tried this recipe yet, but I am going to. Looking at the ingred., it would have been my guess that it poss. would need something. (at least spices)

Ingred:
chicken, onion, tortillas, cheese 
/ butter-flour, chicken broth-sour cream, green chilies

But here is why I am writing: 
The chef stated: "There is NO canned cream soup in my enchiladas." 

(Other than added spices), could it be that it IS the "missing something, but can't put my finger on it" ingredient?

Also, as most experienced cooks know: A can of cream soup can add "consistency" to ingrediants of this type, and also add a little more flavoring.

And think about it, it would give even more options to play with, besides playing with the spices.

Cream of Chicken, Golden Mushroom, Cream of Mushroom (etc.), might be able to even find some type of "Mexican" style cream soup.  

This chef obviously has a great base recipe, no doubt.

But I, for one, am not only going to play with the spices (possibly different spices, on different days), I am also going to play in the cream of soup isle, too. I am going to double the fun. The possibilities are endless!

Again, congratulations to this chef, and I cannot wait to play. 

This recipe (as a base) is a "goldmine", and the endless possibilities are bits of gold.

This is a great recipe and a perfect alternative to the canned soup version my mom used to make. I agree that, as is, there is not enough flavor. I always add garlic powder, chili powder and cumin (and maybe a little cayenne) in with the chicken. And, I add chicken bouillon to the sauce---it's really bland as is.

This is a great recipe...but I've made a few changes that I prefer. I like to add some shrimp in with the chicken and for the sauce substitute a can of enchilada sauce to mix with the sour cream.....sooooooo good!

This tasted like a dish from a fantastic Mexican restaurant! Even my foster son loved it- and he is a picky eater. He is Mexican and usually cringes when he hears I am going to cook Mexican food- he says I can't cook Mexican food like a real Mexican. I guess I can cook Mexican dishes after all now thanks to this great recipe-it is delicious! Thanks!

This is an excellent recipe for enchiladas. I am not much for enchuladas being too spicy(heartburn central) but this was very mild and oh so very good. Thanks for such an easy and delicious recipe. I will definitely be making this a few times a month. :)

WARNING: Once you start, you can't stop!! This was sooo comfort-food-good. DH and I ate 2/3 of this by ourselves tonight!! >>blush!<< We didn't have the canned chillies, so I substituted two "medium" green chillies & 1 whole orange bell pepper (pureed together). Very good enchiladas.  I made half a recipe and it was easy and soooo good.  I used leftover roasted chicken and just added it to the onion just to warm through.  Served with Quesadillas for an appetizer, Recipe #117892 and Recipe #303397.
I would give this recipe 10 stars for the sauce alone, the rest just doesn't even matter! YUMM!

Wow - these were yummy and very easy to make.  I did add some extra spices to the sauce but otherwise made no changes.
Thanks!!

VERY TASTY!! I used some chili powder, cumin, salt and pepper on the chicken. I used fresh roasted garlic salsa on the inside and by accident I grabbed sour cream with chives, but it tasted great!! Will def keep the recipe to make again and again!

I thought they were fantastic.  I added cumin, red and black pepper, a touch of salt, and minced jarred jalepenos to the meat.  Oh, also 2 cloves garlic minced.  To the sauce I also added cumin, crushed coriander, a touch of red pepper, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, and about 1 1/2 tbs minced jarred jalepenos (out of green chilies).
Yum, finally a recipe that does not call for a cream of something or other soup.  I used a fat free broth and light sour cream and it turned out great.
Very good. I may try to season the chicken a bit next time but the sauce was spot-on and delicious.

These are SO good!  I'd give you 10 stars if they'd let me!  But then, I'd expect nothing less from someone with SUCH an awesome name!   hehehe! ... Okay, so I pretty much followed the recipe as is, with the following exceptions:  I used chicken meat I'd picked from the carcasses after butchering our home-grown fryers, so didn't need to cook the chicken.   I sauteed the onion, added that to the meat, plus the green chiles.  I ended up using 10 tortillas (had a bit more meat than one pound's-worth).    The roux was excellent as I used my own chicken broth, plus added 1 tsp cumin and 2 tsp chicken bouillon (sp?).  Oh, before making the roux I chopped another half onion, sauteed that in the butter for the roux.    I also added some "quesadilla" cheese to the top, which melted into the sauce and made it R-I-C-H beyond words!!!   At the table we added some scallion slices.  Mmm-good!  DEFINITELY A KEEPER!

Oh my!  There are no words...AMAZING!!  I live overseas and don't have green chilies, so I added some chili powder and cumin right to the sauce  to give it a kick.  I also used less chicken and instead added some beans to the filling to save some money.  This is a DEFINITE repeat, and great for company since it can be made ahead of time and served with a simple salad.  Thank you for posting!!
Great!!!  Everyone loved it!

Holy tortilla! This was really good! Not much more I can say than what's already been said. I too added a little cumin and chili to the sauce. This would be a great dish to serve in a buffet with spanish rice and refried beans. Definatelty a do-again!  Thanks for sharing.
These are really good! Only change I made was to add 1 tsp cumin as someone else suggested. My husband and I both loved the sauce. I'll be making this again soon!
These were absolutely delicious! There's absolutely nothing wrong with this recipe! Thank you, Deb!
Yum!
Made these for DH, he loved them.  Will definately be making these again.  Thanks for the recipe.

My father usually hates Mexican food, so I wanted to try something different than the typical 'spicy tacos'.  He absolutely loved these, and the fact that they didn't use canned soup was great.  I liked how the sauce was thick enough to stay on the enchilada, instead of running off when plated. Thanks so much for the recipe!

I made this last night for myself and my hubby, and we both really enjoyed it.  I did make a few modifications to add a little extra zing. This will definitely be added to my list of favorites for the family!  Thank you!

I have done a variety of variations from adding ground beef in a pinch, to using ricotta in place of sour cream and throwing in homemade salsa in the sauce. Always delicious. Mmm good. I added corn and used wheat tortillas and fat free sour cream.

These were the best enchiladas I have ever made.....they were a big hit with my family....I used some turkey meat that I had left over from dinner....worked wonderful....I will be making these alot...

A big hit!  I prepared these enchiladas as directed, except I used jalepenos instead of green chilies (because that's what I had on hand), and WOW were they fantastic!  Thanks so much for a great recipe.  I'll be adding this to our rotation.  :)

I made this last week for my husband and my anniversary.  He had been saying that he really wanted some enchiladas.

wow!! would give this 10 stars if possible. delicious,easy and no soup in the mix. everyone loved it in my house. the only change i made was too use lots of cheese inside the enchiladas and out.

This is such a great recipe!  SO DELICIOUS!

VERY VERY GOOD!  I accidentally bought the large tortilla's (burrito size) however, I loved how they came out! OH MY, THIS IS WONDERFUL!!!!  I followed your recipe exactly, and it is perfect!!!  I doubled the recipe so that I could make one dish to eat now, and one for later.  Well, the dish that I froze won't be in the freezer very long...I can't wait to eat this again! ha! Thanks for sharing a great recipe.  This will definitely become a regular meal at my house.

The sauce was very good. I boiled some jalapenos and used these instead of canned chiles. It was real spicy just like we like it. My husband said he wants to try it with steak or shrimp instead of chicken next time. I think it would be just as delish! I'll never do the soup in a can version again!

My Hubby was crazy about this!!!  I used 3 left over Lemon & Garlic Grilled Chicken Breasts,  (Recipe #222713) sliced into strips and about 2/3 cup of  Sauted Spinach (Recipe #7231) for the filling. This is a great meal.  I've made it before and loved it and forgot to review.  I recently made a batch with left over turkey and have it in the freezer.  I may just have to pull it out tonight!

Very good!  Spiced chicken with onion powder (left onion out), garlic powder, cumin, garlic salt, pepper and a dash of chili powder.  Just added a little garlic powder and pepper to the sauce.  Also used all low fat or fat free stuff - cheese, sour cream, chicken broth and tortillas.  I may have to double the recipe next time - DH ate over half of the pan!  Thank you!
These are very good. I added garlic, chili powder, and onion powder to the chicken. These are nice a mild and I love that they don't use cream of soup. I also used extra cheese. Thanks!

Thanks Deb for posting such a fantastic recipe, I followed the directions as stated for half of the batch, and for the other half I added a slice of 98% fat free deli ham the long kind and rolled it up with the chicken to make like a chicken cordon blue tortilla wrap I have to say both were excellent. This will become a new addition to our menu of meals that we eat thanks again for posting this super recipe.
Ps we also thought about adding Spanish rice to the chicken mix, this is such a flexible recipe that you could just go crazy with it.

Another satisfied customer! I was a little worried about the parmesan but it really worked well!  I sprinkled some fresh cilantro on just before serving oh..and  I made the tortillas since I was out . The finished result was truly delicious and I think we will all be fighting over the leftovers.  A definite make again.  Thank you so much for sharing, Deb!

I did not make the whole recipe, but I made the sauce. It is wonderful! I added Rotel tomatoes and cumin after I tried it. I think it was even better! My husband and kids loved it! Sorry but we did not care for these at all. Were not flavorful at all to my family. I followed the recipe exactly except for adding a little chili powder and cumin.

THE BEST enchiladas I've ever had--and I MADE them thanks to this recipe! SO good! I might pull this out to impress the in-laws next time they're in town...

I have made this once already and cannot believe I haven't rated it yet!  This is absolutely delicious and I am not one who normally likes enchiladas.  The whole family thought this was so yummy and tastey! Thanks for posting.

Excellent! Easy to make, delicious and totally re-heatable. Thank you for posting: it's a great dinner after a hard day.

Can I give this more stars then 5....This is so so very good! These are wonderful & my family *loves* them. I make them using Taco Chicken (recipe 4957) I already have cooked.

Another tip is this recipe is very easy to double & freeze for a quick dinner. I like to assemble enough enchiladas for another pan and freeze them on a cookie sheet, when they're frozen I put them in a large freezer bag. When it's time for dinner- all I do is make the sauce to put on top and place it on top of the frozen enchiladas. I cover it with foil & cook it around 30 minutes. Then I remove the foil, add the cheese on top and cook another 15-20 minutes.

This recipe was very good, I will be making it again. I served it with spanish rice and the Bean and Cheese Taquitos recipe also located on recipe zaar.
