This turned out very bland and looking back I should have known better with the lack of spices.  It was good enough but I would not call it mexican by any means.

Excellent!  My husband loved it, as well as the rest of my family.  Delicious; and I did add a little cumin and garlic to the chicken and onions, and I ended up using only five tortillas because we like to really stuff ours.  Other than that everything else was the same.  So good!

I made this a while back. I used shredded chicken that I made in a crock pot with salsa! The chicken itself turned out incredibly tasty! But.. I wasn't so impressed when I made the enchiladas. I just wasn't crazy about the sour cream/flour sauce you use on top... you could tell it had a lot of flour in it. Next time I'd just bake the enchiladas and top with plain sour cream.

Wow! This was so incredibly good! I will most definitely make this over and over again! I used canned shredded chicken so I didn't have to spend the time cooking it, and it turned out really tasty. I also thought you might want to add some black beans to it, and some fresh tomatoes cut up on the top. Overall, very very very good! A new favorite : )

I've made this recipe numerous times and I always get rave reviews.  I usually add a can of rotel to the chicken before I fill the tortillas.  I also use 2 cans of green chilies instead of just one, and I love cheese, so there%u2019s always a little extra added.  Most of the time I will make half of the enchiladas with chicken and half with creamed spinach.   I think I like the spinach and cheese ones better, but they are good both ways :)

This was totally wonderful! I used a whole slow cooker chicken. it made double the recipe. there's 6 of us and we were able to get 1 good meal and 4 leftover meals out of this. My favorite thing is that it doesn't use cream of soups and it tastes really close to my favorite dine out meal! Has anyone used it with beef? Should I use a beef stock instead? yes i'm really in love with this! Gonna also try to make Shrimp chimichangas with it!!!

This was enjoyed by me and my family. I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs. Threw in a couple cloves of garlic with the chicken and onion. Gave it a few good grindings of black pepper. For me, the sauce is what makes this so delicious. Very nice.
Really good! I used corn tortillas instead of flour (personal preference) and they were good!

This this was delicious!!!  I have a 1 year old and cook all my chicken for the week on Sunday so my chicken was already cooked the day before.  I put the precooked chicken I was going to use in a bowl and added a few teaspoons of cumin (I like the taste of cumin) and 1/2 can of green chilies, combined the ingredients and then filled the tortillas.  I think it made the filing more flavorful....but I like things a little more spicy.  I then added a can and 1/2 of green chilies to the sauce.  Having the chicken precooked made the recipe prep really fast!!  I'm originally from AZ and am so glad I finally found a recipe with no cream of mush or chicken soup....no mexican restaurant makes it with that.  So thank you for sharing your recipe!!!

The sauce, on it's own, is Five Star. After the dish has been assembled my hubs always wipes the saucepan clean with a plain tortilla. The enchiladas themselves are very bland though. I've made so many changes to the filling that it's become a totally different recipe. Maybe I'll post it.

This has become one of my favorite meals. I've made it probably 5 times now and never changed one thing from the original recipe. (Well I might be a little more generous with the cheese, but that's all.) No changes or additions are required. It's very easy to put together and taste fabulous. Highly recommended.
Very good...I took the advice of others and added cumin to both the onions/chicken and to the sauce.  I also used a can of Rotel in lieu of the chopped chiles.

This recipe is a 5 star recipe if you make some minor changes.  You need to season the chicken!  I use a chicken taco seasoning.  Also to the sauce I add chili and cumin seasoning.  Gives the recipe more flavor and not so bland.

The best enchilada recipe ever!  My husband and I LOVED them.  We even mashed some up for our 15-month-old son, and he couldn't get enough of it!  The flavor is amazing.  Can't beat how easy it is, how inexpensive it is, and oh so delicious!!!!

Very yummy!  I made a small change and added some chopped mushrooms ( small enough so the kids would eat them! ) to the onion/chicken mixture and mixed thru 125g of cream cheese, fresh chopped coriander (cilantro in the US n Canada) and a liberal sprinkle of cumin ( as previously recommended - definitely a great addition!).  Rolled this up and made sauce as stated ( added more cumin here too!), was soooo good but definitely couldn't be good FOR you!  Kids loved it and asked for more.  Served with fresh chopped avocado and mexican rice!

Delicious! Added 1 tsp salt and 2 tsp cumin to the chicken while sauteing. Used Swiss cheese inside the enchiladas, which went nicely with the green chilies. Contrary to other reviewers, I think it may actually need less cheese. Next time I'll put some cheese inside each enchilada but no cheese on top, just the sauce.

I've been making this recipe for a while. I'm surprised I haven't put up a review yet. I love this recipe. I make the sauce a little thicker by not adding all the chicken broth at once and then adjust the thickness after I put the sour cream in. I do this because DH likes the sauce thicker. I also sometimes use taco bell taco seasoning on the chicken (like you would for taco meat). By far it's one of my favorite chicken recipes due to yumminess and also because of it's versatility. You can add a lot of different vegetables to it in addition using different cheeses.
I also tend to use lower sodium chicken broth and low fat sour cream.

I am always trying new enchilada recipes but I think I will be sticking with this one for awhile! So simple and so delicious. I made this recipe per the instructions but I did season the chicken and onions with cumin and some New Mexican Chili Powder as they were sauteeing. Highly recommend.
Simply the best Chicken Enchilada Recipe I have ever made!! Wonderful! 5    stars!

Wow!  I'm throwing my condense soup enchilada recipe away.  This taste like authenic Mexican!  I used extra green chillies and chopped green onions on top after cooking.  I also used McCormick's enchilada sauce mix and added 1/2 tsp coco powder to the sauce.  LOTS and LOTS of flavor.  You can even add chili powder to the enchilada sauce to spice it up.  Yum!
Wow, very simple and very very good!

Awesome! The family really enjoyed this! Easy to put together, and I love that it contains no creamed soups which always tasts a little off to me. Will definitely make again. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
So good!  I think this has replaced our old creamy enchilada recipe.  I didn't have canned chilies so I chopped up some pickled jalapeno slices and it was perfect with just a hint of heat.

I should have read more of the reviews before I cooked this.  The recipe was good but could have been awesome if I had followed people's suggestions to add some spices to the meat.  It was a bit bland for our family but still tasty!  Thanks for posting!
Very good.

Love it! My entire family has requested this meal at one time or another. I always add 2 tablesoons of cumin to the chicken and onions at the end of cooking. It adds a wonderful smoky flavor without being too spicy for the kiddos. Mmmmmm!

My boyfriend and I both enjoyed this recipe. It wasn't the greatest thing I've ever made, but it was good for what it was! As for changes, I adapted some of the suggestions from other reviewers here, including adding garlic and cumin to the chicken-and-onion part of the recipe. I also tried to chop the chicken up as much as I possibly could, instead of just dicing it, per someone's advice here, and I think that worked out well. I'm also a big cheese fan, so I put a lot more of the monterey jack cheese both in and on top of the enchiladas than what the recipe mentioned, and I also added some leftover shredded mild cheddar cheese to both the inside and top of 'em. I used two cans of green chiles instead of just one, and I also added jalapenos (and a bit of the jalapeno juice), for some extra kick and flavor, on top of the enchiladas once all of the other ingredients were on top and before I put it all into the oven. Anywho, partnered the enchiladas with some quick Spanish rice for dinner that first night, and it was just great! Ate up all of the leftovers during the following few days. I'll probably make this again at some point... The only thing I could see doing differently is being sure to not have them in the oven for too long - the top was a bit hardened and crunchy rather than the softer, borderline-liquidy layer I had anticipated. It was still great and probably didn't make much difference, as everything underneath that layer was surely soft and moist, but would still like to try for next time!

This is a great base recipe to get experimental with! I used corm tortillas as that is what I had on hand. I bought a roasted chicken from the deli and it worked out great. I prefer a bit  more spice so next time I will add some jalapenos and maybe some cumin to the meat. Will definitely make this again.

Great recipe! But alas, I don't need to tell you this...looking at all the informative reviews, this recipe will not let you down. I followed this pretty closely, except after cooking my chicken, I used my smaller food processor to  chop up the meat, the onion, and some jalapenos. Not to much! Be careful here, you don't want baby food. I just used this small chop for about 1-2 seconds, opened up, moved the contents around, and whirled about 1-2 more seconds. Warmed tortillas on non-stick with no-stick spray - and they became soft and pliable. Other then that, you're all set for a lovely dinner/lunch/or pot-luck. Go get em, Mildred....and enjoy! Thanks for posting!

These turn out so good and tasty. I added 1TLB of Cumin, some Cayenne Pepper, and salt and pepper. I used chicken I had on hand, shredded it, added it to the onion mixture. After serving we added pico de gallo. We live in Mexico and they don't have green chiles (really doesn't need it), go figure, only jalapeno peppers. These would be great with Charro Beans.
We've made this recipe many times and it is SOOOO good.  We make the full recipe and since there's only two of us, we take the leftovers to work for lunch.  They reheat very well!
we realy liked this,if you dont want spicy food this is for you.It was creamy and flavorfull.

This is a very good recipe and easy to put together (though a little time consuming in assembly).  I like it with a can of Rotelle instead of the green chiles, though DH likes the plain chiles better.  I do add some garlic and 1 Tbs cumin to the chicken (as others suggested) and I do think it needs the extra flavor.  I also use a bit more chicken with 10 enriched whole wheat tortillas to really fill up my pan.  We serve this with guacamole and it is one dish where DH doesn't complain about leftovers!  Thank you for a keeper!

I made these tonight and they were very yummy, however missing something. Perhaps I didn't get it quite right, but either way, thanks for a great recipe, I'll definately make again and play around a little with it.
Excellent recipe!  Pretty easy and very tasty.  My teenager suggested I add more chicken and green chilies.  He said they'd be perfect then.

Awesome, such a tasty and easy recipe!!! So happy I came across it! Everyone absolutely loved the enchildas.  I used a pre-cooked bbq chicken from the store and shredded it up. I also fried up some onions and garlic and added it to my chicken mixture with a bit of seasoning salt. I will definitely be making these again, thanks so much for the wonderful recipe!! :)

Easy and delicious.  I seasoned the chicken with my go-to spice blend and sauteed in butter, to impart more flavor.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe as written.  Served with Spanish Rice, Smashed Pintos w/ Cheese and a salad.  This dish also freezes very well.

Tried these tonight. Found them to be bland.  Added tomatillo salsa verde to the sauce, which helped.  Next time, I'll add even more salsa verde.  Maybe I'll add it to the chicken and onion mixture. I also used corn rather than flour tortillas.
Soo incredibly delicious, my families favorite enchilada recipe, I wont even order them when i go out anymore, the only change I make is I like the corn tortillas better than the flour. DELICIOUS!!!!
Simply amazing!  I used Breakstone's Jalapeno sour cream and skipped the chiles but the flavor was out of this world.

I just made these tonight and they were SO SO SO good!! I added a little cajun seasoning to the chicken while it was cooking with the onions to give it extra flavor. The other thing I did that was not mentioned in the recipe but suggested by other reviewers, was to add a can of Rotel to the sauce mixture. I used the Rotel tomatoes with habenero peppers to give it some extra spice. It turned out to have such a great flavor! Much better than anything I've had in Mexican restaurants. Thank you so much for posting! This will be made again real soon!! :)

This dish turned out sooo well!  I substituted 3/4 cup cream cheese and 1/4 cup sour cream instead of the 1 cup of sour cream.  I just happen to have only 1/4 cup sour cream on hand.  WOW, the sauce was rich and delicious!  Topped with diced tomatoes, chopped chives, taco sauce and shredded lettuce...YUM!

These were so delicious and they made for excellent leftovers as well! I prefer shredded chicken to diced in a dish like this, so instead of cooking the chicken on the stove, I threw 3 frozen chicken breasts in to the crockpot (next time I will do four) with a few ounces of chicken broth, a teaspoon of Tony Chachere's, some fresh cracked black pepper and a sprinkle of kosher salt. I meant to add diced onion, but I forgot and will probably add that next time. It only took about four hours to cook and then I shredded the meat. It was really tender and flavorful.  I can't wait to make these again!

I cooked the chicken with the onions (like the recipe said to), but also added a little minced garlic, salt, cumin, and some hot sauce (Topatio brand) to the skillet. It gave the chicken a lot of flavor!  For the sauce, I left out the green chilis and added one can of drained Rotel.  Other than that, I followed the recipe and it was AMAZING!!  My husband said he thought it was the best dinner I've ever fixed.  :)
this was good, the chicken itself was a little bland, will definitely spice it up a little next time
Best enchiladas EVER!!! Delicious!  Yummy!  I can't say enough!!

What a great recipe - simple and easy - and you can add your touch to it!  I added about 2T of Wildtree Adobe seasoning, garlic, 4 oz cream cheese and about 1-2T milk to the chicken and onion mix.  I also added some Wildtree enchilada sauce to the sauce - and it was GREAT!  Can't wait to make it again  - and change it up again.  Thanks so much for sharing this great recipe - and LOVE that it doesn't use canned soup!

This was my first time making enchiladas, but it won't be the last! These were delicious! I added some green enchilada sauce and diced jalapenos to the sauce to spice it up a little. Thanks for sharing!
I have made this several times and the whole family loves it.  I use rotisserie chicken.  Great recipe.

I loved these enchiladas, but no one else did. Not sure why. I think the tanginess of the sour cream sauce did it for my husband, and I also cooked the chicken by boiling it and then shredding it, which he didn't like either. Oh well ;(

This is the best chicken enchilada recipe I have ever tasted!
My hubby likes a little hot sauce on his.
I hate cubing chicken breast (I cut the breast while still slightly frozen to make it easier) but it was worth it. The chicken soaked up the onion, the sauce is delicious.

Thanks for sharing!

Love the base recipe. I added in bell pepper, jalapeno, garlic and tomato with the chicken, and seasoned with cumin and cilantro. I also added a sprinkle of chile powder to the sauce. Turned out scrumptious - will definitely be making again!
Very good recipe! I made half the amount and used a pre-roasted chicken, but other than that I made it as it says and loved it.  It came out better than I had expected and my boyfriend loved it.
Excellent.  Used to use the cream of blah blah soup, but these are sooooo much better.  I actually use two cans of green chilis because I love the flavor of them.

I love this recipe! I also appreciate the fact that there is no tinned soup in the recipe. The sour cream made the sauce delicio us.I made these with my 10 yo daughter along with rice recipe #217662. This was easy to put together and full of flavour. I will probably change it up next time and add a tin of rotel to the sauce. I will NEVER use tinned soup to make enchiladas. Thanks for posting....another great recipe.

I thought this recipe was going to be out of this world! But it just didn't do it for me! I was dissapointed, as I wanted it to be wonderful. It was kinda bland and needed something.? I may try to make it again and add maybe more cheese,garlic,and some spices. Thank You for sharing! I followed the recipe exactly!

This recipe is great. However, I used this recipe for the chicken http://www.food.com/recipe/crock-pot-chicken-taco-meat-4957. To the sauce, I added some pepper, garlic powder and a handful of cheese. YUMMY!

I enjoyed the enchiladas, but I think I will make the sauce spicier next time, or maybe look for another enchilada sauce to go with it that's a little more Mexican.  Overall though, a very tasty recipe!

I thought this was great! I love to tinker with recipes but this one is great as is. I made one batch with flour tortillas and one with corn tortillas. The flour tortillas were WAAAYYY better. My husband wanted more spice, but I loved the creamy sauce.

I love this recipe and make it all the time!  However, when followed exactly, I feel there isn't *quite* enough flavor, so I like to add a can of green enchilada sauce.  I usually make a double or triple of this recipe and I RARELY have leftovers. For what I usually make, it's only a small can of enchilada sauce (don't know the oz), but for anything bigger, I add a large can of the green enchilada sauce. Absolutely delicious!

FANTAB-U-LOUS!!  We've eaten these at least a zillion times.  I often cheat and use pre-made chimichangas or burritos (family pack) and just use the sauce...makes life easier on a busy night.  Man!! We love these!
My FAVE enchilada recipe, love the sauce! This recipe is perfect, doen't need any modifications, well done!!

So good!! Even my mother-in-law (who specializes in home cooked Mexican food) loved it.  I will definately keep in the monthly rotation. I used corn tortillas and lightly fried them to keep them from splitting open during rolling.
These are a HIT.That cream sauce is AWESOME! Nice! Thankx!
I made these for dinner the other night, I thought they were delicious. Perfect mix of chicken and cheese yumminess. I did add some cumin to add a little more spice.
Made this yesterday and I'll say this, it's a bit time consuming but I'll get faster because these were DAMN good!

These were good but they were really bland. Also a bit too much sour cream for our taste. My son the sour cream hater even ate them.
I will make these again with some adjustments to the sauce and will add some heat to the chicken and the sauce I did use corn tortillas instead of the flour.
totally a choice favorite. I'm never ever making the other kind again.

This was awesome!  The only thing I did different was to add a fajita seasoning pack with some peppers and onions to the chicken. This time, I will also add some rotel diced tomatoes to the white sauce that goes on top. This recipe is fab and you can easily adjust it ti fit your tastes :)

I usually try to keep as true to a recipe as I can the first time through. A few reviews reported it as a bit bland, and we like it spicy over here, so I did make a little change. I put the green chiles in with the chicken mixture. For the sauce, I took half a can of chipotle in adobo, chopped it up and blended it in. It was SO good! Everyone in my house really liked it, thanks so much for sharing!!
Addendum: This continues to be a family favorite. I have made them with chicken breasts, ground turkey and ground beef, all to equally great reviews! Love to make several pans at once and freeze for another time!

I am crazy about sour cream enchiladas and these are the best I have ever eaten!  These are even better than a famous restaurant in the Houston, Texas area.  I plan to fix this dish for my daughter and husband in a couple weeks when we will be together on a trip to the lake.  They are fans just like my husband and I are of sour cream enchiliadas.  I fixed a side of mexican rice, black beans and guacamole.  I am so happy to have found this recipe.  I have tried to make this dish before and it never quite tasted just right.  This is a keeper!  THANKS !

This recipe is just delicious. Made it tonight with things I had on hand that I needed to use up (sometimes those are the best meals!). Only changes were to use corn tortillas, which I steamed until soft in the microwave, and to use frozen roasted Hatch green chiles, doubling to 8 oz. I also added cumin and braised the chicken, then shredded. This will be a new entry into my regular rotation, without a doubt. Thank you for sharing such a wonderful recipe.
So good and so very simple and quick to put together. Thank  you for this delicious posting.
Easy recipe that my picky daughter actually loved!!! I thought it might be too bland, but it wasn't.

I made these based on the first few reviews that I saw and now wish I had read further into the reviews.  They are easy to make.  However, other than the salt, they are not very tasty.  I will not make them again.

OMG!!!!  SO GOOD!!!  In the past I wasn't huge on Mexican dishes, but since finding some great recipes (like this one) on this site, I am really beginning 2 think I may like Mexican. A short story here:  I wasn't ever much of a chef, but getting much better, again, thanks 2 this site. Just 2 prove my point, my idea of cooking was (notice past tense) popping a Stouffer's enchilada entree in the oven, one of my niece recommended (and she too is not a chef at all).  She said she tried the Stouffers enchilada with cheese sauce and didn't like it.  I had decided I would give this recipe a try, and then when I thoroughly read the directions I was a lil hesitant when I noticed the cheese sauce.  Well, let me tell U, I will NOT EVER buy Stouffers enchiladas again! Made exactly like recipe, no complaints, but may try adding some rice into the enchilada next time?  Or maybe just serving over rice?  This was easy and GREAT!   For someone who is watching there waistline, this was SO worth the calories!

I knew this recipe would be a winner when I had my friend from Mexico check it out!  She did have me make a few minor changes.  I used corn tortillas instead of flour, and chihuahua cheese instead of monterey jack.  I also diced up some jalapeno for a little extra kick.  These were restaurant quality, and although they are so fattening, I'll definitely make them again!

Talking about easy! This is just about the easiest dish I have ever made and tastes great!We had a Roasted chicken already cooked from Kroger,tore it apart,got rid of the bone. Cut it up in small squares. Made the sauce. Mixed the chicken in and I was done. I made it step by step followed to a T, other than adding a little more cheese! I like mine gooey and oozing with cheese.Put it all together, popped it in the oven,took a shower and it was done when I got out! This is a keeper for me! I am not a big Mexican food person but I really liked this! Thanks for the Vine like Jim Rome says!

This was umm.... amazing! yup! AMAZING! What a great starting point recipe, it was not spicy so my kids gobbled them up as well! (I have PICKY eaters!) There are endless possibilities on where you can go with this recipe and I think it is a great base recipe if you want to get creative or just fabulous by itself! I have some leftover from dinner last night...I kind of want to eat them for breakfast :)

Made this the other night and divided into two 8 x 8 baking dishes.  Cooked one that night - easy, lots of flavor, OUTSTANDING!.  The other I put in the freezer. I followed the recipe exactly aside from using HOT green chilies and I topped with a can of Rotel tomatoes with chilis for added color.  Served refried beans and easy spanish rice from this site.  Great worknight meal.  Thanks for the recipe.

We loved this recipe. I will admit, I read a lot of reviews before hand and tweaked the recipe based on comments. I used a Rotisserie chicken from the store and shredded it. I sauteed the onions in the oil with some Nature Seasonings. Once done I added the chicken, a pinch of garlic powder, pepper, salt and 1 tsp taco seasonings. I then added a can of original Rotel (that I drained of liquids first). I used this mixture and put into the tortillas with the cheese. The sauce I did just as the recipe suggests and I even used fat free sour cream. I added more black pepper to the sauce as well. We also served with a bunch of toppings. I topped mine with fresh cilantro, fresh diced jalapenos, lime slices and avocado slices. The others also topped theirs with salsa and/or hot sauce. I will be making this at LEAST once a month and sharing the recipe with others as well!! Thanks!!

Wow!  These are great!  I sauted a lot of extra vegtables to put in with the chicken - bell peppers, carrots, tomatoes and wilted spinich.  Sauce made as stated in recipe.  Used corn tortillas instead of flour.    Definitely in the monthly rotation!!

My family loved this dish, and I'm so proud that I got this easy-to-put-together-dish right - on my first attempt! I will be making this again. I made my own tortillas, and added a teaspoon of garlic powder to 4 cups of flour. I think that lent a great taste to the dish. Next time though I will go for low sodium broth. Otherwise this one is a keeper! Thanks for sharing Deb!
Followed the recipe to the letter.  Turned out great!  What a lifesaver!!

I made this dish last night for my boyfriend.  It was absolutely delicious!!! I try out recipes on him all the time so, by now, he has no problem in giving his true opinion.  He RAVED about it!  The only adjustments I made were based off of lack of some ingredients.  I did not have green chiles, so I added about 2 tsp of pesto to the sauce and I also used about 1/4 cup of heavy cream, as I had used some chicken stock the day before and only had 3/4 can left.  I added a few dashes of hot sauce to make up for the lack of spice without the chiles.  It turned out WONDERFUL and I'm sure it will be even better on the next occasion when I have all the ingredients.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!
Have made these several times now - delicious :)

I made these last night for dinner and everyone loved them! I made a little more sauce to pour over the top- which was just a mistake on my part, but it turned out pretty good. And I had some of the chicken mixture left over so I put it in the sauce too so it wouldn't go to waste. We will definitely make this again.
These were great! The whole family loved 'em!!!

These were simple & delicous!  I used less chicken & added some black beans & fresh cilantro to the batch I made.  Served with some shredded lettuce, chopped green onion, & fresh salsa.  SO GOOD.  Thanks for a great recipe!

Very good! followed the recipe except i used rotel tomatoes w/ green chillies b/c thats all i had on hand and i used a 4cheese blend and seasoned my breast with salt pepper garlic and onion powder bc i hate the texture of onions but i like the flavor and i used a lil cumin and chili powder..great recipe thx!
This was delicious. DH said it looked liked a picture out of a book. I think next time I will add some salsa to the sauce with the chillies. Yum
This meal was good, my sister n law made it with black beans and Spanish rice. This was the first time I had sour cream chicken enchiladas and I will make it from now on.

i agree with this post.. ate one and threw the rest away. would give less than one star if i could..

I am not a great cook but I have no problem following the instructions. This was simple and easy. If you can chop, fold and mix, you can make this. It was delicious. I made this tonight and it was delicious.  My whole family really enjoyed it.  I layered the ingredients in a 9x13 pan rather than rolling the enchiladas.  I used 16 oz of sour cream instead of 8 and a lot more cheese than what was called for.  I'll definitely will be making it again.  Thanks for posting!

I followed this recipe exactly the first time and it was fantastic! It was such a hit that I made it again (very soon after), for friends, but this time made it as a casserole, layering the ingredients in an eight inch round dish. it was again delicious. Definitely a keeper. Thank you Deb.

REALLY GOOD!!!   You have to love sour cream to make this particular enchilada recipe. I was very surprised at the taste.  I love the sour cream sauce that they have at some Mexican restaurants - this recipe fits perfectly!!!  I didn't even add the chilies.  The flavor was really good. Thank you!!!

Wow! These were amazing!!! I hated enchiladas as a kid but my dh asked me to make some so I grudgingly agreed. I'm soooo glad he did and I found this recipe! We will be making these again, without a doubt!
now in high rotation on our family dinner playlist. very tasty, very easy.
Loved this recipe we did add Rotel to the chicken , it turned out awesome will make this again!!!
Seriously, the best chicken enchiladas I have ever had. I followed the recipe exactly and they were very easy to make.

Next time I will not put cheese on top . . and I may add the can of Rotel tomatoes, but I think I will puree the green chilies and Rotel first so it permeates throughout the sauce.  Great recipe - just needs more "umph."  Oh, I used corn tortillas instead of flour and heated them first by frying them for a couple of seconds on either side in hot oil so they would roll easily.  Always tops with fresh cilantro.  Delish.

I loved this so much more than my local restaurant's! I usually eat sour cream enchiladas because the red chili and green chili sauce burn the hell out of my tongue! I love the subtle, creamy flavor of this dish, not to mention a little kick from the canned green chilies.<br/><br/>My only reason for deducting a star was the texture. I followed the recipe to a T, and even though I'm adopted into a huge Mexican family, I didn't question the strange choice of softened flour tortillas. Big mistake. They came out VERY soggy and clumpy. It was too much for my gag reflex. I also tried not softening the tortillas, but they came out the same. Last night I made them with corn tortillas (white or yellow are fine) and they were MUCH better. I'd recommend sticking to these traditional enchilada methods if you like a little more crunch.

I have made this several times and keep forgetting to review!  Everyone LOVES these!  We follow the recipe pretty much to the "T".  The only change I made was to add about a 1/4 cup of taco seasoning to the sauce before pouring over the enchiladas.  I found it just gave it a little "something".  I also use the rotisserie chicken breast from Costco to save time, since it is already cooked and lightly seasoned.  It makes this dish so easy and delicious.  Thank you, Deb, for a wonderful recipe! This will be in my recipe box forever!

I thought this recipe was very good. It was simple to make (minus all my slow choping). I realized after eating it, I personally am not a fan of creamy enchiladas. It was too rich for me. I added an extra case of green chilies to the enchilads themselves. I also, as others suggested, added in fresh garlic, chili pepper, cumin, and ceyene pepper to the chicken and onions. I can't give it 5 stars because I felt like it wasn't spicy enough, for the heaviness of the cream sauce. But if you like those creamy dishes and aren't too big on spice, this is a great one. I also have a lot of leftover sauce. Will be trying to make some sort of queso dip with it. Any suggestions are welcome.
Family loves.  Did add 1 envelope taco seasoning and 1 can Rotel tomatoes.  Love that you can prep and freeze!

Made twice, once with original recipe and once with additions.  Original recipe just did not have enough flavor.  I added 1/4 tea of cumin and chili pwr to the cooking onions and chicken. Increased the roux to 1/3 cup each butter & flour. Added 1 10 oz can of Old El Paso Enchilada Sauce and 10 oz of chicken broth to roux.  The 4 stars are for the tweaked version or otherwise it would be a 2 star recipe.
These are good but very mild.  The flavor reminds me of chicken ala king.
Easy to make.  The whole family loved it and we fought over the leftovers.

Absolutely delicious! Fairly easy to make to boot. We used shredded rotisserie chicken to save a bit of time and effort and the chicken with its nice flavor worked well with the dish. We used a bit more cheese then the recipe suggests and added rotel tomatoes with habenero peppers to the sauce as suggest by other reviewers. My husband has not been the biggest fan of enchiladas in the past but he loved these!
It's baking right now and smells ono!  That sauce broke da mouth, the best I have ever made!<br/>Mahalo for a killa recipe Deb.

I've made this several times, and think it is a great base recipe, but it needed some adjustments for our taste.  Now when I make it, I add green chile, garlic, red pepper flakes, and a little chile powder to the chicken mixture.  I cut back the sour cream in the sauce by 1/3-1/2, which gives you the flavor without all of the heaviness.  I've also found that corn tortillas work as well, if not better than the flour tortillas (the flour tortillas tend to get gummy in the sauce, especially with the leftovers).

These were AWESOME. I was tempted to put some kind of seasoning with the chicken and onions, but left it alone and made the recipe exactly as directed. I'm glad I did! The recipe is perfect as is. I'm so glad that this is freezer friendly, too. This is in our meal rotation for sure!
Family favorite. When I'm in a hurry, I just buy a roasted chicken from Costco. I quickly piece the chicken apart and assemble the enchiladas.

Good recipe with a few adjustments. With adjustments = 5 star.  Added cumin and taco seasoning to the chicken as well as some taco seasoning. Added a can of Rotel original to the sauce. A little more cheese than the recipe called for as well. It was delish, just needed some oomph in the form of seasonings.

The one thing I tweaked was I added minced jalapeno and cream cheese with the chicken mixture so it wouldn't be so dry. I like things really spicy and am not a fan of bland flavors. Also added minced jalapeno to the sauce as well. TASTY!

I made this for my family & it was a hit with the kids. I used the meat from a grocery store rotisserie chicken and had about 2 oz of meat for each enchilada. Yes, it is mild, but the chilies add nice flavor. Rich & creamy, we will definitely be making this again.
My family loved this one.  I doubled the cans of green chilies and added fajita seasoning to improve flavor.  Great hit and very easy to make!
Thanks for sharing Deb! Great Dish! I served it with my family's favorite enchilada mole sauce.

Followed the recipe exactly and LOVED it.  A little different, in a good way; from the usual red or green enchiladas and couldn't have been any easier.  A mild, creamy sauce set the chicken of so well.  I think next time I might even add some cilantro and jalapenos just for a little kick to see how that works, but it's perfect just the way it is.  Had a lot left over (there's only two of us) and have frozen the rest for another meal, will be anxious to see how that works out

Made this for dinner. Super creamy. I used home canned chicken as it is what I have. I Carmelized the onions in butter then added a little cumin and taco seasoning to the onions then added the meat after draining. I let this warm through. Then I stirred in some leftover rice.<br/>We were having the missionaries for dinner, plus we expecting a friend as well. Cooking for 12 people, this was fabulous! Served it with salad and pie for dessert of course. <br/><br/>Oh, I also puréed the peppers before adding to the sauce so I wouldn't hear complaints of grossness.. Even my picky eaters scarfed this down and had seconds! This was requested to be added to the monthly plan! Hurrah!

I've been looking for a recipe that didn't include "cream of...." anything. This was really a tasty version. I changed the recipe a little; I used corn tortillas, and green enchilada sauce to make the tortillas more pliable. I also seasoned the chicken with Fiesta Taco Seasoning. Very good dish-LOVE the sour cream sauce!

OMG thank you this recipe was great, I didn't change a thing it came out moist, yummy, and most of all my picky husband loved it.<br/>Thank you I printed and saved will be added to our regular meal menu
These were very tasty..did not change a thing.  Will definitely be making again.
This got a range of reviews from my family - from "great" to "so-so".  I upped it to make 10 figuring 2 for each of us mad and 4 leftover. It's pretty filling.

I tried this recipe months ago and I always come back and make this for entertaining! I love it and always get rave reviews! It's not often I feel it necessary to write a review but this one deserves it and everyone needs to go it's delicious!
delicious. will definitely make again.
This is a keeper.  It was creamy and delish!

I made this gluten free by using corn tortillas instead of flour and replacing the flour in the roux with cornstarch. I reduced the fat content by using half the butter, half the cheese, nonfat Greek yogurt in place of  the sour cream and I used diced tomatoes with green chilies instead of just green chilies. It tasted awesome!
very very best chicken enchiladas I've ever had in my life and I am a very picky eater.
I love love love this recipe...sometimes I mite add a can of rotel to the chicken just to spice it up but it is amazing how its written also!

I read A LOT of reviews before making this and decided not to adjust the recipe at all. I followed the recipe exactly and it was pretty flavorless. It definitely needs some added ingredients. I do think this is a good base. I like that it doesn't include any condensed canned soups...those just gross me out!! Next time I might simmer the chicken in enchilada sauce and maybe add a can of rotel to the sour cream sauce.

Great recipe. As a displaced Texan living in New Mexico, we love the food, but sour cream enchiladas are rarely on the menu. This was an easy and tasty taste of home. My only alterations were to cook the chicken and some RoTel beforehand in the crockpot, and to use some of the local green chiles instead of canned. All in all, this is a winner.

I just made your recipe tonight... though I did change it up just a little bit... I added spinach and Cilantro to my chicken as I cooked it... I drizzled a little sauce into the enchilada before I rolled it up... and I put Mexican cheese inside, and Pepperjack on top... it turned out really good... The sauce was definitely spot on.
This recipe is fabulous! I did exactly as the recipe states and it is perfection! We will definitely add this as a regular to our meal plan!
Followed it to the t and found it to be a flavorless recipe...

Really yummy recipe and I'm glad that I read a lot of the reviews before trying it.  I decided to use chicken thighs (juicier) and to sauté them in a chipotle garlic sauce to add flavor, and after shredding them, folded in a can of chopped green chiles before dropping a bunch of cheese on it and wrapping it in a low carb flour tortilla.  In addition, I added a can of red enchilada sauce to the sour cream mixture to add flavor and color and the family enjoyed it so much...I'm making it again for the 2nd time!  Thanks for the great ideas and recipe everyone:)

This was so easy to make, beautiful to look at and budget friendly to boot. I absolutely loved it as did everyone else. I have been requested for a repeat next week. Served it with some Spanish Rice and a bit of salad.
I'm going to try adding 2 c shredded zucchini and 16 oz cottage cheese to the filling.  I'm looking forward to making this.
I'm trying this tonight

This recipe is something my mom has made for years! I saw the picture and thought it looked amazing!! I was going to try the recipe but after a quick read I realized it's identical to my mother's except that she layers it out in a casserole of sorts. 

This has been my favorite dish since childhood! The only difference is when we make it casserole style it takes a can of cream of chicken soup across the whole top so it isn't dried out. 

I actually think I would prefer to have it the way this recipe states. In a more individual enchilada lay out instead of a casserole, which I've never been big on. This recipe has inspired me to revisit my mother's old recipe in new ways, Thank you!
Followed the recipe, the only difference was that I added rotel.. It was okay.

This is simply an AMAZING recipe. My family absolutely loved it. I served it with Mexican rice and ranchero refried beans. It was a huge hit. Thanks for posting. This will be a treasure for years to come.

Cooked exactly as described, not impressed. Too much onion, and the final result seemed too dry. Been around excellent Mexican cuisine all my life, this recipe falls short. Taste isn't worth the calories and saturated fat. 
Try adding a 1/2 cup fat free yogurt for some tang, one large Anaheim pepper and 1/2 cup cilantro. That would probably bring it to life.

Good!  We enjoyed it with my modifications of sauteed onions, garlic, and chopped fresh spinach added to the chicken mixture. I added a total of 7 oz. green chilis, and it was a little spicy for me. The hubs ate 3, and I had 2.  No flaming, please!!

These enchiladas were delicious, no doubt. But it occurred me to while I was making them that the recipe doesn't call for any salt or pepper, which I thought was peculiar. Sure, there's some salt in the chicken broth. But I imagine this dish would have turned out pretty flavorless had I not added salt and pepper to the chicken and onions while cooking. Also, just before serving, I topped the enchiladas with some fresh, diced tomatoes and cilantro.  Turned out to be a nice touch. All in all, my family loved this recipe, and I will definitely make this dish again.
I made these for supper tonight and they were terrific.  Definitely a recipe that I will save and use often.  Simple and tasty as written!

Followed exactly except I added chopped jalapeños to the sour cream sauce and some capsicum to the chicken and onion. It's nice but could be better, maybe with some sort of Mexican seasoning. That might make them taste like enchiladas. I don't know il try that next time.
Fabulous. Made it for me and my boyfriend and it was delish! I even added a can of hot rotel to the sauce instead of the peppers.
Sooooo good!!!! Simple and easy to make. Loved it!!
Amazingly delicious! Kids cleaned their plates! So, so goood.

I decided to make this after seeing the recipe on Facebook. Wow it is absolutely amazing. I followed everything except I boiled my chicken because I didn't have time to thaw before cooking. This is probably one of the best recipes I've found online and it was easy to make. I will definitely be making this again for my family.

My second go at this recipe is in the oven right now.  The first time it was soooo good.  I didn't put cheese in the enchiladas either time (forgot both times, go figure) and while I could see it being better that way, it was great without cheese inside.  Also, I just used green peppers from the garden and onions in the roux instead of canned chilies and put raw onions in the enchiladas because I boiled the chicken before shredding (in my KitchenAid!!) instead of cooking in oil.  I cannot stress enough how good these are.  The sauce is so good that I want to make twice the amount but it won't fit into the pan if I do.  First World Problems.  So so good, thank you for this new family favorite!

Overall its a good base recipe but I found this recipe a little bland and not very healthy with 1 cup of sour cream and a butter roux cheese and additional oil.  So I changed things to make it healthier.  Cut the fat to less than 1/2 with the addition of cornstarch to aid in thickening and adding a fresh Pico salsa and seasoning to the chicken and cut out a little cheese as well.
This recipes is amazing!  I live in Singapore, so some ingredients can be hard to find. I substituted plain yogurt and lime juice for the sour cream. It was still fabulous!

I put left over shredded chicken and fresh chopped tomatoes in the tortillas (with the cheese of course). I didn't have chili peppers but I did have a can of jalapeños in adobo, so i added about a tsp of that the the flour/butter mixture. It made a delicious sauce.

Wow, what a dish! Wanted to do something different and this came up! very easy to make. Had to substitute cheddar for monterey jack and a whole jalepeno for the can of chilies (didn't have them on hand at the time) but I don't think it mattered. The dish is rich, flavourful, creamy, and best of all, no cream soup! Wonderful, will definitely make again!!

Ok I only changed it cause I had to work with what was in the cupboard. I didn't have green chiles so I added some chile powder to the cooking chicken. And I didn't have chicken broth so I just used chicken bullion. I also added black olives to the mix since my 5-yr-old loves them. Anyway, they're amazing! Thank you.

It was a good recipe. I'm going to make this again but tweek it some. I always follow directions and then make it again my way. I would definitely shred the chicken and I would also add more seasoning. I put a sprinkle of cumin and taco seasoning over the chicken and onions as they were cooking, but it wasn't enough. Maybe using rotisserie chicken would give it more flavor. Also add two cans of green chilies (which I chopped up more in the ninja, and may add jalpenos too!) into the sour cream rue for more flavor.

SO good! The sauce was the perfect consistency! I did throw my chicken in the crock pot with some, salt, granulated garlic and a can of rotel, which was a good call. Will definitely be making these again!!!

This is an excellent recipe! My entire family loves it and I love that it is "from scratch". I cannot stand the tast of canned chicken soup. This recipe is perfext as-is, however, I prefer to add a 2nd can of diced chiles for the flavor. Definitely a 5 star recipe!
Yummy and easy!  Husband likes spicy so I added Rotel w/ Habanero.  Served with re fried beans an Spanish rice. Quick Friday night dinner. Thanks!!!

Made this for dinner tonight,it is soooo good,I did not have exact ingredients,I used beef broth and salsa Verde instead of chicken broth and green chilies in the roux,but It definatly turned out GREAT! I made it with the 
John Wayne green chili squares,found on this site, good combination. I highly recommend this dish and next time I will use exact ingredients!

Made this scrumptious, decadent recipe last night for the sisters and they loved it.
I suggested next time I will cut the butter in half and use low fat sour cream or 2% plain yogurt to make it healthier. They said "no! don't change a thing, it was fabulous and its not like were eating it everyday." Plan to double and make for a bigger crowd in a couple of weeks. Thanks for sharing!
I added hot red pepper and jalapeno and rice and mozzarella cheese and some seasoning, cilantro and scallions.

For the life of me, I simply cannot understand why I see so many enchilada recipes that are prepared with flour tortillas.   That is not an enchilada ... that is a burrito.  Corn tortillas are how enchiladas are prepared.  I haven't yet made these, but I will be using corn tortillas, cumin, cilantro, chili powder, garlic, onions, green chiles, fresh tomatoes, oregano and queso fresco.  I should have waited to make any comments, but I am tired of poring through enchilada recipes for ideas only to see so many that use flour tortillas.  Maybe because I'm in Texas and have my choice all over the place for Mexican, Spanish, Southwestern and Tex-Mex that the flour tortilla "enchilada" annoys me so much.  SMH

I just used this to make the sauce because I was craving a good sour cream enchilada sauce. It's amazing!! I love it. I poured it on quesadillas. I now have some left over in the fridge to use for later. It was tempting to eat all of it. :-) Thank you so much for this recipe!

These are so yummy! I have now made them 7 times in the past six months and followed the whole recipe. Friends and Family have raved about them. Making a roux is easy.  Nothing extra needed. Easy to make; the hardest or time consuming part is cutting the chicken.  So I just crank some tunes and have a tasty beer while I cook this home run meal! You won't be disappointed and your family will thank you! Mine did!!

I made this recipe last night and was disappointed! If people think this is tasty, they have not had a really satisfying, yummy meal. The meat mixture was bland...this recipe needs to be discontinued...what a waste to spend time on a meal for my family and have a downer...onto a better website!
I, on the other hand followed other's advice from the review section and added Cumin to the chicken.  Receipe was great!  I loved it.

Great recipe. These are also great using corn tortillas. Side note: if you're going to list a dozen alterations you've made to someone else's recipe, perhaps the fair thing to do would be to post one of your own :)
I didn't change/add a thing!  Much better than my old recipe(soup).  Served with homemade salsa and rotel rice.  A new favorite here!  Thanks.
This is awful.  You should never make Enchiladas with flour tortillas.  YUCK
Even my picky son loves them!!!!! used a whole rotesiere chicken,add cumin and chili powder.Layered the shells didnt roll.yummy!

Made this the first time and doubled. It was so good, even as leftovers. I am making tomorrow and to save time, boiled chicken and then shredded with a hand mixer. I'm sure it will come out equally yummy.

This is my second time making this and it is absolutely delicious.  My new 'go to' recipe for sour cream enchiladas.   I seasoned my chicken w/ homemade taco seasoning and added a can of fire roasted Rotel tomatoes to chicken/onion mixture at the end.  Would have added a jalapeño if I had one.
Seriously consider doubling the recipe so you have some leftover to freeze.  Wish I had done the same.

The picture for this recipe looks very tasty, but what are the green pieces that I see in the filling of the enchilada? I personally would have to add peppers (probably jalapeno) to the filling, and I think they did too--- they just did not mention that in the recipe! Mexican food without chilis of some sort is unthinkable.

The sauce was good, but it was just missing a little something... maybe because I don't like hot food and left out the green chilies.  The second time I made this I added 1/2 tsp of garlic powder to the sauce and layered 10 oz of enchilada sauce underneath it.  That made it a top notch sauce for spice whimps.  Additionally, I thought the chicken filling was a little boring.  On my second try I replaced it with a corn and black bean filling from another recipe.  This recipe really isn't about the filling as much as it's about the lovely sauce.
The BEST Enchiladas out there.  I can't even count how many times I have made them.  Hubby would most likely eat them every night.
Made this over the weekend.  I was ok.  Kind of blah..needs something to spice it up a bit.

These enchiladas are very good.  I would mention that, sometimes when people tweak recipes, it could be because they have a digestive issue that doesn't allow them to eat a lot of heat or of a certain food due to allergies.  Also, many people's tweaks help some of us, who may not have all ingredients on hand, but do still like to try the ideas, and do enjoy the end result.

This recipe was a hit. I saw that many reviews added some canned diced tomatoes to the filling so I did too and I'm glad that I did. It added more depth of flavor to the dish. My favorite part was the chicken sauce at the end. That really gives it a bang. We will definitely be adding this recipe to our regular meal rotation.
This was so boring. I had to put a lot of Sriracha on mine

I like this recipe but haven't tried it yet but I will.  I prefer recipes that don't use canned soups.  I try to stay with basic ingredients and avoid ones with lots of additives, of course that's hard to do.  Just read the ingredients on any Campbells soups or anyone else's sometime.  Thanks for the recipe.

I have just made these tonight with refried beans and Spanish rice. I really liked them and plenty of leftovers for tomorrow. My husband did not enjoy them as much as I, who cares more for me tomorrow.

This was truly the best Sour Cream Chicken Enchiladas I have ever made or eaten.
I gave the recipe to friends that all reported it is outstanding. 
It is even better the next day if you have anything leftover.
Family loves these including the kids.  Easy to put together.
Reminds me of a Chi chi's dish from the past. Good, rich, filling, changeable. Needed a bit more spice. A winner.

I was a little hesitant to try this recipe because it sounded bland. I am so glad that I did make it, because it is delicious! I made as stated except for a few changes; I used corn instead of flour tortillas - personal preference - cheddar cheese because that is what I had; my can of chopped chili's was 7 ounces instead of 4 ounces. I also put about 1 teaspoon of softened cream cheese inside each enchilada. I do that with hamburgers also, it seems to add a richness, but no one even knows it is there! It is the delicious sauce that really makes these enchiladas a stand-out!
This recipe was easy and soo good!
I baked chicken breast tenderloins with onions then diced and shredded - other than that followed recipe pretty closely - they were excellent- better than my favorite restaurant's
Yum. Followed recipe exactly and it was perfect.

I made the recipe as written and it is hands down the easiest and best tasting dish I've made in ages! I had a couple of friends over and made traditional enchiladas and these. These went in a flash, the others not so much. One friend requested these again and I promised to make an extra pan for him to take home and freeze. Superb. NO CHANGES NEEDED IN THE RECIPE!!

I am so glad I found this recipe. I made this for a weeknight meal, and this recipe was perfect for that. It was quick and easy to make. But best of all, all three of my kids loved it, which includes the picky teenager. This recipe has now been added to the regular flow for quick weeknight meals that all my kids devour. Also, I would not change anything about this recipe!
We us corn tortillas for enchiladas. Not flour. This recipe is the best homemade version that I've used!
Really good I added salsa to the chicken while frying in small pieces , half can of rotel tomatoes with green chilis

This is one of my favorite recipes here. I have made this so many times over the last few years. The only things I have done different were to use low sodium chicken broth and use half cup greek yogurt and half cup sour cream. I think next time I may add some fresh jalapenos just to spice it up a little.

This is an all time favorite in our house. I always double the sauce because my 3 kids (one is daddy lol) are obsessed. They put it on EVERYTHING. I have made these for a bbq and all three pans were licked clean. Always a hit and on the request list! *life hack: I boil my chicken for these and use the fresh broth rather than canned*

Without a doubt these are the worst chicken enchiladas I have ever made. Followed the recipe as written except I used my own frozen New Mexico chilies. Bland and tasteless. Sauce tastes like white sauce. Total waste of ingredients and I am going to have to figure out a planB for dinner becuz no one is going to eat this.

Honestly by itself this is pretty bland! After realizing this, I added a taco seasoning packet, can of Rotel, black beans, lime and cilantro to the chicken filling. With my additions my whole family liked this recipe. but having already tasted it without the additions, I can't give this five stars. It's a great base but all by itself would be the blandest enchiladas I've ever had!
My go-to Chicken Enchilada recipe - I like a few extra green chiles. I've also tried with the Rotel added and that's pretty good but I like the original better.
Wonderful!! It was easy to make and tastes delicious, I recommend to friends

I bought deli-style garlic herbed chicken from Sprouts. I then diced it and sautéed it in olive oil with onion, some fresh chopped Jalapeno, cumin, and 1/2 pack of taco seasoning. I made up the tortillas with the chicken and cheese mixture. (I was able to make five big ones with the chicken package.) I sprayed the dish and poured just a little bit of red enchilada sauce in the bottom of it before putting in the rolled tortillas. I made the roux with the butter and flour. I added in a small can of the diced green chili peppers along with the sour cream and the rest of the can of the enchilada sauce. I poured all of it over the tortillas. It was a lot, it filled up the dish. I then sprinkled a blend of Mexican cheese all over the top. I cooked it at 400 for only 15 minutes. After I took it out, I sprinkled fresh cilantro over it. It was a beautiful dish and smelled yummy. The guys absolutely loved it! They like things spicy, so I might try the Rotel next time. I am not sure. These were the best enchiladas I have ever had! Thanks so much for the recipe Deb!!

I almost never take the time to write a review, but his was absolutely FANTASTIC! I was anxious to try this because I had never come across an enchilada recipe that uses a roux. I used the liquid that I cooked the chicken in for the roux. I did add a fair amount of salt and pepper. This will be my only enchilada recipe!
Excellent! Wouldn't change a thing! But to save time, I used a rotisserie chicken. I think it has a better flavor!

Sorry. Did not like and will not make again. With all the high reviews I thought this would be a sure thing. It's BLAND. I followed the recipe to the letter. It needs FAR more seasoning. I would LOSE the monterey cheese, it's creamy but has little flavor. I would add cheddar or something with a little bite and I would definitely add seasoning to the chicken when cooking.

I am definitely giving this a 5 star. I believe if I had actually followed the recipe to a tee I could probably give it a 10 star but for some reason I could have sworn that it said one cup of flour when it was a fourth so I added an extra can of chicken broth but my mistake was only trying to fix the mistake that I made not to improve or put my own twist on this recipe. I think that the enchiladas were wonderful and if I had followed the recipe correctly they would have been phenomenal. My family was raving about how good they were with my mistake next time I'll know it's a fourth of a cup and not a full cup thank you so much for this recipe it was wonderful.
This makes 5 regular size flour tortillas in a 9x9 pan.
My guys loved this. I thought it could use some tweaks but enjoyed it just the same. It was easy to make and made the family happy. Score!!

I can't get canned chopped chillies here in Australia, so I used jarred jalapeños and chopped them up. I only used about half the amount because I didn't want it to be too spicy for my kids but still have a little kick. Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly. My kids didn't love it, they still found it a bit spicy, but they tried it at least. I enjoyed it, but I don't think it will be a regular meal for us. I have had nicer enchiladas made with a kit. I feel I can still give a star rating as I'm not adding or leaving out anything, but rather subbing something that shouldn't change the recipe much in my opinion.

When I made this recipe, I had high hopes. When I had it for dinner that night, I wasn't too impressed. It seemed bland. I almost pitched it, but don't have money to just throw away. I froze the remainder in two 8x8 disposable pans I had. Not knowing what to get out of the freezer, I chose one of these casseroles. It was absolutely amazing! I guess the same result could be had by making one day and having for dinner the next. I think the extra time just heightened/melded the taste. Will definitely be making over and over. As far as tweaks, I believe I added a can of Rotel w/cilantro to the chicken mixture. I DIDN't make a note of it because I DIDN't think I would be making again. Thank' s for the recipe Deb!
Wanted something simple but have it taste like I was slaving all day making food and this was perfect for just that. Yummy
This recipe turned out great I love it!!!!!!!!
I left our the green zombies, as don't like them, but I found I had add salt to the sour cream/flour mixture. Otherwise, @THIS DELISH. My husband LOVED IT.
Enchiladas may also grow spicy with sour cream, cheese, chicken, and flour tortillas even when baked.
Amazing!!! Most definitely a keeper. I love spicy so I added more onions, some garlic and jalapeño peppers to the chicken when sautéing.

OK, this has really been bugging me so here goes ...I am a born and bred desert rat from NM. FLOUR tortillas make Burritos. CORN tortillas make enchiladas...PERIOD. In 2 yrs this is only the second comment I have posted. I use many recipes from here and most are very, very tasty.

Made as listed and directed except I added more fresh (Hatch) chili than called for and I didn't have enough sour cream, so I toped it off with yogurt. It was good but a bit more tweaking next time.

This sounds like a great start for making sour cream enchiladas. Some of the reviews started that the finished product was not flavorful enough. My suggestion would be to simmer the chicken in a combination of water and adding one chopped onion, six chopped garlic cloves, Bay leaf, salt, half a tablespoon of peppercorns and a Serrano chili. Simmer chicken until it can be shredded. When done, the chicken will have more flavor and can be used in the enchiladas. The broth from the simmered chicken is extremely flavorful and can now be used for the sauce. I love the simplicity of this recipe and can't wait to try it. Thank you for sharing this with us

This recipe was the best! Using chicken stock, instead of cr of chicken soup, was brilliant! The enchiladas were not as heavy as I've had in the past. My husband couldn't say enough. Will be making it again.
Best sour cream enchiladas I have ever made. Thank you so much for posting the recipe. I did use corn tortillas instead of flour only because my family prefers them. Your recipe is delicious.
Really enjoyed this dish, so did the whole family! I'm going to make some tweaks next time though as I found the sauce too thick and not enough of it.

Made almost exactly and they turned out great

Made the enchiladas wow wonderful thanks for your recipe definately make again!
Easy and delicious.
Best Chicken Enchiladas ever!

I made this and wow. Phenomenal. I added my homemade fresh pico/salsa to kick it up a notch. I also cut the chicken in thin strips and made my own chicken stock. You won't be disappointed.

I make enchiladas and have not used this recipe...I use rotisserie chicken...the breast...I fry onions and garlic and add a few red pepper flakes and sauté...then add my cooked chicken and a sprinkle of taco seasoning. and a small can of green chilies..not spicy. Remove from pan and let cool a little and then stir in sour cream to make a pasty mixture...put this in corn tortillas and put echilada sauce over...bake...I like to add cheese on top the last 10 min. this way you have a creamy mexican spiced center...you can add more pepper flakes if you want spicy..or add a dash of ceyanne to the enchilada sauce....and a nice saucey outer...I also like to spinkle finely chop green onions or cilantro on top before serving and serve with a simple crunchy salad...just lettuce and cucumber with a little avocado....this is the best...you can fry the chicken..put in the refrig. the nite before...add the sour cr. and roll them right before you are going to make them....add sauce and bake...you can add a little rice or black beans to the mix...I use this over and over and it is great!!!!!

I have made this a few times now. The first time I made it exactly as written and it was good but bland. The next time I used Rotel instead of chillies and it helped a little bit but not everyone cared for the spice. I made it again tonight as a double batch but added a McCormick enchilada dry sauce packet (just the seasoning, ignoring the packet directions) and about 3 spoonfuls of minced garlic to the meat and onions while it cooked. Then when I made the sauce, I used garlic butter for half the butter. This helped the flavor tremendously while keeping it very mild. I served it with salsas too so people could up the spice individually. Also, I used the carb smart tortilla wraps and they worked just fine!

Holy Guacamole! These are delicious! I love the idea of starting the sauce with a roux. I used poblano peppers instead of canned green chilis. I blistered them with the flame on my gas range, peeled, seeded and diced them. I also added about a 1/2 tsp to 1 tsp (didn't measure) of smoked paprika to the sauce. I roasted the chicken breasts instead of frying on the stovetop. I rubbed them with evoo, salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cumin, and chili powder. In the end, I dont' think how you prep your chicken will make much of a difference in the final dish, but just wanted to share what I did as a suggestion (I prefer the passive cooking of roasting - haha). I do suggest using your choice of fresh peppers, as I think that can really elevate this dish.

LOVED IT. Though I am a person who likes to tweak. The only thing I did different was how I made the chicken. I boiled my chicken and as it was boiling I chopped the onion up. Then I just mixed it together and followed the rest of the instructions.

OMG was this good.  I was eating it out of the pan. We just love this recipe thankyou & it is busy bubbling away again in the oven right now. It is so quick, easy and adaptable to whatever is in the house at the time.

I did add some garlic and used regular onions, I added the two (probably closer to three) tablespoons of sour cream to the cream of chicken soup.  I also added a few splashes of half & half, and I sprinkled cheese on the top in the last 10 minutes.  I also let it rest about 15 minutes after it was cooking to let it thicken up a bit and to let the flavors kind-of meld together.  Another thing: I added some pasta!  Even though it had potatoes, it was a very small layer of thin potatoes.  It was really good. Oh wow, this is just a classic. Easy to make and very different. The pepper does give them a nice kick, but blends so well with the vanilla, you'll love the combination of flavors. I can see why HeatherFeather loves these so much. I'll make these often.
