I did half the batch with fresh black peppercorns(ground ultra fine), and the other half I did plain with cinnamon sugar on top (just in case the pepper wasn't to my liking).  I really loved the pepper, and would do a whole batch with it next time.  I made a reduced calorie version (4 T butter, 1 T lecithin, 1/2 c applesauce, 1/4 tsp guar gum, 1 c splenda, 2 T corn syrup) instead of using 1 c butter and 1 c granulated sugar.  Using a small cookie scoop, my batch turned out 38 1/2-oz cookies (might've been 39 or 40 had I not pilfered some of the dough before baking...).  Little pillows of yummy goodness!  These would be great with a lemony glaze.

Wow, what fantastic cookies, Heather!! I made them yesterday to be sent off to family in Canada, and I know they're going to love them as much as hubby & I did - these little gems are like a really good quality sugar cookie with a little zing from the pepper. I found out halfway through measuring out the pepper that I'd run out of black pepper, so I used half black pepper & half white pepper, which still worked really well. I might try using all white pepper, so that people *really* can't tell by looking at the cookie that it's got pepper in it! Thanks for a really great recipe that will be made over & over again around here :-)

These cookies are wonderful!  It made my mouth water as I was making them, and couldn`t wait to try one...2...3..! When hubby was looking for something for his sweet tooth, he found these and just scarfed them down....so zingy...but yet just the right amount of zing!  Luckily I managed to "save" a big tin-full, for part of my Christmas collection of cookies!  Thanks, Heather, for sharing this.

These are a big WOW!  They're incredibly delicious, pretty, and simple to make. I used freshly ground pepper. The recipe works perfectly, and I love the size of the cookies.  Thank you for sharing this amazing recipe!
these are great!  i had to add an extra egg to get it to stick together.  also used 1/2 splenda--can't tell!  next batch i'm gonna sue red sprinkles for the drinking glass step.  THANKS!!

I, too had to add an extra egg. I don't think LARGE eggs exist anymore unless you happen to live on a farm or near one. Hubby took a batch of these to a potluck at work and there was enough dough left over to make ourselves a batch and then some. We love the "secret" ingredient. Thanks HF!
Delicious!  I was a little afraid of the pepper, so I used less than what was called for, and wished that I had used it all.  Thank you for a wonderfully different recipe!

I've never had black pepper cookies before, but I was so intrigued by this recipe, I had to give them a try.  These were my absolute favorite out of the cookies I made for Christmas this year.  You taste the pepper (mine was ground pretty coarsely) but it somehow tastes like it belongs.  I bet this would be an excellent butter cookie recipe without it, too.  Thank you!

The pepper in these cookies is a little too strong and I wish I would have only used 1 tsp. But my DH really liked them. I will be making these again with a few modifications. I plan on keeping them small "two-bite" cookies. This is a great recipe to make from what you have in the pantry.

I made these at Christmas time to add a little something different to the cookie tray. They were easy to make and people asked what was in them, but very few would have guessed pepper. Good recipe. I will make it again, keeping the cookies on the smaller side, as someone else suggested.

These are delicious cookies.  Mine browned perfectly on the bottom and top and looked picture-perfect.  You could tell that it was a butter cookie, and also a pepper cookie, so the intended flavors came out divinely!  Thanks for posting this recipe!
These were ideal with coffee/tea! You have to watch the clock carefully to take them out of the oven at the perfect time. My first batch was good, but the second divine!
Yuck! I wanted to like these, but man. Pepper and cookies do NOT mix. BF didn't like them either. Sorry, these were just too spicy for a cookie of our liking.

heather, these were wonderful!  in fact, i used 2 tsp of pepper to "step" the taste buds up!  i will do one thing different....i made them too thin;thus, they were a little fragile...easy to crumble.  thanks for the unsusual recipe. patsy

These were delicious!  I made a few changes--I decreased the pepper to 1 tsp (fresh ground) and added 1 tsp rubbed lavender  buds.  I flattened them very thin, and baked them for about 5 minutes, and got about 75 cookies. I pressed them down, and then topped them each with a small pinch of demerara sugar.  They looked beautiful, and would be perfect for a classy tea party!!  This recipe is definitely a keeper, and I will use the base dough for other add-ins!  Thank you, HeatherFeather, for a tasty treat!
Very easy to make and they look great. They're very mild as far as spicyness goes (to me, anyway) but still a nice butter cookie.

I will start by apologizing for not using the correct amount of pepper.  I chickened out after having read some of the reviews.  These cookies are great and the next time I will use the 1 1/2 teaspoons.

These cookies are great! I have made them several times, and sometimes I seperate the dough and make some without the pepper just so I get a variety (also, some times I ice some). A trick I use is to put the dough into logs in the fridge for a while.  That helps me make even balls as I can just slice evenly and then form the balls from the slices.  Thanks for a great recipe!

Wow - I was really intrigued by the idea of black pepper, and all the positive reviews - I couldn't resist trying them. They were straightforward to make, and came out pretty well. Very much like a sugar cookie, with a bit of something - but you Really couldn't say what. I used fresh ground pepper, mediumish grind. I liked the flavor, and even my picky 4 y/o DD, who won't go near food with specks of pepper in it, enjoyed these. I never told her - tee hee. Actually, I did find them very mild, and would up the pepper next time.  (Only reason I didn't rate them was because I'm personally not a big fan of sugar cookies.) I will definately try this pepper-in-cookie concept again, although I would probably try a shortbread recipe. Now, I am also thinking chocolate fudgy with pepper...

Wow - these "zing" in your mouth! I wasn't real impressed the first day I made them - maybe because they were still warm. If I like a recipe I review it; if I don't like a recipe I don't review it because it may be that I didn't follow    directions exactly, etc.  But the day after I made them I tasted one and it was excellent!  A very good butter cookie and then the pepper hits - but you really can't tell it's pepper; it just seems to give it some extra zippity doo-dah!!  My four grandsons loved them!  Please try this recipe and give the cookies a day for the flavors to meld together!  Excellent recipe!!

I hardly ever bake, but these were easy to make and came out delicious.  I didn't have baking soda so I left it out and they were still tasty!  I also added an extra egg.  Plus, the dough was very stiff and almost burnt out the motor of my cheap RiteAid mixer.  I recommend these for other inexperienced cooks like me,  just use a better mixer.

Made two batches today.  One with pepper and then used recipe to make wonderful Chocolate chip cookies. Love the bite of the pepper.  Very light in color with I love for CC cookies.  Definately a keeper.  Thanks a lot

these are delicious. i think the other members of my family are having a little trouble with pepper in their cookies, but its a very subtle, engaging flavor that is best when savored (not a cookie to be gobbled). Also, they turned out very pretty, which was a welcome surprise to a beginner baker like me -- my cookies are usually just brownish lumps. 
  Just a note; mine spread out a LOT during baking, so wide spacing is a good idea.
I thought these were great.  Sort of a sugar cookie with a bite.  The pepper is very subtle. Not too sweet, just a light cookie to enjoy.  Thanks for something different.
Excellent.  My kids love the idea of Mom using PEPPER in cookies!  Used this recipe for the Xmas Cookie Swap.
These were great!  a very sweet start, then a hint of "oh my".  Will definitely make more.  A pampered chef small scoop makes them uniform.  I'll use coarser sugar on top next time.
I really enjoyed these cookies, but after I ate some, all I could taste was pepper - even though I only used 1 tsp. I will definitely make these again, but without the pepper.
These are a great butter cookie. My kids bit into them and immediately recognized the pepper. My husband says these are his new favorite.

I made these during Dead Week this year (pre-finals week)because I needed something to do during my break from studying... so I decided to try a new recipe and I'm glad I stumbled upon this one. 

It's good but so different then other cookies. I used fresh ground black pepper from my pepper mill and the spicy flavor really popped. I think I will add a dash of cayenne next time as well.

Yummmm... I didn't tell my family that there was pepper in these cookies until after they had eaten and raved about them :)  They are really good - and something a little different.  Thanks for the recipe HeatherFeather
I wanted to like this but I just couldn't. Just so I could eat it, I added more sugar topping.  But still..I didn't like the pepper. I'm sorry.

I accidentaly used bread flour instead of all purpose, but mine turned out great!!They were a little puffy, not flat, they were soft on the inside and crunchy on the outside, tasted real buttery, couldn't even tell I put fresh ground pepper in. I don't think I am gonna tell my family about the pepper, because even though they had no complaints so far as soon as I tell them they will change their minds. Oh yeah I used real butter . Thanks for the recipe, terri

I LOVE THESE! This is definitely one of those things that people are either going to love or hate. I made a half batch as I thought they may not be for me. I thought 1/2 in balls seemed very small, so my balls were probably 1 in. I rolled the balls in the sugar instead of dipping a glass. I then smushed my balls with a glass. After seeing how thin they ended up, I don't think I'll waste my time smushing the next batch. I will make these alot. They leave a little after-zing in the back of the throat, which just makes me want to go eat some more. Thanks for posting!!!!

This is a scandinavian cookie. Prepared in the cold winter to warm your palate and  body while drinking coffee or hot toddies. I have made these for years and have not dipped in sugar but will do so now.Sometimes I use white pepper when I put them in a Christmas basket for neighbors. I usually get calls for that "special cookie"
that was in the basket. Great recipe, I am glad that you have posted. My Grandma was Swedish, other relatives Finn, some German and some English & Irish so take your pick, they all knew and cooked this recipe which is delicious!

These are awesome cookies. I added more pepper than the recipe called for by about another teaspoon, I love the black pepper kick. I also added a half teaspoon(ish) of ground ginger, allspice, cinnamon, and ground cloves. I was craving super spicy cookies and these were the perfect cookies to host all the spice. I love that they are not overly sweet and they get beautifully crisp when cooled.  Perfect for this rainy, grey day. 
Thanks for the recipe!!
These are fantabulous! Great flavor.Thanks for sharing. Joanne
These are definitely interesting.  The pepper surprises me every time I try one.  I'm not sure the pepper/butter cookie combo works as well as the spicy ginger cookie combo, but is novel and fun.

I really liked this recipe.  I think I will try the suggestion of adding other spices like ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg along with the pepper.  A nice "adult" cookie, but even my two granddaughters liked them and didn't realize there was pepper in them until I told them.  Mary

I found these last night while searching for a spiced cookies recipe I used to have. Made a batch last night to try out then made a second batch today to give my DB & DSIL. I didn't have any sweet butter and not enough of the other so I used Butter-flavored Crisco. They came out great although I only got 32 out of the batch as I used a scoop and it made a larger cookie. Thanks for a great recipe, one that will be used often.
Really enjoyed these.  Not too sweet, with a subtle bite of pepper in the finish.

These should be illegal, so addictive they are probably bad for my health.
I had never heard of black pepper cookies but was intregued enough to read a few reviews and eventually bake some.  Well.....I've baked these three times in the last week.  They just seem to disappear.
Fantastic taste and texture and a great base recipe for other flavours.  I havent yet but intend to try these with nuts and chocolate but still love the pepper.  
If you aren't a big fan of pepper on't worry.  My husband hates pepper so I just offered him a couple and once they'd been swallowed told him.  He thought they were different but also thought they were fantastic and was not put off having more lol.
Happy baking.

We really liked these.  DH didn't think they sounded very good but he was pleasantly surprised and enjoyed them.  I used freshly grounded pepper.  Maybe I made the cookies too small, but I had over 5 dozen cookies.  I baked mine for exactly 8 minutes and let them cool on the cookie sheet for 3 minutes and then moved to wire racks.  Will definitely make again.

I made my first batch as written, and while hubby loved them I found them a bit bland.  So the next batch I added 1/4 tsp of nutmeg and that was perfect for me.  Hubby still liked original better, so I will have to keep making half of each.
Thanks for such a unique recipe!
These were great! I took them to a potluck and got several compliments. Thanks!!!

These are incredible.  I've never had a pepper cookie,  I wasn't going to put the sugar on top but it gives it the final touch.  I baked a batch, along with some oatmeal cookies.  Rolled the rest of the dough and put it in the freezer.  When I want more I just thaw and bake.  YMMM

These were spectacular.  I wasn't sure what to expect...and on first bite, I was disappointed because I thought this was just like any other sugar cookie.  But that little peppery kick followed and I was delighted! I might "smash" them a little less next time because mine looked nice and rounded on the way out of the over and when I turned around they had flattened! :) Thanks for the great recipe!

These will make my Christmas cookie list for sure. Wonderful little cookie. Ease of prep-10 stars; taste- 10 stars; weird ingredient-10 stars; and your wonderful cooking tip about eggs and shrinking in size-10 stars. Thanks, Heatherfeather, for this GREAT cookie recipe. UPDATE: made these for Christmas baskets and everyone loved them. Try this recipe today!

Very good cookies.  I made them as written except used salted butter.   My picky 15 year old says you can taste the pepper and so he wont eat them but I think they are marvelous.  They do have a bit of a bite to them but in a really good way.  I will make them again to keep some dough in the freezer in logs.  They will be great for last minute company.  I'd like to try them using the added cinnamon that some reviewers mentioned and maybe some chipotle powder to kick the heat up even more.  Yummy.

A good cookie. 5 stars for being different. I wimped out and only used 1 tsp of pepper. I used a scooper for the balls and was impressed with the uniform shape that resulted after squishing with the sugar/glass. I wonder if there is another spice that could also be used in place of pepper. What about cardamon?

These cookies are interesting to say the least and very soft. I really like how the pepper gives it a kick that is totally unexpected. I was skeptical about using 1 1/2 tsp of pepper but it isn't overpowering at all. Overall, my batch yielded a little over 2 dozen. Thanks for sharing this unique recipe!

These were very good.  Not as peppery as I would have liked, but I was still able to catch some in the flavor.  I think these would be good with a bit of ice cream inbetween two.  Will be doing these again.  Thanks for posting!

Interesting... I haven't decided if I like them yet.  They were nice and buttery with a little peppery after taste.  My kids hated them (and I didn't even tell them before they tried them what the "secret" ingredient was), but I was on the fence.  They are nice with coffee... not overly sweet.  Not bad tasting... just maybe an acquired taste. I doubt I will attempt them again as I was the only one in the house that would eat them.

Nice cookies! I rolled the dough into balls and dipped them in sugar. They turned out very nice. These cookies form a nice base for lots of future experimenting and variations on a theme. They'd also be nice without the pepper for just regular sugar cookies for the less brave among us. :) Thank you, Heather.

Fab.U.Lous!  followed the recipe exactly and I used freshly ground black pepper. I might add just a tiny bit more pepper next time to up the "kick" by a notch. Thanks for sharing a recipe I will definitely use many times. They're just different enough.

I loved them, my husband thought they were weird.  He actually tried to convince me not to put them in the gift baskets I was preparing, but I think he was turned off by the idea of pepper in cookies.  Everyone else who tasted them loved them, so I'm giving them 4 stars in honor of my husband.

Love. Them. These cookies are wonderful and intriguing. I like making people guess what the secret ingredient is. I've made them twice now, and the second time I changed three things. I didn't flatten them, i rolled them in sugar, and I ground some fresh pepper on top of a few of the hot ones. I whole-heartedly recommend all of these things (only the extra pepper if you like the kick). When you don't flatten them they come out a little more fluffy but they still flatten nicely - I prefer that to how they are when you flatten them. Thanks Heather!

ok, we had high hopes for these. But, they were a total let down.  You fail to mention if you use the store bought already ground black pepper or fresh. We only use fresh, and well.. Yuck. The dough was so sticky and hard to work. We ate them so as not to waste the food, but otherwise they would have been in the trash. I am soo very glad I didn't double the recipe like i usually do.  These were gross. sorry.
What a wonderful cookie! They are very easy to make, and taste great! Don't be afraid of the pepper, in  fact, I'm going to up it to 2 tsp the next time I make them!

Ok, I'm hooked! These are the best butter cookies! They're sweet and buttery and that subtle pepper taste just puts the flavor over the top. I used coarsely ground fresh peppercorns. I should have doubled the recipe. Next time I will. Thanx so much for posting this!
I hate black pepper...don't like it in any of my food, but was really curious about this recipe.  I tried it and to my surprise, liked it!  It's a weird combo but pretty good

I put these in my Christmas baskets/trays and of the dozen included they were probably the biggest hit or miss cookie.  People who enjoyed them absolutely loved them and those who didn't enjoy them didn't like them at all.  I rolled mine in the larger decorative sugar and they were very pretty cookies.  I'd also make them as just a butter cookie, omitting the black pepper as they have a great texture to them.
We love this recipe. I make it with and without the pepper depending on my mood.
These were just okay in my opinion. The pepper part was good but the cookie was lacking something...flavor.

Review is based on the dough, alone!  I know, not safe to "lick the beaters" but I did.  Yum.  I put my pepper mill on fine and would probably use slightly courser next time around (and a full 2 tsp) but I like things spicy!  I also added half a bag of white chocolate chips and toasted, thinly sliced almonds for a bit of crunch and extra flavor.  YUM!  Thank you for sharing!  I will definitely make these again and add orange zest to see how that goes...

After seeing a photo of these on Spice of the month I KNEW I had to try it.  I was so NOT disappointed.  Followed the recipe to the letter and the kick of the pepper was just enough to wake up your taste buds.  Everyone kept asking "what is in these that makes them so good"  These are a sure repeat whenever I want something a little special.  I think next time the only thing I'll do differant is put the dough in the fridge for about an hour before flattening to see if they spread a little less.  But it couldn't make the flavor any better than it already is.

These cookies came out super tasty and youre right people say: "Mmm, this is good, but what is it?". :) Everyone loved these buttery delights. I had a bit of trouble with the dough, though. It was too buttery and the cookies spread a lot, I almost ended up with one giant cookie. lol
Next time Ill simply reduce the butter by maybe 1/3 cup. I milled my pepper very finely, but only used 1 ts as I thought it might be stronger than the store-bought stuff. Also I reduced the soda by half as the German soda seems to be a lot stronger.
THANK YOU SO MUCH for sharing this unusual, but great recipe with us, Ill add it to my cookie tray this year. Cant wait to give these to all of my friends.

I love this cookie.  I already added a little extra pepper. I am going to experiment with 25% more, 50% more 75% more and double pepper.  Today though, I am baking them for a High Tea after the dedication of the library at church.  Added after the event:  people were really talking about this cookie AND going back for more and more.

I wasn't sure how much I liked them the first time I made them, but other people thought they were great. The second time I added finely grated zest of one lime, lovely and subtle....I would try adding a little more zest next time.
I liked these, but I thought they would have been better without the pepper.  Thanks for sharing, though.

A very odd cookie. I expected it to be a little different but it really wasn't my favorite. They would excellent cookies without the pepper but with it they are simply okay. My family had a similar reaction, it's a weird taste, but edible. For me 7 minutes was perfect. I greased one of my cookie sheets and left the other ungreased both came off very easily.
This recipe was bad. I made it exactly as it said and the cookies came out way too greasy and spicy. Will not make again.
hope you dont sneeze while making this recipe due the pepper

Oh my gosh!!!!  This is wonderful!  I made it for friends and family on Superbowl Sunday.  Everyone loved it.  They not only licked their fingers clean but also cleaned the dip bowl.  I will not wait for a party to make this again.  My teenagers want it for after band practice next week!
This dish is excellent!  It is a great appetizer (or meal) to bring to a party, or, have at home anytime!  Very tasty!
I made this for an office party and it was a H*U*G*E hit!  Very easy and creative use of Hidden Valley Ranch products that I always have on hand.  This is going in my "go to" recipe file!
Delicious! Made these for my Bunco group and they cleaned the plate. Everyone wanted the recipe. Definitely a keeper recipe for get togethers.

I was looking for something new to serve, so I thought I would give this a try.  WOW, by the time I was finished cooking EVERYONE was in the kitchen, and couldn't wait to take a bite.  LOVED IT, am going to make it again, and again and again.
You should make these again, they were really good! I went back in the kitchen to get more and they were all gone!
This recipe was delicious! I can't wait to eat these again!
I thought this recipe was fantastic!  My kids are very picky and they have asked me to make it again.  It was also very easy to make after work.  I'll be making it again!
These were tangy and spicy--really good!  I ate most of them myself and only left a couple for dad.  Thanks for letting us be your taste testers!

I would give it fice strs, Really tasty and esy to do .Could be used as a main dish or appetizer.Would be good with ramen noodels or rice as a main dish .Good as an easy appetizer  too. You can also cahnge the heat by using a milder chili sauce rather than sirachi.
Wow!  What a great recipe......will be making it again!
I definitely will give this recipe a try. Looks great.
Delicious!!  Great way to get your kids to eat cauliflower!!

I could not believe how well this turned out.  And did not have to mess with deep frying.  I added some Italian Seasonings just to give a little more somethin.  Turned out great and had a really different take on cauliflower.  Thanks for sharing.

This is a great cauliflower recipe. It was so simple to make that I thought it couldn't possibly be that good. How wrong I was, it was delicious! My boyfriend said it was the best cauliflower he has ever had.

I made this again, but this time, tossed in garlic powder and curry powder. I used minced garlic last time, and the garlic tends to burn and not stick onto the cauliflower.
I loved it!! I wonder if using broccoli would be good...?? Probably!!!

This was a good way to cook cauliflower.  My 3 year old son actually ate it!!! My DH, on the other hand, still didn't care for it.  My sister really liked it.  I would not, however, consider this to have incredibly changed the taste of cauliflower.  It still tastes like cauliflower.

Yummmmy!!! I have just discovered my love for cauliflower, mostly due to this wonderful recipe! I used garlic salt in place of regular salt. The only thing is I left it in for about half an hour, instead of the whole hour because they were starting to burn a bit. I never knew I could like cauliflower so much! I'd recommend this to everyone! Thank you! :-) Oooh I also did it with broccoli and it was just as tasty!
Good!  I added chili powder to the mix and I think it covered up the taste of the cauliflower.  Next time I will make as written!  Thanks!
This is delicious just as is. It's also great with some garlic powder, or even butter/popcorn seasoning.

Wow, what a great recipe. I had baked cauliflower before, but this was just as good with a lot less ingredients. Just be warned, you end up with a lot less than you started with. I thought I had made plenty, but ended up with barely enough for everyone to get some. It didn't help that everyone was fighting and raving over it. Thanks for a great hit!

Let me say this first: I don't like cauliflower.  Whenever Julie made cauliflower I covered it in cheese sauce.  But this cauliflower is completely different and completely delicious!  I don't care that it takes a long while to prepare; I'll be making it myself, too.

This was definitely worth a try....and it was suprisingly good!  Next time I wouldn't add the whole tsp of salt....I found that this was too much for our tastes, but it was really good!  THanks for posting!

Easy,delicious and healthy. What more can you ask for?  We absolutely LOVE this recipe!  Roasting makes the cauliflower sweet, mellow and crispy. Who cares about side dish?  We've had it as the main meal!

Soooooo yummy!  This is now my favorite way to eat cauliflower!!! Both my kids (4 and 2) ate their share and asked for more "popcorn flower".  The four of us (my husband) finished off the whole batch (one head of cauliflower).  At first I was only going to make 1/2 a head, but decided to just make the entire thing.  This is a great side to almost anything, although I baked chicken as well so I made good use of the oven time!  (Update: Try this with fish, it's a perfect side)
Thanks Julesong!

Fantabulous!!!  My husband & I are doing one of the soup diets and finding interesting vegetables to go with it is a challenge.  I made this recipe as stated...except, we couldn't have the olive oil so I very very lightly sprayed with pam.  It was so good that I don't think I will ever use the oil now!  Thanks so much for the recipe, it's as addictive as popcorn!
very good
DH said, "This tastes like popcorn!"  I said, "That's what it is called."  Added some minced garlic.
WOW these were super good. Made 4 batches. 1 sprinkled with dill seed, 1 with fennel seed, 1 with caraway seed and the last but not least with slivers of garlic.  Thanks so much for sharing.
My family devoured this!  I can tell I'll be making this one a lot!

I made this with dinner last night and it was wonderful. Even my picky husband, who "doesn't like cauliflower", loved it. In fact, he had seconds and asked me when I was going to make it again! This is definitely a keeper.

update: I sprinkle a little shredded parmesan cheese over top, and even my picky kids will fight over the last bite! I love this recipe and make it often. (I'm mourning the use of my oven now that summer is here)

I was once broiling veggies in my gas broiler, and I decided to toss in some broccoli florets.  Some were tossed with oil, as in this recipe, and some were just rinsed with water.  The broiler is much faster than the oven,  but the effect is much the same. The broccoli gets a rich, sweet toasted taste with luscious charred bits.  (Take care so they are only bits!)  When the dry roasted cauliflower came out of the broiler, I IMMEDIATELY tossed with finely chopped parsley and drizzled with  EV olive oil.  Superb AND faster!  And greener too, because it saves so much energy, takes only about 10 minutes max in my broiler, versus an hour in the oven.

I HATE cauliflower but had gotten some on sale and needed to use it.DH normally eats it but didn't want it. I found this recipe and tried it. I fell in love!!! To me, it tasted like fried oysters. Gave  DH some without telling him  what it was and he thought it was pork. This is a must try recipe!!!
This is a really wonderful way to serve cauliflower.  The roasting method takes all that sulfurous bland taste away.  Thanks for a great recipe!

This is so frickin' ridiculous, my husband and I couldn't believe it! We tossed it with olive oil and a Santa Maria tri-tip seasoning which includes garlic, sea salt, shallot, and a little onion powder. Fantastic.

I thought this was yummy, and used 2 tbsp of olive oil instead of 4.  Still crispy outside and moist inside- good.  Tried to tell my 2.5 year old it was popcorn but took one bite and spit it out, and my hubby didn't like either, but I will make again for me.  Thanks!
My cauliflower didn't get too sweet...just ever so slightly...but it was very nice regardless.
LOVED this!  Used slightly less oil, and let the cauliflower get pretty brown. Very, very tasty!!!
What can I say but this is outstanding, my kids ate a whole head of cauliflower between them, and said it was better than fries ;-)

Even after reading all of the reviews, I couldn't imagine this could be this good.  IT IS!  I only used half a cauliflower, still doubting, and we all looked at each other wanting more.   Who knew we would finally like cauliflower?  I can't wait to make this for people...they won't believe it, either.  It really is unbelieveably good and fun to eat.  I thought of dipping sauces, but it was gone before I could act on it.  THANKS!
This was very good, though I definately expected a bit more flavor from all the reviews posted.  We used garlic salt, and next time we might add paprika for a little more flare.  Good all around!
Superb!  I served it with sauteed chicken breasts with leeks.  Really yummy.  My DH and I ate the whole head in one sitting.  *burp*
Very quick and easy to pull together. So delicious-even my seven year old ate his veggies tonight!
YUM!  'nuf said.
Yum, this is really good. Definitely a keeper and I find myself buying cauliflower every week now!
Delicious, first thing off everyones plate..

Hate to be the naysayer here because I was really excited about this recipe.  I had a head of purple cauliflower and wanted to try something different.

My head of cauliflower was huge, yet I only needed to use three tablespoons of oil. This was great and easy!  I made this for the German portion of the ZWT II.  I used a wheat beer (hefeweizen) because that's all I had on hand, curious to try it again with a bolder, darker beer.  Used lots of garlic and fresh sage from my garden.  I didn't have anything to spread on it, and so I just ate a piece plain (and then another piece and another piece!).  I thought I had rolled it thin, but I could go much thinner than I did.  The dough is pretty springy so it takes some patience to get it really really thin.  Great recipe Thorsten!
this was really good, like a thin pizza crust. used shiner bock for the beer, and put an italian blend on top. thanks for an easy bread recipe!

Crisp and yummy and sooo easy to make! I made this recipe at 9AM, and I felt a little strange cracking open a bottle of beer so early in the morning! Haha! Remember no drinky before noon! I think I'll be using this recipe often for get togethers or just for snacks. It's a great way to use up that left-over beer too!    
I used dried oregano to decorate. Lovely bread!
I did it!!  Breads are not my forte but even I could do this.  Easy & tasty.  I added a potpourri of fresh herbs from my garden as a topping.  Thanks for sharing!
Very easy to make and very good. We put 4 different blends on 4 sections of bread, all were good. great with a beer and dipping sauce.

Absolutely terrific.  I made it up in no time and we're all presently snacking on flat bread and Thorsten's Domatosalata recipe.  Fresh oregano, basil, rosemary and marjoram were my herbs of choice.  Excellent recipe.

I was overcome w/guilt as I told my teammates "I don't do bread - I'm just not good at it!" So I gave this a try & must say you've ended a decades long "Bread Curse". I used smashed roasted garlic & rosemary as my only herbs & got it just a little crispy, but it was great! Thx for saving me from the "Bread Demon". :-)

Thank you, Thorsten!  I am a military spouse living in Germany and after 3 years living here I have learned that Germans are expert bread makers! (smile)  The bakeries in Germany are simply the best!  This bread proves everything I have loved about Germany!  It has a wonderful, thin texture complemented by herbs and garlic.  Recommended!
Excellent bread!  I made this without any herbs to serve with some Cajun crab dip.  I can't wait to try this again using fresh herbs.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Delicious and crispy. I served it with grilled shrimps and a cucumber salad. Great summer food!
What can I say, it's QET (quick, easy and tasty)!   Thanks for sharing.

I loved this!!  This is so simple to make...I made it to serve with a Tomato Salad it was perfect!  I used Italian herbs!
Thank you!

This is just too easy to make. I love it!! It tastes great with everything! Thanks so much for the recipe!
mmmmm... crispy breeeead :)
Another winner.  I used all oregano on my bread and next time, I will have to adjust the cook time a little...but that is an oven thing!!

As a relatively inexperienced baker, I might have flubbed this somehow, but I'm not exactly sure what I did wrong.  Everything went smoothly until I put it in the oven.  The only ingredient adjustment I made was the amount of olive oil, so if you try this don't cut down on it.  I baked this for over 10 minutes in a preheated oven and preheated tray.  Although small bubbles formed it did not get brown.  I left mine a bit on the thick side, maybe that had to do with it.  It came out a bit soft like it was supposed to.  I used the 4 recommended herbs too.  They tended to fall off the baked bread, maybe because I cut back too much on the oil.  The herby taste was nice though, and it went well with a yogurt based dipping sauce.  I wish I could have been as enthusiastic as the rest of the reviewers:(
Really good and easy!!  I topped mine with a little Parmesan cheese, oregano and the garlic.  I served it with a shrimp scampi and it was great for dipping in the sauce!

Amazing what you can do with flour, beer and salt!  Topped my bread with herbs and caraway seeds and Mr B was suitably impressed.  Although the flavour was terrific, I've given this 4 stars because although I measured carefully, I found the dough was very sticky and difficult to work with.  And the finished result was chewy rather than crispy.  However I suspect that this was my fault as I tried to 'cheat' by making this in my food processor with the dough hook.  I also think I should have tried making two breads from the dough like Inge 1505 did.  Lessons learned for another time.

This is an excellent flatbread recipe, we thoroughly enjoyed it!
I added some sesame and poppy seeds to it as well.
Thanks for a simple and delicious recipe!
I am SO not a baker, as I'm a bit avant-garde when it comes to measurements, but this was really easy and tasted great! I used a combination of fresh thyme and oregano

This was so much fun to make and delicious to eat! A keeper for sure! I've made mine very thin and loved it that way! I ate it with Katia's Tirokafteri (Greek Feta Dip) #170679. Both are great recipes and they work well together! Thank you Thorsten!

WOOHOOOO!! It was JUST as I had hoped it would be!!! EVEN better!! My whole HOUSE smelled like a bakery!!!! NOTHIN' better than bread baking in the oven....ooooh, man!!!! Thanks Thorsten... this will be made ALOT!!!! :)

An excellent quick-bread recipe that is so easy! The toppings for this bread would be almost endless - I chose to top mine with dukkah. I'm very impressed with this recipe and will certainly make it again!!

A great bread. I made it few hours ago and we had it as an snacjk with gouda cheese. I use for the ropping a clove of garlic, oregano, rosemary, thyme and white pepper. I also reduced the olive oil to one tablespoon but next time I 'll use the whole amount because my bread was too crispy. A great recipe that its defenatly a keeper.Thanks for posting Thorsten!

These were very good,although I think I overcooked mine, b/c they came out very tough. The next time I make them, I think I will use butter instead of the olive oil, but all in all it was great. My husband loved it.
Thanks!

I read this recipe tonight, and made it about an hour ago.  It is soooo gooood!  Everyone loved it!  It is a for sure do-over!!
I used garlic powder in the olive oil, and then for the spices on top, I did half with Rosemary and Garlic and the other half with sundried tomatoes and basil.  Excellent!!!

Terrific flat bread.  Absolutely loved it-- easy to make (even last minute), popular with kids and adults, and endless possibilities as far as the toppings one might select.  Of the three we made, basil and oregano was my favorite.  I love garlic, so I actually heated the garlic in the oil over medium heat (not so hot that it browned) to get all that garlic flavor infused into the oil. Thanks for posting!
great bread .dee
Very good recipe.  Easy and straight-forward to make - and disappeared very quickly.  As a bonus, the left-over garlic oil came in very handy the next day for cooking other things!

I have prepared this a bunch of times now with all different kinds of beer from dark to ultra-light.  It was delicious everytime!  Instead of brushing with oil, I sprinkle the top with a small handful of cheese.  Thorsten, thanks for posting such a great recipe!
This was outstanding, I served it with Hummus. The bread was unbelievable and so easy to make.

Loved this used newcastle brown as the beer and it wasn't as bubbly as I thought it was going to be will try a different one next time! Topped mine with Chilli flakes and sea salt. I also baked mine on a pizza stone, if you are going to do this make sure you flour well though!

Super easy and fast! I used Guinness Stout for this recipe. I thought the stout may have been too strong, but was pleasantly surprised. Even the two kids that were here gobbled it up! I used extra virgin olive oil mixed with fresh Parmesan, garlic and basil and a touch of rosemary. Thanks Thorsten.
Made it last night and it was a big hit.  I roasted galic and brushed on with olive oil, then added rosemary...it was gone in the matter of seconds. Thanks easy, and good.
Had it last night with a herb topping,  tasted great!  Will fix again tonight with olive oil and garlic topping. Thank You

Excellent bread, it is crisp and chewy at the same time.  I doubled the recipe and added a bit of cayenne powder to the dough, the dough is beautiful to work with. I formed two free form type of flat breads. I crushed the garlic and added it to the olive and nuked in the micro for about 30 seconds so that the garlic would give off more flavor.  Brushed the oil on and sprinkled on the herbs and baked.  It was delicious I couldn't stop eating it and it was the only thing gone from the New Years Eve Party Buffet.  Thank you for this great recipe.

Wonderful, crispy bread! I loved how quick and easy it was to make, but especially loved the texture and flavor. Rather than using a baking pan, I rolled the dough out on parchment paper, then used a baker's peel to slide it right into the oven onto a hot baking stone. We love garlic, so I did use garlic in the olive oil; for the herbs, I just used Penzeys Italian herb mix, but I can think of many variations I would like to try. I'm sure I'll be making this again often, Thorsten--thanks for sharing the recipe!

This was wonderful and very similar to the expensive bags of pita chips at the grocery store....the only flaws were errors made on my part! I didn't work in enough flour at the end and the dough was difficult to roll out. Will  definitely try again and have fun with testing out different seasonings.
pretty good. i made with some rye flour mixed it. i should have added more salt. i'm a salt monster though.
"Addictive"

Oh, my goodness1 What have you done to me? LOL I am a Bread Addict! Them minute I saw this i ran/not walked to the kitchen and made this. I am munching onit while i type this! :-0. I used fresh rosemary from my garden and dried oregano, alittle garlic salt and red pepper flakes.( maybe a few too many pepper flakes. My Mouth is on fire) I did have some trouble getting the dough to cooperate.  I know flours react differently. It took morr than 10 min. to get golden brown.
Ps; I just discovered that I accidentalyused Lite Beer. That could have made a difference. Thanks for this recipe. It's a KEEPER!!Ingrid

Very good! I made this when my sisters and niece came over. I served it with Spinach Artichoke dip #1209. We loved it- great together. Although the bread can stand alone. So easy, yet so good! Thanks Thorsten.
It was pretty good right out of the oven, but it didn't keep well, even overnight.  An excellent bread for immediate eating, but otherwise not the best.
I took this to work and it was a hit! We enjoyed it as a snack. Very good flavor, (I used  1 teaspoon of thyme, rosemary and oregano.) Will make often. Thanks Thorsten!

I made it for a picnic. everyone enjoyed it and wanted the receipe.
I added sesame seeds to the dough and it gave it a nutty flavor. In the second batch I added italian herbs in the dough and then sprinkled parmesan cheese on top...
A quick and tasty bread.  Used it to dip in olive oil.  Thanks.

I have had this twice.  The first time it was fabulous.  A friend made it and brought it over.  He used a dark beer.  I made it the 2nd time using lite beer and it obviously did not have the strong beer flavor as when the dark beer was used.  For personal taste from now on I will use the dark.  However, the texture was consistant w/ both.  I doubled the batch and used italian herbs on both w/ the olive oil.  I put a colby/cheddar shredded cheese mix on one batch and it was great too.  Thanks for a versatile recipe Thorsten.  I will definately make again!!

What a mission but it was worth it! I was going to cook these on my pizza stone until I realised I didn't have a rolling pin. After I divided the dough in half I put oiled baking paper on either side of the first half and placed it between a chopping board and the pizza stone and.... well stood on it :) It worked like a charm! I put garlic, sesame seeds and cumin seeds on the first one (tastes like it has dukkah on it!), then cheese and dried mixed herbs on the second. I'll be using these instead of cornchips for nachos tonight. Cheers!

Divine.  We loved this bread.  I have never made anything like this before and DD#2 couldn't quit eating the bread.  She has asked several times since then to make it again, so I'm making it for dinner tonight.  It really is so good. I served it with an olive oil w/ pepper flakes and herbs and it was delicious. Thank you Thorsten for this yummy extra to our meals.....Stephanie
This was so easy to make yet it was a HUGE hit at our house!  I will make this again and again thanks so much for posting

Fast, simple, great taste & texture, and versatile. How much more could one ask for? I made this just with a sprinkling of onion/garlic powders to eat with a thick chili. I can see this being great spread with roasted garlic and cheddar. And all kinds of other things! I used about 3/4s cup whole wheat flour and the rest white and it worked out just fine.

I did add the garlic to the olive oil and the house smelled so good!  I also cooked this on a pizza stone--helping to crisp the bottom.  Very fast and easy--served with Pam-I-Am's artichoke and white bean dip----great hold over for yet another late weeknight dinner.

This was very easy to put together.  I sprayed a cookie sheet with cooking spray so it didn't stick.  I didn't have olive oil, so I tossed some garlic powder and dried onion flakes into the oil to sit while making the dough.  I made mine into two pieces because I wanted them quite flat.  One had rosemary, fennel seeds, fresh cracked pepper, thyme and oregano.  On the other, I used Sesame seeds, sea salt, and an italian herb mix.  This is tasty bread, but make sure to eat it fresh.  I put leftovers in a ziploc bag and it wasn't too good the next day.  This is fun to experiment with different herbs.

This was tasty, but a bit too chewy for me. I brought it to a friend's house and four of us shared it. My jaw was tired after eating it, but maybe I didn't roll  it out thin enough. Great flavor though.
I made this twice and both times it came out different I was not happy w/either so i give it 0 stars.

I followed the recipe exactly, and have been impressed so far.  The dough should be split in two, for two manageable pieces that can be rolled out fairly thin.  I used Sapporo Beer - one of my favorites - and used garlic, rosemary, basil, onion powder, a dash of nutmeg, and then sprinkled shredded cheddar cheese over all of it.  Thanks for the great recipe!!

Wow, quick and easy! I made it with a white beer, it came out perfect! I've put a mix of olive oil with basil, rosemary, Provence herbs, garlic salt, minced garlic and it was fabulous! I think that would be great with garlic butter on top! I think I'll try that soon. Thanks for this simple recipe!

Add another 5 star review to this recipe! I took others advice and separated the dough into 2 pieces before rolling. I used Bitburger beer and topped with granulated garlic, coarse ground sea salt and cracked black pepper. I used a regular baking sheet, but will try my baking stone next time. An easy and delicious snack. Thanks for sharing.

Sounded so delicious I made a special trip to the store for a couple things I didn't have on hand.  They are very proud of the parchment paper locally (over $6.00 for a small roll) so I oiled the sheet instead.  Ingredients as directed, used a dark porter beer (it's what I drink) and Italian Herb Seasoning premix.  Only thing I did different was I used a cutter to cut rounds BEFORE I baked the bread.  Photo of how it came out is posted.  First batch was baked at 480f at top of oven for 10 minutes, too soft.  Baked second batch at 500f for 13 minutes, much crisper (note, I live at 2400 feet elevation and I've noticed some things take longer to bake).  Very tasty.

The first batch I made followed the recipe exactly (however I took the suggestion of cutting the dough before baking it) but it was tough, chewy and once it cooled, inedible.  I made a second batch with 1 2/3 cup of flour and baked it for 7 minutes at 480. It was soft on the inside but still crisp on the outside! Delicious with spinach dip!
I wasn't sure how well this would turn out, but it was so easy and extremely delicious.  It was much like a focaccia!

Maybe I just expected more based on all the high ratings, but this failed to impress us all that much.  I made it to go with artichoke dip, and it really tasted just like a cracker.  I was hoping to get more flavor from the beer, but I couldn't taste the beer at all.  Overall, this was okay, but I have other flat bread recipes I like better, so I don't think I'll make this one again.

I loved the flavour of this bread fresh from the oven. However, by this evening when I was ready to serve it, it had gotten really chewy and just hard to eat. I am not sure what I did wrong - maybe I needed to roll it thinner. I will  experiment with it again though as the taste is great. Another reviewer mentioned that she had success reducing the flour so I might start there.

Very tasty!  We prepared with an American amber ale and stirred in 2 tablespoons of sesame seeds. I let the breadmaker do the kneading on the pasta cycle for 5 minutes.  Rolled to less than 1/8 inch thick, necessitating baking on two sheets, but the resulting crispy crackers were terrific.  I held one piece back to see how it held up to storage and found that completely cooled then saved in a ziploc kept fine overnight.  Especially good with hummus and tapenade.
I liked these, might try with a dark beer next time.  You MUST roll these very thinly it you want it really crispy.  I might try my pasta maker for rolling next time.

I've made this a few times with great success.  I love it with the dried herbs on it with extra garlic for brushing on top.  Plus, it's easy.  If you like a chewy thin beer bread, try this one; it has great flavor.  Thanks for posting, Thorsten!
So many things you can do with this!  Individual pizzas, use for dips, a plate in itself if you're camping, etc.  I used Longboard (it's a light lager).  Soooo good!
Loved it with our soup fresh from the oven.  WOW!  I only added kosher salt so will try other combinations.
I followed the recipe. I'm not a fan. It came out hard & w/ not much taste.

I used this as a flat bread pizza crust and it was AMAZING! The first time I split the dough in 2 and baked until 3/4 done, pulled it out of the oven, put on sauce and pizza topings then baked til it looked done. It was a little on the crispy side, but great. The left overs heated well in the toaster oven. The second time I didn't prebake, just put the pizza together on the raw dough and baked at 475*. It was chewier. It depends on how you like your pizza. I can see so many possibilities with the recipe! I have tried several "thin n crispy pizza dough" recipes and this is the first one that I have really loved! It made two crusts that basically filled 1 large flat cookie sheet (2crusts on 1 sheet) Thanks for a great recipe.

I have made this receipt twice now and I love them.  They don't last long at my house and I'm the only one eating them.  I also gave them in gift baskets with coffe.  Everyone I gave them to have ask for the recipe.

I've made this a few times and everyone always loves it. Homemade biscotti is always SO much better than storebought because it doesn't hurt your teeth to bite into it. I usually substitute half of the flour with whole wheat flour to incorporate more fiber, vitamins, and minerals, and it still tastes great!

This recipe is delicious! I made it for the holidays with my mother. The butter made it rich, and the cranberries made it festive.

This one is a keeper!

This is the best biscotti recipe I have ever made! I've had people tell me that they would pay for this in a coffee house. This recipe is easy, and looks great! Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.

I was about to post the identical recipe, which I've made for years.  So instead, I'll just give this recipe the 5-star rating it deserves.  Make them just as directed with a couple hints-  1 1/2 cups dried cranberries equals a 6 ounce package, and I only use about 1/2 cup white chocolate chips for the drizzle.  I also enjoy using dried cherries as an alternative to cranberries, as suggested, but I chop them and soak them first in 2 T. amaretto - yumm!
Very tasty! I used macadamia nuts instead of almonds, very good biscotti

Wonderful!  I used the extra 1/2 cup of sugar and sprinkled raw sugar over the egg white before baking.  My BF kept saying they were "so-so", but I noticed that he ate almost the entire batch!  And this with several other cookies and candies around!  I made another batch to give as gifts and they went over very, very well.

Very good and easy recipe. This is my first time trying to bake biscotti and I like the results. I've never eaten biscotti so I don't have anything to compare the results to but they're tasty.

I did have one question: when I mixed everything together the batter was dry, crumbly dry, and it didn't expand at all in the oven. I only was able to get 17, 1/2 inch pieces out of my two loaves.

Any suggestions out there? Will be trying this again very soon!

Love this recipe! I used craisins and chopped them up in my food processor a bit before adding them to the batter. I also used a Silpat instead of parchment paper which worked very well. Now to experiment with the recipe a bit to make it lower in fat and sugar.

Fantastic!!!  These were so easy to make and are so, so, so tasty!  Like another reviewer, I increased the almond extract by a teaspoon.  Used craisins that I soaked in orange juice for about two hours beforehand, then drained and squeezed all the liquid out.  And, because the dough was a bit wet, I added two tablespoons of polenta, which stiffened up the dough a bit and gave the finished biscotti a nice little crunch and texture.  I was a bit worried about how soft the dough was, but all turned out ok.  Just make sure not to put the two logs on too small a cookie sheet - because they do spread quite a bit. Can't eat nuts, so left them out and didn't miss them at all! And no chocolate drizzle because I have to draw the line somewhere - LOL!  Note:  I think the wetness of the dough is due to the amount of water in the butter here in Costa Rica, not fault of the recipe.  Thanks for posting, Kittencal!
I like this recipe but the cranberries got hard after baking.  I guess i should have soaked them in some kind of liquer before putting them in the batter...thanks for the recipe
Excellent recipe! Very easy to make.
This was a great lunch that we ate during the week. I only used the yellow corn...store didn't have any white. I also used a red bell pepper. Made for PAC Spring 2013.

Very good soup! The only change I made was I used 1 tsp. cumin since I wasn't sure if 1 Tbls. was a typo or not. I figured under spiced was better than too spicy. :) I really enjoyed the hint of lime in the soup. I served it with tortilla chips. Thanks for posting!

Sorry, but neither my husband nor myself cared for this. First of all, Maple syrup is expensive and in this dish it was wasted because the extra sweetness was not needed and the good maple flavor was overpowered by other flavors. The cinnamon and ginger fought with each other for dominance and I don't know which one won. The end result was a dish that had many good things in it but none of them tasted good.I doubt I will try this again but if I do I will leave out the Maple syrup and cut way back on the cinnamon and play with the ginger. The idea is good. Again, sorry for the poor review.

Very interesting recipe. I have to agree with the previous reviewer in one respect. I think the maple syrup wasn't in keeping with the rest of the flavors, I know it's there to avoid processed sugars but it just doesn't jive with the rest of the recipe in this case. I cut the raisins back to a scant 1 tbs to cut the sugars and that amount was plenty for me. After tasting the cooked cereal I added another 1/4 tsp of cinnamon to balance off the ginger. I should say that I made a single serving. I didn't use the soymilk simply because I never use milk in my porridge. It was a nice change but I would skip the maple syrup next time.

I liked this, but based on the other reviews I did tweak it a little.  I soaked overnight 1/2 c oats, 1/2 c water, & 1/4 c raisins.  In the morning I added 1 T maple syrup (1/8 c just looked like too much), 1/8 c Recipe # 295198, 1/4 tsp cinnamon, & 1/4 tsp. ginger.  I thought it was great!  Reviewed for Healthy Choices ABC Tag.
I made this a loong time ago, but forgot to review it.  Pretty good, probably nice to take around for a quick lunch too.

These were so yummy! I love the flavors! I served with some salsa and some sour cream. I liked them so much I took them to a fellowship dinner(vegetarian) and they were all gone in no time! Thanks Cheryl!

These just worked so well; they rate as the most succesful fritters I've ever made.  Spot on for consistency (i.e. the mixture holds together beautifully - not too wet or dry) and excellent flavours.  Thanks for posting, this recipe is a keeper.
Great fritters!!  I loved the feta...it made the fritters special! The ingredients were spot on, I didn't have to add extra flour or liquid. Perfect.  Even better when they cool to room temperature!!
WOW! The feta cheese really lends itself to this dish. These were exceptionally good. I couldn't resist rolling them in cornflake crumbs cause- well- I'm just a rebel and will never be any dang good.
They are like Latkes but better~~~!!!!  Wonderful with scotch bonnet sauce~!
Great!  I used feta cheese and served them with a yogurt sauce that had a bit of mint in it.  The texture of these is just right--very crispy outside, lovely and soft within.  Thanks, Cheryl!
Absolutely fabulous.  My family loved them.  I made as directed and servered with the Creamy Cucumber Dip (Recipe #29455). We will be making this again!! Thanks for a great recipe.
OMG, these were fantastic!  I used feta cheese and dried dill as I didn't have fresh.  I can't wait to make these again.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I've had this recipe in my cookbook for who knows how long! Simple to make and delicious! Who can resist feta? Used fresh Italian parsley from the garden. Served with Palestinian rice and lentils (#81339), dinner rolls and fresh fruit. Others are right, this is an excellent way to use up a bumper crop of zucchini. The fritters could also be served as a breakfast entree for a change of pace from potato pancakes. Thanks for posting! cg ;)

I've made these twice now, once with Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (didn't have kasseri or feta on hand) and once with feta. The feta really makes the recipe & gives the fritters a unique taste. Next time, I'd like to try the kasseri. As suggested by Chef Fredo, we dipped these in Creamy Cucumber Dip (#29455). Thanks for a very nice fritter  recipe!

Delicious, unique flavors-I loved these! I used feta and dried parsley, and cut the fresh dill down to 1/4 cup. I served with sour cream. Wonderful recipe, I'll be making more as soon as my zucchini plant produces some more! Thanks!

Outstanding! Now I look a my zucchini plants with LOVE.
I forgot to add the dill, I used fetta cheese and I added a little extra parsley.I could eat this fritters every day.
Very flavorful. Easy to make, I used feta cheese. These made a wonderful side dish. Thanks for the recipe.

This was my first time making fritters and they were fantastic!! We ate them warm for supper and the following day my company ate them cold and couldn't stop raving! I sent them home with zucchini from my garden and a copy of this recipe. Yummmmmmmy

Holy cow, were these good!  I omitted the dill since I don't like dill.  I also rolled the mixture into small balls and fried them for appetizers instead of making patties.  This worked great!  Thanks.

NcMysteryShopper- thank you thank you! I was amazed at how great these were both hot out of the pan and cold the next day. I used Haloumi cheese and sage and mint for the dill and they both suited really well. Oh -and I couldn't resist a squeeze of chili paste! Hope you don't mind me altering the recipe a bit! Excellent recipe find for me!
I served these for Easter dinner and received rave reviews!!!  What a wonderful change from plain ole veggies.  Made exactly as postedâ€¦ PERFECT!
Oh my goodness. These were so delicious. They came out perfect. (I think that I used Feta Cheese instead.)
These were really great!  I had an extra yellow squash & used that in place of one zucchini. It added a sweet taste, overall a little time consuming but worth it!
This was really delicious.  We make something very similar (well, identical, really) in Greece so I was quite aware of what to expect.  This is great served with tzatziki.
Loved it - easy and fabulous - so very tasty
Really enjoyed these. Used feta cheese, and didn't change anything in the recipe. We had them as a side with Turkish Meatballs recipe #83793, sliced tomatoes, and warm flat bread.

This was delicious!!!

I have an overabundance of yellow summer squash in the garden so I used it instead of zucchini.  I also used about twice as much squash as the recipe calls for and added one more egg, a bit more flour, and a little baking powder.  We had it as a vegetarian meal with tzatziki and a greek salad.  YUM!

I made these first with the dill and no cheese and served it with tzatziki. I also made it without the dill and feta and used Italian seasoning and pecorino romano, and served it with marinara.  BOTH were delicious.  Next time I'll try baking them around 425 and flipping them to get them crispy like frying without the calories.  This is a great recipe.  Thanks

I do believe I've found a new favorite side dish! These were wonderful!!! I added a little red bell pepper for color and had to use dry dill. The flavor and texture was wonderful. I used a good extra virgin olive oil, and sprinkled with kosher salt when finished. I also made a quick sauce out of garlic, greek yogurt and lemon juice to serve on the side. Thank you for this wonderful recipe!

MMM!  The first time I made them I used dried parsley and dried dill and they were really good.  The second time, I used fresh herbs, and increased the amount of feta slightly and they were outstanding!  Thank you for posting this one.
These were really yummy! Easy to make too. They go really well with tomatoes and salad, this will be great in summer when I have heaps of zucchinis in the veggie garden!

This was excellent! When I was back in college, I had many friends from Turkey and have tried many sweets, but nothing savory. This was so delicious; I could not stop eating them. These fritters have such a refreshing, herblike flavor, and my family loved them with hot sauce. Thank you for sharing such a wonderful and tasty recipe to be made again and again.

YUMMY as can be!
LOVE are low fat, healthy for me!
LOVE dill/feta combination,
Enjoying these now with GREAT elation!
Thanks!

I'm not a huge fan of fritters,   but these are pretty good.  They are a great way to use up zucchini.  I only had frozen Zucchini and they still worked out fine.  I will like them even more with fresh.
Great when freshly made or even teh next day cold. I love to make a large batch and will snack on them for the next day or two. They are fantastic as breakfast.
I have to give this 5 stars. My dh and dd's both said. "Make this again!" With 2 veggie girls this is great for them.

Ev, since these were cooked on live fire, I changed the procedure a bit. Really wanted the recipe but it was 95 degrees and didn't want to heat up the kitchen.
I mashed the garlic between foil. Chopped up fresh Greek oregano and added both to the olive oil and lemon juice in a large skillet. I put the combination on low heat and infused the herb and garlic into the oil and juice mixture. By the time the garlic turned a light tan, the proportions were just right. Then I strained out the solids and brushed the tater sections with the oil/juice before miking 8 minutes. Then skewered them, put on the grill after brushing with the goodies. Turn, brush, turn, brush, etc., until done. I brushed them again with the oil/juice before serving.

Amazing, it was the hit of the BBQ.

I can't believe I forgot to rate this recipe.  This became a quick favorite at our house after the first try.  Have never even tried it cold yet - it's all gone while its warm.  Thanks so much for the great recipe.

A good little potato salad recipe.  Only thing I did differently was to add a couple of chopped hard boiled eggs.

Absolutley wonderful!!! I had my family over last weekend for a BBQ and I made this salad and it was a hit. I would definently make it again.

This potato salad is SOOOO good! We made it twice this weekend for some gatherings with family and friends. It was a huge success! Both times we doubled the recipe and the bowl was scraped clean. Thank you for such a wonderful variation to the old standard!

Delicious potato salad! This is only the second time I've made potato salad.  I don't like mayonnaise, so I've been looking for one that has more of a sour cream base. This was great! Will definitely make again!!

This recipe was great. My husband is a big fan of the potato salad at the deli around here and I thought I would give this a whirl. OH MY GOD!This is a great potato salad.I made this for a barbecue when friends popped round-they demolished it!My husband demanded that I made more for the next day!The second time I mixed some cheese,bacon and onion through the salad itself,and it was delicious.This is definately the only way to make potato salad!Thank you!
This is the best potato salad anywhere.  Be sure to chill for at least a couple of hours. YUMMY!

I served this for Easter family dinner and it was received with mixed reviews. I loved the taste, but I did add more dressing as I felt it was too dry. Not that this salad needs another 5-star rating, but it really deserves it.

Glorious!  I used new red potatoes and left the skin on, and combined everything while the potatoes were still warm.  It went over like gangbusters!

went looking for this recipe after I tasted the version at our local grocer. i don't even like potato salad, but I could sit and eat this all up in one sitting. I removed the skins which I will continue to do in the future when i make this. But this first time I didn't have any cheddar cheese - will try that next time.

This went so well with my ribs and corn on the cob last night.  I loved the flavors in this potato mix.  I used red potatoes with the skins on, and it came out great!  We will have again soon, as it was enjoyed very much here!  Thanks for sharing with us Lois!

If I could rate this any higher I would definately have to!!! For a potato salad hating family (I'm the only one who likes it)I got lots of moans when I told them what our side dish for dinner was, but by the end of dinner they had eaten it all AND were asking for more! Holy Cow!! This was soooo good. Made it today for Easter dinner and everyone scarfed it down. Will be making it a staple for BBQ's, get togethers, etc. Thank you so much for the best potato salad recipe
What a great and different way to prepare potato salad!  This went so well with my ribs!  Make sure you let this sit for awhile in the fridge for all the stuff to meld together.

This is my fav baked pot salad recipe.. it's perfect

I have been looking for this for so long! Thanks for posting, it is wonderful!

I think this is the best potato salad I have ever made!  I followed exactly as written and it was perfect.  I enjoyed the bacon and cheese, there was just the right amount of dressing, thanks so much for posting

this was good...potatoes stayed well formed and everything...first time that ever happened for me.  thanks for posting
This is the most fabulous recipe! Every time I make it we get rave reviews!  fantastic! don't change  a thing!!

This recipe rocks!  The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because it could stand to have more chives.  Also I used celery salt and I think a bit of season salt would give it more flavor.  We had a barbecue last night and this was everyone's FAVORITE dish!

This was very tasty and the dressing is super creamy!  The reason I took off one star is because it didn't really blow me away, but it was really good.  I may adjust the seasonings next time to reach the "wow" point.  Goes great with BBQ brats & burgers.

This was a great recipe. The only problem I came accross, is that it needs to be made at least a day in advanced for all the seasons to combine. After 1 day it was GREAT!! This is just like Corky's BBQ in Lexington KY.... Its one of the best you will every find.

Excellent!

This is awesome! I don't have alot of experience making potato salad, but I have and often end up a little disappointed. Not so here! Will be saving this recipe - thanks for sharing!

Great recipe although I think it could have used more sour cream and less mayo. Thanks.

Fab! All my guests loved it! It certainly wasn't a potato salad they would expect!

Oh my this is so amazing!  I hate potato salad and this one was just delicious...everyone loved it!  Brought it to a BBQ and it was gone quick.  I'd almost suggest doubling the recipe because it only makes a small batch.
So so so good. And I don't even like potato salad! This is delicious, hot or cold.

This was good and easy to make. I used two cans of sliced potatoes. I followed the rest of the recipe as written. I did have to add a bit more sour cream and mayo. This was different but we enjoyed it. I liked it better the longer it sat.
I adore potato salads, especially homemade ones and this was a real winner! Mind you, with bacon, cheese and spring onions, what's not to love? Tasted great the next day too!

Loved it! I baked my potatoes in microwave - 7 minutes on each side. Only thing I added was from another's review that suggested red wine vinegar - it really bumps up the flavor. Hubby said this is the best potato salad he has had (he generally prefers American style with the mustard).

This was delicious!!  I made it for another family, but got to enjoy a piece with them.  The only change I made was to use some garlic powder in place of the thyme.  Thanks for posting... I will be making it again!

I made this for a barbeque I was having, and EVERYONE loved it! Very good! Easy to prepare too!
Very easy to prepare - used it for a superbowl snack.

Pretty tasty.  It definitely was easy and fast to put together.  I used only a 1/2 pound of kielbasa, halved the ketchup & sugar, and used all the pineapple.  It is VERY sweet. This was really good!  WAY-SUPER easy and the sauce was a mix of barbecue-y, sweet, and tangy.

My family and I loved these sweet and tangy sausages. I served the sausages and sauce over rice as a main dish. Very tasty, easy, and economical. Thanks Denise.

YUM YUM YUM!!!  This was so delicious...and so easy to make!  I cooked it for 1 hour on high and then 1 hour on low, and it was heated through and the flavors well-blended.  Everyone in my family agrees that this was one of the tastiest kielbasa dishes they have ever had.  We ate it as a main course with rice and veggies.  I have a habit of only making the same recipe once or twice, so my husband told me "Please keep this one handy, and make it again!"  Thanks for sharing!

What a RAVE REVIEW!....I swear the entire neighborhood has now made this easy to prepare dish.....I made it last week and since then three of the neighbors have called for the recipe. Wow...My husband said...make sure you by more Kiebalsa this week...this is awesome.

I've made this twice now and it has been enjoyed by all.  Served over rice.  My husbands response was how much more tender the kielbasa becomes when slow cooked. A little on the sweet side but I  loved it! Ran out of kielbasa so ended up using some smoked sausage I had along with crushed pineapple instead of chunks. I had ALOT of sauce left over so I froze it... planning on throwing it on a ham I toss in the toaster oven someday!!!

I've made this twice now. The first time I used packaged meatballs and this time I followed the recipe. It turned out a winner both times. Very good and sooo easy to make and best of all, no leftovers from the potluck! Thanks Denise, this ones a keeper.

Liked the sauce a lot. My 2yo loved it, and she's not a big meat eater. Can also cook the kielbasa per pkg directions and mix up the sauce and simmer the kielbasa for 30 minutes in a saucepan if you don't want to use your slow cooker.
Thought this was a little too sweet. Perhaps some vinegar, some green pepper and some onion would even this out a bit. Thanks, though. Definitely an easy one!
I added 1 onion, 1 green pepper and a few splashes of soy sauce.  Very good; very easy.

Hubby and I loved this! Hits the spot and super easy.  The only change I made was to add some chopped onions and bellpepper.  Might have to start using my crockpot more often!  Next time might buy skinless kielbasa (personal preference).

DH gives this 5 stars all the way. He gobbled most of it up the second it came out of the crockpot. I halved the recipe and cooked on low for 2 hours then kicked the temp up to high for the last 30 minutes. Served over rice. Inexpensive and really easy. It only cost $3.78 to buy the things I didn't have on hand. I will be making this again very soon!

Denise, this was a big hit at a recent Christmas get-together.
Thanks!!

I am a big fan of this recipe. I love it mixed with plain white rice.

This gets 5 stars on the ease of making it alone! DS wasn't to crazy about the pineapple chunks but he's 13...what does he know? I loved the sauce.BF ate two plates of this and said that I could make it again. Thanks!

I may try it again, monitor the cook time carefully and add some soy sauce as a similar recipe had this listed as one of the ingredients.

We really liked this.  Even my picky toddler ate it which is enough to warrant 5 stars in my mind! I also made sure that my pineapple was unsweetened.  I'm thinking if you have sweetened pineapple you should probably cut back on the sugar.

I hate it when I am the lone dissenter, giving low marks to a popular recipe...but honest reviews are what make this website successful.

husband really liked the flavor on these!

This was good. I made this last night for dinner and my family liked it.  The only thing I will do different next time is add less ketchup.  I served this was buttered noodles and green beans and it made a nice meal for something different.  Thank you for posting....Stephanie
This was a huge hit at our annual church "Luau".  I will absolutely make this again!
Very good, made it as a side for Easter dinner, everyone enjoyed. Thanks.
Not bad. A little too sweet though. I served it with rice to tone it down. Maybe a little less ketchup would help.

WOW!!! This was so quick and easy to put together and it was a huge hit at our annual 4th of July barbeque.  I plugged the crockpot in out on the cottage porch and it was ready when our guests arrived.  Thanks, Denise!

this was just not something we enjoyed as a family. way too sweet and the saltiness of the keilbasa just didn't mesh well. I paired it with rice like others suggested but it still just didn't do much for us.

Loved this simple, easy dish. I made it for a work lunch and served it over rice. I liked it so much, I made it for us to nibble on during the Sunday football games. Tangy and sweet, but not too sweet. Thanks Denise.

I served this as an appy at my Christmas Eve party and it was a total hit!  It was sweet, but a bit tangy as well. Thanks for posting!!
tasty! even the non-kielbasa eaters ate this! I did cut back on the sugar like some have recommended. can't wait to make it for my next party. Thank you for sharing!
