And being the first time I had bought a roasting chicken, I was shocked at how cheap they are! So much more affordable than the seperate parts. I am wiser! Thanks!!!!!

Flavor filled, moist chicken with all the fat cooked out of it - excellent recipe.  The juice that cooked out is totally a jelly and will be put to good use as soup stock.  I used a large fryer and cooked it for 5 hours on low then turned to keep warm for another 1 1/2 hours.  For the last 1 1 /2 hours I added small whole onions to serve as one veggie, also served Garlic Mash Potatoes & steamed fresh green beans.  Wonderful meal.  To night I am have chicken Enchiladas and I know they will be very good filled with this tasty chicken - Thanks Kathydesrosiers

This is so good!  I used a chicken with a pop up timer and it popped up after 9 hours - I used the high setting for 2 hours and then turned it down to low for the remainder of the time.  I used the seasonings and measurements exactly as stated and it was so delicious!

Delicious!!  I had to make mine in the oven alas, as I found this recipe four hours before dinner - but was it ever good!!!  I used your advice and subed in the lemon- wow!!!!  Thanks for sharing this one!

My chicken was pretty small cause , well so is my crockpot.  Chicken had great flavor, couldnot have been easier to make.  Think the time might be a little long but followed directions exactly in that respect.  Leftovers made fantastic pot pie and another dish we will just call chicken surprise.

This was FANTASTIC!,I have only had my crockpot a few months and I must say, this is one of the best things I have made in it so far! I followed the recipe exactly except that I cut the cayenne down to 1/2 tsp. and this was still plenty spicy for me. I did not have a ziploc bag large enough for the chicken,so I placed it in a stainless steel bowl and covered with plastic wrap, and popped it in the fridge overnight. I cooked it as directed on low and it was ready for me in 6 hrs. I too ,as others, thickened the juices with some flour & water and this made an unbelieveable gravy, did not have to add a thing to it, so much flavour! Hubby got up from the table and exclaimed it one of the best meals I ever made! We had the leftovers for supper again tonight and he is still talking about how good this chicken is!,as a matter of fact, our grocery store has roasting chickens on sale this week, so he picked up 2 more for the freezer today....something tells me I will be making this chicken again very soon!!!!!! Thanks, Kathy for a fabulous recipe!

If I've learned nothing else about crockpot cooking (I use my crockpot at least twice a week), is that chicken is very unpredictable when done in a slow cooker. One second too long and it turns out terrible.  So I've sworn off chicken in the crockpot forever.  I've made this recipe twice, the first time it was great, this week it was terrible.  Just be careful of the time cooked, it will ruin it if it's done too long.
This chicken is delicious!  I used BOTH the onion and the lemon!  The flavor was delicious, and the meat just fell off the bone!  Thanks for sharing!
Very good, smelled great while cooking.  I followed the advice of others and rubbed some of the seasonings between the skin and chicken.
Just adding yet another 5 stars!! This is a fantastic recipe and I will use it every time I make a whole chicken! Thanks!

I had to go to work, so my daughter did the cooking.  It was too late in the day to do it in the crock pot, so she did it in the oven--(also no time for the overnight refridgeration).  When I got home from work that night she said it was a really great flavored chicken.  There was none left for me to taste :(      So when I went to the store I bought two chickens and put in the freezer...the next time we make it I will get to taste.  :)

This was my first attempt at a crock pot recipe in probably 9 years!  It was very easy to follow.  I think we overcooked the chicken b/c my husband had to work late and I was at school.  It ended up cooking about 11 1/2 hours on low!  It was still very good- just a little dry on the bottom.  I didn't have any cayenne, and I think that would have added the zing the chicken was missing.  I will DEFINITELY try this recipe again when I will be home earlier!  Thanks for a great chicken recipe!

Can We Say KEEPER!!!!! I followed the recipe and my Chicken came out so very good. We are having it again tonight. It only took 4 1/2 hours to cook. I watched for the little timer to pop out. Great thank you very much for such a tender good tasting chicken.

Fantastic! I made this for my family several times, we love it!
I went to visit the folks at Christmas and made this for my parents, they loved it too. This recipe is being pasted around to all the relatives. Thanks for sharing!!!
Love it, love it, love it, what more can I say?!?!  I have also made this in the oven, 250 degrees for 5 hours!  Wonderful both days!

Decided to remove the skin from the chicken first, then apply the rub and refrigerate overnight. A 5 pound hen finished on low in 5 hours.  A bit spicy for my taste but perfect for Dh and the juices made an outstanding gravy when thickened with cornstarch and served over mashed potatoes.

I have made this several times and forgot to rate it...My family just loved it and has requested it several times.  The chicken falls right off the bone and I put some of the juice from the crockpot add some flour and gravy master and it makes for a nice gravy to add over chicken along with mashed potatoes ..YUM YUM :)    Thanks so much for sharing

What a great recipe this is. Instead of putting a chopped onion in the bottom of the crock pot, I put a quartered lemon. I also put some lemon slices in the cavity of the chicken. Well, I'm telling you, the gravy is fantastic, it has such a nice lemony flavor. The chicken was moist and delicious. I only thickened a small amount of the juices to make gravy. There's so much left over that I  will use to make a great tasting lemon chicken soup. Thanks for a keeper, Kathy

This is fantastic and so very easy.  Loved the spice combination.  By cooking one of these on Friday you would have chicken for sandwiches all weekend.  Much cheaper than going out and buying a BBQ Chicken.  Thanks for posting.

This has to be the BEST crockpot chicken recipe! I have used this recipe for a year.  First time I made this recipe, I did not have white pepper, so I sub'd it for black pepper, and I still do not have Cayenne pepper in the house. Tasted absolutely delicious!!!! Chicken falls right off the bone, and the juices are amazing "as is" over the chicken and mashed potatoes, or as a thickened gravy.  I have tried the rub on a pork roast, cooked in a CP as well, and it is delicious that way as well.  I have also used chicken pieces vs. whole chicken - equally as good!  I have even reduced the salt to 2tsp.  You can even by-pass the refirgeration part - I've used both, and the chicken is equally as good.  If chicken wasn't so expensive here in Canada ($10 for a large chicken) I would be making this every week!  We love, love, love this recipe!!!! Thank you so much for a wonderful family recipe.  Steph in Ontario
This was very good and so easy to make.  My family enjoyed.  So tender andjuicy.  Will definately add this to one of my favorites.  It took 6 hours in my crockpot.

This was out of this world fantastic! I cut the spice mixture down to 1/2 and cut the salt down to 1 tsp. I only used a 5 lb chicken and it was done in 8 hours on low. So tender and the liquid made a wonderful gravy. My husband says this is the best chicken he has ever had. Will make this a staple for sure!
Wonderful! This is the first time I tried cooking a whole chicken in the crock pot.  My family loved it.

Very good!  I kinda steer away from chicken in the crockpot because my experience has always been that it comes out dry.  Not this one!  I used a Butterball chicken (which I feel is more flavorful) and placed chopped onion and about 10 cloves of garlic in the bottom.  Great recipe!

There are already so many great reviews of this recipe..but I'll add mine too.  This is the absolute best way to make a whole chicken. It truly falls off the bone!  I now buy several chickens when they are on sale & stock my freezer....it's an unbeatable economical meal when you add a salad and a simple vegetable.
I thought this recipe was wonderful!!! It will now be a regular weekly menu item!  The meat was very juicy and full of flavor!  It was just excellent.

Great recipe, very moist. Chicken was 3 1/2lbs. Cooked for 6hrs. on low. Browned in oven. Used onion,garlic & 1/2 a lemon.Used leftover meat for casserole. Will be making this again when chickens are on sale. Thanks Kathy.
Yum!  I left the chicken in the pot for six hours and the leg fell off as I was taking it out.  Followed the recipe exactly and will make this over and over.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Outstanding!  We've been making this on a weekly basis now and it's become my standard chicken recipe.  The drippings make a delicious base for chicken soup, although I "tone it down" a bit with some chicken broth.  It doesn't get any better than this!!!!

Wow! You get 3 sets of 5*'s from my family!

I had to do them in the oven (I was doing 2 , heck I don't even think ONE would've fit in my crock pot) and did them for 5 hours at 250°.

This is absolutely the best chicken I've had in a long long time! NOT dry , very tender, the flavor is wonderful! I can't handle much heat, this was fine for me. Great balance of flavors , MMmmMmm!!!!

I served it with mashed potatoes, and gravy made from the incredible drippings.

This is definitely a keeper in this house!!!! Thanks for posting it Kathy!!

There is nothing quite like coming home to a prepared supper and this recipe makes for one terrific meal.  The wonderful combination of spices make for an aroma that greets you before you open the door! There's not much I can add to what has already been said other then yes this is an absolute winner which is equally good  made in the crock pot or in the oven. Thank you  Kathy for posting this fantastic tasting chicken recipe.
Excellent and easy! Thank you Kathy for this wonderful recipe that I will be fixing again and again.

This is one of my "fool-proof" recipes that I make when I am in the mood for leftovers, or if I find a good sale on whole chickens.  You really can't go wrong with this recipe!!  Everyone always asks for it! Thanks for sharing.

I made this for dinner last night, and it was fabulous!!  I followed the recipe exactly, refrigerated the bird overnight, and cooked it for 9-10 hours on low.  The meat was so tender, there was a lot of juice that made great gravy and the spice mix was very tasty, just the perfect amount of heat, not too hot.  This is definitely a keeper!
I believe that the name of this recipe should be changed to "AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS AND TENDER WHOLE CHICKEN CROCK POT RECIPE".  Need I say more?...Okay, I will... This was tasty goodness!  Ten stars!

If there was 10 stars I would give this 10. Absolutly fabulous. I made exacly as shown used 4 lb chicken, not roaster, in crock pot for 4hrs low then 3 high just because I came home, and decided to eat earlier. Fixed brown rice and turned drippings into gravy. I only skimmed fat. Poured gravy over rice. I had to stop myself from overindulging. As a weight watcher, I am very very grateful for this recipe, because I'm not a big fan of chicken, and it gets really hard to eat it all the time. Kathy I'm in your debt.

Nicely seasoned without being too spicy (I was concerned about all that pepper!)and fell right off the bone. Too keep it from sitting in its juices I made some foil balls and set the chicken on top of it. This worked great.  Thanks for a keeper recipe!

I didn't get the big taste thrill that so many others did. I made as directed, who no creative additions.  The kids loved it, but I felt that the chicken was mushy and not very flavorful. The chicken disintegrated in the crock pot, so I used the meat for a chicken and rice dish. This was just not what I had expected.

Great recipe  for chicken in a crockpot!! I did the last half hour of cooking in the oven to crisp the skin up a bit.The texture of the chicken was very good too, often I find that the let down of chicken in a crockpot. Nice flavor and color because of the spices.
Will certainly make this again!

This was beautiful and tastes great! I let the spices only sit for an hour and I forgot to put my onion in, but neither mattered where taste is concerned. Talkin' about falling off the bone- it most certainly did...and moist! I mean moist! I almost added a tad of water to the bottom because I was going to bed when I put this on, and I'm so glad I didn't and followed Kathy's directions because I had liquid all the way to the top. I have high and low on my crockpot, so I put it on high for two hours and dh cut it down on low for me and then it cooked for about 8 more hours. I know that seems like a long time but the chicken was perfect and moist. I didn't plan to cook it that long but I was exhausted and couldn't get up. Main thing is- it didn't hurt it one bit. I used the pop up timer as suggested so I am posting a pic. I will be using this recipe with the same spices again! Well deserving of it's stars! Thank you Kathy!!!

The method was perfect - 6 hours in my crockpot made the chicken very tender yet still juicy.  As for the flavour, we just found it to be too much onion.  We'll definitely do this again but with half the onion.

This recipe was ok.  I was a little dissapointed ... 79 reviews and it wasn't the best chicken I've ever had.  We thought it had too much cayenne pepper (a little too spicy) which played down the taste of the chicken.  It just wasn't all that I thought it would be.

I made this chicken tonight, followed the recipe with no changes and 5 stars it's not enough !!! Definitely a keeper. Cooked on low for 7 hours, and the meat was very juicy. Thanks Kathy for posting a great recipe :)

Wonderful! One of the best crockpot recipes around! Chicken is moist and tender with lots of flavor. I used 5 chicken breasts with bone and skin, rubbing some of the spice mixture under the skin before refrigerating overnight. Cooked in my 5 quart crockpot for about 5 hours but I think 4 would have been plenty. Used the time bake on my oven for some macaroni and cheese and had a lovely meal ready when we got home from baseball tonight. Thanks, Kathy, for sharing the recipe!!
Thank you so much Kathy for this recipe. This is the best whole chicken i ever made. My DH and friend loved it.

I thought this was a really good recipe. I was a little unclear in the recipe when to add the chopped onions, so I tried this recipe two ways; by adding the onion with the overnight method, and also just slicing them into rings and making a bed out of them before adding the chicken to the crockpot. I also tried it the second time with out marinading it overnight and it still turned out fabulous! Thanks for the keeper, it's great for us working people!

Fabulous, Fabulous!! I followed the directions for prepartion as stated and wrapped the chicken in plastic wrap.  I  cooked it in my crockpot on Low for 10 hours. The chicken was Fabulous and the gravy was outstanding. I love cooking chicken in the crockpot because it remains juicy and tender. The meat just fell off the bone. This is a true keeper.
Does this recipe need another 5 star review? Yes! Excellent flavor, moist chicken and makes great leftovers to boot!

This is truly great!  I wanted roasted chicken but it's too hot to use the oven (105 in Texas today).  I was skeptical about how this would turn out but I couldn't be more pleased with the results.  I cooked a 4-pound bird on low for 10 hours and used shallots, fresh rosemary, lemons and whole garlic cloves as the "base layer".  I also altered the spice mix a little because I wanted it less spicy and more "herby".  It came out moist, tender and delicious and it couldn't have been easier.  I served steamed new potatoes with capers and crumbled feta on the side.  This will be added to the regular repertoire.

I used an oven bag for marinating overnight then had my teenager place the chicken right into the crockpot, bag & all, when she got home from school.
Dinner was ready when I got home and the clean up was a breeze!

Finally a crockpot chicken that came out tender and moist.  I did cook the chicken breast side down, just wanted to try it that way.  The gravy was the prettiest color and the flavor of the gravy was the best we had ever tasted.  Great recipe!!

This chicken was great, however a tad on the salty side. I gave ya 5 stars anyways because it was very tender and moist, and my kids loved it! However i'd cut down the salt to 2 teaspoons and see if that does the trick :) Also made a gravy/au jus sauce out of the drippings and it was great I had to add about 3 cups of water though because of errr the salitness but again the taste was awesome and I froze the rest for stock. I also stuffed the cavity with the lemons and added the onions on the bottom of the crockpot. :)

I love making Roasted chicken but it's been so hot this summer that I've been forced to alternative means of cooking whole chickens.  This is a really good substitute.  The skin won't crisp up but oh well!!  The flavor is very good.  And it's just SOOOOO easy.  I made 2 of them, so one marinated a day longer.  The 2nd was even more flavorful. So if you plan ahead I would suggest marinating an extra day.  Also I recommend you rub the spice under the skin as well.  Thank you so much for a very good crockpot recipe!! I rarely use mine but it's a lifesaver this summer =)
This was awesome.  My chicken came out moist and tender and the taste was out of this world. I will definitely make this again.
This was perfect. Easy to make and I made a thick gravy from the drippings which was really good !!
Great tast and easy to make, gives the chicken just a little bite
I made this today and will make again , hubby loved this , I served it with MizzNess garlic potatoes and green beans ,What a meal, Thank you for sharing
Very good and easy........ I added carrots and celery made a great broth to serve over rice:)

Very good and easy chicken recipe.  The broth makes really great tasting gravy.  I shredded the leftover chicken and the next day I had hot chicken sandwiches with mashed potatoes and gravy.  Mmmmmmmm!  Thanks for the recipe.  It is definitely a keeper.

Kathy, This is a wonderful recipe. I put my spices on the chicken the night before and wrapped it in saran wrap and put it in the crock pot the next morning. The family loved it and wasn't too spicy even with all the pepper's.. This will be made again and I didn't change a thing. My cook time was longer because I used a large chicken but had a nice broth when finished. Thank you for a keeper!!
Yum-O!  This was wonderful falling off the bone chicken.  Couldn't have been easier!
Very good, made the recipe as stated and turned out great.

Five Stars Kathy ! DH "not-so-fussed-on-chicken" actually liked it more than a lot of chicken recipes I have made in my efforts to convert him, so this makes it a keeper and a 5 star recipe in my book any day.  I'm glad that you mentioned that no liquid needs adding because I was a bit worried about that..  and yes it produced far more liquid that I ever thought so the bird wasn't dry at all. No pop up timers here, I cooked mine for 6 hours and it almost fell apart as I lifted it out of the crockpot. DH and I ate our portions with the meal and later nibbled the bigger leftovers between us, and I popped the bones and smaller scraps of meat into the crockpot later that night and made Recipe #55282 for chicken stock that turned out brilliantly. Thanks for a wonderful easy chicken recipe that DH less grudgingly approves of ...and that's saying something! LOL.

I am a vegetarian, but I was recently given a free organic chicken to try. I thought I'd cook it for Christmas dinner for my meat-eating family. This recipe was such a hit! I will definitely cook it again!

This was the best chicken I've ever eaten and my husband and his mom were in total agreement. Next time I make this I'll use less of the cayenne and black pepper and salt. I added some flour to the drippings to make a tasty gravy.
Can't wait to make this again, thanks for the recipe.

This recipe was fabulous!!!  (I did cut back on the salt though) Like another reviewer, I thickened the resulting juices but made them smooth with a hand blender rather than strain out all "the good bits" !  What little was left over I added back into the gravy left in the crockpot and it made great hot roast chicken sandwiches.  Served with fresh hot biscuits and a couple of different veggies it is an instant family fave!  I'm a very succcessful lowcarber so next time I'm going to thicken some of the juices with a flour alternativwe for me.  This might be my new comfort food!

Brilliant & very easy recipe which I made over the Christmas period to help me out - we had cold chicken sandwiches! I put fresh thyme inside the chicken instead of using dried - only because I had it in the garden, it was lovely & subtle.I also placed a whole lemon in the cavity which gave it a bit of a zing. Wonderful recipe - thanks for sharing it with us!
This was fabolous and so easy!  I thought that it was unusual that there would be no liquids but the chicken produces its own!  Wonderful recipe, will make often!

this recipe was excellent!!   My niece and nephew slept over last night and I made this for dinner.  There was enough for me, my husband and all five kids!  plus some leftovers.  The chicken fell right off the bone and was very tasty.  I didn't have time to marinate it overnight in the ziploc bag but it still came out great.  I will try that next time though.  And the chicken cooked on  low for about 7 hours, then high for 1 hour.  My crock pot is an older model.  Thanks for the great recipe, I'll be making this one over and over again!

Kathy, I finally got to make your fabulous crockpot chicken, well I can see why there are so many wonderful reviews on it, it bakes out SO tasty, moist and tender! I browned mine firstly on all sides before adding to the crockpot, I used a 7-pound roasting chicken and used all the spices that were stated in your recipe, I love this and plan on making it many more times, THANK YOU so much for an outstanding recipe!...Kittencal:)
I tried this with chicken thighs and drums and baked in clay roaster for about 2 hours. This was so tasty!!! I'll be making this often. So easy to make.

You forgot to say that this is melt in your mouth chicken! I love the way it turned out. There was a little too much cayenne pepper for me but I don't eat the skin anyway. It literary fell off the bones. Quickest chicken I ever deboned! I made this for dinner and we ended up not eating dinner due to to much snacking from the super bowl...lol. So, I it the next day for chicken tacos, GREAT for that. And then, I used the leftovers in my chicken salad(check out my recipe). Very yummy. I will definatly be making this again. A whole chicken is so much cheaper at the store and with this recipe I can use it for so many different things! THANK-YOU for sharing this with us!

I'm not sure what the 111th review can add, lol, but here's another 5 stars from me. I cut the cayenne down to 1/3-1/2 tsp because I wasn't sure how strong it would be for the kids and bumped the garlic up a full tsp. It had a nice zing to it and I think with the cayenne overtones, the leftovers would be great in tacos or burritos. Thanks so much for posting!

I FINALLY got around to using this intriguing recipe and it will become a mainstay for sure!  Due to time constraints, I ended up using one of those oven bags, placing the 4 1/2 lb. bird...with no timer!...into it after applying the rub.  Bag directions suggested cooking time of a little more than 1 1/4  hours but a phone call sort of distracted my clock watching and it was more like 1 hr. 40 minutes in the oven.  Not to worry... chicken was perfect.  I immediatedly  picked the bird clean, licking my fingers as I went along (ssshhh!)... the flavor is just outstanding!  I used the meat for enchiladas. Talk about delicious!  My advice is to grab a couple good -sized roasting chickens when they're on sale and use this recipe to prepare them...Way better than a deli rotisserie chicken, bigger, MUCH CHEAPER, and wonderfully flavorful... GB

Awesome, I made it for my sister and her boyfriend and friends, everyone loved it.
Tracey

I really don't think that this  recipe needs yet  another rating,but I will review it anyway.Superb.Easy to do,minimal preparation and the end result is excellent.This recipe is a keeper.I plan on making this in  the summer and shredding the meat to make lots of chicken salad!
Easy and delicious!  I didn't have cayenne or white pepper, so I used extra black pepper and some Old Bay Seasoning.  Worked great.

Lowered salt & added a little brown sugar to the rub. Refrigerated overnight. I lost a couple of limbs on the way out of the pot as chicken was fall of the bone tender for sure. Texture was a little different but we did not find it bad. Made nice sandwiches the next day. Thanks!

I'm not ready to give this stars, yet, as I forgot to put it in the crockpot yesterday. However, I roasted the chicken in the oven after having left is in the spice mixture for 24 hours. I have to say it was the best roasted chicken we've ever had! I can't wait to try the crockpot version...
This was one of the best chicken recipes.  The smell while it cooked was divine and it was fall of the bone tender.  It is a keeper for sure.  Thank you for posting it Kathy.

I wanted to post a picture of this, but we ate it before I could!  This is really good.  I have to confess though, in my haste this morning I put in 2 t of cayenne and forgot the onion powder.  I also didn't let it sit overnight.  I smeared the rub on, put it in the crockpot and ran out to work.  It was terrific to come home to such a nummy dinner!  I added sauteed greens and potatoes and it was perfect.  Thanks so much!

This recipe was delicious and the first crockpot recipe that I have ever tried that was really good! My husband loved it and he is not usually a lover of chicken. Easy, easy, easy! My son was supposed to turn it off for me after 5 hours, but it ended up being 7 hours and the chicken was perfect!!

This is the second recipe I've tried from Zaar for whole chicken in the crockpot.  I loved the spice combination, and the cayenne gave it a nice nip. This is my preferred recipe.  We had the leftovers tonight (there's only the two of us) and it was still moist and flavourful.  I saved the drippings, and will find good use for it I'm sure.  Thanks Kathy for an excellent recipe.

This worked out great! Seasoned the chicken the night before and put in the crock in the morning. Cooked on low 8 hours- the chicken literally fell off the bone! Used the leftovers for white chicken chili the next night! Thanks for posting

Well seeing as I am limited to what I can do with recovery from gall bladder surgery and all. I decided to take out a chicken and just pop it into the crokcpot. So I decided to give this one a shot and it was absolutley scrumptious. I actaully cooked up 2 chickens in the cp this week and froze some. Thanks Kath !

Was really good, the cayenne gave it a real kick. My cayenne says extra hot so the juices were extra hot, I didn't make a gravy this time as I didn't know if it would have been too hot for a gravy, next time I will probably try less cayenne. Thank you!

I can clearly see why this is one of the highest rated recipes. It's DELICIOUS! I skipped the cayenne pepper (don't like too spicy) and skipped the overnight refrigeration. This is one of the most tender and juicy chickens I've ever had. I sliced the onion and set the chicken on top. Mine cooked for 8 hours and it was done to PERFECTION. This is the only recipe I need from now on. Thank you Kathy!
I have made this recipe a few times now and it is always fabulous.  And so easy!  Last time I also poured in a can of beer for a different flavor and it came out great.

delicious and so very simple. nice short list of ingredients that most people have on hand.  i added some potatoes to it so had to roast it at 250 in the oven as it wouldnt fit in the crock pot with the potatoes.  also had no cayenne pepper but will make this again without a doubt and will use it then.  very good; did fall off the bone; better than any chicken ive gotten out.  did not marinate overnite as this was a last minute thing.  thank you so much for sharing.
This is by far the best Chicken I've had. The meat is so tender and it makes a great gravy.  Will make my chicken this way for a long time.
My stepdaughter, Crystal fixed this for my Birthday and it was excellent, so tender and juicy.  I have forwarded to Family and Friends.  She served with rice.

Wow!  This is a keeper!  I wasn't sure what to expect - but my DH and I were very impressed!  I cut back on the cayenne, only because I was planning on using the leftover meat to make some baby food.  True comfort food - and easy too!
This was great! Very tender! The only thing I did different was instead of using a whole chicken, I used leg quarters!  Thanks!

TO DIE FOR!!!!!!!!!   I may never cook beer butt chicken again!  So easy and so delicious.  First, the idea of a whole chicken in a crockpot kind of grossed me out (skin, fat, yuck), but with all the reviews I had to try it.  Used all the spices except for thyme and didn't wait to cook, rubbed and put in the crockpot. 3.5 lb chicken on low for 4 hours and it was falling apart delicious.  The only thing I would change is to use a bigger chicken the next time!  Bones and skin fell off as well as the small amount of fat.  The skin was actually more appealing then I thought it would look (looked just like my grilled chicken, not white and slimy like I feared), but we don't eat skin anyhow.  Thank you a million times for this recipe!
This chicken is unbelievably easy and good.  Not much to add to the numerous comments already made here.  Just wanted to put in my vote of 5 stars, too!
I have a few recipes that I make on a regular basis that I buy a rotisserie chicken for.  Not anymore...this was simple, cheaper and has much more flavor.  Thanks!

I made this the other night when my parents came for dinner, it was the first time I have ever made a whole chicken, and it was fantastic!! Everyone loved it, even my picky husband and 2 yr old! My parents even asked for the recipe, thanks for such a simple, delicious recipe!!
Excellent!! This chicken was superb and the spice combo is incredible!!

Like this really needs another five-star review...but here I go anyway. This was so good. It was easy as can be. I did substitute a few seasonings, due to pantry restrictions. But this was so good. And now I have at least one more dinner's worth of chicken already done! And my critters got to have two or three days worth of treats too! (Not the bones. Just the stuff that doesn't look as pretty.) It was almost 90 degrees here today, and this was a great way not to heat up the house. Definitely making this one again. Thanks for posting!

I loved the taste of this chicken.  My only thought was maybe trying it with some boneless breasts, the bones literally fall apart!  (That's just a personal preference though)  It definitely did not take away from the amazing flavor!!  Great recipe!

I used a 3 1/2 pound fryer that I found in the bottom of my freezer. I used 3/4 of the spices and let it sit in the refrigerator 24 hours... Cooked on low it was done in 5 hours..I found this recipe to be very tender and moist..I did place it under the broiler for a few minutes to crisp the skin..My DH loved the spicy skin on the chicken. Thanks for the recipe and don't waste your money on deli chicken - This one is the best with little effort!
This chicken is amazing!!  It was so tender and the meat fell right off the bone so there was nothing wasted.  Plenty of flavor, I've already made it twice!

This is so good, it is unbelievable. My hubby and kids don't care for it too much because they complained it being to spicy. I hope they can be like me who enjoys all the spices.  This is a real easy and good recipe.  Thanks!

Easy & wonderful.  Leftovers work great as well.

Wonderful to come home to dinner being done!

I usually add carrots, onion, celery and water to my chicken when I do it in my crock pot so I wasn't sure how this was going to turn out without adding liquid.  This made plenty of broth to make gravy with.  I served this over Recipe #26110.  It was so good with the gravy!  I wanted more broth so I cleaned the chicken off the bones and added the skin, water to cover and the fat that I had skimmed to make gravy.  I forgot about it and it boiled hard for an unknown amount of time.  It made a nice, rich looking broth.  Just as I finished staining it and was letting it cool we lost power.  I was to afraid to open the refrigerator and put something so hot in for fear it would bring down the temp of the refrigerator.  The power was out for hours and I lost the broth.  I was very disappointed.  I look forward to making this again.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.

There is nothing better than a whole crockpot chicken; it is undoubtedly the best, easieast crockpot dish. Throw a bay leaf in the bottom of your crock and after it's all said and done, you have a wonderful stock to use or freeze! Summer is crockpot season for me here in the south, so I don't have to heat up my kitchen with the oven being on for long periods of time, therefore having the AC running non-stop!

This is the best chicken! It is so tender. My crockpot did great for 8 hours on Low setting. Whole chicken is extremely affordable and this recipe makes for some wonderful leftovers!!

This recipe ROCKS!! We have made it several times now and it never fails! Moist, delicious chicken that keeps you coming back for more. When my kids ask for seconds in the meat department, you know you have a hit! Thanks Kathy!

I used the spices as directed and then put minced garlic in cavity and rubbed more on chicken before rubbing on the spices.  I did let marinate overnight.  I also made the gravy from the drippings and it was also excellent.  Thanks Kathy for an easy and delicious meal.

Last minute decison to try out this chicken so didn't refrigerate overnight.  Didn't have any garlic powder so used minced garlic.  So tender & very nice flavour.  Even hubby gave it the thumbs up (his always very nervous when I try something new).  So happy I cooked this chicken.
Excellent!  DH loved this, he couldn't stop eating it.  I will definitly make this again, it's so easy!

This was WONDERFUL!  My husband loved it! This was oh so easy and oh so yummy... it made the whole house smell wonderful!
I used the chicken broth in the bottom of the pot to make couscous... it was the perfect side dish for this chicken since it captured all the flavoring of the chicken...
thanks for such a simple yet amazing dish!
Excellent! My first attempt at a whole chicken! I have another in the fridge going into the crock tomorrow using this same recipe! Thanks for posting!

Both my roommate and my boyfriend LOVED this recipe. They were fighting over the chicken. LOL And my roommate told me she had to stop herself from eating the whole thing. This is such an easy recipe - almost no work at all. And now I have a little leftover chicken to make chicken enchiladas. (And the broth is definitely worth saving, too!)

Awesome!  I made this with split chickens in the crock.  My husband was surprised at the zing on the skin.  I did as another reviewer suggested and skimmed the fat from the broth at the bottom of the pot.  I made a thick gravy and served it with four cheese mashed potatoes.  It was easy and wonderful.

This was excellent and I think the next time I make it I will put cook potatoes with it. The spices were just right and it was very easy to prepare as others have said. I had prepared a zucchini souffle with this so I saved the dripping for a later date by refrigerating them. I will skim off the top and use the rest for gravy. Don't want to waste a good thing. Thank you for sharing this recipe.
Fall off the bone chicken! Love it! Very tasty, and so so easy!

I've also made this many times.  I love it.  And the leftovers are great for all kinds of things, my favorite is chicken soft tacos!  My 2 year old can't get enough of this chicken.  Thank you!

PS - I have made this with a semi-frozen chicken and still works great!

This was my first attempt at cooking a "whole" bird. I gave it a shot in preparation for making a turkey come this Thanksgiving. It was a little scary, but the chicken turned out fabulous. I only let the seasoning sit for a few hours prior to throwing it in the crock pot, but that did not seem to matter. I am looking forward to throwing the left over meat on a salad for lunch tomorrow. I can't wait, thanks for this tasty recipe!

This recipe always turns out wonderfully tasty and juicy, and is the only recipe I use for chicken now!  I add in some crushed red pepper flakes, omit the cayenne and white pepper.  I always just rub in the spices and place the onion and chicken in the crockpot insert to leave in the fridge overnight.  The next morning, I just take it out, pop in place, and turn on the crock pot.  Easy and delicious!

Wonderful!  I didn't have time to let it refrigerate overnight, but the flavor was wonderful as is.  It was very tender, unlike most of my roasted chicken.  I strained the broth, skimmed off the fat, and made gravy with cornstarch and water.  Served with mashed potatoes and lima beans.  Whole chickens were on a really good sale today, so I'll be using this recipe to cook the rest up to freeze for casseroles.

OMG! This Is so good, and you are right about falling off the bone. I did make just a few adjustments. I used 2tsp of salt and 2 tsp of season salt. Also I didn't have cayenne so i use red pepper and didn't have white pepper so i just omitted all together. I added 1 tsp of lemon pepper also. I didn't chop the onion i just shoved a whole onion up the cavity. I rubbed the spices all over the chicken and under the skin, i did not let it refrigerate overnight it still came out perfect. I also took the advice of another reviewer and put it in my oven on broil and cooked for about 6 mins to get that nice crispy skin. Yummo!!! Thanks for posting i will be passing this along to everyone I know!!!!!!!!

275 reviews and no wonder! This is an easy way to make a a delicious chicken. I used it for Recipe #141578  which called for a store bought roasted chicken but instead I bought a whole chicken on sale for $3 and it turned out just as good as the $7 chicken the store roasts.  I used only about half of the dry ingredients but will use the rest the next time.

Yum yum, yum.  By far, this was the very best crock pot chicken dish I've ever prepared.  And so easy to prepare.  My entire family absolutely loved this recipe, which I will certainly make again--and often.  The chicken was so fork tender, and it was moist and very tasty.  What little leftovers we had will make a great chicken soup for one of the chilly nights ahead of us.
Wow! This was the best chicken ever. Most of the time chicken comes out too plain or too dry. This recipe came out PERFECT. I will definitely be making this one again and again.

This is the best chicken I have ever made and it is so easy!!  I am a mom of two young children so it is difficult to cook sometimes.  This recipe allowed me to make a home cooked meal and gave me more time with my precious little ones!

incredible moist and yummy chicken!  as mentioned, this is the first time i've had crockpot chix that was moist and tender.  i loved the seasonings, but will only use 2 teaspoons of salt next time. i didn't do the overnight in the fridge step.   i used lemons inside and both onions and lemons underneath.  my gravy was lemony and flavorful.  i have a nice new rival smart cooker crockpot and the chix was perfect in 4-4 1/2 hours on low.  thanks for a wonderful recipe which will be a winner for this busy mom!

This is a wonderful crock pot chicken recipe.  I used a 6 1/2 pound Perdue Oven Stuffer Roaster and added 1/2 cup of shredded carrots and 1/2 cup of chicken stock to the onions  and it took about 4 hours on low and 2 1/2 hours on high when the timer popped up (in a 12 qt crock pot). Before finding this recipe, I always cooked my chicken in the oven or on the grill, but my husband likes this version so much that I will cook it this way from now on.  I think that three things should be noted on this recipe though...1) definitely use a pop up timer chicken when cooking this in a crock pot and take it out as soon as it pops up - otherwise it WILL be a little dry (made it twice and the first time I came home to a very dry chicken)  2) once the chicken "pops up", transfer it to a metal baking dish, pour some of the liquid from the crock pot on top to keep moist, and cover it with aluminum foil until ready to broil and 3) absolutely broil this just before serving.  I put my oven rack in the middle position and broiled it (i have a gas oven) for 10 minutes until it was crisp and wonderfully browned.  After the chicken was transferred to a baking dish (prior to broiling), I strained all of the juices and vegetables into a saucepan and thickened it with 2 packages of Knorr's chicken gravy combined with 1 1/2 cups of boxed chicken stock until nicely bubbly and thickened.  It made the perfect gravy and chicken.  Great recipe Kathy!

I tried this recipe for the first time and decided to follow the recipe exactly, except that I did not refrigerate it overnight. The chicken was very tender with great flavor! I will definitely make this again but next time will use half the salt as I am not big on salt and will refrigerate it overnight. I cooked it on high for 5 hours and it was falling off the bone. My teenage daughter however, loved this recipe and ate almost half the chicken!

Absolutely delicious and no sweat needed. I skinned the chicken before I put the rub on (my boyfriend and I are on a tiny health kick) and stuck it in the refrigerator overnight. Threw it in the crock pot before I went to work, came home and Vwala! Dinner with no sweat. Was almost like Thanksgiving. I also made some gravy with the chicken drippings and it was different because of the rub. Love it Love it Love it!!!

The chicken literally fell apart when I removed it from the crockpot! It was *that* tender! Everyone loved the meat, but most of us found the skin too spicy to eat. An incredibly easy way to make moist, tender chicken. Thanks, Kathy, for the recipe and all you do for us here on Zaar. Hugs!
I made this tonight and it was awesome!!! I had a 7 pound chicken and I cooked it on high for 4 and 1/2 hours. My family loved it. I made a gravy with the broth!!!

I'm not much of a chef, so I thrive on easy recipes... this recipe was so effortless yet insanely delicious!  I couldn't believe how tender it was.  The only reason I didn't rate it 5 stars is that the "rub" was a little too "peppery" or "spicy" for my taste, but I'll play around with it!  Thank you SO much for sharing this delicious meal I'll be making a regular in my household!  :-)

This was my first time using a crock pot and I absolutely loved it! This recipe is amazing! The chicken literally falls off the bone. No need to carve this bird! The first time I made it took over 12 hours to cook on low in my little crock pot from the 70's. So the second time I made it I started it the night before at about 10pm and it was perfect for a noon lunch the next day. I made this again for Christmas dinner and everyone loved it, young and old! I served it with mashed potatoes, carrots and peas. It's really amazing how easy this dish is to make considering how good it is!
This chicken was simply awsome... and very easy to make.  I added some Brussels sprouts for some added flavor and it turned out great!  I will definitely use this recipe on a regular basis!

This was fantastic even though I screwed it up! Didn't put the onion on the bottom but used minced onion in the spice  mix. Only used 1/2 the amounts of spices. Also screwed up by first putting the mix into the chicken cavity. Then corrected and spread most of it on the skin. A great cook I am not. Let it cook all day while I worked. Came home and it smelled great. Served with buttered noodles ans enjoyed. Thanks fot sharing.

Made this yesterday for dinner and it was outstanding! We came home and the aroma was wonderful and the meat fell off the bone and was very juicy. I took the other reviews and put onion, celery, garlic cloves and lemon on the bottom of the crock pot and put onion, garlic and lemon inside the chicken. I can't say enough...thank you! 
P.S.  I noticed that I forgot to put the stars on the recipe again.  Sorry and here they are...more if I could.

Did not plan far enough ahead to spice the chicken then put into the fridge.  Put all the spices on the bird and onions on bottom.  Cooked all day.  It was really good.  Only caveat was that I made gravy with the skimmed juices and the gravy was waaayyy to salty for me.  Will probably cut the salt down 1/2 next time.  Otherwise really good and dinner (mashed potatoes and rosemary carrots) got rave reviews!  Thanks!

this is a delicious, moist chicken.  a great fuss-free crockpot dish.  now, if it could be done stuffed-that would make it a 5 star recipe.  thanks for a fantastic recipe!  i made gravy following another viewers suggestion & it was delicious.

This recipe makes for some awesome chicken!  Love the spicy rub.  The only changes I made was to use a frozen bird, so I put the slow cooker on high for the first few hours then reduced to low.  I also used smoked paprika instead of regular.  Great recipe - thanks!

Holy moly, that was good and juicy! This was my first attempt at making an entire chicken in a crockpot. After the bird was done I removed it from the crockpot and mixed in a box of Stovetop Stuffing with the broth that was produced. We had a complete meal that was easy & fantastic! Highly recommended.

Wow, this recipe is the bomb!  We absolutely loved it.  I reduced the salt to 3 tsp (as others noted it was salty) and I think next time I will go down to 2 1/2 tsp salt.  Also, reduced cayenne to 1/4 tsp as we don't like things hot. I tied the wings and legs so that it would be easier to get the chicken out of the crock pot.  The meat did not fall apart so tying it worked out well.  My crock pot didn't cook it in 5 hours so I cranked it up to high for one more hour.  Thx so much for this one Kathy.
This was good. I would make it again.  Thanks.

This is an excellent recipe. So simple and tasted wonderful! I made it exactly as written and wouldn't change a thing. The spices were perfect. This was the prettiest whole chicken in the crockpot I ever made. My chicken was pulling away from the bones at about 4 1/2 hours (I set it on 6 hour setting on my crockpot.) It was tender, juicy and *Delicious* I used the shredded chicken in my Recipe #257149 which added great flavor. I did nibble on the chicken when shredding and know this would be great as a stand alone! Thanks for sharing Kathy, this recipe will go into my "Favorites by Zaar" cookbook!!!  I will definitely make this again. ~V
Very nice recipe.  I made it just as directed and found it good but a bit bland.  Will make it again with the Mexican seasoning.  I really like the idea of making an onion base for the chicken.

Great Chicken,  The Wife and I both being up in our 70's and not having company this Thanksgiving we figured a chicken would suffice. WELL, your recipe is TOP SHELF. I made it as written. I never modify recipes before I try them. Over 60 years of burning the biscuits I have learned to make it as written. Then and only then do I make changes. The only change for us is reducing the 4 teaspoons of salt to 2. Thank you so much for winner that will be used in this home many times. Merry Christmas to all. Cap'n Jack
good and eazy
My family loved it. Was VERY quick and easy to do!!!

We love sticky chicken in this house, and my children request this dish frequently.  I don't marinate mine, I just rub the seasonings on, and then place it in a crockpot and cook on low for about 7-8 hours.  It always comes out delicious and fall off the bones moist.

Simple, wonderful recipe. Crock pot cooking is so easy, but so many of the recipes are bland. Not this one. It tastes great and if you can manage to get this out of the crock pot without it falling all to pieces, it looks great too!

This is one recipe that I often use...in fact, I make several batches of seasoning at the same time and store them in ziplock bags so that really makes this a fix it and forget. Thanks. I like to put the chicken on a sheet of aluminum foil in the crockpot and then leave extra long sides so when I am ready to take the chicken out--it comes out in one piece.

This is wonderful...so much better than baked chicken!  I followed the recipe exactly.  It has good flavor, and I love that I can stick it in the crockpot and forget about it until it's time to eat.  I'll have this again soon!

I have never made chicken that my whole family was entirely silent during dinner. Some ask for ketsup, some bbq sauce. This chicken only recieved silence and mmmmms. I have never made chicken so unbelievably delicious. I want to give this recipe more than 5 stars. God Bless you for sharing this recipe! Want to impress someone? MAKE THIS CHICKEN!!
Simple and delicious. I used smoked paprika and added a few green bell pepper bits on the bottom with the onions. This is a keeper. Thanks.
This was my first whole chicken ever and we loved it. Lots of flavor and really different. Will definitely make this again! Thanks!!!!

Fabulous!!!! I used black pepper instead of white.  I only used half the amount of seasoning on the chicken because it was really small.  I saved the rest for next time.  Gravy was delicious and the leftovers will make great chicken and dumplings.

Oh yeah! Now you're talkin' !
This is so easy I could cry! On board for this week for sure!

Wonderful! Couldn't be easier - or tastier. Thank you for sharing!
Great recipe! Chicken was so good. My first time using whole chicken and now I will never stop! Thanks!
was simple and a real time saver. But I didn't like how the chicken just tasted steamed or boiled. I cooked 2 chickens and used the second to make a huge bowl of chicken salad.
Excellent chicken recipe, everyone loved that the chicken was so moist. I will use this recipe again but omit the onions as they truely optional.
I am new to this whole cooking game, and this was my first recipe. My wife and kids just loved it. Thank you for making my first attempt a success.

I have made chicken in the crorckpot many times and my husband never really cared for it. He said it was to greasy. I tried this and he loved it. He even asked me to make it for a potluck at church and they all loved it. It has the right amount of spices, its falls of the bone,and its not greasy. the left overs we used for soup and it was great.
Made this one last week, Great tasty, everyone enjoyed!

This was the best chicken I've had!  Never thought to do it in the crock pot.  I took some liberties with the seasonings, because we LOVE garlic and onion and added some halved garlic to the onions on the bottom of the pan.  We also carefully (it was falling apart!) put it on a pan to broil for a few minutes to get the skin crispy.  EXCELLENT CHICKEN!!!!!
Great spices!

I have made this several times now and can't think of anything I would change about it.  I make it as written and my husband just loves it.  It was an immediate family keeper and we like to use the leftovers in Delicious pot pie. Thanks for posting!

O M G!!!!  This is nothing short of fantastic!!!  I have to admit to being a bit worried about the spice combinations but decided to try it.  No regrets here!!!  I thickened the juice, of which there was ALOT (We raise our own chickens - Cornish Rock Crosses - that tend to produce alot of juice!) and the gravy was terrific!  My "Reason For Living" is still raving about it!!!  Thanks for the post!!
Love it!!!  Thickened the gravy and served with mashed potatoes and roasted carrots.  I was great, thanks.
I made this already twice and tonight I'll make it for a third time.  I don't think I'll try any other way to make whole chicken again. Thank you for the wonderful recipe.

DH said he could just drink the gravy or eat it and rice for dinner.  The chicken lasted for a few days so a great way to stretch the grocery dollar ;).  Love that it had a great flavor and I didn't use any "packaged" dry mix (with MSG and other chemicals).

Wow!  at 53 grams of fat per person, no WONDER it's delicious!

I'm hoping all that fat can be removed before making the gravy.

I will try it soon; I did a similar one recently and it turned out delicious!  yum!

FANTASTIC!  What else needs to be said.  I bought a whole chicken at the market this afternoon, BF massaged the bird with the spices and we stuck it in the crockpot on a bed of onions and let it go on low for 5.5 hours (the timer popped out).  We followed suggestions and put it under the broiler while the potatoes were mashed and broccoli was steamed.  I took all the stock and separated it except for 1/2c which I added some cornstarch to attempt to thicken for gravy (didn't work to well but it was delicious).  I'll use the stock for some soup that Ill be making tonight as well.  Next time I'll add the lemons but keep the onions (I love them) and reduce the salt to 2t.  Thank you!

Very easy and fall off the bone tender.  My only complaint is that the skin is rubbery, but then you just don't eat it.  Nice to come home to a cooked chicken.  Easy to remove the meat from the bones and then use for whatever recipe you need.

Best. Chicken. Ever. The only change I made to this recipe was removing the skin to save some calories. Not only was the chicken delicious, but the leftover juices in the Crock Pot made one of those enviable stocks that sets up like meat-flavored Jell-O in the refrigerator--something I've never managed to do before when I tried! Just FYI, since the recipe doesn't specify a specific size for the chicken--we made a 3-1/2lb chicken for three people and hardly had any leftovers. (Of course, my fiance did go back for seconds...and thirds...;p)

This is outrageous!  Easy and the smell while cooking - mouthwatering!  Made gravy with the juices and it was oustanding!
Great recipe and looking forward to having leftovers for dinner tonight.  Thanks Kathy!

I couldn't believe how flavorful this chicken was! It was some of the most juicy & tender chicken we've ever had. It was hard getting it out of the crockpot because it was falling apart! I followed the directions, but didn't use cayenne or white pepper since I didn't have any. I did use 1 1/2 tsp of chicken seasoning instead. Oh- and a tip for those who've never made whole chickens with the skin on before- make sure to put seasonings on the meat, under the skin. So that way the meat will get seasoning & it's not all wasted on the skin that just gets taken off.
Makes a flavorful and moist chicken.  My picky-eater kids loved this and it was so easy to do!  Great recipe...thanks for sharing it!
It was good; my guests enjoyed it. We all agreed that it would be easier with boneless chicken breast, though. It was a pain getting the meat off the bones! It did have a spicy kick!

The chicken was soft, tasty and spicy and everyone enjoyed it (I toned down the spice a bit for the kids).
It also had 4 tsp of salt which is a lot of sodium. I think the salt could easily be halved and the dish would still be enjoyable.
This was okay, I went exactly by the directions but is just didn't turn out that tasteful. The chicken fell off the bone but it was just bland.

We use this recipe for our OAMC cooking. We clean out the chicken, put it in a gallon size bag and put the mixed ingredients on top.  It freezes great and slides into the crock pot (thawed).  It has been a hit with the (3) families that do our OAMC cooking.  It is a bit spicy, but we really enjoy it
LOVED IT!!! So tender and juicy. I did throw some taters and carrots in with the chicken, and that seasoning soaked right in. Delicious all around thank you!

We loved this chicken!  I did marinate overnight in the spices and stuff the cavity with both onion and lemon.  My left over hating husband was even rooting around the fridge looking for the left over chicken the next day!
Good and easy way of cooking a whole chicken!
love this recipe and it's really flavorful! made this twice per my husband's request, yep he loves it! thank you for sharing this recipe.

This chicken came out very moist and it was easy to cook. The only thing I would do differently is take another reviewers suggestion to crisp the skin under the broiler. Our family likes crispy chicken skin. Thanks for a seriously easy recipe.

I used a talking thermometer, and when it said it was 20 degrees until done, I popped the dish out of the crock pot, and put in the oven at 400 uncovered until it was done (only about 15 min.) 
This gave it a crispy skin and no new dishes to wash! I am a breast person and I always have a hard time getting crispy, flavorful white meat, but this did the trick.

I have an almost-identical recipe called "Roast Sticky Chicken" which I've been making for 10 years or so.  Same ingredients, but I roast the chicken in a 250Âº oven for six hours.  YES, 6 hours!  This makes the skin nice and crispy.  I never thought about putting it in the crock pot, but I'll try that the next time!

Since I don't eat chicken skin, I didn't put this under the broiler. What I do like is tender, moist chicken breasts and this recipe delivers that.  I will try other seasonings, too, like you suggested. Thanks.......

I didn't want to rate this recipe with stars because I didnt think it would be fair to Kathy that I didn't like it. One son likes this and another didn't. The reason I didn't like it is I don't like thyme and didn't realize this. I would try this again but leave out the thyme and add more cayenne pepper.

This chicken is fantastic!  It always comes out tender!  I put a frozen whole chicken in the crockpot the night before and cook on low for 12 hours.  This is a restaurant quality recipe, with hardly any fuss!  I usually do put two cups of water in the crockpot with the chicken as the juices make a great gravy, too!

Great chicken!  My bird was about 4 lbs. and was only 1/2 thawed, but I rinsed it and was able to rub some of the spice mixture under the skin.  I then cooked it on high in the crockpot for 5 hours and then "crisped" it under the broiler for about 5 minutes.  Delicious!!!

Made this recipe again &again. I even printed a copy for the butcher at the grocery store to share with customers when whole chickens are on sale. Now I just make a big batch of the rub so it is handy anytime & give it to friends who can't cook. When the chicken is done I like to transfer to oven to brown but certainly not necessary.  Thank you for sharing with us....

Wow, this recipe is a keeper.  The chicken is very flavorful and indeed "fall-off-the-bone tender."  I seasoned the chicken and put in in the refrigerator for a few hours before cooking it in the Crock-Pot and it didn't seem to suffer from any lack of seasoning.  My Crock Pot too cooked the chicken in 5 hours.

I followed this recipe precisely and we LOVED it!  I had never cooked a whole chicken in the crock pot before.  When the chicken was done, I reserved the juices, strained off the fat, added a flour slurry, and made the BEST chicken gravy we've ever had.  Finally, I put the bones, scraps, and skin back into the crock pot with about 2 cups of water and let it cook on low overnight, strained the broth the next day to use for the next several days worth of recipes!  Ulta-FRUGAL!

Thanks for this great recipe.  I will consider pre-mixing the spices and sharing them in gift bags with the recipe attached for friends and family.

This is my favorite chicken recipe. I followed it exactly, and it turned out terrific. So far I have made it three times. I do stick the chicken in under the broiler for a few minutes after taking it out of the crock pot, to let it brown and finish draining. I highly recommend this recipe.
Wonderful recipe and easy! Everyone I serve this to loves it!
This recipe was so easy to prepare and I already had all of the spices. The chicken was very moist!!! Thanks

Thanks so much for this! I used onions underneath and lemons inside and my gravy was waaay to lemony - I don't recommed quartering 2 lemons like I decided too - the gravy was strong! The chicken was tender and delicious and was done in exactly 7 hours on low. I just got a new crock pot that has a probe and keeps the food warm when it reaches the desired temperature. It was perfectly cooked when we had it an hour into being kept warm. Thanks so much, it was great. If you don't like heat, maybe cut back on the cayenne and paprika, but that's it!
Made this last night. The kids loved it! So easy! Totally forgot to prep it overnight, so just did it and tossed into the crockpot.

What a great meal. My wife prepared it just as is. She only cut the salt by half, we don't like to use too much salt, the taste was great, It was so tender and moist, it fell apart as I took it out of the crock pot.
She does not like food that is to spicy, so next time she'll also cut the cayenne pepper in half. My son and I loved it the way she maid it. We will have this again for sure.

chicken was very flavorful and superduper tender.  It was so tender I couldnt pull it out the crockpot without it falling apart.  I let it cook for the 8 hours decscribed by my machine, maybe next time I will cook it for an hour less and use a temp probe.  thanks
The chicken was so flavorful! I used the left overs for tequitos.  My four year old loved it as well.

I've made this twice now.  The first time I didn't marinate it overnight and just baked in the over at 375 for 1 hour and 45 minutes.  It was very good, but so much better the second time when I actually marinated it overnight. The spiced soaked into the meat and we didnt need to eat any of the skin to get the flavor.  The cayenne can add a lot of kick so you may want to add less than the teaspoon.  Also, stuffed it with a lemon and onion and it was so moist.  Served it with some steamed veggies and it made for a low calorie, low carb dinner that was delicious!  Thank you for the recipe.

very good and so easy.  The chicken was falling apart while trying to lift it out of the crock pot.  Added flour mixed with water to the leftover liquid to make gravy.  Will make again on those busy days when I can't stand over the stove!!!!
Thanks, Michele, Cambridge, Ontario

Made this two nights ago now and even the left overs where great. I didn't put as much cayenne pepper mainly because I have lil ones who that might have been to much for. I loved it and so did the family very flavorfull. Will def make again!

This was very good. I have made it twice so far and have not remembered to marinade overnight. I just season it and immediately put in the crock pot and flavor is delicious. I can only imagine the flavor marinated overnight. I also only used 1/2 tsp. cayenne pepper and no pepper because of kids.
made this twice now.  it really is great.  i left the cayenne pepper out the 2nd time for the kids, and it is still fabulous!

Fab! It was good enough for my husband to compliment it - which is BIG for him! He even asked me what was in the rub, because he liked the zip. I laid my chicken (it was about 4 lbs) on a quartered onion, quartered lemon, and a couple of whole cloves of garlic, and stuffed it with a quartered lemon that had the rub sprinkled generously on. I cooked on high for about 4 hours and it was so juicy and flavorful, especially since I put the spice up under the skin where I could! I pulled out the juices and made a nice gravy to go along with it. Thanks for this recipe! I'll definitely be making again, but I get to enjoy these leftovers for the rest of the week now. (PS I used only 2 tsps of salt and 1 tsp of black pepper total, since I had no white pepper.)
Great recipe. I added some poultry seasoning, lemon pepper, some oregano and red peppers... so colorful and flavorful!
This is tasty and if you squeeze a lemon over and inside the chicken before you bake, it makes it even better.

Absolutely delicious!  I used 3.8 lb. chicken which fit perfectly in a 4 qt oval crock pot. I did not have cayenne pepper or onion powder so I used Cajun seasoning and Adobo seasoning instead. I rubbed the spice mixture above and beneath the skin as noted by another reviewer and tossed the rest in the chicken cavity. While cooking in the slow cooker, the house smelled amazing!  I used a barbeque fork and a spatula to pull the chicken out of the pot. It was so tender it was literally falling off the bone! A quick 5-minute broil in the toaster oven and it was all done! This dish went very well with Dana-MMH's Greek Oven Roast Potatoes (#32566) as well as peas and carrots I had tossed into a chicken-flavored rice-a-roni dish. Such an affordable dish too! We purchased the whole chicken on sale for less than $3 (79 cents per pound) and we'll be getting 4 meals out of this one dish! I highly recommend this recipe to anyone interested in saving money without compromising flavor!
Yummy, will make again!
WOW- This was the best find. We buy the roasted chickens at the store. Never again- this is fall of the bone chicken- simple. Perfect. Thank you Kathy!
This was great and the kids were begging for more!  Thank you!

This turned out quite good...wasn't sure what to expect, never cooked a whole chicken in the crockpot before.   We had a 3 1/2 lb chicken, cooked it on low for 10 hours and it was very tender.   Next time, I won't cook as long for the same size bird b/c the bones themselves about fell apart in the pot as I was trying to get the meat off.    the breast meat was a bit dry but I think it was due to my longer cooking time.   i would also reduce the salt a bit as it was a tad salty for our tastes.  Definitely will try again!
This was really easy to make, but it did come out too dry and stringy for me. A good technique, but need to refine the cooking time based on how much chicken you're cooking.

My family LOVED this chicken and the gravy that I made with the drippings!  The cayenne was a bit much for the little ones in the family but we remedied that by taking the skin off theirs.  I also seasoned between the skin and meat.  I was fearful of using the crockpot with no liquid but it turned out beautifully!  We will be making this many more times!

This recipe is fantastic!  The seasoning is spot on and the meat falls off the bone.  I pop the bird under the broiler for a bit to crisp up the skin and we used the left overs to make an amazing chicken noodle soup.

Definitely a keeper!  We have used this recipe twice with great results.  Each time we've used a 7lb. bird, and cooked it for around 6 hours on low in a large crock pot.  If your chicken is already brined or packed in broth, you can leave out all the salt, and this recipe still gives the chicken great flavor.  Also, cook the chicken breast-side DOWN to keep the white meat from getting dry (you might have to remove and/or relocate the pop-up timer - we've never used one, because the bigger birds don't allow the timer to work because it hits the lid of the crock pot.  Just use a probe or a regular thermometer after about 6 hours on low).  As others have said, rub some of the spices under the skin for the best results.

All in all, a very yummy recipe that we will turn to again and again.

Wow!  I was skeptical, mainly because I am fairly new to crock pot cooking.  I did not think that the entire chicken would be cooked through or that it would be moist.  I must say that I am very happy to have been wrong!!!  Very moist and DELICIOUS!!!  Thank you for such a fabulous recipe!!!
Made this recipe tonight for supper.  It was definately a keeper.  The chicken was tender and flavorful for crockpot.   The recipe was easy.  Can't go wrong with this recipe.

Delicious! The house smelled so good! I started a small frying chicken at noon and after tball in the afternoon I couldn't even get it out of the crock it fell all apart. Even my picky kids ate it. Moist and easy. Thank you.

My husband said this was the best chicken he had ever eaten in his entire life. :D!!!  When I took it out of the crock pot, it was so tender, it literally fell apart.  So moist and delicious and EASY I will making this again soon!

Amazing flavor! And, it couldn't be any easier or faster.
Thank you.

I made this the other night, and it was absolutely fabulous!  I used a very large bird (5-6lbs) that was skinless, as we raise our own meat chickens and can't be bothered to pluck. cut salt by 2/3, all else the same.  crisped skin under broiler, whole family loved this. Super simple & great for summer.  thanks!
So good!  We cut back on the salt but kept everything else as is.  Definitely a keeper!  Thanks so much!
Fantastic recipe. Easily one of the best slow cooker meals I've ever had. I plan on trying it again with different spice combinations, but would highly recommend it to everyone.
Thank you for a wonderful recipe!  I only had limes, so I used them instead of the lemon.  It turned out great.  It made wonderful chicken fijitas!!!

I thought the recipe was just OK. The chicken meat fell off of the bones, but the meat was also very dry and overcooked. Might be a very good recipe if a person wanted an easy way to prepare chicken for chicken salid or something with a gravy though.  06/26/09 - I have since learned that my crock pot runs REALLY hot. By the next day (14 hours later) it was almost submerged in its own boiling juices.
Wonderful taste to this chicken recipe.  I threw in some red potatoes and carrots the last couple of hours for a complete meal.

Yummy, yummy, yummy! Loved this chicken. I cooked for 5.5 hours in crockpot with aluminum foil balls on the bottom and chopped up onion. Also added less salt and added lemon pepper. This was very tasty. Thanks for a new chicken recipe.

Split breasts were on sale so I stuffed filled the crock pot with those instead of a whole chicken. At 99 cents a pound the breasts were a fab deal!  This turned out so good that there were no leftovers!

This is definitely in my top 5 of favorite recipes. Very easy and delicious! I typically use this recipe for "taco night". I use chicken breasts with the skin on (split breasts). Loved this chicken!  I put cut up celery and baby carrots under the bird along with the onion as I like the combo of the vegetables.  A few people stopped by as this was cooking and commented how heavenly it smelled.  The juices made excellent gravy.  I will definately make this again!

I wasn't sure how this would turn out.  I was actually very pleasantly surprised.  The meat just falls off of the bone.  It is well seasoned.  The skin does not get/stay crispy but I'm OK with that.

I have made this chicken half dozen times now, each time leaving out a little more of the salt.  I am down to ZERO salt, and my family never misses it! I'll be passing it down to my daughters-in-law!

Easy and good. We've had people picking the pieces off the carcass when we were done & we've been given free chickens so long as we do this recipe and give them some.
Really good- I used my husband's chicken rub.

This was very good.  The only change I made was cutting the amount of salt in half.

I made this twice in one week!  I skipped the onions, didn't have any on hand but it was great anyways.  I also used my own mix of seasonings, I don't think anyone could mess this up. The chicken turned out beautifully, just as advertised! I dialed back the Cayenne a bit for personal taste, omitted the white pepper because I didn't have it, and I added lemons into the cavity. I usually oven roast chicken but I think I'm a Crockpot convert on this one!

Fall off the bone good.

I don't know why it has taken this long to review this recipe...I have cooked it about 20 times.  Add carrots, celery, potatoes, and whatever else to make it a full meal...all the ingredients soak up the delicious flavor. AMAZING!

Absolutely the BEST slow cooker chicken recipe I have found! It turns out so moist! A new favorite way to make my whole chickens!
This has all been said before--easy, delicious, super tender meat, great seasoning. My bird was done in 5 hours. Will use this recipe many times over. Thanks.

Another satisfied customer rating!  I've made this several times and with rave reviews from my tribe.  As such, I wonder why I haven't taken the time to rate this before .
