This recipe has so many reviews I almost feel silly leaving one, but I wanted to add my two cents into the pot -- this chicken was so good! I followed the recipe exactly as written -- including refrigerating the chicken overnight in the plastic baggy with the spices, except I added a couple of quartered potatoes to the pot when there was about 2 hours left. I did use the optional onion in the bottom of the crock pot.  There is a subtle kick to the chicken, which we liked, but I can imagine young children might not like the heat.

Very good. Had to add some seasonings because it was kind of bland but the meal didn't suffer at all, I just sprinkled and flipped it twice and let it cook. Cooked in two hours, wish i threw in potatoes also but the onions were great.
Delicious! This tasted just like Swiss Chalet here in Canada. I even made "the sauce" from the leftover juices in the crock pot. This is a keeper! Thanks for posting.

Absolutely amazing!  Have made this chicken twice.  Out of the park grand slams each time.  I don't put any cayenne pepper, use half the salt and a mixture of peppercorns.  I have a 4 qt pot and use an almost 7 lb chicken.  The bird fits snuggly in the pot and I cover it with the spice mixture.  Thank you for this recipe.  I will use it every time I make a whole chicken.

I served this with mashed potatoes, asparigus and rolls.  Then used the leftovers in chicken wild rice soup.  The flavor reminded me of a rotisserie chicken.  Very flavorful and easy.  I will make this again.
Fantastic chicken!  My husband requests it weekly!  We like to cook it until it falls off the bone, chop it and make unique chicken salad sandwiches.
Delicious! I used lemon in the chicken cavity and put it under the broiler like LisaLouWho and served it with Parmesan-Rice-and-Pasta-Pilaf-5034. Thank you!

This was simply to die for!  Amazing!  Everyone in my family ate it and even asked for seconds. I took some advice from the comments and put the chicken under the broiler at the end to make the skin crispy and it was fantastic. I didn't find this recipe until just before I needed to cook the chicken so I couldn't marinate it but it was still so tasty. This will be our go to whole chicken dish from now on.
Made this today - wonderful!!!  Definitely a keeper!!

If I could give this 100 stars I would. I just couldn't believe the taste of this chicken when I pulled it out. I added some carrots and celery in there, just to give it a little extra. Also, a clove of garlic and lemon inside the chicken. Honestly, this will be my go-to chicken recipe. Thank you so much, Kathy!

I really loved this recipe! The flavors from the seasoning is so wonderful and full of flavor. I squeezed fresh lemon juice over the chicken and then rubbed on the spice blend. I also added the lemons inside the chicken. Very yummy indeed! Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

The reviews don't lie! It's a great recipe. My 5lb bird was done in just less than 4 hours....and broiling it for a bit at the end (carefull not too long) is the ticket!
Thanks

Haven't tried yet.....looks GREAT! But the nutritional info says one serving has 737 calories!!!
When I looked at 'how calculated' it says there are 12,077 cal in a large chicken and 50 cal for 2 tsp paprika! YOWZA!!!

Wow! I loved this recipe so much I finally decided to make a account on here (after getting recipes on here for about 6 years.) The chicken was so tender and had a great flavor! I did what the other posters suggested by broiling it after it was done in the crock pot. MmmMmMm. It was a huge hit! Also I added celery, carrots and garlic and lemon. It made a wonderful gravy, thanks so much for the recipe. I will use this often :)
Loved loved the taste of this chicken, the flavors were wonderful! I have made this several times already and everyone is very happy! Thank you!

"Wow!" was the first word my husband said after taking his first bite!  I would have to agree!  This chicken is full of flavor with just enough kick to tingle your tastebuds!  I did place 1/2 of a lemon and 1/2 of an orange inside the cavity, then squeezed some fresh lemon & orange juice over the bird before placing in the crockpot!  Perfect for a Sunday lunch!
Just a comment. Sounds like a very tasty and easy way to make chicken but for those of us who must watch salt this is way too high at 2553.6 mg and 106% salt.

Amazingly good. I got this recipe from a GF in 2008 and finally made it. This could not be easier. I was concerned that the chicken would be mushy but the texture  was perfect. It was a bit salty  so I will cut back a tad next time, ( my fault cuz I increased the amount of seasonings).  I used a 7# bird and didn't have a bag large enough so I seasoned and left it in the crockpot insert, covered & chilled overnight. Once cooked I lifted the chicken out, in sections removed the skin & deboned it and served it rustic style on a platter accompanied by roasted carrots, parsnip & potatoes. The gravy is fantastic. I stuffed the cavity with quartered onions. YUM!

Really really good!!  It was a bit spicy for my tastes (I'm a wuss) so the next time I'd ease up on the cayenne a bit but everything turned out super good and moist.  It was so tender I wasn't able to get it out of the crock to roast to brown up the skin but that was OK.  Next time I will try adding the spices beneath the skin and lemons inside.

Super good and very, very easy!! I skinned the whole chicken then applied the spice rub. I've found if you take the skin off, your meat will keep longer and doesn't retain a greasy taste. As a single guy, I usually have one breast for dinner, then debone the chicken and use the meat throughout the week for soft tacos, chicken salad, and chicken quesadillas.
Hands down the best tasting baked chicken.  Now, my family loves baked chicken!

I know there are a lot of reviews already - but I will never do a whole chicken any other way ever again!  I took the advice from one review and left skin on, removing as much fat as I could pull off, and just rubbed spices under the skin.  It makes sooo much chicken with such great flavor and sooo moist, I used it for chicken tacos, chicken enchiladas and had some just the way it came out of the crock pot!  Thank you so much for the recipe!
This recipe was unbelievably easy AND delicious. We had a small chicken so we used 1/3 less salt. Thanks!
Thank you "Kathy" for the recipe. I love my wife more now that you shared this with her. AMAZING flavor, tenderness, and reheat-ability. Possibly the best chicken I've ever had. WOW!

Seasoned the chicken the night before.  We ended up roating this in the oven for an 1 hour and 20 mins.  I preheated the oven to 475 then droped the temp down to 400 degress.  I brushed with olive oil and squesszed 1 lemon into the cavity and left the lemon in the chicken.  I was amazed at how tender and  flavorful the chicken was.  It looked beautiful coming out of the oven.  It made the house small amazing too.

I can't believe I haven't said thank you for this recipe yet!! What an amazing, quick and easy way to make my first whole chicken 3 years ago. Even though I leave out the thyme, don't even bother marinating it, it still turns out incredible every time! My picky PICKY boyfriend even licks his fingers! (He also doesn't like onion so I sub the onion with 2 chopped garlic cloves). THANKS AGAIN!

Gorgeous flavor! Was running late so cooked in crock pot on HIGH for 2.5 hours. Came out perfect. Falling off the bone. The whole family was literally licking their spicy fingers. Slurp. Will be a staple in my home!

This was very nice and oh the smell was great! I did reduce the salt to 1/2 tsp as I am on a sodium restricted diet. I also did not have regular paprika so I used smoked paprika. This was so moist and I served it with scalloped potatoes and roasted balsamic vegetables. I will definitely make this again.Thankyou!

This was very good and very easy. IMHO, it doesn't compare to roast chicken, but it makes nice juicy meat for use in recipes or sandwiches. I cut a large onion into 1/6ths and threw in a couple handfuls of garlic cloves, and instead of the spice mix specified, I ground some lemon-pepper seasoning over. It was tasty and fairly juice, though the breast meat was borderline dry after the max time (it was a very large chicken and barely thawed at that). Definitely start at the minimum time, especially for a smaller hen. Thanks for sharing, Kathy!

I took a 5 pound Chicken and put Mrs. Dash Italian medley on it instead of the mix submitted (as italian medley has most of the same stuff without all the sodium. cooked it for 3.5 hours and it is wonderful,

This is so easy and so good!  I can put this into the crockpot over my lunch hour and have it ready to eat when we get home from work in the evening.  The leftover chicken makes great chicken tacos, also.  Thanks for sharing, we love this one!

Made this one evening and it came out extremely tender, juicy, and bursting with flavor. Threw in carrots and potatoes and voila, a classic crock pot meal you can't go wrong with, so thanks for the recipe.

Thanks for the recipe.  I would have screwed this one up by adding some kind of sauce.  I never would have thought it would create enough broth to keep it juicy AND make gravy.  I used Morton's Nature Seasonings, since I did not have all the spices it called for.  I also did not do a whole intact chicken, I substituted a whole cut-up chicken.  I added chopped garlic to the chopped onion.  When the chicken was cooked (yet still moist), I broiled the chicken and made gravy from the broth.  VERY GOOD and EASY!!  I do not know how longed I cooked it, but no more than 6 hours.  I kept switching from high to low, since I was home all day.  With 3 active children this one is most definitely goiuing to be repeated...Thanks :)
Yummmmmmm! Super easy and terribly good!

This was the first time i've cooked in a crock pot other than pot roast and it was amazing!  I got the whole chicken as a git and didnt know what to do with it so i found this recipe.  Please try it out!  You'll be glad you did.

Wow!  I don't even like chicken.  I usually eat as little chicken as I can get away with but this chicken was good!!!   We also peeled an apple and stuffed it inside the chicken.  Maybe that did something.  The crock pot was small so the chicken was in it head first (minus the head) and it was a snug fit so the juices were almost covering the chicken legs that stuck up.
Amazing, even better than a rotisserie chicken. This is the only way I'm going to cook a whole chicken from now on. Thank you for sharing this fabulous recipe.

This recipe was so good, it had me open an account here so I can thank you, Kathy, for revealing the evil lies crock pot manufacturers have been spreading about not cooking whole chickens in them! You've got the spices right, but I think most are on board about the salt being a bit on the heavy side... with that said, this recipe is not only a keeper, but has very much inspired me! With this myth gone, I'm gonna try out cooking my favorite Filipino chicken this way. Thanks for the new keeper recipe!
great recipe, the family loves it. easy prep and since it's in the crock pot you set it and don't have to worry about it for hours

I made this for dinner today and the only things I did differently was that I did not measure the spices and I also added the remaining 6 cloves of fresh garlic that I had on hand as my husband loves garlic. I will definitely use this recipe often. It was very melt in your mouth good!
I used a reviewers suggestion and used bone in breasts. The spices really make the dish.I roasted a bit in oven once done.Yummy!

This was wonderful! I did change a couple of things though. I used half as much of the cayenne, white and black peppers since we're not big fans of spice. We really loved the flavor. I also quartered a few red potatoes and put them in with the chicken. They took on the wonderful flavors of the rub and really helped complete the meal. We also added steamed carrots to round out everything. A yummy meal with not much effort!

Really impressed! Thank you!! I made this so that I could use the chicken meat in other things. I like to keep some in the freezer with a quick defrost for nachos among other things. I was shocked to see how much liquid one bird produces on its own! Wow! My breast meat was a little dry, so next time I will pull it before the 8 hours is up on my crock pot. (The shortest setting for low that I have it 8 hours.) I will certainly keep this in my "make again" folder!! Thank you!

The best chicken I ever made! Super delicious and tender. The best part of it is the soup I made with the left overs. I added some lemon, white wine and chopped garlic and low sodium organic chicken broth. It is the best soup I have ever had.

FANTASTIC!! I couldn't believe how moist and tender my chicken turned out. Great flavor!. Along with the onions under the chicken, I put some celery and carrots. Super tasty stock for outstanding gravy. This is a keeper for sure. Thanks for posting!
This was SOOO good!!!!

I have made this recipe many times now in my slow cooker.  Way better than a store bought rotisserie chicken!  I do the spices just as written.  I do cook in with a lemon, cut in half, and stuffed inside the bird.  I usually cook a 5 lb chicken for 5-6 hours in my 6 qt. slow cooker.  It is the juiciest and tastiest recipe yet!

I made this with the hope that it would be moist enough to feed to my 9 month old baby. And it WAS! He loved it. It's moister than Rotisserie chicken and so flavorful. I don't agree with the others about going overboard on the salt. We don't eat the skin so really how much salt are you getting when just eating the meat?? Also one of the comments below said the breast meat was a little dry, that's hard for me to believe unless it's cooked without the skin to hold in the moisture OR the lid was removed during cooking. It's pretty difficult to overcook in a crockpot, so I don't think that was the issue. I did also stuff it with garlic cloves and lemon wedges. I was able to use the leftovers in many other recipes for the rest of the week. Great way to save money and it's the BEST whole chicken recipe ever! Thank you!

Like everyone else here, I loved this recipe. I made it yesterday. I used two small chickens...each under 3 lbs and was able to fit both in my crock pot (side by side). I cooked it for 7 hours on low. I did mix up some minced fresh garlic with the onions. It was incredibly moist and flavorful. The liquid didn't start showing up till about the 3 - 4 hour mark. I was amazed at how much liquid there was at the end.

After I took out the chicken to put it on a platter, I poured the liquid into a saucepan on the stove. I then added a cornstarch mixture (cornstarch and cold water) to thicken the gravy. I served the chicken and gravy over rice.

For anyone with a slow cooker, I highly, highly recommend this recipe. I have emailed it to my friends to share it with them.
This recipe was just ok...I think I may have cooked a little too long because everyone else loves this!I will try it again...

OH MY GOSH!!!  This recipe was perfect! I bought a chicken for my husband and me for Easter dinner and this was to die for!  I added two gala apples and one johnny smith apple with a whole onion chopped while it was cooking.  I made a chicken gravy with the liquids only adding cornstarch.  It was so rich and wonderful, we didn't add anything after it got done.  I cooked it for 7.5 hours.  I ended up having to put it in the oven on warm while I finished the other parts of our dinner and it was perfect.  Thanks for posting this recipe!  I now have a wonderful chicken dinner recipe that literally cost me under 6 bucks.

This was delicious! Great flavor and tender meat. It cooked on low for 8 hrs. while I was at work. When I got home, the smell from the kitchen was incredible. The only thing I did differently was to add celery, onions and garlic to the chicken cavity, and a little garlic to the onions on the bottom of the crock pot. The gravy was awesome with just the right kick from the cayenne. My whole family loved it.

This is probably the best crock pot recipe I've ever tried using a whole chicken. It worked perfectly. The flavor is wonderful. I loved the hint of spice. The chicken is very moist. Straight into my best of the best file it goes. Thank you!

I was surprised how good this was! The skin wasnt crispy but I put the chicken under the broiler for about 15 minutes and that did It ...tender juicy moist what more could you ask for?  I had left over chicken so the next day I made chicken pot pie so we had 2 great meals with that 6lbs chicken! Thanks for sharing!!
I have made this at least 5 times now.  AWESOME!

I don't know what to say except this is perfect!  The spice blend is perfect - the chicken turns out perfect - add some corn starch to the liquid in the pot and blend with a stick blender and the gravy is perfect!  If you don't need or want gravy, the liquid makes, well, perfect soup!  All this perfectness and it's easy, perfectly easy!  I use two smaller chickens to save money.  Thanks for posting the recipe!

My husband and I *love* this method!  After removing the chicken, I put the crock pot on "keep warm" with the liquid, then add the bones and skin back to it after we've had our "first" dinner.  Then I add 3-5 cups of water (depending on how I am planning on using the broth), put the crock pot back on low and let it go all night.  If I don't make soup (or whatever) right away, I freeze the broth.  Oh yeah, and I only add a few sprinkles of salt to the whole recipe because we're both on low-salt diets, but we don't miss it.  Benefit is my broth is natural and low-salt as well!

I followed the recipe exactly. However, 4 tsp. of salt? Come on people! That is simply way too much. It was like brining the chicken and not washing off the brine. I have made this with 3 tsp. and it was much improved, but I think next time what I will do is do the full amount of salt and wash it off after the refrigeration, then add all the other spices again with zero or only 1 tsp. of salt. That way, you will get the succulent quality of the meat without all that sodium.

Note (after the previous review) - I tried this recipe again, but instead of seasoning the bird prior to refrigeration, I brined it with recipe #66414. Then I rinsed the chicken, then followed this recipe exactly with the exception of adding zero salt. It turned out GREAT!
Lovely!! I used this for the meat, and ended up using the broth too!!! Fantastic. A keeper.

This is almost identical to the "Tticky Chicken" recipe we've been doing in our oven for years now. I threw a chicken in the slow cooker using the ingredients and came online to look for cook times and here it was! So happy to see that others have already converted it for slow cooker use. Already know that it is scrumptious in the oven...can't wait for it to get done now. Yum!

This was a very good recipe.  I'm so glad that whole chicken can be made in a slow cooker, and that it turns out so great!  I followed the directions exactly, except that I forgot the garlic powder.  The chicken was still delicious, and the house smelled so scrumptious when we came home.  I did not find it too salty as one reviewer stated.

This recipe is one of my favorites.  I was a little put off by the nutritional content so I took the skin off most of the chicken and then put the spices on.  This worked out great because the first time I made it was with the skin and it is not crispy or appetizing anyway.  So taking that off made it healthier and it was still REALLY moist.  In fact, I kept the juice to replace "beef broth" in other recipes and that has worked out really well as well.  Bon Appetite!

I added no salt but kept all else as listed. In a Word - DELICIOUS. Fantastic broth from the drippings if you keep all the juices in teh crock pot on low all night after dinner with all your bones and skin. The broth had a nice kick to it from the rub and I will never make chicken soup old school again =)

This is a fool-proof recipe. Love it. I transfer the chicken to a cookie sheet to brown under the broiler for a couple of minutes (it eliminates the most of the "greasy" parts that people complain about). Also, the gravy from the sauce is amazing! Pour the juices into a small pot on the stove. Add 2 Tbs cornstarch to about 1/2 cups COLD water, let it dissolve, and then slowly pour it into juices on medium heat, so the gravy starts to bubble and thicken. (Don't pour too much in too quickly or it'll turn into cement!) :)

My boyfriend and I always have this with mashed potatoes, corn and biscuits! Also, quesadillas with the leftovers are highly recommended! We also like to use the chicken for deluxe salads. :)

Great recipe!  I loved how simple it was and how tasty.  I left out the onions and it worked out fine.  It takes about 5 hours til done in my crock pot, but I kept it on low for 3 more hours and it was fine. I made the sauce that some mentioned making in their reviews with 1/2 cup cold water and 2 T cornstarch.  Yum!
Loved this, thank you so much for sharing! So simple and easy and made the house smell great. The meat was so moist and tender and left a nice bowl or two of great smelling broth.
I made this for dinner. Wonderful turn out and NOT TOO DRY! Very good and I have a lot of leftovers. DELISH

This is a fabulous recipe! I double it because my cooker runs hot and I need it to be on for at least 9 hours. I was able to make dinner, chicken salad(twice!) and a great chicken vegetable soup with all of the leftovers! This is definitely a staple in our home from now on. The chicken was very tasty and very versatile....thanks for a keeper :)

Wow!  It works!  I don't know why I just didn't think it was possible.  It is so tender and so easy you don't have to slave over dinner.  It is nice to cheat lol I also put in the oven for a little bit just because I like cripy skin.  Great recipe thank you so much!!!
Utterly delicious, especially for the ease.

This is a delicious dish but also a real gut buster.  The sodium (@ over 2500 mg) and over 15 g of saturated fat are over the top.  I suppose it is because of the skin on the chicken.  I plan on doing a repeat without skin and less salt - hope the seasonings will carry the dish.

This was so great, fell apart tender.  Will use less pepper next time, maybe my pepper was too fresh, was just too much for us.  Also only used 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper.  Actually the gravy was the spicy part, not the chicken itself.    DH does not like spicy foods.  He did love this chicken.  The flavors from the spices carry well with the chicken.  I also did not use any salt to decrease sodium content and it tasted great.  Thanks for the recipe, I probably will use this as the new "roasted" chicken!

Loved this.  I am not a huge fan of baked whole chicken because the flavor never seems to saturate the chicken.  Not the case with this one.  It was very tasty.  I did add carrots to the bottom and a few extra seasonings like rosemary and oregano.  My crockpot is slow, and I let it cook for 11 hrs.  Will definitely make again.  Thanks
This was easy, and delicious. Our entire family was begging for more and with 5 children that is saying a lot.

Fixed it just like you said in the recipe, but wasn't in no hurry, so defrosted the bird, rubbed with the herb & spice mix, put in plastic bag & in fridge overnight. Have a 6 1/2 Qt. oval slow-cooker, coated it with Pam, followed the recipe to the "T" & cooked it for the full time. Came home & house smelled heavenly. Bird feel off the bone & meat was simply wonderful. Used juices to make gravy. Won't change a thing. Looking forward to making it for guest. Thanks much.

What a wonderful and easy recipe! I used a whole (Gn'P) chicken (w/o giblets & neck). I have a 4 quart slow cooker so I thought it may be to small, but it fit perfectly. I lined the bottom of the slow cooker with chopped onions and seasoned as the recipe directed. I didn't have thymes so I used a few sprinkles of oregano). I also halved the salt amount to 2 teaspoons. Topped it off with a quarter cup of chicken broth (which was totally unnecessary - I learned at the end). And voila! Yummy chicken: tender, moist and falling off the bone!

I should have read the reviews because after 5 hours on low, my chicken wasn't even close to done and had to stick it in the oven when I got home from work.  I still can't wait to eat it and am learning the crock pot way...4 hours on high or 8 hours on low seems to be the standard.  Smells great!

This was really good!  We are a family of 6 (with 2 teenagers) so I made 2...one in the crockpot and one in the oven.  They both turned out great!  My husband really liked the spices.  I did as suggested and marinated it overnight.  Will make again for sure!
Love it, love it. I have the chicken in the crock pot now. Its so easy! This is the second time I made this and its deliscious

perfect!  We rubbed the herbs on the chicken right before cooking in the crockpot and it came out flavorful and tender.  We put carrots in the crockpot as well, and they were so yummy (with the taste of the herbs) that we will add more veggies next time!
Just Delicious my even my toddler who is very picky loved it!
My family LOVED this recipe!!! :D The chicken was so tender, and the drippings made the PERFECT gravy for our mashed potatoes. So simple....definitely going to become a regular meal here.

I have made this twice now and it is WONDERFUL!  The meat is fall off the bone tender, juicy and so flavorful!  Instead of putting onion in the bottom of the crock, I used an aluminum foil packet filled with cubed potatoes seasoned with salt, pepper and butter.  Oh my gosh, the potatoes were soooo good.  I used the leftover chicken breast to make Recipe #105202 the next day.  Yum!!!  *Update* - I've discovered if you add the bones and skin back into the liquid that was left in your crock pot, add 5-6 cups of water and whatever vegetables you have on hand (carrots, celery, onion) and cook overnight (12 hours) on LOW, it will make a WONDERFUL stock.  Filter the bones and veggies out, and store the stock in containers in the fridge.  After a few hours the fat will solidify on the top and can be removed.  The stock can then be frozen until needed.

I actually made this with two whole chickens at once in my 6.5 Qt slow cooker.  It came out amazing! I did the full prep with the overnight in the refrigerator, and just doubled the spices to be able to cover both chickens. I also placed the chickens on a rack (breast down), and added 2 cups of water to be sure they didn't dry out. Did one hour on high, then 8 hours on low.  It truly came out fall-of-the-bone perfect. Thank you, Kathy!

i love what you did on recipe, it was very delicious, slow cooking in crock pot really is the best, especially when you put some twist on it like that spicy crock pot Mexican chicken i found at gourmetrecipe.com they twisted crock pot a bit and added some spice.

This recipe is truly excellent. I had all of the spices at home already. I did not use onion powder, but dried onion flakes instead. It was the best chicken I ever tasted. So easy in the slow cooker, I cooked overnight for 8 hours on low and it was perfect. Thanks for sharing!
This was soooo delicious and soooo easy. I let it marinate overnight. The flavor was out of this world. Thanks so much for posting. I will definitely be making this one often.
Extremely good chicken! I love this, with a whole roaster I can have enough chicken for 2 dinners, and leftover broth. I may have to half the cayene for the kiddies.

This is so awesome.  I've done it with your spice mix, with the "normal" herbs and with citrus.  I've never refrigerated - always just plop it in on top of some chopped veggies.  Never fails - so delicious.  Thanks Kathy for a great recipe.
This is so good. My huby says it is just like Thanksgiving. I made gravy out of the juices.  It is a great recipe.I put it in the broiler for a couple of min. to brown a little.

I gave this 4 stars. My family really liked this recipe. Even my picky 9 yrs old newphew ate this right down. When I made this I added some baby carrots and chunked up potatoes in the bottom of the crock so I did add like 1/4 cup water so the veggies wouldn't stick. Our only complaint about this recipe was the amount of Peppers. This was a bit to spicy for our taste. So next time I will cut back on the Peppers. I reserved the juice from the crock and the next day I made chicken n' biscuits. So loved this recipe as it fits as a cook it once it 2 or 3 times meal! I will make this again for sure! Thanks for posting a great recipe! Christine

Great recipe. I halved the amount of salt. I also added smoked paprika and a little chipotle powder to the mix. I chopped up an onion and threw that in as well. I cooked on low for about 5 hrs and then increased it to high for about 45 min. It was fantastic. Thanks for an easy, outstanding recipe.

The flavor was excellent, and so easy to put together. I used boneless skinless chicken breasts and they fell apart to almost a pulled chicken consistency.  I did end up adding some water as it seemed to be cooking really dry (most likely due to using breasts only). I took half of what I cooked, cooled it and mixed with mayo, celery and chopped onion to make chicken salad for lunch the next day. So flavorful. I would definitely not use more than 2t. of salt, it was plenty salty with just that amount, I would consider reducing the salt more if I made it again. Thanks for sharing!
Not bad, but the white meat turned out dry rather than tender. Very easy. I found it a bit spicy, but would probably not reduce the spice because I did like it.

Let me just add to the hundreds of other reviews.... I will never again buy a roasted chicken from the grocers...this is no work, really.  Tastes absolutely fabulous.  Try blending up the cooking liquid and onions, after straining off some of the fat... delicious! great as gravy without anything extra... I am so pleased I found this recipe!
Turned out great!  Flavor was good and even white meat was very tender.  I used a 7.25 lb chicken and it took about 6 hours in my crock pot, which tends to run hot.

I guess I need to admit I'm not wild about crockpot chicken, although I tried this recipe with high hopes based upon the other reviews.  Followed the directions precisely and did end up with a falling-off-the-bones bird, but the meat turned out stringy and a little bit flavorless.  The bright side is that I ended up with some terrific broth to make soup with the next day.  :-)
Wow. I would put 0 stars if i could. This recipe is terrible. No taste whatsoever. Whoever likes a flavorful chicken, please do not try this recipe.
This was good and easy to make. I put my chicken on a bed of onions and used the fajita seasoning as you stated in the notes. It was easy to put together in the morning. Mine cooked up in four hours.

This slow cooker method saves time and energy. Quick and easy, and the best part is, no stove heating up the kitchen all day. You can easily put this together the night before, and just start it the next morning. So, easy my husband actually made it.(He's not really the cooking type.) It was super tasty too! Also, the left-overs make awesome sandwiches, and a throw together soup. one of my go-to recipes if I'm busy, but want a nice dinner at home.
absolutely great tasting chicken. will pass the recipe around the family. thanks for posting.

I recieved the highest compliment you can get for Crock Pot recipes. "It was good. Tasted like you baked it".  I did make a few modifications. I lightly coated the chicken with olive oil.  Then,   I did not add salt but added seasoning salt, italian seasoning, garlic salt, and poultry seasoning along with the other seasonings in the recipe.  I placed the onions on the bottom along with 5 diced cloves of garlic, and 1/2 of diced haberno pepper. Then I placed the chicken on top and allowed to marinate all night.  I cooked on low for 8 hours in the morning. When I got home that evening, I put the chicken in the corningware pot (from the crockpot) in the oven and broiled on low for about 15-30 minutes until lightly browned.

This is the easiest and most delicious way to make a whole chicken.  This recipe has become a staple in our house. After cooking I put it under the broiler for 10-15 mins to make it extra crispy and golden brown.  Thanks Kathy!

I was skeptical, but it was great!  Started it off in my crock pot, cooked it for about 4-5 hours, then put it in my oven to brown it.  Since my oven has a built in thermometer I used that to gauge how cooked it was.  After it was browned, I put in a dish, covered with tin foil and transfered to my lower oven to keep warm a couple of hours.

Normally I don't tweak recipes, but I didn't have white pepper on hand so I used black pepper.  I let the rub stay on overnight, but used a rotisserie.  This chicken was nothing short of PHENOMENAL!  I'm quite sure I would get the same results in the crock pot.  My petite wife ate as much as I did!!  This chicken is "off the charts" good!!  Oh, I only used 2 tsp. of salt (as suggested by other reviews).  Thank you for posting this wonderful recipe!
This was so easy and delicious!!  I didn't use a large roaster chicken - just about a 3 1/2lb chicken and it only took 4hrs on low.  It was falling off the bone!

This recipe was delicious! The chicken was very flavorful, tender and juicy. I just made it with a little twist. I didn't have the garlic powder and onion powder, so I used 1 clove of garlic (minced) and 1 tbsp of dry onion (minced). I omitted the cayenne pepper and put a bunch of fresh golden lemon thyme inside the cavity. I served it with roasted vegetables and my husband loved it! My stepdaughter is coming to visit next Friday and I will prepare this chicken again. Thanks for this wonderful recipe.

This my go-to roasted chicken recipe. I haven't tried it in the crock pot yet, but I definitely want to try it that way sometime. I mixed the spices together and put them in an empty spice container. I've found that for a 4-lb chicken, I only need about 1/3 of the amount of spices listed. Brining the chicken first makes it so tender. This tastes so good! It's got such a great flavor, with just a tiny bit of spice. It's really good on grilled vegetables, too.

This is just brilliant! I use half chicken as there is only hubby and me, rub the spices all over the chicken (skin, under the skin and bones) and let it sit for 3 hours before cooking as recipe suggested. I cooked it for 4.5hours on low and the chicken came out soft and moist but still sticking to the bones so it didn't look like a gross mess. I skimmed the fats off the stock and made gravy with it by frying some mushrooms with 2 tablespoons of butter, add 1 table spoon of flour and then pour the gravy into it so it'll thicken up. The gravy is superb and very flavourful!
Great flavor and very moist.  I made stock with the broth and cant wait to use it in soup it was so good.

I loved this recipe for the simplicity of it!  I had a small roaster that I had taken out of the freezer last night.  It was still partially frozen when I put it in the crock pot this morning and cooked it on low for about 6 hours.  Since the weather has changed and it got hot, I will serve the meat cold with some pasta salads.  The meat turned out nice and tender.   I would definately do this one again!  Thanks for the posting!

Melt in your mouth chicken with amazing flavor. This is definitely going into my favorites file!!!
I have some fresh rosemary, so I cut one in half and put it on each side of a turkey breast with everything else.

I was reviewing the comments on this recipe with the intention to try it out, and I saw a few people mention how it says not to cook a whole chicken in a crockpot. I did some research on it, and here's what I found: "I've heard you shouldn't cook whole chickens from frozen in a crock pot because it keeps them at a warm, not hot temperature for too long while they are defrosting and bacteria can grow." So as long as the chicken is fully thawed prior to cooking in the crockpot, it should be okay.

Very tender and tasty! My husband kept complimenting the flavor. It's a keeper. I put onions on the bottom of the crock pot as recommended. I would recommend that you cut the salt down though. Almost too salty.

Ok I rubbed the whole chicken with EVOO then rubbed the spices on under the skin and cavity of chicken omitting the white pepper because I didnt have any. put it in the fridge over night and put it in the crock pot around 11am until 5pm. This was so moist and flavorful everyone loved it! I used water , cornstarch and the chicken juices to make a rockin' gravy let me tell ya this recipe is a total keeper! thanks for sharing Kathy :)

I did not like the spice mixture, a bit more cajun than expected, too hot/spicy (even after I halved the cayenne) and peppery, and didn't like the blend w/thyme for my taste buds.  The chicken was tender and juicy.  I would go with some other rub, maybe more rotisserie style....
I have made this twice now, and it's an incredible chicken. Makes amazing cold chicken sandwiches for the next several days.
Very delicious and the best part was that it was EASY!  The chicken practically fell off the bone when I lifted it out of the crockpot.  Thank you for this recipe :-)

I did not refrigerate the chicken but followed the recipe as written, otherwise. I put the
chicken on a square of cheese cloth and tied the corners together and in the cp it went.
When the chicken was done, it was fall-off-the-bone tender, but I lifted it
out quite neatly and laid it on a sheet pan to remove the cheese cloth.
It was delicious and so was the broth.

Finally tried this recipe and it is keeper; about time there's a recipe for a whole chicken in a slow cooker.  I doubled the spice ingredients because it didn't seem enough for the chicken I had.  I reduced the salt to 2 teaspoons (doubled to 4), used 1 medium onion chopped, substituted amarillo (hot) chili powder for the cayenne, and eliminated white pepper (I don't have any).  I did let the seasoned chicken refrigerate overnight (turned 3 times) and poured the leftover spice rub into the bag with the chicken.  This recipe is a keeper and I will use it again.  It took about 6 hours in my Hamilton Beach slow cooker for the chicken to be done.
oh so easy, and cooked chicken for meals later in the week.

Excellent!!  Made as directed.  I added a cup of rice the last 1/2 an hour of cooking as another reviewer suggested.  DH couldn't get enough, lovely blend with the broth, mushrooms and rice.  The one thing I will do differently next time is to remove some of the oil that accumulates from the chicken before I add the rice.  It will definitely be in my rotation, thanks for posting!

So good!!!  Like others, I halved the salt... added lemon and garlic to the cavity...  added carrots and celery to the pot... rubbed some of the spices under the skin...  didn't marinate overnight...  crisped up under the broiler for the last 15 minutes....   The mix of spices is just wonderful!!!!  Saved some juices for gravy and the rest is back in the pot with the bones and skin to make some stock!!  Thanks for a great recipe!
Love the simplicity and flavor of this recipe.  I added sliced fingerling potatoes into the bottom of the pot and then served it all with a pan gravy which was unreal.  Nice and easy recipe!

YUM!  Followed the recipe as closely as I could, with the exception of subbing smoked paprika for plain, and using all of the cayenne pepper left in my bottle (it was probably 1/4th tsp instead of 1 tsp).  So, so good!  Used all of the spice rub, but only left it in the fridge for about 4 hours prior to cooking on low for about 5 1/2 hours.  It was so well seasoned throughout!  Tender, and juicy, but I think the breast meat was a little too done for my tastes.  I'll watch it more closely next time.  So good and so easy!

Family loved this chicken's great flavor. Even better, I was able to use that rich broth that was left in the pot to make a soup the next day. I strained the onion/broth mixture to remove any bones. Chilled and skimmed of the fat and added onion/broth to soup pot with 2 more cups of chicken broth, 4-5 small red potatoes, quartered, 2 stalks of celery and 2 carrots cut in thick chunks. Brought to boil and simmered until vegies were tender. Yum!

I made this recipe as written, I changed nothing. I threw the chicken out, the taste was awful,
I have been cooking for 60years and this is one of the few recipes that I would not put on the table. I gave it one star and that is too high.
EXCELLENT! The only way I am doing a whole chicken from now on. The spice mixture is perfect! Took 5 hours in the crock pot. Yummy

My whole family LOVES this recipe!  My 3 stepkids have requested it for everytime they are over - which I will definately do since it is so cost effective and EASY!  I double the seasoning recipe for 1 chicken because I like the extra flavor.  I rub it generously outside and inside the chicken.  Since we don't eat the skin (only because it doesn't get cripsy) the seasoning doesn't get too spicy.  My husband and I did the math & todays dinner cost less then $1 per person - we fed 6 with a small lunch leftover.  We all recommend this recipe highly.

Made this for the first time yesterday and it was delicious. I struggled to get it out of the slow cooker as it just fell to pieces it was so tender. The spices had given it a lovely taste and I did as someone else had suggested and put the chicken on onion, celery, carrots and parsnips to cook. I then added an extra 1.5 litres and all the skin and bones back into the slow cooker for about 7 hours on low and got a beautiful stock. Will definitely be making this my normal roast chicken recipe, so much less stress when its in the slow cooker!
ps I had my chicken upside down to keep the breast moist, but will try breast up next time. The skin was lovely and crispy on top though, my husband loved it!

Ideal for later use in soups, stews, pot pies, etc. because after slow cooking on low for about 8-9 hours, the meat completely fell off of the bones.  Wouldn't recommend cooking for 8-9 hours if intend to have anything left to slice, but again, PERFECT if intend to use the chicken later in other recipes that are calling for pulled/shredded chicken, or even diced chicken.

I am making this chicken for the 3rd time in the last month! I just put a 7 lb bird in the crockpot because my son, his wife and 2 small children are coming to visit from Chicago. These are the very important things I learned from reading many of the reviews. I cut my salt to 1 tsp, used half the amount of cayenne, and 1 tsp. total of pepper. I lifted the breast skin and put the seasoning under it, also 2 small pats of butter. I seasoned the cavity well and sprikled the rest of the seasoning over the rest of the chicken. In the cavity I placed 2 crushed cloves of garlic, slices from half a lemon and a large sprig of rosemary from my garden bended in half. This is what I have done each time and it has been amazing.

If you read a recipe and it sounds like too much salt or anything else use common sense and don't use so much. I think some of the folks are cooking these chickens too long, I have been able to lift the bird (carefully) from the crockpot with succulent, moist tender meat including the breast. My 6qt oval Crockpot cooks a 5 lb chicken on low in around 5-6 hours.

Like everyone says, chill that broth and remove the fat which will harden on top for some amazing chicken noodle soup! I have not tried putting the bones back in to simmer but plan to this time.

I NEVER expected this recipe to be so good and it it fabulous!!! Thank you so much!

First Delicious!

Very moist tender, falling apart goodness. Now, I knew I wasn't going to eat the skin, so I didn't care. It made it for sandwiches and for leftovers in the freezer. But it would be equally good for dinner; the skin just didn't that golden brown crisp which I like. But I knew it wouldn't.

The seasoning was good, but I cut back on the salt; I tend to go light on the salt personally.

No pop up timer, but I know my crock pot pretty well. Also, I had a smaller chicken - 5 hours on low and it was perfect. I also have a larger pot. If I would of used a large chicken, 6-7 would of been the right amount of time.

Easy and came out very very good.

Awesome! Its so tender and falling off the bone. We did leave it in for 8 hours on low and it was just fine. Plenty of 'juice' for a gravy. I halved the salt but followed all other instructions. The skin was even a little crispy which was surprising. Will be making this again.

This was my first whole chicken in the crock pot, and will certainly be the only way I prepare one from now on!!  I adjusted the seasonings per our tastes and cooked it right away.  Not sure about the weight of my bird, but it was done in about 2 3/4 hours on HIGH, or 180 degrees on meat thermometer.  Even though it was very moist, I was able to remove it from the pot all in one piece using a wide spatula.  The meat is wonderful on its own, but can also be used in a host of recipes calling for cooked chicken.  Can't wait to make it again.  Thanks for the inspiration to try new recipes.  My crock pot is becoming my new best friend!  :))
Excellent! The only thing I'll do different next time is remove the skin. With a few changes in spices this will make delicious shredded chicken tacos.
Come on over, I've got a chicken just coming out of the crockpot. I'm just itching to have someone over for dinner. We can party? Yes??

I am now in the process of making the chicken. I followed the recipe to a T and will have a follow up when it is done along with step by step picture's from beginning to end! My crock pot for some reason is much hotter than others. I guess you could call it a super hot pot. I have 2 crock pots and I chose to use the hotter one and will see if it gets a little crisp on the out side of the chicken.I set it on low because if I set it on high it would be done in no time and would loose the flavor of all the spices combining together on the chicken. I combined onion and fresh chopped garlic on the bottom of the crock and then sat the chicken on top of the onion and garlic. I put 1 tablespoon of lemon juice in also. Follow up ///// :There is no doubt that what ever you put in a crock pot will always be tender no matter what type of meat or poultry you put in it if you leave the crock pot go long enough.There is way to much salt in this recipe for me. I would cut the salt in half then go with the other spices. I had it in the crock for 8 hours. I added no water and there was 2 cups of broth for gravy. The skin was not crispy because of all the broth but it did have a good taste (minus the salt) if I would of cut the salt in half.
This is deliciously easy!!!!

This doesn't need another review but it was great. I remembered it today so didn't prep it overnight but it was fine. Used an 8 lb roaster on low for a couple of hrs then high for the end. I used half the salt & may skip it next time (yes, there will be a next time). A little peppery but not bad. Fell apart when I took it out but strained it & made a tasty gravy.

Wonderful recipe, cut the dry ingredients in half using a small chicken for 2 of us.  Next time I will pull up the skin and put the spices directly on the meat to get the full flavor thru the meat bypassing the marinating part.

This is a great alternative to roasting a chicken in the oven.  I would reduce the amount of each spice if you are cooking anything less than a 4 lb bird.  DO NOT put any more than 1 tsp of salt, that is insanity. I used less than 1 tsp of salt, I omitted the onion powder and added lemon pepper seasoning.  Obviously the cook times vary greatly if you are reading any of these reviews. My 7 quart crock pot cooked a 3-4 bird on low in about 7 hours, yielding less than a cup of liquid. The liquid was strained and used to make gravy which was exceptional, if a little too salty.  Definitely crisp up the bird under the broiler for about 10 mins then wrap in aluminum foil for a few minutes before serving.  Very tender and juicy.  Throw all the bones, skin, onions, etc back in the crock pot, cover with water and cook on low for several hours to make some chicken stock which you can freeze for later use.  The aromas while cooking this recipe are heavenly.  I only wish a turkey fit into my crock pot because I would be making it this way every Easter/Thanksgiving/Christmas.  Enjoy.
Easy and fast.  However, it's very similar to the Costco chickens and that' even easier.

I love this recipe.  I have made it for my two boys and they loved it.  I am making it for my fiance' tonight for the first time. I seasoned the roaster and placed it in the fridge last night.  This morning, I added my onions and placed the pot on low and out the door to work I went.  He called me when he got home from work this morning and said the kitchen smelled wonderful and he could not wait to eat dinner tonight.  I am going to make a pan gravy from the juices and make some mashed potatos and a vegetable to go with it...Thank you again Kathy for such a wonderful recipe.

This was very good, and I will certainly try it again. I made it with a little "nest" of chopped onions under it so the chicken would not be sitting in grease; that worked pretty well, but a friend also suggested balls of tinfoil, which I think would work even better. This really does need to cook 8 hours, in my crockpot. I was surprised that I needed to cook it so long, as my pot is usually speedier on most recipes. I ended up finishing it by roasting in the oven after 7 hours so we could eat dinner. The flavor was superb, texture quite good. Worth a second try, next time on low for a full 8 hours.
My 4.5 lb. chicken cooked in about 5.5 hours.  The rub imparted a good flavor to the meat.

Delicious and easy!  A great recipe for a busy day and the aroma wafting through the house is wonderful:)  Next time I make this, and I will:), I will cut the cooking time back at least an hour as the breast meat dried out.  I poured the juices into a container and will skim off the fat tomorrow after it cools and separates then will freeze for soup.  ***If you like fall apart chicken this is a must try!

Kathy - I'm so impressed with this chicken...moist, juicy and bursting with flavor from the top down!  Mine took 6 1/2 hours in my crockpot but I had a larger sized chicken.  Really a great way to prepare a roasted chicken without the oven.  Loved coming home tonight to this meal and so did the hubby and son!  Thanks so much!

This is such an easy recipe, and it turned out amazing! I did not prepare it overnight, I just put it all together and cooked all day, it literally fell off the bones. The chicken was so moist and flavorful.  I can't wait to make this again.

Delicious! I left in the crock pot on low for 9 hours. I could have shaved a couple of hours off the time, but it was still wonderful. We had it as a main course. Next time I will use leftovers for chicken wraps or tacos.

This is now my go to chicken recipe!  I only used 1/2 tsp of salt like other suggested and it came out perfect.  The chicken did create its own juices so there was no need for liquid and it was super moist.  This is a keeper!

After 6 hours, mine came out a bit dry and tasteless. Definitely couldn't taste the spices and it needed more salt (I used 2 tsp). Fortunately, I just put everything back in the crockpot with water and a couple bay leaves and made soup, which saved the chicken!

Not impressed. It took 7 hours in my crockpot until the popup timer popped. Meat did fall off the bone as advertised, but was very dry (even the dark meat), even though the crock was almost full of juice for a good portion of the cooking time. It's pretty obvious that all that juice came OUT of the meat! Much moister on the rotisserie on the grill or just plain roasted in the oven. Won't waste another whole chicken like this.

This litterally took me 3 minutes to get into the crock pot in the morning and the house smelt amazing when I walked in the door. The chicken fell apart taking it out of the pot, it was so moist and tender. The whole family enjoyed it. I used a small chicken and a very large crock pot - the breasts were a tad dry, I might turn the chicken upside down next time. I stuffed the cavity with lemon wedges and made a bed of onion in the bottom of the crockpot. I cut way down on the salt (1/4) and it was perfect that way. Thanks!
Made this recipe with 4 chicken thighs..came out great.. 4 hrs on high was plenty

This honestly has to be one of the easiest crock pot chickens I've ever made and it is just so delicious. A little bit of homemade gravy, a quick side of rice and dinner was done! I featured this recipe in my blog - http://danasfoodblog.com/?p=464.

This recipe is by far one of our favorites! It could not be any easier. Occasionally when I prepare it, I might be out of one of the spices so I substitute another one and it has always turned out great. I will admit to adding a stick of butter to the recipe! I place 2 of the tablespoons under the chicken skin and the remaining 6 tablespoons inside the cavity of the chicken.
As everyone else says, "fall off the  bone tender". The broth was fantastic!  Thanks
Super delish! Falling off the bone. Skipped the whole overnight thing.

I had quit cooking chicken in my crockpot a couple of years ago because it always turned out dry, but I saw this recipe and decided to give it a try. I am so glad I did because the chicken was fantastic! I followed the recipe exactly, including marinating it in the fridge overnight, and it turned out moist and flavorful. Thank you!

I some how forgot to rate this and have been making it for over 12 months!  Fabulous and easy, great to cook a chook for meals that require coked and shredded chicken or to have shredded chicken in the freezer.  If I am making this for that nights dinner, I always add small new potatoes on the bottom.  Such a great recipe!!!
Absolutely delicious!!!! I followed the exact recipe and couldn't be happier with the way the chicken turned out.

Almost 100 degrees all week and trying to not use the oven. This is the best chicken I have ever made, bar none. The seasoning is perfect. A little spicy for the kids but they loved the meat from deeper inside the bird. I made two changes based on necessity, so I only had black pepper, and I cooked this chicken on a layer of baby carrots since I had no onion. I put the rub on the outside and cavity of the bird, as well as rubbing it under the skin on the breast, back, and thighs. The only sounds at dinner last night were "mmmmm"s, so thanks for sharing a great recipe. I'll try this in the rotisserie next time to crisp the skin up. Yum.
I can't believe I haven't rated this recipe.  I have made this a dozen times and always always turns out perfect.  This is my youngest daughters favorite crock pot chicken.
Absolutely love! I cooked the chicken on low for 6 hours and the legs fell off when I was trying to take it out. Never thought that cooking such a delicious whole chicken could be this easy!
yeah tender but the skin is nasty putting mine in the oven to brown it up...

I tried this recipe on a whim and glad I did! <br/><br/>I followed the recipe exactly, however I left out the white pepper and the onion powder, since I didn't have either. Also I only added 2 teaspoons of salt (like the suggest). I also included the onions. The chicken was falling off of the bone by the time I finally took it out (about 4 hours).<br/><br/>My only suggestion is to broil the chicken for a few minutes after its cooked, this will make the skin crispy! It's well worth it. This recipe is super easy, I think i've found my preferred way to make a roast chicken. With the left over juices I'll be making a broth.

Absolutely wonderful fall off the bone chicken. I highly recommend using the left over rub to marinate the vegetables you use when cooking it. Our family adds carrots and potatoes to the recipe and it makes a meal you won't forget.

Made this for dinner tonight and was very well received by my family.  I put  2 tsp. of salt, but maybe for our taste, 3 would be better if the 4 is a bit too much.  I used the cooking liquid that was with left with the onions for a delicious couscous side dish.  I finely chopped the onions and added some fresh cilantro when i added the dry couscous to the cooking liquid.  There were some leftovers too, so chicken salad will be in our future.  Thank You Kathy for a easy and delicious recipe.

Best whole chicken I've ever tried! I didn't change a thing in the recipe (only used less salt, around 3 tsp); the chicken was so tender (it was cooked for 5 hrs on high mode in the crock pot). My husband & I love it & love the great spice mixture. Thanks a lot for posting this recipe.
Good with domestic rabbit. Added spices to 1/4 olive oil and rub on skinless meat. Done in 7 hours on low.
<3

This method of cooking the chicken was perfect!!! I imagine you could do any blend of spices and it could be perfect. The salt was too much. Maybe cut it down to 2 teaspoons. I used a whole chicken that was cut up instead since I didn't have a whole chicken. I put it in for 5 hours and it was falling off the bone and the most moist chicken. Even the skin was good! Will be making this with different spices often.

Sorry, but this chicken had a weird taste.  Yes, it was nice and tender and that was due to:<br/>1.) brining overnight 2.) first cooking in a crockpot and 3.) then cooking in the broiler.<br/>I will use this method next time I make chicken but I will change the spices to herbs, like rosemary and basil.  My family did not care for this particular combination of spices in the recipe.  And i don't see how anyone could make "gravy" out of the chicken drippings, which consisted of salty orange grease (orange from all the paprika.)  the technique for cooking is good, the choice and amount of spices is not!

Made this exactly as the recipe said. cooked on low until timer popped up. A roasting chicken that was 6-7 #'s. I have to tell you that this was the driest chicken I have ever eaten, though there was tons of liquid when I removed it from pot. 2 of us ate dinner and I threw the rest away. A waste of time and money.
Am I the only one here who was not impressed with this recipe? Moist, yes. Uninteresting flavor, though. I wouldn't make it again.

Although this recipe was tasty I am going to rate it just "Good"<br/>3 different peppers calling for 2 1/2 in total is an awful lot of pepper. I cut that back to 1/2, 1/2 and a few turns of my pepper mill.<br/>The fact that this recipe didn't call for any liquid whatsoever had me very skeptical so I did add a bit of water and chicken broth to the bottom. My chicken was completely thawed, maybe you are using a frozen chicken? That would make sense then that it makes its own liquid. Other than that I followed the recipe to a T, including the onion at the bottom. However, it was burnt to a crisp on the bottom due to no liquid. And I do mean burnt. I did cook it on low for about 6 - 7 hours while I was at work.<br/>I will try this again as I do like the flavor of the spice mixture (minus all the pepper it calls for) and will add some white wine, chicken broth and vegetables as other reviews have suggested.

One of my favorite crock pot meals!  So simple and cheap!  Feeds my family of 5 plus leftovers and then I make a chicken stock!  See how I make my whole chicken and stock:  http://mrscrislip.wordpress.com/2014/04/14/beat-the-clock-crock-pot-chicken-stock/

Holy chicken! This is the BEST! Literally! I am a chicken lover, always have been. This is by far my favorite chicken I've ever had, EVER! I think it's even my favorite meal ever! lol. I started to take another reviewer's suggestion about using potatoes in place of the onions. I'm SO GLAD I DIDN'T though! The onions really made the flavor explode and throw parties in my mouth! If you make this, be sure to get a little bit if onion with each bite of chicken. You'll be in heaven! I served this with Greek potatoes, roasted cauliflower, and beets(just for a splash of color truthfully, lol) went amazingly with the chicken! Again YUMMIEST chicken EVER! That's a huge compliment coming from me, I Promise! ^_^
I've been making this for years.  Good basic recipe for plain chicken. Unless you want over one hundred percent of your daily recommendation of salt, skip it and salt your meat at the table.

Tried it, loved it, and it follows my rules in the kitchen,,,KIS (keep it simple). Had the family over for dinner and made this in the morning and that evening wee all tried it for the first time and it is amazing. So tender, and the seasoning is perfect. Used the printer a lot that night cause everyone wanted the recipe. Definitely this is a keeper recipe.

I'm not sure how I could've screwed this up but it did not turn out.  I am giving it the two stars cause we did eat it, however it was in the homemade chicken pot pie recipe I made.  I cooked it on low for the day and when I came home, it did have its own juices like the recipe states.  However, when I pulled the bird out of the crockpot (and ye was really falling apart) and set it aside, it just did not have a good texture to it.  And, I had my husband taste it after it had come out of the crockpot for about 20 minutes and he said it was dry!  I honestly don't understand how meat that's cooked in its own juiced could be dry, but it was!

Getting ready to try - looks like delicious recipe; my Hamilton Beach slow cooker has settings for High, Low, and Warm; leaning towards setting it on low since it will cook 8+hours unsupervised tomorrow...I did not notice a setting recommended in the recipe. (did I miss it?)

This is an awesome recipe. I usually don't like slow cooker chicken cause I feel like it is bland. This is anything but. (Note, 2 teaspoons is PLENTY of salt). I like to cut up my whole chicken and arrange it on top of sliced red potatoes, carrots, and onion in the crock-pot. I think I would like to try it with zucchini some time. If you cook it on high it will be done in plenty of time for an afternoon Sunday dinner. I only cooked mine 4 1/2 hours and it was plenty done and not at all dry. I was skeptical when it said not to add water, but the chicken really does make plenty of its own juices esp. with the skin left on. I did use half the amount of cayenne cause I was afraid of it being to spicy for the kids.
A nice way to cook a whole chicken. Tender and flavourful. I still prefer the oven for a whole chicken though.

Back in 1985 when I was single and working long hours, I used to make sure I had supper ready for myself and my roommate by putting a whole frozen chicken in the crock pot before leaving in the morning and let it cook all day.  Sometimes, the lid wouldn't even close completely until the chicken had cooked for awhile.  I'd just sprinkle whatever spices I could grab over the frozen chicken and let 'er rip on Low.  No liquid was necessary because the chicken made the most wonderful juices and the skin crisped up so nicely.  It smelled so good when coming in the house when you're exhausted.
This is my go-to recipe for slow-cooking a hen.  I have had nothing but rave reviews each time I serve it.  Leftover chicken from it can deliciously be turned into an awesome pot pie.

This was the first time I made a whole chicken in a crock pot.  It was absolutely wonderful.  The meat was so tender it fell apart when taking it out.  As I am always in a rush, I skipped the overnight part but made it exactly as the recipe called, and it was perfect.  My entire family loved it and they want to know when I will be making it again.  This is a keeper recipe.  Thank you!

This is a great recipe!  The spice is spot on (though I did not have white pepper or onion powder and did cut salt to 3 tsps).  To everyone that complains about how it cooked - follow the directions. Use a large roaster with a pop up and be flexible about the time.  This was my first time so after 7 hours I put chicken and juices in a stainless roaster (before it popped up) for about 45 minutes and let it brown.  I could  tell by the legs it was almost done.  Took it out to rest and Voila the popper popped!   Sliced nicely - again use a large roaster! Served with mashed potatoes and fire roasted whole corn kernels with scallions sauteed in butter and 1/2 can of green chile's and some cinnamon.  So good!  If you use a large roaster as the recipe states the spice ratio is YUM!

I've made this twice, BUT NOT this recipe. This recipe is nearly exactly the same as "Roast 'Sticky' Chicken," also on Food.com. But 'Sticky' chicken is roasted at 250 degrees for 5 hours and comes out perfect every time. It was deja vu looking at this Main Dish Chicken recipe. After rubbing inside and out with the spices the other chicken is put into a plastic bag overnight in the fridge. I use a Reynolds Oven Bag, but the recipe writer uses a "food-grade garbage bag," and I don't care if the EPA or someone says that that is okay, I'm not doing it. So, now I guess I'll try this recipe and see how it does up against the other chicken recipe.

Made this for dinner tonight and it was delicious. Used some of the broth for gravy and the bones and the rest of the broth are simmering for soup base.  I cut the salt down to 1 tsp, but that is a little too light. 11/2 - 2 tsp would be better.  I was very liberal with the paprika which was a little too much, added chilli pdr instead of cayenne and omitted the onion powder because I didn't have any. I may use onion soup mix for the salt and onion powder next time. I have a new crock pot, for my 2kg (4.5lb) chicken I set it to auto which is high until it boils then low. Even my low is above the boiling point. I cooked it a total of 5.5 hrs, 3 hrs at low and 2.5 hrs at high because I thought it would't be done.  Next time I will leave it on low. Also I will put the breast down, it was a little dry. My comments are notes for myself for the next time I cook this, they are not criticism.  We really enjoyed this and I will definitely be making it again.
Very yummy!!! I had drumsticks only and I added a cup of red wine and cooked it on high for 3 1/2 hours. It was great!! Thank you!
I think I cooked it too long (8 hours on low). The chicken was super mushy. I'll try it again sometime and maybe lessen or eliminate the cayenne pepper as well.

Great recipe! I'm a lousy cook, and I made this (without the onion powder + white pepper, b/c I was out), and it was excellent. (I added a couple of sprigs of fresh rosemary, and put some of the spices inside the bird. Halfway through cooking, added one wedge of lemon, cut in 2, inside the bird.) Tonight I'm trying it w/onion powder + white pepper. <br/><br/>Note: I'm using the Hamilton Beach "Set and forget" slow cooker; has a probe, that cooks it according to optimal temperature (180); once that temperature is reached, the cooker automatically switches to  warm. Nice.

I can't even say how many times I've made this recipe and it ALWAYS turns out absolutely perfect. The chicken literally falls off the bone and melts in your mouth. I've become a vegetarian since the first time I made this, but I still make it for DH for a dinner, then vacuum seal shredded leftovers in one cup portions to use in casseroles, soups, chicken salad, enchiladas, you name it! Don't pass this one by!

So, I thought I would come onto food.com to find a new way to cook my whole chicken just to see if there was anything better.  The top recipe is the one I've made since 1999?  Yep, I'll stick with it then.  You won't go wrong with this recipe.  I put the onions into cavity and underneath.  LOVE!
AMAZING!!!  I only avoided cayenne paper as my kids don't like spicy. Very easy and simple to make.  LOVE IT

I have made this a couple of times now, and the  recipe is awesome.  It's so easy, and the chicken is moist, and flavourful.  I follow the recipe exactly, and it turns out great.  I've also used that spice combo for other meats too, and it was equally as good.  It would probably be better if I actually "marinated" it for 24 hours, which I haven't done.

This was amazing! This is going on our supper rotation. It was a bit spicy with a 3.3 lb chicken but that's what made it good. I used the liquid generated in the crockpot for gravy (added liquid to pan, boiled, added flour, then added milk to that) and it was fabulous: thick, flavourful, and spicy.

UPDATE - May 14th 2015
Have made this so many more times with and without the onions (frozen diced at bottom of crockpot). I LOVE the spice mix so much that at Easter I tripled (? or quadrupled) the spices in the recipe and put it on my turkey. Cooked it in a bag in the oven for the normal amount of time but the turkey and resulting gravy was AMAZING!

I wish I could give more than five stars! I just made it for our dinner tonight and everybody loves it! The meat was so tender, juicy and so flavorful! I cooked on high for 4 hours and the meat was pulled off easily. I think if I added about 2 more hours the meat would be more pull apart. After it's done, I broiled for about 5-7 minutes for browning the skin a little bit. I made the gravy from the juice which was so tasty. Overall, this recipe is so easy and delicious!
Best chicken recipe and s real family pleaser. Go to work and have an amazing dinner waiting for you at home. I just added 1/4 c white wine, 6 cloves of garlic, and 6 red pototaoes. It's amazing!

A good recipe for beginning cooks, and those new to crockpots.
I just realized I had been using this recipe, but I thought I had come up with it! ;)
Around 2004 I found 2 recipes on "Zaar" (back in the days) and combined them. Roast Sticky Chicken and Crockpot Roast Chicken. The result is almost this exact recipe (which appears to have been posted in 2002).
The changes I make are: cutting down the salt and cayenne, adding about a teaspoon brown sugar to the rub, and a pat of butter to each chicken breast, under the skin. Oh, I will usually rub olive oil over the top to help the rub stick. Make sure to add rub under the skin, and cavity as well! When done just thicken the juices with a little cornstarch (in a sauce pan), or go all out and make gravy!
The texture of the crockpot chicken will differ a little bit from roasted, but I, and the many people who have eaten it, do not have a problem with that. 
Any one who finds the flavor bland, really should definitely check the freshness of their spices...and did you really follow the recipe to the letter? The salt alone, if you do not reduce it, is a lot of flavor. Was the correct sized crockpot used? 6 qt would be best, but I have used the round 5 qt on a small chicken. Crisping it up under the broiler does put this over the top, but I don't feel the need to do it often. 
If you get the technique down, then the variety is endless! Change the spices to your whim!
Very tender and made great gravy!  Cooked faster than anticipated, so be careful with the timing on your crockpot!  Thanks!

Great recipe! I love crockpot meals and this is one of my favorites. I add potatoes,carrots and celery and experiment with the spices, but it's always awesome. My boyfriend loves it, too and always buys whole chickens when he's at the store for it. We make it about once a week, if possible.

Well..I made this knowing what was going to happen,mushy stringy chicken...I've made chicken that anyone without teeth would appreciate.. But I was more interested in making a stock for dumplings.. And indeed if you have no teeth please have some overly soft chicken.. But the seasons for a stock worked as planned.

This recipe is great as is. But, I've also added the juice of one lemon, put the chopped onion into the cavity of the chicken as well as the lemon peel. It gives it just a little bit of a zip. Either way, it's really a winner.

Very nice and juicy , but I have a great couple of tweaks! Cut down in half on the salt, buy black truffle oil and use that to marinate it in for 10 hours at least. Add rosemary and put lots of lemon and the cut of lemon should be put in the cavity. Use sweet paprika for a better taste and add some honey. Also add some Gin, and it will be the best meal You ever had. Needs 5 hours of Crock pot time
Made it just the way it says. Added a tsp. of Rosemary though, and threw a couple lemon wedges inside the cavity. Put under broiler on low for 10-15 mins to crisp up skin... it was EXCELLENT!

Yum! Like other reviewers, I reduce the salt by half, and add a lemon (quartered) to the cavity. I also omit the black and white pepper, as I find the cayenne more than pulls it's weight. I put onion on the bottom of the crockpot to keep the bird from sitting in the juices, and getting too mushy. Then I take a piece of foil longer than my crockpot, fold it in half long ways, set the foil on the onion, and put the bird on top of the foil. This serves as a sling, and makes it easy to lift the bird out when it's done. I cook this 3-4 hours on high. Once it's done I use the sling to lift the bird out, set it on a parchment lined baking sheet, and broil in the oven for a couple minutes to crisp the skin. This recipe is something my kiddo asks for weekly.

This is probably the third or fourth time I've used this recipe in one way or another and the bird came out perfect yet again. I have not actually done the overnight marinate with the spices (although the spices are great!) but every time I've made it, it gets better and better. In my crock pot, I have to cook it for 4-6 hours on high. This time I used the spices exactly but also added one quartered lemon inside the chicken along with about 3-4 ounces of amber beer in the bottom. I have not eaten all of the chicken (just a wing!) because the rest of the meal isn't finished yet but it's wonderful. I do believe that adding a bit of liquid in the bottom really helps with the cooking, at least in my crock pot. I believe I will be using the bones and broth plus extra veggies to make a stock that I will freeze for later.

I took another reviewer's suggestion and made overnight broth with the bones and extra veggies. I've made cxn soup many ways but this had to be the most flavor-filled broth I've ever made. It was not even necessary to enhance flavor. Granted, in my opinion, good homemade soup takes a bit of time (sieving solids from liquids, skimming fat off cooled broth, squeezing every bit of juicy broth out of cooked veggies) but it was worth it.
YUM! I put the lemon in the cavity instead of the onion and it was very good. It took a while... and the skin wasn't crisp but the meat was juicy and flavorful

YUM!!! Very juicy and tasty. I filled the cavity with lemon wedges, and set the chicken on top of 2 carrots and 2 stalks celery layered on top of 1 chopped onion in bottom of crockpot. Set on low, the 5 lb. chicken was done in 7 hours (instant-read thermometer said 165) in our old 4-qt crockpot. I seasoned it exactly per recipe and used 2 tsp. salt which was plenty. Will definitely make it again.

Great recipe for fall off the bone chicken! Skin doesn't crisp up, so spices wasted on exterior of chicken if you don't enjoy eating rubbery skin. Put rub on bottom of bird to ensure flavors absorbed by juices formed while cooking, but I put the majority of spice rub under chicken skin on the top part of the bird, so skin can be removed after cooking & allows meat to have tons of flavor. Used only small amt. of white pepper, omitted others & added little extra thyme (as well as using only 2 tsp. kosher salt as suggested by others). Put cut lemon in cavity along with carrots & celery on top of chopped onions underneath the bird. Took only 4 hours on high to cook 5lb chicken (in a 6 qt crockpot). Important to watch for timer to pop up to insure white meat is juicy & not over cooked. Everyone in the family liked this one....even my picky kids!

This recipe made delicious chicken. I followed the "2 tsp salt" and it was perfect. With the cayenne pepper it gave it a little kick. When seasoning, I pulled up the skin up and put the season under to ensure it soaked up the flavor. I also did one cup of onion, carrots, celery each and layers the bottom of the pot and used one lemon on the inside of the chicken and let sit over night. Placed in the pot on low. My crockpot cooked faster than expected so it was ready in about four hours. Next time I will check the temp after three hours so it doesn't cook too fast and may be a little juicer.
Sounds great. Definitely going to try this.

I made this for my family last night and it was amazing. I used 2 tsp of salt instead of 4 and followed the recipe exactly. When I went to take the chicken out of my slow cooker, it broke in half and the meat literally fell off the bone. This was the most delicious and tender chicken I've ever made!
I just made this. I stuffed it will lemon and garlic and it only took 4-5 hrs to cook in low. It is sooo good!
Whole family LOVED this!! So easy and yummy!

Love, love love this!!! I have never done the overnight thing and there are no complaints. I put in in early in the morning and the house smells amazing all day. Leftovers are good in salads, soups etc. I also do the lesser amount of salt.

This is as simple as it gets - I have a hard time rating 5-stars on slow cooker recipes, as it seems they're never quite up to par with the real roasting/baking recipes. But us mom's, know the value of a slow cooker! I think the chicken turns out "good", but my young boys love this (age 10 & 13)! So I'm on board - do this about 1x/week, with leftovers being used in salads, quesadillas, burritos, or snacking. I also make extra packets and set aside so it's an easy prep on any night of the week - I let my chicken "air dry" with the rub over night, versus putting in a plastic bag. A tip I got for a Thanksgiving turkey from San Francisco Chronicle. Try it - skips one less step and works out fine!
Yummy yummy delicious! I love this!!! Excellent turnout in 2 hours on the bake/roast setting. Will make again.

i made this last week and my husband loved it..it was absolutely AMAZING.. love the tenderness and love the juices, the juices taste better on the next day,i guess i'm gonna cook it the day before we eat it.lol i put it in the oven to make the skin crispy too,it was really TASTY.. thank you for this recipe,i'm making it again today by request of my husband.. :) it's the best chicken i had...i'm keeping this recipe.yummmmm *^_^* again thank you for the recipe. God Bless!

I had cut back on the salt (2 tsp as suggested)...but needed a little more, so next time will go with the 4 tsps. Turned out great even though I had already cut up my chicken. Love recipes where you can’t go wrong. Cooked on high 1 1/2 hours and low 2 hours. Making my stock now.

THE BEST!! Cut the salt and cayenne in half and its GREAT! Cooked on high for 2+ hours and low for about 3. It was so yummy! Great way to use a chicken that has no preservatives and organic rather than the rotisserie chicken from the grocery store. I couldn't find the white pepper in 2 of the food stores nor could I find the pop up timers in 2 food stores or the dollar store or the 2 drug stores. Might only bring them out for thanksgiving.
