2 teaspoons of salt and a teaspoon of soy sauce and it was nummy! Also I love cayenne pepper so I doubled that and the paprika! Came out whole, and melted off the bone!
Super tender chicken,the gravy is out of this world!!
Great, recipe needs less salt but the flavour was awesome, I actually used a bit more of the herbs and spices to give it a bit of extra flavour and it was great.

I was so excited with the end result that I texted all my friends the recipe. I will definitely be making again!
Amazing. Best chicken ever!
Memories of childhood!  Sunshine, the garden and one VERY yummy sandwich.  Definately a Southern favorite!
My fav sandwich ever!

Teresa

use to eat these all the time in Nebraska.  Mix a little basil in with the mayo... Great recipe

I have been making these for years, growing up in an Italian family plenty tomatoes were grown every summer, these were a great snack eaten all of the time.A nice sandwich on a HOT summer day!

I was turned on to these sandwiches as child by my mom and I intially thought yuck until I took a bit of her sandwich and fell in love with them. I've been having these sandwiches for years (usually during the summer months).  I love them! They are great!!  If I feel like "cooking", I'll toast the bread before making the sandwich.  ;)

These are the greatest. I can't remember not eating them. Yes, fresh, fresh white bread, and add some good cheddar cheese is the way to go. I thought everyone liked tomato sandwiches like this.
This is what i call a sandwich, only we called them door steps when i was a kid

Nice to know I am not alone in the loving of this sandwich!  I was first introduced to this sandwich when I married my DH.  He was raised in a family of 10 kids, so this was a usual lunch or snack. This is one of my all time favorite sandwiches to eat in the summertime.  Beefsteak tomatoes with that lovely acidic taste combined with that tangy Miracle Whip.  To be daring, sometimes I add a slice of Texas 1015's.  Have a handtowel ready, as paper towels can't keep up.  5*'s all the way!

I used to order this from the deli across the street from my office.  This wasn't a normal menu item, I just told them what I wanted and they made it.  I have been eating these for years and I am so glad someone else sees the beauty in them.

I make this too but I put it on toast! I eat one every day during the summer!
Wow--what could be better, fresh summer tomatoes, white bread, and of course, it has to be Hellmans!!  I grew up on these sandwiches, and I'm from the North!! Fun to find this recipe!!!!

This really is my favorite sandwich.  I think the key to it is having good tomatoes, not the orangy-red yucky ones!  There's nothing like nice big red tomatoes from the garden!  Sometimes I also add a slice of american cheese, but I don't think it is needed! yum yum
A classic!  You must have garden ripe tomatoes for this.
Hubby's favorite sandwich. Especially on Country White Bread recipe #97431. Besides fresh from the garden tomatoes, lots of mayo and salt is the key. Definitely a classic.
Yummy sandwich - I eat these all the time during tomato season!!! Thank you for reminding me of this wonderful meal

Forgot how yummy this could be!! Used whole wheat bread, fat free kraft american cheese slices, and low fat cheese, and juicy vine ripened tomatoes and was very very happy. Thanks for the idea, takes me back to when I was younger and used to eat these!

This isn't a recipe; it's a Southern tradition.   My "recipe" for this is not to even chill the tomato, but just cut it, fresh off the vine.  This "recipe" only works with tomatoes in season, and not those hard "pretend" tomatoes that could be used as baseballs.

I never knew anyone who hasn't eaten a tomato sandwich and loved it!
Also, if you add a few slices of some good bacon, and some lettace... we call that a BLT. If you've never tried one, they are awsome too.
Nothing better in the summer than a good tomato sandwich.  As another reviewer said; a Southern tradition.  And something even better; use a yellow tomato.  Not as much acid and just as good.  Yummy!
I grew up on these and still eat them today. Such a yummy lunch!!!
I used whole grain bread as that was all I had and low fat mayo.  Fresh, just picked tomatoes from the garden really made this sandwich zing.
I've been eating these marvelous creations all summer and just realized I hadn't written a review.  Five stars all the way.  Sunshine in a sandwich.

I love this recipe.  I grew up eating it.  A quick sandwich to make and it is especially good in the summer.  I usually add some onion on top of the tomato and use hamburger buns instead of bread.

I have always had these but I don't chill my tomato (I will try it) and I only use one thick layer of tomatoes on my sandwhich. There is nothing better than a fresh tomato sandwich, especially when it takes you over the kitchen sink!!!
Brings back wonderful childhood memories...you just can't get any better than a fresh tomato sandwich!  I can't do the Miracle Whip, though...I'm strictly a mayonnaise girl!
I had never had a tomato sandwich before, but it was really good!  This is a great Weight Watchers recipe if you use 35-calorie bread and lite mayo.

My absolute favorite sandwich.  Made exactly as written using Best Foods Mayo and has to be on soft, fresh white bread to taste the same....IMHO.  No pepper on this one for me.  Just picked two huge tomatoes from the garden yesterday and I'm going to the store for my white bread so I can make this for lunch. Yummy!
Best sandwich in the summer.  Only thing I would do different is not to refrigerate the tomato.
When I was a little girl this is what my mom would feed us for dinner on a hot summer day. Brings back wonderful memories... I still to this day feed them to my kids and grandkids.

Funny, I am born in Germany and I grew up on that food. We use Butter and Ryebread:-)
and lots of Onions !!!!!!!!!!!
Thanks for throwing me back into my "old Country memories".
I love this sandwich! I too will sometimes add sweet pickles & cheese.mmmm.
Had this last night for dinner..  Very delicious with our famous Jersey tomatoes!
It's so easy to fix and simply delicious.
I grew up in Georgia eating the same sandwich! You can also vary this by using homemade biscuits instead of sandwich bread.
I have made this so many times as a kid.  The tomatoes really do have to come straight off the vine for it to taste the best but it is yummy even with store bought ones.  Summer on a plate.
Loved it!

When I read this recipe it took me back to my childhood spending the summers on Long Island and eating freshly grown local tomatoes just like this recipe.  I live in NJ now and after reading this I went out and got fresh tomatoes from the garden and feasted on a sandwich.  Thick slices are the key and lots of mayo!!!  Thanks for reminding me about this submitter.
I eat these all the time!  I add  lettuce (real creative, I know) for some crunch if I have it around. Soooo goooooood!
love it   can't wait for summer
One of my absolute favorite sandwiches. I love it! Who needs a BLT when you can have just a tomato sandwich thats even better? :-]
As someone who was born and raised in Tennessee, I have to say this is the only way to eat a tomato sandwich. ;)
Yummy and healthy! Thanks for introducing me to this!
i love it!!! i used veganaise. it tastes like a blt in a way :)
One of my favourite sandwiches! Easy and very satisfying!! I sometimes use tartar sauce instead of mayo, you should really try it!

Made for lunch today using a toasted whole pita pocket and Duke mayonnaise.  I added some lettuce to make it a huge sandwich and I was in heaven with each bite!  With vine fresh tomatoes in season, this makes for a juicy run down your arm sandwich that is low in calories!  Yummy to my tummy!  Love em!  Thanks so much for sharing Danny!

Yum, this ranks right up there with my love of catsup sandwiches.  I did not need the help of my kitchen sink as I seeded the Roma tomatoes that I used.  This is a fast light lunch or a late night snack when your in a hurry. I used sea salt for a little extra crunch.  Made for *Zaar Cookbooks Tag 2008* game
This has been my favorite sandwich since childhood, and still is.  MMMMMM.

I ate so many of these last summer that my mouth developed blisters from the tomato acid. (Citrus fruits do the same thing to me). I would stop for a few days, then start on the tomato sandwiches again.  They are so simple, but yet  so wonderful.
this is when i know summer is good i always can't wait for fresh tomato so i can eat a ton of these  it is nice to see so many people eat and enjoy these
Love Love Love this - it was also my go to sandwich when I was pregnant

This doesnt sound like much but once you eat it you will be eating more and more. My mom used to eat these and I never understood it till now. Being prego it actually sounded good so I gave it a try and wow! I could eat these everyday! They are even better on toast I have to add. ;)

One of the best things in life during the summer is a sandwich made with fresh garden tomatoes! I love it with lots of salt and pepper. I grew up eating these, but my children think it's gross. Hey, I'm not complaining - that's just more tomato sandwiches for me.
the only thing I do different --I love this sammich- is use whole wheat bread---this year's garden is absolutely loaded with tomatoes, so my bread, mayo, pepper and knife are just waiting!!

This is indeed a classic southern recipe which my family has enjoyed for years and correctly needs to be cited as being plagarized from the late Ernest Matthew Mickler's classic southern cookbook and oral history, White Trash Cooking. This was OUTSTANDING!  My husband is a 'meat expert'.  He loved this, but not as much as as I did.  I love to share recipes, but I won't share this one. There is no other way to roast a chicken!  This was far and away the best roast chicken I have ever made in my life! I was uncomfortable with the low cooking temperature and went to http://www.fsis.usda.gov just to make sure it was safe. There is a pull down at the top of the page “fact sheets” that says the safe temperature for chicken is 350!! I called the toll free number (888-MP hotline) and was told that it is very unsafe to cook chicken or turkey this way, because it gives bacteria time to multiply while it is reaching the safe internal temp of 180. 
I went ahead and cooked the chicken at the safe temperature of 350 and it was wonderful, but I am concerned about someone getting sick.
I have now made this about a dozen times. It always comes out perfect.Thanks!

Really delicious!  I used the rub as written and found the combination to be fine for our family, kids and all.  I read the various opinions on the slow-cooking method this recipe calls for and the concerns. For my own info, I looked up the government website and found a section on 'slow cooking' for chicken. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/Fact_Sheets/Focus_On_Slow_Cooker_Safety/index.asp   It states: "The direct heat from the pot, lengthy cooking and steam created within the tightly-covered container combine to destroy bacteria and make the slow cooker a safe process for cooking foods."  So with that, I felt more comfortable using my Necco Roaster which has a cover.  Turned out great!  I would suggest that those cooking in the ovven use a roasting pan with a lid as well to be safe.  Pam :-)

Did check http://www.fsis.usda.gov/thermy/index.htm 
This is what I found
The minimum oven temperature to use when cooking chicken is 325 degrees F. Using a food thermometer is the only sure way of knowing if your food has reached a high enough temperature to destroy foodborne bacteria. All poultry should reach a safe minimum internal temperature of 165 degrees F as measured with a food thermometer. A whole chicken must reach a minimum internal temperature of 165 F throughout the bird. Check the internal temperature in the innermost part of the thigh and wing and the thickest part of the breast. For reasons of personal preference, consumers may choose to cook poultry to higher temperatures. For approximate cooking times for chicken, go to: Focus on: Chicken <http://www.fsis.usda.gov/fact_sheets/Chicken_Food_Safety_Focus/index.asp>.

I do add about 1/2 stick of butter, cut in pieces for even distribution, to the cavity along with the onions.  Adds moisture, and who cares about the calories when you bite into this savory and tender chicken!  I've never written a review before, but just had to share my enthusiasm for this recipe!  I have shared the recipe with everyone I know!
amazing!  used to make sandwiches and for a meal.  I used an organic chicken for the first time and it made an large amount of brooth.  It was delious.  I can not wait to make again.

This chicken was very nicely seasoned, moist and tender.  I used a "butterflied" chicken, weighing about 3.5 lbs.  When ready to roast, I cut a large onion into thick slices and used it as the "rack".  I split the differences of opinion and roasted it at 325.  It was done in just over two hours.  The skin was perfectly brown and crisp, and the bird was delicious! I'll be using this recipe often...thanks for posting it, C!

Like everyone else says, very good and easy! Definitely a keeper!
For the marinating part, I used a plastic bag from the meat section of the supermarket - the ones they have available for you to put around your cello packs before you put them in your cart - I would hope those are food safe!
I roasted it the way I learned to slow-roast a turkey (from the foodtv, so it should be legit): start in a medium hot oven preheated to 400F (the preheating part is important here) for 15 to 20 minutes, then turn it down to 300 for the remainder of the cooking time. It took exactly 3 hours for a 5 lb bird this way.
Does make a pretty bird, too!

This was great! I seasoned exactly as called for except I cut the salt in half. Because of time constraints I only refrigerated mine for 3.5 hours. I started off baking at 275 degrees and lowered it to 250 degrees. After about an hour I basted it with melted butter. I used a meat thermometer to make sure it was done. Very moist, even the breast meat. A keeper.

I have been cooking this chicken for several years now and we love it.  I have yet to marinate these and I ALWAYS cook two at a time and freeze the second one.  Sometimes I'll cut them in half for smaller meals or leave them whole.  I wrap with a double layer of plastic wrap then heavy duty foil.  I've left them in the freezer for months and once reheated they are always just as moist and delicious as when I first cooked them.  I also keep a container in the pantry of pre-made rub so it's always available when I'm ready to cook these.  Great on turkey breasts/thighs too!  Just adjust cooking times accordingly.
It came out nice and moist. Tasty too. Thank you!
Great tasting and so moist!

This was excellent.  I used a little less cayanne and salt, I didn't let it sit overnight- just sprinkled the seasoning on before baking.  I baked it, uncovered, at 350 degrees for about 1 1/2 hours.  Very, very tasty.  Thanks for sharing.

Cooked this last night and it turned out great! We were actually working in the yard while this cooked so it didn't get basted quite as much as it should have. We also cooked it for 1.5 to 2 hours at 350 in the oven. I was out of white pepper so used 1 tsp of black pepper total instead. Not sure if it changed the taste as I've never tried it with the white, also didn't marinate overnight but just seasoned the bird before cooking. It was sooo tasty and the skin and onions from the cavity were DIVINE! We'll be doing this one again. Thanks!

Proud to be the 210th reviewer for this winner! I also did not marinate overnight, but rubbed the spices on just before roasting at 375* for one hour, then at 250* for 3 more hours. Also, it didn't get basted at all since my guys at home "forgot" while I was out. It was still fabulously juicy and enjoyed by all. I did roast the chicken  "breast side down" to allow the juices to keep this part moist. Served with Recipe #260383 which uses many of the same spices. Perfect!

Great mix of herbs for superb flavor! Having read the reviews, I opted to use the coating ingredients (cutting the salt in half), stuff the chicken with herb stuffing, and "roast" the chicken in a bag, surrounded by potatoes and carrots cut into 1 inch pieces. I baked it at 350 as per the bag instructions for almost 3 hours (my chicken plus stuffing plus veggies weighed in a 6 pounds). The herbs gave a wonderful flavor to the chicken, to the vegetables, and to the drippings, which I used to make gravy. Tonight I am using this "rub" mixture on turkey drums for the grill. This mixture is truly tasty--thanks C Chatwin!  UPdate (dec 4)--very good seasoning mix to use (with lemon juice and olive oil) as a marinade for grilled turkey and chicken drumsticks. Had them last night--my DH said the chicken drums were "better than El Pollo Loco", which he loves.

I wonder if I did something wrong when I don't like a dish as well as everyone else did. However, I didn't think the finished product was worth the preparation effort and cook time.  The skin wasn't very crispy and the long cooking time produced a texture in the meat I really don't prefer.  I did enjoy the chicken and so did my guests, so I certainly don't regret making it, I just think there are other cooking methods I prefer more.
Oh my! Wonderful.  I rarely eat meat but I made this for my family.  I sampled it and couldn't stop eating it! We all loved it.

Made this today for dinner and loved it!  The only thing I did differently was instead of oven roasting, I put it in the crockpot and cooked on low all day. Meat fell off the bone and was a wonderful flavor. Will certainly make again.

We made this today for Christmas dinner (there are only 3 of us, and none really like Turkey!) and it turned out wonderfully! I have read many reviews that gave advice regarding temperature. I put mine on at 325 for the first 2.5 hours, and then reduced to 250 for another 1.5 hours. Instead of putting my turkey in a bag overnight, I placed it in the roaster and covered it with saran wrap (it seemed like the most logical thing to do...). The flavour of the chicken was incredible - it was soooo moist and tender. I added a little bit of butter to add extra flavour when I began basting. I will definitely be using this recipe over and over again! Thank-you C Chatwin for making our Christmas dinner a smashing success!!

Made this recipe a directed, except the baking part cuz I was too worried to do it that way after reading the other reviews.  I marinated a 4 pound chicken with the rub overnite, then roasted at 375 until internal temp was 180 degrees, that took about an hour in my oven.  The rub added a nice flavor to the chicken.  Not too salty as others complained, but I had some rub that was unused due to the size of my chicken.
Loaded with sodium this chicken tasted great but it had way too much salt.  I will make it again and just add a sprinkling.  I loved the spice mix!  I wrapped mine in saran wrap.  Worked for me!

I made two 4 lb. chickens for Christmas lunch, using this recipe.  The chicken was so tender and moist and my guests loved it!  Thanks for such an easy, delicious recipe.  I will be making this again.

Hi! This chicken made me and my husband very ill. We were both throwing up, etc after eating it. Slow roasting the chicken can be dangerous and unfortunately that's what happened with us. I even used a meat thermometer to make sure it was 180 inside but we still got sick. Proceed with caution because salmonella can kill small kids and grandparents. Sorry for the bad news. But I feel obligated to share.

To the previous poster. Only meats cooked at less than 250 degrees can make you sick, and people eat slow roasted meats all the time cooking at 250.  If you got sick, it was probably something else that made you sick.  We truly enjoyed each and every bite of this deliciously seasoned chicken. It was nice and moist and the skin was nice and browned and so good!  We will have this again and soon, because we eat a lot of chicken and this is a 5 star recipe for us!  Thanks!

This was the best thing I've ever cooked!!! Even my 7 year old ate - who usually only likes things his father cooks lol!  Thank you so much for this - definitely a family favourite - and no one got sick ;)

okay , so!!!! This was not done after 5 hrs and 10 mins, I was really embarrassed as I was sliding it back into the oven at 400 for 30 more minutes... not to mentin my dessert was all ready in the oven!!! The chicken was okay tasting obviously probably not as moist as it was cooked at 400 for 30 mins. Probably won't try again.

Oh My Gosh! This was the BEST chicken I have ever had in my mouth. It was moist and the spices added sooooo much to it. I didn't even get to marinade it overnight and it was good. Marinading it overnight would probably make it just that much better. For the person that said it didn't get done she probably needs to check that there isn't something wrong with her thermostat.

Perfect roast chicken! I put the chicken in a casserole, rubbed it with spices and covered it with plastic wrap for 2hrs. I stuffed it with chopped onions and green apple. I cooked it at 325F for 2 1/4 hrs.  No need to marinate overnight or cook for 5 hours. I added a bit of vegetable stock to the pan, and basted the chicken with it. The chicken drippings made a great gravy -- mix 1/2 c flour with water to make a paste, add to 1 1/2 c drippings in a saucepan (add water if needed), and heat over medium stirring with a whisk until thickened.  Delicious!
My whole family loved this chicken.  It was nice and moist and the flavor was awesome!  I can't wait to make it again soon!

GREAT RECIPE!!!!  Placed the chicken in a deep  bowl and covered it.  This way the spices wouldn't come off the chicken and stick to the plastic.  Did add a few slices of butter under the skin.  Also add some of the spice mix under the skin.  Placed a few lemon slices in the cavity along with the onion.  When I did check on the chicken the skin did look a little dry so I poured a little olive oil over it.  We will certainly make this delicious chicken again.
So yummy and easy - love it!

Iâ€™m a believer in slow cooking, especially for pork and beef recipes, so needless to say I was pleased to find this slow cooking recipe for chicken. The following day, I took some of my leftover â€œSticky Chickenâ€� to work for my lunch, and after warming in the microwave oven, everyone wants this recipe. Iâ€™m from Canada, and they all swear the aroma is like Swiss Chalet, which is a chicken franchise restaurant up here.
Another 5 star review from the whole gang here.  We loved it!
We loved this chicken.  No ands ifs or buts about it!  The chicken was tender, juicy, and with all the spices it was delicious too!  Potzi
Great recipe! Tripled it and used it on a turkey cuz i have a huge family!!! ThanX!!!
I really liked the spice combination. I didn't have a whole chicken so I just used bone-in chicken breasts. Thanks for the recipe.

WOW!  This is the best roasted chicken yet!  I have made this recipe as posted 3-4 times with the following exceptions:  first, I used just one onion to stuff into the cavity and found it to be plenty, maybe my onions are bigger or my chicken smaller; I did not use a black garbage bag to cover the chicken; and, I put it on a roasting rack then inside a shallow baking pan (I don't like the soggy part on the bottom otherwise).  Moist and wonderful chicken and the skin is so fabulous (too bad it's not too good for you!).  Thank you, thank you, C Chatwin, I will use this recipe A LOT in the future.

Delicious! I skipped the marinating time because I decided too late in the day to make it. Was good nonetheless. I used some of the drippings to roasts some chopped potatoes. Very satisfying and easy meal.

This was delicious.  I reduced the salt to 3 tsps and added a clove of garlic with the onion and it did not sit over night to marinate.  Unfortunately we didn't get to eat this the night I cooked it, so we ate it for dinner the next night as sandwiches and it was AWESOME.  I've never had leftover chicken taste so moist and delicious before.  The next day I turned it into chicken salad using recipe #53508.  It was awesome.  Hubby wants to try it on the rotisserie next time.  Thank you!

You can't get any better than this.  It was so moist and the flavor was excellent.  I was limited on time so I only marinated the chicken for 4 hours but the flavor still came through.  I also only used 3 teaspoons salt and next time I will only use 2 teaspoons, just a little too salty for my family.  I also cooked it at 300 degrees and for 3 1/2 hours (5lb chicken) and it was great.  I will share this recipe with friends and will cook it often, Thank you.

This was wonderful.  Beautifully browned, crispy and juicy.  I roasted 2 chickens.  We ate one and I froze the other to put in the RV for an easy and delicious meal when we are on the road.  NO MORE walmart rotisserie chicken.  Thanks for a wonderful treat.

I'd give this 10 stars if I could.  Perfectly spiced!  My kids announced (after only a bite) that it is their new favorite meal.  I did cook it at 350 for a shorter time due to the warnings indicated in some of the reviews, but it still turned out perfectly...crispy, juicy and a perfect blend of spices.  Thank you for sharing this amazing recipe!!!

4 thumbs up from the 4 very different taste buds living in my home!  Because of all of the concerns about oven temperature, I cooked in an oven bag on 350 degrees for 3.5-5 hours.  It was moist and delicious!

This is a great chicken rub!  I've used it a couple of times with just a few modifications.  I melted a little butter (maybe 2 tbl) and drizzled it under skin and also on top of the skin before adding the rub - also under and over the skin.  I did decrease the salt to 2 TBL, just a personal preference.  I then cooked the whole chicken in my crock pot (high 4 1/2 hours, or low 6-8 hrs).  I poured about a half a cup of dry white wine over the chicken at the beginning of cooking, and the result was a perfectly moist, deliciously seasoned roasted chicken with very minimal effort!

Fantastic rub. I rotisserie the chicken with this rub on it an it tastes wonderful. Sometimes I put the rub on right before cooking and it still turns out fine, but if you can do it ahead of time I recommend it.

What a delightful roasted chicken. My family really enjoyed it. My only complaint, me and thyme just don't hit it off. LOL It's just too overwhelming to me. Anyway, I made chicken and noodles with the leftovers and they were KILLER! The broth was to die for. Put it over mashed potatoes...YUMMO! Thanks for the recipe.

I started this late so the rub only had about two hours to flavor the chicken, but it was excellent!  I did rub the skin and under with olive oil and put the rub both on and under the skin.  I poured a half cup of dry white wine over it when I put it inthe dish.  I used a stoneware baking dish and there was no juices after the first hur so I added another half a cup but by the end there was awesome juice for basting.  I threw a bunch of carrots, onion, and potatoes with about three hours left and in the future I would put them in earlier.  Excellent recipe, a real keeper, thanks!

I made this using my George Forman rotesserie and it turned out awesome! The spices are so delicious! It turned out so moist and juicy in 1 and a half hours and no basting since the rotsserie is self basting! I don't think I've ever had roasted chicken this good! Thanks for posting!

OMG!!! This was the easiest thing I've done. Yes, it takes 5 hours, but well worth the wait. the only thing I added was mix unsalted butter with spices, but wouldn't change anything else in this recipe I also my chicken around to broil the other side to get it crisp, that made a huge difference. Thanks for the recipe.

This chicken was simple and great tasting.  I cooked the bird on a bed of vegetables, celery, onion, carrot and spices so I got a fabulous gravy too.  Tip - Make sure the bird is very dry before applying the rub.  Served it with garlic mashed potatoes and caramelized brussel sprouts.  Definatley a wow meal

I made this recipe as directed. Once this chick is marinating in the fridge it really doesn't take any time really in making other than popping it in the oven.  I sat mine on a bed of carrots. I guess all chickens are different because I really didnt have any juice to baste with. I had put in about a cup of water in the bottom half way through cooking just to have some juice so I could baste. This was still a very moist chicken and tasty. The only thing I didn't like was the skin, and I love the skin when it's crispy but this had too much cayenne/paprika flavor on it. I am sure it was healthier that I didn't eat it though. But the chicken was really yummy. We had this with mashed garlic potatoes and fresh green beans. Thanks for sharing your recipe C Chatwin.

This was my first attempt at a whole roasted chicken so I have nothing to compare it to, but it was delicious. My friend and her kids all loved it too.  I used an organic bird and rubbed some of the spice under the skin too since I don't eat the skin. I also didn't have white pepper but I don't know if it mattered. The chicken was super moist and tender and flavorful!
This was very good, with nice crisp skin and a little bite from the cayenne;however, mine was on the dry side.  Next time, I will reduce cooking time.

"Easy and yummy! Love the two step process. I don't think I'll ever have chicken that isn't slow roasted again. The way it was so moist, tender, & even somehow sweet made it the best chicken I've ever had.  Thanks for posting this!"

... This was my original review from 5/1/2007, but I have to say that I now roast the majority of my chickens using this recipe 2/12/2010... and just made one today! I have made some minor adjustments... instead of cayenne, I use chili powder b/c it's more flavorful and since I had a baby I avoid making food too spicy so that he can eat it. I personally don't like white pepper, so I just use a little extra black pepper and it still turns out fine. In our convection "roasting" oven, sometimes it only takes 4 hours for a 7 1/2 pound bird.
This chicken is awesome... and makes a good flavored stock afterwards.

I followed the instructions exactly. My husband (who loves just about everything except beets) did not like this chicken. He said it was "too much" and taste like the herbs. Sorry but ruined a perfect whole roaster.

I tried this while my husband was out of the country because he will spend a fortune on the store bought chicken.  I think I have found a way to save a lot of money!!  This was the best chicken I have ever had or fixed.  It was perfect the way it says to do it!

Its been awhile since I've made this so I don't remember the exact details. But I'm pretty sure I followed the recipe except for how long to cook it. I did it at the "norm" and it was okay. I'd probably make it again but wouldn't bother doing it overnight again. Didn't seem to add anything to it.

Yummy! I followed the recipe except I didn't have any white pepper or onion powder so I left those out.  I meant to prep the chicken the night before, but actually did it the morning of so it was only in the refrigerator about five hours before roasting.  I used a Reynolds oven bag and didn't even baste.  It was delicious and easy.  Thanks!
Fantastic recipe!  My friends and BF loved it!

Although I didn't roast the chicken (and yes, 250 degrees for 5 hours is very safe) the spices are very tasty.  I like to brine my poultry, so brined overnight, then seasoned and let set in the refrigerator overnight.  I chose to put the chicken on the outdoor rotisserie.  The smells wafting through the air were divine!  Very tasty end result.

This is simply the BEST Chicken ever! Fall of the bone tender and the taste is wonderful. The only thing I do different is add more cayenne pepper..just because I love my chicken with a little more heat. I've made this recipe several times already and making one right now. If there are any leftovers I make a chicken and rice casserole.  Thank you so much for sharing! :)
This is now my favorite rub! I cooked as the recipe directed and the chicken turned out dry.  I used this rub on a chicken and dropped it into a crockpot and it was fantastic.

So simple and so delicious!!! I did have to add a bit of liquid and it cooked for only 3 1/2 hours (there were 2 very small chickens).  I used chicken broth instead of water to give it even more flavor.  Rave reviews from the family!  Thanks!

For us I used garlic salt instead of plain salt, left out the cayenne, used about 4 T (if not more) of dried onions along with the other ingredients which I zapped in the food processor.  I also used a lime chopped up along with the onion which I stuffed inside the chicken.  Cooked on a rack basting often and it cooked up beautifully.  Great recipe, thank you.

I made this for my family last night. It was a huge success! I mixed a little olive oil w/ the spices to make a wet rub. I left in the fridge for 6 hours, and roasted as directed, but I used a Reynold's Cooking Bag. Juicy, moist chicken perfection! I forgot the cayenne, but it was still just as good. Will definitely make this again.

Oh my gosh this is good.  I made this for my family and we couldnt get enough.  I loved the seasoning blend and plan on using it often for all our chicken recipe.....grilling , frying, roasting.  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe with us....we loved it.

Amazing flavor, best chicken I ever made.  Cooking it slowly made all the difference.  From now on I will always cook my chicken nice and slow.  Thanks for a great recipe.  My family loved every morsel.
This was my first time roasting a chicken and it was wonderful, the flavor was all the way though .
While you were off Christmas shopping, I was here making your Sticky Chicken.  Too bad you missed the smiling faces of my family as the juices ran down their arms.

This chicken is wonderful! Made exactly as directed, my chicken wasn't very big so I was only able to fit 3/4 of a big onion inside. Basted three times, filled the house with a fantastic aroma that had us wanting to eat long before it was ready. I added about a 1/4 cup of water and three little pats of butter to the glass baking dish to help the basting juices along. Tasted great, fell off the bone. Can't wait to make broth out of bones and make soup! Oh! I marinated overnight in a Costco bread bag, I save them all the time because they come in handy for so many things, chicken bones for instance! Don't throw them away! Marvelous chicken, easy to do. Made me look like a star! I'll make this again, thanks for the recipe.
Family Favorite! We look making and eating this...i always use the left overs for chicken pot pie....Thanks for the recipe!!!
What great ideas!  Dry rub "marinade" ... slow cook w/o sauce ... so unique

I LOVE the seasonings on this chicken!  I had to use a different method to cook (crockpot with a liner) due to my schedule and I rubbed the chicken with butter (but you could use olive oil) and I added 2 tablespoons dried parsley and 1/2 tsp of turmeric to the seasonings because I wanted to try it.  The flavor of the chicken was so good.  I saved the drippings and skimmed the fat for soup broth later.  Thank you for a great chicken recipe.  I'll have to try the roasting method when I have more time and can be home with the oven on.

I did not read the recipe through and realize that it needed to marinate overnight until the day I was planning to cook it. So I just followed the recipe and skipped putting it in the fridge overnight. It was still delicious and the seasonings are versatile enough that I could incorporate the leftover chicken into many different recipes. I made some chicken salad and also a chicken noodle soup. The chicken literally fell off of the bone so easily I couldn't even pull the drumstick or wing off without everything falling open. Made it super easy to get every bit of chicken and no waste! Next time I will plan ahead and refrigerate overnight and I'm sure it will be even tastier. I will probably shorten the cooking time by 30 minutes because it was starting to dry out...but that is just an adjustment I need to make because of my oven and not a problem with the recipe.

I have always been afraid to cook chicken at such low temperature but decided to give it a try, 280 people can't be wrong!  I followed the recipe exactly and found the spices perfect.  My DH drove me crazy all afternoon asking when it would be done as the kitchen smelled wonderful.  I especially liked the taste and texture. Thanks for a great recipe.
Really good! I wrapped my chicken in a few layers of cling wrap instead of a trash bag. Juicy and tender.

I've made this recipe many times and it's always great. We recently bought 6 large (10 lbs ) chickens from local farmers and they were awful. Very tough and tasteless. Old birds I guess! I remembered this recipe and gave it a try. Worked like a charm : ) Saved the day. Thanks for this excellent recipe!!

Yum. Yum. YUM! Five star fabulousness! I was expecting a huge mess with all the "messy" reviews, but it wasn't so bad. I skipped the bag and seasoned my 6lb bird right in my 9x13 glass pan. I stuffed one quartered onion, 5 cloves of sliced garlic inside, 2 whole sprigs of fresh rosemary, covered it with plastic wrap, and stuck it in the fridge. When I was ready to roast it, all I had to do was take the plastic wrap off, and stick it right in the oven. I added a 1/2 cup white wine and 1/2 cup chicken broth and a few pats of butter. I sliced potatoes and added them the last four hours... they weren't quite done with one hour to go, so I raised the temp to 350. Everything was unbelievable PERFECT. Made gravy with the drippings, homemade rolls, green beans, and wild rice. The kids could hardly stop eating it, and my very picky hubby was impressed! I'm going to turn the leftovers into a yummy chicken and wild rice soup. Can't wait to try this method with a turkey!!!

True to the reviews, this was a fantastic recipe.  Seeing a five hour roasting time was a little intimidating, but honestly it turned out to be a really easy, low maintenance recipe.  The chicken was SO unbelievably moist.  I'm a huge fan of brining meats and have done so every Thanksgiving.  This dry rub brine was different in that the cooking method is slow roasted, resulting in a great meal! :)
Delicious moist tender chicken every time I make it.  My family adores this one!

i've tried this recipe at the cooking time and temperature given.  I've also tried this cooking it at 350 degrees.  Each time I've had excellent results.  I did reduce the salt to 2 teapsoons,  added a teaspoon of curry to the seasoings; and stuffed the cavity with lemon, onion, and garlic.  The chicken is moist and maintains its moisture and flavor the next day.

This recipe is amazing! The chicken just falls off the bone and it is so easy! I prepared it in my roasting pan, covered it in plastic wrap and put it in the fridge over night. I did use less cayenne pepper and it was still spicy, but not too much. I will definitely be making this again!

Really good rub. I cut the salt in half and only used a pinch of cayenne pepper, omitted the white pepper as there already was regular in it. Used it on 5 thighs and 5 drums (and there was still about a teaspoon left over.. I sprinkled mine on with one hand and rubbed with the other so that any left over wouldn't go to waste by becoming contaminated.) and it sat in the fridge for 8 hours. I didn't use the low cooking temp, I went 350 for hour and 20 minutes.  The result was a delicious end product. The cayenne still had a kick so I am glad I only went with the small amount. My Husband even mentioned using this on the next turkey we do.. and I think I have to agree that this would be another great use for it. Thanks for the great recipe! It is definitely a keeper.

WOWZA!  We just finished dinner, and this chicken was a HIT!  I made the spice rub exactly as the recipe stated, and the only change I made was to stuff the chicken with an onion and a lemon.  I let the chicken marinate in a poultry baking bag overnight, and pulled it out of the fridge about half an hour before I started to bake it.  I always bring meat to room temperature for even cooking.  I lined my baking dish with raw potatoes and carrots tossed in a little olive oil, salt, and black pepper to make a one dish meal.  I put the chicken on top of the veggies and cooked it as the recipe stated.   I let it rest (very important step) for about 10 minutes before carving.   There are 2 of us, and half of the chicken is now gone!  I loved the carrots that cooked with the chicken too: next time I might just add all carrots since they were really tasty.  DH said this was a keeper, and he really doesn't care one way or another about roasted chicken.  I can't wait to make a chicken sandwich tomorrow out of the leftovers!  Next time I think I am going to make 2 chickens, since I can already think of dozen of things to do with the leftovers.   Thank you for sharing a great recipe!  This is truly a keeper!!

Just plain delicious!  I may try Tony Chachere's Cajun Seasoning next time in place of the cayenne pepper and cut back on the salt a little bit as it is in the seasoning.  The chicken was tender, juicy and well worth the effort involved!

I cut up my chicken before preparing this recipe and cooked it for 4 hours instead of 5.  I cut up one onion and put it in the bottom of the pan.  It turned out beautiful and delicious.  I had to add some water as it was baking to make some more juice.  My whole family commented on how good this was so I'm sure I will be making again.  Thanks for posting.

This was my second attempt at cooking a whole chicken and I thought that buying a small 'young' chicken would cut down the cooking time. Boy was I wrong! But, this chicken was worth every minute of the 5 and 1/2 hours it took to be done. My chicken was just small enough to fit in an all-purpose Ziploc bag. I followed the recipe with the exception of loosely covering the chicken with foil from fear of it drying out. This was the most flavorful, MOIST chicken I've ever had!
great

I've been making this chicken for years. I found a similar recipe on another site way back when and loved it. I gave this recipe to my DD to make as her first meal for her in-laws. Even though she can't cook.....they loved her meal! :lol: Thanks C Chatwin for a winner. Made for Cookbook Tag.
Amazing chicken!!

I like to give credit to when due is the is actually the famous chef Paul Pruhomme's mother's recipe. I have been using this recipe for over 10 years and it is still by far my favorite for seasoning. Now the only thing that I do differently sometimes is us the cooking time of Ina Garten and use high heat first to get the chicken crispy and then drop it to finish cooking. Five hours does not yield a crispy skin, but deiivers on being the stickiest for sure. I also use the seasoning for fried chicken that is to die for.

Absolutely delicious!  My DH (who can be pretty picky) loves this chicken and we always pick it clean.  I have found however that there are never enough "pan drippings" to baste with and I add 1/2 cup to 1 cup chicken stock to the bottom of the pan to use for basting. I always leave out the cayanne as its too spicy for the kids. Also if i am short on time i will just throw the spices on top & stuff w/ onion and roast this at 425 for about 50-55 minutes & its still amazing!! I prep 3 ziplocs at a time of the spices so i am always ready. It's our favorite chicken and I've been making it for years now!

I was so surprised how well this chicken turned out. The chicken was cooked perfectly and was really fall-off-the-bone tender. We enjoyed the spice mixture, which made the chicken very flavorful and different from my regular roast chicken. Thank you for a great recipe!

This is by far the best roasted chicken I've ever tasted! I cheated a little and put the chicken in a Reynolds Oven Bag...that way it went from the fridge straight into the oven and the bag does the basting for you. My whole family loved it! The only bad thing was that there were no leftovers for lunch the next day :(  Thanks C Chatwin for a great recipe!
Very good and easy.

Poultry should never be cooked below 325 degrees. Yes the USDA may give you doneness temps but you are ignoring time and temp factors in cooking poultry.   5 hours at a low temp means danger when cooking chicken

Very Yummy!  I put the whole chicken in a 2 gallon food baggie, dumped in the spices, and shook the heck out of it until the whole chicken was coated, thus eliminating the messy rubbing process.  Everyone loved this, including my 9-year old son...he likes things a little spicy, so the cayenne wasn't an issue for us, but I can see how other children might find it a bit on the spicy side.  Thanks for a new staple recipe in our house!

Love this chicken! This is my picky daughter's favorite meal. I don't use the onions inside as it's just another ingredient and isn't necessary in my opinion. Everyone who's had this just raves. I make the seasonings up in bulk to have on hand. I use a couple of teaspoons of this seasoning each time. I cut the cayenne pepper in half and add more garlic (for our tastest), but it's good just as is. It works for other things as well such as drumsticks or leg quarters (which are sale quite often in my areas). Thanks so much C Chatwin!

I just made this and this is nothing special...the rub is good but not great i actually prefer my usual recipe...I guess for the non-cooker this is a start but REALLY nothing special! Sorry but I think it deserves a 3 only because it is fool proof for amateur cooks!

This is my son's favorite chicken.  He calls it Spicy chicken.  It does have a kick that's why I reduced the cayenne to a 1/2 teaspoon.  I serve it with rice and we love to spoon the juices over the rice.  I make this several times a year. Our family really enjoys it although its a bit spicy for me.

I caught this recipe while I was well on my way through my standard chicken/turkey prep which involves a day of soaking in a brine (water/salt/herbs/mirepoix). I also butterflied the chicken I was using - about a 4-5 pounder. After applying the rub and leaving it sit in the fridge til the next day (so now we're 2 days into the recipe) I stopped in at home for lunch and reluctantly started the 5-hour roasting process. Five hours later, not only we were eating the best chicken to come out of my oven, but the drippings made for the best gravy as well. Five hours!! Who-da thunk it!?

I love roast chicken and this is the best recipe.  The chicken is moist, flavorful and EASY!  This is the new "go to" recipe for my Sunday dinners.  The the leftovers make delicious chicken salad for lunches the next week.
I loved it, Quick and Easy. and good too.

I didn't marinate, and cooked for a shorter time at 325 degrees.  I also made a mistake and added chili powder (grabbed the wrong bottle when looking for paprika!).  I thoroughly enjoyed the seasoning.

This is so yummy! Cooked it at 400 degrees for 15 min then 300 degrees for 3 more hours for a 5 lb chicken.  I was out of thyme (punny but true) so I used rosemary, also no white pepper.  Otherwise the spice mix was followed and it was all around delicious.

Very good! I didn't bother with the bag; just covered the pan of chicken wi/ plastic wrap while marinating. We needed to eat earlier than I expected and the chicken was done nicely, at 4.25 hours baking time.<br/>**Made it again, but it's too hot for the oven! I put it in the crockpot, on high for 2 hours and low for 2 hours- WONDERFUL! Even the breast was moist!!

I have made this many times with the following observations: I no longer use all the spices--just white & black pepper and salt--because I think this allows the chicken flavor to shine through (and no butter, oil, or basting). Convection speeds up the cooking considerably--4 pounder in 3-3 1/2 hours; a 7 lb roaster would, of course, take longer. Dressing the cooked meat lightly with some melted butter or warm chicken stock makes a nice touch. I always use this recipe (rather than braising or simmering) when I need cooked chicken for other recipes. Cooked this way, the chicken is super easy to pick.

This recipe makes an unbelievably delicious chicken!  I've made this several times since I found the recipe and each time it's perfect.  I followed the advice ns from another reviewer to put the chicken and the rub into a big bag and smoosh it all up onto and into the chicken.  Works great and not a bit messy!  I'm making it again today and expect it to impress the guests as it always has...it's so beautiful and so delicious!  What's not to love?

I've been making this chicken for years now, forgot to review -- <br/>So juicy, tender and delicious! I don't use the trash-bag -- just set the chicken in a small roasting pan and cover it with plastic wrap for the overnight. I rarely have garlic or onion powder in the kitchen, so chop-fine fresh and make more of a 'paste'.  Also, I use vinyl food-handler gloves to keep the mess down when applying the rub.  Tomorrow's chicken will be served with garlic smashed potatoes and broccoli.

this is quite possibly the best chicken I've ever had! I set on 300 as I didnt have 5 hours in my day...(needed it before soccer) I went a little heavy on the cayenne but thanks so much for the recipe. I will make this again!!

This is fabulous!!! To all who work outside the home, you can actually put this one in the oven before you leave and it's perfect when you get home. I've left it in for much longer than the 5 hours and it's still super moist and delicous. Thank you for sharing this one C. It's my new favorite recipe!!!!
Delicious roast chicken. Perfectly seasoned, skin crisp, meat tender. Made exactly as directed, no changes. Thanks.

I just made this today and it was awesome! I cooked it at 425 for 20 minutes, then turned the temp down to 300 for 2 hours and 40 minutes for a 5 pound chicken. Stuffed with carrots, celery, apple, onions and garlic, and a little olive oil on top to help crisp the skin. It was delish!
This is my favorite roasted chicken.Made this 5 times.Every time great.Falls off bone and skin has a great flavor also.5 star for sure.
Thanks so much for this recipe! Its reallllly good. So good that I tacked this recipe onto my kitchen board! Delicious blend, whether I marinate in fridge or use right away. Thanks again :)

I've loved a version of this for over 20 years! You get tender, delicious, stick to your fingers chicken. I add a bit of brown sugar to offset the cayenne for my daughters. Throw in some potatoes the last couple hours with some butter and baste away. Making again tonight!

I found this recipe, but didn't have time to do the overnight marinading. So, I mixed all the spices, coated the chicken (5 lbs), and popped the bird into the oven at 250. I also added a cup of chicken broth to the bottom of the pan since the chicken had very little fat. I basted the chicken every 30 minutes as stated. I have to say, the chicken came out very moist and delicious. You might read some articles saying not to cook the chicken at such a low temperature because of bacteria growth. They are wrong!!! I smoke chickens on my pit at the same temperature. This recipe is an excellent way to roast chicken in the oven. It's a save recipe for sure.

Great recipe! I followed it as written except that I could only fit 1 1/2 onions in the cavity. Also, when I went to baste the bird after the 1st hour there was nothing to baste with. Like some of the other reviewers, I ended up adding a cup or more of chicken broth to the bottom of the pan to have something to baste with -- resulting in a tasty pan gravy. Thanks C Chatwin!
Cooking at 250 and opening the oven door every 30 min to baste probably significantly prolongs the cooking time since heat keeps being lost which is a bigger deal at low temperatures.
When do you add the vegetables to the pan?
will this work with a turkey??

This sounds absolutely delish! Cant wait to try! Anytime I bake chicken, whole or boneless breast, I use wax paper loosely over the top and tucked into the pan. The juices don't escape (super moist) and it's kind of self basting.

Confession time:  We were invited out for lunch on Saturday and my hostess told me "Bring a salad".  This was the salad I brought.  It was such a hit, I took all the credit myself!  But Kisha, I give you credit here, this salad is wonderful.  Another confession, I used frozen corn, had a bag in the freezer.  I just nuked it for a few minutes. I used mostly cider vinegar, but about 1 tablespoon was balsamic, which gave it such a lovely, sweet/tart taste.  I'm going to be making this again for sure, and will make sure to use fresh corn next time!  Thanks for posting this recipe!

This is great! I added a small cucumber diced and large tomato diced. It's even better the next day!

I was going to post a picture of this, but it disappeared too fast!  This is a great summer salad.  I was out of cider vinegar, so i used white balsamic, and it tunred out yummy! Next time I'll use cider vinegar.

I really enjoyed this salad!  Unfortunately, I was the only one in the family who did.  I will say that they are all VERY picky eaters though.

I found this salad to be very refreshing.  I am not a big vinegar person so when I make it again I will probably use only 1 1/2 Tbs.  Other than that it was WONDERFUL!!

Delicious.  I have tried so many things from Ina, just this week I made meatballs and spaghetti, beef bourgignon, rice pudding, all amazing.  This salad is perfect.  Follow the exact recipe.  I didn't have fresh basil so just used about 1 tablespoon of dried basil.  Better after it sits for awhile.  Great side dish.

Linda

I liked the idea of this salad very much and really wanted to like it. However, the cider vinegar, onion, and olive oil bittered the sweet corn and the basil was too overpowering. If I ever made it again, I would switch to a balsamic next time and decrease the amounts of onion and basil. I somewhat enjoyed the freshness of the flavor combinations, but by fiance didn't like it all. I give this recipe a 3 for creativity.
I made this salad yesterday it was delicious. I microwaved four ears of corn in the husk for 8 mins. And I also added a small can of sliced olives.

My sister made this salad and my Mom and I were all over her for the recipe after the first couple of bites :)  It is SO good. I think it is best when corn is very fresh and in peak season. It is fresh and delicious~ Thank you for posting :)

Light and flavorful.  I loved it.  I have not ever used fresh corn in a recipe so this was a first.  It was not as cumbersome as I thought it would be - so I am more likely to do it in the future.  I have a small pot of basil growing in the kitchen (highly recommend this - easy and delish!) so I just picked some leaves and added the finishing touch, just wonderful!  Thanks.

In a pinch, I tried this with frozen corn that I just thawed under a warm tap. My pantry was in such a state I was even out of cider vinegar and subbed red wine vinegar. I also added a dash of cumin for some extra depth of flavor but this was a wonderful dish even with the frozen corn. I will definitely be trying with fresh soon!

SO perfect! I couldn't believe it. It tasted sweet and green and lively.  To chiffonade (slice) your basil easily - roll up the leaves like a cigar.  I didn't have red onions, so I substituted finely chopped green onions.  I wanted to load a picture - but it was gone, baby, gone!

I can't even describe how happy my taste buds were when I ate this. Love, love, LOVE it! I omitted the onion cuz I don't like it. I also didn't even measure the vinegar or oil but used them sparingly, and used fresh corn that I grilled in foil - perfect! I had some super sweet orange cherry tomatoes from the farmer's market so I added those, along with some cubed mozarella that I had to use up. The flavors were so delicious that I can't even imagine using anything but fresh corn, fresh basil leaves, etc.  Heaven!
Two words summarize this dish: The bomb!
I steamed my corn and was very good but won't add as much basil.  Still good the next day for leftovers.
Good! Nice fresh side dish when summer grilling. Fresh corn made this dish very sweet. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Great salad.  I cut back on one ear of corn & substituted a cucumber to add color/texture.  My son thought it was a little sweet, so I may substitute rice wine vinegar for the cider vinegar next time.

These muffins were delicious. We loved them fresh made or frozen & thawed. It doesn't matter! I was a bit skeptical about using fresh, cut-up grapes in a muffin recipe, but they turned out great. Thanks for a different & tasty recipe.

Fantastic, moist and ohhhh so flavorful.  I was skeptical, too, about using grape pieces, thinking that it would make them mushy.  Not at all!  They came out perfect!  Thank you for the wonderful recipe.  The kitchen smelled like heaven! :)

My 3 yo kept asking for grape muffins so I googled it and got this recipe. He loved them! Thanks so much.

Very good muffin recipe. I froze batches of grapes in 1 1/2 cup portions for when I make more and I will be making more! I, too, used half whole wheat flour, half canola oil/melted butter and Splenda. A nice way to start the day. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

A very nice muffin. It came out just like the picture.  My children wouldn't touch the grapes that I put in their school lunches, so I used them in this recipe. This was fabulous!  When I saw this... I just had to try it!  Definitely a keeper!

Wow! Such  a great recipe, thank you!

These are some of the BEST muffins I have ever made or tasted.  They are so sweet, and moist!  They remind me of the Little Debbie muffins you can buy individually, but are so much healthier since you know what is in them and can make your own substitutions (splenda for sugar, etc).  THANK YOU!

Excellent muffin. I made this recipe with apples. I doubled it and used half whole wheat flour. I also added 1 TBS of cinnamon and a dash of clove. It's a very dense muffin, with an almost custard like flavor.
I will absolutely make these muffins again, maybe even with grapes.
Made this exactly as stated and they turned out wonderful! I will be making them again since I froze quite a few grapes when they went on sale. Thanks for giving me a recipe to use them.

These are really yummy and a great use for the grapes I bought that no one ate!  I followed the recipe exactly except I substituted 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce for the butter/margarine. These are good.  My sister gave me a bushel of concord grapes and freezing some of them was quick and easy...a great idea that I hadn't thought of. Liked this. Never knew you could freeze grapes. Next time would add a pinch of cinnamon for some spice.
They were great - crunchy on the outside and soft within; although I halved the sugar, they still came out very sweet. next time I would use even less sugar.

These are straight-up delicious. I found this recipe because I had a bag of green grapes that were just past ripeness. These looked so good, I tried them with what was on hand. I drained a can of sliced peaches and chopped course. Added a teaspoon of Pie Spice. They were wonderful.

Turned out very yummy!! The only thing I did different was I used 1 C pure coconut sugar. It lowers the carb count a great deal and less sweet then regular sugar. A lot better for us who are watching our blood sugar but want a real sweet.

Fabulous muffin . Easy to make and exactly the recipe I've been looking for such a long time .I froze some and they were still delicious. If I wanted to make a chocolate version of these how much would I add because I know adding cocoa powder can make some recipes dry

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this recipe! turned out amazing. I made 1.5x the recipe, used black grapes and baked in my jumbo muffin pans. Great muffin tops and wonderful taste. Grapes will never be wasted in our house again.

This was a wonderful coffee. Rich, strong and robust, with a deep dark flavor. The molasses sweetened the coffee perfectly. I loved it and will make this over and over again. Thanks for sharing this tasty recipe.

I never would have thought of adding molasses to my coffee.  What a nice change in place of traditional sweetners.  I agree with Sharon in that it definitely is a deep, dark flavor and I for one was glad to see the added cream.  Perfect.
Made for 123Hit~

Molasses brings something different and unusual to coffee -- rich, but with a bit of a bite. I'll use less cream next time since I'm not a fan of milky coffee. I thought as I was drinking it that this must be how coffee tasted to the pioneers, who rarely had the luxury of white sugar and used molasses for most of their sweetening needs.

Oh, my, this is excellent! Amazing how such a small amount of molasses really brings out an added richness in the coffee, without making it overly sweet. I used a little less cream than recipe called for, and it was still delicious!

I loved this and wish I had a piece of pumpkin pie to go with it, as suggested in the description :)  I really love the flavor of molasses so i might be tempted to add a bit more next time.  Made for Partying the Diabetic Way tag game.
I loved this simple to do coffee, the cream mellows out the molasses making a smooth tasting but robust blend. Thanks!
This was good for something different....I did not add the cream as I prefer my coffee black.

Perfect balance of molasses and cream! I used almond cream for dairy free. This was a lovely treat for an icy cold morning! Thanks for sharing :)
Made just for fun :D

What a lovely rendition that brings out the undertones and enhances the coffee perfectly. I add whipped cream I addition to the cream to give the photo more pizzazz. Made for Casual January 2013 Veggie tag.

I wasn't sure that I liked this much after my first couple sips. But it really grew on me. I imagine it would wonderful with a piece of pumpkin or pecan pie. Thanks for sharing this recipe, I'll be making it again.
I halved the recipe, and added a 1/2 teaspoon of sugar and topped it with some Reddi Wip. It was delish!
These were really great! I used mixed fruit preserve and omitted the glaze. DH and DS loved them too. Will be making them a lot. Thank you Angela! for this delightful cookie recipe ;) Fay

these delicious treats don't just taste grand - they are so pleasing on the eye too that they would be great for entertaining. i found them to resemble what we know to be pasties in SA, more than cookies - but  semantics are irrelevent when you are so high on a taste sensation. i really would recommend going the whole hog and making the glaze too if you make this - not only does it dress it up prettier but the berry preserve tinged with the almond flavor is irresistable. i had not even heard of kolaches before but i will be making this again with different filling - thanks for the opportunity to sample some czech cuisine, angela:)

I am so glad I decided on this recipe! It made a beautiful platter! I made half with Strawberry and Half with Cherry....both were divine!!! Everyone loved them and could not believe that I made them and didn't purchase them from a bakery! Thanks Angela!

I made these a couple of weekends ago as a trial before Christmas, everyone raved and raved about the taste not to mention the fact that they make for a beautiful presentation.  I am adding these to my "Must Make For Christmas" list.  Thank you for sharing such a delicious recipe!

These were beautiful not only in looks but taste as well.  Not too sweet and easy to make.  I used apricot preserves, didn't have strawberry at the time .Will definately try again with strawberry too.
Thanks for the recipe.

These were so good. I made them with strawberry preserves and cream cheese (4 oz. cream cheese, 2 Tbs. sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla, 1 egg mixed well) I didn't have almond extract so I used vanilla in the glaze. Superb, and professional looking. My son said he could eat a hundred of them! That won't be happening any time soon ;)

While these are just beautiful cookies the taste is more along the lines of a scone. On my second batch I doubled the vanilla and added 1 teaspoon of cinnamon to the flour mix and sprinkled sugar on them after the egg wash and they were much more along the lines of what I like. Good recipe for not to sweet cookies.

Delcious and well work the effort! I had alittle bit of trouble with the corners coming apart in the oven but on about my 3rd batch in the oven, I finally got them to close by pinching them together real tight! For the jam flavor, I used rhubarb cherry and it was to die for! This was a great addition to our xmas tray! Thanks for the recipe love4culinary!

This was fun for me! My Girl Scouts are learning about the Czech Republic for Thinking Day, so I needed a traditional Czech food that they (8 year olds) would be willing to taste.  I know they will like this one--the shape is fun and they look pretty.  Next time I make them, I will try harder to roll them thinner (as the recipe says) to get a lighter look.  Thanks for the easy to follow recipe that used simple ingredients I already had, and for the opportunity to "broaden our taste horizons"!

Having lived in the Czech Republic for 8 years, I was thrilled to have found a recipe for one of my favorites. One suggestion I have is to garnish the tops with finely slivered almonds after drizzling the glaze on, it enhances the almond extract in the glaze without being over powering and adds a more elegant presentation.

These are delicious!!I used strawberry jam.The flavour of the strawberries and the almond is perfect.I had trouble keeping the corners together once they were in the oven,even though they were pinched quite well.I had to take them out and use toothpicks to keep them together.That worked fine.These are more of a pasrty than a cookie but amazing no matter what you call them.
What an excellent kolache recipe!  I took the advice of Maggie and added slivered almonds on top of the glaze.  Beautiful and delicious!

I made some of these for the girls in the office and everyone just adored them!  I used strawberry preserves in some and raspberry in the others.  Next time I may try some dates and finely chopped nuts in them and see how they come out.  Sensational recipe to say the least!

i don't know what recipe everyone used but, i am a professional pastry chef and thought to try these cookies.  growing up in an all polish neighborhood i had tasted the best.  this dough was very difficult to work with.(it was extremely wet, pasty and stuck all over as soon as it warmed up).  i am surprised at the reviews because the taste was just not there.  possibly.  the cookies has a very doughy biscuit taste.  anyway very very disappointed.

This is essentially the same recipe that my family has used for generations and it is amazing. I think of them more like a small pastry than a cookie, so the dough is not as stiff as a cookie dough. We use a homade apricot filling and it is so delightful. Thanks so much for sharing this wonderful recipe, Love4Cullinary.

5 star all the way- My Mom used to stuff a shoulder of lamb with parsley and it was wonderful and so is this recipe. The garlic and lemon zest combined with the parsley give just enough added flavor to the lamb. Thanks Pianolady for a great recipe
This is a great easy way to make rack of lamb. The flavours of garlic & lemon & parsley blend so well. Thanks for posting :)

I never thought lamb could be so easy!  I made this for Easter dinner and really enjoyed it.  Thanks for posting!

Excellent!  I made 1 rack of lamb (already frenched) from Trader Joe's and followed the recipe exactly. It was easy to prepare and the lamb was cooked perfectly medium rare...the way we like it. Thanks for posting!

Delicious! It's amazing the subtle it is the taste of fennel when it's cooked. It is like if fennel has dual personalities. This is very similar to the first fennel dish I ever had. That's the one that convinced me that I really do like fennel. Otherwise made and thoroughly enjoyed as written. The whole family thanks you very much for posting.

Scrumptious!  Hubby is converted-YEAH! Lovely dish--and quality of parmesan has a lot to do with what you think. Easy too.  Served with a wonderful lime marinated chicken, rice, and coconut cream pie. I am a newcomer to fennel and this is a very tasty recipe!  I made half of the recipe and used a little less oil than called for. These green beans were very tasty, but my 11 yo green bean gourmet said they weren't quite as good as the ones at Cracker Barrel.  Based on that assessment, I assigned 4 stars.  I used 1/4 of pre-cooked bacon, but followed other recipe directions as given.  We'll have these again.  Thanks!
Very good green beans!!  This will really come in handy when cooking for a large group.  Thanks, mcb22902!!

I do have a specific order that I add ingredients and feel it helps dough blend easier. I whisked eggs with vanilla, then added sugars, whisked, and last the oil and whisked. I took rounded teaspoonfuls made a ball and flattened in palm of hand, then dipped one side in white sugar before putting on parchment paper on cookie sheet. Baked six minutes in gas oven. Turned out awesome!

I absolutely LOVED this recipe! I like my sugar cookies sweet, as does my family, so I decided on 1 cup of sugar rather than 3/4. I also wanted to experiment with the flavors, so I decided to use almond extract instead of vanilla, and they turned out delicious! Wonderful recipe!
loved these cookies they stayed fresh all week! i think i will be making these again very soon!!!
These came out delicious! I will continue to use it.
Very good we added 1 cup of sugar and 1 tbs vanilla 2 tbs of cocoa and 1/2 cup of coconut and 2 splashes of toasted marshmallow syrup delicious

Oh my goodness these cookies are skool amazing!! I literally signed up just so I could comment because I am so imoressed. My husban d loves when I make sugar cookies but these really are out of this world!!!

It’s came out absolutely great! This is the first time I made a sugar cookie and it came out. The texture was soft and delicious. I made it for my boyfriend and he asked me if I made it because it was so good. I never thought you could make cookies without milk and butter!! Thanks Genius kitchen, you are truly amazing.

If your going to use coconut oil =To substitute for vegetable oil, use the amount of oil called for in the recipe, melt the coconut oil and be sure that the other ingredients (eggs, liquids, etc.) are at room temperature or at least warm enough so that they do not cool the coconut oil enough to make it solidify

I decided to do half butter and half oil. I also went for the full cup of sugar, and added another teaspoon of vanilla. They turned out great. I noticed I need to let the cookie sheet cool down before cooking second batch. Made two whole baking sheets full. My child is thrilled.
I recommend that you just use butter. It works and tastes much much better,

Twice I've made these. I can't figure out what happened with the negative reviews. Perhaps they were expecting a different batter texture? I assumed since these were made with oil and were dropped in the pan instead of cut and shaped that the dough wasnt going to be very thick. And I was right. I even got nervous and was prepared to add extra flour if my first batch ended up running too much. But it was fine. Perfectly fine. I didn't tweak anything. I did cut the recipe in half the second time around. Still came out fine. I throw brown sugar on top before I bake them. I make them extra sweet. Oh. Guess I did tweak them. I added extra sugar. But you don't need to if you plan on frosting them.
GREAT AND EASY

Excellent Panzanella Salad.  My SIL actually liked this more than the rest of us.  It had a very strong basil taste, but he loved it.  I'll decrease the basil then next time for our taste.  SIL took the recipe and some of my fresh basil home with him.  Thanks

This was wonderful!   We had overnight guest last night and served this for dinner.    I also added some red bell pepper to the salad, other than that followed your recipe.   Unfortunately forgot all about taking a picture until it was too late . . . blame on the wine!  It was perfect, thanks for sharing.

This is just delicious. I didn't change a thing, just reduced the amount of servings and just a tip - it isn't light if you eat it all, LOL. I did use turkey bacon, next time I'll just use real bacon, the amount of fat it saves is minimal. This is a keeper.

By far the best Panzanella Salad I've ever made!  Super easy to make-flavor explosion in your mouth!  I was cleaning out my "need to review" pile and this one was on top with a huge star-it really is over the top good!

The first time I've made panzanella and I'll look no further for another recipe.  This was fabulous! I don't usually eat raw tomatoes, but the seasoning in this salad made them wonderful. I used a peppered bacon, so there was a bit of a spicy bite to the salad. Easy to make and just wonderful for a hot Florida evening! Thanks for posting - this is a keeper for me! Made for ZWT7 - ITALY and the HOT PINK LADIES!
Loved it!  Can't go wrong with balsamic vinegar, bacon, tomato & basil.  I will be making this fresh salad often.

What a great salad! One tip I would offer is get the best balsamic vinegar you can find to make the dressing. Chopped the onion so it was in smaller pieces,  DH doesnt care for a lot of onion, used turkey bacon, and an italian loaf of day old bread. I will be making this for us again! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Cruisin' Culinary Queens.
Simply splendid.  Used some sourdough that was getting stale.  I could up huge bowls of this!

I have made this salad from your recipes for several years. We love the flavors and the ease of making this recipe! I have had to stay away from this for the 2 summers as I have to really watch the carbs, today I decided to make it more carb friendly and it is STILL JUST as wonderful as before. I used only 1/3 of the bread your recipe called for and increase the tomatoes and lettuce. Color me happy, Happy, HAPPY! Thanks for a great recipe!

This is a great little breakfast.  DH had made some of those Grand canned biscuits the other night so I used the leftover biscuits instead of bread.  He took one look at me and shook his head yeah...even mentioned that we should give the recipe to his mom - that is a big complement.  Thanks for a tasty easy recipe that's such a treat!

These were absolutely delish! My kids asked me never to make plain toast again. I wasn't going to have any, but my will power disappeared quickly. I would never have thought to do this on my own. Thanks for posting a great 2 minute recipe, and thanks to jb4 for pimping it! :-)

Ok, I shouldn't be eating this as I am on a diet, but when I saw this recipe I knew I just had to try it.  Wow, it is fantastic.  I am eating it as I write and can't wait for everyone else to get up so I can make some for them.  Everyone should try this recipe.  The taste is wonderful and it is sooo easy! I got lazy and used canned frosting that I put in the microwave for 30 seconds.  It turned out fabulous. Thanks for a recipe I know will be a staple in my kitchen. I will make this often! (diet or not!)

I will try this again since the stars never showed up the first time.  My son had 10 pieces himself.  It is delicious and deserves so many more stars.  Talk about saving time without all that work.  It tastes so much like cinnamon rolls. These will be made in my house alot.  With school starting soon, it will be a great addition to breakfast!!!!!
This is too good to be called toast.  Its so simple I cannot wait to make it for school breakfasts.  My son could not stop eating it.  Its delicious eaten warm.
This was so easy to make and yummy to eat!  The icing really adds such flavor to this.  It was a hit in our house, thanks for posting.
This was a very classy tasting toast. It is not overly sweet, making the mellowed flavor of the cinnamon stand out! It is very good. Even my 3 yo boy was asking for more!! Thanks for posting!

I made this using whole wheat raisin bread and thought it was fabulous.  Very quick and easy, but great tasting.  It was a great midnight snack for me, but is easy enough for even busy mornings.  Thanks for posting!

I just made this for breakfast for my boys and their two friends who slept over last night!  What a hit!  Simple, easy and good.  Also great because I realized that I was out of pancake syrup and milk and needed something quick and good to feed those eating machines!  Thank you for posting - perfect sleepover breakfast!
The taste was very close to a cinnamon bun/roll. Sinfully good :)

I have done this for years.  My step mother thought I was crazy when I handed her a piece...until she tasted it.
Quick easy and yummy.

Oh, this was delicious, my kids were amazed and I will be making this again, the right way! The second time around, I messed it up trying to shorten the time by melting the butter and cinnamon together, then dipping the bread in it (like french toast). This was NOT a very good idea.
This was great made this for breakfast with some cut up fruit> It was like eating a cinnamon bun YUM, YUM
Ummmm! I just had a couple pcs. of these for breakfast. Wow....very easy and very  tasty I used 12 grain bread and it turned out great! Thanks Riff!
Take a simple slice of bread and turn it into a breakfast pastry!  Great for last minute sleepovers when you need something to serve the kids' company.  Love this recipe!!!

Wow -- hard to believe that something so simple could taste so much like cinnamon rolls!  This was delicious -- as well as quick and easy!  You couldn't ask for a better combination.  I had to thin the glaze down a little (I added a little milk instead of more water), but that is the only change I made.  Thanks for this great recipe for a quick breakfast!!  Dianne

Today is a cold and icy "No School" Day.  The kids were really dissapointed that there is no school so I made this to ease the burden a bit *grin*.  They loved it.  I used light whole wheat bread and spray butter.  Of course, they liked the icing the best!  Very fast and yummy.  Thanks.

OMG!! These are soooo goood!!! Very simple to make, how could ya know something simple would be to die for???? The kids are gonna love these, that is if I don't eat them before I can serve them up. Thanks Riff!!!

I thought I died when i tasted these were fantastic.
I used whole wheat toast, I would really like to try this on english muffins or crumpets. Thanks so much for a dream breakfast Riff.
Yum!  This was very easy and very tasty.  Thanks for sharing!
All of the flavor of a cinnamon roll with none of the work. Wonderful quick breakfast or snack idea. The kids loved it! Thanks, riffraff!

Thank you, Thank you, Thank you for such an easy recipe that finally got my super picky 3 year old to eat breakfast again. I even made this on whole wheat bread and cut it into a circle with a cookie cutter and told her it was a "cinnamon roll".  She ate every bit (which is very rare) and asked for more. Thank you for a simple, kid pleasing idea!
