Therr is plenty of room to customize this recipe with different flavoring options. I am a sauce person so I love it with BBQ sauce. Extra onion? Garlic? Cumin? Experiment to suit yourself.
I add some dry beef bouillon. It's delicious!

I'm a vegetarian and hubs is not. He lives this recipe! I use this recipe as my go to meatloaf every time! Tonight I made meatballs! I added a bit of pic-a-peppa sauce and some smoked paprika to the mix and then baked them in a mini muffin tin. They took about 40 minutes give or take. Yum!

The best Recipe for a veggie loaf !! I add a little salt and pepper and garlic powder to mine as well. Topped off with Ketchup and Parmigiano cheese. Even makes a great cold meatloaf sandwich for the next day :-)
I have made this since I was a teenager. I always have used George Washington broth in it in place of the soup mix.

This is soooooo good! Tastes and smells like real meatloaf. My husband and kids, who are not vegetarian, LOVE this. I was very skeptical when I first made it because the ingredients sound too funky and put together I couldn’t picture what it would be like, but it is delicious!! The walnuts give it a nice texture. I’ve tweaked it by adding fresh parsley and it comes out great too. You don’t need it but it does add freshness. It’s def a family fave!!

I have been searching for a good vegetarian "meatloaf" for a while now. I have found a few good ones. The ingredients in this one sounded so weird that I had to try it. This is definitely the BEST recipe I've ever found for veggie meat loaf. It's also full of protein. The kiddo ate it and never knew it wasn't ground beef. Thanks for sharing this! We loved it and will most definitely make it again and again.

As I'm (forcibly) gaining experience with vegetarianism, I mixed well this odd combo of ingredients with bitter, fearful tears. To my surprise...voilia! A decent meatless end product for my grass-eater (a term of endearment). What veg dish will I make next? Perhaps a leafloaf? ;-)
Easy and refreshing with the lemon. I used roasted garlic in place of fresh, used home grown broccoli. Thanks for posting this quick & easy recipe.

A delicious, simple and quick microwave recipe for those all too frequent occasions when you don’t have a lot of time, and want something tastier than steamed vegetables.  I used fresh garlic and omitted the pepper flakes (personal preference), and added a small sprinkling of cumin which worked well.  Just loved the lemony flavour too.  Thanks for a really fabulous recipe, which I know I’ll be making often.
Great Flavor and super easy! Thanks for a quick and healthy side dish!!!
This is a nice combination of flavors and easy to make.  This is a keeper.
Fast, easy & 'better than I asked for' according to dd.  Thanks!

My favorite way to fix a quick and easy veggie side dish, in the microwave!  Used less than 1 tablespoon olive oil, as posted garlic powder and red pepper flakes.  Was much better than my usual sprinkling of parmesan cheese!  Thanks SOOO much Hope, this will become my new standard!

This is a great way to fix broccoli.  I used fresh broccoli crowns which were separated into flowerets, rinsed and put in a microwave safe dish.  I did not add the water and the garlic was thinly sliced and cooked along with the broccoli.  I reduced the oil to 1 tablespoon, lightly sprinkled the dish with salt and used 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.  Something I know I will do again.

This was a very good broccoli dish. I really liked the flavor of the sauce. I added red pepper flakes and fresh garlic. Will make again.

Thanks mama's kitchen

Bullwinkle.

This was a superb way to cook broccoli.  So easy, yet delicious.  I made this for a dinner party and it was a huge hit with everyone.  I used fresh broccoli, and the garlic powder, but omitted the red pepper flakes for certain guests.  Definitely one I'll be making again.  Thanks for posting.
Great recipe for fast and tasty broccoli. Omitted the pepper flake, but kept everything else the same. Came out perfectly! Thanks!
This was wonderful!! We really enjoyed the combination of flavors!!!  Thanks for another winner!!!
This was so quick and delicious!  I opted to use fresh garlic, rather than the powdered, and I omitted the red pepper flakes. Loved the lemony flavor combined with the garlic.    Thanks so much!!

Excellent!  Delicious, simple and flavorful!  What else could you want?  Sure beats the usual "broccoli in butter" that I've made for my kids for years!  Definite keeper -- so easy to make, yet so impressive!  Thanks for sharing!  :)
Very, very nice! I used fresh broccoli and fresh garlic and although I thought the garlic might be a bit overpowering, it turned out great. Thanks for a great recipe that revs up boring broccoli!
Very good and very easy.  I, like the reviewer below, used fresh broccoli and it was great.  I didn't use the red pepper flakes.  We eat A LOT of broccoli and this was a nice change of pace.

I hate broccoli, and so am desperate to find ways to make it palatable (because of health concerns).  This was WONDERFUL.  We used 6 garlic cloves, which was just fine.  Next time I'll cut the olive oil and salt in half, just to make it a little healthier -- but the lemon/garlic combination was unbeatable.
I used fresh broccoli and it worked fine.  I always enjoy the mix of garlic and lemon.  Thanks for posting a keeper for us.
Wonderfully tasty way to get broccoli into a recalcitrant husband or children.  I used half broc, half cauliflower.  It was fantastic.
Very good dish. Will cut red pepper down next time and add chopped walnuts.

I made this as a side dish with dinner last night and loved it!  I used a bag of broccoli and cauliflower, but did everything else per the directions.  Next time I think I will cut back on the red pepper flakes just a little bit because it was pretty spicy.  I will be making this often.  Thanks for posting!
I love lemon juice on veggies and this was no exception. YUM! So easy to half this recipe. And thats exactly what I did. Delicious dinner for 1;) Thanks Mama!

This was a great change from plain steamed broccoli.  I used only 1 tbsp of olive oil since we are used to it without any toppings.  Also I left off the red pepper flakes because of the kids, however I am sure my husband would have liked it even more with them.  I enjoy pairing this with lemony fish dishes such as Recipe #169764. Thank you!

Yes! This is a wonderful, healthy, easy and flavorful way to make broccoli! I made it just as stated but increased the lemon juice and used fresh broccoli. I served it with recipe#88333 and recipe#168890 for a delicious lemony meal. Thanks for this keeper recipe!
Loved this....I halved the garlic powder red pepper flakes and salt and sprinkled with parmesan cheese to serve.

Fast easy and we couldnt keep from picking at it before dinner. My only worry was the salt seems to be too much. I only used 1/2 t. and it was a tad too much even with that adjustment. Yummy though, better then plain ole broccoli with butter!
I wish I could give this 10 stars!! I'm 6 months pregnant...and I want to eat this broccoli every day! Fresh garlic and fresh lemon juice is definitely the way to go!
Wonderful! Thanks so much for posting.

I tried the recipe last night, and it was delicious! I did however add baby carrots to the mix and it came out wonderfully. The lemon and garlic pair very nicely with the crisp carrots and broccoli and the pepper flakes give it just a little bite. All in all the dish comes together nicely and simply. 5 stars for easy preparation and wonderful flavor. I will definetly use this recipe again!
My husband thought there was too much lemon, but I loved it!!

I cooked fresh then added the ingredients. I quickly wrote down the ingredients & couldn't remember if it was fresh garlic or powder that I wrote my measurement for so I went a lot less to be safe next time I will use what is called for. I do think the lemon juice over powered it so I would use less lemon juice next time. My husband even ate some & he is not a fan of cooked broccoli. Thanks!
I thought this recipe was absolutely amazing! Very quick and easy, and very worthy of 5 stars. It will become a regular side dish at my house. Thanks!!
This was a yummy dish, very strong flavor, I'd definately make it again :)

This is a GREAT alternative to adding cheese to your broccoli. Much healthier and much tastier! If you are intending on using fresh broccoli, I suggest using a minimum of two heads - that, or cut the other ingredients in half. I made the mistake of using only one head, and it was a bit strong :)
We loved this take on broccoli!  I made just as the recipe says, using the fresh minced garlic.  Next time I'll probably just steam the broccoli on the stove top (just as easy).  Thanks!

I have been looking for some new ways to make veggies. My family loves broccoli so I thought I would give this a try. Unfortunately, this didn't work for my family. We thought the flavor was too strong, it really overwhelmed the dish. I think I will try it again and cut the sauce in half.

This is a fantastic simple recipe.  I drained the cooked broccoli then just added the other ingredients to it, unintentionally leaving out the olive oil and I still thought it was wonderful.  I was just cooking for myself so I cut the recipe down for one and was very disappointed when it was gone.  Generally I leave broccoli on my plate.  Not this time.  Thanks for the recipe.

Outstanding! I used fresh broccoli and minced garlic. I steamed the broccoli cuz the microwave was in use for my main dish. This was so easy to prepare. Great flavor. We didn't find it over powering at all. I also cut the recipe down to serve 2. Worked great. This dish looks wonderful on the plate. Thanks mama's kitchen for posting.

Aug06: We loved this... we didn't use the pepper flakes (kids) but it was so great. I have to admit I was a little hesitant about the frozen part, but it was perfect!!

Jan08: Just wanted to update this. We make this every other month or so. It's quickly become a family favorite. We recently added some dried lemon rind to it and it zips it up pretty good (we really really love lemon!) Thanks for a family favorite!
Very easy, but I didn't care for the flavour. Too sour for me.
I omitted the red pepper flakes, placed all the ingredients in a microwave steamer bag and microwaved for 6 minutes. Served this with recipe#40832 and recipe#70173

This was too salty and lemony for us BUT I think I would sprinkle lemon juice and some salt and garlic powder over some microwaved steamed broccoli because I liked it but it was too tart and salty for us.

Delicious flavored broccoli! Tasted so fresh and flavorful, and it was so quick and easy to make! I steamed it in a microwave steaming container (basically a bowl and lid with slits in the top for air to get through). For the last minute I threw in the fresh garlic to make sure it would cook well and it did. We used a sprinkle of cayenne pepper instead of red pepper flakes.  My family will be eating this broccoli again! Made for ZWT 4 Hot & Steamy challenge.

I thought this was very good and flavorful. It was light and refreshing. I think it would go very well with a chow mien dish or lemon chicken. I wouldn't recommend it with a heavier soy sauce or sweet flavored meat such as adobo or kung pao chicken. I didn't use the crushed red pepper and used fresh garlic, letting it sit about 4 minutes with the cover on to cook it a bit. Delicious!

Perfect in every respect!  I used a microwaver steamer bag, added the broccoli, and microwaved.  Skipped the oil and salt, but did add the lemon juice and red pepper flakes. Easy, healthy, and I always have these ingredients on hand.  Thanks for sharing mama's kitchen.  Made for ZWT4 the Flying Dutchess' team.
Great and easy way to make broccoli.  Much tastier than the usual steamed broccoli.  Thanks for another great recipe.  Made for ZWT4.

Excellent lemony recipe;always on the lookout for a diiferent way to serve broccoli.I did use fresh broccoli;thanks for sharing.
I am reviewing this again. I used fresh broccoli and real lemon juice; it makes it better.
I made this for WT4.
Rita

I love brocoli and this was a wonderful way to make it. This time I used frozen broccoli, lemon juice from the bottle and did add the a pinch of red pepper flakes. The lemon flavor is so nice and fresh along with the garlic and bit of zip from the red pepper flakes. Perfect for summer, light and even good cold. Made and reviewed for ZWT 4.

Wow! A great way to serve broccoli. DH doesn't like broccoli and liked this one alot. I made as directed, using fresh broccoli, however I probably got a little carried away with the red pepper flakes. I mixed up the 'other' ingredients ahead of time, and didn't stop to think that the oil would absorb some of the flavor of the pepper flakes, lol. Very easy and very good. Thanks mama's kitchen for yet one more keeper! Made for ZWT4 Family Picks.

This broccoli was stellar!  It had a great lemony zip to it.  I think that red pepper flakes are a definite must.  However, one teaspoon of salt ended up being a bit much for me, even though I usually like salty foods.  Next time I will only go with half a teaspoon.  The broccoli was still excellent though, and it was so easy to cook with the microwave method.  Thanks for the yummy recipe!

Made this tonight and was shocked at how tasty it was given that it was cooked in the microwave!!  I increased the garlic (I'm a garlic nut!) and used fresh lemon juice.  I also increased the crushed red pepper in this and thought it was really great!  Will make this again when I'm in a pinch for time and want a delicious veggie!  Thanks for posting!
This was VERY tasty!! THANKS VERY MUCH.

DH loved this dish.  I used fresh garlic.  I used fresh broccoli and cooked it 1 minute more.  I don't really like broccoli that's why DH had it all for himself LOL  Thanks Mama.  Made for I recommend tag game

Awesome! Delicious, fast, and easy clean up also a great way to make sure it doesn't get over cooked. I used fresh broccoli and followed your directions. Thanks! I'll use this method instead of the steamer.
Delicious and easy! I used fresh broccoli and garlic. I loved the addition of red pepper flakes. I'll definately be making this one again. Thanks!
Super recipe! Loved the ease of prep and cooking method and had wonderful flavor. I used fresh broccoli as I don't really care for frozen. :)
Nice recipe.  I made this to go along with lemon rice and grilled fish, and it complimented it all very nicely.  So simple and yet so tasty, thanks for posting.

Delicious! Took PaulaG's suggestion and cooked the garlic along with the broccoli (I never add water when cooking broccoli in the microwave), then tossed with 1 T olive oil and 1 T fresh lemon juice. Sprinkled with Kosher salt. Will definitely try with red pepper next time. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This was good, plain, and very simple to prepare. Great to make when you're out of fresh vegetables and in need of something green on the plate. My only issue was that the garlic never lost the raw flavor. Next time I will cook along with the broccoli. Paired this side with grilled salmon and herbed rice. Thanks for posting.

I really enjoyed this.  I halved the amount of lemon juice, just as a personal preference.  I didn't add salt, instead opting for a splash of soy sauce, since we were pairing this with an Asian-themed dinner.  I tried it before adding the soy sauce, though, and it was really good that way as well.  This is a quick and simple side dish that really would complement many different foods.

I made this tonight for my Passover seder. Left out th salt and red peepr flakes. I used garlic powder. It was very good, but next time I will cut back on the lemon juice as it was a tad too tart for my taste.

I made this delicious broccoli side dish as part of my Easter spread, and what a crowd pleaser!  I loved the zip of the lemon juice and would even add a bit more next time.  It doesn't get much easier than this and the broccoli was just perfect.  This is a keeper for sure!  It accompanied my chicken francese just perfectly.  Thanks so much for posting!

Amazing! I am on a crazy detox and since I discovered this recipe (last week), I have made this recipe 6 times. This is one I will make even after the detox is over. It is so easy and everyone seems to love it!

I skipped adding the water since our frozen broccoli seems to have enough moisture in it to steam properly.  I will also have to play with the proportions to get them right for just the two of us.  It was really tasty, though, and we gobbled a bunch down, while D  suggested we could try it on the stovetop as well.
5 stars for ease of preparation, but I thought it was too salty and also a bit too tart from the lemon juice, so I can't give it a full 5 stars.

Absolutely perfect broccoli!  I've made this about 3 times now for family and for company - everyone loves it!  Only problem is, there are never any leftovers!!  I always use the garlic powder for a lighter taste and it's very easy to change up the flavors by changing up the spices.  I do go a little lighter on the lemon juice just because my son likes a little less lemon flavor.  Great recipe - thanks so much for posting :-D
Easy and good. I used steam in bag broccoli from the freezer, cuz it's what I had on hand. Can't wait to try this with fresh broccoli!
Easy and simple recipe. I didn't use the oil.
Great recipe! I will make this again for sure. All I had was frozen broccoli pieces (chopped) they worked just fine. Used the garlic powder just to be lazy. Perfect!

This was really very good, I have been dealing with lots of morning sickness and not able to even look at broccoli....but I am starting to feel better and wanted to try eating it again. This is a keeper, thanks! (I did use only half of the olive oil as it seemed to be too much.

The DH couldn't stop raving about this, so even if I didn't like it (which I did), I'd still have given it 5 stars!  All supper he kept saying, "Boy, this is better than just plain ol' broccoli with butter and S&P!!!!"  I used butter instead of olive oil, but other than that made as directed.  Thanks for a GREAT side!

I thought this was super!  Hubby only thought it ok (didn't like the garlic), but I'm going to make this again and again.  I was going to substitute the olive oil for butter, but decided not to, and am glad I didn't.  You know how when you try something and immediately you're like WOW!!! - that's how I felt.

Another one of Mama's fantastic recipes that I served for Thanksgiving. I needed a vegetable recipe that wasn't baked or done stove-top as everthing was used up on those devices, so this recipe fit the bill. Not only was it easy, it was also SO good that we will have this often!
Surprising how tasty this basic recipe is. Will use for endless garden broccoli- also was a nice balance for the Christmas dinner table- something simple and green.

This is a great quick way to fix your veggies. Like PaulaG, I did not use the water. I also did not measure, just drizzled and sprinkled, so much less than the recipe calls for, except the lemon. Two of us easily ate the whole thing with dinner.

I use this recipe constantly! It's so easy, my husband and I both love it, and it tastes great. I slightly reduce the amount of salt and garlic powder, and use a little less cayenne pepper instead of the red pepper flakes - we like it spicy!
Just tried this tonight for supper...it was great and will be a regular addition to my meals...simple, fast and excellent. Thank you!!

I used a microwave cooking bag to make the brocolli, so I skipped the 1/4 cup of water, but otherwise made as stated w/ fresh lemon juice and garlic cloves.  Skipped the red pepper b/c of the kiddos and used about 1/2 tsp of salt, which was plenty for us.  A great way to dress up brocolli when you don't have time to fuss in the kitchen.  Even Mr. Picky ate his portion, which is high praise indeed.  Made for ZWT6--Whine and Cheese.
Very fast and easy - on the table in no time.  Don't know why this recipe is in the Asian cookbook as it's more Med in flavour and inspiration, but we ate it up all the same. ;-)  Thanks.
I love quick and easy recipes for Friday nights and this sure fit the bill. I liked the lemon garlic flavor. I used the red pepper flakes and it gave it a little punch. Made for ZWT6.

We thought this was a lovely side dish and a nice change of pace..  I will reduce the lemon by half next time, as it was too tart for us.  I used only 1/4 tsp of salt and skipped the red pepper flakes. Thx Mama!

I've never put olive oil on broccoli and with the lemon, garlic and spices it's a great combination. I was making this for one so didn't use exact measurements, I use fresh broccoli, cutting the stem section into coins along with the florets. After steaming I drizzled on a little olive oil, Squeezed the lemon over it and sprinkled on the spice using garlic granules, Kosher salt and a pinch of red pepper. I can't wait for my DH to try this! Thanks Mama another great recipe! Made for the ZWT 6 Asian Forum Diabetic Menu Challenge as part of Menu #39537, by one of the Unrulies Under the Influence

We loved this broccoli.  It was a delicious change of pace.  I was afraid in might be a bit too tart for us, so I used only 2 tsp. of lemon juice and since children were eating, I halved the red pepper flakes.  I chose to use the garlic powder over the garlic cloves this time around; and there will be another time around I assure you.  Made for ZWT 6 - Asia

Great tasting broccoli side here, & easy to prepare, too! I did use the fresh stuff! And the lemon juice, garlic & red pepper flakes = A great seasoning combo, always! Will be making this one again! [Made & reviewed during ZWT6 for Family Picks]

I used frozen broccoli and didn't add any water (frozen vegetables usually don't need any when microwaving).  I also subbed a little smoked paprika for the red pepper flakes.  A really nice way to jazz up a simple veggie.  Thanks for posting!  Made for ZWT6 Family Picks.

This was delicious and a nice change (and much healthier) from the normal cheese, butter, etc.  I used loads of fresh garlic and lemons juice and it was simple yet amazing.  A keeper for sure -- thanks!

Finally, I found the restaurant-quality broccoli seasoning I've been searching for with this recipe!  Since I didn't have fresh garlic or red pepper flakes on hand, I substituted 1 1/2 teaspoon Lowry's Garlic Salt (coarse ground with parsley) and 1/2 teaspoon chili powder.  Even with the substitutions, the flavor was wonderful!
This was amazing.  What an easy way to prepare broccoli, and much better than something that is so high in fat.
I'm not going to rate this dish because DH and I thought it was bad and very bitter, so I'm wondering if the broccoli was bad. Not sure if it was that or the lemon.
This was great and so much healthier than some of my casseroles.  I loved that it was in the microwave for just a few minutes so it was still nice and green.
Great and Easy!  I don't love broccoli.  We are trying to eat healthier foods and I don't love to cook.  So, this is perfect.  It is flavorful and so easy to make.  My husband liked it to.  Thanks!
Very nice way to liven up broccoli! I used frozen broccoli, fresh lemon juice and left out the pepper flakes. Next time I'll use fresh broccoli and include the pepper. Made for Best of 2010 Tag Game.

Excellent way to fix broccoli. I used fresh broccoli and cooked it in my steamer (rice cooker).  I did not add any salt or red pepper flakes, but I did let the mixture sit while the broccoli was steaming.  The garlic flavor really came through and made other seasoning unnecessary (for me).  My kids weren't overly impressed, but my husband and I both enjoyed it very much!
Delicious! Even my picky 13 year old ate it!
Quick and easy... loved the garlic flavors. Made for My review tag; Dreamer in Ontario.
This will become our newest fav broc recipe. Quick and tasty!!
Well this was fast and easy! I will use this recipe for those rushed dinner nights (with sports nights, that happens a lot!). I used the garlic powder. Thanks!

I think this has just the right amount of lemon to garlic and it is so easy. I used fresh broccoli and left out the red pepper flakes. I loved the ability to use fresh garlic and not get the raw garlic taste.

I used frozen broccoli, because the fresh at my store was all wilted and limp.  I'm afraid I can't recommend this using frozen broccoli.....can't say anything about using fresh!  I followed the recipe exactly, and this just turned out sort of blah and mushy....sorry so much!  I'll try it with fresh and hopefully redo my review.  Hate to leave a bad review!
Wonderful! The only changes we made were to add baby carrots to the broccoli...and lemon peel to the olive oil mixture.
Another 5 star rating! It was very easy and very flavorful.  Thanks!
I didn't care for this.  I like my food served HOT (as in temperature) and it seemed as though this got cool really quick,and besides that, the flavor was just OK 4 me.  I might make again?

What a nice, simple way to enjoy broccoli!  I used fresh broccoli, garlic infused olive oil, a bit of garlic powder, and bottled lemon juice.  So easy, and a nice change from the everyday broccoli and butter.  The pepper flakes gave it a nice kick.  Thanks for posting a great weeknight side!
This was very bland, I thought I added some butter and it still didn't liven it up any....

This is NOT HEALTHY at all. Microwaving vegetables completely defeats the purpose of having vegetables. It takes all of the nutrients out. You may ass well just eat garlic and lemon by itself, because the broccoli loses all nutritional value.
Super easy, fast and full of flavor! Served it with barbequed chicken and brown rice. Perfect weeknight dinner. Made for Healthy Choices tag.

We only used about half of the mixture on the broccoli, and it was really all it needed. Personally I loved it, but other members of my family said it was too salty. I didn't add the red pepper flakes in the mix, but I sprinkled them on afterward, which was great. We used garlic powder. Very simple recipe!

I made this recipe almost exactly as specified and it got rave reviews from 3 broccoli HATERS! I did used minced garlic from a jar rather than either powder or mincing my own. I chose to use the optional red pepper flakes and I highly recommend them. This had SO much flavor and actually made me *want* to eat the broccoli (I'd bought it to be healthy, I honestly think that plain broccoli tastes like lawn clippings). It was so good I made it again the very next night but with only 1 tbsp of olive oil and a bit more lemon juice. Result was the same...delicious. Overall I suggest only 1 tbsp of oil and adding the red pepper flakes.
My husband really liked this and even commented about how good it was.  He ate a second helping. From my perspective it was tasty and super easy.
Really easy recipe!  The red pepper flakes really make the lemon/garlic mixture pop, so I wouldn't neglect them.  I'm not a big fan of spicy but they added the perfect amount of flavor.
So good!  So easy!  Do not skip the red pepper flakes.  Thank you for posting.
Loved how easy this was to make.........I did half the red pepper flakes because I'm a sissy lol......but the whole hive loved it!  Thaniks..........part of the rotation from now on!

We loved this. I did not change ingredients, only technique. Cooked the frozen broccoli in the microwave for six minutes; while it cooked I chopped the heated the evoo in a frying pan and added chopped garlic. When the microwave was done I added the broccoli to the oil and garlic with the red pepper flakes.  I squeezed fresh lemon juice into the broccoli dish and tossed the hot sauteed mixture in it. The flavors were perfect together!

This is good.  Very bright flavour and I like the peppers in it.  The only concern I have is that even tender crisp broccoli doesn't "mix" well with a tiny amount of liquid carrying salt and dried peppers and garlic.  I found it hard to get the broccoli evenly coated.  But maybe that will come with practice.  I will definitely make it again.
Made this exactly as directed. It was delicious! Bright flavor. Will always make broccoli like this now.

I have made this several times and I could eat the whole batch by myself. We lost our recipe file box in the flooding after Hurricane Harvey and this is one of the recipes that was a must find to replace!
I loved this dish, no garlic added added butter instead of olive oil i made it as a side for dinner and oh my delicious. It was so good i had to have a bowl for lunch..
This is a great cake that comes out perfect everytime I make it. My family loves this one:)

Scrumpdidleeumptious....  I followed the recipe exactly including the pineapple cake.  Had it for a desert at my oriental flavored dinner party.   Everyone was so full they asked for a small piece... BUT..  they all went back and got a bigger piece..  The best part was that it came out looking just like the picture..  great recipe Nanita... thanks.
Very moist.  Next time I will use the pineapple cake mix.  The yellow mix was good but I bet the pineapple would put the extra zing in this cake.
This was dessert at our pig out Mother's Day brunch. I love pineapplle, bundt cakes and baking with doctored cake mix recipes.  Rich and yummy. Everyone loved it, not a crumb was left over. Sigh

This is my new all time favorite for Pineapple Upside Down cakes!  I made it this weekend for a family get together.  It makes a beautiful presentation and tastes even better than it looks!  Oh, I also added 4 T. of butter in the bottom of the bundt pan rather than 2.  It covered the whole round bottom of the pan better and made it more moist.  YUM!!!

Wow.. not only easy, but delicious!  I used golden cake mix and used a cup of the pineapple juice and only a quarter of a cup of water.  The cake was so moist and tasty!  This is definitely a keeper and I will be making it again.  Thanks for sharing.

Nurse Di-- I would give this more than 5 stars if I could. Have mercy. Did not make any alterations. Adding the small amount of bacon drippings to the oil is the secret. Gave a slightly smoky flavor that we all liked. Also the cayenne was a nice addition. We really enjoyed this.

I got a cast-iron Dutch oven as a wedding present. I have been seasoning it to get ready to cook something in. This is what I chose to cook to initiate it. This turned out even better than I had hoped. The batter fried up crisp and the okra was tender on the inside. I really like the combination of flour and corn meal in the batter. The cayenne gave it a litte kick. This was as good or better than my mom's. Thanks Nurse Di.

My husband is from the south (Mississippi) and loves southern home cooking. I am from Reno, NV and have never eaten okra, much less attempted to fried it. My husband selected this recipe and the cooking was collaborative. The result was excellent. Crunchy, slightly spicy battered okra. Tasted so good and was really very easy. My husband said that it was better than Sweetie Pie's (his grandmother). Now that is quite a compliment. Thanks!!

My sister and I grew up eating fried okra as kids. She and her family were visiting and I thought I would surprise her by making this. My cooking skills are limited so I wasn't sure how it would turn out, but I do remember my grandmother soaking the okra in buttermilk when she made it. It turned out perfect. The batter was golden and crisp after frying. The okra was not slimy. I don't usually save bacon grease but I did just for this recipe. It definitely adds to the flavor. Thanks Nurse Di. My sister and I are in your debt.

It doesn't get any better than this. My husband likes every food ever created, but when preparing it he's hard to please. I could not keep him out of the kitchen when he tried this okra. He kept going on about how wonderful this is, and how this is how okra should taste. Thanks, NurseDi, a fantastic recipe!

Delicious -- this is the first time I ever had fried okra and was happy with the delicious result. I did subsitute Crisco for the bacon drippings and also added 1 tablespoon of baking powder because I only had regular corn meal. Even my non-vegetable eater ds liked this. Thanks for sharing!

First time fixing fresh okra.This recipe was very good.I fixed way too much but I believe it will all get eat I can't keep my husband out of it.Thank you NurseDi for a good recipe will fix this way again.

NurseDi, this is another one of your winners! I have made fried okra for years, living in SC it's staple. But I never tried soaking in buttermilk. AMAZING! I will add that step from now on, and coach my daughters to do the same. Thanks!

This was just scrumptious!  I also used it for green tomatoes and just dipped the tomatoes into the buttermilk and then breaded.  Brought back many fond memories of childhood.  Will make this again next summer!!

I have never had okra before but was curious about how it tasted. I was sure impressed with this recipe! The crunch from the cornmeal is wonderful and I loved the taste of the okra. Even my 4 year old loved it and asked me to make it again. The only thing I would change would be to add a touch more salt next time. Thanks for the recipe!

I also used four tablespoons of butter and the one cup of pineapple juice and a quarter cup of water. Used extra brown sugar and used pineapple cake mix. Very rich, Very sweet!Such a pretty cake also. Thnks!Peggy Lynn
I really liked the flavor of this cake.  It was very moist and didn't last but a day in our house.  Great recipe!

Excellent presentation and so easy to do! Looks like you've put heaps of effort into it but haven't. I used glace cherries for topping. I was a little confused about the cake directions I didn't know whether to do it as directed on cake mix or use cake mix and add your 3 eggs and juice. Turned out anyway. Thanks!

Moist, delicious and easy. Has a beautiful shape! I would have liked the topping to have a slightly more caramelized flavor, but that was probably due to the type of baking pan used (bundt). Cake was enjoyed by all. Thanks for posting!

I baked this cake tonight.  It looks just like the picture.  I was a little disappointed that the brown sugar mixture was still a little grainy.  I like it a little more carmelized also.  I will bake it again and I think that the next time I will melt the butter and brown sugar in an iron skillet and then pour it into the bundt pan.  I believe this will give it the carmelized texture I prefer.  It's definitely a keeper recipe.

I made this the other day and my family ate it up in no time. Absolutely delicious and easy to make. I didn't want to use the oil so I substituted 1/3 cup of applesauce instead.  Cake was still super moist.

I made this cake and cut down on the brown sugar, and added it to the margarine while melting. I think it made for a less sweeter cake. I also used a 9x13 inch pan and added a bit of shredded coconut. Thanks for the recipe.
My wife loves pinapple upside down cake and this was a real hit with her. Thanks!!

This was very good! I made this for 2 co-workers and the only problem I had was I dont think I drained the pineapple enough because when I flipped it over, it was a little messy. Other than that, the taste is great!
I used pineapple rings instead of crushed pineapple. It came out great and didn't even last the weekend. This is my new upside down cake recipe.
Very light and spongy cake with a very good flavor.  Was a hit with young and old alike!
A lovely, juicy pineapple cake.  Extremely easy to make.  Beautiful presentation.   Will make again.
I made this for thanksgiving, it was great!!  I added extra brown sugar and pineapple cake mix.  We loved this and I will probably make it for xmas!!

I can sum this recipe up with one word...WOW!  I made it for Thanksgiving day dessert and my husband and I had to practice a LOT of restraint to not eat it the night before!  The only change I made was to use 3 tablespoons of butter instead of the recommended 2 and I used a yellow cake mix, since I couldn't find pineapple.  This cake is simple AWESOME!!!

Pineapple upside down cake is one of my favorites and this one is great. I used pineapple cake mix and the reserved juice. It was gone in a flash at a Church function. I did use 4 tablespoons butter and a little extra brown sugar for the topping. The only concern was my daughter commented it had an "aftertaste". Maybe I should have left the topping as it was. Thanks for a great recipe. The presentation is great
Beautiful presentation, easy to make and tastes great! It's a keeper! Thanks!

Thanks for posting this outstanding recipe.  I actually have made it in a 9 X 13 inch glass pan, and it just came out to perfection each and every time.  I followed the recipe but I added 1 1/2 Cups of Pinapple Juice/Water combination.  I felt it needed the extra moisture.  Great cake to take to a BBQ or Pot-Luck, everyone couldn't say enough great things about it.  A keeper for sure....  Thanks for posting it Nanita.

Yummy! I made this for my father in law's surprise bday party and had so many compliments on it! I'm making it again today for my kids. It came out very moist and flavorful. I don't think I will make it from a box again!
What a great cake! Easy to prepare, and gorgious to look at. I took another reveiwers advice and upped the butter to 4tbs. I can't wait to show this one off at work!

Very moist and a nice twist on the traditional pineapple upside down cake.  I agree with other reviews, the topping needed additional melted butter, I used three tablespoons.  Thank you for the delicious recipe!
Beautiful cake!  My family loved it!

In response to the "recipe hint" from Djemcee: your sandwiches only "sucked up grease" because your oil was not hot enough. When your oil is the right temp it will instantly seal the batter and prevent any oil from soaking into the sandwich. An oil thermometer helps.

I actually found the batter to be too thin and the resulting breading just didn't have the right texture compared to how I remember the Bennigan's Monte Cristo.

To remedy this I doubled the dry ingredients, then separated them into 2 different bowls. In one of the bowls I added milk instead of water, but only enough till I got a thicker, more pancake-like batter. Then when it came time to batter the sandiwches (held together with a couple of toothpicks) I dipped them in the wet batter first, then let the excess drip off for a few seconds and tossed them in the dry mix, then quickly into the fryer.

This method gave me a little crunch to the breading rather than the more french toast like covering.

This worked great for me! I do not usually bake my own bread due to the time and effort it takes, but this seemed so simple that I decided to give it a try. It is so nice to just take out what I need, and have hot, freshly baked bread or rolls whenever I want. Thank you French Tart for answering my yeast question, and also for sharing this wonderful recipe! UPDATE: Now that I've made this a few times, I still love it. I have realized though that it really doesn't need to be kneaded, that seems to knock the air out of it too much. Just use plenty of flour while stretching and folding it onto itself into the shape you want. I do this on a well floured board, then plop it on parchment liberally sprinkled with cornmeal. Then I slide the parchment onto a board that fits in my microwave. I heat a cup of water to steaming hot in the micro, then quickly open the door and stick the dough in there- I leave the cup on the board if there is room. This way you don't need to cover the dough and it rises very nicely. After 20 min or so, I slash the top, and slide the parchment onto a preheated baking stone, then dump the cup of hot water carefully into a metal baking pan(also preheated) on the shelf below the stone, then shut the door quickly to keep the steam in. Sorry this is so long, but I thought my trial and error might really help someone.

I wasn't sure if you meant to place the dough on a hot baking pan to rise, so I just left it on the cold one. (Maybe that is why it didn't rise a lot.)  I baked it at 450 degrees for 20 minutes and the top was brown and hard.  When I let it cool and sliced it up for dinner, it disappeared.  The kids loved it.  I guess my oven is hotter than most. I can't wait to experiment with this wonderful dough.  Thanks again!

Wow!  I am enjoying this recipe so much.  I have done this countless times now, and have tweaked it a bit to get it to work for me.  At first I was having a hard time getting it to rise after coming out of the fridge, so I tried rising it for 2 hours in the oven with the light on.  That seems to work well.  Also, I add a bit more yeast then called for, as that seems to help the rising too.  Also I add 3tsp of sugar when I am adding the salt.  I find this rounds out the flavour a bit.  I have done this with a mix of white and whole wheat bread flour, as well as just all whole wheat, which I think I like better.  I also found that baking it at 450 was giving me loaves that were a bit too crusty for my liking, so I have been baking mine at 350 for 25 mins, and I find that they are perfect!  I have also used this as a pizza dough with great success!  I rolled it thin with a rolling pin and brushed it with olive oil, and baked for 7 mins, then added sauce and toppings and put it back in the oven until done.  It is amazing to have bread/pizza dough in the fridge all the time ready to go when I am.  Thank you so much for posting this.  I hardly buy bread anymore, so this recipe is also a big money saver, as well as being fun and easy!!  I would recommend this to anybody....it is quick, easy and great!!

Dear dear Ms. Tart, your bread is marvelous and INSPIRING! I replace at least half of the flour with fine semolina and sprinkle the parchment with coarse semolina, and the result is very similar to the Sicilian bread that my DH admires. I have also used this dough to make scacciata, which is a eastern Sicily stuffed bread, with great success. Very good olive bread as well. I don't have dry yeast available so I use 25 g of cake yeast per recipe. I wish my oven would go to higher temperatures so that the bottom of the loaf was as crispy as the top. I have been using the convection option, and have been skipping the parchment to get a better result. Thanks to you for my new found interest in bread baking!

Thank you so much for this recipe.  It is such a timesaver.  We loved the first loaf we made, and the flavor of the next loaf after it stayed in the refrigerator for a week was so wonderful. Thank you, this has made making homemade bread so much easier.

I almost didn't try this recipe because I had already found a no-knead bread recipe that worked for us.  I'm so glad I did!  This recipe is a-mazing. I'm not giving this any stars at this point ~ only because I'm still in the experimental stages with this. I spoke with MsTart prior to making this recipe as I wanted to try making it gluten-free. I used the following: 1 cup brown rice flour, 1 cup white rice flour, 1 cup potato flour, and 3 1/2 cups GF baking flour. I also added 2 teaspoons xanthum gum, and the other ingredients as written. The dough came out nicely and I made 1 loaf after th initial prove. It was rather small (about 6 inches long/4 inches wide) and I baked using the boiling hot water in the preheated oven. The loaf had a wonderful crust but was not done inside ~ still doughy. I did taste test it and the flavor was good, it just wasn't done. I will make another loaf tomorrow, cutting the temperature to 400 and not kneading as much. I'm convinced this is the perfect recipe for my gluten-free bread craving, I just have to figure out what the adjustments are that I need to make. I've never baked any kind of bread other than quick-bread (cake-like) breads, so this is ALL new to me. Will update this review tomorrow. But thanks so much French Tart for sharing this wonderful family recipe. You've obviously made alot of people very happy to have access to this recipe, and I'm sure I'll be one of them too. UPDATE: Well, I finally figured it out ~ after 3 loaves, I figured out that I killed my yeast! No rise from any of the loaves I made. So I must start over again and redo this recipe. Will update again at that time.

I may try baking at the original 450 F to achieve a crisper crust, but the interior was absolutely perfect.  Thanks for helping me achieve breaddom in this lifetime!!

I've been a bad cook.  I have been making this recipe for quite some time and haven't reviewed it yet.  I love that I can keep it in the fridge and have fresh bread on short notice.  We have made free form loaves, breadsticks, and pizza from this dough.  I frequently brush it with melted butter and sprinkle with garlic salt. I rolled up the dough, starting with the side the that the filling went all the way to the edge, and pinched the seam closed and placed seam side down in a small, greased loaf pan. I let it rise again and used kitchen shears to cut tiny snips in the dough's surface for a spiky effect. It turned out lovely, flavorful, and perfect with barbecue chicken and garlicky dill pickles. I have so many ideas I want to try out with this wonderful dough. Do try this, its so simple and rewarding.

The texture and flavor of this bread is fantastic! I was concerned because the dough was much wetter than I expected, but light kneading on a well floured surface turned out a lovely loaf. This was absolutely the BEST. Other than making half the recipe, I changed nothing. I love this. I made it to go with a pan of spanakopita and grilled yellow squash. OMG - it was a delicious Greek dinner.

When I first looked at it I thought it would taste like yogurt with chopped cucumber, but it magically turned into that wonderful Tsatsiki sauce.  I used about 1-2 Tbsp of olive oil per cup of yogurt.  Thank you for the great recipe!
Easy and delicious.  You are right, the Greek yogurt makes all the difference. Thanks for another great posting.
This is quite tasty - both with and without the mint.  I've made it twice already and used Fage brand 2% Greek Yogurt both times.

This is delicious. I did change it up a bit, so I don't know if it would be considered authentic Tzatziki.

so easy to throw together, i made 3 trays of these for the school choir's bake sale. everyone loved them.

I took these to a Christmas gathering, and they were very well-received!  With no bowl or mixing, they were a snap to prepare, and they were really tasty and sweet! Hint: be sure to spread melted butter around the sides of the pan, as the bars are hard to loosen from edges otherwise.
good gooey easy yummy. Enough said about these treats.  They are beyond 5 stars.  You can easily keep all the ingredients on hand- for friends to go with a cup of java. Slurp.

These are so terrific-great right from the oven and even better the second day! I used 4 TB of butter, 1/2 cup coconut, and just a handful of butterscotch chips. Perfect holiday bar cookie!

I made these for Christmas treats to snack on, They were a great hit. I had no flaked coconut so I substituted Heath Toffee Bits. Oh they were so good. Next time I will use both the toffeee bits with the coconut flakes. They will now be a family tradition. Oh so easy,and so good.
Wow -- these are what I loved in grade school, back in the 70's!  So glad I found this old friend!  Its the real thing!  Delicious and simple to make.
I loved these!  I might try using macadamia nuts next time, and maybe white chocolate chips!
Did I really NEED to make these right after the holidays??   WoW!  These are really good and really easy = 5 stars for me!  I did use pecans and fat free condensed milk and it was FABULOUS!

LOVE THESE!! My Mam-Maw made these for Christmas.  My DH never had them before and in restoring some traditions I made them this past holiday.  I use pecans (like a good Texan) and use about 6 Tbls of butter.  Yum Yum and Super Easy. You can't go wrong.
My family liked these. So easy to prepare...might use a 9 x 7 pan next time to make a little thicker.
Very easy and tasty.  I used half chocolate chips and half butterscoth chips and I replaced walnuts for a basic nut topping.
Excellent, and SO EASY.  Will definitely make these again when I forget I needed to bring something to work the next morning.  ;)  Very rich and yummy!

We really enjoyed these!  I made it according to directions, but next time I think I would put the coconut in a food processor to make smaller, flakier pieces.  This was a delicious, very different dessert which was so very easy and quick to make!  Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!
Dianne
I was wavering between 4 and 5 stars and here's why.  Although these tasted wonderful half the graham cracker crust stayed in the pan.  It never solidified.  I will try more butter next time I guess.

I made these today, and they are great!  They couldn't be easier.  I went with the 6 Tablespoon suggestion on a previous review, and they turned out perfect.  Thanks!

These are magic squares! I love these things! If you go to the magic brand website they have aton of versions of these-- YUM!

Awesome, my children's favorite.  Sometimes I add more graham wafers and butter. Sliced almonds replace the walnuts in our nutfree household

So easy to make- and tastes great too! Used pecons instead of walnuts. thanks for posting!

This is a huge favorite for our family! One time I realized (too late) that I was out of chocolate chips! I doubled the nuts (pecans) and made them anyway. They turned out so delicious! I have been making these for years now. I true "never fail" dessert. I tend to add more butter sometimes as well as a mixture of diffrent chips. The only problem is these babies dont cool fast enough!!!

This was such a great recipe to make. It was so quick to put together that I could make it while helping kids with homework; and the best thing is they taste so good. This is a simple 5+ star recipe that I'll make again and again and again . . . may my figure forgive me!  Thank you Karen. One of my all time favorite treats growing up!  I didn't know anyone else called them Hello Dollies! absolutely amazing and sooo easy and quick!

I was looking for a delicious, easy dessert recipe to take to Christmas gatherings this year & this is it!  This is an excellent base recipe. Fabulous, added a little more butter.  Easy to double.  A great treat to give as a present for friends.  The outside slices are my favourite with chewy caramel!!!

Yummy, yummy, yummy!  My granny used to makes these.  This is my "go to" recipe when I have company coming & have no time to make anything too time consuming.  They always turn out perfect and everyone LOVES them!  Thanks for posting.

These are absolutely ridiculous.  These are incredibly easy too so they are definitely worth 5 stars!  They are crispy on the edges and very  chewy/gooey in the middle, wonderful!  A few things that might help others : The graham cracker layer should definitely be doubled, there isn't much of a crust at all if not.  Also, make sure it all gets some of the butter (this isn't so much of a problem if using full amount.  If not, then mix it up with the melted butter first to make sure it all gets wet.  Also, I took mine out at 25 minutes but they didn't end up setting up....until the next morning.  So don't cook them any longer, but they really need a while to firm up into bars.  We ate ours with spoons in little plops a couple hours after baking, but the next day we could hold the little squares with our hands no problem.  Great dessert!

These are awesome. I made them ahead as part of my Christmas baskets, they froze great (I only froze them for about a week), they were so easy to make, and they tasted great! I used a store brand of sweetened condensed milk, and it worked fine (not too runny or anything). I doubled this recipe and used an 8x8 pan for one batch and a 9x9 pan for the other, and I think I prefer the 9x9 pan - that seems perfect. Thank you, I will definitely keep this recipe!

3. ADDED- 2 tsp of Pumpkin Pie spice sprinkle it over crust (OR you can add it to the condensed milk).
I made in a 9 x 13 pyrex pan and just bumped up the quantities used to more like 1 1/2 cup of most ingredients because like most of you, I like a thicker bar.
