Overall the salad is excellent and I've already made it 4 times now. Thanks for a great recipe Kelley :)

This was very good.  I'm not a fan of olives, but I did use them.  I think probably the next time, I'll omit those.  I used the pepperoni as stated, but I think I might trade off for ham the next time, and possibly use feta cheese.

I had decided to half the recipe, and I'm delighted I changed my mind.  I ate a ton of this after our Christmas dinner--I was starving at midnite.  

It's absolutely a keeper, and I'll make this again and experiment slightly (but not much).  It's so good as is.
Try adding a little parmasean/romano/asagio cheese(s)to the dressing mix if you're a fan of Olive Garden's house dressing. I also like to add a little pepperoni to the salad mixture.
really tasty!! thanks so much! :)

I made this for a high school sports pot luck dinner and went home with an empty bowl! The adults couldn't get enough and even the teenaged football players kept coming back for more! The dressing is divine and the salad is so colorful making for a beautiful presentation.  I didn't change a thing as it is perfect already! I received a ton of recipe requests and will be making this again and again....Thanks!

I made this last week for a family event  and agree that it really IS perfect! The dressing wasn't too oily, but I did reduce the sugar just a bit. Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly as written.

We loved this! The salad is so festive with all the bright colored pasta and veggies. I did add the cubed cheese and will do so again. I may add a bit more oregano next time, but other than that we loved it!  I also took your advice on the olive oil and vinegar brand since I was out. Very good choice. Thanks so much for sharing. Nick's Mom

Yum!  That is one tasty little pasta salad.  My family and I really enjoyed it and will use this recipe frequently, I'm sure.  I made it exactly as the recipe states and wouldn't change a thing!  Thanks for sharing your recipe.

A 10- star recipe!  I used feta cheese, added 1 jar of marinated artichoke hearts, 1 green pepper and 2 medium tomatoes.  So I didn't follow exactly, but I think this recipe is such a good one that you can change it around to fit your personal tastes.  I took the huge bowl to a cookout (it makes alot) and ate 2 servings there.  I had leftovers and ate them all when I got home!  This tasted so good that you can stand at the refrigerator with the door open and eat a whole bowl before you know what hit you!  I can't make this one again unless I am sure that there will be no leftovers or my pants won't zip!  I was still thinking about how good it was today, and it's all gone!  Don't hesitate to take this dish to a potluck, you won't be sorry.  The others at the cookout enjoyed this salad, too, by the way, they just didn't act like the piggy that I did!

Delish!!!  We truly enjoyed this pasta salad.  I am taking the rest to a get together tomorrow.  I made as directed excepted I added feta cheese along with the provolone cheese, parmesan cheese and doubled the pepper in the dressing.  I only used half the amount of green pepper due to personal preference of DH.  Thanks for the recipe Kelley.

ok. I hardly got this in the fridge! It was good before it had time to "meld"! Couldn't find the pompeian brand of anything, so used what I had which is Star brand of red wine vinegar and some generic olive oil...which I used some canola oil in place of  part...used salami instead of pepperoni, and feta cheese instead of provolone. I used red bell pepper in addition to the green, and I added a cubed up cucumber. I added a bit more dried oregano, and some minced fresh basil. I'm standing with IndianaNana in front of the fridge eating, eating til the bowl is empty!!!!! Next time I will add more fresh basil, and maybe try some garlic in there too, but this is GOOD just the way it is!!
We enjoyed it.

Loved this pasta salad! It was a snap to prepare. The flavor of the dressing is outstanding. To suit the tastes of a group of younger kids, I omitted the green pepper and provolone cheese. Even without those goodies, it was fabulous. Thank you!
great salad we enjoyed it

Came across this recipe the other day and because of the reviews, decided to give it a try. I followed the recipe exactly except to use red pepper instead of green, and smoked gouda instead of provolone. I'm giving it four stars because the ingredients are wonderful together, and colors and textures of the salad are just great as well. The only downfall it has is the one thing that everyone else loved, for me it was the dressing, it's sweet, and I should have realized it would be because, knock, knock, it has a quarter cup of sugar!  Anyway, I'll make it again only I'll cut back to two tablespoons of sugar, or leave it out altogether. Just thought I was obligated to write this as a bit of warning to others who may not care so much for a sweet dressing. Good recipe though!

This is a wonderful pasta salad! I made a few changes to the recipe though.  Instead of green pepper I used red (personal preference), grape tomatoes cut in half, reduced fat feta cheese instead of provolone, turkey pepperoni instead of regular pepperoni because there's much less fat and calories, added 1 diced cucumber and a small jar of chopped marinated artichoke hearts. For the dressing I used about 1/2 the sugar it called for and added more oregano and some basil.  This is a wonderful light summer meal.  Thanks so much for posting!

We liked the salad, (7 people over for dinner) however we did find the red wine vinegar was too strong for our tastes.  (I used a high quality red wine vinegar but could not find the brand you specified). Also, I followed Nougat's advice and decreased the sugar as we don't like things too sweet - good move there.  I would maybe try this again but reduce the vinegar and play with the spices a bit more.  Good starter recipe that you can alter different veggies or cheese. Thx Kelley.

It was perfect for us.  I halved the recipe, left out the pepperoni but added a chopped zucchini.  However, I made the complete recipe for the dressing as I find that pasta seems to soak up dressing like a sponge and I plan on having this as leftovers for the next couple of days for just my husband and myself.  We really enjoyed it tonight and I'm looking forward to having it tomorrow.  Thanks Kelley.

This is a great pasta salad.  We were taking samples before I had everything added.  The dressing is perfect, and I won't change anything.  I used ham instead of pepperoni and feta cheese instead of provolone because that is what I had on hand.  Simply delicious!

This was good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written but next time I would change the ingredients  to suit my families likes. My hubby thought the black olives overpowered the salad so next time I would not add them. The dressing was good but was a bit sweet so next time I would add a bit less sugar.

I made this about a month ago for a Tupperware party; everyone loved it! I was also asked for the recipe. Next time I think I'll add just a bit more Pepperoni. My husband liked this pasta salad w/ Italian dressing as well.
Thanks, Kelley! This was a big hit at our house. My son especially loved it, as he doesn't like mayo. We'll be making this all summer long!

I was looking for a pasta salad that would be able to make a road trip so I gave this a try.  I'm sooooo glad that I did.  It is wonderful.  I didn't have peppers so I added peas.  I used salami  instead of pepperoni and added some garlic and basil to the dressing.  I too was concerned about the amount of vinegar but it is the right amount.  Thanks so much for sharing.

This recipe is fantastic! It is the ONLY cold salad my boyfriend will eat which says A LOT about how good this salad is. I followed the recipe exactly as written and it came out perfect! Thank you sooo much for posting.

Fabulous!! I doubled this to feed 30 people and it was plenty. I added grape tomatoes, cukes, and brocolli and skipped the cheese and pepperoni for cost purposes. I made the salad the day before to intensify flavors and it was a crowd pleaser. Per another reviewer, I did add parmesean cheese to the dressing. Very addictive!

Excellent. 
I used 3/4 cup of olive oil and 3/4 cup of vinegar and that was plenty.   Added fresh mozzerella instead of provolone, grape tomato's and red pepper instead of green pepper.
Will make again.  My family loved it.
Awesome recipe, made a couple modifications to the ingredients, but the zesty dressing is what makes this one a killer. It definitely lives up to its name!

This is the best pasta salad I've ever made.  I doubled the recipe and it was plenty for a barbecue with about 30 people there.  I did NOT double the amount of cheese (I subbed mozzerella) and I used only 1/2 pound of pepperoni total.  I used a bit less sugar and I left out the tomato and onion (my husband begged me to) and it still looked beautiful and tasted great!

Yum, yum, yum!!!  Absolutely loved this dish.  Super easy to make and the presentation was beautiful with all the different colors.  I halfed the cherry tomatoes but left out the cheese (didn't want it soggy) as well as the pepperoni (don't eat meat) but it was fantastic.  Making it again this weekend for a BBQ.  Thanks so much for sharing.

I expected this to be awesome. It was awesome. I was super hungry for pasta salad that I ate it right after I made it. I know it will even be better after it sits for awhile.  I think you could add in what you like and mix with the dressing. The dressing makes it. It is sad to say but I probably would eat alot more if my family was not watching. This will be in my rotation of pasta salads.

I take this to every potluck I go to, and I've never brought home any leftovers.  It tastes wonderful, and it disappears quickly.  I substitute green onions for the red onions. And I know other reviewers have raved about the dressing, but I actually prefer to use Italian Dressing instead.
I must have done something wrong. I didn't love this as much as I thought I would.  The dressing was missing something.  I will try again with more spices.

This is a 10 star recipe. It really is INCREDIBLE. I love the dressing. That is what makes this dish. I have made others like this but this one takes the cake. I cut the recipe in half and I swear it makes 8 servings. The only change I made was to use turkey pepperoni. This is a keeper and going in my best of 2009 cookbook. Thanks for posting. :)

DO believe the hype - people really did beg me for this recipe!  I have made it twice now, and will be making it again this week!  Perfect for a warm-weather lunch or light supper.  I did change just a couple of things, as one of my guests was allergic to raw peppers (cooked peppers are OK) and I really hate raw onion personally (even red ones) and so in place of the green peppers I added a small jar of mixed roasted peppers and instead of the raw onion, I actually roasted two large red onions in the oven (in some olive oil for 20 mins) and then added the chopped roasted red onions at the end, after they had cooled.   I also added some fresh basil, and used spicy chorizo sausage instead of the pepperoni.  But otherwise I did everything exactly as instructed and it was DEE-licious.  Apart from anything else, the dressing is awesome.  I will making this again and again!!

I was looking for a classic pasta salad recipe, and this was perfect! It was a great hit at our cookout. I left out the peppers because my husband doesn't like them, but the flavors were great and were really lite and delicious!

I can't believe I forgot to review this! It was amazing! I made this for my husband's work party. Everyone loved it and asked me to bring in the leftovers the next day. I was constantly in my refrigerator sneaking forkfulls! I made everything as suggested (Pompeian brand)...perfect.

I normally don't like this style of pasta salad very much, but it was good! I'm already thinking of making my next batch.

Next time, I'll use just red peppers, which I prefer to green, and I'll try salami, too.
YUM!  This was very good.   I made it for a party and of course, like you said, was asked for the recipe.  It is definitely a keeper!  Thanks!

I would give this 10 plus stars! It is incredible! All the reviews saying how great it was are correct. I was never a big pasta salad fan but this made me change my mind. I will throw out all my other recipes for pasta salad. Go ahead and make the whole amount -it will be gone. I made it yesterday and there are 3 people in my house-my hubby, me and my son and I gave one small container to my friend and it's all but gone. I saved a small container for my self in back of the fridge-he he. My friend is now making it too. No one can stop eating it.I added in roasted red peppers along with the green peppers, grape tomatoes-(love'em) and used mozzarella instead of provolone. I added about a 1/4 cup of grated Parmesan in there too. I had the Pompeian red wine vinegar, but used Sam's Club extra-virgin olive oil. I used 1 tablespoon dried oregano and 1/2 teaspoon dried basil. I used seasoned salt instead of regular and I grated a garlic clove into the dressing as well. I used the full amount of sugar. The dressing makes this salad perfect! Thanks Mrs. Jaye for the recipe and answering my question!
Wow........we really enjoyed this salad.  Thanks for sharing!
delicious!  I changed it up a little.  i used white onion instead of red and subbed feta for the provolone.  i will make this again.

This recipe definitely lives up to it's name.  It was delicious and everyone loved it.  I left out the pepperoni and used less sugar (not sure exactly how much less since I tripled the recipe and just threw some in).  I have to say though that it definitely tastes 10x better when it has sat in fridge for 3 or 4 days.  The flavor really soaks in.  Thanks for sharing; this is a great recipe!
Very good.  Rave reviews at a family party! Thanks!

The BEST pasta salad ever!!! My first time making pasta salad as I was craving it and hate store bought ones. I was pleasantly surprised that this came out so good since I was a little nervous. The brand of red wine vinegar recommended is perfection. I couldn't find the same brand of olive oil so I used another but it was still great. I used thick cut turkey sandwich meat cut up instead of pepperoni to cut down on fat and I forgot the olives but it was still good. I will make this often! Thanks so much for sharing the recipe!!! *** Update: I made the recipe again (less than a week later), this time with the sliced olives and I love the taste of olives in the salad too (I usually don't care for olives). God, this is good! I plan to make this dish for future potlucks and parties as I taste a hit!

This was delicious!  Thank you so much for the recipe.  Substituted pepperoni for salami I had left over in the fridge and also subbed the provolone for feta cheese.  This was delicious!  The dressing was so simple to make and I love the fact that you can basically sub a lot of the veggies for what you have leftover in the fridge.   I will definitely be making this again!

really delicious! i made a couple substitutions (based on other reviews) and we all loved it- i used the onions and olives, but instead of chopped tomatoes i used sliced cherry toms, red peppers instead of green, salami instead of pepperoni and feta instead of provolone- thankfully there were some leftovers which i will enjoy tomorrow:)
I made this for my sister-in-laws wedding reception and it was a HUGE hit!  Thank you!

I'm not usually a pasta salad person, but this might have been the best pasta salad I have ever tried! I did sub green peppers for red bell peppers, omitted the onion and cheese, subbed salami for pepperoni, and I added 1/2 teaspoon dried basil and a few shakes of shredded Parmesan cheese into the dressing. I also reduced the sugar in the dressing by 1 Tbsp (so I used 3 Tbsp). I was a little worried because it looked really oily, but the dressing was perfect! I used Star brand red wine vinegar. I got many compliments at the BBQ I made this for. Thanks for posting this recipe!

I had some pasta and meat balls ealier in the week. Had some of the pasta left over so I searched a little and found this pasta salad dish.This was so easy, I encouraged my 15 year old son to make it.He cut the ingredients in half since there were just two of us eating.Even cutting in half there is still enough for four people.It turned out great.I had everything on hand so all he had to do was follow the directions. I used green olives instead of black olives,that was the only change made.If your looking for a great tasting salad that is easy to make,here you go! The only thing I would suggest is to make it a few hours in advance to give all the ingredients time to mix together.Thanks Mrs Jaye

I found this recipe before our church conference. I just doubled for lunch, since we were not having that many. I got so many people who loved this. They said it was like a mouthful of explosions of flavor!! 
It was easy and tasty.

This was super easy, cheap and good!  I ran out of red wine vinegar in the process so I added half a bottle of Kraft Greek Salad Dressing.  I also left out the meat and black olives, but added broccoli and artichoke hearts.  Great for hot Georgia summer picnics!

I needed something to bring to a cookout so I thought I would try something new.  This was great.   It made so much, but I didin't have to worry about leftovers.  Everyone was looking for some to take home.  The leftover container we brought home was quickly devoured by our 20 year old.  He loves it.
Love the slightly sweet taste of this dressing!

I made this as written and thought the sauce was a tad overpowering and not as sweet as I would have thought based on other reviews (maybe I did something wrong?). Loved the ingrediants of the salad though. Alto took the advice of another review and added marinated artichoke hearts.
Very good... I reduced the sugar just a bit and we loved it!

Delicious! I used a 12 oz box of tri-color rotini plus 8 oz penne and there was plenty of dressing even with the extra pasta. I left out the diced tomatoes and onions and added celery. I used swiss cheese instead of provolone and green olives instead of black olives. Thanks for sharing this great recipe. I will definitely make this again sometime!
This is a great pasta salad.  I made this to go with our sandwiches tonight and we loved it.  Thank you for sharing.

Wonderful recipe!!  It truly was the hit of our easter dinner.  I substituted cubed sharp cheddar and eliminated the pepperoni.  Thought it was still perfect.  Also for those who know of Penzey's Spices, I swapped out the tablespoon of oregano for Penzey's 'pasta sprinkle' spice mix.  REALLY great!!
Very good! I will be making this again and again! Thank you Mrs. Jaye.

This was great.  I followed the recipe as stated with a couple of exceptions....substituted fresh mozzarella for the provolone, red pepper for the green, left out the pepperoni and tossed in fresh broccoli.  The dressing is what makes this dish and I did not find it sweet at all.  I made this for a tailgate for my daughter's lacrosse game.  I received so many compliments.  Thanks for such a terrific recipe.

This is just the best recipe ever! The dressing is incredible. Now I've come up with some extra/different ingredients to add to the salad and maybe you all would like to try it to.
I add everything it says on the recipe and then...
a jar of green olives
a can (rinsed) medium black olives
a jar of artichoke hearts (if marinated then I throw in the marinade with it)
Genoa salami instead of pepperoni and have the deli cut it thick so you can cube it at home.
Leave out the cheese cuz it can get soggy.
Every color pepper, orange, red, yellow ...but leave out the green...husband doesn't like green pepper.
jar of baby corn, rinsed.
And ta-da!
I made half a recipe but it was great.  Let it cool for one hour and served with Recipe #80934.
Well done and easy to cook!

Wow, wow, wow. Gorgeous flavors. I put in different veggies: roasted red peppers, peas, and carrots. The dressing was so good! I only used 1/2 cup olive oil and reduced the sugar to 2 tablespoons. Absolutely delicious. I'll use this again-- I have been trying to find a nice flavorful pasta salad dressing and this is it.

The name of this salad is very appropriate- this pasta salad is perfect! I would not deter from the original recipe at all, the flavor combination is just right. I didn't have provolone cheese so I just left it without cheese and it is still amazing! Thanks, Mrs. Jaye!

Very good! Thank you for the recipe!

I used store brand noodles, vinegar, and olive oil with fantastic results!

Only change I made (besides brand names) was that I used cubed pepper jack cheese instead of provolone. 

I also decreased the sugar to 2tablespoons instead of 1/4 cup. 

Thanks again!

Turned out very well.  I had to eliminate some ingredients since I didn't have them on hand but it is really the dressing that shines.  Yes, there is a lot of sugar and tasting it before mixing into the pasta is scary and way too sweet.  But something magical happens if you let it sit in the fridge overnight, the dressing isn't sweet at all and enhances the other flavors.  I ended up not using all the dressing as I didn't make quite enough pasta or use enough added veggies but it worked out beautifully.  And I have a little bit of leftover dressing to use for something else.  Thanks!

Really, really good salad!  I tweaked the dressing a bit since there wasn't enough of a vinegar taste to me, so mine ended up being 1.5 parts vinegar to 1 part olive oil, but otherwise I followed the recipe with great results!

Thanks for a great pasta salad recipe!  I didn't have provolone or black olives on hand, so I used a little bit of cheddar and some parmesan and omitted the olives.  I also added a little bit of crushed red pepper.  The dressing for this is great!

Very nice salad.  I only had a 12-ounce package of rotini so I scaled back the amounts of the other ingredients accordingly.  The dressing is sweeter than other pasta salads I've had, but I rather liked it and it seemed that my guests did too!  Thanks!

I changed this up to use what I had on hand and made it vegetarian to use as a side dish with grilled fish. I made half the recipe using pasta shells, chopped peppers, red onion, broccoli florets and, tomatoes. I also substituted cider vinegar, cut the sugar back to two tablespoons and used a tablespoon of italian seasning. My family loved it. Thanks.
This was very good!  I served it at my daughter's 3rd birthday party, and both the children and adults enjoyed it.  Will make again!

Very nice. I think it's better to use tri-color pasta because the balsamic vinegar will darken the white pasta. I did not add the pepperoni or provolone because I couldn't imagine that tasting good. But it was really good without!
Perfect dressing. :)
LOVE THIS! The only changes I made was omitting the peppers, onions and cheese due to our preferences. The dressing is SOOOO GOOD..not too oily or strong! Perfect!

Great! Everyone loved it. Makes a great big bowl of yummy pasta salad. Used mozzarella instead of provolone, gemelli instead of tri-color twists, and omitted the pepperoni. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Amazing!  And you're right! Everyone asked for the recipe! :) Thanks so much for sharing!
Super good! I'm not a big fan of pasta salads, but this had lots of flavor and texture that I really enjoyed. Thanks for posting the recipe.
Very good pasta salad.  Easily customizable.  Dressing quite good.

I agree.  This is a very good pasta salad.  The dressing is so good and allows for the addition of your favorite vegetables.  I added broccoli along with the ingredients in your recipe.  Thanks for the recipe.  Had with grilled pork chops, green beans and garlic sticks.

Made this with salami instead of pepperoni, and omitted the green peppers.  Made for a picnic with my family and it was perfect.  I made a triple batch as there were 14 of us.  My sister-in-law saw the big bowl and thought I was crazy for bringing so much, but I didn't bring any home!
I left out the pepperoni and tweeked the dressing a little bit for my taste.

Perfect Pasta Salad, for sure! Loved every bite! I added some sun-dried tomatoes, and some celery, but other then that, stayed perfectly to the recipe. This is indeed, one happy, lovely, and delish pasta salad! Made for Cooking Out of the Pantry 2012 -Canning Forum
Loved the combination of crunchy vegetables and zesty dressing.  Tasted even better the second day. Nice recipe for gatherings
Very good... wasn't thrilled with the amount of oil, but it tasted scrumpcious!  I used the mini-turkey pepperoni

Excellent pasta salad.  I especially liked that it did not have any mayo in it.  I took it for a luncheon we were giving and it worked out fabulous...I did not have to worry about keeping it cold as it is 83 here in Traverse City MI today...which is nuts....everyone must have loved it as I tripled the recipe and have very little left....

Not our preference, I guess. Husband really doesn't like strongly acidic tastes, and I thought this was very vinegary. I discovered this after it sat for several hours in fridge; I made it palatable for him by adding more sugar and salt to cut the acid, but now it just lacks flavor. I read elsewhere that one should emulsify oil and vinegar for a pasta salad, otherwise the vinegar soaks into the pasta (resulting in strong flavor) while the oil clings. But others like it...!

This pasta salad is very very good!!  Made using tri color penne pasta and it turned out perfect. The dressing is awesome and it's very colorful. I made as written and wouldn't change a thing! It was a huge hit on a hot summer night! Thanks so much for sharing-will be making this again and again.
Really good salad.  Will make often!!

Amazing! I did change a few things like;
Bocconcini balls instead of Provolone, Raw Blue Agave syrup instead of white sugar and I also added chick peas
But, this still gets 5 stars because they were personal preferrence and it would have been just as good either way!!!!
Thank you Mrs.Jaye

This pasta salad is by far my favorite to date.  I made a few small changes for my own taste.  I reduced the amount of onions by half a cup, omitted the olives, and used turkey pepperoni.  This was amazing.  I cannot wait to share this with others.

Made this for Summer on the Porch Diabetic Forum and what a wonderful and tasty salad.  I added some celery and used turkey pepperoni and the salad made a delicious meal on a hot evening with some french bread.  Definately a keeper!

First off, the dressing was perfect us. I used my favorite olive oil and red wine vinegar, so don't let the recommendations stop you from trying this amazing recipe, use what you have on hand. Think of this as a fantastic base recipe. After the pasta and dressing make it your own and add whatever your family likes. I did emulsify the dressing with my stick blender. Great stuff Mrs. Jaye! Thank you for posting.

This recipe certainly doesn't need another 5 stars review but here goes...Perfection! I scaled everything down for 2 as there's only DH and me and didn't change a thing. I took one reviewer's suggestion of emulsifying the dressing in a blender and I believe by doing so it makes it better. DH couldn't stop eating it so big Thank You, Mrs. Jaye!

Absolutely wonderful!  I suggest letting it sit at least 1 day, but in my opinion the flavour is perfect at about 2.  I've made it several times, and each time is just as good as the last.  I find I prefer red peppers in the place of green, just because the sweetness adds an extra snap.
Very tasty pasta salad.  Yummy.
The sweet and tangy dressing makes this pasta salad the best I have had. I added chopped tomatoes, sliced olives, cubed swiss cheese and pepperoni. I will add roasted red peppers next time.
Delicious! I made it for my family and everyone loved it!
I would use only half the onion next time, but otherwise very good!!

This salad is incredible! Even hubby, who isn't a pasta salad person loved it and asked for some leftovers in his lunch today. I followed the recipe exactly, except for the pepperoni. I always buy pre-packaged pepperoni at the supermarket deli but accidentally grabbed hard salami this time. Didn't seem to make a any difference. This will definitely be a summer staple for us.

Thank you for this keeper of a recipe! Very pleased with this one. I ran out of red wine vinegar and used half rice vinegar and it was still great. I used string cheese cubed as the provolone, yum! Used sliced pepperoni and should have seperated the slices before adding to the mix. I will use a pepperoni stick next time or manually seperate the slices a they do not come apart while stiring. This will be made many times this summer.

This pasta salad is really good!  I used sharp cheddar cheese in place of the provolone.  After tasting it, I decided to add 2 tbsp of grated Parmesan cheese.  It also needed a little garlic, so I added 1/4 tsp of garlic powder to the dressing.  I would definitely make this again - thank you for the recipe!
Used 1.5 boxes of pasta and kept other ratios including dressing the same and it was perfect!

Used the dressing recipe but changed much of the veggies & cheese to what I had on hand.  I enjoyed the flavor and will be making this again.  I used tomato, broccoli,cucumber, zuchinni, cheddar, and feta cheese.  I  see that this recipe is versatile to your liking.

Good pasta salad. I made as written, but the possibilities are endless of the type of vegetables that can be added. After making and tasting I decided to add capers and green olives. I also used shredded mozzarella cheese on top, mixing it in when served. What I like about this recipe is that it wasn't oily, I did make a half recipe of extra dressing just in case it got dry after chilling.
Very good pasta salad.  Daughter is a vegan so no meat or cheese.  Added some red bell pepper, a carton of cherry tomatoes, and I may add garbanzo beans next time too.
I messed up the second time that I made it and bought the pomegranate infused red wine vinegar. WOWED. What an awesome mistake. That kicks it up 3 notches.
Yum!  Everyone loved it!  Adding this to my list of crowd pleasing recipes,
Good - but dressing needs some tweaking.  Maybe garlic, Italian seasoning.
Added 1 to Italian herb mix to the dressing - fabulous.
I believe this is the best Pasta salad I have ever had!!  Really good, well balanced sweet/sour/salt and outstanding flavors.  Boost it right before serving with some fresh Italian Parsley!

This was GREAT! At first I thought the dressing might be too sweet, but after it chilled for an hour, it was perfect. Of course I added a few things... like salami, pigmentos and crunchy celery. But overall it wears really good.

Absolutely delicious. Very light and fresh pasta salad. For the dressing I used a roasted garlic olive oil, but I'm a bit of a garlic nut. Also for the pepperoni I purchased a pack of pepperoni snack sticks. Same great flavor with a nicer appearance.

First and last pasta salad I have or ever will make. Friggin delicious. Every time I've ever made it, I feel like I'm going to have so much left. But folks are licking the dressing off the bottom of the bowl! I used grape tomatoes and cut them in half because I don't eat them but others do and they're easy for me to avoid, and so pretty in there! I also add red bell pepper; as others have said, it's easily customizable. But I do follow the dressing directions, and it's wonderful! I'm making a batch today, and it will probably be gone by tomorrow. This is a forever recipe!

I have no idea why this has been rated 5 stars.  The dressing is TERRIBLE.  It may possibly be due to a mistake in the amount of red wine and/or olive oil.  If you want a good recipe, go to the all recipe site and search for the "awesome pasta salad" recipe.  This recipe was nothing but a waste of time and money.  It was not good at all and I would have been highly embarrassed if I had to bring this to a function.
I figured I would try this recipe. I absolutely  loved it!! Easy to make and is very good I wish iIadded more cheese.

It is great! I'm on the Rec Committee here for our HOA. Plus I love food and feeding people at a good party. I googled Best Pasta Salad and came upon this recipe. I highly recommend undercooking the pasta to absorb the dressing so it doesn't get soggy as one of the tips I'm going to recommend is doing it the day before. In fact, if you chop all the vegetables for the dish, you will need the time. No way could this properly be prepared the day of and taste so great. I also recommend a huge bowl to prep in. Need to stir without ingredients flipping out. I went heavy with red, green, and yellow peppers. Try to keep everything equal size fir bites. Artichokes in water were diced and added. I used mozzarella circles soaked in oil (half drained, keep spices- Trader Joe's) Parmigiana cheese (BOTH grated and shredded) Salami quartered slices same size as cut up cheese. Olives are optional. I bought a can of sliced black olives and put them alongside serving dish. For the tomatoes, I quarter heirloom and marinated in extra virgin olive oil with fresh oregano and basil. The base dressing is spot on with the red vibe vinegar, olive oil, and sugar. But upon serving I offered jars of Tuscan Italian dressing and nonfat Balsamic. Just in case anyone wanted to add a little to the top, which I did. For the red onions which were added the day of, I diced and put in bowl of ice. It cuts the harshness of the onion and renders the taste excellently. I had extra so I put in a baggie with ice and use them when I need them for up to two weeks! Everyone loved both versions. People were taking it home and I heard compliments afterwards. Just make sure it's out in a big bowl so it can breathe. And add anything you want. It can handle additions. For a shortcut cheat and red wine vinegar dressing would work. I decorated mine with a long strip cut red pepper and a blossom of basil in the middle.

I've never tried using cheddar, chives, and mayo.  However it sounds interesting, I'll have to try it.

This was delicious! I actually made it with 1/3 less fat margarine because my boyfriend has high cholesterol, and it was still fantastic.  I can only imagine how much better it is with butter! Thanks for the great recipe!
Too dry for my taste. I would probably use twice as much butter and actually take the slices apart and cover both sides next time, but the flavor was good.
I made this to go with chicken marsala.  It was PERFECT as usual. Thanks Kitten everyone thinks I am the best cook because of YOU

Kittencal, this is The Best garlic bread I've ever had! I like the PP's comment about everyone thinking they're a good cook because of You - I feel the same way! I couldn't find any non-skinny and long French bread, so I got a loaf of foccacia bread from a local bakery and sliced it length-wise like a PP suggested, baking at 350 for 10 minutes and then on low broil for 1.5 minutes. I also used 3 larger cloves and one small clove of garlic. Magnificent! And I loved the color that the parsley added!

I make garlic bread alot for the family.  So, I decided to try this recipe because I have tried a few of Kittencal's recipes and have never been disappointed.  I wasn't with this one either.  It came out GREAT!  The only thing I added was mozzarella cheese.  My kids love CHEESY garlic bread.  Thanks Kittencal for another great recipe.
Yum yum yum!  I wanted to dress up plain spaghetti and jarred sauce.  This did it!  I had all the ingredients on hand and also added the 1/4 c mayo. . yum yum yum!

I've never made garlic bread before, but this was easy!  I wanted to do something homemade for a college golf team party to accompany a store-bought lasagna.  Everyone thought I was a hero!  My only note is that I doubled the recipe but only used 1 1/2 T of fresh pressed garlic and it was still VERY garlicky.  I will try to make the garlic pieces as small as possible next time and will substitute some of the fresh garlic for garlic powder.
Loved this! Quick, easy and tasty...what more could you ask for? Will keep this one in my freezer! Thanks Kittencal!

Easy and tasty! I measured pretty loosely, and used roasted garlic and light rye bread, so this isn't a fair review of the ingredients, just the procedure. I was using this as a guideline for HOW to prepare the garlic toast, and it was lovely!
WOW!  Great garlic toast!  Wonderful flavor, particularly with fresh parsley.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Excellent!!

Good, not great. I did use unsalted butter, and in my opinion it would have been better with more salt. I also added approx. 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder, and was glad I did. This is a good mixture of ingredients; I just play around with the ratios! Thanks for sharing!

This was really yummy garlic bread.  It was very easy to make, and we served it last night with leftovers of your Recipe #162445 162445.  We actually did use a baguette, but it turned out fine. Thanks!
This was a very nice recipe for garlic bread.  Only complaint was that mine was not done, even at 20 minutes.  Will try again but definitely needs more cooking time.

I chose the garlic toast option and glad I did.  This amount of garlic butter was the perfect amount for my loaf of Italian bread from the bakery.  Perfectly toasted under the broiler for just a few minutes.  Served this with a few appy's and nothing more was needed.  This would go perfectly with any italian dinner which I plan to do soon.  
Made for Chef's Pick in KK's forum. ~

Excellent bread, Kitten!  I split the French bread horizontally and loosely covered the bread with aluminum foil.  Mine was nice and toasty in 15 minutes.  We just cut off pieces off the halves, and it was wonderful.  The fresh parsley really brighten the flavors.  Thank you for posting!
Yum, I used 2 Tbs garlic and a mix of fresh and dried parsley.  Went for the toast and baked about 15 minutes. Turned out great.
very, very yummy!

Excellent! I made this tonite and it was a big hit. I used some mayo as well as the butter and had to use sourdough French Rolls as that is all we had. And they were very delish! Thanks for posting, KittenCal!
very good.  Thanks

Oh good!  Now I know how to make garlic bread!  Have you ever looked at the ingredients list on the freezer kind?  It's like a mile long.  This is much more wholesome and has far more garlicky goodness.
Soooo good! And very easy, too. Thank you for sharing :-)

We made this using the garlic toast option. We sprinkled shredded Cheddar on top of half of it. It was enjoyed by everyone. We liked the Cheddar topped pieces the best. The only thing I did differently was to finish cooking it under the broiler. The rest of our meal was already on the table and I needed it to cook a little quicker. It turned out great. Thanks!
Update: We had grilled Corn on the Cob tonight and used the extra garlic butter mixture on it.  
It was good this way as well.  Thanks Kittencal!
Yum!!!

There is a very good reason why this recipe has 130 reviews, all 5 stars.........it is delicious and so easy to make! I used a very fat pain (French bread) and we both gobbled it up with our soup today for lunch.............naughty but VERY VERY nice! I made it exactly as posted and used fresh parsley from the garden with fresh local butter, divine thanks Kitten! Merci encore for another wonderful recipe. (Photos to be posted, here with watermarks or on your blog) :-) Karen/FT
Excellent!

I knew this would be excellent - as everything I've tried by you, Kittencal, has been marvelous. In order to get to the 2 tablespoons of fresh minced garlic you recommend it took 8 good sized cloves unlike some of the reviews who stated they only used three - perhaps where I live they make them smaller:) At any rate, there will be no other garlic bread paste used in our home from this day forward. Thank you again Kittencal for ALL your fantastic recipes.
7/16/11 Update - I prepared this for my DD and her husband tonight - I couldn't use garlic so instead used shallots and in place of parsley used fresh rosemary, what a completely different twist on this bread - as good as with garlic & parsley (if not better).

Kitten, Kitten, Kitten...what can I say?  A simple, delicious recipe from a poster I've come to count on.  Needless to say, you didn't let me down.  I used finely chopped flat leaf thyme instead of parsley, and added a bit of EVO to the butter along with the garlic and fresh parm.  Sigh.  YUMMY!!!

Best garlic bread I have made in years!  My son is visiting from Louisiana and I made recipe#39087 and wanted a good garlic bread to go with.  I am glad I choose your recipe.  I will be using your recipe anytime I want to make a great garlic bread.  Thanks for posting Kitten.
This was excellent and will definitely make it again.  My family really enjoyed it.  Thanks

Kittencal, your recipes never disappoint! This garlic bread was soo delicious! I halved the recipe for a small batch of garlic bread and still have some extra garlic butter for tomorrow, though man, I'm craving more already. Thank you for a great recipe, and for the epic and delicious garlic breath :)
I didn't have enough Parmesan cheese, so I didn't use any.  Also, I just sliced the bread in half and spread the mixture on that way.  Was delicious though, thank you!

Really great garlic bread! I used only butter, didn't use salt because all we had was salted butter (as a pastry chef, this drives me nuts!), added some fresh rosemary (because we have a shrub that grows like crazy), a few splashes of lemon juice, and a pinch of pepper.

I mixed the spread 2 days before I needed it. I didn't want to store it in a plastic container because it would be ridiculous to get the garlic smell out of it. So I put the spread in a quart-sized freezer bag, pushed it all into a corner, and a put a twist-tie around bag at the top of the spread (what I do with all my pastry bags). When it was time for the bread, I snipped the corner, piped the spread, and smoothed it over with an offset spatula. I spread a thin layer on each side.

I like my garlic bread to be pretty toasty, so I baked my slices at 400 degrees, for about 4-5 minutes on each side. Then I put them under the BROILER for less than minute on each side. Crunchy and delicious!
Tasty!  The method sounds daunting but it really is easy to do.  Nice presentation!

This is another hit by Kittencal!  So easy and so delicious.  I used fresh parsley and probably a little more parmesan.  Served on rolls one night with recipe#99870#99870 and another night on some sourdough bread.  Thank you for posting.  Made for Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup ~ Jan-June 2013 tag game.
Delicious! I had to use soy parmesan and dairy-free margarine, and it was still pure comfort food. And so easy! Great recipe.
Will never use any other kind of garlic butter again.  Yummy!
Made mine as garlic toast using a loaf of Italian bread from the bakery.  Garlic butter spread is delicious!
Excellent - loved the amount of garlic and the addition of the parmesan.  Will be using this spread from now on.
Kittencal, you are a legend on this site!  I am going through a number of your recipes to print off and make a cookbook of all your gems!  Thanks so much!
Very good. We reduced the amount of parmesan for our taste.
Made this as directed, except used 1 tsp garlic powder in place of fresh garlic.  Delicious!  I put mine on an Italian loaf and served with Lasagna Soup.  Yum!
Oooooh yeah! Yum! Thanks for the keeper recipe!

I was in such a hurry when I made this..I totally forgot the onions!!! NExt time I will not forget. I thought this dish was very good and comforting. My mom and grandmother both loved it. Will make again. Thanks.

This is a flavorful recipe. I am usually disappointed in casserole recipes, but this one is a keeper for sure. Hubby had THREE helpings and then I found his fork in the casserole dish to boot. Served with roasted grape tomatoes and he really liked the way the sauce tasted on the tomatoes too. Thanks!! :)

I thought this was great, easy to make and tasted soooo good! I was out of cheddar cheese, so I used only parmesan. I used yukon gold potatoes instead of russet(was all I had). I also snuck in some pureed cauliflower (from Jessica Seinfeld's cookbook.
Will definitely make again, thanks kitten :)

I have not made this type of casserole in a very long time. I usually find that this type of casserole comes out tasting very bland or is dried  out. That was not the case with this casserole at all. It was so full of flavor and nice and creamy. I did not add dried chili pepper flakes and I was out of cheddar so I used marble jack. I added extra cheese(I shredded to much so I added it - just to use it up). This was Yummy Kitten Thank you for sharing your recipe !!!!
My boyfrend LOVED this and he is so picky and hard to cook for.  He gave it an A+++.  I used ground turkey instead of beef and it was delicious.  So simple to make too!  Thanks Kittencal!

We enjoyed this tasty casserole. I used ground beef and 1 teaspoon chili pepper flakes which gave it the right amount of heat for us. It's a keeper. Made for tag a thon. 

Thanks Kittencal.

Bullwinkle

Excellent!  I made it just as you recommended, and the pepper flakes gave it just enough of a kick to be interesting.  With my crazy schedule, I wondered about using frozen hashbrowns to speed up the prep time?  I may try that next time around.
This is very tasting casserole. My family loved it. I did reduce chili pepper flakes though to 1/2 tsp and it was still hot for my children. I wll make this again. Thanks.

Mmmmm-mmmmm!!!!  I followed Kitten's recipe to a "T" and can't imagine what I would have done different. Soooo good and yes, comforting.  I'd venture to guess that even if your fella wasn't big on casseroles, he'd probably love this since it's mainley meat, 'taters and cheese!

Everyone really enjoyed this Kitten!  After a day of tobogganing it really hit the spot as great comfort food and warmed our bellies.  I found that   the cheese made the top of the casserole greasy so I had to spoon off the fat but other than that no problems.  Left out the chili flakes as we don't eat spicy food, and left out the green peppers since I didn't have any.  I will definitely make this again since the kids ate seconds and thirds! Really good, thank you.

Comfort food for sure!  My husband has been eating this meal for lunch and dinner for 2 days straight now, and it still tastes great!  We used veggie crumbles instead of beef and I sprinkled some bacon bits on top, hoping to give it some smoked flavor, and that was a good addition.  We used green pepper, as suggested, since we could always use some fresh veggies, and you can't taste it much anyway.  I definitely didn't read the entire intro very well because I put all of the cheese on top of the soup mixture, and none on the top, but it was melty goodness, so whatever!  Thank you also for the suggestion to toss the taters in the soup mixture (we used mushroom), it felt like we were eating au gratin potatoes.  Very delicious, I'll be putting this recipe into heavy rotation!

This turned into one of the best one dish meals I have made in a long time. Added both corn and green beans and it made a complete meal. Tried to cut the recipe in half buth ad to add a little more liquid than called for. Even when cut it still made a lot.
Thanks hanche

This was a great meal.  I made it for my parent while my fiance and I were home visiting.  My dad wasn't feeling great, so I looked for some comfort food with some beef in it (my dad feeds cattle).  This was a great recipe!  We all loved it and it was easy to make.  I went lighter on the garlic and didn't use red pepper to keep is less spicey for my dad.  I also knocked down the servings to 6 and there was still plenty left with four of us.  All in all, great recipe.  I'll use is again soon!

This was easy and delicious.  Like a lot of people, I (sort of) halved the recipe (adding a little bit extra of this and a little bit less of that!!) and it still worked out well.  I also added some frozen peas and corn.  Unlike everyone else though, I cooked this in the slow cooker - put everything in together (didn't bother with layering) and put in on low for about 6 hours or so.  Will definitely do this again, but I think I'll try it with diced chicken or with lamb chops as I'm sure it will be delicious with either of these.

This is very easy and quick to make.  I added cooked bacon to the meat mixture and used cream cheese instead of sour cream because I didn't have any on hand.  I am wishing I hadn't cut it down to 4 servings, it was so delicious!

This was awesome!!  Super easy and my DH said definitely make this again.  He said the leftovers were even better.  I can't wait to make this again when I have more people to cook for since the prep isn't long just the cook time.  Thank you so much!

Wow!  Followed your recipe and subbed red bell pepper for green.  Only made half and got 5 good sized, delicious servings.  My husband said this definitely needed to be added to the normal meal rotation in our house!  Thanks so much, Kitten!

I made this for my family tonight and it was SO good! We only used 4 large potatoes and that was enough. Also just mixed the potatoes with the sauce and poured the ground beef on top. Didnt use the optional green pepper or chili flakes as my 6 yr old was eating too. Thanks for another winner Kittencal!!!!!!!! :)

Made this last night.  Easy to throw together, had all ingred. on hand.  I didn't layer it, potato on bottom, sauce, hamburger and cheese.  We all loved it. We have a large family of boys and this does the job of filling them all up.  Will be making this again and again.

really good! my daughter and husband really enjoyed it.
did just what the recipe. Yummy!  Will definitely make again.

Was really good, I omited the red pepperflakes and the green peppers due to personal taste. I think next time I will add some corn to it for some added color and taste (and a good way to sneak in a veggie for the kids). I used motzarella,swiss, and colby cheese  that is all I had in the house and it was really good and cheesey! I sliced my potatoes very thin and the potatoes were just perfect, not to soft not to hard they were great! Thanks for sharing this I will be making it again!!

This is my new favorite comfort casserole!  I used a pound of mild Italian sausage, only 4 russets and the full amount of sauce.  This filled my 9 X13 pan completely.  The flavor was outstanding.  Oh, I also added fresh mushrooms to the meat mixture and used cream of mushroom soup.  I often make meals for people and this one is going on the list!  Thanks Kitten!

I was looking for something that I could "throw together" using ingredients I had on hand...in fact my potatoes were going to be trash in a couple days if I didn't use them.  This recipe was perfect...I had everything available.  I can't just say that my family liked it...cuz they all had thirds!  SO I am going to say that my family loved this recipe!  We will definately be having it again!  I did make a half recipe for my family of 4 and it was perfect.  There were no leftovers.  Great comfort food recipe!
wow no wonder there are so many great reviews on this recipe, this is YUMMMMO!, thanks for yet another winner Kit.

Amazing flavor!  I used my pampered chef mandolin on the thicker setting for slicing the potatoes and I had to bake it for 1 hr 45 mins - longer than I expected.  I added the cheese before I baked it, and it became really oily, so next time I won't add it til the end and just bake it for a few minutes to melt.  I used 5 med. potatoes and it was perfect - made a lot of food!  Thanks for a keeper!!!!  Really good!

I followed the recipe with the following alterations: I used the red skinned rosemary and garlic "Simply Potatoes" wedges; I did not have cream of chicken, so I used one can cream of celery and one can cream of mushroom; had no onions, so I used a liberal amount of onion powder; and I added fresh diced jalapenos to the ground beef instead of the red pepper flakes - and no green bell peppers; and then a healthy dash of nutmeg to the cream mixture.  That taste was excellent - a bit too creamy for me, but my DH loved it.  Thanks for another stellar recipe Kit!!

I served this up and 20 year old son tucked in and asked as he was inhaling it was this a recipezaar dish and it was one I could do again - high praise indeed!  My husband agreed with him.  I left out the onion and green pepper because of son finding these foods a bit of a challenge, and I used a can of cream of corn and bacon soup because that was what I had.  I found that the potatoes were not quite cooked enough, so I think I wil par-boil them and then slice them next time.  We all enjoyed this dish, and it will become a regular.  The left overs were much sought after the next day.

I know if it's a Kittencal recipe it's going to be a keeper!  I made this the other night when I was in need of comfort food and it was fabulous!  Next time I will increase the amount of meat just a little but this recipe is going into my favorites file for sure.  Thanks again for a fantastic recipe.

Yummy!!  Just made this for dinner and it was delicious.  I only had one can of cream soup so I used the idea from another reviewer to add a can of creamed corn.   It was creamy, flavorful and filling...perfect meal for a cool day!!  Will defintely be a regular at our dinner table.  Thanks for the great recipe!!
Family loves this without green peppers.  I also used cream of mushroom soup and garlic salt.  Yum!
This is so good.  I use fat free cheese on the inside of the casserole and it melts nicely and no one can tell it is fat free.  I use low fat or regular for the topping.  Yummy!

Great comfort food!  We were starving, so I had no time to take pictures.  My son picked out the green peppers, which I knew he would.  I resisted putting mushrooms in, but I think they'd be great in this.  I sliced my potatoes thin, and they were tender in the lesser time stated in the recipe.  I also halved the amount of onion because of my family's tastes.  But I really enjoyed having something everyone in the family would eat!  I made this for Alphabet Tag!

Once again AMAZING Kittencal. I thought this was an absolute delicious casserole. I halved the recipe because we are just 2. Even at half it made alot. But Yummy....lunch for tomorrow. I chose cream of mushroom soup over the chicken soup, just what I prefer. I put mozzerella over the sauce mixture and put some cheddar over the meat mixture. The flavors were fantastic. Well Kittencal another one of your recipes I will me making often.
Truly a great casserole.  A big step up from just ground beef, onion, potatoes and a can of creamed soup that I try to get by with from time to time! Thank-you for sharing.

Good, but it took me forever to put together, so I'm not sure I would make it very often.  The meat was really good, and smelled awesome while cooking.  I didn't want my onions crunchy in the sauce, so I sauteed them with the garlic and spices.  I didn't have the green pepper but would try it if we did.  I did use 2 tablespoons garlic, and it seemed like a lot but I thought the meat was very well seasoned, and not at all bland like  these casseroles sometimes get.  My hubby thought the potatoes could have cooked longer, but I think they were as they were meant to be.  Warmed up well, too!
Very good!  We really enjoyed this dish.  It was even better the second day.  I made as directed except for the bell pepper & parm cheese, I was out.  It went together fast too, a quick yummy meal.

Update: At first I said this was just OK.  The guys liked it a lot but, you really need to cook the potatoes a bit first. They were no where near done after an hour. Yes, they were sliced super thin. I think this is a man meal.  However, the leftovers the next day were perfect and it was really good.  I definitely will either boil the potatoes for a bit or zap them in the microwave next time.

Just made this dish last night, and the flavor was excellent, but I also had a problem with the potatoes still being raw in places.  Yes, they were sliced thin, and I baked this for an hour and a half at slightly more than the 350 degree called for.  Next time I'll zap the potatoes first.

I've made this twice so far...in a month.  My family loves it.  I personally did not have an issue with the potatoes being done enough after an hour and a half.  I also leave the green pepper out, but everything else is the same.  I love the flavor!...I think it's the seasoning salt and pepper flakes that give it the zest I love.

Wonderful comfort food!  I did make a few changes.  I substituted ground turkey for ground beef, and I threw in two hot turkey sausage links for some kick.  I also only used four large potatoes.  I can't imagine using 6.  I think the potatoes would greatly outweigh the meat in that case.  I kept everything else the same and it came out wonderfully.  Everyone went back for seconds!

I made this for dinner a few nights ago. My bf gobbled up two helpings. I took the advice of other reviewers and pre-cooked the potatoes. I'm glad I did. I then cooked it for 30 minutes covered and 30 minutes uncovered. My only gripe would be that it didn't reheat too well. I think it lost something the next day. But I will definitely try this again. Perhaps with sausage and I will probably cut the amount of potatoes in half. Thanks for sharing Kitten.

This was so creamy, so rich, so good!!! My DH & I loved it, he got two BIG servings.  I used cream of mushroom soup and boiled the potatoes before for awhile, I only had to put it into the oven for 40 minutes.  Other than that I followed the recipe as is and I thought it tasted great the next day too.  Thanks for the great recipe.

This is a kid-friendly dish but, I'm sorry to say, did not suit my personal taste.  My grandkids said it tasted like "that stuff in a box that has the hand on it" (Hamburger Helper).  The dish is easy to put together using basic pantry items.

I am giving this five stars based on the flavor and the fact that I am not an experienced cook.  The potatoes just would not cook for me.  They were sliced super thin but even after two hours they still were not tender.  I will try this again and cook the potatoes before baking and hopefully that will help.  Thanks!!

We enjoyed this! I didn't use the canned soup though, made a white sauce instead but did incorporate your seasonings and sour cream. Dh and I just finished the rest of it for leftovers, still tasty! After taking the foil off, I rose the heat to 400 degrees, and the potatoes cooked just fine. I'm thinking about cubing the potatoes next time. Very good casserole!

This was really yummy! I made a few changes to bring it down to 7 WW pts: 4 lg. potatoes, only 1 c of 2% shredded cheddar which next time I will put ALL on top of the casserole, and of course FF soups, light sour cream, skim milk, etc.

I omitted the onion in the sauce just because I didn't feel like chopping more. I'm glad I did - it might have been too onion-y with it. Also, I sliced my potatoes about 1/4" thick and it took 90 mins. to bake. Will definitely make this again!

I easily reduced this recipe by half for my family size. The only changes I made was omitting the green pepper (due to preference) & I reduced the onion to 1/2 total. It was a really good, filling & tasty dinner. The only change I would make next time is reducing the seasoning salt in the sauce. The dish was just slightly salty. But it will definately be made again! Thanks Kittencal!

I've made this 2 or 3 times now and could swear I already reviewed it!  Well, we really like this!  Last time I made it, DH had 2 friends over so I used 1 1/2 lbs of ground beef and a couple extra potatoes.  We normally have at least half a casserole leftover, but this time it was almost gone!  I commented to my DH and he said one of his friends had 2 huge helpings because he thought it was so good.  So here I am getting ready to make it yet again, this time for OMAC.  Only change I made was to leave the onion out of the sauce.  I feel like I'm always thanking you for your great recipes, Kittencal!  My family and friends wouldn't be nearly as impressed with my "cooking skills" without your great recipes!

This is a good budget stretcher, I used minced pork since thats what I had and added corn and mushrooms. The kids ate it all up without the usual carry on and there was plenty of leftovers for lunch the next day. Thanks again Kittencal
Crazy good! Whole family gobbled it down.
Very good! We'll be having this again. I'm always on the look out for a new hamburger casserole meal.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.

This was amazing! We were running low on food and I didn't feel like running to the store. I had all ingredients on hand and tossed it together. The only thing I did different was boil my sliced potatoes for about ten to fifteen minutes. It took about an hour to bake. Excellent recipe and will be making it again. My usually picky children ate two and three helpings!
This was so incredibly good I couldn't stop eating it LOL
This was very well recieved at my Sunday Dinner, but I had to cook it longer to soften up the potatoes..though I did add extra potatoes...tasted great
This was a great easy recipe. Everyone loved it!!  Thanks

This recipe was wonderful.  I made it directly as the recipe stated and did find it a bit too salty and the potatoes took a little longer to cook.  But taking that into account for my next time this is an excellent recipe that is great for a quick-throw together meal.  Thanks Kittencal!

This was awsome, creamy, gooey, cheesy and tasty!  I cannot use onions as my family doesn't like them so I used onion powder.  Will double the beef next time per the request of the family and potentially par boil the potatoes.  The dish cooked for the required time and potatoes sliced using a food processor, but cook definitely use a little pre-cooking.  Awesome dish though the whole family loved it.
My family liked this a lot! Mine baked for about 1 hr 15 min. Definite make again. Thanks Kittencal!
This had a "delicious" taste, however I did not like it with the potatoes. The next time I make it I will use Egg Noodles or even Tater Tots.

I really like this recipe.  It's a bit richer and a little saltier than what I normally try to make - but that doesn't mean it wasn't YUMMY.  In fact, I find it to be an addictive comfort food that I can't stop eating!  I ended up using one can each of Cream of Mush. and Cream of Chick., because that's all I had.  Also, I used a red bell pepper.  The red pepper flakes are great in the meat - gives it a nice zing!  I did have to cook it almost two hours to get it really bubbly and the potatoes cooked through.  I might have cut my potatoes a bit thicker since I cut by hand - not a mandolin or processor.  Thanks Kittencal!

I halved this recipe, and cooked for the recommended time. It turned out perfectly. We really liked the flavor, especially using about a teaspoon of bacon fat to the meat mixture. Thanks for yet another great recipe!

Yummy! I made this for dinner last night thinking that there was going to be so much leftover that I would need to freeze some, but my hubby said that wouldn't be necessary. Between the two of us, we ate about half the pan! I think both of us are having some for lunch today too. I added mushrooms to the beef mix and used american slices in place of cheddar between the potatoes and beef and sprinkled mexican blend cheese on top at the end  (that's just what I had on hand). It did have to bake longer than posted for the potatoes to cook through and it did take me a little longer than I had envisioned to assemble the casserole. So next time I will microwave the potatoes a bit and cook the beef a day ahead. I did feel it was missing something in the end - needed something to brighten the flavors (maybe the absence of cheddar cheese is the reason for this). My hubby put some sour cream on his and I reached for the ketchup he despises - we were both very happy. :) Thanks!

I thought this was pretty good and had a lot of flavor, my husband thought it was just ok.  I decided to preboil my sliced potatoes and I left them on a little too long so they were pretty much cooked when I put them in the casserole.  I was worried so I adjusted the cooking time to 20 min uncovered then added the cheese and it actually sped things up nicely since I didn't have time for it to cook 1 hour.  It did take a good amount of time to assemble and filled up my dishwasher pretty good so I might look for shortcuts next time. My favorite part was the crusty cheese on top of the beef. thanks!

Delicious!  I was surprised how wonderful this casserole tasted, considering the basic ingredients, which I had readily available at home - bonus.  Very tasty and satisfying dish.  I did microwave the sliced potatoes first, due to a shortage of time.  My family loved this casserole and I will make it again.  Thank you Kittencal for sharing.  I've made several of your recipes and they are always a delight.

W-O-W this was good! Boyfriend called it "an instant classic." I followed the recipe exactly, except for the sour cream, I used http://www.recipezaar.com/Mamas-Cilantro-Cream-Sauce-166779 which is my standard sour cream substitute. Was absolutely fantastic. I actually halved the recipe, and was thinking that I would have to send some to work with my boyfriend, I always send the extra food for him when I make too much, but I was surprised to find that there wasn't any left to send him! This was absolutely amazing! Thank you!!!

excellent recipie which my whole family enjoyed
Excellent! Tender, moist and flavorful. Loved the combination of seasonings. Used homemade yogurt and cooked on the stovetop in a grill pan. Thanks for sharing!

Great recipe with a nice blend of flavors. Each one had a turn to stand out, but no one flavor dominated. very tasty, we are doing a low carb thing so we switched out the sugar with spelenda and couldn't tell a difference!  it was great!
This was good...not great, but good. I used cinnamon instead of cumin. Very easy to follow.

Flash fried in a frying pan to get some colour on the chicken-didnt need to add oil to fry at the yoghurt mixture made sure it didnt stick then finished off in the oven

loved this recipe!  served it with a side of steamed green veg and rice

Love it..kids love it too! Made this tonight. Everyone loved it. The spice blend is just right. Served with grilled eggplant and salad. Great meal!

Despite all the reviews, we didn't find this very flavorful at all.
This is an awesome recipe. Perfect for summer grilling and having a middle eastern type dinner. I have hummus, pitas and cucumbers to round out this meal.
This was good.  Marinated overnight.  I added some Essence from Emril on it.  I will do the same next time or try doubling the spices.
Great recipe!  I didn't add the oil at all and it was still REALLY good!

Seriously?  This is dream chicken! I marinated the chicken for a good 48 hours and I baked them babies in a Pyrex dish for 45 minutes @ 450 degrees and I was in heaven.  Soooo moist, sooo flavorful.  So easy too! Definitely a dish I will cook for the rest of my life.
Great flavour and wonder combination of ingredients.  We thouroughly enjoyed this marinade, thanks for sharing.

this was pretty popular with the family although not exactly to my liking as i'm more a fan of spicy than sweet but when my 5 yr old cleared her plate i knew this recipe was a keeper. thanks
We love this! The blend of sweet, sour and a hint of heat are perfect! This is going in my "favorite recipe" file as I know we will have it again and again.

I enjoyed this a lot. Wonderful flavor.  Will definitely make again.  Would be great for company, too.  My husband made a sandwich with the chicken, sauce, and some salad on a french bread roll. This is really good… a little more work, though, than someone like me who is not overly fond of cooking likes to do, but I will definitely make this again because the flavor is well worth it. Loved it!!! 
I am passing on to all the Italian in laws!!!

amazing!
