Unfortunately, I hadn't saved this to my cookbook, and I wasted 30 minutes tracking it down to make again tonight at the request of my kids -it is cold and snowing! My kids give it 5 stars!! (my picky 6 year old son actually gave it 11 stars!)  The kids even helped make this one.  They LOVE this recipe.  Makes a TON!!! Nice cross between a dumpling and a noodle! Thanks for posting - these are far better than bisquick and better than the tortilla "dumplings".  These are terrific!!! A must try!!!!!!

Fantastic Recipe!!!!! My whole family loved it, I used the paper bag trick described in one of the reviews.  It worked! I had to tape the bag down so it would stay put. Thank you Susie for sharing your recipe, It has become a family favorite!

This was the best chicken & dumpling recipe I have ever tried, each step explained very well. 
It took me awhile & I made huge mess but it worth it! The dumplings turned out GREAT!
It was delicious!!
This is a great recipe.  The dumplings are very simple to prepare.  My picky six year old and 3 year old twins had 2 big bowls each.  Thanks for posting.

This was a very good chicken and dumplins.  I used four bone in, skin on chicken breast instead of a whole chicken because I don't care for leg and thigh meat.  It turned out just wonderful and will feed us for a few days.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe.
The best Chicken and Dumplings that the family ever had! True southern comfort food. Thank you for the recipe.

I made this for dinner last night and it was a big hit.  I will add this to my recipe collection.  I served this on top of homemade mashed potatoes and it was fantastic.  Perfect comfort food for cold days!

Thanks for the great recipe!

I normally don't like to give star ratings if I don't follow a recipe EXACTLY as written but in this case I will make an exception.  The only thing I changed was the dumpling.  The chicken part I followed to the letter.  The DH thought he would like to have biscuit-type dumplings.  This recipe is so delicious.  Today's left-overs are going to become chicken noodle soup.  I will make this again and again!  Thank you, Susie!
Absolute perfection! This is one of my family's favorite meals, now! Excellent flavor and consistency. And it's really quite easy to make!

Just perfect! I'm so glad I found this recipe--I have always had trouble getting it just right. I followed the recipe with the exceptions of making half as many dumplings and adding homemade egg noodles (which was not necessary). I used Seasoned Salt where poultry seasoning was called for, same amount and white pepper rather than black pepper. This dish got rave reviews and is definitely a keeper. I can't imagine it any better.

The best chicken dumplings I've had in a long time! The flavor was just how we like it; the dumplings were nicely seasoned. The only change I made was to use butter instead of margarine. This is now a favorite for us. Thanks!

perfect!! i used some leftover chicken and cut the dumpling recipe in half (cause there are only two of us to eat it). the dumplings were great, the flavor was great, and my husband couldn't stop moaning. he gave this recipe 10 stars. thanks for the awesome recipe, susie :) you texans sure know your chicken and dumplings!

This recipe was very good. The meat, the broth, the dumplings were all very flavorful. The only problem I had was that when I halved the dumplings to roll them out, that half was plenty for the pot, so I had a whole half of dough to roll out. I when ahead and cut the extras, froze them flat, and bagged 'em for later. Thanks for the posting!

Fabulous dish!! The dumplings are the best! One tip: if you want to make the dumplings ahead, after cutting them, dip one side with a little flour so they won't stick together and put in refrigerator until you are ready to use them.

Very good! I've never made dumplings that were rolled before, and they were delicious and easy to do with the pizza cutter. I rolled out on a wax paper covered counter. Only changes I made were to use butter for margarine and 2 tablespoons chicken soup base for the bouillon cubes. I wouldn't cut down the amount of dumplings, but more chicken could be added if desired. Reheats beautifully. So comforting on a cold winter day! Thanks, Susie!

Another Texan who absolutely loved this recipe!  My five year old daughter enjoyed helping me roll out and cut the dumplin's- the whole family gobbled it up!  Much better than the "drop" dumplings grandma used to make!  Thank you for sharing!

Great Chicken & Dumplings! DH devoured them. I usely make the fluffy kind,now these will be the kind that I will be making. The recipe is very easy to make, I halved the recipe for the 2 of us, used 2 LARGE chicken breast all the veggies & spices that the recipe called for. Instead of chicken bouillion, I used chicken base. The leftovers was delicious for lunch. Thanks, Susie!
absolutely delicious!  this reminded me of the chicken and dumplings dish at Cracker Barrel- made TONS of dumplings- a huge pot full!
This was a very tasty meal. I had never use eggs in my dumplings but it made them so much better.  Will be using this from now on.  Thanks for posting.
This is wonderful and well worth the effort to make.  My 7 year old asks for this one when we have the can bicuit kind by saying she wants the "good chicken and dumplings"

Every once in awhile you come across a recipe that just knocks your socks off and this was one of those recipes!! The entire family scarfed this down and it was just so delicious! I used about a cup of Rescued Turkey Stock and only 4 chicken boullion cubes. I frozen the leftovers in single servings so that I could reheat a small amount to stick in the thermos for lunch. Thanks so much for posting this, I will use this recipe again and again! :)

I had never made dumplings before.  These were delicious.  I took some to work for a co-worker to try- She said she has been making dumplings for 20 years and these were better than any she had ever made!!! Thanks for a wonderful recipe.
Oh my gosh, this was wonderful.  And the leftovers were even better!  I had it for my DH's birthday dinner party and it got rave reviews.

This was my first attempt at chicken and dumplings and what a success!  My husband loved this dish.  He orders chicken and dumplings at restaurants whenever he can.  Now I've got a restaurant-quality version to make right here at home.  Thank you!

Made this for dinner tonite,used half recipe. Excellant flavor, don't know what I did wrong, dumplings mashed up when chicken was folded in. Dh really enjoyed it.  Said it should be rated higher.Will make again. Thanks for posting
Wonderful recipe!  Reminds me of my mom's homemade noodles instead of dumplings!

I am new to the dumpling world, but if this is what they should be like, sign me up! This was a hearty and soul satisfying meal for a family of sickies, and I would easily recommend it to anyone. Thank you for sharing such a heart warming recipe.

Susie...these were the absolute best chicken and dumplings I have ever made...and I am famous for my FORMER recipe!  Easy to put together from everyday ingredients but so full of flavor. The dumplings rolled out nice and easy and cooked up yummy!  The only change I made to your fabulous recipe was to add one can of cream of chicken soup to the broth ala Paula Deen.  I am under strict orders from the entire family to only use your recipe from now on!  We will be making this often during the cold months ahead..true comfort food.  Thanks for sharing.
My family enjoyed this but we all thought 1/2 onion was overpowering.  Next time I will use green onions.
This recipe is very good..... My whole family really enjoyed it.
This was a great new way of making this dish. The dish was awesome.Dumplings makes alot only used half. Froze the other half for next time. Thanks
Excellent flavor!!!  My men love dumplings but I found it just made too many so next time I will halve that part.  Thanks so much!

What can I say that hasn't been said? This recipe was awesome. We could not stop eating it. What comfort!! The only thing I did was add cornstarch/water mix to thicken it up a bit. Thank you for a keeper.
This was awsome, the only thing I did was add a little chicken stock to give it more soup. But otherwise this recipe is awsome!

I halved the recipe and modified it (because I only had three chicken breasts on hand), stewed it in the crockpot for seven hours on low, dumped it in a large pot and threw in baby carrots, onion, and three diced potatoes.  It got raves from five of my party guests and my mom and I ate two bowls myself.  Awesome recipe.  Reminds me of my grandma's homemade noodles too!  Remember not to make this too far ahead of time (I let them sit for 3 hours on warm), the dumplings will absorb all the broth and you'll be left with dumpling stew.  However, no one complained ;)

I used a 8 piece cut up fryer instead of a whole chicken, much easier for me to handle.  I did not add bouillon cubes and the poultry seasoning was salt enough for me. I used butter for the dumplings and made them a little too thick so had to increase the cooking time and broth, but still very good, my husband loved it.  Next time I will add more onion and carrots and then frozen peas at the end as well.

This was an awesome recipe! My teenage sons couldn't eat enough--neither could I!  I used two cut up chickens and boiled them in chicken stock.  I used a large whole onion and about 10 carrots, chopped.  The taste was perfect.  I WILL be making this again.

The chicken in this dish was very moist. Many recipes I looked at recommended that the chicken be cooked for 2hrs. My whole chicken was 3 1/2lbs & the 1hr was "perfect"! I removed 2c of broth from this recipe for a future recipe. I used two other recipes for the dumplings Recipe#182140 Recipe#151771. I will use this recipe again for the broth & instructions on cooking a whole moist chicken. Thank you Susie in Texas!

This review is for the dumpling part of the recipe only. I usually make chicken and noodles with more of a bread type dumpling, but I wanted to try something different this time for the noodle/dumpling thing.  They were easy to make and tasted delicious.  They also filled my need to have both since these are much like a chewy noodle without being dry like a bread like dumpling can be.  I used a little garlic and onion powder instead of poultry seasoning.  This recipe makes a huge amount of dumplings.  Next time I think I will halve the recipe since it is only my daughter and I.  Tip:  Do not make these too far in advance unless you can leave them in a single layer on the counter until you need them.  If you try to stack them, they will stick together and become a solid mass once again.  You will need to re-roll and cut them again.  Even heavily flouring them did not prevent this from happening.  However, the heavy flour will help thicken your broth nicely.  Thank you for a different dumpling (then what I am used to) that I plan to use again.  I love the texture.

Susie, thank you so much for this AWESOME recipe!! My hubby and I loved it! (my puppy did too!) I halved the dumpling recipe--it made plenty! I also cooked the chicken  and veggies in the crockpot. This recipe is so simple and so good. Thanks for sharing!

I'm giving the soup here five stars becuase I absolutely loved the flavor, but I really didn't like the dumplings - I ended up taking them all out and throwing them away.  Then I called my mom who is from the South and got her Dumpling Recipe which made the soup perfect!!!

I've made this 3 or 4 times now, and didn't realize that I hadn't posted a review!  YUMMY!  It makes great dumplings, the prep time is certainly rewarded by an excellent meal!  My kids fought over the leftovers to take in their lunchboxes this week!  Thanks for sharing!
Yummy!!!!  Rolled dumplings have a better texture, and these are perfect!

I made this last night while DH was watching the superbowl. This is just wonderful- comfort food at its finest! I started this the day before and let the fat come to the top of the broth in the refrig and skimmed it off before continuing.I also used freezer paper, shiney side up, to roll the dumpling out on and it worked great! DH said "yummy" with his first bite and " you can make this antime!" as he was getting his second bowlful! Thanks for posting this- it's a winner!

judt liek i remeber when i was growing up....   i did cook it just as recipe cooks  except i didn't have time to roll out the dumplings , I made a half a batch of dumpling mix  & used a tsp  & made small fluffy dumplings with it by scooping it out by the tsps full... I will defentility make this again & again....just the thing to warm up with when cold weather hits....

This is definately good southern comort food. It is a lot of work, so you may want to save it for a weekend. 
I made half the batch of dumplings, and only used 3 bouillon cubes to cut back on salt. Save the leaves of the celery, chop them, and add them at the end for extra freshness and flavor. I may also add a bay leaf for next time for flavor depth. Very good meal!
This was great - ultimate comfort food :)  We halved the dumplings and still found there were tons!  This was a really good recipe - thanks for sharing it!

this is dish brings me feelings of nostalgia. this was my favorite dish as a little girl, my late grandmother made it for me when i came to visit her in north carolina. i am 23 now and havent had them in like 17 years, mainly because no one could make it like her, this recipe seems like her own. great job!!!!!!!!

Tried this tonight...it's now an all-time favorite!!! Such a flavorful and comforting meal for a cold day! And it's a lot easier to prepare than it seems. I used 1/2 cup of butter, green onions and I sliced 3 carrots instead of shredding them. I didn't have any poultry seasoning so I mixed equal parts dried basil, oregano, thyme and rosemary with a few cracks of ground pepper as a substitute. It turned out wonderful!

I made this last night for my sick DH and he said it was the perfect dish to make him feel better!  I myself enjoyed it too, what comfort food!  I did make a few changes:  I used 3 1/2 pounds of bone in, skin on breasts, made half the amount of dumplings, sliced the carrots and added peas towards the end (I love my vegetables).  I thought the chicken/dumpling ratio was perfect for us, but I think this is the first time we ever had chicken and dumplings!  It was great, makes a ton, and I am looking forward to trying it to see if it is as good after being frozen!

These were really, really good and flavorful.  My mom always made dumplings with drop dumplings, I'd never rolled them out like this recipe, but I loved the texture, and the poultry seasoning added so much flavor to the dumplings.  I made a double batch and there were not any left!!
What can I say we loved it and will be using this recipe again, thanks

this is the BEST,Chicken and Dumplings I have ever put in my mouth.The dumplin's were very tasty and easy to make.Thank you Susie in Texas for such a fine recipe.What a comfort food keeper!
Rose of ShaRON
Wonderful!!!  Needs fresh ground pepper!

With the first hint of fall in the air, I was craving some good, simple comfort food. When I mentioned this dish to my BF, he replied, "I've never had that!!!". I couldn't believe it! I knew I had to make it then. I just finished preparing it, and all I can say is WOW! I followed the recipe exactly, but doubled the onions, carrots and celery since we both love our vegetables! I also added an extra 1/2 c of the chicken broth at the very end as I folded in the chicken to add a little extra gravy. It was exactly what I was craving...will post again once BF gets home from work and tastes it for his very first time! Thanks Susie!

The best yet.  This is the third recipe for Chicken and Dumplings I have tried from this site.  All of them were good, but this was the best.  Ad a bay leaf to make it even better.  Even my picky eater wife (the Princess) liked it.
Greg,
Barrow, Alaska

My family really liked it. My dumplings didn't look as good as Pamela's. I guess I let the dough get too warm. And my dumplings did soak up the broth so I had to keep adding more. No problem though. It was still good. Will make again.

I did make it again and cut the dumpling amount in half for us it was just right

This was fantastic! My family just inhaled it- and with 9 people eating and everyone liking it- that's a major accomplishment! lol Thanks so much for posting. This is now my family's default chicken and dumpling recipe!

The flavor is out-of-this-world delicious! You weren't joking when you said it makes 'a bunch of dumplins'. I only made half the recipe and still had more than enough. And mine were kind of doughy. Next time I'm going to try the old standby drop dumplings and see if they work better for me. Thanks so much!!

This is soooo GOOD! I changed so many things..I can not rate this properly. (I used what I had on hand).  But, I will tell you what I did. ;) First I read all the reviews. A must!
Chicken Substitutions: 4 Leg quarters. Ingredient substitutions: 1 tsp dried minced garlic, Pinch pepper flakes, 1/8th tsp celery seed, 1/4 large onion, Frozen green bean and carrot mix (3 large hand fulls added with one hour remaining in cooking time), I packet of poultry gravy mix **extra: added I bay leaf.

Halved the dumpling mix. added the egg to the stock and mixed the egg in with a fork, added to flour mixture mixed well. Sprinkled with a bit more flour (1/4 c) and mixed until just not  wet looking...but not OVER mixing. 
Placed the de-boned cut up chicken back into the pot..returning pot to a boil. Reduced heat to soft boil, dropped large tsp fulls of dough into stock. Cooked 15-20 minutes. Covered. Stirred gently about 2 times.

At first I was afraid to make the dumplings because my husband is not a lover of soggy bread/dough...I too have never been a fan of the Dumpling part either...But this was not the case with this. We both absolutely loved it! I had never made Chicken and Dumplings...As a child, my mother used to make it..and I just dreaded it. She was a great cook..but not with dumplings! LOL This recipe..the dumplings have this awesome flavor. This recipe is so versatile you can add or take away anything you like to adjust it to your own taste! Great recipe! And It was really easy to do. Thanks for giving me a new staple recipe, I will definitely pass on to my children. ~sandesnow

I was tempted to give this recipe 3 stars just because I had such a hard time putting it together. But, in the end I am accepting responsibility for that. I cut the amount of dumplings in half and had a REALLY hard time getting the dough to a consistency that I could roll out. I had to keep on adding flour until it seemed like I must have doubled the amount! Maybe I measured something wrong... :S Anyway, we weren't very impressed with the final product but I think I should have kept cooking it longer so it would thicken up more. I reheated the leftovers on the stove and let it boil for a little while and it was MUCH better! I will definately make this again and am confident it will be even better next time around!

Lots of work; next time I'll be sure to pace myself. My whole family really liked it (even my brother, who had previously claimed that "all dumplings taste like nothing"), and I even got my picky fiance to eat some vegetables (apparently they were too small to pick out). Followed recipe exactly, save for the carrots, which I diced instead of shredded. Thickens significantly if left to sit for a few moments, or reheated. I may need to add a can of broth to our leftovers.

As I was making this, I told myself "This had better be good, cuz it is sure alot of work"... then after one bite I realized that it was totally worth the time and effort!! Used boneless chicken breasts as a time saver... will definitely make again!

Have made this twice now and we just INHALE the stuff!! Haven't found one similar recipe for chicken and dumplings here on Zaar that can hold a candle to it!! I halved the dumpling batter and it was perfect for the amount of chicken mixture. This goes into my permanent file :-) Thanks!

After all of the great reviews, I honestly was disappointed with the result.  My dish, while it had flavor, lacked depth which left a kinda flat feeling in my mouth.  My family liked it, but didn't get real excited.  

On the broth, I think part of this may have been my fault - my only change here - I used 4 chicken breasts instead of a whole chicken which might have been more flavorful.  Next time, I think I will use thighs and legs like my Grandma used to and brown them in a little butter and evoo first, before adding the water. I will also use a bigger pot so that I don't have to worry about boiling off some liquid to make room for the chicken and dumplings. I ended up having to add a can of broth at the end because my result was too thick.

The dumplings (why I chose this recipe) reminded me of what my Grandma used to make minus the poultry seasoning.  I used garlic and onion powder instead along with a few tablespoons of the chicken fat (replacing a little of the margarine) that  I skimmed off the broth for flavor.   Just note that your flour may not need all 2 cups of stock.  Mine didn't, but my daughter wasn't listening so the result was a gloppy mess.  After lots more flour (almost a cup) we saved the dumplings.  Yes, it really makes a whole lot and no, I shouldn't have cooked them all.

Thanks for the recipe, I will use it again with a few changes and a sprinkling of chili powder on top!!

just to add to my previous review, once i posted it a friends daughter came up for a bowl and she inhaled it.  LOL she did not even sit down to eat, she stood in the kitchen and ate so fast that she never got to the chair. i did change the broth a little by browning the chicken pieces and deglazing the pot with water and using the roast chicken seasoning that comes in a grinder spice jar instead of regular poultry seasoning. This gave extra flavor.  Some things i will try next time are making it a thicker stew,as well as using more onions and deglazing with white wine. Probably removing the dumplings after cooking to thicken/change the base and then readding them.  I think that they need the lighter broth to cook in. 

However just as it, its a flavorful deep chicken stock. Best way i can describe it is the perfect combination between homemade chicken soup and stew with dumplings.

Good home cookin'. Just like my Mom's except she never put poultry seasoning in her dumplings. I can't wait to make this again and again. This is a good recipe to work with as everyone can tweak it to their own tastes and make it their own and no one will leave hungry. That's for sure. *wink* Thx for posting this Susie. I'll be sure to add a photo the next time I cook up a batch. :)

This made a very nice meal.  I halved the dumpling mixture and this made an ample amount of dumplings.  I also managed to have enough uncooked dumplings left over for freezing (stored in between sheets of baking paper to prevent sticking).  The dumplings reminded me of potato gnocchi.  My husband thought the meal was like a combo soup/pasta dish.  Being Aussies we don't come across food like this very often, so it was a lovely change!  Thanks

Wow, this is pure comfort food.  Didn't change a thingwith the chicken and broth part except next time I may cut some of the skin off the chicken because there was alot of fat on top.  Did use my dumpling recipe I've used for years.  Which is just flour, baking powder, salt, oil and milk.  Was worried that the broth wouldn't thicken up but it did nicely after adding the dumplings.  Thank you for sharing a great recipe.

One of our household favorites -- the kids get soooo excited when they see the chicken simmering on the stove, because they know the dumplings are coming soon!  Only additions were to include a lemon, cut in quarters, to the broth while cooking the chicken, and a little extra parsley and thyme to the dumpling mix.  Great recipe, thanks!

I made this about a month ago and forgot to review it. These taste just like what my grandma used to make. Thanks so much for the great recipe.

I am new to this site and this is one of the first recipes I came across. I had to give it a shot this weekend as my husband was born and raised in Texas and "craves" his grandmother's chicken and dumplings, made with the rolled-out dumplings (and I don't have the recipe). Thank you, Susie in Texas - another validation that Texans cook this stuff up right! p.s. Oh, I did add one large can of cream of chicken soup to the broth when I added the veggies just to make it a little creamier.

OMG this was DELICIOUS!!!!  My boyfriend loved this so much, he had me make it twice in one week! I also made only half of the dumplings... there were plenty! The first time I made it, it was a HUGE mess... but so well worth it! The second time was easier! Thank you!
Really good stuff!  I halved the dumplings and still ended up with a ton of them.  There's no way I'd even try to fit in the amount that the recipe calls for.  I'm not sure they'd fit!

Perfect!  I hadn't had chicken and dumplings for over 10 years, much less tried to make them myself, and these were exactly what I'd hoped for!  I was going to freeze both servings, but have changed my mind and am having one for dinner tonight...I did already freeze the other or it'd be eaten also!  Just for the record, I loved having all of the dumplings, but I thought it could use more carrots and celery.
Old-time comfort food worth the effort.  Only thing I would do differently is add a little Tony's to up the flavor a bit.
DANG!  So Good.

I finally got around to making this recipe, I've had it printed out forever.  Anyway, it's just delicious and really makes a lot of food.  My family of 3 plus 1 guest ate ourselves silly, then I sent some to my ex-husband and the guest took some home and my husband and I had enough for another full meal tonight.  I made it exactly as written, though my chicken was a 5-pounder.  Thanks for posting this comfort food, perfect for Autumn, recipe Susie!

This is one fine recipe! I have never made this type of dumpling before and we really enjoyed the little devils. I did have to make a few changes because of what I had on hand. To start with I only made a half recipe and used 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts. I used about 3 carrots cut into rounds. I did seem to run a bit short of stock so next time will increase that a bit. However, the flavour is wonderful. My family says it is a keeper and we thank you for sharing your recipe.
Awesome stuff...I like my soups and stews to be thick so I thickened it with a roux (equal parts of butter and flour cooked over low heat until browned). USE A SUPER BIG POT...this is good stuff.

This is a very good recipe.  I do like biscuit type dumplings better, but my hubby is just raving about these dumplings!  So...I will compromise and make a batch with both biscuits dumplings and these! =)  Makes a lot of dumplings, just like I like.  I did add another celery rib and an extra bouillon cube.  I think next time I will add more chicken.  But all in all...this is FABULOUS! Thanks

Hubby, kids, and I loved this! "The best chicken and dumplings we've ever had" to quote them.  I gravitate toward home cooked meals from scratch.  My two-year-old even got in on the action and helped roll the dumplings out.  A true keeper.  Thanks for such a wonderful recipe!

Again... I'm from Seattle and DH is from Georgia. "Can you make Chicken and Dumplings?" he says. I reply: "You want me to dump chicken on what?". Easy dish - the directions are great for anyone to follow. I used butter-flavored shortening and made the dumplings (per request) quite a bit larger, so the cooking time was closer to 25 minutes. This was an exellent Chicken and Dumpling recipes.  Full of flavor and just what we were looking for. I've had this recipe saved in my cookbook for some time and am so glad I finally got around to making it.  Thanks Susie.  Just wonderful.
This is great! I made it, we ate half and froze the other half. I defrosted it last night and it was just as great as the first night. Thanks for sharing!
This was a real winner! Next time I think I'll half the dumplings as there were a ton. Thanks for this really good recipe!

This rating is for dumplings only, I used my own soup. This is a great dumpling recipe.  Very easily altered and manipulated.  I did not use stock I used water and I used plain Crisco shortening.  I also added dill because I use dill in my soup base and cracked pepper and so I left out the poultry seasoning.  NO mixer used either just a heavy fork.

Just made this and boy oh boy was it great!! I am not a fan of chicken dumplings but this has converted me and DH hasd raved at how great it is!! I did make a few changes since i thought I had items on hand and didnt. 1. I added the bouillon cubes with 3 large breast (the kind you get in the bags) to boost the taste of the stock (a trick Grams taught me). 2. I cut the celery back by 1/2 just our taste. 3. I thought I had all-purpose flour but only had self rising and only 3 1/2 cups of it. I did use whole wheat to roll the dough out with it added some really good flavor and texture. 4. added a teaspoon of garlic powder to the dough (i will a a bit more next time). Oh make sure you let the stock cool!! I didn't and I had to pop it in the freezer to get it a workable texure. My DH loved this and will have this diuring these cold winter nights. Thank you for a great recipe Susie!! additional comment: We got hit with snow and ice  Wednesday night knowing  most of the local delivery places were not delivering Thursday I made this for work. I trippled the recipe for the soup and doubled the dumpling (worked this in batches to make it easier to handle). I work with all men and every single one of them LOVED this. That may be, but it can be made with far fewer calories, without sacrificing the great taste. Use a lean chicken and be sure to remove all fat and skin, use whole wheat flour instead of white, and use Smart Balance butter instead of shortening. For this to work you'll need to add more liquid into your dumpling dough - I use almost double. Try adding a bit at a time, until feels and looks right. If you want to get really picky you can use four egg whites instead of two eggs, or one egg and two egg whites. Once these changes are made, you are left with a healthy, tasty comfort food. Enjoy.

Most of that I froze for later because it made 6 gallons or so.  I used about 2 gallons for this recipe.  I used all the remaining turkey meat from the bones and added chopped carrots and onions and seasonings to my tastes (I used some sage, rosemary, and basil, but the original recipe or whatever you like would be fine too).  For the dumplings, I forgot at the last minute that I was out of eggs, so used Ener-G egg replacer, and it worked fine.  I was also in a hurry and had no time to roll out the dumplings, so dropped them by teaspoofuls into the broth.  They cooked up fine!  I suspect the texture is a bit different done this way, but the dish was still delicious and my husband loved it.  The kids, unfortunately, refused to even try it!  This is the first time I have made such a dish and it looked very strange to them--too mushy looking I think.  More for us though.  I plan to try again rolling out the dough, but will probably half the dumplings.  I cannot imaging how they all could fit in only 1 gallon of soup.

I usually make drop dumplings.  This is my first try at rolled dumplings. This is the only way, for me now. Turned out perfect.  I mixed them in my processor, first I mixed the flour and seasonings, without the poultry seasoning.  Then the rest of the ingrediants. I had to add a little extra flour until it came away from the sides of the bowl.  Then I cut small pieces of dough and rolled it out a little at a time on my cutting board.  They were so tender and good.  I like my soup to be brothy and it was. They did not break apart or make the soup to thick. Thank you so much for these dumplings.
Best Chicken and Dumplings ever!!!! I even liked it better left over!

Hubby LOVES chicken and dumplings and is really picky when it comes to them. I took it as a huge compliment when he said these were the best he's ever eaten! Only thing i did differently was used boneless skinless chicken breast (partly because I got them really cheap but mostly that's the only kind of chicken I will eat). This is a great meal on a cold day so will be a staple in our house in the winter months! Thank you for posting!!!
My husband loves chicken and dumplings.  He raved over your recipe...and he is very picky.  Thank you for a wonderful, hearty and very tasty recipe.  This will be a staple in our house from now on.

This is my FIRST time of ever fixing chicken and dumplings. I have not had this since my mother passed away in 1996. I love to cook and I really suprised my DH. DH says,"this taste just how mom would make it." LOL Thank you for posting this wonderful reciept and making my life easier. I added more carrots, onions and celery plus added chicken broth for a little more flavor! This is an awesome reciepe that will be in our household forever.

This was a huge success with my family.  I used Wondra to prevent the dumplings sticking to each other and froze the dumplings I didn't cook on single layers of waxed paper sprinkled with Wondra.  The Wondra, in addition to preventing sticking, also helps thicken the broth without changing the flavor.  Tasted great!!!  Thanks so much!

I vegetarianized this recipe using Quorn Chik'n Tenders and it was delicious! The dumplings weren't what I was expecting, they didn't cook up right, but that could have been my own fault. I am typically satisfied with a single bowl of soup, but I went back for seconds, that's how yummy it was. Thanks for sharing!
I thought this was just Ok. I guess I don't really like THAT many dumplings.

Came back to print this again, my other one has been worn out LOL! (need to get it laminated or framed HEHE!)
This is just the most incredible recipe for chicken and dumplings we have ever made.  I love the addition of poultry seasoning to the dumplings instead of just the usual flour salt baking powder.  It gives them an even better flavor and you can eat more and more, thankfully this recipe makes a good bit of em!  My daughter is leaving for Army boot camp in a few weeks and gets to pick our menus till then, this is on it twice and a must have the day she returns!!  Thank you Susie!
5 STARS ALL THE WAY!

HOLY SMOKES BATMAN! These dumplings are crazy wonderful! It does make a huge huge amount. But I think they taste better the next day. The soup is tasty too! I have recommended this recipe to many , many. It also is my stand by for making a dish to give away. The poultry seasoning in the dumplings make the difference..I actually upped it too 2tsp. Try this recipe , you wont regret it!

Why is there no 10 star options for recipes as fantastic as this one!  Despite the fact that it was over 90 degrees on the day I made this, every last bite was eaten in one meal by my family   guests!  I have already been asked to make this again!  And have also been told to "can & sell it"!  So to say it's a hit, is an understatement!  Total perfection!!  The time it takes to make it, is completely worth it!
I found the dumplings to be tough. I like a more fluffy dumpling and the broth wasn't what I expected.  A little too bland for my liking.
Very Good!  Used canned biscuits because I was short on time.  Soup flavor was delish!

Made this for the family last night.  I am not a dumpling fan and neither is my oldest daughter, but my husband and youngest daughter loved it.  My Husband said it reminded him of the chicken soups his mom and aunt made when he was a child.  I thought it was seasoned perfectly, except I did add quite a bit more salt and pepper as well as veg then called for.  Also the recipe wasn't clear as to when to add the veg, so I added about 1/2 way through the boiling and then removed with the chicken while the dumplings were boiling.  I think out of personal preference next time I will bake the dumplings like biscuits and then add them individually to each bowl.  Thank you for posting, this will be my new chicken soup base recipe!!

WoW! This one is a real keeper! Not the easiest thing in the world to put together, but the instructions are like gold! This was really homey- delicious Thanks so much for taking the time to instruct on making the perfect chicken n dumplins in my opinion!

I made this for guests tonight. I'm usually scared to try a new recipe for the first time on guests. I had a fairly large Dinner party and it's cold today so I doubled the recipe. That made A LOT. This was great I didn't have chicken seasoning so I used seasoned salt, added more than specified. One of our guests are from the South and they all loved it! Thank you so much for sharing. I will use this again for SURE!

very good! I felt like the dumpling ratio was perfect, and so did our guests. when making the dumplings, i added a teaspoon of powdered chicken stock into the flour mixture and thought it gave it a bit more flavor than it would have had other wise. also, I sauteed the onion, carrots, and celery in a tea of olive oil for 5-8 minutes covered in the stock pot before adding the broth back in. I chilled the broth slightly after removing the chicken to separate the fat out. don't feel it was lacking any flavor from removing the fat. we feel like it could have fed 6 adults as a main dish.

The dumplings were gummy and pasty. I like mine puffy. I did like the poultry seasoning in the dumplings. I browned my chicken in a dutch oven first, then removed the skin and added chicken broth (not bouillon), boned the chicken and returned to the broth with the celery and carrots.  The recipe was easy to follow and the flavors were good.

Given the time and effort required to churn out this soup, I found the results to be disappointing. My boyfriend and I both found the stock to be bland, which surprised me as I added much more seasoning than I usually do (heaping teaspoonfuls of rosemary, thyme, sage and garlic powder as well as four or five bouillon cubes to the stock, chicken seasoned with a hefty coating of salt and black pepper).

As for the dumplings, even though I planned on halving the recipe and forgot to halve the emulsifying ingredients along with the dry ones, the dough was still way too flaky and dry, and I had to double the amount of margarine and stock (resulting in four times the ratio of emulsifying ingredients to dry ones). The end result, as others have mentioned, was thick and gummy dumplings.

I think my results might be a fluke given the multiple rave reviews, but I'm not sure I would invest the time and energy for a second try.

Added more veggies & made a roux to thicken the soup.  Had lots of extra dough for dumplings & didn't care for them much.  Think we would like more biscuit like dumplings personal preference.  Loved the soup.

The flavor in the broth wasn't bad, but kind of bland. Now let's talk about the dumplings.  They were horrible.  So thick and gummy and slimy.  The texture was just awful.  I can't believe all the great reviews.  I wonder if they really made them!  I will stick with my drop biscuit dumplings.  They are so much better!!
Made this tonight & loved it!  I didn't have any celery & was out of poultry seasoning, but it didn't hurt the flavor.  I halved the recipe, & it still made a large pot of dumplings.
awesome, the best!

We are southern transplants. The first time I ordered chicken and dumplins' at a restaurant here, I thought they must have run out of dumplings and substituted with thick egg noodles. They were very good, just not what I was expecting. When the owner of the restaurant asked how we enjoyed our meal, I asked about the dumplings. She said she always gets questioned by visiting "yankees". I now know that how this dish is prepared is very regional. These are not my grandmas dumplings, but they are really,really good. Sometimes we're in the mood for "northern" ones and sometimes in the mood for "southern" ones. It's great to have a choice. Thanks for posting a great recipe.
Never had bad chicken and dumplings but this is one of the best I've had!

This dish is truly restaurant quality. As a matter of fact, it beats the chicken and dumplings I last had at a restaurant. The broth was just insanely good. The dumplings -- yes, there were a ton of them, were chewy and just-right-dense (scrumptious). I did add more veggies, and used chicken breasts; and froze half of the dumplings, not so much because there were too many, but I wanted some in the freezer for a quick repeat of this meal on a busy night. Susie, you made me look like a master cook! Try this recipe. I'm so glad I did.

Wow! This recipe is the one! FABULOUS!!! I made these tonight and changed up a few things. I didn't do any of the vegetables. After the chicken got done boiling I put my 2 cups of broth to the side to cool. After I got the two cups out it didn't seem like enough juice for me. I like a lot of juice so I opened up 3 can of chicken broth and added 4 cubes of the chicken seasoning and 2 cans of water and and added a tad bit of chicken season. I then let that cook for about 15 minutes while I was making the dumplings. Rolled out the dumplings in 2 sections and they turned out AWESOME! This recipe Rocks!! Thanks for sharing it!!

Wonderful recipe for Chicken and Dumplings!!  I used about two-thirds of the dumplings, but wish I had only used half.  I froze the remaining dumplings for the next time I make this.  Yes.  There will absolutely be a next time.  It's terrific.  Thanks for sharing your recipe, Susie.

Have made this a dozen times with the leftover rotissierie chicken from Costco.  Works perfectly.  I toss the entire chicken into a large pot of boiling water, add boullion cubes, carrots, garlic, onion.   A few hours later I remove the "chicken" and take all of the meat off the bones and proceed on with the regular recipe from there.   My 3 kids beg for this recipe whenever we have leftover chicken.  I usually serve it with mashed potatoes.
Yummy recipe.  My pot was a little small to fit a whole gallon of water, so I didn't end up using all the dumplings.  It makes a LOT of dumplings.  Great recipe!
Excellent
I thought this was a very bland recipe and the dumplings were very heavy and tasted like pure flour.  Will not be making it again. :-(

This makes a lot of dumplings.  I only cooked half because I was afraid I wouldn't have enough broth once I added my chicken back in.  I probably could have made more than I did.  This recipe was good and could probably serve more than it states, but that's ok, it just means more leftovers for us.  A great rainy day meal.

Delicious!  I totally believe that review about a diner selling out of this recipe and having to make two more batches that day.  This recipe makes classic good ol' Southern chicken 'n dumplings.  Not fluffy dumplings (so if you want that, this isn't the one for you).  You can halve the butter and use some oil to make up the difference (just as yummy).  Only thing was I needed to add salt and pepper to the broth.  Completely filled up our largest soup pot.  Love it.

We got our first snow of the season here yesterday...of course it was a chicken and dumpling night!  ;)   I doubled this recipe, didn't include the veggies, added just a tad of milk with cornstarch (we love ours thick) and it turned out WONDERFUL!  Doubling the recipe made a HUGE amount and I love that not only can I now freeze a very large amount, we will have this amazing hot comfort food to eat on all week!

This was excellent! I had never made rolled dumplings before and the dough was wonderful to work with. I added a little milk at the end as we prefer a creamy sauce with our chicken & dumplings but otherwise, I made as directed. Thanks for a great recipe that I will make again!
12.13.12 Updated - Made this many, many times now. It's still a great recipe. This last time I used split chicken breasts that I roasted in the oven. Roasted at 400? for 30 minutes to crisp up the skin then put into the pot of water with the pan dripping. I must say, it really made for a richer, deeper chicken flavor. Did everything as written and the family just ate and moaned (with delight). Thanks again for a wonderful recipe that I make quite often!
Mighty tasty!
The chicken and gravy in this were delicious, but the dumplings were really doughy and heavy.  I will make this again but use mini biscuits instead.
Great!

This is a very good recipe and easy to make. It was very much like the chicken and dumplings my aunt in East Texas made but I think the dumplings in this recipe were better. I like the rolled dumplings cut in squares in this recipe better than the old fashioned drop dumplings. I had the neighbors over and we fed seven people with plenty left over. Was surprised at the number of servings in this recipe. The only thing I did differently was to use chicken with herb and spice bullion cubes rather than the ordinary ones. VERY GOOD! I will make this again and again.

This recipe is AMAZING!!! Except for the fact I added a whole tablespoon of black pepper instead of 1/2 teaspoon the recipe calls for (oops!!) ...it came across a bit peppery, but luckily, my husband is from the islands and loves spicy food, so he really enjoyed it! I LOVE the dumpling recipe, they came out PERFECT!!!! This is will most certainly be a weekly meal in my household!
Delicious!  The dumplings in particular are heavenly- like little clouds bursting with mild flavor.  The broth was basically just a broth, but I love these dumplings!

Can I give this 10 stars? This recipe is excellent! Very easy! This tasted just like my grandma's recipe! I used 3 big boneless chicken breasts for this and cooked as directed, and still had a ton of flavor. The dumplings was easy to make, and tasted awesome! Even my picky kids loved it! The next night we had left over's, and I fried up some chopped bacon, and added it to the soup, and oooh LA LA! It was wonderful. I paired this with home made biscuits to sop up the juice. This recipe will be filed in my recipe box! Thank you!
Very satisfying on a cold winter evening.  I did cook the chicken the night before, also skimmed the fat off the broth. This was great because of all the dumplings.  Thank you!
If you just "drop" the dumplings, they aren't real Texas or Southern Dumplings. They must be rolled or they are just dough balls.

I only made the dumpling part of this recipe and it was exactly what I was looking for. I wanted a dumpling that didn't crumble apart during cooking and these were just right. I only made half the recipe and still had a decent amount of dough left once I filled my pot of soup full of dumplings. I used the leftover dough to make some thick, country style noodles, once I rolled the dough out a bit thinner, and froze them. Can't wait to try them in some beef Stroganoff. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

I've been looking for a recipe for chicken and dumplings like my grandmother use to make.  This is it.  I made it exactly as the recipe stated.  At first, I thought the broth would be a little too soupy.  However, it thickened just the way my wife and I like it.  The dumplings were excellent and are the way dumplings should be (Southern style).  I thought I was putting too many dumplings in the pot, but they cooked just fine and my family had plenty of leftovers.  This is a saved recipe for us.

This was a fantastic chicken and dumplings recipe that my entire family loved. I made a mistake somewhere though because my dough ended up being more of a thick goo so I just dropped it into the broth by the teaspoonful instead of rolling the dough out. The look wasn't as pretty as the flat dumplings would have been, but the taste was still amazing. I'll be using this recipe from now on.

I have made this many, many times. It is one of my families favorite meals. I make it just as the recipe is written which says a lot! I almost always make a tweak. This is just one of the most delicious soups I have ever had. We fight over the leftovers!
worst soup ever I puked bare

Phenomenal! I had originally printed this recipe in 2013 and just now got around to making it - big mistake! I wish I had made this sooner! This recipe got rave reviews from all in attendance. I used a 6 pound chicken and made the full batch of dumplings. This has so much flavor. It took me around 2.5 hours from start to finish. I added ground red pepper for a little heat, not flakes, ground. Now that we're headed into summer I'll probably tuck this away until fall, but I cannot wait to get it back out!
Decent soup but not chicken and dumplings.....it's soup with dumplings in it.
Pennsylvania Dutch call this slippery pot pie.

That's what I call noodles, not dumplings. Dumplings are fat, puffy, soft things and I use biscuit dough with extra milk and just drop them on top of hot stew, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until done and not gooey on the bottom anymore. Chicken or beef stew, works with both, and everybody loves it.

I was stuck in the house with the weather and wanted to make dinner with what was on hand. Had all but red/yellow bell peppers. Added mild banana pepper instead. It was great! What a pleasant surprise meal. I can't wait to experiment with this one.

Excellent! I've made this almost 'by the book', (I usually use Basmati Rice.)and in all sorts of variations. I've subbed. Shredded beef, shredded pork, shredded turkey, and precooked pork charizo. It works well with pinto, white, great northern, and kidney beans. I've even used 'Ranch Style' brand beans, un-drained. It's also fun to play 'mix and match' with the cheese. A blend of sharp cheddar, jack, and asadero is particularly good, so is sharp cheddar and mozzarella. thanks for posting this great recipe. Pierre

The only thing I did differently was add about 1 1/2 t ground coriander with the spices, and the juice of a lime at the end.  I also did not drain the beans, so I omitted the water.  I only used one poached and thinly sliced chicken breast halve, and we didn't miss the extra meat.  We ate it with lots of hot sauce.  Quick, easy, and reheated very nicely.

Super easy and delicious! I was in a 'clean out my pantry and fridge' mode and this recipe really fit the bill. I only had a green pepper so used that plus a can each of corn and chopped tomatoes, both drained. I also added chopped jalepeno slices for heat. This recipe is very forgiving; it would be hard to go wrong. I will definately be making it again. I served it with a little salsa on top, and sour cream might be good on it as well.

This was good and really easy to whip up.  Didn't have bell peppers on and.  Tossed in half a bag of frozen corn instead of the peppers.  Also tossed in a can of diced tomatoes, and skipped the cheese for a healthier dinner.  This was good and worked really well for everyone including kids.
The kids loved it. It was easy and a great use of leftover chicken. I used converted rice, it keeps its texture better than white rice in dishes like this.

This was a very tasty, one pot meal that was perfect for a weeknight dinner.  The combination of ingredients worked well together and everyone enjoyed it.  Very colorful too, from all the bell peppers.
This recipe was great.  I made it cold to compliment some warm miso soup.
This made a delicious, healthy and filling lunch!  I used a green chili pepper (including the seeds), otherwise made as stated.  Yum!  Thanks for posting!  Made for PAC Fall 2009.

This is very tasty with a strong Asian flavor. I normally have my soba noodles warm so this was a nice change. I made as posted, including the cilantro. I like that it is low in calories and fat. Thanks for posting. :)

This was so cute!  I forgot the buttermilk, so I made the box recipe, and they were still wonderful.  I couldn't find orange M&Ms (found black), so I used Reese's Pieces instead of M&Ms and the taste was fantastic.  Finally, I only made 24 cupcakes, so I arranged them a little differently, using 3 on the bottom, 4 next, and then followed the arrangement listed.  Since I absolutely stink at frosting, I was glad to find something that didn't require that, although I way underestimated the amount of time it would take.  It was well worth it though.  Thank you for sharing!

This is such a fun Halloween recipe!!! I only managed to get 25 cupcakes instead of 26, so he had a bit of a shorter stalk at the top, but I don't think it really mattered; the overall result still looked amazing! I imagine kids would love placing all the M&Ms on the top. What a fab way to use cupcakes!

Mmmmm.. I loved this - then again, I love mushrooms.  Very easy to make and quick too, as long as the ingredients are prepped ahead.  I didn't use any white wine, and subbed in chicken broth.  Made for Went to the Market Tag Game.  Thanks for posting!  YUM!

Excellent Chicken Scaloppine. What great flavor even without the wine. I used homemade chicken broth in place of the bouillon and white wine. I think it added an enriched flavor. I also dusted my chicken breast with a little flour before browning. Just before adding the chicken and mushrooms back to the sauce, I added a couple of tablespoons of cappers.  Yummy.  The sauce was just wonderful and the chicken was so moist and tender. Thanks so much for a keeper.

This is fabulous! I loved every single bite. I served it over fluffy mashed potatoes and everyone loved it, except of course the picky DD that hates mushrooms. But even she liked the chicken and sauce. I didn't use a cube or wine, just used chicken broth in place of both. Made and Reviewed for 123 Hit Wonders Tag - Thanks! :)

Very good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written other then I didn't use the wine but added water instead. My kids even liked it, they just pushed the mushrooms to the side and daddy ate them. Loved the sauce and the chicken was so tender. Will be making again.
By the breadth and depth of the "kiss-the-cook" kiss I received from my husband, I believe I just might have to make this more often.  Made for Everyday Is A Holiday.

Easy to prepare and SO wonderfully delicious. I added some minced garlic and rosemary, sage and thyme to my mushrooms (must include ingredients for me), used my Recipe #135453 rather than the bouillon cube and a low fat cream which was certainly creamy enough for us. We thoroughly enjoyed this with my Recipe #330028 and steamed spinach. Thanks so much for a delicious recipe. I had several serves to put in the freezer, and we look forward to enjoying those in the future! Thank you for sharing this yummy recipe, wicked cook. Made for Zaar Stars Tag.

This was a hit for the family last night at dinner.  This was very different from the Scaloppine recipes I have had in the past, no lemon juice or garlic, but still tasty.  I used 5 thin chicken cutlets and subbed regular onion for the green onion (personal preference) and did add a teaspoon minced garlic.  I also coated the chicken lightly with some seasoned flour prior to browning.  I first cooked the mushrooms, onions and garlic and then set them aside while chicken browned.  I then added them bake with the chicken and followed as written.  I served it with my Recipe #345703, green beans and bread sticks for a wonderful meal!!!  Thanks for sharing a new twist on scaloppine.  Made for Stars Tag.

Following suit here, a wonderful addition to your family table. I flattened my chicken breasts with a hammer and placed in between plastic wrap. (the chicken :) ) and used chicken broth instead of bouillon. This made a beautiful presentation especially with the green onion and mushroom sprinkled about. Will be making this again! Made for *Everyday is a Holiday* August 2009

I enjoyed this very much. My only regret one thing and that is not making enough sauce. I decreased the recipe to feed 2, therefore I decreased the sauce amount. the sauce was tasty. Made for I Recommend Tag.

We enjoyed this but thought there was something missing...like a spice, sage, thyme, oregano not sure what but it lacked the wow I was hoping for. It's very easy to prepare and the chicken was nice and moist. Overall a really good dish. I served it with recipe #360824. Thanks for posting. :)

This was a really great dish. I used chicken broth in place of the wine as well. I also sprinkled my chicken breasts with a little flour, salt and pepper before cooking. We really enjoyed this dish. It is light tasting and not heavy at all. I served mine over penne pasta with broccoli. Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag November 2009!

I think the sugar must have been left out of this recipe accidently? Granted I didn't have wheat bran or soy protein (substituted with more flour). But I still think maybe it needed a cup of sugar. Also, I diced the fresh cranberries. I think whole ones would have been too much. This recipe has potential, so if anyone has any tweeks, I'd be willing to give it another try.

This batter was excellent! A must-try the next time you want something fried with a very crisp, not too thick coating. Excellent taste as well. I did some chicken tenders, then some fresh flounder fillets, then some shrimp. It was all incredible! Next time I will make some hush puppies, and it will be just like eating at the restaurant! Thanks for posting. :)
I thought the batter was terrific. I used it on scallops, chiken and Fish. They all turned out excellent. My family really enjoyed it.
I made this batter for fish, turned out really good, nice and crunchy. I did not deep fry the fish, I shallow fried and was surprised the batter stayed on the fish. Excellent!!
Fantastic.  Easy to make, and the batter stay on.
I made this for frying catfish fillets.  (we caught them!) I was getting tired of the beer batter and was craving Long John's fish.  This was exellent!  Thanks for posting!
So good!  Worked great, I fried them up in my electric skillet with some canola oil.  MMM!

We tried this recipe with some sole. We'd estimated the amount we'd need, and put the rest in the freezer. After the first batch had been cooked (we cooked in a large frying pan with some oil) we added some extra spices and quick thawed the remaining fish. No dessert for us that night, we had an extra serving of fish instead. This recipe would be good to batter anything....veggies, chicken, fish, apple rings, mini chocolate bars, etc. Just vary the spices to whatever flavour you want and go to it.
Excellent batter! I used it on catfish as well...and it turned out fabulous. My grandparents arent thrilled about fish, but they even enjoyed this!!! Made it with hush puppies and oven potatoes!

This really was an excellent batter.  I made it up an hour before I used it as I have heard that this makes batter 'stick' better to whatever you're frying.  Anyway, it stuck.  Light, crisp and not greasy - exactly what I was looking for.
mysterygirl this was the best.  I have been looking for a good fish batter for a long time.  I tried it with flounder, deep fried.  I can't wait to try it with scallops.  Thank you so much.

I tried this on onion rings and I took some sweet banana peppers and split them and removed the seeds and battered them and fried to a golden brown, excellent. I think you could batter any thing with this recipe.

I'm not a fish lover, but my husband caught fresh fish this weekend and I had no choice but to cook it.  It was great!  I followed the recipe exactly, and it was light, crunchy, and not greasy.  I can't wait to try it for onion rings.  Yum!

I tried this batter with some Orange Roughy filets and it turned out delicious.  I also took a cue from Jim's review and used the remaining batter to make onion rings.  WOW!  Deep fried them both in my trusty Fry-Daddy.  My whole family loved this fish batter.  Thanks for sharing! :-)
Bought the parents an oval fish fry pan and this mix was a great addition for the theme.
Fantastic batter!  I used this on some fish last night.  Unbelievable!   I've never made batter that came out this good.
I used cod, and the recipe turned out excellent.  It took about 5 minutes at 375 degrees.  Wonderful flavor.  Thanks for sharing a keeper!

This recipe is exactly what I've been looking for! This batter is perfect, it was quick and easy to prepare and the results were great. I'll be using it again and again. Thanks for posting it Mysterygirl!

Great recipe. The first time I ever got batter to stick. Since my husband loves to fish I'm sure I'll be using this alot. Next time I think I will add some spices and kick it up a bit. Thanks for the recipe.

Mixed this batter up for some fish my brother-in-law brought over and can I just say how impressive they turned out!!!! They fried up so brown and puffy and looked like they came from a restaurant!!! Followed the recipe exactly, although I used seasoned salt, and would probably use a little more than the 1/4 tsp next time. My husband also dipped mushrooms in the leftover batter and fried them up too. Thank you for such a wonderful recipe, will come in handy during Lent!!!!

this was a great fish batter.The only problem I had was I have a wire basket in my deep fryer and the fish stuck to it.The next time I'll just fry them up in a pan.But this is a great fish batter recipe will use it again

i've always had a problem getting batter to stick,i just used this recipe and it sticks great and it tastes great as well.thanks so much!!!!
        susie
Talapia never tasted so good!!! This was excellent, it was identical to Long Johns. It was so crispy and crunchy, but not greasy at all....Thanks Mysterygirl
This is an excellent recipe--very light and tasty.  It will be a regular with us.

**********
There, ya got the ten stars you deserve...
Since some recipes call for Club Soda, I replaced that with the plain water...Don't know if it made a difference but it sure was good...My fish choice was Cod...

This batter is good in terms of its crispiness/texture, but 1/4 tsp. of salt is totally inadequate unless you're on a restricted salt diet.  I thought this sounded like an awfully small amount, so I added twice as much, and it was still a tad bland.  Next time, I will add a full teaspoon.

Of course, we all have our different taste preferences, and this is a terrific base to work with!  Thanks a bunch!
I thought this batter was excellent!  It has a nice crunchy taste and doesn't overwhelm the fish.  It's better than beer batter.  I used a little more than 1 lb of fish.

First, when this recipe was first posted LJS was running commercials saying they were using Pollock. Lately those commercials have been saying Haddock. You might want to look at those types of fish if you want the LJS taste. My review is based on whether it tastes like LJS. I see a lot of people criticizing others for basing their reviews on that. Isn't that the point? This is pretty much just a variation of most Fish and Chips recipes you find. It does not taste like LJS. It was somewhat bland. That's not to say it's not a good fish recipe, but it's not LJS. Anyone who's ever had LJS knows it has a somewhat odd taste to it. This doesn't have that. It takes like a standard Fish and Chips recipe. I did it no dredging, cornstarch dredging, flour dredging, and season flour dredging. None gave me the taste or consistency of LJS. That might be hard to pull off. The consistency of of LJS is almost like a fillet. I don't mean fish that was filet but actually more like a processed fish filet or a boneless chicken breast. If you've ever had LJS fish and chicken, the consistency is about like a McDonald's chicken nuggets. It might be hard to get the exact consistency unless you use some type of fish streak. But whatever that odd taste that LJS fish planks have, this does not have it.

good heavens this is amazing!  took to two parties and it was the talk of the foodies!!  recipes was given out to several people!  excellent thanks so much for sharing :)

LOVE this stuff! It's sooo good with gingersnap cookies!
I wasn't sure how this would be, but I trusted the ratings and it was really good.  I took it to a party and it got some good compliments.

Easy and quick to make and tastes just wonderful!
this is delicious! I read the ingredients and had all of them on had because this is very basic recipe. IT WAS GREAT. thanks!!!

Yum. I made coffee-gingersnap cookies to go with it, and apple slices. Though I didn't chill it, it was still fairly cold. Tasted awesome.
So good and so dangerously sweet! Everyone wanted to eat the whole thing.
I thought this was very tasty. Makes a lot.
Delicious.  Made for a party tomorrow.  I think it will be a hit.  I alsom made granny's gingersnaps to go with it and will slice some apples to take as well.

This was really yummy dip I served with homemade snicker doodles that I had cut into strips before baking and with the apples as suggested.  Thanks this recipe is a really great alternative to pumpkin pie and it makes a lot of dip!!

This dip is very good! It wasn't the least bit runny like some said. The taste is great, the texture is great and the color isn't yucky like some suggested either. Mmmmmm! Try this!
mmmmmmmmmm great recipe!!! THanks!

MMMmmmmMMMmmmMmmm!  I brought this to a jewelry party tonight and didn't leave with any leftovers!!  Everybody raved about it, more than the jewelry :) I served sliced fugi and green apples and homemade gingersnaps #355691, turned out wonderful! Thanks so much I will make this very often!
This turned out great, everyone loved it.

Ok, I was SO dissappointed in this! This was fabulous!  I did not have pumpkin pie mix, so I used a can of solid pack pumpkin and added 1/4 of a batch of recipe #192409.  This went over great at the family gathering that I took it to. This was fantastic!  Will be making this again and again.

I brought this to a holiday party and it was a huge hit!  So easy to make and absolutely delicious!  I sliced granny smith and fugi apples and soaked them in a water/lemon juice mix for about 5 mins and then dried them with a paper towel before putting them in a feezer bag to transport - they stayed crisp and didn't get the slightest bit brown all night. Great recipe! I actually made two batches for a holiday party- one of them with soy cream cheese so that my boyfriend could eat it since he is lactose intolerant. Both tasted great and surprisingly the lactose free version was the favorite! Thanks!

I made this to take to work for a potluck and it was fabulous!  I had requests for the recipe.  It was so easy to make and tasted great!  I served it with graham crackers and cinnamon graham crackers.

I had pumpkin dip at a friend's house and fell in love.  This must be the recipe she used because it's as wonderful as I remember.  Thanks for posting!

I made this for our annual sleep over with my cousin and it was a huge hit with them and me. I love the spicy flavor and with ginger snaps it has even more zing. Great dip for any Fall event. Everyone wanted the recipe, too which makes you know it's a hit.

Wow, how yummy! One of my friends commented that I should just give her the spoon and she would eat it all by itself!

Delicious-this was the hit of the office potluck with ginger snaps and graham crackers (some people even added whipped cream on top to make mini pumpkin pies). Yum!

I made this to take to a pot luck lunch at work. It's the first time I've come home with a container that's almost as full as it was when I brought it. Placed all the ingredients in a lightly buttered casserole dish and kept warmed in a 325 degree oven for about 10 minutes while I finished up preparing the meal. Served with lemon wedges. I made these to go along with a spicy chicken dish. They were delicious!

Easy and delicious! Thanks!

MAKE THIS!!!! This is so good and a breeze to make. I cannot get over the flavor this has for being so easy to put together! I will dream of these tonight they were so good! Thanks Lennie!

My kind of recipe!  Very easy to make and the flavors are not overwhelming.  The panko is a interesting touch.  It creates a little more crispiness than regular breadcrumbs. This recipe is great for a quick weeknight dinner.

Somehow magically I had exactly enough of the dry and wet ingredients.  That truely is a rare and beautiful thing.  I too wish it had browned up a little more but it was a delicious easy to prepare dish none the less.  I increased the garlic to 6 cloves, pulverized in the mortar and pestle.

I liked how these came out and I'm going to use this again!

Another wonderful chicken recipe to add to my cookbook.  I finally found panko but had to go to an Asian store for it.  This is a very flavourful recipe and we just loved it.
Very nice, very easy and used ingrediants I always have on hand. I didn't change anything! i served this w/baked sweet potato fries. YUM!

I can't believe I never reviewed this recipe ! I will never fry chicken strips again. I mixed the panko with some italian bread crumbs just to get some additional flavor. Absolutely delicious ! I had honey mustard and hot wing sauce on the side to dip them in. I make these often.

Delicious.

This is a great recipe. I made it on Monday and my husband wants me to cook it again tonight. We are on Weight Watchers and this is one we can enjoy and it fits our points.This is my first experience with Panko. Its truly delicious.

Very light and tender, I finally tried this recipe after having it in my cookbook for months! I think this would also make a good appy with a dipping sauce. Thank you for turning me on to panko! My local Kroger even carries it. It's so light that I threw away my regular breadcrumbs. This is a great, simple recipe and very kid friendly.

This was so good! I had never used panko before, but I really liked it. Our chicken did not get brown really, but was super moist and delicious. Next time I'll turn up the oven to 425, as other reviewers have mentioned. Thanks for the great recipe!

I can't believe I haven't rated this recipe yet. I love these chicken strips and so do my kids and DH.I have made them several times. Great recipe! I just used boneless chicken breast and fellowed the recipe as stated and made chicken sandwiches instead of strips. We loved the flavor and we also liked the panko breading. Thanks for sharing this garlic chicken recipe.

OVERALL great flavor and texture however took more time than stated to get it to brown.  I ended up cooking it 15-20 minutes ON EACH SIDE.  I used all ingredients listed with 1lb of boneless chicken strips.  Will likely try this one again in the future.  Thank you!

Excellent...simple...tasty!
Thank you for sharing it has become a weekly staple at our house. :-)
Really terrific mild flavor. The panko is light and crispy and the chicken was really, really tender. We tripled the garlic.

All in all this is a great recipe especially for garlic lovers. Thanks Lennie!

Made these on Super Bowl Sunday (I'm not a hot wings fan, so had to have something I could eat!) and really enjoyed them.  I prefer the Panko breading to traditional because it has a different and lighter texture.  Will be making again!

so yummy!
