Great recipe! I added some salt to marinade and Italian seasoning to the crumbs. The four of us didn't take long to finish these off.

I'm giving this 5 stars because I got 2 picky eaters to enjoy these!  I used seasoned breadcrumbs and went light on the cayenne.  I love hot, but the kids don't!  I let it marinate for about an hour and made these more into strips than into bites.  Really easy and my strips baked for about 20 minutes.

These were very nice and quick to put together.  I doubled the garlic and the cayenne pepper and used Italian Seasoned Bread Crumbs which gave it a nice flavor.  Cooking time was right on.  Used this to top off a salad for dinner tonight.  Thanks.  Made for I Recommend Tag Game.
Quick, easy and super tasty!  I cut the recipe in half and served the chicken with tater tots and a side salad for dinner.  Yummy!  Thanks for sharing, Mirj!  **Made for I Recommend**
These are delicious - tender and flavorful.  Such an easy recipe to throw together.  I made as you posted except that I found 1/4 cup oil was sufficient.   Thanks for posting.

Nice. These were easy to make and eat. I used panko instead of breadcrumbs. My chicken breasts were huge, so I could have used more evoo, and did use closer to 1 1/2 c of crumbs. So much fun to eat with my kids! We made a finger food supper night and they had a blast. These litlle guys had some bite to them. WE LOVED that!! Thank you!!

Sensational for Picky Kids, they gobbled it up! We all loved it.  This was so moist and flavorful. I used panko bread crumbs and omitted the cayenne pepper (for the kids). Simple and good.  Easy to serve and holds well in a crock pot or steam table. I had to make a huge number of appetizers and this was one I chose.  I served them with a thai chili sauce for dipping.  I would season the crumbs a little more next time and maybe serve a variety of sauces.  They did take longer to cook than suggested. Thanks for a great appy.
Really easy and good.  I make these for dinner and my kids eat them like nuggets.  So much healthier than store-bought nuggets.  Thanks for the recipe!
Awesome! I would love a bit of salt though!

Delicious & easy finger food! I made the marinade in a ziploc bag (less mess!) while frozen chx breasts thawed in the sink. I used panko bread crumbs instead of regular & added some salt to both the marinade & bread crumb mixture. Also went easy on the cayenne b/c we don't like our food too spicy. Will definitely be making this recipe again. Thank you for posting! :)

These do not disappoint on the garlic flavor at all!  I made these for our New Years Appy Buffet... for 2.  I used a pound of chix tenders and cut them into thirds. I used Italian flavored crumbs and baked on 400 for about 20 min cuz that's what I needed the oven on for the other stuff.  The flavor was even better tje next day.  May use this recipe to make my cutlets from now on.  Thanx, Mirj!

Excellent, excellent recipe. Well obviously this is a classic taste that is as good for snack, a dinner party, a great appy, or just eating them on their own. I changed nothing except used cornflake crumbs (out of breadcrumbs) mixed with the cayenne pepper and garlic powder. Just such a special treat, so easy, and quick. this chicken recipe was awesome!!!!! the chicken stayed really moise and juicy. all of the flavors of the marinade and the coating could be tasted in every bite

These are delicious.  We just ate them for dinner.  I added 1/4 tsp of salt and cooked at 425 for 15 minutes.

This came out awesome! I made this for an office potluck and it was the first thing gone! Everyone wanted the recipe!

So good, so easy and a great recipe to prepare.  I made these for game night and my family loved them.  I plan on making them this fall for football Saturdays as I know my guests will lvoe them.  My kids want me to make them this weekend for dinner.  Thank you for posting this highly loved recipe.
i should have added less cayenne pepper

My husband said he'd give these 7 stars if he could! The chicken was so tender and juicy. I baked them for 10 minutes then turned them over to brown the other sides for 2 more minutes. 
Yum! This recipe is stellar!

The recipe only needs a little tweaking with salt. I had looked through the comments beforehand, and added salt to the breadcrumbs, but this was not sufficient. The next times I make this recipe, I will add 1/2-1 tsp salt to the marinade. Thanks!
Lovely! I made them with just garlic powder and omitted the cayenne because the picky kid was going to eat them, but you can bet I will make as directed next time. Thanks, Mirj!

Thanx Mirj!!

We liked them pretty well, but I felt like it was a lot of prep. I thought they were very dry (but my husband likes that, so good job). If make them again I will make one tray as directed for my husband and one tray at about 450 for 15 minutes instead of 475 for 10 so they're moister.

Very easy to prepare  Nice and quick, and they taste a lot better than frozen store bought chicken nuggets; however I want a bit more flavor so I'll probably add some onion powder or other herbs next time. We enjoyed these very much! I added more cayenne pepper but other than that, made as is. Going in make again file. Thanks for this one. Made for I Recommend Tag Game 2009.

Mirj.....This was AWSOME!  The only thing I did different was that I ran out of breadcrumbs so I used cheesy garlic croutons. Oh ... and I tripled the recipe and it still didn't last. Made this so many times and keep forgetting to come in here and review it!!!! Easy to make, kids love them, a hit everytime!! thanks for posting Mirj

Wow, this is so good. I made this as written, no changes. I did double the recipe, and I'm glad I did. Lots of flavor for little work. Everyone loved this. The garlic and cayenne go well together.. I will definitely save it to my favorites!! Thanks Mirj!
Excellent way to make chicken. I used Italian flavored panko instead of breadcrumbs. Everyone loved it!

I made this last year at my baby shower so i cant rember perfectly but i think i recall these were delicous TY mirj

Oh yah! This is a GREAT recipe! Super easy to do, and SO good! Made it for my hubby and our two little ones. My son probably at half a chicken breast all by himself, he loved it! Simple and good.  Thanks for sharing.
This was really good! I used crushed red pepper instead of cayenne because it's all I had, but followed the recipe exactly. I cooked them at 425 and they were still done in 10 minutes.

Great coating for chicken! Loved it! Thanks for posting!
I made a tofu version of this that wasn't good on its own, but which got devoured once we coated it in barbecue sauce. :)

Very good and very easy.  Two of my favorite things.  I did a trial run of these because I'm going to be making them my shops Christmas party. We served this at a party and they really went away fast... with several dips and salad they were really tasty. Thanks for this recipe!
Marinated overnight to serve my sister who loves boneless chicken during Thanksgiving. She devoured them and my dad who stole some off her plate said it tasted "gourmet...like a restaurant."Thanks.

A big hit, except a little too HOT for some, because of the cayenne pepper. Needs to have "cool" dips...

I can't remember if I've reviewed this one yet, but these are VERY easy to make and taste great!  My son will even eat them which says a lot considering he doesn't usually like chicken at all! I do have to add a little less spice to it though when he is eating them, but no big deal to us!
These were not a hit at our house, almost half the batch went in the green bin!  I would not make them again, they were pretty much just garlic coated chicken nuggets.

These are amazing! I made them last week and am already craving it again. Ranch dipping sauce is a great idea!
I used italian breadcrumbs, and I put a little more cayenne pepper than the recipe called for.
This chicken was very good and very easy to make!  Will definitely add this to my favorite recipes.  Thank you!

This was very easy to make and can be dressed up with a variety of things, depending on your preferences. I think the best thing about this dish is being healthy since there was little fat and olive oil is used instead of other fat. For the people who says that the chicken turned out to be dry, you might have overcooked your chicken. I only cooked my chicken for 10-15 minutes and they turned out perfect. Make sure you have a high temperature to have that golden brown exterior and tender chicken inside.
Excellent recipe and so easy to make.I used Panko instead of breadcrumbs.

Excellent little chicken bites! Quick prep with tasty results. I used Italian breadcrumbs and added some shallot salt for a little more flavor. My husband and I loved these! I marinated for a couple hours used italian bread crumbs for the coating and served with homemade ranch dressing. What an easy delicious recipe.
I loved these! I added Tony's and garlic powder to the breadcrumbs. They are even good cold from the fridge IF you have any leftovers. :)

We made a huge batch of these with panko and no cayenne because we have toddlers. The kids loved them. Thank You!

I made these for a somewhat large gathering of people (I tripled the recipe) and they were great! Everyone really enjoyed them. They have a nice little kick to them but they are not overpowering as far as spice is concerned. I highly recommend this recipe.

These turned out awesome! I made exactly as directed. The chicken was juicy and had the perfect amount of spice. My husband loved it as well. I served it over pasta with alfredo sauce. I'll definitely be making this again!

These turned out to be great chicken nuggets. I only had italian seasoned breadcrumbs on hand, so I used those instead of plain breadcrumbs. Other than that, I followed the recipe to a T. These chicken bites were easy to prepare, and were quite delicious. I'll be making them again soon.

My DH was such a huge fan he started coming up with other alternatives like making them with a pasta sauce/tomato paste mixture, chicken or beef, and mozzarella cheese.  I froze the leftover packets, and they heated up just nicely in the oven (crunchier) or in the microwave (a bit softer)

My family thought these were just okay after I spent hours preparing them ahead. I took them to a church function and many of them came home even though I fixed only a couple dozen. May try some other stuffing ingredients.

These are wonderful!  My sister actually made these for me after a surgery and I took it out of the freezer today, put them together and the kids are enjoying them.  I will definately make these again!!  The only thing I might do a bit different is used seasoned croutons per out taste.  Excellent recipe!

This is definitely one of my family's alltime favorite recipes! A few times we didn't have any croutons so instead we crushed saltine crackers and another time used crushed Doritos. My boys just loved it.

Four stars for the idea and the possibilities it inspires, but we weren't extremely fond of the taste of these.  That said, I'll definitely make these again, maybe using a taco/cheddar cheese filling or something along those lines.
I made these for Mother's Day lunch.  They were a huge hit.  There was not a packet left.  Everyone raved about them and I had several requests for the recipe.  Thanks for a wonderful main dish.
Loved it!  This will be a regular at my house.  Keeper for the cookbook.

We thought these were delicious! I made ahead as a OAMC dish, but since we are a small family, I split it into 2 bags. I pulled one out last night and made it up- easy and yummy! After putting the filling on the crescent rolls I had a little left over, so I put it onto a tortilla. I rolled it like a burrito and brushed it with some of the margarine- it turned out great! It was a great alternative if I ever forget the crescent rolls. Thanks for a keeper recipe!

I really liked this...well the filling anyway because I haven't tried it with the crescent rolls yet. I decided since cream cheese is cheap and I've never really done this before that I would fiddle around with the filling to see if I could come up with some alternatives. I made a couple but the one that we really liked was I left out the chives and salt and added 2 tablespoons of creamy horseradish and 1/2 teaspoon of dill weed. It was REALLY good with the chicken but it would also make a nice spread without! Thanks for posting this one!
These are delicious and creamy! The whole family loves them. I love to crouton crumb coating. You can experiment with different fillings . . . I haven't found one that I didn't like yet! Thanks!

Absolutely amazing recipe! Really easy to make! I made a small portion (half of the recipe) to test out before I add it to my OAMC cooking day list. Forgot to add the croutons, but it was still really amazing! These packets are huge

I have to give this 5-stars.  Not only did my DH and I like it, but my VERY (underlined 5 times) picky 3 year old DD ate 1/2 of one.  I used seasoned breadcrumbs instead of croutons, and onion and chive cream cheese.  Very easy to make.
Very good!  I didn't have chives but mixed in onion and garlic powder to taste and we loved it!  Next time I want to try making it with the chive and onion flavored cream cheese.
Very good!  My husband and I enjoyed this very much.  We will definitely try to spice up the cream cheese mixture next time.  Delicious, though!

WOW is the best way to say it.  My family loved these.  I purchased the new large size crescent rolls and stuff them really full and they turned out great.  My niece asked me to make them again the next day.  Thanks!

Made as directed and they were pretty good but a little bland for my taste.  Next time I'll add some salt, pepper, and garlic powder to the mixture.  Maybe some Parmesan Cheese?  Also, I was unsure if the croutons were measured before or after they were crushed.  I crushed 1/2 cup and only had enough to cover 4 packets so next time I'll crush a whole cup.  Note that doesnt' effect my review; I made a mistake a grabbed one Pillsbury can and one "generic".  Do not skimp on cost and purchase the generic.  Pillsbury was much better in taste, look, and was much easier to work with and held together better.

This is always a part of every OAMC day for me--my kids love these in their lunchbags--they actually prefer them cold.  I leave off the rolling in butter and croutons to save on a few calories and they are still yummy yummy.

These were very good, I loved them! I would absolutely suggest using the crescent rolls that are in one solid sheet instead of being perforated, then just cut the sheets into quarters. This way you don't have to deal with sealing the edges that tended to come apart for me. I also used 2 Tbsp. 'chive and onion' cream cheese in place of 2 of the regular and that worked really well. Thanks for posting Tish!

These were amazing!!  Even with some of my changes...I used 1 8 oz. pack of diced ham, 1 can crescent rolls, 4 oz. cream cheese, a few sprinkles of TS onion onion, garlic garlic, and some spinach and herb seasoning (TS too).  I also threw in some cheddar cheese...it was DELISH!  I wanted to make it with chicken and do it that way, but well it was frozen and ham was my easier alternate!  This recipe is great to use and make up whatever combo of flavors suit you and your family!  I'm so happy I came across it.  Thanks so much!  Oh, I also just sprayed the tops with Pam and sprinkled on some whole wheat bread crumbs...amazing...so happy :)

I actually was given this recipe/idea from a young couple I went to church with years ago...her mother had made these.   It's great to do w/ any leftover poultry.  One time saver I have started doing is just using the soft cream cheese w/ chives already in in (when it's on sale I grab them).  I like to use thigh meat for these, it makes them so flavorful!  I usually skip the croutons and just sprinkle italian bread crumbs on the top once I brush them w/ butter.  You really do need to mix these by hand in order to break up the chicken and get it all mixed evenly.  It helps if your chicken is a *little* bit warm when you mix it, as well.
These were good but a little bland as others have stated. I will make them again but add a little seasoning and maybe some cheese.

I had to sub a lot of ingredients but the basics are the same.  I tasted the mix as I went along and this is what I ended up with  - 1/2 of a rotisserie chicken, 3 oz of neufchatel cheese, 1 small can of green chilies, a little less than 1 tbsp onion powder, and a sprinle of shredded sharp cheddar, 1/4 cup of broccoli chopped, and reduced fat crescent rolls.  And I used cooking spray and seasoned bread crumbs instead of margarine and croutons.  This was so fantastic.  Next time I am going to try using crab meat and adding more veggies.  I think this would also be good using all veggie and no meat.  If you are making this for the first time I would go light on the cream cheese at first then add more to taste.  And make sure you either season the chicken as you cook it or add some herbs to the mix.  So so so very good.  I love recipes like this that can be changed up a million ways.
Family loved it! Easy and tasty!

These sort of remind me of a hybrid between a Costco chicken bake from the food court and a pot pie. I didn't have any croutons so I used panko crumbs with bacon salt. I think with my next batch I'll add some peas to the mixture. I will definitely try this with left over smoked salmon and dill.
This was fantastic! I basted my pockets with butter and sprinkled them with italian crumbs, but this was super easy and I can't wait to freeze a couple bags of this this coming weekend!

Just made these. Made half the recipe for a taste test. Very good. I seasoned my chicken with a packet of goya sazon for a bit of flavor. I dipped the packets in butter but it soaked up a lot, so next time I'll baste with butter. I also doubled on the croutons. They were actually filling. Thanks :)
Delicious!!! The only thing I forgot to get from the store was the croutons, but it was really delicious. Will make again.

My family loved these, and making a large batch and freezing the filling for later is great!  I am making for lunch today and adding a little cooked broccoli to the mix (maybe a little spinach) to toss things around.  Thanks so much for the recipe!

I found these very bland when made as written which is what should be reviewed.  It needs something else like cayenne or red pepper chunks to give it some flavor.  The packets are a great idea but the recipe as written is not very good unless you are looking for bland mushy food.  It also took 30 minutes to totally cook so the croissants were actually brown and not mushy.
I made these this week, and they were wonderful!  The filling is delicious, and the rolls cooked very nicely around everything.  Thank you!
I skipped the crumb coating and instead just coated the top lightly with oil & sprinkled some coarse sea salt.  Great recipe; thanks!
bland.
It was alright. My boyfriend and I weren't too fond on the bread part. Not bad though to whip up and stick in the freezer for a quick dinner. Probably won't make it again though.

Loved by all! Made this for my family as directed, except for 2 small alterations. First, I shredded the chicken after cooking. This made the mixture easier to scoop and spread around. Second, I used italian breadcrumbs on the outside because it was all that i had on hand. These are pretty easy and filling. Dad liked them so much he ate the extra chicken mix out of the bowl. Good cold, better toasty warm. I'm going to try making them and then freezing, because I know nobody in my family will want to put them together to cook.

Fairly easy and good recipe.  The crescent roll breading wasn't quite for us.  Might try making with pizza dough or pie crust.  The filling is very tastey and my family did like that.  Thanks for posting.

Family Friendly Recipe!
Hubby and litle ones loved this recipe.  We dipped ours in ranch dressing.

These were easy to make, and I liked the idea of croutons as a coating.  However, we found them bland.  My husband and I both agreed they needed a sauce or a dip or something.  I will agree with other reviewers that they're easily portable - I took one for lunch the next day and ate at room temp.  One really bright spot was that my 2 year old really liked it and was able to hold it and feed herself.  In summary, they were fine, but I probably won't make again.

One thing that I love about these kinds of recipes is that they are easy to play around with and change up. If you find this specific recipe too bland, I'd suggest using garden and herb cream cheese instead of plain. I really thought it added great flavor. And don't quote me on that - that was my sis-in-law's idea!

These little guys are so easy and SO good! I made them for Girls' Night and my friends loved them. My husband also loves them! Just be sure not to get the 10 oz pkgs of crescent dough, because there are only 6 rolls instead of 8 and there is just too much roll. Some of my first batch turned out doughy. If you aren't going to follow a recipe exactly- do a trial run first! They are also good if you forgo the croutons.

A great recipe, very versitile. I used Neufatchel cheese (lower fat) and garlic and butter flavored cresent rolls.  I spiced it up a bit by adding more chives, garlic and onion powder, ground pepper and a few dashes of hot sauce.  I also brushed butter on top vs dipping for less mess.  I let mine get pretty brown in the oven, which made the outside nice and crisp.  This recipe can be changed a multitude of different ways, as bland as you like it or as spicy.  Thanks for posting, we will make again.
I'm doing this rating for my hubby, as I wasn't a big fan but he was! He LOVED this. I've made it twice since the 1st time I made it. Pretty easy to put together, but also rich.

I had used canned chicken, and half italian crumbs and the other half plain bread crumbs. The italian tasted much better. Next time i may put less cream cheese in it, as I never even got a piece of chicken in my pocket! I will also use fresh chicken this time.
added oct. 2.- i now use biscuits, flatten them. use one rolls to put stuffing on, then take the next roll and put it on top then squeeze the edge together. its much easier!

These were great! I did change a few things. First I used ground chicken added 3 cloves minced garlic, and  s&p when I cooked the chicken breasts. To the cream cheese I added, to taste, Buttermilk Ranch seasoning from Penzeys spices. I did coat the outside with melted butter and sprinkled panko bread crumbs on top. All in all they turned out great. My Tim and teenage kids loved them. We had the leftovers the next day heated up in the microwave. I would use the oven or toaster oven next time to reheat.

16 yr old rated 9/10, 14 yr old 5/5,  DH rated 6/10.  This is certainly easy to fix ahead of time, take 1/2 hr to throw together, 20 minutes in the oven and done.  I was a bit confused on pinching the triangles together but then getting 8 pockets.  The 8 roll, only makes 4, easy enough to double.  I also like the versatility and will try to vary to get DH's rating higher :)

The Once A Month cookbook actually says 3 ounces of cream cheese. Everyone that I have served these for has loved them and requested the recipe. But the recipe alone is missing something. The first time I made these my husband and I thought they were good, but they were missing something. My husband suggested the white cheese dip from our local Mexican restaurant. Next time we tried it and THAT was it! You have to serve these with white cheese dip. They are yummy. Very much a comfort food!

I love this.  This is my GO TO Recipe for when a friend has a baby.  They are the ultimate comfort food.  I make them a bit different.  I use either Rotisserie chicken (the best flavor) or I boil chicken breasts with carrots and celery and seasonings.  Then I steam some chopped spinach and squeeze as much of the moisture out as I can.  I also finely chop some vidalia or red onion into this.  Italian breadcrumbs on top are the best flavor and I never ever have used butter on the top ( I spray LIGHTLY with PAM to make the breadcrumbs stick) and mine are golden brown.  ENJOY

This recipe was very easy to make.  So far we have made it twice, the first time just as it says to.  It was a little bland for my taste, so the second time we added 3 cloves of garlic when cooking the chicken, and instead of croissants we used the regular biscuits.  The biscuits made putting them together a little easier, but my DH said that the croissants heated up in the microwave better.  Overall, this is an easy one to do and makes great leftovers too!

Wow! My guests loved these! I truly made them ahead- I even wrapped and baked them as specified, but removed them from the oven while just lightly browned. I cooled and froze them; the day of the party I thawed them in the fridge, then baked at 400 degrees for 10 minutes. (I wanted finger food, so I made little packets- using one triangle of dough for each.) They got hot all the way through and were nicely crisp like fresh croissants!  As per other reviews, I used 8oz. chive cream cheese and 3-4 cups chicken. This was the perfect amount for 3 tubes of croissants. I added a few spices to increase the flavor. Very delicious!

I've made this several times and it's great! I've used crescent rolls, I've made my own dough and wrapped them up and I've also made a pizza out of it. Fantastic! We also add a bit of garlic and basil in with it.
I made these for dinner tonight and didn't read any of the reviews first. While they were good I'm going to try some of the suggestions listed here to make these really great.

This recipe worked and had a pretty presentation, but we found it just not as tasty as I thought it should be.  The dough was pretty bready and the interior was not as flavorful as I'd hoped.  Sorry, I see I am in the minority.

A hit with my two picky boys! I often make meals for them, thinking "this sounds really tasty, they'll love it!"...yet they don't. This is an exception, and I'll definitely be making it again. The boys (2 & 4) wanted seconds, a rarity, unless I've made macaroni and cheese from a box.
I had no croutons so made my own crumb mix with bread crumbs, Panko bread crumbs, Italian seasoning, and Parmesan cheese. I'll make a bit more next time, as the amount called for wasn't enough, I ran out. Also I used a basting brush to apply real butter, as dipping filled raw pastry is just not easy. The packets were stretching out, so basting was the way to go.
These are fantastic with 8oz. cream cheese, fresh from the garden chives, and topped with chicken gravy.
Another winner in my house. I like the crutons  Gives them good flavor.

This is a wonderful way to cook an inexpensive roast. It does make a tasty gravy. I have also used cream of chicken soup and a package of dry brown gravy mix. You can also use cream of celery soup and the onion soup mix.
Great taste and so tender!
I have made this recipe with Campbell's Golden Mushroom soup and a can of sliced mushrooms. A quick gravy to serve over noodles or mashed potatoes. Quick, easy and a nice meal for your family.
This was easy to make, and the flavor was very good. My whole family liked this alot. I will definately make this again!

!! Soooo good!! My husband would rate this a 20 if he could. The roast is so tender and the gravy was fantastic. I did cut everything in half as I only used a 2 lb roast and cooked it on low for 8 hours. I also added some black pepper and garlic powder to the roast before pouring the soup on. A+++++

This was delicious.  I thickened the gravy with some flour and water on the stove after.  It was my husband's 66 birthday and he had requested a roast beef dinner.  I had to work all day and so this fit the bill as it could cook while I was at work.  We thoroughly enjoyed it with all the trimmings.  Thanks!

Excellent!!   I used 1 can cream mushroom soup and 1 can cream mushroom with roasted garlic. I used beef broth instead of water. The gravy was terrific over mashed potatoes...just a little salty for our taste. Will try to find low sodium ingredients next time.

Took me a while to get to posting this recipe.  This recipe is easy and makes a tender roast.  I did not use the amount of water listed.  I cut that in half - it made a thicker gravy.  I used 1 can regular cream of mushroom and 1 can mushroom with garlic soup.  Very tasty.

This is definitely a man pleaser.  I made this with just 1 lb of chuck steak/roast using 1 can of soup, 3/4 can of water and 3T of onion soup mix.  Worked beautifully and was a much appreciated comfort food.  Great recipe, kc.
This was a great recipe! I did put more water in it than the recipe called for, in order to cover the roast completely. It came out falling apart and tasty! Thanks!

Great flavor.  So quick and simple.  I also threw in potatoes with the roast.  Cooked 6lb roast on low for 12 hours.  It fell apart when pulling it out of the crockpot.  I used the drippings to make an incredible gravy.  The trick to cooking roast - you can almost never overcook it.  I always undercooked my roasts and that is why they were so tough and chewy.

We enjoyed this last night for dinner but I must admit I've been making this for years! It is one of the very few recipes I will use a "cream of" soup in. I slathered it on steaks last night and cooked them for about 3 hours on 325 and they were so tender and delicious! The flavor is incredible. Served with Macaroni & Cheese & Honeyed Carrots. Real comfort food on a cold, snowy night.
Great recipe, thanks.
This is fast, easy and great.  I used a bottom round roast and it was tender and juicy.  I served the juice over penne pasta.  DH loved it.
Very good and real easy to make..so good in fact, my wife is still eating gravy on toast three days later! Hard to believe it only has four ingredients. Thanks for sharing!!

I made this for supper tonight.  We loved it. I put the sauce in a pot just before we ate and thickened it to make a gravy. It was great on the mashed potatoes & the roast. Very tasty.  Will definately make it again.

A Great comfort food. Made this with a big pot of mashed potatoes. Made gravy out of the drippings and used to cover everything (not that it needed it, just because the gravy is out of this world). There are only two of us, so I cut up half of the meat and added it to the gravy. We have been eating that on top of toast ever since (along with cold beef sandwiches). Thanks!

I have been making this recipe for years now.  I brown my roast in a large skillet before adding to the crockpot along with some extra onion, potatoes, carrots and sometimes I add a few cans of the small button mushrooms.
This is easy and very good. Thank you.
This is a favorite for my husband, and trust me- he is hard to impress. I put a 3lb roast in for 7 hours, and it turned out tender, and savory. Thanks for a good and simple recipe.
All I can say is wow!  This was a great tasting meal.  The gravy was so good.  I fixed some baked potatoes and the gravy went well with the potatoes too.  I also had only a 3 1/2 lb roast.

This recipe has been a favorite of our family for a long time!  The only difference in the way I make it is that I don't add the water.  I also add 1-2 cans of canned baby potatoes (drained) and they come out great!
Best pot roast I've ever had.  I added potatoes, carrots, and celery to bottom of crockpot and then added roast, then the soup.  Very good and easy.
I have made pretty much this exact recipe for years......the only difference really between this one and mine is that instead of the water, I use about 1 cup of wine.
I LOVE this recipe. The only difference is that when i make mine i slice a garlic clove and insert the slices into cuts i have made into the top of the roast. My whole family loves it!

This was EXCELLENT and exactly the “taste” we were looking for in a pot roast, we both agreed on that, so the Awesome Slow Cooker Pot Roast title is the perfect description, as it don’t get any better than this.  I had a much smaller roast (3 lbs.), so only needed 1 can of cream of mushroom soup, reduced the water to 1 cup to compensate for the smaller roast, and then added about 3/4 cup of water and 1/4-1/3 cup of cornstarch blended into it in the last hour to thicken the gravy a little more.  I also added 2 very large potatoes (thickly sliced) and 5 sliced carrots and that was just right for 2 people and plenty of wonderful leftovers for two-three people, plus some great beef sandwiches for my husband’s lunch, and probably mine too.  I also did add more than several twists of freshly ground peppercorns.  
This is totally comfort food at it’s finest with whole wheat bread and butter.
We really  both love this recipe, and I’ll know how I want to do my roast time.  Thanks KC so much for sharing this! ;)  It’s my favorite recipe on Zaar so far, and that’s no small thing!

This is a very good & easy roast recipe.  This is how I've been cooking roasts for years!  I also add a few potatoes (peeled and thickly sliced) and a couple of carrots (peeled and cut into chunks). The only difference is that I use only 1 can of cream of mushroom soup and 1 cup of water, mixed with the dry onion soup mix.  The gravy is to die for!  Thanks for posting this, kcdelong!  :)

Awesome though really sodium filled!

Try a few splashes of red wine in it too!!

amber

I'm not sure I've reviewed this or not, but I've used this once or twice per a recipe from the ladies I used to work for.  I had my serious doubts, but it's really delicious.  I usually put in more onions (chunks) and some carrots.  It's a keeper.
Wonderful and so easy...gravy was great!!!!!!!!!!!
It is AWESOME!!  My guys loved it
I never use canned soup for anything.I pride myself in scratch cooking.This was so good my wife thought it was from scratch.I added celery, carrots, and mushrooms.I will do this again.

I made this recently, but made it into a stew type dinner with onions, carrots, potatoes, green beans, and peas. It turned out quite nicely. I did, however, add salt, pepper, and a little thyme. I'll use this recipe again. Thanks!

Very good!  Used a 3 1/2lb chuck roast instead.  It was excellent. My picky kids ate up their helpings at dinner.  Gravy was great over the meat and the mashed potatoes served with the meal.  A certain "do again."

I made this for my neighbors. This is the only way I can try out big recipes. I used 6 lbs Roast and had plenty for me and next door and some frozen for me for another day. This is really good. Thank You...I will make this over and over. Have a wonderful day. Hugs 2 U
Very good, Gravy was awesome. I used a chuck roast...turned out wonderfully.

I have now discovered my new favorite crockpot pot roast!  The flavor of this roast is perfect.  Not too salty and not too bland ~ just right!  This makes the perfect gravy and you will not have to do a thing to it to serve.  I served this roast with mashed potatoes, peas, applesauce and crusty Italian rolls.  A perfectly comforting and very easy to prepare meal!  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe which will be enjoyed in my house for a long while to come : )
Delicious and soooo easy to make... used 1 cup beef broth instead of water
Great pot roast. Just throw it in and by the time you get home you have a great dinner. The gravy is terrific too.
This was not only easy to make, but also very good. The next time I make it I will use a little less water so the gravy gets a little thicker.

This is how I grew up eating pot roast.  The only difference is I use one package of onion soup and 1 can cream of mushroom soup mixed and no water. (This amount is perfect for a smaller roast.) The juices from the meat are always enough to make a nice gravy.  I'm going to have to make this soon - it's a good one, you won't be dissappointed.

This was very easy and the roast came out fairly tender as well. I seasoned with garlic powder and greek seasoning before I started cooking.....it still was very bland when it was done, so I had to add more. I hate to be the bad guy here, but this wasn't very flavorful to me.

I made this up, at shapeweaver's suggestion, to take to some neighbors who are expecting a baby.  (I'm trying to stock their freezer a bit.)  I snuck a taste when I sliced it and packed it for freezing.  My roast was small (about 2.5 pounds) so I used 1 can soup, 5/8 cup water, and 1/2 pack of onion soup mix.  Great recipe.  Thanks.

Absolutely the best pot roast that my family has ever eaten.  So tender and moist.  The gravy was great also.  Will be making this many more times, I'm sure.  Thanks for posting such a fabulous recipe.

Terrific recipe with awesome gravy!  Prepared it just as you printed it with one exception.  I am a fibre freak, so I added a can of unseasoned white beans to the gravy.  Served over rice, this is a keeper for sure.  The white beans and rice made an excellent side, along with a serving of kale.
Thanks for posting it!

we loved this roast. it was so tender and juicy, and the gravy was perfect! the only think i changed was i salt and peppered the roast before i put in in, and i added a little pinch of sage to the cornstarch/water mixture someone else used in another review. it was great, thanks for sharing!

This pot roast is amazing and couldn't be easier!  It's so tender that it literally falls apart - no prebrowning necessary!  Have made this multiple times and will continue!!  I definitelly add potatoes and carrots during the last few hours of cooking.  Thanks for posting!

Delicious!  This was the first time I ever made a roast and it turned out fantastic!  I also added some veggies  just because I had the time to cut them up and throw them in.  I added a little cornstarch at the end to thicken too!  yummy, I thank you and so does my husband :)

This is how I have been making roasts for over 30 years now, first in the oven then in the crockpot. I usually will toss in a sliced onion, sliced carrots, cubed potatoes & sliced mushrooms. Then you add a tossed salad on the side & you have a complete meal. It is my family's favorite.
I also have made my roasts like this for many years....always turns out perfect.  I also will use steak instead of a roast sometimes. Thanks for sharing!

Wow!!! So simple and so delicious!
I had a crappy cut of beef roast in my freezer that I really did not know what to do with. I had purchased two of these roasts, made one about 3 months ago with my regular recipe and it was sooooo terrible. Tough and nasty. So here I was left with one more roast, and NO WAY did I want to even eat it LOL, but I couldn't bring myself to throw it out!
So I gave this recipe a go, and guess what? The most beautiful piece of meat was the end result! I was so pleased!
Tender, and so flavourful, this recipe will save even the worst roast, I can't imagine how tasty a good cut of beef would be!
Thanks for a terrific recipe that I will always use in my slow-cooker!

I have been hunting for a good slow cooker pot roast ever since my electric skillet bit the dust a few months ago and this recipe hands down is the best.  It has a wonderful flavor. I used 2 cans of golden mushroom soup and of course in this family we have to have our garlic so added some of it to the mix. Very yummy and so till I get my electric skillet for Christmas this recipe will get used often. My oldest announced last night that I can even use this recipe for pot roast after I get my skillet every so often. High praise indeed. :)
I have never used a slow cooker before and used this recipe to break it in. I used brown gravy mix instead of the onion soup and it came out so moist and yummy...will definitely make this again

Personally, I'm not a big beef fan, so this rating is mostly based on the reviews of my parents, husband, & kids.  I made the recipe as shown but added 1 can of white navy beans (I LOVE beans!!).  The meat basically fell apart, and the gravy was actually nice & thick.  Everyone loved it (a rare event) and I had a wonderfully relaxing dinner with no complaints!
Another family winner! The DD who doesn't eat anything ( age 4 ) said " I love rot post " LOL this is a winner in this family thanks for posting :D

We really enjoyed this dish!  I made this oamc by freezing the roast w/ the water and onion soup mix during one of my sessions.  I then added the cream of mushroom soup to the defrosted roast in my crockpot. Only problem was that the soup didn't mix in well- but it did not affect the taste, just the look.  Dh ate so much that there were not any leftovers!  Thanks again for sharing!

This is BY FAR the quickest way to make a flavorful pot roast!!  I used cream of chicken since my DH doesn't like mushroom and it turned out great.  I also added a few baby carrots (which were deliciously flavored).  I usually have to have gravy on my carrots to like the way they taste.  Not this time!!!  Yummy!!  We had some mashed potatoes and rolls.  Great dinner!!

I have made this so many times and always have forgotten to rate it. I add canned mushroom pieces to it also. This is so simple and good. It's one of the old standbys I make when nothing else sounds good. Terrific recipe!

This came out great.  I actually used one can of cream of mushroom and one can of cream of celery as that is what I had but it worked!  I also added a can of mushrooms for extra flavor.  We really liked this a lot!  And super easy!!Thanks!

I made this for New Years Day dinner.  My family and I really enjoyed it.  Plenty of leftovers and the gravy was AWESOME!  I only made one change.  I added a can of beef gravy to the crock pot.  This is one I will be making again.  Thanks for the great recipe!  :)
This is a wonderful,easy recipe. I did add beef stock instead of water and added a sliced onion and mushrooms also. The gravy is so delicious,who would have thought it was so easy! Thanks :)
My wife and I have used this recipe for years.  We add less water (1/2 cup)and often add potatoes and carrots.  Terrific.
This pot roast was just delicious and tender as could be.  I added Potatoes and carrots. Just great.

So simple yet soooo lovely. I used one can of the low fat version of Campbells mushroom soup and a can of low fat chicken soup. 

Brilliant

We had it again for dinner the next night since there was enough leftover and it was even BETTER then. This was soo very good on a snowy winter day. The gravy was fabulous; I too added carrots, beef broth and a splash of red wine. I will make this over and over again.
This was so easy and tasted great!  The gravy was excellent!
This was very bland.  I won't make it again.
I've used this recipe 4 times since this was introduced to me.  My family absolutely loves this recipe and is a keeper in our house.  It is very easy to make and delicious.  Thanks for sharing.
This was a really awesome roast, and my family loved it. I used beef broth inplace of the water and I added carrots and potatoes. It was great and I will be making this dish alot. Thanks !!

This was SOOOO yummy!  My husband and I both give it 2 thumbs up and 5+ stars!  I used beef broth instead of water, added onions, potatoes and carrots, and mushrooms, studded the roast w/ sliced garlic, and rubbed it with black pepper and garlic powder before putting in the crock-pot. came out soft and maded the house smell great...but to much onion taste for me...won't put the whole thing in next time...
Tried it with buffalo meat (much leaner). Also, some baby carrots, rutabaga and potatoes were thrown in. Awesome smell in the house. We devoured the stuff!!! Yeah baby...
Super! I added 3-4 carrots and 3 potatoes; used a 3 1/2 lb. roast- was done in 7 hours on low.

Subbed one CoM for a can of cream of celery since I had that on hand.  Used a 2lb roast.  Added red potatoes, carrots, and mushrooms.  Next time I'd add even more veggies and probably a little flour afterwards to thicken the gravy.

This was delicious.  I added some baby new potatoes and carrots to the whole mix and they came out just perfect after 8 hours on low.  This will definitely become a winter staple in our house.  Try it!

This was yummy. I added Potatoes and Carrots, but other than that did not make any adjustments.  I have made many Pot Roasts in the crock pot, but this was a little different than my usual recipe.  The gravy was great.  Will Make again.  Thanks for posting.
This is the recipe I use for roast, my family loves it.

Good recipe...my DH really liked it. It was moist, tender after having been in the crockpot for about 8 or 9 hours on low. DH added the potatoes, carrots and onions during the last 5 hours of cooking, but the didn't get a lot of the taste.

I was skeptical of the cream of mushroom soup, but WOW!  The beef turned out tender and succulent!  This tasted as good or better than my husbands mom's recipe that I can never get "perfect".  I also added, carrots, potatos and celery.  

Thank you for such a easy, wonderful meal.

Yummm! I have actually made this recipe off of the allrecipes site, but didn't realize it was the same until I read the description. Either way, it is good! This is my husbands favorite meal, and he really liked it because he prepared it this morning! After it cooked for about 6 hours, I came home and stuck some potatoes and carrots in there... a few hours later it was falling apart and the veggies were done. Yum!

Wow - I made this two nights ago and my family had no problem last night when I announced that we were having leftovers (which usually go un-eaten in my house).  I decided to do it as a stew, though, so I floured/browned the beef pieces in a little oil before throwing them in the crock with the veggies.  I also doubled the onion soup and water to make sure there would be enough gravy.  Started cooking on low before work, stirred (and tasted) it at lunch, and it was phenomenal by dinnertime.  I agree with my family that it was the best beef stew I've ever made.  Thanks for sharing!!  8)
I've made this recipe for years and it's a winner everytime. Every once in a while, I will try a different pot roast recipe, but they never seem to be as good as this one. And it's so simple!

Wow this was fantastic and super easy...made a lot of excellent gravy!!!  Served it with potato muffins, excellent will definitely keep this and make again....thank you kcdelong for posting and sharing....

This was really good. I followed the recipe exactly, and the gravy was thick and delicious. A little salty for those who are watching their salt intake. I didn't have it over potatoes or pasta yet, so that will be on tonight's agenda. A really simple and tasty meal.
Thanks so much for posting.
Very very good--DH really likes this.  Like some other reviewers, I add potatoes and carrots.  Thanks, kcdelong!!

Absolutely awesome! I added 2 large potatoes, 2 tins of peas, a tin of baby carrots, 3 sm. cloves of garlic, together with 2.75lbs of meat for 6 very hungry people. Also added 1/2C of Valpolicella wine in the final hour. Very, very delicious!

This was one of the best "homestyle" pot roasts I have ever made.  I used a 2 pound roast and added a couple handful of baby carrots and a tablespoon of garlic.  Other than that I followed the recipe as listed.  My husband noticed that this was not my normal recipe, stating that it seemed richer in flavor.  Definitely a keeper.

This recipe's been around for a while...

Turned the crockpot to low...I cut 2 small/medium onions and cut them into 8ths...They went into my oval crockpot first...I added 2-4oz. cans of mushrooms...I mixed the soups and water in a separate bowl and then poured into the crockpot, stirring it around the onions and mushrooms...

Sprinkled a generous amount of garlic powder on the soup...

I then criscrossed slices into the roast about a half in deep, half inch apart...

I poured on a goodly amount of Kitchen Bouquet seasoning and worked it into the slices...I then added a liberal amount of garlic powder on top of the Kitchen Bouquet...I placed the roast in the pot...The soup did not reach the top of the roast...It cooked that way for about 3 hours on LOW and I flipped the roast and finished cooking about 3 more hours...In my view, pot roast and gravy doesn't get any better than this...

There are lists and lists of pot roast recipes and this one gives you the perfect 'comfort food' version. Nothing fancy - just downright perfection. I used Fat Free Cream of Mushroom and Eye of Round.  Fantastic, Thanks.
Yum, everyone liked this - kids, too.
Very nice! Quick to fix and the meat was so tender. Great dinner and now it sure is making wonderful roast beef sandwiches. Thank you very much for a very nice recipe.

Found this as wonderful as all others had!! Added some dried mushrooms, potatos, carrots and onions. Used beef broth instead of water and the gravy is awesome. Thanks, KC, for this fabulous and easy recipe.

I loved this quick recipe.  Used Elk meat and substituted dehydrated onions & salt for soup mix and added a teaspoon of beef base to it (I halved the recipe). Left peeled potatoes in pot of cold water on stove as with carrots to turn on when we arrived home.  After a long day of ski lessons, it was a wonderful tasteful, and EASY treat to come home to.  Gravy with meat was actually on the verge of outstanding.  Even got the neighbor to go back for seconds.

Wow! Soooo GOOD! My DH has decided that this is now the only way I can make pot roast. I could only find a 3 1/2lb. roast and I decided to go with the others suggestions of using beef broth instead of water. Other than that I followed the recipe. It was so easy to put together before work and then come home to a wonderful meal for an extremely cold night. Thanks!

I don't see any reason to ever use another crockpot roast recipe !  I had a 2 plus lb roast, so I used 1 can of soup.  I only had cream of celery on hand, so I used that.  I used the whole envelope of onion soup mix and one can of water.  I browned the roast in my dutch oven, placed the roast in the crockpot, surrounded it with chunks of baked potato, deglazed the dutchoven with the soup mixture, then poured over the roast in the crockpot.  4 hours on high. Delish !!!!

This roast was tender and delicious.  I must add that I made a few changes, and it was wonderful.  I started with a 3.5 pound roast, so I cut the recipe in half.  I didn't have a can of the cream of mushroom soup on hand so I used my Condensed Cream Soup Substitute recipe using beef broth.  Also, in place of the water I used a mixture of beef broth and red wine (a pot roast isn't a pot roast with out a little red wine.)  I also added carrots, celery, and fresh minced garlic, and served with mashed potatoes.  Excellent!!!  Thanks kcdelong!!!!

Quick & Easy!! I sub beef broth for the water and use a boneless chuch roast. Baby carrots & whole new potatoes always make it in the pot too. I always have left overs so...I shread the meat into small chunks & the next day put the whole thing, meat, carrots, potatos and some gravy into a pie dish and cover w/1 9" pie shell. Bake for 45 minutes at 375.
I have made this pot roast several times and it always turns out delicious. I add red potatoes, onion, carrots. and celery to mine.
Yummy and delicious.  The PERFECT easy entree recipe to use in our camper.
This is a favorite recipe that I've been making for years.  I also add a splash of Sherry.  Sometimes I add a can of beef gravy in lieu of 1 can of soup.

I made this for New Years and everyone loved it. I eat it for lunch the next day and dinner the next night. I really loved how it makes it's own gravy. I made a pot of rice and had the cabbage and black eye peas for good luck and it was one of the BEST dinners I have ever made. Thanks so much. Sorry I got all the credit from my family about how good it was. LOL.
This was amazing. I dumped a bag of baby carrots in with a couple hours left to go, and they were delicious also. I served with mashed potatos and it was all fabulous. It makes plenty of gravy.
Soooo good.  I have made this with venison as well.  I like to make extra sauce and serve it over egg noodles.

i ended up using cream of mushroom and cream of chicken since that's all i had in hand. i also used beef broth instead of water. added baby carrots on the bottom. wasn't salty at all. in fact my dh added a little more seasonings to his plate. very good recipe and so easy. maybe it's my crockpot but it took me 12 hours on slow to get my roast tender. luckily i put it in really early.

As some other reviewers did, I cooked my 6 pound roast in the crock pot for 12 hours on low.  I also used a can of beef broth in place of the water.  About an hour before serving, I took out approximately 1 1/2 cups of the liquid, cooled it down with ice cubes (my mom always said that if you tried to put flour into a hot mixture it would lump up), put in about 1/4 to 1/3 cup of flour, mixed it all together and put it back into the crock pot with the meat.  I also added two cans of sliced carrots at that time.  When we were ready to be eat, we had a wonderful gravy to eat with our roast and rolls!  Thanks so much for this recipe.  It is down home cooking at its finest.

I have been making this for years and am always pleased with the results. I add carrots and potatoes to mine as well for a one pot meal, perfect to come home to after a long day at work. Put it on low when I leave the house in the morning and come home to a great homemade meal. Thanks for posting this one.

Made this for a big family get-together and it was a hit! Used one can cream of mushroom soup and one can golden mushroom soup (that's all I had in the pantry). Cooked on low for about ten hours and it was perfectly tender. The gravy was wonderful served over mashed potatoes. Thank you!

This roast was really good!  I used a 3 pound roast, so I only used one can of soup.  I used the full amount of dry onion soup mix and water.  The roast had a great flavor and was very tender.  Thank you kcdelong for posting!
I think the recipe was alright but would make a couple of changes.  I would add less water and use Golden Mushroom Soup next time.  Very easy!

I make this whenever I know I have company coming over after work.  Its so easy to throw together in the morning, turn on the crock pot, and run out the door!  Its always so tender and delicious by the time we get home and get the rest of the meal ready.
I found this recipe on allrecipes as well, and then found it in a "Fix it and Forget It" Cookbook.  It is a great pot roast.  I love it, and we all enjoy it every time I make it!  Thanks for posting!

The amount of water barely covered half the roast which was only about 4lbs the recipe of course doesn't specify the size for the roast.  Flavor was good not sure if measurements are correct.
This was a FABULOUS MEAL!!!!!! I made it for my husband and his friend - they LOVED it!!!! I did use beef broth instead of water and added red potatoes. VERY YUMMY!

This was a great recipe, though I am not sure I can rate it fairly. I used a 3 lb. chuck roast and the dry onion soup mix along with 1/2 cup of water but no cream of mushroom soup. The onion soup mix is more affordable. I cooked it on low for 9 - 10 hours. Thank you for sharing, it was tender and delicious.

This was just awesome.  My roast was so tender and juicy.  My mom used to make roast like this all the time.  The only changes I made was that I browned the roast really well before adding to my pot.  I used my LeCreuset dutch oven to cook it in instead of the crockpot.  Set the oven to 300 and baked it for 4 hours.  Added some potatoes and carrots after 1 hour of cooking.  Perfect for us.  Thanks

This was wonderful and so easy! I made it a day ahead and then put it outside overnight (it was snowing) and then warmed it up in time for dinner. This the way I've always done a pot roast, too!  I usually cook some noodles to serve the gravy over.  This is Very good.

This was so incredibly easy and the gravy is amazing.

yummy, yummy, yummy.  I used beef broth as suggested, but other than that kept everything the same.  This is the only roast I'll make from now on.

I've made this numerous times and it always comes out awesome!  Sometimes I put some sliced onions on the bottom.  It makes its own gravy and the roast is always super tender.  One of the better crock pot recipes in my opinion.

My husband and I love this pot roast.  I am making it again tonight and he can't wait.  I usually use a small roast since it is just the 2 of us and add mushrooms, celery, baby red potatoes, and baby carrots.

My husband and I loved this recipe. It was so easy and tasty. This recipe is a keeper!

I made this with a shoulder roast (because the butcher recommended that cut since it was on sale) and it was DELICIOUS! Wonderful!! This recipe is now a family favorite!
My family loves this pot roast.  We always throw potatoes and carrots in with the meat, too.  Great recipe!!

east and so good
Fantastic!  My whole family loved it and that doesnt happen often!  I halved the recipe (only 3 of us) and cooked it on low for about 6.5 hours.  I also added cut carrots.  Delicious!
