I DO wish i would have had some brown sugar, as I believe that could have taken the sauce to another level, but it was definitely delicious and I will definitely be making these again.  Thank you!
This was absolutely wonderful. Didn't change a thing. yummers!!!
Very easy and very good. It is a great any night meal too. I did the recipe just as shown but next time I will add a little more chile powder and some celantro. Thanks for a great quick recipe.

These were so unbelievably fall apart delicious!I don't normally even buy pork chops anymore because I can never get them tasty or tender enough.Problem solved!I used 4 pork chops,no bone.I cooked them on high for 2 hours and then on low for 2 hours.I served them with fried rice and the leftover sauce was good on the rice also.

I must say that this was an awesome recipe.  The only changes I made were to make more of it.  lol  Like I used a family pack of 8 pork chops with bones and doubled the sauce recipe.  As previously submitted, the sauce is great over mashed potatoes! Almost forgot, I didn't have the 7 hours to make this, so I placed mine on high and cooked for 3 and a half hours.  Everything came out beautifully!

Made this today using Penzeys medium hot chili powder. Gave it a really nice 'bite', we really liked it with the pork chops. I would definitely double the sauce mix if we had made more than 2 chops. I bet this would be awesome with venison steaks, I plan to use those next time. Thanks for a super easy, great tasting dish.
I didn't feel the sauce penetrated the chops and if I were making again I would use boneless chops
What a great chop recipe.  I loved the sauce in this.  Thanks for a great recipe.
I used 4 boneless chops that I had in the freezer and used more onion and garlic than the recipe called for and it came out delicious.  Great recipe.

Simple, yummy and flavorful. The pork chops (mine were thin) basically fell apart (tender). I would love to try this again with thick cut pork chops. I too placed unpeeled whole baby red potatoes, a whole vadallia onion and the garlic in the bottom of the pot, placed the pork chops atop the vegetables and topped with the sauce.  Probably used half of the amount of the water called for, doubled the cumin & chili powder, lastly adding a dash of cinnamon. This was a keeper. I may try a little lime juice in the sauce next time for that chili-lime flavor. Served with steamed broccoli. Thanks for sharing an inspiring recipe!
Very good!!  Will make again for sure!

Delicious! Served with Tex-Mex Rice on the side. I put a few chunks of onion in the bottom of the crock-pot, and only used 2 chops. Kept the sauce ingred. the same. Delicious! We ate 1 1/2 hours later than I had planned, but these were still perfect! Fall off the bone tender.
These were very good pork chops and so easy to make.  I made them with baked mashed potatoes.

We had a lot of work to do today and I knew I wouldn't be able to make dinner later, so I threw these in the crock pot this morning.  Used a whole medium onion, and followed the rest of the recipe exactly except I just put the pork chops in frozen because I knew we'd be back late.  About 8 hrs later we had a great dinner.  Served with buttered noodles and steamed veg.  I'll make this again.  Normally I think all crock pot meals taste the same, but this was really good.
My DH and I love this... I put baby carrots under chops (they come out so yummie) <br/>also I use .... 1 CUP - ONION... 2 TEASPOONS - CHILI POWDER... 1/2 TEASPOON - CUMIN...1/3 CUP - WATER
I would have given this a 5 but I felt it need a tad of brown sugar. I also used center cut chops. served with mashed potatoes and corn ... great dinner. Thanks for sharing!

I followed the recipe exactly and served it with rice. The meat was tender and delicious, and my kids gave it a 10/10, said they would eat it again. Win! Thanks very much for sharing this recipe. Who knew pork chops could taste so good!

I forgot to make a note in my previous post.  I also used boneless chops, and since it was almost noonish.. and I didn't really have 7 hours on low, I did 4 hours on high, and they were falling apart.   -  I am confused about the Nutrition information that is provided.  I have to have LOW sodium, and one of my roommates is a diabetic.  All of the ingredients are low in sodium, (I didn't use any salt ) and low in sugar, but the Nutrition information says that it is high in both.

Just put this in the crock pot. My house already smells amazing! I added another tsp of chili powder, and I used chicken thighs instead of pork. The sauce tastes amazing! I'm sure I'll LOVE this. Thanks!
This recipe is an absolute nothing. Sorry. Just could have put my favorite bbq sauce over pork chops and had the same result.
A friend made this for a pot luck party and it's delicious!  There were no leftovers to bring home and everyone asked for the recipe.  It will definitely be a requested recipe at parties.

Easy to make cheese dip and so good! I used one package of the ranch dressing mix and dried chives instead of the green onions. Also used 1/2 cup of Miller Lite beer to get it to a creamier consistency. This will be a family favorite! Thank you Mean Jeanne for posting this recipe.
This dip is da bomb! I made it for a holiday party and it was gone within 30 minutes! Definitely a keeper, thanks Mean Jeanne!

My MIL made this over the holidays and I was craving it recently.  I could have waited til she found the recipe, but thought I'd try to find it here.  And this is it!!  This is REALLY good.  Funny thing is I don't care for beer but I love this!  I used cut up bagel pieces (which pairs with the beer wonderfully!) and omitted the green onions.  I will absolutely make this again.  Thank you!

OMG! This so tasty & soooo easy ! 
My Co-workers BEG my to make this for special occasions, it's so easy I almost feel guilty just bringing this dish.
Geat dip with ritz crackers and wheat thins toasted chips!!!!  Thanks so much for the recipe.
Fantastic!  Everyone at the party just loved it.  Very easy to make.
This is the greatest! Works on crackers, veggies, anything!  Easy and quick, I only refrigerated 2 or 3 hours.  Everyone loved it.  Personally I like it best with celery!
I tried this and it's wonderful now I can't stop making it

This is exactly what I was looking for! My aunt made it and it was sooo good and she said how easy ot was to make.  I made a batch for a party and the only difference was that I used about 1 tbs of fiesta ranch mix and 2 tbs of regular ranch because I could not find the package a bought at the store anywhere! It still tasted good and had a little bit of a zip to it because of the fiesta mix....everyone enjoyed it and it went fast!
Interesting blend of flavors.  Although I didn't love it, most of my guests did.  I used Recipe #27560 for the ranch dressing mix, which turned out wonderfully.  Thanks for sharing!
My sister makes a similar recipe without the ranch mix which I love.  This one was even better, the ranch mix add such a nice flavor!

This was one of the appetizer/dips I made for this year's Thanksgiving.  No effort to make...which was helpful.  Good reviews from everyone, but boy....is it thick and RICH!!  Personally, I thought it was at it's best the second day.  I'm tempted to use whipped cream cheese next time and see what happens.

This was a hit at my Christmas Eve party last night. Everyone raved about it and wanted the recipe. Thank you for posting such an easy and great tasting recipe. Everyone here was right on the reviews-no one could stop eating it! Iwill use this for many more parties/gatherings.

I remember eating a dip like this about 10 years ago, and I've never forgotten how delicious it was! Recently, I remembered it when trying to come up with a football game menu, and of course went to recipezaar for a highly-rated version of the recipe to try. I was not disappointed! This dip is great with veggies, potato chips, and (my favorite) pretzels! The last step, refrigeration overnight, is not completely necessary but really helps all of the flavors blend together. It's even better after two days. Also, I use whipped cream cheese to cut down on the fat, and the taste isn't affected at all (However, I have also tried using fat-free cream cheese, which is NOT a good substitute!). I definitely recommend this recipe as a welcome variant from the traditional ranch or french onion dip! Great game day food!
A really tasty twist on the original! I wasn't too sure about it the first day, but WOW! It was a definite second-day hit at our house! Will make again...thanks for posting it! :)
Great recipe! I make this all the time for football games and tail gating. Thanks!
Made for superbowl and everyone loved it! I added a bit more green onion for personal preference. Big hit! Thanks for the recipe!
Me and my son enjoyed this dip while DH didn't like it as much as us.  I used Stella Artois beer.  Thanks for posting :)  Made for I recommend tag game
Really good dip that goes well with pretzels, chips, and crackers! I especially enjoyed it with Chicken in a Biskit crackers.

This was a yummy dip that suited my craving!  I used Colby Jack because we didn't have the sharp cheddar.  I think the sharp cheddar would have been better, but it was really good this way, too.  I minced up 1/2 medium yellow onion because we didn't have green onion and that was good - maybe could have even used more.  I used Miller High Life light and thought maybe I should have used a more flavorful beer - maybe a dark or hoppy one - to add more flavor, but I liked the bit of flavor it did add.  We also added a bit of garlic powder, tomato paste, and a teaspoon of light brown sugar.
My friends loved it!
I thought I had rated this.  LOVE this dip and everyone in the house has started fighting over the bowl and bag of pretzels.  We may have issues as we all stash some away from the other's  LOL.
Perfect!! Yum!!

To give this recipe a little ZIP, I added a little finely chopped jalapeno to the mix. It made the dip addicting! Thankfully, I made a triple batch, as it disappeared very fast. Cant believe how many bags of wheat crackers we went through.

Made this for company and loved how easy it came together.  The only think I did different was cut it in half as we didn't need this much.  Everyone enjoyed the creamy texture and flavors, though I'm thinking next time I might add a little hot sauce for just an extra flavor and a little kick.  Served with crackers

This is definitely tasty and easy, but it needs something more to really shine. I used more than two green onions (not just the tops, either) and I think that was needed. I'll probably add 1/2 tsp of garlic powder next time and experiment try a darker beer. I used a lighter colored beer and it didn't provide enough flavor. Green olives would be a natural addition. I'm also going to try with horseradish.

What a great alternative to canned gandules which are usually loaded with hidden salt. Also cans are often lined with BPH Dplastic) which can leech into food.  I assume you mash the peas to make the paste. I needed them for arroz con gandules, so left them whole.

This was very good and easy.  I used a 3 lb. boneless pork roast and used chicken broth instead of water.  The meat was tender, but it was so soft, it ended up almost pasty.  After an hour on high, this was boiling like crazy, so I turned it down to low for the next 7 hours or so.  I think that maybe the cooking time suggested is too long, or maybe it is just the differences in crock pots.  It does have a very good flavor and gravy, when thickened with corn starch, is awesome on mashed potatoes.  Thanks for posting!

The family loved the flavor and it was very easy to make. However, I have to agree on the cooking times.Start on high then reduce to low for the remaining 6 or so hours. I have made this twice now and the first time was overdone,on my second attempt we got it right !! and it was excellent.Thanks for sharing Karen!

Delicious! This was my first attempt at a pork roast & it came out quite good! I had a 2 lb roast so I used 1 env of onion soup mix, 1/2 cup ketchup & 3/4 tsp of the seasonings. I used chicken broth to cover the roast (about 1 cup) as well. Cooked on low for around 5 hours. Came out so moist, tender & flavorful! This is a keeper! Thank you!
Very tastey, 7 hours was perfect timing.My family loved it, plan to make it again soon thanks for posting!
Wonderful way to cook pork, so tastey.  I made first exactly like above, second time I substituted crushed Pineapple for the ketchup.  WOW  now I have 2 keepers.  try it you will like it!
I made this tonight.  It was great.  Served over white rice.  The only thing I changed was I took it out, let it rest, and sliced it and put back into sauce for about 30 mins.  Fantastic!
I'm not very fond of pork so I'm always looking for new and different ways to prepare it and let me tell you this recipe is the best I've ever tasted. I absolutely loved this recipe.

Absolutely a delicious recipe! 
I used Recipe #24952 for this recipe. I keep this on hand at all times for when I need a onion soup mix. Also I only had a small pork roast so I halved the recipe.  I used 1 cup of broth from this recipe to cook some rice which I added a few veggies also. Our dinner was wonderful! The pork roast was very tender and the broth was very flavorable. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Loved this. Only thing I change is only 1 pkg. onion soup mix and no salt as the seasonings are enough. Mixed sauce together  using 1 cup water and pour over roast. (not fully covered-was just fine). Served with rice. thanks

This was a great recipe.  We had a 2 pound pork roast so we used 1 package soup mix, just over 1/3 cup ketchup, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp. garlic powder and 3 bouillon cubes.  I mixed everything in a bowl with 1 cup hot water and poured over roast.  Cooked on low for about 5 1/2 hours, cut up and then put it back in the sauce on the keep warm setting until we ate supper.  Thanks for the recipe!!!

This turned out wonderful. I followed the recipe exactly. The pork was very tender. I used the liquid to make a gravy, just made a roux from butter and flour and added the juice. The gravy was a little salty, so next time I probably will just use one package of soup mix. Served it up with mashed potatoes. Very good, whole family loved it, and EASY!!!!
Very tender and very good but very salty. I will leave out the salt next time altogether. Thanks for sharing!

Good and easy to make roast. I had a two pound roast so followed someone elses instuctions and used 1/3 cup of ketchup, one packet of onion soup, 1/2 tsp of all the spices and 3 bouillon cubes. Next time I would omit the salt as we thought this was a bit salty. It made a very tender roast. I cooked mine on high for four hours as I was pressed for time.

DH and I both really loved this recipe; him for the fall apart tenderness and wonderful taste and me for all that but add on a breeze to make.  I did add a cut up potatoe, some celery, onion and carrots to it and omitted the salt.  The veggies blended well with the gravy and made for a delicious and filling dinner that we'll be making again.  Thanks so much for posting.
This turned out moist and quite tasty.  Love easy recipes like this!  Thanks :-)

Dancer, these are a great way to grill pork chops! I have a George Foreman grill and used that. I cut the recipe in half for just two of us and the pork was tender and moist. I love anything with garlic and this recipe is a keeper. Carole

I cut half a boneless loin into 1 inch chops and dubbled the amounts. I substituded a Cajun spice mix for the salt and pepper to add some bite. It fed a firehouse crew of ten and there was dust for leftovers! Thanks

Very good !  I also tried it on a G. Foreman type grill and they were great.  The sauce is AWESOME!  Would go great with chicken or ribs.  I have a feeling it would have tasted better on a real grill... but this was still yummy.

These were great, everyone loved them.  I, too, cut up a third of a boneless pork roast and they came out wonderful on the grill.  Not one person in the family complained (very unusual!) and they were looking for seconds.  Served with corn on the cob and caesar salad...yummy and healthy!  Thanks!

Great sauce!  My family loved it.  We only made it for three people so we're using the leftovers tomorrow for grilled chicken.  I also thought it would be good brushed onto kabobs to flavor the meat and veggies.
Great sauce! and the more garlic, the better. I scaled this down to 2 servings, and served with a salad and baked potato.

very easy and delicious!!!!
will try on chicken next time.

Dancer I have made there twice now and they are finger licking good. When I first saw the ingredients I was a bit weary but these turned out good. If my boyfriend find's pork chops in the fridge he immediatly asks to make the yummy ones like last time! Thanks for posting :)

Yummy- we all liked it. I marinated the chops in some of the sauce for a few hours before grilling. I also reserved some sauce to use at the table. At first I was going to add more garlic (we love garlic), but chose to stick with the original recipe. It was just right. My mouth had that nice garlic taste for about an hour after dinner!!
These pork chops were excellent!  I added a little bit of ginger and reserved some of the sauce to pour on top. I served with brown rice. Thanks for the recipe.

We were making port wine sauce with grilled pork loin tonight and the port wine sauce went totally south.  I had this one saved, so I threw it together quickly and you saved our Valentine dinner.  It was wonderful and we will be making it again for sure.  Thank you so much for a quick, easy and delicious recipe.
the sauce was great!i marinated the pork all day. very flavorful. since it's freezing here-not grilling weather i baked the chops. thanks for another great recipe dancer!
I'm putting this in the 20* file!  I loved this sauce on our porkchops!  I made sure not to double dip while I basted and served the extra sauce on the side for our dipping pleasure!  Thanks Dancer!
This is a great pork chop recipe.  The sauce is not too sweet unlike some many others.  It would be great on chicken also.

this sauce is awsome..i used white wine and garlic.Everyone loved it.This will definatly be made again.I will make more next time,just thinking of it makes my mouth water.best grilled pork loin i've ever had.ty,dancer.
this sauce was awesome.I used dales steak seasoning instead of soy sauce since i was out at the time.Flavor was still very good and will try the soy sauce next time
My husband and I loved this sauce.  Nice and easy, too.  Will definitely make it again.

These were great.  Although I ran short on ketchup, the sauce was very tasty.  I didn't grill my chops (it was cold outside) but cooked over the stove using waterless cookware they turned out perfect.

Even though I overcooked them a bit (I'm just learning to master my BBQ grilling skills and my chops were frozen so I didn't quite know how long to cook them) they were still great! Loved the flavors, even better than I expected! Thank you Dancer!!
This was quick & easy compared to marinades and really good.  I added extra honey to make it less tangy. Thanks for sharing.
I made this for my husband and I last night, it was awesome. I'm planning on having my parents over and making it for them. Thanks so much!
Was expecting a ketchupy taste but they had a great mild flavor with no ketchup taste to them. Thanks for sharing, will make again.

Wow! I wasn't sure about the outcome when I was adding the ketchup to the sauce, but WOW! The taste isn't ketchup-y at all, only scrumptious! Thanks for the great recipe; I definitely will be adding this to my favorite recipe book!

So easy to make and as other reviewers said it isn't ketchup-y tasting despite the amount used. I pounded my boneless chops out and grilled them on the George Foreman.
Great last minute BBQ item especially since no marination is required. Very good recipe thanks =).

This is the best pork chop recipe I have ever come across and I've tried a few.I marinated 2 pork chops in a ziploc bag with the mixture overnight.I cut the ingredients in half.Then I bbq-ed them....delicious!Thanks for posting this one!
These were wonderful.I marinated for about 3 hours, and will probabaly marinate longer next time. They did not have a ketchup taste at all. A keeper!

Although Dancer doesn't say to marinate the pork chops, it sounds like most reviewers did (so did I).  Nothing could be easier, and the pork chops tasted great--a nice subtle garlic flavor seeps through the sweetness.  Thanks so much, Dancer, for an attractive, tasty pork recipe.
Very easy and yummy !! Made as directed but I did marinate them for a couple hours before

Oh, man, were these good.  I grew up an hour away from Memphis, and these reminded me of home.  We baked the chops since it was raining outside, and they really couldn't have been better.  We sauteed some onions and tossed them in with the chops; other than that we used the prescribed ingredients.  Like other reviewers, we marinated for about an hour before baking.  Yum!!!
These were pretty good and something different than the usual.  I did marinate the chops for about 90 mins before cooking in a skillet (too cold for grilling!).

I decided to try rack of baby back ribs using this sauce.  Very good ribs!  Everyone enjoyed them.  DH said they were "Finger Lickin' Good"!  I made a double batch and let the ribs sit in some to marinate, then used the rest to brush on during cooking over med. heat, so they didn't burn.  Turned out great!
This was great.  I chose to bake it because it is too cold to grill.  I will try it on chicken and ribs next time!!
Took the pork out of the freezer in the morning, and marinated it in fridge till dinner time. Raves all around, so we will be making this often. Thank you for sharing.
Loved the sauce!!

The weather did not co-operate with my grilling plans so I turned this into an oven recipe and it was still very good.  Because my chops were about 1 1/2 inches thick, I pre-browned them in a cast iron skillet and then cooked for about 20 minutes at 350, drained the grease and then added about half of the sauce and cooked them another 20 minutes.  The extra sauce I put on the table at serving time.  We all enjoyed it. Thx Dancer!

These were great pork chops. I loved the sauce flavor. Although, next time I think I'll decrease the soy sauce amount just a tad.  For 4 pork chops, I halved the basting sauce and it was the perfect amount. It was a rainy, cold day outside so I used my grill pan on the stovetop. My whole family enjoyed these very much. Thanks!

Agreed with the others--- I thought these would be wayyy too "ketchupy" but they weren't.  Tasted like a sweet and kinda tangy BBQ sauce.  We had ours on chicken (about 2 pounds worth) marinated our chicken for an hour with some of the sauce, then basted with the leftovers, and had a LOT left over--- I saved the leftovers for pork chops later this week!  Thanks!  Hubby was drooling from the sidewalk when I was grilling!

Sorry I couldn't give this 5 stars.  Just a little too sweet.  I think I will cut the honey down to 1/4 cup and see what happens.  Other than that, these were good.  And agree with BrandNewJen, this was a LOT of sauce!  Thnx for posting, Dancer.

I really don't care for ketchup much, but gave this a try based on other reviewers' comments.  unfortunately, I could still taste the ketchup and was really hoping that would not be the case.  However, the meat was still nice and juicy, and I enjoyed it even if it was a tad messy.  I will just cut down a little on the ketchup next time.  I might also add a sprinkle of ginger to it, too, since I think that would blend well with the soy and honey.
Big thumbs up from everyone.  Very tasty, thanks for sharing.

Smiles from everyone at the table.  My GD wanted another chop and she's only 3!  I doubled the recipe as I had a crowd for dinner, and everyone loved them.  The recipe is now in my "Make Again" file so I won't forget about them!

I was a bit skeptical when I saw ketchup in the ingredients.  (I have ketchup haters in my house)  But I decided to throw caution to the wind and risk my family's outrage.  
Since I was making dinner for another family as well, I doubled the recipe and marinated the pork all day.  It smelled very promising.

The chops turned out to be a huge hit.  Even my two year old loved them and my ketchup haters as well.  I reserved some extra sauce and added mustard to it... voila!  a delicious dip for the kids hot dogs a couple of nights later.  Is there no end to the genius of this recipe???  Thank you for sharing.

Quick, easy and oh so delicious!  I grilled boneless pork chops the first time, and made the mistake of using all of the sauce before and during grilling.  It was so yummy I had to make more for dipping!  Tonight it's going on chicken.  I have to reprint the recipe because I gave the original to a friend to try.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I only had 2 chops, so I put some of the remaining sauce on some chicken. In my opinion, the chicken was much better than the pork chops. Also, this made way too much sauce. When I make it again, I'll halve the recipe. Very tasty however.

This was wonderful. It doesn't seem like something so simple would taste so good.  I am not a huge pork chop lover, but even I ate them. I agree about leaving some sauce for dipping...it's great. I basted about every 2 minutes and then turned them. PERFECTION!!

This recipe was nothing special.  I looked at the ingredients and then looked at all the reviews and thought there must be something I was missing.  It may come down to personal taste, but this recipe is better suited for chicken or you can just use a bottle of your favorite bbq sauce.  I appreciated the recipe but will not be making this one again.
Really enjoyed this sauce.  Kept some for dipping in.  I marinated the pork chops for a couple of hours, and then fried over a low heat.  Really tasty.  Thanks!
With low sodium soy sauce this was just salty enough for us.  We loved the chops.  They were tender and really yummy!
Perfect- and reserving some to dip is a must. Do not change a thing- it is superb!

I literally found this recipe and made it about 1/2 before putting the chops on the grill and it was wonderful! I made it exactly as posted. It was easy, inexpensive, fast, and of course, tasty! My boneless chops came out nice and moist. My 10 yr old yummed them up and said they tasted like they were from a fancy restaurant ;-) Thanks for a keeper recipe!

Wow these are very good chops!!I was not that sure about the outcome when I was adding the ketchup to the sauce but the taste was not kethcupy at all!!Thanks for the recipe which will be repeated again and again :)
Fantastic! Might try adding a little ginger next time, but this was delicious as is.
Delicious simple very easy recipe.  This is a great recipe if you want some tasty chops but dont have a lot of time.
Great on spare ribs too.. I added some brown sugar
This was a really great flavour! We dont eat pork much so we use this sauce with chicken too & its very tasty.
VERY flavorful sauce!  Followed this to the letter and was loved by all!  I did increase the garlic.  YUM!
Great recipe and so easy to prepare!!!  We used it with a pork loin and poached in the oven as we don't have a grill available.

very good! nice simple and the honey isn't over powering so its not too sweet. i marinaded them for maybe only a hour a head of time and basted them with the remains of the sauce as it grilled. it was very savory, one of my favorite pork chop recipes to date.
...oh and i used bone in chops ^_^
Very tasty.  It was like a homemade BBQ sauce.  Will definetly make again

This was very good!  I made it in the oven on 375 for about an hour turning and basting half way through.  Also, I did marinate these for about 2.5 hours.  They were easy and good, not to mention quick to put together :)))  Good things don't always have to be complicated and gourmet.
7/12/10--- now I did chicken breast in this and put a splash of apple cider vinegar and some sliced onions in it while it baked. Again....very good sauce!

The whole family loved the pork chops, even my daughter who is not a great fan of pork.  I took another reviewer's advice and marinated them for an hour or so - they had great flavor - and not that grocery-store barbecue sauce taste.  We will make these again!
These pork chops are wonderful.  Quick and easy recipe to make.  Thanks for posting.

My boyfriend LOVED these. I was only making one good-sized pork chop so I scaled it down: 1/4 C. Ketchup, 1 T. Honey, 1 T. Soy Sauce. I didn't have any garlic cloves, so I just through a bunch of garlic powder into the mixture. I even forgot to season with salt and pepper before hand (oops!), but he still loved them. He wished I had made him two! Will definitely be using this again.
Really good

I finally got to use the stove-top grill I got as a wedding present for this. We loved it. I only did three chops, but I kept the sauce the same. I didn't like that the honey made the sauce blacken very quickly, but it still tasted really good. I rarely make things twice, but I'll use the sauce on chicken wings at some point.
These are so good.  My family is a big condiment family but we used nothing with these, they were wonderful.  Thank you for sharing your recipe with us.

This SOOOOO good. I knew i liked even before i made because I like all the ingredients in this dish and i also have them on hand all the time. It was very very good. I also loved that this recipe is easily adjusted to taste. Thanks for sharing this wonderful receipe.
I got great reviews from my family on this one! We just loved the flavor of them and gobbled them up in no time!   This is going into my go to files for great tasting new recipes.
Easy and delicious!  What more could you want?!?

Made this tonight for my husband, 6 kids and one of my kid's friends: 9 people of whom 3 are pick as hell and EVERYONE loved it   Unfortunately, I did not make enough for seconds for everyone; so, some kids felt robbed. I scaled this down to two servings and made a pork chop for the hubby and a seitan "chop" for me, and it was very tasty! I baked them at 180 degrees for about 30 minutes, as I don't have a grill. So very easy to make, so this will definitely be in my regular recipe rotation!

I only made a few changes: Substituted low-sodium tamari for regular soy sauce (didn't have any), used garlic powder instead of garlic cloves (didn't have any), added a dash of cayenne, and a little bit of liquid smoke (to better imitate the grill taste!). I put way more garlic than the recipe called for. I love garlic!

An excellent, quick, and easy dish. I added a little extra garlic and also brined the pork chops to keep them tender.  My son is already asking when we can have these again!  Thanks for the great recipe Dancer!
super yummy! simple, easy, on hand ingredients. wonderful taste! Thanks for posting Dancer!
Pretty good!  We thought the flavour was more reminiscent of bbq than honey garlic.

These were so good! Easy to make and few ingredients, I love it!

Wonderfully easy and quick!
Very Yummy! My Husband and kids loved it, will definitely be making this over and over again.
My family loves this recipe!

Great flavor! Husband and kids loved it. Though I did not grill it (used a grill pan), I had a good amount of marinade left over (I had used 8 chops). Next time I'll probably cut it in half.

I love this salad. I took it in to work for a hawaiian theme potluck. I was afraid that it may be too healthy for the group (as they don't typically like "healthy" foods), but they loved it. Yum!  A good combination of ingredients.

Thanks for the recipe!

YUM! I love this salad! Thanks so much for posting. It's such a tasty option for the summer especially. I used a rotisserie chicken from the store as well as frozen mango...just made the prep a little easier on me and the salad still turned out great. Thanks also for the tip on not using as much rice - lessening it or leaving it out is a great way to lower the carbs and the salad is just as good.

This is very flavorful!!  My mom is going to a New Years party tonight and she requested that I make something light because we've all been overloaded on the comfort foods this holiday season.  This was the ticket!!  Made exactly as indicated except I used a grapeseed oil for the oil so it would be as healthy as possible.  Who says healthy can't taste great?  We put the salad into dixie cups to serve as mini appetizers.  Awesome recipe:)  Thanks for posting.

This was awesome!!!!!  I made it without rice since I'm watching my carbs.  I used olive oil for the ooil and the other flavors are so strong you couldn't taste it.  I had a very juicy mango so I only need the juice of 1 lime.  After the first batch disappeared, I had to go get more ingredients to make it again!    This is in my way more than 5 stars list
I used quinoa (very healthy) instead of rice, scaled the recipe to serve four but used the whole mango, and added cashews and fresh snipped chives from the garden.  Delicioso!!

Ooooohhhh, this is SOOOO yummy!!  I followed some other suggestions~~used orzo instead of rice and doubled the mango & avocado.  I also used vidalia onion since that's what I had and used Fri-Chik (veggie chicken).  It was absolutely delicious!!  My hubby gave it an 8.5/10, which is a HUGE compliment!  Thanks so much for sharing!  :O)

I had some champagne mangoes I bought in bulk and searched for a recipe to try.  This sounded very strange to me but had great reviews so I decided to try it even though my husband looked at me funny. He didn't get to try it yet but I did and it is amazing!!! I was pleasantly surprised!  Such a simple recipe too!  I poached my chicken.  I used two champagne mangoes and 1 avocado.  I used only 3/4 cup uncooked rice and that was plenty since other reviews mentioned using less.  I used a Videlia onion since their sweet.  I was a little short on my cilantro because my plant is on the end of  of its season but more would have been even better!  Thank you for a nice lite and refreshing summer recipe!  I will make again!
This was a totally awesome salad! I made it with quinoa instead of rice, and used frozen mango chunks, and it was soooo good! thanks for this recipe, I am sure I will be making this one again.

This is so creamy and heavenly, everything kheer should be. And so easy to make! My DH loves this one and is thanking you; I am thanking you, for such a tasty treat I could share with my family. Thanks, Chinu!

This was very creamy & rich with the addition of the condensed milk, turned out beauutifully, i doubled it.  My Indian family was very impressed. I made a few changes, used 1/2 coconut milk, 1/2 1% milk (2 cups of each), 1/2 tsp cardamon, we love ground cardamon and 1/2 can of low fat condensed milk, plus 5 tbsp of shredded coconut. If you add less condensed milk then you can add a touch of sugar to compensate for the sweetness lost.  Thanx for sharing a great recipe !

Char, this was sooo yum and creamy. I used 2cups whole milk and 2 cups of skim and low fat condensed milk. I had to add 1/2c sugar extra to suit my family's tastes. I added a few drops of rose water for that 'shahi' taste. This recipe is way better than the ones you get at Indian restaurants. I found the same recipe on daawat.com

I've had kheer before at Indian chains, but they were very watery. The things people try to pass up as "authentic" in the States!! It was really easy to control the consistency with this recipe; thank you! Even my sister, who hates sweets, loved this. Strange, since it is very sweet..

Charishma, you really do post some nice recipes!  I used 1 can of condensed milk but doubled the amount of rice and milk and it was quite sweet for us.  so i can just imagine...the original recipe is really for those for a very SWEET tooth!
Very tasty and so easy to make. Definitely a recipe I would recomment to anyone with sweet tooth....

I love this recipe!! I did tweak it because I like it much thicker. 

Here's what I did:

I used 3 cups of skim milk for 100g of rice. I also used only half a can of condensed milk (because that's all I had) and it was plenty sweet. It was still too thin to my liking, so as I would in a rice pudding, I beat and egg that I warmed up slowly with the liquid before pouring it in. I left it on low heat and stirred until it was thick enough.

Next time (because there WILL be a next time), I'll use 2 cups of milk for the same 100g of rice. Depending on the thickness, I may not add the egg.

This was very nice... the only reason I gave it four stars is because of its consistency (which really is my personnal taste).

Thanks for posting this :)

I made some changes to the recipe. This was a great jumping off point for creative cooking.  I used a can of coconut milk along with 3 cups of whole milk.  I also used about 1 and 3/4 cups of rice.  I added a little bit of vanilla and used 1/2 cup each of almonds and pistachios.  I used a whole tablesopoon cardamom powder.  I thought it was delicious!!

Delicious and very easy!  I reduced the milk to 3 3/4 cups, and increased the rice to 3/4, because I like it to be more ricey and less soupy.  I used 1/4 tsp cardamom which I thought was perfect, but hubby found a little too much.  And I added just a -touch- of rose water.  I didn't find the almonds added anything and will leave them out next time.  DELICIOUS!!!!

The only change I made was to add about 8 whole green cardamom seeds to the milk in the first step (and kept them in throughout the entire process), to decrease the cardamom powder, and to add some nutmeg with the powder.  The condensed milk gives this kheer a nice, gentle sweetness, and is not overpowering at all.  Excellent!

After years of going to a particular Indian lunch buffet on Fridays just so we could eat the AMAZING RICE PUDDING DESSERT my daughter asked the owner the name of the dessert. "It is called kheer" said he. "We should look up a recipe online when we get home" said she and we did! And this has far exceeded our expectations! This will be my 3rd time making it in as many weeks and I use a tea ball and fennel seeds and cardamom pods and a stick of cinnamon when I boil the milk. I also add pistachios at the very end and we LOVE LOVE LOVE IT!!! Thank you!!!

This is even better than the kheer at our favorite Indian restaurant.  My whole family loved it.  I used green cardamom pods and ground my own cardamom to add as well.  I just can't get over how terrific this is.  Thank you!
I love this recipe! It was so easy and delicious. I used 150g. rice, half whole milk and half skim, and whole cardamom pods. Thank you - I will be making this often!

Great recipe! I usually double the recipe and use fat free milk. I omit the condensed milk and sweeten with 60ml of agave nectar. I like it with 1/4 tsp of cardamom.

This gets "sampled" straight from the pot and enjoyed when it's cooled.

It makes a terrific cool desert for after a nice spicy Indian meal.
Perfect EXCEPT?there should be golden raisins as well.    :)
Just wondering how the poor milkmaid likes being popped into the pot?! Sorry, too hilarious for words! Glad we lower the heat in the pot for her!
Very good. I doubled the sugar, cornstarch, water and vanilla.  I like extra filling.  Made it for a crowd.  Everyone was pleased.

This was so good and a breeze to put together! I subbed fresh  strawberries for the blueberries since I had some to use up (and lost out in the dessert vote). The only other thing i did differently was to use raw sugar instead of granulated. The filling was more then enough and perfect sweetness. I can't wait to try this with blueberries!!! Thanks Kitz!

This is so-o-o-o good! I loved the vanilla and lemon juice combination.
I made half a recipe in an 8x8 pan and I have very little leftovers. I also liked the higher fiber content. This is such a versatile recipe. You did it again Kittencal. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

So good!  I made it last night for a family treat. We had it with vanilla icecream.  My husband said it was the best dessert I had ever made!  It is a great recipe.  Just note that the brown sugar goes in with the topping ingredients, not in the saucepan.  I almost goofed!  Thanks for this recipe!
I didnt like this recipee.  The flavor was great but consistency was awful.  I made it twice and both times it turned into blueberry stew.  The crisp part became buried and was no longer crisp.  Yuck

The flavor of this crisp is great! Like some of the other reviewers, my "crisp" doesn't stay very crisp but I thought that was because of my substitutions. I used light butter, splenda baking mix and whole wheat flour. My husband loves this, even without a very crisp top!

This was great!  I was surprised how much the cornstarch caused the berries to gel.  It seemed like there was a lot of liquid when it went into the oven, but it gelled up in the oven.  A big hit at a summer barbecue!

I cut the recipe in half and baked it in a 6x9 pan because I don't really eat blueberries. I just wanted to make a special treat for my BF because blueberries are his favorite. It was a little runny, but he liked it. He says he wouldn't change anything about the flavor. There was just the right amount of crisp and it got nice and brown and crispy. He suggested next time maybe baking it in a pie crust with the crisp on top, so that may be a suggestion to other cooks who can't decide between a pie and a crisp.

Superb! I made it for my sister's baby shower several days ahead of time and froze it; even after thawing it was still delicious and I had several people request the recipe. Thanks for a great, easy summer treat!
I am not a fan of blueberry crisp but even I liked this recipe. My family and friends went crazy for this recipe. Very easy to make and smells divine. Great recipe Kittencal!
No wonder recipes stand the test of time.  This crisp was the best!

I was leary of making a blueberry crisp over an apple crisp but decided to try it with some of my frozen blueberries. I figured if it was one of Kittencal's recipes it had to be good. AND IT WAS! My family loved this. It makes plenty, too. I made a little extra topping simply because we like it with lots, but other than that I made it exactly as directed. Thank you for another yummy recipe!!

Thanks Kittencal!!! This recipe rocked! I've never had blueberry crisp before so I didn't have a clue how this would be. My family loved it. I used frozen berries and only 2 Tblsp. of lemon juice but other than that followed your instructions as written. We served it with chocolate ice cream because that's what we had on hand. I put this in my tried and true cookbook and will certainly make it again. It's a real keeper. Thanks so much for another great recipe.

I doubled the recipe because I had about 8 cups of frozen blueberries.  There was too much topping for my 9 x 13 pan, so I'm saving it to put on muffins sometime.  

This was terrific.  It was a little runny, but no one complained!
This was really good. I had half the blueberries so I halved the recipe, except the topping, and used a 9x7 pan. I am sure we will be making this again as we head into blueberry season.

I followed the recipe exactly. It was fantastic. I didn't think it needed any more sugar. It's blueberry season now and I plan on freezing lots of blueberries to make this later
in the year. Just delicious, and so easy...

This was soooo good! I used fresh bing cherries as that it what I had on hand and needed to use them before they went bad. I used 6 cups of cherries and I doubled the ingredients for the crisp (we like lots of crisp) and baked in a 9x9 square pan.  Came out beautifully! Hubby is making "nom-nom" noises! Thanks for posting! :)
This was a very nice crisp but if you're halving it, make sure and make the full amount of topping.  I didn't and it definitely could have used more.
Fabulous!  I have made it quite a few times as a company dessert, and it always gets rave reviews!
We really liked this. I used frozen blueberries and it turned out great, but I think it would have been even better if I used fresh blueberries.

This crisp is delicious!! I decided to halve this since I was only feeding 4 and I wish I had made th whole thing! I did use 3 cups of blueberries which made it nice and juicy. The crisp part was perfect--not too wet, not too dry, you have a real winner here! I only had reconstituted lemon juice, and it was just fine in this recipe.
The filling in this crisp never set up for me. I cooked until thick on the stovetop, but after the oven baking and cooling it was very runny. It tasted good though.

A couple of shortcuts, no changes.  I used a glass 2-cup measuring cup for the cornstarch/water/lemon mixture and heated it in the microwave until it just started to boil, about 90 seconds on high.  For the topping, I put all of the ingredients in a microwave safe bowl, sliced the butter into 1/2 inch thick squares on top of the unmixed topping, microwaved the whole bowl for about 90 seconds on high.  After the butter was very soft, some edges were liquid, I used a potato masher to mix everything.  Very good recipe!!!

This was wonderful, but got to admit I made some changes (I don't know why, but I've got to put my own spin on things).  I added the zest of the lemon to the syrup.  Used almond instead of vanilla extract.  Used 3 c berries and 2 chopped apples.  Decreased flour to 3/4 c and increased oats to 1 c.  I think I would decrease sugar slightly next time.  Everything came out perfectly: bubbly thick fruit and a nice, crunchy topping.  Served with a dollop of whipped cream.  This is definitely going into my arsenal of dessert recipes.  Can't wait until our nectarines ripen to try this.
Super simple and DELICIOUS! Thanks for sharing!!

I followed the recipe to the letter, and mine turned out a little runny. It tasted really good, though. Will make again with some adjustments - want to add chopped pecans to the topping and thicken the filling a bit more. Overall a really good crisp.
This is an excellent crisp!  Very flavorful and not soggy at all.  Love the oats.  My husband declared this his favorite crisp and that's saying something!

Another winner from Kittencal! I used frozen blueberries so allowed them to thaw and drain thoroughly. Also, I rounded my tablespoons of corn starch so as to counteract any juiciness from using frozen fruit. A 9 x 9 pan worked just fine. Turned out great and so easy to make!
I made the recipe "as is" and loved it.  Used fresh blueberries and thought it went together easily and was wonderful with vanilla ice cream. Thanks Kittencal - we love your recipes!
Used other suggestions and had almond extract instead of vanilla.  Not enough frozen blueberries so add frozen strawberries-----results were Yummo!   Will make again :)  and again:)
This was good but mine turned out runny! I will make it again though! thanks

Another great recipe from Kittencal. Served it to a group of 7 and nothing but thumbs up around the table. Followed the recipe but used white Splenda (1/2cup) with the berries and brown Splenda (1/2 cup) in the topping. Taste your berries for sweetness before deciding how much sugar or Splenda to use. I like almond extract with blueberries so I used it in place of vanilla. No other changes, really very good and will be the go to recipe now.

Kittencal!!! Another amazing recipe chika!!I have to tell you... went out to eat and ordered a blueberry crisp that was awful.I returned it! Went to the market and bought some berries came home and knocked my hubbys socks off with yours!! I used frozen berries so I used a bit more corn starch to compensate for the extra liquid.The lemon syrup seemed weird as thats a new idea for a crisp but it totally worked in the end.Thanks so much for another winner!!
I should have known this would be wonderful!!  OMG....so good...so good!!  My blueberries were BEAUTIFUL....the old man will be so surprised when he gets home from work..teehee...
It was excellent. I had frozen blueberries so I added 3 tsp of cornstarch instead of 2.. It turned perfect. This is now my go to blueberry crisp. Thank you.

FAVORITE blueberry crisp. We could not stop eating it! The best part was that the topping stayed crisp. I used fresh blueberries and made the recipe as written. I will definitely make this again and only hope that it will taste just as delightful with frozen blueberries. The 11 x 7 pan gave it the perfect amount of thickness. Thank you for this recipe.

This recipe was phenomenal and met with rave reviews! I love that there is not butter in the topping. I used 4 cups of blueberries and used an 9X9 baking dish. I ended up having about half of the topping recipe left but kept it in a ziplock bag for the next time!
I made it. it is too sweet and not enough crisp on top for me.

This was pretty runny (even after thickening the sauce well and 40 minutes in the oven) and despite cutting the sugar to 1/2 c. and the brown sugar to 2/3 c., it was still WAY too sweet for my taste. I'll try another recipe next time.
This was fantastic!!  I don't know why it never ocurred to me to do a crisp with blueberries before!

This was really good an I did the almond extract like many suggested. It was runnier than I would have preferred, but that may have been because I didn't have regular oatmeal. Will try again with the correct oatmeal.

Good Recipe.  I made it as written except I omitted the sugar in the blueberries.  After tasting it - it was plenty sweet enough for my tastes.  My berries were nice and sweet however.  I felt the topping was a little too "oaty" for me [again - everyone has different tastes, thats just mine].  When I make it again, I would adjust the flour to oat ratio a tad and maybe add a dash of vanilla in the berries.  Thanks Kittencal for taking the time to post a very good recipe! I cook from scratch almost always and experienced in cooking so I am a tough critic.
Great recipe. I used 6 cups of blueberries but did not increase the sauce. Doubled the topping and added 1 cup of chopped walnuts. Didn't have oats so used Muesli that was lying around. Yum.

I halved the recipe and used a 8X8 baking dish. The fresh blueberries came out running on the topping but it tasted great, especially with vanilla ice cream! Will try to make this again with full ingredients.

Love this!  the only change I made was to leave out the lemon juice (I was out), but we didn't even miss it.  For the person who said it was runny, you really have to make sure the sugar mixture is boiling thick and clear before pouring over the blueberries (for me this took a few mintues).  My blueberry mixture was nice and thick.  The only thing I would do next time is to make double the topping, as I made it in a 13x9 pan and the topping didn't cover it completely.  It was so good, and my entire family liked it (with some vanilla ice cream).

I reduced the sugar in both the topping & the filling to 1/2 c. (each). I believe I could've reduced them both more as it was quite sweet. Overall, a very good recipe and quick to put together. I made in a 9x13 pan and used more blueberries (and frozen) than called for. Thanks for sharing!

I was a little short on blueberries so I subbed some sliced apples.  Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly.  It was FABULOUS!!  Just sweet enough, nice saucy blueberries, and crispy crunchy topping.

Followed the directions perfectly for the perfect crisp.  I did add a couple peaches that I had on hand.  Otherwise made no changes.  Kitten's recipes are always great!  Crisp topping with a delicious blueberry filling.  I added vanilla ice cream to top.  Will definitely make again!
Phenomenal recipe. I followed the recipe (almost) to a tee -- just added about 1/2 pint more blueberries. Served with vanilla gelato, it was summery perfection in a bowl.

Wow! I'm still sneaking this lol! Delish! I made as directed, used almond extract instead of vanilla...added more berries...9x13 pan...wish I had increased the topping...I will make this again and again! Thanks so much Kittencal for another great recipe!! YUM!!

Overall a good recipe, but when I followed it exactly it was way too sweet.  The second time I made it I used raspberries and blueberries, 2 cups of each.  I only added 2 Tbsp of sugar to the syrup.  To the topping I only added 3/4 cup flour and 3/4 brown sugar and increased the oats to <br/>1 1/4 cups.  Way better.  You really could use whatever fruit you want.  It is runny right after you take it out of the oven, it does thicken up as it cools though - if you can get it to last that long!
Made this in a round 2 quart dish with frozen blueberries (added maybe 5 cups).  This was so good we were all just going mmmmmm while we were eating desert.  This is a keeper and easy to make.

So yummy ! My boyfriend loved it and think's it's one of the best desserts ever. 
I served it warm with vanilla ice cream and a dollop of whipped cream.
Looking forward to making this for the 4th of July.
Very good. There is a lot of juice but I don't think that is a bad thing. Like the topping.

Runny mess!
I'm guessing that Cup of water should have been a half cup.
Topping was nice though. And the local blueberries were still awesome. I will try again w some adjustments

I made this per the recipe in a 9X13 and it was tasty but I would make some changes the next time around.  It was a little thin and definitely could have used more topping because of the larger pan.  The next time I will add an additional tablespoon of cornstarch and make an extra half recipe of the topping.
We used fresh picked blueberries that made it much juicer, so you need to adjust for that. We also doubled the crisp because we love crisp. Awesome recipe!!

The name says it all! This really IS the best! I've made this crisp a couple of times now. The first time I made it as written, and while it was to die for, the next time I just reduced the sugar! Our Newfoundland wild blueberries are sweet enough :-) I also added some chopped pecans to the crumble...mmmm, top with some vanilla ice cream and you're good to go!

Oh my goodness!  I just took this out of the oven and tasted it. OK, so I had to blow on it first because it was hot, but it looked so good, I couldn't wait.  It is delicious, perfect, not overly sweet, just the best!  Thank you.
Delicious! I made the recipe as written. I did, however do a mixed berry with raspberries, berries and blackberries. It was runny a bit so next time I would thicken a bit more.

I made this with fresh, like harvested this morning at the farm down the road fresh, berries and the taste was great. The consistencywas an issue though, it turned out runny and overpowered the topping a bit. Bonus, there was plenty of delicious blueberry syrup to spoon on top of your ice cream��.
Great. I used a smaller baking dish which made it deeper (and more delicious), added 5 mins to bake time. Substituted dextrose for sugar in the blueberries. Reduced brown sugar to 3/4 c from 1 c.

This was great. I made it with two pints of fresh Nova Scotia blueberries and threw in a bit of zest from the lemon I juiced. I also put a little splash of maple syrup in with the liquid, and some chopped pecans in the crisp, and topped it with unchopped pecan halves. Served it with a dollop of unsweetened whipped cream because the crisp was plenty sweet on its own. The pecans and lemon zest add a nice depth of flavour. Next time, I'm going to use less water and sugar, and add a bit more maple syrup.

When looking for new recipes for a particular dish, I usually save several variations to try out before deciding which one to keep. This was the first blueberry crisp recipe I tried, and after trying this, there won't be any need to try others. It was simple, easy to prepare, and just delicious. I had three pints of blueberries to use before they went bad, and this was the perfect recipe for them. The only difference (temporary) was I didn't have cornstarch, so substituted flour, and it worked fine. This has definitely gone to the "keeper" file. Thanks so much, Kittencal.

This is a family favorite by all! Ive been making this recipe for years now and know I can't go wrong at any family function if I make this. I don't use that much sugar, and I double the topping (we love our crunch!)

I only had quick cooking oats but they worked fine. I did half fresh blueberries and half chopped apple. I used almond extract instead of vanilla and I subbed coconut sugar for the white sugar. So so so good!!

So disappointed. What's the point of a recipe that needs so many tweaks?? HALVE the sugar. It was Way too sweet - totally drowned out the blueberry flavor (I used fresh). I also added 1/2 roughly ground almonds to the topping, which was good, but didn't compensate for the ridiculously sweet filling. I added some lemon zest - drowned out by sugar. It was also pretty watery, but it might have been OK if I had had time to let it cool, so the jury is still out on that one. Ugh, I thought crisp was foolproof! Apparently not :/
I used almond flour and reduced melted butter to 1/2 stick...also added 1/4 teas. Nutmeg...it was delicious and a little less calories. Also used 8" square pan...would have been too thin in 9x13
I substituted coconut oil for the butter and got RAVE reviews. For a 13x9 pan, I made 1.5 a batch of the blueberry mix and doubled the crumble top. I did not quite use all the topping.
Followed the recipe but it turned out way too sweet.
Super good. I made it in a 9x9 dish and baked for 35 minutes. Five adults had no problem finishing this off. Everybody loved it. Pretty fast and easy to throw together. I will make it again.
Just ok. I thought it was a little heavy on the crust part. I'd prefer a higher fruit to crust ratio.

I followed many peoples advice by only doing half the white sugar. The brown sugar in the topping i used the full amount. I would recommend only using half brown sugar as well as half the white sugar unless your berries are all under ripe. It was a little too sweet, but loved it otherwise

Great recipe! I made it in an 8 x 8” pan so the extra crumbles were nice. ?? I used a combo of fresh picked huckleberries, blackberries and blueberries and cut back on all the sugars. GF flour worked fine. Yummy!

I made this as part of the pick your chef contest and was not the least bit disappointed. Great recipe and so easy.  I served it with a prime rib roast and it was gone in a flash.It is almost sinful how little preparation goes into this dish.  I think I might also try it with fresh baby carrots as well.  Many thanks Lorac for another great recipe.

Nice way to fix carrots!!!Very tasty,not too sweet and quite easy to fix.A nice contrast in taste from the dressing mix and brown sugar!I used the fresh baby carrots and just cooked them til crisp/tender and they were very good!!

I love baby carrots and am trying to get my family to join the club. These turned out great. Nice and tender with a very tasty sauce. I never would have thought to use ranch dressing mix in carrots. My kids even ate them and that is a major accomplishment. Thanks Lorac.
Best carrots I ever had. Your were sure right about the sweet and savory part. I served them with a turkey dinner and everyone loved them. I will make them again and again. Thanks again.
What an interesting twist adding the ranch dressing mix!  I used fresh baby carrots and cooked them for about 8 minutes.  Would probably be great with a few peas thrown in as well. Thanks

What a great new way to fix baby carrots!!  We were not too sure at first about the combination of flavors, but it came out excellent, and was very easy to make. We will definately be having it again in the near future!  Thank You.
I made this at a bbq, and my friends loved it! It really adda a kick to carrots. Thank you for the recipe!

Wow, wow, wow!!! This was the best baby carrot recipe I have ever tried, and I've tried a lot! Delicious buttery, sweet and ranchy taste. I love these! I used fresh carrots instead of frozen and the recipe turned out perfectly.
Thanks for sharing this recipe. We will be eating this over and over again at our home!

LOVE 'EM!!  I made these for a dinner party and everyone loved them, especially the kids.  I used fresh baby carrots and made a 1 1/2X the recipe - it makes a lot of sauce so you really could use double the carrots and just the amount of sauce for 1 lb.  My family really loved the sauce and was dipping everything in it. So glad I saw KC_Cooker's pic of these on a BB, this one is going to be made often.

I do not like veggie's at  all but my husband is diabetic so I try to find things he can eat. I love these, the first carrot I have eat in years. My husband absolutely loved them. Great for any side dish!

My husband doesn't like cooked carrots-or so he thought until we had these for supper last night!  These are great!  Cut the recipe in half for the 2 of us. Some of the sauce ran onto the rice on my plate and that was great too!  Thanx for converting my DH to a cooked carrot eater!

These were delicious! I didn't have an envelope of ranch dressing so I just used around 4 tablespoons of bottled dressing. They turned out great that way too if you need to improvise! Thanks for a keeper!
I was a bit skeptical about the combination of flavors, but am SOOO glad I tried these.  They are fabulous and a great way to get our veggies in!

Easy and delicious way to prepare carrots that's not overly sweet. Ranch flavor is also appealing to picky kids. I used fresh baby carrots and served with meatloaf and mashed potatoes. We'll be having these again! Thanks, Carol, for a great recipe!

This was a very simple recipe that used ingredients I already had.  It is an unusual combination of ingredients and I was a bit skeptical at first, but it was one of those  that the more you ate the better they got!  Thanks for sharing this yummy and unique recipe Lorac!

This is a great, although unusual, recipe for carrots!  I don't like many cooked veggies, but this was great -  a little sweet, and totally unique.  I used fridge temperature baby carrots (not frozen) and it worked perfect!  Thanks!

This is "pan-lickin'" good!  It is an unusual combination of flavors but it works!  I'm thinging it might be great to glaze pork chops or chicken with, too.  There is a good amount of sauce for the carrots so don't be afraid to double the carrots and make the same amount of sauce.  Yum!
This is the second time I have made these - this time I thickened the sauce up with a little corn starch so it would stick to the carrots better. My kids loved it! Thanks!
Great recipe.. Have to say I was very skeptical of the ranch, but I'm sure glad we tried....

I made these for Thanksgiving last night, and I wasn't quite sure if I liked them or not at first. I thought they tasted a little too artificial with the ranch seasoning. However, today I find that the ranchy-ness has mellowed out and it's delicious! Yay for leftovers!

This is a staple side for many of my meals when company calls.  I sometimes have trouble when it gets hard to stir at first, when the ranch mix is added, but I add a tsp of hot water and keep stirring and it works out.  We don't thicken this, because we use the leftover sauce for gravy.
Loved it!!  Not sure what the ranch dressing does, but we sure enjoyed it.
Made these for easter dinner and these were liked all around the table, thanks for posting!

I made this a couple of weeks ago, to try on my kids (there are not veggie eaters)!  My daughter (6 year ould) the pickiest of the 3 said.. mom can you make these every monday now until I'm in college!!  As far as I'm conserned these are a winner!! I’ve enjoyed everyone’s positive comments about Essence. I agree 100%. I plan to share them with my customers. However, here is another thought for those who have heart and high blood pressure problems.. Omit the SALT! I had folks coming in and buying their spices to make their own Essence, from the Internet recipe. Having been in the business for 21 years, I figured that for every person who will make their own batch, 25 to 30 won’t take the time. I was right. I started offering our SALT FREE version, and it is the jar that I refill the most, out of over 150 jars of herbs and spices. I had to scale up the recipe to make it in pounds, That is when I found out the recipe on the Internet is 43% SALT, by weight! I like the NO SALT version so much that I take it with me when I eat out. I carry it in my pocket, in brass camper matchbox. One of the chains has a broiled fish lunch that they put Blackened seasoning on. It is way over on salt. We just tell them to make it without salt, and we shake on some of our essence. Perfect! Try NO SALT essence on French Fries that are SALT FREE. Also, try Hungarian Paprika in the recipe, instead of Sweet or Domestic Paprika. It is better. You can add other herbs and spices of your choice to make you own customized essence. Use it to cook with or at the table. Use it as an “all-purpose seasoning”. Add some Chili Powder and you have Emeril’s “Southwest Seasoning”.Enjoy.
