Easy and yummy recipe! I changed it a bit because of the ingredients I had on hand. I decided instead of chips to layer the bottom and in between each layer with flour tortillas. Love this stuff! It's so quick and easy! I added onions and garlic to the beef mixture, and it turned out great. Even my picky daughter liked it and she doesn't like tacos. It's good with sour cream on top.

Fantastic! Everyone ate their plates clean, even the fussiest that doesn't like anything but<br/>peanut butter. Thank you for sharing.

This really is fantastic! DH, who is a hot-dish hater (boo to him!) really liked it. Simple and quick - can't get much better. I think might have added a can of black beans to beef it up. If not (it's been a while since I made it) I would add it and it would be good!
This is definitely one of the better taco casseroles I've tried. I only had to bake it for about 10 minutes, which kept the chips from getting soggy.

I have tried many taco casserole recipes, but this one was quite different from any I have tried. The refried bean layer is what makes it so incredibly delicious. Added a few sliced jalapenos on top. Perfect. Thanks for posting.
Really good!  No corn chips on hand but I did have tortillas that I cut into bite size pieces and browned up in canola oil.  The recipe is a keeper and I will make again with the corn chips.  Thanks!

This recipe lived up to its name. It was pretty fantastic. I made it as described though I did go with low-cal organic corn chips since regular corn chips sneak on quite a few extra calories. My entire family loved this. Easy to make and a one pan meal.

We loved this casserole.  It was easy and fast to make.  Next time, we thought we would save half the corn chips to sprinkle on top when it's served, to add some crunch. This is definitely one of our new favorites!

Very good Taco Casserole!   To make things easier, I heated the refried beans in the microwave for two minutes and then added the cheese and salsa, stirring well. Made this last night, and it was sooooo good.  The kids liked it too, but the taco seasoning was a littl to spicy for them.  So next time gonna not use taco seasoning on their half.  Have to figure out what other seasoning I can use for them.
very good

I just made this last night and loved it.  I made it the way the recipe called but then added some crushed up corn chips to the bottom of the plate & the top of the casserole when I served it. Thanks so much for the recipe, it's very tasty.

I did put a little salsa on the top of my share, however.  It was soooo good!

Yummy! Talk about a good old fashioned comfort food. A+

Found this recipe a few months back and use it all the time. I had never used yeast before because I didn't realize how simple it could be to make fresh pizza dough. The only thing I do different is I mix the sugar with the water and yeast and let sit 10 minutes, add the flour and salt together, after the 10 minutes add the oil to the yeast mixture and then add the flour and salt and stir until the mixture follows the fork around the bowl and then I let it sit in a warm place for 10 minutes. When I drop it on the pizza pan, I start from the middle and work my way to the edge leaving about 1 to 1 1/2 inches from the edge as poofy as I can so that I can have a "mock breadstick". It taste like a warm roll and sometimes I add 1 to 2 tablespoons of sugar to make what my MIL calls sweet bread. I also bake it for 6 to 8 minutes on 400 degrees and then put the toppings on and bake for another 6 to 8 minutes to a golden brown. My husband's favorite is to top it with a sloppy joe type sauce and microwave 12 frozen meatballs for about 3 minutes, cut in half and put rounded side up on pizza, layer with thin onion circles and top with motzarella cheese. Delicious and easy!!!

For a perfect thin crust pizza, roll 1/4 of the dough into about a 10 inch diameter pizza. Top, and bake at 425 for 15 minutes. I use a holed aluminium pizza pan and get ideal results. Remember to bake your pizza on the lowest rack, closest to the heating element. The dough does taste better after it's aged at least a day in the refrigerator.

This recipe produces exactly what I've been looking for in years of almost daily trials with different recipes and techniques. Yes, I make pizza almost every day, and dough almost every week. Unfortunately at this point I can only speak to how well this recipe holds up in a thin, cracker-like crust pizza. Because it is so good I haven't bothered to try it with thicker crusts. I have never been able to make a thin crust pizza as perfect as this. The dough bakes up perfectly firm and crunchy with perfect browning around the edges. Flavor is a little dull on the first day, as should be expected. After at least a day in the refrigerator the flavor improves dramatically. When I remove it from the refrigerator I let it come to room temperature before using. I like to have prepared dough on hand. This dough ages very well. I'm currently on day 4, and I would say it is as good if not better than its second day. I haven't been able to keep it long enough to find what age it reaches peak flavor.

I love, love, love this recipe!! Why would anyone buy a pizza crust when this one is a cinch to pull together and sooo yummy!? I use garlic powder and italian seasoning in the crust and it is so flavorful. Thanks.

I used fresh tuna for the fish, and used cream cheese and Extra sharp Cheddar for the cheese.  It was a delightful combination and blended really well with the fish.  This will be made again!

Perfection for a Spring nite. This is as beautiful a dish as it is to devour. You could serve this for so many things. At a shower, (cut in smaller pieces, with that beautiful sauce over/top) for a wonderful dinner presentation, a brunch, anything, anytime! I followed this exactly, except used fresh chives instead of the grated onion. The colors of the sauce were so pretty! I used tilapia, and some mild cheddar cheese in the sauce. Very, very easy to prepare and I broiled the fish and it was perfect and flaked wonderfully! Made for your win, *ZWT Six* "Zee Zanies Cookz" May 2010

Yum! We used fresh dolphin which was cooked to perfection in 10 minutes. For a thinner fish like snapper I'd probably reduce the oven temperature. This makes lots of sauce - maybe enough for 5  pounds of fish.
Good!   Very easy to make, I used frozen California Vegetable Mix instead of all broccoli.  Thanks for posting.
WOW!!!! This soup is AMAZING!  its good hot or cold... fabulous! I added a bit of an extra kick to it by adding parsley leaves and blackened seasoning right as it was finishing up.

Wow. Yum, yum, and yum! DH and I devoured this stuff, and not for a minute did it taste low fat! I added a sprinkle of garlic powder, onion salt, and black pepper, all of which went nicely with the recipe. Thanks so much for this--it will definitely become a standby!
Very good and very low points!  I have been eating it for lunch every day!  It was a little spicier than I was expecting, but not too spicy to eat.  Thanks for a great recipe!
This is good stuff.  My daughter and I enjoyed it very much.  I can make a pot on Sunday and eat for lunch all week.  Thanks for posting!!

YUM! I used regular Velveeta as the grocery store I went to only had that. I put in 8oz. instead 10oz. to try and keep the point values close. I also used fresh broccoli instead of frozen. I must have made larger portions though because I only got 7 servings...still figure it to be under 3 points. Thanks for the recipe!
This was a very good and SIMPLE soup to make.  It did turn out spicier than I would have thought.  Still very tasty!

I used this recipe as my starting point, mostly because of ingredients I had in the pantry.  I only had 1 bag of broccoli so I added a can of cream corn.  I did not have Velveeta so I used a 2-cup bag of low fat shredded cheddar.  I thought I needed more spice so I added a couple of teaspoons of chili seasoning.  Finally, I added a couple of cups of cooked, shredded chicken from the freezer.  This ended up tasting really good.  Sorry to change the whole recipe almost, but it turned out really well this way.  Thanks so much.
Wonderful, easy soup for such a low point base.  Will make this often.
YUM!  Loved how spicy it was!  This was so easy and full of tons of flavor.  Thanks!
Crazy easy & crazy good!  I used a stick blender to sorta puree it & loved it!  I've made it several times & recommend it to everyone... Thanks for posting it here!

Five HUGE stars!! This was awesome; I made half the recipe for supper last night and DH and I really enjoyed. Since I used broccoli florets, I had to transfer them to my food processor for just a quick chop (otherwise it would have been too hard to eat) - I'd recommend buying broccoli cuts for this recipe. Will be making again!
This was sooo so good! Even  my kiddos ate it! The only tweaking I did was use 1 box of beef stock and 1 box chix stock. It was awesome!! Thanks!

YUM! This is wonderful! Its filling and satisfying too! IT does go great with a small piece of crusty bread. It hits the spot! Especially on a cold winter day! My husband really liked it also.  Anyway, thanks for the great recipe!! Its a keeper for me!
This was so easy and so delicious.  My picky 6 year old ate his whole bowl...now that is saying something.  We all loved it!  Thank you for sharing this with us.
Great soup!! I make this every week so I have it on hand. I just love it. It's an easy way to get a veggie in and a nice low-point snack that keeps me on track. Thank you!

This taste just like any other Broccoli and Cheese soup. You can't tell a difference in the lower fat/calories. I chose not to put the can of tomatoes in it. This makes the recipe 2 pts per cup. I will try the tomatoes next time to save that point. This is a great snack for in between meals or before a meal so you don't eat as much of your main meal. Thanks so much for sharing. (I also garnished with green onion)

Very tasty soup, I think it's going to be a good option to eat some when I'm hungry between meals. I'm not sure why 1 pt is posted, I calculated and it's 2 pts per serving (this is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5). Even when I calculated pts using the calories for all the ingredients I used (followed recipe to a T) it still comes out to 2 pts per serving. Still tasty though! :o)

This is very tasty and easy to make.  I calculated the points and agree with levz44, it is 2 points per cup, which is still great!  A group of us at work are doing WW together and 5 of us have a lunch group going.  Each one makes lunch for everyone else one day a week.  I made this today for the group and it was a big hit.  I gave each of us 2 cups and it was very filling!  Thanks for the great recipe.  I will be making it again. :)
Very good.  Big hit at work.

This was okay.  Broccoli Cheese soup is a huge indulgence of mine, so this low fat version, didn't really cut it for me.  DH did not like the addition of the tomatoes at all.  It's an okay soup, think, but taste is okay.  Just don't compare it to "traditional" Broccoli Cheese soup and you will enjoy it.

Sorry for the lower rating, but just not my fave.  Thanks for posting!
YUM! The only difference I had was that I used vegetable broth. But, this was so yummy. My consistency was a little weird, but that did not stop me from eating every last drop! Thanks so much!
WINNER!  Thanks for posting...only added onion and celery and cooked for a bit then added broccoli, just because that's how I've always made it-DELISH!
I've made this before, it's been awhile but I always loved it! It's easy and quick and oh so yummy.

I love this recipe.  It is much better for  you than most broccoli cheese recipes, but it doesn't taste like it.  It is super quick and easy, and very tasty.  I like to use fresh broccoli florets, but when they are tender I put about 1/2 in the blender. This adds a little thickness to the soup, without adding thickeners.
Great!  I will add this to my regular soup rotation!
this was sooo easy!  It was a little spicy, but it's worth it!  very yummy!!

Easiest soup I have ever made.  And it is delicious!  I wanted it creamy so I took the soup mixture and put in blender and pureed it....yummy!  Warning... let soup cool before pureeing or else you will have soup all over your kitchen too :-{

I made this last night using a bag of california blend mixed vegetables instead of broccoli (it's what I had on hand) and it is fantastic!  I used about 3 1/2 cups of reduced sodium chicken broth and added a couple of tablespoons of cornstarch/water to thicken at the end. Very good - glad to find this posted her for future reference!

I must have forgotten to review this. I LOVE this soup, and it's so easy to make. I like to use broccoli florets, as opposed to brocolli cuts because sometimes you can get some hard-to-chew pieces in the cuts. I also use the mild Rotel, it's less spicy but still has a kick. Going to make some right now! -- UPDATE: this past time I bought the wrong Rotel, I got the kind that's made for chili... it was okay, but I won't do that again!

I can not believe how easy this soup is.  It is great.  I made exactly like the recipe is written for some friends and got great raves.  The soup is much thinner than you normally find for broccoli cheese soup, but the tomatoes added a little extra kick that was a nice make up for the thinner texture.

We loved this soup!  DH said I could make it every night if I wanted.  I didn't choose this recipe for the WW points, but because I wanted a healthier Broccoli Cheese soup.  I did use 16 oz of 2% Velveeta instead of the 10 oz, just to make it a little more cheesy.  I also used only 32 oz of chicken broth.  I didn't want huge chunks of broccoli, so I used 3 10 oz boxes of chopped broccoli.  I'm not a tomato lover (most of the time I eat around them), but while I could see the tomatoes, I coudn't really taste them or the texture of them.  DH liked the spiciness the Rotel added.

Easy and delicious!  We loved the added flavor of the Rotel.  I like my broccoli a little crunchier in texture, so next time I will probably only simmer it for half the time, but that is just me :)  Thanks for sharing!

This was good, but way TOO HOT!  I used regular rotel, not hot, but next time I would use only half a can.  For this batch I added some milk and that helped cut the heat.  We liked it, but it was way too hot for us.

I loved this!  I made it exactly as written (using frozen broccoli cuts).  As for the heat that many have mentioned, I don't like spicy things at all, but didn't feel this was hot.  It gives a subtle burn in the back of your throat, but didn't have me reaching for water.  For a meal, I have 2 cups of this, but one cup is great for a snack.  
I felt this has the same flavor as traditional broc cheese soup, but a much thinner consistency.  That was fine with me.  I have eaten this for lunch 3 days in a row!
It was so easy, I know I'll make it over and over again.

What a wonderful guilt free soup! I also made as written, but I used an immersion blender to cut up some of the larger broccoli pieces and I thought it had a nice texture. My husband, who needs no diet, thought it was one of my better ww meals. I served it with an Orowheat sandwich thin toasted for dipping for 1 added point.

WOW!!!!  This was a WONDERFUL recipe- wish I'd found it sooner!  I'm planning to make it again this week, double it and freeze half of it!  Easy, quick and great flavor with so little ingredients!  I think it would be great with half broccoli and half cauliflower, also!  YUM!
this was really really good. I wished I had doubled the batch so I could get it for the next week. Thank you so much for posting this.

What an easy recipe to make.  It would have even been easier if I used frozen broccoli.  But I used the leftover fresh broccoli from Easter that I had cleaned for the relish tray.  I did need to buy another bunch of broccoli to get 2 pounds.  I saved all the end stalks and used them after I took the "bark" off.  Before adding the cheese, I  used an immersion hand blender to puree the soup.  The Rotel tomatoes gave this a hint of heat.  Made for *I Recommend Tag Game  April 2010*  recommend by *Starrynews*
I had been looking for a great Broccoli Cheese soup for weeks...never thought I'd find one that tastes so good AND point-friendly!  It was VERY good.
This is a very good Weight Watchers recipe!

I absolutely adore this recipe! I don't do well with spicy things, but I didn't find it hot at all, just left kind of a pleasant burn in the back of your throat. This was a big hit when I had my parents over and they've mentioned it several times. I did change the recipe a bit, just because of availability - I used a 32oz carton of low-sodium chicken broth and 16oz of regular Velveeta (that was just because I knew I wouldn't use the leftover Velveeta anywhere else, but I like the cheesiness). Thank you for a wonderful, exciting recipe!

I've been making this for a while and, like another reviewer, use California blend frozen veggies because it has more variety in the veggies.  Will try it with just broccoli sometime, too.  I don't think it's too spicy.  You can taste a little kick but I don't like really hot stuff & think this is perfect.  I do make it because it's low in WW pts & very filling.

Love this soup!  It has to be the easiest, quickest soup I've ever made, but it is packed with flavor and has a nice kick to it.  I opted to puree the soup in the blender as I like my cream of broccoli soup creamier and without chunks of vegetables in it.  This is really good stuff...love that it is also healthy, too.
Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe! I was in real need for comfort food tonight and this recipe hit the spot! I will make this over and over. So cheesy and delish!
Much too thin for my liking.  I added 4oz extra cheese, pureed the broccoli stalks, added 2 tsp of corn starch and about 3 T of potato flakes and it was more what we were looking for.

This soup is incredibly great!  Quick, easy and full of flavor!  My husband the chef loves it so I know it is something I can make and he will love.  Everyone asks for the recipe!  Will make this often!!!!!!

Thought this was very good. Made this for my wife who is on weight watchers. Lots of flavor used fresh broccoli instead of frozen. The only thing i wish was that the soup was thicker in texture. But the flavor was there and we both enjoyed it very much.

This is a great recipe.  I was skeptical of how flavorful it would be given the simplicity of the ingredients however the Rotel (I used mild for my childrens sake) added a nice flavor.  I too love a thick soup so I added a TB of corn starch mixed with water at the end which did thicken it up.  This is a keeper and my 11 yr old son loved it!
OMG.  Yum. Yum Yum Yum.  :)

This was awesomely good.  Granted, I substituted Velveeta Queso Blanco since that's what I had on hand so I don't know if the low fat version would have made much of a flavor change.  I never would have thought to add Rotel to a cheesy broccoli soup but it added a lot of flavor and spice that we all really enjoyed.  Like other reviewers suggested, I added a cornstarch slurry to thicken up the soup and it was just the thing it needed.  The recipe says it serves 10-12 but I got about 5-6 large servings out of this.  I look forward to making this again with the low fat cheese.

It doesn't get any easier than this!  This is a good hearty vegetable soup for low points.  I used a combination of frozen broccoli, cauliflower and carrots and pureed some with my immersion hand blender when cool. It turned out nice and thick this way. Next time I will try with just broccoli cuts and not puree and see what I think.  Also will try with petite diced tomatoes as my daughter thought it was a bit too spicy even though I used mild rotel.  I think this is a perfect lunch soup for winter.  Thanks for posting!
It had a nice flavor but was a lot thinner than I expected.
Absolutely delicious!!  It was even better the next day!

Delicious!  I had to thicken it quite a bit with cornstarch.  At first I thought it was light on cheese taste, but as I ate it, it really grew on me.  By the time I finished it, I was in love.  I also added 2 garlic cloves and onion softened in Pam.

Made this tonight to start off our New Year's diet. Super good. My husband, I, and 3 of our children ranging from ages 12 to 3 gobbled this up and said it was the best soup.;) I added two Tbls. cornstarch and sprinkled with garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper also added 12 oz. reduced fat Velveeta. I also pureed one of my bags of broccoli,but left the other one as whole florets. We will be making this again.

Quick and easy guilt free soup. However, it is not thick and creamy. It is more of a cheese flavored broth.  Also, using Rotel makes it spicy. If you do not like spicy food, just use diced tomatoes instead of Rotel. The taste is delicious and it is incredibly easy to make and freeze.
Really Good, has a nice kick but thats what makes it great, I used regular velveeta because I  could not find low fat at my local walmart. I put the entire 12oz of cheese. Thx for the post!!!

OK this isnt haute cuisine, but I'm giving this 5 stars for what it is--good tasting , low calorie and reasonably healthy.  And very easy to make.  What's not to like about that?  I read the reviews and added some red pepper flakes for some kick, and added about 2 teaspoons of corn starch to thicken it a bit....but I just added extra broccoli florets for bulk and didnt find it too thin at all.  Thanks for the recipe.

This was delicious!!! I added some diced onion and a t. of garlic paste. I also used hot Rotel which was TOO HOT. But flavor was great. Next time Im going to double it and use one hot and one mild Rotel. Also I recalculated and it loosk like it is now 3 pts per cup. THANKS!!!
Delicious!  Perhaps I'm just a wimp, but I have to make this with mild Rotel or else it's way too spicy.  Otherwise this is perfection, and I'm not even on a diet!
I could eat this soup all day!

I am a beginner when it comes to cooking and also wanted to cook something within a small budget and that was healthy. This is the best recipe for health and budget it taste delicious I will be making it again!
Made this soup today and it is yummy!  I added grated carrot, onion, and spinach. This one is a keeper!

Just made this... added some corn starch, but this is going to be a staple item. I also used lower sodium, fat-free chicken broth. I made a half batch and will use a little of the left over lower fat cheese to make a half of a grilled cheese sandwich for lunch tomorrow.

Some alternatives I'm thinking of might be to add a bean of some sort to add protein, but this soup is very satisfying already.
Very satisfying! I used mild Rotel and loved the kick to it! Just love it
Excellent recipe! I added two pinches of garlic powder and I only used 2 cans of chicken broth and 8 oz of velveta cheese.
Did not like this soup @ all, was way watery.  And it was spicey hot from the tomatoes with green chiles which I thought was odd for broccoli chees soup,  Will not be making this again.

I made this soup last night and followed the directions precisely. My family loved it and I would definitely serve it to friends. I made a double batch and froze into portions so that my family could take it for lunch and eat healthy. WOW! Made this last night and it was deeeelicious! So sorry, but I really didn't care for this recipe.  I was making for my family and knew the kids would not like the big chunks of broccoli so I decided to puree a bunch of the veggies. This is me and my Dad's recipe!!!!! So excited to see this on here and feeling pretty fortunate someone placed it on the internet because when we got robbed, sadly they also took out USB with weight watchers recipes we'd come up with. There was a recipe for something similar in the weight watchers books that wasn't very hearty or good to be honest. We like our food with a little bit of spice so this was our way of putting a healthy spicy spin on a classic. Glad someone else enjoyed it as much as we did!

Love this soup! I usually mash the broccoli a little bit and I think that thickens it plenty. We usually eat it with french bread or some other type of crusty bread/roll and it's perfect. Just the right amount of spice but would be easy to add more if you like. This went into my regular meal rotation after the first time I made it - great warmed up too!

This is delicious!!! I have made it several times and don't know why I haven't given it a review until now.. I love broc/cheese soup but tried to avoid it due to it's fat and calorie content. thanks to this recipe I can go back to enjoying it guilt free!! Thanks for posting !!!

I made this yesterday, and boy oh boy is this delicious! I followed the recipe to the letter with the exception of blending it until it was kinda smooth with some chunks. I seasoned it with garlic salt and some red pepper flakes to spice it up a little. This is something I will always keep on hand.

5 star flavor, but 2 star consistency. i read reviews before completing the recipe so i added 2tsp corn starch and 3T potato flakes... it really does help!! this recipe is super fast and easy to make... not to mention i only spent 9 dollars on ingredients. i have plenty of cheese left over so i might make cheesy couscous another night :)

I made this a couple weeks ago... a very hearty, good soup. It was a bit spicy for my liking, next time I might just use the original Rotel. But a very good soup to have for leftovers! And with it being so low in calories you can divulge in a nice slice of crusty bread with it, or even add some crackers to it! Will definitely be making this again... (With that one change!)

This is a 3 to 4 star rating.  I think this is too thin and the rotel tomatoes were a bit much for the kiddos.  I tried to thicken by adding more cheese and cornstarch.  I loved the cheese flavor but the frozen broccoli is mostly stalks.  I think next time I will use fresh broccoli and one less can of broth. One fun things is I did not have the slightest amount of time to cook.  I threw it all in the crockpot and cooked it on HIGH for 4 hours. Worked great. Thank you fro the recipe it is a great starter to personalize with.
Wow! I very much liked this. Great taste with so few ingredients. The right amount of heat and good broccoli taste. So low in calories that I will be making this a lot. Thanks a thousand times.

This is a delicious and easy soup. If you find it too thin let it boil without a lid for a few minutes and it will thicken up.<br/>I found that using fresh broccoli instead of frozen made it thicker too.
Love this soup...it taste great and it's easy to make.  I used fresh broccoli and thickened it up a little with corn starch. Yummy!
loved it!
Excellent soup.  I made exactly as written and it was spicy enough and has a wonderful taste.  I love cheese and Rotel together and will try with other veggies as well.
Wow love this! I used off brand tomatoes and just added chili powered and garlic. Like others said, it was a bit thin, so I added more cheese. Even still, you can't beat the points on this :)
When I first got this recipe it called for Diced tomatoes with roasted garlic and a bag of California Vegetables. My family loves it!!
I loved this soup! Very easy and very tasty. The only thing I added was some diced ham. Thanks for the recipe! This one is a keeper!

I loved this but with the modifications I made. <br/>Add to existing recipe:<br/>1 small onion, finely chopped (0 points)<br/>1/4 cup whole wheat flour (1 point)<br/>1/2 cup carrots, finely chopped (0 points)<br/>1/4 t. nutmeg (0 points)<br/>Salt and Pepper to taste (0 points)<br/><br/>Spray the pot with cooking spray <br/>Place onions in pot, cooking for 3-4 min until they begin to soften.<br/>Sprinkle flour over onions & stir to combine, cooking for about 1 min.<br/>Slowly stir in broth and Ro*Tel<br/>Add broccoli, and carrots, nutmeg, dash of salt, and pepper; simmer 20-30 min until broccoli is tender.<br/>Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring to melt the cheese after each addition.<br/>At this point use an immersion blender to break up the broccoli,  or transfer to a blender in batches to puree completely.  <br/>Serve. <br/><br/>*Adding the flour will thicken the soup eliminating the complaint from other reviewers that the soup is too thin.  If you're worried that the Ro*Tel will make it too spicy, don't.  I'm a wimp when it comes to spicy food but this was just the right amount of kick for me.  The cheese balances the Ro*Tel.  If you like your broccoli soup with an even bigger punch then you could add crushed red pepper flakes and/or more green chilies to taste.  Since I didn't make the original recipe it's difficult to score but I'd feel bad giving it anything under 4 since I used it as a base.  With the modifications I made I'd give this 4.5 stars.

I did t make the recipe as is based on comments. I added 1 cup mushrooms, 1/2 cup each chopped onion, yellow bell pepper and parsley, 1 clove garlic chopped, 1 stick lemongrass, 1 tsp Thai seasoning, 1/2 tsp cayenne and black pepper.
This was delicious and had to share with my friends. I only had 2 cans of chicken broth so I added some veggie broth, no difference and I used fresh broccoli. Perfect. Thanks for sharing.
This was quite good.  I cooked some carrots first then added the other things.  My kids couldn't even tell that there were diced tomatoes in this...they thought they were red peppers (bwahahaha)!

Very good recipe and very easy. I definitely will make this again. I would recommend cutting back on the amount of chicken broth just a bit and adding more as needed. It was a bit thin and I didn't want to add anything to thicken it and ruin the points value. The broccoli will soften up after reheating so if you plan on saving some leave the broccoli on the crunchy side after the initial cooking (maybe steam it instead?). Freeze it in several small containers instead of one big one so you're not reheating it several times over.

Made as posted.  Used a bit of cornstarch to thicken and used my immersion blender (best invention ever) .  not really thick but perfectly good. I would probably skip the tomatoes with peppers next time or not use as many.  Just personal preference.    Thanks so much for a good quick recipe that has saved my day a couple of times this week already! !!

If you want a REALLY delicious broccoli soup, go to Looney Spoons.   I call theirs Dream of Broccoli and serve it to guests all the time getting RAVES.    It's low in WW points but it's actually good enough to make a complete lunch with just some good bread on the side.
Hello, I am new to this and caregiving to a family member ...wondering how big is a portion? I just bought a portion dish but what about soups? Thank you for your input.

This is my go to cold weather recipe for when it is late and I have nothing planned. Everything can be kept on hand. If you get a large Velvetta block the remainder freezes well. I use a bit more cheese. Not gourmet, but quick, easy and good!
Interested in making this, but don't want to use precessed cheese. Can you recommend a real cheese to use instead?
A three day ice storm was predicted for outer area so I made plans to make many of the recipes I had been wanting to try. My family loved this soup.

Tried this recipe this weekend and YUM! The only thing I changed was I used 16oz regular Velveeta instead of 10oz reduced fat (didn't know what I'd use the extra 6oz of Velveeta for, so just tossed it in). I also added a liberal sprinkling of pepper and a bit of salt right at the beginning. I did notice that because the broccoli is frozen, it doesn't really "simmer" until the broccoli is actually done. Next time I make it I might add a lb of dice chicken breast, seems like it would go well with this soup.
It came out great! And I made a double batch and froze several containers for a quick lunch.

For my taste, this was far too watery to even taste any cheese. I used a full pound of the cheese, added a little miso, and still had to add some corn starch slurry to thicken it (which worked very easily). This cake was excellent.  I replaced the pecans with walnuts.  It also stores very well.
I have made this cake about 15 times since I found it on the website: it is easy to make and it is incredibly delicious. Thank you for posting it.
Super easy to make and incredibly moist. Nest time I was thinking about adding some nutmeg to the cake batter. Great brunch cake!

I just made this cake for the first time.  It is dense, rich, and just nutty/sweet enough.  The only thing I may do differently is I gambled & used mix with pudding in it (plus adding pudding). But even with the extra pudding, the cake is delicious.

FABULOUS!
Very easy to make and sooo moist! This was wonderful, I will be making it again, and again, and again <grin>
Just made this for the crew at work and it was great. I used butterscotch pudding and dusted it with confectioners sugar, what a great recipe, I know I will come back to this one!
i went on a baking binge this weekend and this was one of our favorites!!! doesn't even vaguely taste like a cake mix cake. we loved the caramel taste the brown sugar gave the cake. yum!!!

What a lovely cake, great flavour and so rich, moist and tender. We absolutely loved this cake. My DH does not like nuts so I subed with fresh sweet bing cherries instead, I also added 1/4 cup of sweet golden sherry  and decreased the water from 1 cup to 3/4. This made a lovely big cake...thank you so much for sharing Ann.

Wow, this cake is marvelous!  Made this for our Thanksgiving Dinner yesterday and it went down a real treat with anyone that had some.  I personally loved it.  Moist, delicious and one I know I will make again. Thanks!

What a yummy cake!  Made it this morning.  The only thing I changed was I left out the nuts as we don't really care for them.  It is lovely - dense, rich, moist, mmm.  Quite sweet, though, so you only need a little bit.  I did not ice this at all but I think next time I might try dusting with a little powdered sugar.

This is delicious!  The outer part is crunchy and the inside is nice and moist.  I think a little cinnamon and nutmeg would be a nice addition.
