It tasted good, it was just a bit too much for me, and a little too spicy.  I always give the benefit of the doubt, and since it was most likely the baking that was the culprit, I am going to try this again, on the grill... and hopefully it won't rain next time.  :)

This was fabulous!  I am amazed that this simple spice mixture produces such a crispy skin.  It is the best grilled chicken recipe I have ever tried, and I have tried many, many recipes over the years,trying to get that crispy skin. Yummy!

We grilled as the recipe stated, but then we put into a pan and baked for 2 hours at 300 degrees for fall-off-the-bone chicken legs.  I nuked one for lunch today.  WOW!!!!  Extremely tasty.  Such an easy recipe.  Thanks for posting!

Wow Rita!! This is terrific! Just a delicious, crispy skin that left the inside moist too.
This is going to be a regular here, and not just for chicken legs, I am thinking all of the chicken! Yummo!
My Dad was here for dinner and said to tell "his sweetie" that her legs are great LOL!!
We all loved this one, thanks Rita!

I made this for dinner last night and the chicken turned out fantastic!  Thanks for posting the recipe.  

I ended up marinading it for 24 hours in a food saver bag and I basted the chicken with BBQ sauce the last 15 min. of cooking time.  This is deffinately something that I will be making often!

Thanks again Rita!

When I read that this recipe only needs 1 tsp of seasoning salt, I wondered if it would work well, but with so many great reviews, I tried it out anyway. Wow, really great chicken, and I used salt instead of seasoning salt cos I don't have any. Baked it in an oven and broiled it for about 2 minutes before taking out of oven. My family thanks you for posting.
I've tried this with thighs and breasts, and it tastes nicer every time I make it.

I tried this tonight, the chicken was extremely tender, but salty, even for my husband who puts salt on EVERYTHING.  Preheated the gas grill , oiled it and closed the lid, they caught on fire within 10 minutes.. so we had charred skin. Maybe we should have kept the lid open and watched it??  We will attempt this again :-)
DELICIOUS! Very easy to marinade. I used on a whole chicken that I roasted. YUM-O!!

Just delicious and simple!!! I didn't even get to marinate it for the full 4 hours and the chicken still turned out flavorful and tender... Amazing!!! Simplicity is the key to the delicious, crispy skin on the chicken and the tender fall-off-the-bone meat... Thanks for sharing!!!

These turned out so delicious!  Only change I made was to work half the marinade under the skin of each leg quarter, and the remaining marinade over the outer surface of each before letting them chill.
These were so juicy and full of flavor- absolutely fabulous!  Thanks so much for sharing!
Used boneless skinless chicken breast. Turned out very good and moist on the grill. Will probably add more spice next time. Thanks for the recipe!
Outstanding! This is the rub/marinade that I will use for chicken on the grill from now on.

I made this for dinner and it was very tasty.  I found it very difficult to get the chicken covered with the marinade using a ziplock bag.  Next time I would mix all ingredients in a small bowl and then rub the paste onto the chicken pieces.  Didn't have a problem with grilling them over indirect heat.  They turned out great!!
WOW!  Great taste, easy to do, simple ingredients--what more could anyone want.  Thank You for a great supper!
I just bought a new BBQ and have to get used to it.  I managed to burn these quite nicely.  However, it will be done again and this preview looks very good.  Thanks Rita

I used this on thin sliced chicken cutlets.I only left them in the bag and marinade for about an hour and then threw them on the grill.
They were very tasty and my whole family enjoyed them.
Fantastic!  Simple.  And more importantly, ingredients I generally always have on hand.  I did add a bit of cayenne pepper.  Leftovers were chopped up for a homemade chicken pot pie.  Thanks!

Nice flavor and tender--I used homemade AHA seasoning for the seasoning salt, and baked the boneless chicken thighs rather than grilling.  Served it with Twice baked potato casserole recipe #26043, a steamed vegetable medly, fresh cut-up fruits and sour dough bread.  My DH and I both loved it and will make it again.  I might add cayenne next time for extra kick, but good as it is.  Thanks for an easy and tasty recipe for marinate-ahead entree.

My legs looked exactly like Marg@Cayman's and I found them to be moist and perfectly cooked. However I will follow the advice of one of the other reviewers and add some red chilli flakes and may be some lemon juice too the next time I make this. It would be really perfect with a bit of zing. Thanks for sharing this easy recipe Rita. I like your 2 -5 ingredient cookbook too! July 13 2007: Today I used 9 leg quarters (weight : 1.800g)and doubled all the ingredients. Still great!

We loved this. I let it sit in the refrigerator all day with the spice mix and then cooked it on a covered charcoal kettle grill for 45 minutes using indirect heat. The skin was golden and very crispy and the chicken was moist and tender.
Just an update - it rained the last time I was going to make these. Baked them in a 350 degree oven for an hour and 15 minutes and they were perfect. the skin was nice and crispy and the chicken was moist and tender.

I made this with thighs and boneless breasts.  I added lemon pepper and oregano, i just cant help myself.  My mom, brother and nephew gobbled it up, along with missy the rodesian ridge back(she snuck a piece off the counter while they were cleaning up)  Very good!!! Oh also I cooked them on the smoker, seared them on the hot side of smoker then moved them to a cooler side of the smoker the temp was at about 250.

I made this with one chicken breast to make a spicy chicken sandwich for him-cannot thank you enough! I played with the spices since he can't handle TOO spicy food, but it came out wonderfully! I topped the sandwich with cheese, bacon, mayo & mustard. I marinated the chicken for about 4 hours (I put it on a plate & covered it with some plastic wrap) then baked it at 400 for 35 min. Will make this again for him for sure!

I love simple foods, simple ingredients, simple prep. This was the hat-trick. I cooked the recipe, substituting thighs for legs, on a Norfolk winter night in the backyard, on the Weber with a bottle of Corona in one hand, tongs in the other, staying comfortably warm near the charcoal fire. Great combination of spices with the smokey flavors from the grill. Awesome. Do not wait for summer time. Marinate some chicken this morning and grill it tonight. Thanks for sharing this piece of summertime.
Just the best rub EVER!  So simple with ingredients most people already have in their kitchen!  You can make it as mild or as spicy as you want!  This one will be with my family forever!

I made this tonight for the second time, the first time I used legs this time I am using thighs. The marinade is really more of a paste that is easier brushed on /rubbed into the chicken other wise it takes a bit of effort to get all the pieces covered in a bag, especially if you double (or tripple the amount of meat like I do). I solved this by simply use upping the amount of spices and oil called for (except the pepper) in order to have enough seasoning/liquid to be able to just throw it in the bag. I prefer to cook mine at a little lower temp (350-375) then up the temp to 400-425 near the end of baking to ensure tender fall off the bone meat that has crispy skin. 
I marinaded 4 hours the first time and overnight this time and they came out very tender inside and crispy outside, did not dissapoint even oven baked.
Used this rub on boneless skinless thighs and they turned out wonderfully.  Thanks for posting a nice zesty seasoning mix!

It's January 5th in Erie PA. To cold to grill. I doubled the recipe and used an entire chicken on a Foreman Rotisserie. Turned out great. Simple recipe with a handful of ingredients. I'll be using the leftovers for chicken salad sandwiches.

Scored a 10 on the picky husband scale.  It was even better cold the next day!  I used thighs and boneless breasts. I found the skin on the thighs a little salty for my taste, but your not supposed to eat the skin (ya, right). The in-laws popped over so I didn't get a chance to chill it for 4 hours, I only had a 1/2 hour and still it was killer. I will try it again in a couple of weeks.
The timing for cooking the chicken was perfact as was the advice for all grills. Loved it.
Best EVER marinade Rita!  10 stars.  I have wanted to try this for a while and we had a BBQ for dinner tonight. Loved by all of my family - will make again.

This is fantastic! I purchased a family pack of chicken leg quarters. Four of them I cooked right away and with the rest, I divided them up in packs of two with the marinade in with them and froze them. Just this evening I cooked two of the frozen ones in the oven for a quick dinner. They are so good! Really good flavor and juicy!
exellent, very good i use chicken thighs. grill started acting funny 3/4 the way through, so finished them off in the oven.thanks
This is very good. The skin was crispy and the meat was perfectly seasoned. My family loved it.

I only had an hour until I had to get these cooking so I used my food saver vacuum 'dish' to marinate the legs quickly.  My husband didn't feel like firing up the grill so I baked these instead - 375 for an hour.  The skin was mostly crispy but it could have used a few minutes under the broiler to finish the job.  They were OK when the were first done.  I think grilling makes a huge difference.  I will say that the refrigerated leftover legs were very good.  I gave this 5 stars because I'm sure it will be fabulous the next time I make them.  I'll let them marinate longer and I'll be firing up the grill if I have to.

I prepared this recipe using a package of chicken thighs, 6 thighs.  They marinated all day, about 7 hours and then I grilled them, skin side down, on my stove top grill.  I flipped them and then stuck the grill pan into my oven, set at 350Â°, and let them roast for about 30-40 minutes.  They ended up crispy, brown and delicious!  We'll be doing this one again, now that the snow is gone from our outside grill.  Thanks Rita!

It was our first time doing bone-in chicken leg-thigh on the bbq.  All the cooking was done at indirect heat.  And at the end (after 35 minutes) I inserted a termometer to know if it was cooked through.  The taste of the spices on the legs were yummy.  I loved it.  The skin was so crispy and delicious.  Thanks Rita.  Made for Zaar Star Game

My marinade looked more like a paste & I was thinking "I don't know about this"?  Wow, I was so wrong!!  Our chicken was so tender & we loved the flavour. My only problem was I didn't think 1 tsp of sugar would make a difference, but before I knew it my chicken had already charred. Next time I'll definitely use the recommended indirect method on our barbecue. Thanks Rita!

Great flavour and truly simple.  I doubled the oil and was more liberal with the spices as I found the marinade didn't quite cover the 4 legs as much as I would like.  Next time, I would do this in a 9 x 13 pan and just baste the marinade on as opposed to the bag method.  We all enjoyed it, thx.

Simply SUPER! If using leg-thigh pieces with the skin ON, I always loosen the skin a bit and use my fingers to put a bit of the rub between the skin and the meat. Works great to get those flavors into the meat. Sous Chef Bently stated he/she had problems with charring. Instead of using regular white sugar, I ALWAYS use TURBINO sugar in my BBQ. Has a higher melting temperature and does not char. Gives a GREAT brown sugar taste, too! Turbino sugar used to be hard to find in stores but I think most of them are starting to carry it now. Look for "Sugar in the Raw"
Rita....great recipe.   I used boneless skinless thighs and the spices listed.  What a wonderful mix of flavors that are  in my cupboard.  I will be using this easy recipe all summer!
We love this recipe. So simple and so tasty. We have used this recipe about 10 times already this spring and we're having it again tonight!

We had boneless, skinless chicken thighs and used this recipe.  So yummy and flavorful!  We all loved this one and especially since it is to easy to throw together.  Plans are to make this again soon!  Wendy

AMAZING!  Perfectly seasoned.   I cooked it slow over indirect heat and it was crunchy on the outside and SO moist on the inside.  I will keep this recipe and impress my family with it soon.  Thanks!!!!

This was super easy to do, the ingredients were readily on hand, and the ever-difficult-to-please Frenchmand seemd to enjoy it. I don't eat meat, so I didn't try it personally, but everyone seemed happy. Awesome! Thanks for posting, I'll keep this stored away for the next time | need to cook for meat eaters.

I used this rub on my chicken. I used a whole chicken cut in half.  Sprinkled on the rub and marinated for about 6 hrs.  I grilled over indirect heat on high for 40 minutes, then the last 5 minutes I lowered the heat to medium and grilled on direct heat until it got a nice crispy skin.  Deeeee licious!  Karen

So simple, so good!
I used drumsticks & grilled them using indirect heat. My favorite recipe for grilled chicken.
Followed the recipe exactly and it is barely enough marinade. Chilled for 4 hours and cooked on the BBQ. Simple but the flavor just OK for me. Sorry, but it won't make my recipe box.

This is a good simple recipe.  Marinated my chicken breasts for 2 days in the ref. and it was really flavorful.  I'm afraid 4 hours just won't cut it for the breast.  We love it and will make it again, low carb too.

Yummy!  I left out the sugar because I wasn't in the mood for sweetness.  Still tasted great!  Also, I don't have a grill - how sad, huh?  So I baked the chicken in the oven at 350 for 35 mins. and then finished them up under the broiler till they were nice and charred.  Thanks!!
These are great!! Easy & flavorful. I used chicken breasts instead of legs/thighs, and doubled the recipe and the recipe for the marinade. Am making this again tonight!!

Very good flavor - definitely a keeper.  A couple things I will do differently next time though:  marinade longer and salt & pepper before throwing on the grill.  This would also be very good with barbeque sauce on the last couple of turns.
Really really good!!!! So flavorful! I tripled the recipe for 6 very large leg quarters.
Awesome flavor!  I did use splenda instead of sugar!  This is a keeper!

Great recipe.  I didn't have time to marinate and chill.  I just rubbed this on and cooked them.
They were really great!

A winner! Although I might have left the chicken on a bit longer (30 minutes on indirect heat), it still came out tasting and looking great. Based on comments made by reviewers, I made a few substitutions (honey for sugar, onion salt for seasoning salt, garlic for garlic powder) and additions (a bit of sesame oil and chili flakes). I also chilled the chicken in the marinade for 8 hours. Thanks Rita.

When I made these one of my guests exclaimed "This is the best grilled chicken I have ever had!" They were very moist/tender and had great flavor. I also put the BBQ sauce on the table and it remained unopened. 
I used Turbino sugar as suggested in some other reviews. I marinated the legs for 4 hours an the were delicious!
Thank you for the recipe!

Well you certainly do not NeEED another review... but this marinade was delicious!!!  I hate it when people change the recipe and then rate it but.. I used onion salt instead of seasoning as I never have it on hand and I used LOTS of fresh garlic and added a generous amount red pepper flakes as someone else suggested.  Since I was grilling for 15 on Fathers Day and dreaded the thought of all the possible flare ups from the grease, I did what I usually do.  I boiled the chicken legs and breasts for about 20 - 30 min the night before to reduce the fat level, and then put it in zip lock bags over night.  Come time to grill, they browned up beautifully and everyone totally pigged out!!! (Today I will make Chicken Soup and Big Thicket Dumplings recipe #52253 with the  stock.)    Wonderful recipe, I will use it again.  Thank you Rita!
Thank you so much for sharing this recipe Marvellous ,Delicious ,very very good . Me and my family really enjoyed this .Thank you so muchhhhhhhh
Thank you for sharing this recipe.  Will be a keeper for our family!
rita as always your recipes are incredible. and the amount of spice was just right. thanks.

Nice flavor but was prononced as we would have liked.  I added a few extra pieces of chicken so that may have diluted the flavor too much--what I could taste we liked so we'll try again.  Just note, that you might need to double the marinade which is so easily done.

Loved it!!I used a whole cut up chicken so I made 4times more of the rub. I didn't measure the olive oil but just drizzle it directly on the chicken. I also added more garlic and a few dashes of cayenne pepper because I love spicy food. I will make this marinate in a bottle and use it often. Thank you!

This was awesome chicken with your recipe for Recipe #76198.  We loved the combination together very much and my sister really loved it for her birthday dinner.  I will be making this often it was so tasty!  Thank you for another great recipe Rita!  Linda

UPDATE: I have since replaced seasoning salt with chicken bouillon granules, halved the pepper to suit my Norwegian family's milder tastes, and omitted the oil to create a dry spice mix that I add to soooooooooooooooo many things.  I keep it in a spice jar next to my stove and replenish it as soon as the jar runs empty.  Absolutely love it.  ORIGINAL REVIEW: Simple, yummy, and uses common ingredients.  I usually prefer to substitute honey for sugar, but as this was a rub rather than a marinade, I used brown sugar.  I replaced the salt with chicken bouillon powder and added onion powder as well.  Coated chicken legs with oil one by one on a baking pan to avoid using more oil than necessary, mixed rub ingredients, and coated chicken thoroughly in the pan to avoid wasting any of the spice mix on the inside of a plastic bag.  I'd tripled the recipe and had enough left over after coating 10 chicken legs to fill a spice container halfway for future use.  Oven-baked for 40 minutes after "marinating" for 5 hours.  The chicken was yummy!  Loved the slight sweetness along with the little bitty bite of this spice mix.  My new Norwegian family doesn't handle spicy very well, so small nibbles for me are huge kicks for them, hehe!

We absolutely loved this chicken.  I used drumsticks and let it marinate for 3 hours.  It didn't take as long for the chicken to cook.  We will make these  many times, as it is a recipe that doesn't require many ingredients.  Thank you so much for sharing this yummy chicken recipe with us, we will be making again.
Excellent seasonings - easy to make - the kids loved it - thanks for sharing.
My family loved this chicken!  Very juicy!
My family really liked this. Tender and juicy!  Thanks for a new chicken to put on our summer menu!

I wouldn't consider this as a marinade, or even a rub, very thick like paste. Unfortunately chicken legs and thighs (fatty skins) are grease fire magnets.  The overall taste was garlic and just a little bit of saltiness. Next time I would  spread this mixture underneath the chicken skin, with hopes it will melt into the chicken rather than getting  burned on the grill.

Good chicken!!  I had a lot of extra chicken, so I mixed the marinade in a large plastic freezer bag along with the chicken and put in the freezer.  Should make really good chicken in the future!!  Thanks for the recipe!

This was very good.  I marinated 4 chicken thighs for about 60-90 minutes before grilling.  They had great flavor and were very moist and tender.  I gave my bachelor brother a plate of leftovers and he raved about the recipe the next time I saw him.

Great flavor, however I tried the suggestion that had been posted about putting foil on the grill to prevent sticking and I almost burned down the house!  The flames were leaping out of the grill and by the time I got the fire out the chicken was toast.  But they were super juicy and the flavor was great where it was not completely charred.  Next time I will broil them

I am NOT a leg-thigh fan AT ALL but we bought some for 29 cents/lb so I had to make something. OMG, this recipe made the meat SOOOO good. Had my folks over and they want the recipe as well. Mmmmm we will DEFINITELY be adding this to the rotation of favorites.

Really great!
Used this as a paste / rub just before grilling on 6 boneless breast halves that had been brined for a few hours.
It was delicious fresh off the grill and also cold a day later.
Tasted good and easy to make.  Thanks.
These were absolutely fabulous!  Great flavor!  I did grill them for 40 minutes.  Served with grilled asparagus, fruit salad and rolls.  The entire family loved this.

Very nice marinade. I did this recipe with 8 drumsticks and it was just about right. I used a one gallon freezer bag and added the dry ingredients with the chicken first and gave it a good shake. Then I added the olive oil and worked it around a bit before throwing it in the fridge overnight.

It helped alot spreading the dry ingredients before adding the oil, as it does get a bit thick if you mix it all up right away.

i followed everything to the T except i doubled the seasonings since i had a large amount of chicken. i marinated overnight....grilled half...then had to bake the other half because it was burning too fast on our grill even on low heat due to the sugar content. for some reason the flavor didn't penetrate into the meat. maybe i should've trippled the amount of seasonings? but i'll definately try it again because there's so many wonderful ratings on this that i must've went wrong on something.
Great recipe!  So easy and tastes amazing.  Everyone, from my 3-year old up, loves these.

I made a big batch of this seasoning mix today and sprinkled it over 2 cut-up chickens then drizzled with olive oil.  I marinated for about 5 hours and my husband grilled.  The flavor was really good and the meat very juicy.  This was so easy and everyone loved it!  Probably the only change I might make next time is to add a little more garlic.  Thanks for posting this great recipe!
Barely had time to marinate, but it was still delicious...3 kids and a husband ate it so cant complain! Doubled the recipe to feed 5. Will make again and marinate to the time recommended.

Great marinade.  I will add some cayenne next time, as I do like more heat, but we had some young ones dining tonight and they loved it!  Thanks for the recipe!  I tripled the recipe because we had 12 legs.

My whole family loves this.  Normally, I use Stevia in the raw instead of sugar and no one notices.  Also, I don't use the oil.  I felt it was too thick and clumpy with the oil.  Love the taste and always make extra.
Great.  Will definitely use this recipe again.

This is delicious. I brined some split chicken breasts then dried them off and sprayed them with a little oil and rubbed this mixture onto them and left them all day in the refrigerator. For the paprika I used 1/2 regular and 1/2 smoked. I'm going to make up this spice mix to have on hand. After baking the breasts in the oven, I took them off of the bone and sliced them very thin and served them over linguine in "Geez That's Good ! Lemon Garlic Cream Sauce for Pasta" by Lisa Gay. Oh boy this was good. My company went nuts over it.
this was excellent!  we grilled 3 dozen drumsticks.  they smell delicious and well, i handed out 4 copies of the recipe.  :)  i did cut the pepper in half.
Mmmm...scrumptious. I doubled the olive oil for an easier distribution of the spice mixture. Great dish! Thank you.

It was a crowd favorite!  I was a bit surprised, because the recipe is so simple ... "equal parts" of ingredients.  And I think that using sugar & paprika was a new one for me ... and I love to grill.  I used chicken thighs.  Final product was moist & juicy & delicious.  The food just flew off the plate!
Good

I rarely give 5 stars but did this time! It was pouring out, so i used the oven instead of grilling. 1/2 hour in oven @ 375, then under broiler for 5-6 minutes each side to crisp, brown, and finish. I took the advise of other reviewers and used brown sugar, put a little under the skin. I didn't use a shake bag, just sprinkled seasonings on oiled skins.
These were just fantastic!  Will make these a lot.  Thanks for posting such a wonderful recipe.

This was good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written other then I only used half the pepper. I lined my grill with foil but the chicken still really burnt. I put it in a roasting pan and then the chicken cooked better.

The flavor of this chicken is outstanding. I cooked it over indirect heat then browned over direct heat. However, I found this is more of a rub than a marinade. I mixed all the ingredients in a small bowl and slathered it on the chicken. I refrigerated on a plate covered with plastic wrap. This recipe goes into my hard copy "Family Favorites" cookbook. Thank you Rita, for posting this.

UPDATE: Since I started using this recipe in 2007, the powers that be decided that injecting chicken with a "flavor enhancing solution", was the way to go. I finally figured out why my grilled chicken was no longer getting crispy! I now buy only organic chicken for the grill and am again enjoying Rita's fantastic recipe.
This turned out really bland for us.. not sure what happened?  Followed the directions exactly.

Oh my. I didn't expect much from this recipe, but I was wrong. I decided to use this "rub" rather than a marinade since I wouldn't be able to turn the chicken turning the day to ensure an even distribution of flavor.  Of course I was almost out of paprika, so I had to substitute chili powder.  Plus I used raw sugar.  It was  terrific.  I grilled the chicken legs and they were juicy and flavorful.  Really, really great.
Pretty good.  I will use marinade again, but really watch the grill. Mine flared up & burnt the outside.  The inside was super moist, but we were unable to eat the skin and ousted the raw suar.

Wonderful! I appreciated the post about using organic chicken, which we did, and we got the most wonderful, crispy chicken we've ever had on our grill. This rub/marinade is truly delicious and so easy. Definitely will make again. I doubled it for 6 legs and four thighs, as I couldn't find the quartered pieces I wanted. Thanks for sharing this great recipe.

VERY GOOD and yet very easy. I followed your recipe exactly, but used 2T of each spice instead of 1t. That worked out perfectly to season a whole cut up chicken. DH couldn't stop raving! He's already looking forward to leftovers tomorrow.

Such a basic set of ingredients with such amazing results. I was a skeptic but the reviews were so good I had to try it. I used chicken thighs which ordinarily I don't even like. As other reviewers suggested, I rubbed some of the marinade under the skin as well. I also baked it in the oven (375 for 40 minutes plus a minute under the broiler) instead of grilling. The only substitution I made was to use half regular paprika and half hot paprika because I wanted a little kick. The results were spectacular - juicy chicken with a nice crispy skin and delicious flavor. And to think this takes only ingredients that most of us always have on hand! It's a keeper!
good recipe

This is a good recipe to cook chicken legs.  The flavor of the legs was very good.  If you are using large legs, then it's going to take longer to cook than the stated 30-40 minutes.  I cooked the legs over indirect heat because the legs were rather large.  It took a little over an hour for them to cook.  So, I suggest you start a little earlier than you think and just keep the legs warm if they do cook sooner.
Loved it...used Splenda in place of sugar.  DH preferred the chicken made with chucks chicken juice 38399 (only reason gave it 4 stars over 5), but I would definitely make this again.  Thanks!
Quick and easy recipe.  I made it for my girls and they loved it.
This is simply delicious!

Delicious! I didn't have hours to wait. Mixed all the dry ingredients in a bowl, then rubbed olive oil on the leg quarters and sprinkled the dry ingredients over both sides. Preheated the grill and initially cooked over direct heat for about 5 mins, then went to indirect heat, then back to direct heat for crispier skin. Overall about 25 mins. Cooked until instant read thermo was >165F in center of thigh. Perfect! Thank you.

These came out really well. I added a teaspoon of onion powder to it and a little more oil. Also, I baked them at 375 for 35 minutes, then threw them on the grill for 10 minutes on each side...Perfect!

This was the perfect side dish for a mojo carillo marinated chicken dish, with the flavors complimenting perfectly.  I loved how pretty the rice looked, light yellow from the turmeric and speckled with flecks of green from the onions and cilantro.  I confess to being a cilantro junkie, so I added an extravagant handful instead of the judicial 1/4 cup.
PanNan, we enjoyed your recipe very much.
This was good -- mildly flavoured and very colourful. I didn't have green onions on hand, so substituted chopped onions sauteed in oil with the rice during step #2.

I thought this rice dish was excellent! I made this to go with my recipe for Fresh Fish steamed with oranges and tomatoes, wich I made for my dad for his 60th b-day this year! I used basmati rice, which I tend to use alot.  The color of this is wonderful from the turmeric, and the scallions and cilantro mixed in at the end give an amazing fresh flavor.  I omitted the lemon juice, because one of my guests is not fond of too much lemon, but the fresh zest seemed to do the trick just fine.  My husband, who is NOT a fan of rice at all, really, really enjoyed it!  Thanks, will make this again!

Beautiful rice dish.  The colors are very striking with the bright yellow and greens from the onions and cilantro.  I liked browning the rice,  it gave a nice nutty flavor to the finished dish.  Lovely flavor and the required amount of cilantro isn't overpowering.  I served this with Island Chicken Wings #56872.  Thanks!!!!

Made last night to go with some enchiladas. I thought it was very bland but maybe that was bc it was standing up to a very flavorful dish. I will make again bc it was very tasty. I will probably add some garlic or additional lemon rind in future. 

Great recipe! 

Thanks Pan

Prepared this simple dish to go with chiles rellenos for last night's meal. I picked it especially because I had a surplus of cilantro and the fact the green onions and cilantro are stirred in last minute. Instead of water I used fresh  vegie stock.

This dish is so beautiful. The bright yellow from the turmeric is offset by the vibrant green of the onions and cilantro. I do think that the lemon flavor was a little weak but I may not have added enough lemon rind.  I do plan on making this again.
We really enjoyed this!  Very colorfull!

great recipe! I used basmati and dried cilantro ( that is what I had) and I loved it.  Will be making it again often.  I served with tilapia and squeezed more lemon juice on the fish and the rice, but that is a personal preference.
Terrific recipe! I made this as a side dish to Chef V's Brandied chicken wings! What a dinner. I will make this again and again. Thanks for sharing.
I added more lemon and cilantro and followed MamiJ and added a teeny bit more salt. This is a great way to switch up your regular rice.

I've made this several times already - it goes well with fish entrees as well as Mexican food.  I don't use the turmeric so mine doesn't come out the bright yellow color as shown in Paula's photo.  Delicious and fresh tasting.

I loved the tanginess of the lemon in the rice pilaf.  I served it with some lemon pan fried tilapia and it was the perfect side dish.  I did add 2 c of water to the 1 c of rice because that was the ratio I always use, but I should have just followed the recipe because my rice turned out just a tad on the wet side.  Still delicious though.  I will be keeping this in my collection and using it for a tasty side dish with lots of fish dishes.  Thanks!
Fresh and light! Added rice to "Rooz Ma Lahem (Rice With Meat)" #83892 and it gave it a nice bright flavor and color! Thanks!

This was so yummy!! Didn't add tumeric because we didn't have any. At the end, when adding the cilantro and green onions iI tossed in some roasted peanuts and a touch of soy sauce. Will be making this again!
Thank you!

My husband really liked this recipe.  He said it tasted very "fresh".  I was not a big fan, I thought it was very bland with very little flavor unless I got a bite with cilantro.  I also paired it with a very intense flavored lemon fish recipe so that might have been why.  Easy to prepare; if you're a rice fan I would recommend.
Light and bright flavored,  bursting with flavors. A welcome new flavorful side dish. Easy to make. Fills the room with citrusy aroma. Thank you for sharing this new favorite.

Fresh and citrusy, but only with some adjustments to the recipe. After the rice was finished cooking, I added quite a bit more fresh lemon juice to the pot to give it that extra punch that I was expecting from the recipe. I did really enjoy the turmeric combined with the lemon. I will make it again.

I cut down the cilantro by half and it was perfect for us. I added more lemon too, as we love the lemon flavor.  This was a most rewarding side dish with our grilled swordfish.  We will have this again and again with other meat and fish choices, and I can't wait!
Made it for a big crowd to go with lemon and thyme chicken and it was a big winner!!

This was easy, delicious and decorative. In all fairness, I might have given a higher rating except I had to make a substitution. As I didn't have green onions on hand, I substituted Penzeys' Fox Point Seasoning (a blend of salt, shallots, chives, garlic, onion and green peppercorns - overall green color). The dish had the green speckles  from the seasoning and the cilantro and maintained the delicate onion flavor.  Next time I'll use the green onions and re-0rate the recipe.
Interesting... but unremarkable. Flavors were a bit weird for us.

This was a very good rice dish.  I added some lime peel to compliment the cilantro, and chopped almonds for a little extra crunch.  I also used 2 cups of water for 1 cup of rice instead of 1.5 cups.  The rice had a perfect texture, and probably would have been a little dry with only 1.5 cups.  I also added 1 teaspoon of chicken bouillon for added flavor.  This is a highly recommended dish that goes well with fish.  I gave 4 stars instead of 5 because I don't think 1.5 cups of water is enough for 1 cup of rice.

The method described in this recipe is called Low Temperature Pasteurization. According to the NCHFP's current guidelines, it results in a better product texture, but must be carefully managed to avoid possible spoilage. According to their directions, place jars in a canner filled half way with warm (120º to 140º F) water. Then, add hot water to a level 1 inch above jars. Heat the water enough to maintain 180º to 185º F water temperature for 30 minutes. Check with a candy or jelly thermometer to be certain that the water temperature is at least 180ºF during the entire 30 minutes. Temperatures higher than 185ºF may cause unnecessary softening of pickles. http://www.uga.edu/nchfp/how/can_06/low_temp_pasteur.html

For optimum shelf-stable safety of any fresh-pack dill pickles, the jars should be processed in a boiling water bath covered by at least an inch of water. Ten minutes for pints and 15 minutes for quarts. http://www.uga.edu/nchfp/how/can_06/quick_dill_pickles.html

Made for Aus/NZ - Make My Recipe Edition 5.  These were very good and I was able to make the gluten free by using gluten free oats.  A nice recipe for when you want cookies, but don't want to heat up the kitchen by using the oven.  Thank for posting this January Bride!

Five star and fantastic - what more can I say except I nearly ate the lot !!

What wonderful little treats!  I didn't have dried cranberries, so I just used more raisins.  For the nuts I used walnuts and pinenuts.  We took these with us on an outing with friends and they were perfect.  Thanks!  Made for veg*n swap Oct 2008.

Yum, these are great and so easy to make as well.  I subbed agave nectar for the honey to make it vegan, and it worked just fine.  I used a mixture of hemp seeds, cashews and walnuts.  Thanks for posting, made for the Dec 08 veg swap.

Great recipe!  Easy and delicious.  I used baby oats and skipped toasting them.  I used walnuts for the nuts and dried cherries for the fruit. Made for February 2009 Veg Swap.
So yummy!  I decided to indulge a bit and put a few premium chocolate chips in and all I can say is WOW!

I love that they're a little easier to transport (and work with) than the homemade bars are. Thank you so much for sharing - it's a keeper!
These are very good! So easy to make. I did not add raisins because of my own personal preferance and used chopped almonds for the nuts. This is a keeper!

Great recipe!  I didn't add raisins because I don't care for them, so I doubled the cranberries.  I used half honey and half real maple syrup, and left out the sugar completely.  I added vanilla flavored protein powder, which has some sweetness to it.  This is definitely a keeper!

These are absolutely delicious. I love the flavour combination of the oats with the coconut, nut butter and raisins. Soo tasty! I was still able to form the mixture into balls, although it probably was a bit less easy without the aditional stickyness.
Thank you so much for sharing this lovely recipe with us, JB!
Made and reviewed for my chosen chef during Veggie Swap #42 January 2012.

Yesterday was our anniversary,and I wanted something special for us. This is a GREAT cake, and it was so easy to make. My hubby said we should make it a tradition. I think we will!!
Thanks for this wonderful recipe.

I used this recipe as a reference and the cake turned out excellent! I used ony 3 eggs, cut down a lot on sugar and also added a tablespoon of Cointreau. Very tasty. Thanks for posting. I used whole wheat flour and round cake pans. I like that the cake is not too sweet. I think this would make a good cake to go with strawberry shortcake. Made for Team SSaSSy for ZWT 6.

Bonnie this is a lovely cake, I made one change I only used one cup of sugar, other than that I followed the recipe. I am taking it to work tonight the girls will love it. Thank you for posting such a nice recipe. Made for ZWT#6 2010.
We loved this cake. I did cut down on the amount of sugar & oil. I also only used 3 tbsp of baking powder & the cake rose just fine. Made for ZWT 6 - No-Nonsense Nibblers

What can I say that hasn't been said already.  We, also, enjoyed this cake tremendously.  I followed the directions completely and agree that it has a nice full bodied orange flavor.  Thnx for sharing, yet again, Bonnie.  Made for the Voracious Vagabonds of ZWT 6.
Moist and very orangey- need I say more! I made this into a half recipe and then tried to do cupcakes. Next time I'll stick to a single cake. The texture is really delicate- lovely!

Made as written for ZWT6 as a Zingo choice, I made very few desserts during the Tour but could not resist this one for 2 main reasons: 1) I wanted a sweet treat as the finale of a welcome home dinner for DH after a fishing trip .. & .. 2) It looked like a flavour sensation that was ingredient-friendly & would easily reduce to a half recipe so I could bake it in ramekins (my method of portion control). The result was a delicious, moist & well-flavoured orange cake that I enjoyed w/a light dusting of powd sugar & DH ate plain. Outstanding cake, most definitely! This is a lovely, refreshing not-too-sweet cake that I think I need to tweak a bit.  Although I made this exactly as posted, the result was somewhat flawed. I think ingredient measurements probably need adjusting. Made for ZWT6 Zingo.

I've been dying to make this orange cake ever since I originally saw it.  This is a very nice cake.  It is extremely light and fluffy in texture.  Be careful not to removed from oven too soon.  I tested mine for doneness 5 minutes before I should have and it fell just a bit.  (I was concerned with overbaking since I only made a 1/2 recipe in a 8 x 8 pan.)  Correct time for that size would have been 25 minutes.  I would have liked it to have had a more distinct orange flavor and next time I would add an orange glaze to it while still warm.  Made for Zingo--ZWT #6--2010.

Lovely cake!  It's been a cold and miserable March here in the north country and  I wanted something bright, citrus-y, and not too sweet.  This fit the bill perfectly! I also made a simple orange zest glaze because I was really craving citrus.  Very nice recipe; thanks, Bonnie!

This cake is delightfully delicious. Not too sweet with a delicious orange flavor. I substituted the oil for unsweetened apple sauce, and the end result was utter fabulousness. This is a great recipe - light fluffy cake - just one thing you need to stir in the orange zest manually otherwise gets stuck on the mixure blades.

To make it xtra special when it comes out hot tip it upside down on a plate and pour some orange liquer on it - tip it the right way up between two plates and add orange liquer to it again - it must be hot when you do this - straight out of the oven - this makes this cake really yummy!!!!!

Delicious!  I have a small ring pan so cut recipe in half to make a smaller cake.  Worked great.  I used the juice and zest of California Cuties (Mandarin) oranges. Loved the smell and taste. Baked for 50 minutes in a glass loaf pan came out perfectly.

This was FABULOUS!!  Super rich, though.  I used devils food cake mix (w/ pudding in it)and it turned out great. Have to say we aren't patient when it comes to eating cake so only initially refrigerated it for 3 hrs.  Only lasts about 2 days in fridge before it becomes too sticky so eat up!
A tasty cake, and not much else I can add that someone else hasn't already said.

The cake was good- but we didn't really find it was something we would rave about.  My children really liked the cool whip on top and asked me to use it for frosting a plain chocolate cake. It reminded me of a sundae.  Thanks for the change of pace.
The name says it all....LOL.

Yum!  I couldn't wait for it to be refrigerated over night so I tried a piece just after a few hours.  It was wonderful but a bit sweet.  The next day it was even better, it was still sweet but not so sweet you couldn't eat it.  It was perfect.  I will be making this many times through the years.

Seriously, all I have to say is YUM.  I used a butterscotch/caramel topping since they didn't have just plain caramel.  I used the new French Vanilla cool whip and crushed peanut butter cups.  There were sighs of pleasure from all over the table!  Easy to make, and everyone tried to guess the recipe.  No one could.  A hit!
This is my version of better than sex cake (or heath bar cake for the young'ns). Its quick to make and works for any gathering! My only problem with it is that I could eat the WHOLE thing by myself!

Absolutely DELICIOUS!  I used a German Chocolate cake mix, because that is the only chocolate cake mix I had on hand. I also had the Heath toffee bits and used those to sprinkle on the top. I loved it even more the next day, but my 7 year old who loves ALL desserts ate one bite and wouldn't eat any more because the cake texture REALLY changes overnight. This was an easy, incredible dessert to serve my family!  Thanks for posting!
I hate choc cake cause it's way to dry but this was AWESOME! Me and my roommmate almost ate the whole thing!

Very moist cake! I used a full can of Nestle Lechera (sweetened condensed milk) and a full jar of Mrs. Richardson's butterscotch caramel. I was worried that there would be a puddle in the bottom of the pan - nope! The cake soaked it up! I used a Butter Chocolate cake mix from Betty Crocker and made it according to the box. I also used chopped Skor bars on top. I kept it in the fridge overnight and had a little left over today, it was still great! My Super Bowl guests loved it!
my favorit dessert ever! Even my husbank loves it and he hates sweet things!
I made this for my boyfriend's birthday yesterday and it was possibly the best cake I've ever made. You can't go wrong with this cake!! Made exactly as written, no need to change a thing!!
Wow!! Great and easy recipe! Made this for work today and went over perfectly. Only thing I did differently was used a 12 oz. cool whip and drizzled some caramel on top! Thanks for posting!!

I made this for a fourth of July party and everyone loved it!  Our 11 y.o. really liked it!  I used a fork to make the holes in the cake, which were apparently large enough to soak up the milk and caramel.  Thanks for an EASY and delicious recipe!

This was my contribution to a deck party featuring smoked & grilled ribs.  All the couples there made sure to save room for dessert when I announced the name of this cake!!!  It certainly lives up to the name!  Very GOOD!
The one and only! I make my chocolate cake from scratch though. Will be making this repeatedly!!

I don't know if this is better than sex but it is still pretty doggone good.  I used Heath bars on the top and everyone loved it.  My son's friend even has requested I make one for his wedding.  Thanks for posting.

I have made this several times too and it is so wonderful!!!  The longer it sits the better it is.  Last time I made it, I dumped a jar of hot fudge on it with the caramel and it was good too!  Thanks for posting.
Very good, everyone enjoyed!  I decorated the top with the extra carmamel drizzled over the top of the whipped cream & candy pieces.
Easy and good.  Everybody wants the recipe.  Thanks.
It's not better than sex! more like better than a making out session. Still good, but not great. I really had high expectations for this one.

This is one of our friends favorite cakes that I make.  Its a fabulous cake.   I used a devil foods cake mix and fellow the direction on back of the box and bake as stated for a 13x9 pan (35minutes)  Than I poke holes in the cake and heat up the sweetened condensed milk with Hershey's carmel ice cream topping and than pour over cake. I use 3  Skor candy bars (crushed) and sprinkle over top of cake. I than let cool completely  than spread the cool whip over top of cake and 3 more crushed up Skor bars. 
Its a rich cake but "all so "  DELICIOUS!!
Thanks for sharing the recipe!
I followed the recipe exactly and the cake was delicious!  I made it for a friend's birthday and I got rave reviews!!  I will definitely make this again.
I made this cake with low sugar products but it did not change the taste any as it was wonderful and moist and yummy.

This was amazing.  I made it for the team I'm on at work and it got rave reviews.   People had seconds!  I thought it might be too sweet but it wasn't.  The sweetened milk added moistness, too.  It was easy!  I baked the cake per the Betty Crocker box directions, added the sweet milk, added the caramel, tucked it covered into the fridge, and the next morning I had a beautiful and delicious cake.  I'll definitely make this again and again.  Thanks Paul!

I thought that it would be too sweet if I used all of the sweetened condensed milk, so I didn't use the whole can.  As a result, the cake wasn't as spectacular as everyone says.  If you make this, don't skimp on anything!
Very good.  Almost too sweet and not the best idea for the potluck that I took it to because it was so messy and the whipped topping did not stand up very well.  Very very rich.
My husband and I loved this cake! It was so moist and decadent.  I didn't use as much condensed milk or caramel and it was still amazing.

This was exactly what I remembered "Better Than Sex Cake" to be...very yummy!  I used fat-free condensed milk and butterscotch/caramel topping.  I sprinkled Heath bits under and over the whipped topping.  So decadent!
It was pretty good.  I have another version I make using angel food cake that tastes better though.  Also I did use german chocolate for this one instead.
I have been making this for years.  I add some hershey syrup and make a desgn on top of the wipped cream, makes it look extra special

Served this cake at a dinner party, I liked it a lot but wasn't over the moon about it. However when I threw my next party I had a few guests actually call to ask if I could make it again and asked for the recipe. So for me that makes it a 5 star recipe.

READ THE WHOLE RECIPE. It needs to go in the fridge overnight. It was really good, but the milk and caramel pooled around the edges and the middle was just plain cake (which is ok... cake is good). Next time I will cut some of the cake off the top in the middle to make flat-- then it will soak in evenly.
Sinful! Great recipe, thanks!

I figured this recipe was a sure thing with over 100 five star ratings.  I was right!  Every loves this.  Make sure you poke a lot of holes in it immediately after it comes out of the oven, and it would probably be best to use something around the diameter of a chopstick (as the author suggests).  I only used a fork, and it was difficult to get the sweetened milk and caramel topping to soak evenly around the center of the cake.  Over all... still absolutely delicious!

Here's another 5 star rating for you.  I can't beleive I did not rate this recipe.  I have made this Dessert 3x now.  I made this the first time on Aug 08 for my daughters baby shower and forgot to rate it.:( Every one loves it every time I make it for family fuctions.  Sorry for late review.  Thank you for easy and delicious cake :)

I've made this cake a few times and each time I come home with a clean dish. It's sweet, decadent and rich. I suggest sprinkling some toasted coconut and pecans on the top for a slight change up in flavor! Thank you for posting this!

This is truly the mother of all BTS cakes out there. I have made this exact recipe more times than I can count. I always receive rave reviews.  Some times I have  to call it the "Ooey Gooey Yummy Cake" due to the ears of children or male co-workers.  I have caught grown men licking up the yummy remains on the bottom of the pan after the cake is gone. You just have to taste it to believe it.
Pretty darn easy and soooo decadent and delicious!

Yep...  This is how I remember it the first time a friend's mom made it.  That was about ten years ago and this is the first recipe that embodies the richness of that experience.  This is the real BTS cake.

If there were 6 stars available, I'd definitely give it 6 stars!  The only variations in my recipe are the cake mix (I actually use a German Chocolate mix), and the fresh-out-of-the-oven topping (I DO use Mrs. Richardson's Carmel, but I ALSO use Mrs. Richardson's Hot Fudge!)  And depending on my sweet tooth when I make the cake, I have been known to use 1 full jar of each!  Talk about a HEAVY cake pan......but SO worth it!  :)
This is my favorite cake ever! I love that its really simple but makes such an extravagant cake. And I think its rather light compared to some richer heavier cakes.
This was a huge hit for Easter Dinner dessert.  This would be great for a picnic or potluck.  Will make again.

Can I say YUM enough?  I made this with Dark Chocolate Cake Recipe #2496 instead of a mix.  I think next time I will leave off the candy bars, add more Cool Whip, and use the whole jar of caramel.  But there will definitely be a next time.  I made this for hubby's birthday and he says he wants this cake every year from now on.  Thanks for posting!
This was good, but not something I would just rave about.  Easy for sure.  I found it hard to get the pieces out of the pan whole since they were so saturated.  It was tasty, just nothing special.

I hadn't had this cake for years! so glad I found the recipe...I made this cake and my husband and I tried a peice without the whipped topping and it was DELISH even without it. I forgot to use the candy bar, It doesn't really need it. I probably only used 3/4 the jar of caramel topping...everything turned out perfect. Very decedent cake!

Yummo! I used a box of yellow cake instead of chocolate and it was to die for. I tried making them into cupcakes but the SCM and caramel sauce made the outside of the cupcake super sticky%u2026so from now on I%u2019ll probably stick to making it as a cake instead. Overall, it was super easy recipe with delicious results.
Good cake, makes a lot of servings, 15 I would say.  I needed to 'baste' the top of the cake to get all of the sauces into it and wound up using a bigger diameter spoon handle.  Otherwise, very easy.
Fantastic!
This is the one! I've made it for years. I used German Chocolate cake mix and Heath bits; everything else the same. And make it in the morning - can't plan ahead well enough to chill overnight!
I made this cake for a party yesterday and it was a hit!! Great receipe and very easy. Wonderful for a party because you can make the night before.
Very good cake, worth making.
This turned out good.  Very rich and moist.  Much better than a plain chocolate cake.

I really expected more from this cake, with all the rave reviews, and I followed the recipe to the letter.  Was disappointed because the milk and caramel soaked the edges, but the middle was just plain cake.  I thought with it sitting that long it would soak up better.  Just average, would not make again.

This is a great cake and one you can change around. I make this with carrot cake and frost with cool whip FROSTING not the cool whip. I used chocolate frosting and crushed butterfingers. Either way it is so good. Leave it in the pan at least overnight in fridge.
Tasty dessert that is liked by DH.  Thank you!

I have been making this cake for over 30 years.  It is always requested at holiday time.  I do mine in a bunt pan.  It looks nice and I have a special hole maker that fits on top of the cake and makes uniform holes all around.  My husband breaks the Heath bars.
I won a best tasting dessert contest at work for this cake! I don't care for chocolate, but it was a hit!

Made this in my new Cuisinart Electric Pressure Cooker. Cooked on high pressure for 40 minutes and let naturally depressurize for about 10 minutes then finished manually.  The ribs were so delicious and the meat extremely tender.  The beer is the secret to the unique flavor so don't leave it out! My husband absolutely love them! Thanks for sharing.

I made this last night and all through dinner my husband said, "These are so good, Mmm."  After dinner he told me to definitely keep this recipe.  I used my homemade barbecue sauce recipe and they were the most tender and delicious ribs I had ever made!  You must try this recipe!

This was my first attempt at using my pressure cooker (electric), I've been a bit scared of it :-)  I used pork spareribs instead. My husband really liked the flavor, but the meat didn't fall off the bone. I cooked them for 40 min and let depressurize naturally. I'll try this recipe again since he liked the flavor, but maybe play with the timing or liquid, Thank you !
Super easy and delicious!

This is my new favorite way to cook ribs.  It was so fast to get tender, well cooked ribs. I never realized how good beef ribs could be. I did not use the tender baby-back, but a less expensive back ribs and they came out as tender as can be.  The only thing was I needed more liquid than the recipe called for.
WOW! This is a keeper! Real
Super easy and delicious. Will definitely make again.
These were so delicious! The cook time is spot on...the meat was so tender...this is a keeper...:)
Tender, moist and full of flavor.  Family loved them.  This is a keeper!
Delicious, if you want to spice it up a little add some Chipotle chili adds to the smokiness of the paprika very nicely.

This recipe was soooo delicious :-). I ordered a pressure cooker off Amazon and was so nervous about using it for the first time(the instructions/manuel/warnings were overwhelming- lol). Thanks for sharing it :-) :-)
The meat was falling off the bones, flavor was yummy....loved it! Thanks for sharing
All the ingredients are fine. But you should greatly reduce the cook time unless you like your ribs overcooked.

There's plenty of liquid (replace your pressure cooker gaskets, and turn the heat down until it just barely hisses or rattles), I have enough sauce for both the ribs, and noodles on the side. The one warning I have is that the order you put the ingredients in matters. Add the wine and stock first (or mix the brown sugar and honey in before pouring it in the pot. If you don't the sugars tend to get stuck on the bottom and burn. A fat strainer is needed at the end. Also, I like to thicken it up with some cornstarch (about 1TbSP in a slurry).
Put them on the grill for a few minutes. Excellent

I enjoyed this both warm and cooled. My boyfriend thought it tasted too sweet when warm, and there is a lot of sugar in the recipe-probably more than necessary. It doesn't have to be completely cooled before cutting, and in fact it's excellent warm with some fresh ripe mango.
I was craving butter mochi ever since I moved from Hawaii and this was perfect! I didnt add the cinnamon because Im used to it plain but it was great. My husband thought it great to.

This is SOOO good!! I've never had butter mochi before, but I love mochi so I figured I'd love this. I halved the sugar and it was just right for me since I also dusted it with powdered sugar. I also omitted the cinnamon.I will definitly make this again and again. Thanks for posting!!
I followed the recipe as-is with the cinnamon and all, and it is DELICIOUS!

Love this recipe! It was my first time making it and I halved the recipe. I also did not have coconut milk so I used a whole can of fat free evaporated milk instead of 1/2 can coconut milk and 1/2 can ev. milk. The crust is so crispy! I love the taste too!
i love how simple the desert is to make! it's the perfect desert for 6 kids and all of their friends.Thanks for posting!
Simply perfect!! just like the Butter mochi I use to buy when I lived in Hawaii!!! The kids loved it so much that they insisted on taking some to their teachers!

This was the easiest recipe and it is soooo yummy! Reminds me of when I was a kid in Hawaii! Thanks for sharing. Note: I only used 2 cups of sugar and it still turned out sweet, so if you are wondering if you can use less sugar, the answer is yes and it didn't change the consistency either! Try it, and you will love it....my kids did too!

I made this tonight (and posted a picture) and it is DELICIOUS!!! I made the recipe exactly as is with 2 cups of sugar, cinnamon and unsalted sweet cream butter. I couldn't stand to wait for it to cool completely and cut into it after 45 minutes and it was melt-in-your-mouth ooey sticky goodness! I can't wait to make it again for the next island friends BBQs!

I halved the recipe and baked in an 8x8 Pyrex pan. I used 2 eggs (1.5 eggs is just too bothersome) and 3/4 cup of sugar (already plenty sweet, no need for more). I stuck with the recipe otherwise. The taste was very good. However, it was more fluffy and less chewy than I would like (not sure how to fix this, may be less baking powder or beat the batter more?). The coconut flavor really came out (so don't use coconut milk if you don't want the coconut flavor). For me, the best part is the crispy surface so next time I might bake in a larger dish to get thinner pieces.

For fun I almost completely veganized this recipe and it came out SO well. My husband couldn't tell the difference. I used Earth Balance butter, ground flax seeds instead of eggs, lite coconut milk, and 1 cup sugar 3/4 cup agave syrup instead of the 2 cups of sugar. I did use the evaporated milk because I didn't find a vegan replacement, though.

Will absolutely make this again!!!

This is an excellent butter mochi. It has the right amount of sweetness, and the crystallized crust which forms on the top and sides of the pan are total bonus points. The recipe makes a 9x13 pan, which serves, um, what, two? Okay, if you gotta share it can serve more folks, but they should make their own. Really.

I made butter mochi for the FIRST TIME EVER TODAY for Girl's Day using this recipe and it was AMAZING! Everyone I gave to LOVED IT! The coconut milk only comes in 13.5 oz so I used that. And I only used 2 cups of sugar. No cinnamon. Just right the sweetness. And I used a toothpick to check if it was done. The crust and the smoothness of the inside were perfect. I didn't wait to cut it cause I had to give it out =) SOOO GOOD!!!
This was so easy to make! I have this memorized now, and will make this my new "go to" recipe for when it's my turn to bring dessert to gatherings. Watch out! It's super addictive.
I make this all the time but I use just 1 1/2 teaspoons of baking powder and instead of 3 I use 4 large eggs. My mochi comes out with a golden yellow color and does not last so I double the recipe

This dessert is different but SOOOO delicious. You eat it with your hands, like a brownie. Its a little sticky. I have also used lemon extract instead of vanilla and its great too (probably added more 3-4 tsp lemon extract). It tastes like a light fluffy lemon custard. I enjoy it both ways.

My dh and I just polished off 2 bowls each of this delicious soup!  This is the best bean soup I have ever had.  I love the addition of the ground beef in this recipe.  It really gives this soup some substance.  We like ours really spicy too so what I did was to include a 10 ounce can of Rotel tomatoes with green chilis in my total 28 ounces of tomatoes.  That really added some heat to it.  I also added an extra teaspoon of chili powder when I adjusted the seasonings. We chose not to puree the soup and really enjoyed the chunky texture better.  We had a sprinkling of monterrey jack cheese on top along with a dollop of sour cream  and tortilla chips on the side.  This hearty, delicious soup is Tex-Mex heaven in a bowl! Thanks Tugar for sharing this recipe.

This soup was great! DH and both loved it.  It is almost like a chili but not quite. I use a can of tomatoes with green chilis for a little extra heat. I've made this twice now and will be making it again and again!!

This soup totally rocks!

I did add a can of black beans on top of everything else...it was wonderful.  I am not crazy about blending my hamburger, so I may blend it before adding the beef next time.  This soup went fast!

All I can say is, WOW! This was so wonderful. The only change I made was that I didn't put the soup in the blender or food processor. I just broke it up with a mixer. I wanted it a little chunky. I made my own tortilla chips with corn tortillas; I added some cheese to the top of it and some green onions sliced. We really enjoyed this and will make it again!!

This soup is not lacking flavor....that's for sure!!!! Instead of a 28 oz can of tomatoes, I used two 14.5 oz cans of tomatoes with zesty jalapeno's which added alot of heat to the soup.I think I went alittle overboard because instead of a green pepper, I used a jalapeno. It was really HOT, but oh...so good!!
I didn't puree it, as we liked the consistency a bit chunky. I topped the soup with some sharp cheddar  and sour cream. Great recipe..thanks for sharing.

Wow, had to have a whole mug full of this soup.  I made this as part of my weekly Sunday cooking session.  Delicious!  I also left everything unblended.  It is delicious and filling.  I also added a small can of minced black olives for extra flavor.  I am glad my curiosity found this recipe.

We liked this soup. We didn't blend ours because my husband likes his soup chunky. We tired it first without the cinnamon and added a little cinnamon with the leftovers. We liked it better without the cinnamon. 

Thanks Tugar357

Bullwinkle
Dont let the name fool ya!  Quick, easy, filling, most kids will love it! Hardy enough for winter, light enough for the rest of the seasons!  Added a can of black beans! S-L-U-R-P!

This soup is wonderful!  I took Susie's suggestion and used 1 can Ro-Tel tomatoes and 1 can plain diced tomatoes.  I also added an extra teaspoon of chili powder and a small can of green chilies because DH and I love spicy food.   This soup was so easy to put together and was a huge hit with the family!  Thanks Tuger357, I'll be making this often!

Bewitching and forgiving at same time. Next time in puree form, I'll turn into a frito pie because of the thickness adding corn chips and topped with cheese and onions. I like this soup in its original soup form (texture more appealing). I'll try with Rotel tomatoes,  black beans, or corn...it's forgiving...it lets you experiment without hurting the soup. Hearty and comforting. TRY IT! Tugar357 hats off to you!
My family asked what I did to the chili--a nice variation, but I guess I'll stick to what they like to eat best--chili.  Still a good, tasty dish.
Quick, easy and with at hand ingredients in our house.  I always follow a recipe exactly the first time and tweak later.  I would definately use more spice next time.  There will be a next time.
Loved this.  topped with taco shredded cheese and thought it was great!
Yum!!  Went together quick - didn't puree (DH likes his soup chunky).  Thank you!
I used Boca veg meat and it was a very good chili. Omitted red pepper and cinnamon as well.

This turned out great! I  did a few things differently: I made the ground beef with a packet of taco seasoning, then added that to the soup, so I didn't have to to add the chili and cumin. I felt the seasoning packet is more flavorful.  I found the texture better pureed, unlike the other reviewers. I garnished it with shredded cheese, chunks of avocado, chopped raw onion, crushed tortilla chips, and cliantro on top. This was a unusual soup, yet hearty and delicious!
Good and warming soup I made with what was on hand-  spiced it up a bit and only pureed a touch. and added corn.  5 stars! Thanks!

Awesome soup! I added MORE than a pinch of cayenne pepper...I was sweating while I was eating it! I only put  the veggies through the food processer and left hamburger chuncks because it needed some chunkiness. We topped it with Cheddar cheese and it was loved by all. Thanks!
I'm a Believer!  This soup is sensational! I added a wee bit more spice but other than that I kept to the recipe.  You won't be disappointed.  This is a keeper !

Made it last night with a few changes: doubled the recipe, using 1/2 Rotel tomatoes and chiles, 1/2 tomato sauce (less pureeing). Like other reviewers, I cheated and used taco seasoning (2 pkts.) instead of all the spices. I browned the beef first and set it in the sink in a colander to drain while I sauteed the veggies and added the tomatoes, taco seasoning and stock. That got pureed with a stick blender, then the beef and beans went in, for texture. We topped it off with Mexican blend shredded cheese and sour cream. Tonight we'll add tortilla chips too. An easy, kid-friendly meal.... kudos, Tugar357!!

Tastes great, filling and really easy.  Thats all a person can ask for.  We loved it.  

Thanks
I wasn't really impressed with this soup.  It taste's OK.  There is nothing special about it, in my opinion.

I really was looking forward to this dish after a long day at work, but was suprised at how watery it was, and I even used a 15oz can of peeled tomatoes instead!  I don't think that I'll make this recipe again, but thank you for posting.

Great soup. I added a can of rotele tomatoes with chilies and a large can of refried beans. I loved the chunky texture so didn't puree. I added a extra pinch of cayenne for extra spice. I would not leave out the cinnamon because of the great flavor. Serving this with Marie Calenders cake like corn bread.#104715 Will review later.Thanks for a great recipe.

Tugar357, this was excellent!  I added some mushrooms (typical for me) and upped the garlic just for personal taste.  I made this last night and it was great.  Today, as leftovers, it thickened so I cooked up some spaghetti noodles and topped with this soup/sauce and had what I would call East Texas spaghetti, since I grew up on these flavors.  Ha!  It's good stuff!  Thanks for posting.

MMMMM...This was good. My DH was very scared by the name but he really enjoyed it. I didn't puree. I also added 1C uncooked rice, can of black bean rinced, about 1C of frozen corn and 2 small cans of green chilies. I also used heaping teaspoons of the spices for more flavor. I will make this again and again. Thanks!

Oh my! I had never heard of refried bean soup before.  This is delicious!  I absolutely love beans of all kinds and have been looking for some different soup recipes. Since the refried beans were already seasoned, there was no need for me to add any of the spices.  Instead of a can of peeled tomatoes, I substituted some chunky black bean and corn salsa. I also added some green chilies and left out half of the hamburger.  I think it would be great topped with shredded cheese, sour cream, green onions, tortilla chips, chili cheese Fritos, the possibilities are endless!  I will be making this often.  Thank you so much!

This is really good even my picky 7y/o that normally won't touch anything with tomatoes in it ate it! Pureeing it is a fantastic idea for kids!!! I really enjoyed it also. DH has not tried it yet but I'm sure he will love it! Will make again!! Add more refried beans next time! Served it with tortilla stars(here on Zaar)

This soup is wonderful!  I left out the celery because I don't care for it, used ground turkey, 1 can diced tomatoes and 1 can diced tomatoes with green chili, and used chicken stock, added a can of black beans and some frozen corn.  It was so delicious!  I'll be making this again, but tripling the recipe so we can have more.

Thick, rich & filling - really good & hearty. Served it w/ sour cream, cheddar, & nacho chips. Great addition to our fajitas dinner. (I had it without the chips- South Beach) it's still very filling.Thanks
My family really enjoyed this soup.  Very good and easy to make.  Thank you for sharing.

YUm! The family enjoyed this and is going to be a keeper!  I did substitiute b-b-q rib meat for the hamburger meat  but I think that just added more flavor.  I also added more broth than the recipe called for because we wanted a thinner soup. Thank you for a great recipe

This was a great a tasting soup...although I did add a lot more stock to thin it out and chopped jalapeno's. I topped mine with a handful of lightly crushed cornchips and grated cheese then zapped in the microwave so cheese melted. Mmm...a tasty Sat night's supper.

This was delicious, and quite easy to make.  The only thing I did differently was to add only 1/2 of a bell pepper (all I had on hand) and I threw in a couple chopped chipotles in adobo for flavor and heat.  My only complaint is that this didn't taste very bean-y... I love refried beans, which is why I was drawn to this recipe.  Next time I'll double the beans and half the tomatoes, and possibly leave out the celery as well.  Thanks!

This soup was good and really different.  We prefer brothier soups which is why we might not make it that often, but its definitely a nice alternative to chili.  I omitted the celery as it just doesn't go with Mexican food IMO.  We added a bit more broth per the suggestion of another user, and although it thinned out the soup amazingly the refried bean flavor was still there making it very unique.  Thanks for sharing - great recipe.

We definitely liked the soup, but I have to agree with another reviewer . . . it wasn't "beany" enough for us . . . so I added an extra can of refried beans.  I also eliminated the celery, due to personal preference.

Made it as listed except didn't add the celery or cinnamon.  I did add a 15 oz can of black beans.  Without the black beans it would not seem complete.  I did not blender it at the end.  The texture does add to the goodness of the soup.  It is a good change from chili.  I would make this again with these changes.  Only gave it 3 stars because it is missing something without the extra beans. 
Enjoy!

A very tasty soup that all can adjust to their own taste.  The basic concept of refried beans and beef broth as the base -- YUM!!   I agree, ditch the celery and cinnamon, and add more of whatever beans you like.  I agree no need to blender, though I did hand-cut the peeled tomatoes with scissors in the can before adding (my personal technique!  canned "diced" aren't as tasty).
I too only gave it 3 stars because no soup with this few vegetables can rate any higher with me, but I threw in some shredded Napa cabbage I had on hand -- disappears into it, and and ups the nutrition some!
Yummy!

I was looking for a pureed soup and made this exactly as described except that I left out the beef. (I don't like pureed meat.)  I didn't really love it (maybe the meat changes the flavour profile quite a bit?) I ended up freezing it in a few batches and I'm going to add it the next time I make chili.  Otherwise I would have thrown a lot of it out.  I would not make again.

This is a fantastic soup!!! I made it with 16 oz can of diced tomatoes and 8 oz can of tomatoes with green chillies. Left out the bell pepper, doubled the garlic. I drained the beef after cooking, for less grease. I added a 16 ounce can of pinto beans and topped with mexican shredded cheese and sour cream. I didn't puree it.  Served with a Caesar Salad recipe #618000 from evelyn/athens and crusty bread. My DH and his friend devoured this. I wanted leftovers, but it's all gone.

Dontcha hate those reviews that say "this was SO good, but I changed everything about it..." Well, unfortunately, here goes....

I was at the point of no return with the recipe when I discovered that I didn't have any refried beans on-hand. (Very odd! I ALWAYS have a can or two in the pantry!) The closest substitute I could come up with was a 16 oz. jar of nonfat black bean dip. Oh. My. Goodness. What a fabulous soup it made! Because the dip was already seasoned, I omitted all the seasoning in the recipe except for adding cilantro, which I LOVE. At that point, I figured what the heck and threw in a little less than a cup of corn I found in the bottom of the freezer. And, b/c I thought the soup might not be "hearty" enough for DH, I threw in 1/2 c of orzo at the end after whirring it A LITTLE with a stick blender. What resulted was a fabulous, thick, hearty, soup that was a perfect way to end the 20-degree day we had in MD. Sorry, Tugar, that I can't rate the recipe the way you posted it. But it was certainly the inspiration for a soup that I will make again and again! :-) FYI, the way mine ended up, it's 7 WW pts/6 hearty servings.
Definately a keeper.
