This sounds like a simple and tasty meal, but I do not believe it deserves to be under the sub-head title: "low calorie meals"

I must be the odd one bc I thought this was really bland. I think I would have been better off just using a jar of spaghetti sauce, or maybe adding in some spices and sauted green peppers and garlic. I could almost taste each ingredient separetly. Even in "poverty" you can have flavor. ;)

I used canned diced tomatoes with garlic & olive oil instead of the stewed tomatoes.  It was delish--my family loved it, and it really helps to stretch our ever-shrinking dollars!  My husband loves the recipe title.  :)

Good and solid, and certainly easy on the pocket.  Not very exciting as written but it's easy to jazz up.  I added various Italian herbs and a cup or so of frozen peas in the last 15 minutes, and grated cheddar on top as we had no Parmesan cheese.

I used a lot of suggestions from other reviews (can of white beans, diced tomatoes w/Italian spices, cottage cheese, frozen peas and carrots, a little extra garlic powder, oregano, and basil).  Then I added an 8 oz pkg of low fat cream cheese, and this made it extra good - creamy and the taste has a tiny tang to it.  Thank you for this inexpensive, easy recipe.  I think it's going on my comfort food list.

Definitely a hit with kids. Paired well with http://www.recipezaar.com/87482
I'm putting it in with the go to quick fixes. I couldn't help but add about 1 t. italian seasoning. I had my first bowl topped with mozzarella and my second with a Kraft mexican blend and then my third... Just kidding, just 2 and preferred the latter. Next time I plan to add celery and carrots.

So easy and so cheap. We were very skeptical, but really enjoyed this meal and a LOT of leftovers. We added great northern beans and about a teaspoon on Italian seasoning. DH liked it with parmesan and I liked it with a little cheddar. I may add some crushed red pepper next time for just a bit of kick.

Very good!  I used Dreamfield's Penne Rigate and Del Monte (original recipe) Stewed Tomatoes.  It was EXACTLY what I remembered as "goulash".  My husband put a whole bunch of mixed Italian shredded cheese on it.  I liked it best just they way it came out of the pot.  Thank you for a wonderful, low carbohydrate, high fiber comfort food!

Wow, this was amazing!  So much better than hamburger helper could ever be!  I used tomatoes that I canned myself and onions and garlic straight from the garden.  I also love monterey jack cheese melted on most anything, so I grated some on top of this instead of parmesan and it was perfect!  I served it with green beans and potatoes also out of the garden.  It gets a 10 from me!

I knew I had to review this recipe when my extremely picky son told me "delicious dinner, mom."  Those aren't words I hear often!  Well, as many have noted this is a very simple recipe with remarkably good results.  Since in my family we all like spicy food I used tomatoes with chilis mixed in, I added a teaspoon of paprika and I substituted 1/2 c. red wine for that much water.  Crusty bread is important too as there is lots of yummy pan juice!
Okay did not reheat nicely.

My mom used to cook up something like this - we called it Mamaroni!  Maybe throw in a can of corn or green beans, too.  She made a pot big enough to last for what seemed like forever.  It was better the first night because as it aged, the noodles swelled up and I thought that was icky.

We made this meal and it was good. One thing to watch out for was that the noodles did not all cook all the way thru even with us cooking for 3-5 minutes over the stated time. This dish is definitely easy and kids will eat it. We added 1 tablespoon italian seasoning for more flavor. Also canned tomatoes in our area were now 14.5 oz so we had to add a little more water to make up for the juice. We also added cheddar cheese instead of parmesan as a personal preference. Thank you Malriah for a quick meal from pan to table on a busy weeknight.

Excellent!  I used 16oz macaroni to stretch it for my family of 5.  Added a can of tomato sauce, green bell pepper and a little taco seasoning.  The whole family loved it and it will be a regular in our meal plan.
Great meal added a 12oz. can of tomato sauce to add a little more favor and more garlic.  Kids loved it.

Made this the other day, but with some alterations (after reading other recipes of this kind).  I added 2 - 8 oz. cans of tomato sauce, 1 cup chili sauce, only 1 can stewed tomatoes, 3 TBSP brown sugar, 1 TBSP chili powder, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp. paprika, some seasoned salt & pepper, some cooked onions.     Added in the cooked macaroni, and OMGolly Gee was it good.  It had a sweet/tangy taste that my husband went nuts over.  He ate "5" bowls in one sitting.  Oh yeah, we also topped it with shredded cheddar.  Thanks for giving me a great base to work from.  I actually can't wait to make it just your way as it will be more economical....
A quick simple and very tasty meal.  I didn't have stewed tomatoes so I used a can of petit diced tomatoes and a con of tomatoe sauce and it turned out very good.
I've never had this until this recipe. I made it for my boyfriend whom used to eat this growing up - he loved it. I doubled the pasta and put in 2 cups. It is on the rotation! Thanks.

This was good. It's a little on the plain side, even though I added some corn. I will make this again, but maybe next time add more garlic, and melt some cheddar cheese over the top. I really liked how quick and easy this recipe is.
Comfort for for a true pasta lover!!!!  I did add garlic salt and melted cheddar on top.  Great kid pleaser too!

This recipe was pretty good. We used a variation of noodles, I had to add a bit more water so that all the noodles could cook thoroughly. I would definitely add corn next time to give it something more. I served it with pillsbury biscuits, PERFECT!

This was very good, but without the addition of the parmesan, it would have tasted bland, in my opinion.  I used leftover pasta, so I didn't add the can of water.  I also threw in about 8 oz of frozen corn.  I'm sure I'll make it again, but next time I'll add a small can of tomato paste, and some herbs.  This is a versatile recipe which is adaptable to additions and changes according to what's on hand at the time!  Thanks for posting, Malriah!

This went over well at my house.  It reminds me of Goulash.  Some reviewers have said that it is a bit bland.  I think this makes it perfect for those "picky" eaters!  There are really no overpowering tastes.  It is just a perfect comfort food.  I will be sure to make this again soon!  Thanks!
Taste was okay but the macaroni was too mushy for me.  I redid and cooked my macaroni by itself and then added.  Tasted much better.

I made this many times for my girls and I; we called it "Creation"; they were home from college in Oct and both asked if we could have Creation.....it's a keeper and extremely versatile to what you have on hand.

My DH is a total Italian sauce snob who normally won't eat pasta that isn't served with his "gramma's sauce".  I knew I was taking a risk in serving this, but it was worth the gamble.  He loved it and now I have a great alternative for when I don't have 6 hours to make his dinner :)

I used this to teach my 12 yo how to cook.  We've been making a meal a week and this one was so easy for him and turned out tasty that he was very proud of it.  We did however change one thing, we added some extra spices just cause our family likes it that way.  But it's a great recipe and makes delicious leftovers too.
Excellent and cheap - One of DH favorites  :)

This is good. I dumped in the whole box of penne (what I had) and threw in 2 bricks of cream cheese (all those noodles 1 wasn't enough)! Very easy; you can use what you have on hand. Any tomatoes would work--I had 1 can of italian stewed and 1 can of mild rotel. I added a can of tomato sauce and some tomato paste, too. I also used ground chicken (what I had) again probably things one has on hand, and you have dinner. Thank you for helping me purge my pantry and freezer (I have been working on that for a while.)

This was absolutely delightful.  So easy and so tasty.  I used a beef bouillion cube instead of salt, because someone absconded with the salt, and it was great.  I also added about a teaspoon of cajun seasoning to help replace the salt. I love this.  I might add some italian spices for a change of pace but I will eat it just like this many more times in the future.  Thanks!

Easy and great! I felt like I had nothing in the house except a lb. of extra lean ground turkey so I searched Recipezaar for something. This fit the bill. I used Barilla protein plus Omega 3 elbows, 2 14.5 oz cans of petite diced tomatoes and 1 mild can of Rotel. I also added black beans. When finished, I garnished with a little dollop of sour cream and a sprinkle of colby jack. Yum! Next time, I might dress it up with fresh veggies--red peppers, mushrooms, green onions and the like. Thanks for a great base that I can make with virtually anything I have!
Simple, good stuff.  I used spaghetti and diced tomatoes with chilis, but it came out great! (Well, a little spicy, but that's my own fault with the chilis.)

This was a winner. I loved how easy it was to prepare and that I could make it all in one pot (I removed the onions and garlic to a bowl in order to brown the meat and then added them back in). My 2 and 3 yr olds ate it, which is my measure of a successful dish. Thanks for posting.

I grew up on this! It was my motherâ€™s version of Goulash (single mother of 4)! I make it for my FiancÃ© now and it is one of his favorite meals (and he is a VERY picky eater). I like to add chopped green pepper and onion to mine, and if I have any on hand some PACE Thick and Chunky Salsa (we buy it at Costco). It is also good topped with any kind of cheese (American to shredded cheese) and I also like to top with crushed red pepper!

I call this my easy lasagna as I use any pasta, put it in a oven dish and drizzle cheese sauce then top with gratted cheese. It makes enough for the next day. If you need more just add more pasta. Great for teens to reheat when hungry.
I do the same dish, but put in a dish, add fresh cream and then cheese on top and brown in oven. This is lush!
easy and taste great...there is so much you can add but it is good all by itseld

Very Good.  I love it when you find these simple recipes and they turn out to be so good.   My Husband loved this.  
 
I have a tip for cooking with macaroni.  I cooked the meat sauce for 20 minutes. Turn off the heat, pour in the macaroni and stir.  Put the lid on and leave it stiing for 10 minutes are so and it will be cooked perfectly.  Sometimes when you add macaroni it continues to cook stting in the pot.  It works for me....eklare
My whole family loved this. It was very easy to make. I used diced tomatoes with green chiles because thats all I had. Thank you for sharing!!
Thank you for sharing but my family and I found this to be rather bland.

This reminds me of something my mother used to make that I make now, same basic idea, only I add in addition some diced bacon, onion, mushrooms and put cheese on top and put it in the oven until it is melted. My mom tops it with breadcrumbs so there is a nice bit of crispiness to it. Yummy!!

Pretty good.  Family (even picky 6 year old!) liked it.  I added a tsp of homemade Italian seasoning as well as an 8 oz. can tomato sauce.  For me, there was too much onion and the tomato pieces were too big.  Next time I'll use less onion and pick a finer-diced tomato.

My grandma made something similar and we called it beefaroni.  This was pretty good and very easy.  I will make a couply of changes next time though, not because anything was wrong, but because my 4yo is picky and I got tired of picking out the tomatoes and onions.  So next time I will use crushed tomatoes rather than stewed and onion powder instead of onion.

Added some herbs to this but otherwise stuck with the recipe. Very simple tasty meal but made way too much. DH took leftovers to work and said it tasted even better than fresh. Will definitely make again.
Even though I added extra garlic and threw in chopped parsley it was so bland. I think toddlers through teens might like it. Won't be making this again.

I also grew up with this type of dish. Fits the budget, quick for those busy evenings and healthy. I use lean ground beef, whole wheat pasta and added frozen corn and peas. Probably wouldn't serve it to company but will make it often during the week. Thanks for posting.

I did add a bit of basil, and didn't have the second can of stewed tomatoes (boohoo!), but this turned out great!

Thanks for posting this nice meal, yum yum!  :~)

Martha
This was sooo good! I have been looking for this recipe forever. Yummy!!!
My grandma used to make this - and despite being so simple it really is a delicious meal.
my family really liked this, its so easy to make. I did add tomato paste like mentioned in other reviews. this is a great meal.

I made something similar to this when I first started cooking and newly married. (I made it so often that my DH told me to give it a break for a while...this and quiche, lol!!!)  I called it my Clean Up the Fridge Dump Casserole.  Basically I used up all the leftover veggies and cheese I had in the fridge.  I would sometimes added a can of chick peas or black beans....adding tomato juice if more liquid was needed.  Any shape of noodle can be used up.  The only thing I did different was that I added the noodles at the end and turned off the heat and let the noodles cook in the sauce, for about 10 minutes.  This way the noodle stayed "al dente" even after heating up the leftovers the next day!   Thanks for taking me down Memory Lane!!

This was a quick, cheap, easy meal, and oh so good!  I especially loved this with the grated parmesan cheese, but w/o it, it reminds me of a goulash,
but I thought that was good too! Since I only had 2 small cloves of garlic to add to this dish, I sprinkled on a bit of garlic salt, and Lawry's Seasoning Salt, instead of using regular table salt.  I cut the recipe in half, and found it only took me 15 minutes to cook this meal over low to medium-low heat.  Thank you Malriah for posting this wonderful recipe.  I enjoyed it, and will be making this often.

i loved this recipe. it was a bit bland so my hubby and i made a few changes to it. we did not have the stewed tomatoes but we used a half of a tomato. we also added some red pepper and some sazon and adobo and it came out spicy and very good. thanks!
I was looking for something quick and easy, and this actually surprised my by how tasty it was.  I did throw in a can of corn, but otherwise cooked as directed!

I make a version of this for my own family. My kids love it. I add tomato juice or V8 instead of water. Sometimes I use different types of stewed or diced (Italian or Mexican versions) tomatoes to switch it up a bit. My husband likes it with corn in it.
Very quick and easy to prepare--I didn't even drain the beef...instead, I added twice as much pasta, and just a tad more water.  It tastes a bit of hamburger helper, yet with tomatoes.

Super easy to make! I added some tomato sauce in place of the water and I thought that gave it more flavor.  I loaded in the garlic.  Turned out great. Next time I think I will use some diced tomatoes.  Thanks for sharing its a hit! Its Great as leftovers as well!

If my kids rated this, it would be 5 stars, they loved it. My spouse and I were not too thrilled with this, so I decided to meet in the middle with the rating. Given the basic ingrediants though, this is a quick meal and easy to put together and my kids loved the leftovers! I would make it again if it was requested, but probably not in the regular menu rotation unless we added some spice.

I made this recipe at the end of my pregnancy so that I could just throw it in the oven when I came home from the hospital on those nights that I didn't feel like cooking.  It made enough for me to  separate it into two disposable casserole pans.  I think it needs salt or a bit more flavor, but was otherwise very good.
Very easy to make and very tasty. I added about a half cup of chili sauce that was in my fridge as well as some itallian seasoning. This reciper is very versatile.
The whole family, including five and two year olds, liked this.  My husband was particularly excited about it.  I added the beans and will consider corn or peas as well next time.  Thank you!
This was so easy and fast. We liked it but thought it was a bit bland so I added some Mrs. Dash to it. Thanks for the recipe.

This was great! Simple, easy and fast. I substituted mostaccioli for the macaroni, because that's what I had on hand. In my opinion, the parmesan is necessary. It turned the slightly bland dish into a wonderful staple.

I have made this at least 15 times since I first tried it. It's great, easy, quick and cheap. I add various things depending on what I have, or what I feel like. I always add: Frozen corn, Italian Seasoning. Sometimes, I add: Cheddar, Cajun seasoning, various spices. If I have it, I also sometimes substitute a can of beef broth for the water. It makes it richer. It freezes and saves well, it's great for lunches and goes with many different side dishes. It's great for potlucks, especially when you don't want to spend an arm and a leg. Another cool thing about this is that you can keep almost all of the ingredients in the pantry for a quick meal, without having to go to the store for it.
Brings me back to my childhood. We always added a can of drained corn. Adding the shredded parmesan really added to the flavor!

I like the idea of this recipe, but it is very bland as is.  You need to season the meat while it is cooking and decide how to spice it up.  On the plus side it makes a huge hot meal, but not too tasty.

This is very close to a dish I grew up with     the difference was   we used  2-3 cans of tomato soup instead of  stewed tomatoes  (can of water for each can of soup)   season  added  pepper, onion powder, dash chili powder.
 very yummy and finicky kids no lumpy  tomatoes =)

My entire family and I loved this meal!  I was surprised that my usual 'non-tomato eating kids' both ate this dish!  Very easy to fix.  Only changes I made, I sauteed the onions alone at first, before adding the garlic so it wouldn't burn.  Otherwise, followed the directions exactly as written.  Very good - can't wait to eat this again.  Thanks Malriah!

As always, I made the recipe as is since it was my first time. I did season with salt to my preference but everything else the same and WOW. It smelled wonderful while cooking and it was so VERY good. Thanks for posting, I could just hug your neck it is so tasty and filling.

While the recipe is cheap, the taste is bland.  It's pretty much a spaghetti recipe - only made with elbow noodles.  My family likes a little spice to our food so I added a whole poblano pepper, 1 TBSP of Italian seasoning, and 1 tsp of Adobo seasoning to add more flavor and to spice it up a bit.  I'm not saying it was a bad recipe - just a little bland for my liking but after I added the above ingredients, it was better.  I'm not sure I'll make it again.

As written, this is kind of bland. This is similar to my mother's "tomato goulash" that I posted here a while back, only has a little more seasonings added. It was good, we doctored it a bit and it was yummy. The kids slurped it up!
This dish brought me back to my years growing up, my dad made this at least once a week for us.  Unfortunately, my own kids & hubby didn't care for it as much as I did as a child.

Oh the memories. BAck in the 1930's my Great Aunt "LO" called this "Dinner in a Dish". This way we thought we were eating fancy. Like some of the others, you could fill this with anything. It definately is a stick to the ribs type of meal and it sure beats the socks off "Fast Food menu's".
Thanks, Cap'n Jack

I came up with this idea independently myself years ago when I figured I could probably help hamburger better than that claymation glove guy, without the aid of all those mystery ingredients found in the powdered sauce pouch. As written here, this is fairly bland, so one should go through their fridge, freezer, and pantry and dump in whatever veggies one happens to have in there (mushrooms, bell peppers, etc), and scour your spice rack in a similar way for things like Italian seasoning. Use whatever pasta you have, but rotini is my favorite because it holds the sauce best. Be the envy of your fellow poor college students who are stuck eating ramen!
Nice recipe to have around for a quick go to meal when you are in a hurry.  Thanks.
Husband and kids loved it.
Bwa ha ha!  I called this "meat slop" as a kid.  Mom made it a lot and we LOVED it.  The only difference was that Mom used Velveeta instead of Parmesan.  I like it with the Parmesan!

I thought this was pretty good.  Super easy to make, but I did make a few changes.  I'm not a fan of stewed tomatoes, so I used a can of diced tomatoes and a can of crushed tomatoes.  I had to add corn starch to thicken because it was really watery.  Next time I will just add half a can of water or beef broth.  Also, I browned the beef in the same pot that I cooked the onions in to make it a "one pot meal".  Also added some chili powder and crushed red pepper for flavor and sugar to cut the acidity.  My picky husband even like it! :)

So fast and easy! I added frozen mixed veggies (corn, green beens, peas, carrots) and that gave it some color and more veggie factor.  I also added more pasta, about 1/2 pound total (1/2 box). Added some garlic powder, onion powder, and some brown sugar to taste.
This was great! So fast & simple to make. I added a can of corn, drained. My family loved it. Thanks.
I grew up on a version of this that also had Ranch-style beans.  We called it Chili-Mac and absolutely loved it.  Still do!
I can barely cook, but wanted to try something. This was a huge hit w/ hubby and kids. Thanks. Oh, and easy :)

This dish was served to us for lunch when I was in high school, but it was called (for some unknown reason) American chop suey.  When I got married, my husband loved this same dish, only he called it goulash.  My second husband also loved it, but he called it sopa.  Whatever name it goes by in your family, it seems to be known everywhere.  Thanks for reminding me of it.

Very easy to make on a work night. I took the advice of the fellow readers and cooked it a day before.  I added a cube of beef bouillon,oregano, and canned kidney beans.  The parmesan is a must.  My toddler loved it. I froze half since I have a small family. Next time I'll enjoy it with a crusty french loaf.

Only in modern America could this be considered a "poverty" meal. With a pound of meat and veggies out of season (canned tomatoes) this is a luxury meal in half the world. Anyone who thinks this is hardtimes food should look at other countries or our own country 100 years ago. The poor in America have it better then the middle classes of most of the rest of the world.

My mother made this when I was growing up.  Raised my kids on it too.  Never knew anybody who didn't like this meal.  The only thing I do differently, is to add about 1/2 chopped green bell pepper to the onion and garlic.  Glad to see this posted.  Thanks, Malriah.

My mother made it too!  We use only macaroni, ground beef, family size tomato soup, and frozen corn.  Still make it today and love every bite!

BTW... it's just a name...
My kids love this... and so do I!
had this last night everyone loved it.  Since I am not a big tomato lover, I think next time I will use 1 can of crushed & 1 can of stewed.  All & All it was fast, easy and tastes great.

Made this last night.  It was featured on the first page and looked yummy so I had to try it.  This was so awesome! Hubby loved it too.  The only things I changed were that I used one can of stewed tomatoes and a can of crushed tomatoes.  I used whole wheat macaroni and lean ground turkey.  So yummy!  Today I'm enjoying the leftovers!!
I have loved this forever! My Grandma called it "Muxi-Moo". Don't know why, but that what we'd ask for. Thanks for sharing.
Awesome.  I used whole wheat noodles, and added corn and black olives (sliced).  Super Yummy!

Apart from using 4 garlic cloves instead of 2, I followed this recipe as written.  It was ok but a bit bland.  I will make this again, but will have to play with different seasonings to give it more flavor. Good basic recipe!

This was a quick and excellent meal.  I was able to get it going while having a screaming 17 month old running around my house.  I could walk away at various times and then meal pretty much cooked itself.
My mom calls this goulash, but whatever you call it, it's good comfort food!
I added worchestershire (1 tblspoon) and a chopped green pepper.   Just like my mom used to make.

This is virtually identical to what I grew up with and still make today - only I use shells & 1 can of stewed toms.  My mother calls it Slumgullion.  And it is really good - the flavors just meld together.

I've been making a very similar recipe for years. I use Honeysuckle Italian turkey sausage (mild or hot).  I remove the casings and prepare it just like ground beef. It's awesome, you would never think that it is healthy when you eat it!! My husband is totally against ground turkey, lol except when he thinks it's the real thing!

I have not tried this receipe, but I made one similar that my kids LOVE.  Taco seasoning instead of tomatoes.  I used seashell noodles and the beef with go inside as you stir it.  I would also add corn.  FREZZES and REHEATs well too!
Wonderful! Thanks!
This recipe was quick, easy, and amazing! I will definitely continue to make it in the future. Thanks!

This gets a 5 on ease alone.  When I looked through the basic recipe (I didn't read the directions) I planned on cooking the pasta in a separate pan and then using another to bake it in the oven.  Was I surprised when I went to cook it and found not only was it easy but ONE PAN!  Made as directed except I substituted 2 cans of diced tomatoes because that's what I had on hand.  Very simple and easy.  The 4  year old loves it and the 7 will eat it.  Thanks for sharing.  I will make this again.

Like many other reviewers, we found this bland. Made this exactly as the recipe states, and honestly it was just tasteless. Added Monterrey/jack, and Parmesan, which helped some. I also added to my bowl cayenne pepper, and brown sugar. After a few adjustments here and there, it came out tasting pretty good. Next time I think I'll use diced tomatoes, and add a little of this and that.

I really liked this.  I added fresh herbs as Malriah suggested. I had hot oregano in the garden. It seems like a great prepare ahead "base" recipe that I can change by adding different spices and veggies. I'm going to try adding zucchini next. Thanks for sharing.

such nostolgia. when i was a child(depression, ww2)mom made this with additions such as canned corn, green beans ,kidney beans. no beans? add cooked potatoes, . mom called it goulash and we looked forward to it. it was hearty, filling and tasty,and could feed an army.

I made this for my family this weekend. Added kidney beans and frozen kernel corn, as well as oregano and a bay leaf.  My family LOVED this.  I had left overs for two days and they heated up great, and they disappeared.  No wasted food. I will make it again for sure. It was so easy.
I love this..ikt reminds my of when I was a kid...My mom made this all the time and we called it "Hobo Casserole".  We added cheddar too.

I LOVE this meal. Have been eating it for years. We throw in a jar of Ragu vegetable  primavera spag sauce instead of the stewed tomatoes and a can corn and it makes a great meal. My mom used to make it for us when we were kids with tomatoes and whatever she had in the fridge and called it goulosh.   If you have some cheddar cheese that's  a great addition to this recipe too.
I've been making a similar meal for years; the kids love it!  We add a can of pork & beans to the recipe. Yummy!

Been making this for years.  Truly an economical, quick, filling 1-dish meal.  I make a triple recipe when my son comes home (from out of state) and freeze it in multiple containers for him to take home.  They stay frozen for the 7 hour trip and, as this is his favorite meal and he won't cook, he can enjoy a little of home from his mother and me for just a little longer.  BTW, I use Newman's Own Marinara Sauce and a can of petite diced tomatoes rather than a regular spaghetti sauce.
Made this for friends coming over because I had all the ingredients on hand. They enjoyed it more than I expected.

I have always loved this as a quickie standby. In the New England we call it American Chop Suey. Add green bell peppers in it along with the onions and some crushed hot red pepper and you have a zesty dish.
I used a pkg of spagetti sauce, small can of mushrooms, and also a small can of sliced olives, baking it with a topping of a few sprinkles of parm cheese. wonderful
This is also called Johnny Marzetti and is taken from Marzetti's restaurant in Columbus, OH.  Great stuff no matter what name.

Oh, my gosh, I've been eating this since I was a kid, and I'm 46 now!!  My mom used to make it all the time and it was really wonderful until she started making it in the microwave (early '70's, when she got her Amana Radarange), which can make it gummy.  But on the stovetop it turns out great.  My mom even submitted it to our school recipe book, calling it, "Joan's Fantastic Dinner".  Yummy!  She would use add some cheddar to the dish after the macaroni had cooked, and sprinkle some additional on top just before serving.  It was quick and easy for a working mom in the 1970's, and would work just as well today!  Thanks for posting this!  I'll be glad to make it for my husband and daughters; they'll love it.  I'll call it, "Before Hamburger Helper."

I too grew up on this dish.  My mom called it goulash, and it was truly a family favorite.  I'm now 64 and made this last week (used about twice the garlic and added lots of fresh basil and some pepper flakes) for my honey (hubby).  It's like going back in time every time we have this wonderful dish.  My sibliings also make this and love it.

OMG! My mother used to make this back in the 40's & 50's as we were growing up. She would add peas to it. There were 10 of us and it would stretch along ways. I've forgotten about this meal for years but now all at once I'm hungry for it. Guess what I'm having for supper tonight?
Thanks for bringing back some childhood memories.
This is a great dinner.  Both my kids love it and although it makes a lot, it doesn't last that long in our house.  We add corn to ours.
Growing up in the '80's my family enjoyed this too...Try it with corn!  Yum!

i'm 44, my mom made this every week without fail!  When I was first married (young and poor) I made it for my husband and he compared it to Hamburger Helper.  At that point, I never had HH in MY LIFE because this was and still is a DELISH dish!
When asked what he wants to eat, my 8 yr old wants "goulash" - this recipe.  He loves it!  Thanks for a quick and delicious meal that everyone enjoys.

I'm very sorry to say that we didn't care for this dish. It looked good, and the aroma was wonderful, but there was a sweetness to it, and it was quite bland. I tried adding more salt, which didn't help much. The next day, I added some marinara and a little chili powder to the leftovers. This helped a bit, but we still didn't like it.

This meal reminds me of the soup we used to have as kids. My dad called it Hangover Soup, and it was like yours, but a little different. Quite a bit more liquid. Funny though, when I make it, I add parmesan cheese to my own too. Yum, yum! Definitely going to try yours. :D

this is great! the version I know and love has one envelope of Lipton onion soup mix added, and then you can leave out the salt. it is easy to prepare because you don't have to measure out anything - 1 can tomatoes, 1 can water, egg noodles (about half a 12 oz bag), onion soup mix, pound of ground beef or turkey or whatever! YUM!! I will definitely try adding the cheese on top next time
We really liked this. A nice satisfying one pot meal. A little bland for me so next time I'm going to use onion soup mix like jjflamingo suggests. Thanks!
Made this for my once-a-week cooking foray. I'm veg, so made for my husband. Used penne pasta instead of macaroni. Husband said this was great, he even had an extra helping! Thanks Malriah.
I haven't made this recipe yet, but it sounds like what we grew up on.  Probably about once a week too, but I loved it!  Who knew it was inexpensive then?

My mom used to make this all the time but she called it "company beef casserole". If you want to make it into a casserole it takes just a few small changes:  While you are browning the meat boil the pasta separately according to the box.  Drain one can of tomatoes before adding it and mix ingredients together.  Add 1 cup of shredded cheddar cheese to the mix and place in an 8x10 cake pan.  Sprinkle the top with some more cheddar and cover with foil.  Bake at 350 for about 40 minutes until the sides get bubbly and serve. Yum!!
We had this all the time when I was a kid, and I still find myself craving it once in awhile now.  We used to add 1 cup of shredded cheddar, and some sliced green olives.  Yum!

My mom made this all the time! I looked at the chef's name to see if we were related :) I add small diced bell pepper just as the meat is browning also use a good name brand ground turkey..1/2 pound regular and 1/2 pound Italian seasoned. You can add red sauce , about a cup for a little extra taste. If your family likes white pepper a few shakes makes it even better. Don't let the simpleness of this fool you it is yummy and teenagers love it!

I use to eat this too as a kid, but my Mom added a heaping spoonful of Sour Cream to the mixture once it was done.  I am making it for dinner, and I plan to add a little sour cream for old times sake.

This was a similiar meal my mother had made also.  She had always used egg noodles in it.  I added canned corn, because it just wasn't right to me without it.  Mom always added corn.  Talk about a meal that can stretch to feed many.  And we never thought of it as a "money-saving" dish when we were growing up. Thanks for this recipe.

Received this recipe in an email....tried it for Saturday lunch after little leage and it worked. We're a busy family of five, I served it with garlic bread and salad in Southern CA outside in the afternoon was nice.

This was a great meal!  The family loved it!!  I omitted the tomatoes and used two small cans of tomato sauce instead.  I still added a can of water, but used double the macaroni.  I also added a can of chili beans undrained.  We like spice in our house.. so I threw in some white pepper, celery salt, and ground red pepper for some kick!!  Delicious!  This will be made again and again!!

If you're going to rate a recipe, prepare it as written and rate it based on that.  Once you make your changes, no matter how small, it's no longer the original  recipe and very unfair to rate it as such.  Go ahead and make it your way, but don't leave a rating.  Okay...I had to say that, not about this particular recipe, but based on several other ratings I've read on other recipes.  

Anyway, this wonderfully simple dish is what we used to call 'goulash', but whatever you call it, it's a great, easy, inexpensive comfort food that you'll want to serve often.  My 12-year-old grandson made this for our dinner and had no problems with directions.  All of the ingredients were in my pantry and freezer, so no running to the store, especially nice since we're 10 miles away, living in a rural area.

The only problem we found was that it didn't make enough!!  The recipe will be doubled the next time, for sure!  Any leftovers, if any,  will definitely be great for lunch!
  
Thanks, Malriah, for warming my memories of seeing Mom at the stove making this family favorite!   :)
My daughter loved this and wanted it 2 nights in a row!  Thanks.
My family really enjoyed this dish.  It was fast and easy on a weeknight.

I absolutely LOVED this!!!  It also reminds me of a meal we had growing up.  It's full of flavor, easy, and fast!  I didn't have stewed tomatoes on hand, so I used diced tomatoes and actually chopped them up a little smaller.  Thanks so much for sharing!
i think its great, and i also think that peoples little additions are helpful, personally its nice to have creativity with a simple recipe. its a great idea and a great canvass for a great meal

Good simple recipe for an easy weeknight meal.  I like that it is very adaptable for everyone's personal changes and additions.  I used 1 can diced tomatoes and 1 can crushed tomatoes instead of the stewed tomatoes.  I served it with the suggested parmesan cheese.  My 3 year old enjoyed it and asked to have the leftovers for lunch today.  I thought it could use more spice, so I look forward to making it again sometime and playing around with the ingredients to figure out what additions will suit our family's tastes best.  Thank you for the idea!

I ate this as a child... but I don't remember it tasting quite this good.  We loved it, it was quick, easy and tasty!  We did add a fair amount of salt and pepper and also the parmesan cheese, and will definately do it again.  Thanks Malriah!

I just made this recipe and it is great!  I didn't know what I was going to make for supper, but this one used everything I had on hand!  I used 2-14.5 oz. cans of diced italian tomatoes and only sauted the onions.  I also added a bit more water and a little more macaroni than the recipe calls for. I put shredded mozzerella cheese over the top.  Very good and will make again.  Definitely a good recipe for those on a budget, but also great for those who don't live close to a grocery store!  Thank you for posting!

This was a really good recipe.  I used ground turkey, and 2 cans of chopped tomatoes.  I like it with the parmesan cheese.  My mom made goulash when I was growing up, but I like this one better.  This is now my "go to" goulash recipe.  Thank you.
Followed the recipe exactly.  We liked it.  Reminds us of what we used to call "goulash" growing up.  Parm on top is a great addition.
Much more flavor than I expected! It was a big hit and easy to make.

Fast and yummo! and like a healthy version of  the Hamburger Helper mixes I used to love as a kid. U used one 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes and little pasta shells. I used more garlic cloves, added Italian seasoning and oregano and some of my homemade taco seasoning. Topped w/grated Parmesan. Delish!
It was o.k.  Very simple and bland.

Loved the recipe. Added some herbs and parmesan. Next time will add some tomato paste. A tip: We cooked the pasta separately and made the sauce without the water. Then froze the sauce and pasta separately. Super easy to just defrost in the fridge, toss in a baking dish and into the oven until hot. Added some cheese, too. :-)

This is SO good! I grew up on this. The only thing that my family does differently is cook the macaroni separately. My mom never added garlic but she was never one for using many herbs or spices. I sort of followed your recipe to a T. I didn't have stewed tomatoes in the cupboard so I used Italian seasoned diced ones and I was out of elbow mac so I used some other kind of noodle. Thank you so much for posting such a favorite!

Exactly how I remember it!  However, to bulk it up, I added kidney beans.  This increased the protein without added fat.  (I doubled the recipe but only used 1 lb of meat)  KIDS LOVED IT!  Thanks for recovering one of my favorite recipes from my childhood!
Noodles were mushy.  I prefer the recipes where the noodles are cooked separately.
I did not like this meal what so ever.  I thought it was really plain and felt like it was lacking flavor.  All I could taste was the macaroni. :(

This ended up better than I thought!  I added some basil, a little Trader Joe's Puttanesca pasta sauce, and chili powder (and lots of parmesan on each serving) and now I can eat it for entire week!  You weren't kidding about it lasting for leftovers!!
Very good.  Even my picky daughters loved it
This was tasty and easy to make.  We used venison burger instead of beef and it was really good...

Mmmmm! Can't believe I never tried this before - so simple and sooo yummy! I doubled the garlic and added 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1/4 tsp cayenne, a few dollops of Worchesthire sauce, a little salt, lots of black pepper, and some fresh chopped parsley which I happened to have. I used 1 can stewed tomatoes, and 1 can diced. Smothered with parmesan. Gave it lots of flavor and just the right amount of heat (IMO).  Will DEFINITELY make agian. Thanks a bunch!!!

It's nice, quick, easy, and we always have the ingredients on hand. Except I used diced tomatoes instead of stewed. But this turned out good. I will keep it as one of those "oh boy, I forgot to figure out what we're having for dinner" night plans. Thanks for sharing!

Fantastic meal for just before pay day!  You can get away with using less than 1lb of beef - I made earlier with about 3/4lb (quantities of other ingredients unchanged) and it was lovely.  Only thing I did differently was, as I made in advance and didn't want the pasta poking out of the top to dry out, I covered the finished dish with a layer of cheese sauce and threw in the freezer.  Like other reviewers you could add almost anything to this to bulk it out.  My beef was fresh and I froze mine (with the layer of cheese sauce on top) and it was great reheated.  Thanks

Good, filling meal.  I used 2 cans of stewed tomatoes with Italian seasoning and a pound of ground turkey meat, also with Italian seasoning.  It fed my family (me, hubby, 10 year old son and 9 year old daughter) with none left in the pot.  I think if I wouldn't have used those preseasoned tomatoes and turkey, that it would have been a little bland.  I served it with some Saltines.  It was a quick, easy and economical meal.  Thanks!
I dont know what I did but this came out horrible. The noodles were super overcooked and it had no taste at all. Super disappointed after all the great reviews.
This dish is so good!! Very economical, easy, and tastey!  Thanks!!
A good basic recipe=but very bland.  I added garlic powder, parsley flakes, whole kernel corn and sliced black olives.  Then it was terrific!

I did have some slight modifications.  I like canned tomatoes, but thought for my taste two cans may be too much. So, only one can went in.  I also used ground turkey.  In addition, my noodles were from mac n cheese, so I went ahead and threw in the the cheese sauce packet.  I shredded some sharp cheddar on top.  Such great comfort food, yum!!

A tasty meal for the price. I added a can of kidney beans as another reviewer suggested, and used whole wheat penne instead of macaroni. I added 1 tsp of chili powder and 1 tsp of oregano, but it was still a bit bland, so next time will add more. Also it turned out slightly too watery, so will try using 1.5 cups water instead of 16 oz. Thanks for sharing a keeper!
I have made this 5 times since finding the recipe early this Fall. It's such a hit! Really good and one of those meals that is sooooo good reheated!! :D YUM!!! Good recipe thanks!
so tasty, easy and fast. The family loves it... makes great leftovers too!!

I planned this specifically for a night I knew I was going to be rushed to get dinner on the table. Less than 30 minutes from start to finish. If the meat was browned in advance you could have this on the table faster than going through a drive-thru. I followed the recipe exactly, added the suggested kernel corn and the leftovers made for a great lunch. Thank you for an easy and quick recipe.
Unique meal idea, and very quick indeed.  A little on the sweet side for me, though...

I made this a few months ago when my family came over for a quick meal. I doubled the recipe and everyone got seconds. I liked the sweetness to it, it is a sure winner.  You could definitely make this in a crock pot by adding the pasta at the end already precooked or even freezing it for an OMAC! Great recipe!
Very good, My boyfriend loved it.

Really good. I put this into our regular rotation, so we have it once a month. I usually add half a can of whole corn, or half a can of peas, although it is great as it is written. We like to sprinkle the top with shredded sharp cheddar before serving. Delish!

As a mom of three picky girls ages 7, 12 and 14, I have to honestly say that I didn't think they would eat this... I put everythign into a freezer bag (except for the noodles) and saved for an oamc meal.  Later in the month, I warmed up the bag and added it to a fresh box of pasta (I didn't re-read the directions and added more pasta than I should have) but it turned out fantastic! Not only did my girls and hubby devour it, my daycare kids did too! This will be a regular meal in my home.

We ate something similar as kids - instead of the stewed tomatoes, we'd add condensed tomato soup.  We called it SLOP.  To the leftovers, we'd add stewed tomatoes and then it was "Goulosh!"  Thanks for the recipe!
take the poverty out of it..... great one pan meal.
This is one my husband's favorite meals. I make as directed and top with cheddar cheese!

This is a good busy day recipe. I made it just as the recipe indicates but would add another clove or two of garlic and herbs, perhaps an Italian blend. Also, this recipe says it serves four but it makes at least eight servings so plan to serve the leftovers another day and/or freeze some of it.

I made this last night and it is a cheap meal and delicious. I cut the recipe in half and used diced tomatoes with chilies and 2 Tbls. of tomatoe paste. I did add some frozen corn and velveta cheese instead of cheddar to make it more creamy. I also added Mrs. Dash garlic/herb seasoning, some basil and a little oregano...turned out great. Thank you for a wonderful recipe that anyone can make as is or add to and turn out delicious!
Simple, easy, and healthy! I use ground turkey for less fat.  Thanks!

This was a great easy meal.  My dad always made this when I was a child and he called it Goulash.  It was never as good as this one, though.  All of my children liked this and some had seconds; which is always a success in my books when that happens.  They don't like tomatoes so I always try to use petite diced or crushed so they won't see the chunks.  I did not do that this time.  I used the stewed tomatoes and not one kid complained!  I used 16 oz. of macaroni and an extra can of water.  I used about 1/4 c. parmesan cheese and mixed that in with everything (a litte before and a little after the noodles were tender).  I then added a little cheddar cheese to the top and let that melt before dishing out.  I made a loaf of garlic bread and a nice salad to even out the meal.

My family really enjoyed this.  I did put a little ground red pepper and a little bit of real bacon bits in it that I had in the fridge. I also put some shredded cheddar cheese on top along with the parmesan.  My one year old cleaned his plate!!!
This was quick and easy and tasted very good, especially the left overs the next day.  I didn't change a thing.

This is an excellent budget meal that I have been making off and on for years.  The only difference is that I will dice up left over vegetables such as carrots, bell peppers, zucchini or celery and will even cut corn off a cob to toss in.  It is a great way to use up a few left overs in the fridge and make a tasty dish that goes a long way.
It was so bland!  Could barely swallow it.  I had to add curry spices for flavor, but I would still only describe it as "edible."

We loved this!! Changed it up a bit; used ground italian sausage instead of beef, added extra canned diced tomatoes, used whole wheat macaroni, and added paprika and two dried red chili peppers.  It was so good, so cheap, and so easy and quick to make! Thanks for the recipe!!
Love a recipe that uses everything I've already got in the pantry.  This was tasty too, thanks!

I think my mom made this for us growing up but called it goulash?  It's a fairly easy meal to make but I didn't like that I had to be stirring constantly for 20 minutes so the macaroni wouldn't stick to the bottom of the pan.  In my opinion, spaghetti is just as cheap, contains the same basic nutrients and is slightly easier to make so I'll probably stick to that in the future.  It was fun to try a new recipe though.

Very good basic recipe.  I used gr. turkey and whole wheat pasta, and added additional spices.  Very pleased with this, as it opens up many possibilities to serve it often yet switch it up a bit each time.
My family enjoyed this meal a lot. I used spaghetti instead of macaroni. Very good recipe I will use it often.

This is such gr8 confort food, my husband loved it.. I did not have stewed tomatoes so I used petite diced tomatoes and I also used ground deer instead. Thanks for posting such a fabuoous recipe... So simple yet so good!!
Liked this very much.  Used coarse ground hamburger and italian stewed tomatoes.  I might double the tomatoes or add corn/green beans, just for variety.  Thanks for posting a delicious recipe.

Once I doctored it all up with tons of seasonings, veggies, and kidney beans it was ok, but it was quite plain and boring just as listed. I used crushed and diced tomatoes since that is what I had, left out the water, and it was still SOUPY. 

A college roommate used to talk about never liking tomato soup because the only way her mom ever made it was to dump all the leftover bits from the fridge into some canned tomato soup. I'm guessing that was her mom's version of this...
Good! I used a little extra water than called for, but it turned out fine.  Thanks for posting.
This turned out pretty well. I doubt it would become my favorite meal ever, but it is super-easy and everyone ate it without complaining. I will probably make this again.

This was an ok meal, and good for a quick & easy dinner, but not a favorite.  I added corn, kidney beans, and Italiano seasoning and it still seemed to be missing something. I may try it again but will read more reviews for ideas to perk it up a little.
Very easy, cheap and tasty! Thanks for posting!

My mom used to make this too, back in the 1960s. She added canned corn, and we called it goulash. (It was years before I found out it isn't true goulash.) I use broth instead of water, and I usually need to double the recipe because I just can't quit filling my bowl! This is great comfort food.
This was good but could use a lot more seasoning.  If you want to choose some spices to add, I would try this recipe.

To add more flavor, I added onion and garlic powder as well as Mild Taco Seasoning & diced jalapenos, and used Mexican-style stewed tomatoes. Both my way and the original recipe make for good, reliable comfort food. Will be saving this and working it into my regular rotation.

Update: I made this again, this time using 1 can of regular stewed tomatoes and beef broth instead of water. I also added corn and chili sauce: this really is a great base recipe.
Very good. WILL make again!
i don't even have to make this to know it's good, because my family also used to make this a lot when i was younger. as i got older they made it less, but i remember it and it's so good!

I have made a similar recipe when my son was very young and was a very picky eater. We went to his friends house an the mother made a box of Kraft Mac and cheese. HE LOVED it, I went out to buy it and saw that it was "plastic"cheese... I came up with a more healthy recipe, Elbow macaroni ground beef cheddar cheese (the real deal) and home made pasta sauce, topped with mozzarella an parmesan.. He LOVED it and I've been making it now for about 40 years, I  think adding beans is a great idea and will try it next tim I make it. Thanx for the suggestion
This is similar to an Egyptian dish known as koushary, but koushary has lentils and rice instead of beef. Comfort food!!

If my entire childhood be condensed, this would be what it tastes like.  I added some cilantro and several other spices and it was fabulous!  This really does go perfectly with some garlic bread and a dark green salad.  Will be making this meal many more times!

I read through this recipe and realized I had a similar one I hadn't made in about 8 years.  I dug it out.  The only difference was that mine adds beef bullion and cheddar cheese instead of parmesan.  I love it.  My husband was bummed when I ate the leftovers and asked me to make this again.  Thanks for posting.  I give it five stars for the ease and time it took to make a pasta meal.

I think this is one of the first things I learned to cook "all by myself" when I was growing up. The only difference is I always add a chopped green or red pepper to it. My grandma taught me how to cook and never used measurements so I never knew how much macaroni to add to make a smaller batch. It is always better the second day though so that is not a big problem. LOL! I do prefer diced tomatoes and have used a can of V8 instead of water if I had one.

You can really stretch the serving by just adding more macaroni too.

I've been making a one dish meal similar to this for years. It too, was my mom's go to supper for us girls when we were children. We called it goulash, but whatever you call it, it makes a wonderful meal. I made this exactly as written with the exception of using regular cheap tomato juice in place of the water, I've found that this one addition makes a big difference in the flavor. Which means DH doesn't feel compelled to pour ketchup all over his, (that used to irritate me). This is also an easy recipe to dress up any way you want, ie. italian seasonings, mushrooms, peppers, hot pepper flakes etc. This is really good, and leftovers are better!

I omitted the olive oil and sauteed the garlic and onion in the ground beef while browning.  I also used tomato juice instead of water so that the elbow macaroni would swell up with tomato juice instead of water.  We're garlic lovers so I also used 5 cloves of garlic.  It turned out amazing.  I just made it again for my in-laws and they loved it!  Thanks Malriah for a wonderful recipe!  This is a keeper and so easy to make.

This is basically my mother's goulash! It's a very wonderful dish that I've never complained about making, eating, or serving to company! This is a recipe everyone has to make once! Great Job!
And THIS recipe itself is the BEST I've tried! Even better than the Paula Deen version!

I have also tried this and I made a couple of changes.
Used the tomatoe juice, topped with Parmesan and Shredded Cheddar, added Chili Powder, just a hint, and then baked in oven in a baking dish for about 15 minutes, just long enough to melt the cheese.
EXCELLENT!!! WAS A HIT.

AMAZING.  I made this with GROUND TURKEY breast and added some beef bullion during the browning to create a strong beef flavor. My family never had a clue!  At the suggestion of other reviewers, I increased the garlic (can't have too much) and added 1/2 cup cheddar cheese, and used all the juice from the tomatoes.  The flavor was amazing.  Everyone in the family said this recipe is a "major" "Do-Over" for sure!  That's equivalent to 10 stars!

I too grew up with this version of "goulash". This is real comfort food. Brings  back good memories and very warm and satifsfying for this time of year. Using  Vegatable juice instead of the water was the only change i made. Perfect

This was awesome!  fooled around with the ingredients to be suitable for 2 people. Used ground turkey,   Also added green beans, bell peppers, yellow squash, mushrooms and corn.  What a hearty meal.  Going to make a ton more for the freezer for when I have the baby, easy meal for my husband to heat up!

There's so much you can with this recipe as a base.  I use Ro-tel tomatoes, rotini, egg noodles, Italian flavored stewed tomatoes, add 1 diced chipotle pepper to the tomatoes, wagon wheel pasta, drained pinto beans, taco seasoning, pizza flavored with some added pepperoni and the list goes on. Make it a themed meal with a Mexican or Italian twist to the entire meal. Use your imagination and your family will appreciate the variety.

I have made a version of this all my life and so does my Mother. I add a green bell pepper and use only 1 can of stewed tomatoes and 1 can of tomato sauce. It is a delicious, economical and easy meal! I usually serve it with a green salad and garlic bread.
This is how i make my goulash.  But i add a can of campbells tomato soup and some chili powder.  A family staple for over 30 years.
Very quick easy hearty meal! Thanks for sharing!

This is a 'memory meal'...a dish that brings back memories of childhood, hence the popularity.
I really wanted to like this but couldn't...it needed a lot of doctoring. Neither my husband nor I enjoyed it, as is.
The concept is good for stretching the dollar, however.

This is really delicious and easily modified as per your taste. I used twice as much onion and 3 times as much garlic - I love garlic.  Also added a can of Primo pasta sauce.  Very nice basic recipe that can be modified to use up what you have.  Thank you!
I didn't try this certain recipe butt we use to eat something very similar! it was like spaghetti but elbow noodles instead of spaghettie! we added corn which was always my fav the corn

Followed the recipe except we used left over mozzarella and cheddar cheese instead of the parm, I threw in a can of sliced mushrooms when I was cooking the onion and then added basil, thyme and parsley to the whole works. My two year old LOVED it. I like it because its filling and goes a long way. I think next time I will double up on the stewed tomatoes.

A good starting place! I used ground turkey, tiny bow tie pasta, seasoned diced tomato, extra garlic, and some cream cheese for texture. Oh and since I don't do onions well, I used powdered onion I had. It was really good!

We ate something very similar when I was a child too.  I don't like stewed tomatoes, so my mother just used regular tomatoes and lots of onion and garlic.  She always called it goulash; I'm not sure why, but that's what my family and I still call it and my kids love it!!

Quick, easy, and filling . . . just a little bland for our tastes. Will certainly make this again, but going to use more garlic and add some other spices as well next time. Overall though, this was a great meal for a busy night!

My family calls this goulash.  We always dice half a green pepper and cook with the hamburger and onions.  It changes the flavor and just doesn't taste right to me without it.  Our recipe also has you boil the macaroni separately and then add it before serving.  Good comfort food.  And yes, the leftovers are awesome!

I made this on 2/24/11 for the " Comfort Food Event "in the Food Photo Forum.The only thing that was done different to this recipe is,that it was cut in half.Even after 20 minutes of cooking the pasta was still hard and had to add about 4 more ounces of water to get it done.The taste was very bland and not nearly enough seasonings.I'm sorry but this recipe just didn't seem to work for us.But thank you for taking the time to post.:)

This is my "homemade hamburger helper recipe" simple, easy and filling. And great because whatever you have you can toss in, add whatever spices you want too. I've made this exact recipe lots of times. Love it :)

This was great!  I made it as directed except I added an extra clove of garlic, and I didn't have macaroni noodles, so I used rotini noodles.  It worked just fine!  Also I was not sure whether to drain the tomatoes or not, so I didn't, and the tomato juice added some nice flavor!  Next time I think I will add some corn and maybe even some chickpeas for an extra little bit of nutrition.  Thanks for the great recipe! UPDATE: I have made this quite a few times and it is always so good. I made it tonight and for a change I threw in some velveeta (I know it is gross, but it was in my refrigerator and I wanted it out but hated throwing it away).  It tasted really good, like a homemade Hamburger Helper of sorts.
This is always a good recipe.  When I make it, I add chili powder for some extra flavor and spice.  I also use fresh tomatoes instead of canned tomatoes.
Great Stuff !! My mom used to add potato cut into chunks and it makes a world of difference to texture and taste.

I was on vacation and my sister in laws mother had made this (who can't really cook by the way but,she tries). I was kind of afraid to try it but i did and I'm glad I did..I have to say it was better than mine I hated to admit..She sent me the recipe and I made it and it was the BOMB...I always have so much leftover I don,t know what to do with but, not this time.There was nothing leftover.It was great.I wouldn't make it any other way...........
I grew up on this stuff, we called it goulash.  I still make it exactly like this once a while when I have the craving!  I sometimes add mushrooms and peppers, but good on it's own!
Sounds like goulash that I've been making for years, and my mom before me.  I like the taste better if macaroni is cooked and then added.  You can change up the spices to please you.
Yummy and filling. I used Morningstar Meal Starter Crumbles to make it vegetarian and topped it with shredded mozzarella .

Oh yes, I remember this and crave it now and then. I raised my family on it.  My grandmother used to can tomatoes and give me 2 cases of them every summer, which lasted me thru the year. I always added a little Worcestershire sauce and used grated Romano cheese rather than the Parmesan. Gave a little different taste which I loved.

I thought this recipe was really good. It reminded me of the goulash my friends mom used to make all the time. I always loved it. I accidentally got the wrong tomatoes (I got diced) But I got the Italian style. I also added fresh basil, and some fennel seed and a ton more garlic b/c I love it.
I really liked it with the Italian diced tomatoes so when I make it again I will stick with that. Great recipe for a quick meal. Will work great on those baseball nights when I need to feed the kids something good hearty and fast.

Similar to my American Chop Suey. I use tomato sauce instead; add water, and add a little tomato paste at the end to thicken. I always cook chopped green peppers in oil first, when the peppers start to get soft, I add the onions, cook until softened; then add and brown the hamburg; then the tomato sauce and water. Spices are salt, black and white pepper, and garlic salt. And, I ALWAYS cook my pasta separately. Any dish is much too starchy if you cook it in the sauce. I have never tried cheese on top; since I love cheese, I will try it next time.
To one lb. of hamburg, approx. 2/3 small can of tomato sauce; approx. 2 cups of water; about 1/2 to 2/3 small can of tomato paste.
Like others have said, this reminds me of my mom's goulash. This is definitely a memory meal. Thank you for sharing!

great dish love it thanks

ha!  my mom called this GOULASH!  I'm going to try it this week, and thanks so much!!!!

Flashback to my childhood.   My mother was always a little vague when I asked her how to make "goulash", but this recipe has filled in the gaps.  Since we're empty-nesters now and - the real reason -  because I had only one can of stewed tomatoes, I cut all the quantities in half.  Thanks to other reviewers' suggestions, I chopped up the tomatoes with an immersion blender before I added them, used a single-serve can of tomato juice as the cooking liquid, adding enough water to bring the liquid quantity up to the appropriate amount, added a couple of dashes of worcestershire sauce and generous sprinklings of chili powder and Penzey's seasoning mixes (Forward and Pasta Sprinkle).   The concoction cooked, lid on, until the penne I used was close to done, then without a lid to let some of the liquid evaporate.  I put the "goulash" in a flat casserole dish and covered it with half a bag of shredded cheddar that was languishing in the refrigerator.  This is a great basic recipe that permits all kinds of customization, and I appreciate all the reviewers who took the time to make suggestions for seasoning and other additions.

The balance of this soup is incredible.  Everybody loved it!  DS asked what kind of meat was in it, & DH said it was one of the best smelling soups I've ever made.  I used bullion cubes instead and felt it was a little salty, but DH & DS both thought it was perfect.  Also used a nice merlot instead of the sherry as a matter of preference. Finally my Mushroom Soup-Grail Quest is over!  I’ve found the mushroom soup that I have always believed was out there somewhere.  When I learnt that Julesong was in my group for the 2005 Photo Swap #2, I immediately thought ‘Soup Fairy’: I’ll make one of her soups.  And I didn’t even look at any of her other recipes.  Serendipitous indeed!  This is a truly delicious creamy, flavoursome soup.  Creamy yet, as Julesong mentions, it contains no milk or cream, so it is also low in calories and low in the bad-for-you fats.  None of the flavours are detectable over the others: they all blend so well.  The only changes I made to the ingredients was because of the availability of two ingredients.  I used some exquisite-looking field mushrooms, undoubtedly similar to Portabellos.  And chicken stock, because I was out of vegetable stock.  I also used several cloves of garlic, beyond what was specified, because I love the stuff.  The main changes I made were to the amount of stock I used and the length of time I allowed the soup to simmer.  I doubled all the ingredients (which would have meant adding 12 cups of stock) but I decided to add only 8 cups of stock.  I wanted my soup thick and it was - but not too thick.  And those who ate it – and everyone just loved the really hearty flavour – said that the consistency was just right for them too.  The recipe specified 15 minutes simmering time, which to me sounded really odd.  I had the soup simmering for just under two hours.  Quite a difference.  Once I decided it had simmered for long enough, rather than transferring it to a blender in batches, I blended it in the pan with a stab blender.  The result was a beautifully puréed soup with some chunks of mushroom in it.  Just the right balance in texture as well as flavour!  Superb.  My quest now over, I shall be making this again.  And because it is so quick and easy to make, that will be often.  As for the smells: I’ve never made anything that smelt so heavenly the whole time it was cooking!  Thank you Soup Fairy, for a truly SOUPERB recipe.
