Thanks Marsha D. 

Bullwinkle.
Really wonderful comfort food...very yummy & enjoyed by all the family.  Thanks Marsha D

FANTASTIC!!! It's fork tender, melt in your mouth, and can't get enough type of steak and gravy. I used two cans of mushroom soup with roasted garlic flavor, one full cup of whipping cream, and 1/2 cup of water. Simmered for 45 minutes covered half way. It was so delicious I had a hard time not going back for seconds. I served it with your cream potatoes recipe#110416 for a winning combination. Thank you Marsha for my wonderful dinner!

Wow.. i must say this was my 1st time fixing these ever... (and yes I'm a beginner cook and these were great!! I'm so proud of my self, the only change I made was i added an onion and bell peper when frying the cube steaks.   Thanks so much.

Made this for supper last night - very good and very easy, even for a weeknight meal.  The mushroom gravy is delicious, especially with the seasonings & brown bits scraped up from the bottom of the pan.  DH doesn't like gravy (too bad!), but I saved every last drop of it that was left - not sure what I'll use it with, but I sure didn't want to waste it!!  Thanks for a great recipe.  -M :)
My Mom made this dish for us when we were little, now I am a grandma and I make this for company and the kids, always a hit.
Had some cube steak in freezer I needed to use up...thought this recipe sounded easy and I had everything I needed...great recipe..easy and the gravy was great...

This was scrumptious and very easy! I used evaporated milk instead of cream, and I didn't have any onion powder on hand. The cooking time was perfect, and this came out tender and flavorful. I served it with mashed potatoes and carrots. Thanks! I'll be making this one again!
Easy and tastes good--can't ask for more than that!

I had some veal cube steaks and couldn't find a recipe for them..This sounded like it would work for veal, and it did.  I deglazed the pan with white wine, and used half sour cream and half heavy cream.  No water.  Popped in the oven at 300 instead of simmering on stove.  Served with poppyseed noodles and a veggie.  Delish!!  Thanks.

I made this last night for dinner, and everyone, including my picky teenage son, really loved it. It was relatively simple, used ingredients I had on hand, and got rave reviews from the family. I call that a success!
Although my cube steaks turned out a bit on the dry side (I think now the 15 min on both sides was too much) this was good and I will make it again.  Served on egg noodles.  Thanks Marsha.
Great recipe. Even my pickest eater loved this recipe. We will make this one again!

outstanding! I used this on cubed deer meat with great results. I also added 1/4 cup Merlot wine to the sauce before adding the cream. Very easy to make. I made this again tonight (beef) this time using a Shiraz-Grenache red from Rosemount. It's not quite as strong as a Merlot but still gave great flavor to the gravy.
Yum! I used pork cubed steak and it was wonderful. Prepared exactly as written. Served with elbow macaroni. Delicious!!

This recipe was easy and good. I added onion,and a package of mushroom gravy to the soup. I used Campbells beefy mushroom soup. By the way, I never skimp on soup for my casseroles and dishes. Campbells is always the best and it is sooo creamy. This dish would have been so much better had I had some good beef. Buying good meat in a market is like buying a pig in a poke. After all the simmering....it was tuff. Not my fault nor the recipes!  My son said..."the flavor was great". I will make this again, and hopefully get a better cut of meat or a better market!  lol. Thank you Marsha D.

I think that one of the best compliments of a dish is how dirty the recipe card it, and my copy is filthy!!!!  The kids and I  LOVE this recipe and make it often.  It's true comfort food.  Thanks Marsha, but the family thinks it's my own creation!!!
VERY GOOD!  I enjoyed this way more than my son.  It is a true comfort food!
Just enjoyed a fabulous dinner featuring your recipe. Only fixed two steaks, so cut the 'browning time' in half. Used heavy cream, but the gravy was not 'heavy'. Thanks for sharing.
A big hit for this Texas family.  My son loves this!!  Made with mashed potatoes and green beans.  Can you get any more hearty than that???

I Loved this recipe. Although I did tweak it a little . As i read from othe reviewers I added a second can of cream of mushroom soup and i used 1 1/2 c of milk. i also added portabella mushroom and one chopped shallot.It was really GOOD!!

Used chicken instead of beef...and since there was really no meat drippings with the chicken, I added about a tablespoon of garlic butter to the mushroom soup/milk.

Baked in the oven rather than simmer on the stovetop (mainly for space reasons) in a cassarole dish on 325...(I was baking a cake too) turned out amazing...DH really like it....it has made his top 5 fave list!

This is the best cube steak recipe I have ever tried!  They have a wonderful flavor and are tender!  I did not use the cup of water, I used 1 cup of milk instead.  I also added some Lipton's Beefy Onion Soup Mix.  It was absolutely fabulous!!

I doubled this recipe, used a packet of onion soup mix, placed fried cube steak in a 13x9 casserole dish, poured the hot gravy over it and baked for 30 minutes...served with fried onion mashed potatoes...yummy and I received compliments throughout the meal...thx 4 sharing :)

I have made this recipe several times and it is always wonderful.  The only thing I do differently is tear up the cube steak in chunks before I season and cook them.  I like doing this and then putting over mashed potatoes with the gravy, you get a bite of meat with potatoes and gravy.  I am going to fix them tonight.  Thanks for a great recipe!
Excellent recipe! The gravy was really delicious...as good as, MAYBE even better than my mom's! Definately easier to make for sure.

I have tried many recipes similar to this ...This one takes the prize..I didn't have any onion powder so I addd some minced onion...I also add a packet of french onion soup mix in with the mushroom soup. Awesome.
Delicious and easy.  I used reduced fat mushroom soup, and it still turned out great!

Good basic recipe. Was looking for something that didn't require a lot of gravy mixes (usually way to high in sodium) for our family. I made a few changes. I used a combination of light flavored olive oil and butter, cause I have found butter by itself tends to burn easily. Instead of onion and garlic powder I used the real thing, sauteing sliced onion till lightly golden, then adding 5 cloves of minced garlic toward the end (it cooks faster) . I omitted the salt, because I used Progresso beef broth instead of water and its got plenty of salt. I sauteed 8 oz. of baby bella mushrooms in with the onion and garlic) so I could omit the can of mushroom soup. I then added milk and cream, using a 2 to 1 ratio. Put in on simmer for 30 minutes, then served with mash potatoes and glazed carrots. It was a big hit. Thanks again.

Marsha - this is a fabulous recipe.  I love how quick and easy it is finished but how tender the beef cube steak becomes after cooking.  My family enjoyed every bite.  Served with mashed potatoes too so I could use some of the extra gravy!  My hubby is going to make a sandwich with the one remaining piece of steak tomorrow.  This is definitely a keeper for our family!
This was very good.  The cube steak was tender and the gravy was so good poured over everything.
I was amazed how tender the cube steaks were. Usually they are dull and tough. Tasty! My "picky" son ate 3 pieces! Great family dish.

My husband and father-in-law loved this.  As most other reviewers mentioned, this is very tender.  I reversed the milk and water amounts (1 c. milk, 1/2 c. water), but next time I will follow the recipe.
This is fantastic.  The cube steaks were tender and full of flavor.  The gravy was terrific.  Served it over white rice and didn't have any leftovers!

I made this with 6 cube steaks. I had trouble with the breading sticking (mostly on the second batch to fry) and the steaks ended up a bit tough because the pan was overcrowded. Also, the gravy wasn't enough for that many steaks and rice. It was flavorful and the family enjoyed it, so I would probably make it again with only 4 smaller cube steaks.
I only make cube steak for my husband,,the way this recipe has you prepare the steaks tenderizes the steaks,,they were delicious and now I eat them too,,I added some grill seasoning to the mix!!!

I wanted something different and this was a hit. Im just learning to cook really and this was so easy for me and the steak was perfect! Actually this is the best my cube steak has ever came out when it comes to frying....VERY SATISFIED

Very good, but you may need to modify. I made this for 2 adults and 3 children and needed to make more flour mixture even though I was only using 5 steaks. When making the gravy I substituted the cream of mushroom with cream of chicken. I also doubled the gravy recipe so that there would be enough for the entire family. I served it over rice and everyone enjoyed it!
Very good, cheap, and easy!  I used fat free cream of mushroom and skim milk because that was what I had and it still turned out great!

I was hesitant to make this recipe because I typically don't like tinned soups as sauces....but.....I'm so glad I tried it! It was delicious and the soup actually imparts a lovely flavour. The meat was tender. The only change I made was to add fresh mushrooms to the sauce. I used skim milk because that's what I had and the consistency was not affected negatively at all.
I served it with mashed potatoes and broccoli....the sauce was lovely over the potatoes. My children have already asked me when I will be making again.
Thanks for sharing, Marsha!

I found that I had way too much flour leftover(1/2C)  after dredging the meat and yet the recipe didn't say to add the extra in anywhere.  I ended up adding 2 Tbsp to the pan drippings and made a roux, then continued on with the recipe.  The other reviews don't mention too much flour so I'm not sure what happened there.  The flavour was good but the meat turned out a bit on the dry side.  I may try this again and perhaps reduce the browning time. I am glad I tried the recipe, thanks for posting.

This recipe is a keeper for my family!  My only change was to sprinkle a bit more garlic powder and pepper for our tastes as the sauce simmered.  For the reviewer who said the meat came out tough, I had to lessen my browning time since my steaks were extremely thin.  I only browned them until they no longer stuck to the pan on each side, which turned out to be under 2 mins a side.
Awsum     This is the best cube steak I have ever had

Made this last night just like many others!! I absolutely love this quick and easy dish, especially after a long day at work. Browning the steaks first makes a huge diff in the tenderness, and don't opt out on the drippings!! That's where all the flavor lives!
Made this last night for dinner... AND IT WAS GREAT!! super easy to do, and not to many items to buy!!! even my picky honey enjoyed it!! thanks for sharing!!

OMG this recipe is to die for!!  My husband and I absolutely loved this. And the gravy....scrumptious! My husband said "Make sure you don't lose this recipe. That is the best gravy you've ever made". The cube steak came out tender enough to cut with a fork and that has never happened for me unless I cooked it in the crockpot or baked it in the oven.Definitely 5 stars!
Simple and delicious, and the kids love it.  This recipe works well with pork tenderloin too.
Great recipe.  I used 1/2 C. beef broth instead of milk and I used Beefy Mushroom Soup.  It was a great supper.  I also made mashed potatoes so that none of the gravy went to waste.  :-)

I followed these instructions but decided tor buy the family size cream of mushroom soup and double the water and heavy whipping cream, then put it in the crock pot. I didn't add any grease or drippings from the pan as the meat had enough grease on it to mix perfectly with the soup. I also only browned the outside of the meat so the crock pot could finish the cooking, did the first two hours on high and last three on low and it was perfect. Was alot better than making brown gravy. Also added sliced mushrooms

Absolutely loved this meal. I made a couple of adjustments to recipe to lower calories from 500 to 468 per serving. And that is I used whole wheat flour instead of all purpose flour. Also used sea salt, unsalted butter, and cream of celery instead of cream of mushroom. I truly knew this meal was a success when the pickiest eater in my (my 3y/o) house wanted more.

My husband and I love this recipe as-is. It is absolutely delicious and simple to make. I've already made it twice. I pair it with greens (kale or spinach) sautéed in olive oil and fresh garlic and add a baked potato or sweet potato on the side.

This has definitely become one of our favorite quick meals. It always comes out perfect. I actually about double the number of cube steaks in the recipe. The only changes I make are: I bread and fry 6-8 steaks, 3 or 4 at a time, removing them to a plate when cooked. After cooking one side of the last 3-4 steaks, I turn them to fry the other side and add one chopped onion stir-frying them until tender. I remove the steaks and then also add one can of mushroom pieces and stems into the soup mixture. Stacking the steaks on top of each other in the last cooking time is fine, as every 10 minutes I turn them so that the top ones are now on bottom and finish cooking. Plenty of leftovers that are awesome, plenty of gravy for mashed potatoes or over rice. As a husband who does most of the cooking here because I'm also self employed working from home, this is a go to favorite now for all of us and quite easy for me to prepare. So much so, that I can't believe I've actually signed up here just to be able to review this recipe. Will be searching here for many more good recipes. This one is a keeper!
all i can say is WOW!!!! Simple, tasty and delicious....my husband is loving this after a long work day.
I like to add a pinch or two of Cajun seasoning to the sauce, otherwise it can be a bit bland.

This is an easy recipe and quite tasty. Good mix of flavours, nice and citrusy! I used half shrimp and half scallops (because that's what I had on hand) and tossed with a spagettini pasta. I did find it a little on the salty side, but that is strictly a personal preference. Good recipe! I will make this again.
Takes just minutes and is very tasty.  My family loved it.  I served it with risotto and broccoli.
Very good - a tad spicy.
This was so quick and easy to make.  The only change I made to the recipe was that I used 1/4 tsp. Habernaro pepper instead of Cayenne pepper.  Thanks for a great recipe
I made this recently and loved it!  I did add a little more garlic, and served with angel hair pasta.  Nice, easy meal with loads of flavor!  Thanks ms_B! :)

I made your seasoning and dumped it on the peeled and deviened shrimp early in the day and just left them in the bag in the fridge till I was ready.  I then grilled them on a well oiled grill for less than 10 minutes.  FANTASTIC!!
I didn't have a lime so I used a fresh lemon instead---The taste was awsome.  I tossed my flavorful shrimp with whole wheat angel hair pasta.

Yum!!! I used baby shrimp and decreased the salt to 1/2 tsp., and otherwise followed the recipe. It came together really quickly & has a light, spicy flavor. I put the shrimp atop some angel hair alfredo -- DH raved & raved :) Thanks!
Wow! What a great shrimp recipe!  Dh has already requested it again (which is rare!) So good and easy to make.  I love the flavor of all the seasonings.  Thanks so much for sharing!

All I can say is outstanding! I made this recipe this weekend and absolutely loved the different combination of flavors. I served with buttered noodles, garlic bread and green salad. Absolutely suburb! Thanks for a great recipe!

Simply wondreful. I did change this up a bit, I put all the dry ingredients in with the shrimp and a bit of olive oil, and let them sit for most of the day.  Other than that I followed the recipe exactly. Wonderful combination of flavors. I will most definately make this one again.

This was great, I used olive oil in place of the butter, added everything but the lime and let it marinate.  I added the lime 1/2 hour before skewering and cooking on the grill.  Nice little kick with the cayenne, a little less salt is needed if cooking this way.  An easy summer meal that did not heat up the house.

This was very tasty. I did cut back on the cayenne by half, as our daughter and I don't handle spicy heat very well. My husband on the other hand liked it alot. Served with pasta and Alfredo sauce as suggested. Nice combonation. :)
Oh my! This is an instant favourite, I absolutely loved the taste. I added a bit more cayanne, otherwise followed the instructions to the tee. Full five stars, will make this again for sure!
This was really good. I did not have lime or lemon so I just ommited it all together. Still turned out great. Thanks.

A top recipe! Wonderful flavors and very easy to make. I did not change a thing and will not when I make it again. I already plan to serve this again next week. I served it as an apetizer. Thanks for posting!!!!

This is an EXCELLENT recipe! It has just the right amount of spice and heat. I used lemon, only because I was out of limes, and some extra paprika when cooking, to make the color pop. (oh, and I upped the garlic, doubled it, actually). DH said it was outstanding, and felt obligated to make sure there were no leftovers. Thanks ms bold, this will be our new go-to shrimp dish!
Really easy to make and very nice flavour although mine came out a little too salty for my taste. I think i may reduce it by 1/4 tsp. Thanks for this!
These were a huge hit for our Memorial Day celebration.  I skewered the shrimp, seasoned, and grilled.  They were gone in five minutes.

These are the best shrimp I have ever made! My entire family agreed! My 6 year old son cried because he thought he couldn't have seconds! Good thing I made a double recipe! My hubby and I are on South Beach, and these fit perfectly into this lifestyle!  My only substitution was dried cilantro for the parsley and thyme, and Smart Balance light in place of real butter. I only used 1 lime, but it still gave plenty of juice. I sauted the shrimp until all of the juices cooked in rather than pouring the sauce over anything. I guess for South Beach the lime juice would make it be a phase 2 and 3 dish. Next time I will make 4 pounds of shrimp!  With such low calories, and the fat lower without real butter, a huge serving would still be good for you! Thanks so much for posting!
Delicious!  So easy and tasty.  We had it tonight with some buttered egg noodles.  The spice combination with the lime is perfect.  Thank you for posting!

I haven't had these at Chili's but my husband said that "these are the best shrimp he's ever had." 
Thank You for such a wonderful recipe.
Excellent, spicy and so easy!

I have never been to Chili's but this recipe is awesome. My family made me promise to make them again- not that I needed any convincing!! I used frozen shrimp, and 4 key limes instead of 1 lime. The flavor is amazing and not too spicy. Thanks ms.bold for a fantastic recipe that we will enjoy over and over again.

We really enjoyed this recipe!  I used a pound of large shrimp and about 6 tbsps. of fresh lime juice.  The seasoning was spot on.  I served over rice.  This is going to become one of our favorites!  Thanks for posting a keeper!

Yum! I made this and originally planned to use a box of Zatarain's French Market Vegetables and Rice mix for a side. Then I remembered my boyfriend LOVES Cajun food. I put the shrimp and juice in with the boxed rice and the combination was amazing! I don't love Cajun food, but apparently the flavor of this shrimp and the Zatarains hit the nail on the head.

Very good!  The shrimp had lots and lots of flavor!  I used frozen cooked shrimp and they turned out great!  I just let them thaw before cooking and only cooked them long enough to heat through.  And instead of using cayenne I used chili powder to cut the heat back a little for my mom.  I will be making these again really soon!
Great recipe! I used fresh parsley and sprinkled grated parm cheese on top.
This was awesome!  Thank you so much for sharing! I put it over some whole wheat pasta without alfredo sauce.  This also would be great on a salad. :)
I used this recipe as a rub. Grilled on skewers. Very good. Enjoyed the leftovers on a lunch salad. Yum!

Oh yes, this is the one! We loved it.
With the exception of substituting chipotle for the cayenne, I made the recipe (doubled) as written, and I will continue to do so. The first night I served the shrimp with pasta and alfredo, and the leftovers were used the next day in a shrimp and pasta salad...even the ones I sneaked out of the bowl cold were outstanding on their own.
This recipe will go in my "best of the best" cookbook.   Thanks for submitting.
I didn't really care for this too much, neither did the rest of the family. It was ok, but definitely not as good as other shrimp dishes I've made. I think I will stick to some of my other recipes.
made this for myself and enjoyed the whole thing. thanks for sharing!
Great dish!  I served it over rice with vegetables, and it was great.  Be careful, though - it is very flavorful and it's easy to make it too strong!

We made these for dinner tonight.  It was very tasty.  I left out the paprika and it still had some spice to it.  Have a 5 y/o who loves shrimp and it was too much for him.  Maybe I'll try leaving out the cayenne and keeping the paprika next time.  Very good recipe though.  Thanks.

There's a HUGE mistake here.  This amount is only enough for half a person!!!   OMG, this is wonderful.  I cut the recipe in half, thinking that 12 shrimp and a huge fruit salad would be enough.  No, no, no, I want more, you hear, I want more.

I followed the recipe exactly as posted, EXCEPT I think I probably doubled the garlic (I'm a garlic lover).  I also accidentally dumped too much thyme in the bowl.  No problem.

Thanks, Ms. Bold, for my new weekly "get healthy" dish.  This was simple, delicious, and I just can't rave enough.

This is an excellent recipe.  I served it as an appetizer for friends the other night - it outshown my enhiladas so it really is good.  I doubled the spice quantities because I like them to  really have a kick.  My guests loved them - not one was left. TRY IT
Really good 20 minute meal!

Fast, easy and fantastic!  What more do you want from a recipe? i used butter cooking spray rather than butter and it was still fabulous. I have made many shrimp recipes with variations on lime/chili/garlic ingredients but I can stop looking because this one is hands down my favorite.
amazing

I used half the shrimp, 1 tablespoon of margarine instead of butter, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and the regular amounts of the other ingredients. It was sooo spicy and flavorful. Delicious dish! It is on its way to being a family favorite!
This has a nice kick to it. I used small shrimp and added it to an Alfredo sauce over cheese tortellini.  Delish! Zero left-overs. DH approved.

Great, bold flavor here. The title is correct..it is spicy! (It was a tad bit too spicy for our family, so when I make it again I'll just had 1/8 t. of the cayenne pepper.)  This is a quick, easy and flavorful recipe. Thanks!!
Very easy to make & the flavor is great. I made for a family gathering & everyone loved them :) I used precooked medium size shrimp and had angel hair pasts. Would make again :)
Wonderful.  Very easy to make and very tasty.  I let the shrimp sit in the seasonings for about an hour.  It cooked up really quick so make sure your sides are ready.

This is fabulous!  I made it according to the recipe, but added more garlic.  I served it with whole wheat pasta and a tiny bit of alfredo sauce.  I tossed the pasta with the shrimp after cooking, which gave the pasta a nice flavor.  This is great - thanks ms_bold!

yummy! for the first time, i made a recipe exactly how it was written...i was impressed! i only added a few drops of Tapatio hot sauce to add heat. and like another reviewer i used 4 key limes as that was all i had on hand. I served over white rice and added the juices to the rice. AWESOME

This is my new favorite way to make shrimp! I doubled the recipe, using two pounds of jumbo shrimp and my boyfriend and I ate every bite. I used key lime juice and probably added a little more than was called for, but the sauce it made was absolutely delicious. I served it with a quick box of dirty rice, and found myself wishing I had made something with less seasoning so I could serve the shrimp sauce over it. I was making shrimp to use up the rest of my homemade cocktail sauce, and these were so flavorful that we didn't touch it. They were really spicy, so if you're making them for kids, I'd cut back a bit on the cayenne pepper, but we loved it exactly as written.
Very good! I used olive oil instead of butter and put it over wheat angel-hair.  A quick, tasty meal!

Can't say enough how wonderful this was!  I served it over linguine with butter sauce and I have to admit there wasn't nearly enough shrimp - next time I will double the recipe!!  Wonderful recipe, simple to make, and the perfect level of spiceness!

Super yummy recipe that only took me 10 minutes to prepare including peeling the shrimp.  I minced the garlic and brown it in the butter a little before throwing the shrimp in.  I also served with linguine tossed in butter sauce.  Friends loved it, definitely a keeper.  Thanks Ms. Bold for sharing.

So incredibly good that I couldn't stop eating them; therefore, it really only serves 2 at the maximum! Very nicely spiced and so super easy it is going into the quick dinner rotation. I served with a harvest grain mix and a jicama slaw, but I think next time I'll do the linguine thing.

Really quick and easy to prepare.  My shrimp weren't defrosted all the way before I threw them in the pot.  The water left the mixture a little runny, but we tossed the spicy sauce over spaghetti.  Yum!  My husband loved it and asked to throw this in the rotation more often.

LOL, I was just watching TV and the Chili's commercial came on for these.  (Keep in mind that I made these for dinner about 30 minutes ago.)  I thought, "Lime? What lime?"  At that point, I realized, I FORGOT the lime. Oh and they were still so wonderful!!! I made about 16 shrimp and boyfriend got stuck at work, so his are keeping warm in a bowl right now.   I swear if he doesn't come home soon, I'm going to eat them!  One person could easily eat ALOT of these!  Thanks for posting, I'll be sure to make them right next time ; )  WITH LIME!

I haven't had these at Chili's either, but I'll sure be having them at home again! Really good. I tossed the spices with the shimp in a large bowl and let sit while I heated about a teaspoon of olive oil instead of butter. I added a tiny bit of chipotle powder, will add more next time. I served with yellow rice and wish I had thought to sprinkle a bit of cilantro on top, but I will next time. I may skewer and gril these as well. Thanks for a keeper!

Great recipe!  The seasoning was great!  I marinated my shrimp in the spices (I omitted the salt) with about 1.5 tablespoons of oil.  Then I stir-fried the shrimp without using any extra butter or oil.
I used this recipe and it was delicious! Modified it a bit by marinating shrimp in a bit of tequila, salt, and pepper. Don't add lime until very end of cooking.
I have never had this dish at Chiles so I have nothing to compare it to-- none the less I made it last night and it was SO very good. Highly reccomended dish for an easy, tasty meal.
I had this the other night for dinner and it was really good. I whipped it up with some pasta. The flavor was wonderful!!!! GREAT Recipe!!!
Great shrimp recipe.  My DS tried these and said that they were the best.  Thanks for posting this recipe.
We loved it!

Spicy indeed!  I was warned, so I'm not complaining.  My husband liked them and didn't mind the heat at all, but this was too hot for me to finish.  I loved the mix of flavors for the 3/4 serving I finished off before the heat got the better of me though.  I used some cubed chicken I wanted to use up along with the shrimp.  Went well with the chicken.  Will definitely make this again-- with about half the cayanne for the sake of my whimpy tastebuds!
We really loved this recipe.  So easy and very tasty.  Served with rice and steamed veggies.  I thought the heat was perfect.
wow ...this is so eazy .. so tasty ... plus the paprika gives it a nice colour  ...exactly what i was looking for

Oh my oh my!  SUPER good!!!  We LOVED it!!  When I started prepping this dish it sounded so bland...but this dish was FAR from bland!  I increased the garlic and eyeballed most of the remaining ingredients.  Served this alongside Recipe #131909 and recipe #132765 and we very healthily feasted tonight!  DEELISH!  Will absolutely make this one again!  Super easy too!  Give this one a try!
Super tasty!! My 2 yr old was all about this shrimp; she loved the spice! Thank you for sharing!

Absolutely wonderful! I shared this with my hesitant 5 year old. Wasn't sure she would want more after the first try because of the spicyness, but she kept pushing her bowl at me for more until it was all gone. And we made the full recipe just for the 2 of us. So that will tell you how good this is.
I only wish that I did have some pasta because the remaining sauce on my plate would have been fantastic drizzled over the top.
We fix these regularly at our house. They're outstanding. I've never had Chili's, but can't imagine they'd be any better than this!
Simply amazing! I can't wait to take them to our Christmas functions :)
Delish and easy!
Easy, fast and yummy.  Readily available ingredients.  Love it.  The kids liked it, high praises considering they do not like shrimp.  Thank you.

never one to actually measure portions, found this one worlks well when you stick to recipe. Had all the dry ingredients and have a lime tree so win/win. Tasted great - sserved with a fresh garden salad for a low fat/great tasting meal. As for the prawns, 400g peeled was still barely enough for two because they are so moorish.

For a simple dish filled with restaurant-quality flavors, make this dish. It was easy, quick, and delicious. Slightly over-salted, but that could have been me eye-balling the ingredients. Thank you for the recipe!!

Fantastic & wonderful recipe!! I am often disappointed with my shrimp dishes but last night I made this and I am now a shrimp superwoman!!!
I followed the recipe exactly and the lime is the ticket to this one... take it from me, don't change a thing!! 
Thanks ms_bold!!
i had some shrimp to use up, but since i generally don't like shrimp, this turned out amazing.  i would make it again if i had the shrimp around

My husband made this with 2 lbs of shrimp and added cilantro, a sprig of parsley (chopped), 4 cloves garlic, adobo, 1/4 cup butter and 2 tbs olive oil, and added chopped up avocado on the side.  Super delicious - thanks for a great recipe!!!
The whole family loved this meal!  I served the shrimp over pasta alfredo with a side of roasted asparagus #12192.  Absolutely delicious!!!

proof that super low cal can be way flavorful with the right spices. Was out of parsley and onion powder so used 2 T of chopped onion, couldn't tell the difference. Served w/Zatarains long and wild rice. Love the idea of making w/an alfredo, will try that next time! Thanks!
This shrimp is wonderful.  I've made it several times and I don't think it taste like Chili's Spicy Garlic & Lime Shrimp it is delicious.
This was flavorful and absolutely delicious! I will definitely make this again but next time I will try it on the grill.

Wow. I did NOT enjoy these shrimp AT ALL!  I am SO disappointed!  I doubled the recipe thinking I would LOVE the shrimp (based on the great reviews), but the spices were VERY overwhelming.  There was also WAY to much heat for my tastes! Yikes!  I will NOT be making these again!
Love this!!  I'm making it tonight AGAIN at the request of the kids.  Thanks for sharing a really great recipe that is quick, easy, and healthy!!
This was good, I did use a steak grilling seasoning for a short cut...we liked it!

i don't think there are enough stars! i ate my shrimp with bread, how could i possibly let all that good sauce go to waste?! it's a great on-the-go meal. next time ill be making this for the whole family and will try overnighting the shrimp in the seasoning. thanks for sharing such a great and simple recipe!
Delicious and easy to make.

Quick, easy, flavor-laden shrimp.
I served them with a cheese quesadilla.   I will make this one often.

Excellent, easy, and scrumptious! I had some parsley and garlic pasta that I hadn't used and tossed it with the shrimp. Out of this world. I added extra red pepper flakes to my dish because I like my mouth to be on fire during a meal... absolutely awesome and will make again.
I recommend increasing the seasoning : shrimp ration and using an extra half of lime

Great recipe!  I have made this several times now and we love it!  I increase the spices by 50% or so, as I like to mix in some cooked spaghetti noodles and fry them up with the shrimp after it is all cooked, then add about a TBSP butter...the noodles end up with a great yummy taste!
Delicious!
The whole family loved it! 3 year old too :)
I added 1/8 tsp sugar, a pinch of salt to the shrimp before putting in the pan. I didn't add the cayenne pepper and I added 2 more cloves of garlic. I mixed it with orzo and it was wonderful!
This was a good recipe, but next time I will add a little crushed red pepper flakes for a little extra kick.

Incredible!!! Like others I only had key limes but it turned out fantastic!! Tossed in some low-carb spaghetti noodles and steamed broccoli and it was a wonderful meal!! Will DEFINITELY be making this again and again!! Thanks for posting!

They were good, but not as great as I expected them to be. After trying them, I added some cornstarch to turn the sauce into a glaze and that helped somewhat. I didn't like them enough to make them again, but I'm glad I tried them. Thanks for sharing the recipe

very tasty!  I added sea scallops to the shrimp, used a bit more garlic than called for, and I took AmandaMcG's suggestion of adding cornstarch, serving over rice, and it was excellent.  very flavorful and easy to make. Thanks!

This was crazy good!  I added a lb of asparagus, 1 more tablespoon of butter, and 1 more clove of garlic.  

Very nice...thanks for sharing.
Outstanding.  Didn't change a thing.  Served with rice pilaf and roasted zucchini. Thanks for a great recipe!

YUM! I love shrimp any way I can get it! My husband prefers shrimp cold but thoroughly enjoyed this recipe. We found the seasonings to be perfect and not too spicy. Love the addition of the lime juice. Next time I will add a titch more cayenne pepper. I did omit the parsley flakes because I don't stock that herb. I served with (leftover) basmati rice. It was delicious with the buttery sauce! A quick and easy dinner! Thanks for posting Ms_Bold. It's a keeper!
SUPER GOOD! :)  Made it exactly as stated.  Next time I will add a smidget less on the heat. Thank you for the Great Recipe!

I thought this was a little salty. Also I increased the garlic to 2 cloves corsely chopped. And I had smaller limes that might be why I needed to squeeze a second one over the shrimp after wards. Other than that they were nice, I didn't detect much heat- but then again I like heat a lot. Thanks so much

LOVED it - great recipe!  I doubled the garlic (we love it) and did not press it - just chopped and added some fresh cilantro.  Also reduced salt a bit to be on the safe side per some other comments. Was perfect. Served it with lemon-pepper pasta.  Husband loved it - quick meal.  Will DEFINITELY make it again. Might become my go-to-recipe!
Really nice recipe. I added a quarter teaspoon of shrimp paste to the mix and this improved it, well I felt. Only problem was the saltiness. Next won't add any and it will be a 5. Thanks for posting.
Excellent entree and a great change!
yummy

I doubled this recipe thinking that there would be left overs for lunch.  Wrong!  We ate every bite, my husband licked his plate (literally) and I licked the pan.  Amazing and super easy.  I would love to try some fresh parsley next time but it's great even with dried.  Lime, butter & shrimp are a great combo.

Excellent shrimp.  I doubled the garlic, upped some of the other spices and herbs and used lemon instead of lime.  I also used just a little more butter.  I also used fresh parsley and added it right at the end, which preserves the flavor of the herb better.  Will make again, thanks!

Adding the lime juice to the shrimp too early produced a shrimp that was more like steamed.  I would prefer to saute the shrimp first to brown them and then add the squeeze of lime at the end.  Also adding the juice at that time washed the spices off the shrimp. I would not make this again.  Sorry.
This had good flavor but was much too salty for us, even when I added some cooked diced chicken to the mix.  Next time we'll leave out the salt and use olive oil instead of butter.
I liked this but my husband thought it was too salty.  I will make again and not add as much salt.
Really good!  Made as written and I wouldn't change anything.  Thank you!
Amazing! I didn't really find it spicy, but it was absolutely delicious.

My boyfriend made this for me last night. He used 2 pounds of shrimp, weighed at the store with the shells and tails on. He doubled everything in the recipe except the salt which he measured as stated in the recipe. We agreed that any more salt would have been too salty, and he likes his salt. Our garlic cloves were quite big. When we make this again (it's a keeper) if the garlic cloves are small, we'll use more because we liked it nice & garlicky. We added the lime almost at the end of cooking, and we squeezed more lime at the table. I don't know how this could be 4 servings. The two of us ate almost all of  the doubled recipe for dinner, but we didn't bother with any side dishes, unless wine counts as a side dish. :)   We loved it. Next time we'll probably use some fresh parsley and for sure have some good bread because the butter and spices make it nice & saucy. .

These are so delicious.  I served the last night to my family with some rice pilaf and cauliflower.  Very good.  We thought the spices were just perfect, wouldn't change a thing.  Thank you for sharing this with us it is a family favorite.
Very good. Next time i will use half the salt. Salt lover, but still way too salty

Excellent! I made this for 1 person, and cut the recipe in half. Only changes I made was using 1/4 teaspoon of salt & adding the lime juice in the last 2 minutes of cooking. Not to leave all that tasty butter sauce in the pan, I tossed in some capellini pasta. YUM!

Really good shrimp, super quick! I planned to serve this on pasta so increased the butter to 4TBL , and used 5 medium cloves of garlic with 3/4 of a lb of shrimp. For the seasoning I only used a 1/8 of a tsp- my pasta water was well salted, but even without that I never would use this much salt. I subbed red pepper flakes for the cayenne and fresh parsley instead of dried. We really liked the seasoning - it had a nice zing without being too spicy and the lime was a great finishing touch. I don't like tough shrimp so rather then worring about browning I cook it at a much lower temp to try and get it to absorb the flavors, and pull it out off the pan when it's just barely done since it will continue to cook. This make for tender flavorful shrimp.   The whole thing was perfect with pasta we added a sprinkle of fresh parm - perfect! Made for Photographing National Garlic Month
Awesome! I made it as written and it was amazing. Even my 7 year old son ate it and LOVED it.
Followed the recipe exactly but squeezed the lime towards the end of cooking as a reviewer suggested.
Excelent fast and easy to make recipe.  Less salt should be better!

I've never had Chili's shrimp so I can't compare.  This is amazing.  The only change I made based on other reviews was to use less salt.  I used 1/4 t, otherwise I didn't change a thing.  Served with corn tortillas, diced cabbage and homemade salsa.  I'm typing the review before I've even finished the first taco.

awesome recipe .. i cut back on salt b/c im not a huge salt person and used dried minced onions and garlic b/c that's the way i prefer ... instead of tossing spice blend in skillet, i put it in a baggie with all the shrimp and tossed it together that way ... worked really nice!

I made this per the recipe and it was excellent! I did not think it was too salty at all. There were so many other flavors dancing in my mouth I didn't even notice the salt by itself. Of course it could also be that I didn't put in as much as the recipe called for. When making very simple recipes such as this one I don't use measuring spoons or cups. I've been cooking since I was a girl so I can "eyeball" things pretty good. Would NEVER do that when I was baking though...
I did love the kick the cayanne gave it but if your not a spicy foods person I'd back off on this just a little.

Delicious. Easy, simple. I made this with much less salt like the others suggested, and made it with penne pasta using the drippings as the pasta sauce, added the lime juice last, and put more lime juice and parmesan reggiano cheese on the pasta, and it was spectacular! I wish I had made alot more shrimp.
Some of the best tasting shrimp I have ever had, but there's definitely too much salt. I won't go over 1/4 teaspoon next time. Thank you.
Very easy to make! I also cut back to 1/4 salt after reading the reviews and it was just right. Thanks!
Absolutely loved it!  Made it with a third the salt and was perfect.  Used Hungarian hot paprika and just about melted our tast buds. Regular paprika next time........
Better than a restaurants! Simply great!

This was pretty good! I took other reviewers advice and cut the salt to 1/4 tsp and it was perfect. Not too salty at all. I wish there was a way to marinate this to get the flavors to permeate a little more. Hmmm.........

Oh my, this is so delicious!  I love shrimp but I usually just wind up frying it or boiling it and I wanted to make something a little more adventurous for once so I chose this recipe.  I took the advice of many others and lowered the salt to 1/4 teaspoon.  I subbed in red pepper flakes for the cayenne and left out the thyme since I didn't have any.  Even with these changes these shrimp were superb; be sure to make bread or noodles to go with this too!

These were yummy! I just cut back on the salt, maybe even to 1/2 (could still do bit  less), and that seemed great!. Put them on a tangy caesar salad, and would be happy to do that again! Thx for sharing!
AMAZING! Tasty and very simple to make! I added some bell peppers & NoOodles (no carb-calorie-fat-gluten noodles) and this recipe was great! My husband loved it and is already asked for it again!
This was really tasty.  After reading some of the reviews, I used 1/3 of the amount of salt and olive oil instead of butter.  We served it with brown rice and veggies and it was a nice light meal.

I rated this five stars because, not only did it taste great, but it was SUPER easy and required very few ingredients.  Like others, I reduced the salt to 1/4 teaspoon, and added the lime juice towards the end of cooking.  Next time I will try doubling some of the ingredients and/or adding a little chicken broth to create a sauce.

These shrimp were wonderful ms_bold. After reading the reviews I used 1/4 of the salt amount, added the lime juice when requested, but also added a little more at the end before serving.  Perfectly cooked, the shrimp were sweet succulent and spicy. We really enjoyed the shrimp prepared this way. This has excellent flavor, but I would agree with others that I would salt to taste and not use the recommended amount of salt. Also, I added more garlic cloves, fresh parsley and squeezed extra lime juice at the end of the cooking time. I received rave reviews from my guests!
Love this shrimp! My family likes to eat it on soft taco topped with creamy coleslaw.
This was very good! I used Smart Balance, 1/4 c. raisins, and 3 whole eggs. I made a sauce of margarine and brown sugar and server it on the bread pudding. Thanks for a good recipe.

Oh my goodness!!!  This is the best bread pudding I have ever had. For this to be low cal, it's better than my grandma's recipe which is very high in calories. I make it once a week.  Thumbs up to the person who submitted this recipe and thank you for it!
Made this with homemade bread,,1/2 white and 1/2 whole wheat.Very moist and delicious.Will certainly make again.

Wonderfull. Best Bread I have ever made. Have tried a lot from diet to not healthy. Was fluffy and light only halved everthing. Used 3 whole eggs and caster sugar. Broke up pieces of stale french stick, just  as good. Thanks for that.

We loved this! Super moist, didn't taste low fat at all. Used some stale hamburger buns, hot dog buns, bread, basically whatever leftover bread was in the pantry. It turned out great and was super easy. Thank you very much, Manuela!

DEFINITELY DELICIOUS! I used a  multi-grain bread, olive oil, and added the optional raisons. This is a simple recipe that even an inexperienced chef like myself can achieve tasty results. Thank you for such a terrific bread pudding!

My husband and I both loved this recipe for Bread Pudding! I used dark brown sugar in place of white sugar and it was delicious served warm with Cool-whip Free...and only 3 points value for those on WW- (I cut it into 9 servings instead of 8, otherwise point value is 4). Thanks!

So great!  I didn't use the oil or the raisins and I used 2 whole eggs instead of the eggs whites, along with 1/2 cup Splenda to replace the sugar.  It was delicious!  And it was so easy to make, too!  There's a lot of flavoring possibilities with this recipe.

I had to force myself to rate this a 3 because of the low calories and good flavor BUT something is off in the measurements. There was too much egg white or not enough bread. If you are not counting calories as I am then find a different recipe. If you are like me, I am going to use 2 less egg whites maybe 3 and more bread. GREAT! I love these cookies they are soo good

This was too good to be true.  My family and friends enjoyed every bite!

This is wonderful.  Very easy and very tasty.  There was a big sale on fresh strawberries at the grocery so I added them into the jello mixture also.  This was enjoyed by everyone I had over for Memorial Day. Thank you for posting.

I used raspberry flavor. This is SO good!! Thanks SaraFish for a great recipe! This goes into my favorite file! :-)

Good chocolate flavor and great chewy texture...this recipe is definatly a keeper...
This recipe works well for "lollipop" cookies to use in a cookie bouquet.  Soak wooden skewers and inster them into the raw dough before baking.  I added sweetened coconut instead of walnuts.  Yummy!

I can't say enough good things about this recipe.  Absolutely the best chocolate chip cookies I have ever made, and I've made a lot!  They came out really thick and chewy, and didn't spread too much in the oven like the Toll House recipe.  My new favorite chocolate chip cookie recipe!

I just made these using my baking ilustrated cookbook.  They are wonderful the only difference is how they shape them, I rolled a 1/4 cup of dough into a ball and then tore it in half with my fingertips.  Turn jagged edges so they are facing up and form dough back into a ball with jagged edges facing up.  It makes them thicker and a nice top on the cookies.  I got 14 cookies and if I had any left I would keep them in an airtight container so they would remain chewy.

My DH loved these cookies, they were very soft and delicious. I don't know what I did wrong though, maybe I did not let the butter cool enough?? I know, I know, you are probably rolling your eyes right now, but I am picky about my cookies! These are a very good puffy cookie though, and my family enjoyed them very much. Thanks for posting!

I'm updating my review to say that this cookie dough is an excellent base for other "mix-ins" besides chocolate chips. These cookies bake up thick, chewy and bakery-like. Be sure to (melt) real unsalted butter, no substitutes. The first time I made this, I used white chips and sweetened coconut. Today I used chocolate chips and walnuts. Delicious!

These are the best cookies I have eaten in my life.  I made them for my husband at Valentine's Day and he also thought they were fabulous.  The only change I made was using salted butter as that was what I had.  This will be a recipe that I will use forever.  Never in my long life of cooking have I made a more perfect cookie.

Great cookies!  My husband is a CC cookie fanatic, and he gave the 'thumbs-up'.
I wouldn't change a thing.

Great recipe, and easy! The only issue we had with the baking was that the cookies did not seem to really brown much, so it was difficult to determine doneness. I have never had success with chocolate chip cookies (they always turned out flat), and I had great success with these!  THANK YOU! :)  I didn't make them quite so big, so I cut down on the cooking time, but otherwise I followed it exactly.

First chocolate cookie recipe that hasn't gone flat on me.  I made them smaller and got 34 cookies and in 4 days my hubby has cleaned the lot off.  Says there fantastic and I have to make these from now on.  I used half milk chocolate and half white chocolate and the walnuts.  Thank-you for posting and looking forward to makeing your Brownies.
Excellent! Just the recipe I have been seeking: one that is soft and chewy. It was easy and fast too!
AWESOME! I love these thick and chewy. They keep well too! thank you for sharing. This is a keeper for sure. ~V

I never actually got to try one of these famed cookies.  I baked these for my friends birthday and he kept telling me how much he loved them.  My family devoured all the extra cookies while I was washing the dishes.  I guess they were great! ill have to make them again so i can actually try them
Great tasting cookie. I made these for the kids after an afternoon of tubing in the snow. They loved them. They dissappeared in no time. Thanks for the recipe.

However I think I do still prefer these cookies with baking soda rather than baking powder (the ones with baking soda come out thinner, crispier, and more chewy) With baking powder, these cookies needed about 15 minutes, but when I make them with baking soda, I tend to bake them for around 8-9 minutes as they're wonderful just a little underbaked. Thank you for this recipe though!
great cookie have made over and over ...I did put the dough in the freg to get cold ....came out chewy and thick...thank you

These came out perfectly thick and chewy for me.  I don't know how they compare to other recipes but they do taste amazing!  I made them smaller and got about 44.  I baked them for a total of 13 minutes, switching the sheets and turning them, at the 6.5 minute mark.

These turned out great! I got about 50 cookies out of this recipe. I did use baking soda instead of powder, per other comments. And I used margarine instead of butter.

I've had problems with toll house type cookies spreading out. These are thicker, chewy, and very tasty. I think the extra teaspoon of vanilla makes a difference as well. This will be my chocolate chip cookie recipe from now on.
These are excellent cookies.  I used an ice-cream scoop to make mine.

Reading your recipe was such a pleasure. You took the time to post the ingredients list in two measurement units, and explained the steps in such detail so people like me won't fail. These cookies really are amazing. No that bitterish/saltish aftertaste that you often get from cc cookies. I used half the dough to make big cookies, and the rest to make smaller ones ( reduced baking time ), and I must say that the larger ones were much better... chewier and softer. My sweets-hating son had two of the big ones. Best part.. no need for vanilla pudding mix!! Thank you so much for posting. Loved it.

I can't imagine good comments are given for this recipe.First of all, it's too sweet. And secondly its impossible to flip the cookies and last of all, I took more than 25mins just to bake the cookies.

This was a great cookie recipe.  Very clear instruction, no room for error.  I don't know how the person who gave this one star could have messed it up.  Probably the easiest cookie recipe and they were fantastic.  Perfect consistency, perfect taste.  Fabulous!  I used half light and half dark brown sugar and they were awesome!

Yeah-I agree that the instructions were perfectly clear-and the cookies were yummy! This will be my new cookie recipe from now on!
Thanks soooooo much for posting.

these were very good, they look just like the picture!While, I was making the batter it was kind of gooey so I stuck it in the fridge for 30 minutes and then made them. Came out great. Very good. Unfortunatly, I added 1/2 Tbs.of baking powder instead of 1/2 tsp. but it didn't seem to effect the tast at all. Good cookies.

A-MAZING!!! My adult daughter tried one of these.  Her comment was, "Now THAT's a cookie!!"  We both agree it's the best choc. chip cookie we've ever had or made. This is the forever chocolate chip cookie recipe in this family!!  Thank you Steve G!!

Tollhouse eat your heart out! I can't say enough about how good these cookies are.  I didn't have butter and used shortening.  While I think butter would make for better flavor, I'm not having any problems watching these babies disappear.  This recipe goes in our "favorites" cookbook.  Thank you!

wow!!! these are definitely bakery style stuff, so soft and chewy and absolutely perfect. mine were already starting to burn after 7-8 minutes so i would be careful about that, but otherwise it was just amazing. thank you!

I'm editing my review because I think I judged it unfairly before. I substituted margarine for the butter, which may have been a mistake, as my cookies were hard. I suggest sticking to the called for unsalted butter, which I may try next time.

I used this recipe when I forgot to take the butter out to soften for my usual recipe. We thought the flavor was good, but the cookies were more crisp than chewy. They disappeared quickly though! Thanks!

These are the only chocolate chip cookies that have worked out for me. Usually my other chocolate chip cookie fall very flat and they get too crispy but these came out perfectly! Thanks so much, this will replace my other recipe and I will make these often.
YUM....Easy recipe, and cookies setup perfectly!

Very nice, I like the look of the cookie after it is baked and the fact that they do not spread and get thin. I followed the recipe as written but found I needed to bake them for only 11 minutes. They did not turn out 'Chewy'. Maybe I did something wrong.

These cookies are amazing! I followed the directions exactly and they turned out delicious. 15 minutes was the perfect backing time for me. Thanks so much for sharing this awesome recipe, I'll be turning to it many times in the future.
Mine came out a bit flat, but still very delicious!
delicious - one of my favorite chocolate chip cookies ever!

These truly are the best choco chip cookies I've ever made! Large, chewy, sweet and chocolate-y - just how I love 'em! YUM!
I can honestly say I have a new favorite chocolate chip cookie recipe! These were delicious!! I took some to work and everyone gobbled them up. Thanks for posting this!!
My family thought these cookies were just okay.  Husband said they were too sweet.  I followed the directions exactly but they took much longer to bake than instructed.  Thanks anyway.

I agree, these are the best chocolate chip cookies I have baked much less tasted. Thank you for sharing.  I wanted to add that I bake the cookies for 8 minutes.  When they come out they are gooey.  I also do this because the kids love to come home and heat them up in the oven and eat them while they are gooey, chewey and yummy.  Thank-you again.
These cookies are wonderful. I followed the recipe exactly and got 18 of the best chocolate chip cookies I've ever tasted. Thanks for the recipe!!

OMG these are AWESOME!  They are crispy on the outside and nice and chewy on the inside.  PERFECTION in a cookie.  I will no longer make my regular cookies.  These are a keeper. My son 10 stars is needed for these ones.  I used a 2" scooper and only got 15 cookies, next time I will use my 1" one so that I can get more.  No more flat cookies here!!! Thanks a million!!!!
This cookies were pretty amazing! I added 1 package of Jell-o instant pudding and it made them even better!

These are good, but they didn't spread out very much...so I have big round tall cookies.  Which isn't terrible but they just look odd.  I would also suggest cooking one batch at a time to keep an eye on them.  By cooking more than one close together I burned the bottoms of some of the cookies.

This is the chocolate chip cookie recipe I've been searching my whole life for!  Thank you so much!  Delicious, chewy, buttery, and simply amazing!  This will be the recipe that I will teach my 6 month old baby girl when she gets older and she will pass this down in our family.  Thank you again!  Blessings!

This cookie recipe is outstanding! I've made them twice now and both times they were perfect. The only thing I left out this time was the additional yolk and they were still perfect. Thanks for sharing!

I had a craving for Choc chip cookies, but I'm the only one in my house who likes them, so I made them thinking I would end up eating the entire batch - hey, sometimes a girl just needs chocolate!

These cookies are lovely and chewy and soooooo moreish!! Thanks for a great recipe, and also the grams measurements.

We thought these were just OK, nothing special. I was expecting a lot more from all the great reviews but I've defiitely had better chocolate chip cookies than these. I will say that they did hold their shape well, and have a nice chewy texture to them. Thanks anyway.
Wonderful cookies! I doubled the recipe and froze some for later. Good right out of the freezer! Watch the bake time, unless you want a firmer cookie. Thanks for sharing!

WOW! I don't know what the secret is, but this recipe produces the best large ch. chip cookie I've ever made! This is the best chocochip cookie recipe I've every tried, they were soft and gooy, and best of all stayed that way even after they cooled. I only put in 1 stick of butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar and they turned out great!

I have tried lots of recipes on this website but this by far is my absolute favourite. I added scor bits because I only had half the chocolate chips required and I am ashamed to say I ate over half the batch myself!!

YEAH!  I finally found the perfect cookie recipe! I really needed for these not to work out. But they are awesome. Hard to just have one (not what my diet needs) So be warned unless you have huge will power do not try (lol)

My bf and I just finished making these cookies, and to our dismay, they did not turn out. OMG....I've been making these for years, this is the SAME EXACT recipe that I use when I want the ultimate indulgence!!!  In fact, I have it in my PRIVATE recipes.  I am not sure where I got the recipe from, but it doesn't matter, THIS IS THE ONLY CHOCOLATE COOKIE RECIPE I MAKE!!

These truly are perfection. I love the fact that I can melt the butter- it doesn't have to be 'softened'. I was told on more than one occassion that i should sell them! Thanks for the best cookie recipe EVER!!

These are kind of a "gourmet" chocolate chip cookie. Excellent! Update:  I took another reviewer's suggestion and used these to make lollipop cookies. WHOA...............!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Just the "quintessential " chocolate chip cookie recipe! I did not melt the butter... just softened it and I added an extra 1/2 tsp. of salt...  otherwise followed the recipe as stated. These were gone in a flash  :-)

Definately a 5 star recipe, but there's just something missing that I can't quite put my finger on. I think maybe next time I'll try useing all brown sugar. I also used a bit less than half a cup of butter (salted - it's what I had on hand) and made up some of the difference with unsweetened applesauce. Made 34 medium-sized cookies. This will be my go-to chocolate chip cookie recipe from now on. Thanks for sharing.

Once in my life I made a perfect chocolate chip cookie.  I've been trying, and failing miserably, to repeat whatever variation I struck upon ever since.  Lots of wasted batches of greasy, flat, hockey pucks,,.  But this recipe is THE ONE!!  The cookies are perfectly dense and chewy, and don't fall flat in the oven. I followed the recipe to the letter (Well except I used baking soda instead of powder per the original Cook's Illustrated recipe) and these cookies came out perfect! I think I'm going to make another batch because the first one didn't last very long. wonderful cookies

Absolutely excellent. As others mentioned, these cookies are noteworthy not only for their taste but for their lack of spread. The only thing that I may change next time is adding a pinch more salt (and no I am not a salt addict, I just think that it could bring out the flavors more).

As promised, these are perfectly thick and chewy chocolate chip cookies.  I'm using this recipe from now on!

if you are looking for the BEST chocolate chip cookie recipe look no further!  The absolute most fantastic, soft, tasty cookie ever...Thanks for sharing!
Wow!  This truely is the best chocolate chip cookie recipe ever!  Everyone who tasted them wanted the recipe!  Thank yo so much for sharing this real hit!

OMG! I was trying to figure out all of the cookie tricks and this recipe has put them all together to make the best cookies anyone could taste. Mmmm absolutely delicious! I didn't follow the ingredients exactly - I used caster sugar and raw sugar instead of brown and granulated, and salted butter as that was all I had. And they're still perfect as perfect can be! Thank you for a fantastic recipe :)

These cookies are AMAZING!  Most like bakery-style that I have ever tried.  I found this recipe on another site, which gives credit to the recipe to Baking Illustrated, page 434.  However, although the ingredient measures are exactly the same, the instructions for forming the cookies were a bit different.  Using the "other" instructions, I formed scant 1/4 cup balls (after refrigerating the dough for about 10 min), tore the balls in half and rejoined them with the craggly/ripped parts facing up as the top of the cookie, placing them 2 1/2 inches apart on an ungreased sheet.  Baked for 14-15 minutes, just until the edges were golden but the middle was still puffy and light-colored, and let cool for about 10 minutes on the cookie sheet.  They turned out big, thick and chewy - exactly what I was looking for.  AND they retain their chewyness, never getting crunchy!  We're still eating them a few days later (there are only 2 of us) and they are truly delicious.  5 stars all the way!

This is the best cookie recipe I've ever found.  I added a little extra vanilla (personal preference) and omitted the walnuts.  They came out big, chewy, and delicious.  This will be the standard henceforth.  Thank you!

This is the best Chocolate Chip cookie recipe that I have ever used!  Hands down!  I have tried maybe 10 other recipes, but none compare to this one.  I am throwing the others away...my search if over. Thanks a ton!

These are cookie perfection!  Made a batch but used an equivalent amount of red & green M&Ms for Christmas cookies...reserving half the Ms for decorating the tops. The picture got me, too.  Just took a couple of days to get to it!! My DH has been asking for CCCs for awhile.

That being said, made several changes for our preferences: 1/2C whole wheat flour to replace some of white, and did not use the additional 2 tbsp wht  as wheat absorbs more moisture than white. I don't really care for the chocolate chip cookies that the cake shop I work at full time uses so I was looking online and found this one to test out. I baked the cookies using the weight measures. This is very important. The reason everyones cookies look different in the posted pictures is because everyone measures things differently. However, if you weigh out your ingredients you get the same result every time. I honestly don't even mess with baking recipes that measure by volume anymore. Please do yourself a favor and buy a $10 digital scale on amazon and start weighing your ingredients. One minor technique change to make sure you get that pretty bumpy texture bakery cookies have is to bang your cookie sheet on the counter a few times when you rotate your pans.
