Tasty. I don't have a bbq so broiled them. Would have been 5 stars on the BBQ for sure!

This looks really good will try it this week.
When I grill kabobs I skewer the meat on one skewer and the veg on another,this way you can have it cooked perfectly by rotating the meat and the veg over the coals!
as they take different amount of time to cook.
Cliff

I've been making a concentrated effort to use the grill each night and took out chicken cutlets for tonight's dinner. Luckily, when I was trying to figure out what to do with them earlier today, I got an email from recipezaar with grilling recipes - and this recipe was among them!!! Delicious and they looked gorgeous! I took pictures :)

This was delicious!  Not a fan of mushrooms so I used zucchini as well as Vidalia onion, red pepper and grape tomatoes.  I doubled the marinade and discarded the marinade used for the chicken. My husband thought it was great.
I'll definitely make this again!

What an easy and delicious recipe!  One change I made was to use fresh pineapple chunks in place of the canned pineapple.  I also doubled the marinade and used the leftover to baste the veggies and fruit while on the grill.   The chicken was very tender after marinating and all of the flavors complemented each other beautifully. We will use this recipe again and again.
I cooked these for my husband last night and they were a WINNER!!!!!  HE LOVED THEM!!!!  This recipe will definitely become a regular at our house!
My family loved these kabobs except for the tomatoes. I loved the tomatoes. Will be making this again!!
The chicken turned out great! Very easy to make, I added a little extra pineapple juice.  Very good recipe & I've made it like 3 times in about a 1 1/2 weeks!
Great recipe! I also added a bit more pinapple juice and about 3 tablespoons of chives to the marinade.  Excellent recipe!
These were excellent! I cooked these in the oven, 400 degrees, for about 30 minutes, but only because I also had red potatoes on the skeewer. They turned out excellent and the marinade was delicious!
Super recipe!  Will make over and over!

Wow - these were super yummy! I baked mine at 400 for 25 minutes (I followed the suggestion of a reviewer & put the kabobs on a wire rack on top of a foil-line cookie sheet). In addition to the chicken, tomatoes and peppers, I used zucchini & red potatoes. However, those were my least favorite (and the potatoes were hard to put on the skewers!), and next time I'll stick to the original recipe. Thanks!
This was awesome!  Everyone loved it and asked for the recipe!  Thanks for posting!

We had a "kabobfest" over the 4th of July weekend.  We made many, many different kabobs and this was the favorite of most of us, perhaps second only to the Soy Glazed Salmon Kabobs.  The only thing we changed was fresh pineapple.  Highly recommend!

THIS IS OUTSTANDING!!!! Getting ready for a trip to Kauai and thought we would get in the spirit. They were moist, tender and the chicken was full of the marinade flavor. I added about 3 Tbsp chili oil to the marinade after boiling it and this gave a good little kick.
I will use often. All the flavors work so well together. Great textures. Love the marinade.

These were attractive with the tomatoes, pineapple and capsicum making a lovely, colourful skewer. The flavour of the marinated chicken was surprisingly mild and quite enjoyable. The only thing I regretted was using tinned mushrooms instead of fresh as they didn't have as much flavour as they could have. A good recipe to impress company with.
This chicken was awesome.  Easy to make and worth the effort.  Will be making this again.  Had my neighbors taste it and they also raved about it.
Wonderful! Even better with fresh pineapple. Made this during the summer a couple of times and the family really enjoyed it, sorry I'm just getting around to reviewing. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I had really high expectations for these kabobs after seeing all the great reviews, but i was a little disappointed coz my chicken didn't taste much of the marinade at all.. except it was pretty bland. I did chill it for 2 hours in the refrigerator. I might make it again but try marinating the chicken overnight.
It could be possible that it had to do something with the sweetened pineapple can that i used, since we dont get unsweetened pineapple can here. And since it was sweetened I skipped the brown sugar.
Im sorry for the low review.. I will definitely update my review when i make it with the changes.

We loved these kabobs.  The marinade reminded me of a teriyaki sauce and we really like that.  I omitted the cherry tomatoes (personal preference) but added some onions.  I let the chicken marinate for about 2 1/2 hours before skewering and then brushed it on while grilling.  I also saved some to serve on the table.  We served this with some rice pilaf and dinner rolls.  Thank you so much for sharing this yummy meal with us.
Wow!  I made this tonight and it got rave reviews from everyone.  I didn't use the tomatoes (instead I added onions).  We will have this again!
I have made these several times and everyone loves them!  Thank you for sharing!

Awesome. Best Kabobs ever.  I've never made kabobs before but I really wanted them for Mother's day so I decided to try this recipe and I'm so glad I did. I used steak, chicken and shrimp, mushrooms and onions on the kabobs.  I marinated the meat over night.  Put it in a plastic bag around 8:00 pm Sat evening.  Then when I woke up Sunday morning I cut the meat in bite sized pieces and put it back in the marinade.  I also soaked the sticks overnight in a mix of water and soy sauce.  This helps there be even more flavor cooked in from the inside out. :) Then around 2:30 on Sunday I assembled the kabobs and grilled.  Even my husband agreed these were the best kabobs ever.   It made about 15 kabobs (I did about 1 1/2 the recipe).  Thank you so much for the recipe. It's a keeper!
The kabobs were absolutely wonderful!  We grilled them for our Memorial Day dinner. My family is still raving about how great they were.  Thank you.

These kabobs were a big hit at our pool party.  I prepared 40  kabobs to feed 28 guests. They all disappeared with rave reviews. The marinade was so wonderful I decided to marinate the chicken overnight to maximize the flavor. Yummmmmm
We made these for our 4th bbq and they were really delicious! Wouldn't change a thing about the recipe, loved it! Thanks for posting!

Made these last night for our bridge dinner and everyone loved them. Made enough for my adult son to have some and he reminded me again today how good they were. Have been asked to serve them again soon.

OMG! OMG! This is EXCELLENT ... entire family raved about how great these were. Made for tonight dinner. Used chicken breast and skinless deboned chicken thighs, with onions, pineapple, red/green/yellow bell peppers, mushrooms, yellow squash, and tomato . Marinated the chicken for about three hours. Grilled them on the charcoal grill. Served with chicken flavored rice. The marinate DEFINITELY made this dish. Before dinner was over I was hearing about all the different ways the marinate could be used....FROM MY FAMILY. I had a lot of left over veggies and pineapple so I thru them in a skillet with butter and a little oil, salt/pepper,  garlic powder and sauteed them  Before serving I added some of the marinate. They were adding the leftover veggies/pineapple to the rice. THIS RECIPE IS A KEEPER. I am actually thinking about making up a jar of the marinate and keeping it in the fridge.....lol... I could drink the stuff. It is SO good. I was also amazed at how moist and tender the chicken was. You could almost cut it with your folk. THANK YOU, THANK YOU for posting this fabulous recipe.
Really liked this recipe. Nice marinade. Took them to a cookout. Received tons of compliments. Thanks....this recipe is a keeper.
This was an awesome recipe .. Loved it & it inspired me to register for food.com so I could find it easily again.
For safety, please bring the marinade to a boil before brushing on the kebabs while they're being grilled.
These chicken kabobs were a big success.  The chicken was in the marinade overnight.  The taste was so good.  The chicken was tender.  Thanks MizzNezz :)  Made for Cookbook tag game
Very nice dish.  Chicken was incredibly moist.  Thank you for sharing.
Simply amazing! There's great balance of flavors. Will definitely make this again!

These kabobs are AMAZING!!  I made them on my indoor grill and they came out simply delicious.  The marinade is to die for and would be good on chops or chicken breasts - anything.  I made a side of lemon red potatoes and it is one of the best meals I ever made.  I have never written a review for any receipe I have tried, but these were just too good to be true. Thank you for posting.  I'll be making these time and time again. YUM!!

I chose this recipe because of all the excellent reviews. I made it for a family dinner. The aroma in the house from the marinade heating on the stove was amazing. I doubled the recipe and it was totally eaten up by 5 adults!!  Raves from all.  I used 3 colors of bell pepper, pineapple, and whole medium mushrooms. Next time I will use fresh pineapple as the chunks would be larger than the canned kind.  As some other reviewers did, I baked it in the oven for 30 minutes @ 350*. I placed the kabobs on a wire rack over a cookie sheet lined with foil. I made 2 batches due to doubling the recipe.  Kept the first batch warm on top of the stove loosely wrapped in foil.  I liked using the oven because you don't have to turn the kabobs over and therefore the vegetables stay intact.  I marinated every 10 minutes.  This is a keeper.  My family is still talking about how good it was days later!  Yes!!

Great recipe! I only did a couple of things different - I let my chicken marinade longer than an hour and I did not put the chicken and veggies on the skewers. I just grilled them all on separate grill pans. We have made this on camping trips and at home on several occasions and it is always a hit! We serve it with jasmine rice and sometimes a side of steamed broccoli. Our kids like to use "shrimp sauce" or "pink yummy sauce from the Japanese restaurant with this dish. The marinade has great flavor and you can't go wrong with this recipe. Thanks for sharing!
The marinade is really what makes this dish! I substituted the mushrooms (ick!) for sausage and also added bacon...it was delicious. Even my kids ate it! :)
This marinade is awesome! I made kabobs for a game night at friends house, and they raved over the flavors. Chicken was soooo tender! This recipe is a keeper!

I made this today, it was fantastic! The marinade is just perfect! I made the recipe just as was said, and I don't really feel any changes need to be made. Its a wonderful recipe and I'm planning on making this again.
My whole family loved this. I marinated the chicken for 2 hours. Instead of grilling, I cooked the kabobs under the broiler for 20 minutes, rotating the skewers occasionally. Excellent!

GREAT RECIPE you have here! I made it to include on my finger food counter for a group I host each month & they loved these TASTY LITTLE BITES! I did cut back on the cayenne pepper by almost half; substituted lemon pepper for the usual S&P; & I used whole wheat bread crumbs that I'd processed fine ~ All for some tasty chicken nuggets that everyone raved about! Keepin' this one around! [Tagged, made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in the current Pick A Chef]
Yummy! We loved it. I followed the recipe exactly and even added more cayenne pepper because we like it spicy. Thanks for posting. Made for Fall PAC 2009.

I was getting so tired of eating the same old chicken.  This recipe added some excitement to our meal.  I was just the right blend of spices.  Not too spicy, but certainly not bland.  I will be making these tasty nuggets again.

I tried this today. I used just regular graham crackers that I crushed. I replaced the 1/2 cup sugar with 1/2 cup of Splenda. The rest I follow as directed. Everyone loved it. I was a light & tasty dessert.
This is one of our favorite recipes. We are from the buffalo area and it doesn't get better then this. We use Rooties or Marie's. A chunky blue cheese works best. Very, very yummy
This recipe should call for franks red hot sauce.

Fantastic flavor weither you fix the blue cheese or the ranch...I used Marie's blue cheese with some extra blue cheese crumbles to top...delicious! Tried a local ranch, with the same delicious result. Served with celery or carrot sticks...it was all gone!  Thanx so much for posting this GREAT recipe!
I agree that this recipe should call for Frank's Red Hot only!  It's the only way to get the true Buffalo flavor.  Tabasco would ruin it!
Awesome...must try! I love blue cheese but if ranch is your favorite use that.  I am from buffalo, NY area and this is a great appetizer.

Whooeee! This is spicy but good. I used only 1/2 bottle of Franks. I think I would like to try with the green tabasco. Definitely like the "no bones" chicken. I think I might try this wrapped up in small warm tortillas next time.

Absolutely perfect!!!  This was so good.  I used the Frank's RedHot sauce.  The only thing I didn't do was add the celery, but I would serve it separate for those who like celery.  Also, I just added the cheese directly to the saucepan mixture.  Also, we used all ranch because we don't really like bleu cheese.  We were just trying it today for the first time and halved all the ingredients, and it still made a good size batch for a smaller crowd.  We will definitely be making this anytime there is a good football game on!  Great party food!

This dip was awesome! I used all ranch dressing but I'll bet half bleu cheese would be good! I admit I was reluctant to put the whole bottle of Frank's hot sauce in but I kept tasting and adding more until I used the whole bottle. My mil loved this dip and she does not like spicy food! Thank you so much for posting this awesome recipe.

AWESOME AWESOME!!!!! I made this dip to serve at a small get together this weekend... what an absolute fantastic dip, I added in a bit of fresh garlic, and the whole bottle of Frank's Red Hot sauce..this dip is going into my favorites to make again and again, thanks for sharing this great recipe Parsley!...Kitten:)

OMG!!!A great dip with a kick! I crockpotted 3 chicken breasts in chicken broth w/ garlic so that they would shred well. I used 1/2 blue cheese and 1/2 ranch dressings and had leftover shredded Cheddar and leftover Jack and leftover Kraft crumbles Cheddar/Jack combo. I also used a whole 12oz bottle of Louisiana hot sauce. This dip is the bomb! Thanks!!!

OH MY WORD is this wonderful.  we had a potluck at work and I chose this recipe to take.  I used the ingredients as list, but varied the preperation a little.  I followed everything up until cooking in the oven.  I cooked mine in my one quart crock pot. (which by the way, filled to the top and I had at least 1 1/2 cups that wouldn't fit.  I served it with Frito scoops.  Since I'm dieting, I only tried about 1/2 teaspoon, but I could have easily indulged with alot more.  I had several requests for the recipe.  I used bleu cheese dressing and about 3 cups of cheddar cheese.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

This dip rocks! I took it to a work potluck over the holiday weekend, where everyone loved it and asked for the recipe. It tastes just like a chicken wing! I used 3/4 bottle of Frank's hot sauce and omitted the 2/3 cup diced celery; for dipping I served celery sticks and Nabisco Sociable crackers. I am on a low carb diet and was able to eat this dip using the celery. I will definilty make this again! Thanks for posting, Parsley!

I used 1/2 bottle of Frank's Red Hot Buffalo Wing Sauce and bleu cheese dressing. I really liked the taste. The only drawback for me was the amount of oil that was on top the dish. I dabbed a paper towel over the top to absorb some of it. All in all it was good and I'll be making it again.

Nice hot dip! Used Franks Red Hot Buffalo Wing Sauce & the blue cheese dressing. Only complaints were that the chicken was overwhelmed by the other flavors, and there was  separation of liquids from solids. All in all a tasty dip; leftovers were good reheated in the microwave.

This is a GREAT recipe!! My son and I loved this so so much!! My husband on the other hand would not even touch it because of the way it looked (not sure what I did)...OH Well his loss!! More for the rest of us!! Thank you so much for posting this...We will be trying this again!!

UPDATE...Husband FINALLY tried it and LOVED it!!! :O)

delicious!!!  i used the whole bottle of sauce, and i also added sliced green onions and serrano peppers.  we wolfed this down!  i could seriously just eat it with a spoon!  i have some dip leftover, so i think i'll make fried wontons out of them for appetizers tomorrow night!!  thanks parsely for another keeper!  made for "went to the market" tag game -ingredient: celery!

I've made this 2 years in a row now for parties around Thanksgiving time and I've gotten rave reviews both times.  This dip is very tasty and easy to make.   I skipped the celery because I didn't think it would go well, but otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly - using the full bottle of hot sauce.  It's great served with Triscuits or bread. It is wonderful when it's hot out of the oven, but also tastes delicious the following day when cold. It's hard to stop eating it once you start. This one is definitely a keeper. Thanks for a great recipe.
Wow- this is a fine recipe! My boys LOVED it. I used more hot sauce than the recipe called for because we like it spicy. I will definitely make this again!
This is wonderful!  I will cut the recipe in half, though, it makes a LOT!  I served it at a New Year's Eve party and everyone loved it!

Outstanding!  I made 1/2 of the recipe, just for DH and myself, using Texas Pete hot sauce and ranch dressing.  Yummy!  I can't wait to share this at a potluck or with the neighbors.  I have already called my BF and told her I had a great recipe for her to try.  I love that you have the great taste of buffalo wings without the mess of bones. Great recipe Parsley!

Big hit for the football playoffs today.  Brought this with me to my brother's house and he even liked it and he is really picky.  I had to leave the leftovers there for him.  I made the entire amount of sauce but only had 3/4 lb of shredded chicken, so when I mixed it together I only used about 1/2 of the sauce.  The rest I am saving for sandwiches.  I think it will be awesome.  I used about 3/4 bottle of Frank's Red Hot sauce and that was plenty spicy for most.

I made this for a Super bowl gathering and there was very little left. I did use Ranch and left out the chopped celery based on previous reviews. I served it with celery sticks and crackers, and some people used the Fritos I had out for something else. My son ate the leftovers as a sandwich on a roll the next day. I am already planning when I will make this next.
I loved this recipe, it was so good. Everyone loved it and there wasnt any left over. excellent.

Really good!  I used 1/2 bleu cheese dressing, and 1/2 ranch dressing.  I don't typically care for the taste of bleu cheese, so I wasn't sure if I would like this...but the 1/2 bleu cheese added a nice tang to the dip.  I'm not sure you'd get the same result with all ranch.  I used the entire 12 ounces of hot sauce (Frank's), because my husband and friends like their food SPICY.  It had quite a bite, and was a little too spicy for me, but dipping with celery helped cool it down a little.  I omitted the celery in the dip, and just used celery sticks to dip.  If I were making it for me, I would probably use 1/2 bottle of Frank's.  I was pressed for time, so I used refrigerated Tyson oven-roasted chicken strips that I shredded with my fingers.  I would imagine it would be very good, and just as easy, using a rotisserie chicken.  Very good, and simple to make.  Thanks!

I made this dip for friends who came to visit.  We all sat around and ate till we were ready to burst it was so good!  I used Frank's Red Hot Sauce at the request of other posters and it was perfect!  Wasn't too hot for us.

I have made this recipe several times except I use 2 large cans of chicken and put in all in a crock pot.  I put it on high for a couple of hours and then turn down to low.  When serving, I put on warm.  It is always a big hit!
Absolutely WODERFUL!!!! This is my favorite.

LOVE IT!!!  I actually make this recipe in my crock pot for parties...so it's always warm!  I cook the chicken on the stove, then combine with the rest of the ingredients in the crock- stir a few times and by party time it's just perfect!!  THANKS!!!

Absolutely delicious!! Rather than heating everything up on the stove top, I just melted the cream cheese and blue cheese together in the microwave, dumped in the Frank's hot sauce, and then mixed it with the chicken and cheese before baking:) THANKS for such a fabulous recipe!!!

Yummy yummy yummy! I made this for a gathering my husband was hosting and it was a hit. I even had some leftover which some of our family was able to taste and they loved it as well. I used fat free cream cheese and Cholula hot sauce which I am pretty sure was the wrong sauce but it was still tasty! I think next time I will use the hot sauce meant for wings. Thanks for posting!

I'm not a fan of buffalo wings, but on a whim I entered this recipe into a side dish cook off ... and won!  It was a big hit.  I made 2-13x9s of it and there was barely any left at the end of the day.  The only problem I had with it was the Frank's Red Hot seemed a little vinegary.  Is there something that can be added to even it out?

Wow.  This dip was a hit at our halloween / birthday party.  It makes ALOT though.  We had 20 adults at the party and still had quite a bit left.  Everyone loved it, even my mom who's not crazy about spicy food.  Next time I make it I will probably add a little less blue cheese.  Also, I used canned chicken and that worked fine.  Thank you, Parsley!

I made this for a party this past weekend and it was great.  I do question the 12 oz. bottle of hot sauce recommended in the recipe. I live in Louisiana and so hot sauce is freely flowing around here, but they are a 6 oz. size.  I bought two bottles though and after putting in all of the first one, that was plenty hot.  I think 12 oz. of hot sauce would be overkill.  I served mine with those scooped tortilla chips.
Excellent!

I make this all the time and it is sooooo addictive. I use 2 cans of the Tyson chicken breast, a whole bottle of Hooter's hot wing sauce, ranch dressing, and leave out the celery. It can be somewhat greasy after baking so I like to dab a paper towel to get rid of some of that. Great recipe :o)
This was great! The kids ate the whole thing! Im not a big hot wing fan because they are so messy. This gave great flavor without the mess of wings!

Great Appetizer!  I made it for a Tailgate party and it was delicious.  I used Bleu Cheese dressing (only) and no celery in the actual dip.  We used celery sticks for dipping.  I also only used half of bottle of Frank's Hot sauce - as I had some folks that didn't like spicy foods.  It still had plenty of spice for us.  Thanks for sharing the great recipe.

Excellent party dish! This was a HUGE success at the party I brought it to.  Two things I did different: used ranch dressing instead of blue cheese and also reserved the celery for dipping instead of chopping it up and including it in the mix. Thanks for sharing!  I plan to make it again for an office potluck at the end of this month!
Excellent! Omitted celery in the dip,used blu cheese and only 2 cups cheese and whole bottle franks. I think I could eat the whole pan myself. Yum. Thanks its a keeper.

Incredible recipe!!  My husband is a huge hot wing snob, and it met with his hard-to-get-approval!  As far as he was concerned, it was the only item on the menu at a recent party we had!  Thanks again!
My daughter made this for her sleepover party.  The girls loved it.
I made this once for a party and since then I have been asked to make it over & over. I wouldn't suggest using anything other than Frank's hot sauce.

Being near the home of the original Buffalo Chicken Wings from the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, NY - I, of course, made this using 1 bottle of Anchor Bar wing sauce instead of hot sauce.  Tastes exactly like the Buffalo Wings we get there!  A note: I skip the shredded cheese.  I use shredded chicken breasts, 1 bottle Anchor Bar wing sauce, 2 pkg cream cheese, 1 bottle ranch salad dressing, and 1-1/2 cups very good quality crumbled bleu cheese.  The Anchor Bar sauce and the bleu cheese crumbles are really what makes this dip.  I put all the ingredients into a crockpot and bring the crockpot with me when bringing this to potluck events.  Sometimes I will triple the amount of chicken and make "chicken wing salad" for sandwiches or wraps.  Super yum!

This recipe is always a hit at the superbowl.  I use fresh grilled chicken breast in mine, and chopped green onion, and instead of bleu cheese, I add my homemade ranch dressing and bleu cheese crumbles.  My friends have a Dip-off every year, and this one always wins.  :)
OK, so this my favorite dip!!!  The flavors are great and its easy to put together.  I put it in a crock pot and let it cook over low heat.  I will be making this one again very soon!!

Took this to a potluck..was a huge hit!  There were no left overs and everyone wanted the recipe.  I used about 3/4 bottle of Franks Red Hot Wing Style sauce with the Ranch Dressing..not too spicy..just right.  Will definitely make again!
Thanks :)

This is my go to chicken wing dip, my brother-in-law insists I make it at every family gathering.  Franks hot sauce, Maries bleu cheese dressing, and used both cheeses....YUM...oh and no celery, just a preference.

Delicious!!  Made it for football yesterday and everyone LOVED it.  I made pretty much as is but tweeked some after reading other reviews.  Used about 85% of the Franks Wing Sauce bottle to the point it had nice zing but wouldn't be too spicy for average joe.  I used all Blue Cheese dressing and served celery sticks on the side for dipping rather than putting in the dish.  The cheese on top does really get oily and when it starts to cool the cheese is a little hard to "cut through" with a chip or cracker.  I really don't think it needs it and will probably make it without the extra cheese.  Ok it's now  this making me hungry thinking about it - time to raid the leftovers!

I pretty much use the same recipe for my chicken wing dip- everyone requests it for parties! and its always gone so fast. I make a few changes tho- I don't put celery in the dip, i just serve it with it. and i layer my cream cheese on the bottom and put the chicken mixture over it- I find the cream cheese always clumps up anyway. I also use mozzarella for mine, and layer it on top as well as in the dip. Delicious!

I've been making this dip for over a year now, and procrastinated in rating it. It's absolutely delicious! Usually I don't add as much Frank's, just because my family can't handle it. I also serve the celery on the side, and use whatever shredded cheese I might have in the house. Thanks for the great recipe!

This was great! I made this for people to snack on during our New Year's Eve Party. Three of our guests loved it so much, that I packed up what was left and sent it home with them in "doggie bags". I will certainly think of this recipe for our Super Bowl party.
Everyone loved this dip! Thanks for the recipe!

This was so good that I ate way too much of it at our super bowl party and didn't have room for anything else!  I only added 2 cups of cheese which I thought was more than enough.  I also left out the celery (personal preference) but mixed in the 1/2 onion and 2 cloves of garlic that I poached my chicken breasts with.  Very delicious!

Made this for a potluck..had to keep giving out the recipe...Only used half  bottle of Franks (because of too many different opinions of spicy at work)  worked good.  three chicken breasts cooked in garlic and other seasonings...half bottle of blue cheese half of ranch..next time will be 3/4 blue cheese.. did not use celery in the recipe but had it has a dipper..along with crackers..actually I am not a fan of celery but with this dip it was good. Thanks for the great recipe...One girl said this was "a keeper".

This is a great recipe to take to get togethers. Most times I have all the ingredients in the house. Family and friends always look forward to this. Also many requests for recipe...I usually use all ranch, family not thrilled with bleu as much as me...Always use Franks also.
this made the boyfriend very happy... and me too! delicious thanks for the good recipe!

Excellent. Simple. Pretty cheap to do and fast. The only way I think it would benefit is if it were kept on low in a slow cooker for dipping all night long. Keeping it warm is critical. I think it would also be fine with more celery if you're serving it with tortilla chips. I used Renee's Ranch Dressing.

I've had about 20 people ask me for this recipe already. Best when just out of the oven. Whole bottle of Frank's hot sauce is a bit much. Perfect with 3/4ths of a bottle. I don't use the celery. FANTASTIC dish.

I just made this dip for my sister's baby shower this past saturday.  The only changes I made was to omit the cheese and celery, and to use just over half a bottle of hot sauce.  I put the dip together friday and then baked it for almost an hour right before the shower.  It was a huge hit!  I served it with chips and thinly sliced french baguette.  I thought it was much better with the bread.  The only thing that I didn't like is that oil seperated out of the dip and looked a little unplesant, but the taste more than made up for it!  Thanks for posting the recipe!

I've made several Buffalo Chicken Dip recipes over the years and this was by far the best! I brought this to a party - it didn't last long and garnered many compliments. I also used only about 3/4 of the bottle of Frank's, thought it had a nice kick but wasn't too overpowering. We kept this in a chafing dish to keep it warm, think either this or a crock pot is a must to keep the dip from hardening and separating. Served with chips and celery on the side, as opposed to in the dip.

Yum! Made this superbowl sunday and it came out so good. I did use all ranch dressing though because im preggo and i cant eat blue cheese ( even though i love it) and i left out the celery because im not a huge celery fan. Came out great though!

This was absolutely delicious and took no time to put together.  I halved the recipe and used 1/4 of a bottle of Frank's Red Hot and it still had plenty of kick for us.  As other reviewers suggested, I dabbed the extra fat floating on top with some paper towels.  Instead of serving it as a dip with chips, my family requested to have this on top of white rice which, at first, I thought was beyond bizarre, but I gave it a try and it really was a great combo.  Served with fresh celery on the side instead of mixing it in with the chicken.  Didn't have any cheddar, so I used Monterey Jack and Kraft Italian cheese blend - yum!  Next time, however, I'm going to reduce the amount of dressing which should help reduce the amount of fat floating on top.  This recipe is also great for buffalo chicken sandwhiches on toasted hoagies with larger chunks of chicken breast.  Thanks for a keeper recipe!

My son made this for our Christmas Eve party and it was fabulous. I'm going to make it for the New Years Eve party but will tweak it a bit. I found the cheese on top was too hard when cooled so will cook mine in crock pot and keep it on warm when finished. I will also use ranch dressing with bleu cheese crumbled into it and use 1/2 bottle of Frank's red hot sauce.. I will also add some fresh garlic when cooking the chicken breast because we love garlic chicken wings. Will serve with celery sticks [on the side], bagel chips and tortillas chips. This dip tastes just like Wings N More medium garlic wings without the horrible mess. Yay!

Thanks to Parsley and all the great suggestion from the reviewers. This is just what I've been looking for. Okay, I think I better try out a batch [right now] before New Years Eve to make sure it tastes right. LOL

This is the best dip ever! I've been making it for years and thought I'd already rated it but hadn't. I used to bring it to football tailgates and is now a favorite anytime!

BEST DIP EVER!

Everybody devoured it - big hit for Christmas Eve!   I opted to use 2 cans of chicken (so much easier) drained and shredded.   I left out the celery.   I used a bottle of 'lite' bleu cheese dressing and about 3/4 of a bottle of Frank's Buffalo Wing style hot sauce.  Served with scoops!
Add more chicken than the recipe calls for but either way so good
I made this for Thanksgiving appetizers, and everyone loved it. We used lowfat cream cheese and substituted greek yogurt for the ranch and added bleu cheese crumbles. It was great!

I made this dip for a football gathering.  The dip was easy to make.  I used half of the bottle of hot sauce (6 oz) and ranch dressing.  I served it with tortilla chips.  I recommend starting out with half the bottle of hot sauce, because hot sauces are not the same.  I also think the bleu cheese dressing would have added more flavor.  To us the dip was ok, but it didn't have the flavor we were looking for.  It wasn't bad, but it wasn't great.  On the other hand, there were only 2 small spoonfuls left.
Awesome recipe

Sometimes less is more...
Simple recipe with little ingredients yet no sacrifice on flavor, I make this for every party I have and everyone loves it. I serve with celery or Tostitos chips and sometimes I will serve for dinner with cut up vegetables such as cucumber, red pepper and carrots (great way to get kids to eat them).
Highly recommend for the buffalo chicken fan

Very good reception at our Christmas celebration!  I was short on time and had fresh chix breasts on hand (1.2 kg.)  Pan sauteed them with some hot sauce brushed on.  Chopped them up with onions and garlic powder, then followed recipe - except put everything in crock pot on high for about 3 hours.  I used the whole bottle of Frank's...and added another two drumsticks and thigh to make it a bit more meaty.  A bit spicy, but good.  Served with bread chunks.  Will make again!  Thanks!

I have made this many times, my changes are: When I poach the chicken I add chicken base, parsley onion powder, garlic powder & pepper. My honey likes the broth + it adds flavor. I also add both ranch & blue cheese = amounts + melted butter abt. 1/2 stick. My cheeses are a mixture of many moz, cheddar, Colby, Monterey I might go over a little but try to stick to amount in recipe. Plus I make my ranch home made with the hidden valley packets. This calls for all mayo but I add = amount of sour cream And us 1/2 & 1/2 or butter milk this is much better then bottled.
I use a ¾ of a large bottle of Frank's celery seed and Marie's blue cheese and I also buy a cooked chicken and use the whole thing even the dark meat. It is by far the best wing dip I've ever had.
I liked this but surprisingly the kids were a bit iffy. Worth a try though.
Very good!! My husband and Son loved them. It was a hit in my house thank you.
Very easy to make.  My 13yo son loved these and said that this is something he can make for himself when he is hungry. This will be a staple in his diet now.

These taste way too good to be so simple and easy to make.  I served with Spanish Rice, 
recipe #59029, very filling meatless meal!  Also, thanks for the great recommendation on the refried beans.  Definately a good choice.

These cheese and bean burritos were AWESOME!!!  I have always wanted to find a good recipe for cheese and bean burritos and this exceeded my expectations!  My family loved them!  The only change I made was to add one small onion, diced.  This is a keeper - thanks much, Mille!
These were really good!  I used the shredded Kraft Taco Cheese Blend to give them even more flavor.

THESE WERE AWESOME! I took the recommendation of using Recipe #10614 (refried beans). Adding the green chilies, cumin and garlic powder really rounded out the flavor for these burritos. Before I put them in the oven I brushed them with melted butter for extra flavor and crispiness. I received rave reviews from my husband, children (who ate every single bite) and my guest. I will make these again. Thanks Mille!
I have made this over and over for my family, and they continue to ask for more! This is an easy and quick way to get food on the table!
Pretty good. Buttered tortillas and made them like quesadillas, served them with sour cream. Thanks for sharing!

Incredible:  I 'dry fried  1.5 tspn whole cumin seeds (and then ground them) and halfed the amount of chillies (next time I'd use full amount). I had intended to serve the burritos with Spanish Rice (see 'Daphne 2002' review) plus salsa etc but the burritos were all eaten up by 'tasters' within 5 minutes of coming out of the oven, I couldn't believe it! A fantastic recipe!

TO DIE FOR!!! I used 1 T. chili powder being that this was the first time I made this. I also halved the cinnamon as I was a little nervous to use so much! I mixed 3 teaspoons with 3/4 lb ground lamb and 1 1/2 lb ground chuck with a generous squirt of fresh lemon juice, a crushed clove of garlic, and a chopped onion. I let the mixture sit all morning and made up patties in the evening. We grilled them and made them into Gyros burgers as Dh forgot to pick up pitas! Even the kids ate every last drop and as picky as they are that's a miracle! This mix will become a staple in our house, I can't wait to try it with other meats! Thanks Annelies!

This spice mix is very tastey, but did I miss something? Couldn't find the kick.  I used it as a rub and before I rubbed, as suggested I added a bit of olive oil,Lemon zest and some juice, also added salt. It was a very good taste but I guess we expected some heat.  I followed the recipe exactly and used about half of it, stored the rest for later.  We really did enjoy it, it just wasn't what we expected. Thanks for sharing.

We had a bbq the other night & I had to try this rub.  Which is exactly what we used it as, just as is on a few pieces of scotch fillet.... to die for, flavour was fabulous..   Definitely a keeper, shall cartainly be trying this spice mix in other things in ther future.  Thanks...

Spinner

Thank you for this recipe.  I had 3 last minute small christmas gifts to get, so I trotted off to my local bulk binn store and for under $2 each was able to make up 3 jars of this mix. I included a copy of the recipe and popped them into gift bags.
Excellent mix of spices! Not being scared of a 'kick' however I did take on board Derf's comments and added two teaspoons of cayenne pepper, and used a hot variety of chili powder and paprika.
Most Gyros I've made are bland.  Finally, something that has some flavor!  We LOVED these!

Wonderful spice mix!  I used this to make my first gyros.  I know lamb is authentic, but we used hamburger and it was wonderful.  I am going to mix up some more of this to keep on hand.  I used recipe #51983 "Mean Chef's Tzatziki".  Thank you for sharing!

Excellent flavor combination!  Made just as posted and it was delicious!  I rubbed chicken tenders with the spice mix, placed them into a greased baking dish & poured in a little white wine.  Baked until they were done (about 15 minutes).  I was eating alone tonight so I can't wait til the whole family is home & we can actually make gyros with it!  Thanks so much for posting, Pets!  :)  Made & enjoyed for the May 2010 LiveSTRONG cookathon.

Fantastic!!! I Love, Love, LOVE this seasoning!  I put it on top sirloin and slice thin.  I also put the seasoning on oven fries to serve with the gyros.  I dip the fries in the cucumber sauce and it is wonderful.

Not right, not good.  This spice mix is like no gyro I've ever had.  It's not horrible and won't make you sick, but it's also not authentic or right-tasting at all.  I tried it based on the reviews, but the resulting taste is not right at all.  I recognize that it includes much cumin and coriander, not enough garlic.  Otherwise, I don't know what is missing or excessive--which is why I looked for a recipe.
This was an awesome recipe, I cook a lot, try different things and this was an awesome Greek legit recipe. Do it! You will be most pleased! I used 2 lbs of ground organic turkey. It was PERFECT!

This was good. I added 4 cloves of minced garlic and the seasoning to the hot pan before adding the chicken. I separately sautéd a yellow onion and and orange and yellow bell pepper. The gyros were delicious.
Hope you like taco meat cause that's what it tastes like.

Another winner, Inez! This stew is outstanding and we loved the flavors of the wine, tomatoes and herbs. I added just a bit more red pepper flakes, as we like it spicy and it was just wonderful. Thanks for the great recipes, keep 'em coming!

The recipe was very tasty, but I expected more of a stew, and, made as directed,it was more like a wonderful spaghetti sauce (lose the potatoes, and it is!).  The next time we make it, we plan to add beef broth and just the one can of diced tomatoes.  Don't get me wrong - the flavor was very nice, it just wasn't quite what we expected.  And I love the idea of a sausage stew - it'd never occurred to me to make a stew with sausage, so we'll be tinkering around with the basics - thanks for the very good basic recipe.

This is a great, simple recipe for a cold evening.  I loved the potatoes; a can of white beans would have made a nice addition, too.  I used my own homemade Italian sausage which has lots of wine and cheese and very little fat.  With commercial sausage, I would have been careful to thoroughly drain the sausage after browning.  A bit of freshly grated Parmesan was a nice finishing touch.

This is a great stew to make during the week. It's quick, easy, tasty, and has ingredients readily available in most pantries. I used Zesty Italian Sausage links and sliced them on the bias instead of crumbling and browning, but that's just a personal preference thing. The diced and stewed tomatoes I bought were already seasoned Italian style, and I think they really complimented the stew. There were no leftovers at all.

This recipe is fantastic. My family really enjoyed this one. I added some green pepper and spinach greens to it and also used hot italian sausage. This will be listed as one of our family's favorites. Thanks Inez.

Quick and easy to make.  The combination of seasonings was good and made for a satisfying dinner.  Even though I used a potato masher to break up the tomatoes, my family balked at the chunks of tomatoes--there ends up being a lot of tomato per bite.  Next time, I would use one can of diced tomatoes and a can of tomato puree.

Was a hit with the family. I did drain the sausage and added the onion, added celery and carrots.Then got the call that the in-laws were stopping for dinner. Panicked so I pureed the can of stewed tomatoes, and added a cup of beef broth, I was worried we wouldn't have enough. It was delicious, I did pair it with a salad and some really good crusty french bread. Small bowl of leftovers which I'm eating for lunch :).Thanks!

We really liked this.  Husband said "its a keeper!"

I added 1 can of northern beans, 1 can of beef broth, 1 can chicken broth.

I used a potato masher at the end to give it a smoother consistency.

Great flavor and easy to make. I used one 32 oz. can of crushed tomatoes in tomato puree because my family doesn't like too many chunks of tomatoes. I prepared this the night before I served it, and added a couple of handfuls of ditalini pasta just before serving. Everyone loved the flavor of this stew, which really is outstanding. Next time, I will double the recipe and freeze half for a quick meal on a winter day.

Yum! This is easy and the flavors are fantastic. I took a couple suggestions from others and used a 28 oz. can of crushed tomatoes and a can of beef broth. Next time I will add carrots and green peppers to it to get more veggies. This will be made again!

It seemed like this recipe needed some broth, because it cooked off so much that it seemed more like stewed veggies. We ended up adding extra tomatoes and a few cups of broth, a can of beans and some ditalini.
I added some cubed zucchini and 16 oz of garbanzo beans.  Hit it with some grated parmesian.  Great comfort food.

YUMMY!
Super easy and so comforting! I added in some fresh tomatoes along with the diced and a small can of tomato soup since I didn't have stewed tomatoes. Also, I quickly cooked stelle (small star shaped pasta) in a cup of chicken broth and added that into the mix. It was hearty and moist. Thank you MizzNizz!
Very tasty and flavourful, yet seemed like watered down spaghetti sauce.  Like it was missing something...

Not bad but it could of used a few more vegetables, onions & green peppers maybe some beans, just seemed to much tomato.  I should of read the previous reviews first and maybe I would of thought to add more.
Overall, perfectly edible food.

I read the other reviews and added extra potatoes, but didn't have any other veggie on hand, so I stuck with the ones mentioned in the recipe. There wasn't much depth of flavor, even after I added chicken stock when I added the potatoes, but this IS a fantastic base. This is definitely something you want to build into your own dish - add veggies or whatever you usually add to other stews. Beans would be a good addition, but my bet would be kidney, not white. Also, serve it with crusty bread and it'll be much more satisfying
This made a hearty and scrumptious breakfast. We all loved it. Thanks for posting.

Wonderful simple morning tortilla!!!!  I made this as written but scaled the recipe down to 1/3 of the recipe.  I cooked it differently due to not having a lid for my small fry pan, so I cooked it the same until I poured in the eggs, then I put it into a 350 degree oven for 10 minutes and it turned out great.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.  Made for Newest Tag Game.

Yummy! We really enjoyed this quick and easy omelet. I only had 3 pieces of bacon, so I diced up a couple of pieces of leftover ham and added that to the pan. Also, I added 3 TBSP. of milk to the eggs when I whisked them together before adding them to the pan. I cooked this in a 10" cast iron skillet, so after adding the eggs to the pan I put the pan in the oven at 350 degrees for about 10 minutes or until the eggs were set. I served this with sour cream and salsa for a delicious, filling breakfast. Thank you for sharing!
**Made for 2012 Football Pool**
This is really good! I made it as written and it was just right. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2012.

Spanish make bocadillos or sandwiches by placing a piece between two pieces of a baguette. Or serve it as a tapa or appetizer. I  likes his with sour cream and salsa. So easy to do! I will definitely make this again. Thank You!! Grpa

I rarely have something this substantial for breakfast but overhead the geese are flying south in their chevrons, there is a thick frost on everything outside and all the ponds are frozen. This was warm, comforting and very enjoyable just like Pammy. This recipe was made in her memory. I'll miss her fun and happiness as well as all of her baked wonders that she used to throw to me from about a thousand miles away. What an arm that girl had, lol. RIP Pammy

I made this with turkey bacon.  I think it would have been better with regular bacon, but was still amazing. DH said - this is good and believe me, that is huge praise.   I made this  for Pammyowl's Cookathon.  Pam I  wish you were here to read your reviews.  You will be so  missed.
Very nice recipe. I did add 2 extra potatoes, but kept the rest as is. Made for pammyowl's Cook a Thon.

I love me a good Spanish omelet, and this one did not let me down.  I usually use cubes of ham, but now I know I prefer the flavor of the bacon.  This was a quick and easy weeknight dinner after we all had busy days.  The only thing I changed was to cut the raw bacon into small pieces, and then fry it.  I just find it a lot less messy when I do it that way.  Plus, I can discard any fat I don't want before it goes in the pan.  I served it with spicy salsa and some sour cream.  Made and enjoyed in Pammy's honor.  We'll miss you!

Hi Kittencal;
Well, you have done it again.  Another excellent, tasty and easy to make recipe.
I made these marvelous Onion Patties last nite and served them along with your Famous Coleslaw and Potato Latkes.
In addition, I made Chicken Strips served with Sweet and Sour Sauce.
WOW, what a delicious meal.
Thank you Kittencal, this is a must recipe from here on in.
"Uncle Bill"

recipes like this have converted me to loving onions! once upon a time i used to use onions only to accessorize dishes, now it can be the centerpiece of a dish - as it was with this great recipe. followed the recipe exactly and i agree with you that it's better than potato patties. DH was snapping his up even as i made it but i bided my time and had them with some ranch dip. will be making these again - thanks kittencal!

UNREAL. Ok, I love onions, but I never would have thought they could be THIS good. This is the kind of recipe that could make me a vegetarian. A vegetarian who only eats onions. Who only eats THESE onions. Slight alterations based on the commandments of my tongue and what I had on hand: I used one large yellow onion and three scallions, just a pinch of cayenne and both the optional ingredients - garlic powder and pepper. I fried them at about 275-300 degrees for roughly 6 minutes on each side until dark brown (the way God intended!), flattening them a bit before flipping. This goes right into my "Encore" cookbook with much appreciation to you, KITTENCAL!

Two complaints:  Not enough of them; no one to clean my pan.

These are delicious.  I've been making another recipe, but this is a keeper.  I'll double or triple the recipe next time, and have tons to freeze.

I've eaten half the recipe today, and I'm busting, but can't stop they are so good.
I made these as part of our Christmas/Hannukah meals and they were gone in record time!Thank you for a really delicious recipe.  I will make these often.

Delish!! Though I did feel my arteries do a jump start. I had really sweet onions, so cut the sugar back to only 2 teaspoons and was glad I did. Froze a few and tried them today, while running the oven.  Just as good. Thanks again, Kittencal for another great recipe.

Kitty, these onion patties are unbelievable! I can't get enough of these things there totally addicting, I made one recipe and then had to make another one, I ate one pan almost be myself, there are utterly wonderful! another great recipe, thanks Kitty.

Wow, another winner from Kittencal!  These really are wonderful.  I used half yellow and half sweet onion as that was all I had.  Next time I will use only the sweet onion.  The yellow is a bit too strong for us.  Can't wait to make it again.  Thanks again, Kittencal!

Kittencal....I made these for the evening meal tonight. They were excellent. I followed the recipe exactly except i cut it in half for 2 people. I will definitely make them again. Served them with bar-b-que ribs, home made hash browns and cole slaw. Thanks for an excellent recipe.
Jim

I was using up the onions I had in the fridge, so I finally decided to try these as they have been in my cookbook forever.  I am pleased to say that all of the reviews prior to this were correct!!  These are delicious and will satisfy the onion lover in you!  Very good, and thank you for a snack I will be making again, and again.
OMG these were wonderful!  I couldn't keep my DD out of them til dinner was done.  I've been planning to try this recipe for months and I'm so glad I finally did.  Thanks for a winner!
This was a quick and yummy way to have the taste of an onion ring when I was feeling to lazy to do all that work,lol.  Very yummy Kitten...I'm keeping this one and passing it on to my mom!

This was a great recipe.  I was craving onion rings and decided to try this recipe instead.  It went together easily with the help of my food processor.  I used a very large sweet onion and one medium yellow onion.  I also used skim milk (all I usually use).  I think the batter was a little looser than it was supposed to be, but they still fried up wonderfully.  It's a a good thing I went to the gym before I made this.  I will absolutely make this again!

Kittencal, I'm your biggest fan. These were excellent, and very hard to stop eating. My only problem was that I did not heed the warning about how much oil they soak up, and I'd pop 'em before they drained properly, resulting in a bit of a tummy ache. But I do plan to make these again, maybe with vegetable spray? Thanks for the posting!
These were so yummy..hubby insisted that  put this recipe in the "keeper" book! Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

These were very good.  I put mine in a food processor and it was very juicy and I had to add more flour..  did not have green onions so just used the white onions.  Son-in-law was here and wanted the recipe, said he was going to try it with cheese.  also, mine were not crisp, but very good anyway.

Oh Yeah - these were terrible (that's what we say when we want to make sure no one else takes any)!  I made these exactly as posted, but only fried half before the two of us ate dinner.  Thank goodness, because we would have eaten the whole batch if I had made them all.  So, after dinner, I fried the rest and froze them for another meal.  We thought these would be extra-tasty with a little sour cream, but let's not even GO there!  Thanks for a great keeper!!

OMG, these are to die for, Dh & I eat the whole thing. These are very easy to make, I used both the garlic and the pepper. I didn't fry them in as much oil, they were delicious anyway, maybe not as crisp. I will be making these again for sure and very soon. Thank you Kitten!!

Oh my, these were soooo good! I got 18 of these lovely babies for just 2 of us & we pigged out! If I can manage to hide the few leftover, I might try them as the base for a breakfast frittata tomorrow. Yum!

DEELY made this for our lunch today....I never would have thought to put this combination together but I'm so glad KITTENCAL did!!  THEY WERE AWESOME!

Thanks for sharing!  I'll be making these a lot in our future!

Kit, These were wonderful. Onion rings without the fuss AND they can be made ahead of time. I made these the morning of our fish fry and refrigerated them, layered between paper towel, until we started frying the fish. I just popped them in the oven at 350* for about 10 minutes. Perfect!!! Another winner sweety:).
Very tasty, we really enjoyed these.  Thanks for sharing!  Crabby
These were great!!  I will add to the 5 *'s of the other raters.  Taste reminds me of onion rings and much easier.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!!

I did not really know what to expect, but these patties were fluffy and pancake-like, and absolutely yummy and super simple to make. My onions were not the sweet kind, so they came out a little saltier than I liked, next time I will decrease the salt a little. Also, I barely used any oil and they fried up nicely. Thank you Kittencal.

These taste great without a doubt! But I had no flour (silly me) so I used a baking mix and I used the same measurements as for the flour and my patties didn't hold together very well, so I had a hard time making these at first, so I added in more baking mix and that seemed to help them stay together.And I think you really have to be careful in how much oil you use to fry these as they do take in A LOT of oil when cooking like Kittencal warns so I had to remove some of the oil with the first batch. I was eating them as I took them out of the pan they were delicious. Also I dont know about everyone else but it took me a while to chop up all those onions and I think it would have made it a lot easier if I had a food chopper type thing, so I don't know if I would make these all the time but they would be a great treat once in a while. I have to say I just found this site a couple day's ago and I think it is the best recipe site on the web. Thanks Kittencal for all of your great recipes ( I have made quite a few of yours already).
Oooh - these are really good.  I used fresh chives from the garden as I didn't have any green onions - otherwise, I made them as written.  My DH was delighted - he thought they were terrific too.

These were GREAT, Kittencal! Onion-loving hubby really loved these! I got about 16 3-4 inch patties with this recipe. I used 1% milk and used cooking spray on a nonstick griddle pan so we could enjoy these and not feel so guilty afterwards! :) This worked well and, like other reviewers have said, they are like onion rings without all the work! Thanks for a definite "keeper", Kit!
Absolutely loved them!  As a garlic lover, the only thing I did differently, was to mince fresh garlic in with the onions.  A real keeper!  Thanks, Kittencal!

Oh wow.  There is a reason these are currently in teh top 20 recipes for all of zaar.  These are excellent.  I used sweet vidalia onion (1 huge one), whole wheat pastry flour, and skim milk.  I used cooking spray on a griddle and we ate them with my homemade applesauce.  So fabulous!  Even the picky 6 year old ate one.  Enough said!

Great sidedish, hosted a party of 3 adults and 3 kids, and they were devoured in no time!! Far surpassed a dish I had tried from a fine cooking magazine. Used the vidalia onion, provided a nice sweet taste, not overly strong. Guests left with the recipe!!!

The recipe was so simple yet the taste was very good. These were best eaten hot out of the pan.  When they sat and became cold, they tended to be a little greasy.
Hmmm, maybe next time I will try them hot from the pan  topped with dollop of chilled apple sauce.

I just used PAM spray with no other oil in a non-stick pan.  Worked out fine.  Great flavor and was well received by my family.  I do think it needs a sauce (beyond ketchep which wasn't bad) of some sort to add a finsihing elegant touch.

WOW!!! I am kicking myself that I did not make these sooner! They are fantastic and simple to boot! I used three green onions, the optional garlic and black pepper. Of course I used the seasoned salt. My family went nuts! I am definitely going to invest in a chopper so we can have these more often. Dh said they reminded him of something his granny used to make. All I can say is the flavor and texture is fantastic!!! I have a feeling I will be making these ALOT!!!
These were great! Make sure you keep a constant temperature on your pan. I will make these on my electric griddle next time. Great recipe, thanks!

if you like onions, these are wonderful! perhaps due to the fact that i used a food processor to chop the onions, which actually makes them so small it is almost a sauce, my batter was to thin when i followed the recipe. when i added more flour though it turned out perfectly. GREAT side dish.
We will make these again,they are good.I just put very little oil in the pan and it worked out great.

Easy to make, perfect with out 4th of July holiday BBQ meal.  I forgot the sugar but I think they were superb as they were without it.  I also added just a touch more cayenne pepper because we like it so much.  My 7 year old son, who loves onions, couldn't get enough of these!  Thanks!  This is a keeper!

You know that sound Homer Simpson makes when he's thinking about food?  That's the only way I can describe these!!  I made the mistake of making them on my griddle and they turned out soft, like pancakes.  After my husband and I had eaten half the batch that way, I threw the rest into my cast iron frying pan and re-cooked them to their rightful crispiness.  Interesting how that extra little bit of grease can make them taste even better!!
These remind me so much of onion rings. They make a nice snack. I will definitely try it with zucchini one day.

Yummy! The idea of onion patties weren't very appealing to me, but from the moment they were out of the pan, I just couldn't stop popping them into my mouth. I used some garlic salt in place of regular salt, and added quite a bit of paprika because I didn't have any cayenne, but they turned out really good. My only gripe would be that they DO soak up quite a bit of oil - which made them all the yummier of course ;)
I have made these a few times now and they are sooooooo good and sooooo addicting! Its very hard to not eat all of the while you are cooking them. Thanks Kitten for great recipe!
Will make these often to keep my daughter happy!!Great taste. A real keeper!!
Girl!!! These are incredible!! I made them every day this week. My father BEGS ME to make these. The taste kind of reminds me of an onion ring but much much better..thanks so much for sharing
Have made these with regular onions and with half regular and half sweet onions (vidalias). Both very good and something different .

Oh my goodness, made these tonight for dinner and by the time we sat down to dinner I was full. I had to make sure they were good. :-) My hubby who doesn't like onions still gave them a 4 stars. I made a few changes, I did the onions in my little food processor so I had to add more flour and didn't use any cayenne. I can't wait to take some of the leftovers to my sisters house. This is a keeper.
These could not be any easier followed recipe to a T. Loved them!

Definitely great! I tried them with zucchini too (on the same say, couldn't wait) cause I wanted to freeze some for later. Managed to freeze just a couple, all the other patties (onion as well as zucchini) magically disappeared.... For the zucchini I used two medium, grated them coarsely and squeezed out most of the liquid. Did try another method of baking them in order to avoid too much oil. WOW and WOW again.
These were scumptious!! I will be making them often. Thanks

Very easy to make, I made them ahead, let them cool & then reheated them in the oven.  Served them with sour cream, tomato salad, french bread & glass of wine for a light summer dinner for drop in company.   Very yummy, none left on the plate. Our company loved them, wanted the recipe!  I will be making these again & again!

I love onions and these were like everyone else says..GREAT.  I started eating as soon as the first one came out of the pan, & didn't know when to stop.  Maybe I can manage to freeze some next time.
Thanks for a great recipe.

A keeper! I didn't fry my patties as suggested as when I saw how much oil the first lot had absorbed I didn't want to do anymore! I wiped my non stick pan with oil instead which worked fine. I found cooking this way made them gooey on the inside yum! We had these the nest day reheated in the oven and they were fab then too!

These were suprisingly sweet and delicious for a veggie side dish.  I used regular onions and did put in the garlic salt. When I got the mix good and compressed, I warmed up some milk chocolate in the microwave (only give it a ten second zap then remove it and stir well EACH time even if the chocolate doesn't seem to be melting. I used a small silicon pastry brush to brush melted chocolate on top of the compressed peanut butter mix.  Then it went into the refrigerator and I went out shopping.

Just made these last night. I was a little leery, since I've never had burgers with feta actually mixed into them before. But, oh, I'm glad I did! These were both flavorful and juicy - we didn't even know we were eating turkey! After grilling, I served them on bread (we're out of buns) with mayo, tomato and red onion slices. Delicious!

Like this needs another review, but... hey, here it is.  This recipe is AWESOME.  I added a dash of rosemary, and it was just perfect.  WE had ours on toasted buns with tziziki (I can never spell this right without looking it up), tomatos, and sliced onion.  The leftover two patties were AWESOME the next day cold, chopped up in a salad with tzatziki(closer?) for dressing.  Like a gyro salad.  Very versatile recipe.  Thanks!

This was so delicious!  We really enjoyed everything about this.  I omitted the olives but made it the same otherwise.  I served this with recipe#59336 and it came together perfectly.  Thanks for a keeper!

I made this exactly as is except I used 1 Tb fresh oregano, 1 Tb fresh parsley and omitted the dried basil.  I served on pita bread with tzatziki, red onions, tomatoes and lettuce and ended up removing it from the pita and eating it with just tzatziki.  The other ingredients just detracted from the burgers which were great on their own!  This is so good and will definitely become a regular recipe!
This wasn't bad.  Maybe I overcooked them, they were dry.  I don't think that I will make them again as there are many other burgers to try.
Very Good!  Served with cucumber-yogurt sauce...mmmm mmmm!  Did not use basil.
Awesome burgers.  The girlfriend said they were the best burger she's ever had!
This was great!! I made it for my boyfriend and some friends and they all loved it.  Best turkey burger recipe ever.
These were AMAZING. My whole family loved it! I served it on large egg bagels with dijon mustard, spinach, and tomato. The only problem was the patty tended to fall apart.

Oh My Goodness!!! And goodness they were.  These are another one of those recipes that you don't want to stop eating because they are so good.  But one burger per person was all we could handle.  Made exactly as directed but cooked on top of stove with a little olive oil.  Served on whole wheat bun with little mayo, thin sliced onion and home grown tomato.  So So So very good!
Wow, these are the best turkey burgers I have ever had and my husband agrees. I followed the recipe exactly using black olives.

What a great recipe!I used turkeybreast and chopped it very fine,there were no leftovers to freeze!
November 24th 2007
Just wanted to say that I still make these burgers on a regular basis and that the only thing I do different is that I use fresh garlic and parsley.
Many thanks for this recipe!!

Wow!  I have never tasted such a flavorful Turkey burger!  We used finely chopped cooked Turkey breast left over from Thanksgiving.  Because of this, the consistency was more like a sloppy joe, but it was still delicious.  My picky husband LOVED it!  Thank you!

I have had this in my cookbook for a LONG time and finally had a chance to make them tonight. I added some greek seasoning and thats the only change. Outstanding recipe and so quick to throw together. I didnt find the feta or olives overpowering at all. Thanks for a great recipe!

These are GREAT! I use a bit less feta, omit the olives, and use fresh grated onion instead of the onion powder. I have served them as you would a regular burger and also in pitas w/ tzatziki sauce, tomatoes, and onions. This has become my favorite recipe anytime we grill burgers!!!

This was a great way to add flavor to turkey burgers! I didn't have italian seasoning and I also used fresh garlic and onions in place of onion and garlic powders. Would definitely make again, thanks!

Another 5 Stars!  I used finely minced onions and garlic instead of the powders and added salt since I used regular black olives which don't have much salt in them.  I made them on the stove top and they stayed juicy.  I can't wait to make them again.  Thanks for sharing this delicious recipe.
This recipe was YUMMY, I omitted the olives (not a fan) and made a great tzatziki sauce and put it on a Weight Watchers english muffin-toasted...a delicious healhty meal

Loved this recipe! The whole family enjoyed this meal. I followed the recipe exactly, except I fried them on the stove because weather didn't permit grilling - they were fabulous.  Thanks for a great recipe.
I will try freezing these. I have made them several times and they are soo delicious. thank you

I made these and put them in pita with red onion tomato and lettuce and mayo.  I served them with Kittencal's best ever greek salad and hummus.  My husband said it was the best dinner he has ever had.  I don't ordinarily care for burgers, particularly home made.  I even loved these.  I made them twice last week and will make them twice again this week.  They freeze well also.
Thank you so much.

This was the BEST burger of any type of meat I have EVER had! I used the pre-packaged 85/15 Turkey. I included the Basil. The burgers rested in the fridge for about an hour before pan-frying in olive oil and 1/2 tbs butter. I lightly salted the exterior only of the turkey burger. To Serve: I brushed Whole Grain White buns with olive oil and sprinkled with toasted Italian Seasoning left on the pan after baking some waffle fries, then toasted buns in oven. I served with tomato, red onion, mayo, tahini & bread n butter pickles. It was SO good!

4 out of 5 because I didn't follow the recipe to the T.

I didn't have any italian seasoning on hand and didn't use the olives. I did substitute fresh parsley and onion for the dried/powdered variety.
