Served it with some tzatziki in a pita with more feta, fresh parsley, lettuce and tomatoes.  Delish!
Really liked these a lot and my husband loved them.  Made some with and some without olives and both were good.  I included the basil and I wouldn't change a thing!  Very good.  Thank you.

My DH can't say enough about these burgers!!  We had to pan-fry them, but they were still wonderful!  DH is counting calories, so I made 6 thin patties instead of the 4.  Thank you!!  I know we will be making these again!

These were awesome!!!! I only changed a few things, I used fresh herbs b/c we happened to have them and fresh onions and garlic.  We served these with the tahini in onion pita pockets and we will definitely be having these again!

Wow. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.  It is absolutely delicious. A definite keeper in my permanent collection.  It is so good that my family ate two burgers each.  Me too. :)  I didn't have the olives but it didn't matter.

We really enjoyed these. IIts a great alternative to the normal hambrger. I thought that  it called for way too much feta cheese, but it was perfect and not overpowering. Will definately make again. Thanks
I used bison with this recipe and it was fantastic!  My husband loved these burgers and we both enjoyed them just as much left over. Thanks for sharing.  Delicious.

This was simple, easy and very flavorful.  I used kalamata olives instead of salad olives.  Even though it is packed with spices, no one ingredient is overpowering.  I will definitely make this again.
Absolutely perfect!

Yummy, Thick, Juicy, These are the BEST Burgers I have ever eaten. Followed the recipe exactly except I left out the Olives. Perfection with the seasonings, and who could forget about the FETA, OMG Soooo  Good...

I used this recipe for my first experience with ground turkey.  I picked a WINNER.   Such flavor and moistness!  The only change I made was using black olives instead of green.  Great recipe, Najwa, thanks for sharing with us!

As a former beef eater, I had almost given up on finding a good turkey burger recipe - until I tried this one.  The scent, flavor and texture of these burger were excellent.    I even ate one cold, right out of the refrigerator.  It smelled so good, I couldn't wait to eat it, so I didn't even bother to heat it up.  Thank you for an outstanding recipe.

I decided to "try something new" and this was a wise choice! Instead of turkey, though, I used ground chicken. This was absolutely delicious and a recipe I'll use many times over...Next time I'm going to use 1/4 C. chopped kalamata olives and 1/4 C. chopped green olives, but keep everything else the same...I don't want to mess with an already good recipe!

WONDERFUL!  I added the basil and made exactly as stated.  I grilled them over a charcoal fire and had them on whole wheat buns with tomato, lettuce, and mayo.  HEAVEN!  The only thing I would do differently next time is to toast the bun before assembling.  I've been trying to eat healthy and with this recipe I believe I am accomplishing that goal!  Thank you!

Very Good!!  Like other readers, I have been trying to eat healthier, thereby giving up red meat.  Needed a burger and decided to try these. I am glad I did.  Very quick and easy to make .  Will be making these again.  ThX

Good Idea! These burgers were flavorful and moist.  I added some Worcestershire Sauce, which make turkey taste a little more beefy.  I also chopped some Kalamata olives and used sauteed onions.  I served them with a homemade cucumber yogurt sauce on pita bread. Excellent meal!
These were fantastic! My very picky 4yr old loved them!! Will be making again. Thank you so much for a great turkey burger recipe

Wow! These turned out so good! The only thing I did differentley was I used ground turkey breast. These were so very easy, and my kids absolutley loved them! My son wants me to make them again tommorow! This is a definate keeper at our house! Thanks so much for a great recipe!

Easy and super flavorful.
I used all white-meat turkey and reduced-fat feta to further reduce the fat content - and you couldn't tell at all. So much flavor from the olives and the feta!
Thanks for an awesome recipe!
mmmm, delicious.  We made just as directed, except we halved the recipe to make 2 burgers.  Will make again often!

The whole family loved these!!  I loved the feta and olive flavor, and all the herbs.  Even my 4 year old ate more than he has in a while!  They were easy to make too.  I served them on homemade buns with tzatziki sauce and tomatoes.

I have to admit, I was skeptical about this recipe.  I've never had a tasty turkey burger before, but these were delicious.  I used the 4 1/2 ounce can of chopped olives and was afraid that's all I'd be able to taste, but I really couldn't taste them at all.

Hmmm turkey burgers. Well I made them last night and really did enjoy them. Would have loved them even more had my husband not over charred the outside (sigh). 
Here is the sauce I made to go with them. 2 cups plain yogurt, 3 chopped green onions, 2 cloves garlic made into paste with salt (a good technique to learn), pepper and about 1/2 tsp dried mint leaves.
This sauce would also be good with pita chips. Thanks for a very tasty recipe!
These were fabulous!  I served them with sweet potato fries...perfect dinner!

I can't believe I finally found a turkey burger my husband likes! I made 2 patties with green olives with pimentos (I wasn't sure what salad olives are) and 2 without because my husband does not like them. I was worried that they would dry too quickly on the grill so I pan fried them covered for a few minutes on each side. Served with Recipe #296559 and dijon mustard like suggested by another reviewer. Thanks for a tasty recipe!
Absolutely EXCELLENT!!  I have made these many times and everyone loves them.  I used 94% lean ground turkey and reduced fat feta cheese.

This is one of the first recipes I ever tried from Zaar two years ago.  I can't believe I never rated it.  It easily deserves 5 stars.  We've had these burgers many, many times.  The flavor is absolutely intense.  I usually thaw a box of frozen spinach, squeeze out the water and add that to the other ingredients.  Thank you for sharing!!

These were EXCELLENT!  I made them with extra lean ground turkey and lightly sprayed the burger w/ olive oil cooking spray while grilling to give some extra moisture and that worked out very well.  Also, we didn't cook them all right away and they tasted even better after sitting uncooked in the fridge for a couple of days- stronger flavor.  Great burgers for 1st time turkey burger eaters!  You won't be disappointed!
Family loved these... minus the olives.  I followed recipe but used only 1 4oz package of feta.  I also pan fried in olive oil and finished at 400 in the oven.  Delicious.

these were so gooooood. my picky turkey burger  boys even loved them. they had a great flavor i had a little over a pound of meat and i still doubled the spices the flavor of them were moist and delicious. thanx this is a keeper.

We had a huge turkey frozen from Thanksgiving, so we thawed it, separated it, removed the bones, and ground everything but one breast (we'll be roasting that).  We used the freshly ground meat to make these burgers, and we were quite pleased with how they turned out.  Good texture and flavor.  We served them with feta cheese and tomatoes on plain old hamburger buns. Yummy!

Treated some friends to this and Kittencal's Famous Greek Salad
Recipe #66596 last night for dinner and what a treat it was! Everything was freat served on onion or potato buns and plates were cleaned. Thank you for posting!
Hubby loved this made with Kalmata olives.  I used low-fat Feta because that's what I had but would recommend regular Feta to get the cheese to melt and become creamier.

These are something that my husband has requested that I make again.  He loved them and so did I...very easy to make.  Just heated some pita bread, topped with some mayo, cucumber slices, lettuce, and dinner was done.  Thanks for the recipe.

This recipe has become one of my regulars.  It's low in fat and high in protein.  We like to serve it broken down like taco meat and served in a pita with lettuce tomato and miracle whip.  

This freezes well and thaws beautifully for those nights when you just don't have very much time.
This was wonderful...really easy, and quick...I used fresh garlic, parsley and grated onion in the place of dried, I used the stove top grill pan, and it worked out well! thanks for the recipe!

My husband and I love Greek food especially after living next door to our Greek landlord when we were in Germany (yeah, I know).  I had 1/2 lb of ground turkey and 1/2 lb of ground pork in my freezer I needed to use which really helped the flavor and the consistency (turkey tends to crumble).  I only added 1/2 c of feta and it still had great flavor.  I served it with Tzatziki (recipe #310246) which was a perfect compliment to the flavor of the burger.  Delicious!

We sure did enjoy these burgers as a break from the everyday. They're missinig something, though. I used an everyday oil and vinegar with lemon and Greek spices (oregano, spearmint, etc) to use on my bun (rather than condiments), and that helped for me. We ate them with tomato and lettuce. YUM! Thanks for the recipe!!
My husband and I loved these burgers.  We are new to using ground turkey and just beginning to accumulate recipes.  This is definitely a keeper!

This was so, so good!!  Even my husband who claims to hate ground turkey said these were really good.  I'm eating the left overs right now.  I love the olives in this recipe.  I topped them with recipe#310246.  I will be making these often.  Thanks for sharing!

I have tried to find a way for us to like turkey burgers, and I must say this is it!  These are fantastic!  Ate them on a crusty bun with mayo, lettuce and tomato.  Really want to try them with the cucumber sauce, thanks for a great recipe!

We really enjoyed this!  DH does not like olives at all, so I only did them in half.  I used kalamata olives and I really thought they added dimension to the patty.  I served the burgers with a sour cream/granulated garlic/lemon juice/salt/pepper spread I made up, as well as some thick slices of fresh cucumber.  We ate them on whole wheat buns.  Next time we will definitely have thin slices of red onion as well.  Thanks so much, dinner tonight was great!!

These are fantastic. We made them as noted ine recipe but with slightly more turkey and got 5 burgers out of the 1.25 pounds of turkey. We increased everything except the feta because I only had a cup of cheese, but they were delicious this way and slightly lower in calories. We also used low-fat feta.
Excellent! Did not eat with buns- but server greek salad on the side. Even DH said they were good!

I am the worse ever!  Cannot believe I never rated!!  50 lashes...

AWESOME!!!  Seriously, I wasn't sure DH would like the feta, but he did and so did everyone else.  We have used ground turkey, ground pork and ground chicken.  No matter what kind of meat, they are always tender and juicy...

Thank you SO much

Delicious! I served these on olive rosemary wheat bread with baby spinach and roma tomatoes as garnish, and fresh lemon-garlic green beans on the side. The burgers were so moist and tender that we didn't need condiments.

I pan-fried mine and used the basil. Note that when you pan-fry turkey burgers, you need to squeeze the liquid out of the ground turkey first; otherwise they puff up while cooking and are kind of gross.
Oh my... these were so good!  My 19 month old who doesn't eat anything loved this! THANKS!!!

Absolutly Wonderful!  I've been trying to start eating healthier and with a recipe as good as this, I don't miss the fast food at all. Seriously.  I made greek potatoes with this #87782.  This is definatly a keeper.

Oh Wow! I made this exactly as posted, and it was fabulous.  I ate this on Arnold Select Sandwich Thins, something new I found at the grocery store. These sandwich thins were a cross between a pita and a hamburger bun, perfect for this burger!  Next time I'll throw some cucumbers and sliced onions on the bun with the burger.  And mix up some tzatziki sauce to use instead of the mayo.  Thanks so much for posting this recipe.  I loved it!  I made this for Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup Tag!

Wow! This was so awesome! I wasn't expecting this to taste as wonderful as it did. I'd give it more than 5 stars. I didn't even use the full cup of Feta. Man, these are good!!  No wonder they are rated so high.  I did not have any feta and used swiss cheese instead. They still tasted delicious.  Next time I will try the feta so they will authentic.  Reminds me of having a gyro on a bun. Mmmm!
I crumbled turkey so it was easy to measure! It was great over salad with a dab of sour cream! I did not add feta lowering the sodium count. It was great with out the feta!
Very quick and tasty mid week meal. Served on toasted turkish bread with lettuce, tomato and mayo. Will use fresh garlic and onion next time for a bit more bite.

Very tasty. I ate it as is with a side of asparagus.  I also used Ground Chicken as that's all that was left. To cook my burgers I pan fried them, then popped them in the oven for about 10 minutes to cook the insides. Loved it! Thank you very much for the simple recipe. :)

We ate these tonight and oh my goodness. These are so good. Anyone who passes this recipe up is missing out!! My husband and I were so happy with these and our 16 month old was too. Awesome. We are definitely making these again!!! 
Oh I used chopped red onion instead of powder. YUM.
I'd give this 7 stars if I could. Wow.
Was afraid that they would be overly seasoned, but they were terrific! A tad salty from the olives, but overall great with a little low-fat mayo, crisp romaine on a grilled whole wheat bun.

WOW we had these for dinner last night and hubby even loved them.  What gandmothers won't do for their kids. These were great - i also added a little sauteed spinach to the burgers - part of another recipe i had for Weight Watchers - these were great - also works to broil them on a rainy day - not as much fat as pan frying

These were very good- the spices were just right. However, I wished they had more of the feta cheese taste.This is just a personal thing. I think next time, I'll also add some feta to the top of the burgers just before taking off the grill.
Delish, used Kalamata olives and even my hubby loved it and he hates it when I mess with "the burger".

So good! I'm a beef girl but both me and the bf are trying to be healthier so I figured I would give this a try. This recipe will make our regular rotation.  Used 6 oz. of reduced fat feta and kalamata olives.  Served on whole wheat buns.  Wasn't sure what to serve with it so we just had tator tots.  Had 1.25 lbs of turkey so I made 5 generous patties.  Thanks for sharing!

We love these burgers.  They are easy to throw together and we usually have most of the stuff on hand.  My non-red-meat-eating mother loves coming to our house for cookouts now.  They don't taste like a hamburger, they are their own delicious thing.
We really like these! I was surprised by how good they are!
Outstanding burger, very flavorful!
What can I say that hasn't been said - best turkey burgers!! Did use ground chicken though!! ;) And did add maybe 1/4 cup of breadcrumbs.  Made the rest as is! Thanks for a keeper! :)

Used 1 1/4 lbs. of 93% turkey and adjusted all seasonings proportionately except for the feta (about 4 oz.) and olives. Ate with whole wheat buns, a slice of onion and homemade tzatziki with a side of simple salad with more tzatziki on top.  Delicious taste reminiscent of gyro meat, juicy and tender. Thanks for an awesome turkey burger recipe! My husband, who is a die-hard cheeseburger fan, was also very impressed. We served ours with avocado, fresh spinach, tomato, and mustard. This will be our official turkey burger recipe from now on.

DELICIOUS!  We thoroughly enjoyed these.  I used thin buns, similar to pitas and added mayo.  They were wonderful.  Wouldn't change a thing.

AWESOME and EASY! I'm not normally a fan of turkey burgers because most seem so bland but this recipe has changed my mind. I really enjoyed making and eating this! I served inside half pitas with tzatziki sauce, tomatoes, lettuce and cucumbers. Thanks for a great recipe najwa! This will be going into my "favorites".
Great burgers.  I did use chicken that I ground myself and served with Recipe #93401, Recipe #66596 and for dessert, Recipe #326367.  Great Greek meal.

Great burgers!  Made as written with the exception of using fresh basil and parley (1 Tbs each) from my little balcony garden, rather then dried.  They held together nicely and were full of flavor.  Thanks najwa!
This recipe is wonderful! I made it after church, with homemade baked french fries and it was a hit! It's so easy and the herbs and feta give the turkey a great flavor!
Wonderful! I used mozzarella instead of feta because I don't like feta (I'm a weakling) and nixed the olives bc SO doesn't like them. These were sooooo good!!! Thanks, Najwa!
These were super delicious. Stuck closely to the recipe, loose measurements and it was an easy, quick meal. yum.
I have been making these since 6/07 and have loved it everytime. Occ adding fresh ground turkey and 1 egg. Everyone I have served has asked for the recipe.
fantastic. used fresh herbs, kalamata olives, served with tzaziki sauce on my favorite flatbread.  these are so full of flavor! this is a keeper!!

I didn't have Feta cheese, but I had everything else, so I substituted shredded parmesan (bagged) in place of Feta and all I can say is THANK YOU! These were great! Very moist and delicious! I was going to submit a photo, but I was hungry and...hey don't judge me! :-)
These were great! I used all fresh herbs from the garden, chopped onion and omitted the olives, very good!

This is my new favorite burger. I added some Lawry's salt and black pepper and McCormick's greek seasoning to the meat. As another reviewer I chopped fresh parsley to add.
I topped with garlic aioli.
This burger will be in the rotation!!

Did I not review these yet?  We have made them a dozen or so times since I discoverd this recipe over the summer!  We like them best cooked in olive oil in a skillet on the stove.  That way all the little bits of goodness stay in the burger and don't fall down into the grill!  These are our new favorite burger!!!
A flavorful burger for sure. Cooked it in a frying pan and wasn't the same. Would make again, especially on the grill. Cut the burger in half and stuffed inside whole wheat pitas.
Fabulous!  We loved these burgers.  Thanks so much for the recipe, we will be making these often!

these are my absolute new favorite.  very flavorful indeed.  i make the recipe as is and only add the olives to half as my husband won't eat them. I usually do these on a grill pan on the stove.  Delicious!

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this yet.  We love them.  I make a few minor changes.  I just cook it in the pan and instead of patties, I scramble the hamburger. My husband and 14 year old really liked these so did I.  I made them per recipe and used a grill pan.  I really wouldn't change a thing.  both DH and DD are asking when I'll be making them again.  Thank you for posting this recipe.
These were terrific!  A turkey burger with tons of flavor.  I made some tzatziki with fat free yogurt and served this on sandwich thins. Satisfying, healthy, and fits in my diet plan!
These were awesome!  Everyone loved them.  I will definately be adding this into our regular rotation for favorite meals. Thanks najwa!

I have been planning on making these burgers after I got some lean turkey on sale.  I followed the recipe except I omitted the olives. This recipe deserves the fantastic reviews and I encourage others to make these burgers.  I did cook them in an electric skillet as my grill seems to always break my burgers apart.
Thank you for posting.

DH didn't sound too thrilled when he asked what was for lunch and I told him greek turkey burgers. I had made greek burgers using a different zaar recipe. I made these for friends, and they have passed the recipe on to their parents. Now, his mom is obsessed with them and makes them all the time. Careful to not cook to long as the turkey can dry out easily. The spicing is excellent though I like to add some fresh garlic.

These are so good! I'm not a huge burger fan in general, but these are hard to resist. They are so flavorful and moist. I've topped them with Tzatziki, hummus, Miracle Whip, all with great results. Even my kids (age 5 and under) love them!

Delicious! I used tomato, basil flavored feta cheese and kalamata olives. The burgers were juicy and flavorful. I stuffed grilled pita pockets with half a burger, hummus, tomato, red onion and lettuce. This will be a permanent addition to my summer recipe book!

Very good change for turkey burgers!! I added a galic clove and used low fat feta cheese to save on a few calories. Perfect in between sandwich thins topped with mayo or roasted red pepper hummus. These will absolutely be made again.
With so many ratings already, this hardly needs another.   Made per the recipe - just delicious!
Excellent!  Used kalamata olives, followed the recipe exactly.  Served in a folded pita with hummus, red onion, tomato and cucumber. Wouldn't change a thing!  Very good!

Being Greek myself, these are great. I added chopped kalamata olives as Bubba'sMommy suggested. Next time I'll try adding minced fresh basil, parsley and mint, red onion, a little olive oil and lemon juice, and sea salt.

Wow what flavour! DH and I *loved* these so much!! I used light feta, cocktail olives stuffed with pimento (is this the same as salad olives?), and 1/2 tsp of dried basil. I cooked them on a Griddler and served them up on whole wheat buns with tomato, lettuce and mayo. I used this recipe to cook breakfast for about 60 people at a family reunion camping trip. I had 4 large pots of boiling water going and found that if you roll the bag up loosely around the egg in the bottom before you put it in the pot it was easier to deal with.  Everyone absolutely raved about it.  You could also prepare individual bags and tuck them away in ice chest for easy camping meal. I wanted to make a comment that Ziploc and Reynold's both do not recommend using their bags for boiling.  Hopefully there would be no ill effects but the bag will melt slightly in boiling water (even the freezer bags) and plastic could leech into your food causing potential carcinogens.

I found this article at sacbee.com that claims Rival Seal a Meal one-quart vacuum storage bags and Food Saver VacLoc Vacuum Packaging Bags are both safe for boiling, it will say so on the box. Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe!  The kids (ages 4 & 7) made omelettes with us this past weekend and had a blast. Our spread included diced tomatoes, onions, red bell pepper, mushrooms, grated cheddar cheese and crumbled bacon.  Using permanent marker (and supervision) we had the oldest write our names on each of the ziplock bags while the youngest counted and handed us two eggs at a time for each omlette. The cooked omelettes slid out of the ziploc bags with ease and not only did they look impressive (better than any pan cooked omelette I've made in awhile), they tasted great too!  Both of our kids ate their omelettes exclaiming that theirs tasted 'better' then the other, because... they made it :).  I found it unnecessary to add milk to keep the eggs moist, they were plenty moist and fluffy on their own. 

Just a few notes I'd like to add of my own:

I did most of the prep work the evening before to save time and placed everything in their own small tupperware container.  Going forward, we will use diced ham instead of bacon - it's just easier and there's less work involved.  I'll be dicing left over vegetables from other meals to keep in the freezer that we can use later on in our 'omelettes".  I always seem to have that extra half an onion or crown of brocoli that doesn't get used but sits in the fridge past its prime - just seems like an easy way to use them up.

Regarding cooking in Ziploc bags - it's safe.  Ziploc does not use BPA in it's plastic products and they are also Dioxin free.  The emails circulating claiming that Ziploc's own site warns against cooking in their storage bags are false (I checked their site to confirm if this was true and found that Ziploc addresses that email as 'misleading' and goes on to explain the criteria needed in order to form dioxide - neither of which is likely to happen from your microwave or boiling in water since you need the combinations of both chloride and temperatures of 1,500 deg F).  Just be sure to keep an eye on the bags and try and keep them away from touch the sides of the pan during cooking.  Our bags held up just fine, no melting or softening of the plastic.  Water also does not need to be at a rolling boil to cook in.  Turn it down to medium heat before adding the ziploc bags.

Something a little different for us, I served it with some warm golden syrup. I particularly liked the crunchy outside bits.

So I sprinkled some powdered sugar on it, and put some syrup on the plate to dip it in, and told them it was called Dutch Babies. I didn't mention they had eggs in it. Well, they ate two helpings! This was good. I liked the crispy edges, they liked the middle. This is one of the strangest recipes I've made, but definitely a keeper. Next, I'll try it with berries. Thanks for a keeper.

I have made this a few times now and have just forgotten to rate it.  It is fantastic!  I have served it with just the powdered sugar and the kids just love it.  I have a little one who is under a year so we use the sugar instead of the honey.  I'm sure it's great with the honey but it is wonderful with the sugar.  And we used all 4 eggs.  Thank you for the delicious recipe!

Fabulous!  Just wonderful for my diabetic DH who misses his pancakes. I replaced the suger, and confectioners sugar with Splenda and my Dutch Baby came out perfect.  He loved it and wants it for dinner, too.  
 Splenda Confectioner's Sugar recipe can be found on splenda.com.

AWESOME!!  I surprised my brand-spanking new husband with this Valentine's Day morning, and I think he almost cried he was so happy/excited to start mowing this down!  He had talked of them (OHOP) LOTS, and I really didn't think I would be able to find the recipe anywhere, but... wha-lah!  I'm going to try a tsp. of vanilla for a little more depth, and the second time I made them, I decreased the butter to just under 3 T, and it tasted the same.  If you have only eaten these with syrup, fruit filling, etc., you HAVE to try w/ lemon and powdered sugar.  These cannot be any better, period.  Thanks!!!
I served mine with maple syrup. Delish! Very easy to make and one I will be making again. Thank you for posting!
Very good!  Went together very easily and left me free to relax while it cook.  I need to watch it more closely next time, it got a little bit to brown around the edges.
i didnt try this recipe but i make one just like it and we serve ours with carmalized apples and cheddar cheese these are my favorite things
What a yummy treat!  We all enjoyed this very much, especially me as it was so simple to prepare and we all love the spectacular results.
This is the second time I've made your recipe. I've made others and I don't like them as much. Maybe it's the sugar in yours that I like? Anyway, we really enjoy this simple breakfast!

This was my first time making dutch babies (never heard of them before).  I thought it tasted like a big, fat crepe.  The cake itself was rather bland.  Next time, I would add some vanilla into the mix.  I did sprinkle it with powdered sugar and served with syrup.  Thank you for a quick breakfast meal idea.
Excellent! Even my picky toddler cleaned her plate! I added a dash of ginger and cinnamon, probably about tsp-ish each.

At my son's request, we had breakfast for dinner last night. I didn't really feel like flipping pancakes or french toast.  Then I came across this recipe - I'd never heard of "Dutch Babies".  I added a tiny bit of cinnamon and it was all puffed up and PERFECT in the exact 25 minutes.  All I can say is my husband and kids were in HEAVEN.  I did happen to have some strawberry sauce, whipped cream, powdered sugar etc... so we had a fun little dinner with sides of eggs, fruit and sausage.  YUM!  They have already requested this one again - my husband said it tasted to him almost exactly like french toast.  Thanks for posting such an easy and family-pleasing recipe!!!!

I made this with sugar but will try it next time with honey. This was the best looking dutch baby I have ever made, and we have them several times a month. This had great flavor but I like my dutch babies with a bit of cinnamon and nutmeg which I will add next time. Great recipe ... definately a keeper!
Easy and yummy!Thank you!

WOW! I have never had a Dutch Baby before, but this has such great reviews, I had to try it. It was really easy to mix up. I used honey instead of sugar and I put it in my cast iron skillet. It was also really cool to watch while it was baking! My toddler loved it! We put maple syrup on ours, and when he tasted it, he said "mmm, tasty!". I will make this again and again! Thanks!
I've made this several times in the past couple of weeks.  Easy to make and the kids LOVE watching them deflate :)

This is my first ever dutch babie ( eating and tasting) and it was pretty good. I didn't know what to expect and was amazed at it. The taste is a little tough but good none the less. It reminds me of a cross between a waffle and french toast. I put some powdered sugar and fruit ( cut up strawberries, a clementine, two teaspoons of strawberry preserves and a dash of memon juice). I used a 9x9 square pan and that worked out fine. Thanks :)

Well this is what happens when I spend time browsing through the day's new pictures and reviews -- I just HAD to make this recipe!  So going overboard as usual, I made two versions, one sweet and one savory.  I left out the sugar in the savory version.  In both recipes I used 1/2 cup all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup whole wheat pastry flour.  I only used 2 Tablespoons of butter for each, but used all 4 eggs in each, and loved the eggy custard centers.  For the sweet one I topped it with by own recipe#254642 and a sprinkling of powdered sugar over the edges.  For the savory one, I topped it with feta cheese crumbles and sauteed veggies (onions, garlic, mushrooms and diced yellow bell pepper).  They were both AMAZING!  But if I had to choose, then honestly I just adored the savory one, and would happily eat it with different veggies on a repeat performance very soon!  My DH, when asked to rate it on a 1-5 scale, gave it a 6.  This is going into my weekend breakfast rotation -- Thanks kiwidutch for adopting this keeper!

Loved these! I made the popover version in a muffin tin, it was nice to have little individual ones. Squeezed lemon and sprinkled powdered sugar over, so left the sugar out of the batter. I also cut the butter back to 2 tablespoons, and it was still delicious!

This was really good. I pureed some strawberries and raspberries and added it to the batter. Needless to say I had to cook it for a few more minutes. I then mixed the rest of those two berries with low fat plain yogurt and used it as a topping. It really went well like that, and was enjoyed by everyone.
This was like having Yorkshire Pudding for breakfast so it went down well as I love the stuff! The only difference was that this seemed to "explode" more - great fun!

This tasted a lot better than the restaurant. It puffed up & seemed lighter & not as dense. Served it with lots of lemon & powdered sugar. The DH & I could'nt believe how easy it was to make at home. We no longer have to go out to have dutch babies!
My family loves these, I have made them several times.  I forget how good they are and easy to make.  Thanks for the reminder.

This is great, we've had it for dessert twice now and I need to make double next time.  I used 3 eggs and less butter as recommended, and served sprinkled with icing sugar.  I may try with 2 eggs and 2 tablespoons of custard powder next time.  Thanks for sharing.
Good! Made as directed with sugar but made batter in the blender. A nice base for fruit or powdered sugar and lemon. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This was quite nice actually. Only 1 serve, i halfed the recipe, used 1 large egg, 1 tbs butter which was PLENTY, it sat in the middle and i drained it after cooking. I made a blueberry/cranberry syrup which was nice but the cranberry added a sour touch to it & i would have preferred it to be sweeter. So next time i'll probably make a plain blueberry or strawberry sauce. I used a small deep 5-6 inch oven-proof dish, my dutch baby rose high and ended up thicker in the center rather than flat. The inside was of thick dense consistency, sort-of cheesecake-like. And im happy with just the one egg as it didnt over-power. I'm getting the urge to experiment with this and add a nice cheese to the mixture and make it a savoury type dish you can have for brunch.

What a great treat for a special breakfast!  I doubled and baked in my 4 quart braiser pan. The Dutch Baby was quite impressive rising  high in the oven, making a bowl shaped appearance, browning beautifully along the edges.  Once removed from the oven, the Dutch Baby quick collapses when exposed to room temperature.  I loved the egg-y  richness and texture!  I served with real maple syrup and blackberries sprinkled on top with powdered sugar for a special treat!  I will remember this recipe when having guests I really want to impress!  Thanks so much, kiwidutch!

This takes me v=back to my younger days when me and my buddy would get drunk and crash at his sister's place. She would make these for us for breakfast.  These are as good as my foggy memory recalls them to be. Now my little girl likes to sit in front of the oven and watch them puff up while cooking. This has got to be on of the easiest breakfast foods there is.  Thanks for the recipe. I have been wanting these for years.
I loved this recipe!  It tastes like french toast, but looks like something you'd serve at a fancy brunch.  I make mine with the 4 eggs, and sprinkle with syrup and powdered sugar.

Thank you for such a treat!  If you like your french toast a little soggy or not quite done, you will love this!  I made 1/2 the recipe and used an ovenable 6 or 7 inch frying pan!  It turned out well in close to 20 minutes!  I slid it onto a plate and doused with powdered sugar!  It was wonderful!  I used about 2 Tbsp of butter and it was perfect.  The butter on top was soaked up by the powdered sugar.  I had never heard of Dutch Babies but was intrigued and the reviews made me need to try it!  Thanks again for another keeper!

The husband really liked this.  He even asked about how hard it was to make. That means he liked it enough to try and make it himself. :-) It was a little too eggy for me...but i don't really like french toast for the same reason. i know i'll be making this many times in the future. Thanks for the recipe!
This is definitely the best such recipe I've tried.

I had never made or had tried a Dutch Baby Pancake and was very excited to try this interesting dish.  I decided to try it out on just myself first, so cut the recipe to serve one.  This worked out perfectly!!  I used a mini pryrex baking dish, which I put in the preheated oven for about 5 mins., then added butter and swirled it around to coat the bottom and sides, then poured in the batter.  It cooked perfectly in 20 mins.  The only difference I made was to cut back slightly on the butter (approx. 1/2-3/4 Tbsp).  I served mine with just some powdered sugar, but next time plan to serve it with fresh strawberries and whipped cream!!
Made for PRMR tag.

Yummy breakfast.  Easy to do.  I used 4 eggs and then read about using only 3 eggs.  I'll try it another time with 3 eggs.  But I still enjoyed it a lot with maple syrup.  I used skim milk, no salt, splenda instead of sugar and 3 tablespoon of unsalted butter.  Thanks Kiwidutch.  Made for Please Review My Recipe.

Having checked out all the photographs before making this recipe, Susiecat too's photograph with savoury ingredients just jumped out from all the others, so I then hunted through the 80 reviews to find her review and basically made my Dutch Babies along the same lines, but I added some herbs: thyme, rosemary and sage! I totally agree with her son's rating of this savoury version as a 6. Just so superby delicious, and certainly a recipe that I'll make again. And I will try the sweet version at some stage - with berries. So glad to have found this recipe: thank you kiwidutch! Made for PRMR!
I definitely recommend cutting the numer of eggs to 3. Otherwise, this is very yummy.
We really liked these.  I topped ours with strawberries and bananas.  We didn't add any syrup or powdered sugar.  We didn't need too.  Thank you for sharing with us.

I'm surprised I haven't reviewed this recipe yet. I have made it several times. I'd never had Dutch Babies before. But my girls and I love them! Just fixed it this morning for my mom who is visiting and she said it's better than regular pancakes. I bake in a cast iron skillet for about 22 minutes. We like it with powdered sugar, berries and real maple syrup on top. Unfortunately, no berries today - out of season. But still great anyway!

I've never had this before but boy I don't think I'll be making pancakes or french toast again! This is very tasty and for me, surprisingly filling.  I made this with 3 eggs and 3 tablespoons of butter as well as whole wheat pastry flour and the results came out identical if not similar to the lovely photos of it. I used a metal pie pan and stuck it in the oven with the butter to melt it down for 2-3 minutes.  In the future I will stick the pan in the oven before making the batter, then add the butter to the pan after my batter is finished.  I loved the crispy outer edges and the soft interior. I ate this with a squeeze of lemon and a teaspoon of honey.  I think this would also be fabulous with a simple lemon glaze made with powdered sugar.  I'll have to try that next time!   This is great, thank you!

These were pretty good, but I should've listened to the other reviewers' suggestions and cut down on the butter and eggs. I think it would be cool to try to make four little Dutch babies instead of one big one to take advantage of the outside crust. I am definitely intrigued with this recipe and would like to experiment with it. I must say, it's much easier (for me) than pancakes and could be just as good with practice! Thank you! (Reviewed for Holiday Tag, January 2009)

I really did intend to take a picture of this...but I ate it first. Oops.  Great recipe.  I've recently been fascinated by the idea of making Yorkshire pudding, and when I saw this recipe it sounded like a breakfast version of the yorkshire pudding recipes I've seen.  

Changes I made:  3 eggs, 3 T butter, a splash of vanilla extract.  Even with using one less T of butter, there was butter pooled on top and it drained off as I pulled each piece out of the pan.  I may see if I can get away with even less butter next time.  

While this was baking I took 2 cups of frozen blueberries, a little bit of water and sugar and cooked them on low, adding a tablespoon of cornstarch after the berries thawed and broke down a bit.  It made a great blueberry sauce that wasn't too sweet.  

My DH ate two portions, with the comment that this was "Really good!" so I think I'll make this again when we have the kids and see what they say.  I'm really tempted to go eat the remaining portion...ooh dear.
Love to make this easy hearty dish for brunch. I follow the suggestion to use 3 eggs, and also leave out the salt. We devour this with softly whipped cream and maple syrup.

This is a good one!  My son loves when I made this for a quick and easy supper.  It comes together before the oven even preheats.  It's simple, cheap, & good!  I use spelt flour in place of the all-purpose flour & only use 3T. butter.  We serve it with pure maple syrup.  Delicious!!!

I tried this recipe because it sounded like something my dad used to make (we named his recipe Ed Schmidtt pancakes after the man who showed it to my dad).  However, Ed's recipe had no eggs, and I must say that after growing up without them, I prefer this recipe that way.  I also tried making it with only one egg, and I think that is the way I will make it from now on.  We always serve ours with powdered sugar and lemon juice.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!!
Good change of pace for breakfast. Used 3 eggs, with my pan/oven combo it only took about 18 minutes to cook. Thanks Kiwi.

This is my favorite thing to make for breakfast, especially if I have company. I posted a step-by-step guide, with photos, on my blog: http://lambaround.blogspot.com/2009/03/dutch-babygerman-pancake.html

So easy and so very yummy. This is a very versatile recipe. I love that you can opt to fill it with fruit or whatever or not at all. I have a sweet tooth so I used brown sugar and added the slightest splash of vanilla to the batter. What a treat. Thank you Kiwidutch for sharing Mean Chef's wonderful recipe.
This was very easy and very yummy!  We thought it tasted like french toast.  We topped with cinnamon apples.

I used too large of an oven safe skillet...the pancake turned out a bit too thin in the middle.  I also cut out one T of butter and one egg as other reviewers have suggested.  It was delicious and will become a permanent recipe in my breakfast "go-tos" due to ease of preparation.  I used a honey, sour cream and fruit mix for the topping-YUM!

I made this for my family for breakfast this morning and we all LOVED it! I followed the recipe exactly except that I realized at the last second that I didn't have unsalted butter. I used salted butter and it tasted great anyway. We put maple syrup on it for the kids, and I simmered some frozen berries and reduced them into a compote to use on top for my husband and myself. This was incredibly easy and relatively quick. A definite keeper!

This turned out great. Massively high crispy sides, rich eggy bottom. Looked so good I had to take a picture. To get the high sides make sure your pan is good and hot. I just put the cast iron pan in the oven while it preheats. Drop butter in and pour batter when it's melted.
This turned out wonderful!  Topped with fried apples- yummy!

Simple and tasty, two of my favorite things!  I did use vanilla-sugar instead of plain sugar and FF milk because that's what I had.  Otherwise I followed the recipe to a T, topped it with some lemon juice and powdered sugar and yum!  My imagination is already going crazy with the many toppings and variations I can try!  :-)

Yummy!  Easy and fast.  I cooked mine in a 12" cast iron skillet.  Used about 1.5 tablespoon of butter.  Cooked for 20 minutes.  It was puffed, brown and ready.  Had mine with powder sugar and lime.  Also had the maple syrup option.  Fresh raspberries went on top.  Thank you.

I had never had an oven pancake or Dutch Baby before, but they looked so good in the pics that I decided to try. I preheated the oven with a 10" iron skillet inside, and mixed the batter in a blender while the oven was heating, using only 3 eggs as others suggested. I also whipped about half a cup of cream to top the fruit intended as filling. It took about 23 minutes to cook, and it puffed up beautifully and had a dark golden crust where it was against the pan, and a medium golden top. The bottom had a 1/4" thick custardy layer, and the top was crispy - a great combination! I cut it into 2 pieces for DH and I , and served it with berries, whipped cream, and a spritz of lemon juice. I also tried a teaspoonful of maple syrup on one side, just to taste it that way. I ate my half with fruit, and it was very filling - I was stuffed! Next time I'll try it with just maple syrup and a little lemon juice. This could serve 4 people with fruit and bacon or sausage on the side, or 2 to 3 generous servings on it's own.
Just like it promised! I admit I was hesitant when I saw the cottage cheese since I'm not a big fan of cottage cheese but you couldn't even tell! Would definitely make this again.
We really enjoyed this with sour cream & salsa.  I cheated and made instant mashed potatoes instead of "real" and it was still delicious! Thank you!

Wow, I just made this and it was a HUGE hit!  I made just a few minor changes to accomadate my families tastes.  I substituted Kielbalsa Sausage (sliced thinly) for the bacon, and put a layer of the Kielbalsa ontop of each layer.  Also, I substitued Ricotta Cheese for the Cottage cheese.  And lastly, my kids refuse to eat onions so I used only Onion Powder.   I even made a pan with no sausage for me as I dont eat meat, it was delicious as well!  Thanks so much for this recipie, it is now one of the Family Favorites!  A great warm, comfort food!

This was so good and so simple to make!  I used the no-boil lasagna noodles and they worked out just fine.  I thought I had more bacon than I actually did - I only had 4 slices. SO... I browned some ground beef, put that on the top layer, then added the buttery onions and bacon.   VERY good!!  Everyone here was very pleased.  Thanks!

So good.  I did used ricotta instead of cottage cheese (it's what I had) turned out very good, but next time I'm going to leave this layer out and double the potato cheese layer.  I also used quite a bit more bacon, added green onions over the top when serving and left out the dill.  Thank you for making it possible for me to mimic the classic taste that my Father-in-law makes only at Christmas! We love it!

Oh my, was this ever delicious!!
Elly was kind enough to bring this to my house for a get together, and it sure went FAST!! Just the right amount of heat and sooooo good!
I will be making this myself soon so that I can have it again!!

We had this recently at a party hosted by another Zaar member and really enjoyed it, especially my husband, who just scarfed them down without the sauce!  I loved them with the sauce as I'm not used to spicy food and the sauce helps to temper the heat of the spices a bit.

Elly herself made this for all of us( Irmgard, Country Lady, At Leslie`s home with all our hubby`s and I also had a friend Michelle and her hubby myself and Hubby)It was just oh so yummy! Loved the heat! My kind of good eats! Thanks bunches!

I also tried this recipe at Leslie party for the recipezaar ladies. I love hot food and this was great for those of us that like really spicey. It put a new twist on raw plain shrimp. I will serving this next time I have company.
Alison T

I must agree with the rest of the party animals - this appetizer was delicious! The cilantro dip was a perfect foil for the heat of the shrimp ......... so much so that I had trouble keeping my fingers out of the bowl. Thanx Elly, for bringing this dish to the party and for sharing the recipe!

We are currently on a chipotle spree and we totally enjoyed this recipe. My hubby blended the sour cream and cilantro frozen cubes which resulted in a very runny sauce but will try and thicken with another pepper and more sour cream or perhaps mayo. Will definitely make again to share with friends.

These were amazing!  The shrimp was really easy to make and would make a great party appetizer!  I had to use dried cilantro in the sauce, (I know, no comparison to fresh), but it turned out great anyway.  Next time, though, I will try making the sauce with fresh.

I served this Christmas Eve and it was my husband's favorite dish of the night! I did cut back the heat but it was still great, with or without the sauce.  I did add a little mayo to the sauce to thicken it a bit. Fast, easy, and sooooo good!!!

These were just 'ok' for me.  I made them exactly as written.  I thought the cilantro sauce was too runny and the lime flavor was very overpowering - by itself it was disgusting, but with the shrimp it was ok.  I don't think I will make this again.  Sorry!
One of my very favorite pasta dishes.  I use olive oil rather than butter and you can never get too much mizithra.

Obviously not the most health-conscious dish around, but a wonderful occasional indulgence. I did use a bit less butter. This simple recipe is great as is, but the garlic-lover in me thinks it would be exceptional with the addition of a few cloves of garlic. :) Thanks for posting!

DH always orders this at the local Spaghetti Factory. He is so happy that I found this recipe. He doesn't  have to wait hours in line to get this for dinner any more. This is a quick and easy, but high fat dish to prepare. (Who doesn't need a little fat to keep your hair shining.) This is so delicious you must try it at least once. I plan to make it again. Thank's Denver cook for posting.
I used to have this at the Spagetti Factory, and loved it then.....great recipe.
Mmmmm, that was good.

Hi Denver cook, have been making this for awhile now and I forgot to review it. I love, love, love it! Easy and yummy - added red pepper flakes for that zing, from now on am going to use mizithra cheese from now on. Thanks for posting, Diane ?)
Yum! Closest I've had yet to the spaghetti factory! Moved away and I've missed it. I added a little minced garlic to the butter for good measure.
Love the crispy crust and the melty cheese.  I made as directed and also with pastrami.  YUM!

Oh my now I know what all the fuss is about! Made these for the super bowl. I did use french bread but to size the grill but add all the other ingredients and also a few banana peppers before grilling. It came out crunchy and simply delicious. I cute the portions down to finger type sandwiches. Definitely a big hit!

What we did with it was slice the bread length wise (we have the large George Foreman grill), and then made it as per recipe. To cook, we put it in the grill, and held the top down (using some force) for 3 minutes, then, we let it cook on its own for another 3 minutes. Then, we cut it into 4 sandwiches. Simply divine. Thanks for a great recipe

Ok, let me just say that THIS IS AWESOME!!!...Thank you for posting this recipe!!!...I live in California (Ohio transplant) and it's sssooo hard to find a good baked/grilled sandwich here...my son LOVED it!!!! Thank you!!!!!
BIG hit with the whole family! Thanks!

This was a really great recipe.  I liked the fact that it could be made last minute and it wasn't just a plain old grilled ham and cheese or whatnot.  Very easy to do and the Foreman Grill was perfect.  Thanks for posting!
These were the best sandwiches I have ever tasted!!  I left out the pepperoni and the peppers and used the old George Foreman. Incredible!  I could eat these every night!  Thanks.

These were awesome.  I served them with Light and Creamy California Salad #98542.  Definitely a step up from plain old grilled cheese.  Serve these with soup and you have a fancy smancy lunch fit for a queen!
These were okay - nothing special.  Tasted like a grilled cheese.

What a great way to use a Forman grill.  My panini came out great. I had fun with the fillings and the most popular was a Reubin panini---corned beef, Swiss cheese and sauerkraut grilled on rye bread.  Thanks for a fun keeper MG!

I have one of the origianal GF grills. I never used it much but when I saw this reciepe I had to get it out. This is an excellent sandwich. I really loved the flavors of the filling and the crunchinous(is this a real word, I don't know) of the bread the grill gave it.I had this for dinner two nights in a row and will make again.
Loved these, as did my family. Made them on my George and they couldn't have been better, even added pickles to them. Will definately make again.
Outrageous! These were just fantastic. I get so tired of making the old grilled cheese and stuff. My daughter and I loved them. I plan to make extra and freeze them for lunches. Thanks so much!

I love, love, love this recipe!  I never knew a George Foreman grill could make panini just as good as (or even better than) the Italian cafe where I used to buy them!  The combinations I have tried are (1) grilled chicken, roasted bell peppers, and mozzarella cheese, (2) marinated artichoke hearts, roma tomatoes, and mozzarella cheese, and (3) thinly sliced fat-free ham and swiss cheese - all were phenomenal!  You have my eternal gratitude, Mysterygirl!  Edited to add: I don't use the butter on the outside of the sandwiches when I make them. I find the bread gets the perfect texture (really crispy) without it. I may try the butter, though, the next time I feel like really indulging! :)

I don't have a George Foreman grill so here's how I made this fabulous recipe:  Scooped out french bread sub rolls, buttered them, added chicken, roasted bell peppers, and mozarella and placed in lightly greased grill pan.  When brown on both sides, removed to microwave to melt the cheese.  Outstanding!  Love the flavors and makes a terrific sandwich!

What a fantastic idea! The sandwiches turned out perfect...certainly as good as I can buy and better because I can make them at home. The variations are endless for individual taste. I'm a jalapeno fan so I just had to try those--num! Thank you Mysterygirl for sharing your wonderful idea and recipe.

Loved this recipe. I don't have a GF Grill so used my gas grill and a brick wrapped in foil. Used a whole wheat loaf (for health purposes) and scopped out some of the filling. Made 1 loaf as directed above was very yummy. Second loaf, added thick sliced tomatoes and it was even better!
YumYumYum
Yummy! thanks for a delicious sandwich! Definitely NOT just a grilled cheese sandwich!Thank you

I made this for my husband and I last night on my Wolfgang Puck Panini maker. It was really good and easy.  I didn't have peppercini peppers so I just omitted them.  Hubby really enjoyed it.  I think next time I will add some Italian dressing! Thanks for posting..we will enjoy it again!
Very GOOD Sandwich!! I dont have a Foreman Grill, so I did these on the Stove top. They were AWSOME!! My husband loved them!! Thank you for sharing this easy recipe!!

These were excellent sandwiches. I made them on the stovetop using a grill pan and pressed them down using a spatula. The sandwiches were well compressed plus had great grill marks. The cheese was perfectly gooey and melty. A very hearty, comforting, filling meal that we all enjoyed. Thanks Mysterygirl.

TOTALLY YUMMY!  I served these with French Onion Soup for some company last night, and the one thing everyone kept saying was, "COOOOL!  You made these on the George Foreman?!".  I DEFINATELY look forward to experimenting with the possibilities on these...I actually remember having a recipe for a grilled breakfast sandwich that I've been putting off making because of the hassle using a regular skillet.

Thanks so much for posting!

Excellent! I made these on my George Foreman grill, also, and they turned out perfect. I love the crispy crust and the blend of the different cheeses was outstanding. I put some Italian dressing on these as well because my husband loves it. Thanks for posting!

Made this at the beach for all of us with my Foreman grill-never had used it before.  Now I make these all the time.  I followed recipe almost to a T as I recall.  I did drizzle some juices from the peperoncini and added sliced marinated red pepper, and Italina crushed red peppers (in liquid) for added heat.  Very versatile! We all gave it 5 stars!
These are the best sandwiches.  I made these a lot while at the beach this past summer.  Easy to make, and everyone loves them.  Didn't change a thing!

We loved this sandwich.  I used some homemade bread which was fairly substantial and I used mayonaise instead of the melted butter on the outside.  That was recommended in another grilled sandwich recipe and it works great.  I could only eat half of my sandwich but the two men I dined with each gobbled up theirs.  I was glad they didn't want to split my left over half as it made an excellent lunch the next day.  It was even good cold!

I was given a Panini Press for my birthday and this was the first recipe I tried on it.  AWESOME!  I used a a whole loaf of crusty garlic bread (without the butter, it's not needed) and added all the fillings.  Everyone at lunch was jealous and I'm making this as my next "lunch bunch" recipe!  Thank you for posting!

We absolutely loved this sandwich! I followed the directions exactly except I used banana pepper rings not pepperoncini (I think they fairly close to the same thing) It was fantastic! DH gobbled up 2 sandwiches in no time at all! Just as good if not better than a store bought panini at any local deli. Thanks for posting!
FANTASTIC! Good combination.  We left out the peppers and subbed mozzarella for provolone.
These were very delicious. The only thing that I would change is next time loose one of the cheeses to make it a little less heavy. However these were very good, and my bf has asked for them again.

Love this recipe. When I try something new, I can tell by the look on my hubby's face if it is a keeper.....he LOVED these. I didn't have a clue what pepperoncini peppers were so I used jalepeno peppers in some and banana peppers in the others. Both worked great. Thanks again for a great recipe :) Prissy
