It is almost the exact recipe that i grew up with for a wacky cake that mom made, the only difference is there was no egg in my childhood one.  if you're a vegan and want a tasty treat i would omit the egg and put about two more  tablespoons of oil to keep it moist.  thanks for a great cake!

Really nice and mine came out very chewy and very moist, I did use carob powder instead of cocoa, maybe that made a difference to the outcome, but it is really lovely, I put rich white choc ganache on top and it made it really something special. Thanks for posting.

Made this last night... doubled the recipe and frosted with Seven Minute Frosting.  It was DELICIOUS!!!    I will definitely make it again.  I'm not sure if it should be stored in the fridge, but I'm doing it anyway because cold cake hits the spot during hot North Carolina summers.  Maybe heaven has an endless supply of this cake for Queen Bead :-)

Excellent recipe for easy gluten free!  My mix was very dry and required double the water and oil, not sure why. The cake turned out well but next time I'd add half the sugar again. Would be great for a layer cake. I used white choc ganache to frost. Next day the cake was too dry to be tasty so I removed the ganache and used served remainder of the cake with hot chocolate sauce & ice cream.

From: Jackie
on july 15, 2008

Have to bake a gluten free cake for party I am catering for and so had a "test run" today. It is delicious. So moist and light, and quick to make. Yummy with chocolate genache,fresh strawberries and fresh cream. was a tremendous hit with my family. Will go into my list of favourites.

I got 16 cupcakes our of this batter. I added a little extra coca power and used half white sugar and half brown (ran out of white)
Next time I would add some melted chocolate to make them even more 'chocolatly!' Yum!
Super easy to make! Thanks!
The best cake I ever ate! I made it with Hershey's Special Dark cocoa. I used Carol's sorghum flour mix and added 3/4 cup of chocolate chips. WOW!!!

I'd bought an expensive box mix at the store but when I found this recipe and saw that the ingredients were nearly the same, I figured I'd give it a try.  This cake was great!  My non-GF family all liked it and no one could tell that it was any different from a regular wheat flour cake.  I doubled the recipe for a two layer cake and for my flour mix I used 1 1/2 c. sorghum flour, 1/2 c. white rice flour, 1/4 c. sweet rice flour, 1/4 c. potato starch.  I also cut back the sugar by about 1/8 c. (per cup of sugar used).  Super easy, will definitely make again.

I lused this recipe to make cupcakes, and I loved them!  They were for a work function and no one knew they weren't "normal", except of course for the fact that I was eating them :) I used Recipe #256259 for the flour and Recipe #22181 for the icing. I had already added xantan gum to the, which ended up doubling the amount called for in this recipe. The result was moist, tender cupcakes. I will stick with that amount going forwards.  The recipe made exactly 12 cupcakes and I baked them for 18 minutes. Thanks Queen Bead for a terrific recipe!
absolutely amazing.  i followed the recipe exactly & made cupcakes.  thanks so much for such a great one.
The best gluten free cake EVER and easy!  I have been making it for a long time...cupcakes, layer cake and sheet cakes all turn out great.

This is a great recipe.  You do not need to tell friends "Hey this is gluten free" and hope for the best.  I doubled the recipe and put in a 9 x 13 pan and monitored it with a toothpick until done.  Turned out great!!

Is this ever easy! Delicious, too! I made 25 mini cupcakes that took some 11 minutes to bake. Topped with whipped cream and sprinkles - they all got gobbled up in an instant! Thank you for a great recipe!

WOW, thank you!!! We were nervously approaching our son's first GF birthday party. I made a "test cake" a few days before the big day since you never know with GF recipes. My hubby who does not like chocolate cake, at 1/3 of the pan before I even got it frosted!! Today I made a 2nd and 3rd cake for the actual party and for cake with Grandma's. THANK YOU THANK YOU!! I made frosting with 1cup coco, 3 cups powdered sugar and 1/2 cup palm shortening and rice milk to get a good consistancy. Whipped it all up and YMMMMM the perfect addition to this cake. I am thinking of how to adjust this recipe to make brownies. I have never mastered regular chocolate cake or brownies. Interesting they they seem easier GF.

I never made a gluten-free cake before, but since my husband has stopped eating gluten (and I won't eat a whole cake myself), I found your recipe. The cake turned out wonderful! I frosted it with peanut butter frosting, which really made the cake yummy...even had a piece for breakfast.

Thank you for posting it!

Thank you soooo much Queen Bead
for giving my pumpkin pie a cake that she can have for her birthday.I even put it in a character pan and it works great! She is allergic to wheat and milk protein so this recipe is the bomb. And also the flour blend gives her mom a base that she can use for other recipes
Thanks again
Kellie

Thank you, thank you! My three little girls were so excited to have a birthday cake that tasted like the real thing this year...moist and light. And it is so much cheaper than the ready made gluten free mixes...yay!

I've been looking for gluten free recipes for some friends with gluten sensitivity.  We made cupcakes for Christmas with this recipe and they were very well received.  I can tell the difference between this cake and a regular cake texture wise, but not taste wise.  Thank you for expanding my growing GF recipe box.

AMAZING texture and rich flavor. I used Trader Joe's really rich cocoa, and used a mix of many different kinds of GF flours. (Rice, tapioca starch, potato starch, millet and almond meal) This tastes so much like a chocolate 'mayonnaise cake' I used to eat. Love, love this cake! Thanks so much for an easy and great recipe.

I made this great cake for a friend's birthday and she loved it. 
Followed recipie but did make an ajustment for high altitude, added 1 Tbs. of rice flour and 2 Tbs. water.

Wonderful and easy! This reminds me of the wacky cake recipe. We're egg free here so the first time I used Ener-G egg replacer(1bsp + 4tbsp water) and then the next time i used applesauce(for 2 eggs so 1/2 cup). I also added some chocolate chunks and made them into cupcakes. I baked for maybe 17min. I also used Bobs Red Mill gluten free flour and it turned out great. When it's raw, the batter is very beany tasting but when cooked, you cant tell. It turned out so delicious. All my kids loved it and only 1 is gluten free. Thanks!!

Perfect!!! I have made this several times now.  It is fast, easy, and fluffy.
Yes, Fluffy never thought I'd ever be able to say that about anything Gluten free.  The texture is superb and the taste is out of this world.  I have taken it to several events, and served for company a few times. No one can tell it's gluten free until they notice that I am eating it too.

Amazing gluten free cake! I made it for my mums birthday so she could at last enjoy a birthday cake and compared to any of the other gluten free cakes I have tried this was awesome. I cheated slightly and used Doves Gluten free Self raising flour but still added the baking soda and the cake doubled in size! Also I didnt use guar gum or xantham gum as I couldnt find any, but the cake sliced perfectly.

This cake came out beautifully. I didn't have the right size pan but I baked it in a 9x5 inch loaf pan and it came out just fine! My gluten free flour mix that I used is 3/4 cup brown rice flour, 3/4 cup potato starch(not flour!), and 1/2 cup tapioca flour.
I only had 1/4 tsp left of vailla extract so used what I had but don't think it made a big difference not using enough of it! It still came out wonderfully! I tried eating this with pudding because I didn't have the suppliews to make frosting for it and that was VERY good. I think this would be a great cake to fill with pudding and top with a buttercream frosting!
Very Very Good!  So light and fluffy and cakelike.  My boys gobbled them up.  Thanks

This cake turned out perfectly! A real treat for my husband who we newly discovered cannot tollerate wheat. You cannot even tell it is gluten free! This will be my go to recipe for cake now! I served with dark chocolate ice cream and whipped cream! Oh yum! Thanks so much for this awesome recipe!

This cake worked perfectly! Quick, easy, and delicious! I used 1 cup of white rice flour and 1/2 a cup of tapioca flour. I baked the cake in a loaf pan (for 50 mins) as I'm new to GF baking and don't have a proper cake pan! It turned out great though and I sliced it up and poured chocolate glaze over it for Thanksgiving Dinner. I made a test cupcake with it and it tasted great so hopefully the in-laws gobble it up! I will definitely used this recipe again.

LOVE IT!!!  Super easy.  I make cup cakes and freeze them for when my kids go to b-day parties.  I have made this for all their b-days this year and no one noticed.  I add chocholate chips for a little exra chocolate.

WOW! I cannot believe how easy this was! :)
I made mini-cupcakes that I baked for 14 minutes & then I had a small pampered chef stone 8" (maybe ?) pie dish... I am baking that now. I added walnuts & choc chips to the top of this. I cannot wait to see how it comes out. The cupcakes are cooling & my imagination is running wild about all of the different ways you can bake this batter & there are so many different options of how to serve it, whether it be with whipped cream, ice cream, icing, cut up fruit... the options are endless :)
THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR SUCH AN EASY GF BATTER 8-)

Did anyone else whisk together all of the liquid ingredients before adding to the dry or did you add the liquid items one by one to the dry mix?

Also, any ideas on how to make this a vanilla cake? Next time I am going to add almond extract in place of the vanilla extract to see how that tastes :)

This cake REALLY is fabulous.  When I smelled and tasted the batter, I thought, hmm, it's the thought that counts. (daughter's bf's birthday)  But when I took it out of the oven, my husband came in asking what smelled so good.  Then I cut this so I had to half circles and piled them with lots of coconut frosting - my GF version of German Chocolate Cake!  WOW!   I made a second layer to use up the rest of the frosting and froze it.  Had a slice of it yesterday - it was still just as good as before!

I'm not sure what happened, but this didn't turn out for me. I used almond flour for the GF flour, and followed the recipe to a T. It turned out kind of soupy and didn't form. Please recommend a GF flour to use! It smelled good, but it just didn't work out for me.

This is good!
here is the link to her flour blend if anyone wants it.
http://www.food.com/recipe/gluten-free-flour-blend-208061

I was looking for a GFCF chocolate cake recipe with positive reviews after trying a bad recipe last week.  I am so glad I ran across this one.  What I noticed first is the the batter is nice and light and not sticky like others I have tried.  The finished texture is fabulous and taste very close to the real thing.  I was running low on white sugar and was shy about 1/4 cup but the cake still turned out good.  I can't wait to try it again with more sugar, more vanilla extract and maybe some coffee to bring out the rich chocolate flavor.  I use my kids as the taste testers and I know if they like it then I have found a winner. Since I am dairy free too I made chocolate butter cream icing with 1/2 shortening and 1/2 earth balance vegan buttery sticks.  Thanks!!
I like the look of this, but a concerned that one of the ingredients listed ( vinegar) would render it unsuitable for a coeliac sufferer if it was malt vinegar.

DD (toddler) says "IT'S SO MUCH YUMMY!!!" I agree it is yummy! I used carob powder to be chocolate free in the same amount and it worked well. For the flour mix I used white rice flour & tapioca starch in half the amount. I used less sea salt, guar gum, canola oil, white vinegar, halal vanilla paste, plus the rest. It took longer to bake but I reduced the heat slightly as I read carob burns more easily plus I cooked it in a smaller pan. I will make this again.

This is the best GF Chocolate Cake I have ever had. So easy. I have used it for a Baked Alaska by wrapping and freezing after baking. When frozen, pile 1/2 gallon of desired flavor of ice cream on top, smooth nicely, cover with plastic wrap, then foil, and back in the freezer. When ready to serve, cover with meringue, toast lightly under broiler. It was a huge hit! Also added orange extract and orange zest to the batter before baking. Then added orange extract and orange zest to cream cheese frosting. Also a big hit. Love, love, love this delicious GF Chocolate Cake.
Very tasty! This cake was moist, not heavy, and just the right serving size.

I've been gluten-free for 9 months and lately, have been craving good, old-fashioned cake.  Up until now, I haven't been able to find a recipe which has the taste & consistency of "real" cake.  The reviews for this recipe made this cake sound like it was "the one"... and I agree!  I was skeptical, but thought, "what have I got to loose?"  It was SO easy to make and the resulting cake is fluffy and light.  This recipe is going in my book of keepers!

I really enjoyed this recipe. The texture was quite perfect. The cake was moist and light and delicious.  I made cupcakes and was so happy that there were no sink holes.  Hooray!  I frosted them with a chocolate ganache frosting that I flavored with raspberry extract.  Everyone raved about them and could not believe they were gluten free.  I froze the left overs and a few weeks later, when I thawed one, it was just as good as fresh made. Thank you for such a great recipe.

Excellent! The only "change" I made was the addition of 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon. Instead of the flour mixture called for in the recipe I used equal parts of Bob's Redmill Gluten Free All Purpose Flour, white rice flour, and oat flour. I will most definitely make this again!

My first GF desert attempt. Could NOT find Guar. I balked at the $13.98 price of the Xanthan, determining spur of the moment that it COULDN'T be that crucial...then did research right before baking and oops! It IS. Soooooo, tried ground golden flax seed in equal amount, w/boiling water poured over it. 13 cupcakes just cooled, and they look great. Oh, I also separated the egg, beat the white and folded in at last moment. So far so good,I took a little nibble and well-not "real" cupcake taste,but hoping with frosting they will be acceptable to the very picky husband of my birthday-girl bf.
I totally will make them again for us. Oh,also added in chocolate (dark chocolate)chips and tart dried cherries. yummy!

Wonderful recipe! I used 1 cup of white rice flour and 1/2 cup of manioc starch and it worked great. The texture was exactly the one of a good gluten-full chocolate cake; taste-wise, it was great, no icky after taste!

I'll be making this recipe again! :)

This was my first attempt at gluten-free cake baking & it was a resounding success! My gluten-full family thoroughly enjoyed it.  I used an 11" round pan & added 3/8 cup more sugar.  I used cream cheese frosting & it was DELICIOUS!

Made this cake for a friend's birthday about a month ago who is GF. Everyone loved it, including me! This is the first GF recipe I have ever used, and I've got to say that it is FABULOUS. My other GF friend who was there requested one for her birthday as well. I just finished decorating it with the same recipe one would use for whipped cheese cake (no bake) and garnished with chocolate covered strawberries... Can hardly wait! YUMMY! THANK YOU SO MUCH! P.S. I didn't deviate from the original recipe at all!

I made this today and OMG it was really good. First time I have made a GF that actually tasted good. Will diffidently make again. Now the big test is when hubby gets home and see what he thinks. I will try making them into cupcakes next time and see how that goes. Thanks .
My daughter, who is allergic to wheat, loves this cake!  My husband said this will be his b-day cake choice w/ the addition of dark choc chips.  Friends really liked it, too.

Not sure what happened - the cake looked fantastic - easy to decorate - but the aftertaste was awful. Maybe too much vinegar? I ate it and my kids ate it but my husband and my work colleagues wouldn't eat more than one bite. I used gluten free flour and just a touch of rice flour.
What did I do wrong?!?!

This cake was Delicious! I made this cake for a friends birthday who has to eat gluten free foods. This is the first time I made a gluten free cake. The comments I received from this cake were. "This is the best gluten free cake I have ever eaten." One lady told me she had bought gluten free cupcakes once and had to throw them out they were so bad but the cake I made from this recipe was absolutely delicious. I frosted it with me own butter almond frosting which     consisted of powdered sugar, butter, milk and almond extract.

This recipe is so great!  Gluten free or not, this is now my go-to chocolate cake recipe...so good, nobody would know it was wheat-flour-less!  Sliced the cake in half and used fluffy vanilla frosting in the middle and on top....reminded me of devils food cake, very moist.  Only lasted 2 days in this house.  The fact it's one bowl makes it even better, very easy. I used a flour blend with xantham gum in it, so omitted the gum from the ingredient list.  Honestly, if you're searching for a chocolate cake recipe, this is it!  Thanks so much for sharing.

Fabulous!  I made it into a German Chocolate sheet cake, using a 7x11 pan and baking it about 35 minutes (I live at 7,000 feet and things usually need to bake longer than a recipe says).  It literally took me three minutes to throw it together.  I used 3/4 cup brown rice flour, 1/4 cup sweet rice flour, and 1/2 cup tapioca flour, and mixed it with a mixer until it was fluffy and a little lighter.  Thanks for a great, convenient recipe :)

I made this cake last night for some of my gluten-free co-workers and it was a huge hit!!  I used BetterBatter gluten free flour which is cup for cup.  I did use the xanthum gum even tho it has it in the mix. The cake was sticky looking when I put it in the pan to bake But when it was done, it looked good and I frosted it with Peanut Butter creamCheese Frosting. When I served it the next day, It was  AWESOME!!! I will be making this for my grain free family often (without the frosting tho!)   Excellent recipe!

Delicious and quick.  I made this recipe into a small round cake and a half dozen cupcakes.  I cooked the cupcakes for about 18 minutes and they came out a bit too dry & crunchy on the outside, so make sure you keep an eye on the cooking time if you make a different size than recommended.  I took the cakes out around 25 minutes and they were nice and moist.  I use a GF mix of 2c rice flour, 2/3c potato starch & 1/3c tapioca starch.  Definitely a keeper, and no awful bloating the next day from flour!

Fantastic gluten free recipe! It was lofty and not dense at all. I did let it sit 20 minutes before baking because my oven was not ready yet. I baked the cupcakes for 18 minutes and it was very lofty and rose beautifully. Most things I make that are gluten free tended to be dense, but not this one. Loved this recipe.
This is a great cake and awesome as whooping pies, made a peanut butter frosting for it, and everyone went nuts for it. They wanted the recipe and could not believe it was gluten free.
Recipe is perfect as is. The cake was moist and rich honestly just so good. Best GF recipe I've found, sweet or savory.
Suprisingly perfect! I'll adopt it.

The cake was quick and easy to prepare, however it was quite flat out of the oven and rather dry. Otherwise not bad. My flour was organic gluten free Namaste all purpose which already had xanthan gum in it so I did not add more... Otherwise followed the recipe to the tee.

*Sorry for all the edits!!!* This was so good! I mostly replaced the substitutes in equal amounts. I used: 120 g white rice flour (this is wrong; it should be 160 g. Still tasted very good though!); 90 g tapioca flour (also wrong; should be 60 g); 192 g sugar; 1/2 tsp salt; 2 tsp baking soda; 3/4 tsp arrowroot powder; 70 g coconut oil; 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar; 1 tbsp vanilla extract; 1 egg; 1 cup full-fat coconut milk. Weighing means even less to clean up ;) I had to reduce the cooking time (probably because I botched the recipe).

I made this cake as-is for my nephew's birthday, and topped it with a dairy/gluten/soy free frosting of 3/4 D/G/S free chocolate chips and 6 T full-fat coconut milk melted in the microwave and mixed together. It was fantastic and everyone loved it! So much, in fact, that I am making another for a family dinner tomorrow night... only 4 days later!
Good and quick! So delicious...only thing I changed was I used dark cocoa as that's what I had....it's a keeper
Very good gluten free recipe, but I found the taste of baking soda a little too strong. Perhaps a little less needed for my tastes.

This recipe is a piece of cake! I took another reviewer's advice and used one cup of white rice flour and a half cup of tapioca starch. I've made it a few times now and it always turns out great. Thanks for the recipe!

Fantastic recipe! I'm amazed at the rise on the cakes! I used coconut oil and about 1 and 1/2 teaspoons of baking soda instead of two. Now waiting for them to cool and going to add buttercream icing and freeze until my gf visitors get here in a few weeks!
This made an amazing birthday cake. Best gf recipe I tried yet

I have been gluten free for about 14 years now and have tried plenty of gluten free cake recipies throughout the years. I honestly didn't care for this cake. It had an extreme aftertaste that I couldnt pinpoint that a few others had pointed out in their reviews. Maybe too much vinegar? I'm not sure what is was but I threw the cake away.
Is this unsweetened cocoa?

This is delicious chocolate cake! Amazingly moist, perfectly sweetened, chocolatey. My kids and I had a hard time waiting for it to cool so we could frost it! I added a bit more xanthan gum (1tsp). We doubled the recipe and made 2-9" round cake pans. Incredible!
Seriously delicious, tastes like Betty Crocker. Made this for my sisters birthday with some vanilla buttercream frosting, cant believe how simple it is to make, totally a staple now!

I must have done something wrong because this tasted horrible. I used Namaste Foods Perfect Flour Blend. I doubled the recipe and split evenly between two 9" round pans. It wasn't dry, but it was chewy and tastes like cardboard. The only person that liked it was the gluten free birthday girl. The rest of us couldn't eat more than one or two bites. I was so bummed.

this was a great EASY dish. i used my own homemade barbeque sauce and added two cloves of garlic-but i think erins version would have been just as good. the honey really adds to the great flavor. the meat was sooo tender and just fell apart- great on kiaser rolls with potato salad and some greens. thanks erin!!!

I used a 5-lb. bottom round,a bottle of dark Mexican beer,and added a large thinly sliced onion to the mix. After cooking on low heat in my crockpot for 10 hours, the shredding was easy. I mixed some liquid smoke in with the (hickory)bbq sauce and honey. This was a great recipe...makes a yummy sandwich on a kaiser roll. I froze portions that were leftover.
Mmmmmmm...this was SO yummy!  I used a pork roast becuse I did not have a beef roast and it was delicious.  Tasted just like "pulled pork" in a restaurant.  Excellent!

I made this recipe exactly as Erin wrote it, except that I used Miller Lite beer (the only beer I had in the house).  It was great, my family loved it.  It's a keeper and I plan on doing it again.  Thanks Erin!
Very good, easy to make.  Had a bit of trouble keeping it moist, but I had it in the crock pot a bit too long.

This recipe was TOO EASY!!!  Loved it!  I let my 3 lb. roast cook for about 8 hours on low and then I shredded it and followed the rest of the recipe as directed.  I served it on whole wheat buns with corn on the cob.  I still can't get over how easy it was.  :) I can't wait to try this with a pork roast as Cruzzo did.

Miss Erin, this recipe turned my urban dwelling into a backyard country BBQ! Served with farm fresh corn, garden tomatoes and home-grown potatoes with chives. As my friend put it "this BBQ has transported me to Yummyville" I did not have any beer on hand so I used dry white wine instead. I sliced up half of a vidalia onion and threw it in as well. This was incredible. With no place to grill, this recipe was a real treat! Thanks so much for a wonderful dinner

Loved this quick, delicious recipe!  I doubled the sauce which kept it moist for a good while.  Absolutely delicious and easy -- thanks so much for sharing!  Served it with smashed red potatoes (#103247), and it was a feast!

Great recipe, and so easy-i used a two and a half pound roast(thats all that they had)it turned out fine-cooked it for ten hours and shredded perfectly. A wonderful meal when you want BBQ but dont want to "fire up the pit"served it on hamburger buns with pickles and a little extra sauce and loaded baked potato salad:)great meal!PeggyLynn

Could not be easier.  I started this recipe last night and added the sauce this morning for a delicious lunch.  What a carefree recipe.  Great for picnics and  potlucks.  I had some cole slaw in the sandwich for extra crunch.
I have made this sooooo many times.  Awesome!  I always make a bit more sauce than this recipe calls for.  I add it to the beef after it's been in the refrigerator for a day or two.

Hey, Kittencal!  This combination of flavors is outstanding and I thank you for sharing.  I love to marinate and your recipe made our top sirloin super flavorful and tender.

Still wondering though about what makes it so special.  Perhaps the ginger?  At any rate, I can hardly wait to use it again.  With gratitude, E.
Outstanding flavor!!!I didn't have honey so used white corn syrup,next time I will use honey.Thanks Linda.

I must agree - outstanding blending of flavours! I scaled the quantities in half going for the lesser amount of soy but the higher amount of garlic, dry ginger (all I had) & included the worstershire. My strip loins, marinated for 8 hours, were moist & tender. Thanx Carol!

This was an excellent way to prepare sirloin steak.  The whole family enjoyed this along with beef lo mein noodles and salad.  I marinated for about 5 hours and the flavors were fabulous.  Thanks for posting this; I will use it often!
Tried this marinade out today and it gave my top sirloin an excellent teryaki-style flavor.  I used powdered garlic instead of fresh, maple style syrup, and left out the worstershire sauce.
Liked this marinade a lot.  It gave a great flavor to the steaks without being overpowering.  I made it as written - and will definitely make this again.  Thanks !
Gave the meat a great flavor and I like that the ingredients are all things I keep in the house..Thanks !!

This is really agreat marinade! I was looking for a marinade for pork tenderloin, saw this, and decided to give it a try-I'm so glad that I did! I scaled down the recipe, since I was only grilling two slices of pork tenderloin for DH and myself and only used 1 T. of oil. It downsized beautifully and the combination of flavors really complimented the pork. Thanks for posting this, Kittencal- I'll be using this again!

This is very good. First time I tried it I followed the recipe exactly including adding fresh minced ginger. The next time I cut the oil down to 1/2 cup and added 1/4 cup teriaki sauce along with the soy,wostershire and red wine vinegar. Both times the meat was so flavorful and tender.I think I like it best with less oil but either way it will have you coming back for more. Thanks, Kittencal.....

This is wonderful!! Have just finished eating and I had to let you know that this is fantastic. I didn't have any worcheshire sauce so i left it out. I also didn't have 24hrs to marinade, so I only marinated for 1 hour, the flavour was great, and I can see how tender and flavourson it would be if left for the whole marinating time. Thank you very much for a much enjoyed dinner. Foodlover1.

I had a real tiny roast so I cut the recipe in half, but cut the oil down to 1/4 cup and used the honey. Very flavourful and did tenderize the meat, I left it to marinate overnight. We love the combination of flavours and will use it again.
Thanks for posting.
Loved this marinade made it exactly to the recipe and left it in the fridge overnight. I'll use this again think I'll try it on pork sometime this week, Thank you.
This is the best marinade I've used. My 23 year old son who lives at University uses it all the time and has had rave reviews from his roomies!

AWESOME marinade. I used it for some cheap steak cuts and marinated them all day. They were tender and so flavorful! I had every intention of using the grill but ended up having to broil the steaks (and pan-fried 2). I have never had such tender, juicy and flavorful steaks out of the oven! I will use this again and again. Great Flavors!

I cut the oil in half, used the red wine and honey options. I must admit I upped the garlic as well. Half the family did not like it at all and the other half thought it was good. I marinated sirloin steaks 24 hours before grilling with an hour to let the meat come back to room temp. I thought it enhanced the meat without over powering the taste of the meat. I liked that alot. Because of the reaction of half the family I don't know if I would use this again, but I thought it did the job just fine.
Didn't have the beer but turned out great anyway. Added a packet of dry italian dressing to the roast while it was cooking for extra flavor. My 8yr old had seconds so that was high praise indeed!

I made this and my whole family loved it.  They were picking at it way before dinner time. I was surprised we had enought to eat afterward.  I had bought rolls to have as sandwiches but no one even touched the rolls.  They wanted the Roast all by itself.
This was yummy yummy!! Served at a neighborhodd BBQ - they emptied the barrel!

Guess I join the crowd in rave reviews.  I have several BBQ beef recipes, but this one is easiest and tastes just as good as the more time consuming ones. Thanks for sharing a very simple, tasty recipe.

I served this when I had friends visiting, everyone was happy! I served the sandwichs with cole slaw.
Tasty & Easy. Thanks!

This was great!  I was a bit nervous as it was cooking.  The meat simmering in the beer does not produce an appetizing scent (reminded me of the basement of my fraternity house in July.)  The results, however, were wonderful.  I used Jack Daniels bbq sauce and a big can of Foster's beer (it was the only kind my local store sold individually.)  Thanks for a great recipe.

I did not read the recipe first about cooking the roast first in the beer. So when I went in the morning to start cooking it, I was a bit surprized. So I just through it all in the crock, added my potatoes and away I went. It was still so goood!

This was so easy and yummy!  I did tweak the bar b que sauce a bit, adding more hot sauce, but other than that, followed the directions to a "T".  Definate staple in our house now.  I served it with coleslaw and carrot sticks with dressing for dipping.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Yum! Yum!  I took this to work and everyone loved it and wanted the recipe for themselves.  I didn't change a thing and it was great!  Thanks for sharing, it's a keeper.

Easy as can be and delicious. Makes a good bit, good for sandwiches for several days. Take the advice others mentined and use a good quality BBQ sauce or make your own--it will be worth it. I may try this next with pork instead.

Yes indeed a very simple, easy and very delightful. The barbeque sauce we used was "Danny's Baldheaded" which we found many years ago at our local Publix Supermarket and has become our one and only sauce so far. I forgot the hot sauce but it didn't matter as the beef was very tender and on a fresh, french bread burger bun.... mmm, mmm, good stuff! Thanks for the recipe

i thought this was ok, didnt have as much flavor as i thought it would. I used country bob barbecue sauce and followed directions to a T. I cooked over night, then in morning put rest in, but when i got home from worked, i tasted it and ended up adding some chilli sauce, brown sugar and wortecheshire sauce. it wasnt bad, just wasnt as good as other recipes i have tried.
I made this with "Recipe #19023" and amber ale. I cannot, cannot tell you how good it was. Thanks for this fabulous recipe!
Who needs to go out for B-B-Q? This stuff is amazing! Far the best I'v ever made. We will definitly make again! Thanks.

I skipped the beer step (didn't have time) and it still came out great. Probably would have been more tender had I used it.
I used my own BBQ sauce and a 5lb roast for my larger crockpot.
This makes a TON! I think this will become a regular potluck thing for us.
Very tasty and easy BBQ!!!

What an outstanding basic recipe!  Since this was my first time making it, I followed the directions exactly.  But now that we've had these wonderful barbeque sandwiches, I can see that adding some onion to the crockpot with the meat and liquid smoke to the barbecue sauce would work very well.  My roast was a little over 4 pounds, so I increased all sauce ingredients by another 1/2.  It was perfect.  The aroma during the day as only the roast and beer cooked in the crockpot was amazing!  This was very enjoyable -- and couldn't be easier.  Thank you, Miss Erin for posting it.

Easy and great! I used a can of Coca Cola instead of Beer. The family devoured it. I had a more complicated version of this recipe and that version just went in the trash. I am all about simple and delicious! Thanks!

I just wanted to add that I also use a pork roast (shoulder or butt) and dr.pepper. To die for!

Delicious and easy what more can you ask for? I made it with pork as suggested in a review and it was very good, not too spicy not too mild. I made a pork shoulder that was just over 5 lbs, pretty much doubled everything but he cooking time was fine. Will definitely make this again and again.

I made this for a party at work and it was very well received. I doubled the recipe using 2 3lb chuck roasts, Wegmans Memphis bbq sauce, Wegmans clover honey, Frank's Red Hot and Lancaster's Amber Fest beer. (I'm not sure how much beer I used, as I just filled the pot from my tap system until both roasts were covered.) Cooking time was 10-11 hours. Will definitely make this again.
I used a beef brisket, this was easy and outstanding. Will make again. thanks for posting.

Thanks for this wonderful recipe! I made this for an all day parade event and everyone loved it. I double the recipe and used 2 3lb chuck roasts and followed the recipe to the letter.This is a keeper.
I only used 1 teaspoon of hot sauce. But the recipe is easy to make & really good.  I shred & then chop the meat, cause it stays in the buns better.  Great recipe, thanks for posting

What a great, easy, delicious way to make beef barbecue! I too added thinly sliced onions to the meat. I just tried it right out of the crock pot after adding all the ingredients and it is YUM-O! Can't wait to have it on a roll for dinner tonight!! Now, what to do with the couple cups of delicious cooking juices that are not used in the sauce?!! Just can't bring myself to throw them out....

I came to this recipe because I needed to use up some BBQ sauce.  My roast was on the small side, so after cooking it for 8 hours, I pulled the meat out, shredded it.... removed some of the liquid and added the BBQ sauce.  I added some of the cooking liquid back into the pot if it was needed.  I added a bit of salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar.  I served this over fresh whole wheat buns and some steamed carrots.  Can't beat this recipe for its flexability.  My DD called them Sloppy Joes and gobbled hers down!!!  That said it all....this will be a repeat!!!  Thanks for the posting!!!

WoW! This was sooo good! I cooked a 4.5 lb. roast for 9 hours with a 12 ounce can of Coors light (its all I had). Drained the juices in a colander. Returned the shredded roast back into the crock pot, doubled the sauce recipe because it was too dry with the amount of meat I used. Let it simmer for half hour, then added 1/8 cup of water, then stirred and simmered for another half hour. It was PERFECT! My sister said it was the best bbq beef sandwich she has EVER had! Which says a lot coming from her since her and her husband are BBQ restaurant aficionados. This will be a welcome addition to my cookbook! Try this you will not be dissapointed!

Yummy!  Along with the beer I added garlic and dried minced onions to the roast and cooked over night.  In the morning when I shredded the meat along with the bbq sauce I also added Liquid Smoke...we like our meats smokey!  Used Stubb's original sauce and just a drizzle of honey, afraid that a 1/4 cup would be too sweet as we like to taste the "vinegaryness" in the sauce.  Also added more garlic after shredding as well.  It came out so tender and yummy, served on buns w/ fresh sliced onion and it was divine.  Thanks so much for posting, Miss Erin!

Great, easy recipe. I think the results really will depend on the BBQ sauce you use, so choose wisely. We used the BBQ sauce from Trader Joe's because we're trying to avoid HFCS, and it was pretty sweet, so I should have omitted the honey. I think next time I'll try something tangier. Thanks for the beer prep tip and easy recipe!

Very easy recipe.  I cut my 4.5 lb. roast in half to make it easier to shred later.  Also, I did chop it too making it easy to stay on bun.  My beer of choice was Budweiser and the barbecue sauce was Stubbs Spicy Barbecue, which we love.  I think the trick is to ALWAYS use a chuck roast, as it is the best.  Pork would be good too!  I think my husband would eat this every day if he could!  Thanks Erin!

I chose Kraft Hickory Smoke barbecue sauce and was out of Frank's so had to try Chipotle Tabasco. I used a can of Busch Light because we had one loner in the fridge and we don't drink it. My husband and I both felt that this had a lot of flavor and was restaurant quality. I will be making this again for Friday nights when we have weekend guests. Thank you!! So yummy.
we used moose roasts....brisket/shoulder/pot.......local brew.....yummy

Excellent recipe. What I loved the most about this recipe is that I literally dumped a roast in my slow cooker and poured a bottle of beer on it. Then I set the slow cooker on low and went to sleep. Making the sauce was a breeze too. I toasted some whole grain bread with cheese and sandwiched the beef barbecue. So good!

This was fantastic! It was easy and very inexpensive to make. I didn't add honey because the BBQ sauce I used was honey BBQ. I also used Texas Pete hot sauce. I just love that sauce. But overall the recipe was a great success and I will definitely make it again. Thanks for sharing this.

Wonderful marinade!! We let our steaks marinate for 24 hours and the flavor was fabulous!!  I'm excited to have found this at the beginning of the grilling season!!  I look forward to trying it with pork as well!!  Thanks!!
This was amazing! I didn't get the full time to marinate this, only 45 minutes about and it was still awesome!
I used this marinade for my beef kabobs I served on Easter...they turned out superb.
Made this in the crock pot. Used only the marinade recipe and beef. It was delicious. Used fresh ginger as I had it on hand. Only used 1/2 cup oil. Thank you.

I cut back on the soy sauce..halved it Also, added a little ketchup and brown sugar...about 2 tbsp. each to add some sweetness. I did this because I was using a pork loin roast I like and wanted a little more sweetness with my pork.
Delicious!! We will be using this marinade again!!
10 stars, Thanks Kitten!

This marinade is really wonderful!  When I first put it together I took one wiff and decided that wouldn't be enough, so I grabbed a spoon and tasted it...YUM!  Okay, so I used a london broil...very tough.  I cut it in chuncks for shish kabobs and threw it in the marinade on Friday, so we could eat it Saturday night.  Well, we were invited out on Sat. night, so I planned for Sunday night...not enough time on Sun. night, so Monday night it was.  I secretly got more excited about it, knowing that the longer it sat, the better it would be!  Well, it was really wonderful, our meat was not that great because my husband overcooked it (totally his fault), however the flavors of the marinade were wonderful and I will be doing it again and again!  Thanks Kitten, you never dissapoint!

This marinade is the best thing that ever happened to beef!  I am not a steak lover because the meat has to be so tender that it just about has to melt in my mouth.  I finally found a marinade that lets me eat steak so poor hubby doesn't have to go without.  I had two Rib Eye steaks and  Hubby likes his meat with no marinade at all but I marinated mine for 24 hours.  The only change I made was to use Sweet Baby Rays in place of the honey because that was all I had on hand.  The results was an almost melt in your mouth steak with lots of flavor.  Try this if you are fussy about your steak like me or even if your not.....you will not be dissapointed.  Thanks for posting.
I will definitely be using this again!  It's wonderful and easy to do.  I marinated pork with it and then made kabobs.  Absolutely wonderful!

I marinated a large pork butt roast overnight, and then into the crockpot on low for probably 8-10 hours. We had the best pulled pork sandwiches we've ever had!  Kitten, another perfect score!! Many thanks for another winner.

WOW!!!  that discribes this marinade!!  if you make this and you are not blown away, then you are hard to please.  i marinated a chuck roast for 2 days, placed it in my slow cooker with celery, onion, carrot and portabella mushrooms. poured the marinade on top and cooked for 6 hrs.  WOW!! thats all i can say.  thank you kittencal.
Excellent tenderizer! DH thought it was too sour though. Thanks!

This does not need another review,but I wanted to thank you for the recipe.I used some tenderized round steak and only let sit for 4 hours,but it was tender and delicous.My DH kept saying how good the flavor was.I will use a good cut of meat next time.I didnt use the powdered meat tenderizer.I think it is the vinegar that makes it so tender,my mother used to rub steak with vinegar. Thanks Kittencal
An amazing marinade.  I marinated steaks for 24 hours and they turned absolutely wonderful!  Thanks for the great recipe!

Holy cow!!!!! I loved this.  I left somethings out (didn't have on hand... store too far away).  I left out garlic, ginger and meat tenderizer.  I used cider vinegar and vegetable oil.  I let the pork roast marinade for about 10 hours and then cooked it on a rotisiere.  That Had Wonderful Flavor.  Everyone in my family loved it.  I am really looking forward to the leftovers today.  Thank you for sharing.  I will do this again.
Very good stuff! Everyone loved it!

It was ok. My DD loved it but the rest of us were ok with it. I marinated a small boneless pork loin overnight and the only thing I substituted was the honey for maple syrup. I will try it again but maybe with a few tweaks!

Wow, We loved it!
I made this with a huge pork roast, didn't have cider or red wine vinegar, so used balsamic vinegar. Added fresh grated ginger, and a sprinkle of the dry ginger too. Used garlic powder, and the olive oil.
Fantastic, melt in your mouth meat!
The sauce in the pan was awesome too, drizzled over the meat. Thanks Kit!!
(I only had time to marinate 2 hours, but poked holes in the roast with a knife)
Very good, even with just eyeballing everything.

Yummy!!!  I marinaded a pork loin for 48 hours, then injected it with the marinade before cooking.  I was kinda skeptical about the amount of oil -- not any more.  I used veg oil and added some liquid smoke.  Thanks for posting
Just OK...flavor was strong and sort of burnt.

loved the slight sweet flavor. Note of caution: it's a nice thick sauce so be careful not to over cook the meat. Biggest Plus: even without the tenderizer it makes our venison softer than beef! Thanks!!

Wow this was a hit with my family!!!  Even my DH, who doesn't usually comment much on food, said how good it smelled while grilling.  My grocery store had a sale on skirt steak this week, so I decided to try it, and bought a 1 1/2 lb steak.  I put it in the marinade around mid morning and then let it sit at room temperature an hour before grilling.  I was lazy and just grilled the steak whole, rather than kebobs, and made a large kebob of red peppers and onions.  I followed the directions as written opting to add 1 tsp. of the meat tenderizer.  Thanks Kittencal for a wonderful recipe!!!  Made for zaar star tag.
Easy recipe woith wonderful flavors - I reduced the oil by half with no ill affects.  We had this on pork this time, will try on beef in the future.  This recipe is definately a keeper!
We used this on a roast, I let it marinade overnight, it was DYNAMITE!!  My only changes were I skipped the tenderizer (didn't have) and added about a tsp of liquid smoke.  Will do again!
Tried this with some pork steaks this weekend. They were very moist & tender, especially for pork. I will be using this over & over! Thanks, Kitten
This is *the* best marinade for just about any cut of meat, it is my only marinade now. I use fresh ginger instead of powdered and I blend it all up in a blender before use.

this marinade already has so many wonderful reviews but I wanted to add mine anyway. I was really impressed with the flavor. I needed my meat in  a hurry so I used my canister sealer that came with my food saver and it marinaded in only an hour. Wonderful tender cuts of meat from a tough roast
Like you can see on my photo, I used this marinade for a steak.  It was maybe 5 hours in the marinade.  I used cider vinegar.  And half the oil needed.  Thanks Kit.  Made for Zaar Star Game.

Wow! Another wonderful recipe. Thanks Kittencal. Used this for beef Kabobs and it turned out wonderful. I couldn't find my tenderizer, it turned out that I didn't need it. This made the meat moist, tender and very flavorful. I will be using it on steaks in a few days. Thanks again!

This is the best marinade I have ever made! I was looking for a similar recipe to one I used in the past and lost and came across this one. I actually have used it a few times for chicken even though it specifys beef and pork and it's AMAZING! I have had so many compliments on this- and I can see why!! This one is definitely a keeper :)
This was fabulous!  Not only did it tenderize the beef perfectly, but it tasted great!  TKS!
Excellent marinade Kittencal.  Used it on two big Prime Rib Steaks and only had 9 hours to marinade.  Worked beautifully.  Thank you

WOW! It's a shame there isn't more than 5 stars! I used this marinade on pork tenderloins and grilled them.  My husband who claims to hate pork, couldn't get enough.  It tasted like beef tenderloin. This recipe rocks!  I cant wait to try it on beef!!!!
Good flavor, melt in your mouth tender, I'm making this again. I used pork loin chops on the grill. Wife and children loved it! I'll try it next time when I grill a chuck roast!
Simply a fantastic marinade!  With one try, it has replaced all my other marinades!  Will never do pork tenderloin another way from now on! Thank you for sharing.  AWESOME!
We loved this and it's one of those recipes that all ingredients are common in the kitcher.  Thanks again Kittencal for another winner.

*~nom nom nom~* .... As usual, it's another Kittencal winner! Made exactly as directed, except my husband overcooked mine because it was his first time using our new grill. Still the flavor was all there and we were "nomming" our way through the entire meal. Thanks again, Carol,  for another terrific recipe!

This was auesome! We followed the recipe except for the meat tenderizer, we didn't have any. I also added two tsp of A-1 for my husband. We only got to marinate our steaks for 4 hours, but they were still so wonderful that my husband and I argued over who got the left overs the next day. I an't wait to make this again and let them marinate for the full 8-24 hours. Thanks.

I've been looking for a good pork chop recipe for the grill and i finally broke down and went with the masses to Kittencal...
I am soooooo glad that I did because the boneless chops I marinated in this for about 5 hours then grilled were the best pork chops we have ever had.
They were super tender and tasted wonderful. I will make this marinade often.
I don't buy meat tenderizer and i didn't use the dry mustard powder and used three minced cloves of garlic.
This recipe is excellent.

Kitten,  I have never had so many rave reviews!  I first fixed this marinade on pork and thought it was very good.  My sister ask if I had a good marinade, so I gave this one to her.  She said that her family had never eaten a steak as good as this and they didn't need to eat out anymore.  Her husband  only eats at one steak house, so that tells you something.  Thanks so much for this wonderful recipe.
left out the worcestershire...family preference. was great.

Made this yesterday, followed directions to the letter for a 2.3 lb london broil (cooked on the grill).  Only had time to marinade for about 6 hours (so I did use the optional tenderizer) - whole family loved the flavor and it was wonderfully tender.  Poor old Mr Motley (the basset) didn't get any scraps last night!  He looked so sad I had to part with a small taste of Cookin-jo's butter roasted carrots (http://www.recipezaar.com/137144)
 Which were just incredible with that London Broil!  Thanks for yet another wonderful recipe!!!
Another five star recipe from Kittencal. This is the best marindade I have used for pork. Delicious! It is a perfect blend of flavors. Thanks!!
I thought this was fantastic.  I let the meat marinate for about 24 hours....ribeyes had a great flavor!  Thanks for another great recipe!

This was pretty good. I used a pretty cheap cut of meat and it was still pretty tender. I marinated this about about 4 hours and nex time if I was going to use a similar cut I would marinate it for at least 8.  I loved the flavour and would like to try it on a better chop just for the flavours.

Oh my, this marinade is WONDERFUL!!! I was a bit worried about the honey w/ steaks but it really adds so much flavor-a delightful surprise! I love ginger so I used 1 tsp and only used 1/4 cup evoo. Marinated 3 chuck eye steaks overnight and grilled to medium rare-they came out so tender and delicious! This has to be one of the best marinades I've ever made. Served w/ Recipe #264966 and a salad w/ Recipe #66593 for a delicious meal. Thank you, Kitten, for a great recipe that I look forward to making again and again!!!
I've used this marinade twice now and it's been great both times. It really makes a difference with mediocre cuts of meat.  They come out very flavorful and tender. Thanks for posting.

The vegetarian wins again! Despite being mostly vegetarian I was in charge of the meat for my boyfriend's monthly family gathering. Wanting to prove my culinary abilities, I searched out the fabulous Kittencal and her mighty marinade. I marinated about 4 lbs of pork chops in a double recipe of this. They were, and I quote, "poison" (you know, in that good way). So, big thumbs up from the whole family - even grandma!
Wow just wow ...simple and delicious ...i marinate all night and cook it on the charcaol with charbon and it was the best pork chop ever
Very good.  I made with pork chops and did them on the grill.  My husband commented on how tender they were.

I thought this marinade was wonderful and will be using it from now on.  Didn't change a thing, although my pork was sliced into strips for a stir fry.  It had been in the freezer for a while.....but this marinde turned meat that was lovely and tender.  After marinating for 8 hours, I then followed a favorite stir fry recipe from the Frugal Gourmet and stir fried the pork with garlic, black pepper, corriander and lemon grass - tasted better than our local takeaway!  Thanks for the recipe Kittencal!

OUT OF THIS WORLD Kitten!  I'm normally a little skeptical of marinades because so many of them don't really offer anything to the meat, but this recipe will be at my table many, many times in the future.  Less than 5 min to prep, added some center cut pork steaks, then popped in the fridge.  When I got home from work yesterday, placed them on the counter to come to room temp while I changed clothes, fed the dog, prepped the grill etc, so they were perfect temp by the time I was ready for them.  Juicey, a nice tang from the ingredients, DH polished off the entire package of pork steaks and he normally doesn't like pork at all!  This would be great on a flank steak too!  FANTASTIC!  (I might cut back on oil next time, however)
Not a huge fan of this-too much garlic for me.
This gave the meat very good taste. I added more garlic and left out the tenderizer (didn't have any). Will keep in the keeper file. Made for Kittencal's cookathon.

I used this marinade/tenderizer on a beef 'tender' roast. I'm not sure why they call it a 'tender' roast. It isn't tender at all...and this 'tenderizer' didn't help. I marinaded two different roasts overnight for 18 hrs. and let it 'rest' & reach room temperature. My husband cooked both roasts on the grill. As mentioned above, they were not tender...however they did have a very unique flavor. Not sure if we really liked the flavor...but it could have just been the cut of beef. I'll use this recipe again...and perhaps give a different rating. Thanks for sharing. Many Blessings
Very Good!

I used the reduced soy sauce, and made with a fresh from the store sirloin steak.  I used my fork to poke holes all over the steak to help the marinade to absorb all through the meat.  It worked great for me and my steak came out med rare, juicy, and it was tender with great taste!  This marinade will be used often, as we grill a lot and love tender and flavorful meats, chicken and pork. Thank you!

I had three left over pork chops from another recipe that I could swear was shoe rubber, thus the beginning of my quest.  To make my experiment even more rigid, I had DH bbq them knowing he has a tendency to overcook and char.  The results produced a full flavored and an absolutely tender fall-off-the-bone, finger-lickin' chop.  The tenderizer was key.

WOW.  Thanks so much for this - just had this tonight with roast pork for our family Easter lunch and it was awesome.  I am having guests for dinner next week, and i am tempted to make it again!!  I did everything exactly as instructed, although i did double the recipe.  It was really, really good and the pork was amazingly tender and tasty.  For anyone that is interested, I marinated  a 3lb loin of pork in this marinade for 24 hours in a Ziploc bag in the fridge, let it come to room temperature (as instructed!), and then roasted it at 450 degrees for 10 mins and then 250 for another 50 mins - then let it rest 15 mins (covered in foil) before slicing - and it was PERFECT.  Thanks so much for the recipe, Kittencal, i have already shared it with my Mom and others!
Great with pork tenderloin!

What a great marinade! 
Thanks so much for sharing! 
I used half the oil and it worked out great!

I had a very questionable and tough cut of meat ( last time my husband buys steak ! ). This marinade did a remarkable job of making the steak edible. It turned out very well.  The flavor of the marinade was really delicious and I will definitely be trying it on a better cut of meat next time. I successfully froze my meat in this marinade and grilled when it defrosted.

Holy Cow!!!!  YUM, YUM, YUM!  I know you don't really need another review for this, but I can't help sharing my story!  My hubby is a hunter and he recently harvested a wild hog.  We ended up w/ lots of pork chops, and I was so apprehensive about them to say the least.  However, I felt very confident in a marinade created by Kittencal, and I was not disappointed at all!  It's b/c of this recipe that I was able to eat WILD HOG MEAT!  My hubby was beside himself with excitement - he had to call all his buddies about how great our meal was!  Thank you, Kittencal, I loooooove your recipes!

I loved the taste of this marinade. My DH can't have a lot of sugar so I made this tonight because he wasn't home for dinner.  My mistake was that I overcooked my flank steak in the broiler. It wasn't  tender but I didn't use the meat tenderizer.  Maybe if let it marinate longer it would have been less tough and also it was over done so that was tougher.  I used cider vinegar.  Thanks Kitten!  Next time I'll watch the meat better but it was a great taste.

This hardly needs another review, but THANKS, Kitten! The first steaks (angus ribeyes) on our new grill, and they were TO DIE FOR! Kittencal, this was as wonderful as I expected from one of your recipes. Worthy of more than 5 stars!!! Thank you for all the time and effort you have graciously provided for this site. You have helped countless numbers of people and their lucky families! And your name has become quite familiar globally because of your dedication and love of cooking. Once again, a sincere thank you.

I purchased a big, tough, cheap piece of meat as an experiment to see if I could turn it into a softer, tastier creation. I poked many fork holes on both sides and as instructed marinated it for a little over 6 hours. Also, I used extra virgin olive oil (I'm nuts for the stuff). I cooked it in my rotisserie until the edges were slightly burned. It turned out fabulous! And, this marinade had tenderized it quite a bit dispite even the fact that I should've let it soak longer. I think the best parts were the burnt edges! Poking the holes in the meat allowed the flavor of that marinade to really soak in and make it taste great! MMMM.. Thanks so much Kittencal! My search is over for a meat tenderizing, flavorful marinade!
Enjoyed it with beef! DD and DS want it again soon!
Excellent marinade.  I've tried it with honey & maple syrup variation, enjoyed both.  Thanks for sharing.

I don't eat beef so my rating comes via the people who ate it...this marinade worked great and was tasty.  Great for grilling as it helps keep the meat from sticking to the grill and carmelized the meat to perfection.

Oh so good!  I made this for a dinner with our nieghbors and it turned out fabulous!  The chops sat in the marinade for over 24 hours so they were extra tender.  Good stuff.  Thanks for sharing!  I will definitely make this one again.

What WONDERFUL flavor this has! I set aside 1/2 cup of the recipe in a separate container from the meat marinade and used it for cooking.  I marinated a 2 lb pork tenderloin for 24 hours.  Put the meat in my crockpot. Made 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth from bouillon granules and mixed it with the reserved marinade.  Cooked it for 1 hour on high, and low for 4.  Pulled the meat apart and stirred it around in the broth and let it marinate for another hour  before serving.  You could use the liquid to make a gravy or just use as "au jus" for your pork or on mashed potatoes or do both.  I made Recipe #19259 Supreme Garlic Mashed Potatoes to go with our meal.  Another winner recipe on here!
Terrific marinade!!
DELICIOUS and so easy to make! I couldn't find meat tenderiser, so did the recipe without it. It was lovely, having left the beef steak to marinate in it for 24 hours!
This was so incredible with steak tips! My husband said it was one of the recipes I have tried. I had to use less honey because I ran out so I'm sure it would have been even more amazing with it.

I made this on a tenderloin steak. I marinated for 24 hours. The flavor was a little strong, tasted too much like soy sauce and no other flavor. I'll try this one more time but will only marinate it for an hour or so to see if the flavor is a little less intense.
My partner thought this was pretty good.

This is the just the best! We buy a 3 lb. cut of inexpensive meat from costco, let it marinade a day or two, and it is better than any restaurant steak you can get. I only make about a lb. at a time, and then, while grilling, pour the leftover marinade over the steaks. (I also add a bit more ginger, as it is very good.) Thanks!

I never actually made it as written, but that was the only sub I made at first. Now I also add some red wine for flavour and some ketchup to thicken it up. 
Another thought; I have had to use brown sugar before and it did turn out fine, with no burning. (but maybe I got lucky)

This is awesome!  I used this with T- bone steaks and pork steaks.  They marinated for about 24 hours, and had great flavor after we grilled them!  I know it's a great marinade when I don't need any A-1 sauce!

In an effort to save money and time, I buy large packages of meat from Costco.  I cook part of the meat right away and freeze the rest for later.  Several months ago, I bought a large package of pork chops, six of which I put together with your marinade and froze for future use.  This week I thawed the porkchops and grilled them.  They were amazing; very moist and tender!  I'm picky about pork too.  I will definitely be making this again and again.  Thank you!  P.S.  I did let the porkchops marinate for 24 hours in the refrigerator first, before freezing them.

For all those who are using candy thermometers for their caramel--always test your thermometer periodically before using.  Bring a pot of water to a hard boil and let it boil heavily for five minutes.  Water at sea level boils at 212 degrees.  If your thermometer reads differently, adjust your recipe temperature up or down depending upon what your thermometer reads for boiling water.  For different altitudes, do an internet search for water's boiling point at your particular altitude.  I make a lot of candies and my good thermometers are always off a few degrees which can make a big difference in how your candy turns out.  I test my thermometer if I haven't used it for awhile.  Before making this recipe, get the apples washed and prepped and compile all nuts or toppings you're going to put on the apples.  You want everything ready-to-go before the caramel is cooked so you can dip the apples right away.  I  put chopped peanuts in a small bowl so that immediately after the apples are dipped in caramel, I plop the apple in the peanut bowl and twirl it around until covered in nuts.  Works fine for mini chocolate chips or whatever toppings you choose.  Sometimes I dip the apples in nuts and drizzle melted chocolate over the top.  You can get real creative with caramel apples.

I'm addressing a few problems people have had. Use parchment paper or a silicone baking mat to prevent sticking. If the caramel is splattering and burning your hand either your spoon is too short or the caramel is on WAY too high! When my bilubnles burst, the 'spitting' was only about 1/2" high! If it is grainy, that is because you allowed sugar crystals to develop on the edges of the pot. You can remove them with a damp pastry brush of scrape the sides as you stir with a silicone scraper rather than a spoon. It would be nice of the instructions included this recommendation. Or it could come from not enough stirring. If you over or under cooked it, try the cold water test to check doneness. I relied on that way more than the thermometer. Google: candy cold water test. If it cooked too fast or slow, be sure your quantity of condensed milk is correct and make sure you aren't cooking it on too high or low heat. If you are in a dry climate, it will cook faster as the water evaporates more quickly and in a humidy climate, vice versa. Hope this helps!

Here is an easy way to prep the mini burgers. Line a jellyroll or sheet pan with parchment paper, and place the ground chuck in the middle of the pan. Cover the meat with a large sheet of plastic wrap. Roll meat with a rolling pin until it covers the surface of the pan; it should be very thin. Remove the plastic wrap, and sprinkle the meat with the seasoning mixture. Fold the meat in half, from side to side, using the parchment paper. Use a pizza wheel to cut the meat into even squares.  I also thought sprinkling minced, dried onion flakes on top might be a good way to absorb the juices and use on top of the burgers for those who would not mind the "excess drainage".
