UPDATE:  I've found that if you use country ham chunk, soak it overnight.  That really cuts back on the saltiness.  And I've gone lazy and just used dried minced onion and it's still good!
Very easy wonderful flavor. Used 1/2 water and 1/2 broth. Terrific recipe for all that leftover ham I have in my freezer. :)

Sue thank you so much for posting this recipe! It is the first time I have made ham and beans and the flavor was wonderful. I did cook for about 9 hours on low and the ham was falling off the bone. A couple days ago I made Recipe #254072 by 2Bleu (Bird&Buddha) so I cut around the bone and had a nice large piece to add to the crock pot. Didnt want onions in the stock so I used dried minced onions, dry parsley, omitted the salt, and used 4 cups chicken broth and 2 cups water. This worked perfectly for me and I will be making this recipe again! Made and reviewed for the Australia/New Zealand Recipe Swap #25.

This is a very tasty, and simple dish to make. Great on a cold night! Wednesdays are always hectic at our house so I like to make crock pot dishes to simplify things. I will definitely keep this recipe handy. I think the next time I make it though I will use a smoked ham for a bit more flavor. I have to admit, I wasn't sure if the kids were going to like it...no problem there as they all had two bowls full!
Made as a recipenap for 25th AUS?NZ Recipe Swap.

This is the best ham and beans I've ever made. Is it the cloves? I don't know but my husband had 2 servings and that's unusual! I used a pound of dried pink beans, 2 ham bones that I had in the freezer and half water and half chicken broth. I cooked them all night and half the next day since the package of beans were old but it didn't matter with the end results. Great flavor and very filling. I served the beans over white rice with cornbread and honey on the side. The leftover beans are in the freezer for another meal. Thanks so much for posting this recipe.

Since this is the third time I've made this recipe in the last six months and thought it was about time I gave it the 5+ stars it deserves.  The flavor of these beans is just outstanding.  We had always used pintos for our ham and beans - and NEVER had we used cloves.  What a difference these are to what we were use to.  Thanks Sue!

excellent recipe for leftover ham!  i've made this many times with either canned black-eyed peas or canned great northern beans.  both were wonderful!  i use about 3 cans.  i also like to add diced carrots and celery if i have some around.  oh, and i cut the liquid down to 3 cups of chicken broth.  thanks for posting.  this is a crockpot keeper!  total comfort food.  always serve with cornbread muffins!

I've made this several times now, and everytime it's a huge hit with my family. I don't use as much salt because i find the ham adds its own salty flavor; also i don't like cloves so i omit that... and i've started adding celery and carrots as another reviewer suggested. this stuff is yummy and cheap! thanks for posting!

This is a great and hearty soup.  I used lentils instead of any kind of beans cause that is all I had at the time.  Cooked it all day in the crock pot and it came out perfectly.  Will be making this again and again.

This is very good!!! I followed directions exactly, but my my beans were still hard after 8 hours ( crock pot must be getting old) and the broth did not taste so good, so I let it cook over night and I also added a chicken cube. Was really good next day the broth was delicious and creamy,the beans and ham were also good, will make this recipe again.

Very yummy! I used half chicken broth and half water, and used 1 ham hock and a pound of cubed ham. It was delicious, I let it cook about 10 hours on low while I was at work all day. My husband loved it as well.  Definitely a keeper!!!!!
Excellent with corn bread!

Had it been up to me entirely, I would of given 5 stars, only to be a leming.  This was so good and warm.  I followed the recipe almost exact, used 4 cups chicken broth, 2 cups water, used prediced garlic, and smidge of cloves.  Used the leftovers of a honeybaked ham, would of liked to add carrots, but didn't have any, it needed some color.  Threw in the gel under the ham, used a white onion,also half cup diced celery, cooked it on high for 4 hours, had enough to share a big bowl with neighbors and still have enough for lunch today. This will definately become a keeper, but next time I am adding a half cup of diced carrots.

New Year's Day!  The tradition is to eat Black Eyed Peas or some type of Lentils for good luck for the coming year.  WELLLLL!  I was lucky to find this recipe from Sue!  Followed it exactly  (as I'm not a from scratch bean cooker).  Added a can of Black-Eyed Peas at the end,just cuz of the tradition! Took only 5hrs in my crock pot. Thankyou, Sue.  Blessings to you and yours this New Year.

Wow! Unbelievable - used homemade smoked chicken broth, mixed dry beans, and smoked ham shank. I've made ham and beans for years....... but this is the best by far (don't forget the crushed cloves - they add a whole new dimensions!)

SOOOOOOOOOO good.  Used homemade beef broth and some vegetable broth.  Also added about a tablespoon of tomato paste.  Didn't have any ham hocks so I used about a lb. of ham steak, diced, and added about 2 teaspoons liquid smoke.  Perfect...didn't even have to add salt.  This made a pot of tasty, tender beans that we enjoyed with cornbread.  Thanks, Sue!

This was a big hit. I used dried lima beans, to recreate my father-in-law's butter beans. DH said it was very close, and gave it a thumbs up. It did take longer than 8 hours to cook - next time, I'll start on high for a few hours, then switch to low. Served with cornbread. Thanks for sharing! -- Update: I've had good luck with cooking it for 3.5 hours on high, then 5 hours on low, or just 5 hours on high.
This is what I was raised on!!  Very simple, easy & cheap.  So tasty!  Great with cornbread and raw onions :)  Thanks for posting this!
Very good!  I made with no changes, except used 4 chicken boullion cubes to the 6 cups of water and omitted the salt.  We loved them!

I never thought of adding cloves to them. Gives a really nice, "I wonder what that is?" flavor addition to the beans.

Great recipe.

I like to chop carrots and celery very finely and add to mine, also.
I love this recipe. My hubby is usually not a bean eater. He went back for seconds, and I was so surprised. We are having them again for dinner tonight. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

Wow!  These were really delicious!  I did not use a crock pot, just soaked for 24 hours and cooked over low heat for 2 hours.  The cloves and garlic add a nice touch, and the beans hold really well in the fridge for those great leftovers :)  I also liked the fact that they were not too salty (I used a 1 1/2 lb. ham steak).  Will definitely make these again. Thanks for the simple recipe!
Very good. Made it for my bf by request and really enjoyed it. Thank you for a great blast from the past :)
wonderful recipe , my husband ate it all in a day and a half :) great taste

Loved loved loved how it wasn't too salty!  I used more beans than called for, but also used more ham, so it all worked out.  Even my non-bean eating son tolerated this, while usually he makes a gaggy face.  I'll be making this again!

Wow, this is amazing .
Emeril has a very similar recipe on the food network web site.
Made a printed copy where it is going to be kept for safe keeping.
Only thing I did differently was to cook it on top of the stove

I made this once and thought I had the recipe down, because it's so simple. I used nutmeg instead of clove. Hope this isn't too weird tasting. Anyway, we love this recipe. I'm serving it with sweet potato biscuits and apple fritters. Since it makes way more than what we eat, I'm even taking some across the street to my grams'.
My family hated it and we could hardly choke it down.  The clove gives this a very funny taste. I will try the recipe again with out the clove.
We made this with our leftover Thanksgiving ham bone and it was really good.  I added some diced carrots, and let it cook all day.  Thank you for sharing.

I made this exactly as written and it was absolutley Delicious! I was afraid because of someone else's review that the cloves would be too strong, but I loved the flavor it gives to this! I cooked mine the day before and rewarmed in the crockpot the next day, so good! Thanks for posting!!

This was so good! Thank you!!! My son just had spacers put in yesterday preparing for braces, and his mouth aches terribly. I knew I needed to make something for dinner that he could eat, and came across this. If I remember correctly, I had a dry socket when I had my wisdom teeth pulled and they used clove oil with gauze to pack it. This was perfect for the soon to be brace face. Yummy, Filling and Medicinal. The whole family enjoyed this! My husband even liked it, and he is not a bean fan.

I had a lot of leftover pork roast, and chose this recipe because of it's good reviews.  I must admit I was a little disappointed.  I made it exactly as written, but when it was done, it was really a thin broth like a soup, and was bland.  I added more of the spices, 2-3 times what the recipe called for, plus some cayenne pepper and nutmeg.  I also added some cornstarch to thicken the broth.  It was good after the adjustments, and we did like the clove/allspice seasoning.
These are good and filling and a little different with the cloves.  Thanks!

This recipe is VEEERY good. Ive never used cloves before so I was a little worried at first after tasting the broth. But it all came together in the end, the only thing I did different was, I added a dash of sugar, and a little less ground cloves. Thank you so much for this great recipe!!
This is good but I could really detect a strong flavor of cloves.  I had trouble getting past that taste, so I probably won't make again, unless I leave the cloves out.

After cooking until done, I have found that I can remove the clear liquid before stirring the first time. Then I add back the liquid as needed for the consistency I want. Also, not all ham hocks are made equal. A large well smoked Hock makes a big difference over an average supermarket one. I add salt add pepper after I have adjusted the amount of liquid. I use the removed liquid to continue extracting flavor from the inedible pieces of Hock for the next batch of beans. A good hock has plenty of flavor to share. My favorites are Split Peas and Butter Beans (large dried limas), but the others follow close behind. I do think the an over night soaking is better than the one hour technique. The texture is different - unless you are cooking until the beans are very soft, then it doesn't matter.

I wasn't sure how this would go over, but hubby loved it (as did I)!  I will definitely make this again.  Like others, I used canned beans.  It came out perfectly creamy!  (Note: We did transfer it to a pot to boil off excess liquid.)

YUM YUM YUM! This was a tasty recipe. I used red beans soaked overnight. I thought it wouldn't be very rich with just the spices that were listed, but it was! Even my picky eater of a son loved it too. Used a smoked ham hock for $4 and the rest was on-hand. Made spanish rice to have a beans and rice dish. My SO made tortas to go to it. Phenomenal and delicious :) Definitely will be keeping this recipe.

Added a carrot for additional flavor.

This called for far too much onion. I ended up fishing out as much onion as I could before it cooked all the way. I also prefer my ham & beans to be creamy instead of a thin broth with some chunks of ham and beans, so I searched online and found a recipe that called for cream of mushroom soup. I added a can of that and it was really good. My husband thought it was too salty, but I thought it was perfect with the modifications I made to the recipe.

I am making this for the second time today, and I can't wait.  This is the best ham and bean that I have ever had.  This makes the old celery-and-onion version just seem bland!  I also appreciate the "quick soak" method for pre-softening the beans.  I think this makes all the difference in the world for a nice, soft yet whole, bean.  I don't have a crock pot, so I followed the recipe exactly and just cooked it on the stove top with excellent results.  Leftovers didn't make it past Day 3 last time I made this.  We LOVED it!

This recipe was so good I even joined up so I could review it. I grew up on my mom's ham and beans and never tried anything different.  I was looking for directions for crockpot beans and came across this recipe.  I didn't like the way it smelled the whole time it was cooking and thought maybe I had made a mistake, but it is scrumptious!  And I prepared it exactly as the recipe states, using chicken 'stock' made with vegetarian chicken flavored base I got at the health food store (simply because I had no stock available) and only a small piece of a ham steak we had for Easter.  We all liked it very much and that's saying a lot for me to switch to this from my Mom's recipe.  We'll be eating it again.

This was a big hit. I used dried lima beans, to recreate my father-in-law's butter beans. DH said it was very close, and gave it a thumbs up. It did take longer than 8 hours to cook - next time, I'll start on high for a few hours, then switch to low. Served with cornbread. Thanks for sharing! -- Update: I've had good luck with cooking it for 3.5 hours on high, then 5 hours on low, or just 5 hours on high.

This is delicious and easy to make. Because we try not to eat pork(because of health and religious reasons) I use smoked turkey wings or drumsticks. I throw in a package of onion soup and a shot of liquid smoke to the recipe. Thanks Sue.

It was too watery and bland.  I was hoping for a hearty dinner with depth of flavor.  really worried but was able to salvage it.  An hour before it was finished  doubled the pepper & added bay leaf & a teaspoon of crushed red pepper.  I left the lid ajar hoping the broth would thicken for the last hour.  didn't use corn startch as some reviews used, ended up thickening the broth with 1/4 cup instant potatoes.

This was fabulous!  I used lima beans since that is our go-to bean, with smoked ham.  I did throw in a dash or two of cayenne. I let it cook on low for 7 hours. I will definitely make these again.  I made homemade buttermilk cornbread to accompany this and to soak up some of the juices left in the bowl.  Yum!

This is hands down the best ham and beans I've ever had. I don't even typically like ham and beans, but I made this for my husband and we both loved it. I made as directed except I added 1/4 cup of brown sugar (packed). Also, I cooked it on high for 3 hours and then on low for about 4-5 hours. If you make this and it's not thickening up yet, it's just not done. Mine started to thicken around the 7 hour mark, and there was a HUGE difference. Thank you for a fantastic recipe, we will enjoy this one a lot this winter!
One more thing.....I cooked them in the crock pot on high for 6 hours as I did not have 8+ hours.  They were perfectly done!
2 thumbs up
I make this all the time. My kids love it. And to the previous post who said it was bland...pork roast is not ham!!! If you don't follow the recipe then don't give it a bad review!

I made this and made a few changes. I soaked the beans for 24 hours in water. Used garlic power and not the real stuff and cooked it in crockpot on high for 8 hours. Was very good and not a real thick and Heavy ham and beans. Was a big hit with my family.

I've made this for my family and big groups. Like the Lady who said it made a difference whether you use pork roast or ham/ham hocks knows what she's talking about! Onions can be changed according to what's on hand but the rest I followed to a T! Sister used to say, "When mamma makes ham fat & beans 3 days in a row, it meant times were a little lean!" I just knew I loved them & knew that some timed we were probably blessed to have that! Hope younger people know that dishes like these can get you through tough times. And very nutritious! Thanks for helping me get back to a recipe so close to my momma's!
I loved it except I used bay leaf instead of cloves.
Sauté carrots, onions, and celery and add to the crock after 6 hours along with bay leafs. Finish seasoning with Herb de Provence. Turned out great.
I use great nothern beans correct?

Ok, mine did not turn out as great. First off, if you are using a large crock pot, i would double the salt and pepper and make sure the liquid is over the beans in the crock pot (i should've known better). My beans were not cooked through after 8hrs with 2hrs on high ( i used the boiling method of soaking to the "t") Also, I ended up adding brown sugar, like 2 tablespoons. I also added savory and more parsley. I followed the recipe but did not put in cloves (can't stand cloves unless its fall or Christmas!) It tastes wonderful now but again the beans are not done so we keep checking with some done and 1/4 not done.

Wanted something hearty, but did not want to heat up the kitchen in this hot weather. And decided to give this a try. I used a mix of both pinto and navy beans, and soaked over night. Had left over ham so used that instead of ham hocks and followed the directions. Beans were done at the time directed and the flavor was hearty and delicious, We did add garlic and wish I'd followed another reviewers advise and added some stewed tomatoes just because we like them. Served with home made sourdough bread and made for an easy, filling meal and didn't heat up the kitchen. A versatile recipe that can easily be adjust to personal taste.

Direct quote from the husband after dinner: “this is the best ham and beans you’ve ever made.” I used left over smoked ham from Thanksgiving. The only tweak I did was I subbed out the cloves and added two bay leaves. Very flavorful! This recipe is a keeper.

If you want your meal be ready, then only use High setting on the crock pot. You will thank me later. Other than that, it is perfect. Also, do not forget to make a skillet corn bread by the Pioneer Woman. It only takes 30 minutes, and it is unbelievable!
I followed the directions exactly. This soup is delicious!

First time I made ham and beans and it turned out excellent I used One tablespoon of pure maple syrup instead of cloves took to my parents and friend and they couldn't stop talking about it will be making this again. Thanks for this wonderful recipe.
Made as directed. My husband ate two bowls! Very good. Will make this again.

I found this recipe a couple weeks ago. We have made it twice already. I never comment on these sites but it's so good I had to recommend! We used chicken broth and 6 cans great white northern beans drained. It was faster. Thanks!

I've always wanted to find a better recipe for ham and beans. They can be so bland! Even with salt and pepper and onions. I tweaked a little because I added a few more beans. I also added 1/4 cup of maple syrup to help a little with the ground cloves. It was excellent!
If you find your broth is too watery, you can use a potato masher and mash a few beans. This will thicken your soup.
This recipe is delicious, I added chopped red and green peppers too. Yummy! I'm making it again tomorrow. I was surprised my teenage son loved it too!

Followed the recipe exactly but it needs something... acidic. Not sure what to try. Maybe some cayenne and tomato sauce or even some rice wine vinegar. Seems like a good base, I like that it doesn't have sugar. Will play with it until I love it!
What reduces the gas in ham hock and beans?
can I use can beans? that's all we have.

Made it and substituted the following: no cloves = 3 bay leaves, put 6 cups of broth plus 2 cups of water. Added 2 stalks of celery, carrots, bit of cumming, salted pork diced up. It turned out delicious! Oh cooked for 6 hrs on high. Family loved it! Ate the whole thing!

Doubled the recipe so I could have some to freeze. It turned out much waterier than I expected, so I mashed some of the beans to thicken it and we ended up with ham and bean soup. I saw that some people had found it too salty, so I used unsalted beef broth. It was very tasty, but missing something. Maybe something acidic? A can of crushed tomatoes, maybe, or lemon juice. Also, I wasn't a huge fan of the warm clove flavor note; I think I would skip it next time. It thickened like crazy overnight, so when I do thaw and reheat it, I will need to add more broth. Perhaps will add the acidic notes then.

It was great...omitted the carrots....it was flavorful and easy.....my husband said he could eat it often....even had it the next day....had green chills/corn and cheese corn bread with it the second night I give it 5 stares
I enjoyed this. It makes a nice, plump log and slices so cleanly. It's pretty versatile; thinly sliced in a sandwich, breaded and dipped in BBQ sauce. Thanks for posting AJO.

This was delicious - very meaty.  I did not have any paprika or allspice so I substituted it with additional cayenne pepper.  It turned out great, super easy and quick to prepare, I will definitely be making this again.   I doubt I'll need to buy meat substitutes again! Next time I will try baking these in smaller logs in an attempt for sausage.  The taste was great.  My boyfriend ate it with mashed potatoes and saurkraut, I had some with bbq sauce.  Fantastic, thanks for posting! *Edit: I just wanted to add that I continue to make and love this recipe. I've had success making a double batch and cooking an extra 15 minutes, I also make meat crumbles out of this by putting it in my food processor.  This is good stuff!

I made this recipe after finding it on the PPK site and loved it. I ended up having a few meals with it (BBQ Seitan and 2 different types of chili). It was pretty easy to make as well. This is going to sound so weird, but it tasted like a mix between pumpkin pie and pepperoni. Next time, I'll leave out or cut back on the cinnamon.

***EDIT: I changed the spices around the 2nd time and it was even better: salt, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, parsley, and used broth instead of water. MUCH MUCH better!

Really good, super easy and SO versatile...a MUST basic for any VEG HEAD...LOVE IT!!! :) my husband has patiently put up with my vegetarian whims for 20 years and he was thrilled with this!!! thanks AJO...made for "Healthy Choices Tag Game" - **A WINNER**

we liked this a lot. I skipped the cinnamon based on one of the reviews that it resembled pumpkin pie flavorings. I also skipped the allsice. I found this to be very easy. Such an all purpose recipe, you could change the seasoning to make it like sausage, pepperoni, chicken etc. Never pay for high priced seitan again!

This was good, very meaty. We aren't vegan or vegetarian, but have been trying to find some healthier and less processed substitutes for some meats, and this is a winner. We put it in the food processor to substitute as ground beef as another reviewer suggested. Next time I think I will change the spices up too, to make it more meatball-like instead of pepperoni-like. Thanks so much AJO!

I too found this on the PPK, and love it!

I am not vegan, but am vegetarian and was looking to not rely on so many foods like cheese and eggs (I still eat them, just trying to moderate things).

I use the spices as-is, but haven't been able to find vegan worchesterschire sauce, so instead, I use 2 tbs red miso.

I love this!

Fabulous! I tripled the recipe, and changed up the spices a bit. I was aiming for a "smoked turkey" tasting substitute. The addition of liquid smoke, onion powder and poultry seasoning helped. I left out the cinnamon, allspice and cumin. I used half tamari, and half Braggs. I ended up slicing this pretty thinly on an electric slicer, and making panini with it and some brie, pesto and baby spinach. Wonderful directions, Ajo, thanks!

This is the THE BEST seitan log I have made to date.  It was very moist and flavorful.  I chose to omit the cinnamon, cumin and allspice.  I added 1 teaspoon of onion powder instead.  It was such a huge hit, we ate 2/3 of it for dinner tonight. Thanks for posting a fantastic recipe!

After discovering this recipe on the site, it is now one of the most versatile recipes in my arsenal.  Like user veggie_mama, I also omit the cinnamon, cumin, and allspice.  I add onion powder in their place.  My household enjoys just snacking on the log throughout the day.  Its so good!  When I make tofu lasagna, I crumble part of the log up and throw it in my vegan "ricotta" mixture.  It gives it an extra kick!  So many ways to use this recipe in others.

Delicious, amazing, and so simple!!  This was my first time making it, so I decided to use the combination of spices as written.  I think I did omit the cinnamon only.  The allspice comes through loud and clear...  I ight make it one more time exactly as written, and then try some other spice combos.  I used the seitan sliced thin for sandwiches: wheat bread, lettuce, tomato and mustard.  I also diced the rest of the log and made it into a taco filling, YUM
This recipe is awesome! Definitely try it once as is and then break out the customizations.

The first seitan recipe I made, and it was a huge success! I always play around a bit with the spices and sometimes add some liquid smoke to make it taste sausage-y, but it always turns out fantastic!

This is delicious.  I made it exactly as the recipe calls for and can't believe how tasty it is.  I am going to try to experiment with other spices next.  I think it comes out much more compact than when I boiled my seitan for an hour in a broth mixture.  That was also very good but the seitan was not nearly as firm as baking made it.  This was also very easy to do.  I highly recommend trying it.

This recipe is awesome! It was my first attempt at making my own seitan & i'm so happy with the way it came out. I didn't use allspice or cinnamon because I didn't have any on hand. I also added onion powder (1 tsp), as suggested by some of the other reviewers. Thank you for sharing!
I'm new to vegetarian cooking and this recipe was easy to follow and turned out beautifully. I look forward to trying other spice combinations.

My first experience with making my own meat substitute.  I left out the "sweeter" spices, but added onion like others did.  I'll definitely make this again, cause I can see flavoring this with crumbled seaweed to make a fish patty, using poultry seasoning for turkey type things.  I will either double wrap this next time or cook less, as mine got pretty dark on the down side of my log.  Tasty though.  Thanks for sharing.

We enjoyed these cupcakes a lot!  The chocolate cake was moist and very light.  The buttermilk flavor helped to make it not so sweet.  I found that overfilling the baking cups is a huge mistake.  The batter seems really light, almost as if you'd added stiff egg whites to it, so I filled them just a little more than 3/4 of the way full, but it was a mistake.  The batter expands a lot more than I expected and it made several of the cupcakes a bit insubstantial.  If anything, I would fill the cups just a bit more than half full to keep all that goodness in!  Thanks for this recipe, it was wonderful and we're going to see if the next batch lasts long enough to ice!
Texture of this cake is great but I found it lacks the chocolatey flavour and am wondering if salted butter might work better. Will tweak this recipe and try again because I do like the texture.

These cupcakes are delicious!  The batter was so smooth and creamy. I made a simple vanilla frosting and since my son is 6, there were lotsa sprinkles on the frosting!  I made them for his kindergarten class and they were a hit with the kids!  Thanks for sharing and posting this recipe!  I'll definitely make these again.
Great cupcakes; nice and moist. It did come out a little too sticky, so I might have needed to leave it in the oven for a few more minutes. Topped it with peanut butter frosting, and it was perfect.
While the flavor was good, the cupcakes were kind of dry and crumbly. Even the adults had a hard time eating them 'neatly'. I used Recipe #261024 and it complimented the flavor nicely. Thanks!

These cupcakes released nicely from the papers without any stickiness (as others have commented).  I didn't find that there was a strong chocolate flavor, which was disappointing because i used a high quality dark chocolate (i didn't offset the sugar in any way either).  The texture was light, fluffy and moist.  For me, regular sized cupcakes cooked by 19 minutes, mini cupcakes cooked in 10 minutes.  Using "standard sized" liners filled 2/3 this recipe yeilded 24 standard cupcakes (no dome-just flat) and 30 mini cupcakes (slight dome).  I would make again, but may add some sifted cocoa to the flour so that the cupcake will turn out darker (it was pretty light for a chocolate cupcake).

Delicious! I just made half a batch of them. Yummy! Im eating one now. I think its actually really good, although I havent tried the buttercream frosting, Im eating it alone. It tastes like Cocoa Pebbles. For a homemade chocolate cupcake recipe it tastes really good. The next day or days, it will taste better. I cant imagine how good it will taste w/ frosting. Next time, I make this, Im going to add some milk choco. chips into the batter, and frost it with a homemade ganache frosting!! Thanks for this recipe. Its really nice to have on hand, you should always have a homemade choco cake recipe and a homemade vanilla cake recipe. You can of course turn any cupcake batter into a cake batter, and just cook from anywhere to 35-50 min, you just have to watch it. Thank you so much!!

I just made half a batch of these. It was my first time making a cupcake period and they turned out great! They were moist, came off the paper easily, and tasted wonderful! I had no trouble with the color- they were a rich deep brown. I frosted them with a different recipe for caramel cream cheese frosting and they were amazing that way! I used very basic chocolate from Baker's brand. To me, this chocolate tastes like Cocoa powder and so does the cupcake a bit so if you want a richer chocolate taste I'd take that into account- maybe a slightly sweet chocolate rather than unsweetened would do the trick? half the recipe make about 15 standard cupcakes. I filled the liners 2/3 full as others suggested. I baked them for 19-20 min. Great recipe!

I made these before reading previous reviews. I made them for a special occasion. Thankfully I made them the day before and had time to make something else. These were VERY dry. I followed the recipe exactly using new and fresh ingredients with the exception that I baked them for two minutes less than the recipe called for -- seems like that would have made them moister. Since the batter was a lot thicker than any cake batter I've made before, I filled the cupcake liners to the top thinking they wouldn't rise as much - they didn't even rise 1/4". I don't even know what 'tweak' would have made them edible. I frosted them with cream cheese frosting. I tried one after a couple hours and decided there was no way I could salvage them - I threw them out. I bake quite a bit and can't figure out how they could have gone so wrong for me, but more than acceptable to others, especially the review that said they are "moist".

Barbara,this is a very good cream of broccoli soup.
I do wish it had been thicker,I like it extra thick.I will just add more butter and flour the next time I make the soup.
I served the soup with sourdough bread.Yum!
Thank you for sharing your recipe.
Wonderful !! Very easy

A flvourful recipe! I didn't have 2 cans of chicken broth, so I substituted it with 1 can of half-fat cream of chicken soup. I also cut back on the butter, by simmering the onion, garlic, and celery in a little bit of the broth. Serve it with some homestyle flavored croutons.
An excellent cream soup.  I didn't have enough broccoli so I substituted some cauliflower and carrots.  I also used cheddar instead of velveeta.  I highly recommned this tasty soup!

I left in some bigger pieces of broccoli because i like the texture, and I substituted Colby cheese because I never have Velveeta, and it was still fantastic. I'll definitely be making this one for years to come. Thanks for a great recipe!

The first time I made this it was going to be my standard.  The last time, we weren't impressed.  I must  have done something wrong so I'm writing this review to remind myself to try again and follow the recipe carefully.  It was bland tasting on round 2.

This soup was FABULOUS! I made a few modifications to fit what I had in my kitchen...
I used frozen broccoli and didn't have Velveeta, so I used some jarred Tostitos cheese dip. I added a few mashed potato flakes in the last step to make it thicker.  Also, I didn't puree, as I like my soup a little thicker. I did use a potato masher a little bit however.  

Thanks for this recipe! It was perfect for a cold afternoon.
This is a very good recipe, I used  part 1/2 and 1/2 and part milk and no cheese. We enjoyed it this way many times. Thanks for posting.

This is the second time I made this and my hubby said it was the best soup I have ever made (I make soup once a week during the winter!) It was great!  I left some chucks of broccoli for added texture.  I think I will try it w/ cauliflower next time. Great recipe base! Thanks!

The celery and onion gives the soup extra flavor but in my opinion, it is way too creamy. I decided not to have a second serve afterwards. Nevertheless, the husband said that the soup was pretty good and he likes it.
Love it! Will now be a staple in my house.

Excellent soup!  Even though there are so many good reviews, I was nervous to make this because I had never made a cream soup from scratch.  It was delicious, easy, and my husband and I were pleasantly surprised.  The flavor is creamy and you can really taste the broccoli.  The cheese flavor from the Velveeta is not strong, it just adds to the creaminess.  The only change I made was to add 3 cloves of garlic instead of one.  Highly recommend!

very good soup!!  i probably put in alittle more than four cups of broccoli..four good sized broccoli crowns, all chopped up..also, i used five or six minced garlic cloves..added one more celery stalk..and i definitely put in more velveeta..at least a cups worth, if not more..in the end, i also sprinkled in 'lawrys salt seasoning' to taste..was a hit!!!  thank you!!!

Well Barb..add another 5 stars to your list !  This is better than any soup I've eaten in a restaurant (and I made it myself....who knew?)
I used 1 c. 2% milk and 1 c. half/half. I also used 4T.butter and 4T. flour for the thickening. I didn't puree all the broccoli (I like to have a few chunks in it), and I diced up 1 medium potato and cooked with the broccoli. 
I think next time I will also add some cauliflower......so many variations keep coming to mind for this wonderful recipe. THANK YOU  ! 
Donna

This was fabulous. I did use 1 cup whipping cream, as I needed to use it up, and then 1 cup milk. I did not have velveeta, so used mild cheddar, and it was the creamiest soup ever. I also did add a little salt and pepper for us it just added a little more flavor. Just wonderful. Thank you for the addition to my cookbook.
Wonderful soup. I made it with non-fat milk and a dash of half-and-half and for the cheese used low-fat shredded cheddar. Tasted fantastic!
It really is the best!

U talk about a game winning touchdown? this easy 2prepare broccoli won the game! barb, very delicious. what a shame that i cant rate more than 5stars 4this recipe. u have a definite winner here! 2thumbs up ma'am ....
If you love broccoli and cheese and warm goodness on a cold winter's day, this is the soup! Thanks, Barb, for a great recipe!
great, easy, yummy! My 9 yr old said it was the best broc soup I've ever made. had to use cheddar and was just fine.

Terrific soup.  We had a large bowl each and still had leftovers.  I put them in the frig for lunch and DH came out with a cup and dipped out another cup full of soup.  He usually doesnt do this but said it was sooo good he needed a little more.  SO much for lunch.  Gloria

This was really good.  It didn't take that long to make and everybody loves it.  I used vegetable broth instead of chicken, and mashed it with a potato masher.  This left big delicious chunks which I love. I also used cheddar cheese and served with croutons.  Yum!

Excellent Soup!  Words can't say enough how good this soup was.  I doubled the recipe so I'd have lots, and glad I did since the family couldn't get enough.  I also like it a little thicker and creamier, so I added an extra single batch of the roux.  Delicous!  Thanks Barb.

This is such a great recipe!!!!

I added a ton more broccoli and about 4 more sticks of celery, plus two cloves of garlic.  Plus, I used cornstarch instead of flour, cream instead of milk, and I used 150g of Boursin cheese instead of Velveeta.  

Thanks so much for posting this!!!!

~~

This was a very good broccoli soup.  I looove broccoli soup and have been searching for the ultimate best recipe.  This was pretty close to the best Ive had.  I did add more cheese bc I love it cheesy.  I also added a little garlic powder.  Very good soup!  Nice and thick like I like it.  Thanks for the recipe.

This is a very good soup even though I forgot to add the milk-- LOL.  I will probably re-rate it the next time I make it.  I made subs:  soy marg for butter, powdered garlic for garlic clove, shallots for onion, no celery, real chicken broth, gluten free flour, and Trader Joe's block mozerella (1/2 cup).  Forgot the milk but would have used orig. almond milk.  Was very tasty.
Great soup for a cold night.

During broccoli season, I was looking for a way to use up my bumper crop besides just freezing it. This delicious recipe was the answer!  I made the base, pureed, and froze it, adding a label with the instruction for the cream sauce.  When ready to serve, I defrost the base in the microwave while I make the cream sauce, then combine the two parts and sprinkle in the cheese (I use Cheddar).  It was wonderful!  It would be even easier using Vina's suggestion of just adding cream to the base.  Thanks, Barb, for a delicious and useful recipe.

I have been making this for years, the only thing I do different is add
a good splash of cooking sherry, and make a cheese sauce (putting shredded cheddar in with the cream sauce until melted) instead of Velveeta, next time I'll try the Velveeta it might be easier.

VERY good soup recipe. I used a cheddar cheese instead of Velveeta and I used about 1-1/2 cups of the cheddar. I also substituted about a half a cup of the milk for with half and half and it turned out great! My BF loved too. Will make again for sure. Thanks!

This was great! Only bad thing is that this is one of those hearty soups that fills you up very quickly! I barely ate enough to fill up a coffee mug. I added a dash of cayene pepper and used about 6oz of velvetta and 4 oz shredded sharp cheese. Used 1 cup half and half and 1 cup evaporated milk. served this with crusty bread and some oven roasted chicken wings. Dipping the bread in the soup was my favorite part. I only wish I could've ate more!
My family and I LOVED the recipe! (Substituted Velveeta with Cheddar cheese though) Thanks for sharing!

Yes, definitely a 5 star recipes.  I used 1/2 of an onion I had left from another recipe and it was still almost too much .. so probably depends on the size of the onion.  I think next time I'll limit the onion to 1/2 cup of chopped onion.  I also used my own homemade chicken broth so it's a little richer than what you buy in the store.  I need to use up the broccoli in the garden so this is going to fill the bill ... I'll have plenty of great soup to eat throughout the year.  Thanks for a great recipe.
Great tasting soup.  Thanks for posting.

Very good.  Even my husband liked it and he is not a soup guy!  I will probably try it with cheddar next time and see how that compares.  With the leftover soup the next day I added some leftover baked potato chunks and shredded chicken... that was quite good too!
OUTSTANDING! I followed the recipe exactly except I used 1/2 cup of Cabot seriously sharp cheddar. Thank you for posting such a wonderful recipe!
Velveeta!  You have to be kidding, this is not even cheese.  As some of the members have done, please substitute with cheddar or even swiss cheese.
Easy and yummy!

I agree with others- This was excellent- and EASY!  I was not sure whether I was supposed to cook the broccoli first or not- I did.  I added about 1.25 cups mild cheddar and it was excellent- I think sharp would have been even better.  Thanks for a great recipe.

Another fabulous recipe Barb!  I added about 1/8 tsp cayenne (could have used more) and a 1/2 tsp thyme.  I also used about 5 cups broccoli (just to use up what I had) and about 1 cup extra sharp cheddar cheese.  DH loved it!  Thanks for sharing.
Very good.  I like that it is easy.  I added just a little sherry to give it a pop.  Also used Cabot very sharp cheddar.  Thank you for sharing.,

Good with Cabot Cheddar.
Has anyone frozen it? It made a lot for 2 people.

Very very good! I used aged sharp cheddar and swiss instead of velveeta, and did 1 cup lowfat milk and 1 cup heavy cream instead of 2 cups milk. But besides that, I followed the instructions down to the hand mixer (great idea!!). It was so easy! Absolutely delicious! I will definitely be making this again! Thanks Barb!
As a new cook, this was easy and delicious!  And yes, I followed the directions exactly, even using the Velveeta. I'm planning on bringing this to a soup luncheon at work!

I thought I found the perfect broccoli soup (Uncle Bill's #19107), but wanted to try one that used cheese.  Now I have two favorite broccoli soups, and both are easy and delicious.  I did substitute sharp chedder, and melted it into the white sauce; then added the sauce to the vegetable soup.  While the soup tasted great that way, I then incorporated one of Uncle Bill's soup secrets--a tablespoon of soy sauce.  You will not detect any soy sauce taste, but it does impart a more robust flavor.  Thanks Barb, for sharing another great recipe--all yours sound good.
Just as everyone else says... quick and easy and very yummy. I also used real cheddar. Thanks for sharing.

Excellent soup!  I didn't care for the other popular cream of broccoli soup recipe on this site, so when I received more broccoli from my food co-op, I decided to try this recipe and I'm so glad I did!  I sauteed the veggies in homemade vegetable broth instead of butter, skipped the flour and butter altogether, added about 1/4 cup of raw cashews (blended in my VitaMix--really makes soups like this creamy), used almond milk and used about 1 1/2 cups of sharp cheddar cheese in place of the velveeta.  I just realized I forgot to add the pepper and it's still delicious!  Normally I'm not a big fan of broccoli, but this makes it easy to like.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Yummy!  And even better the next day! Thanks for sharing - a great way to use broccoli when it is on sale.

I just made the soup and it is rich and delicious. I added more garlic and backed diced chicken (I used the gravy from the chicken in addition to the broth) to make a meal out of it. I had broccoli given to me from a veggie tray at a picnic and I could not eat all of it so I went online for this 5 star rescipie. My Mother is very picky but loved it also. I used the Velveeta but added cheddar also as I love cheddar.
This is so good and easy! I followed it exactly except used 1 cup half n half and 1 cup 1% milk. What a great recipe! Creamy and rich and savory. This is a keeper.
This was really good! I added a little salt and a few shakes of nutmeg and it sent it over the top. Thanks so much for sharing!
Not amazing but very good.
This soup is very good.  I did add a little extra cheese.  It was easy to make and inexpensive to make.  This recipe is a keeper,  thanks for sharing it.
This was good, but the velveeta made it too salty. Will try again with cheddar.
Absolutely delicious! I made it this week for my family and am now making it for a work potluck lunch. Thanks for sharing this great recipe!
A great soup!!

Just wonderful! I love making simple homemade soups in the winter! I used velveeta this time becuase it was left over, but I will normally use cheddar since its cheaper. I did not puree it becasue I like to chew my broccoli. I hollowed out 2 round loaves of sourdough bread and it almost tasted like I was at Panera! what a great comfort food!

Wow! I was really skeptical of this when preparing it. With no spices and the way it looked, I didn't see how it could taste pleasant.  I was very surprised! Like another person suggested, I added 1T soy sauce and I threw in cheddar cheese instead of Velveeta. I topped it off with pepper and yum! I can't wait to have it for lunch this week!
Really very good. Doubled the white sauce as it was too thin, added 1T soy sauce and used shredded mozzarella cheese as it was all we had.

The flavor of this soup is very good, but I took a star off because it was not very thick.  I will make this again for sure, but next time, I will either use less broth and/or milk, or more flour.  I also used real cheddar, not velveeta.
Absolutely delish!!! Worthy of 10 stars.....thanks.

This soup made 3 of the 4 troopers happy!  Like others here, I found the soup thinner than expected; I heartied it up with a cup of leftover roasted potatoes (everything pureed).  Nutmeg and a can of Cambell's mushroom soup was also added for extra flavor.  I was well-pleased with the end result.
Oh, and if your bechamel is to thin, keep it on the stove longer, and whip it up with a whisk until it has the consistency of cream cheese icing
Loved it , Velveeta included ;)

I found this to be a very comforting soup.  I made this for our dinner the other night and served it with paninis.  I pureed half the broccoli in this and left the other half whole.  I lovedthis.  Thank you for sharing this with us.

A bit bland at the start, but easy to tweak. I used lots of fresh grated sharp cheddar, added salt and I was surprised the recipe did not call for any salt. By the time I was done.. I loved it. I am giving this 5 stars because the base is great and easy to tweak. Let's be honest, since I didn't use velvet cheese and made other adjustments, I would have the right to rate this since I didn't follow the recipe.
Loved it!  Did use gouda instead of velveeta (maybe even 1 cup) and left out celery b/c we didn't have any.

Loved it! But in fairness, I changed it ...I used 1/2 cup 1% milk and 1 1/2 cups of pureed cauliflower (my own favority sneaky trick on my kids) instead of the 2 cups of milk, I cut the broth in 1./2 (due to many reviews about the thinness of the soup) and pureed 1 cup of brocolli and put the rest in chunky to compensate with heavier liquid. Also, I cut the velvetta and used fresh chunk mozzerella with a sprinkle of fresh parmesan crumble. That was a taste-based change - We opt more for the Italian cheeses than the cheddars and such. Plus, I like to keep this a white soup base (again, that is a child-based negotiation).

Nutmeg!!

Yummy!!! Thank you for sharing and inspiring.

Excellent soup!  And so easy.  I was limited to what I had on hand so used frozen broccoli, red onion and Half & Half in place of milk.  I was also intrigued by several reviewer's use of a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce - so I added that and I must say, the flavor effect was subtle but very, very nice.  And I have nothing against Velveeta, but I don't keep it on hand, so I used sharp cheddar.  Overall a very nice broccoli cheese soup that I will make again.  Thanks for posting!

This soup was excellent.  However rather than using Velvetta I used 4 oz of cream cheese.  I don't have anything against Velvetta it is just that it is not something I purchase.  Cream cheese is a staple in our home.  This soup was fantastic.
Delicious! Never made soup before so I was a little anxious to try this out, but it turned out really well!

My family loves this,we have it at least twice a month during the winter months. I have tweeked it a bit. Instead of doing plain milk,I use 2 cups FF evaporated milk and instead of velveeta I use 1 1/2 c shredded cheddar cheese soup. I am in the process of attempting to convert this to a Crock Pot recipe. If I am successfull,I will post a comment again.

I can't believe this is the hightest ranking cream of broccoli soup, not a single review even follows the ingrediants to any detail.  I tried to follow it but couldn't.<br/>My recipe:<br/>4 cups water<br/>2 tablespoons boullion  I use "Better the Boullion"<br/>4 heads of broccoli<br/>3 stalk of celley<br/>1 leek ( just because I had one)<br/>I small onion<br/>3 Yukon Gold potatoes<br/><br/>boil 15minutes<br/>mash with potato masher<br/>Add:<br/>4 T butter<br/>4 tablespoons flour or less of cornstarch<br/>2 cups milk<br/>blend in separte pan before adding<br/><br/>ad 3/4 -1 cup cheese (not velvetta)
Fabulous!  wasn't paying attention to detail and mixed my milks:  1 canned milk and 1/2 cup skim.  Think I'll do ths from now on tho.  Velvety smooth.  Great recipe-good times.

Great recipe, very easy to tweak to your own personal tastes. I put in a cup of regular marble cheese instead of the half cup of  Velveeta, and used carrots instead of celery. Also steamed a small head of broccoli to throw in after the blending to make it a little more chunky. <br/>The kids absolutely loved it, and it is quite filling so it goes far!<br/>Thanks!

This was excellent.  I used a broccoli crown and shredded the stems before cooking (in a blender with one can of the broth).  I used an extra can of broth because two cans didn't cover the amount of broccoli I used.  I used a pint of half and half instead of milk. It probably wasn't as thick at it should have been due to the extra can of broth but the taste was superb.  I'll be making this again for sure...

Clearly, this recipe does not need another 5* review, but I couldn't resist. I had some broccoli & cream that I needed to use up, and selected this recipe. I omitted the celery (didn't have any), used a head of broccoli without measuring, used part cream and the rest whole milk, and used Gouda and a small handful of Parmesan (actually Grana Padano, which is just as delicious & cheaper). Followed the method in accordance with the recipe. This is terrific! I loved the delicious broccoli taste, and do not agree with those who said the soup needed additional flavor - I feel that other spices would disguise the taste of the broccoli, which was not my intent. For me, this was a WOW! recipe that I will be making again frequently.
amazing soup

I love this Cream of Broccoli Soup.  I made it today and it is delicious.  I don't know what people have against Velveeta, I think it is great.  Melts wonderfully and gives the soup a smooth creamy taste.  Thank you for sharing.  I will make this often.

Good, but too thin, grainy instead of creamy, and just not very robust flavor. If I make again, I will add the teaspoon of soy sauce as suggested and I will eliminate the homemade "momveeta" cheese that I used (google it if curious) and just use a nice rich whole cheese like the boursin mentioned below. Gives me a good idea as the base though.

I can't believe I've never reviewed this, as I make it ALL the time. It makes 6 big bowlfuls and is delicious. The only thing I do different is use 1/2 cup shredded cheddar for the cheese - but otherwise I follow the recipe exactly and it always comes out perfect.

I made these cupcakes for a party which included kids of all ages.  To add to the fun about half the batter was used to make regular sized cupcakes and the rest small 2-bite mini cupcakes.  Since this was rather last minute, except for the butter, my creations were made with all non-fat or reduced fat ingredients as that is what I have in the house. The cake was delicious and I forsee making it again with fresh fruit for more formal occasions. Its the kind of cake that holds up well to additions but enough good flavor and texture to stand on its own.   The highlight was the fantastic peanut butter frosting.  Incredibly creamy and delicious.  Totally sinful and decadent.  Worked really well in this recipe, but should be considered for other cakes such as a dark chocolate cake.  I did add a touch of salt which elevated the peanut flavor.  The cupcakes themselves were a huge hit and while the minis were a bit more labor intensive than I planned, they were by far more popular.  Everyone had fun grabbing one and trying to guess what kind of jelly was inside.  (I did some with grape jelly, some with strawberry preserves, and the rest blackberry jam. Such a clever idea.  Thanks!

I love this cupcake recipe, it is perfect for any filling to be used. Instead of filling it with jelly or jam, I had some strawberry pastry filler that needed to be used up so I filled the cupcakes before baking. Then I iced them with powdered sugar icing. They are DELICIOUS! Next time I will follow the recipe, which I'm sure they will be gobbled up. Thanks for sharing.

I MADE A DOUBLE BATCH, 1 batch for my husband to take to work and 1 batch for me to take to work. THEY were a hit, My husbands boss took 5 to take home to his family and asked for the recipe. And my co-works kept repeating Lori have I told you how good these cupcakes are?
They are requested often. I have made a chocolate version also.
Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.

I saw this recipe and had to make it.  I thought it would appeal to most people.  I made them and brought them to work the next day.  At first, I didn't get much feedback but the next day people were raving about them.  If you just like a basic cupcake this isn't your choice but if you like a tasty treat this will fill the bill.  I put a little extra milk in the frosting so I could pipe it out of a pastry bag and they looked professional.  I also used Polaner All Fruit Seedless Raspberry for the jelly.
Wonderful flavor...cupcake AND icing.  Maybe my sugar loving children will say otherwise, but I had way too much frosting leftover.  Next time, I'll probably cut that recipe it in half.

This was an easy recipe to put together and it has a delicious blend of flavors! I used regular cheese as that is what I had on hand. I served it with condiments of picante sauce and sour cream.  (I will probably add a bit more tomato suce next time, but that is just a personal preference.)  If my family is any indication I would plan on this serving 4-5 people, not the 6 indicated in the recipe.  I guess that's a statement about the recipe in itself!  Thanks for sharing this recipe!
I wasn't very impressed with this recipe.  It definetly wasn't enough to fill a whole casserole dish.  If you do make it, double everything.

this recipe is pretty amazing. it's become a staple in my household. i use cuban black beans (which have spices added) and that really made this flavorful. it's quite filling and yummy, and probably does serve closer to 4 people. awesome recipe all the way.
YUM!  This is delicious.  Tastes like an enchilada with black beans inside. It served 4 for our family, not 6.  It is too yummy to serve 6, you'll run out!

We really enjoyed this.  My husband was skeptical as I called it a "casserole".  It was really comfort food for me and I loved it.  I added a small red pepper and used flour tortillas instead of corn (as I didn't read the recipe very well).  Also--a question for meow--the directions mention cumin but it is not listed inthe ingredients??  I used 1 tsp cumin.   We topped with sour cream.  This might also be good with corn added.  Loved it and will make again.  Note to above reviewer--did you use the 9x9 pan that the recipe called for or a larger pan--this worked perfectly for me in a 9x9 pan.  Thanks MEOW!
We loved this.  I was going to add corn, but once I got the black bean mixture together, it just tasted too good to mess with.  Very easy, cheap, yummy.
Great Recipe! I used flour tortillas due to personal preference and fresh black beans. I had no problem serving six with this recipe. These will become a regular item at my house. They are Fantastic!

Great recipe!  Very tasty and easy to put together.  My DH thought it could use some meat so next time I will add 1/2 lb. of cubed chicken or ground beef.  I only had flour tortillas...next time I will try corn.  Thanks for a delicious recipe!

Very good. I used flour tortillas -- with 10" tortillas, I found 6 was enough. I mixed monterey jack cheese with the cheddar. Also added some chopped jalapeno to the tomato mixture. Quick and easy. I'm sure to use this again.

Quick, easy & delicious! I used 12 ounces of my home-made tomato sauce which is fairly spicy, whole wheat tortillas & a combo of cheddar & monterey jack cheeses - with salsa & sour cream on the side. Thanx Meow!

Very good.  I followed the recipe exactly, except that I added a little extra garlic and used only ten tortillas, since the package I bought only contained ten.  I would definately suggest using corn tortillas for this recipe instead of substituting flour ones, because the corn tortillas give it an excellent enchilada flavor.  Great recipe!
Yummy. I know I will make these again. I made them according to the recipe. Thank you for sharing.
just made these for my cookie trays yummy!

Another winner!  Very good cookie.  Easy to make and have turned out well each time I have made them.  

Thanks, Kristen

OK, what do you do when you can't sleep and are wide awake at 5:00 in the morning?  Why you make these wonderful cookies....that's what you do, ha, ha ha.  Seriously,  I did, and they are wonderful.  Since I had no idea I was going to do these, I had to make them with semi-sweet chips.  But I can't wait to make them again with the "swirl" chips. These cookies are soft and ooey-gooey.  Thanks for sharing, KC Cooker.

Excellent cookies!!! I made half a batch since I only had one bag of chips. I used 1/2 cup white sugar and 3/4 cup brown as it was easier than measuring 5/8 cup of each. I used real butter and followed the recipe exactly otherwise. Even though placing the chips on top was a little more time consuming than just mixing them all in, it does give the cookies a neat look in the end. Thanks so much, Kristen, for a lovely recipe!!
these are great!! my kids loved them.

You can't beat a cookie that looks great AND tastes better than it looks!  I only bought one bag of swirled morsels, so I used semisweet for the cookie batter.  Everyone loved them at our Trivia Night Party!
These cookies are perfect. A little crunchy on the outside and moist in the middle. Just the way we like it. I only used 2 cups of chips because we don't like a lot a sweet. Thanx

WOW!  These were fabulous.  Let me just say, that I made a mistake and put in 1/2 a stick of butter less than called for and they still turned out great!  Probably not as gooey as they would have been if I'd used all the butter, but the flavor was wonderful.  It was hard to keep my hands off of them.  I used chocolate chunks as that is what I had on hand.  This makes a lot of cookies, so I froze half of the dough and will make them again soon.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe.
Family loved this recipe. Very easy to put together. I used a combination of white chocolate chips and milk chocolate chips. Thanks for the recipe.

Better than our local Mexican restaurant!  That's Dh's verdict and mine as well.  Just terrific made with whole wheat tortillas.  I used Mexican style stewed  tomatoes and it's juice rather than the tomato sauce.  This is too good to serve 6 people.  Four diners will gobble it up in no time.
IT was a great dish. I added a few things to it though. I added some cream cheese and left over roast. It was very good. Thank you.

Very good comfort food.  In order to satisfy my carnivore hubby, I added some of the shredded chicken leftover from Tahiti's Chicken Tacos (recipe #94613).  Because of this addition, I also needed a bit more tomato sauce in order to keep the filling moist (and soften the tortillas as they baked).  The flavor of this dish perfectly fit the comfort level.  It wasn't too spicy, but had a nice subtle heat...it could easily be spiced up (addition of jalapenos or cayenne pepper to the bean mixture), for those times when you just feel like more heat.  :)  Good weeknight  or even casual entertaining fare.

This is ver good!  I used both flour and corn tortillas since I had both on hand to use up. Using the Flour tortillas on the bottom helped hold it together.  I used a whole 15oz. can of tomato sauce, canned stewed tomatoes, chopped, extra green onions and 2 garlic cloves instead of 1.  I also added a few pinches of sugar to help cut the acidity of the tomato products.  Yum!

I don't know if it's cool to post two reviews for the same dish, but I made this and gave it a 4-star review based on my personal taste.

However, it is about a week later and my mother and brother have been raving about it.  My brother is not too fond of spices like cumin, so I was shocked that he liked it SO much.  Therefore, I am adding a 5-star review on their behalf.

This dish tastes fantastic - really flavorful and incredibly healthy because it's high in fiber, vitamin C and low in fat.  I agree with other reviewers in that I would also decrease the number of servings to 4 instead of 6.  My only problem was that it was drier than I expected.  That may have been my fault, as my tortillas were frozen so I put them in the oven to defrost and they may have become too dry.  So to increase the moisture I added about 1/4 cup of V-8 juice I had in the refrigerator, but it was still too dry.  Next time I try this recipe I will add more tomatoes or tomato sauce.  Still deserves 5 stars though because of the intense taste and good nutrition.

Great taste plus it's so quick & easy. I subbed Rotel tomatoes and added more garlic. Next time I may add a jar of Pace Picante sauce to the layers-we Texans like it spicy. Leftovers were wonderful. Thanks Meow!!

Good stuff.  I also added a can of Rotel..I think it would have been too dry without it. Also used a mixture of flour and corn torillas with good results.  In the end it was really good (even using half the cheese). Served it with salsa as a topping. This is definitly going in my recipes. Thank you Meow!
YUMMY!!~~~ I am so happy I tried this! I did add picante sauce and used a mexican cheese blend in place of the low fat cheddar. Thanks for sharing Meow.  I will be making this often.
yummy..yummy... try it you'll like it and if my picky hubby did so will yours
What a great simple meal. I wouldn't change a thing...perfect as is.
We loved this! No such thing as black beans in Australia so I used pinto beans instead - delicious! Thanks for posting!

Fabulous recipe - Being in Australia I found dried 'Black Turkey Beans' in my health food shop. To use these black beans in this recipe I followed ketchupqueen's advice "You can soak beans overnight in cool water, or bring to a boil, boil for 20 minutes, turn off heat but leave the cover on, and soak for at least 2-4 hours. If you have hard water, you should add a tsp. of baking soda". Other than that I followed the recipe exactally except to subsitute the fresh tomatoes and sauce for a tin of tomatoes. Thanks you meow! for introducing us to black beans and for posting a recipe that I will use often.

Delicious!  I didn't have any cilantro but did add some jalepeno pepper and extra garlic.  Also needed about 12 oz. cheddar cheese.  I was worried I wouldn't have enough filling, but it all baked up perfect!  Served with fresh guacamole.  I will definitely use this recipe again!

Very flavorful and healthy at the same time!!  Yeah!!  And very quick & simple to put together.  I used enchilada sauce instead of tomato sauce, and cut way back on the cheese since I didn't have low-fat & we're trying to eat healthier.  Thanks for a great recipe!!
This was great! I followed the recipe for the most part, except I added extra cilantro (personal preference) and I didn't have any LF cheese on hand, so I used regular. I'll be making this again!

Loved this!  I didn't have the cilantro on hand so I left it out and I used flour tortillas that I had.  I also didn't have any green onions.  Still this was wonderful.  I'll make this again for sure.  For the two of us, this amount made 4 servings.

This was really good although a bit dry - will definitely add more tomato sauce the next time I make it. Great recipe for getting lots of fiber!! I wonder if you could eliminate one layer of tortillas or would it all fall apart?

Love this, made it twice.  Like the others I doubled the tomato sauce and bought 2 extra cans of black beans to serve on the side. Surprisingly delicious for how simple it was to make and so cheap to buy (I believe the black beans were the most expensive items I bought, my total was $5.50 at the store). Tastes great re-heated also!
Easy to make, tasted well, but very rough on the stomach. It is good, but just be careful if prone to indigestion.

I liked this, but it wasn't as great as I had expected. Of course, that could be due to my preparation, not the recipe itself. I thought it could have used some olives and corn...the corn to give it some crunch, because it was a bit mushy for my liking.

Excellent and very quick to fix. I made exactly as directed, and DH and I loved it! Precooking the sauce ingredients really helped the flavors come together quickly. Will definitely make again. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Excellent dish! I made it as posted with the exception of adding in an extra can of tomato sauce, I used the hot mexican style by el pato to add some extra spice to the dish. I will be making again. Next time I plan to try using whole wheat tortillas to add even more fiber, maybe some jalapenos... This is a recipe that you can play around and be creative with. Thanks spatchcock for posting.

Perfect for a quick weeknight meal. DH loves meat, but I have been making meatless meals at least once a week - and we both really liked this one. I didn't have any cilantro and I used full-fat cheese; I think this recipe is easily adaptable to what you have on hand. We topped it with a little sour cream and served with baked chips & your Recipe #36401.

This was a big hit when I made it!  I did add chicken since I was going to be serving this to some individuals who don't care much for onions, peppers, etc.  Overall, this was very good and I will definitely be making it again!
What a yummy meatless dish!!  Lots of ways to change it up according to tastes!

Delicious! So simple and quick and so tasty. Some of my family/friends still can't wrap their head around the idea of using tortillas in a dish like this but they're always pleasantly surprised when they try it! Thank you!
We enjoyed this very much.  I doubled the tomato sauce per other reviewers and also threw in a can of chopped green chilies.  Very healthy and inexpensive to make.  Thanks for posting.!
I found this excellent, but it could use a little more kick.  Next time I think I might add some diced jalapeÃ±os or maybe some more chili powder.

Simple and delicious! My DH was hesitant to try this once he found out there was no meat - but he decided he couldn't even tell the difference. He doesn't like tomatoes so I substituted 1 cup salsa and it turned out perfect.

Very tasty.  I added an additional 1/2 cup of salsa to the mix and it gave it just enough kick.  Even the meat eaters in the house gave it five stars.  Thanks for the recipe that we now make once a week.

Just wanted to say thank you for this idea - although I didn't follow the recipe, I used the concept to make an alternative lasagne (my other half doesn't eat it usually) and it was a great success and a nice change from the pasta stuff!

A fast, easy pantry dish for us as we often have the ingredients on hand and it's easy to make substitutions.  We double the recipe for our family of 5 (plus leftovers for the next day's lunch).  For a doubled batch, I used a large yellow onion (no green on hand), three 8oz cans of tomato sauce, added a small can of green chilis, and omitted the 
tomatoes.  Thanks for sharing the great recipe!

This is very good... it's one of the best mexican-style casserole that we have had.  I used a 13 by 9 inch pan and did two layers.  It helped keep the tortillas from getting too soggy and was much easier to serve this way.  I enjoyed the strong cumin and chili powder flavors.
This was a hit with my kids.  I think next time I'll add some green peppers and use only three tortillas per layer.

This was very good.  I doubled everything except the tortillas (I used handmade tortillas) and then baked it in a 9x12 glass dish.  The bottom tortillas were very chewy.  I think that next time I will put sauce on the bottom first and then the tortillas.  I served plain yogurt and chunky salsa with it, which were great additions.  Excellent recipe.  We will be enjoying this again and I'm very glad there are leftovers to enjoy tomorrow.

Good... had to make some changes because of what I had on hand and personal peference... used 4 large flour tortillas, more garlic and tomato sauce, also added corn and black olives... served with salsa and refried beans and it made a satisfying meal. I love that it's so light too, thank for sharing!

We really enjoyed this.  I used 1 can rotel tomatoes with green chilies instead of chopped tomatoes and it worked very well.  Gave it a little kick!  The leftovers reheated nicely for lunch the next day.  Thanks for sharing!

Wow!  Had my vegetarian bro over and family, and EVERYONE loved it!  Which is amazing, specially for him.  I am making this again tonite using the rotel as suggested in the previous post.  I think it will turn out great!  The only think I changed was substituting a red pepper for the tomato, just b/cause I had it on hand...YUMMM!!
This was OK.  My family seemed to dislike the corn tortillas, and I thought it was a bit dry.

This is a great toss together recipe.  It's very easy and tasty.  The first time I made it, I only had flour tortillas and I used canned tomatoes.  It turned out far too soggy. It was much better and firmer with corn and I didn't notice a whole lot of difference in the taste. (I normally don't like corn tortillas)  This is a good vegetarian dish which tastes great served with rice.  I also like to up the bean content just because I really like black beans.

This recipe was Excellent!!  My husband and my very picky son ate the whole thing.  My husband loves meat so I added a lb. of ground beef and some corn for extra veggies.  I was a little afraid that the recipe would be a little dry because I didn't add any additional tomato sauce but it was perfect.  I did, however, topped it with a little salsa before serving.  This will definitely be a regular meal in our family from now on.

We enjoyed this recipe. I added Chicken as one of the other reviewers  suggested and it was a little dry (I needed to add more sauce). I served it with salsa and avocado and it was great. I might try more sauce and maybe corn next time.
Found this recipe to use as a meatless meal. It was great. A make more than once meal, for sure!

I loved this recipe. I recomend using the corn tortillas (my flour ones got a little soggy). I didn't have any fresh cilantro so I used about 1 tsp dried. I was didn't have enough tomatoes so I probably only used 1/2 c. chopped and about 14 oz. tomato sauce. I had some corn so I added a 14 oz. can of that too for a little more bulk. Great dinner! Thanks spatchcock!

This was very nice.  We like spicy foods so I increased chili powder to 1 tsp., cumin to 3 tsp., cilantro to 2 Tbsp. and I will add more next time because it was still a little mild for us.  Maybe a chili pepper would be a good addition.  We topped this with sour cream and served it with our favorite mexican cauliflower salad. Very nice.      Bobbi

Very good and easy to make. I used flour tortillas- I picked up the wrong ones at the supermarket. I think this recipe would also be good with the addition of chicken or ground beef. I will make this again.
edited to add:  I have now used the corn tortillas- picked up the correct ones this time.  The dish is so much better with these.  Great meatless meal.

Delicious and filling. If you like your Mexican spicy, then definitely do not be afraid to up the amounts on the spices and add in some of your favorite chilis. I highly recommend this nutritious dish.

We made this recipe the other day and it was pretty good. I read the recipe wrong and used lowfat cottage cheese (which I think is lower calorie than cheddar) and it was wonderful. If I would add anything to it I would put some cayenne pepper in it.

My husband and I made this today. It was good. Definitely could tell it was healthy. I'm lactose intolerant and hate cheese so I made my half without it. Thus, my serving was 0 fat =) My husband had it per recipe and thought it was good. We just wish it had some more flavoring or spicyness.

Great recipe - we loved it!! After reading other reviews, I added a small can of corn, a can of sliced black olives, and a small can of green chiles. I keep fresh roasted poblanos in the freezer for dishes that are "worthy" of them, and this one definitely is, so I'll use them next time. I also used a whole onion (no green onions), and instead of the fresh tomato and tomato sauce, I added a can of Rotel and a 10 oz. can of tomato puree. I used maybe half again as much cheese as called for, combining sharp cheddar and jack. It was a perfect consistency. This will definitely go in my favorites file!
We totally loved this.  Made a perfect side dish with my slow cooked mexican baked chicken.  This is definately a KEEPER!!

I think it would have been better to use salsa rather than just a cup of diced tomatoes.  Maybe you could use chili sauce rather than tomato sauce.  Also, maybe some Mexican style cheese rather than just cheddar cheese.  It would have been nice to have some sour cream for serving.  The dish is a good idea.  I think it can be very flexible (e.g. you can add meat).  In my opinion, the base recipe just needs more flavors.

This was fantastic! The only thing I did differently was to use regular cheddar. Since this recipe uses very similar ingredients to many things we make I thought it would taste like the same old thing but it didn't! Maybe the cumin or cilantro? Anyway, what a great way to use ingredients we already have on hand.  Thanks for the new addition to our standard fare.
I am not a big black bean fan so I made it with pinto beans and it was wonderful!  We added this recipe to our menu rotation~we really liked it!

I love this recipe!  Made it two nights in a row, the second night I added a finely chopped chicken breast to the pan with the onions/garlic.  I also substituted one can of Rotel with chiles (drained) for the chopped tomato, and stirred in  a couple of tablespoons of sour cream.  My husband even ate it and he is not a big bean eater.  Yumm!

I took this to a dinner party and a few weeks later one of the guests hunted down my husband at church to ask for the recipe - he said he could not stop thinking about it!  Made it as directed however, added 1 pound lean ground beef.  Next time I will try chicken as others have done!  Thanks for a fantastic recipe - this one is in our rotation regularly now!

I made in a smaller casserole dish and used a combo of wheat, corn, and flour tortillas (they all tasted the same when baked). I added some chopped broccoli into the simmering tomato juice (used 2 small cans V-8). I didn't bake for very long, since I wanted it more "saucy." This was nice and hearty tasting. Thanks Spatchcock, for posting.
Roxygirl

This was good!  Easy too I preped ahead of time and then just threw it in the oven.  If I make this again though I would only put in two layers instead of three because I like stuff that's really saucy and the extra third layer of tortillas kind of absorbed more than I would have liked.  Great flavor though!

This is a fabulous idea. I used two cans of diced tomatoes (one with chiles) and one 8-oz can of tomato sauce. I added corn and ground beef to the mix and put sour cream on top before adding the last layer of cheese. This made enough for a 9X13 pan. I even made one end low fat - with lower fat cheese, nonfat sour cream and no meat.  Like another reviewer, I put flour tortillas on the bottom. My DS loved the layers and thought there should be even more. Thanks for a great dinner.

This went over SO well in my house! My husband took the leftovers to work the next day and his co-workers were asking for the recipe! The only thing I changed is the cheese (use full-fat) and I didn't use cilantro.
What a great summertime recipe!  Everyone loved the flavors.  We served this over rice and had a fruit salad as a side.  It was perfect!  Thanks for posting!

Great recipe as a jumping off point! I used everything the recipe called for, but added some shredded chicken and a can of Rotel tomatoes with green chiles.  I also had half a leftover green bell pepper I tossed in, and half a can of leftover refried beans.  Results were awesome!  Thanks for this Mexican Lasagna idea I will play with over and over again.  ETA: second time i made it i added corn!  highly reccomended...

I've been holding off making this recipe for a while. I honestly thought it wouldn't be that good. I was WRONG. It was very tasty. Since I'm watching calories/points I used the low-carb tortillas (1 point each). It helped to lower the caloric/fat content. Super great recipe worth keeping.

This is a great recipe. I used spaghetti sauce instead of tomato sauce, parsley instead of cilantro and flour tortillas instead of corn. That's what I had at hand and it still turned out great! I served it with sour cream and salsa. Thanks for the recipe!
this was really good...and easy.  I might throw in some corn/chicken strips next time - just to add more for the meat eating boyfriend, but i'll definitely be making this again
Yum! I will double the sauce next time and reduce the cilantro- way too strong for us! A little corn would be nice in it also! We really enjoyed it and will make it again! Thanks!

I didn't make the recipe exactly as described; I used more garlic ('coz we love it!!), no green onion (just increased the other onion), tinned tomatoes instead of the tomatoes & tomato sauce, my own spice & herb blend (similar to chili powder, although I used some chipotle paste rather than cayenne pepper or whatever) instead of the chili & cumin, borlotti instead of black beans (as that was the closest I had), no coriander leaves as I'd run out, and full fat cheddar. Oh yes, and a little bit of cocoa powder as I always add it to anything chili-ish! I fried the onions for a few minutes with some cumin seeds before adding anything else, but otherwise followed most of the recipe approximately as written.

I also layered it differently to the instructions as I had a round container which was a fraction smaller than the tortillas so I just pressed a tortilla into the bottom, spread a layer of the mixture on & sprinkled with cheese, repeating until it was all used up. Consequently it ended up being a bit more like a pie, as the edges of the tortillas formed a sort of crust!

I served it with creme fraiche & a guacamole-inspired avocado & cherry tomato salad.
