I didn't have honey and instead used maple syrup. It was delicious!
Great recipe with good flavor! Sometimes my husband and I get tired of chicken but this was very good! Made rice pilaf for the side, went perfect together! Will definitely make this again!

Both of us enjoyed this recipe, even though the better half usually doesn't care for honey. I scaled back to 2 breasts, since it was the first time trying it. I did leave it marinate in a zipper bag for an hour, flipping it over after 1/2 hr. I think you could marinate a little longer but I understand that the lime juice will "cook" the chicken and change the consistency if left to long. I also zested the lime before I squeezed it for additional flavor since I often use lime in marinades.

Added extra garlic, of course, and used some parsley instead of cilantro. Pounded the chicken a bit and they marinated for about an hour. Turned out really delicious from the grill. I think the leftovers will be versatile for salads or orange chicken.
We absolutely loved it!  I made a mistake and ended up with one more cup of broth as I misread instruction #4.

Thanks, Annacia, for a really yummy recipe!  This combination of ingredients hits the nail right on the head for perfect "chicken gumbo" flavor!  Since I'm trying to drop some pounds, I left out the canaola oil and flour, and omitted steps 4 and 5.  There was no compromise, just fewer calories. Very delicious!
Fantastic! This is a keeper. Very flavorful and filling. Next time I think I might omit the red pepper flakes, as it seemed to have a little too much heat for my taste.

Right nice gumbo, keeper!  Seasoning was right on for our taste.  I recommend making the brown rice earlier.  This is like a fancy Chicken and Rice Soup.   Not too spicy for aged MIL, that's a coup!  Thank you for sharing this recipe, Annacia!  Made for Photo Tag.

Delicious!  I added more okra than called for (just seems to go with gumbo!), and added some tabasco to add some heat.  I guess I like a spicier gumbo.  I took the flour off the heat when it was golden brown, and my "gravy" wasn't as dark as most gumbos, but the flavor was delicious.  Perfect dinner tonight.  I'll save this recipe to make again!  Thanks for sharing.  Made for Rookie tag.
Very good! Thanks for sharing this, A! I am not diabetic, but it looked just right and it was, LOL! Made for ZWT9
absolutely amazing.

Oh my, my, my!!!  This soup is delicious!!!  I had to make a few adjustments since I had the long-cooking Uncle Ben's Rice.  I'm assuming this recipe is for the quick-cooking version since it said to pour in the rice and remove from heat.  My adjustments were to use 7 cups of broth (to make up for the long-cooking rice soaking up more liquid), 1/2 cup of butter, scant 1/2 cup of flour and 2 cups of heavy cream.  I changed the amount of flour because I was afraid of it turning too thick.  I knew I could add more later if I needed to.  I'm very happy with the way it turned out.  I have never had Panera's version of this soup......but I can't imagine it tasting any better!!!  This was sooooooo yummy!!  Thanks so much for posting!!
This soup turned out yummy just as you submitted recipe! Thank you! Not sure why people needed to feel like they had to tweek... but perfect as submitted

This soup ROCKS!!! I am a mother of 4 boys so, of course, I doubled this recipe .I served it with French Baquettes, also.  I got great reviews from my family!  This is a go to recipe now!  I am making it again tomorrow for a friend who is dealing with a family illness. Thank you, thank you, thank you!!!

Yum! This is the soup I love at Panera, so I was glad to find a recipe at all. And this one was excellent. I was glad I read the reviews, though, and used half the flour; it would have been like cement if I had any more! I also used a wild rice instead of the Uncle Ben's because I had it and we're trying to avoid the high-sodium mixes (and I had about 1 1/2 cups already cooked). I used an additional 1/3 cup uncooked rice boiled in 4 cups of broth with finely chopped carrots, celery, onion, and garlic. I also used half & half because that's what I had.

Thanks for posting this recipe, Raquel! I can't wait for something like having the girls over for lunch to make it again!
Fantastic!

Panera's rice soup is my absolute favorite! I've been looking for this recipe for about 3 years! I used all ingredients as called for. Soup was just the right texture and thickness. The only thing I will change for next time is the seasoning mix in the rice. I will cut that by at least 1/2. The flavors of the spices were way too intense! Panera's has a subtle flavor and I didn't feel like there was anything subtle about this. Had company for dinner & they all enjoyed it, just too intense for me. Can't wait to try it again, as I can certainly see the potential for this to become my favorite soup at home!  I live a long way from Panera's and I crave this soup all winter long! Yum! Yum! It's October so I'm ready to master this! Thanks SOOOOOOO MUCH for the recipe!

I've been on the search for Panera's secret soup recipe for some time, and while I can't say this is really it, it is darned good.

Made it pretty much according to the directions, with the exception of a little more chicken and veggies. Next time I will be cutting the flour and cream by a third to a half. That way it shouldn't be quite as thick, and won't hurt the scary nutritional content percentages either! Thanks for posting. This will be a go-to meal this winter.

Just made this tonight. Followed the directions, but did use the 3/4 cup flour and the evaporated milk (what I had). I like the thickness of Panera's soup. I'm thinking I'll use half the seasoning package the next time, and add some tarragon, maybe some white wine.
Otherwise, excellent. (the entire pot is gone btw, kids ate the whole thing).
Very hearty and yummy soup.  I used half and half and it came out great.

Love it! I tweaked it a little- added a little more flavor with chicken boullion and a little white wine and some salt. I used Uncle Ben's rice and the flavor didn't overpower the soup. Served it in a breadbowl. I added a little bit of water too- 3/4c wine and 1 cup water too (4cups of cream) Deelish!

Very good soup.  I only used 1/2 cup butter and I used Uncle Ben's Chicken and Wild Rice (not the quick cooking kind) and it turned out very well.  The soup was not as thick as Panera's, but that is easily changed with more flour.  I will definitely make again.

I served this in bread bowls and was really impressed.  The only thing I would change is to substitute some of the cream with nonfat milk.  It was a little heavy.  Still, very good soup that I will make again.  Fantastic in a bread bowl.

I made this for company tonight, and it was loved by all!  We served it with garlic toast and salad.  I doubled the recipe and decided to adjust a couple of things based in part on other reviews and in part on trying to lower the calorie count.  So for a DOUBLE batch, I used 1 cup butter total.  And I also therefore cut the flour for the roux to 2/3 cup.  I used 3 of the rice-a-roni long grain & wild rice mix (the 4oz. box size), but only 2 of the seasoning packets, and it was perfect.  And then I used part evaporated milk and part half n' half for the cream.  It really turned out wonderful & we will definitely be making again!  Thanks for sharing a great recipe!
Definatly a keeper! Made exactly as stated except used fat free half and half and it turned out rich and creamy and my kids gobbled it up. Great recipe:)

This is my first time using this recipe site -- glad I did. Feeling a little under the weather so decided I had to have some panera wild rice/cream of chicken soup. They didn't have it today! So, I hopped online and found this; happened to have the ingredients and it was great. I followed exactly with just a few small additions -- added 4 garlic gloves, finely minced, sauteed with veggies. Used half a seasoning packet but added about a 1/2 tsp of dried tarragon, I would probably add at least 1 tsp next time or maybe use the whole seasoning packet - I was being conservative based on what I read in the reviews. I simmered the soup for a good extra 20 minutes past the recommended time, also added some more salt, fresh ground black pepper AND some red pepper flakes (again about 1/2 tsp) for a little zip as it simmered. I happened to have the Uncle Ben's wild rice quick cook rice, which worked out great. This soup recipe is excellent and hit the spot.
Great recipe other than we cut down on the flour as 1/2 cup makes it to thick for us, other than that my wife the judge of all says it is spot on to Panera.
Thank you for sharing this amazing recipe! I used less flour per other reviews and it was perfect with just 1/4 cup. I used half and half and it was delicious!

This was perfect as posted. It tastes exactly like Panera's Cream of Chicken with Wild Rice which is my FAVORITE. I used half/half but that was the only change I made. Next time I will serve it in a round bread bowl and play classical music and I will pretend I am at Panera's(which is only about 5 blocks from my house).

I used all the ingredients as specified. Although, I cooked the two breasts as a whole and chopped them after cooking. I also added all the flour, but added a small portion of it right at the end because it does get a little like cement while cooking. I also didn't use all the chicken in the soup and saved some for chicken salad tomorrow. I did add all of the rice spice and also some extra S&P. This tasted almost exactly like Panera's!

Everyone loves this and I will most def make it again!
PERFECT! I added a handful of wild rice to this also but that was the only thing that I changed. This was wonderful! Thanks!

This recipe is awesome!!! Our Panera Bread tends to run out of things when the weather gets chilly and rainy :(. I used regular half & half and it worked out just fine and a little more flour (1/8 cup), we like our soups a little thicker. Kudos to the genius who deciphered this recipe!!!

This is a wonderful recipe and I've made it twice in a month already! I did change the flour amount. But on my second time around I made the mistake of using "chix and Broccoli" rice from uncle bens, I added some mushrooms and an extra 1/4 cup of the three other veggies. It's turned out really fantastic so I just wanted to promote experimented for those that are brave enough with different soup mixes added. I loved your soup, thanks for the help, I craved Panera so much it was breaking the bank!

Also, use a really good quality chicken broth, it definitely matters in the final flavor, I felt.

Courtney

Amazing soup. Replica of panera bread. I brought all the ingredients (the ones which i already didnt have at home) and decided to give it a try. I think I added a little too much of chicken broth which resulted the soup having a very thin consistency. So I added corn starch to make it thicker. That was my own fault.  Otherwise very good soup. Highly recommend it. Right now I'm enjoying it with french bread. Thanks !!!

This tastes exactly like Panera's (only this one actually has some chicken in it!) I didn't use a seasoning packet but instead made a mix of dried parsley, cumin, turmeric and a dollop of ginger paste, and I only used the half cup of flour recipe.

Wow...I have to add my words of praise to this great soup !  Although I have never tried Panera cream of chicken I am now a new fan......this soup is the bomb!  Had 2 bowls tonight and looking forward to another one tomorrow......I made a few goofs with the recipe but it was very forgiving.  I bought the express Uncle Ben's rice which has the seasoning mixed in with the rice.....also got ahead of myself and added the veggies to the broth mixture......but no harm done as the end result was heavenly !  Thanks so much for sharing my new favourite chicken and rice soup!!!!
Fantastic!! I added chopped frozen kale and I love it.  thanks

Excellent recipe! Though I added some sliced shiitake mushrooms to the vegetables as they were sautéing and instead of the Uncle Ben's roasted chicken wild rice mix, I used a wild rice mix with a herb seasoning packet. The herbs gave it a milder taste, but it was delicious!
This was delish! I followed the recipe with the exception of the rice. I used zatarans wild rice mix. It's right on with panera bread! Thanks for sharing
So good!  Loved this and will make all the time.  Only used 1 1/2 c. ff half and half and 1 stick butter.
Wonderful soup! I made it again today. This time I made a slight adjustment by adding 6 ounces of sliced pickled jalapenos with juice and some corn. Gave it a little southwestern kick.
I like the soup but it doesn't taste like Panera's. I am a little dissapointed :-(
excellent, use half of the flour and add extra as needed
Delicious perfection! I used half 'n half and added crimini mushrooms and it was as good, if not better, than what I had at Panera. This is a keeper!

OMG!!!! This soup is soooooooooooo delicious! I can't get enough of it! I've made it 4x since I saw this recipe online and have gotten excellent reviews from friends who've tried it. I did tweak it slightly and only used 1/3 cup of flour instead of 1/2 to tone down the thickness. I also only used 2 cups total of dairy products (1 cup of light cream and 1 cup of evaporated milk). And lastly, I used low sodium chicken broth. To prepare my chicken breast, I boil them in low sodium chicken broth and add fresh garlic, pepper, and onion powder.  It's so amazingly delicious! Thanks for sharing! :)

I found this recipe winter of 2012, after visiting Panera several times with my boyfriend and watching him order their Chicken & Wild Rice Soup.  I made this for him with a few modifications (1/2 & 1/2 combined with milk, sometimes a little heavy whipping cream, as well as extra veggies, some garlic & I always add mushrooms- yum!)- he thought this was better than Panera's.  Even after visiting Panera again- he still thinks my version of this recipe is better!  This recipe is definitely a keeper for anyone who loves a creamy soup on a cold day- I've made it so many times since the day I first tried it- swapping in & out different ingredients, and it never disappoints.  So flavorful & delicious!  Thanks for sharing!

I made this soup with the Rice a Roni Wild Rice blend.  It was very sweet.  I did not like it at all.  I did like the other recipes and used 1/2 c flour.  I still think would be too much, but I lessened the chicken broth since my chicken was already cooked....so that could have contributed to the thickness too.  I probably won't make this again, but if I do, I will definitely try the chicken flavored rice or may just use plain rice.

I made this last week and it was delicious! Thank you so much, I will definitely make it over and over!  I always get this while eating at Panera but they often times are offering it while I'm there so I'm happy to be able to make my own!

This was delicious! Way better than Panera! I followed the recipe as written and it was perfect.  I saw other reviewers had changed it somehow but it didn't turn out like cement as others had written. So yummy I'm definitely making this again! Thanks for sharing!
This was amazing!  This soup is creamy and rich-a great comfort food.  Made this for my mom after having some medical tests and was just the comfort she needed.  It was gone very fast!

I just followed this recipe to a tee because I wanted to really copy the Panera soup. This is so delicious I think it taste even better than the Panera however the soup is so thick that the left over kind of solidified the next day. I need to do minor adjustments like lessening the flour and the cream to thin out the soup a notch. Also keep in mind the calories, with the butter, flour, cream and the rice this is really in the 400-500 per cup.

I liked the soup a lot.  I used a little more chicken stock to finish up the box.  I used more rice.  It was way too much butter.  I would use a lot less or even none at all.  I also used half and half.  It was very good.
Delicious! Delicious! Delicious! I was seeking a recipe like that of Panera's for this very soup, and this recipe gets it right!  It's as close as it gets! Yummy good!  Highly recommend!

First of all let me say that the flavor of this soup is mind blowing! I used 2 boxes of rice and a few extra carrots and celery- mine thickened up too much so next time I will either increase the broth or omit the flour. 
But even thicker it was ridiculously good :) 
Will make it again and again
I have made this twice before it's wonderful. I cut the flour and butter in half as other reviews have suggested and use fat free half and half. Tastes wonderful. Very filling. Eats like a meal.
Sounds great can't wait to try.  Has anyone tried to freeze it?

Better than the panera version. My fiance loves it and he doesn't like soup! I didn't change anything aside from adding my usual house seasoning salt, pepper, garlic and onion powder on the veggies while cooking and a little into the soup once done. Delicious!

Wow!  This was delicious!  I made this using low sodium chicken broth, tripled all ingredients except I only used 3 1/2 sticks of butter, and  1 32 ounce container of 1/2 and 1/2. (it's all I had)  and I used brown rice (I had in the cabinet, and cooked it as directed in the broth, and added some  of the spices listed on line for Uncle Bens wild rice box, turmeric, paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper)  It turned out delicious.  Everyone can add there own salt and pepper to taste, and it freezes in individual containers beautifully.   I will be making this for many years to come.  Thanks for the recipe and adding the substitution.  It made it less intimidating to substitute.

DELICIOUS!!!! I've made this a few times and followed the recipe exactly! I did notice that with leftovers it can be a little to thick, so I usually add a little me chicken broth to it. This is definitely a keeper. BTW, I noticed one reviewer only gave this recipe two stars and stated it tasted too sweet. That person used RICE-A-RONIE! I think you really need to use the uncle ben brand. Just my opinion.
I made this tonight, and wow! Delicious! Very easy to follow recipe and excellent results!
I made this the other day and it is amazing and very easy to make!! I followed the recipe as written and wouldn't change a thing!!

This was awesome!  I could eat this daily!  I used Half/Half and Almond Milk, only because it is what I had.  I also used Rotis. Chicken that was cooked (huge time saver) and Added mushrooms.  I would recommend this recipe to anyone!


I would like to get away from the Prepackaged Rice seasoning...any suggestions on the spices/herbs that I could use to replace?

Thanks for the awesome recipe!

I never comment on a recipe but I have to comment on this one.  It is soooooo good.  Small adjustments I made after reading some of the comments: 1 stick butter,  2 1/4 cups of half & half and only half of the rice seasoning packet. I also used chicken stock instead of broth.  This added just a little more flavor.  Other than that,  this recipe is a keeper.  I have 1 picky eater and she ate THREE bowls (which she probably shouldn't have :) but I was just so thrilled that I couldn't say NO.
Not really like Panera's, but still delicious! I added extra black pepper and next time will add some Paprika to give it a little more depth.

This soup was amazing and fairly easy. Made it on Sunday evening and my in laws came over. Everyone loved it including my 4 boys ages 9,6, and 2 year old twins. One of the twins is very picky. I used evaporated milk because I was low on half/half and was saving it for my coffee!!

I've made this soup twice now...first time was with a different recipe and it was similar but not nearly as delicious as this one! I wish it didn't take so much time to prepare (chopping, measuring, etc.) but honestly, it's worth it. I used half and half for my cream and Uncle Ben's original recipe rice. Next time I will try the roasted chicken flavored rice but I already had the original at home so decided to use it. So glad I googled other recipes because I will be using this one from now on!
not a review--just a note

This was absolutely DELICIOUS!!!! I used 1 stick of butter and fat free hand and half so that cut down quite a bit on calories. I also added about a half of a cup of diced shiitake mushrooms.. OMG, talk about heaven!!! It was amazing! Thank you for the recipe!!!!!!!!
Turned out awesome!!!!
My family likes it even better than it's namesake!! Thank You!!

People who like Panera's soup love this recipe.....When it comes to quantity of flour, I use the same amount as oil (or butter in this case) for any roux. In this recipe 3/4 c. butter = 3/4 c. of flour. Came out perfect

Turned out Great! 1/2 cup of flour is plenty unless you want to eat it with a fork I think. I used canned chicken breast (apologies to all you real cooks out there). I also wanted mushrooms and canned corn so in they went. Maybe add more wild rice to it next time. Half & Half worked great. Real easy even for a guy to make.

Ok this is some SERIOUSLY good soup. I followed the directions exactly and used 2 cups half and half and 1 cup whole milk. It was simply divine. My picky 7 year old loved it and my husband and I rated it a 10 out of 10. The amount of flour is perfect. I'm not a fan of super thick soup and this was the perfect consistency. I served it with some super fresh Publix sourdough bread. Absolutely divine. It will become a permanent addition to my recipe book!
This is delicious! Definitely a "keep" recipe. I used half and half, smooth and creamy.
This turned out great! I made it for a play date, and everyone gobbled it up and asked for the recipe. Served this with crunchy sourdough bread. It was amazing!
This soup is now a perenial favorite in my house! I use canned chicken to cut the time down and it works out perfect! It’s the absolute besy soup I’ve ever made!!!

This was absolutely delicious! I used Rice A Roni chicken & garlic that has both rice and vermicelli and it was perfect. This is incredibly high in calories so it isn’t something I’ll make all the time but it fit the bill perfectly for a filling and hearty meal on a cold night!
Just made this and it came out great! I ended up adding a little more broth toward the end because he rice absorbed a bit and more chicken.

Thrilled to find this recipe!!! That’s my favorite soup at Panera and they don’t always have it. Just made a pot and I think it’s better than Panera!! I followed instructions but did want to lighten a bit. Used 1 stick butter, 1/4 cup flour and 2 cans evaporated skim milk. Perfect and so delicious!! Thanks so much for posting!!

Great flavored soup - but very RICH! I even tried to save a few calories by using part half & half and part evaporated milk but it still ended up so rich we could hardly finish our bowls. I used a small rotisserie chicken to make things easy. The only other change was that because my packet of Long Grain & Wild Rice didn't come with a flavor packet, I threw in a little powdered chicken base & salt. And I think it could use more rice. I'll probably use 2 packages next time. But for flavor, you can't beat this recipe.

After finding this recipe, I finally decided to make it today. Made a few modifications. Instead, I used 5 cups of chicken broth and 1 cup of water; 2 rotisserie chicken breasts including the bone; and instead of cream, used 3 cups of low-fat milk, and some salt. Came out delicious! So hearty! Had 2 bowls for lunch! Next time, I will use 2 boxes of the Uncle Ben's rice and add potatoes.

I used fresh chicken breast s and white and Minnesota wild rice I had on hand. I seasoned with poultry seasoning and squeeze tube garlic and some thyme. Thickened it a bit more. It was fantastic! Keeper recipe
LOVE this soup!

Tried at least 10 times to get a recipe that works and finally found it! Perfect. I get this soup every time I go to Panera and it is so expensive. I made this whole pot for the cost of a big bowl. Delicious

Thank goodness for this recipe with a little tweak. I had tried this recipe before and it wasn't quite the same, but my MIL suggested using the Progresso Tuscany chicken broth and it tastes just like Panera. This is now my go to instead of buying it on the few days they have it available.
BEST Soup Recipe EVER!!! I've always loved Panera's version, but I do believe this is even better! Everyone in the family loved it & is already requesting it again.

I've made this soup several times and it is always a hit with my family. Today I had to make a couple of substitutions...dried chopped onion and I also used boulion cube with water in place of the chicken broth. It stilled turned out perfect. Thanks for recipe! :)
It came out great, but can you freeze the leftovers.

Absolutely love this soup! I’ve been making this recipe for a few years now. I use Rice A Roni Long Grain and Wild Rice. I cut down on the fat by reducing butter to 1 stick and I don’t use the cream. I’ve used 1% milk and also milk and evaporated milk. It’s plenty creamy for me! Oh and I also add more rice. I use regular rice and it cooks up fine. You could use Minute Rice if you want. I use thighs usual instead of breasts. . Love ?? it when it starts to cool down so I can make this. Today was finally the day!
Best soup ever! My company loved it and I have eaten it as leftovers for 3 days!!! Love it with cornbread! Follow the recipe exactly.
This soup is amazing. Added a couple squeezes of lemon like Panera does. It's amazing!!!! And now all gone

This soup is fantastic! I was feeling a little disappointed that it didn’t taste “exactly” like Panera’s, but then I read a previous review to add some lemon juice, which made it perfect!! Exactly like Panera.

It tasted very close to the real thing. My kids always pick out the celery and onion in Panera's so I omitted those and added corn instead. They loved it! If I were to make it again, I would only use 1 stick of butter. It was a bit too buttery for me.
Yummy!!  This was so easy to put together the night before and stick in the oven while the kids were picking up.  By the time they were done it was ready and they loved it.

Great taste if you like Auntie Anne's pretzels.  Big hit with my family.  Very easy to make.  I put all the ingredients in my Kitchen Aide with a dough hook and it works perfect.  Makes them even easier to make.  We make them almost every Sunday night now.  The kids love to shape them.

I made these with my pre-k class and baked them in a toaster oven!  They were so easy to make and tasted fabulous!  They really do taste like the ones from the mall, too.  Because the students are so young, we made big,fat, chewy pretzels, rather than lots of thinner ones. Now I'll be making these at home.  Thanks for the great recipe.

My family loved these.  So easy and very good!  I dipped them in a butter/garlic powder mixture.  I did not get 24- I guess I made mine really big.  I also learned that we liked rolling them thin because they do puff up quite a bit in the oven.

These were absolutely delicious. We don't get Auntie Annies in Oz but it is one of the first things my kids get when in Asia. They loved these!!!! So thank you so much for the recipe. I made them in cinnamon sugar. I wonder if these can be frozen succesfully?

These are the best homemade pretzels I've ever tasted! I have 5 kids who come home "starving" everyday from school and these fill their cavernous bellies right up! Super recipe. I've tried a lot of soft pretzel recipes and this is the one I'm sticking with for good! Thanks for sharing. btw... This recipe only made 7 pretzels so I guess I need to roll them smaller next time; but they were so yummy!

These were great, and really did taste like mall pretzels - it must be the brown sugar.  I looked up "occidental" flour, and it seemed like regular all purpose, so I used 4 cups of all purpose, and my dough was a bit on the dry side - maybe I'll use a bit less next time. Overall though, they were great!

I have never made pretzels before, and these turned out great!  I halfed the recipe and ended up having to add some additional water to get the flour to incorporate, but the taste was fantastic.  I baked them on my pizza stone and the bottoms came out brown and toasty in just four minutes, while the inside was still moist and chewy.  I got four big, fat soft pretzels out of the half recipe.

These were fantastic!!  So quick to mix up, let sit for a few minutes & then bake up quickly!  My whole family was delighted and kept coming back for more!!  I used cinnamon sugar on some and salt on others, and both were great!  I didn't get quite 24 out of the dough, but maybe 18-20.  Also used 4 cups of all-purpose flour.  I look forward to making these again and letting the kids make their own shapes.  Thanks!!

These come out great but I think some of the numbers are off.  The water/baking soda dip seemed like way too much, so I cut it in half.  I still had over 3/4 of it left when I was done dipping my pretzels.  I also made very thin ropes about 18 inches long and only got 12 small (about 4 inch) pretzels out of the batch.  My first two pretzels were quite ugly, but after that I got the hang of it.  I had to roll and stretch my ropes on a lightly floured counter and also found that they came out nicer if I twisted all the pretzels first and then dipped them (instead of twisting and dipping, twisting and dipping, etc.)  My pretzels baked at 500 degrees on the top rack for 4-5 minutes and came out perfect.  My family thought they tasted like the mall pretzels, except they were much smaller.  Thanks for sharing...next time I'm going to try 6 big pretzels.

This pretzel recipe is awesome.  I couldn't figure out what "occident" flour was, so I just used around 4 cups of normal flour; also, I only used 1 pkg of yeast (not 1TBS)... and it still turned out great!  Usually I am a complete klutz in the kitchen, so the fact that this recipe worked simply rocked my world.  Thank you so much.
These were so yummy, I made some with  cinnamon and sugar but the plain butter ones were the best. My husband and I had fun making these, thanks for posting.

Leta, this is a FABULOUS make-ahead breakfast dish!  So easy and so tasty.  I had guests over for breakfast and I served this dish along with my breakfast casserole and fresh fruit.  What an easy way to serve a group of people.  I had to make copies of your French Toast Casserole for everyone!!!  This is surely a dish I will make over and over again.  I also made a hard copy of it and it is now in my "keeper" notebook.  I'm so glad I found this.  Thanks for sharing.  :-)rn

When I came across your recipe, I couldn't wait until we had a "family breakfast," so I made it in the morning for supper that night!!  DELICIOUS!!!  I set syrup out but nobody even used it.  This dish stands well enough on it's own!!  Thanks for the great recipe  :)
My family ate the whole dish!  This was a huge success.  The only thing I might do different is reduce the amount of sugar.  I will be making this again soon.

I made this for a breakfast potluck at the office and after baking it I cut the the bread slices half to be able to serve more people. I also used thick sliced bread (Texas Toast).  Everyone loved it and I was asked for the recipe several times. I plan on making this for my family during the holidays.  It is so easy to make.

Five stars for a delicious breakfast dish that is easy to prepare ahead (which I love). This is a great make ahead dish that turned out moist,sweet, cinnamony and everyone raved over it!
I used the thick texas toast bread and increased the eggs by one. It is soooo good.
We had this for our Christmas brunch and it was gobbled up in a hurry.  I doubled the recipe because of the number of people we had, and everyone loved it.  I will certainly be using this again.
Good stuff! As with Shae, we didn't need to use the syrup. I cut the recipe in half since there is only two of us, but it still came out well.  Yum!

I haven't made this yet...but excited to try it for Christmas Day. It looks like it will convert to vegetarian by substituting Silk Soy vanilla-flavored for the milk. This could become a new tradition!
This recipe was easy to make and the house smelled so good. Everyone woke up in a good mood for a change.

Excellent recipe; So easy to put together the night before and ready in no time. Turned out perfectly. Excellent.My kids loved this. will make often. Served 6 for my family

This was so easy to prepare the night before, and then we took it to church and cooked it there for Sunday School! How easy!! Thanks so much... YUMM!!!

Excellent.  How easy is this? Most people have this stuff in their houses, so you can decide at night you'll have a nice stay home Sunday brunch.  Thank you for posting.  The picture doesn't do the casserole justice, in my opinion.

Just excellent! I used bread maker bread that was just a teeny bit old/dry. As you make it you kind of think to yourself, "Is this right? Can I be doing this right? ooook, we'll see!" but it turns out GREAT! I agree that there's no syrup needed with this one! Totally a keeper for me, thanks!

I really, really liked this...but I'm so disappointed because my husband did not!  He wouldn't even touch his portion.  He said he wouldn't eat it because of the texture.  So, I guess I won't be making it again, but I wanted to let you know that I thought it was very good!

I made this recipe and scrambled eggs for a father's day brunch.  Everyone enjoyed it.

This was wonderful!  I will never make french toast the old way ever again.  I did reduce the sugar and increase the cinnamon.  I had to use extra eggs and milk because I used texas toast and then I cooked it longer.

This was so yummy! I made this for some guests over the weekend and everyone really enjoyed it. DH said he thought it had a bit too much sugar so I may decrease that next time per your suggestion. This is so good.  I made this for my family on Saturday morning.  We loved it.  Its easy to put together adn the taste was very good.  Although, you didn't need syrup we served this with blueberry syrup.  thank you for sharing.

This was so yummy this morning for Easter breakfast! It was so nice to take it out of the fridge and put it in the oven. The house smelled so good that my teenagers were at the table before it was finished baking!  Thank you so much!

I have made this for so many potlucks.  Everyone always asks for the recipe.  Easy and wonderful everytime!

This is my go-to recipe for when we have company or my children have friends sleep over.  So easy and so good!  I've made it with whole wheat bread and replaced half of the eggs with egg whites and it's still delicious.

I will make this often, thanks so much for posting!

Adults said it was ok....Kids loved it!!!

Just made this today for Easter Brunch.  It was wonderful!  I'm always skeptical of overnight recipes, but this one turned out great! I used Texas Toast bread,  real butter, 6 eggs, and I used 3/4 cups half & half and 3/4 cups skim milk.  I saw others say it was sweet, but I still used the full 1 cup of brown sugar and added about 2 tsp vanilla and extra sprinkle of cinnamon in the milk/egg mixture.  I baked covered for about 30 mins and uncovered for about 20-25 more.  The bottom had a nice caramelized coating and it smelled sooo good baking.  Needless to say it was devoured, with just a drizzle of maple syrup on it.  I will definitely be making again!!

I LOVE this recipe!  I have made it a few times and it is always a hit.  I especially love how easy it is and that it can be made the night before.  So much buttery, sweet goodness for barely any work...my kind of recipe :)

Love this recipe!  I assembled it last night and cooked it this morning for a Christmas Eve brunch.  Everyone raved about it and ate it up!! Some used syrup and some ate it without syrup.  Everyone loved it!  Thanks for posting this keeper recipe!!

Very easy, and I bet even better making the second time.  It was quick, easy and a cinch to finish with happy stomachs. Easy and yummy!!!

Made for a party yesterday and ever bite was gone! Everyone loved it?.thanks for sharing!

Delicious and easy!  Ive used sourdough french bread, sliced in half and add a tsp of vanilla. I'm also generous with the cinnamon. Its very sweet with 1c instead of 2/3c option, but you don't even need syrup!  A keeper and crowd pleaser!

There was one large piece leftover......made for a yummy dessert for me and my boyfriend tonight!

Excellent!!! I used white sandwich bread the first time in my test run. I used Italian bread the second time and that is what I recommend, it rises a lot more and is nice and puffy. This was so good!! This is the only way I will ever make french toast , it was so easy. I did reduce the brown sugar as others had suggested and it was perfect. This made my Christmas breakfast a breeze , Thank you for that :)
Great recipe, it was a hit with my family. ??

SEE BELOW FOR *STUFFED PRETZELS : )* -Made this 3 times-I halved the recipe each time, which make 8-10 pretzels, depending. I used a little less of each flour, and kneaded/combined the dough about 2 minutes. If someone is having trouble rolling out the dough into ropes, it works well to put the dough on a floured counter, hand-shape into a retangle 3-4 times longer than wide, and cut the dough into sections (half the recipe will get 8-10 small rectangles). Then it's easy to hand roll them out into uniform ropes 12"-15" long for a traditional twist-pretzel. (-keep the dough on the floured counter-don't pick it up, and just roll it out w/the palms of your hands.)
The last time I made it, I made less pretzels (using almost twice the amount of dough per pretzel) and made pepperoni/cheese stuffed pretzels. I took my larger dough-piece and using a rolling pin, rolled out the piece into a flat rectangle about 12"-15"long and maybe 2" wide. I put cheddar, provolone, and mozzarella shredded cheese and diced/sliced pepperoni down the center and then carefully folded/rolled the dough over the filling and made it into a "stuffed rope" (careful to seal seam/ends...don't overstuff). I gently "squished" the rope from one end to the other to make sure there were no air pockets. I then form a pretzel (just layed one end over the other, didn't "twist" the center because of the stuffing). Baked like the recipe said...came out GREAT. You can be creative and stuff them with whatever...really good.
