When the eggs were done to my preference, I took them out of the oven, they seemed to break apart a bit at the potatoe "crust".  The last ones out held together better.  So, next time I will let the pan cool off for 5 minutes before taking them out of the pan.  Thanks for posting this tasty combo.
wow fast and easy .dee

I made this for breakfast this morning, cutting the recipe in half. I thought it was very good, although I'll probably tweak it a little. I can see that there is the potential for many variations (add sausage, sprinkle with herbs, sauces, etc). My husband really loved it--he took a bite and pronounced it "the perfect food." I won't say how many he ate--just that I had to make another bunch! UPDATE: Almost 1 1/2 years after I first made this, it remains a favorite with my DH. I cook his for 15 minutes for a more custardy yolk, and mine and DS's for 20 minutes for well-cooked yolks. Here's a tip: I find that a gravy ladle works better than a spoon for mashing the tater tots into the muffin tins.
I have been crazy about this recipe for years!  I actually dip the tortillas in the white sauce to soften them and remove excess before filling.  It's messy, but helps them roll better.
Very tasty and easy to make.  I added corn to the chicken mixture, which added some sweetness.  Next time, I'll probably add a pepper with more kick than the chiles...perhaps some habanero.

I absolutely love this recipe! My family gave me a thumbs up. 
I added garlic to the onions and I didn't have coriander so I decided on turmeric. It turned out delicious!
I don't think there was enough meat filling though. I ended up with six tortillas. Next time I'll double up on that. Can't wait to try these with tuna, beef, salmon or even vegtarian meat. I will definitely make this again. It was so easy and fun!

Not much to say that hasn't been said.  But wanted to add my "YUM!!!" to the list.  I did use corn torillas instead of flour because that is what I had on hand, and they were great.  I used left over grilled chicken, so the smoky flavor of the chickens with the peppers and onions was fantastic.  I will keep this recipe in mind for all that left over chicken.

Happy family, especially our daughter! I like spicy, but not too spicy, and I found the way...instead of regular Monterey Jack; Pepper Jack! Wow, was this ever good. I was in a bit of a rush, so I cut the tortillas into about 1" strips, layered half on the bottom, sprinkled the chicken mixture (without the sauce) on top, then spread all the sauce over. (Used the 1/2 cup of flour in the sauce and it was thick and perfect). Layed more strips on top and then the cheese, I used a little more cheese! Thanks Karen!

My family really liked this! I used corn tortillas and pepper jack cheese which added the perfect amount of kick for us. We served over yellow rice mix and a dallop of salsa on top. Really yummy! Thanks!

This is a great recipe! I used the pepper jack cheese like the other commenters did because we like a little spice.  The sauce was really wonderful and the filling was great too! Very easy to make! Thanks!

This was my first attempt at chicken enchildas and it was easy AND delicious!  I was fooled by the amount of sauce, thinking I had too much so I didn't use all of it on top of the enchiladas; next time I'll use it all as it was yummy!

Made these last night and, after the first bite, DH said "This is a keeper!". I did take some liberties with the enchilada filling tho. I added a drained 7 oz. can of mushrooms, a defrosted and squeezed dry 9 oz. box of frozen spinach, and added two minced garlic cloves to the onion/pepper mixture. The sauce is really outstanding in this dish and I used a four cheese Mexican blend in place of the MJ cheese. Thanks for posting this, Karen- we really enjoyed this!
Yummy, Yummy, Yummy!  My husband and I loved this so much there were no leftovers!  I used pepperjack cheese to spice it up a little.  This is a new staple for our family!  Thanks for the recipe!
We really did enjoy this meal.  The sauce was so creamy and good.  Will be using this recipe again.  Thanks for posting.
Good & simple

These enchiladas are just yummy! The sauce is simply delicious. I've made these twice recently and they're big a hit with the entire family. I tried both the flour and the corn tortillas. We strongly preferred the corn tortillas, as the corn adds a great flavor, and they hold up better than the flour. I didn't use the green bell pepper, as we don't care for them. Thanks for the wonderful recipe. I'll be making these often!

I liked this, didn't love it. It is super mild and super rich. I have to admit I didn't add the corriander because I didn't have any. Maybe it would have made a big difference. My husband enjoyed it very much. I did like that is was from scratch and no soup involved like in so many other recipes. Ooooo, some jalepenos would be goood.........

Wow Wow and Wow! This was excellent, and so easy to make!
I did add extra chicken to the recipe because I had a house full of teenagers to feed on short notice, and it turned out wonderful. the coriander added a really nice flavor that we all liked.  
I was totally surprised when the kids descended on the dinner table and inhaled the enchiladas! They not only ate all of them they even scraped up the extra sauce from the bottom of the baking dish and ate that up too! Every single person at the dinnertable commented on how great they are! We will make this recipe over and over.
Great recipe and easy to make away from home. We travel for business more than 10 months of the year and this is one of our favorites to make over and over!

Muy Bueno! The sauce is delicious! I used white corn tortillas and added some chopped jalapeno peppers to the chicken mixture. I also topped the casserole with some sliced black olives. It was sooo good! I'll be making this often.
My gosh is this fantastic. Everyone loved the flavor and the sauce was wonderful. My husband & I finished off the leftovers today. Thanks so much Karen!

I made these this weekend and they were a hit with my mom and my sister. They aren't quite like Chi Chi's were, and now that I think about it, those had mushrooms in too, but these certainly were yummy. I used a little extra cheese and sour cream because that was what I had left and, well, my family likes cheese! lol I also used the blended mexican cheese (from Sargento) which gave it a little milder flavor than just using MJ probably would. My sister couldn't stop eating it, so I had to send the rest home with her! Thanks for the recipe!
Made this with leftover turkey. It wasn't what I was expecting.  I don't know if I'll make again.
Absolutely yummy!! I used double cheddar cheese since I had no MJ on hand, and it turned out perfectly. Very rich, very filling, and I will very definitely make it again. Thanks!
Used lower fat versions of all possible ingredients  but still thoroughly enjoyed this.  Excellent flavors, Karen.

Thanks for sharing Karen. I made as written but left out the green pepper as I didn't have it on hand. Turned out awesome! Mild enough for the wife and 5 YO, and I threw some spicy salsa on mine at the table to add a kick. Will definitely make again.

This was so good but also very rich!  I added crushed chilis to the cheese sauce as I did not have green peppers.  I also used the whole wheat tortillas.  And when I cooked the chicken, I added cumin, chili powder and garlic.  This was really good and will definitely make again.  Yum!

Just fininished enjoying this great dish. Followed it exactly and the only change I'll make next time is a dolop of spicy salsa on top....it just, for me, needs a little more 'kick'. Thanks for sharing.
oh yummm!!! My family loved this recipe. I kicked it up a notch with sweet red peppers with the green pepper and added a dash of cayenne pepper to the sauce. This is a keeper!!! Thank you Karen!

This is a really great recipe!  The sauce is so much better than anything I've ever made with canned soups and so very easy to make!  I made exactly as written and we loved these enchiladas.  Thanks Karen for posting such a wonderful recipe that I will make again...soon!!
This is delicious, it was a big hit at my dinner party. Thanks for sharing...i will definitelly do this again!

This was so so good!  My family loved it.  I sprayed my pan with non-stick oil spray before adding anything to it and everything came right out.  The sauce is what makes this sooooo good.  I also used red peppers instead of green to sweeten it up for children and no canned peppers, same reason (my kids don't like spicy), kiddoes.  I will definitely make this again, thanks for a great recipe!
One word. MMmmm!

I cannot believe I haven't rated this yet. I prepared for a family get together and it was a smashing success! Absolutely delicious! I made one with flour tortillas and one with corn tortillas- both were excellent. Thank you!!

I can't believe someone else has this recipe!!! I have been making this with my grandmother for 20+ years!!!! I layer the ingredients instead of rolling and have subsituted garlic for onion, and I use A LOT of chili powder!!!!!!!!!
Thought it was very good.  Did not have coriander and used PepperJack cheese for a little bite.  Between 4-5 stars.
Unbelievably good!  Really, you have to try this.
I made this recipe two nights ago, it was delicious and reheats wonderfully.
Wonderful!  Even my 6yo gobbled it up.  Not too spicy, but by no means tasteless.  I am looking forward to the leftovers this week and will make again.

Made this for Easter. Just like everyone says - really good. Got compliments galore. I followed some of the alternative suggestions from other reviewers:

added: sauted garlic, 1 package chili seasoning to chicken mixture, topped with black olives - gives it color. And used corn tortillas instead of flour- fried lightly in olive oil and drained.
I used `1/2 tsp. cumin instead of the coriander, and they were great!  These sure hit the spot!

I usually use a recipe using a "cream of" soup, but decided to try this recipe since I had the ingredients on hand.  Wow, I don't think I'll ever go back.  It was super easy to prepare, and just had the extra oomph in taste.  I didn't use peppers, and used cheddar instead of jack, but it still was amazing.
This is definitely a 5 star recipe! We loved it.  I cooked it with half butter/ half EVOO.  I also used light sour cream and it still turned out perfect.  Thanks for a great recipe!

Loved this! Used corn tortillas and layered ingredients, alternately. Also, left out green pepper b/c we don't like them much. This was really easy to prepare. It's our new go-to "Mexican Chicken" because there's no canned soup with MSG in this but it's still creamy and delicious! Thanks!

Sooooooo delicious. I had no coriander, so I used a shake of thyme and a sprinkle of curry. And no green chilies so I used extra green peppers, but definitely will make again! A++++++++++ Thanks for posting this!
This is a very good recipe. I wouldn't change a thing.

Amazing both me and my husband really enjoyed this we were surprised at how tasty it was, not quite as HOT as I would like it but the taste was that good I didnt mind that..... Thank you for sharing this great recipe

I had some leftover rice so I doubled the sauce and put the rice in the bottom of the pan with a little of the extra sauce and just followed the recipe from there. It was a big hit with everyone, including my husband who hates Mexican food.
Excellent. My husband and I loved this. I think the secret is to use full fat ingredients. I made it once before w/ low fat cheese and it wasn't nearly as creamy and tasty.
Made this exactly as written and we both really enjoyed the end result.  Leftovers taste great too.  I will definitely make this one again.

Exceptional - family loved it.  I did add a 1/2 teaspoon of cajun spice to add a bit of zip since previous posts seemed to feel it was a bit mild.  Definitely worth the prep time.  Worthy of a dinner party!

Very delicious. I used reduced fat sour cream & margarine and my sauce was absolutely wonderfully creamy. Also, I substituted a poblano pepper for the green pepper which  added nice flavor, not spice.
Delicious!  My husband and I loved it.  Next time I will add a little more spice for our taste.  I did use a little more chicken than what the recipe called for.  Definitely a keeper!

What a great dish! Nice, creamy sauce which I thought was going to be too much... but it was perfect! Made for a Cinco de Mayo family dinner and everyone loved it. I added a little more chicken (3 cups) and shredded it instead of chopping/dicing. Will keep this recipe! Thanks Karen!

Very good.  I used a poblano, per another reviewer's suggestion, and the taste was great.  I also added probably 2x the chicken since I had plenty enough onion/pepper and sauce mix.  Not reading the recipe carefully enough, I dumped all the cheese in the sauce by accident and next time I won't do that!  I also added a few shakes of mild chili powder to add a bit more flavor, but I'm not sure it was even noticeable.

This is a very good recipe. The sauce is what makes it so delicious. However, cut the salt by half or more. The other ingredients (like cheese or the cooked chicken) add salt. Also it needs a little heat, the poblano, as suggested by someone else, is still not enough kick. Very good though.

I've finally found my go-to chicken enchilada recipe!  Thanks!  Changes I made:  Added 1 poblano plus one jalapeno (incl all ribs and seeds) into the green pepper + onion mixture.  I used low fat sour cream in the sauce as well as pepper jack cheese.  I added fresh cilantro over the enchiladas upon serving.  I liked the idea of garlic from other reviewers.  Also - my flour tortillas were high fibre cilantro + pepper.  The enchiladas had a lot of kick this way!  Will absolutely make this many many times more - using high fibre tortillas and low fat ingredients plus extra peppers for kick.
Actually nicer than we expected, though it looked a bit dodgy when I cooked it, especially the sauce.  Turned out well in the end!
This was DELICIOUS and so EASY!!! Thanks for the recipe and I will be making this again for sure :)
Yum!  I cant make this enough!

Wonderful recipe! Quick, easy, and delicious.  What a winning combination.  As others suggested, I added a huge clove of fresh garlic while cooking the onion and substituted corn tortillas for the flour (family preference).  The only thing I regret is leaving out the green chilis.  Didn't have any.  But that would have taken this dish to the next level.  Next time I will be sure to add them.  Thanks for sharing.

Family loved this!  Thanks for a great recipe!  Only thing I really did different was use Pepper Jack, because it's what I had.  UPDATE: Made this again tonight.  Grilled the chicken with a Tex Mex blend of spices.  Really added some umph!  Great dish.  Also, with the sauce....taste before adding to the dish.  We found we needed a little more salt and pepper, and added just a dash of Cholulu for some added flavor.  Turned out spectacular!  For what it's worth, Pepper Jack is a really nice dash....good flavor, and not hot...just another layer of flavor.
outstanding! Only change I made was to use pepper jack cheese to spice it up even more!
They were OK, I think if I ever make this again I will thin out the sauce some more and not use so much of it to cover the enchiladas.

Yum, yum, yum! I made it exactly as directed; only I used plain cheddar cheese. Oh, I did change up the spices. Coriander? Don't have any. I put in some taco seasoning (Penzey's 'Arizona Dreaming- 2010). Just taste the sauce before you put together the dish! (I had a hard time adding all the liquid at once- usually that would make it lumpy! But it did work with very few lumps, none of which were noticeable in the final dish.) I made it a day ahead for company. Great recipe; thanks for sharing!!!

I made this recipe to use up some leftover turkey. I used a Mexican blend cheese and reduced fat sour cream because that is what I had on hand. Quite honestly, we are so used to reduced fat that often if we go out the whole fat version tastes odd to us.  Even with the reduced fat sour cream, the sauce was still nice and creamy.  DH gave it four stars after adding hot sauce otherwise the family gave it three stars (i.e. good)

I am from Texas, and sour cream enchiladas are a staple offering at many restaurants and I love them. I have never been able to find a recipe with a sour cream sauce that did not break apart into little curds, until now.  This is the best sour cream sauce recipe I have tried, and makes a very good enchilada. Thanks!

This was very tasty.  I used corn tortillas instead of flour tortillas and omitted the ground coriander (didn't have any).  My kids ate it without complaint, which makes it a winner in my book.  It was better the first day as the sauce thickened after refrigeration.  I made enchiladas but had filling left over so I spread it on top of the enchiladas and tore up some more tortillas to go with it, then poured sauce over it all.  Next time, I'll just tear all the tortillas and mix it all together.

This was delicious.  We're not into spicy/hot meals and we found this recipe to have a perfect combination of flavor and mildness from the peppers.  I even at leftovers for breakfast the next morning.

I had some leftover turkey from our holiday dinner and I chose this recipe to make something different with it.  Very yummy, a bit rich, but really good.  I served this with spanish rice and refried beans.  Thank you for sharing.

Made this 1 week ago and it was fantastic. I am not a fan of Mexican foods but wanted to try something different. This was it. Only thing I did was add a few slices of chopped up Jalepenos from a jar to give it a kick. They were actually better the next day. I took extras to work and shared lunch with some co-workers. They all asked for the recipe !! I also used fresh chicken that I boiled and added some perdue ready chicken I had left over as well. This was SOOO delicious and will become a regular with me !!!!!! Thanks Karen !!!!

One of the best dinners I have ever cooked.  I doubled the recipe and followed it exactly.  I froze one tray and served the other for dinner.  My family loved it.  I have always been intimidated about making chicken enchiladas and this was a snap.
I used rotisserie chicken and it came out great.  The only thing I would do different is make it a bit spicy, just because I love the heat.  Great dish!
I have made this recipe countless times this past DECADE.... THanks Karen from Colorado and food.com for featuring her today :)
Yummy enchilada.  Loved the sauce with the chicken.  I used 1/2 of 7 oz, can for the pepper.  Easy and delicious.

I liked the mixture of 8 ozs Mexican cheese plus 4 ozs Monterey Jack. I used 2 cups of rotisserie chicken (dark and white). Followed the recipe and LOVE it. I like extra heat but my SO has GERD, so the green chilies did add the needed flavor with no heat.
I thought this was a good recipe, but like many others, I thought it was too salty. I made it as directed. It needs some tweaking to be GREAT.

This was great!  I made 6 of these and then at step 8 I put 6 of the Recipe #150765 ones in the other half of the pan.  I made the bacon for Recipe #150765 the night before.  I'll be making these for DD and friends for breakfast after Prom this spring.  Made for *PAC Fall 2007* game
This is a really great idea!  I omitted the egg, and browned some breakfast sausage, placed it in the tater top cups, and then topped with cheese.  These work great for OAMC.  Thanks for posting!

This was very good.  I added a little pork sausage.  A very small rubbermaid container that I use for storing sauces in worked perfectly for pressing the tater tots into the muffin pan.  It would have been great to have had a deeper muffin pan so that I could have put extra cheese or more ham.  Mine stuck to the muffin pan but it could be because I sprayed mine with Pam instead of using the oil (or maybe I just did not use enough Pam).  I will definitely make these again.

Quite tasty, but I think this dish would be better suited to a family with kids.  Unfortunately, we don't have any, and while we thought it tasted quite good (made it twice and added hot sauce to the cheese layer the second time aroud), we thought it was a bit too much work to make for just the two of us.  That being said, it would be a great recipe to make ahead for an easy, kid-friendly breakfast.

Very yummy, but a little dry for our liking.  We ended up dousing them with ketchup in a dish, so it kind of defeated the muffin shape.  Overall though, they were very tasty and I'll probably make them again, just in a 13X9 pan or something other then the muffin tin.
All of us loved this.  I did change it up a little by adding some cooked cubed ham to the cups.  This was a fun way to serve a meal and the little ones were delighted.

These were pretty good. I needed to use a LOT more oil since mine stuck to the pan and they need to look like they aren't done on top. I kept checking on them and they didn't look done and when I thought they were ready, I ended up with hard boiled eggs!!

Tasty little bundles.  They're somewhat similiar to my recipe#243619 but with less steps and ingredients.  I will definitely make these again, but will use pepper jack cheese and some sauteed onions and mushrooms.  This time I added chopped jalapeno to mine, but everyone else enjoyed the original version.  These would be great for company since they're simple and easy.

I may have overcooked it, but after 20 minutes, the eggs were a little hard on the outside (sort of rubbery) but otherwise done perfectly.  I wasn't sure I'd make it again, but my husband thought they were very good!  I'll give it another shot.

These were pretty tasty.  I defrosted my tator tots in the microwave to speed things up.  I made exactly as directed, cooked for eggs for 15 minutes and they were perfect.  The yolks were a little runny but not too runny.  Thanks for posting!

I made these for Breakfast for Dinner Night. Only after they were all eaten, and we were discussing the meal, did I learn that no one is keen on over-easy eggs. Go figure...none left! These were easy to make which is always great for me!
This was really tasty and I made one for my son to eat tonight. I tasted it though and liked it alot! Thanks for posting.

I just made these this morning.  I really adore the idea of them.  The taste was kind of bland, though.  I'm thinking that if I can add a few bacon crumbles or sausage or something to it, that will solve our problem.  They are definitely a perfect on-the-go meal, though.  I could only fit 4 tots in each cup, and that was still too full.  Next time, I'll cut it down to 3.  I wonder if you could replace the tater tots with shredded hashbrowns?
My grandson liked these, but I thought they were a bit greasy, maybe they could be made with hash browns that are not as greasy

I followed the recipe as written other then I made eight. I also scrambled my eggs and added some pepper before putting them in. These were good but very greasy. I think they also could have used more seasoning.
Such a simple idea but great presentation!  For some reason, I could not find tater tots, so I used potato patties & they worked very well.  Delicious!

I made this this morning and I was in a hurry. I had already baked my tater tots last night. Short on time, I decided to raise the temp to 425 degrees. I used only a few of the egg yokes and all the whites. I whipped them up and poured them in and sprinkled the cheese on top. Because of the higher temp I added water to the empty muffin cups but filled only 1/4 of the cup. At the higher temp they baked in about 15 mins. At that higher temp the cheese became a nice golden crisp consistency. I didn't use much cheese. Just enough to top them off.  I will make them again and add sautéed onion or red peppers and add a fresh spinach leaf or two in there. A few fresh clippings of chives would be a wonderful touch.

I used bigger muffin tins because I wanted to add chorizo sausage between the tater tots and eggs. I also sprinkled a little more cheese on top of the eggs before setting them to the oven. When the cups are done. I sprinkled them with old bay seasoning and ground black pepper, garnished with chopped green onion. The cups turned out very well. My DH said that they were very delicious and filling. Will make them again, but next time I will decrease the baking time. 15 minutes seemed to be a little long for the eggs. Thanks for posting this recipe!

Definitely keep in mind that it looks over easy but is actually cooked through. 375 for 15 mins is a bit too much on a new oven. It won't be mushy in the middle, even with not completely thawed tots. Very good, very easy. I added cooked bacon and grilled onions. Needs lots of salt & pepper. I missed the garlic salt and chives on top. Even avocado or sour cream would be yummy.
Delicious. I added lots of sliced mushrooms with the mince because I love them. I will make this again many times.
This is a great recipe!  Simple to make and delicious. Thanks Caryn!
This was another great dish.  Made plenty, ate the leftovers the next day, it tasted even better if that is possible.
This was very good..my family loved it..definitely filled a 9 x 13 pan..thanks for sharing this recipe.

You know, I had never had baked ziti before - even eating out. I found this recipe when I was "on the prowl" for something totally different a couple of nights ago. Followed the recipe to a tee (except I subbed salt-free homemade meatless sauce and low-sodium chicken broth so that I could enjoy it without feeling guilty!) and BINGO! I was in business. Served it with a very crisp green salad topped with very spicy Greek olive oil dressing and my homemade sourdough croutons, and it was a meal to remember.

The Classic Baked Ziti was great!! My kids and husband loved it. So easy to make. Was great to put together early in the day to have on a busy sport night. Made great left overs too. This one is a keeper. Thanks.

Thanks for the great recipe!  I only had a 26 oz. jar of spaghetti sauce on hand, so I decreased the chicken broth to 1/2 cup, and it was wonderful!  My husband loved it and told me I need to make it again... so it's a keeper!

This turned out really well.  I served it with a nice green salad and fresh bread and my whole family enjoyed it.  I followed the recipe to a "T" and it came out perfectly.  I will definitely make this again.  Thanks for posting, Caryn.

Wow! I would give this recipe 10 stars if I could! It was a very yummy dish and I would not change a thing. I used Prego chunky garden and it turned out awesome. This will be a favorite to make in my house again and again! Thank you!
What more could you ask for:  Taste Great and it's Quick and Easy.  Thanks for the recipe.
This recipie is wonderful! Even my picky toddler finished her plate! I used sweet Italian sausage instead of hamburger. This is going in my dinner rotation! Thanks for posting it!

Absolutely delicious! I used small penne pasta I had on hand instead of the ziti, and added a bit more sauce than called for. (We love LOTS of sauce). Turned out perfect. Eating the leftovers tonight for dinner as well. I just have to make some more homemade garlic bread to go with it! Definitely a keeper! Thanks for posting.

Very good and reasonably easy.  This really makes a lot, I hope I can find the room in the fridge for the leftovers. I don't expect them to stay in there too long though. :)  I used a 28 oz can of spaghetti sauce, and one cups worth of chicken boullion with a cup of water instead of broth.  I think next time I'll use a jar with the full amount.  Judging from my husband's reaction this will definitely be going on dinner rotation.

Delicious! I made this for dinner last night and it was really good! I almost doubled the recipe because it didn't seem like it would make that much but everyone is right, it makes PLEANTY! a really good simple recipe, thank you:)
Excellent recipe- very easy too!  Thanks for sharing!
Followed this recipe exactly.  Not our favorite, but certainly passable.  Might make again, increasing the garlic by quite a lot as we love garlic!
Ummmm...omg so good...I can't stop eating it!!!!

Great recipe for clam chowder. I used 5 slices of bacon and half and half. I like the grated carrots in this soup. I also used instant flake potato to thicken the soup. I cant wait to make this again and I am going to try the 1/2 tsp curry as you suggested! Thanks for sharing this recipe with me Gerry.

Made this recipe for supper last night. Easy to make.  Good flavor.
The bacon I used gave it kind of a smoky flavor.  I served this with home made bread from scratch.
Husband and I both think that this is a keeper.
Good Job Gerry999

16 oz of pasta seems like a HUGE amount.  I just put the dish in the oven, and used less than a 16 oz box of pasta, and had nearly an eighth + (2 oz, a medium tupperware dish of rotini) left over.

I'll let you know how it tastes afterward, but if I followed the instructions right there is way too much pasta...

Even though I messed up on a few things (like putting in the whole can of chicken broth instead of just a cup and putting the cheese on top as at the beginning of the cooking time instead of just at the end) it was incredibly delicious! Everyone loved it. Thanks for a recipe I can use regularly because it was so easy and quick to prepare.

Sorry, but I did not like this recipe. I was very interested in using this recipe and followed it with no variation.  But with these ingredients combined it had a taste that was, to me, odd. Perhaps I used a weird & different sauce or somehow botched it up (only human!).
Great recipe - my whole family enjoyed it and I will definitely make it again.

I made this tonight and followed Miller's lead using homemade meat sauce (only kind I had).  I don't know if it was the addition of the chicken stock, but this was just delicious.  I thought that the proportion of sauce/liquid to pasta was perfect, and reducing either would have resulted in a skimpy dish.  I was careful to leave the boiled pasta undercooked so that by the time it came out of the oven it still had some bite to it.  Thank you for a wonderful recipe, we'll make it often!
It was very good.  The only thing I added to It was ricotta cheese and I cooked It a little longer than what It said.

Delicious and easy!  I had 10 family members for dinner and needed something simple and quick because I work full time.  Received many compliments. Even the picky toddlers who don't have long attention spans ate 3 plate-fulls.  Because I like people to eat their fill, I did double the recipe and now have plenty of leftovers for everyone's lunch.  A definite keeper!

My husband and I both thought this was very good. I only made a few changes to the recipe; I added additional garlic, some Italian seasonings, half of a red pepper, and then some red pepper flakes (we tend to like things on the spicy side). Quite tasty!
This dish was OK.  I followed the recipe exactly and it was good but not great.

I made my own meatless sauce the day before and it was a breeze to put together the next evening.I had 7 people for dinner and the two teenagers had two huge helpings.
I served salad and french garlic bread.Someone said in a review that 16 ozs of pasta was to much.
I did not find this to be true,but the right amount.I did have some left over,but this is a plus for me,we love leftovers.Thanks for sharing your recipe it was enjoyed by all :0)

My family and I thought this was a very yummy ziti. The only addition was I added 1/2 lb. Italian sausage. It made the sauce meatier and tasted more "Italian". I served it with salad, fresh bread, and a good ole bottle of wine. It was an easy recipe to prepare and something that I would like to have again. Thanks Caryn.

Very delicious recipe!!  The only changes I made was that I used a tablespoon of chopped fresh oregano leaves from my herb garden and I used "Italian Blend" cheese because it is what I had on hand.  For those who haven't tried it, it is a blend of mozzarella, parmesan, provolone, romano and two others I can't remember.  It worked great!!  Thanks for sharing this recipe.
Everyone loved this, even my picky niece & nephews.  Omitted parmesan and used ricotta instead.  Very easy to make and the whole family loves it.
This was a wonderful meal!  I actually froze half of it afterwards and it was even good reheated!  I will definetly be making this again!

I made this without the meat and definitely missed the flavor.  However, I added a bit of thyme to the sauce as it was simmering, and replaced half the chicken  Merlot for some depth (just personal preference).  The only suggestion I might make is to crank up the heat for the last 10 mins. of uncovered cooking time so that the cheese can brown a little more.  Great recipe!

Made this exactly as listed except I couldn't find Ziti in my supermarket so I used Rigatoni instead.  This recipe was okay but it wasn't anything special imho.  Hubby thought it was just okay too.  We had it with crusty bread only so maybe a salad or some other side might have made it more special however, I probably won't make it again.
Tasty!!!  My family loved this.  I reduced the recipe by half and had plenty to feed 6 of us.  Definitely will make this again!
Very easy to make and everyone loved it!! There were no leftovers! It was very tasty. Thank you!

I simply don't understand how anybody could have any complaints about this dish--it's fantastic, five stars all the way. I'd assign more if I could. I followed the recipe as best I could--pasta sauce is not sold in 32oz jars in Canada but 28oz, so I made up the difference with plain tomato sauce which I seasoned with extra oregano and some thyme--but also added some sliced fresh mushrooms to the meat-onion mixture. This was so easy to prepare, even after I was pooped after a day of xmas shopping, and makes an enormous dish of pasta--enough to generously feed 6, definitely. I was worried it wouldn't fit in the 13x9 pan, but it did. This recipe is a true keeper; I'll be making it often. Thanks for posting this winner!

Absolutely wonderful dish!  My family and I definitely noticed the difference from the regular ziti I used to make.  I used 1 1/3 lbs. of ground chuck (as packaged), 45 oz. of Ragu sauce, 1 1/4 cups of chicken broth, and added a can of mushrooms, along with a touch extra of the spices and I have enough ziti leftover for this evening!  Thanks so much for sharing, Caryn!  This is a keeper!

Wow, this was great.  Last night I made Sharlene ~W's Jo Mama's World Famous Spaghetti #22782.  I used the leftovers for this tonight.  Incredible.  I can see why some people would think that there is too much pasta.  I like my noodles covered in sauce - but my DH who eats a lot more baked ziti than me said it was the perfect the amount of noodles to sauce for this dish.  
This is a great dish and I will be making it again!!

WoW!!! ...I made this tonight and it was clearly the best Clam chowder I have ever made. Another winner by my dear friend.  This is without a doubt the best clam chowder on the site. Made this for Best of the Best 2010 Tag Game.  This isn't the typical Clam Chowder that I usually go for, but this was a wonderful change.  I used half fat free evaporated milk and half fat free half and half and did not take time to add the roux.  Because of this, mine was not the thick type I usually go for, but the flavor was outstanding!  I also liked having some of the added veggies in there to make it healthier. My family really enjoyed this dish and it had a wonderful flavor. I am a New Englander, so  I was skeptical at first, but this was a delicious and different way to make "chowdah"! I made this for Best of 2010 Cookbook Tag.  Thanks for a new family favorite!

I followed the recipe right on down, deferring to your suggestions along the way (although I did add almost twice as much of the clams!), & the chowder was outstanding! This time around it was just for the 2 of us to enjoy over several days! A wonderful keeper of a recipe, that's for sure! Thanks for posting it! [Made & reviewed in the Best of 2011 recipe tagging event]

I changed the recipe significantly in that I used diced rutabaga rather than potato to cut back on carbs. There I varied again, adding 1 cup half and half and a half cup of buttermilk to help thicken and flavor the soup.  It still seemed like it was missing something to hubby and I, and after adding a bay leaf and a dash of ground thyme, it was much closer in flavor to the clam chowder we were expecting.  Hubby still didn't care for this, telling me that if I never made it again he "wouldn't be UNhappy."  I on the other hand, thought this was really tasty, even if it wasn't the New England style flavor I was expecting, so I'm splitting the star rating between us.  Very filling as well.  Thanks for sharing!  Update:  I am bumping up the star rating on this regardless of hubby's opinion after re-heating this on day 2.  All the flavors melded, and there's a subtle spiciness from the curry (I used red) that was missing the first day.  I'll make this again either in the crock pot or the day before I plan to serve it for best flavor.

This is delicious!  I love the extra veggies.  I used root veggies instead of potatoes.  In addition to the curry, I added garlic, a bay leaf and old bay seasoning.  I thickened it with corn starch which worked beautifully.

Awesome!!  Thanks Gerry!  I added over a cup of diced squash because the garden is cranking that out right now.  I doubled the chicken stock and didn't end up adding any milk or cream.  It worked out great!  Thanks for the base concept of amazingness here!
If I made it again, I would still increase the proportion of egg a bit as I felt the egg mixture was a bit thin.

I had some guests coming over this evening, made these for them using raspberry jam. Needless to say, they loved them and took the recipe and went off home:)
A very simple and quick recipe, I particularly like the name as well as the colour once these are done. Thank you for sharing this:)
How unique!! I made them with my homemade strawberry jam, and you're right!  I can't believe how good they are. Thanks for sharing.

Bergy has asked that I give this recipe an unbiased test, since I do have experience in this area (recipe testing), and I was pleased to do so and had the following results. Jailhouse Doughnuts would have rated a full five from me based on taste, but the instructions could be a little more explicit so I chose a 4-star rating. The proportions of milk to egg were fine; I believe any less milk would result in too eggy a concoction. I lightly dipped each "sandwich" in the egg mixture, then slipped them into several inches of hot oil (375F) and deepfried for 2 mins per side; then placed them on paper towels to drain. They were quite crispy on the outside, and quite jammy (I used blueberry) on the inside; they did not remind me of french toast at all. They made for a lovely treat; I just wish they "looked" less like sandwiches :-) Perhaps a different cutting method would help. I believe the trick here is having enough deepfrying oil in your pot, and making sure it is at at least 375F before adding each new batch. Also, don't undercook; the one batch I specifically undercooked (at only 1 minute per side) was edible, but definitely not as good as the ones fried longer.
These were definitely not as good as I had hoped.  Too mushy and too greasy.

These were really good and easy to make.  My son and his friend thought they were great!

The name of these got me in. I found them to be really very good. I made them one night when I was having a sweet attack.  They went down well in my family. Yummy!!
Absoloutly addictive! I fried in veg oil then switched to salt-free Becel for the second batch both were delicious.

This was very yummy!  I had a bunch of fresh vegetables left over from Saturday lunch and used them up to make this for Saturday night supper. Yummy! I make this every couple of weekend for my husband and me. I just made another batch to freeze so I can have a quick alternative to cereal on weekdays.
This was one of the best french toasts ever! Not the healthiest, but one of the tastiest for sure! My hubby, who is not a french toast fan, even liked this a lot.

This is amazing french toast.  I saw a tutorial by Alton Brown, host of "Good Eats". for french toast and implementing some of his techniques.  He suggestions to make the custard at least 8 hours ahead and refrigerate.  Make sure to dry out the bread ahead of time.  When ready to eat, pour the custard into a shallow dish.  Let bread sit in the custard for 30 seconds (no more, no less) on each side then let rest for two minutes on cooling rack over a cookie sheet. Swirl butter in non-stick pan instead of using oil.  Once brown place the french toast on a cooling rack (this allows the french toast to stay crisp). Bake in a 375 degree oven for 5 minutes. Before serving, while still warm,  I sprinkled the cinnamon sugar on the french toast and served with maple syrup.  My mouth is salivating just thinking of them.

I made this recipe this morning and I have to say it deserves much more then 5 stars. Its definitely hands down the best french toast I have ever ate. It will be a regular breakfast in my home and a staple in my freezer! :)

After years of trying many variations on the milk/egg recipe, this a refreshing change! Made for my family, who visited last christmas. This was great. Reminded me of a funnel cake but better. I used Texas Toast and turned out just great. Thank you for sharing

This is the best recipe for French toast. I made it for the first time today and boy was it a hit! I cut the Texas toast into strips before coating them, then fried them up. It was great for dipping... my kids loved them! Will recommend to everyone I know. So good!!!
This was a hit with the kiddos! Definitely a sweet treat and could easily be modified as a dessert.

We will be making this more often. Thanks for the quick, easy and tasty dessert.

Yum, great recipe, and soooo easy.  Having just started on the WW program - this was a nice ending to my meal, it solved that craving for something sweet without going off my points.  So good too, DH isn't on a diet and he loved it too.  This is something I'll be keeping in my fridge for those days when I'm running out of points but hungry.  Thanks for posting.

Good pudding-like dessert, fluffy is right! Used 1/2 tsp cinnamon + 1/4 tsp ginger + 1/8 tsp allspice + 1/8 tsp nutmeg in place of pumpkin spice (per 'zaar suggestion when clicking on pumpkin spice mix).  My kids love this, and it's definitely a point friendly sweet way to end the evening. I'm not a fan of the aftertaste, and I think it has to do with the jell-o mix.

Love this stuff! So good and so easy... and it tastes just like pumpkin pie. Thanks for posting.  Update: BTW... a full 8-oz container of ff cool whip makes this an even 2 points per serving (according to ww recipe builder) and makes for a much fluffier, smoother texture.  I highly recommend going that route for only a 0.5 point difference.  My whole family loves this.  Thanks again!
Woah, the cinnamon in this was overpowering. Next time I'll leave it out. I agree with Holly, more cool whip makes it better.

I love pumpkin so I really liked this.  Like the others I used the full Cool Whip 8 oz.  I'm wondering if the recipe owner used prepared vanilla pudding and maybe that's why the rest of us used more Cool Whip?  Prepared would be very different.  This is a great recipe for things you can keep on hand for a last minute idea.  Thanks
SO good.  SO easy.  What's not to love?

This was excellent! Pasta with clam sauce is a treat I seldom get to enjoy, as my family doesn't much like clams. I divvied the recipe by 3 and had a generous solo dinner with this -- something I will definitely repeat next time I'm dining by my lonesome. This was very easy to prepare, used ingredients I had on hand, and was ready in minutes. The only alteration I made was to omit the onion (my onion looked way past its prime so I left it out); I also used fresh basil and parsley, rather than dried, since I have fresh herbs growing right now. Thanks for the recipe; it's a keeper!

I made this for a special romantic dinner for me and my husband. Very delicious and surprisingly easy to make. The pepper flakes were an added twist. We both thought we were dining in a classy restaurant. Thanks Maine-iac.

Delicious!!  I used two pinches of crushed red pepper, but it was a little spicier than necessary.  Next time, I will stick to one pinch.  My husband absolutely loved this and said it satisfied his seafood craving (we used to live in VA).

I'm sorry but we did not find this recipe enjoyable at all.  I did not use "old bay seasoning" not sure what that is but I don't think the absence of that would have made it any better.  I felt it needed a taste of white wine and maybe some cream in the sauce.

Delicious!  Family absolutely loved this--even one who has an Italian grandmother who makes her own version of this.  I left out the red pepper flakes, but they could be sprinkled on while eating.  The Old Bay gave it enough kick according to DH.  Unfortunately, I don't eat clams, so this rating is from my family.  It's a keeper, and I'll definitely make again for them!  Thanks for posting.

This is perfect.  I loved it so much except I can only have a scant bite because I'm allergic to clams as I recently found out.  I think the Old Bay Seasoning really adds something to this.  So good!  I'm still pouting Clint got to eat enormous bowl fulls and I got just a taste.

I've looked so long for a good recipe for linguine and white clam sauce, i just about gave up.  This is restaurant quality.  I used juice of 1 fresh lemon, fresh basil,2 cans of clams and 1/2 lb of linguine as there were 2 of us. Wonderful blend of flavors.  Thanks Maine-iac.
This was great!  I made it one night when the kids were out and my husband and I ate all of it ourselves!  A keeper!
Quick, easy and 5 stars!  DH loved it.  Thanks for the great recipe!  I used 1/2 cup fresh parsley and a few leaves of fresh basil~very fresh taste.
This was soooo good! My fiance and I enjoyed the rich taste, and it was so wasy to prepare. I think I may use less Bay Seasoning next time because I found it a little salty.  Yum, though!

Awesome recipe!!  Have been looking for a long time for a real good linguine and clam recipe, and this is it!!
Thanks, Maine-iae.
Yummay!  I didn't have the oregano and parsley and only had two can of clams.  It was still delicious.

DH loves white clam sauce with linguine, so I searched and decided to try this one.  I made it exactly as it said, but I doubled the sauce because the family loves alot of sauce. It was so darn spicy I couldn't eat it!  Kids ate it, but said never again.  DH said it was 'sorta OK'.  Never daunted, I tried it again and still doubled the sauce.  Only this time I added ONLY 1 tsp of Old Bay, and a pinch of pepper flakes!  LOVED it!  Just spicy enough for us.  DH loved it, said it was the perfect dinner.  Linguine and a salad was enough for him!  Kids sucked it all up...no leftovers!  Having never used Old Bay before, I was not aware it was soooo spicy.  Now I have learned.

As is, it was too spicy for my family.  Cut back on the Old Bay, and this turns into a GREAT recipe!

Cathy

This was delicious!  Everyone loved it.  I used chopped clams, 1 tsp. of Old Bay (as per cathyat)and added a splash of white wine.  I'll make this again for sure. Thank you so much for this great recipe! Next time I may try the full amount of Old Bay and will probably make even more sauce!

Wow! I grew up around the Chesapeake Bay and never even thought of adding Old Bay seasoning, and it really does make a delicious difference in this recipe. The measurements were in perfect proportion and the taste was just incredible. We sopped up  the leftover sauce in garlic bread and it was heaven! Thank you!
I've made this twice now and its definitely a keeper. The people I work with now think I'm a culinary genius. Thanks Maine-iac and a big thanks to all the Zaarites for all the help!
so very good. careful w/ the peppers, i almost got it too hot. could not find a better more flavorful sauce even in the best eateries.
Although I decreased the amount of  both the Old Bay seasoning and the red pepper, this was too spicy for my feeble tastes.  The recipe is easy to prepare and is worth trying again.

I hadn't made clam sauce in a very long time and this was as close to my original recipe that I found.  It was outstanding. It uses an extra can of clams, which is a great idea.  A quick dinner that is pretty special too!

I could eat this every day! It was really great and reminded me of my Italian nonna's recipe.   I even used  jumbo can of clams from Smart and FInal to make a bunch and it was awesome.  Thanks for the memories!
Easy to follow instructions.  The taste was good, very clammy.  I would do this again.

This was really good.  The only changes I made were to substitute the parmesan cheese with 1 tbsp of nutritional yeast and use whole wheat spaghetti noodles.  It made enough for 2 generous dinner portions, and a small portion for lunch.  I've never had clams and pasta before, and thought it would be really salty, but it was surprisingly sweet (maybe the sweet onion I used?) and delicious.  I will definitely make this again. Thank you.

I would give this 10 stars if I could- it's THAT good!! I made this last night for DH, myself and two of my sons and followed the recipe except for adding 1/3 cup white wine and decreasing the Old Bay to 1 teaspoon. Although I used a good pinch of the red pepper flakes, we couldn't detect much heat in this at all, so next time (and there will be a next time for sure!) I'll add 2 teaspoons of the Old Bay and see how that is. Thanks so much for posting this, Maine-iac. It's restaurant quality and will be enjoyed often here!

This is a great recipe.....what flavor!  I did the recipe just as it is written, with the addition of 1/2 cup of white wine.  What a nice find to add to my cookbook.  I will definitely be making this again.  Many Thanks for posting!

I've been using another Zaar recipe for linguine with white clam sauce for a couple years now.  This one has more flavor and has 3 Tbs of butter vs a whole stick!  Lower in fat and calories, just as quick and easy to throw to gether AND TASTES BETTER!  Add a side salad and this feeds 3-4 people elegantly and inexpensively.  Great recipe, I've thrown the old one out!

Had this Friday and it was the best clam sauce I've tried so far.
I was leery about the Old Bay Seasoning being of Italian descent.  I never would have thought to use it. But it turned out delicious. Served with a salad and garlic bread.

Great recipe!  We like things a bit spicy and used a half Tbsp of red pepper flakes.  Also drained one of the cans of clams and replaced the liquid in that can with white wine.  This could easily feed 6 people when served with salad and bread.  Next time I will cut the recipe in half when cooking for only a few people.  Thanks for the great quick meal!

My husband and I loved this recipe....this is one of our favorite dishes to order in Italian restaurants.  Like Aunt Maimes, I'd been using another Zaar recipe but I prefer this one due to the lower fat content.  My husband said this was spicier (not good, to him) but that was my own fault as I was very heavy-handed with the crushed red pepper flakes...I love spicy!!  I used fresh basil and parsley from my garden but dried mediterranean oregano.  Also, I used a large 14-oz. can of sea clams that I bought off a bargain table at my grocery store, along with one of the smaller canned minced clams.  The sea clams were awesome!  They're about the size of a silver dollar and they were tender and tasty, I hope I can find them again.  I served this over some imported tomato/basil linguine and dinner was excellent tonight.  Crusty bread is is needed to sop up the delicious juices.  We'll definitely be making this again but I just may be not so heavy-handed with the crushed red pepper, darn it.  Thanks Maine-iac, this is a definite keep in my house!

I always made linguine with red clam sauce for my DD, so I thought I would give this a whirl.  Husband and I ate for supper and really enjoyed.  Followed recipe except for no red pepper flakes and used vermicelli.  It has a small bite to it but not bad with the tablespoon of Old Bay.  Will make again.
Perfect! I was so happy with this flavor. We added a splash of white wine and used angel hair pasta. Thank you Maine-iac, for a lovely recipe.

Not bad but not what I expected.  I didn't know that the Old Bay seasoning had celery salt in it until after I tasted it.  Since I don't like celery, I found it a bit overwhelming.   If I make it again, I'll probably either use less Old Bay or take it out altogether.
We loved this! I'm just cranky because it's far better than my own Clam Linguine recipe. Thank you for posting!
This is the best Clam Linguine I've ever had...the addition of the Old Bay really makes it special.  Thanks for a great recipe!  This will go into our regular rotation immediately.  :-)
This is a very very very good clam sauce recipe and it's really easy to make! Not for people who can't handle mild spicyness
Quick and easy...I added 1/4 cup white wine to this.  My boys really thought this was wonderful and I liked that it only took 20 minutes.

My BF and I loved this. It was light and flavorful! I made it as is  with the exception of using capellini noodles. I could also only find big cans of clams but I enjoy lots of clams anyway. I read the other reviews and I disagree that this was overly spicy. I will admit that I use a lot of spices in my cooking, so I may be desensitized. Thanks for such a wonderfully easy and cheap but amazing meal! I will definitely be making this again!!
Love this recipe!!  It's so easy, and convenient, everything is from your pantry.  Nice and spicy!

My whole family really loved this recipe!  It was easy and very flavorfull.  The only change I made is that I used fresh clams in their shells (they were on sale at my seafood market) rather than the canned clams and a small bottle of clam juice for the sauce.  I steamed the clams in the sauce to get them to open up and release more of thier flavor.  Other than those changes I followed the recipe exactly.  I used about six lbs of clams but in my family there are never enough clams to go around.  All of the linquine went too!
WOW! my entire family loved this. i will definitely make this again - soon!
I really liked this recipe! I made it exactly as the recipe said and I didn't think there was too much Old Bay Seasoning. My family all gave it a thumbs up! Thank you for the recipe Maine-iac!

Fast and easy. Did not have Old Bay Seasoning, so I used a Penzey's blend called Tuscan Sunset. Tasted wonderful. I was happy to find a delicious white calm sauce recipe that did not require me to open a bottle of wine for 1/4 cup of use.

This was the best linguine with white clam sauce recipe I've tried.  I've tried so many different recipes in search of one that was restaurant quality and this was it.  The only addition I made was a little bit of white.  My husband devoured this in seconds.
My husband felt the spices overpowered the clams.  He prefers my less spicy recipe.
Delicious!  We omitted the crushed red pepper, and I added 2-3 t. of flour to the butter/oil before adding the clams & juice to give the sauce a little more body.

I don't know why but I had a sudden craving for Linguine and clam sauce. I decided to try this recipe and it really satisfied my craving. I thought the sauce was a little salty so I added some water and more lemon juice. It worked just fine and hey more sauce. I also added some flour to it because I like thicker sauces. Served with a nice crusty bread so I could soak up the sauce. Yum!
I made this exactly as stated and it turned out great. Thanks!
This was really good...A nice change from the red sauce I usually make.  I did add some white wine to it as everything is better with a little wine!
This was very good and easy to prepare.  Added just a bit more garlic and onion.  Thanks for posting!

Yum!  This was my first time for Linguine and Clam Sauce and I loved it.  Very easy, too.  Like some other reviewers suggested, I drained 2 of the 3 cans of clams and replaced with white wine.  I also reduced the Old Bay a bit.  My husband said it was right on the edge of being too lemon-y for him, but I thought it was perfect.

Yum! I haven't made linguine with clam sauce in such a long time.  This was a great recipe.  Like some of the others, I added some white wine.  And didn't use the red pepper flakes but still delicious.
First time I made clam sauce and I loved it, I added the white wine & parmesan cheese while simmering, not at all difficult to make, will definitely make this again and again. Thank you for sharing.

You don't need my review to say this was the pineapple at the top of the pineapple hill. Just incredible, and I think the cows even wanted some, the aroma coming through the valley below must of called every neighbor along the country road, cause' they all showed up. Easy to boot. I tossed in some fresh corn (cut from the cob - had it sitting on my counter) and this served as a nice little crunch. A great taste as a Sunday supper at the farm and we thank you!

This is now my favorite clam sauce recipe.  I followed the recipe exactly but added a dozen littlenecks on top of the sauce for the last few minutes, just until they open.  Put a cover on the pan as they open quicker with steam.  Being from RI, fresh clams are easy to come by, but using canned clams with a few fresh clams was perfect with the right seasonings.  I would serve it to anyone.

This was a great recipe.  My DH loves white clam sauce so I decided on this one and so glad I did.  He wouldn't stop eating it.  The next day I took what was left (not much) for lunch and it was delicious even then.  The only thing I did differently was add another can of clams, used fresh parsley, added about a tablespoon of 1/2 & 1/2 and sprinkled a little flour to thicken sauce.  Yummmmmy.  Thanks for posting, I'm already getting request to make for Valentine's Day!!!! But I'm not cookin!! He is.

Great recipe. I hate it when people rate my recipes but have changed around 10 ingredients. I admit I did this. I had an excess of shrimp, so I used shrimp instead of clams. Because I did this the sauce needed something extra, so I added 1/2 cup of cream. This was really wonderful. Thanks for the recipe, sorry I changed it.

This is a wonderful recipe.  I made this last night along with a green salad and garlic bread.  My family and I loved it.  I made 1 1/2 times the recipe and we ate the whole thing!!!  I love the slight heat in the background, also the old bay gives it great flavor.  I plan on making this again and again, as its so quick to make it will be great on those "gotta hurry and eat" nights.  Thank you so much for sharing this with us, we loved it.
My entire family loved this! I used the Old Bay seasoning with garlic and herbs. My kids want me to make this already next week.

This was quite good and we enjoyed this comfort food! My husband has been a little bit ill, and he requested pasta with clams. And although I usually eyeball it, I looked and saw this recipe. I left out the oregano and basil, because I thought it should be more bland for him at this time, and it was wonderful! I loaded it up with garlic, left out the Old Bay as we don't like it, and used Johnny's Dock instead, some lemon pepper in the grate bottle, then served mixed with the parmesan, (plenty of it, probably 8 ounces), more fresh lemon juice...and HEAVEN! This is a pot of happiness! YUM!

This was good but a bit too spicy for me.  I didn't know that Old Bay Seasoning already had red pepper in it or I wouldn't have added more.  To kick it down a notch I had to add a bunch of parmesan which masked the flavors of everything else.  I'm giving it 4 stars cause I think it could be delicious just without the extra red pepper.

My husband and I enjoyed this recipe. I prepared it exactly as written and I would not change a thing!  The spice from the old bay and red peppers gave this dish a delightful kick.  I served it with a tossed salad.

Tasty and Easy! 4 stars because ds and i liked it and finished ours but dh didn't care for it much and left half. I halved the recipe and used 8 oz pasta and 1 10oz can of clams. I reduced the liquid by half and added some heavy cream because dh and ds love creamy pasta. I thought it was a good addition, and the lemon and old bay were wonderful. I will make this again when dh is working late for ds and I :)

I've made this dish 3-4 times now and we really enjoy it.  I gave it four stars because I wish the sauce was just a tad bit thicker so it would stay on the pasta more.  I added some alfredo sauce to the dish and that made it creamer & thicker.  Thanks so much for posting =0)
I have been making this recipe for a couple years now.  My husband and I love it.  Thank you for introducing me to Old Bay and thank you for the recipe!!

i made this tonight and it was awsome the best i have ever had in 70 years i made the white clam sauce 8 hrs ahead so the spices could meld
wayland 3/8/11
OMG!  I was a little skeptical about the Old Bay Seasoning but this recipe ROCKS!   I didn't change anything except that I doubled it. Kids and BF agree... this is a keeper!  Thanks!
This recipe turned out so well! I think the Old Bay really made the difference; I also liked how spicy it was. This is the linguine with clam sauce I will be making from now on. Thanks for sharing!

This was great.  the flavor is really mild but tasty.  It was super easy, which is always great for me!  I used half chopped clams and half fancy baby clams.  I went for the baby clams because I thought it would be better.  Next time I'll stick with the chopped clams.  The chopped clams are chewier which the think the dish needs.  Overall, just a plain great dish!  Thanks Maine-iac....
Just wanted to add my 5 stars to the rating.
This was so delicious, my husband and I both enjoyed it and I can't wait for the leftovers tomorrow!! Made it exactly as written and was not disappointed!!

Doubled the recipe, DH and in laws loved it!  Finally a linguini and clam sauce that actually has clams!  I did thicken the sauce a little with corn starch and some clam juice~~per another review.  Lovely meal with crusty bread.

Can't believe how easy this was.  I remembered I had a can of clam sauce that I bought for the first time and hadn't used yet, so when I saw this recipe I was thrilled.  I didn't see that you needed 3 cans so I just made a smaller portion and it was delish! So simple.  I used dry seasoning but fresh parsley.  I like that it had a little heat to it with the pepper flakes.  Will make again.
LIke going to heaven!  Made exact with a little white wine! made twice this week!

For the first time in 20 years, I made Linguine with White Clam Sauce that we loved!! I made it as it was with very minor changes. I added fresh clams too, about a dozen, and I drained the clam juice - replaced it with white wine. Great recipe, we loved it!!!
Thank you so much for this recipe, it is now a staple recipe at our household!
Delish!  And very quick and easy to make!  My husband called it "restaurant quality."

although this is nothing like what my family considers "traditional" clam sauce, it was so delicious that we are sticking with this recipe.  i use frozen minced clams, and fresh herbs.  it is so good!

I made by following the ingredients and instructions exactly. It was fantastic!! Used for company ans everyone loved it. I am now going to cut the recipe down for the 2 of us. Thank you so much for sharing this great recipe.
Fabulous.
Love this recipe!  I make it exactly as written and it turns out perfect every time.  Just like a restaurant.

My goto recipe for when I have friends coming on short notice.  I let it simmer a bit longer so it become thicker and really grabs the pasta.  This is a phenomenal recipe with or without the extra time.
I have tried a lot of clam sauce recipes - this is now #1
Wanted something quick, easy and healthy.  Substituted regular butter with Earthy Balance, used fresh basil and substituted vegan parmesan. Also used fresh linguine pasta.  It was delicious!
Just great and easy recipe which will now be a staple in my household.
Excellent! Just as it is.  No adjustments necessary. Easy and delicious. Try it!

My wife is usually the linguini and clams cook, but for her birthday I thought I'd give it a go. So found this recipe on my Kindle and went to work. It was amazingly simple, and with a little added ingredients like a few more pinches of red chilli flakes and a little extra fresh parsley and coarse black pepper... WOW! We paired with a hardy Tobin James 'Fat Boy' Zin, a nice garden salad and candlelight, and felt as though we were in a five-star restaurant.
best I ever had

this recipe is delicious but no Italian would ever put cheese on a seafood dish.  I remember watching an argument in a wonderful Italian restaurant in Brooklyn between a waiter and a customer who wanted some cheese for her clams.  Seafood and cheese is a huge no-no
The sauce came out perfectly, I made this sauce for my mom's anniversary and it was just perfect!!! I loved it and so did they!
Sounds great but I need the size of the cans of clams or ounces. We plan to make this tonight and we have 2 huge cans of clams. Thanks

Linguine and clams sauce is a great meal but your recipe is off. And why you call it "old fashioned" is a mystery. There aren't any noveau pasta and clams recipes that have trended beyond the standard ingredients. And speaking of ingredients, you may be one of those Old Bay addicts, but here, it has to stay in the cupboard. The spices in Old Bay have no place in this recipe. Ground celery seed? Ginger and dry mustard? Are you joking? And save the butter for tossing into the cooked pasta. Adding it in the beginning with the EVOO is not traditional.

Honestly, giving no stars to the recipe simply because 'no Italian would EVER put cheese on a seafood dish' is not only ridiculous but a bit pompous. We aren't all Italian.

My picky eating teenagers LOVE this recipe. I bought a bottle of clam juice for added moisture but that is about all I changed. Thank you!
By far my favorite recipe. I double the recipe, use angel hair pasta, add extra red pepper flakes, old bay and an extra can of clams. Perfect, fast, easy and everyone loves it!

First of all I'd like to say, "WOW!". Last night was the first dinner I'd cooked for my boyfriend and it was a hit! I definitely think he will trust my cooking from here on out! I omitted some of the clam juice and used white wine instead (I needed an excuse to drink wine while I cooked!) and I used fresh parsley and fresh basil. I cannot believe how much flavor the Old Bay added to this sauce. One reviewer said they added cornstarch to their sauce to thicken it, but I don't think the sauce needs to be thickened (purely a personal choice). I left the Parmesan in a dish so people could use it if they chose to, but I found no need for it. I served this with a sourdough baguette covered in garlic and parsley butter and a Caesar salad. Will definitely be making this again and again!

A very nice version! I like a heavier clam flavor and added a full bottle of clam juice, reduced to a sauce consistency. But you should have some good crusty bread to go with, not to waste any of the remaining flavors. Very nice recipe, Thank you.
This is easy, quick, and delicious! I used fresh steamed clams & pot liquor, as that's what I had. Added a bit of corn starch to thicken the sauce just a little. Lovely recipe! A real keeper.
Excellent!! Delicious, easy, and fast. What more could you ask for? Thanks for a great recipe. Al

I made it tonight for my family and everyone loved it. My husband, 18 year old son, 8 year old son (who is allergic to dairy (used olive oil no butter) and my 6 year old daughter. I would definitely make it again.

This was SO salty and I'm not usually sensitive to salt. I followed the recipe exactly and I think it's the 1 Tablespoon of Old Bay that ruined it. I would suggest adding it a teaspoon at a time and tasting after each addition. For me, I ended up having to make so many additions to try and correct the salt issue that it become an entirely new recipe (which, still, wasn't super great).

I have now made this recipe 8 times. My boyfriend is a lover and connoisseur of linguine with white clam sauce. This is by far his favorite. Last time I gave him almost three helpings just to see how much of a glutton he was and he finished every single bite!

This is by FAR the BEST (and easiest) white clam sauce recipe I've ever made. It came out so good even my picky 4 yr old, 7 yr old and clam-hating husband ate this up. My hubby even said he enjoyed it and to feel free to put it on our regular rotation. Big win!!!

Seafood and cheese may not be traditional in some Italian households however that doesn't mean it isn't delicious. I added some white wine, roasted red pepper, capers and chopped kalamata olives to the sauteed veggies and let it reduce by half before adding the clams and juice. Enough liquid to skip adding some to the al dente pasta for the last cook off. If this interests you and you're salt sensitive cut the Old Bay in half.

This made for a wonderful birthday meal for my wife. Even the kids devoured it. The garlic and splash of red pepper flakes made for a nice bite of heat. I know that it breaks with the tradition of the dish but the addition of some fresh mushrooms would add another wonderful layer to this dish. We tried out a 2015 Happy Camper Chardonnay (California) with the dish which went great. The citrus notes contrasted well with the buttery sauce. It also enhanced the lemon as well. This is definitely a keeper and is already in the recipe box.

Wow, fantastic dinner! I only used a teaspoon of old bay seasoning. Definitely only use a pinch or two of crushed red pepper. I made the mistake of adding too much (about 5 heavy shakes), but luckily we like spicy food and the resulting dish tasted slightly cajun. I highly recommend adding zucchini to this dish. Add it in a minute after the garlic. Cut it up like a thin fry beforehand and toss out the seeded inside. Serve the pasta separate so that each person can scoop as much noodles and top it with as much clam sauce as they would like. Enjoy! This is a keeper.
I make this often. I put crab meat & canned shrimp in along w/the clams. Very easy & very delicious!!!
I don't use the Old Bay. A splash of white wine into the butter and herbs is fabulous. Basil and oregano into the butter and oil then hit it with wine and clam juice. Enjoy.
Great flavor. I did use more garlic. Garnished with green onion tops sliced thin.

Great recipe! I tripled the parsley and red pepper, and left out the Old Bay. I used a citrus & pepper spice mix instead. I also added some white grape juice (instead of wine ) & simmered all a few more minutes. For pasta, I used fusili instead of linguni thinking it would hold more of the sauce and it was just right. Really enjoyed this recipe.
This is super yummy--my family loved it! And it was fairly easy too. I had a package of frozen shelled clams and added most of a bottle of clam juice. We will definitely be making this again.
Made this tonight and I must say it was absolutely delicious. I added clam juice but other than that I followed the recipe..My 4 yr old son is quite picky but he loved this.

My photo does this recipe justice , this easy recipe was so good I had to use my finger afterwards to scoop up sauce so that sauce wasn't wasted since I didn't have any crusty bread. The only thing I didn't follow was I left out in the parsley (didn't have it available) Go ahead and try it you'll love it!

This has become one of our FAVORITE recipes over the past couple of years and the last time I made it I thought I should take time to review it. My husband actually found it while I was laid up with a broken shoulder and he was doing all the cooking. He loves Linquine & Clam Sauce AND he LOVES Old Bay (we're from Maryland) and he wanted something quick & easy to make and this recipe fit the bill. I stock up on the clams at Costco!! It is sooo easy to make and topped off with fresh parsley and parmesan it's just perfect!! It's DELISH and a family favorite now!!

I am going to try this recipe because this one is the only recipe I have found that looks like it has enough flavor. I will leave out the red peppers because I can't stand spicy food. I will give a review after I try it. I love Old Bay Seasoning! I put it in everything that has seafood and I also put it in my V8 juice because it is a very tasty and versatile spice.
Love love love this recipe. It has become a standard at our house. I double the sauce for extras. Thank you
Loved it. Made it twice and my son and his partner can't get enough. I make the whole quantity of the recipe and they finish it all up. So simple!!
Easy dish with Wonderful flavor. I Made this dish for the first time last night. This recipe is a keeper! Thank you

I've made this a lot, my daughter gave it to me, usually use 6.5 oz Bumble Bee chopped clams, drain juice off and save. Depending on how many your feeding I use 3-6 cans. Also add chicken stock simmer to blend flavors.
I tried this recipe and loved it. I now make it for a fantastic Pasta Salad. Just add Mayo.

I usually make a red clam sauce but my husband is on a low potassium diet so tomatoes are out! I finally decided to try this (after 6 months) because we were hungry for a pasta. He doesn’t like Alfredo sauce! Next time I will add more garlic and forget the red pepper. This is a keeper. I will make this again.
Pertext rainy day Sunday meal.

This recipe was easy and delicious. I omitted onions because I have always made this dish with garlic only.. Also omitted Old Bay since I'm not a fan of Old Bay in recipes with the exception of cooking shrimp in it for shrimp cocktail. Made this dish with homemade pasta using our new Philipps pasta machine. One can of clams has 350 mg of sodium. Not taking into consideration the sodium in other ingredients, like the butter and the pasta. I think the flavors will be great, but will have to try to "downsize" the salt!

I made this recipe by mistake. I had saved several recipes for pasta with clam sauce in my Evernotes recipe file. The first one I tried was perfect, which I have made several times to rave reviews. I should have deleted the others because I brought this one up by mistake and made it tonight. I followed it fairly closely except used only two cans of chopped clams with their juice and 16 fresh clams and some pasta water which I added at the end, covering the pan until the clams opened up. I think the Old Bay overpowers the dish, and we love Old Bay. If you decide to try it, I recommend cutting down on the Old Bay. Next time it's back to my favorite by Giada De Laurentiis. Her recipe has shallots, white wine, and some lemon but no Old Bay, oregano, or basil. I tweak it by adding 2-3 cans of clams with their juice, along with the fresh clams that are called for. For me, fish and seafood dishes can be overpowered by too much seasoning.
Delicious and so quick to create

Usually i like recipes off this site but this one was a fight. I used can-juice from two cans of clams and it was a salt bomb. I know some people like it and perhaps I just have more sensitive taste buds but I just wanted people to know it may require some work trying to cut salt.

Will definitely make this again:) Thank you Bev!
Perfect creamy, cheesy heavenly!

First attempt at homemade macaroni and cheese and it was pretty good! I think the cheese I used wasn't sharp enough for me (I used a medium cheddar) and for some reason my sauce was a little bit grainy in texture. But all in all a very simple recipe with nice results.

Love it Love it Love it!!!!  I knew a guy who made the best mac and cheese but it was all in his head so he couldn't tell me how to do it....but then I found this recipe and it was the best!!! I use extra sharp cheddar and it has never been grainy.  Now I am making it for my 6 1/2 month old son:)

This is very good mac and cheese!  My kids love it!  Sometimes I even make this without baking it; resulting in a very creamy macaroni and cheese dinner.  I also use this cheese sauce/roux and pour some over broccoli.  Very yummy!  I usually use mild cheddar or co-jack cheese with great results.  Thank you for this recipe!

Wonderful! Even my daughter, who keeps the company that makes Velveeta in business, really enjoyed this mac & cheese. ;) I loved it as it reminded me of what I had at family gatherings in Kansas when I was very young. Thanks for sharing with us, Bev.

I made this with 1 cup of colby jack and 1 cup of a mozzarella/provolone blend.  I also added a couple of shakes of garlic powder to the cheese sauce.  We ate it as a main dish, so we only got 2 (generous) servings out of it.  I can't wait to try this again with different combinations of cheese.  Thanks for a tasty yet simple recipe!

I have made this twice since first finding it, and both times it was awesome.  My brother in law commented how good it was this last time (after finishing the last few servings).  This is by far the best mac and cheese recipe I have come across.  Thanks for making our taste buds tingle!
Lovely thick and gooey comfort food!
this was not cheesy enough and had too much pepper for our tastes. t was nice and creamy however.
I have to re-post, after 3 years of continually making this, it is by far the best.  Thank you so much, Bev!!!
This is the best mac n cheese ever.  I have made it a dozen times  in the last year and EVERYONE  raves about it.  It is so easy, but so creamy.
I make this mac n' cheese and every time I get asked for the recipe. Thanks so much for such a great staple recipe. It will be in my family for years.
This is so delicious! Love the flavors and how creamy and cheesy it is. Great comfort food!

Bev...this recipe has been in my kitchen for the last 3 months. Ever since I found it I keep making it over and over and I even give it a little kick of my own with some pepperjack cheese and cayenne pepper and it's absolutely delicious! Thanks for the great recipe! For weight watchers just eleiminate the butter (or 1/2 the amount) and it still tastes great! This is so easy to make and very enjoyable for the whole family!!

Wonderful recipe!  I had to double it and it still came out great.  Don't add too much cheese, because I discovered there can be too much.  I think it would be creamier with the amount the recipe calls for.  I purchased a disposable casserole pan so that I didn't have to wash a pan.  It re-heats well in the oven.  I would like to try some jalapenos  for a little kick to try to mimic a recipe from a local restaurant that serves jalapeno mac & cheese.  Definitely good for a whole meal or a side dish.
This mac and cheese recipe is incredible! My 15-year old mac and cheese lover went nuts for this, he has asked that this be the recipe that I make from now on. Very creamy...pure comfort food.
Awesome!
