I literally JUST made this for dinner and had to jump on the computer and review! This recipe is amazing!!! The creamiest homemade mac and cheese I have ever had!
Fantastic!  Followed it as written.  Thanks for sharing.

I made this for a dinner I catered and it was enjoyed by both of the ladies I cooked for. I followed this recipe exactly except that I did also add about 1/4 cup of Velveeta cheese. I've been asked to make this again and I definitely will.  Thanks for posting!
I'll be making this from now on.  Easy and even better with parmesan grated on top.  I should have doubled it.
Wonderful! I made this with mexican shredded cheese, and it doubled well.

Easy and oh so delicious.  This was made gluten free by using gluten free flour and rice pasta.  Everyone really enjoyed it.  There were no leftovers. It is easy to see why the recipe have so many wonderful reviews.

I made this dish long ago, but forgot to review it.  Little Miss (DD) had a friend over for her first sleep over.  The little girl said her favourite food was "Macaroni and Cheese", so I made it for her.  The girls really enjoyed this recipe..  Served it with ** Jubes ** Chicken Cheese Nuggets and it was a hit.  Thanks Bev for a great recipe.

This is my far THE BEST baked mac and cheese recipe on here. I had all the ingredients on hand and ready to go. The sauce was perfect in consistency, not too thick or too runny. I added a full two cups of cheese to the sauce for extra cheesiness and used rotini for a twist (no pun intended!). Other then that I followed it to a T and it turned out PERFECT! My 17 year old son gobbled all the left overs and asked when will be having it again?? =)

We've had this a few times.  A lot of times it doesn't even get out of the dish we bake it in.  As soon as it is out of the oven we start picking at it, especially the golden crunchy topping.  Awesome recipe Bev.  A family favorite.  One that is printed and in our little special recipe box in case our internet connection should fail us when we want this comfort food.  Deserving of 20 stars:)

Just made this for dinner.  I have probably made macaroni & cheese from scratch 3 times in my 61 years.  I made it with 2 cups half & half and 1/2 cup milk because I wanted to use up the half & half.  Otherwise, followed the recipe to a T.  Hubby and I both LOVED it!  Will have the leftovers for dinner tomorrow night!  Thanks for this recipe!

Oh thank you!  Used skim milk, about 10oz. Penne, thought it seemed too soupy but after baking it was just perfect.  Used mix of white vermont cheddar and extra sharp cheddar, thought it came out fantastic and so easy!  I will make it often I am sure.

My family really enjoyed this! It's not gourmet, but it's still very tasty for homemade mac! It has that warm, mild, country-cooked taste. Don't leave out the mustard, it really does add to the flavor. I added a few dashes of garlic powder and paprika. Delicious! I do wonder how it might be a bit more flavorful using different cheeses. Thanks for the great recipe!
I loved the flavor , but it was too sooopy.  I used the recipie exactly as it was written.

Like you need another review! But I want to keep track of the recipe, so here I am. =) I like how versatile this recipe is... made it the other night with 1/2 Vermont Sharp and 1/2 Extra Sharp (yum!) for our DD who had wisdom teeth out (owww). And last night for us... and since we can't take all that fat, I used 0% milk, and 1/2 lowfat sharp and 1/2 part skim mozzarella. Not as decadent, but certainly a wiser choice for the over 40 crowd. Since Easter just passed, we'll be having some with chopped ham for lunch! Thanks, Bev. [Oh - btw, I didn't read 235 reviews, but there is a lot more cheese sauce than fits 8 oz of macaroni... try 12 oz to avoid waste or soup when you choose not to bake it.]

great dinner side and was so easy to make! I secretly thought the cheese would not be enough and the mustard powder would make it taste funny. I was determined to try it as written then tweak it next time I make it... it was PERFECT. There is not one thing I will change when I make this again. This is definitely going into my arsenal of regular dishes...Thanks to Bev!

This was so good!!  I made this tonight along with Bev's meatloaf for a totally awesome meal... I've tried many different mac and cheese recipes with all different kinds of ingredients over the years...and this simple recipe proved to be my favorite.
Very good even with the whole wheat pasta I used. next time I will use a bit extra cheese though. Thanks for sharing!

Amazing!  Made this years ago for Easter, then again last minute for my son's b-day party.  Everyone loved it- I agree with other reviews, use a whisk for the butter/flour.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I make this a couple times a year and cannot believe I've never rated it. The basic recipe is good, but I find it a little bland. I kick up the seasonings, add garlic and a little paprika, and usually use some pepperjack cheese to give it additional flavor. I had a leftover piece of smoked gouda that I threw in once and that was phenomenal. I do usually have more cheese sauce than needed.
We loved this.  Doesn't take a lot of ingredients and turns out perfect.  I like powdered mustard so I added a teaspoon.

We really liked this recipe. The cheese came out creamy, not grainy like other one I have tried. It was even delicious the next day! We had it with chicken drumsticks and it was awesome. We will be saving it for another cold day. My husband usually doesn't like mac and cheese but he ate most of it!
This is where you stop for that yummy mac and cheese you've been dying to have.  I doubled the recipe and had leftovers (2 adults and 2 kids 7 and 8).

This was very easy and delicious! Next time I would for sure add more noodles. Another 8 oz. The sauce was a bit over powering to me. We like more of a balance of noodles to sauce. I also would add bread crumbs to the top. We like a bit of a crunch. I did add a little chill power for more of a kick. This was a great base recipe to start and dress up to your liking! Great job Bev!

This was pretty delicious.  I agree that sharp cheddar should be used.  Next time I will try to add a little garlic powder and/or paprika as one reviewer suggested. Also seemed to taste better the longer it sat out.  I'll try to remember next time to have it ready about an hour before ready to serve as it stayed very warm for a good while.

I'm going to give my honest review so I know I've tried this recipe. I will say what I enjoyed... I like the consistency of this. A nice creamy, rich consistency to the macaroni & cheese. I did use 1/2 milk and 1/2 heavy cream instead of all milk. What didn't I like? It was way too bland. I tasted it after all the ingredients were combined and it really lacked flavor. As-is, my family wouldn't have eaten it. I would try it again because I like the textrure, but to boost the flavor will use sharp cheddar. For my tastes, I add in some dried garlic, nutmeg, maybe a pinch of cayenne for more flavor.
Yum to the num! I used light cheddar amd mixed it all in instead of bakng it on top. We also added two drops of Tabasco for an extra tiny zing. My 13 year old fussy eater loves this recipe!
Way to much milk it was more like macaroni soup

I used this recipe for Christmas dinner two years ago and it was a winner with everyone. Since then I have reccommended it to friends and family and it has always received rave reviews. Thanks for sharing Bev.

This was so easy, we have tried multiple mac and cheese recipes with much more complicated combinations of cheese, loved the simplicity and flavor of this. We did this recipe + 1/2 which perfectly fit a 9x13 pan, fed 5 of us with just a bit leftover. Only modification I did was add a couple TBSP of Franks hot sauce, sprinkled on some garlic salt, then the shredded cheddar topping, then a layer of panko crumbs. Will make again with crumbled bacon and green onions next time. Thanks for this quick and versatile recipe!!

I was in doubt that this would really be creamy but it is! We loved it and I followed the recipe as written except..(there is always and except) that I added some gouda cheese and did not decrease the cheddar amount. Very good and a keeper for sure

The best recipe I've seen for macaroni cheese! Always turns out near enough PERFECT! I tweaked the recipe a little though, by added half a teaspoon of ground nutmeg, a few drops of Maggie liquid for extra flavour into the milk sauce. I also separately stir fried a little spring onion and a clove of garlic, before combining all the ingredients into the dish. (Also if you want it a little meaty, add precooked diced bacon/pancetta) The whole family enjoys this recipe, vegetarian version or not. Yummy ??

These are the best little cookie. Thanks for posting. The recipe is very easy to make, it tastes like chewy rich chocolate brownie, I had a couple with fresh strawberries and blueberries. Nice treat when watching your intake of calories.

These ended up being quite good.  As they first came out of the oven I found them sort of funny tasting.  But after they cooled, they were fudgy little brownie bites!  The kids and dh loved them!  I used splenda instead of sugar.  I don't like to use splenda as the only sweetner (I think it gives it a weird taste), but with the Karo it worked out well.  Yum!

Uber-yummy.  thanks so much for passing the recipe along.  the batter seemed dry at first, but i kept stirring and they came out beautifully.  I used 1/2 cup whole wheat flour and 1 cup white.  delish.

Hallelujah!  55 calorie cookies!!  55 calorie CHOCOLATE cookies!!!  Now, they're not butter-laden, gooey chocolate brownies but they ARE good and satisfyingly chocolaty.  I subbed Splenda and thought it worked just fine.  I, too, thought  they were better after cooling.
For a no fat cookie, very good!  Be careful not to overcook, and I agree with the other, they are better after coling.

These are very good for being fat/cholesterol free. I was looking for a snack for my chocoholic dh and these may just be the ones. They did smell a bit unusual while baking but tasted fine after they cooled. They are very moist after being baked, enough that they stuck together in the box, but that didn't seem to slow down dh and the kids, lol. Sprinkling them with powdered sugar helped with that a bit and made them very festive looking. I think they'd be good with a dash of peppermint extract in them, too, for the holidays. I might try subbing applesauce for a bit of the corn syrup and see how that does next time. Thanks so much!

These are surprisingly good.  I baked two trays of cookies, the first one for about 7 minutes and the 2nd one for 9-10.  The 7 minute cookies were still slightly gooey when I took them out, and they turned out great. The others were starting to taste more bread-like.  But after storing them in a tupperware container overnight they all tasted moist and good.  The only thing I would change would be a touch more sugar (and I'm not a sugar fiend).
Great recipe. The cookies are moist and chocolatey, not too sweet. Very good. I made 3 dozen cookies from the dough. They were a little smaller, but only 31 calories each.

It's a good thing I can type and chew at the same time, or I'd never have reviewed these!  To make mine a bit healthier, I used whole-wheat pastry flour and evaporated cane juice, and they were great.   They were dry, but I put them in a ziploc while still warm, and that made them perfect.  Thank you so much for contributing to the not-so-delinquency of a cookie fiend!!

I used a 1 tsp. scoop, rolled them in sugar and baked them on a baking stone.  I baked them for 9 minutes.  They were done on the outside but still soft on the inside.  They taste wonderful right out of the oven!
Thanks, Kree for giving me an incredible fat free, dairy free cookie!

This recipe was very good but it was a really, really thick dough.  I added 1/4 cup of water to thin it out some and also added 3/4 cup of butterscotch chips.  The cookies came out light and chocolatey with just a hint of butterscotch.  Very, very good.

I went back and forth on whether to rate these a 4 or 5.  They were quite tasty with a dry exterier and a fudgy brownie like interior.  Mine were a bit smaller - about 3 dozen - which made the 3 for 2 points, a deal for WW folks.  My challenge here was the dough was really quite dry and hard to handle.  I eventally gave up on mixing them with a spoon and turned the dough by hand.  It did evenually soften and was even sticky by the time I finished.  Next time I will let them sit a minute or so before trying to mix.  They are not sweet which was fine for me but the family thought they needed more sugar. All that said, they are definite keepers for satisfying that chocolate craving without feeling the slightest bit guilty. Thanks Kree.

These are very tasty!  I made them with whole wheat-whole grain flour and splenda, which brought them down to 1/2 point each.  Hubby said they taste more like a chocolate muffin than a cookie.  I have to agree.

One more comment...
I used a baking stone to make these & they stuck like glue to it.  I ended up smushing almost all of them.  On the last pan, I got smart, broke out some dental floss & "flossed" them off the cookie sheet.  Worked great!  Hope that helps someone...
I've made these twice, the second time was even better than before...I added a small amount of vanilla extract and it was delicious!

Great, easy, cookie!  It's almost like a brownie when you bite into it.  The dough is very sticky and I'd very much recommend lining your baking sheets with parchment paper, so the cookies will peel right off.

I made these cookies this afternoon, they were good.  I added about 2 Tsp. instant espresso powder and 1/4 cup mini chocolate chips to the batter.  Just because I had them leftover.  They are definitely quick and easy, nice chocolate flavor.  I'll probably make these again : )

My whole family loved these cookies! It's hard to balance healthy eating with chocolate lovers passion, but these are like eating fudgy cookies without all the guilt! I tried adding peppermint extract (1 tsp) and it ended up very good, but I think if I try that again I'm going for 1.5 tsp instead. The cookies are delicious without it though!
The dough was SO hard to work with. I couldn't get it to mix well, and I was using my kitchenaid. They did taste pretty good, and got stars for the calorie count. Just really  hard to make!

These are awesome for being fat free! I used 1/4 c. sugar, 1/4 splenda and they tasted great. I'm impressed. This definitely satisfies my chocolate cravings! I added almond extract to half of the batch and that tastes great too. Thank you for this recipe! I put these in a plastic bag and they got a little too moist.  Next time I'd put them in a container with a loose cover.  They got a little dry after a couple days so I heated them up in the microwave.  Tasted great again.

Great taste and super easy. I initially wasn't going to try this recipe because it seemed like the dough might be too much hassle, but it really was no problem. For me the stiffness made it easier to drop the cookies. I used 1c all-purpose and 1/2c whole wheat. Baked them for 8 minutes and they turned out crispy on the outside and nice and fudgy on the inside. These are really just like miniature brownies. Also, I would suggest rolling them into balls or just shaping them a bit as they tend to keep their shape while baking. My first batch turned out sort of lumpy looking.

These were really tasty, especially considering that they were only 55 calories each! I only made a half batch and used whole wheat flour. I think that next time I'll stick to white flour or add a little more cocoa, since the whole wheat flavor seemed to overpower the chocolate taste a little bit. 
I think these would be delicious with some dried cranberries added in, too!
These are great for anyone looking for a way to satisfy a chocolate craving and not having feel guilty about giving in!  Thanks for the great recipe!  :)

these are really really really good!  the dough is hard to work with though i had to end up mixing with my hands which got messy.  i also added chocolate chips and dried apricots (diced) which im sure alter the calorie content but with it already being so low i thought, what the heck.

i made these today and they were absolutely delicious!  i had to add a little bit more karo syrup, just because they were SO thick!  they were in the oven for about 9 - 10 minutes and they came out PERFECTLY!  they are so soft, but fudgy on the inside.  i ate two of them, and don't even mind because they're virtually fat free!  they're so amazing!

Yum, yum YUM!!!! I made these for myself a week ago and swapped the sugar for 1/4 cup of granular Splenda since I don't like the sweetness of regular cookies. Amazing! Chewy, rich and definitely a keeper! I've even added them to my bakery menu!
These were great, especially for the calorie and fat counts. I did at a splash of water just to thin the mix out a bit. My kids even loved them

These are so good! They are not quite sweet enough, though, so I added just a tad of melted chocolate chips to the top and spread like frosting and that took these cookies to a whole new level. :) Great recipe! Oh yes and MAKE SURE you don't over bake-mine were done in about 5 or 6 minutes.

I made these twice now and the first time I made followed the recipe exactly. The batter was pretty hard to work with and I thought the cookies were a little bit dry. The second time I made these I altered the recipe as follows: 1. changed from 3 egg whites to 2 egg whites & 1 whole egg (adds 4.5 g fat to entire batch, still a minimal amount of fat per cookie). 2 Added a tsp of vanilla. 3. added 1/4 cup non-fat milk to make the batter a little more smooth. The result was a cookie that was a little more moist. These definitely satisfied my craving for sweets!

I made these today for snack and used the Jennicat's suggestions, only I split the egg yolk in half, because I detest eggs...haha.  The vanilla was RIGHT ON, for sure.  I used splenda for baking and that was a mistake, because they didn't turn out very sweet at all.  So, I tossed in a few white choc. chips to sweeten the load a bit.  I'll probably make these again tomorrow possibly with brown sugar and dark choc chips.  I suppose the worst that can happen is I'll end up taste testing a bunch of chocolate dough until reaching my goal.  I take on that responsibility for you all, if you really want me to.  :D

Thanks for the recipe!  I'm gonna have fun with this one!  ;)
These were great...I followed the original recipe.  My son took them to school for his birthday treat.  I loved the chocolate!

I made two batches, following the recipe exactly and the other adding more liquid to thin the dough somewhat. While both tasted very good, the dough was exceptionally hard to work with using the original recipe and although the second, thinner batch was easier, the cookie came out very sticky. I will make them again for the taste alone, but perhaps adapt the recipe so that they can be made as brownies rather than cookies.

These were great 5 of the six taste testers of our house loved them.  Only one didn't, but to be honest I think he was trying to be difficult.  I added 1 teaspoon of strong coffee and a 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla.  I will be making these often for sure.  I think next time I will try the whole wheat flour as I have seen some have done, but I want to try the dark cocoa also.

Oh I am SO DISAPPOINTED.  After reading all the rave reviews of these cookies, I had to try them.  I follwed the recipe exactly and WHAT A LET DOWN these are.  All I can think is that the people who gave the rave reviews must have tried some REALLY nasty cookies before they tried these, I won't make these again.. Sorry.

This is an excellent alternative to regular cookies, especially if you're trying to take off a few pounds. I made these instead of brownies tonight & I substituted Splenda; turned out soft,fudgy & good. What more could anyone want from a LOW FAT cookie!?Thanks for a keeper!

These were very good, but not ultra-fabulous.  The dough/batter was a little hard to work with, but that's not really a problem ... and they spread more than I expected, but that wasn't really a problem either.  My only reservation was that they weren't quite as chocolaty as I'd hoped for ... they were a little bland for me.  Texture was very good though.  I'll definitely make 'em again -- the slight loss in flavor is MORE than made up for with the low-fat, low-calorie nature.  Thanks for posting this!
I used 1/3 of the recipe because I wasn't sure how good they would be. Not very sweet, but tasty considering how low in fat they are. I will make again but I'll make a whole batch next time.

Oooh, these are divine little treats that I can make and enjoy in FRONT of my DH...no more hiding out in the closet with my secret goodies! I made them mainly for my DD in college who's trying to keep the freshman *15* from inching up on her. Her dorm friends were grabbing at them as I left. Now to make another batch for home! I did use 1/2 Spelnda/1/2 sugar and added a small handful of mini chocolate chips to the batter. Also, 2 regular sized choc.chips on top of warm cookies made a quick spreadable frosting. Thanks so much Kree!
Nice little light cookie!  Don't burn the bottom of the cookie like I did! If you do, take a knife and scrape the bottom.  I am on a low fat diet but have a big sweet tooth, these fill my craving.
very tasty little cookies!  You can't really even tell that they are fat free!  I made up a half a batch and gave some to a friend who is on WW.  We both enjoyed them a lot.  Thanks for sharing!
Very chewy and yummy.  You wouldn't know they are fat free.

Very good. I halved this, getting 12 cookies. I used 1/4 cup ww flour and 1/2 cup white. Since i couldn't half an egg white, I added 1 1/2 tablespoons skim milk instead. Out of habit, i added some applesauce in where oil would be. But the batter wouldn't come together! So i mixed in more milk, but i think i went a bit crazy and added too much to it was very sticky and the cookies were soggy, but still yummy!
Sorry but these turned out bland, no taste at ALL..

Unfortunately, these didn't turn out that well for me. Stuck with the recipe and in the final result, there are a couple of things:
1. These are REALLY sweet, almost sickenly so. I had dark Karo on hand and wouldn't use it again--imparts that "raisin-y" "0h-yeah-it's-fat-free" flavor store bought fat-free stuff has. Ick.
2. They stick to cookie sheets like crazy. I used spray AND non stick pans and still had difficulty getting them off without destroying half of them even though I let them set, which the recipe doesn't mention. They also stick to each other, making a large chuck of cookies if you stack them for storage. Overall I was really disappointed with them after the buildup. Martha Stewart has a really good fat-free chocolate cookie that you slice and bake--if I can relocate it, I'll post it--Really dense chocolate flavor. Sorry these just didn't do it for me.
Thanks for the recipe, for a low cal/low fat cookie they are very good. I made them gluten free and added 1/2 cup chocolate chips. I will make them again.

I followed the recipe up to the Karo syrup part. I substituted that for an internet-found substitution of mixing 1/4 cup sugar with enough water to make it syrupy. I don't know what went wrong, but I strongly recommend not using that substitution. The cookies didn't turn out bad, but they just weren't that good. Stick to the recipe. It sounds like it has been pretty successful just the way it is.

These cookies are the greatest!  I have been doing Weight Watchers and was looking for good recipe that would be few points and these are it!   One WW point.  I read the reviews and to solve the problem some were having with getting the cookies off the cookie sheet I used parchment paper.  When I took the cookies out of the oven I moved them paper and all to the cooling rack and once cool I removed them with a metal spatula.  They came off great.
I also used Splenda in place of the sugar and they were fine.

These are wonderful! I can't believe they are nearly fat free. The dough does seem very dry and stiff at first but keep at and use your hands if you have to, it works out well in the end. I got exactly 30 cookies and I thought I used more of a tablespoon then teaspoon of dough. Chocolately and almost brownie like - YUM! Thanks for sharing the recipe, I will make these again soon :)

I suppose that for a fat free chocolate, these are quite good, but I found the original cookie to be quite flavorless. I'm not a real fan of plain chocolate cookies, though, so if you are, these are probably right up your alley. I ended up adding 1 c. craisins and 1/2 c. chopped walnuts to make them interesting enough to eat. I also followed JenniCat's advice and changed the eggs to 2 egg whites and 1 full egg.

I love these!!  I don't quite know if mine are fat free seeing as you cant easily get hold of Karo syrup over here in England so I used Golden syrup and they came out amazing!! Crunchy on the outside and chewy in the middle.   I've been searching for a low fat cookie recipe for ages  To get past the sticking issue i used a baking sheet and they slid right off.  Thanks so much!!
Very good.  Surprisingly fudgy and tasty for non-fat cookies.

These are very good! I don't understand how anyone could have a problem with these. If you sift the flour into your measuring cup then you're not going to have a problem with the dough being too stiff or hard to work with. I had no problems with this recipe whatsoever. I used Ener-G egg replacer for the egg whites and used brown rice syrup instead of the Karo for my fellow vegans and it worked wonderfully. They're nice and soft all around. I halved the recipe and they baked in only 7 minutes. I had no issues with them sticking to the pan either. I will be making these again. Thank you for sharing.

For being fat free and not having any butter in the recipe, these turned out surprisingly good. However, I do think the cookies taste a little bland and I could taste the flour in the cookies. But they were chewy and soft and can probably still satisfy one's sweet tooth!
These cookies are very good! No problem getting them off the cookie sheet, and just the right amount of chocolate to satisfy the craving! Will definitely make them again!

I have made these twice and I think they are so good!  Just DON'T over bake! They won't really look done but they are.  Also both times mine held their shape, didn't spread out at all, so I flattened a little bit before baking.  Even my teenage boys like them!

I have made these twice now, and had great results both times.  The first time I followed the recipe exactly.  The second time I used half splenda/sugar, and I used about a T or more (eyeballed it) of honey when measuring out the 1/2 cup of syrup.  So together the two made the proper amount.  Both times I simply sprayed a nonstick cookie sheet well with cooking spray and had no issues at all with sticking.  The dough is a little hard to work with as some have mentioned, but it's definitely not impossible.  The resulting cookie is reminiscent of those snack wells cookies in my opinion with a nice firm outside and fudgy middle, and though they are not particularly strong in flavor they are a very nice little treat for so little calories/fat.  I used light karo in mine, but would like to try them with dark sometime too.  I also meant to add vanilla both times, but forgot, so maybe that would be a nice addition as well.  Or perhaps even some flavored syrups like used for coffee drinks.  In my oven 7 minutes is just right and you definitely don't want to overcook these.
Sorry, but these e low fat.  They are very sticky after baked.  Okay, but wouldn't recommend or make them again.

Wow!  REALLY good for a fat-free chocolate cookie!  We were really surprised and pleased with both the appearance and texture, to say nothing of the good chocolatey flavor.  Even though there's no oil, the cookies have a little crispiness on the outside, and a moist "brownie" texture on the inside.  Great combination - and good even without frosting!  Just made our second batch - baked them for the full nine minutes this time.  Delicious!  Baked them on parchment paper instead of using a non-stick spray and they came off quite easily.  This recipe is a keeper!

Really good and easy. Obviously they have that low-fat taste-as though they are missing something. but they are just as good anyhow. Nice and chewy. If you prefer your cookies crunchy, leave them in a container with the lid open for a day and they crispen up nicely. when they are like this, they are nice dipped into coffee or milk and they just melt in your mouth :D double thumbs up

Good cookies.  I shaped the cookie dough into balls the size of small walnuts and then rolled them in sugar.  I then baked them on parchment paper for 7-9 minutes--no longer!  They easily came off the parchment paper.  I did add some chopped walnuts for interest-walnuts are healthy for you-even on a low fat diet.

I still can't get a handle on this one. It's too sticky to form into cookies so instead I make brownies. But placing it into the form kills me as it sticks to the spoon and brownies do not come out perfectly square. However, tastes delicious.

To solve the sticky issue I chilled the dough for 3 hours. (This increases baking time to at least 10 minutes or more) Then dropped the cookie dough using a mini ice cream scoop into a bowl of granulated sugar. I has mixed my sugar with a teaspoon of coco powder but the cookies look a little dusty. Next time I'm using plain sugar. Use a teaspoon to sprinkle sugar all over the ball of dough. then they handle easily. I greased the pan with cooking spray and had no problem removing the cookie. The sugar makes a nice crust on the cookie. They still had a fudgy middle. I got this procedure from a recipe for soft fat free ginger snaps.

We loved the creamy texture of this dish.  I didn't know that homemade mac & cheese was so easy.  I added ham & broccoli to make it a main dish casserole and my husband, who doesn't care for mac & cheese said that it was a keeper.  Thanks for the suggestion, Lennie.

I have made a zillion and one different versions of macaroni and cheese, but never with cream cheese in it.  This one was so luscious, we're going to be having it more often.  It's a cross between mac and cheese and elbows alfredo.  Thanks Lennie!
Delicious!  Creamy, tasty and oh so good!!  Thanks, this one is a keeper!!

I made this last night for dinner and I love the creamy texture and the melted cheddar cheese.  I will be making this again for sure.  My daughter said it was way better than the one I normally make.  Thanks, Lennie.

This was very yummy! Went great with BBQ
ribs in the crockpot and Caesar salad.
Thanks for the recipe!

I have wanted to make this recipe for months and I knew that has it was baking in the oven I was in for a major "good thing."  It was so good that I have been sneaking nibbles of cold mac and cheese.  Lennie, this is a very addictive and wonderful recipe. I just wish I had made it sooner!
Wow! A great recipe.  I made this for July 4th and the family went nuts.  I doubled the recipe and didn't have any problems. Thanks for another addition to our family gatherings.

I love mac and cheese, and have collected many recipes.  This review was inspired by a recent thread in "everything else" that I started.  Lennie reccomended this one, which I already had in my cookbook.  This one truly deserves a place in the "mac and cheese hall of fame"!  So creamy and rich!  I didn't have fresh parsley, but substituted a few sprinkles of dried.  It doesn't get any better than this!  Thanks Lennie!

This was soooooo good and creamy.  We all loved it, there was so much cheese everyone was too full to finish.  I made an error reading the recipe however and added 1 TBSP of dry mustard instead of dijon.  I tasted it after mixing but prior to baking and it had a bite and I was afraid it wouldnt turn out okay to eat but to my suprise it seemed to almost totally go away after cooking, noone even noticed and kids pick things like that out.  Thanks Lennie!
My mom always made hers like this, but she also added a SMALL jar of pimientos.  To die for!!!

Yum Yum - I used the reduced calorie cream cheese and left the butter out of the bread crumb topping (I have this compulsion to reduce calories when I can) but it didn't matter - this is the most delicious mac n cheese ever!

Lennie, this was GREAT!  I've never made homemade mac and cheese before because I feared it would be runny and taste kind of bland, but this was delicious!  My picky family even approved!  I'll be making this side dish again!  Thanks!!!

This Is extra creamy. Not at all dry.
I used shredded cheese, right out of the package to cut down on prep time. Great for potluck.
This was REALLY yummy! For some reason, though I followed the instructions precisely - mine was a bit drier than we care for - so I'll just add more milk next time! SO yummy! Thanks for sharing!
OMG, this is wonderful! so creamy and wonderful flavor. It was really easy to make too, and had everything on hand! Great Kid pleaser!!! Definatly make again!

Yummy!! First time making mac & cheese, and this recipe made it so easy and good!  I did leave the bread crumbs out, and I added more mustard to it.  Interesting...putting cream cheese in...try the recipe.  It yummy.  Comes out nice and golden brown from the oven

Absolutely fabulous recipe!  Thank you for posting.  We made this for Thanksgiving and it was divine.  None left.  Now I'm using up my left over ham that I chopped into bite size pieces and froze.  Naturally I plan to make this recipe with ham chunks in it for dinner.  :-)  Thanks again.

WOW!!! What great macaroni and cheese! I would give this 10 stars if I could. Very creamy and cheesy...PERFECT! I never would have thought to add mustard and cream cheese before. The addition of the cream cheese and Dijon mustard made it elegant mac and cheese.

I made this today for a pool party for eight people. We were having ribs on the grill.  Mac and cheese sounded like a good match.  Wish I could have enjoyed more of it but it was gone in a flash.  People came back for seconds of this before anything else.  Very creamy, tasty, and unusual.  I have already been asked to make it for the next party.  Thank you!
I think this recipe is just right! I added just a little more salt and halved the recipe.  I will definately make this again. Thanks Lennie!
This recipe was delicious.  I made it exactly as the recipe stated and was not dissappointed.  I sprinkled smoked paprika on top.  We will be making this again!  Thanks!

Wow, this was awesome!  This was my first time making homemade mac & cheese and this was the best tasting homemade recipe I've every eaten.  I followed the recipe exactly; used extra sharp cheddar chese.  I served this with some little smokie sausages.  Melt in your mouth creamy delicious!
Fantastic creamy recipe, I made this last night and the directions were clear and easy to follow.  Thank you so much for sharing!

Help!  There's something wrong with me!  I like cream cheese, and I like mac and cheese, but I didn't like the cream cheese in the mac and cheese.  Obviously I'm in the minority.  Actually, I am the minority.  On the other hand, the texture was fantastic, the topping was yummy, and the instructions were very clear and easy to follow.  Thanks anyway - I love trying new things! :)

Ms Lennie, Thank you for one of the best mac & cheese dishes I have ever had. I premixed this for the crockpot, let it cook for 2 to 2 1/2 hours and it was wonderful! I did precook my pasta but not all the way. I added an extra cup of milk and a can of cream of celery to help it not get too dry while cooking. I didnt use the topping. I will try the cream of cheddar soup mext time I have to make it in a crockpot. Cant have too much cheese can you?? LOL  Thanks again for this amazing recipe!

Ok, I guess I'm a mac and cheese lover because this is like the FOURTH mac and cheese recipe I've reviewed on here (and I've loved all of them)... but I had to try this one because of the cream cheese.  Mmmmmmm!!!!  Five stars all the way!

This was delicious!  I added steamed broccoli and sauted onions, and used seasoned breadcrumbs on top.  It was so rich that neither my fiance nor I could finish our helpings!     I'll definitely repeat this one when it's cold outside and I need some comfort food.

I'm not sure how to rate this because I don't know what it's supposed to taste like. I've never made mac and cheese from scratch so the texture is totally different from what I'm used to.  It is very cheesy and creamy but using the sharp cheddar makes it a little more cheezy than I like...I will try it again though cutting back the cheddar.  A great recipe that's very easy to make.

OmG, this recipe is the best homemade Mac and Cheese ever!! My bf and I were practically dying over every mouthful of this creamy, rich casserole. I will be making this luscious, decadent dish  often. I used extra sharp cheddar and cut it into many tiny cubes so it would be better spread throughout the casserole dish. We also made and seasoned our own breadcrumbs (Italian style) to top the dish. We didn't happen to have fresh parsley so I just settled for the dry stuff. Not the same, but still, Mmmmm! I never have to settle for the boxed cheap-a-roni and cheese ever again. Thanks Lennie!!
This was my comfort food while I was pregnant!  I think I made it at least once a month! It is not the healthiest meal around, but it sure is tasty!!  Great recipe!!!

Does mac and cheese get any better than this? Not in my book! For just a little more effort than mixing up boxed mac and cheese, you can prepare this recipe and put a meal on the table that will make you proud and make your family smile.
I've never added cream cheese to mac and cheese and didn't like the addition. Although it was very creamy, I thought it diluted the cheddar taste which is what mac and cheese is all about.  Sorry.

I'm a major fan of Luby's Mac and Cheese and thought this would be a wonderful change of pace.  Unfortunately it didn't come out quite as nice.  I followed the directions with no changes, but the end result just wasn't that appetizing.
I made this dish for a pot-luck at work. Everyone LOVED it and there have been requests for it at our next pot-luck during the holiday season.
Wowzers!  The taste was superb.  The texture, was thick.  The only thing that I didn't like was it wasn't good for my diet.  Well worth the cheat though! ha!

I made this tonight with my expectations a little low because every homemade mac and cheese I've made has been pretty bland. So, when I tasted this I was floored! It is the best mac & cheese I have ever had. The dijon and cream cheese give this a very unique flavor. My husband also loved it and went back for seconds. Thanks Lennie!
Was so tired of dried out mac and cheese, this recipe is the best Ive tried yet, has become a house favorite..Thank you for the recipe

I used regular cream cheese and 2% milk and it was great.  I am making it tonight for the second time.  It was requested.  It is the best macaroni and cheese I ever tasted and I have tasted A LOT.  It will be my standard now.
This was pretty good, but I think I will cut back on the mustard to half next time, it was just a tad too tangy. Otherwise it had a good texture and good taste. Thanks.

My 16 year old grandson wanted mac and cheese for our Memorial Day barbecue -- so I picked this recipe -- and so glad I did.  I think the cream cheese really helps to make the sauce creamy and rich.  I did skip the breadcrumbs on top -- just because I didn't think DJ would like them.  It's so nice to see an empty dish after trying a new recipe.  Thanks, Lennie.

Utterly delicious! I was in a hurry to get dinner on the table so I skipped the topping-baking step and was still delighted with the way it tasted. As is often the case, we use what we have on hand so I substiuted pasta shells for the macaroni and used a good white sharp cheddar cheese. This recipe is a keeper and next time I'll bake it with the topping. Thank you, Lennie, for this yummy dish!
awesome mac and cheese. made it just as the recipe says and it turned out perfect. yum!
This was a great recipe.  The cream cheese made it extra yummy.  Mine did get a little dry for my taste.  Thanks for such a delicious recipe!

I have made this recipe twice, and it was great both times. I make it with "swanky" pasta, in unique shapes, and I used Tipperrary white sharp cheddar. I also used 1 1/2 cups cream and 1/2 cup milk. Oink but yum. I used a whole teaspoon of ground peppe, and dumped fresh parsley throughout. Since I had already been piggy with the cream I just sprinkled dried Progresso bread crumbs on top, but it was really wonderful. We liked it so much, we had it for breakfast the next day! Thanks Lennie!

This is IT!  Since I hate Velvetta and don't consider it a real cheese I haven't been able to find a great mac & cheese until now!  I used fat free cream cheese and plain soy milk and it still came out nice and creamy.  Loved the breadcrumbs on top and the bite from the sharp cheddar.  DH said that I should ONLY use this recipe.  P.S.  Made a second batch to take to a pot luck and came back with an empty pan.

This was very good and very rich.  It will occupy a place in my recipe binder under dishes that are very good to eat and very bad for the waistline!  I didn't change a thing except to add a bit more cheese because I didn't have a conversion tool handy for 1/2 pound.  I figured better safe than sorry.  Thanks so much for posting!

Made this for lunch on a cool fall afternoon and really liked it a lot.  Ultimate comfort food. I halved the recipe as its just DBF and I, but otherwise did not at all change the recipe.  I think next time i'll either use less breadcrumbs or maybe omit the breadcrumbs altogether and top the casserole with extra cheese as DBF and I both thought there were too many breadcrumbs.  I will definitely be making this mac and cheese again.  Thanks for posting!
Thanks for sharing, will make it again ;-)

I wanted to update my review because I made this again and it was amazing (again). I doubled the recipe so I could make it into a casserole. The only thing I didn't double was the cream cheese and it actually made it a bit lighter than the first time we had it (which we liked). I also added a little white pepper along with the black pepper. Instead of breadcrumbs used whole wheat Ritz crackers. YUM! I definitely suggest doing that if you can. I used soy milk in place of regular and used half white sharp cheddar and half orange (or yellow). I love this recipe. It's one of my favorites!!!

This was one of the best mac recipes I have ever tried.  It was creamy and cheesy...everything that a good macaroni and cheese should be.  The only thing that I would change is using shredded cheese on top of the mac instead of the breadcrumbs.  I thought the bread crumbs took away from the creamy taste and texture of the mac.  I will be making this again at the next family function.

This is the best macaroni and cheese I've ever made--I don't see making all those three and five cheese jobs. It's Mac & Cheese for crying out loud. What a great little impromptu cheese sauce with the cream cheese this one has!

I gave it 5 stars--it's that good! It's wholesome and I think you could very well add other things to make it a main dish. It wasn't difficult. I used only 2 Tablespoons of butter for the sauce.

For expediency, I also left off the bread crumbs and used shredded cheese rather than cubed, but I think I'd take the time to use cubed cheese next time. I added shredded cheese on top and only baked it to bubbly goodness--I don't like browned/scorched cheese!

WOW!!! I am not a fan of mac n cheese but my BF loves it. He grew up on that nasty stuff from the blue box. He didn't even know what real mac n cheese tasted like until he met me!!! I was contemplating making only half a recipe since he is the only one who eats it... but I had exactly 8 oz of macaroni left and decided to go ahead with the full recipe... I am soooo glad I did. I used 2% milk and full fat cream cheese since that is what I had one hand. The sauce came together so beautifully... at first I thought it was just going to lump up on me but after 4 minutes it was smooth and velvety. I loved the cubed cheese mixed in... it gave great pockets of melted cheese when you bit into it... I chose not to sprinkle with the breadcrumb mixture since my BF isn't a fan of "crispy" tops on his mac. I loved how the top got golden brown and a little crispy without it... it was my favorite part. Yes, I had a taste and that taste led to a good sized portion that I ate happily. It was very rich and delicious. Next time, I may reduce the Dijon by half since I liked the tang but thought it was just a little strong. Thanks so much for a mac n cheese we can BOTH enjoy!!!

Very Good! I think the chunks of cheddar are the best touch. I noticed some of the 'commentators' just added shredded cheese and I think they missed the best part of the recipe. A little dry for my taste I may try it with 1/2 the amount of flour or maybe none next time.

This is the same recipe I've been using for years, always to rave reviews. What fun it was to find it here. I admit to always using 2% milk, regular cream cheese, and a full pound of cheddar. This is naughty, but it's sooooo good. I always try to justify it that we eat less when it's richer, but I know that's a full blown lie. Thrill your family and make it tonight.

This was good.  My 20-month old devoured her serving.  It was definitely a different flavor than I was used to.  I think next time I will leave out the Dijon, as it was a little strong and it's not an ingredient that we typically have on hand.  Other than that, lovely and creamy, cheesy and don't skip the breadcrumbs.   I almost did, but they gave a lovely crispy crust.  YUM!

I have tried hundreds of mac and
cheese recipes looking for the ultimate one.  Well, this is it. Absolutely the best one ever.
I did use whole fat milk and regular cream cheese.  I served this to friends and they are mad to get the recipe.  A winner!
This is a great recipe.  My DS loved it.  I used whole milk and regular cream cheese.  This one is a keeper!  Thanks, Lennie
This is the best mac and cheese ever! I've been making this for 4 years and it never gets old!

This was great!  I did change a couple things, just to make it even easier and to go further (my kids eat like they have hollow legs).  I used a whole pound of macaroni so I had to increase the amount of salt to 1tsp. I added an extra 1/2 cup of milk. I also added 1/4 tsp (scant) onion powder.  Instead of baking it, I just mixed the cheddar (actually used 1/2 cheddar/1/2 Velveeta) in until it was melted and poured it over the drained macaroni (that I'd put back in the pot) and ate it just like that...no topping. It was super yummy.  I've been looking for a great mac and cheese recipe and now I have it!  Thanks for posting this!!

My DH decided to cook this for us for lunch.  He used whole wheat noodles, as we try to watch our carbs when we can.  They worked fine.  DH followed Viennagirl's advice and made more so we could have leftovers. He ended up using more cheese than called for and he too used half sharp cheddar and half Velveeta to get the creaminess we like.  No crumbs for us on top.  Just added calories we don't need.  Great as is!  Thanks for sharing Lennie.

Thank you for this recipe Lennie!  I love the creaminess of this.  I didn't have cream cheese, so used ricotta instead.  Also grated some nutmeg into it.  I doubled the recipe for a 9x13.  It was fabulous.  Due to personal taste, I will probably cut the bread crumbs by half the next time I make it.  My day care kids (who are very picky) gobbled it up!  Thanks again.

I am a huge fan of Mac and Cheese. This is definitely one of the best I've tried! You are so right about it not being a diet food, but hey, isn't it comfort food that makes us feel so good?
It was creamy, and very interesting with the mustard. I've never put it in mine before. We fight over the crumbs on top, and I make sure I use a pan that gives me the most surface area!
I'll definitely add this to my faves. Thanks for posting a real winner! I may get a lot heavier, but I'll be happy!

Really rich and really creamy and really yummy.  I made it just as stated except adding a 1/2 lb of chopped and browned spicy sausage links.  I would add another whole cup of sausage next time.  Thanks!
I made this yesterday and everyone loved it. Excellent flavor and very, very creamy! Thanks for sharing this recipe.

I picked this recipe to make because it used up some ingredients I had on hand.  I was quite pleased with the outcome.  I used less butter, and about 1/4 lb. non-fat cream cheese.  I had a parmesan/bread crumb mix which I used instead of the fresh breadcrumbs.  I think if this recipe used full fat ingredients I would have found it much too heavy.  As is, it's still not low fat but pretty tasty nonetheless.  This is the first time I've used cream cheese in macaroni and cheese, and while I'm not quite ready to go with cream cheese in the future (mainly because it reduces the cheddar taste), it was nice for a different take on regular mac and cheese.  Thanks Lennie!

Unfortunately I did not feel the same about this Mac & Cheese as most of the other reviewers.  I thought it was just OK.  It was creamy and the crust golden, but it was bland to me.  I guess I was looking for something more / different.  My search continues.
Sorry Lennie.  Deb in Texas
great mac and cheese! I added 2 tbsp hot sauce and 3 chicken  breasts (baked then cubed and mixed in). came out awesome, thanks lennie!

My first taste of mac and cheese and i'm hooked. Never had it before, not even packet mix stuff. This recipe is creamy, rich and downright luxurious. I used a garlic and herb cream cheese which added a bit of extra flavour, i also had to substitute english mustard for dijon but it's still gorgeous. Definately woth the effort and glad i made enough to last, gonna have a go at freezing it and taking it for lunch at work.
This was good, but a little bland for my taste.
Very luxurious
This was the best and creamiest macaroni recipe I have ever made! Perfect!

Such a great dish.  It's a regular here, everyone loves it.  I serve it with a recipe I have in a cookbook of mine, bacon wrapped breadsticks AKA bacon twists.  Thank you very much for posting it.  I only have 3 changes to this.  I just cut out the middle man and use italian bread crumbs to top it, shredded cheddar instead of cubed, and coarse ground mustard instead of dijon (Which adds a pleasant flavor it imo).  If I could give 10 stars I would.
I've been making this every Tuesday night for a few weeks (and will continue to do so). My family loves it! Thanks!
Loved this!  Perfect comfort food!  Instead of breadcrumbs I used crushed Corn Flakes and no butter mixed in the topping.  Thank you!

Like another reviewer, we added ham and broccoli and it was delish!  Very hearty main dish.  We left out the butter at the end and I wish I would have used crushed corn flakes or panko instead of bread crumbs so it was more crunchy.  Otherwise followed the recipe to a T.
This is the best mac and cheese recipe I have ever made.  I put in 1.5 cups of cubed black forest ham. Also, I used Panko bread crumb. FABU!!!
SUPERB!!!  Made for the church potluck.  Thank you!
Yummola!

Absolutely amazing. My daughter in law wanted macaroni and cheese pizza. I've made many different pizzas but never that one. So looked for what sounded like a great Mac & Cheese recipe to do this, and boy did I find one.

I didn't use the mustard and didn't technically bake it accoring to the directions. I made as stated and then put it on my crust that had been brushed with some melted butter and minced garlic. Top with bacon and just a few ounces of mozerella. Fantastic. I'll certainly be doing this again.

Thanks for posting.

You know how you search and search without rest for the perfect recipe?  I was doing just that for mac and cheese.  I know for sure that I've tried 8 different recipes.....who knows how many I've already dropped into the "no-way-not-again" pile and into the garbage disposal.  But I am thoroughly finished with my search with THIS amazing mac and cheese recipe!  I've made it 3 times now with gut-busting results and rave family reviews.  I know mac & cheese is a very personal thing...seriously now.  But this recipe has got me doing the "amen".  Thank you thank you!

This was delicious!! My family loved it and it is SO creamy and cheesy! It was the best mac'n cheese I've ever had and it is awesome! I will definitely use this again because it's actually easy to make and it turns out great!

Comfort food at its finest.  I made this last night to go with our ribs.  I did leave off the breadcrumbs, but otherwise followed the recipe.  We loved it.  The cream cheese adds an extra amount of creaminess.  Delicous.  thanks for sharing your recipe with us.

I made half a recipe to test before Thanksgiving. I used small shells instead of macaroni, otherwise followed the recipe exactly. A little to alfredo-y for me and kind of bland. Needed a touch of hot sauce or cayenne.

Truly incredible!  Only thing I would change is not fully mixing the cheddar cubes and leaving them partially unmelted to create a bit more texture, and adding a bit of tabasco for kick.  Otherwise, it was exactly what I was looking for, and a perfect kick-off recipe for tweaking to personal tastes.
This has become a huge favorite in our house. My daughter doesn't normally care for mac & cheese but she begs me to make this one often. I like to use Vermont Sharpe Cheddar cheese.

Very creamy and yummy!!! Nice variation on MAC & CHEESE. I didn't do the breadcrumb topping as I'm not a fan and I only had Neufchâtel cheese which is similar to using low fat cream cheese. I also used shredded cheese. Thanks for sharing.<br/><br/>UPDATE: I've made this twice now with shredded cheese. First time mixing in the cheese into the sauce so that it completely melted. The second time mixing cheese in the casserole so that it stayed in tact prior to baking. I prefer the second method better. It's cheesier for some reason.

Very creamy and fairly easy to make, but it lacked the depth of flavor I was looking for. I wanted something with a more intense cheese flavor and bite. If you're looking for a more mellow creamy flavor this recipe is for you.

Very good basic recipe that is fool proof and can be tweaked many ways. I like adding about 50 grams of smoked Gouda for a nice smoky Mac & cheese. Also try adding bacon and jalapeño for a southern spicy twist.

These griddle cakes are terrific!  I made the recipe just as specified and my cakes came out moist and fluffy.  The brown sugar adds a perfect touch of sweetness.  I served them with syrup and enjoyed every bite - thanks for posting this recipe!  Made for Fall PAC 2008
Wow, did I love this.  The flavors were a terrific mix.  It was so simple, fresh and special enough to serve for an elegant meal.

Of the 100 recipes submitted for the RSC #7 contest, I choose to review three and this is one of them. So very good on you!  It is a tall order to made a better recipe then the traditional Italian Shrimp Scampi with Garlic... This recipe is a good alternative to the traditional scampi and I am sure others will like it. But for me the traditional shrimp scampi is still numero uno.

I think I have died and gone to heaven!! I prepared this recipe for a dinner with friends, we all (4)agreed this is a winner, a definite 5***** + recipe!
Easy to follow directions! The flavours are so very Mediterranean we all thought we were eating in a seaside restaurant! The key to this recipe is to use all fresh ingredients. This dish will be one of my favourites!
A very good combination of flavors but I found the butter to overpower everything and to become almost the pre-dominant flavor of the dish.

I started by sauting the onions and peppers (which I didn`t roast because of time. I wish I had jar roasted peppers)in the butter then adding the garlic letting them brown then adding the tomatoes (I used cherry tomatoes halved) and the rest of the ingredients. Ending with the shrimp. I did find the olives and caper overpowered the dish. Loaded with so many flavors. Love all the garlic. I did feel the butter could have been cut in half along with the olives. I`m having a hard time rating this. 31/2 stars it is. Because I think the directions could have been made easier and the olives and capers were overpowering as was the butter.But since there is no 31/2 I`ll go up and make it a 4 star recipe.

Do these epople not use salt and pepperto season anything. If you cook shrimp for 45 minutes they will become rubbery. Why did this person remove the garlic and the onions from the heat only to add them  a few seconds later.
Taste was okay not great. This dish was not very difficult to make. I would have served this on a bed of couscous.

This was the most raved about dish at a luncheon of Zaar chefs, hosted by LoisM! Although I wasn't involved in the preparation, I've reviewed the directions - they seem to be clear & complete. The result was awesome - a real taste treat! If you forget the baguette, you'll probably want to lick the sauce from your plate!!

This is a definate keeper! Beautiful blend of flavors, and an easy dish to make,I preped the veggies the day before, and just assembled and cooked when my guests arrived, I did make a mistake though, I used 1/4 lb of butter instead of 1/2 lb, I will make this again using the correct amt.

This was made for me at our Ontario Zaar Luncheon at Lois M's home.
All I can say is WOW!!! I absolutely LOVED this dish...if I could give it 10 stars I would. This is a fantastic blend of fresh herbs, I could taste all the ingredients well.
Very flavourful and delicious, and I will be adding this one to my permanent collection.
Thanks for a winner!
What a wonderful dish. The combination of my favorite seafood with the fresh herbs and wine was just amazing and so right about having the bread to soak up the sauce.  Definitely a keeper
An interesting dish which we enjoyed with pasta. I did cut the amount of garlic in half and used a bit less shrimp than called for  personal taste. Thanks for sharing this interesting dish.

Who doesnt love a  great scampi.  This was very good, but I did have a few things I probably would have done differently.  I thought the 1 cup of scallions was overwhelming in this recipe.  I would have preferred using some shallot, and then maybe garnish with chopped scallion.  I love garlic, but my head of garlic was HUGE, and I think if Id used the whole head, the garlic in the dish would have consumed everything... I dont know that I would have tasted anything but garlic.  I used 8 cloves of garlic, leaving aside about 1/3 of the head of garlic. The red bell pepper and the olives were a lovely addition to this dish, as were the capers.  I prefer a dish like this made with sherry, but for the purpose of this contest the white wine was sufficient.
I have made this recipe twice now, and thoroughly enjoyed it both times.  Thank you for a lovely meal.

I have just tried this recipe as I had a bag of prawns (shrimp) on hand wondering what to do with them.  This meal was easy to cook and the taste was fantastic.  It was a treat to have prawns this way.  Thankyou.

Made this for dinner last night.  This makes generous servings which are wonderful.  The blending of fresh herbs makes for flavors that come alive on your taste buds.  Did not have a baguette, which I sorely missed, but opted to serve it over couscous with a side salad.
Delicious, absolutely delicious. We certainly enjoyed this easy to make dish. What can I say about the lovely combination of flavours except... muummmmmm. Thank you so much for sharing.
This is wonderful!

My Goodness!  This is a fabulous recipe!  Loaded with flavor and color!  I am ashamed to say I have neglected in the past, the recipes of the RSC contest.  According to my results of this recipe, I now know I have missed a lot. This is not a mistake I will make again. This recipe contains more prep time than I normally would give to a shrimp recipe.  But this particular recipe is definitely worth the added time and effort. I made as directed including roasting my own red bell pepper, chopping an entire clove of garlic by hand and pitting and chopping kalamata olives .  I will definitely make this recipe again and when I do, I may add just a touch of crushed red pepper flakes. Thanks very much to the contest chef for creating this wonderfully flavorful recipe!

Halved the recipe for the two of us, fresh French baguette on the side and it was wonderful. I loved the amount of garlic in this recipe and it was easy to put together because the instructions were clear. A winner for me!!

Restaurant-quality delicious!  I made a 1/2 recipe, just for DH and myself and wish I'd made the full version as we were both waxing ecstatic with each and every bite!  This chef's technique is right on the money; instructions thoughtfully and correctly written out and recipe easy to follow.  The result is divine and a recipe that will be repeated again and again in my repertoire (especially for company).  The sauce is too wonderful and perfectly complements the shrimp (I used #1 size and left the heads on for extra-delicious eating).  Bravo, chef!
Fantastic! Made according to recipe, easy & delicious. Added to my "Keepers" folder!

This is EXELLENT! I organised a dinner party just with finalists' recipes and this was the overall winner of my test team! I made sure to cook the finalist recipes with as little changes as possible, and I didn't add salt as this recipe didn't ask for any. I was astonished how flavourful this was, although there is no salt in it. I did use slightly less butter as stated, but I think you shouldn't cut it too much, since the butter makes this so tasty. Thank you so much for creating such a wonderful dish. I will do this again!

Toolie, you have outdone yourself! Used only 1/4 lb. unsalted butter and Spanish capers, but the result is still incredible.
Will pass this recipe on to friends.. there are no leftovers for them to try...
This was just too buttery.  It overpowered the other flavors.  I followed your recipe exactly.  I expected "wow" because it won a contest....sorry, this didn't "wow" me.
Way too much butter, and calamata olives should not be mutilated if you want to enjoy the real essence of GREEK. Iam not impressed and I can't beleive this is the #1 recipe. How sad.

after reading all the reviews, I will be curious as to how it will turn out.  congratulations and i will let you know how mine turns out
ROSAMARIA
Was very good reminds me of greese

Dude!  I would rate this a 6+.  I was tasting this all day before I started cooking.  Moron me, I served this with rice instead of noodles (mediterranean right?) Oh well, it was like I-talian gumbo.  Very flavorful.  I used 1-1/2 sticks of butter, used 1 can of diced tomatoes with juice (close enough to 2 cups).  For fresh herbs that I did not have, I used half the recipe with the dry.  This stuff tasted better than restaurant quality.

This was an awesome recipe!  I did not use 2 lbs of shrimp as I thought it might be too much.  I did add some cooked chicken since one of my sons doesn't like shrimp. I also served it over angel hair pasta..It was delish!!  Overall I would highly reccomend this dish!!!
I love scampi, and this was a great scampi recipe.  Not much I can say that hasn't already been said, except....great job!!!!

I followed this recipe to the letter...apart from using both red and green bell peppers. This recipe is bursting with flavour...love the addition of the olives and capers - capers happen to be one of my secret loves!! I'm lucky to have basil, oregano and continental parsley growing in pots, so the herbs were super fresh.I served this very simply...with french bread and a green salad (and a lovely bottle of Wolf Blass Chardonnay). Thanks Toolie for an enjoyable meal!

I've been holding onto this recipe for weeks now, always meaning to make it. Last night I finally got all the ingredients together, but was in a time crunch.. I used cocktail shrimp to save time, used a bit less butter, and  regular tomatoes. I was afraid I probably ruined the taste, but when it finished simmering, and I ladled it out into huge bowls for DH and myself.. it was outstanding!! I bought fresh garlic infused baguette from the grocery store... my husband raved all night long about the taste! The lemon and herbs blend so beautifully. Without a doubt this recipe will be in my permanent collection. I'm emailing it today to my mother in Virginia. She has frequent dinner parties, and I think it would suit her well. Thank you for the recipe!!
This is worth more than 5 stars. What can you say only WOW!!!!

I made this recipe a few nights back, and have to say that is was fantastic Worth much  more than five stars,  Followed the recipe as close as possible except I did use  three different colours of bell peppers.This just added to the colour presentation.I also added   six large scallops   in the last couple of minutes of cooking.These I  sliced in half. Served this with orzo, cooked in beef broth,because that was what I had opened from asian food prepared  the night before. Soaked up the sauce with the last of my homemade french bread which I had drizzled with evoo and freshly grated parmesan cheese, and toasted under the broiler.Did not use garlic on the bread because I did`t want to take away, or overpower the garlic in the sauce  
What more can I say.This is definately an upscale restaurant quality recipe   Thank you Toolbelt for sharing this wonderful recipe... 
chef 199947

I finally got around to trying this dish today, being Greek-born, this recipe has all of my favorite ingredients in it! This is a dish that has complex flavors, but all blend together well to create a very tasty dish. I did increase the shrimp and olives, served this topped with freshly grated Parmesan cheese, and homemade rolls for a late weekend brunch. I am very impressed with this recipe, and plan on making it again soon, great recipe Toolie, we really enjoyed this dish!...Kitten:)

what a creative recipe! I loved it. The only change I made was to use a really good Greek EVOO since I just bought it and omit the butter & add red pepper flakes. It was heavenly. Served the dish with couscous but next time I will go with a good crusty bread. Thanks!

This dish has alot of great flavor.  I did change it up a little;

I used chicken instead of shrimp - we just cut it up into bite size pieces and cooked it first, seasoning with salt & pepper.  Then began adding ingredients as listed.  I cut back drastically on the butter and used EVOO - about 2 Tbsp and only 1 Tbsp butter (just for flavor).  We also used a can of diced tomatoes.  Served this over whole wheat pasta from Trader Joe's.  This is definitely a keeper.  Thanks for posting.

This was suggested to me in the Request forum to fix for an evening with DH and martini's. It was great!!!  I made thin spaghetti noodles to go with, but I think you could use rice or even fettuccine noodles as well. It was fanstastic.

This was absolutely fantasic. My husband is not a shrimp fan and he liked it. I put about 1/3 of the butter in and added " a splash of olive oil", sorry I'm not famous for measuring things. I jut pour; I would say about 2 tbsp. I added a little extra basil and oregano (just because I chopped too much and didn't want to waste it. I served it over chinese rice vermicelli. I may cut out or add less capers (only because I'm on a low sodium diet. I have taken a picture and will send it once I have down loaded it.

Thanks for posting this recipe. It is the best I have tried so far.

Delicious! I read the other comments before preparing and completely agree with cutting down the butter. There is so much flavor with all the other ingredients. I also added marinated jarred artichoke hearts.

Finally found this one!! I found it when I first got into Zaar, and then wrote it down and made it and couldn't find it again to rate it!! I served this over wild rice this was very different than a lot of the shrimp dishes that we've had in the past. I left out the kalamatas (personal preference) and next time I would leave out the capers too they just didn't do it for me in this dish. It was a really intersting way to make shrimp though. Thanks for posting!

This is delicious.  I note that it did take me considerably longer to make than the 45 minutes noted.  However, it was well worth the time spent.  I used chicken broth instead of white wine, and I took the tails off the shrimp to be able to enjoy the shrimp whole without having to worry about not biting into the tail.  Thanks for posting.
Pretty good.  My bf said it was a bit "fishy" and I thought the capers stood out too much, but other than that we enjoyed it.
This was amazing!  The only thing I changed was I used chicken broth instead of wine. I will be making this version alot.  Thank you for posting.
My family really enjoyed this dish!  I normally do not make dishes this high in fat, but occasionally it is worth the calories.  I found the directions clear and the dish easy to prepare.
This is a fabulous full flavored dish. I paid heed to the reviews and reduced the butter.

I doctored this one up some replaced the tomatoes with Sun-Dried Tomatoes, and replaced one pound of the shrimp with scallops. Man it was GOOD. If you like scampi, you will LOVE this recipe! I also cut down the butter in 1/2 too.

I thought this was a good recipe but I didn't find it to be great.  In all fairness, I used jarred roasted red peppers rather than fresh (since I couldn't get to the store to get peppers) and I cut the butter in half per previous reviewers recommendations.  I actually think I would have preferred a bit more butter to thicken this up (and that says a lot coming from me who cuts the fat in all recipes everywhere possible!).  On the flip side...my husband thought it was GREAT!  I think feta cheese would have been a great topper for this but I didn't have any on hand to confirm this.  I would give this 3.5 stars...my husband would give it 4.5 stars so it's a 4 from us.  Neither of my kids (age 2 and 4) liked this much but my 2 year old did enjoy the shrimp out of it.  I will try this one again and increase the butter a bit, add REAL roasted red peppers and top with feta and report back!  Nice change of pace from regular scampi!!!  Thanks for posting.

Seriously - this took me FOUR hours to make from start to finish. I have never been so irritated with a recipe in my entire life. I don't know how anyone could possible prep this in 20 minutes (as it's listed). It was good, but certainly not great. That is 4 hours of my life I will never get back. I would highly recommend against making this. If you decide to make it, use canned tomatoes, bottled roasted peppers, ez-peel shrimp, and bottled minced garlic. Thank God that I got lucky with the olives - when I opened the jar, I was surprised to find that they were already pitted. I never want to see this recipe again!

I had printed out this recipe long ago. I just ran into it again, sounded good, so I made it (without reading any reviews). My DH, friend and I all thought it was terrific. 
I did make a few changes: used half butter, half olive oil, regular onion, red peppers that were not roasted, half the tomato. I sauteed the garlic, onion and red pepper together and didn't remove them. Followed the directions from here on, used thawed, pre-cooked shrimp. Served over brown rice. I would definitely make this again!

Awesome! Don't know how I missed reviewing this fabulous recipe! While I only made half a recipe it was super easy to put together. The garlic easily prepped and sauted - the tomatoes given a quick hot dip to remove the skins and on to some quick chopping. Other then using a touch less of the olives  (because that is all I had on hand) I made as directed with winning results! Definitely a winner. Only change I will make next time around is to make the whole 2 pound recipe and share with my shrimp loving family!
Everybody raves about this recipe, and I have to make it for all parties.
Lovely, fresh, flavorful. Used jarred roasted bell peppers and dried basil- but otherwise followed your recipe exactly. Served over linguine. Mmmm- So, so delicious!!!!!
Let me just say that after my guests tasted this dish last night, they tried to convince me to open up a restaurant... Thank you.
Wow! I made this last night for a BBQ (as an appy)  and it was not only a beautiful presentation- but delicious! I will keep this in the keeper file!! Thank you so much for the recipe :)
In one word, "excellent"

This is possibly the best dish ever! The house smells like a 5* Italian restaurant. Seriously, make this, then go outdoors for a minute and come back in. WOW! I figured if this tasted half as good as it smells, it will be a winner. Well it tastes TWICE as good as it smells. No two bites taste the same. You get a kick from a medley of ingredients that somehow magically changes with each bite. 
We took tails off before cooking which is definitely the way to go. Otherwise it would've been a mess to get the tails off while eating.
Served over steamed rice. 50 bazillion million gagillion stars!!!! Thank you so much.
This was absolutely delish!  My boys had never eaten Mediterranean anything before and were wowed by how great all of the flavors melded together, me too!  Thanks for posting

I chose this recipe last night because of all the votes. I am not normally such a creative chef, but our dinner guests requested Meditteranean so I gave it a try. SO glad I did! I ask my husband to rate my new recipes on a scale from 1-10. I've usually gotten 8,9 or 10- but this recipe got a 12! A first! The guests loved it too. Not only was it aromatic and flavorful, the presentation was nice, too.

I made a few subs- I used chicken broth instead of wine (actually think it would be okay without it), I used regular tomatoes instead of plum, I used half the butter, I only had one roasted red pepper so I used jarred for the other, I only put in a few tablespoons of olives and about 1 (or less) TBS of capers (I was nervous about them). Even after ALL those substitutions, everyone still loved it. Served it with salad and a crunchy bread.

It took me about 2 hours to make from start to finish- the major time killers were roasting the red peppers (1 hour total, but super easy, you can be doing other prep while you wait), and peeling, crushing and chopping all that garlic. Both of these things can be done the day before (store red peppers in oil), so I will be doing that next time. Now that I've done it once, it will be a breeze to do over, which I certainly will (again and again!).

THANK you for this recipe, I loved hearing what a great chef I am! :)

I think it took over an hour even with my shortcuts below, but well worth it.  I used chicken (husband doesn't eat shrimp), 2 tblsp olive oil and 1 tblsp butter, garlic from the jar, a jar of roasted peppers (chopped), canned, crushed tomatoes, cilantro (no flat-leaf at the grocery store), no capers, no lemons.  I also used a couple of squirts of bottled lemon juice.  And it turned out FANTASTIC.  I tasted before and after the olives (my husband is not a fan of those either), and they really made the difference.  I forgot, I also added about 1 tsp of crushed red pepper.  It needed salt to taste and we ate over pasta.

A lovely variation on scampi, I halved the recipe and substituted regular tomatoes for the plum as i had a ton from my garden.I served this with caesar salad, Ev's baked feta (#67949)and hot french bread.DH said this was "slap your Mama" food.Its a keeper!!
just made this recipe again..timed myself..took 20 mins start to finish.did use jarred red peppers.but still fabulous recipe.and really quick to whip up..maybe im a really fast chopper .lol!

This was amazing!  The prep time did take a while but it was a whiz once that was done. I cut the butter in half and saut?ed the garlic first for about 1 -2 minutes then added the onions and took them out together.   I added about 3 T of olive oil before adding the tomatoes.   I used probably twice as much oregano and basil.  Followed everything else as written.   Served with piping hot Fenech baguette and feta cheese.  Beyond Delish!!  Happy New Year indeed!

This soup is to die for !! DS said it was a 'cracker' soup - high praise indeed !! I altered not one thing when making this but offered sweet chili sauce swirled on top to the eaters. It is such a beautiful colour and makes a generous amount - thanks KE so much for this fabulous meal.

A really good soup with a lovely blend of flavours. The coriander is the perfect herb for this dish. Next time though I would sub out one of the sweet potatoes and change it for a regular potato- although I love sweet potatoes, I found this just a little on the sweet side. Just personal taste! Thanks for a lovely recipe that we'll definitely be making again!

Yum! I tried this recipe both ways, first time around I stopped at step 4 and served warm and the next day blended the remaining half and served chilled with yoghurt. While very enjoyable warm I thought it was spectacular chilled, the sweetness was ideally suited to a chilled soup and the yoghurt and coriander were great additions. I used unsweetened OJ from a bottle so ommitted the orange rind garnish and stirred through a nice Greek yoghurt.

This soup was pretty good. Refreshing and comforting at the same time. We like smooth soups, so I ded puree it. But I left out the yogurt. Thanks for posting :)
Made for PRMR

Did this soup up the other day & although we do like pureed soups, this time around I left it chunky, though diced everything fairly small! A great combo of flavors, & a really nice change from the usual vegetable soups that we have! Also a  keeper recipe, no less! Thanks for sharing it! [Tagged, made & reviewed in Please Review My Recipe]

Just finished a bowel of this tasty soup.  It was so simple to make.  I followed it to a tee but for that (coriander)stuff!  I did use my immerser to blend the soup thus having the best of both ways...smooth with small chunks. THe fresh squeezed oj made the difference with this dish.

Delicious hearty vegetarian soup! I blended in the blender which it very silky and smooth. I did not use the fresh coriander as I don't care for it.
Made for "Veg*n Swap 17 ~ Dec 2009 ~ Let's Play!
This is wonderful!  I didn't have coriander so substituted a little cilantro. Also, I didn't puree it since we like chunky soup. Amazing!

These little gems turned out great.  I did get nervous because I shure could have gotten more then 12 mini cheesecakes.  I think I "over beat" my cream cheese mixture.  I kept adding more and more mixture to each cheesecake.  As it turned out I did get 2 extra.  These do puff up alot, almost like a soufle.
