I thought I blew the whole recipe, but everything turned out great.  My store eve has mini nilla wafers I thought I might try those next and make some bite size next time.  I saw Paula do these and I to had to try them.

These look fabulous in the photograph, and they taste just as scrumptious as they look!  Although Sharlene~W’s instructions couldn’t have been clearer, the photograph helped me enormously in having the confidence to proceed with this recipe.  I wasn’t entirely sure what sort of wafers had been used but looking at the photograph enabled me to improvise an appropriate base for these tarts: crushed Granita biscuits mixed with melted butter, a popular base for cheesecakes in Australia.  These were SO easy to make.  I filled some with halved, pitted black cherries and some with raspberries (both from cans, as they’re not in season here).  The contrast of colours looked great.  Absolutely delicious: everyone just LOVED them, and clearly imagined that they had taken a lot longer to make than in fact they had!  I’ll be making these again when berries are in season.  Thanks, Sharlene~W, for another fabulous recipe!

I never try new things but I thought this sounded good.  It was! very tasty and easy.  My only problem was removing them from the paper cups. They stuck to the paper and fell apart.  I need suggestions on keeping them together and pretty. Otherwise they taste great!

I love these tarts!!! I'm also a fan of Paula Deen and made this when I first saw it on FoodNetwork.  Everyone always asks for the recipe, and it's so simple!  It's great for parties or potlucks.  
Try using the new silpat cupcake liners (lightly spray the liners?).  Besides that it is a little difficult to get the cream cheese tarts out of the paper liners, who cares, it still looks great topped with pie filling and yummy ofcourse!

Yumm-o! I served these for a baby shower that I threw and there weren't any left over! I doubled the recipe and I made 1/2 blueberry and 1/2 peach. They had a very nice presentation and couldn't be any easier to make. Thanks for posting!! :)
My wife and I made these. She had 4 of them eaten before they even cooled. We use the blueberry pie filling.

Paula can do no wrong in my eyes!  This was great and can be made using other toppings.  I put together a homemade pineapple kiwi pie filling that I put on top that my friends and family won't stop requesting.  Thanks for posting!
OMG! These tasted just like baby cheesecakes. Everyone loved them! Although.. I forgot half of my audience were diabetics (oops) next time I think I'll try Splenda instead of sugar.

I made these delicious little tarts for my niece's senior music recital at Gettysburg College.  They were a BIG HIT.  I made them along with a few other recipes from Zaar and they all came out wonderfully!  I used the little tiny mini cups, and bought the mini Nilla Vanilla Wafers.  They fit in the bottom beautifully, although during baking some of them rose to the top.  It didn't matter though, as I put canned strawberries and blueberries on them and they looked adorable.  The pics didn't come out the greatest, but I will post it so you can see.  Thanks so much for this recipe Sharlene.  I saw Paula make them and knew they would be delicious!

Linda

I made these to take to the annual family Thanksgiving get-together, as an alternative to the usual Pumpkin pie. They were delicious and a huge hit. I have never made cheesecake before, but this recipe was so easy to make. I used cherry and blueberry pie fillings for the toppings. This definitely falls into the "keeper" category!

These are a real treat! Super pretty and ridiculously easy. I served on a cake stand along with 'whatever floats your boat' brownies and some clusters of grapes. It looked fabulous and tasted even better, go Paula!!!
I made these after I saw Paula make them on her show.  I used the mini-muffin pans and they still worked out great!  They're so easy, yet so tasty.
These are WONDERFUL snacks.  I put blueberry pie filling on top and it was absolutely indulging.  They make great desserts for a small party, which is a success!

Found this recipe in TOH years ago and have been making them every since. My family and friends love these. I used to make them for my kids on George Washington's Birthday with Cherry Pie Filling for fun.

Oh yeah!  5* for sure.  My son loved these.  I made a few changes out of necessity.  I only had 1 1/2 bricks of cream cheese so I put in 1/2 C of 1% cottage cheese and reduced the sugar to 3/4 C.  I had to cook about 5 minutes longer but that is probably because my filling was a bit thinner.  Topped with cherry pie filling. Thx for posting this easy recipe.
Delicious! Everyone enjoyed it. It's one of my favorites because I can count on it to deliver on taste and visually!

I'm singin', "Ain't no Scrooge in me. Ain't no Scrooge in me"! I did adapt the recipe slightly from my usual sour cream-topped standby. I doubled the recipe to make 24, baking just short (about 2 minutes) of the 20 minute baking time--turning off oven. I had prepared, in the meantime, 2 cups sour cream with a 1/2 cup sugar, stirring to dissolve sugar. After waiting about a minute or so for the puffed cakes to sink slightly, I topped each with the sweetened sour cream mixture, dividing evenly among the 24 cakes. Immediately, I replaced the cakes into the already heated oven for an additional 2 minutes to set the sour cream topping. A fruit topping adds a festive touch covering the imperfections that naturally arise during baking. These tasty treats will make a believer out of ya for sure!
These are so delicious!  What a great easy to make dessert.  Great anytime!
I love cheesecake with cherry pie filling, so this is dessert heaven for me.  Easy to make and super yummy!

I've been making these for practically every function I attend since finding them in a magazine - there are NEVER any left!  People rant and rave, and beg for the recipe (they can hardly believe it's so easy).  If I make them too far in advance, they mysteriously disappear from my fridge, with my husband and me accusing one another about who illegally ate more than whom.  :)  Thanks for posting!  This recipe is a keeper!
Easy, great taste and presentation!

This recipe was AMAZING. It was by far one of the easiest things i've ever made, and one of the most delicious. I did leave them in about 7-8 minutes longer because they were still undone in the middle but by the time i took them out some of them sunk so i may have left them in longer than needed. But i definately recommend trying these out if your looking at it. I will be making these again!

I made these last night for our office Christmas party. Very easy to make. This is definitely a keeper. Thank you for sharing! I wanted to add that this was a hit at the Christmas party. One of the few dishes (and only dessert) with no leftovers. Some even went back for seconds! I kept hearing Mmmmmmm when they put some in their mouth. THANK YOU!  Note:  my neighbor, who happens to bake a lot, suggested adding meringue to the mix to lighten it.

My mom made these when we would go to see Fireworks to Music in Las Colinas. She made them other times too, but that was the most memorable for me. They are delicious, and every time I see fireworks, I want one!

Yum!  I cut the serving size to four and used lactose free milk.  These were so easy to make and they tasted so yummy.  Other changes I did were I brushed the dough with some olive oil and sprinkled a little garlic on top of the dough before placing them to the griddle.  Thank Enjolinfam
This was great. Easy to make, and close to what I am used to eating at Indian restaurants, but without all of the unhealthy things...
A bit dry. Think perhaps some oil is needed. Had to add a bit more liquid to it for a decent rise, but that could just be due to my flour.

The family loved the Naan.  I live in Honduras and can't find vegan sour cream here so I used the local sour cream.  Other changes: I used skim milk, added the fresh garlic into the dough while kneading, added black pepper & garlic powder.  I also brushed butter on one side when done.  Thanks so much for sharing!
I love indian food and just recently started trying to make it at home for my vegan family. All of the naan i find in the store has buttermilk, but making it is so much fun! This recipe is awesome.

This was so good! Thank you so much! My fiance and I have been missing naan TONS since we adopted a vegan diet over 2 years ago. This recipe fixes it all. I used a plain soy yogurt instead of the sour cream because that's what I had on hand. The coriander really shone through & it was exciting to see the dough transform with the brown spots & bubbles! Next time we'll add the garlic. This is great! 2 thumbs up & 5 stars! (Toddler loved it, too!)
Very yum!  Next time I'll double the lime.  This is a wonderful refreshing summer salad--would be perfect for summer bbq's--served ice cold!
This turned out nicely. I like the taste of the lime. I added a touch more sugar(just personal preference). Thanks Kato!

This is a terrific salad I can see myself making all summer. I reduced the amounts to 1 large cucumber and 1 onion and made half of the dressing.  I waited about 6 hours before sampling and taking the photo...it was good then, but so much better after waiting the 24 hours.  The cucumbers are not swimming in a watery mess here.  They are lightly coated and have a mild taste. Good job Baby Kato!

This was as refreshing as it was easy to make!  I loved the fresh taste of the lime combined with the cucumbers and vidalias.  So easy to throw together and I am sure this will become a favorite at our summertime table.  Thanks, Baby K!

Another WOW recipe for cucumber salad! I agree - the flavors really are amazing.The vidalia onions perfect with the lovely garden fresh cucumbers - loved the dressing! Looks great tastes great! Thank you Baby Kato, be sure to thank John,  for sharing a recipe that is just so good -  going right into my 'Favorites Cookbook'
A nice cucumber salad.  I did add more sugar (personal preference).  A great side dish to summer grilled foods!  Marinating for 24 hours or longer is a must.  THANKS

Delicious!  This salad is a tasty way to use up the overabundance of cucumbers from my garden.  I didn't have vidalia onions, but used fresh red onions out of the garden and they worked perfectly.  Also, I added some additional sugar as my family prefers a sweeter oil/vinegar dressing.  Thanks BK for sharing this wonderful recipe...it is definitely a keeper!!

This is a tasty and quick salad. I used an English cucumber which didn't need to be seeded. The cucumber was simply sliced thinly and the rest of the recipe was followed as written. I usually make cucumber salad with an oil and vinegar dressing. This recipe is a nice alternative. Made for Zaar Stars Tag.
I used pickling cucumbers for this for some added crunch, and what great taste to this salad!  Loved the dressing!  Thank you!

Excellent salad.  Crispy, with a bite.  I used mini cucumbers, which are about an inch in diameter.  No need to remove the seeds in this particular case.  I did let it marinate for about 48 hours.  Even after that amount of time, they were still quite crisp and very fresh.  Thanks so much for a terrific way to serve cucumbers.  Made for the Auzzie/NZ Swap #30.

Great stuff! Cool and crisp with a kick from the red pepper flakes. I was able to let mine marinate for almost 20 hours. I agree, the longer it chills the better it gets.  I used extra sugar, but otherwise stuck to the recipe. Thanx for a new use for my cucumbers!
I was looking for a salad to have with some ribs I was cooking up to have when company came.  Everyone loved the salad, including me!

Yum!  After 24 hours this was like a semi pickle cucumber and onions salad.  I don't normally eat raw cumbers because my stomach gets upset, but I was able to eat this without a problem because the cucumber were "pickled" and the acids that make my tummy upset didn't affect me.   My daughter loved the juice, even with the chilli (which is unusual for her).  Thanks Baby Kato for a lovely recipe.

This was very refreshing served next to a spicy pork chop.  I love the flavors of this since I am not a big cucumber fan - but I love pickles!  I will definitely be making this again as it is so easy.

Made yesterday and yum!  I increased the sugar to 1 teaspoon and may go even a bit more on that the next time.  I also peeled my cucumbers and cut them using a mandoline.  So I would have some "kick" I added one dash of cayenne in addition to the hot pepper flakes, great!  Thanks for posting, Baby Kato, this is a great recipe!

Very nice recipe. I used English cucumbers, left the peel on, scooped out the seeds and sliced them on my mandolin, along with the sweet onions. I also added the zest of the limes, as they are too expensive to just use the juice. Took it to our church pot luck where it was well received. :)

Attractive salad!  A mandoline makes easy work of the cucumbers and onions.  I made a half recipe as listed for my small family and it was plenty.  We love cucumber and onion salads, but I will need to adjust the dressing on this one next time.  Thank you for sharing, Baby Kato!

After growing tired of what I thought was a pretty good chocolate chip cookie recipe, I decided to search for a new one.  So glad I found this one!  Made these according to recipe, used butter and half semi-sweet and half white chocolate chips.  Delicious!  If these six dozen make it through the night, it will surprise me!

YUM!! Soft, chewy, delicious cookies! I cut the recipe in 1/3, and they turned out great! I threw in crumbled up Reese's into the last few cookies, and it was amazing! This will definitely be my new go-to chocolate chip cookie.

Soooo good, thanks for the keeper!
Good cookies, I used 50% chcolocate chips and 50 % walnuts. Baking time had to be adjusted to 18 minutes in my oven.
If you like soft cookies this is great! It is the only recipe I use now. LOVE them!!!
These are wonderful!!  I have been using a Java Chocolate Chip recipe, which is good, but this is my new favorite!!  Followed the directions to a tee, thanks for posting!!
My family devoured these cookies!!! Awesome recipe!

These will definitely be made again, TNT cookies. I was worried the dough would be too dry but it mixed up and was just very firm. Wow! This is a really good chocolate chip cookie.  The main thing in my opinion to remember is only cook them for 8 minutes.  Let them cool on the pan.  They turn out perfect.  Thanks for sharing.

I made 2 dozen. These cookies are amazing, they fluffed up and did not flatten out.  I added a little more chocolate chips and a little maple syrup because i didnt have enough vanilla on hand. This is my new chocolate chip cookie recipe thank you for sharing it.

I'm a novice in the kitchen but even i could follow the instructions! really simple, easy to follow, minimal mess with just one bowl...and the cookies, my kids can't stop raving about them :) thanks for sharing!
I lost my old recipe that made 5 dozen and found this one! Excellent cookies! I'm not telling my family it's a new recipe..... I'll see if they notice! stay tuned! :-)
First time trying a recipe using margarine instead of butter. They turned out great! Soft and thick, didn't flatten or spread.

I made these because of the stellar reviews. Please don't waste your time or ingredients. These cookies came out terrible. I'm not a novice at cookie baking either, as I make dozens upon dozens of cookies every year to give everyone at Christmastime and everyone raves about my sugar cookies and others. But I've been on a quest to find the perfect CC cookie recipe. This is not it. These cookies are soft yes, but that's the only thing they have going for them. They are more like a cake than what I would call a cookie. I hate cakey chocolate chip cookies. They have far too much sugar, both brown and white. After they came out of the oven, I gave them a hard tap on the stove top to help flatten them a little while they cooled. After they cooled, I put them in a container with a lid, with wax paper between the layers. Went to get a cookie last night and they're soggy. I mean soggy, like I dropped them in water. Um they are very cake like, not soft and chewy. Very disappointed.

well, the cookies themselves taste mediocre, but the amount of ingredients was absolutely excessive. the recipe says to use an ungreased cookie sheet, which i was a little suspicious of, but I just went along with the recipe..... The cookies will not come off of the sheet.

It thrilled me to see this recipe on your site. I used it 25 yrs. ago and lost it during my move. This is a delicious recipe! This was the best my husband and I ate it up in 12 hrs.  Thanks for a GREAT recipe.
It was pretty good.  I used Durkee Onions on top instead of croutons and they made it ready yummy.  I will make it again.
What a hit last night!!! Everyone  raved about the flavor and asked for seconds. I did however use cream of celery soup because I'm not a mushroom fan. Thank-you for a delicious recipe.
OK. This worked. Great pasta that my children enjoyed.  Any healthy recipe I can get them to eat deserves 5 solid stars!
Very good.  Be sure to squeeze the juice out of the frozen spinach so the casserole isn't runny.
Very cheesy.  I love spinach so I'm willing to try almost anything with it in it.

Karen this is the way I will fix my spinach from now on. Loved it!! I like spinach anyway, but is the BEST! I had to make a couple of substitutions: 1. awesome recipe, i have always liked spinach, but could never get my family to eat it. This casserole turned out awesome! I used french fried onions instead of croutons, next time I might eliminate the salt though. Thanks for this recipe!
Good but I don't think I made it right.  I have to tweak it.
Very good!
We thought this was just ok.  Thanks for posting.

this food is heaven.  i loved it.

Very good! Used NO salt and topped with a 2.8 oz can of french fried onions instead of croutons and a packet of Lipton onion soup mix , instead of the chopped onion, still was a little salty, will use reduced salt soup next time, but still a very, very good recipe.Don't forget to drain the water out of the spinach or it will be soupy.
Delicious! I'm trying to find new ways to incorporate spinach into my diet, and this did the trick! However, as others have said, I would also omit the salt next time, as it was very salty!

Our company and ourselves really liked this recipe it was a good way to make spinach. I used 2% sharp cheddar to make it less fattening and I didn't have any croutons so I used Italian style bread crumbs.

Delicious!

Really nice.  I used fresh silverbeet but it still came out well.

Both casseroles are a great way to eat your veggies!
I only gave this recipe 4 stars because my husband was not a big fan. He thought it would be better served as a side dish. I thought it was pretty good, but I don't think I will be making it again.
Fast, easy and absolutely delicious. I file this under what I call "Pantry Perfect REcipes" as its a tasty dish made from all readily available ingredients that are almost always on hand.

God bless you and your recipe - you got my very picky toddler to eat a whole plate of spinach, and I even hid some chicken in it. THANK YOU! Couple changes - I omitted the egg and the salt. This was delicious! next time i will try it with the awesome homemade french fried onions i found on recipezaar! #44115  they are yummy! thanks for making spinach good! LOL my DH loves it and i USED to hate it!!

This is a great change of pace recipe. Since it's richer than most veggies we eat, it'll be an occassional indulgence. Nice dish for the kids, also subbed mushroom soup with cottage cheese and added dried herbs and garlic cloves to the mixture. Also added chicken sausages in slices.

I had higher hopes for this recipe. I may try it again with fresh spinach. Thanks for sharing!

What can we say??? Absolutely Delicious !!! My Husband and I loved this recipe !  The only thing I did differently was to saute the onions first only because I use frozen chopped onions.  Thank you !!

This was excellent with chicken but I bet it would be just as good without it for a vegetarian meal...If you try that I would double the artichokes and cut them in larger chunks...I think I'll be trying that! Thank you for a keeper recipe Lauralie41! Made for Holiday Tag.

I think this could be a great dish, but mine didn't turn out like the pictures here and was a little too dry. I did leave out the tomatoes, maybe that made a big difference. We really enjoyed this, Lauralie! I made as directed, only substituting canned tomatoes for fresh, which worked very well. I enjoyed this combination of flavors and will certainly make again!  Thanks for a wonderful supper, Lauralie!
A good tasty recipe, but it seemed like too much noodles and not enough of the real substance (chicken, tomatoes, etc.) Adding 1 1/2 pouds of chicken would not have been out of place.
great flavor, we reduced the amount of penne.  could try other pasta other than penne (not my personal favorite).

Thanks for the great recipe! I made a couple additions/substitutions: canned tomatoes instead of fresh, added 1/4 cup of chopped spinach, 1/4 tsp of crushed red pepper and omitted the butter since I used marinated artichokes. My DH and I both thoroughly enjoyed this dish!
We don't give out 5 stars very often.  Will make this again and again.  Didn't sub anything and it was outstanding.  Thanx for posting.

this was a great dish! we made it last night for dinner and it was a big hit! we'll totally make it again! my friend and i actually added greek dressing to it and went together really well! my mom had just the way it was and loved that too! made for Recipe Swap 16

I am thoughly impressed! This was SO tasty. I had to use canned diced tomatoes because we're having a tomato scare (salmonella)just now here in the USA. DH and I made this for dinner tonight and thought it was very nice.  We enjoyed the combination of the feta with the fresh herbs in the pasta. I now see that other reviewers either used either jalapenos or Greek Dressing.  I think either would have done the trick, and if I made this dish again, it would be with those additions.  Thank you for a nice meal.  Made for ZWT4.

Very nice recipe!  I substituted kidney and garbanzo beans instead of chicken and made the dish somewhat vegetarian.  I really enjoyed the flavors as they were very delicate. Thank you for posting this recipe!

My Husband and I really liked this.  Next time, yes there will be a next time, I will not use all of the pasta, it seemed a little much for the chicken amount.  The flavors went together very nicely.  Thanks.

I really liked this recipe! The lemon juice compliments all the flavors. I will be making this again soon. Thanks for the post!
Excellent and easy to make.  I definately would cut back on the amount of pasta as well.  We really enjoyed this recipe!

Was pretty good, although I discovered mid-prep that I did not, in fact have any artichokes handy. Could use more feta, and would agree with other reviews that this works better with olive oil.

I am a huge fan of feta, artichokes and tomatoes, so I really liked this.

Thanks much!  Will be a regular.
Very good. Very easy and quick to make. This is a very nice staple dish to make as a regular dish for a very busy family. Like me! Thanks so much for sharing.

As other reviewers have posted, with tomatoes, artichokes and feta, "How can you go wrong??"

I would like to say however.... all the crumbs and stuff seems to be a waste. I used the same recipie to a "T" . I used 6 butterfly chops...boneless...and I still had about a cup of crumbs left.  But other than that... GREAT. The slight lemon taste from the grated peel was PERFECT. I used the Garlic Herb crumbs like you called for... Spectacular!
Great flavour of sage & parmesan with the hint of lemon.....Turned out very tender.  Have made these twice already.  :)  Thanks for a keeper.  JenT

This was very good.  I followed the directions to the letter and was rewarded with juicy chops with a crunchy crust that was full of flavor. I did make a tiny change and use fresh sage in place of the dried. I will make this often.  Thanks for the recipe!

This is one of the best pork chop recipes that I have tried! Lots of flavor and the chops were moist-not dried out. Aside from my outside grill recipes with various basting sauces, this is way high on my list. Will definately make it again!

This is from Bon Appetit.  I also liked it very much. I used 2 THICK chops and 1/2'd the crumb mixture. I really packed it on since I like lots of crust.  I also used fresh breadcrumbs, which I think worked better than dried.

Terrific recipe Donna. Definitely a keeper. Couldn't find Progresso crumbs so I added some garlic powder and dried parsley to dried breadcrumbs. I used 6 pork chops and used up the leftover egg and crumbs by double dipping the chops into the egg mixture and crumbs (my husband likes a thick coating on pork chops).  Since I don't have an ovenproof skillet, I transferred the chops to a shallow baking dish in a single layer and baked them for about 30-40 minutes until they were fork tender. Thanks Donna for a new family favorite recipe.
A lovely simple recipe thank you. Loved the lemon and parmesan in the crumb mix. We used pork scotch fillet, (a boneless cut that may only be available in Australia) and sage flavoured breadcrumbs.
Excellent recipe! My husband loves pork chops and I'm always looking for new ways to cook them. Thanks for sharing.

This recipe puts a nice thick crust on your chops.  I found that when turning them in the pan to use a fork and you will not disturb the crust.  My chops were 2" thick so I baked 5 minutes longer they were done but could have gone another 5 minutes.  My husband thought he was in heaven!  Thanks for this easy recipe with great taste.
Best Dog gone Chops Ive had in years.. thanks!!

Very good! I used Romano cheese instead since I did not have fresh parmesan on hand, and it was delicious. All that left over breadcrumb mixture made me curious about how it would taste on fish since it has that lemony zing that is great with fish!

My husband and I both enjoyed these but my kids didn't care for them. I think maybe because of the lemon. It is a great recipe with good instructions for any type of coating.
My kids prefer their chops simply with garlic salt and pepper and then broiled. Thanks for sharing!

Absolutely delicious chops! Easy to prepare, too. I did cook them in the oven for 40 minutes at 325F, rather than at a hotter temp for a shorter time, but that was out of necessity as the oven was already in use and so I couldn't jack the heat up. My only quibble would be with the amount listed for the breading; I didn't want to save any for a later use, so I cut the amount in half--I used it to bread 6 large pork chops and I STILL had a lot left over. Other than that waste, I loved this recipe. My son, who is not crazy about pork chops, ate two large ones, so I know I'll be making this one again!

Yummy was the reaction all around to these!  I used a pork loin cut into 1 inch slices and got 6 with enough breading left over in the freezer for a couple more.  Didn't have a lemon so I used lemon peel and only had about 1/2 cup of parmesan too but they still were wonderful.  NIce crust and flavor from the garlic and sage and mine were fork tender.  Thanx!!!

This is a great recipe!  Very tasty. The breadcrumb mixture is outstanding.  It does make a lot more than you need, though.  Next time I'll make about half the amount of breadcrumb mixture, and make it fresh again for other uses.  Thanks for sharing this one!

We really enjoyed this recipe, love the sage and lemon flavourings.  I breaded these in the morning, didn't cook them on the stove top but just popped them in the oven, covered for 15 min and then took the cover off so they could crisp up in the last 5-10 minutes.  Thanks for posting!

This was excellent! I prepared fresh baked bread crumbs for this recipe and omited the lemon rind (didn't have any) and it turned out wonderfully! I couldn't believe how juicy the pork chops were and how crunchy the crust was... Absolutely Wonderful!
This turned out great.  The kids and the hubby ate them up! He loves fried porkchops but I hate the grease. These were a happy medium! Actually beyond happy!
Delicious moist flavorful pork chops!

I used this recipe with chicken breast, and it turned out awesome! YUMMY_SOO GOOD!!! Followed the recipe exactly(well besided the fact that I didn't use pork). I served this with Cauliflower Popcorn  Recipe #115153.

Ron, this Pork Chop recipe is delicious. Quickly browning them to carmelize the parm-sage crust and popping them in the oven made them so flavorful and juicy. I too topped them each with just a teaspoon of lemon-sage sauce (recipe #53845, thanks for suggesting, Sharlene :))garnished with sliced lemons and extra sage for color.I also surrounded the chops with sugar snap peas just steamed then sauteed in EVOO and a diced shallot which made for a colorful presentation. A big hit with the entire family, including 2 teens and a pre-teen. Thanks Ron!
This recipe was awesome and my husband and the guys at his work loved it!  It was easy to make and delicious!  Thanks!

These chops were moist and tender.  I liked the idea of browing them on the stove, yet finishing them off in the oven.  My only problem was that I didn't have an oven-safe skillet, so I preheated a glass baking dish in the oven while I browned the chops on the stove.  Then I just transfered them to the glass dish when it was time to put them in the oven.  Thanks Ron for a great recipe!
5 Stars all around from this household!  We loved this blend of flavors in the coating and the porks was cooked to perfection, moist and tender. Thanks Ron!
I loved this recipe. The chops had alot of flavor and smelled so good while cooking. I will definitely make this again.

Yum, Yum, Yummmm, did I say YUM!  These pork chops were oh so delicious, gave leftover chop to DH for lunch, wished I wouldn't have.  :)  I didn't have lemon, so I grated up some lemon pepper, used lots of it, and could taste a little of the lemon zing, yum.  Thanks for the recipe, can't wait to make this again.
Great!  Turned out as I expected.  No changes made. Thanks

I must agree with the others that posted to this recipe. This was excellent! I was looking for a new recipe for pork chops, and am extremely satisfied that I tried this particular one. I didn't change a thing, and it came out wonderfully. Thank you for sharing.
Excellent! My husband isn't a big fan of pork chops, but he certainly liked this dish as did I!

My DH really liked this and said he'd like to have it again.  I thought it was fine but bland.  I used boneless pork chops and cooked them for 8 minutes in the oven.  I served this with scalloped potatoes and   Cauliflower Popcorn #115153.
This is one of my absolute favorite recipes.  Very easy to make, and just delicious.  I've made it often using small pork tenderloins (baking a bit longer).

This was great!  I gathered all my ingredients and when I went to my spice cabinet....I had no sage!  I made it anyway following the directions exactly and the flavor was still yummy.  Next time, I will make sure I have sage for that added flavor.  Thanks for posting!

I've used this awesome recipe probably half a dozen times now. While printing it off (again) I realized I'd never gotten around to rating these fabulous chops. These are excellent, Ron, and this will continue to be one of my favorite recipes for chops. Thanks so much for sharing it.

I made this today and loved it! The chops turned out so tender and tasty. I ended up just eyeing the amount of breadcrumbs and cheese that I would need. It turned out just about right and I didn't waste hardly any at all.  Thank you for the recipe.  I will definantly make again.
Easy to make and we enjoyed them.  I suggest making half of the breadcrumb mixture for 4 pork chops.  I like how the breading really stuck to the pork after being cooked.  Thanks!
My daughter made this today. It came out tasty and tender.

I really liked these. What can I say that hasn't been said? I especially loved the lemon zest and got to use a new citrus zester.  My kids were split on this dish. One is super picky so I took the breading off for him.  The other asked for some tomato sauce for dipping. Thanks for an easy and different flavored pork chop recipe!

To die for!!!!  I made this dish for my bf who travels all the time and he just loves it when I make him a homecooked meal.  He just ooohh'd and aaahh'd over this dish.  I made one little addition to this recipe.  I added a little lemon juice to the egg mixture.. I think it really enhanced the lemony flavor.

I've made this a few times and kept forgetting to review it!  My DH and I love the combo of flavors and how crispy the crust ends up!  The change I made was that I first rub the bare pork chops with extra sage, garlic powder, salt, and pepper for an extra boost of flavor (personal preference). The only difference I'll make on my third attempt is that I'll skip coating it in flour before coating it in the parmesan-sage crust because the flour just seems to make it slip off when you go to cut into it and take a bite.  You're right though- definitely the way a pork chop should be- Thanks!

Excellent pork chops! ( I also substituted minced fresh sage leaves. I served it with the lemon-sage sauce from a similar recipe for chicken, Recipe #53845 and it was to die for (although the chops are excellent without the sauce as well). Rounded out the meal with a salad with Recipe #144172 and Recipe #144172. (See photo of whole plate I posted). Mmmm can't wait to make these again.
Really good.  I think the sage and Parmesan made these so good.  I sliced a pork  loin into 1/2 inch slices, so mine cooked a bit more quickly.

These pork chops are great!  Used dried sage from last year's garden, dried breadcrumbs instead of fresh, and added just a little cayenne pepper to the flour.  I can never leave well enough alone! This was as good as everyone said ... most important, the pork was tender, not dry and chewy. These were okay, but not a favorite.  But I am not a big fan of pork chops to begin with.  I was looking for a recipe that I could use some pork chops up, and this was sufficient for the task, but kind of bland.  Thanks!

These pork chops were very tasty and tender! Very easy to prepare and throw in the oven. I did not use butter and lemon, only because I had neither,and used olive in place of the butter, I can only imagine how much better they would be with the lemon zest.
This is actually the 2nd time I have made these, the first time I had no sage  or lemon and used in its place lemon thyme and basil with equally pleasing results.
Nice, but they ended up overcooked.  I needed to monitor the oven time closer.

Yummy!  I didn't have the seasoned bread crumbs or the sage so I added some italian seasoning instead and it came out wonderful.  I can't wait to try it with the correct ingredients.  Thank you Donna!

We liked this but I found the chops were a bit dry.  I would try this again and maybe reduce the oven to 375. Thx for posting.
These were so good! We had thick porkchops and they were not dry. I want to have them again!

This is our new favorite pork chop recipe.

DIVINE.....these are awesome.  I made these last night for dinner and they were enjoyed by all.  The parmesan and sage are wonderful compliments to the pork. Wouldn't change a thing!  They were deliciously moist and flavorful.  Quite simple to prepare, with wonderful results.  I served them with mashed potatoes and honey glazed roasted mushrooms.  Yum!
Delicious pork chops! Made exactly as directed. Thanks for posting.
this was great!! i even accidentally knocked the seasoning mixture on one of my dogs and she even liked it!!! LOL!!

Fantastic!

This were so juicy and delicious!  I was tired of making the same old fried chops and having them turn out tough.  This recipe solved that problem and my husband loved them too.  Definitely making them again!

I agree - really good!

Thanks.

I liked the crust flavor and it does make a lot of crumbs.  I used the 1" thick chops and they were not as tender as I would have liked after the recommended cooking time.  I will probably make these again, but I will use thinner chops.  Thanks for the recipe.
Very nice simple recipe, chops come out tender and very tasty. Thanks for sharing!
These pork chops have great flavor. You must not omit the lemon rind--it makes this dish. I'll be making this one again and again! Great recipe.

Pork Chops are not usually my favorite thing to make, but this recipe is really really good.  The only thing is I had way too much of the parmesan cheese/breadcrumbs portion so next time I think I'll cut that in half. Great recipe...we really enjoyed these pork chops, mine were pretty big so it took longer to cook, otherwise followed recipe to the letter...

Had with twice baked potatoes and roasted asparagus for a meal to remember.  These chops are tender, and cooked up really easy.  I used Italian bread crumbs which added to the flavor. This was OK.  Had a nice flavor, but the pork chops turn out mushy on the bottom after cooking in the oven.  The addition of lemon is really nice with the pork.  Thanks.
First there is way to much coating for 4 chops. I didn't use butter. Baked in oven on a rack to avoid to mushy part. It was very good but I added some season salt to enhance the flavor.

My kids and I had 2 each we liked them so well!  I loved the combination of flavors from the sage and cheese.   I used Italian bread crumbs for mine.  Kids say these are to be made again, and I have to agree.   We loved them!  Thanks Donna!

Wow. This was DElicious! I made half the breading mixture and STILL had way too much! I used 1 egg and half the flour, too. Maybe my chops were just small...but I still had just a little leftover that way. Would have been a waste to do more. Also, I used 1T butter and a dash of EVOO. BUT WOW. These chops were soooo tender and buttery...yum! I'll make them again for sure!
Hubby made this for dinner.  He added a little bit of white wine and used panko bread crumbs.  It was very good.  Nice and moist.  Thanks for sharing!
This a great flavorful recipe and the one I like to use for boneless port chops if I have the time to do all the breading. It's worth it though!  Thank you, Donna!

Very good pork chops. My husband and I were hesitant in trying different kinds of pork chops since we have already found our favorite.(Kind of like the saying if its not broke, don't fix it.) WOW! These were so good!  I loved the zip of the lemon zest. What a nice combination of flavours. Thank you for posting this, I'll be using it again for sure!
Great!  I added ample butter to the left-over bread crumb's and added them around the chop's when about halfway done.

My husband loves this!!  Great recipe, thank you so much for sharing!

Great tasting pork chops.  Was looking for something different and this was delicious.  Loved that they are cooked in oven.  Bursting with flavors.

This was great! Husband gave it 4 1/2 stars. I used panko bread crumbs and quite a bite more sage than called for. I served it with roasted asparagus and roasted red potatoes flavored with. These are very good pork chops. My chops were still partially frozen when I put them in the pan and cooked through very nicely after browning and baking 25 minutes. I saved the breadcrumbs (in the freezer) to make this again--there really were a lot of breadcrumbs! Thanks for a great recipe, Donna!
Edited to add: this has become my go-to recipe for pork chops.

These were awesome chops :)

Fantastic, my husband loved them! I didn't have lemon, but he didn't seem to notice. Next time, I will try it with lemon. Thank you!

Donna all I can say is MMM MMM GOOD!!!!!! This is a fantstic way to make pork chops. They came out juicy and the hint of lemon was AWESOME! I used a combination of Italian flavored panko crumbs and regular panko crumbs because I was out of other bread crumbs. I also skipped the parmesan (I know, I know - it's even in the title) because what I had on hand was shredded rather than grated and I didn't want to waste it. (I would have just moved on to another recipe, but by that point I was completely out of time.) Also due to the time crunch I skipped both the flour and the egg steps and just put the wet chops in the crumbs, like you do with commercial Shake n Bake. I baked them on a wire rack over the pan and used a probe thermometer set to 150. I don't know how long they took, but it was quick and might have been close to the stated time.
