Thanks for posting - I'm sure I'll be making them again.  -M =)
Excellent and easy!  I made only half a recipe of the glaze and that was plenty.

I LOVE these cookies!!  They are like little mini pumpkin cakes.  I did add a little nutmeg to the dry ingredients, but stuck to the recipe otherwise.  Baked them for the full 12 minutes and they came out nice and soft and full of pumpkin flavor.  Might try adding so raisins next time just to be experimental!  :)  The glaze is sweet, but I didn't find that it overpowered the cookies in any way.  I liked the "caramely" flavor of it.  I brushed a thin glaze over the cookies with a basting brush.  I'll only make half the glaze next time since I had a lot left over.  Thanks for my new favorite cookie!!!
Loved it!  Added nutmeg to it....fantastic!!!!

This is a great soft cookie, but I felt it needed more spice added ... so I am adding nutmeg and ground cloves to the next batch I make (plus some chopped walnuts).  Definitely keep the glaze in the pan on a burner turned to a low setting to keep it from solidifying .... it made just enough for the cookies.  Do not halve the recipe for the glaze as some have stated ... it takes it all (depends upon how much icing  you put on each cookie). The glaze is the same as the frosting we put on spice cakes, jam cake, and zucchini bread.  It hardens quickly!
Great recipe! My husband took one bite and announced that he'd found a new favorite cookie. I added one tespoon of apple pie spice since I was out of nutmeg. This is definitely a recipe to keep!

This was a good and easy recipe.  It reminded me of pumpkin bread with glaze.  Very sweet... and very much a dessert.  I might cut back on the powdered sugar in the glaze and just let it cool a bit for spreading consistency next time.  My husband and son have gobbled up at least 1/2 of them in the last 24 hours.  Thanks!
These were excellent, but I only used about half the frosting, and added nutmeg, cloves and ginger.  They made a nice Halloween treat for those not trick-or-treating!

Boy, I've made other pumpkin cookies, but these are sooo tasty!  They didn't spread as nicely as the cookies in the picture, but who cares when they taste so rich.  I omitted the glaze as I wanted to concentrate on the pumpkin flavor...thanks for a new favorite Sara!

The name of this recipe says it all. These are absolutely the best pumpkin cookies I've ever had. They were so good right from the oven that we left off the glaze. We could not imagine the glaze could improve them. I added about 1/4 tsp. of pumpkin pie spice after reading the other reviews. This is a great recipe. Thanks for posting!
I thought these were sooo yummy.  They remind me of the top of a cupcake.  Very soft, delicate and the icing is yumy!  Hubby said they were too sweet though.

If I would have rated this cookie recipe the day I made it, I would have only given it three stars.  It's a good thing I waited because these cookies taste soooooooooo much better the second day!!!  The day I made them, the cookies seemed a little bland and the glaze seemed a little sweet.  However, after the second day, the glaze and cookie seemed to join forces to bring out a full body of flavor.  The only change I made was to sprinkle the glazed cookies with chopped walnuts. Great recipe..........if you have the patience to wait for the flavors to blend!  Thanks, Sara!

When I made these my reaction was at the first bite...."Oh my god" These are the BEST! Everyone loved them!! I only wish they would freeze well so I could pull one out whenever I crave one. Thanks for the great recipe!!!

First time I tried it I was a little too liberal with the pumpkin and used more than 1 cup. The result were cookies that were too moist, they fell apart. This time I measured more accurately and they came out fantastic, the whole family loved them. I am making another batch today. Didn't have brandy or liqueur so I used fresh squeezed OJ and some orange rind. A fantastic way to use that leftover cup of pumpkin after making pumpkin pie. Thanks for the recipe, Sara, it's a new family favourite!

Every year my church has a cookie exchange before Christmas.  The little old ladies were surprised when a 53 year old man showed up with his pumpkin cookies.  They were a big hit!  Made as discribed except I used pumpkin spice instead of straight cinnamon.  I used Orange Glaze #73743 instead of the listed glaze.  The combo was fantastic.
Big hit at Pumpkin carving party! I definitely agree with just drizzling the glaze...it's very sweet!! Great recipe all around.
These cookies have good flavor.  I omitted the glaze and sprinkled powdered sugar.  However, they didn't keep well, getting too crumbly and soft.  I baked them the full twelve minutes.

These went over very well- I have been asked for the recipe numerous times after making them.  The glaze is really integral to the cookies- I thought they were a little bland without it. Overall, this is not my favorite cookie recipe ever, but I have had such good feedback from everyone who has tried them that I will definitely make them again.

Origianlly, I found these cookies  a bit too bland for my taste. I thought I would not be making them again. THEN I ate the remaining cookies the next day. Wow, what a difference! The flavor was more intense and the texture had become smoother. 

I find myself craving them again. This time I will let the cookies sit overnight before serving.

Thanks for this "sleeper" cookie.
the best cookie we ever had..10 stars

Fabulous! These cookies are amazingly simple and easy. They turn out like perfectly bite-sized cakes if you use a cookie baller and have quickly become a regularly requested favorite. I omit the icing and serve them plain, and my bf AND his neices and nephew practically inhale them. Because they are so soft and moist, I keep them cool (they are wonderful cold from the fridge with milk) for the day or two it takes for them to disappear. Thank you for this wonderful recipe!

Thank you for this recipe! My sister loves pumpkin so I made this for her, she comes home today so I will see her verdict, but I had a bite and it tastes great! My mum agreed. It wasn't too much of a fuss to make, the frosting is perfect, I did add 1tsp of nutmeg like some of the reviews suggested. They smelt glorious too :)
I'm not a big fan of cake-like cookies, but my husband liked these.  They were really easy to make.  Just be sure to let the cookies cool COMPLETELY before icing them.  Thanks for sharing!

These really are THE BEST pumpkin cookies! I am in trouble because I am supposed to take these to an open house tomorrow...I hope I don't eat them all before I get there!!! I also added a teaspoon of nutmeg, and I definitely wouldn't leave that out! This is a great recipe!
Three words...oh my god.  The name says it all.  Best pumpkin cookies EVER! :)

We found these unbearably sweet, to the point we didn't feel comfortable eating them. I even tried eating one without any icing and found the plain cookie too sweet.  I would definitely cut back on some of the sugar and probably avoid the icing.  Also, they were very soft cookies, kind of mushy.  Maybe because I used fresh pumpkin? Not sure.

These cookies were good however there was the slightest baking soda-y flavour in the taste.  As well, due to the extremely soft texture they would have been better with the addition of nuts, chips or raisins.

My girls (ages 8 and 5) made these yesterday and they are a huge hit!  Aside from how wonderfully yummy they are, I don't think I saw mention of how heavenly my kitchen smelled while baking them!!  The girls used the entire can of pumpkin which I only now realized was in error.  Other than not really flattening out, they were just fine!  We ate about half of the batch before I got around to making the glaze for them and they are great plain, but the glaze is definitely worth any extra effort!!  I have actually been searching for over TEN years for this glaze recipe.  I had something very similar on cinnamon rolls in a little cafe, but have never been able to recreate anything that resembled it.  Thank you for ending my decade of searching and for providing a new, wonderful cookie to our kitchen!!

I don't even have these in the oven yet and already KNOW they're going to be good. The raw batter has a light, velvety feel.(It looks like an expensive facial treatment! lol) I can hardly wait to bake them off and eat the finished product! I did some minor tweaking: used 1 whole 14 oz can of pumpkin (it was just a few tablespoons more than 1 cup!) and I spiced it just like a pumpkin pie (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves).
I really liked these, they are not too sweet and have a great texture. I did not use the frosting yet, but that sounds like it will be real good

This makes a very moist delicious cookie. It is a winner. I added 1/4 tsp. nutmeg plus 3/4 tsp. pumpkin pie spice. I used less confectioner's sugar, butter and milk for the glaze and it still made PLENTY. I also froze a few left over cookies and a couple weeks later ate them straight out of the freezer since I did not want to wait for them to defrost. YUMMY! They were absolutely delicious, so I have no hesitation recommending freezing them. The only thing is I do not know how they would be after defrosting since we ate them all when they first came out of the freezer!
YUMMY!  They are absolutely delish and even better the second day.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe.
These are amazing! So soft and delicious. I added a tsp of nutmeg and glazed them with a basic powdered sugar and milk icing instead of the penuche glaze.

These cookies are very good. I tried one straight out of the oven expecting them to be a little bland based on a previous review, but they were very good. I made them last night for Thanksgiving tomorrow, so hopefully they will keep OK. I'm wondering if I should refrigerate them. They are very delicate and moist cookies. I've let four people try them so far and everyone has said positive things. I did not use the glaze as I thought they were sweet enough on their own. Thank you for the great recipe!

Fantastic cookies. Thank you for adding to my love of Pumpkin baked goods. I love the delicate cakey texture. Even my 4 year old who protested "Not pumpkin cookies!" while we were making them, is begging for more. I did replace one teaspoons of cinnamon with one teaspoon of Pumpkin Pie spice.

It was my week to make the snacks for my dd's kindergarten class. I thought this would be a nice treat for them...cookies but with some healthy pumpkin. Well, the cookies never made it to school. These are soft little pumpkin pillows. Not dense and cakey like I expected, they literally melt in your mouth. EXCELLENT! EXCELLENT cookies. Thank you for this recipe. It's gone straight into my special favorite recipe binder. :D

Wow, these are yummy.  I sent the ones I didn't eat into work w/ dh for his Christmas party.  He had a few requests for the recipe.  Don't pass on the glaze, it really sets these cookies apart.  Do be careful when you are putting the glaze on, it's extremely HOT!  I burned myself a couple of times not paying attention :).  These are going to become a Christmas classic at my house!

My DH is not a huge fan of pumpkin, but he adored these cookies. I don't love things that are too sweet, so I was a little worried about glazing after reading prior comments, but the glaze was perfect. It definitely made the cookie. This is a keeper recipe.

these are so amazing!
i made my first batch without the addition of nutmeg, and i was a bit worried about the baking soda-ee taste, but by the next day (when they were served) i proclaimed them my favorite cookie of all time. even my grandmother agrees that they are to die for.
my next 2 batches i added in about a teaspoon or so of nutmeg as i saw others had, and that really fixed the baking soda problem, making them scrumptious out of the oven, but they werent exactly "to die for," the next day like my first batch was.
im sticking to the original recipe from now on.
I made these cookies for the second time this year.  They are easy to make and taste great.  The cookies stay nice and soft and the glaze sets up perfectly.   Thanks.

These are very, very good cookies!  I had made a note to add some nutmeg and raisins -- but completely overlooked it.  The next time I make them, I'm going to add those two ingredients.  I used half regular sugar and half Splenda.  For the brown sugar, I used all Splenda.  For the glaze, I also used the Splenda brown sugar.  It doesn't make the cookies sugar free, but it does cut back on the amount of sugar.  I only got 36 cookies -- but I think my cookie scoop is more like 2 T. instead of just one.  I used my silicone basting brush for the glaze as suggested by Sara.  It worked like a dream -- I also took her advice and left the glaze on low in the pan while I applied it.  I might also add a few chopped walnuts the next time -- but I don't want to change the recipe too much -- the cookies are fabulous just the way the recipe is written.  Thanks for sharing, Sara.
I took these cookies to a cookie exchange for Christmas and eventually got emails from everyone there asking me for the recipe! Always a hit!

Great cookies. Love the pillowy texture. I don't love how the glaze gets so crunchy but I guess that's just what glazes do. Didn't change a thing.. Thanks a lot! Will make again. *** Update: In agreement with Southern Polar Bear, the cookies are even better the next day and days after that.. If they last!

these cookies are delicious and so so easy to make low fat!  i eliminated most of the butter (used 1 tablespoon) and substituted with extra pumpkin (mostly because i wanted to use up the entire 15oz can!) .. amazing!!  this recipe is definitely forgiving and easy to "play with".  thanks for sharing.

My nephew requested pumpkin cookies at our summer cookie extravaganza and I chose these. It was a very forgiving recipe for a kid to make. He added chocolate chips and didn't want frosting but they were still popular.

Very Yummy! Not really like a cookie though. They were pretty much just tiny pumpkin breads, which tasted great, but I was hoping for something more crunchy. Still, the flavor was great and I added a little bit of ground cloves too. Yum!
awesome!!! easy to make thanks for the tip on keeping the glaze warm.
A simple, yummy fall treat!  Perfect for today's gloomy weather! :)

Awesome cookies! I added 1 cup of golden raisins ( soake first in boiling hot water for 1 hour, then drain and add to batter: they plump up beautifully!) and 1 cup of chopped pecans. I spread on some store bought cream cheese icing...OMG to die for! A family favorite in our home during the holidays!
They are so moist! I didn't even use the glaze. Definately make again

OMG!!!! This is why I love the Zaar.  I found this recipe today and wanted to try it since I had some left over pumpkin from making bread.  Wow!!!  I heard cheers from everyone.  It is so good and yummy.  I called them pumpkin pillows.  I don't think the frosting is too sweet but I was very conservative with it and did not put a lot.  I followed the recipe exactly and I really don't think it needs anything else.  It is a keeper for sure.  Thanks for sharing such a special recipe.  Kids loved it when they came home from school and smelled the goodies baking.
The name says it all....these cookies are the best I've ever had! I have made these twice now.  I frost them with a cream cheese frosting.  Thanks for the amazing recipe!

Awesome, moist, and cakey!  I kind of messed up the frosting as it turned out too runny (too much milk since I didn't measure it out) but they taste amazing!  I had a whole can of pumpkin puree so I put the full 15 oz. into the batter, but added a 1/2 cup of whole oatmeal and they turned out lovely!  I also added some ginger and more cinnamon.  Awesome recipe!  I'm definitely going to make it again.

Wow, delicious! Thanks for the tip about the silicone basting brush. I had picked a couple up and was going to use them for BBQ, but now I have found another way of using them--icing these cookies. My glaze never did set up--not sure what I did wrong, but the cookies were great. Will make again and try the glaze again. Thanks for a keeper.

made these today and they turned out really good. my youngest child said it was like eating pumkin pie with your fingers. didn't have the confectioners sugar to make the glaze for the top but they tasted great without it. will try it next time. thanks for the recipe!
My picky kids ate these before I could get the frosting on them. What more can be said? Thank you for sharing this nice Fall recipe.
These were so so good. I am not a big fan of pumpkin but we all loved these. They were soft and sweet. I could not have asked for anything better.
Everyone enjoyed these cookies and the dish was empty in no time!  I made for my annual neighborhood Halloween party, and they were great!  Thanks for sharing!
Everyone at my Halloween party loved these cookies!  They will be made on a regular basis now!
I was looking for some type of "fall cookie" and these were the perfect one!  A hit with everybody.
I have recieved so many rave reviews and requests for this recipe after I made it! Thanks :-)

This is the second time i have made these, they are so good.  This time i subbed in oil for butter and it still tasted amazing!  also used pumpkin from an actual pumpkin my friend grew(had to squeeze out so much water, lol).  and the glaze is great as well, subbed in oil for butter too and it is still fantastic.  i got like 30 cookies but i made them sort of big.  Love em! my friends have been nagging me since last year to make these again!

After I read the reviews, I had to try these right away, but was disappointed with the outcome.  I followed most of the recipe, except I sub. splenda for the sugar.  I felt they were a little bland.  The glaze was awesome tasting by itself, but got lost once it was added to the cookies.  I might try to make them again without splenda and see if that makes a difference.

These were good cookies. They remind me of pumpkin bread with icing. They are like mini pumpkin breads! Plain without the icing, though. I did not have any brown sugar so I used regular sugar with molasses- yummy! Nice way to use some extra pumpkin from my garden.
These were great with or without the frosting.
These ARE the best pumpkin cookies and didn't even last a day in my house!  Thanks for the recipe.
Yummy, are these tasty. I am just using some cream cheese frosting for mine. Thanks for posting this great seasonal treat!

I made these cookies and my sister made a different recipe for pumpkin cookies. We took them to my mom's for the family. Everyone thought that this recipe was the best and I think it was because of the penuche glaze. Sis put a cream cheese gaze on hers. Great Recipe!!!
These were great cookies more of a cake consistency than cookie.  The frosting was a little too runny and made a complete mess for me.  I'll probably leave it off next time.  Very tasty tho!

AWESOME!  Everyone loved these, even those who don't typically like pumpkin.  My 21 month old couldn't get enough.  The glaze is tricky but very good.  I only used 1 1/2 cups of the confectioners sugar.  I am big on cream cheese icing, so I am going to use it next time.  Very yummy nonetheless!

These really are the best pumpkin cookies ever!! I have been making them for a few years now around the holidays. Everyone always asks for the recipe! I can't believe I have waited so long to write a review because they are soo good! I also like to use the cream cheese iceing. Thank you for the post Sara in FL!!
These cookies are the bomb! You won't stop eating them. Beware!

I agree with Huntergirl, these ARE the best pumpkin cookies.  The frosting is sooo yummy, the taste reminds me of something (haven't thought of what yet). The first pan the cookies turned out very thin and didnt cook good, so I added more flour to the batter. Worked great!!! Thanks Sara!!
UPDATE: I realized the reason the first batch turned out runny was because I had melted the butter for the batter instead of having it room temperature. For those who prefer thinner cookies, have the butter melted. For thick cake like cookies, have butter at room temp. Also, the frosting is MUCH better if you use real butter, not margerine. :)
Fantastic Cookies, these were a huge hit at the Turduken Party!!
Nice soft cookie. I cut the recipe in half, except I used 1/4 cup butter and 3/4 cup pumpkin. I got 25 small cookies that taste great. I didn't use the icing, I'm trying to save calories!

I am sorry but these just did not work for me.  The cookies fell completely flat (could be the high altitude) and were so moist that they were falling apart and the icing was tooo sweet for me.  They looked so yummy from the pictures I was really looking forward to them but they didn't turn out for me...sorry!
Made these again, but used Cream Cheese Frosting Recipe #55530 to frost them. They were MORE than a huge hit. I had about 10 people ask me for the recipe! Delicious!

Wow! I have finally found the ultimate pumpkin cookie recipe! These cookies are more like little cakes. The first time I made them was for a holiday party at work. Everyone raved over them and wanted the recipe! I did change it up a bit. Instead of the 2 teaspoons of cinnamon, I used 1 teaspoon of cinnamon and 1 teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice. They turned out fabulous although I only got about 2 dozen out of the recipe - but I do like big cookies! :)

these were so yummy!  as others suggested I did add a little nutmeg and cloves, but otherwise stuck to the recipe.  These come out delicate and soft, moist yet light.  I used maybe 1/4 of the glaze recipe and thought that was just right, I just took the pot off the stove and used my whisk to drizzle the glaze over the cookies.  These are "mild" cookies, not like the overly sweet kind we normally have.  But oh so addictive!

I loved the cookies, but the glaze wasn't quite what I was hoping for. The butter and brown sugar combined gave it a nutty flavor, which was good, but just not what I anticipated. From the pictures posted I expected it to taste a little more creamy. I would make these again but I think next time I will try one of the other frosting suggestions, such as the citrus cream cheese.

These are the best pumpkin cookies I ave ever made!  I skipped the glazed and instead frosted them with cream cheese frosting then dusted then with cinnamon.  It was amazing!  I brought them to a friend's house for Thanksgiving and his family ate them all up within a few hours! I will definitely make these again!

I had several pumpkins left from halloween and needed to get them used up.  I was looking for additional pumpkin recipes to use the pumpkin in, and I thought this one was perfect.  I actually made pumpkin creme sandwich cookies.  I made a creme filling with 1/4 cup real butter, 7oz marshmallow creme, and 4 oz cream cheese, plus enough powdered sugar to take away the stickiness, probably about 1/2 cup.  They turned out very good.  Thanks for the recipe :)

i had a terrible time with these cookies!  i finally ended up increasing the baking time to 20 minutes to get them firm enough to handle.  My family found them bland and the icing waaay too sweet.  i won't make them again.

I wanted a quick recipe to use up some of the partial can of pumpkin that I had left at Thanksgiving.  I whipped these up without the glaze and they were very tasty!  I'm enjoying having them with my Thanksgiving leftovers to give that great flavor of pumpkin and cinnamon!
By far the BEST pumpkin cookie ever! The frosting is perfect! Thanks!
Wow! These are so good! Definitely love the glaze. I used 2 cups confectioners suger. These are really nice and soft and I can't wait to make again!
Someone said their to sweet, gee their cookies.   I would  walk miles in lots of snow for a plate and some coffee. Yummie!

Oh my goodness, these were so good! I experimented making bigger cookies, and I found they were the best. Cakey, and soft. I also used pumpkin pie spice instead of the cinnamon, and used E.D. Smith's pumpkin which was already spiced. I found them to be really nicely spiced. These will become favourites!

Wow! What more can I say? These were wonderful. My DH likes them better without the glaze, but I thought the glaze made them taste over the top. This isn't your traditional, run-of-the-mill cookie. A wonderful change of pace. Will be making these for our Christmas party for people to enjoy. I'll make sure to have copies of this recipe ready to hand out. Thanks for an outstanding cookie.

My new *favorite* cookie!  Only had Golden, not dark brown sugar, so I added 1 TBS of regular molassas to both batter and glaze.  Did add 1 tsp. freshly grated nutmeg to batter.  Absolutely TERRIFIC - THANKS!
OMG! These are great! Its like a nice moist slice of pumpkin bread, only a cookie! I took another reviewer's advice and added pumpkin pie spice to the mix. A really GREAT cookie!
These are great cake-cookies. I didn't make the glaze. They're sweet enough already. Also, I subbed the cinnamon for pumpkin pie spice mix.

I've had a can of pumpkin in my cabinet since November, and I gave this a whirl as a result.  I am SO glad I did.  These cookies are so light and...cloud like.  They also make your house smell great as you're baking (always a cool bonus!)

These cookies are great!!  My husband requests these quite frequently!  Nice and moist, and easy to make!  We like to add chocolate chips or cinnamon chips too!  Oh, and so yummy in the freezer!  NUM!
These were fantastic~we couldn't stop eating them.   They were gone before we went to bed the day I made them!  I omitted the icing and threw in some milk chocolate chips.  HEAVEN!

Hi Sara,  thank you for sharing this recipe.  It is incredible.  Like you said,  it is cake like.  I usually don't like cake like cookies but the flavor to these are AWESOME with or without frosting.  I frosted with some cream cheese icing and some with your frosting recipe.  My family just loves these.  Thank you again.  Keeper.

These cookies are amazing.......and sooooooo addictive.  I cannot stop eating them.  They are so soft and very "cakey"  and quite different from your average cookie.  I will make these again and again.  Thanks  for the great recipe!

Awesome cookies.  I made them as directed, but then topped them with chopped toasted pecans.  The pecans stuck to the icing - was great either way.  I also froze some - defrosted great also.  Best cookies ever.

i have been making these for years and just realized i haven't reviewed them yet!  i make these every year now and look forward to them.  they are great to take to parties as everyone always loves them.

This is one best recipe for pumpkin cookies I've ever tasted!! I decided to try it out since fall is in the air lately & boy were they a hit!! Everyone asked for the recipe. One note I would like to make: I like my cookies soft & chewy so I usually take them out of the oven early. With this recipe, you do not need to do this. The cookies are moist & chewy at the recommended cooking time.
Very good cookies. I used 1 tsp. cinnamon and 1 tsp. pumpkin pie spice. They are a very soft cookies. The glaze compliments the cookie very well. Delicious!

Very good.  I love the glaze!  It reminds me of a donut glaze.  I'm a cookie lover but I wouldnt really call these cookies, it needs a different name.  I think I will call them Pumpkin Puffs.  Would also be great baked in a madeline pan.
Very good cookie.  I had a lot of the glaze left over.  The glaze was good but I think next time I will cut it in half.  Thanks for sharing!
Delicious. I substituted the canned pumpkin for canned pumpkin pie mix and instead of the glaze on top I added white chocolate chips. BIG HIT! Incredible.

These are great.  They are light and tasty.  My 5 year old put them out on the pans for me.  I made as directed except with the addition of a tiny bit of cloves and I used the combination of margarine and shortening due to my dayhome girls allergy to milk products.  I didnt make the glaze...I went with a cream cheese drizzle over the top.  Thanks they are a great easy treat.

i love these cookies, although some of my friends/family have mixed reactions to them. my mother said something along the lines of they're not a cookie, it's a small cake!
but i love that about them, they're soft and moist and similar to madeleines. however, i did not make the glaze, and used some canned cream cheese frosting on some. but i love them as is!
Made exactly as described, delicious! The glaze recipe made a LOT, I think a half batch would be plenty. But still, very good cookies.
Totally yummy cookies, I have not even frosted them yet and am loving them!  I added a few chocolate chips when I was down to the last pan and they are excellent. thanks.

I was surprised that I didn't like these. I made them with cream cheese icing, and dyed it orange, for Halloween of course. It looked like melted cheese, my fault of course. I sent them to work with my boyfriend, who loved them, and got rave reviews from his office. One girl even said, "those are like the best pumpkin things I have ever had in my life." Great recipe, just not for my tastes.

(3.5 stars) I love how the pumpkin flavor comes through.  Good cookie, but doubtfully THE best.

Glazed: good, I liked it; my dad would prefer cream cheese frosting
Plain: unpleasantly bland
Plain with pecans: unpleasantly bland, pretty texture
Plain with semi-sweet chips: good but chocolate smothers pumpkin flavor
I think these were delicious! I used pumpkin pie spice instead of the cinnamon. I will be making these many times this fall.

Guess how I made this? Made the dough in my bread machine which I often do with roll doughs. Turned out great. Thought those with the machines that had never done this before just might give it a try. Bet you'l love it. JH

YUM-O! Easy Cookie to make, but the glaze definitely makes the cookie.  The glaze will harden up quickly so be sure to have an extra set of hands if you plan on adding the chopped walnuts.  I may try to add them directly to the glaze to begin with next time.  Also the glaze seems to work better (less overpowering) when it is drizzled on instead of painted on top. Thumbs way up & will be making again very soon.
these were wonderful! i added just a little more cinnamon for personal taste.
Mmmmm... so good. I made a cream cheese glaze/icing for my cookies, but only iced half of them; I think the icing is overkill and the cookies are fabulous unadorned.
These cookies were really easy!  I thought they were pretty bland when they were first out, but after they were cooled and glazed they were amazing.

My favorite cookies in the world! I love these cookies! I've been cooking for team of middle school wrestlers, and these were the only cookies they actually thought to ask for repeat of. I made them ahead of time for the kids once and that was a mistake. I had to make them again :) I LOVE these cookies.
Edited to add: 
I've adapted these also to make for my toddlers. I cut out the butter, adding instead a TB of oil and doubling the pumpkin. I then cut the sugar nearly in half. I also used whole grain spelt flour and I did replace the egg with flax meal and water (egg sensitivity). I also did not glaze them. The kids loved them - when I was cleaning the bathroom, they snuck off to eat more! DH even liked them this way and if it's not sweet enough for you, you can still glaze them - still taste amazing, plus you get a little less sugar and more pumpkin! They do take a little longer to cook this way though.

Wow! These are good. Of course I changed it. I can't help myself. I used 1/2 whole wheat flour and 1/2 all purpose flour. I cut back 1/4 cup of butter and added 1/4 cup of maple syrup. I stirred in chopped pecans at the end. This is a solid recipe. I will make these again and might add some flax seed and oats next time. Thanks. It feels like fall at my house.
Delicious and easy to make with the kiddos!
This is my new favorite fall cookie.  I agree with others that these taste even better the next day.
DELICIOUS!! The best pumpkin cookies, maybe even cookies I have ever had!
These were so soft and delicious, I will be making again on  Thanksgiving.

Wow these were good! I'm making my second batch in as many weeks. The first time, I accidentally put in 1/4 C of each sugar instead of 1/2 C. I think this made the cookie the perfect balance to the super-sweet icing, so I'm cutting the sugar in half again this time.

The five star rating is for the GREAT cookies. I didn't make your penuche glaze. Instead I frosted them with some cream cheese frosting. These cookies are soft and wonderful. They only lasted a day at my house. I will be making them again for sure. Thanks.

Sara in FL you have a great recipe here. And laugh2survive thanks for the modifications. Even with all the healthy changes except the eggs these were really good. I didn't even bother to glaze them and they were good. I did use squash instead of pumpkin because the garden really did well in that area this year. These will be made for the holidays with the glaze.
Update: Made these for Thanksgiving...everybody loved them,  and when I did make them with 1/2 the fat,  and whole grains.  I made 1/2 a batch of penuche and it was plenty.  These went even faster than the cheesecake.

Very tasty, cake-like cookies.  I took laugh2survive's suggestion on doubling the pumpkin and just adding a tablespoon of oil--it was great! Plus, it makes me feel so much better about eating and making these when I know I cut out a whole cup of butter! And please note, these are great without the butter, and yes, I mean great cookies (they don't taste like healthy biscuits!) Anyhow, I also subbed 1/2 a cup of the pumpkin for mashed sweet potatoes, just because I had some extra sitting around from thanksgiving. Lastly, I added a bit of nutmeg and allspice and the tiniest bit of ground cloves, plus two tablespoons of milk.  I love these! Plus, the never-eat-anything-healthy BF loves them frozen. What a winner! Thanks!

Scrumdiddlyumptious! Very moist. I agree, the flavor intesifies the longer you let them sit but good luck trying not to eat them all on day one. I used my last cup of butter to make the cookies so instead of the Penuche I simply mixed powdered sugar and water to make a glaze. I wanted a little extra sweetness, thought it worked well. But I'm looking forward to trying the penuche next time.

Made these specifically to use up extra pumpkin in the can, and it turned out to be better than my original dish!  Thanks for sharing, I have 1/2 a pot of the glaze left because I couldn't keep everyone from eating the cookies while I made it!!

Im from New Zealand, so this was the first time my family, friends and I have ever tried pumpkin in a dessert. But we all found these cookies SO DELICIOUS!!!
People were shocked to hear they actually had pumpkin in them! Im definitely making these again, thanks so much for the recipe!!
These are very tasty! They are so moist that they are a bit sticky but still taste very good and they are super easy to make.

As I was glazing these I thought, "never again."   First of all, the cooking time was not long enough and I had to return them to the oven after they had already cooled, but it worked.  Then I started putting the glaze on before it had thinned enough because I was afraid it would seize.  They looked awful, and I wasn't sure I would add them to my cookie platter.  However, everyone, including my non-pumpkin loving husband, raved about them.  I will definately make them again, and I believe I have ironed out all the problems I had the first time.

WOW! What a GREAT cookie this recipe makes! I did make a change regarding the amount of butter used in the recipe. Instead of 1 cup of butter, I cut the amount in half and substituted and extra 1/2 cup of pumpkin! These cookies turned out fantastic! They are really moist and delicious! The glaze is really sweet, but I think it goes really well with the cookie! I can't wait to try them tomorrow (like the others suggested) to see how they taste! Thank you for a great recipe, Sara! We will certainly be using this one often! :)

** The glaze is great to use for coating nuts, too!
Always looking for a way to use up extra pumpkin. OMG these are GREAT!! Everyone would not stop eating them.Thanks for a great recipe

WOW  This a fabulous cookie.  We just tried it and since have had to make 4 more batches.  Friends and family can't get enough.  I did up the spices by adding pumpkin pie spicing and they are awesome.  Thanks for posting this great recipe.

These are amazing, seriously addictive!  I made homemade cream cheese frosting to put on them and have made them twice so far!  I do agree that they are even better the next day.  These have went to the very top of my favorite cookie list for sure!  Thank you for sharing this recipe! :)
I wanted something pumpkiny without the typical overwhelming spice. This was it! I liked them even before putting the icing on so I can't imagine how good they'll be tomorrow. Thanks Sara!
I had some homemade pumpkin puree frozen and came across this recipe.  They are quite tasty.  I've packed a batch to send to my brother for his birthday.  The icing really makes them.
These cookies are awesome! I've brought them to work many times and they disappear quickly. If only it were easier to find canned pumpkin!

I make these every year with fresh pumpkin puree instead of canned and they always turn out great. I do get more of a cake consistency than cookie but I sort of like that in these particular cookies. I have made with white or whole wheat flour and the white works better to me but the whole wheat was ok too.

Cookies were ok. Nothing outstanding. The glaze was difficult for me I just put the cookies on wax paper just drizzled it over the cookies. It worked. But I wasn't found of it either. I think they tasted better without. I don't think they were horrible just wont make them again.
Awesome cookies.  So moist and delicious!  I brought these to work and my coworkers devoured them and then requested the recipe!

Sorry, I don't get it. The cookies were so mushy and soft they were falling apart in my hands. Didn't even bother to glaze them as they didn't even taste good so threw them all out.  Couldn't see anything that I did wrong but noticed some others had the same problem. Won't be trying these again.

Holy cow these are good!  I added 1/4 cup pecan pieces & used cream cheese frosting because I had some to use up.  So moist and delicious!  I thought they might sweat like banana bread does, but it's day 2 and they're still the same.  So good and almost gone already!  Thanks!
These are amazing. I brought them to work for my customers and i still have people asking about them. These are great anytime of the year
These are just the best cookies and they are so simple to make!
Very good!!  I loved them and made them just as the recipe stated.  We even loved the glaze - it was the perfect finishing touch.  The only thing I did was top each one with a pecan half.  Mmmm!
I made these wonderful gems tonight, topping them off with a pecan half before baking. The glaze was like a praline candy topping. Can't wait to share these.
Amazing Cookies! Everyone loved them.  I added some crushed toasted almonds to the top.  Will make again!!!

Delicious cookies! Soft and cakey with a delicious penuche frosting (do not omit!). Plenty of frosting for the cookies, used 2 cups powdered sugar for the perfect consistency. Used a silicone basting brush to frost the cookies which was so fast and easy. Thanks for sharing that tip, and thanks for sharing the recipe!

LOVE this recipe!  My only complaint is that I didn't get quite 48 cookies out of it!  These cookies are soft and moist and the because the cookie is not overly sweet the glaze is delicious on them.  I used a basting brush to put on a thin layer of the glaze because my oldest always complains about things being too sweet, but not this time...Rave reviews all around.  This is a keeper for sure!!

The cookie is great and is super moist, but the glaze is WAY too sweet.  I replaced the glaze with a little whipped cream on top.  It added a nice flavor to the cookie and turned it into a little single-serving pumpkin pie in cookie form.

Fantastic!  Made as stated this time and LOVE them, will try Meag's suggestion of subbing half the butter with a half cup of pumpkin next time to cut the calories, and might try adding nutmeg too, but these are wonderful made as stated.  The icing is da bomb!  Thanks Sara!
These are getting rave reviews today at work. Thanks so much for posting. The glaze is a must I think, and it's not hard to make at all.

The texture of these cookies is different from any other pumpkin cookie I've ever tasted.  Not too cakey, but slightly firm and soft.  Perfection!  And the frosting is to die for, do not skip it.  This is my new favorite pumpkin recipe of all time.  Thank you Sara!
Excellent cookies! I used pumpkin pie spices along with the cinnamon, and only drizzled a few stripes of the icing on top instead of frosting them. Looked and tasted wonderful - everyone loved them!

I made the recipe as written, but added 2 tsp of pumpkin pie spice. I used canned, unseasoned pumpkin. The cookies baked well, looked good, but they don't flatten out during baking. That is okay, they are much better that way- like little pillows. These cookies are much, much better then next day! After cooling the cookies tasted bland, not sweet, and had a slight taste of baking soda, but the next morning they were delicious! They taste like pumpkin bread. I made the icing and it gave a caramel flavor that went very well with the cookie. But there was a lot of leftover icing, so cut in half the amount called for in the recipe. I think that cream cheese icing would also taste great! I got 48 cookies using a teaspoon to drop onto the cookie sheet. I am going to try the lower calorie modifications that others suggested, but this recipe is very good as it is written. Those who complained about their results must have made a mistake in their measurements. NOTE: it calls for 1 CUP of pumpkin, not 1 CAN, although some said they added more pumpkin with good results. Be careful in reading the measurements. I made these for my daughter's class, so we'll see what the verdict is when she gets home!

My results were like miniature cakes--very soft.I followed the ingredients and cooking time exactly; they just didn't come out cookie-like for me--I'd better prefer them to be crunchy and/or chewy. However, the taste was very good kinda like a spice cake--I will probably add more pumpkin if I try it again, because I could only taste a hint of it in my cookies. The glaze spread fine on my first batch but quickly got hard, so some went without glaze at all. That's okay though, I'll just spread some maple syrup on them in the morning for breakfast. The glaze was tasty and sweet. Overall, I like the taste of my (cookies-cakes)--the only thing is that it took me forever to prepare, bake and make the glaze.

I would love to give it 4 1/2 stars. They were really good! And one person who ate them swore they were the best cookies he had ever eaten! I really liked them and will defiantly make them again- I just can't say they are my favorite.
I made two batches- the first batch was the recipe followed to a tee- except for the glaze. I omitted the butter, added pumpkin pie spice and eyeballed it because I only wanted to drizzle it across the cookie. I must say, the cookies with more of the glaze were much better IMO- so next I will follow the glaze recipe. Anyway, this batch baked up really fluffy and cakelike. I smoshed some of the before I put them in the oven so they would bake more like cookies and less like muffin tops!
The second batch was made the next day with the remaining pumpkin (waste not, want not!)- which did not measure to one cup (I didn't even bother measuring it- but I would guess 1/2 cup). The batter was a good consistency, so I didn't think I needed to add any extra liquid to make up for the pumpkin. But I did mix in about a cup of chocolate chips to make up for less pumpkin flavor (if I had pumpkin flavoring I might have added that- yes they make it, King Arthur Flour.com carries it). These baked up much more like traditional cookies and less like muffin tops. I didn't glaze these.
I had some family members who preferred the original posted recipe and some who preferred it with chocolate chips! So I will make both again- it was a great way to use up the rest of the pumpkin.

I used the recipe calculator to match my 1.75 cups of pumpkin I needed to use up.  Yield: 84 cookies.  The recipe was made as directed.  The cookies baked beautifully, and remain exceptionally moist in the storage container!  Did not make the glaze because I ran out of time.  I will make these again and will try the glaze too!  Thanks so much for sharing!

These are the best ever!  Delectable little orbs of goodness!  The only change I made was to use cream cheese frosting in place of the glaze.  These are amazing, and I'll be making them again this week!  Thanks!
OMG, love these.  Made and enjoyed as written and I eat one a day from the freezer!  I will make them again for our cookie exchange and add the chopped nuts on top!!!

Thank you so much for posting this recipe!  I have been baking this recipe for years but couldn't find it tonight.  A google search and a short dig later and it brought me straight to yours!  This is the BEST recipe and I won't be making any changes!  Thanks again!

The taste wasn't bad but it wasn't particularly interesting either. The texture was what my family didn't like; they think cookies should feel like cookies and cake should be cake. So I was pretty disappointed. If you like cake like cookies though, I'd say give it a try, but rev up the flavor with some bite.

These were simple enough to make, I made as written except I made one and a half batches.  I used a tablespoon to drop my cookies, perfect size.  These are a very good, cake-like cookie.  Very very moist and soft.  I definitely think they need the glaze, even if it's just a little bit.  Then toss a couple toasted pecan pieces on top and that triple combo all in one (or two) bites is amazing!  Toasting the pecan pieces is soooo worth it!  These kind of remind me more of a top of a cupcake then a "cookie" per se... everyone loved them.

I made these cookies the day after Christmas and they were GREAT!  I did make some minor changes.  I was looking for a good pumpkin cookie that I could add chocolate chips and this one worked great.  I used 1 and 1/2 cups of pumpkin and 2 and 1/2 cups flour and added approx. 2 cups of chocolate chips.  I dropped them on a stoneware cookie sheet and baked at 350 for 14 minutes.  Cooled for 2 minutes and served warm. They came out so moist and the chocolate enhanced the pumkin flavor. Next time I might add 1/4 more brown sugar (kids thought they could be a litte sweeter) but otherwise PERFECT Pumpkin Chocolate Chip cookies, thanks!
Yummy.  Enjoyed these with a glass of milk.  I used 1/2 c butter and a whole 15oz can pumpkin. Thank you for a great cookie!

OMG these are the best cookies.  I made these for my family this afternoon and we all loved them.  They are such moist and soft cookies, and the penuche glaze was to die for.  Yes the glaze is really sweet but it really make the cookie.  DH came home and said a buddies mom use to make these for them when they were younger as he was grabbing another cookie.  Thank you so much for this awesome cookies.

Absolutely delicious! I made it just as directed, and they were perfect! I spread the penuche with a small spoon because it was a bit runny (I didn't thicken it for very long) and it's delicious. I'm surprised that anyone thought this was too sweet. One of the reasons I loved it is the cakey, not overly powerful flavor of the cookie with the light, sweet penuche. THANK YOU! This is going to be made in my house again and again!
Unfortunately, this recipe did not work for me. I couldn't taste the pumpkin at all. If I try this recipe again, I'll need to add more pumpkin to it by substituting it for butter.
excellent! did not use glaze and my 4 year old loved them!!!! Nice way to get her to eat pumpkin...Next time I will try them with the glaze and see the difference in taste

I just made this cookie for a carving pumpkin party tomorrow. Wow is the word. They are great and very moist. I tried the glaze on some cookies only because just looking at the recipe, it looked like it would be really sweet...and it was. Good, but too sweet for my taste. My family loved it without the glaze. I'll either look for a recipe for a lighter glaze or just bring the cookies as it since my family devoured the first batch without the glaze. :-) Thanks for the recipe. I will definitely make this again!

Oh my goodness...nothing to say but DELICIOUS! Even my husband loved these and he rarely compliments!  These will be a Holiday favorite from now on....starting with Halloween through Thanksgiving & Christmas!  The balance is perfect...
Excellent pumpkin cookies! A nice soft cookie with the added flavor of that delicious frosting.  Thanks!

This is GREAT!  I made some substitutions with the last batch - Splenda for white sugar, ICBINB for butter, 1/2 wheat flour for white, Watkins pumpkin pie spice for cinnamon, fresh pumpkin puree for canned.  Also added sliced, fresh cranberries.  Oh, my!  They are sooooo yummy!!  (This is my all-time fave icing, too!)
Wow. These are great. The whole family loved them and the kids are licking their plates. lol

OMG!  These are to die for - they are divine!  I bought a can of pumpkin to make a pie for the family Thanksgiving Dinner, but my aunt reminded me that her kids don't like pumpkin pie.  I got online and searched for a pumpkin cookie recipe and found this one.  I am not one to cook, but this was pretty easy and will now be a yearly staple for Thanksgiving.  I almost didn't make the frosting, because the cookies were good enough without it.  Went ahead and made it and I'm so glad I did - they are absolutely heavenly.

Continuing my review from last night, I just made the glaze, which actually tastes like a caramel sauce.  It's brown so it makes the cookies not the prettiest things...I had some leftover little round colored sprinkle-things and sprinkled them on top for some color.  But man do these cookies taste GREAT!!!

My daughter (5) ate a dozen of these cookies unfrosted before I was even done cooking them. My son liked them as well, dh was another matter. I liked them frosted. All around enjoyed by most! I made just a few changes - I doubled the recipe and only used 1/2 cup butter and subbed the rest with pumpkin.

This is a great start to a pumpkin, cranberry cookies. Add 1 cup coarsely chopped toasted pecans and 1 cup dried cranberries that have been plumped (by adding 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup water, bring to slow boil and stir until plumped up and sugar is dissolved. I also added some Matilda (strawberry liqueur) about a Tablespoon. Let the cranberries cool and stir in with the pecans.
Delicious

These are delicious cookies, with or without icing.  I made the cookies mostly as directed, but did sub a teaspoon of nutmeg for one of the teaspoons of cinnamon.  I also struggled with the icing a bit.  Mine turned out dark brown, and I ended up adding another half cup of milk to get it spreadable.  It still tastes great.

AWESOME! made them without the glaze. They are easy to make. I used partial whole wheat flour the first time I made them and thought it came out fine and the second time i used a little less butter and i don't think it did any harm at all. I thought a great touch would be to fill them with a little bit of rich cream cheese frosting. I've made these a zillion times now, and they are always a huge hit! Also, you CAN freeze the dough, but they don't come out quite as fluffy that way.
I made these cookies and they were very delicious and very easy to make.  I used unsalted butter though and the glaze was to die for!  Our all a very good combo.
The cookies were great. My only complaint is the glaze. It harden VERY quickly even on the lowest possible heat. It was impossible for me to glaze a dozen cookies because of the quick hardening.
Good recipe! I turned the cookies upside down and dipped the top in the glaze. It was faster that way, as the glaze gets hard quickly.

I like how these cookies came out-- sort of like frosted scones. And my co-workers seemed to really like them.

I had a little bit of trouble with the glaze though--- my glaze did not thicken, and I ended up needing to use far more confectioner's sugar than the recipe called for. I'll add less milk next time.

I added extra cinnamon and nutmeg to the cookie batter, and I think that was a good addition-- it added a little extra spiciness. I might also dust the glaze with extra cinnamon next time.

Kinda just tasted like pumpkin bread without the icing. The icing makes this cookie! I chilled my dough and rolled it out with lots of flour and cut them into pumpkin shapes. I also used 1/2 cup of butter and about 12oz or pumpkin puree. Delicious! Thanks!!!

I prepared the recipe exactly as written and the cookies were absolutely delicious. Because my tablespoon was a heaping one, I got just 33 cookies from the recipe. (The larger cookie required an extra minute or two.). Next time I'll follow the advice of another reviewer and sprinkle some toasted chopped pecans on the moist glaze.

I wasn't sure I would like these, but they turned out to be really delicious. They had the perfect amount of pumpkin flavor. They were very fluffy almost like a cake. In my opinion they were a little too soft. But still very tasty. They taste great with or without the icing. I also substituted half a teaspoon of cinnamon with nutmeg.
Turned out great!! I also added a tsp of pumpkin pie spice in addition to cinnamon and cut back on sugar a bit and used 1c whole wheat flour/1c white yummy

These were awesome! A great substitution for pumpkin bread if you want them "to go". <br/>My first batch didn't last long enough to make the frosting. I didn't use the butter at all and used a 15 oz can of pumpkin, added a bit of nutmeg and they were great!

Fantastic cookie!  Love the soft texture.  Made with gluten free flour mix, crisco instead of butter and apple sauce (1/4c) instead of egg. Also used soy milk in glaze.  Really super tasty.  There might not be any left in about 15 minutes :)  One thing I noticed, the glaze does set up rather quickly so next time I might wait until all the cookies are baked and cooled before making the glaze.  Keeping it on low only worked for about 10 minutes, it's like a pot of pralines without the nuts,  and I still have another sheet to bake.

This is a great recipe for a cake-like cookie.  We did make some slight adjustments to make it our own, which included reducing the butter and sugar, increasing the pumpkin and adding mini-chocolate chips.  We reduced the butter by 50%, the sugar by 25%, and added 50% more pumpkin.  The spices, eggs, and flour we used as directed.  We wanted to decrease the fat and sugar, and increase the healthy pumpkin, and as chocolate lovers, added some sweetness with mini semi-sweet chocolate chips.  The cookies are very moist, not very sweet, but are delicious. We also omitted the top glaze due to the sugar content.  We will definitely make these again, thank you for sharing!

Nice moist cookie. I had trouble with the glaze hardening in seconds. I think it was probably user error. I barely managed to get any on the cookies. In the future ill use a smaller saucepan. I'll definitely be trying the recipe again. Even though the glaze is a little hard it has a great sweetness that complements the buttery pumpkin pillows.
BEST COOKIES EVER........, they are easy and delious . We made them for thansging and they turned out PERFECT. Love this recipe. You really should try them
These are very good, even without that yummy frosting.  Figured after Thanksgiving we didn't need the extra calories of the frosting.  Great way to use up that leftover pumpkin.
Not sure what I did wrong but they came out really thin. Everyone loved the flavor though.

I made this recipe with 1/2 quinoa flour and they are delicious! I have two fussy kids who didn't know they were pumpkin and loved them - and had to admit they loved them even after when they wanted to know what kind they were!

This is a great recipe. The whole family loved it. I could eat the frosting all by itself..<br/>I used the 2 tsp. cinnamon and added<br/>2 tsp Nutmeg<br/>1 tsp ground ginger <br/>used the whole can about 1.5 C<br/>and just added 1/2 tsp more baking powder and soda.<br/>bake longer but really turned out moist, and Great. these will not stick around for long...

Awesome ! Some of the best cookies , of any kind, ever ! We cooked the first batch a little less (barely any brown on the edges) and after they were completely cooled, they nearly melt in your mouth! Great idea to use a silicone basting brush for the glaze.   Better the next day.

These are great.  Second year making them.  I add a tablespoon of maple syrup to the icing (I know, extra sweetness to an already sweet frosting) - anyway, then I top them with pecans and coarse salt crystals while the icing is still hot.  The not so sweet cake like cookie with super sweet frosting and pinch of salt and nuts is to die for.  Enjoy!
I added some pumpkin spice. Very delicious and most cookies!

These cookies are very dangerous! I made them for a party last night.  Read the reviews before and baked them a day ahead.  Not sure why because I thought they were just as good the first day.  Everyone loved them.  I did have some leftover but decided it was better to give them away because I can't stop eating them! I did have to bake them a bit longer than 12 minutes.  The recipe for me made 40 small to medium size cookies. Definitely a keeper! Thanks, Sara! Next time, just for fun, I might try adding semi-sweet chocolate chips. Sara, what to you think?

So tasty! It is most definitely a cake like cookie. I followed the recipe as it was written and it had a nice pumpkin flavor. I think the only thing I would change is to add either nutmeg or pumpkin pie spice, just to spice it up a bit. 
Some reviewers stated that the glaze tightened up on them very quickly and they couldn't frost the cookie. The recipe calls for 1 1/2 to 2 cups powdered sugar. My suggestion is to use only 1 1/2 cups and if needed add more a tablespoon at a time, but mine was perfect with 1 1/2 cups. I also dipped the cookie tops as suggested by another and that worked great. This is a recipe worth trying. Yummy.

EXCELLENT flavor! I love these, and so does my 2 year old (finicky) daughter. Instead of making them into cookies, I filled my large cookie sheet with the batter, spread it out evenly with a spatula, and baked it for 20 minutes -- after resting and glazing, I cut it into bars with a pizza cutter. I did 1/2 cup pumpkin and 1/2 cup finely shredded (almost near pureed) zucchini. I also used bread flour, all brown sugar (no white), and two egg yolks instead of one whole egg instead. For the glaze, I used white sugar instead of brown and a milk alternative (Milkadamia Macadamia milk). Next time, I will see if I can substitute out some sugar for (pure) stevia or unsweetened applesauce or some other kind of natural sweetener, and sub in some oat bran or flour for the wheat flour to make this even healthier.

These cookies seem like a muffin recipe put in the shape of cookies.  I was looking for a cake-like cookie, but not cookies that turn out like mini-muffins.  I also think that they need more spice in them.  I will consider using this recipe as a pumpkin muffin recipe but replace the 2 tsp of cinnamon with: (1) 1/2 tsp all spice, (2) 1/2 tsp cloves, (3) 1/2 tsp ginger, (4) 1/2 tsp nutmeg, (5) 1/2 tsp cinnamon.
My husband said these were the best cookies I ever made.
Kids love them. Made exactly as written, except I didn't even make the glaze. We just eat them plain.
These are more like cake than cookies. I added ginger and nutmeg and they still didn't have a whole lot of flavor. The icing helped but after reading other reviews, I was really disappointed :(

These cookies are yummy with the glaze, but not very pumpkin-y, very bland without the glaze, do not omit. I think they could be better with more added spices and more pumpkin. Definitely need to tweak more.
I liked the cake like consistency of the cookies.

An absolutely fantastic recipe. I followed another reviewer's advice and cut the butter in half and substituted with extra pumpkin. For the flour, I used half white flour and half whole wheat flour. I doubled the amount of cinnamon, used freshly grated nutmeg and also added a sprinkle of ground ginger and a tiny dash of black pepper. For the icing, I added a sprinkle of finishing sea salt to give it a salted caramel taste. These cookies were a huge hit and I will definitely be making it again! Thank you so much for submitting it!
Can you use Pumpkin Spice instead of Nutmeg?
The cookies were amazing! But the icing didn't turn out..
These cookies are wonderful. The icing makes them even better. I changed the recipe to 24, I got 14. Very easy!

Modified the spices a bit since I wanted to make sure they had plenty of flavor. Used a total of 1/2 tsp of salt, 2 tsp of cinnamon, also a sprinkle of ginger and nutmeg. Put a few chocolate chips in half of the cookies. After the first sheet of them baking at 350 and having them still seem very doughy I increased temp to 375 and that seems to bake them through better. The flavor was bang on, I wanted to wait to see if they needed icing after cooking and they really didn't so we skipped it, meaning I could eat more cookies guilt free :)

I made mine with a gluten free flour blend. I used half flour and half oats and then added a cup of sliced almonds and limited the glaze. They're perfect for an easy source o f carbs and protein after I run! Thanks for the base I worked from!
Great recipe...easy to follow and fabulous tasting cookie cakes...I upped the measures of cinnamon and nutmeg cos that's how I roll... will make again !!!!

This cookie recipe is DELICIOUSLY PERFECT! I made it EXACTLY as the recipe instructed and it turned out fantastic! The cookie itself was exactly as I hoped—tender, cakelike consistency and perfectly flavored. The icing was over the top scrumptious! Yes, it’s sweet-but it goes perfectly with this cookie. And like someone else said-it’s even tastier the next day—like the flavors meld. Please, make this recipe EXACTLY as directed first, and review it. Otherwise, you’re not reviewing THIS recipe—your reviewing your own version-and that’s not fair to the author. You can always post your own version for review. This cookie doesn’t disappoint. Great job Sara in FL!!!!
Yummy Sauce!  Makes this a special ham and cheese sandwich!  Perfect for weekend lunch or weekday dinner.

I made this sandwich for DH today.  He LOVED it!  He likes big, tasty sandwiches and this is fits that category.  The dressing is wonderful.  The only thing I left out was the poppy seeds.  I used swiss AND cheddar.  Fabulous!  Thanx for a great lunch.  I'll be repeating this one.

This is a perfect sandwich for a cold day. I had everything on hand except the horseradish (which DH wouldn't eat anyway). I made one and he ended up eating both halves (this is a true compliment!). I'll admitt to cheating as I didn't want to wait out the oven time. I put the ham on bottom bun amd turkey on the top, sprinkled both with cheese and slid them under the broiler to melt the cheese. The top and bottom stuck together very well. I did get a couple of bites and this is delish! (it's ok, I also made soup for me and told him that if he didn't care for the sandwich I would take half of it)
Quick, easy, and delicious!  Keeper!
Excellent sandwich! I used swiss cheese and skipped the horseradish due to personal preference. Other than that, made exactly as is and it was delicious!

These were so good!  Reminded me a lot of an Arby's sandwich (a guilty pleasure for me).  We only used the dijon & butter on the rolls.  Made extra for lunch the next day - great idea!!!  Perfect "rescue" dinner for a busy night!
So good! These are really great sandwiches. Like the others, I also skipped the horseradish- too strong a taste for me =) THANKS for posting!
These were pretty good. The only thing I'd suggest is flipping the sandwiches halfway through if you use french or sourdough bread for a more even browning on both sides. Thanks!

Enjoyed these pancakes, that DS and I had this morning, though I usually don't care for orange flavor, everyone else does, it was all right, and we enjoyed these this morning.  DS wanted more.. Made for Holiday Tag

DD (toddler) and I liked this for a one time breakfast. I liked the fact that the topping didn't contain added sugar but we both agreed we didn't love the topping. I made ours gluten free by using recipe#342995 instead of the mix and water and I added the banana chopped up into it rather than mashed. Made for ZWT7 Pacific Islands, for my team Food.Commandos

Delightfully easy and delicious!  I used gluten free baking mix and, therefore, adjusted the water accordingly to get a pancake consistency.  I brought the strawberries and orange juice to a boil and then simmered the topping the entire time I was making the pancakes.  I served with an extra garnish of sliced bananas and strawberries and a dollop of whipped cream (I know - not as healthy, but it was fat free :) )  Thanks for sharing!  ZWT7

What a lovely pancake recipe this is....great way to use box mixes.  I added vanilla to the batter.  The pancakes were thick and light and tasted of bananas.  I really enjoyed the sauce, I used raspberries instead of strawberries.  Thanks for sharing, made for ZWT7 for the Witchin Kitchen.

Tasty and fruity pancakes!  The banana flavor was subtle and the pancakes were nice and fluffy.  I enjoyed the strawberry/orange topping; next time I think I'll add some pecans to the pancakes and a bit of cinnamon to the topping.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I used a whole wheat blend mix for these and they turned out very nicely. The batter was a little thick so I added a few extra tablespoons of water. It was still a thick batter but the pancakes were nice and fluffy. The strawberries were a nice topping, but not the best part of the recipe :)

i used some ground pecans in this the strawberries were liked by me but not mr picky  i think the ones i used were to watery and needed sugar to make sauce , i by cheaper stuff and i swear its half water lol i love banana pancakes and these were no exception these were very fast to make
These were so easy and delicious! I wouldn't have thought to use a mix with bananas, but it really worked and that strawberry topping is divine!

I am so glad that I picked this recipe to make for the RSC contest because it is a real winner!  I made this dish exactly as instructed and got perfect results and a wonderful meal for two with one serving left over.  I actually made this recipe the day before and reheated it with outstanding results! The meat balls are so very tender and the sauce filled with flavor. However, it was very spicy (fine for us) and some people might want to cut down on the cayenne pepper just a bit. 
I know I will make this again, not only for my family, but as a great dish to serve to company. Congratulations on creating an excellent recipe.

we really enjoyed this recipe.  my husband kept raving about how buttery the lamb tasted and couldn't believe that the recipe didn't have butter in it.  Unlike Geema, the sauce wasn't quite spicy enough for MY taste so i doubled all the spices.  This made it spicy but not too much, my 18 month old ate it.  We thought the meatballs would be delicious on a pita with some raita.  We served it with rice as directed which was quite good.  I also substituted milk for the 1/2 and 1/2 to cut down on the fat, i don't think it affected it much.  Thanks for a great recipe!!

These are just too good for words! We are trying to stay away from beef and this is an excellent choice! I doubled the recipe and served them over rice pilaf with a tzatziki style cucmber salad on the side. the meatballs were tender and flavorful and the sauce is just beyond description...tomatoey,creamy,spicey yet mellow, very comforting. I will be serving this often. Thanks Kelly for creating this scrumptious recipe!

I made this recipe exactly as directed; unfortunately, this dish didn't overly appeal to DH or me.  It smelled great while cooking, but didn't have the flavor we expected.  The sauce seemed extremely sweet to us, with a less pronounced tomato flavor.  However, the lamb meatballs were quite good, with a nice spice to them, and I plan to use that portion of the recipe again to make lamb meatballs in a different tomato sauce. This is definitely a unique recipe, with unusualy yet pleasant taste, and if a sweeter tomato sauce is what you're looking for, this recipe may be just the ticket.

The reviews were so positive for this recipe that I boldly decided to quadruple it before I even made it. I'm glad I did because the flavor is glorious!   I decreased the amount of sugar by half because, like Lizzie-Babette, I didn't want a very sweet sauce. Other than that I didn't change a thing. I thought the spices were perfect - smoothe and comforting with just a little bite! I served the meatballs over brown rice with a cucumber raita on the side.  My husband and I enjoyed it very much and I look forward to serving it to my in-laws.  Thanks for a delightful recipe!

Yum yum and another YUM!! Made a couple minor changes - only used about 1 1/4 tsp sugar and also 1/2 cup canned tomato puree instead of fresh tomato. Also used fat free half-n-half which worked great and reduced the fat level but not the richness! Wonderful delicious, spicy, creamy, rich dinner. I cooked my rice with some garam masala. Thanks soooo much for the recipe Kelly!!

Kelly, this is wonderful. We really enjoyed this with french bread and green beans. I'm really glad I doubled the recipe! Actually, I doubled all ingredients except for the broth, added more like triple the curry powder, and used only 1 tsp sugar. This was great. Thanks for posting! -- posted Jun 4, 2005  UPDATING because I forgot to say before that I used nonfat milk thickened with cornstarch instead of half-and-half...yielded a rich-tasting but lower-calorie result. Fantastic meal. Thanks again.

This made a lovely rich curry sauce with meatballs. I did need about twice the curry powder, but the strengh of curry powder, as well as individual tastes, varies. I used somewhat less broth and heavy cream. I simmered the sauce until it reached the desired thickness, so didn't need to thicken it with flour. Oh, and only used about 1/2 teaspoon sugar. Thank you for a nice recipe. I'll be making it again.

DH and I had this for dinner last night and absolutely LOVED it!  It had a nice texture and spicy flavor.  I doubled the garam masala, tripled the curry, and halved the sugar as suggested by other reviewers.  I also used cream, only because I didn't have half and half on hand, and used slightly less chicken broth; again, because it was all I had on hand.  My DH remarked how much he enjoyed the dish, which is a real compliment as he is somewhat difficult to impress.  We will definitely be making this again. We had the meatballs over Jasmine rice, and served this with Recipe #60415, Potato and Zucchini Curry by Love4Culinary.  It was a nice compliment.  Thank you for this keeper!
These are yummy~~My DH liked them very much.  I doubled the curry powder and the garam masala.  I put in 1 1/4 tsp. sugar, and I think next time I will leave it out.  Thanks for sharing!!  :O)

I thought this was great. We love spice, so I took others' advice and doubled the curry and the garam masala. I left out the sugar and added a chopped jalapeno with the onion.  It was definitely hot, but delicious!
These were different and pretty good.  I too doubled the curry powder and garam masala.  Thanks!

Absolutely stunning. I'm not one for trying to make "a healthier version" of good recipes, but if you sub the cream for some low fat yogurt, there's no real difference. The meatballs are still beautifully juicy, and the sauce goes perfectly with boiled, sticky rice.

This was a great recipe.  I had been wanting to make it for awhile but lamb is hard to come by in my area - especially ground lamb.  Upon reading the reviews I doubled the garam masala, garlic and curry but left the cayenne the same.  The dish had a nice kick but it wasn't overwhelming.  The tomato sauce turned out great.  I served with sticky rice and broccoli.  Thanks for posting!

Very good.  Loved everything about it.  The sauce was to die for.  I served it over white rice.  When I got home my husband told me after he ate his dinner, he put some more of the sauce over his noodles.  Again, awesome
Really a great sauce. I doubled the sauce ingredients, used milk instead of 1/2 and 1/2, used Panko for crumbs. Meatballs were good but could have been baked, its the sauce that makes this dish.

This was a winner! We pureed all of the sauce because we like a smooth texture with our curries. The meatballs are so yummy! We ended up eating it with ground turkey instead of lamb because that is what we had, but I can only imagine it is even tastier with the lamb.
I really loved this recipe.  Very comforting, very easy for a weeknight meal.  I will double the recipe next time though!
Made this for a dinner party and didn't change a thing. They were a hit! The flavor of the sauce and the meatballs is divine.

Great recipe! doubled w/o problem. Kept meat seasoning proportionally as written but doubled curry and cayenne in sauce ( quadrupled as I doubled recipe). Absolutely delicious! Served with a scattering of chopped fresh Italian parsley and steamed Super Basmati rice. Will make for company and proudly serve.  Seems like a perfect dish to cook up and then throw in the crockpot on "warm" to serve buffet style with rice and a salad and maybe creamed spinach on the side - easy entertaining! Thanks for posting Kelly M.!

Wow, this recipe is fantastic!  I immediately added this to my recipe notebook.  I brought these to a party and everyone loved them.  Only made a couple minor substitutions: substituted crushed canned tomatoes and used yogurt instead of half and half.  Let the sauce cool a bit before adding  the yogurt so it doesn't curdle.  I served it with white rice.  Thank you Kelly for this great recipe!  Oh, one more thing: 1/2 lb of lamb is not enough.  Quadruple the recipe because everyone will love it and you'll want the leftovers.  2lbs of lamb would serve about 4-5.

These made nice french fries.  I used 3 large potatoes instead of the 5 called for (it is what I had) but I found that it was too much for just 1 cookie sheet.  (And my cookie sheets are large.)  The flavor was nice and I loved the shape of the fries.

I ignored the part that said '3 sprays of oil', I used release foil hoping that would suffice-but I was wrong! They were starting to stick to the foil so I did end up I spraying them with canola! Fantastic fry, we loved the zip from the cajun seasoning. Thank You Kimke!

Kim, good "fries" great taste and low fat!  I did make mine a little thicker so they did take about an hour and 15 minutes and then turned about every 10 minutes (pain), BUT they were well worth it!  BF liked the spice!  TY
Really good for a low fat fry! Crunchy too, which can be hard to achieve without oil. The egg white must be the magic ingredient! I'll be making these again, thanks.

Crunchier and crispier than my usual oven-baked fries. I cut them smaller so they only took about 30 minutes to bake. Instead of cajun seasoning, I used chili powder and paprika. Thanks for a good recipe!
I was really skeptical, at first.  But, these turned out really tasty & crispy!  We devoured them before the rest of the meal came out of the oven.  They were a lot of work - but well worth it!!

Beeing french it is with grate hesitation ,i did your recipe.
However i must admit they turned 
out tasty-crispy and yet the inte-
rior still moist.Thanks we will
definitely recur.

Perhaps I should have cut these thinner to achieve the 45 minutes cooking time? However, they were done, just not crisp like I expected. The egg seemed to help the seasoning stick to the fries, but also to help the fries stick to the baking pan! I also had a great deal of trouble turning the fries (even after I got them unstuck) - as they became more done, they crumbled each time I moved them and were quite fragile and "mealy." I simply did not get the results I was hoping for.

These turned out very good.  I sliced the potatoes pretty thin, about 1/4 inch, to make sure they were crunchy.  They did turn out browned and crunch!  I recommend these becasue they tasted just as good as traditional fries, but must be much better for you.
This is a great method for oven fries.  I used a sweet potato (could've used two), and one egg white, with Lawry's seasoned salt.  MMMM..good!  And, healthy!
These were good fries!  I did have trouble with them sticking though.  I will try them again in a different pan.  Thanks for sharing!

These were great because they ended up crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.  Usually when I make oven fries they turn out too soft.  I used all-seasoning for the spice and it turned out very tasty.

I never would have thought to put egg white on fries to make them crisp!  But it works like a charm!  I've been trying to figure out a way to make french fries without dousing them in oil, and finally I've found it.  These were so tasty...but it was hard to clean the cookie sheet up afterward.  Next time I will make sure all the excess egg does not bake onto the sheet.  Thanks for the recipe!

These were pretty good. I think I had too much egg white, because there was a huge mess on the cookie sheets. I did like the spice, and I thought the fries were good as well. I will try these again with just one egg white and see what happens. Thanks for a neat idea!

Only 3 WW points per serving!!! I have been making this for year's. They are the best. Quick and easy to throw together and they come out so crispy and tasty too! I'm so glad you posted this recipe Kimke.

This was good, however the egg whites created a MESS on the pan. I too think next time I will use only one egg white. I think the excess egg white caused a few of the fries to burn also. Mine only took about 30 minutes to bake, but these are so good and WW Friendly! Will try again with modifications!

I messed this up.  I tried to use parchment paper (What was I thinking?!?).  I quickly realized the error in my ways and slid them off the paper onto the tray.  I will make these again and post a proper review then.  My fiance (who is suspicious of anything healthy) loved these and asked that I make them again.
Very good.  The kid's loved it.  I used about 3/4 of a cup of milk instead of egg whites and it worked great.

Always on the hunt for new versions of baked fries, these were a terrific addition to a great weekend comfort meal.  Having used egg whites in another recipe once before, I knew it was important to let the excess drip off before placing them on the baking sheet.
