Alas that also meant much of the spices added to the egg whites also dripped off.  I think it would have worked better to sprinkle the spices on after placing the spuds on the baking sheet.  Delicious nonetheless.  Thanks!

For "fries" that are not fried these are really good. I used 1 egg white to 1 large baking potato for 2 servings. I sprayed a little circle of cooking spray on a large cookie sheet to hold parchment paper in place and then sprayed the paper also. I've made these a few times now and found that if you wait about 15 to 20 minutes to turn the fries they don't seem to fall apart so much.

We liked these a lot!  We didn't have any cajun spices so my husband used a different spicy mix, he also cut the potatoes a little thicker than directed.  Thanks, this is a great way to enjoy my fries without the guilt.  Only 3 WW points per serving.
My husband thought these were the best fries he had ever had!
Wonderful lowfat treat for a potato lover!  Beware the egg whites sticking to your pan!
These fries were great!  They baked up to a woderful crunch.  I won't be making my fries any other way from now on!
These were great!  Crunchy and brown on the outside, soft on the inside.  Best if eaten immediately.

I LOVE these fries, and I feel they are even BETTER than McDonald's.  I used to large baking potatoes, didn't peel and cute with a fry slicer (didn't take them down to matchsticks) then soaked in cold water for about 1 hour, rinsed, dried and followed directions as listed.  They turned out crispy on the outside and soft inside.  Even my VERY picky DGD (2yrs) loved them and kept asking for more.  So easy to make and not to bad for you either - we really enjoyed this and will be making it often.  Thanks Kimke for sharing a great recipe.

I didn't put stars on because everyone else seems to love these, but they kind of didn't do it for me. I just used salt and maybe didn't put enough on. I cut them bigger than matchsticks...hmm...chalk-stick size? My husband, who liked them, suggested that maybe I should have baked them longer. Maybe I'll try them again. Reviewed for Healthy Choices ABC tag.

My Brother-In-Law's Mother made this tonight for dinner and we all asked to take home the recipe (I should have known it was a Giada recipe). It was downright delicious and she said she made it to exactly as written. I didn't try your recipe but I know a lot about dq cakes.
I worked in a dq for 4 years, I made a huge amount of cakes in that time. I would freeze the pans first(there was no top or bottom on pans). Then put a ring of vanilla all the way to the top (around the rim). That is so you only see vanilla ice cream from the outside. Then put chocolate ice cream at the bottom to about half way up. {Then for the cookie layer, it is called krunch with cold fudge. The best description of krunch is a plain chocolate wafer cookie. It is the same type used for treatza pizzas and the wafer of their ice cream sandwiches. Now most dqs use a pre made insert for the cookie layer but you can just blend krunch and cold fudge to make it.} Place a thin layer on top of chocolate then finish with vanilla. I would scrape the top smooth and then freeze in the pan, later I would let it sit out 5-15 min to soften, for pan removal then scrape the sides for the line pattern. Refreeze then decorate. I think heavy whipping cream was used for that. We wouldn't use gel that often for writing since it looks horrible when frozen.

I then followed the rest of the recipe as stated, but, instead of putting the chicken back into the frying back with the sauce to simmer, I took the sauce (made exactly as stated in the recipe, by the way) off the heat and let it cool down a little.  Then, I put the chicken in a ceramic baking dish and dumped all the sauce/mushrooms straight onto it instead, and then stuck the dish in the fridge.  That way, after my guests had arrived, all I had to do was let it come back to room temperature, then slide the baking dish into a preheated 350 degree over for 45 minutes - and the chicken came out moist and juicy and perfectly cooked. Note: I tasted the sauce before putting it in the oven and it tasted VERY lemony and I wasn't convinced, lol, even though I followed the recipe exactly  . . . but it toned down very nicely after baking and actually was perfect. Since it hadn't gone into the oven yet, I added about 1/4 cup of vegetable spread, and 1/4 cup of liquid (I used eggnog, since many reviews said it needed something).  That batch didn't rise and came out looking like dense mini cornbread, but the flavor was pretty good from the 'nog.  I added 1/2 cup of milk and eggnog to the batter so that the batter was more loose, like a cake batter.  I thought it didn't leaven properly the first time, so I added 1 tsp of baking soda as well.  Viola!  I have the most amazing, delicious, fluffy eggnog cupcakes ever!  I think the best overall fix is to add the baking soda, 1/4 c of butter/margarine, and 1/2-3/4 cup milk/cream/eggnog to loosen up the batter.

Made these last night. The recipe is similar to the Tollhouse chocolate chip recipe except for the addition of cocoa and there's the problem. Although the flavor was good the cookies were too dry. Whenever you add cocoa powder to a recipe, you need to reduce the amount of flour by the amount of cocoa powder you'll be using. So the flour used should be 1-1/4 cups flour and 3/4 cups cocoa powder. The result will be a moister and chewier cookie. I also used 3/4 cups granulated sugar and 3/4 cups brown sugar instead of 2 cups granulated sugar. I also divided the dough in two and rolled it into two long logs in plastic wrap and chilled the dough for a couple of hours until it was firm enough to slice. Chilling will help to keep the cookies from spreading too much and slicing a log is less of a hassle than scooping out 1 tablespoon of dough for each cookie.

Our Christmas Prime Rib was perfect, all the way down to the Au Jus.  Thanks Kittencal for a simple yet perfect recipe.

Delicious! Tender and flavorful.  My first ever attempt at a roast, and it was guest-worthy! Answered all my questions! Made a beautiful prime rib!

Again Kittencal, another wonderful base recipe! This made for a perfect Christmas Day Dinner for my Daughter and myself, Kitten !!  This was perfection on a plate. Oh so tender and juicy with such a delicious flavor. A definite keeper that I will make again soon..
This is a no fail recipe....turns out perfect everytime! I am not afraid to fix prime rib roast since I now have a perfect recipe! I usually fix this when I want to impress my dinner guests.
Another Amazing recipe!  It is foolproof and so delicious!

Great recipe.  I bought a great five pound prime rib (2 ribs serving 4 people) from my local butcher.  Pretty pricey, but so worth it. This was PERFECT! I thought I would mess it up but it turned out so perfect and tender that I will definitely fix it again. Thanks so much!

Internal tempature 140f?! Small amount of salt?.... salt after it's cooked!?!? Only take it out for 2 - 2.5hrs prior to cooking!?!?!.... we have very different methods of cooking... Came out better than any prime rib I have had in the restaurant and that was my first try, thank you, outstanding

The meat was moist and delicious and perfectly medium rare with a final temperature of 140 degrees. Everyone enjoyed the meal. Great instructions! This recipe is a keeper! Very happy cook.

Cooked to 125 degrees, good medium to medium rare, 3+lb. roast. Used 6 garlic cloves. I like garlic, but that was all I could taste. Like the cooking method but will skip the garlic next time so I can taste the beef. A vampire free neighborhood tonight!

I cooked this for Christmas Eve and it came out perfect! I had a large crowd to cook for, so I followed your instructions for 14 min per pound (after the initial 20 min at 450 degrees). This was very nice! I din't change a thing.:)

Then I dumped back the veggies and added the marinade and let it all bubble up. As another reviewer said, I needed a bit (1/2 cup maybe?) more of liquid, part white wine and part water. Ta-da! Thanks CoffeeMom!
really good! i didn't have any green onions so i left them off. i used 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes & left out the red pepper. wonderful taste; thanks for sharing!

Delicious sauce!  Very flavorful!!  My family loved it.  The bit of sweet from the honey made it very appealing to my sometimes picky kids, and I also appreciated how low fat it is. Very yummy and really easy.  Add peanutes and mushrooms for a great Kung Pao Chicken recipe!

This is no way to cook eggs!
     First, use a pin to punch a hole in the big end of the eggs.  This prevents cracking, that is caused by expansion of the air bubble in the big end.
     Cover the eggs well with COLD water.  Cover the pan, and bring to a boil over medium heat (this method works only on an electric stove).  As soon as the water is bopiling, turn off the heat.  Leave the pot on the element.
     After some hours, once the water is at room temperature, peel the eggs (use a spoon to crack the shell all over, then, under a running tap, roll the egg between your palms.  The shell can then be easily removed.
     DEVILED:  Slice an egg lengthwise.  Spoon out the yolk.  Repeat for the rest of the eggs.
Add a spoon of DILL PICKLE JUICE (!), season to taste, mash the lot with a fork, and spoon into the egg-white halves.  Or use CURRY instead of the pickle brine.  Or EXPERIMENT!

I had to get into the discussion on this one! I have always been told to start the eggs in cold water,add few drops vinegar should one crack this seals it, bring to boil, turn off heat, cover and let stand 10-15 mins. Run under cold running water, add ice to water to get the eggs cold as soon as possible, this will ensure fluffy tender yolks, and tender whites, but also eliminates the black ring that occurs around the yolk if you don't cool the eggs. Tap the eggs on the counter top and roll them with the palm of your hand and under running cold water the shells will peel right off. I know this is basic stuff to us old uns, but please remember all the newlyweds, and those new to cooking, these tips make all the difference in the results they get.

This is a great recipe, with a few changes.  I read online how to cream butter and sugar, so here goes a double recipe that turned out great. Soak dried cranberries just to cover in very hot water. Stir together 2 cups flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 c vanilla instant pudding and 1 1/2 cups blended oats.  Cream butter at room temp for 1 1/2 minutes.  Mix 1 c sugar and 1/2 c brown sugar together, then add mixed sugars to butter gradually for 5 minutes.  Add 1 tsp vanilla, 2 eggs, and 2 TB cranberry water, blend. Add flour mixture.  Stir in remaining oats, drained cranberries, and 1 package white chocolate chips.  Line sheet pans with rubber mats, then with parchment paper.  Scoop 1 tsp balls onto paper, bake at 350 for 11 minutes, or until edges turn brown.  Do not overcook!!!!!!  Remove to cooling racks.

This was the first time I'd ever deep fried anything, so I was pretty nervous, but it turned out I had no reason to be!  These turned out beautifully!

I didn't have a thermometer, so I flipped through some other wings recipes until I found a great tip; when you drop a tiny bit of bread in the oil and it sizzles immediately, the oil is ready.  That same recipe also said to fry for about 12 minutes.  Turns out, that advice was spot on!  My husband and I don't like wings that are too hot, but these really had absolutely no kick to them.  Next time, I'll add maybe a teaspoon of Tabasco or some ground cayenne to the mixture of butter and Frank's red hot sauce.  Oh, and I melted the butter in just a small Pyrex measuring cup, and added the hot sauce.  I removed each wing from the oil one at a time, dipping each very quickly into the hot sauce/butter mix, then immediately put into a container.  That seemed to be the easiest way to do it.  Next time, I'll line the container with a paper towel to absorb the excess hot sauce; the bottom layer of wings were left laying in it for a while, and were soggy, as opposed to the nice and crispy wings that were not left sitting directly in that excess sauce.  This recipe is definitely a keeper!  I will keep looking for one more recipe, as I'd like to have two great wings recipes; I'm thinking wings with an Asian feel would be a great alternative!

I drained the fried wings on some paper toweling, then transferred to a cookie sheet in the oven as I (slowly LOL) fried the remainder of the wings. These wings did not dissapoint! I made a few changes though. For the flour mixture, I did not have cajun seasoning on hand so I used 1 tsp soul food seasoning as well as 1 tsp Paula Deen's House Seasoning that I made up myself and keep on hand. The breading was perfect--not too salty nor too bland. Prior to breading I did soak my wings in Frank's Red Hot Wings Sauce(imo the best for chicken!) for 8 hours. Just so you know if you like your wings really hot, Frank's has all the flavor but only has a little kick to it. Instead of deep frying, I baked my wings at 500 degrees(Frank's provides this alternative to deep frying on the bottle) on a rack on top of a foiled cookie sheet(an absolute must if you want crispy chicken) for 20-25 min. I've made this twice now so the last time I made one other change. Instead of 1/2 cup of butter, I only used 1/4 cup of butter because I was appalled at how much fat was still floating around the bottom of the bowl--this after all the wings had been thoroughly soaked. I did not--nor did my family notice a change in flavor by this adjustment. Thank you Mystery Girl for providing this wonderful recipe!

I tried these tonight and wowzers, what a fabulous result! I added to it a bit by making them twice baked by taking the insides out, smooshing in some sour cream, chives, salt, butter and cheddar cheese, re stuffing the skins, re wrapping them and putting them back int he pot for about another 30 mins on low. I think I need to play a bit with the second times length in the crock pot, but the result was very, very good. Thanks. From now on baked potatoes will be back in my regular schedule.

Yum!  I stumbled upon this recipe when I was looking for easy crock pot recipes for a friend.  As soon as I read it, I went, "Well, duh!  Why didn't I ever think of that?  Baked potatoes without heating up the house!"  I did six large potatoes, rubbed with olive oil and seasonings, on high for 5 hours, and they're wonderful!  Thank you Audrey!  :)

Thanks for a great recipe!  Many times I'd like baked potatoes with dinner but just don't want to hassle with the oven, etc, and I never thought to try them in the crock pot!  I made them over the weekend making extra to use up a bag of spuds.  Worked fantastic, and DH was happy to have extras to take in his lunch!
These were fast, easy, and delish to prepare. Served with Recipe #63887 -- will use this a LOT!
Perfect!  I had an oven full of baby backs and this worked out perfectly.  Thank you Audrey M for a keeper.

Pure genius!  I can do this when I get home from work, in seconds, and clean up is easy. I popped two medium-small potatoes in the crock pot (after washing and pricking with a knife), without the foil, on high for 2 hours and they came out perfectly.  I don't like the peel, but roommates do, so I will oil and salt the outside next time.  Thanks for sharing!
This was great.  I was grilling steaks later that day & pop these in the crockpot.  Steak & bake potatoes.  UMMM Good

I absolutely loved this! I used really large potatoes and thru in some sweet potatoes too, everything  cooked perfect on low for about 8 hours. I used them for loaded baked potatoes and everyone loved them! cooked way better than in the microwave.
Awesome idea! I use this quite often now I found it! THANKS
Worked out great!

I never would have thought of baking potatoes in the crock pot, but now that I've followed your directions I don't plan to make them any other way. This is the perfect way to fix baked potatoes for a crowd, particularly in the summer! (My crock pot puts out a little heat so I put it in my garage while cooking. LOL) Thank you, thank you, thank you!
I'll never bake a potato any other way after trying this!  Thank you!
Great.  I cooked 6 medium Yukon golds.  Sprayed the foil with a bit of cooking spray and then salted the outside of the potatoes before wrapping them.  Yum, this is so easy!
This is great!  It was SO easy!  Just make sure your potatoes are all about the same size, I had 1 little guy in there and it ended up way overcooked. Otherwise, such a great idea!!!
These are simple and taste far better than cooking in the oven or microwave.  Highly recommended.
Easy peezy!!  <br/>Thank you,

I can't believe I never reviewed this recipe. We use it for every holiday meal. It frees up the oven and makes fantastic fluffy baked potatoes. We have been known to rub the potato with olive oil and sprinkle with kosher salt before putting on the foil and putting in the crock pot.
This was my first time making baked potatoes in the crock pot and it worked perfect.  I was worried about the top potatoes not getting cooked enough but they were.  Thank you for sharing with us.
WOW .......... Great idea lol
I would have never thought of this! I can't wait to try it.  has anyone tried it with sweet potatoes? I think that would be a good idea too...

just a comment:  these are STEAMED potatoes, not baked.  Many people like their potatoes this way.  I don't mind steamed, but I prefer the dry flavor of roasted potatoes.  I have years of food service, and a baked potato is NOT wrapped in foil, until after it is baked (and only to keep it warm if not going to be eaten or served immediately).

I used to have a crock pot/slow cooker and remember reading somewhere that you shouldn't cook in it without liquid in the pot so this recipe is mind boggling in more ways than one! Has anyone else ever come across that rule? What is everyone using to make this recipe? I have to buy a new crock pot so am open to suggestions! Thanks.

When I saw this recipe, I was thrilled.  I too thought " why didn't I think of this "?  I made these a couple week ends ago. I used 4 med. yukon golds, rubbed with evoo and koser salt.  Cooked on high for 4 1/2 hours and they were perfect, I won't make baked potatoes any other way.  I will save on propane AND  my a/c.  Today, I have 12 medium boil in a bag red potatoes ( I want to make a cream cheese potatoe salad).     I wrapped all 12 in foil,drizzled with an  evoo lemon/ garlic& jalapeno dressing that I make and keep in the fridge to use on salads and such.  I will post the results, when the results come in : )
I would like to ask the reviewers why they would slow-cook baked potatoes for 4-5 hours when the microwave does the same thing in 8-15 minutes?  I'm serious - are they that much better?

Cooked six medium size (pretty small for russets) in small crockpot on high for 3.5 hours and they came out perfect! I washed the night before and let air dry. Then wrapped in foil before placing in the crockpot. I was sure to put the larger side (if there was on down in the crock. I also put part where the foil overlaps against the side of the crock so that they wouldn't get too hot right against the heat. Perfect.

I've made this recipe twice now, both with great results. I first rubbed the potatoes with a garlic-infused olive oil and instead of salt (can't use it, unfortunately) rubbed them with ground pepper. Cooked them on low and they came out great. Any leftovers are great for making hash brown potatoes or potato salad. The olive oil gives the left over dishes a lovely flavor.

I've been doing this for years and it is a huge time saver.  In addition, at the holidays I put my sweet potatoes in the crock pot, not wrapped or coated with anything and basically let them steam until they are soft (on high a couple of hours depending on size). The benefit is the skin just slides off and they are ready to mash.  If you use a crockpot liner,  just let the crock cool and put it away.  No clean up.
Really easy, and very favorful! And very little cleanup-I used bargin brand foil!

Nothing is as good as an oven baked spud but these potatoes done in the crock pot are great when oven space is tight. Often serve with the works along a with prime rib roast using the "closed door method" to cook the meat.

This was a delicious salad! It had a delightful Thai flavor from the dressing, but was not spicy when mixed into the salad. However, a few fresh Thai chiles served with solved that! The dressing did have a nice sour taste (important to Thai cooking) that complemented the sweetness of the fruit. The pine nuts were very flavorful and added a nice touch, too. There were lots of toppings, and if one added some more salad mix, this would easily serve a couple more people. Very good! Thanks for a wonderful recipe!
This is a superb recipe and was enjoyed by everyone.  I didn't have any chillies on hand, so left them out - but it was still fantastic. I will definately be making this again!

This was very good.  I made it as a side dish, so I left out the chicken.  And I used mango instead of papaya, almonds instead of pine nuts, and my store didn't have any ripe avacado's, but that would have been a nice addition.   I'll definately make this again.
refreshing

We didn't have red capsicums (and did't really know what they were) so I substituted a pepper.  I only used one papaya, one avocado and used a whole cucumber and I'm glad I did.  I think two papayas would have been a bit much.
Honestly fantastic!  Will definitely be making this again.  I also used mangos instead of papayas and I used leftover chicken (poured over half the marinade and heated a little).

Sorry- I hate to give a bad rating, but this wasn't good. I only had a few tastes and then threw it out. It had an odd texture. It wasn't smooth like I thought it should be. I guess that could have been something I did wrong, but I followed the directions to the letter... It was really just the texture that got me.
MMMmmmm!!  A great twist on Key Lime Pie!  The whole family loved it; including our cat who loves citrus fruits!!

What a unique and different dip. I made this for a women's luncheon. It was a big hit with all the ladies. Very creamy in texture. Wonderful key lime flavor. I served it with graham crackers for the luncheon. I made this again for me and my husband and we spread some on our bagels. Yummy stuff.

Oh yummmm!! I made this dip for me and nobody else. So delicious, I was in heaven. Creamy, pudding-like texture with the zippy tartness from the key lime juice. I used graham's for dipping. This would be great for a bridal or baby shower.

A lovely and refreshing dip. I used fresh squeezed key lime juice and I think that is what makes this taste so delicious. The texture was creamy and it had a nice sweet-tart taste. I did like others and used graham crackers for dipping. Something different and will probably make this again for Easter. Thanks Nurse Di.

I made this for a family gathering and we all thought it was yummy, but very rich dip. I used graham crackers but we also thought it would be good with shortbread cookies or chocolate graham crackers. The recipe indicates a serving size of 6-8 portions but I thought it made a huge bowl, I had 10 adults and alot left over. Overall our guests rated it 4 1/2 stars.

Made this for a get-together, served with graham crackers, grapes, sliced apples & oranges, & cubed angel food cake -- Everyone LOVED it!  Good thing I had so many things to serve with it, because it makes a lot.

I made this for a sweet touch on my Christmas Eve appetizer table, and was it ever a hit!  I almost didn't make it, because I couldn't find key limes, but decided to go ahead with regular lime juice.  As good as it was, I can't wait to try it with key limes next time.  I served it with shortbread cookies and very thin gingerbread crisps.  Both were delicious.

This dip was very tasty, but very, very rich.  Everyone liked it, but it just was so sweet you couldn't eat a lot of it, and the recipe makes A LOT!  I might try to half the recipe and cook it for 10-15 minutes and see what happens.  Really good, but it just makes so much!

Boy is this good!!! I took it to a party and it was the star of the evening. It goes great with graham cracker sticks. It does make a lot though. Even though about 12 of use were eating it as fast as we could, I still brought home about 1/2. Thanks for a refreshing, light dessert that is impressive because it is so different.
Sorry - because it seems I'm the only one who didn't like this. I served it with graham cracker sticks and ended up throwing it away as it didn't get eaten.
I took the key lime dip to a party and it was a hit.  Everyone loved it.  I highly recommend it.

I made this over the weekend and served it with graham cracker sticks. I don't know if using the "double strength" key lime juice did it but it was really too sweet and had a odd smell about it - too limey. It tasted okay but I'll have to figure out a way to cut down on the sweet/limey taste. It was just okay. It was very easy to make and the texture was okay. You have to really stir it after baking it so not to get a weird texture.
Great recipe!  Had alot of flavor!  Thanks for a great recipe!
Loved this recipe! Better than Chicken.
Very tasty!!  I'll be making this often.  Easy to prepare.

Have always made the old
cube steak/mushroom soup
recipe, till this one, and how much better!!  It is far easier to control than the other,
and turned out very good.
May add a small can of
mushrooms sometime to keep DH happy, but will be making gravy just this
way.  Should have thought of this myself!!!

This was great comfort food for my steak and potato husband!  I never make gravy that turns out and this was perfect.  I didn't have unsalted butter so I used regular and it was tasty.  Will definately add to my faves.

This recipe is delicious! I cooked the steaks just long enough to stay moist and the the crust got nice and crispy. I also fried the steaks in bacon grease and made the gravy in the same pan as I fried the steak.I will definately make this again!!

VERY tasty.  I really enjoyed the flavors of both the steaks and the gravy.  Milk gravy is TOUGH to make, without it tasting like flour and/or pastey, but this was perfect.  Even the kids ate it up.  Thanks!

excellent.  i prepared for a family of five and they really enjoyed it.  served with mashed potatoes and salad.  this recipe reminds me of the South.  i prepared this in an electric skillet at 250 to brown turning every 15 minutes for the first 30 minutes, then reduced to 200-225 turning every 30 minutes and simmering for 2 hours (be sure to add water to the skillet to keep the meat moist and sprinkly salt/pepper on the meat to retain the seasoning)...meat is very tender prepared this way.  the milk gravy as noted in this recipe goes along way.  kudos to your Father for a wonderful recipe!
Delicious!  I've made this recipe a few times and we love it.  I don't make the gravy, but the ingredients and instructions for cooking the cube steaks are right on.  This is a keeper!
I can't say enough good things about this.  Awesome!  My husband actually complimented me on this and that means a lot coming from him.

I can't say enough how wonderful this recipe is.  I don't make it any longer because, well frankly it isn't very healthy.  But it is amazingly good.  Instead of using butter I will leave a little of the oil from the meat frying to make the roux.

As much as my doctor may discourage these, I love them.  The flavor is great and one of the ultimate comfort foods.  I usually make more gravy since you can never have too much of it.  I served with mashed potatoes and a side of cooked spinach.
Made this entree tonight. Instead of Season-All, which I didn't have, I used Old Bay. Everything else was as you directed. The cube steak was fall-apart tender! Very nice meal. Thank you.
This recipe was alright.  It was easy to make, but the flavors were a bit bland.  I think I'll keep searching for a cube steak recipe.
This recipe was quick and easy. I used a bit more seasoning, including cayane. I used the same skillet with pan gunk to make my gravey.
Also made the gravy in the pan drippings, I think it's a must for that extra flavor! Delish!

Good flavor, and the gravy was tasty [especially cooked in the pan drippings] but I thought they were cooked with too much grease.  I also feel that this cooking method doesn't break down the cube steaks well enough.  It's a cut that really should cook in a crock pot...which will be my preferred method.  I did really enjoy the gravy and the overall seasonings as posted though.

Thanks for posting.

This was amazing!  I had never made anything like this before but wanted something different.  My husband raved over it several times during the meal and he can be picky.  The only change I made to it was that I crushed Ritz Vegetable Crackers into the flour mix and then used Mrs. Dash gralic and herb seasoning in the gravy.  The pan dripping are a must in the gravy!  Thanks so much for the recipe.
just finished this quick easy classic. worked like a charm!!! great texture, and even spiced it up a little with my own seasonings.

First time ever making country fried steak and this recipe turned out awesome! For people who say that the cube steak is a tough meat still when you make this you should really try using pork cube steak. When I was placing the meat in the egg mixture it pratically fell apart. It was my first time making homemade gravy as well and the directions actually yielded some pretty good gravy. Will totally make this again for my husband who doesn't usually like new things but loved this. Thanks!

I first tried this recipe a few months ago but forgot to review it. I usually make it with my regular breading mixture; but I really like the milk gravy, seasoned to taste. This has already become my go-to recipe for milk gravy. Thank you!

Made this recipe for dinner tonight. I halved it as its just me and DH, and I used regular salted butter instead of the unsalted for the milk gravy.  It was delicious!  The crust on the cube steak was just perfect and the milk gravy was thick and delicious.  I will definitely be making this comfort food again.  Thanks for posting!
great.  i'm from texas and know my chicken fried steak and this was awesome.

Easy and delicious!
I must admit that I over seasoned my flour, thus making it too peppery. My own fault as I did not measure.
I served with mashed potatoes and steamed veg.
NICE!
Thanks for posting this great recipe

This was a HIT at dinner tonight!   The gravy turned out very tasty and a good consistency.  The Cube steak turned out well.  I made sure it was done on one side before I flipped it over.  We ate with biscuits and mashed potatoes. YUMMY!   Thanks for sharing.

Thank you for submitting this delicious recipe. I drained the grease in my pan and made the gravy in the skillet so I could get all the "brown bits." Husband thought it was very close to the gravy his Mom used to make. Served with mashed potatoes and garden fresh tomatoes. It was a hit which doesn't happen too often with my "Picky Eaters" Will definitely make this one again!!
Great. This was exactly what I was craving!!! Been feeling poorly, and nothing perks you up like good ol' comfort food!

so now i can renew my GRITS (girls raised in the south) registration because thanks to you i can make GRAVY!!!  country fried steak is an old staple here, but i always cheat and buy a jar of brown gravy while secretly pining for this gravy instead.......so i'm late to the party but i've arrived and the hive couldn't be happier!  i also LOVE that i can make this along side my meat, not with drippings......great flavor, thanks again!!
Excellent.  Very easy to make and I loved the meal!
Awesome !!! Simple and Easy... used the pan dripping for the gravy, after draining off the oil
Can pork cube steak be used instead of beef? Is it still tender? I was "gifted" a ton of pork and from what I can tell it's cube steak cut. I'm just trying to find some way to use it.
This dish was excellent.  The sauce turned out wonderful and was an excellent choice for the pork chops !
Excellent taste, especially the onion sauce.  I will definitely make this receipe again.
Delicious.  DH and I both rated this a thumbs up, 5 star, A+, etc.  Used coarse ground black pepper and a little garlic powder and it couldn't have been better.
One word.........AWESOME!! We'll be making this again soon!
Thank you for a great recipe. I will be making it again, I hate onions but had no problem eating this.
Really enjoyed the chops,will make again.Very tasty.

The sauce is spectacular! And the chops were tender and well seasoned. My husband would like the onions diced, so I'll do that next time. And since my kids were eating this I omitted the beer and just used a whole cup of beef broth. This is a delicious recipe. Thanks!
This was excellent. I also diced the onions but other than that, didn't change a thing. Made a wonderful dinner.
Tender and flavorful! My DS that won`t eat pork chops had this! And that says a lot! he does like onions so that may have helped! I did add an apple to the onions. Thanks for a great recipe!
Yum! This is another way to enjoy pork rather than just plain fried pork chops. I used a dark belgium beer that made the sauce really yummy! Thanks!

The sauce is what really makes these pork chops special.  It's a little sweet from the onions, and the beer was not overpowering.  Great with mashed potatoes.  I'm glad you decided to post this one Beck D!

WOW, Great tasting pork chops. We loved the sauce and the pork was very tender. I did add a sliced golden delicious apple with the onions like Rita had added. I think that this added a lot of flavor. Served the chops with a baked sweet potatoe and a salad of baby greens. Thank you for this yummy recipe that I will be making again.

These Schweinekotelett in Zwiebelsosse were just fabulous. I made only a few small adjustments. I added 3 cloves of chopped garlic with the onions, and I followed Rita’s suggestion of adding apple (apple always goes so well with pork; I used a Granny Smith apple, unpeeled, thinly sliced) and I used my Vegetable Stock Recipe #135453 in place of the beef broth. The beer (and I’m not a beer drinker) added a great flavour; just a bit of a dilemma as to what to do with the rest of the beer. I’ve put it in the freezer.  Only time will tell whether it’s okay next time I make a recipe with beer in it!  All the flavours blended superbly. It’s a great recipe, Beck D. perhaps now you’ll give it a try!

Good - especially liked the onion gravy with mashed potatoes.  Added a granny smith apple as suggested.  I had a bottle of Corona at home, so we used that.
Thanks.
These were very good!  I will be making them again.  Next time I will try them with the apple added.  I made them with boiled red potaoes.  Thanks for sharing!

My family totaly enjoyed this.  It was quite easy for me to make for them.  This is just not a recipe I cared for.  Maybe it was the Miller Light beer my Dh bought for me to use.  The next time I am going to use a much better beer well see how it turns out.
I gave this 5 stars because that was how they rated it.
Very good...a nice basic pork chop recipe.

One bit of advice for anyone making this dish -- and you should -- make extra onions. Scaled this recipe down to two and prepared as directed, albeit with a little less oil and flour.  While I really enjoyed the chops, the onions with thier beefy-beer gravy were just divine. I used a regular beer but I think it would work better with a darker more full bodied variety.  Thanks Beck!
Outstanding! I was out of veg. oil (of all things) so I used 2 tablespoons of butter for the browning.  Yum!  Really enjoyed the beer flavor of the sauce.  Thanks for posting!

These were so SCRUMPTIOUS!!!  They seemed to melt in your mouth.  I made coriander rice to serve with it, and the sauce from this was so good with the rice.  This will probably be requested often at my house from now on!  It's like a pork and beer flavored version of my chicken in tarragon sauce, "Recipe #125589".  Thanks for sharing!

I would never have thought that these ingredients would make such a tasty dish!
I only had a pork fillet on hand so used that (took it out of the pan about 8 minutes after adding the beer and broth - returned it for the last couple of minutes).  Easy and packed with flavour - served with mashed garlic potatoes, glazed carrots and Brussels Sprouts recipe #102677.
Thanks for another winner Beck!
Excellent, a new way for us to cook pork. I agree with Toni wish we had more onions.
Absolutley wonderful pork chops, the onion sauce is outstanding!! (must be the beer!) We very much enjoyed them and will be making them again for sure!!  Thanks Tebo, another great one!!
This was pretty good.  I thought it would turn out too oniony but they were soft and yummy with the sauce.  Plenty to pour over potatoes, too.
Very nice flavor and so easy to make!  Thanks!

I think I can say, this is about the best pork chop recipe. I did use 1 cup each of the broth & beer. wanted more gravy.
and did cook a bit longer. It was wonderful.
Thanks, for this recipe
Tebo.
This was simple and good.  I will definately make again!

This is a great recipe.  The pork was so juicy.  The only change I'm going to make the next time I do this recipe is to leave off the flour in Step one, and pan sear the chops in some butter.  The steam given off by the resting meat in Step 6 left the floured surface mushy.  The onion sauce was wonderful.  My 17 month old grandson, who hates PB&J, loved this meal.  You will too.
This was simple and very tasty. I did as others suggested and doubled the beer and beef broth. Thanks for the recipe.

My family enjoyed this recipe very much.  My two kids (5 & 8) ate it up.  It's always great when you can make a meal this flavorful with so few ingredients and such little work.  I doubled the beer and broth as others suggested and had more gravy than I needed (I'd do it again though, I also look forward to trying it with an apple added).  I went with the recommended scalloped potatoes on the side, what a perfect match.  I'll be making this again and often.

I have never been able to get my pork chops to come out tender, till I made this for supper last night. I was FABULOUS!! I doubled the recipe(I had 6 to feed)except for the beer, and I can't stand the smell. I thought I might have some left for lunch today, but I was WRONG! The family and myself LOVED it! Thanks

I wasn't so sure it sounded good but tried it because it had great reviews. I doubled the liquids (plus adjusted everything for 6 chops) and it looked like it could still use some extra liquid so added a bit more. My family loved it - including my picky eater son-in-law and 2 young grandchildren. It's a keeper!
It is great! Fast and easy weekday meal. Even my picky husband loved it!
I liked it but I believe it needs more spice.  It was rather bland. Easy to make and quick for dinner when you are running behind.

This was a really simple and quick way to make great tasting chops and gravy. I used boneless chops and the only thing I'd change would be to make more gravy, as we would have liked to have more with our mashed potatoes. Thanks for sharing.

Oh MY Gosh!!!! This was the best recipe for pork chops I've ever found. I'm sending it on to all my family because I know they'll love it too!

I didn't change a single thing. Thanks Tebo

I was a little worried when I was making this because the beer had such an overwhelming aroma but it did not taste strongly of beer at all.  It actually added a very unique and really great flavor!  I will continue to make this regularly.

Good enough for quick and easy week night dinner, but otherwise it's a little bland for my taste. Maybe adding garlic and some rosemary would give this dish a little more punch? However, I must say that the beer makes the chops really tender, much better texture than the one I'm used to for chops.
I made this dish tonight for dinner and loved it.  I skipped the flour, but kept everything else.  The chops were tender and the sauce was great on my potatoes.  This is a keeper. Thanks!
This was good but rather bland for us.  I will make it again but perhaps add some additional spices - perhaps some garlic.  Thanks for providing a solid base!

This was  quite good. While it was cooking, I tasted the liquid and I thought it was a little bland. So, I quickly read some of the reviews and saw that a few of the other reviewers added Garlic Powder to theirs, so I did the same and it really perked up the flavor. I think it may have been bland at first, because I used a thick boneless pork steak instead of a pork chop. I think bones add to the flavor of meat juices and liquids in the recipe. Even though I used only 1 pork steak, I didn't cut down on the beer or the broth. That may have been part of the problem as well. But, I love gravy and like to have plenty of it. I poured some of the sauce/gravy over my Recipe #240456 which was really good. The meat was really good with the gravy over it too. I will make this again, except I think next time I will use a couple of pork chops instead of a pork steak and see if that makes a difference. Thanks Tebo for a great recipe.

The sauce comes out very sweet, but good.  Chops are very tender.  I added rosemary and 2 cloves of garlic to the gravy, and I seasoned the chops with italian seasoning before breading. I may try less onion next time, and/or dark beer, to cut back on the sweetness.
Great flavor and such a nice gravy, husband loved it, thank you!

This recipe was delicious.  Everything was perfect.  The pork chops were moist and tender (I used my favorite pork rub for seasoning in addition to the salt and pepper), added a bit more garlic.  Dark amber ale was a perfect beer.  Some dry vermouth or dry white sherry might make it less sweet, but it was great the way it was.
These pork chops were wonderful (and we had great fun trying to pronounce them!)  Would make again and thanks for posting!

This is my favorite way to make pork chops! I found this recipe in an old cookbook and have been making it for years. I don't measure anything anymore and so I am usually generous on the beer part (plus I love to watch it fizz when added)!! The smell and taste is just heavenly.

My husband gives this one 5 stars! Like many others, I added 3 cloves of garlic. I also added about a teaspoonful of Worcestershire Sauce. I will definitely make this again but think I may add a bay leaf and 1/2 cup of white wine. Think of pork chops with a rich French Onion Soup-ish gravy! YUMM!

This was very good.  I added some minced garlic, but otherwise followed exactly.  My pork chops were fairly thick but still came out just a little dry.  We'll definitely be having this again though, perhaps with a longer, slower cooking time.
I liked these better than the rest of the family.  You should definitely use a good beer to get better flavor.  They were better the night we ate them and not as great as a leftover.
Very good...I was pleasantly surprised as I do not drink beer, used a dark ale and it was great...
I used a dark ale also, very good, easy preparation,  Served with scalloped potatoes as suggested.  Very nice meal...Thank you for sharing
I followed the recipe to a T except I substituted chicken broth for the beef broth.  When hot the chops were tender and the sauce was good.

We had this tonight for dinner and it was fabulous. I was a little worried the beer flavor would be too strong but it was perfect.  In fact, had it not been there the dish wouldn't have been nearly as tasty.  We didn't change a thing from the recipe.  I'll be making this again and again.  Thanks for posting.

This was sooo good.
I made this with dark honey beer and made a double batch. YUMM!!!

Thanks for posting this it did remind me of moms Schnitzel mit Zwiebelsosse.
Another easy family favorite. I always double the gravy ingredients (not the onions) so we'll have enough. Everyone just about licks their plates, we like it so much!

This is GREAT!  My daughter said she'd eat this every day if given the choice.  My husband and 
I both loved this. I highly recommend doubleing the gravy.  I cut the onions a little thicker than I should've, so I just pulled the chops out of the pan and let the onions cook a little longer.  I added some garlic and extra beer since we only had lite.  I let it simmer a little bit before adding the chops back in and then simmered for 15 more minutes. I think a darker beer would've had more flavor.  We had this with mashed potatoes.  What a delicious meal!  Thanks so much!!!
My husband made this for us last night and I thought it was pretty darn good.  Will definately make again.  Only thing different he did was cooked the chops and let people put their own gravy on.

I was looking for something on how to cook pork chops and this was great !  The chops were tender the onion sauce was delicious.  I took the advice of another reviewer and took out the chops while cooking the onions and adding the beer and broth, then put the chops back in and covered to cook.  Worked great thanks for this one.  Hubby loved it!
So easy and good.  The kids tasted the gravy and felt the beer taste was too strong, so I added a can of beef broth and everyone loved it!  So tender and such good gravy for mashed potatoes.

Fantastic!  When I lifted the lid on the onions simmering the aroma reminded me of beer battered onion rings.  This dish was a big hit with the whole family.  I maded exactly as directed.  Served with brown rice and sugar snap peas.
Really simple to make and the onion gravy was delicious.
These were so delicious and made the yummiest gravy!  This was served with German Potato Salad.

This was an instant favorite.  I have made it several times.  The advice about doubling the sauce is right on target.  I love that there is a relatively low cal sauce I can make that is so tasty.  I will try making it on its own for other meats.  I buy beer just for this!

This is delicious!  And easy!  I don't even like pork chops that much!  I've made word for word to the recipe, but tonight I experimented because I had no beer.
Modifications:
I used one onion, and one green pepper.  Instead of beer I used the tomato sauce from a can of diced tomatoes - then I added the tomatoes. The rest stayed the same.  I was very proud of myself, it was amazing!

I used this as a base recipe -- I used red wine instead of beer, and chicken broth instead of beef broth. I didn't need the cornstarch to thicken the sauce, the flour worked fine. I was able to use 5 chops as well. I think part of the reason I did not need the cornstarch is I used slightly less liquid than the recipe called for. Very good, very easy and will prepare again.
These are the ultimate in comfort food.  I followed the recipe EXACTLY and it is perfect as is.  My family loved them and we will be having them often in the future.  Thank you Tebo.
Very nice. I didn't change a thing, served with mashed potatoes and a veggie.  Easy, tasted great and the gravy on potatoes was delicious! Thanks.

This is fantastic. It may be unorthodox but I did add some ingredients to boost the flavor. A teaspoon each of worchestershire, soy sauce, and tomato paste, and I also used the apples as another reviewer mentioned. Great stuff!
This wasn't anything special.  It was pretty much just pork chops in an onion gravy.  No WOW Factor.
The pork chops tasted bland.

Delicious comfort food. Easy too. The only change I made was to add 3 cloves of garlic with the onions. I don't think it's bland, as several reviewers have said, so much as it has a simple down-home taste that might disappoint someone expecting something fancy or exotic with all the rave reviews. My chops didn't come out super tender, but DH prefers meat to have some texture anyway. Served them with mashed potatoes and used the gravy over the top. Great dinner. Thanks for sharing.
Fast and Declicious. Husband loves it and so do I, even though I don't like beer.

This makes it to my "make again" file. I love the onion sauce, like everyone else. I did add a little "wurze" to the sauce as I simmered it. I also didn't bother with the flour. I doubled the sauce ingredients and I'm glad I did because I would have hated to be short on that wonderful sauce.  Thanks for this great, easy, fast recipe!!

Delicious recipe however the chops were tough. Next time I will remove the chops before adding the onions and return them when the liquids have been added. I omitted the flour and added fresh thyme. Because your ratings are so favourable, I realize that contributing factors such as my stove and the cut of chop may have resulted in tough chops...not your fault, therefore five stars!

My 15 year old son made these last night for us with little help, and they really turned out great. We did add an apple and doubled the onions, 'cos we like them together with pork. We also put the seared chops in the oven to finish and made the sauce in the same pan, which worked beautifully for us. Served them with scalloped potatoes and broccoli. Thanks, Tebo ... it's a keeper.

Wow, made this without the beer and still turned out fabulous! I am a beginner cook and this was a real treat for us! My husband is german and enjoyed this dish very much! (Next time I will have beer on hand and add it) Bravo!

My family enjoys everything German and we found these to be delicious and simple.  This made a great weeknight meal as it cooks under and hour and goes well with simple mashed potatoes or rice, along with a veggie or salad.  Others have suggested that one might add a bit of seasoning but it is actually quite nice to have a mild flavored meat and serve a more robust flavored vegetable/salad alongside - then the flavors don't compete.  Thanks Tebo!
this was the best....I used a huge onion and it seemed to have added some sweetness to the recipe. my DH loved it and said I could do this anytime!! yuuummmm. I did double the sauce.

Yummy!  I used some gourmet grill seasoning instead of salt and pepper and I seasoned the flour with it too.  I didn't have any beer so I used all beef broth instead.  It was easy and delicious and the gravy was wonderful over mashed potatoes too.  Thanks for posting!
This wasn't one our favorite 'zaar dishes, but looks like I'm in the minority with all the 5 star reviews.
What a great recipe! I would definitely make this again. I did double the amount of onions and the amount of broth and beer. Thank you!

Yummmy!  I loved the gravy!!  I started brainstorming of what else might be good to cook in such a delicious gravy....beef tips?...chicken?...I think I will try almost anything.  It was great!  Thanks for the great recipe!
I absolutely LOVE these pork chops!  I have the same recipe and was checking to see if it had already been posted.  Very flavorful and moist!  I think they go great with mashed potatoes.
Used more onions, extra liquid, added garlic and an apple. Yum.

This is an easy chop recipe.  We love chops in our house and this is a good recipe.  I really liked the onion sauce too, the beer and broth are perfect together.  I served this with scalloped potatoes and corn and my family was happy. THank you for sharing.
Great recipe!  I think the next time I will brown the pork chops and cook them in the crock pot for awhile.  Thanks for a great recipe!
Very good!  The gravy was so flavorful!
This was an easy to follow recipe with tasty results.  Thanks for a great pork chop!
Extremely delicious although I made it with a little bit more beer and broth.  Accidently, left on the stove after done simmering for an hour and it carmalized into a much better sauce.
Absolutely fabulous!  And sooooooo flavorful!  Paired very very well with some sauteed brussel sprouts.  Thanks for the recipe!

Enjoyed this very much--our city has a strong German heritage and unbelievably, no decent German restaurant! This was basic and good. Due to time constraints I didn't simmer it very long but gave it more oven time. I did follow the recipe but doubled it. Will increase the onions and gravy next time!
my 5 year olds and i are eating this right now... very good. i didn't have beer so i used moscato, and it is still amazing.

I knew this would be good just looking at the ingredients list. I had no idea it would taste as good as it did though! This was very delicious, and actually very easy as well. The biggest job was slicing the onions! The smell was reminiscent of Chicken Marsala while it was cooking so I added a handful of sliced mushrooms to the pan before it was too late. YUM, Pork Marsala made with beer??? Oh yeah! Thanks for this fabulous recipe. I will be making this again without a doubt!
Delicious! I made the recipe as directed using 2 boneless thick pork chops. DH loved the onion gravy.
Turned out good.
Needs some spices!  Really tasted too bland to me without any excitement, other than the basic onion salt and pepper taste. Need to add some zest!
Easy. Pork chops came out tender and flavorful!
We liked these! Made per recipe. Thank you.
A delicious recipe. I needed to make 6 pork chops rather than just 4, and I found it easy to increase the other ingredients, and still have a really good result.
Recipe does not state how long to bake in oven.

I am going to make this tonight. I noticed no one responded to how long to bake the chops. Generally, medium-thick bone-in chops can be baked for 25-30 minutes in a 425 degree oven. I will let you know how this works!
My thinking is that the chops are being kept warm while you are making the sauce no need for further cooking.

This recipe is REALLY good. Because of what I had on hand, I used normal chopped onion (instead of spring onion) and broccoli (instead of peas and carrots). I also used a different type of hot dog, called makkara here in Finland, but to an American like me it tastes exactly the same. Needless to say, it turned out incredibly and my husband and I ate it like it was our last meal! Delicious and incredibly easy, thanks so much for sharing :)

My husband LOVES fried rice, and this is a pretty good recipe. It doesn't quite taste like restaurant quality, but that's probably because it doesn't call for MSG. x] When it says cold rice, it says that for a reason. If you use warm rice it won't have that Fried Rice texture, it will be more moist and sticky. But still yummy. I even substituted canned chicken one night, and while it wasn't as good as the hotdogs, it was still good. One of my staple recipes!

DELICIOUS!!! This will be a staple in my house from now on!! Did not put in eggs, onions, and wouldn't next time either. Plates were licked clean by hubby, me and daughter!! Thanks for an awesome recipe!! :)
We followed this recipe to a T, and it was awesome. No leftovers for me :(
A bite of this quick bread will just melt in your mouth. Goes together in just a matter of seconds and the end result is a wonderfully moist quick bread.  It is hard to stop at just one slice.

I made this bread for a neighbor to thank him for helping us cut down some bushes. It smelled soooo good cooking that I was kind of bummed I couldn't have any. Well, as fate would have it, the bread completely fell apart when I was trying to remove it from the pan. At first I was peeved, but then realized this could be a blessing in disguise. I could now try a piece! The first bite was heavenly, and every bite thereafter was even better -- moist, sweet, and melt in your mouth good. A word of warning...let this bread cool completely before trying to un-pan it. It is so moist and tender it is especially prone to breakage.

Excellent quick bread!  It is tender & will indeed melt in your mouth.  Be sure to let this cool completely before removing it from the pan ... I had intended to get up early this morning & let it cool for breakfast, but I slept late.  I went ahead & mixed it up & baked it, but was too anxious to let it cool since it smelled so good & we were hungry.  Part of it stayed in the pan, but rest assured it did not go to waste!  Then we demolished half the loaf just between the two of us!  This recipe is easy to mix (I did it by hand in about 10 minutes) and the results are yummy!  I will make this again but will let it cool before taking it out of the pan.  I highly recommend this recipe ... thanks for posting! -M

This is really good, yet simple to make.  I would recomend using the cinnamon/sugar mixture mostly on the first 2 layers.  I had too much left over by the time I got to the top layer and a lot of it fell off.  I also plan to try using an 8x8 pan, making this a coffee cake.
What a great versatile recipe! I just used this to make a creamy walnut raspberry vinaigrette. Yummy.

These are so easy to put together and I had the ingredients sitting in the pantry or fridge.  I made the basic and seven of the other combination, I didn't made 'Lighter Bacon Dressing' as the only meat I have is chicken and fish.  We sampled them all on salad, chicken and pasta, Hubby's (DH) favourite was the Italian Vinegarette and I like that one and Mustard Dressing.  Thank you 3KillerBs
This was nice.  Made the Mustard Dressing with some hot mustard I have.  Easy, tastey salad dressing. I will make this again and try the other variations.  Thank you 3killerbs.  Shirl
I like the creamy garlic version. I added a little powdered parmesan cheese to mine.
Loved the vinaigrette variation!!  Got this marked as a favorite salad dressing!

I used the Lemon Dressing version over a tossed green salad with cherry tomatoes, spring onion and julienned carrots added to and it was delicious.  Will definately be trying the other versions.  Thank you 3KillerBs.

We loved the lemon dressing! Which could also be called Greek dressing. I doubled the oregano since I used fresh, used one clove of garlic and added 1/8 teaspoon each of salt and pepper. Next time I will cut the oil back by one tablespoon so it is more lemony. Had it over arugula and it was sensational!

Please note that the nutritional information is not correct, as the software cannot distinguish between the original an all the variations, so all ingredients in all versions have been added together. This has been asked several times in the Cooking Q & A Forum.
Tried the mustard version tonight, we doubled it for a simple green salad with grilled dijon chicken and it was excellent. Will definitely make this again, thanks for posting.
Great source for variations of my favorite dressing. Bookmarked.

Really well done, very useful and I will be using it a lot.

Thank you!!
I made the creamy garlic dressing last night with nonfat Greek yogurt, white wine vinegar and 2 garlic cloves.  I love love love it. It's so much tastier than store bought!!!!

I have been looking for a great vinaigrette recipe. This one is perfect as you start with the basics and learn the options are limitless. Made the Creamy Garlic and it was delicious. Will definitely try all the variations. Thanks for sharing!
Extremely helpful. Recipe you'll use over and over again
Very good fish.  It has plenty of flavor.  Made it exactly as written.  Will use this one again for sure.
This is exactly what I was looking for: versatile, well-proportioned, SMALL batch vinaigrette. The variations are a great bonus.

I would just like to say thank you 3KillerBs for the recipes. My entire family love the creamy garlic vinaigrette. We found that if you pour it on porks, seasoned to your liking, about 3 to 5 minutes before they're done it's amazing! Good work nice recipe, we hope there is more o follow
I made the pepper parmesan and it was to die for. I used what i had vinegar wise and that was applw cider and i used mayo cause thats what i had.
Great recipe ! Thanks for posting!...I added my tweaks using your options!!
Hi am looking for nice dips
Great receipes but can I use a wine vinager
Amazing, how long can you store it, especially if it has been made with mayo?

I made the Lemon Vinaigrette salad dressing - tweaking it by adding a few extra spices - Mrs. Dash No-Salt table seasoning and Mrs. Dash No-Salt Garlic and herb seasoning. I also added splash of low sodium soy sauce and a drop of honey. I made the dressing for a salad I was bringing to a party and it was a big hit! Definitely much better than bottled dressing.
Thank you for these recipes and ideas. Great stuff. Just made the basic and it was great.

i did a caper dressing. Instead of vinegar used caper brine and minced a few capers to taste. we like capers and it was a nice change on a tossed green salad. added wee bit of dijon mustard for immulsification.

This was absolutely the best cinnamon bread. The texture of the bread is perfect- I think the butttermilk had a lot to do with that. Very quick and easy to put together. I doubled the recipe and made two loaves. Like some of the other reviewers, I also had a problem with the bread sticking to the bottom of the pan, even though I had greased the pan. Next time I will try flouring it as well to see if that helps.

I cant believe I forgot to review this recipe!  It was sooooo good.  Made a special trip to the store to pick up the buttermilk, and man was it worth it.  I love baking and cooking, but my household is only 2 and in many cases we end up with a lot of leftovers and/or wasted food.  Not with this bread!  I don't know who ate more me or my boyfriend, and let me tell you, it did not get time to cool!
BTW I used PAM for spraying my pan and had no problem with sticking.

This quick bread is wonderful. It takes no time to prepare and is so good!! We all loved it, I'd  give it 10 stars if I could. I lined my loaf pan with parchment paper and let the loaf cool before removing it from the pan. I had no problem at all with sticking. I will be making this again and again. Kim, thanks for posting this delicious recipe!!!

I used PAM as well and did not have any sticking problems. The bread was fantastic, although follow the advice about the cinnamon sugar. Use most of it on the bottom 2 layers, otherwise you'll be left with a lot leftover as well as too much for the top.

"This is the best food ever" from the lips of my 4yro this morning says it all! I will probably line the pan next time...mine was trying to stick and as several someones said before, use most of the cin/sugar mix on the first 2 layers!
This is a wonderful cinnamon bread.  The 8x4 pan was too small to hold all of the batter, but a 9x5 pan worked perfectly.  We will definitely enjoy this again.

Very good. I made it as a coffeecake (9-inch sq. pan)and added pecans to the cinnamon sugar and therefore altered baking time. Other than that, I followed the recipe. Eating some right now and it is delish. Will make again.

I agree that the 8x4" pan was too small - my first attempt at this, and the mess that was on the bottom of my oven, attest to that.  However, I gave it another shot in a 9x5" pan, and it was a HUGE hit.
With how quick it was to make, impressive and well received the finished product was, I will definitely be making this again.
This is VERY good.  Perfect with coffee, or as a midnight snack.
This was the best! It was very easy to make. I added about 1/4 tea. of vanilla to the butter,egg,sugar mixture.

Very quick and easy- I baked in a loaf pan. I always keep a shaker jar of cinnamon/spice/sugar mixed up, so it made this recipe even quicker. Kids loved being the ones that got to sprinkle in the cinnamon mixture. DH and kids and friends ate every crumb.
Good recipe. Perhaps I did something wrong but I found this a tad bit dry. Maybe I should have added a bit more buttermilk?

I had some leftover buttermilk from another recipe and was looking for something to make which used buttermilk.  The reviews on this bread were good and my family loves cinnamon, so I thought I would give it a try.  It was easy to mix, smelled terrific while baking and was moist and delicious.  We all liked this recipe and it is going on my list of favorites.  Thanks for sharing.

This was a very easy bread to make and it turned out great.  I used most of the sugar/cinnamon mixture on the first two layers and only sprinkled about a 1/2 tablespoon on the top of the bread.  The bread came out very moist and everyone liked it.

This bread was pretty good. It was easy to make and my daughter enjoyed helping.  I didn't have any problems with this recipe at all.  I expected it to be a little sweeter than it was, which only means I can adapt the recipe in the future :)

This turned out a lovely and easy coffee cake, moist and dense with good flavor.  I added a handful of chopped pecans with the cinnamon/sugar, about half a cup total.  Next time maybe adding chopped nectarine.  Later in the fall, apple or pear.  This is better than Bisquick!
Completely AWESOME.  Just don't put too much sugar on the top.

This is a lovely quick bread, easy to make, moist & flavorful.  It fit well in the 8x4" pan.  I do agree that it is important to use most of the cinnamon/sugar mixture in the 2 bottom layers.  I ended up discarding some as the tope was completely coated before I ran out.  Thanks, Kim

I made this for DS last weekend to take with him when he moved into the dorm at college for his freshman year.  He and his roommate said it's "super" bread, and would I make another loaf the next time he comes home for a weekend?  They've been eating it for their breakfast before class.  Thanks for sharing this, Kim.

This was awesome.  I kept an eye on mine and took it out of the oven about 8 minutes earlier because I had a bigger pan.  The texture is just like coffee cake.  I love all things like cinnamon rolls, toast etc.  This is a keeper!  Thanks!

WOW -- great flavor and very moist -- cooked in 8 x 8" pan -- took 30 minutes.  Did follow the reviewers before me, and used most of the cinnamon/sugar mixture on the two internal layers, leaving just enough to coat the top and not fall off.  It zoomed out the pan!

Delicious.  I wasn't paying attention while reading through the recipe, because I poured half the batter in, sprinkled it with half the cinnamon/sugar mixture, and repeated.  It made for a delicious center, but there was way too much "topping"; it fell off when I removed the bread from the pan!  Still, enough had baked on the top to form a delicious crust.  Thank you for sharing such a good recipe.  This bread is more cake-like than bread-like, and I will make this again and again.
Really quick and easy to make and the taste is delicious - light, fluffy and very 'more-ish'.  Will certainly make it again and thanks for submitting this recipe. Give it a try!

This bread was great! Very easy and quick to make.  I did find that making it in a 9x5 pan was better and to put more cinnamon/sugar mixtue on the first two layers and less on top.  I will definitely make this again. My husband and I could not stop eating it!
Thanks
KEP

Very nice & moist!  As a few previous reviewers also stated, next time I make this (and there will be a next time!) I will put more of the cinnamon-sugar mixture on the bottom two layers and much less on the top.  I highly recommend this recipe!

I just finished making this bread for breakfast and it was great! Sooo moist and soft- We loved it! I took the other reviewer's advice, and put most of the cinn&sugar in the first 2 layers. When we cut into it we could see perfect swirls of cinnamon! Delicious!
I made this bread this morning for a light Saturday morning breakfast.  We all loved it.  I thought the bread really tasted like eating a cinnamom roll.  This is a definate keeper.

This is amazing! It smellt so irresistable that to follow people's advice I had to leave the house to allow it to cool before turning it out! However, my patience paid off because the cooling time coupled with a heavy butter greasing meant that it just slid out of the pan. I only had an 8"x4" pan but with the mixture spread out evenly it stayed put and we had the most delicious breakfast! Thanks for this, it's a keeper!

This makes a wonderful quick breakfast or snack.  I used a 9x5 pan and it came out perfectly.  I made sure to grease AND flour the pan after reading some of the other comments.  I highly recommend this recipe!
Oh boy, did my kids LOVE this cinnamon bread!!  I have made 3 loaves since last week - one to give a neighbor, but not a single loaf has actually made it to the neighbor yet!
I thought this just tasted like your average coffee cake, but my fiance loved it!  Thanks!

Very good bread, smelled wonderful as it baked.  Rave reviews from both of my fussy children and my husband.  I did take a greased knife and swirled the batter and the cinnamon mixture after alternating, to mix it through the entire loaf.  Thanks for the recipe!
Fantastic!  DH ate the whole loaf in one day, OK I helped.  This would be the best on a cold morning or evening or anytime.  I used a 9x5 pan and extra grease so it wouldn't stick.  Super yummy!
This was a big hit at my house. I have to add my 5 stars to the rest. Thanks for posting!

Fantastic recipe! Though I would cut the cinnamon/sugar mixture in half, covered all 3 layers and still had more in the bowl.
 
As to those who had trouble with the layers separating - try not sprinkling the cinnamon/sugar all the way out to the edges, leave a 1/4" boarder all around. This will allow the layers to adhere, otherwise the cinnamon/sugar will prevent the layers from sticking together.
easy a good recipe, thanks for sharing.

One more review won't hurt...This is worth it!  I made this as a special Christmas morning treat before we left for family gatherings.  It was SO good.  I wasn't sure I had made it right as I too had extra cinamon sugar left over; and it was a little hard to get out of the pan.  I will flour it a little next time, but this tasted wonderful (isn't that what counts??)  The layers actually made swirls too.  Thanks so much Kim D.
Tastes delicious. Smells sensational. Easy to make. I used non-stick cooking spray and it came right out of the pan.
I just made this as an after school snack for my kids.  I made it into 12 muffins.  They were delicious!  The kids loved them and so did I.

this was a great recipe!  I did find that the cinnamon was a tiny bit strong, and i love cinnamon.  i will reduce it just a bit next time.  I didn't have any buttermilk on hand, but instead put a Tbl.  of vinegar,then filled up the measuring cup with milk to make 1 cup and let it sit for about 5 minutes.  I also buttered and floured an 8X8 square pan and baked it at 350 for about 35-40 minutes.  Also, next time I think that i will dot some butter on the top.  that will keep the cinnamon sugar from falling off and will give it a nice crumb topping texture.    yum!

I had some buttermilk I wanted to use up and liked the sound of this quick recipe.
The texture is lovely, light and moist.
Love the cinnamon flavour throughout, thanks for sharing.

Thank you so much for sharing your tasty recipe Kim D. My family and I enjoyed this bread very much, it reminded us of Amish Friendship bread, but is much easier to make. This easy to make bread recipe produces a rich, flavourful,light, moist and tender cake.

Great! My DH is on his second slice as I write. Did have a problem with the cinnamon sugar pouring of the top when I removed it from the pan, glad I didn't add oleo to top layer though because this definately does not need any extra moisture! Nice and moist loaf(so I'll just put up with the extra cin/sugar mess)
Thanks for a wonderful post Kim D.
This is very good-and very easy.  The batter was much thicker than I had expected.  Also, Next time I would add less of the cinnamon/sugar mixture on top and put more of it in the cake.

Truth be told, I didn't think this was that great.  I was expecting big things after reading the reviews, but it was just average to me.  It took much longer to bake than what the directions said, and when the middle was finally done the outside was a bit burned.  It smelled so wonderful I could hardly wait to taste it, but when I did it tasted like regular old cinnamon bread.  It was okay, but I probably won't make it again.
This was a good fast coffee cake bread...I did not think it was exceptional but good

This was a very nice bread.   I did add a tablespoon of cinnamon to the batter in addition to the "filling" cinnamon.   It will be a nice addition to the things I make for dh to take to work for breakfast.
YUM!  I loved it.  The texture is wonderful!  I used a 9x5 pan and it turned out great!  It was absolutely delicious!
This was an excellent breakfast quick bread. Very rich, moist and smells incredible while baking. With a hot cup of coffee, it is the perfect start to a cool, crisp fall day. Thanks Kim.
WOndeful, so soft and so delicious. Next time I might add a bit less sugar, but overall it was really the best cinnamon cake I ever tasted. THANKS!
Easy & good tasting bread, i did put too much cinnamon/sugar on top, but it's  still good and the next time i make this i'll know better, lol. Thanks Kim.

Very tasty. Like other I used less of the cinnamon sugar mixture on top, baked in a bigger pan, and sprayed it with Pam cooking spray then sprinkled flour on the pan. It sunk a bit in the center but it was very easy, quick, and delicious.

This is so GOOD!  I used an 8x4" glass loaf pan which proved to be the perfect size.  I also used a knife to swirl the cinnamon/sugar mixture into the batter to make sure the cinnamon was evenly distributed throughout the loaf. My bread was done in 45 minutes.  Makes a great snack or quick morning breakfast bread on the run!  Thanks, Kim : )
Loved it! Very moist bread. This recipe is definitely a keeper. Agree with others about putting most of the cinnamon sugar mixture on first two layers.

I made this today and I used a 8x4 loaf pan and it was perfect.  I sprayed Pam on the pan and had no problems taking the loaf out.  A little sinking in the middle but nothing to get upset over.  This was a easy quick recipe and I would definately make it again.  P.S.  It makes to house smell really good while it is baking.
I had some extra buttermilk after making those yummy knock-off Red Lobster biscuits. My husband said make sure you save this Cinnamon Bread recipe! We loved it!

Great recipe! My friends and I love it.  For the first time, I tried it with yogurt, it came out very dense but so delish!  For the second time, I used milk and lemon, came out much fluffier and delish as well.  Will cut back on the sugar (personal preference) in future.
I din't have a loaf pan so I put the batter in a square pan.  It was sooooo goooood that I went out and bought a loaf pan and will be making this one again soon!!!
OMG- this was so good!! It was moist, light, fluffy and tasted heavenly! This is now one of my favorites! Thanks for posting Kim D! :D

I tried this using a large muffin tin this time. Tastes just as fabulous as the first time I made it, but it baked faster - about 20 minutes. My kids love these and I know I will be making them often.
Yummy and moist!

Great recipe!  I added raisins, and "swirled" the batter for more of a swirl effect.  I also added pats of butter on top of the bread before baking, and added a cream cheese glaze to the top after.  My family loves it!

i'm so impressed.  i didn't have buttermilk, so i used someone else's suggestion of 1 tbl spoon of vinegar in milk and let it sit. well, i dont know if it made a difference over regular skim, but this loaf is wonderful. 

i swirled the cinamoon/sugar mix right in (i split the batter in half, swirled about half in then, poured batter on top, swirled almost the rest of it in, then dusted the top with the little bit of the remainder).  so good. 

i dont know if this is *supposed* to happen... but all of the top got this gorgeous (and delicious) hard cinnamon/sugar coating on it. 

i let it sit for more than 15 minutes, then flipped it out onto a plate and righted it from there. it stayed together no problem. 

i used a 9x5 pan like the others had suggested. i will definitely make this again!

Umm... This bread is really good. So good, in fact, I'm going to post my review despite the fact that it will highlight my inability to follow directions! I failed to notice that you are supposed to layer this bread.  Ooops.  What I did was put the cinnamon and sugar on top of my loaf. I don't know about the 'real version', but my loaf made GREAT coffee-style cake.  I used raw sugar for the topping as well, which gave it a nice 'crunch' ontop.  Fantastic recipe!!

This is an AWESOME recipe! I wanted to use up some buttermilk I had and decided that this bread looked quick and good. I made it for myself and two other people and we had it eaten by the end of the day, with them begging me to make one the next morning as well. :-) The only change I made was to cut the salt in half and add cinnamon and nutmeg to the batter. The only pan I had was a 9 5/8 x 5 1/2, but it turned out just fine--I only had to cook it for about 35 minutes.

Thanks for the great recipe!
This bread is awesome!

This obviously does not need another rating, but that has never mattered to me!  SUPER good.  My whole clan (that would be 7 these days) loved this and the whole loaf was gone in a flash.  Guess what I am doing this morning??? Making more!  Thanks!
Fabulous.  Great w/ a good cup of coffee.  Thanks for the recipe.
This was an easy bread to put together. The kids loved it. Thanks for the recipe.

This was INCREDIBLE! The only change I made is I used only 1/2 of the cinnamon / sugar mixture and it was PERFECT. I'm afraid anymore than that would have been too sweet for us. Thank you so much Kim D you made our autumn evening just that more cozy!

Quick and easy. Really liked this
delicious bread.

This is just flat out GOOD!  I also didn't have buttermilk so added almost a tablespoon of vinegar to a full cup of milk.  It turned out just right, not too dry, not to moist.  I really liked this and will be making it again and again.  I'm anxious to share it with my friends.  Thank you very much, you did a great job on this!
LOVED IT....it was perfect for breakfast and afternoon snacking. Thank you!!!!

Absolutely delicious and it smelled so good while baking! I had no problems with sticking in the pan. I made a few changes: I used a 9x5 pan. I baked it for 70 minutes. I only used two layers of filling. Instead of the cinnamon filling mentioned here, I use King Arthur's Flour Cinnamon Filling. http://www.kingarthurflour.com/shop/detail.jsp?id=3037 I also made a glaze: 2c confectioners sugar; 3 oz cream cheese; 1 tbls softened butter; 1/2 tsp vanilla; 3 tbls milk. Beat with a mixer and pour over the bread while it is still warm.
This is a wonderful Christmas gift when paired with a pretty tea towel, loose leaf tea, and some pretty tea cups. Yum!

Delicious, easy to make and beautiful presentation! I didn't have buttermilk so, I added a tbsp. of lemon juice to a cup of whole milk and it worked great. I didn't have trouble with it sticking to the pan(I used a nonstick cooking spray that had flour in it). Wonderful with a hot cup of coffee or cold glass of milk!
Excellet and so delicious!  Cinnamon is one of my favorite spices and this bread tastes so good.  Thank you Kim D!

What more can be said for this delicious quick bread, except maybe "Yum"! It is crisp on the outside and so soft and spicey on the inside.
