This was a pleasant surprise.  I have never used Garam Masala before.  What a treat.  My dh & I enjoyed this spicy dish very much.  I served it over top of recipe #117468.  It was a perfect blending of flavors.  Thanks for sharing this quick and easy to make recipe.  Made for my Pac Baby :)
ZWT6: What a delicious blend of spices!! The entire dish is perfection!
We loved this! Easy to prepare and very flavourful, I served it with couscous for an amazing dinner! Made for ZWT 6 :)
This tasted great, but I'm used to curries that are smothered in sauce. I'd love it with more sauce! Made for ZWT6: No-Nonsense Nibblers.

Found this recipe looking for a quick and easy way to use garam masala.  It has quickly become my new weeknight go-to meal.  DH and I were never fond of tomatoes, but they are our new favorite fruit because of this recipe!  I used canned whole tomatoes, and use the food processor to chop them finely as we do not like large chunks.  I use nearly double the amount of tomatoes called for and substitute juice from the can for the water.  I also use an extra half teaspoon of garam masala because we love it so.  I make naan bread (perfect for sopping up the delicious sauce), saffron rice or potato samosas to go with this dish.

Reviewed for ZWT8 tour India- loved this chicken dinner. Super easy to make and the garam masala wasn't overpowering. I liked the fresh tomatoes in this dish and used two large diced tomatoes. Photo also to be posted
Very good. I made the recipe as directed using 1 1/2 tsp of Garam Masala. We don't do spicey food and this was just spicey enough for us. Nice flavor!
This was very to prepare and had a great flavor. A friend of mine from India gave me some garam masala to use for the meal and it was great. Made for ZWT8

So good and So easy, this recipe is win, win, win. Used a 1/2 breast and it was fully cooked and tender by by just following the recipe right down the line. I served it with cinnamon rice and a mix of carrot, yellow bell pepper and apple that I also added some Garam Masala to. :D

This was ok.  I love garam masala and am always looking for recipes that use it, but it just din't taste right to me when used in this dish.  The acidity of the tomatoes changes the flavor I guess.  But hey there's a lot of 5 star reviews, so maybe it depends on your palate.

I can see why this recipe has so many five star reviews - delicious and done in 20 minutes! I used wine instead of water, and stirred in a cornstarch paste at the very end to thicken the sauce. Served with whole wheat pearl couscous. Yum!

Easy and healthy.  Added zucchini, you can add many vegetables on hand to the recipe.  I also cut the chicken breasts into about 2 inch pieces served with the Coconut Basmati Rice.  Recipe is a keeper.
Really easy dish! Taste delicious with a few adjustments! Love the sauce that made the whole dish!

We loved this quick and easy chicken dish. I used 3 large chicken breasts and cut them into pieces instead of leaving them whole. Also, I sauteed the chicken in garlic infused olive oil for added flavor. Next time I would double the sauce ingredients, it was our favorite part of the dish. **Made for 2017 Culinary Quest - Himalayas for Smok'in Chefs**
This was quick and easy and we loved it!
4 stars only because it is too salty. Definitely switch off the slow cooker before you put in the noodles.

It was very easy to put together and I actually had extra chicken left over.  My only comment is that it was a little bland.  I will make this again but will replace some of the water with chicken broth.

Real old time chicken noodle soup. I used chicken stock as author suggests and with a long slow cooking I got a rich tasting lovely soup. It's perfect for a cold Jan evening. Very simple recipe, no special skills required. I used fresh Penzeys thyme and a tiny amount permeated the soup well and added a very nice aroma. Thanks Lainey for a taste of home.

This is a great basic soup! I set the cooker going all night and woke up to a delicious-smelling house. I even had a bowl for breakfast! It's about 20 degrees out today and I can't wait to get home from work and have some more soup for dinner.  I set my bread machine timer to have a hot loaf waiting for me when I get home!  Life is good! I used four split chicken breasts for the meat.  I didn't have canned broth on hand, so I used water plus chicken bouillion cubes and half of the salt in the recipe. The other recommended seasonings and herbs is just right. I'll be making this recipe often!  Thanks for submitting it!

The soup was perfect for my family.  I tend to like soups that are a tad exotic, but this is the kind of soup that's right up my teenagers' alley.  I took other people's advice and used 8 cups of stock instead of water...(homemade! my first ever!).  I used 4 spilt chicken breasts which produced a LOT of meat at the end.  Great soup.  Very easy, great smells, happy family, happy Mom.  Thanks!!

My mother in law and I loved this soup and I will make it again. However, 3 cups of egg noodles was too much for this recipe. I used 2 cups and that was still too much. It was too bland for my husband's taste but that's his problem. I'll fix this again except I'll use less noodles.

This came out quite delicious and I will make it again.  My husband thought it was the best batch of chicken noodle soup I ever made, but the rest of us felt it was missing just a little something.  Next time I make it, I'll try adding some parsley and a dash of dill to see if that kicks it up a bit.  (I did use chicken breasts, so I added concentrated chicken stock base along with the water to make chicken broth, as suggested, and cut back a tiny bit on the salt).  Thanks for posting this easy to make soup!
This is your classic chicken noodle soup with all the right ingredients to make it delicious. It really hits the spot on a cold day. It is very flavorful and easy to make.

THIS is how chicken noodle soup is supposed to be! Lots of chicken, lots of noodles and lots of rich flavor. I used 3 1/2 pounds of bone-in skinless chicken thighs.  Because my chicken was thighs and had bones, I used the water.  That made for a great stock!  I halved the amount of salt and thought it was fine. I'd say this makes more than 6 servings, and that's agood thing. ;) I highly recommend this recipe for the chicken noodle soup-lovers out there. Thanx for posting it!

I used chicken leg and back quarters when making this soup and like the previous reviewer used the water option. This is wonderful chicken soup. DH had 3 bowls! I will definitely be making this again.
The kids loved it.  I used 2 boneless chicken breasts and broth, and only 2 teaspoons salt.  Plenty of flavor with lots of noodles.
Very delicious comfort food especially when you're sick or you want something hot on a cold winter day!

Absolutely wonderful! I used 4 cups of water in the crock pot (which is a smallish one), and added 4 cups of chicken broth after stripping the meat from the bones. I also added about 1/2 of a head of garlic (minced) with the onions, and several stalks of parsley on top of the chicken. 
Delightful! Even my picky stepdaughter ate a bowl or two, and she won't anything I cook! I did strain the stock through cheesecloth and pick through the vegetables to make sure I didn't accidentally include any smaller pieces of bone.

What a fantastic way of making Chicken Noodle Soup.This was added to Zaar Our Favourites Cookbook. I added 2 Tablespoons chicken broth powder and didn't put the bay leaf. I trimmed as much of the fat on the chicken as I could;turned out great.
Thank so much for posting this one.
Rita

I liked this but I think I will love it if next time I leave out the bayleaf and thyme and just use parsley and dill as I usually do. I didn't care for the flavor of the herbs. I used all stock, extra carrots, celery and garlic. I also used 2 split breasts and only two cups of egg noodles which was the perfect amount. Thanks for posting!!
absolutely delicious!!!!

Very, very good soup with old time taste and very little work.  I used a whole chicken and added 1/2 again all the veggies.  Kept the seasonings (except salt) as written (measuring in palm of my hand) and the 8 cups of water and cooked on High for 5 hrs. Only used 2 1/2 t. salt to start and when I tasted I had to suppliment w/2 t. instant chicken bouillon....so the 4 t. salt in recipe is just right.  This will be my "go to" for chicken soup as you don't have to "tend" the noodles or chicken.  Many thanks for posting, Lainey.

This was really easy!!  It tasted great too.  On top of the chicken, I put a bunch of fresh parsley and dill and then removed it when I removed the chicken to shred it up.  I then chopped some more fresh parsley and dill and added that to the actual soup.  The dill added great flavor.  I also used all chicken broth instead of water and would do that every time.  Very tasty.  Oh I also didn't have to skim any fat from the soup - there was none.
great soup, very easy to make. instead of 8 cups water or 8 cups chicken broth, i used half of each.  thanks for posting

DH was home yesterday with a bad cold and sore throat...so I made this...as suggested I used 1/2 water & 1/2 chicken broth...2 chicken bullion cubes instead of salt...leg quarters that I had in the freezer (defrosted)...garlic pepper & 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes...cooked on high for ~ 4 hrs...turned out great...DH loved it...he's eating leftovers right now!!...I will add more red pepper flakes next time though.

I'm a chicken breast kind of cook most of the time & I used them here, too! Also used homemade chicken broth & substituted lemon pepper for the usual S&P ~ & we had A GREAT TASTING, WONDERFULLY COMFORTING SOUP! Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Tagged, made & reviewed in Please Review My Recipe]

So yummy! We were all feeling a bit poorly today and this really hit the spot. I only used half an onion, a whole tsp thyme, one tsp oregano and changed the pepper to lemon pepper. I used Recipe #95311 for the noodles. It made it perfect! Thank you.

Yummy!  My kids loved it.  I loved it--it was so easy.  I used low-sodium, fat-free chicken broth and decreased the salt by a teaspoon.  Next time, I'll only use two teaspoons of salt.  I was out of garlic (a tragedy!) and substituted a 1/2 tsp. of garlic powder.  I also added a 1/2 tsp. of poultry seasoning.  I used four bone-in, skin-on split chicken breasts--a bit too much, next time I'll use three.  The egg noodles basically dissolved--I plan to try penne, ziti, or elbow pasta next time.  And I plan to double the carrots.

Really tasty!  I used more chicken broth than water by far.  I used maybe 1 cup of water.  I also added a chicken bouillon cube - it had great flavor.  I would highly reccomend using a pasta instead of an egg noodle.  As mentioned in other reviews, the egg noodle just disolved.  Next time I will use rotini pasata but I would deffinetly make it again.  Thanks!

This is fantastic! This was my first attempt at Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup and I was a little intimidated because my mother and grandmother make such wonderful soup. This recipe was fast and easy and my kitchen smelled amazing while it was cooking. I didn't have bay leaves so I added a little poultry seasoning and did half water and half chicken stock with a few cubes of chicken bouillon, I also added in a cup of potatoes and left out the celery, also after reading some of the reviews about the egg noodles dissolving I decided to use some lumaconi pasta I had laying around. Everything came out great and this will be a definite keeper at our house. Thank you for a great recipe!

I made this recipe last night and added corn, and chopped up red potatoes, and the broth like the author recommended. Like others said, yet I neglected to read, the egg noodles disintegrate in the crock pot. I left them in about 20 minutes. Also, I had it on low. Next time, I think I will turn off the crock pot, then put the egg noodles in while the soup cools.

This is one of the best chicken soups we've ever had.  I cubed the cooked chicken, added a few chopped mushrooms and used all low-sodium chicken broth, with no water.  As other reviewers suggested, I added the noodles when I turned the crockpot off; they cooked through and didn't get mushy at all.  All the proportions of ingredients were perfect, which made this such an extra-good chicken soup recipe.  I'll definitely make this again -- we loved it!

After being sick for several weeks and making one chicken soup recipe I found on this site (that we didn't care for too much!) I decided to try this one.  Wow!  It was soooo much better than the first one!  I used 4 whole boneless chicken breasts and by the time the soup was done the chicken just fell apart when I shredded them - they were incredibly moist.  I didn't have any problems with the noodles "dissolving" as other had, but did notice with the second day leftovers the noodles did fall apart a bit, - it really wasn't a concern.  This recipe is a definite keeper!

Soup was tasty.  I had the same issue with the egg noodles.  I used the extra wide, turned off the crock and let them sit for 20 min and poof, they were in tiny bits..  I added some alphebet noodles that I had just made for the kids to add to their soup.  It was still very good though. Thanks for sharing.

Both of us were sick on a Sunday and for some reason I thought that was the time to try out a new recipe! Thankfully this slow-cooker chicken soup recipe was just what the doctor ordered.  My slow cooker was too small for 8 cups of liquid so I made the recipe as it is, but with only 4 cups of canned broth and a 2.5 lb chicken. I used wide egg noodles and only cooked it for as long as it took us to shred the chicken (about 10-12 minutes). Next time shall try making this with pieces of chicken (breast & leg) in order to squeeze in more liquid.
Great soup!  I used 8 cups water, tripled the garlic, and used Mrs Dash and Oregano instead of the other spice.  Also, I used 3 pounds worth of drumsticks.  Will definitely make it again!!
I love this recipe however I use Orzo instead of the egg noodles they last and hold up well

My family has homemade chicken noodle soup every Thanksgiving and Christmas. Since we have evening holiday meals, the soup is available to have while the meal is being prepared and family members are arriving. We use Kluski noodles in our soup. They hold up very well.

I made this recipe exactly as written. I think it would have been excellent if I had used boneless, skinless chicken breasts, or if I had trimmed the skin off prior to cooking. The broth was beyond rich - it was oily.  Having said that, it had everything else you could want in a chicken soup - I want to try it again with boneless,skinless breasts, and I am hoping this will improve the oily texture.

Very tasty...Would make again..Maybe next time I would add some potatoes and other veggies. Very good. Anyone wanting to try a chicken soup you should make this. I cooked on high for 5 hours and it was delish.

First time making chicken noodle soup and it was AMAZING! I used 2lbs of split chicken breast with the skin removed and did 4cups water and 4cups broth. Only used one teaspoon salt.  My hubby thought it was excellent! Defiently a keeper and so easy to do

Perfectly delicious plus easy! I used 3 chicken breasts, 6 cups broth and 2 cups of water with 1 1/2 teaspoons of salt.  Appreciate recipes that use ingredients that I have on hand. Thanks Lainey for sharing.
So easy!!!  Even I could make it.  I used mostly Chicken Broth and it was great!

After I got married this was the first recipe I used in my slowcooker, and it is not my go to chicken soup recipe! So delicious and gets rave reviews every time! My changes: Make it a day or two in advance to be able to skim the fat. Add in chopped sweet potato or two- delicious!

This soup came out great!  I used water instead of chicken broth.  At the end I added one can of chicken broth.  I added my egg noodles at the proper time, but they still dissolved.  My entire family was pleased with this soup.

Made this twice now. First time came out amazing, used chicken breast and followed the suggestion of 4cups chicken broth 4cups water and I used 2tsp salt.

Second time making it I didn't think and didn't measure out the noodles so I just put a whole bag in, and the noodles came out broken and mushy. So I'm thinking that's what other people's problems with the noodles are. You MUST measure out the nokdles!

Will make again and remember to only use 3 cups of noodles

I made this soup using frozen chicken skinless boneless chicken breasts to make it healthier. I was worried it wouldn't come out well but it came out fantastic! The second time I used Brown rice, cooking it separate and adding it to soup when it was done. Again it came out fantastic, everyone loved it even the kids!

This is a great recipe! I did not have problems with my noodles. I used 3 nice sized boneless chicken thighs but ended up only using one to finish the soup, so I have left over chicken for something else! My picky husband (pizza, chicken fingers, take out, etc) even LOVED this soup! Yum Yum! ill make it again and again!

Great recipe, although the nutritional info seems REALLY off -- almost 700 calories and 43 grams of fat in a bowl of soup?  I suspect they neglected to notice that the recipe tells you to remove the skin & fat from the chicken after it cooks (and of course if you use boneless skinless chicken breast, the count will be WAY lower as well).

I LOVE this soup.  I use low sodium chicken stock, add sliced mushrooms and cook it on high for 4 - 5 hours.  I also make sure I only use real egg noodles.  I tried using cheaper noodles, but they turned to mush.  This is the best tasting, easiest chicken soup I've ever had.

Smelled so wonderful, and I used boneless skinless breasts instead, but 4tsp of salt was way too much it was awful we couldn't even eat it was soo salty! I would make it again but leave the salt out you can always add it to the bowl after!

In love with this recipe! I received a crockpot for my birthday and tried 4 other recipes and decided this slow cooker business was not for me. Then I had a nice 3lb frozen chicken and I said lets try one more recipe before I yard sale this thing. Well I am now in love, thank you! I basically followed this recipe to the letter. My only changes were doing 4 cups of low sodium chicken broth and 4 cups of water. I also followed the noodle suggestion of wating till the crockpot was off to add the noodles. I let them soak for 20 minutes. Pure perfection! My very very picky 1 & 3 year old LOVED it! This is a winner in our book.
Easy recipe with amazing results! Thank you!

Personally I would never use a whole chicken and have to hassle with the bones and fat. However turned out great using chicken thighs (only a few bones to pull out yet the little bit of fat adds flavor). Also used some chicken tenders. Cooked on high 4 hrs turned out perfect. Used home style egg pasta. Don't forget crockpot liners for easy clean up.
Great soup!  I use a whole chicken, and add some poultry seasoning and parsley.  I also use Kluski noodles.  Never have a problem with the noodles becoming mushy or soggy.

Loved this recipe. So did the husband. I did add some red pepper to the recipe and put in different noodles. The one thing I would recommend is adding the noodles right before you serve them. I loved that I could just put the whole chicken in and worry about cutting it up later. I will be making this recipe again soon!!

Ugh! This recipe is good..but I am a little frustrated that I wasted my time to get to the noodles and now it's ruined. I read the other reviews about the wide egg noodles..so when I turned my crock pot off (after cooking all day) I added the egg noodles and they were literally dough 5-10 minutes later. My 2nd time and 2nd recipe of making chicken noodle and this recipe kind of ruined dinner because of the noodle choice. I also added a can of cream of chicken because the soup was very liquidy before the noodle mistake. I will use this recipe again, but will definitely use a different kind of noodle.
The best chicken I've ever made!!!!  the family loved it!!!

This soup was so good!  I did use boneless chicken breasts like someone suggested.  I washed them and put them in whole.  They were just falling apart when I took them out to cut up.  I cut down on the salt as well, used 1 teaspoon then added just a bit more when it was done.  Came out perfect!  Will make again!

On a snowy new years day, I made this with boneless chicken breasts and some untouched, leftover vegetables from a party tray. I used only chicken broth. Stock is too rich/heavy for soup. Water is too bland. I added poultry seasoning, garlic, green onion, parsley and red pepper flakes to the pot. Add the salt gradually to your own individual taste. I prefer a lot of salt in my soup. I added some flour to give it some body. Then, at the end, I substituted (prepared) Zatarin's long grain and wild rice for the noodles before serving. There. Problem solved.

This is one of the best chicken noodle soups that I have ever made.  However, I did make a few changes.  I used 3 split chicken breasts (with bones), and for the chicken broth I made my own by using Better Than Bouillon chicken base that I got at Costco.  I did not add the salt since the chicken base is very salty.  The chicken came out so tender and tasty.  Since the chicken feel away from the bones I had to make sure that no small bone pieces were left behind.  For my noodles I used Pennsylvania Dutch Hearty Homestyle Egg Noodles.  They came out perfectly.  I will be making this again.
Super easy to make. Chicken was succulent! I did add 2 uncooked cups of spinach for more greens, but otherwise stuck to the recipe.
This was delicious!! SO easy too! I do like more veggies in my soup though. Next time I will for sure add 2 cups of both veggies. Will make again!

DO NOT ADD NOODLES. Regardless of what Lainey6605 claims, wide egg noodles or not, they dissolve. I recommend cooking them separately and adding the stock to the noodles as you serve. Other than that, this is a FANTASTIC RECIPE! The dissolved noodles will ruin it slightly; however, not as badly as some in their reviews claim. The ONLY reason this recipe received a four from me was because of the dissolved noodles, and I only have my self to blame for that. I should have listened to the reviews and not the poster. WILL USE AGAIN.

I make the noodles separately and only add when putting in the bowl as we have a gluten free family member. I store the cooked noodles in a Baggie in the fridge separate from the leftover soup. Fantastic soup and the noodles (egg) go great with it.

This recipe was disappointing to me.  There was no depth to the flavor.  Made exactly as written with the exception of cutting salt to 1 Tablespoon as that was all I had.  It needs more herbs and perhaps leeks instead of onion.  Salvaging the rest to make individual pot pies with a savory crust.

This recipe is extremely good and easy for all practical purposes.  It has turned out perfect every time for me.  I use all eight cups of water instead of broth to keep sodium down and then I let the mixture cool while we clean the chicken so I can trim off the fat.  We then add Delicious Homemade Egg Noodles from this website as another reviewer suggested and it turns out perfect every time.  The only difference we leave out the celery since my family isn't fond of it, and double the carrots and onions.  Still it is perfect every time.
One of the easiest soups I ever made. My wife and her co-workers ask for it monthly. Easy, and healthy. I just add some olive oil, 1 or 2 tablespoons, and only two tablespoons of salt

I've made this soup a couple of times now.  I made a wonderful mistake that I think has really made it what my family is calling "the best soup ever".  I bought a couple of BBQ flavored already roasted chickens from the store deli & threw them in the pot whole as I didn't have a lot of time for using raw chicken.  A couple of hours later, I took the chickens out, took bones & skin off & returned to the pot & finished up the recipe as-is.  The BBQ flavoring that had been on the skin seeped into the soup & gave it a wonderful light smoked chicken flavor.  My family couldn't get enough & now I have friends that are cooking it this way.  I've done this with the "traditional" deli roasted chicken & it was still very delicious.

I made this soup today and just tasted it, DELICIOUS!!!!!  I can't wait for my hubby to get home so we can eat. I did not have a whole chicken so I used a couple of thighs, and a couple of legs (skin removed) and a couple of skinless boneless breasts.  I also did not use all of the salt.  We are not big salt users.  I used 6 cups chicken broth and 2 cups water.  I will definitely be making this again.  Oh, and for the noodles, I used spaghetti pieces by Barilla.  Awesome!!!!!

Having never made chicken noodle soup from a recipe like this, I was excited to see how it turned out. I used whole wheat egg noodles, added 2 tsp. rosemary, and used baby carrots. I also used a young chicken as I find them to be more tender. This soup was a total hit! Following this recipe, I was able to feed my boyfriend and myself twice each with half and froze the other half for a rainy day dinner later. The rosemary is definitely a great addition, and the broth alone was amazing to sip while recovering from dental surgery. I will be making this again --- and again!

Very good, super easy chicken soup that you can prep and forget.  Without question, the simplest and most delicious chicken noodle soup recipe I've ever tried -- and there have been many!  I used half water and half chicken broth, kept the salt and spice proportions exactly as they are in the recipe, and added only some chopped fresh parsley at the end.  I used tiny star shaped pasta.  If you are a white meat person, be sure to use chicken breasts on the bone, with skin, for the richest and most flavorful stock.  Don't hesitate to make this one!

I can't believe I haven't rated this before.  I use chicken legs/thighs and remove the skin prior to putting them in the crockpot.  I also use chicken broth or stock (purchased) and not water in this recipe.  After the soup is cooked and turned off, I put in homemade egg noodles (No Knead Homemade Noodles recipe from this site - highly recommended if you're not pressed for time - a 1/2 recipe works great.  Cook them in plain water, drain, THEN add them to the soup.)  Perfect for a cold, Northeast winter day!

this is a fantastic recipe if you ignore the 8 cups of water or 8 cans of chicken broth and do the chicken stock instead it is a much better flavor I also recommend you use time spring not dried thyme three springs of time or more shold do.

I was surprised how tasty this soup is, it is seriously delicious. I will definitely make (and play with) it again.

Ingredient variations :

- I used red onion because I was too lazy to go to the store. Probably affected flavor, but not in a negative way at all. If that's all you have and you're worried about any "bite" you may get from the red onion flavor, worry not!
- I love garlic, so I went with 4 cloves. Wasn't garlic-y at all, don't be afraid to go with more than 1 clove.

Thoughts for next time:

- I broke down a full chicken and tossed the two breasts and legs/thighs (all with bones) in. Next time I may try to take some of the bones (smaller ones only, the bones are good for flavor), because after cooking 8+ hours, the bones just slide out and the little ones can be a nuisance.
- I used 32 oz chicken broth and 32 oz veggie broth, again, because that's all I had. I wished I had a little more broth though. Next time I will probably add more than the 8 cups of liquid, probably a reduced-sodium chicken broth. May need to add a pinch more thyme and pepper, possibly onion, depending on how much more broth.
- Speaking of adding more, I also wished I had a little more carrot. Next time I may go for 2 cups carrot, maybe somewhere close to 2 cups celery.

Special note on the noodles - I took another reviewer's suggestion on turning the slow cooker off then immediately adding the wide egg noodles. They were perfect in a matter of minutes. If you're going to eat the whole batch in one sitting, you can probably add them all. Otherwise, they cook quickly enough that you might be better off either adding them as you want more, or adding them into the cooled down (warm, but not cool) soup.

I make this a couple times a month and everyone loves it.  I use a whole chicken that is already roasted at the store and break it down.  I also double the power and thyme because I like it a little spicier.  I also use low sodium chicken stock.

I never write reviews on anything, but I had to write a review on this recipe. It was so easy! I have been sick with all-day "morning sickness" for the last 12 weeks of my pregnancy and have had to change what I eat around. I was advised to eat bone broths and broth soups, so I figured why not try to make some homemade chicken noodle soup? I was nervous because my nausea makes cooking impossible at times, but I figured a slow cooker soup would be safe- just dump it in and forget about it. I didn't have a whole chicken but I had some bone-in chicken thighs, and that worked perfectly. Other than that, I used the recipe as is. It was done in 5 hours on high, and it is absolutely delicious. There is nothing I would change. Wait, there is one thing... I'd cook the noodles separate next time and add them as I go just to avoid super soggy noodles. Other than that, this fool-proof recipe is perfect!

Used 8 cups of broth not water celery salt instead of regular and two pounds of chicken breast with skin and bone. Cook the noodles separately and add when serving to avoid mushiness. Absolutely perfect recipe just season to taste as any chef wood.

I failed to read "3 cups of noodles" and dumped the whole bag. I would NOT use egg noodles in the future because they did break up. I think 3 cups of a regular bowtie noodle would be much more suited to this recipe.
Used 3 chicken breasts cubed as recommended and they ended up tasting a tad bit overcooked. I would perhaps add them maybe two hours before cooking is done
I need to try this recipe again with different noodles and chicken cook time. The broth and veggies were good though. Not too salty! Thanks

I changed it a Lil bit I boiled the noodles bought a cooked whole chicken can peas, carrots and corn...used eveything in the ingredients then put in crockpot for 2 hours to let everything soak in the juice...and threw in some tapatio for a spicy kick...so good...thanks for the help in making a good homemade soup for my husband with a cold...

This recipe is easy and delicious.  I add about 2 cups of Kale to the recipe for extra nutrition, flavor, and color!  The egg noodles were great when serving immediately, but didn't hold up well over time (when storing in fridge) so I may try orzo or penne this time.

This was a simple and fantastic recipe! I used 3 skinless, boneless chicken breast, 8 chicken bouillon to 8 cups water for the broth and added No Yolk extra broad egg noodles after turning the crockpot off, letting it rest for 15 min. It was delicious!  Definitely a keeper!
first time making chicken noodle soup. This recipe is AMAZING. Great flavors. Only 4 stars because noodles get a dough texture. Don't know how to avoid this

For the noodle problem in any soup, I always cook my pasta separately and add just what you want to your bowl before pouring soup in it. As when rice or pasta is sitting in the soup it always seems to soak up all the broth.

The best chicken soup recipe I've used! I made some small alterations...I take a 'kitchen sink' approach to herbs, so sprinkled a dash of half my herb cabinet in with the ones listed. Dill, parsley, oregano, basil, and a tiny touch of msg were the more major players I remember. I also pan roasted the garlic before cutting it up. Good suggestion on putting the noodles in at the end!

I always try to make things following the recipes exactly, but this time I couldn't because I only had chicken breasts that I needed to use up. I never have a whole chicken. I also did not have enough noodles. I used 3 very large breasts, cut in half and since I only had about a half a cup of noodles I added elbow macaroni. I like a tomato taste in my soups so I added a can of diced Italian tomatoes. My noodles disappeared too even though I followed all of the instructions. The macaroni was fine though. My Mom and I both really loved this soup and I will be sure to make it again! Thank you for sharing this great recipe.

This is an excellent chicken noodle soup recipe. I used broth, doubled the celery and carrots and used 6 bone in thighs with the skin removed. Cooked it on low for 9 hours. I added kluski noodles as several reviewers suggested and they were perfect even in the leftover soup the next day. This will be my go to recipe for chicken noodle soup. Thank you Lainey!
Great recipe and base for several modifications.
Wonderful!! Only changes I made was reducing salt to 2tsp, added 1/4 poultry seasoning & 1/4 tsp celery seed. Will definitely be my go to Chicken soup from now on!

I am going to make this while I sleep. I have made the chicken tortilini(sp) soup and that calls for chicken breast. You pull them out at 6 hours and spread them. As suggested I am not going to add my egg noodles until later as I don't want them to be crap even though I am not using white egg noodles so they will take longer to cook. I am also going to add corn to the recipe just cause I think it sweetens things up a little and I like corn in about everything.
Good stuff!

Delicious. Used whole organic chicken and low sodium chicken broth. No water. Left out thyme. Cooked on high for 5 hours. Added egg noodles, turned off crookpot and let sit for about 30 minutes before eating. I did cut salt in half. Next time I will probably only add 1/4. We are fighting the flu in our house and I swear, I woke feeling better than I did yesterday. Will definitely use this recipe from now on.
Great recipe! I put in 4 cups of water and 4 cups of chicken broth. I also added a whole parsnip (which I removed when the soup was done) for extra taste.
For a creamier version of this recipe check out https://thekitchensinkk.com/2017/02/28/slow-cooker-chicken-noodle-soup/

Nothing wrong with ingredients. Spot on. One step that needs revised-Do not add noodles to crock pot. Makes broth cloudy and noodles taste chalky. Keep it separate. Boil noodles separately and add to broth and serve.

I never submit reviews for recipes that I shamelessly steal online, however, this one was soooo good that I felt that I had to submit! I actually like to read the reviews and see the tweaks others have made before I start cooking. Having said that, I will let you know the changes I made. I did use a whole chicken but I didn't actually measure the veggies. I filled the whole bottom of the crock pot with carrots, onion and celery until I felt that there would still be room for the chicken and broth. I boiled 8 cups of water and added 4 chicken bullion cubes (run of the mill knorr). I went with 4 cloves of garlic (didn't taste garlicy at all) and upped the thyme to 1 tsp because I love the stuff! Since I used the bullion, the only salt I added was a tsp of celery salt. All of the other spices I added as the recipe called. Once the veggies, spices and chicken were in the pot I poured the hot water/bullion over everything and set it to high. After 4 hours I removed the chicken and also poured the rest into a large bowl that I sat in the refrigerator while I stripped the chicken of skin and bones. Once the chicken was ready to go in I took the rest out of the fridge and skimmed the fat off the top. I dumped it all back into the crock pot and set it to low for another hour. I then cooked some orzo in chicken broth and added it to each bowl as I served it. This was BAR NONE the best chicken noodle soup I have ever made and I think the best I have ever had! The entire house (all of which had colds!) raved about it! The nice thing about leaving the noodles out is that the next time we have it we can add whatever noodles we want, I think we will go with the extra wide egg noodles next time around. Thank you for the AWESOME recipe, I will never make chicken noodle soup again without using it!

Wonderful. Ive made this soup 3x. My tweaks this time: Full sodium broth, no added salt(we like salt with anything chicken) Used the8 cups broth,filled to brim with water..perfect. Did not add noodles because I like them,but half goes to my mother and she likes rolls. Increased spices because i topped it off with water. Did not have an onion.used 3/4c jarred minced. Too much so skimmed them off when I removed the chicken. But.. it gave the broth incredible flavor! My mother asked me to make it again. 84 now, but was an amazing cook. Thankyou!!

Delicious and easy. This turned out really nice! The flavors work well together. We added a lot more vegetables and it was still really good. Note: Be choosy about the noodles you use as they can get mushy quickly which makes for funky leftovers.
Delicious! No leftovers. :(

Loved how easy it was the prepare and the thickness of the final product! Nothing’s worse than watery chicken noodle soup! The only thing I would suggest is starting off with like HALF the amount of salt suggested and then adding more to taste.
Take the note about the disenigrating noodles as a warning. Do not put the noodles in the slowcooker. They turn to sticky mush and disappear, making the broth thick and lumpy.

Really yummy soup! I should have read the reviews here first though and avoided putting the noodles in. I put them in for only 30 mins on low at the very end (up to this point the soup tasted AMAZING) but the noodles turned to gummy glue style mush! Gross!
This was my first attempt at chicken noodle soup. Although I did it on the stove top and not the slow cooker, I must say the flavor was superb. A keeper for sure.
Tried this recipe with a rotisserie chicken and it turned out great. Great for a very cold evening.

You cannot ruin this recipe! I use 2 giant frozen chicken breasts and we have plenty of chicken. I use 1/2 chicken bouillon and 1/2 water and that made the perfect broth. Added noodles at the end without difficulty. I have even served it from left-over to drop-ins with additional broth and noodles added-to rave review. On defrosting, I added a few fresh noodles, as the noodles were not as firm...still tasty.
Horrible. 2 Bay leaves is total overkill. That's all the soup tasted like. A 4 teaspoons of salt is also overkill even using low sodium organic chicken broth

Instead of soup, I made chicken and noodles what a hit it was!! I used 4 cups of chicken stock, no water and one package of Reames frozen noodles. Other than that, no changes. This is the ultimate comfort food and it makes a large batch. Super easy, the house smells delicious and the food is devoured.

This soup is amazing. I have used both whole chicken and just chicken breast. I prefer the chicken breast because it is less fatty and still delicious after sitting in the slow cooker all day. I also used better than boulian with water. When I used the low sodium version I did actually want the whole 3-4 tsp of salt for flavor. When I used the regular version I had to half the salt. I almost always use more carrots and celery than instructed to add more substance, but other than that this soup is amazing and I make this soup regularly now. Like it more than canned versions, that is for sure
Great recipe. I added 1 more cup of broth, use chicken thighs and lowered the salt content. I also used 1 bay leaf but it can go with out it.
I used boneless chicken Thigh meat and used penne pasta noodles
Excellent soup. The best I've made. I added 1 t. poultry seasoning and used chicken thighs. Really easy using the slow cooker!

Very pretty and tasty too!  I doubled the recipe and served it at our school potluck.  I would definitely recommend making twice the dressing called for as the pasta really sucks it in, especially when sitting overnight.  I'd also increase the garlic and oregano a bit to give the pasta an extra punch.  Thanks for sharing!  **Made for PRMR**

Easily and quickly  prepared,  I was really happy to have found this recipe.

Thank you!   Made for PRMR tag game.

This is really good!  Made as is except left out the olives (next time will try some green olives).  The dressing has a nice mellow flavor too it and was just wet enough for us (didn't double the dressing).  Will be making for an upcoming family BBQ!)  Made for Everyday Holiday 4/2010.

Made this for a neighborhood potluck & it was a huge success! There were 5 couples there, & I kind of expected to have some left over, but no such luck! Followed your recipe right on down &  was very happy with the results! I'll definitely be making this one again, for sure! Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Tagged & made in Please Review My Recipe]

Yum, what an excellent tasting sauce! Mascarpone in a savory sauce is great.  A lot of people limit mascarpone to sweet recipes, which is a big mistake

Easy and so delicious!
good recipe but i love ur nickname ;-)
Awesome recipe! Turned out just like roasted, as described, but without having to turn on the hot oven in the summertime! THANK YOU!!!!!
I absolutely LOVED these potato recipe! I made it Tuesday and am making it again tonight! Thank you for sharing!
Yum!  And it's so simple..thank you!!!
This was delicious and very simple to make!  The seasonings were perfect.  Will definitely be making again!
These were good and easy to make but I cut the seasoning down because I knew it would be too much for us. I used all the seasonings but only used 1/2 teaspoon of each which was good for us.
Surprisingly good. I will make again. It did take a little longer to brown than the recipe specified.
I'm a nanny/cook for a nice little family. I prepared these tonight as a side to grilled turkey burgers and corn on the cob, and they were quite a hit!! Can't wait to make them for my hubs. :)
Quick and easy! Taste great!  And I heated  the leftovers on top of the stove and served them with a couple of fried eggs! They were even better! :)
Excellent recipe,I added a little panko breadcrumbs mixed with smart balance butter substitute. Delish!
We loved these potatoes made just the way the recipe read.  Next time I might throw in some rosemary too.  But they were really good just the way the recipe was written.
Loved it! Easy and quick, and I added a little rosemary to the recipe.
We LOVED these!! They disappeared so quickly haha! Seasoning was great, as was the prep. Really easy to make such a delicious side dish!
Good recipe. I would just recommend adjusting microwave time to accommodate your specific microwave wattage. 10 minutes would have cooked my potatoes all the way through.
I crave this all the time. It's my favorite roasted potato recipe! Delish!
It is an easy way to cook the potatoes but the mix of seasonings was terrible.  Way too much pepper.

These are great, the cooking time takes a little longer to fully brown them and I add in 1/2 tsp of Rosemary too. I never use all the spices though I keep them and usually get 2-3 batches out of it

Wow! Such a simple recipe, but it is delicious! Using the microwave first makes this recipe come together super fast. This recipe was fantastic! My husband, kids, and company loved it! I didn't have onion powder so I used minced onions! This was so fast to microwave the potatoes first. I will be making it again!

This is a good recipe. Roasting red potatoes doesn't work out well, they tend to lose crispness quickly. That's avoided with this recipe and they come out more flavorful as well. I used a cast iron skillet and added a bit of fresh rosemary.
These were so good ????. I use olive oil or coconut oil and keep them on the stove for about 10 minutes so that they are extra crispy.

This recipe is perfect. I love that its quick to make and tastes just like the real deal. I can't rave enough about it. It doesn't work well with large cuts of potatoes, so 'bite-size' is really 'bite-size'

I made these potatoes on the weekend along with chicken and asparagus. They turned out pretty good. I found they took a lot longer than 6-8 minutes to saute in the pan though. I think next time I will cut the pepper in half as we found it a bit strong.
Excellent recipe! Making it for second time this week. Using 3# organic red potatoes.

Super easy to make and so very tasty. I used half butter and half olive oil. I've found my new way to make red potatoes!

I wish I could give this recipe more than 5 stars! I truly don't remember ever having a better blueberry muffin. I made a half recipe and got 6 glorious muffins. It's also very nice to eat because inside that lovely golden crust is the lightest, most tender and fluffiest muffin ever. I was lucky enough to find very fresh huge blueberries at the market and this recipe is most worthy of the purple/blue treasures. The only drawback is that even as big as they are, it takes will power to stop at one. Thank you Kit of a truly magnificent muffin.

This a an excellent blueberry muffin recipe. They bake up beautifully with nicely rounded tops.The lemon, buttermilk & cinnamon are a wonderful flavour combination. My entire family really enjoyed them and I will definately be making them often. Thank you Kitten for sharing this recipe with us!!! from another Canadian

Awesome muffins!!! I loved these, they were very good and I couldn't stop eating them! I halved the recipe and made them into 12 regular sized muffins. I really love the moistness, lightness and flavor combination of these with the lemon, cinnamon and blueberries! Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe Kittencal!

These muffins are very tasty!  I was in the midst of my recipe when I realized I did not have any blueberries in my freezer.  I did however have a tri-berry mixture of raspberries, blueberries and marionberries which proved to be an awesome combination. I also used the almond extract, suggested by Kitten. Using Kitten's instructions, my jumbo muffins popped out of the tins without issue.  Thanks again for yet another wonderful recipe, Kittencal!

Wow! I made regular-sized muffins and ended up with double the amount. I'm giving them to my new neighbors, and I'm sure they will love them too!
Very light and fluffy and delicious!
Great muffins; very easy to make. I brought a batch to our church bazarr and all the muffins were gone in a jiffy; they were enjoyed by everyone.I will make a big batch for christmas.
I doubled this recipe and it made 30 jumbo muffins.  These were moist and wonderfully light.  Very nice recipe, and definitely a keeper.

I substituted 3/4 cup of brown suger for some of the sugar and rice milk for the buttermilk, and it worked just great. Also left out the lemon zest, and put a few drops of lemon juice in instead. Yum! It made a 9 inch "cake" and 15 medium sized muffins. Thank you for the great recipe!

This recipe is great!  The muffins were sweet and loaded with berries with a slightly crispy outside and fluffy center. Even with these heavier dry ingredients, the muffins were still light!  I will definitely make these again!
delicious! i halved the recipe and used 2 c. white flour and 1/8 c. wheat germ (and it couldn't be detected in the taste or texture). i also used orange zest, since i didn't have a lemon around.

I've made a lot of blueberry muffins but this one puts the others to shame. They have a beautiful rise and they aren't too sweet--just right. I made 12 large muffins and 12 mini muffins for the kids. You don't need to change a thing with this recipe. Thanks Kit!
SOOOO Good. Moist and full of berries. I had a hard time stopping at just one.

OH MY GOODNESS!!  These muffins are amazing--they are perfection!  Thank you so much for posting this recipe.  I love blueberry muffins, and I have half a dozen recipes that are very good, but I've never stopped searching for "the one."  I can't believe I've found it now!  I can stop searching--this is the one I'll be making for my grandchildren in 30 years!
I love what the mixing of the butter and dry ingredients does for the texture, and the buttermilk keeps them soft, too.  They are fabulous out of the oven, and fabulous the next day, too.  
The flavors are fun to play around with and alter to taste, and I've used fresh-ground whole wheat flour with great results.  Thanks again for a really great recipe!

These muffins turned out fantastic! They make the perfect size Jumbo Muffins and the quantity came out to exactly 1 dozen. I used frozen blueberries and my cook time was exactly 35 minutes. I will be taking these muffins to a birthday party to share.  Thanks again Kittencal for another perfect recipe!

hey kitten...it is just me again (I guess I am turning into a devoted fan of your recipes...lol) these muffins are excellent as with any of your recipes!!! and were a big hit at the restaurant. I made a second batch and modified it slightly to accommodate all of my black raspberries that my garden produced. Tried as my first batch of blueberry muffins...Terrific! Left some w/o berries and the kids ate them up. So easy to make and came out beautifully!!
Holy Kittencal! These are amazing! Just the smell of them baking makes me want to make them again! I can't say enough about how yummy these are!
These muffins are awesome! I followed the recipe exactly and they came out great! Thanks for this recipe.

Oh my gosh are these Soo Good!  My DH made this recipe for my office party  but after trying one of them we will have to split them between his office and mine.    with out a doubt we will be having this recipe over and over again.

oh my kittencal, you are the GODDESS of the kitchen! i have made several of your recipes, but this is the first one i rate.  i will rate the others later.  thank you so much for sharing your secrets with us on the ''zaar; we all look forward to buying your  cookbooks someday!!!
these muffins are the best!  the recipe is very versatile in terms of what frozen fruit, dried fruit and/or nuts you add to the batter.  the first time i made them i followed the recipe exactly as instructed, using unbleached organic white flour, raw sugar and all organic ingredients.  they were a hit.  the second time i made them, i also used all organic ingredients but i halved the recipe to make 12 regular-sized muffins. i substituted organic whole milk with 3/4 T of red wine vinegar for the buttermilk, skipped the vanilla because i had none, used 1 cup frozen organic blackberries instead of the blueberries and added a little extra cinnamon and about 1 T of raw honey to the batter.  end product: spectacular!  thank you thank you thank you

I guess you can't go wrong with Kittencal's recipes because once again this is wonderful. I agree it IS the BEST tasting blueberry muffin I have ever tried. The lemon zest just makes them! I made one batch with white flour and organic sugar- forgot the baking powder and they were great. Then I immediately had to make more with whole wheat pastry flour and organic sugar with the baking powder this time and they were great too. My kids raved! This is a keeper and will be my new blueberry muffin recipe- it makes plenty- I got 18 large muffins out of it. Kittencal needs to have a cookbook to sell- I'd buy it!!

These were sooo yummy! I only had one since I made them for my fiance and theyhad real sugar in them, but the taste was just awesome!
I got 15 large muffins out of this recipe, maybe because I loaded up on the blueberries.

I made these for breakfast this morning, and think they are just wonderful. As I was mixing up the batter, I was concerned that I didn't have enough liquid. The batter was thick and elastic which I thought would result in a dense, heavy muffin.  I think this may have been due to the fact that I used Medium sized eggs instead of Large. I compensated by adding the white of a third egg, & 2 T milk. This made it easier to fold in the berries.  I split the dough in half and added to one half, 1 c frozen blueberries, and to the other half  3/4 c frozen red raspberries and 1/2 c white chocolate chips.  The texture of the muffins came out perfect - not too heavy. The top was crisp, but not too hard. Here's what I would change next time.  I would omit the cinnamon completely. I only add 1/2 t and my roommate didn't like the flavor in the muffin at all.  I thought they tasted great so I'm still giving this a 5 star. Cinnamon is optional, I would say, and add it only if you like a muffin with a bit of spice.Thanks Kitt for another fabulous share.  I'll definitely make these again.

Best blueberry muffin reciped I've ever had!  Everyone loved these.  I made one change for personal taste.  Used baking soda in place of baking powder.  Worked great, rave reviews!!  Quote from a friend "this is exactly how a blueberry muffin SHOULD be!".  Thanks for posting this winner!

Wow what a muffin recipe Kit. These beautiful big gems are wonderful. Sweet, flavorful and just bursting with blueberry goodness. I love the addition of the lemon and cinnamon, you could taste them in every bite.

Yum! These are good!
  The method did produce a lovely textured muffin. I ended up making regular-sized muffins -- about 16. The cinnamon adds a lovely dimension that I normally wouldn't have thought of to be paired with a blueberry muffin. The lemon -- delicious, of course.
   They also look so beauty-full! Thank you!

Wow these turned out great! I didn't have any lemons, so I didn't use the lemon zest, but that was the only change I made. I even used your Recipe #78579 and they came out perfect! I didn't have a jumbo muffin tin so I just made 24 regular sized muffins. Thanks Kitten, your recipes always turn out wonderful!

Kittenkal you sure do have a way with food :)  Thank you so very much for this delicious recipe.  I baked these tonight for the morning and of course had to sample :D  I love them.  I did a batch without streusel and one with.  I have not tried the ones with yet but the ones without were awesome so I know the others will be as well.  I did not have buttermilk so I substitued 1 percent milk and add about 2 TBS Lemon Juice to it.  The muffins are perfect for me. Thank you so very much for sharing the talents that you have been blessed with.  I know many of us truly appreciate it more than words could ever say.

Thanks Kittencal! These muffins are simply delicious,the struesel part makes it extra special .I used half the measure of ingredients and even added 1 cup(half measure) of wholewheat flour to make it healthier.Im enjoying one right now with a cup of hot chocolate.
The muffins were everything that previous posts said they would be.  Always a hit.  Thank you for your generous sharing.

I was so excited to make these when I read all the fantastic reviews. I followed the recipe word for word. I was so disappointed. They have a lovely texture but absolutely no taste. The "streusel" was gross. Hubs will eat anything and asked that these not be made again. I could not agree more.

These came out beautifully.  As usual I started baking without checking the cupboard.  Was almost out of vanilla so used what was left and almond extract to make the full tablespoon. Also I had some raspberry cream cheese that I needed to use up so hid a tablespoon of cream cheese in each muffin, no need to butter them up! Thanks Kitten another hit.

Great recipe! My muffins came out light and fluffy with great flavor. I made slight adjustment had no buttermilk so added 1 tbsp to 1 cup of milk. There was a great flavor to these muffins. Thanks for a great recipe!

These couldn't get any better!! Kittencal, your recipes never cease to amaze me! These are just great - they have a nice rise and are just beautiful! I used jumbo paper liners and had exactly 12 muffins. I didn't change a thing in the recipe - these are just perfect!!

I really loved the muffins, excellent muffin batter recipe.  My family wasn't crazy for the topping, they like more topping like a struesel, so I think next time I will change out the topping but keep the excellent muffin recipe.
Yum! Another awesome recipe! I really like this recipe, very tasty and easy to adapt. Thanks again for another terrific recipe.

These were delicious! I used regular organic whole milk in place of the buttermilk and used a mixture of thawed frozen blueberries and strawberries. Didn't seem to matter! They were all eaten up quickly...
Amazing!

Kitten, these muffins are beautiful!  They certainly look the part and the taste does not disappoint.  I could have put aside 1/4 cup as opposed to 1/2 for struessel but other than that, PERFECTION!  Thanks again!

Yet another of your WONDERFUL recipes, KITTEN. I used whole wheat flower and they were light and had a nice rise anyway. I loved the combination of flavors and have added lemon, cinnamon and vanilla to many berry muffins since trying these. Thanks!

These were amazing! I didn't do jumbo muffins, just ordinary ones, and ended up halving the recipe because I was short on buttermilk. Great recipe, I would definitely make it again!

Great muffin.  DH usually isn't big on muffins but he loved these.  Will make many times while the blueberries are in season.  I made half a recipe and got 12 regular size muffins.  Cooked them for 20 min. and they were perfect.

Absolutely wonderful!  My kids told me they were better than Starbucks and that I should sell them!  Thanks for another wonderful recipe Kittencal -- I know anything I cook that came from you is going to be great!!!

Wow! these are so good!! I used the blueberries as I had some in the freezer. My DH even tried one and LIKED it!He's so hooked on your banana bread I didn't think he would ever give those up! These are actually the second time I've ever tried to mame muffins! I am so pleased. Thanks kitten for another winner!

These really are bakery-quality muffins!  I have been wanting to make these for the past couple of months, and today I finally did. SO GOOD!!! :)
Best muffins I have ever made or eaten!    Everytime I find a really fantatic recipe, it turns out to be Kittencal's  -  I'm going to have to start calling this place Kittencal-zaar!

Another winner!  I've made these twice now....once with fresh strawberries and once with fresh blackberries...so delicious both times.  I served these to my guests with a wonderful homemade chicken pot pie....true comfort food at it's finest!  Thanks!

FANTASTIC MUFFINS!!!!!  This is my 1st time making blueberry muffins and I am so glad I picked this recipe.  The muffins were light and fluffy and tasted WONDERFUL!!!!! I don't even like blueberry muffins and I can't stop baking and eating these!  So good!!
These are the worst muffins I have ever tasted or made!  I followed the recipe exactly.  They are heavy, doughy and tasteless.  Not worth the ingredients or the time .

These are great!  Anyone who said they weren't doesn't know how to make muffins...(If you overmix the batter after the flour is added, you will get tasteless bricks!) Result: I liked the blueberry muffins better than the cranberry nut ones. I had frozen raspberries on hand... so in addition to the lemon zest, I added some fresh lemon juice and came out with a DEEEEELICIOUS muffin!!!  They're so cakey and fantastic.. Great, great muffins!  Thanks so much for the recipe - my family absolutely loved these!  I also liked the tip of putting parchment paper on the bottom - I've never had muffins come out of the pan so easily!  Given how easy this is to do, I'll be sure to do this from now on with all my muffins!

THANK YOU THANK YOU THANK YOU!    Every homemade muffin that I have made in the past have been completely uninspired and nothing like what you could get in a bakery, and mixes are not any better and I don't like mixes anyway.  I left out the lemon zest, cinnamon and blueberries to make a plain base, I added butterscotch chips to half and chocolate chips to the other half, one word AMAZING, exactly the texture and flavor that I was looking for.  I left off the struesel topping and used sanding (sparkling) sugar on the tops, like I have done in bakeries that I have worked in.  I made them in the standard size muffin pan and got 17 out of it, I used a #24 disher and put 2 scoops in each, this made a nice tall muffin, they rose perfectly and didn't spread all over the top of the pan.  This will be my go to muffin recipe, the search is over!!!!!!!!!!!!!
amazing recipe!  thanks for sharin.

Very very good, my mom noticed that these were better than the ususal recipes. I liked it better w/o the topping. I would recommend filling muffin pans all the way full with these, as they don't rise much. And don't panic if the batter is VERY thick- mine was and turned out fine :)
I don't know what happened, but my muffins turned out quite dry.  The flavor was nice, but the muffins were not quite as good as I had hoped overall.

Another 5 Star winner, Kitten! I made these to take to work for treats and came home empty handed. Each muffin had a lovely rounded top that rose so high that allowed the topping to cling tightly. I will use this method in making other muffins...so glad you shared the secret to fluffy muffins! Thanks again!

These turned out exceptionally well. I did cut the recipe in 1/2 and got 12 good size regular muffins. I used 1 and 1/4 cup white flour and 1 cup recipe#404288. I used 1 cup blueberries and 1 cup strawberries because I didn't have enough of either one for a whole batch. Absolutely the best muffins ever.  Seeing the name Kittencal on a recipe is like a guarantee it will be perfect.  Thanks

I've never written a review here but I just had to.  After so many failed muffin attempts with other recipes, I finally have a winner. (mine always came out pointy). And then when we ate it, yummmy! I think the lemon zest definitely added a little extra kick. I also made some with frozen strawberries and blackberries.
I made this recipe exactly as written and am fairly experienced in the kitchen. The muffins were heavy and bland.  I won't make these again.

My advice on these muffins is DO NOT SUBSTITUTE! I waited until my third try on this recipe before I felt it was fair to write a review. Finally I *followed* the recipe (though I left out the zest as I have no lemons) and they were delicious. I'll be making them again.
These came out wonderful.  The crumb topping didn't do much for me but it's still my favorite fruit muffin.  I used fresh black cherries and expected they'd come out mushy but they were perfect.

These are very moist muffins that easily transitioned from a dinner muffin to a pastry-like morning breakfast. I added a bit more sugar to the crumb topping. Additionally, in place of buttermilk I used 2-6 oz Yoplait yogurts - one in orange and one in lime. This gave it a fresh, light taste. Additionally, I used raspberries which were fantastic. A great recipe!

I just got done baking these and eating my first one. They are VERY good! I like the addition of cinnamon to the batter, and the mixing method makes them very tender and fluffy. I don't have and couldn't find a jumbo muffin tin. I also used paper liners as opposed to greasing the pan. 5 stars! Thanks for sharing!

I would probably either skip this step or make a brown sugar topping which I find has a better flavour. Other than that very nice texture and baked perfectly.

I will NEVER again make another blueberry muffin.  These taste great and they ALWAYS look absolutely BEAUTIFUL.  I have subbed applesauce for half the oil... whole wheat pastry flour for half the white...used canola instead of butter... dried blueberries instead of frozen or fresh... it's ALL GOOD!

I do think jumbo is the way to go with blueberry muffins, because more of the juicy berries get into each muffin. I loved these. I can't quite give stars because I altered the recipe a little. I did like the sweetness level...just right for morning. I also thought the method was not any harder than others. I will probably omit the streusel next time (leaving in the 1/2 c mixture and perhaps adding a few more T's liquid). I used vanilla last time but can't wait to try these again with almond. These were delicious. I followed the recipe exactly and couldn't imagine changing a thing. I used the milk/vinegar trick for buttermilk and cannot believe it hurt the recipe in any way. An easy muffin recipe and just the right amount of sweetness but prefer a more cake like texture.    If followed exactly, this recipe works out perfectly but if you make your own substitutions then you can only expect less than good results.

Delish! Good ol' home cookin'. I used Jimmy Dean hot sausage and still added a little red pepper flakes. Yum. Thanks Kitten for another great recipe.
