This was really, really good. Everyone in my family that tried it really liked it. It was a little thick, so we thinned it a little bit, and did not add the dried pepper flakes. We ate this over freshly-baked bisquits.
delicious Kitty, we loved this, thank you
Although this is really "not my thing", I made it for my husband (who had been begging for it) and everyone ended up liking it!

Wow! What an amazing recipe.  You can definitely use milk to cut down on the fat because the flour thickens it up nicely. I used sausage with sage flavor and it was marvelous! This is definitely one that's going in the permanent cookbook. I added more pepper flakes because I like my food spicy but other than that I followed the recipe and it was great. Ten stars!

This is a great recipe! I've made it twice now for DH and he LOVES it! We haven't had leftovers yet, and there is just the two of us! I use skim milk, and cut out the red pepper flakes all together. 
Thanks!!
Fabulous!  It's only little tweaks different than my usual version, but this is a delicious improvement.  This is almost silly with the pork sausage, but I don't buy milk, so I used soy milk instead.
My all time favorite breakfast !!!! I love to have this before a day of golf!! Somehow I think I will work the calories off but swinging so much !!!!!!!!! Thanks Kitten.Pollyw

Very good.  I've not tried red pepper in gravy before; my husband liked it and I thought it was okay (he loves heat, but I don't, so "okay" is a good thing).  I loved the flavor of the gravy itself; it came together easily. Excellent!

I'm not a gravy person...but my husband (who is very picky about gravy) and I loved it.  We didn't time the biscuits and the gravy being done at the same time and so my gravy got a little too thick while waiting on the biscuits...we thinned it with milk and it was perfect.  We made half of this recipe and it will be our go to gravy for biscuits!

Made this for my family as they were all home this past weekend--first time since Christmas 2007.  Wow, I did double the batch and almost didn't have enough.  The best gravy recipe I have ever used.  Will only use this in the future.  Thank you.
just what i was looking for!

Just wanted a lite dinner , this came out perfect, great taste, easy to prepare and concistency couldn't have been better.. didn't have red pepper flakes, substituted a little cayenne pepper.  My motto is "if you want a great recipe use kittencal's"

A solid 5-star sausage gravy. I made it for a brunch for 14 people so I tripled the recipe with no problem adding 1 tsp pepper flakes. I used whole milk and it was plenty thick. Everyone loved it. Leftovers were doggie-bagged! Great recipe Kittencal.

This was awesome!!!  I had a horrible hankering for sausage gravy and biscuits and this hit the spot perfectly.  It was incredibly thick (but I think I just added too much flour) and a bit spicy for me - but my DH found it to be perfect.  Thanks for another wonderful recipe!

This recipe made it into our Book #231450. 3/5/08 - This was simple and fast to make. We enjoyed the unique flavor the worcestershire sauce brought to this great southern breakfast dish. We used Tennessee Pride sausage as it is Buddha's favorite brand. This gravy is scrumptious and very filling, with terrific flavor. My MIL had 2 generous helpings which says alot as she normally has more of a nibbler type of appetite no matter how good the dish. Thanks Kit, for sharing this wonderful recipe. ~Bird

I made this for breakfast on Sunday.  My dh accidently bought ground pork instead of pork sausage so I had to make my own with seasonings.  I found the recipe a tad bland but I think it was because I wasn't using the real thing.  I'm going to try it again in a few weeks and see what happens.

MMMM-mmmm, this is so delicious and filling and absolute comfort food for cold wintry nights.  I used a medium heat bulk sausage from Purnell's.  Because of the bit of nip already added I only included about 1/2 t. of the red pepper flakes.  Used 1 cup 1/2 and 1/2 and 1 cup skim milk.  Perfect outcome.   I made my biscuits using Bisquick.  A great satisyfing meal for the men here Kitt.~
Made for ZaarStars!!!
I've never attempted biscuits & gravy before- I made this for dinner tonight & it's excellent. Made exactly as written, over sour cream bisquick biscuits....Oh man is this good :-D

Delish!  We enjoyed breakfast for dinner tonight.  I used Jimmy Dean Hot Sausage and still added the pepper flakes.  I used about 1/2 cup 2% percent milk and the rest half and half.  Thanks Kitten! I think the worcestershire sauce was a nice touch.  We will be having this often.  Made for The Best of 2008 Cookbook swap and recommended by 2Bleu.
My roommate and I loved this! We're normally night people but making this for breakfast definitely makes the morning more appealing :)

This is a very well written, easy to follow recipe. I used low fat sausage and the meal  lacked flavor because of it. I think you really must use hot sausage. I also noticed the taste of the Worchestershire more than anything else. I only used one teaspoon.
I did use the half and half so the sauce was very creamy and rich. The entire dish just seemed to lack the flavor I was looking for. I may try it again but using a hot sausage. 
For us this was good but not great.

This was great comfort food for a rainy night! I added some italian seasoning to the sausage as it cooked and a lot of garlic. I used whole milk which thickened very nicely. The bf had seconds and is looking forward to eating it for lunch today- thanks for another great meal Kittencal!

This is exactly how I was taught to make sausage gravy and it's so funny to watch people who have never had good sausage gravy try it for the first time.  LOL, you can actually see their eye's light up and a look of pure pleasure wash over their face, hehe.  I agree that the secret to good sausage gravy is that the sausage has to be browned properly and also use half-n-half.  We love it over home fried potatoes, mashed potatoes, a bowl of grits. fried grits, fried green tomatoes, corn bread and biscuits.  If it will sit still on the plate long enough, one of us will pour sausage gravy on it.  I also make it with venison sausage and it's wonderful!
simply yummy! easy to make.  i never knew I could make tasty gravy.  this is definitely a keeper. thank you kittencal.

This was excellent.  I had never had sausage gravy that was very appealing.  This is excellent. Now, if I can learn to make biscuits that are not similar to hockey pucks.... (The saga continues...) ;-)
Great Gravy!

Made for KK's Kittencals Chefs Top 25 Picks.  I can understand why this recipe is one of her top 25 as it made up into a wonderful and yummy breakfast.  Our family has been longtime fans of biscuits and gravy with our eggs and bacon.  This recipe will now become my go to recipe for this as everyone here raved wildly and since making two days ago, has been requested both days thereafter.  Even my picky eater DGS gobbled down his biscuit with "Lumpy Sauce" .  Thank You Kitz for another fantastic recipe.

Scrumptious!  I served it over refrigerated biscuits for my family, and on white rice wrapped in a flour tortilla for myself (the carb-aholic).  Even my pickier family members liked it!  This is a keeper!  :)  Next time I may try with faux sausage for my vegetarian sister.

Good gravy, what good gravy this is!  It's so good served over hot fluffy biscuits.  The little dash of red pepper really adds a spark.  I used Irish sausage (with garlic and basil) and milk.  Another great one from Kittencal!  Made for KK's Chef's Pick Top 25.

When I have tried to make sausage gravy all I tasted was milk and flour but with this recipe I had great flavor.  I did use the Jimmy Dean sausage in the  roll, one small onion and milk instead of half and half. Also made Kitten's Recipe #337664 to serve with the sausage gravy and there was not one bit of gravy leftover. Next time I will double the recipe so DH will have enough to finish up the biscuits later in the week. Thank you hon for teaching me a very tasty way to make sausage gravy.

Great recipe!  I always use Jimmy Dean sausage roll - the light one.  Not only is it a bit better for us but we like the taste much better too.  Also used biscuits from the freezer case.  DH likes his with cheese so I always add some grated sharp cheddar to taste in our gravy - it really is yummy!
Sooo good that hubby decided this was THE recipe!  Thanks for posting!

Thank you from the bottom of my heart.  I am now good at making sausage gravy!  Previously, I was only good at eating it.  Excellent recipe.

My only question was that the ingredients had 1/4 cup and 2 tablespoons of flour written and the recipe said 1/4 cup and 2 teaspoons.  I suspect that I should have used the teaspoons, as two tablespoons made the gravy so thick that I added more milk.  But it was still wonderful.

This was super. I didn't use the onion and used a little cayenne instead of crushed red pepper flakes. I aslo used Cavender's Greek seasoning instead of seasoning salt. I love the recipe and the method. No lumps and it tastes great. You can't ask for more.
Great sausage gravy ~ made to use with another recipe, but it was quick to make and tasted quite good. Thanks ~ into the keeper cookbook with this one!

You did it AGAIN! This is an amazing recipe. We all gobbled it down. A total hit, right outta the park! Thank you SO MUCH for sharing this recipe. The flavor was SO good. It's a keeper. Thanks Kittencal for yet another insanely fabulous recipe!
SOOOO yummy!  Hubby was grateful for the breakfast after a hard weekend of work.  Thanks for the awsome recipe!

Kitten I've loved  your  recipes forever, however if you happen to find Tennessee Pride sausage in your  area, stock up!  This sausage is sooo full of flavor!  And if you  can't  find  TN Pride add  a  few  dashes of  Louisiana  Hot  Sauce....melds through  the gravy better
Excellent for Ozarks biscuits & gravy.

Worthy of lifting the ban on plate-licking!  Subbed finely ground white rice flour for the all-purpose flour due to a wheat allergy.  Used 2 tsp. onion powder instead of the fresh chopped onion.  Even just 1/2 tsp. seasoning salt was too much for our taste; maybe the Banquet/Swift Premium brown & serve patties I used are higher in sodium than the bulk roll called for in the original recipe.

Well, this was my first time to make country gravy and I'm so glad I chose this recipe - the reviews helped make my decision.  It was delicious!  So easy and my son called it "stellar"!  A hit with the whole family - my s-i-l can't wait for me to make it for him!  Made no changes - used Jimmy Dean Hot sausage and a few of the pepper flakes and milk rather than half and half.  It was creamy and delicious and perfect amount of zing!  Thanks so much for sharing this great recipe!

I attempted to make this recipe the first time and chickened out because I didn't trust the sprinkle flour over the sausage until dissolved. So, I did it again exactly as written and it came out perfect. Thanks.
Another winner by Kitten.  Made as directed with excellent results. Thank you.
Good an yummy.  We took the onions down a bit and didn't add the crushed red pepper because my wife has a sensitive stomach.  Was still very good though.

I added the onions and used Turkey sausage, the seasoning salt and 1% milk. I did not use the chillies.  I added 1 tsp of chopped fresh garlic and 1 tsp of chopped fresh ginger and 1/3 cup of no fat sour cream for a bit of extra flavor.  Absolutely wonderful!!! I will make it over and over again
Perfect sausage gravy! Just as good as what you'd get at most restaurants. Will definitely use this recipe again & again. Thanks!
This is very good.  I made this after DD requested it for dinner the other night.  I was on the lookout for a creamier gravy then mine and this is it.  Thank you for sharing, we loved it.

Made it with jimmy dean hot sausage and a little extra black pepper, it was a hit.  Made biscuits that were "ok" and it didn't matter, the gravy was awesome!  Thanks again, dinner tonight a hit!  A special meal, not a once a week kind of thing.  Used 1% milk and I can't imagine what it's like with a more rich milk base.  Very rich and tasty!

On a recent trip to the US I had biscuits and gravy one morning at breakfast -- sold!  There was a part of me that was feeling a guilty but that part was completely run over by the part that was just loving it!  Was having a bit of a longing for that once more and the recipe not only matched but surpassed memory.  Thank for posting Kittencal -- as usual your recipe is spot on!

I never made sausage gravy before. My bf & I had gone to Bob Evans recently & had a bad experience with cold, old gravy. My bf said "I bet you could make better". When we were at the store, he threw a roll of sausage in the cart & my fate was sealed. Didn't know which recipe to try first..when in doubt pick a Kittencal recipe. Did not disappoint. The only thing I did differently was add more red pepper flakes. We like spicy. Really good! Thanks Kittencal!
Yummy--I substituted scallions, and some cream because I had them---great recipe!
I was making chicken fried steak patties and wanted a sausage gravy topping. This was perfect!

This came out absolutely perfect and didn't take forever. Although I did use a full pound of sausage, because who really keeps a quarter pound of sausage in the fridge and actually uses it. Every one gobbled it up.

I have never "loved" sawmill gravy before. It isn't something that I would make for myself. If I make it, it is for my husband (who would have the same reaction to sawdust as he would a gourmet meal) . However, I loved this. I mean, I really loved it. My husband had one helping and over the next two days I ate the rest (on toast - don't care for biscuits). I don't usually ever use worshestershire in anything because I hate it but I dared to use 1 tsp in this recipe and I LOVE IT! I also used the whole milk instead of the cream, and sage sausage. Man, if you are going to make biscuits and gravy use this recipe!!

FINALLY a sausage gravy that tastes exactly how I remember it tasting as a kid. This recipe is spot on. I used 1 lb of Tennessee Pride mild sausage instead of 3/4 lb because I can't do much with an extra quarter lb. I upped the spices slightly, used just over 2 cups whole milk, and it was mouth watering. Very easy to make, I followed the steps as instructed. I was a little worried about pouring milk over the meat, not sure if that much milk could thicken. But it was thick and creamy and inhaled after about 12 minutes. Keeping this one around!

This is a real winner Kittencal! And very easy to make. The onion and red pepper flakes and Worcestershire make a real difference in the flavor and actually this recipe is even easier than the recipe I used to use. I used a heaping 1/4 tsp of the red pepper flakes & 2 tsp of the Worcestershire. I used Shilling's Peppered Season All seasoned which really enhances the flavor too. Thanks!
Very good recipe, Thanks
Very easy to make and the taste is out of this world!

I followed the recipe to the letter first try and found that the soup, even though condensed, made the mixture far too sloppy and salty. Its not a hard recipe to make and I thought Id give it another go. I left out the soup mix full stop, and it was much better. The flavouring stand well as they are, the onion soup is not really needed.

I made gravy from scratch using stock and Bisto powder, it took less than ten minutes and tasted fine. I would make this recipe occasionally as its a good standby when funds are low. I served it with creamed potatoes, fresh green beans and oven roasted tomatoes.
I made this exactly as posted and me and my family enjoyed it. It was simple enough to be made again. Thanks for the resipe
This was excellent! Perfect consistency, easy to make, quick, and delicious. Thanks so much for a wonderful recipe!
Very easy to make. As Lennie said you need a GOOD hard brick parmesan cheese. I guess I used up all my good parmesan and had to go with Kraft Italian Parmesan Wedge.

Love the colour, love the 'nuttiness' and crunch.
The shaved Parmesan is a definite for this vegetable dish.
Thanks for another winner Lennie.
Definitely an impressive recipe! My husband (who doesn't like veggies as much as I do) loved this recipe! Thank you so much Lennie, if I could give you more than 5 stars I would!!
Very tasty, great way to dress up green beans.  I brought them to a Christmas dinner and everyone seemed to like them (either that or they were just being polite!)  Very easy to prepare, as well.
A nice change from plain green beans.  I especially loved the parmesan cheese flavor, and the walnuts added a great little crunch.  Definitely a nice way to dress green beans for company!
Great recipe!  I added onions, which to us made it even better!

Fantastic way to serve green beans. I used pecans and absolutely loved the result. A vegetable peeler made short work of producing the parmesan shavings. A very quick but quality recipe. Thanks Lennie!
I love green beans, walnuts and parmesean.  Put the three together and you have a fantastic combination.  The nuts and parmesean cheese add such great flavor.
We loved it.  I couldn't believe it.  My husband actually ate more of the green beans than he did his New York strip.  We will be fixing this a lot.  Thank you so much.

Wonderful bean dish, Lennie!!  I had pecans so that's what I used. I also sliced some garlic into the butter and then mashed it with a fork once it was soft.  I microwaved the beans until crisp and added them to the butter mixture...too simple!  Thanks for the recipe! Come back Lennie...we miss you!! 
M&Mers

Oh, Lennie!!  This has to be THE BEST green bean recipe I've tried yet! It is my absolute favorite and I would recommend it to anyone and everyone! Only changes I made were adding 1 tsp sea salt while the beans were boiling, and I boiled them for about 15-20 minutes.  My whole family went nuts over them, and my husband won't share any leftovers!  He is taking them in his lunch tomorrow!  Thank you so very much for posting this!!  :-)

What a flavorful delight!  I am not a big fan of fresh parmesan because it is so salty, so I went sparingly on the parmesan shavings.  Needless to say, I took the dishes back to the kitchen and shaved away.  The parmesan is DELICIOUS on these beans, and so very necessary!  This was such a pleasant surprise to me and my husband.  Wonderful flavor with the added crunch from the walnuts.  This will be a regular side dish in our household.  Thanks!!!

I love a recipe like this; simple additions that really make a vegetable special. While sauteing the walnuts, my butter got toasty brown and added another flavor dimension.  The presentation is nice with the whole beans and shards of parmesan. Great.

Brought these for a Thanksgving dinner and they were a big hit.  Even the little kids devoured them.  My only alteration was to add two cloves of garlic to the butter- made it heavenly - I live for garlic.  Thanks for the post.
WOW.  Excellent.  Wonderful.  WAY fab.  These are great and will be a staple from now on.  Thank you SO much for sharing Lennie!

It was very good!!!  I made this for Thanksgiving and my only mistake was that I tried to cook the beans earlier in the day and then reheat them with the butter/nut mix.  Unfortunately they didn't get hot enough, but it was still a great dish.  Next time I know better.
The parmesan cheese gave it the extra "bam".  Everybody loved it, and although I basically fixed the green beans like this before, the parmesan was a new and very impressive hit.

I thought I had already wrote a review for this recipe, but I guess I never posted it!  Very good recipe and the nutty flavor is a really nice change.  Didn't have walnuts or pecans, but did use slivered almonds and we enjoyed it very much.  Thanks for submitting a tasty easy bean receipe.
These are great! I omitted the nuts (personal preference) and everyone enjoyed them. So easy and delicious!
These are the best green beans.  I took them to my Bunco group and the ladies all wanted the recipe.  Thanks for this great dish.

Wow! I'm not a big fan of green beans (my fiance and son are), but even I ate these. I should have known the cheese would make the beans very tasty, since everything is better with cheese, :)  but I was happily surprised at how well the walnuts and parmesan enhanced the dish. I will definitely be making these again, and will not change anything.
Great recipe Lennie - easy and yet so tasty. Using fresh shaved Parmesan really does make a difference.

This is such an easy dish to prepare, and a darned tasty one, too!  I used pecans and freshly shredded (shaved with a vegetable peeler, thanks Missy Wombat!)parmesano reggiano. Tried it out on DH first, but this is definitely the way I'd serve green beans to company! Thanks for the recipe, Lennie!
Skipped the butter and didn't miss it a bit.  Just excellent, Lennie.

I must admidt, I am not usually a fan of fresh green beans but these have changed my mind!  They were SO good!  Made them for a special anniversary dinner and they were a hit.  I could not get enough of the combo between the beans and the cheese, actually wish I had used a little more.  The only addition that I made was that I sauted some shallot before the walnuts.  Great dish!
This was just wonderful. I substituted almonds for walnuts but it was absolutely delicious. Thanks

This was very good.  The pecans, green beans, and parmesan is a lovely combination of flavors.  As I don't typically add butter to the veggies I prepare, I think next time I'd either eliminate the butter, or perhaps use a smaller amount of olive or grape seed oil instead.  I added some fresh cracked black pepper and a sprinkling of salt at the table.  Thanks for posting this!

What a great combination of flavors. Pecans & parmesan really go well together - throw in green beans and you have a true flavor treat.  They taste wonderul and are attractive on the plate Thanks Lennie for yet another recipe that I will make over and over again

Loved it!  Everyone else gave it two thumbs up, too.  I didn't have walnuts, so I used pecans.  I'm eating the leftovers in my lunch today, and I can't wait.  Thank you for sharing this recipe -- I'll definitely be making this one again.
i used walnuts and thought it was very good. the walnuts were very fragrant and really made the dish great. there is a good chance that next time i make green beans i will make them like this.

These really were impressive green beans!! So delicious and fresh-tasting, easy to make, and the walnuts added just the right amount of toasty, crunchy goodness. I recommend seasoning with salt and fresh-ground black pepper, especially if using unsalted butter. Also, I used pre-packaged grated parmesan cheese (but *not* the powdery stuff) and it worked just fine. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

Really good and they DID impress my Thanksgiving dinner guests.  The combo of green beans, walnuts and Parmesan is perfect, just delicious.  I'll definitely be making this again and not just for guests, for US!  Thanks for posting this Lennie :)

We like to try new vegetable dishes, and this was new to us.  It was very good and will become one of our standbys.  We served it with our Christmas Eve dinner along with Standing Rib Roast and all the fixin's.  It went together at the last minute and was easy to do.  I used a vegetable peeler to shave the cheese, and it was perfect.  And the flavor of the nice, fresh beans came through.  This is one we'll do again, especially when we want something delicious and quick.
The fresh parmesan really makes the difference!  I used pecans.  This lived up to its name.

Pretty good beans.  Used pecans instead of walnuts as that's what we had on hand. Also used the grated parmesan instead of fresh, although bet it is better with fresh! Have to serve really fast because hard to keep warm. Thanks a lot for sharing!

A great twist of the plain jane beans! I used both chopped almonds and walnuts and thought this dish was superb.  My family also was impressed.  I like my green beans to be a little on the cruncy side, like the texture of the nuts.  YUMM!
We enjoyed these. The walnuts and parmesan added a nice touch. Thanks.
Excellent and very easy.
Fabulous!! Thanks :O)
Very simple, but very good dish.  Thanks.
I really liked these green beans....will make often..
Made these over the weekend, what an easy and simple way to make fresh green beans.  My husband is not one for fresh vegetables, but he has already asked for these again.  Thank you.
These were great!!!!  Had no walnuts so used pecans and they worked perfectly.  We will be making this again soon.  Thanks for such a wonderful recipe.  :)
This is so tasty and so easy. I was in a hurry and used a bag of whole frozen green beans and microwaved them. I then prepared the recipe as posted and it was fantastic.

I used this for a Thanksgiving dinner instead of green bean casserole.  Really good!!  I also slightly browned/burnt the butter before adding the green beans.  Like another reviewer, I also used frozen green beans and microwaved them.  I don't like walnuts, but i used slivered almonds.  Will make this again soon!

Simple, fresh and delicious! I used sliced almonds and add them after I toss the beans in the butter. After a minute or two of cooking the beans in butter, I turn off the heat and put a lid on the pan until I am ready to plate the meal. I will be making this often, especially during garden season! Thanks for sharing!

So addicting!!  I have 4 servings of these green beans.  Best way I have found to eat them!  The flavors of all these ingredients are amazing together.  I used shredded parmesan cheese and it turned out great

Lovely way to enjoy green beans.  I have to admit that I didn't add the cheese...after I tasted the beans with the walnuts, they were delicious as is...no need to add anything extra....I'll be making these again the next time we have green beans.  Thanks for a great recipe!
Wow!  These just seem so "fancy" on the table.  I made these for my family and we all enjoyed them very much.  I plan on making them this weekend for our family Christmas.  Thank yo for sharing.

What a great recipe!  I've made it several times now for company and everyone loves it!  It is so simple and really delicious.  Try it with pine nuts, it is fantastic!  Thank you for sharing this recipe!

Something was off for us with this recipe. I know it has rave reviews, so maybe something I did? I liked the texture of the green beans with the nuts, but the flavor was not our favorite. Hmmm... Thanks anyway for posting!
Excellent! Added a bit of salt, but other than that, made as directed.
These were really good even though I thought I had frozen whole green beans but ended up using  canned. And almonds instead of walnuts.
I had some fresh green beans that I needed to use.  While these were good, we all felt the flavor could be stronger.
Easy, easy, easy!  And people love it!  What more can you say....?
Tasty and easy to make. Definitely will have this again.
Where is the 1/4 cup of water used???????
Yeah, baby! This was great! My DH requested a "diner dinner" so I made this. Quick, easy and delish! Well done! Thank you!

This recipe is the ultimate if anyone is looking for a fabulous salisbury steak and sauce dinner some night. The flavor was excellent as per husband and son who wasn't sure if he would like it
His plate was cleeeeean! This is a keeper for sure. This was my addition to the recipe sause,  mushrooms!! and lots of them MMMMM.

Oh boy, did we love this.The only thing I changed was the soup. I couldn't find "french onion soup" so I used Campell's fat free Vegetable Broth with Onions. So freakin' delicious. I will be passing this one around!

This is an awesome recipe.  This is the only one I have used since finding it in a "Taste of Home" magazine years ago. Fabulous served over buttered egg noodles with a touch of parsley.  Glad you posted it...it deserves it!

The sauce for this dish is just wonderful!!  It tasted so yummy over mashed potatoes. Oops, I guess it wasn't completely "as is", I did add a small can of mushrooms as some others did.  This a nice easy, comfort food dinner and I'm sure I'll be making it again.
This recipe is a keeper.  Loved the sauce.  We really enjoyed it - even our finicky kids liked it (and that's saying a lot, believe me).  I'll definitely make this again.  Thanks!

Loved this recipe! It was just was I was looking for. Very simple to make, and the taste was great! I did make it as is, but next time I will take advice of chef to double up on gravy recipe, as well as the addition of some mushrooms. My boyfriend had seconds! A new favorite!

Yum! I made this for dinner last night and it was great.  I doubled the sauce, using golden mushroom soup for the 2nd can of soup, and served this with mashed potatoes. Very good - Meat, potatoes, and gravy - how can you go wrong?

I thought this was just ok.  I made the recipe exactly as stated, and found the sauce to be a bit overpowered by the Worchestershire, and the oniony flavor of the sauce was lost. I made this last night for me and my husband.  This was absolutely delicious - the best Salisbury Steak I have ever had.  This is a definite keeper at my house.
Really nice recipe. The gravy very tasty...wonderful over the mashed. Will definitely make again.

Made this last night and it was so so so so so so so so good.  Hubby wants this at least once a week now.  Thank you for a great recipe, served this with Potato Pie recipe number 95345 and what a combo.  Thanks so much for a keeper recipe.
This was a really easy dish to prepare that we both enjoyed! My husband said the flavor reminded him of his childhood and he REALLY liked it!  Will definitely make this one again!  Thank you!

This recipe just wasn't to our liking. Everything cooked up nicely and it was very easy to prepare. We just didn't care for the flavor the ketchup imparted to the sauce. It wasn't what we had in mind when we were thinking salisbury steak.
I followed Ginny Sue's lead and added more liquid. All I had was chicken broth - so I added a cup of chicken broth and a little cornstarch. This is very easy and very good.

These little steaks were quite yummy!  Not exactly what I always thought a salisbury to be, but good none the less.  I will make these again, but might change the name to something more apporproiate.  Thanks for a good recipe!
So good and so easy!  This has become a staple at my house.  My 10 year old wants to learn how to make it so he can have it all the time!!!
This is fantastic!I loved everything about it.It was simple and fast to make and great tasting!I will definately be making this again.Thanks for posting it.

I made this tonight and we all loved it. I did, however, make a few changes. First of all, I sauteed some fresh mushrooms in the pan first, removed to a paper towel covered plate and set aside, then browned the beef patties. When making the patties, I had to get a little creative. The recipe does not say which size egg. Since the medium egg is the standard for cooking and baking, I used that as a yard stick. However, I only had jumbo eggs. Since two medium can roughly equal one jumbo,, I separated the yolk from the egg and only used half of the white, reserving the other half for a facial mask for tonight....put it in the fridge and get it cold...great for those bags under the eyes. I seared the patties and removed them to the plate with the mushroom. Scraping up the fond on the bottom of the pan (the brown goodies), I added the flour, stirred until the flour was cooked, then proceeded with the sauce. Because of the review which said it was too sweet, I used half of the catsup and replaced it with water. Next time, I think I'll glaze the pan with red wine first and proceed with the recipe. That is, replacing the additional water with wine - about 1/8 of a cup. I returned the mushrooms and patties to the skillet, covered and simmered per directions. We served it with buttered egg noodles and a nice, fresh salad to cut the richness. Soooo good.
