Thanks for a great recipe! The only change I made was to use a rounded teaspoon of zest, 'cause I'm a big fan of that particular ingredient! Otherwise, I did as directed & my cookies were a big hit! Definitely something to make again! Thanks for sharing! [Tagged, made & reviewed in Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup cooking game]

Made for Comfort Cafe Summer 2009. These are excellent cookies.  Love the great orange flavor that the orange juice gives these.  Will definitely make these again.  Thanks for posting this recipe Queen!
I wish I had doubled this recipe- it's so good that we wanted leftovers for the next day!! Took SloppyJoe's advice & served with stir-fried veggies... it's a keeper!
Awsume

I used pork chops instead of pork steaks. The smell was amazing and the taste wonderful.  I did not change anything other than the cut of meat and the quantities.  I doubled the recipe so we would have plenty for lunches tomorrow.  This will certainly be used again.  Thanks for a nice supper Chef Dee.

I did this with a cut down recipe, had a big thick pork cutlet just a  good size for me.  Cut the ingredients to go with this and it worked out perfect, just the right combination of flavours.  This is just so easy to prepare and let cook by itself, but the smell and the flavour eating is to die for.  The meat was fork tender.

The pork steaks were just melt-in-your-mouth tender. I marinated them overnight and then grilled them. there is a slight sweet flavor to them after cooking, KIT you have the best recipes on this planet! and this is another 100 stars! I will make my pork steaks like this for ever! thank you.

Thank goodness this was an excellent recipe, as the first time I tried it we took it to some friend's house for dinner.  I cooked the pork steaks in the slow cooker and ended up cutting them into bite size pieces for ease (little kids there).  This made me think of taking this to pot luck suppers or serving as appetizers.  Great any  way you serve them!

3 stars for an average rating, would give 3.5 if I could.  I made this in the crockpot, and reduced soy to 1/2c (added water).  My kids refused to eat it after the 1st bite - the flavors were too strong for them and that was a disappointment to me.  It's rich, deep, dark, a lot more tang than sweet.  Dh said it was "ok", I liked it better, especially on the noodles I served it over.

I made this using chops in place of the steaks and I also added some crushed red pepper.  While it had a very nice flavor, I found it to be way too salty.  I will make this again, but cut back on the soy sauce.

This was so amazingly tastful....I doubled the sauce as we love our sauce here, I used some of the sauce the next day with my chicken stir fry and it was even better with that!!  This will be regularly appearing at out supper table from now on.  Thanks again!

Wonderful recipe with a touch of the Orient.  I used the Chili Sauce Substitute recipe #52689 in this recipe with delicious  results.  I also used the low sodium soya sauce and the taste was just right for us.  I intend to use this sauce on chicken as well as salmon in the future.  Thank you, Dee.

Amazing recipe!!  The flavour was perfect & the meat was very, very tender.  I actually used thick centre pork loin chops (since I wasn't really sure what a pork steak was).  This is one of those recipes that is easy to prepare but would knock the socks off dinner guests!
Excellent recipe-have made several times.  I'm not a big fan of ginger, so I cut back to 1/4 tsp.  I also always have a LOT of sauce left over; it's great on rice or mashed potatoes.

This was Sooo good! My 3 pork steaks were thin but big and were about 2 1/2 -3 lbs total. Never bought them before or tasted and was a bit leery about this cut of meat.  BUUUTT...It was delicious and tender, marinade flavor was great. 1 1/2 hour cook time was right on...did take foil off for the last half hour.  Not only did I give it five stars but my whole family (including picky kids!) loved it so this will obviously be a regular in our house!  thanks.

Oh my, this is a great pork steak recipe.  We like a sweet, sticky pork meal and this didn't disappoint.  I have already suggested this for my in-laws and a couple friends. (non of whom have the internet??????) I also love a meat that can be put in the oven and forgotten about for a bit....thank you again for another tasty meal.....Stephanie
This was so good ! I will be making this again soon.

This was great!  I used it on a pork loin.  The only thing I did differently was to use a raspberry chipotle sauce instead of the brown sugar.  We really enjoyed it.  There was a lot of sauce left over so my husband wants to use it on another pork loin, but grill it instead, I am sure it will be fantastic!  Thanks Kitten!
Awesome recipe. We loved it. The sauce was so good I added some Chinese veggies and made a stir-fry in the oven.

This recipe works for I and my wife.  I accidentally used regular soy (thought maybe someone had high blood pressure).  The sauce was unbelievably salty; however, it cooked off somehow and we loved it...  I was sure to save the leftovers.  Next time I will try the "low sodium".

Scrumptious!! I cut the serving proportions down to 4 servings and followed the recipe exactly. This was so easy to throw together and smelled terrific while it was baking. Tender, tasty and totally on my make-again list! Thanks Kittencal!

I used a cheaper cut of pork chops for this knowing it would be okay with the long baking time & they were moist, tender & very flavorful.  
I used 4 good sized pork chops but kept the sauce portion as written - perfect!  Lots of sweet/tangy sauce to pour over the meat & rice.  
Very easy to make & was forgiving enough to let me put it together in the morning, toss it in the fridge & them bake that evening.  It will def. go on my repeat menu list.  Thanks for another great recipe!

Just Plain delicious.  Wasn't sure if you meant heinz chili sauce or siracha.  All I had was siracha  so I used about 1/8th of acup and 3/4 cups kethup.  Turned out great.  Absolutely perfect with some steamed Jasmine rice.

WOW!!!  This recipe is going my new favorite way to cook pork.  I served it with jasmine rice (covered in this great sauce) and steamed broccoli.  I made it using 4 small pork chops and 1 hour in the oven was plenty.  I removed the foil during the last 10 minutes and cranked the oven to 400 to thicken the sauce.  I also added a spicey asian spice blend to the sauce before baking.  Thank you!
Simply awesome flavors made for some great chops!  Thanks!
I made this using pork chops and it was very good. My husband loved it. Next time I will try it with chicken.

kittencal.
This worked out very well.I halved the recipe for the meat I had.
Have entered it in my keeper and redo book for next time.
Don Steele

I really enjoyed this recipe.  I love main dishes that can be fixed and thrown in the oven for an hour.  Five stars for ease of making and the flavor is great too!  A little salty for my taste, but DH said it was perfect.  I am afraid decreasing the soy sauce would compromise flavor, so I will leave as is next time..except a healty shot of red pepper flakes to bump up the heat, as I am a heat junkie.   I used 4 thick pork chops and they were perfectly tender after an hour.    Great recipe!
Kids LOVED it. I used boneless chicken breast instead of the pork. I did forget to add the cornstrach though so the sauce was thin. Served with rice and steamed broccli yum...will make this again.

I gave this recipe 2 stars. I made this recipe for my families dinner. This smelled great cooking. When I took the meat out of the pan it just fell apart which was perfect. I made 1 minor change to this recipe. I used 2 pork steaks. I left the sauce as it was. I did use Splenda brown sugar. Overall my family didn't care for this recipe. My future hubby said it was to spicy. My 6 yr old newphew just liked the rice. I thought this was to sweet and I reduced the sugar when I used the Splenda. Overall I just don't think I'll make this again. Thanks for posting anyway  Christine (internetnut)
A little on the salty side, but we loved them anyway!  DH wants to try the sauce on chicken, so next time chicken it is!  We will have again with the pork too!  Thanks!

This is a tasty and tender pork dish.  Served to my non-rice eating DH with baked potato, and even he (the pickiest of the picky) thought they were "good" (a high compliment, as many culinary attempts meals are only "fine").  I don't understand people who change the recipe almost entirely (using a third of the specified meat but the ALL the spices) and then say it is too spicy or too sweet.  Kind of like pouring 1/2 cup instead of a jigger of whiskey into a glass with coke and then saying it is too strong!
Only had 3 boneless pork chops but made all the sauce recipe.  It did make a very tender, tasty meal.  Too much ginger for DH so I'll reduce that next time.

Hello my favorite cook!! Made these using pork cube steaks..YUMMO!!! They were fantastic!! We enjoyed them so much. DH loved all the great flavors.(me, too). Served with hot green beans and rice, delightful supper. Wanted you to know you are in my thoughts, sorry to hear about your precious husband. Take care, my friend!!
YUMMY! My family and I really loved this recipe. Thanks for sharing it.
Very easy recipe to make and was delicious.Didnt find this salty at all but did use the low sodium soy as directed.Thanks for a wonderful recipe.
This was great!  I always look at the pork steaks, but don't have a wide range of recipes that use them.  It's great to add this to my collection.  Thanks!

I really like this sauce!  I cubed my pork, and browned as you said.  Then I tossed meat with sauce in the pan, and finished in the oven.  I have enjoyed this on salmon, also.  I was out of chili sauce, and substitued Sriracha hot chili sauce... delicious!
This was alright, but not spectacular. Changes I made to the recipe may have been responsible for this.

I found another AWESOME pork steak/pork chop recipe :D
Thanks for posting

This is an amazing recipe! I havaen't had much luck with frying pork chops lately, they get so dry, so I tried this. What a difference from my dried out pork chops! Followed this to the letter and both my hubby and I are very pleased. Thank's Kit, for sharing a wonderful dish!

I really enjoyed the recipe and the chops had more of a sweet taste. Also, the recipe was easy to assemble. I mixed up my sauce and let the chops marinate in the sauce for an hour. I let them cook for about an hour and a half. Thanks for another winner!
The Pork was so tender you could cut it with a fork and the sauce had so much flavor. Had it with White Rice and Broccoli. Delicious !!!

A family-pleasing main course. The sauce was perfect for serving over rice.  When I'm busy, I love recipes that take little time to prep. Toss it in the oven and forget about it for an hour or so.
Served with brown rice, broccoli to make a complete and delicious meal. Thanks! ~Made for KK's forum~

I made this last night for supper and was really disappointed.  I have a brand new baby and was looking for a quick and easy recipe.  The pork turned out very tender but I did not like the texture of the meat - kind of like boiled pork.

I love pork steaks and my husband usually pan fries them with lots of seasoning salt or coats them in shake n' bake and fries them.  I have also had them grilled with barbecue sauce. 

The flavors of the sauce itself are good but it did not thicken up at all and did not form a nice glaze as I had hoped.

Against my better judgment, I did not brown the pork steaks first and I wish that I had because I think that this would have made a difference.  Also, I think boiling the sauce on the stove first to thicken it, and then putting it on the browned pork steaks and then in the oven might have really made a difference also.  I also think grilling the pork steaks and then basting them with this sauce might be good (or using this sauce as a marinade).

Now, I have all this leftover pork steak that tastes kind of gross and I have to figure out a way to salvage it for supper tonight - stir fry maybe...

I may try this recipe again with the changes I suggested, but I would test it out on a couple of steaks first instead of all 6.
Absolutely delicious.  Made the recipe exactly as written.  The whole family loved it.  The pork chops were so tender.   I served it over rice.  Will make again and again.

This was really good!  I followed the directions for the glaze but made the dish more like a stir fry.  I stir fried some onion, red and green peppers then removed from the pan.  Tossed in some diced pork loin and stir fried til almost done.  Added sauce and pre-cooked vegetables and let simmer for a few minutes.  Served over rice.  It was a great weeknight meal and leftovers were good the next day for lunch.  Thanks for posting!

This was really good! I was pleasantly surprised since I don't have the best luck with Asian dishes. I made a few changes -- I used cubed pork tenderloin, stir-fried it and added the sauce at the end until it got thick and bubbly. I reduced the soy sauce but still felt it was a little overpowering, so I added additional brown sugar. I was so pleased with the end result! I'll definitely use this again with pork or chicken breast.

We loved it!  We are always looking for new ways to cook up meat and this was excellent and tender and full of flavor!  Thank you so much for sharing. I have already written it down on a recipe card to add to my recipe box!  YUM!

This recipe is simply amazing! I made it tonight for dinner, using 2 lbs of pork steaks, and it was so delicious there was nothing left! I did not change the recipe. I did sear the steaks in a little vegetable oil before I placed the dish in the oven. The meat was so tender it just fell off the bone, and the sauce was too good for words! I will make this over and over, and will always use pork steaks!

Yet another fantastic recipe! My family devoured these chops in a heartbeat. When I made them, I marinated them in the sauce for 3 hours beforehand and then threw them on the grill instead of baking them. We used a little bit of the sauce that I saved to brush on the pork as it was cooking and they turned out about as perfect as pork chops can get! Thank you for the recipe. This is going in the keeper file.

This is a really good recipe and super easy too which is a big bonus.  I typically like to brown the steaks first for a little boost in the flavor, but it is not essential to do this...they are still tasty.  I also like a little thicker sauce so I increase the cornstarch to 1 1/2 tbsp, but that is a personal preference.  The flavor of the sauce is wonderful and great served over rice as suggested in the recipe.
Very good recipe.  The sauce was great, but I found the meat didn't absorb the flavor.  I think the pork would benefit from marinating in the sauce for at least 24 hours prior to cooking.

We grilled our pork steaks and made the sauce (reducing) on the stovetop, then glazing the pork the last few minutes on the grill. My spouse was expecting just another barbeque sauce, however to his delightful surprise, the sauce is far from it! Delicious Asian flavors. Will make these again. Thanks for sharing!
6 thumbs up!!!!

This is very good. I did not have chili sauce, so I subbed a little tobasco sauce. DH wants to try this with chicken. I almost forgot. I did not have low sodium soy sauce, so I used 1/2 water and 1/2 regular soy sauce.

While looking for something new to do with pork chops found this & knowing I love Kitten's recipe gave it a try.  Followed the direction with no changes & it was great, used thick cut pork chops & the timing was perfect.  Served over steamed rice with the left over sauce over it all.  Great blend of flavors.  The pork was nice & moist, not dry at all.  I do think StacL has a point though, as good as this is, next time think I'll poke a couple of holes in the pork & marinate for awhile in the fridge prior to cooking - want to make sure this awesome sauce gets completely trough the meat.

I forgot to egg batter and dip in breadcrumbs so I sprinkled bread crumbs on top and worked out just fine.

I loved the balsamic vinegar flavor that came through the chicken. I topped with sliced tomatoes and added a touch more of balsamic vinegar.

Another keeper! Won the husband and kids approval!

this was so yummy and simple! i love making cuban food, and had never really seen this one before, so i thought i would make it, as it is  healthy too... man it was definitely a hit in our house. thanks for a keeper!

This is essentially Ropa Vieja.  Growing up eating spicy latino foods, I can say this beats the test.  

It's incredibly easy and delicious.  No need to cut the pork or potatoes.  I threw all ingredients in (except potato) and cooked on low for 10 hours.  About halfway through I shredded pork with a spoon and threw in a halved sweet potato.  My boyfriend went crazy and suggested we have it for lunch today!

Tasty and easy! I cooked for 10 hours on low and added the cubed sweet potato at hour 7 and it was mushy.  Next time I'll still add the potatoes at hour 7, but only cook for 9 hours total.  Served over brown rice with a fresh salad on the side.  Perfect for a rainy evening!
Is it just me...or are the cooking instructions incomplete?

Smelled so bad cooking we had to throw it out & order a pizza. Maybe they left something out or this simply doesn't appeal to mainstream America who aren't accustomed to the exotic combination of flavors. It didn't say how long to cook it. I cooked it on med-high for about 5 hours. It seems like a weird combination - sweet potatoes & tomotoes, but I had the ingredients on hand. I tasted it and it was really ODD. Don't go there if your family isn't adventurous. Sorry, I really wanted to like this.

I put in leeks instead of scallions and I used a jar of my favorite salsa instead of canned tomatoes and chiles. best thing I have ever eaten.

Thanks!!
I loved it.  I'm always looking for a good non-typical slow cooker recipe and this fits the bill.  I did double the amount of cumin and garlic.  Delicious!

I'm not even on ww and I love this stew. I added the sweet potato during the last hour of cooking. I also added one white potato. I cooked this on high for 5 hours. I didn't cut the pork chops, I just threw them in the slow cooker whole, semi frozen and then shredded them with a fork. I served this over brown rice. I also added extra OJ. I did not use the scallions, used onion powder. Also didn't have any lime and forgot to add the cilantro until I was halfway done eating it and it was still good! I googled Pork and Sweet potato stew and this recipe came up and also the orignal one from WW.
We enjoyed this recipe! I think next time I will put the potatoes in closer to the end as others have suggested. Overall, the flavors were great. Makes a very nice fall meal. Thanks for posting!

This was very good!  I did add celery simply because I had some that needed to be used up.  I didn't have beef bouillion, but had beef stock, so used that and used less water.  Of course, I added salt and pepper and hot sauce since I add those ingredients to all my recipes!   Will definately make this again!  Thanks!
Very easy and tasty!
I LOVE this soup!!! So easy to make. My husband LOVES this too, and he's not the one to like soup. Thanks!!!

The whole family loved this recipe!  I wanted to make it a one-pot meal so I browned and drained the beef first, and then added everything else to the same pot.  Near the end of cooking time I made some fluffy dumplings with recipe #213949 (using gluten-free flour for us) and the end result was total comfort food that everyone really enjoyed!  Thanks for sharing your recipe, Tinamama!  We'll be making it again!  Made & enjoyed for Spring 2011 Pick A Chef!
Good recipe. I also added celery, cabbage, and peas. My husband love cabbage and celery in almost everything. I sometimes add rice as well.

Thank you Tinkerbell for making the Fluffy Dumpling suggestion--and especially for noting that you made it gluten-free. I used it too, and it was delicious!
This recipe looked like a great stew, but bland. I added Mrs. Dash, savory, oregano, marjoram, coriander and salt and pepper--in addition to the optional garlic! Quite satisfactory!

This was good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written but mine didn't get as thick as the picture showed (which was what I was looking for). It still tasted good but we thought it needed more seasoning. I added salt and pepper.
Great recipe!  Quick and easy, but the best part was that the family loved it!!  I made the recipe as is and couldn't have asked for it to be any better!!

When a search for ground sausage soup turned up no results that looked tempting today, I changed my criteria to ground beef.  Needless to say, instead of the ground beef I used sausage - with most excellent results.  But......after a few tastes I decided "more" was needed so I added a can of diced tomatoes, then a bag of frozen mixed vegetables......then some cooked macaroni. Naturally I had to add some more water and let it simmer a bit longer. It turned out to be a delicious "stewy" type of soup that when hot garlic bread was added, will be a family favorite. Thank you so much for the great recipe.

This is a great "starter" recipe. Using what I had on hand, I used 1 cup chicken broth instead of beef bouillon, 12 oz. tomato sauce (next time will try w/ petite diced tomatoes), 1/2 tsp. diced oregano, 1-1/2 cup frozen green beans, 1/p red bell pepper, 1/2 cup chopped celery. I used oil to brown my meat b/c the meat was extra-lean. After browning the meat I stirred in the garlic, diced carrots, diced potatoes bell pepper, celery and frozen green beans. (If using frozen corn, could toss in now, too). I simmered until veggies were soft. I served with biscuits. Next time I make this I want to try using Italian sausage instead of ground beef.
This was a really big hit. I added a can of cheddar cheese soup to mellow the enchilada sauce a bit, and I used chicken instead of beef. I'll be keeping this one on rotation for winter.

Very good and DH loved it.  I wanted to hold down the salt, so I looked at the ingredients of Mexican stewed tomatos...and used diced tomatos, jalapeno, garlic, cumin and coriander (but in very small amounts).  Very tasty and so easy to put together!
If you like enchiladas, you'll really enjoy this.  It's so simple to put together.   I made no changes to the recipe.  I'll be making this again; thanx!

This was very tasty! I could not find enchilada sauce here so Chef1Mom was kind enough to send me a recipe! It was very good. I cooked it on high for 4 hours, but had to sneak some after less than 2! ;) It was excellent with just a little sprinkle of cheese and some broken tortilla chips. Yum! The only change I made was to use a 6 bean blend that I rinsed. I will try to take a photo of my next bowl and post it. Made for my fellow Kitchen Witch for ZWT5. Thanks!
This was a very good soup.  I added diced tomatoes with jalapenos, black beans, garlic, cumin and a little fresh cilantro...yummy!  Thanks for posting...made and reviewed for Zaar Chow Hounds...ZWT5
Great soup! Made as directed, except added shredded cheese at the table, along with homemade tortilla chips. This is comfort food! :) Thanks, Chef1MOM! Made for ZWT5, Kitchen Witches.

Made as directed, using Chef #89831 's Recipe #168653.  This was good but seemed like it was missing something - not sure what.  Tasted more like a chili rather than enchiladas.  Made for Saucy Senoritas Zingo ZWT5.

This was very good! I added rotel tomatoes and recipe#12877. My DD and I added cheese. It really didn't turn out as thick as I would have liked but is still great with tortilla chips. Thanks! Made for THE GROOVY GASTROGNOMES and ZWT5 Zingo.

This was really good!  Made it for my husband's lunches.  Instead of pinto beans only had ranch style and one can of enchilada sauce so also added a 14oz. can of green chili enchilada sauce.  He wants it hotter so next time I'll add a can of HOT Rotel.  Put a dollop of sour cream and shredded cheese on top and he added crushed tortilla chips.  I'm going keep all of these ingredients in stock so I can make it anytime.  Thank you!

My, my, what a wonderful mouthful of flavors!!!
Artichokes and garlic are wonderful together.  I did not change the recipe at all.
We are not Sunday nite dinner eaters, just bites or appetizers.  This dish was just perfect.  We loved the flavors, and so easy to make, and was very satisfying.
Thanks Miller for posting this one!
this was okay, i think the smaller you can cut the hearts and still handle them the better,
I made this for an "emergency" snack tonight and they were superb.  I didn't bother to saute the hearts, just poured the butter with garlic that I'd microwaved over them.

Best artichoke appetizer I've tried so far, and I've been trying a lot lately.  Such a refreshing change from the dip recipes!  I also didn't sauté the chokes after frying - and I didn't have unsalted butter, and I used quartered chokes, might do smaller next time because I just love the flavor.  Very yummy, simple, and unique.

Great appetizer!  And so easy!  I too just drizzled the garlic butter over them.  I did have some left over, and the next evening I heated them up in the oven and melted a piece of provolone on each --Mmmmmmmmmmm.  Thanks for sharing a great recipe!
--Marla

I can't believe I forgot to rate this recipe!! I'm so sorry! I love artichoke hearts and made this recipe with them.  My family fell in love with these, and so did I.  Like other people I did saute my hearts in garlic butter but instead just poured it on top of the hot hearts.  They were fabulous.  Thanks Miller for such an easy yet great recipe!! :D

We would like to make this another time before rating it.  We think it has potential, but a couple of things just didn't go right for us.  First, we don't think we rinsed enough of the brine off, because they were very sharp tasting.  Second, they didn't seem to coat well.  It was more like a stuffing than a breading.  The taste of the breading was good, but with the sharpness of the artichoke, we just dind't eat many.  We'll try again though, and hopefully do better!

I always fine large jars of artichoke hearts and wonder what I can make with them? So I found your recipe.  I didn't have regular bread crumbs so I substudited cornflake crumbs instead. I dipped artichoke heart into egg first. Then into dry ingrent's: garlic salt, grated asiago or any hard cheese grated is fine,pepper, and/or what ever seasons fancy your buds. 
then i sauted/fryed in oil till lightly browned. i then place on a cookie sheet and continued to bake them so they we more crunchy so they could be eaten with fingers. my kids at these up so fast that i didn't have any left to serve to our guest...also a little lemon squeezed over them after would be a good touch. i didn't have any on hand but will do it next time.
thank you 
lauri from Cleveland

Tasty way of using the jar of artichoke hearts that was threatening to outlive its welcome in my fridge. I used mostly canola oil, and enough butter to go head to head with a bottle of Drain-O and still tasted the artichoke flavor when biting into the juicy center(s)!
Gonna try this recipe tonight for my family
This was a really great homemade soup.  I shredded my carrots instead of chopping them and added a bit more pepper - truly delicious!!

Uncle Bill, I am a huge fan of your soups. I made this recipe for the second time last night and it was just as great as the first.  I love this soup. It is very easy to make and tastes better than restaurant soups. The only change I made was I used a 32 oz package of broccoli florets, instead of 16 oz. I also used ground white pepper. Thank you very much for sharing.

Very tasty!

The cabbagey taste of the broccoli intensified a lot after refrigeration, so I added extra half and half, extra soy sauce, and some ground mustard.
gotta hand it to him, this is great-tasting soup and very easy to make. i halfed the recipe which was a bad idea because when it ran out, i still wanted more. will be making this again soon.
Uncle Bill this soup was great.  This was very easy to make.  It had a great fresh taste. I will be making this again. Thank you for a great soup recipe.

I am on a low-fat diet, and had remove some of the "good stuff", but even by substituting low-fat broth and skim milk, I found it to be very enjoyable...Thanks for submitting this, and will definitely make this soup again... SharonP.

I have now made huge batches of this soup. And frozen into portion serves so I can have this lovely soup whenever the urge takes me.Yummmm!
Bella

Great soup! I made this exactly as the recipe states, except that I added most of the liquid after I pureed the vegetable mixture to make it easier to transfer from the pot to the blender and back. It worked very well and the results were delicious! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

Rich and delicious soup! Perfect alone or with a sandwich on a cold day. I cleaned out my crisper with this one, using about a cup and a half more broccoli florets and chopped baby carrots. Mine did not require thickening, I would assume because of the extra veg. Using a hand blender in the cooking pot made this even easier. Would also be wonderful with a low fat sub for the half and half since the soup is quite substantial with a lovely blend of flavors. Thanks, Uncle Bill, I'll make this one again!

Myself and my husband enjoyed this soup on a chilly  Sunday evening.  I quite honestly threw this soup together while he was at the store.  Absolutely delicious!  Easy and quick if you decide not to puree the cooked vegetables in the beginning.  I happen to like the "parts", and it was quite tasty in spite of the lack of puree. Thanks for a lovely recipe, and a quick way to get rid of a bit of broccoli and half an onion.  I did by the way cut the recipe in half....we are only two...Way to go!

Uncle Bill....ANOTHER WINNER!
Just made a big old pot of this and I'm on my 2nd bowl.  I bet it will be better tomorrow too.

THANK YOU for another great addition to my file.
Very tasty!  Great soup!

Yum!  A super tasting soup.
Strayed from the recipe in only one way....I didn't add the extra 1/4 c. water and the flour.  Instead added another 1/4 c. of half 'n half then thickened it with potato buds. It's a real winner in any case.  Thanks Uncle Bill.

What a great recipe!  I love the carrot base, yet with no 'carrot' flavor.  I added 1/2 tsp. garam masala per another recipe's recommendation.  I also used home made, unsalted, chicken stock so, I had to add about a 1/2 tsp. salt to the finished product.  My family LOVED this and I will definetly be making it again!
Thank you for a broccoli soup without cheese, cheese is great, but it is refreshing to have a recipe listed that is different and good.

THE MOST DELICIOUS SOUP we have ever tasted. We've made it twice now- once substituting 1 cup cream and 1 cup milk for the half and half, and the second time using evaporated milk in an atempt to be more healthy (I don't know what half and half is- I don't think we have it in Australia). I say forget being healthy and go for the cream. It was still fantastic either way, though.

Uncle Bill always come through!  I had alot of broccoli that needed to be cooked...soup was another way to sneak veggies into the kids!  I added a small diced potato to help thicken the soup (omitted the flour and water), used some ready made broth and used my stick bender to puree the soup.  Do not omit the soy sauce and black pepper, the take the flavours to another level!!
Thanks,  Michelle

As a family broccoli is probably our favorite green vegetable so I was excited to make this.  I have never made cream of broccoli soup, only broccoli cheddar soup so I was hesitant would we like just Broccoli.  I made only minor changes like less vegetable soup base do to salt and I used whole milk.  To start off it is the most beautiful color green, and then when I took the first bite it was bliss, so velvety smooth I can only describe it as Sensational.  I will make this again and again maybe try a different way of thickening it up, for friends that canâ€™t have flour.  Thanks for another great health soup.

As with all Uncle Bill recipes, this one is delicious.  Four tablespoons of chicken soup base seemed like it might make very salty soup, but I have learned to trust Bill's culinary instincts.  So glad I didn't improvise--the flavor was perfect if you follow Bill's exact directions.  MichelleAnne's suggestion about using a stick blender was very helpful too.  So easy, so quick, so good.
This is the most delicious broccoli soup I have ever tried in my life. This is definitely a keeper.
Wonderful soup thank you so much for sharing your recipe I loved the soy sauce!

How come I don't uncles with recipes like this ;-) It was delicious and satisfying on a cold winter night. Yum! The only small change I might try next time is to reduce the carrots to 2 or 3 since the color was a little bit too "orangey", but that could have been due to my definition of "large" :-) Thank you.

I liked this soup but I felt that it was over seasoned and a bit heavy. The beauty of making soup from scratch is that you don't have to use that much sodium. The soup base was way overpowering as was the soy sauce, and I didnt like the sweetness the carrots added. You could barely taste the subtle flavor combination of garlic, onion, and broccoli that are so signature in cream of broccoli soup. This recipe is great if you love flavor packed foods, but I cook to avoid foods like this, so I was pretty disappointed overall. A tasty soup for those who can't taste. Don't make this soup unless you want cream of broccoli with a flare.
WOW!  That's all I have to say!

If my kids ask for seconds, I give a recipe 5 stars. They asked for seconds! Great use of veggies! I especially liked that it didn't have Velveeta cheese in it (unlike so many other broccoli soup recipes), just standard veggies and pantry items and easy to make. Oh, I didn't use soup base, just homemade chicken stock. I added salt to taste after the soy sauce. I used raw (whole) milk instead of half-and-half and I doubled the onions because I had a lot on hand.

We enjoyed this very, very much with our dinner tonight. It is simple to make and tastes great. It really has all the flavours we enjoy. It's been very hot here, so I let it cool to just above room temperature and ate it as a salad. I will be making this again often thank you KB.

Oh-h-h so good. I served it with grilled tuna and marinated cucumbers and tomato salad. I used baby red potatoes, kalamata olives and oregano, I am not real fond of rosemary. We about licked the dish! Thanks, Carole in Orlando

Thank you so much Kittencal for sharing this excellant recipe. We had it for dinner tonight and loved it. My family won't eat black olives so we substitued with jumbo stuffed green olives. It was very very tasty, we will be enjoying this dish often.

What a simple, but lovely side dish.  I used baby Yukon Gold potatoes, fresh rosemary, and roasted garlic.  I prepared the dish in a cast iron pan on my grill.  It was easy to prepare while grilling some chicken and had a wonderful flavor.  We will make this side again.

Great flavor, crisp outside and soft inside.  I was not clear wether to include the chicken stock when I baked the potatoes so I did them dry and they were perfect.  If the stock had been with them they would have been softer outsode which some may prefer.  Thanks for a super recipe

Holy YUMMAGE! What a pleasant surprise these were! I mean, it looked good when I first laid eyes on it, but then I saw your name by it, Kitten, and knew I had to try it. So happy I did. Both my husband and I loved the tangy addition of (chopped) kalamata olives, which, because I had to cook my yukon gold potatoes a tiny bit longer, took on a lovely crispness. They were so good, we were almost reduced to fisticuffs! (Not really, but I wanted to use the word "fisticuffs". *lol!*) In any event, we were most certainly protective of our kalamatas! These were really tasty and perfectly suited to my husband's lower cholesterol requirements. BAH, I say, to the calories!  Thanks, Kitten, for potatoes that pegged the "Yum-Meter"! (Yum-O-Meter?) ;)

I used russet potatoes, which tend to be large, so I cut them at least into quarters.  They marinated in the bag most of the day.  When I put them in the casserole dish, I DID cover the bottom with the marinade.  I timed them for 45 minutes, and they were still hard.  Added 10 minutes 2 times, most were done, and the casserole was dry.  They tasted good -- but I have done another recipe which was better.  It would be helpful to note size of potato pieces, and whether or not to bake with marinade.  I have leftovers which I will nuke with some of the marinade.  Thanks for posting, Kitten

We just came back from the trip to Greece and Islands and I was craving some Greek food. Unfortunately this recipe did not deliver. I followed directions exactly. Baked potatoes in the marinade for 45 minutes ( I cut them on quarters) but they came out too acidic and lacked flavor. I think one needs to decrease amount of lemon juice and oil . On the good side they looked spectacular ,too bad I didn't think of taking a picture.
I made this, and everyone absolutely LOVED it! Will definitely make it again.

I made this last night for New Kids on the Block tag game 2010 and served it with Recipe#409790#409790. I did cut the recipe in half but this was delicious! My DH wondered when he saw me get this box of "WHAT"....he loved it and wants it again. I followed the recipe completely (I might have added a little more Parmesan cheese and garlic) but otherwise kept it the same and used homemade chicken stock. Thank you for a wonderful dish!

Really wonderful quinoa, loved all the fresh vegetables melded into the wonderful mix of grain. I ran out of quinoa - (for the full servings) so I added a bit of wild rice along side. It's so wonderful, you will have to eat the first bowl all by yourself, and then squeak in for a second helping! Very easy to put together, and the topping of the parmesan cheese is a perfect addition. Made for *Photo Swap* Photo Forum January 2010

Another wonderful quinoa dish! I added sauteed prawns to finish and it  was a big hit at dinner.  I used all red pepper that I had skinned...because the skin doesn't agree with me.  Thank you for sharing.  Will definately be making again.
This is so delicious it took me to my happy dinner place! Loved it! Thanks, Bayhill, for a great recipe!

A new favorite dish for me! This quinoa pilaf reminded me  of a pilaf I made with brown rice, enjoy that hint of nuttiness. I used vegetable broth and dried parsley since that was all I had on hand. Perfect for lunch or a light supper! Made and reviewed for the Australian/NewZealand Forums Recipe Swap #73.

This dish is really full of flavor and has the added plus of tons and tons of veggies throughout.  I used red quinoa and just eyeballed the veggies.  It was served at room temperature with Recipe #169824 for a delicious Bayhill meal.  Made for PAC Spring 2013.
The absolute best quinoa recipe ever. Period.

Because I hate to over-salt a dish, I only added what the recipe said. It was a little on the bland side, so I doctored it up with a little more salt and some extra garlic. Anyway, it turned out just fine - loved all the veggies. And quinoa is the cutest grain with those little circles!!

Will be trying this recipe tomorrow. Realy sounds great. I will use CHANGS protein enriched Egg Noodles with it as weight watchers recomend it. I think its only a product of australia though. Love crock pot meals. Can be left to cook while working. thanks from Jackie:

We were starving...this was delicious over noodles.  Trying to limit white rich sauces, this seemed rich and a treat...did use almost 2 lbs. of chicken but added nothing else....Wonderful to top of the meal with fresh fruit.....Nancy

WOW!!!!!!! This was easy and delicios. I did quite a few modifications. I used regular sour cream and mushroom soup. I didn't use the crockpot, I browned the chicken in butter on the stove top,(added) sauteed onions and mushroom in a seperate pan, mixed remaining ingredients then added soup mixture, onions and mushrooms to the chicken. Simmered 20 minutes and voila a quick easy delicious dinner!!!
Very good...husband said it was a little rich, I might dilute the soup next time.  My picky 5 year old looked at it and said yuck, when he ate it he said this is really good!
This recipe is ok, it's a little on the thick side. I had it with rice, it would probably taste better with noodles, though.
This was very tasty and it smelled wonderful while cooking.  A little too much liquid but everything I make in the crockpot is.  We enjoyed this!!

This was scrumptuous! I cooked a whole chicken cut up in this sauce (doubling the sauce.) We ate some of the pieces with the spinach salad #26701. The rest I deboned (no problem it fell off the bone!) and left the meat in the sauce. We will eat it later this week over potatoes or rice and with creamed peas. This recipe is a keeper.

Tried this dish last night.  It was great!  DH liked it too.  I used full-fat soup, never-frozen chicken, 8 oz. of regular sour cream, and added a drained can of sliced mushrooms.  Cooked it in the crockpot on high for 4 hours.  The chicken pretty much fell apart.  I served it over egg noodles.  I'll make it again and will probably add some sliced onions.  Very good and rich as is.

I fixed this tonight and we really liked it. Very easy and readily fixed with most of ingredients on hand. Since we are moving I'm trying to use up my kitchen staples, so used celery soup instead of mushroom; garlic & herb seasoning instead of the onion soup and added fresh, sliced, sauteed mushrooms toward the end of cooking time. It was great, will try it with the "right" ingredients again.
Tried your recipe today, plenty of flavour in a low calorie meal but looks weren't very appetising. My family prefers the beef stroganoff and I have 3 daughters.
Very yummy, and I loved being able to use frozen chicken!  The chicken just fell apart as I was serving - will fix again often!
Thanks for the recipe, it was easy and tasted great!  I'll be making it again and again!
Yummy!!! And easy, two of my favorite things! I used both fat-free soup and sour cream and it still was good. I do think I'll add onions next time. A great WW recipe.
This is great (and VERY easy).  Thanks for the WW points!  Both myself and DH loved it (and he's hard to please).
Great taste and one of the easiest recipes I've cooked.

This was a huge hit with my husband and even my sister and my son, who are very finicky eaters.  I used 3 chicken breasts and added a can of mushrooms in the last couple of hours and it was done in 5 hours.  It was so easy and delicious.  I will definitely do this one again.

I made this over the weekend and was very pleased with the taste.  It was so easy to do.  I had it all put together in minutes.  However, I just used regular mushroom soup and only 8 oz of sour cream and the sauce was just right.  I served it over rice and it made a delicious supper.  Thanks for the recipe.
This was excellent! I didn't have a package of onion soup mix so I used a can of french onion soup instead. We all really enjoyed this one, including my picky two year old.
My family, every last one of them loved this recipe.  I even tried adding chopped spinach to it for a few extra vitamins and they liked it even more.  Great with brown rice.

Made this recipe this evening and it was very, very good!  I cooked it on high for 4 hours and added 1 can drained sliced mushrooms.  Smelled so great while it was cooking and tasted that way too!!  I served it with NO YOLKS Kluski noodles and fresh green beans.  Will certainly prepare this again.  Thanks for sharing such a simple, low fat, tasty recipe.
This recipe was simply great!

Loved, loved, LOVED it!
Even with the low fat, it tasted like I was eating something I shouldn't.  Thanks for the WW points on this one.   The leftovers were even better!  This will be a regular at my house!
Outstanding Crockpot recipe!  Couldn't believe how well it worked with fat free sour cream and 98% fat free celery soup.  Thanks for such a great and easy recipe!!db
My family really enjoyed this recipe.After having the chicken for lunch he had the sauce over noodles for dinner. Will make this again. Thanks!

This was a wonderful, and quick recipe to pull together.  The taste was great.  I shared this with co workers before I even tried it, and two of us tried it this weekend, and both thought it was great.  For variations, next time I will add mushroom pieces, and fresh onion.  I like my sauce a little thinner so I will add just a little chicken broth.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

I'm sure you don't need another rave review, but you are getting one anyway. This was easy and extremely good, although I did change stuff a bit. I used golden mushroom soup (like someone else) which added a really pleasing visual apperance, I didn't have 16 oz of fat free sour cream so I used 8 oz regular and 8 oz yogurt. And, like another someone else, I threw in a can of mushrooms. This really is a very pleasant and tasty dish. And again, so very easy. Thanks for sharing it Sisty.
Nummy. Good comfort food, especially for winter.

Thanks for such a easy and great WW meal. My kids loved it.  I did not have Cream of Mushroom soup so I tried Cream of Chicken and it turned out great. Next time I will probably only add half of the onion soup, it was a little strong.  This recipe is a keeper!! Thanks again.

We loved this!  I had 5 minutes to put something in the crockpot before I had to leave. We came home to a Fabulous Meal. Now that's easy! I did use regular mushroom soup & sour cream, and in the last half hour of cooking I added sliced fresh mushrooms. DEFINITE KEEPER, 5 stars!!

It took me less than 5 minutes to throw everything into the crockpot and then went out to play all day. When I came back, a gourmet meal was ready, waiting for me. Taste too good to be a calories counting recipe. I used 3 chicken breasts, 1 can of reduced sodium cream of mushroom and 1 can of reduced sodium cream of chicken. The chicken was so tender and the texture of the sauce was just perfect over my wide noodles. A very satisfying meal with no guilt attached. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
I can only ditto most of the other comments.  The sauce was wonderful.  This was a big hit at a small dinner party I had.  Thank you for posting this.
I added bowtie pasta to this and it turned out wonderful. Good stuff for a lowfat dish!

This wasn't as great as I hoped it would be but it wasn't bad either.  My hubby liked it the night we had it but the next day he said he didn't care if we ever had it again.  I had it over Jasmine rice and I think noodles would have been better. I added a bunch of fresh sliced mushrooms that I had already sauted just at the end too.  Not bad, but not a keeper.
this is the first recipe on here i have tried.. and it was great.. my whole family loved it.. and it was easy too.. but dont tell them that.. thanks hevn

Yummy!! Followed recipe as close as possible with what was on hand.  Campbell's Healthy Choice Mushroom Soup, homemade onion soup mix all else same.  Served on no yolk noodles cooked in water with poultry seasoning and low sodium chicken bouillon(I was out of Fat free Chicken Broth). Made a double batch luckily-so we have dinner for next night!! A hit with the whole family!
My whole family, including my two teens, love this recipe.  I added a few cloves of crushed garlic.  It was truly delicous!

This was very tasty!! My whole family enjoyed it. Definitely a keeper! I sprinkled the chicken with granulated garlic and freshly ground pepper. I also used "regular" soup and sour cream. I don't like fat free anything. This would be great with broccoli or mushrooms, but it can also stand on its own. My kind of recipe! I made both wide noodles and brown rice and it was delish over both! Thank you Sisty Gin!

Have been trying different crockpot recipes  these past few weekends at camp because I like to fish and I like to eat as well.
I used regular cream of mushroom soup and 8 oz of reg sour cream and used Mushroom Onion Soup mix.  Also added 1/2 can of water at the beginning because it appeared it would be too thick.   The last 30 minutes of cooking I added another 1/2 can of water and 1/2 lb of wide egg noodles and let it all cook together.   It really was quite wonderful..
Thank you very much. Margie

This great recipe is nearly identical to my own.  (I use 1-2 buillon cubes instead of the onion soup mix, but tried it your way & loved it!)  Adding a package of fresh sliced mushrooms, a chopped onion, & a bit of chopped celery (all in the beginning, with the chicken) gives this meal a extra depth, and stretches it father too!  (More portions, and even less fat/calories per serving.)  I usually use only 8 oz. of FF sour cream, and mix it into the sauce while my pasta/rice is cooking.  This is fabulous for anyone who's just learning to cook with the crockpot -- fast, easy, and delicious!

I used Healthy Choice cream of chicken, ff sour cream, and an off brand onion soup packet (and 3 large frozen chicken breasts).  Forked the chicken apart after 7 hours.  Wonderful.  The boys and the husband had it over "no yolks", and myself over rice.      Quick, easy and tasty.  Would add a small green pepper, finely diced, fresh onion, and maybe some diced celery next time.  
Thank you!!

Absolutely yummy!  I threw the chicken breast cutlets in the crockpot and topped them with some chopped up onion I had in the fridge.  I mixed a can of 98% Fat Free cream of chicken soup with half fat free sour cream and half fat free yogurt, and then added a package of lemon and herb soup mix.  It cooked all day while the kids and I did our thing, and then was wonderful and hot over rice for dinner.  It cooked almost 12 hours and was still wonderful!

Incredibly easy and it passed my picky boyfriend's tests. I only had Lipton Beefy Onion and it was fine, and I added a drained can of mushrooms in the last thirty minutes. I'll make this again.
(6 weeks later - BF took a frozen portion out of town for work and his coworkers all asked what he was eating 'cuz it looked and smelled so good!  BF wanted to know what I did to the chicken since it simply falls apart.)  Thanks again for this winner!

This was a hit for dinner. My husband is a fire fighter and is accustom to eating scrumptious foods, so finding food that pleases his taste buds is often a challange.  I made some slight changes.  I used Cream of Chicken Soup in place of the Cream of Mushroom Soup, I added fresh sliced mushrooms, (along with the Lipton Onion Soup) fresh sliced onions and Worcestershire Sauce.  I served my portion and my daughters over Brown Rice and my husband had his over No Yok Noodles.  My husband said that this receipe is a keeper, therefore I plan on making this receipe again.

This was one of those to die for recipes.  "We loved it"!  I had used 3 very large boneless,
skinless, chicken breasts, but because there was so much sauce/gravy, you could use 4-5. For the canned soup, I used the regular cream of chicken vs the cream of mushroom instead.  I also used the regular kind of sour cream.  I added 1/2 of an (8 oz.)pkg. of sliced, fresh mushrooms, (but next time will use the entire pkg.) and I added thin slices of onion from 1 medium size onion.  The onions tastes so good in this recipe, they help in adding more flavor.  The next time I'm going to add some minced or chopped garlic.  I seasoned this recipe with lots of ground black pepper.  I had expected to cook this on high for 4 hrs., but hubby was home 1 hr. later, so it was cooked for 5 hrs. on a high setting.  I served roasted, garlic mashed potatoes with our chicken, instead of the rice or cooked noodles.  I don't understand why others said the sauce was too rich or thick, and needed to add more liquid to thin it out.  The sauce made a perfect gravy for us.  "This recipe was superb"!  Thank-you for a delicious new recipe Sisty Gin.
SOO easy and yummy!  I used "light" sour cream instead of "fat free". I served it with mashed potatoes to soak up that delicious gravy.  Wonderful as leftovers!

This recipe had it all!!! Convenience and incredible flavor all while being healthy!  This got RAVE reviews at our table and we thought it tasted like it was A LOT more work.  Thank you-what an easy week night meal!

this chicken was okay...not as good as i had expected. my husband said he doesn't want to have it again. i used regular cream of mushroom soup and reduced fat sour cream. the chicken was very tender and moist and the recipe was very easy.
This a very tasty meal. My DH really thought it had great flavor.  Very simple to make.  Will be making this many more times.  Thanks for posting such a wonderful recipe.

Thank you so much for this recipe!  It was fabulous and so easy.  I always loved a hamburger stroganoff my mom made, but we're cutting down on red meat, so this was perfect!  Even my VERY picky 5-year-old said "it makes my taste buds dance!"  I will make this regularly from now on.

I thought this recipe was the greatest! Love easy crockpot recipes, and when you can put the chicken in as frozen, that saves me so much time when I need to make dinner and I have a busy day ahead. I used reduced fat sour cream and low sodium and fat free mushroom soup and the taste was great.
Thanks Sisty!

Super Simple! This was easy and quite tasty. I cooked on high for abut 3.5 hours, it was too long. I recommend, if cooking on high, start checking on it at the 2 hour mark so as not to overcook. It should also be stirred a few times while cooking.
Very good!  Served with egg noodles and broccoli.  Hubby loved and the house sure smells great!

Very simple and easy to prepare.  My chicken dried out a little.  My husband said it was just ok and my kids really liked it.  Not sure I would make again as I need to try and please the group.  Thanks!
This recipe was super easy, but the flavor was nothing special.  It wasn't bad, but I probably won't make it again.
Simple and delicious!  I like it even better with cream of chicken soup.

Excellent easy and yummy crockpot recipe! I used Light sour cream since we don't care for the texture of fat free things, and it was great. I'll make this again, and when I do, I'll throw in a chopped onion. Thanks!

I needed something easy to throw into the crockpot as I had a busy day ahead and this was perfect. I used 1/2 sour cream and 1/2 yogurt and 2 small (220gram) tins of 'windsor farm' buttered mushrooms. I also added a small sliced onion. Really lovely to come home to. I served over rice. Thanks for posting!

This was an excellent dish that was very easy to make! I used light sour cream rather than fat free. Also used refrigerated rather than frozen chicken. Cooked in crock pot on high for 2 hours. Served over rice and my family and I loved it!

This was delicious and as easy as it gets!! I used the "fat" versions, as my family sniffs out fat free in a heartbeat. I added onions at the start, mushrooms (fresh, sliced) halfway through. I made a complete meal dish by adding steamed peas, and fusilli(sp?) pasta. SO good, comforting, filling. Thanks!! -Joanna
LOVED THIS ONE!! So easy to make and very tasty!!
This was fantastic and easy. The chicken just melted in my mouth. I did use an onion and my boyfriend sauteed mushrooms for himself. I did use regular sour cream.
This was good, an easy change to Beef stroganoff.  Thanks :)

Based on the reviews, I really expected to like this.  I did use the regular versions of sour cream and soup.  The consistency was nice and creamy and it was very easy to make, but it just didn't taste good.  DH said it had a "sweet" taste, but I thought it just tasted like warmed up french onion dip with chicken stirred in.

Excellent recipe and so easy!  DH loved it too which is always a plus!  I used regular cream of chicken soup and sour cream.  Didn't have dry onion soup mix (thought I had it!) but did have Golden Herb with lemon soup mix and used that.  DH absolutely raved about it.  Next time I will try the onion soup mix to see how different it tastes.  May even try putting lemon juice in it to still get the lemon flavor.  Thanks for sharing!
This was easy and delicious! Served over egg noodles with broccoli florets!  I used frozen chicken tenderloins and they were done in just 4 hours on low.  Thanks!!!

WOW!  The flavor was just what my taste buds were looking for from a childhood meal I remember.  I cut back on the chicken due to my on hand qty was short.  So, the cook time was cut down to about 4 hours.  *If cutting down on chicken cut your cook time in order to keep your sour cream from curdling. ~Thanks for a recipe I will make over and over again!

easy & delicious.  i was short on time, so i cooked chicken on the stove top, added ingredients and dumped into the crockpot for 2 hours so the flavors could come together & soup mix had a chance to rehydrate.  good with brown rice & a salad!

With all the rave reviews I had to try it. Wow.. was I REALLY disappointed. The chicken was awful as it sat in a mess of what is supposed to be a sauce? I added some chopped onion as another reviewer mentioned. I'm glad it worked for them but still didn't help me. This dish needs a BIG flavor boost of some kind. I expected more after all the "WOW", "GREAT", "TASTY", "OUTSTANDING", "EXCELLENT" reviews.
This turned out great.  It's easy to make and tastes very good.  I added fresh mushrooms to mine.  I'm considering broccoli the next time.

We loved it! Great flavor, my 13 year old niece was visiting and she made me email the recipe to her mom. It is so easy and if you are on Weight Watchers only 3 points per serving. I served it over whole wheat noodles to keep it low in points. Very yummy. Thanks so much for posting:)

Eh? We weren't the biggest fans of this. Granted, for the amount of time invested in it, it was a decent return. I think if I was out of options of what to make for dinner, I'd throw this in the crock pot and have it again. But it's not something I'd plan on. I found it be SUPER salty, so if you can find low sodium onion soup mix, I recommend it.

I might try it again with some changes. The onion soup mix completely over-powered the cream of mushroom soup in ours, so maybe try adding some fresh mushrooms or less onion soup mix.  Overall, I don't think it tasted much like a "stroganoff" at all. It tasted more like onion flavored chicken with onion flavored sauce.

We loved this recipe.  After finding a recipe to replace canned soups i use it for everything...so i used "Cream Soup Mix (Replacement for Cream of __Soups)
 Recipe #57287".  LOVED it my whole family had 3rds each including my picky 2.5 year old.  I served this over white rice and it was great.  my husband told me not to tell him that it only took about 10ish minutes to prepare because it tasted like it took much longer!  I did also add a little bit more chicken and a little more water when mixing the soup because there was worry about the salt flavor.  this is a great dish when the day goes crazy with 3 small children or anyday for that matter!!  THANKS!
made this the ther night, so easy! I did add some paprika because i thought it was just a little bland for our taste. served over egg noodles, yummy!!

This is an easy dish to prepare. My whole family (of 3) loved it!! I will be making this more.  I replaced the dry onion soup mix with one I found here, on Zaar. My FF sour cream was very runny (not sure why?). So half an hour before supper I add a mixture of corn starch and water to thicken it all up. I wanted to add mushrooms and onions but I knew if I did DS wouldn't eat it. I glad I didn't because he said he really like this one!! Thanks for posting this wonderful and easy meal!!

Good recipe!  I didn't have a whole container of sour cream, so I used the half that I did, plus a 1/3 cup or so of FF italian dressing, a small can of mushrooms and can of diced tomatoes.  I also used cream of mushroom instead of chicken because thats what was in my cupboard.  Toward the end, I added some leftover roasted root vegetables, which helped thicken the sauce perfectly.  I served over small shell pasta with some parmesan cheese. Very good ! I'll definately make again.
Great meal on a budget.

Excellent! I followed directions with one exception. I used regular sour cream instead of fat free. This was amazing! The chicken was fall apart tender, the sauce was nice and thick and full of flavor. I served this over egg noodles. This was so easy and so good. Will make this often! Thanks

We loved this. I shredded the chicken after it cooked and served it SOS style on toasted white bread. Would be wonderful over egg noodles, mashed potatoes or rice. I don't know how much chicken I used. I am sure more than 1 pound. I used 2 cans of mushroom soup but left everything else alone. Served with a can of peas this was a quick and yummy meal and inexpensive to boot. AND it was very filling so we had leftovers.  Thank you for posting this keeper.

This meal is amazing! I will be making this again! I doubled the recipe on the soups and sour cream and put cooked egg noodles in at the very end and served corn and green beans on the side.  My whole family loved this..we had it last week and they are already wanting it again..they did not have to twist my arm too hard! :O)  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe! If I could give it more that 5 stars I would!

I thought this recipe was just okay.  I added one onion and a can of mushrooms to the recipe as well.  I think it was lacking in flavor.  I added pepper and garlic powder after it was done to try to help a little.  I would not make it again.  My husband would not even eat his.  It was super easy to make and used just a few ingredients.
This was a big hit with my family, and so easy to make. I will be making this often

I loved this because 1) it was extreamly easy and 2) my kids seemed to really like it - even my picky son. I gave it four stars because it seems to be missing something but I am not sure what yet. I did add fresh mushrooms because that is one thing our whole family loves.

Everyone loved this!  I didn't read all the instructions first and had defrosted the chicken breasts.  I cut them into bite sized pieces and only cooked it 4 hours.  I also added some leftover sliced mushrooms.

We've made this a number of times now and always enjoyed it. The best thing about this recipe is the ease of preparation - throw in the frozen chicken and dump the rest on top (I'll admit I don't bother to mix the other ingredients before they go in the crock pot).  We also add a can of mushrooms to the mix and serve over white rice.

Probably the easiest thing I've ever made!  Good flavor, I added some chopped onion which I think was a nice addition.  The sauce was a little thin for my taste, but that may have been due to the fact that I didn't have a full lb of chicken.  I will probably make this again!
Wonderful!  I added a quarter of a yellow onion-diced and sliced mushrooms.  Added 1/2 can of water and used corn starch at the end to thicken a bit.  I will make this many more times!

I agree,This recipe is wonderful.
Don't try putting this together at 4:30am...I added a extra can of cream soup & almost for the sour cream :S,We got home about 4:30pm,I started the rice which didnt take long.
meh... i must have made this wrong because i don't agree with these 5 star reviews at all.  It was just OK for me
Tasty....but a bit too salty for me. It is easy, but I think I prefer the extra work from scratch. Thanks for the recipe though!

I used an envelope of Knorr's French Onion Soup mix because the store was out of regular onion soup. This added a little tang, but my husband gave it 5 stars! Thanks for such an easy and yummy recipe!
This was easy to make and tasty.  I used half the pkg of onion soup mix based on a reviewer saying it was salty. I served it over rice and my husband loved it.  Thanks for a great recipe.

Love the easy idea of chicken. I mixed soup, sour cream, and dry mix together. Set aside. Made sauteed mushrooms (16 oz) and threw in chicken near the end to season it. Added soup mixture to mushrooms and chicken. Delicious!! I'm not sure if I would like this as much if not for the sauteed mushrooms and onion soup mix. Key things!! Will totally add to regular menu
This is great! You can make this with so many different ingredients. I can just eat the juice a soup over rice yummm. I did add onion, garlic and mushrooms.

Followed recipe as given. I don't think there was enough sauce, I didn't have quite enough sour cream (got used night before on tacos) but it still wouldn't have been enough with the extra ounce or two. I think I'd add another can of soup next time. Consequently the chicken was a little bit dry. The onion soup was a bit over powering but all the bad things said I thought overall it wasn't a bad meal for how simple it is. Served over egg noodles.
The family really do not care for it.
Excellent!  I didn't use fat free sour cream, just the regular stuff.  I also put only half of the envelope of dry onion soup mix in and added some white wine.  It turned out great!

I gave this recipe 4 stars. My family really enjoyed this recipe! I loved the fact that it was a super easy to make recipe! I followed the recipe with a few exceptions. When I made this recipe I doubled the recipe. I used Campbells low sodium cream of mushroom soup for restricted diets (future hubby's suppost to watch salt intake). I used regular sour cream. I also used boneless, skinless chicken thighs. I followed the rest of the recipe as directed cooking the chicken for 7 hours. I served this over rice. My only complaints was there was way to much sauce, which got very thin and my chicken was still intake and had to be shredded. I don't think using using thighs was the problem but maybe. Overall I'll make this again for sure! Thanks for posting! Christine (internetnut)

Very good! I didnt follow the directions exactly, I didnt have frozen chicken so just used thawed, and when I put the chicken on the bottom I also added some red cooking wine! I added mushrooms as well.  Very good and very easy!
My husband and I thought this was an okay dish using ingredients I had on hand.  I was looking for crockpot meals for baseball nights but my kids didn't care for this.  Thanks, though.
The chicken was super tender and very tasty. I think it would be good to make meat loaf patties or meatballs and put it in this sauce.

WOW! Delicious! Even my anti-crockpot friend loved it :) I added 16 oz of fresh mushrooms at the beginning & used low fat soup & sour cream, not a fan of fat free. Had to thicken it w/a bit of corn starch, fresh mushrooms have so much moisture. Poured it over fettucine & mixed in fresh steamed peas, amazing! Looking forward to my leftovers for lunch. Thanks for the fabulous recipe Sisty!
Followup Comment - This freezes very well!
It was ok. Not to our family's taste. We will not be making it again.

We loved this, it is absolutely delicious!  I used fresh chicken and cooked it on high for 4 hours.  Then, I shredded the chicken and let it sit uncovered while finishing the sides, maybe 10-15 minutes.  It thickened right up and was served over plain baked potatoes.  Next time I might add some onions and pepper, but I would eat it again with out changing a thing.  Thanks for this keeper!

Okay, I am just not seeing what all the rave is about. I am a very experienced cook, and going into it, I had a feeling it would not be as good. I was right. I added fresh onion and mushrooms for extra flavor and texture, but the sour cream cooking all day produced a horrible, curdling flavor. I had to whisk the sauce to blend in the curdles, and added corn starch to take away the soupy consistency of the sauce. Needless to say, I will NOT make this one again.

This was good, but it didn't taste like stroganoff. If you aren't expecting stroganoff, then you'll probably like it. It as SUPER easy to make. I like that I almost always have the ingredients on hand.

Things I did differently: I took the inside pot of my crock pot out the night before and put it in the fridge with all the ingredients. This allowed the chicken to thaw in the pot overnight. I also added onions, garlic, and green peas. I also used light sour cream instead of fat free.

I ate it on white rice the first night. The second night, I ate it over a pile of romaine lettuce. The romaine lettuce gave it a GREAT crunch without the extra calories of noodles or rice. I didn't miss the rice at all (which is weird because I LOVE rice).

Overall: simple, easy to make, quick, and low calorie.

Made this exactly as directions called for and the reviews in our house were mixed. It smelled great while it was cooking. My husband loved it and I did not like it at all. The sour cream had a curdled texture and onion soup imparted an odd flavor after cooking for so long. But maybe it is just me!

Super quick and easy.  I used cream of chicken soup, since that's what I had on hand.  I meant to put in an onion, but forgot.  It was a very "white" meal served over rice.  Perhaps some peas and carrots would help with that.  Cooked on low about 3 hours and high for an hour and a half.

I'm giving this recipe 3 stars but by the time I finished it, it was probably up to 5 stars. As a basic starter this recipe is good.

I wasn't sure if the recipe meant to use condensed cream of mushroom soup? But that's what I used. It looked gluggy at the start but thinned out after a few hours in the slow cooker. I added a few shakes of thyme and mixed herbs. I also used fresh chicken thighs which I browned with a brown onion and chopped garlic cloves before putting it all in the pot.

I listened to other reviews and waited until I served to mix in the cream to avoid it curdling.
I also put in 3 sliced fresh mushrooms and frozen green beans an hour before I served it.

It lacked flavour so I put in a teaspoon of Vegetta and some black pepper.

By the time I finished with it, it was devine.
But it needs tweaking. Thanks for the great starting point!
This was very good,I totally enjoyed it.

Mmmmmm....so good.  I have a confession to make though.  I forgot to get these started in the crockpot, so I made this on the stovetop.  Didn't hurt the recipe at all, it was still very flavorful and delicious.  We served ontop of buttered and parsley noodles with some corn.  We really loved this.  Thank you for sharing this with us.  I will make this alot, using both the crockpot and the stovetop.
This dish is a must try! I used full fat products due to the dislike of fat free. The flavor was a bit rich so go light when serving. We served over egg noodles.

You cannot get any easier than this one. It was good. I served it over egg noodles. It was very easy to put together. I used bone in thighs, just let it cook longer which was good because I was gone longer than the 4-5 hours suggested cooking time. Thanks for posting Sisty!

Very quick and easy crockpot recipe! The chicken is a good surprise as I've only had stroganoff with beef. Prefer this recipe with rice instead of pasta. Overall, good recipe to have in your arsenal :)

I loved this recipe!  I was afraid it would taste way different than beef stroganoff (which I love) but it really didn't.  Using the cream of mushroom made it taste just how I like it, even though I was using chicken instead.  Oh and it seemed a little runny when it was done so I added cornstarch in cold water to thicken it up and it worked great.  Thanks for this easy recipe!

DD didn't care for this at all and opted to have plain buttered noodles instead. Everyone else felt it was ok. I had a few mushrooms left over from another recipe, so I added them to it.  I served this over tri-colored fettuccine.

Very tasty! Easy to make and my husband loved it. I used 24 oz (1 package) of thawed tenders, added a little milk to thin the sauce and seasonings! Served over rice! Delicious! <br/>We will absolutely be making this dinner. Comfort food!

Couldn't be easier.<br/><br/>When considering this recipe I noticed numerous reviews indicating that the dish was "too bland," despite a flavorful sauce.  I suspect that that has more to do with using lean chicken breast, which can taste a bit flavorless after slow cooking all day.  To fix this, simply marinade the chicken overnight in a marinade of you choosing (we use a salt/garlic marinade that blends in well with the recipe, but you could also use a lemon pepper brine or something similar).  That one simple step seems to make a world of difference.<br/><br/>The dish is tasty despite, i merely added the recommendation for the many reviewers seeking a more flavorful result.  Try serving this over homemade noodles for a truly spectacular dish.

This is another winner. I had to work overnight,so I set everything up the morning before. When I woke up from my nap and started getting ready for work. You could smell the dish all over the house. MY God! it smelled so good. As I was leaving the family was heading home. I love getting texts from the wife and kids,telling me how good it was.
Nice recipe BUT as a "stroganoff" it needs paprika... I suggest Hungarian paprika, such as Szeged. Add to taste, not too much though!

I did a few tweaks however. I only used 2-3 chicken breasts. I used Healthy Request Cream of Mushroom - has no MSG; a finely diced fresh small onion; 1 Tablespoon each garlic powder and Mrs. Dash Original Seasoning; 8 oz. full fat sour cream; and 2 -3 chicken breasts that I defrosted in the microwave first to guard against salmonella. I also sprayed my crock pot with a PAM type cooking spray first and seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper to taste. Came out great!! Served it over mashed potatoes. Yum!!

I've made this twice now - the first time I followed the recipe exactly and it was really very good. I read a few comments and followed the advise to add garlic powder and Mrs Dash - I would strongly advise against this particular tweak and just stick with the original, I felt like the garlic powder in particular was overpowering and ruined the dish. Super easy to make and great as leftovers!

Not good and not sure why. I’m giving up trying to slow cook frozen chicken. Second time I’ve tried and it just comes out too dry and gritty. But the bigger problem was the mushroom soup/onion mix/sour cream mix came out tasteless. I don’t know why. The only mod I made was adding chopped onions. Cooked for 7 hours on low. Just wasn’t very good. I was thinking about adding the sour cream later. Puzzled ?????
Excellent, super easy to make and a great way to start those hectic mornings. I baked the eggs in muffin tins and used full sized bagels. Delicious!

I made a few of these the other day and ate one and froze the rest. They tasted great fresh, but haven't tried any of the frozen ones yet. I did add a dash of salt to the buttered slice. Thanks Pamela!
These are AWESOME!!!!  I made mine some with bacon, some with Jimmy Dean Sausage Patties and some with both.  They are a hit at our house!  It's hard to just eat one at a time.

What a great, easy idea!! Making the egg in a mug is such a good idea. I didn't have any bacon, so to liven mine up I add 3 or 4 yummy cherry tomatoes from "Oven-Dried Tomatoes" #14681.  Wow! They added so much flavor.  I will use this bagel recipe many times during the rush to get the school this year. Thanks!

I loved the idea of cooking the egg in the mug!! So smart and the eggs dont fall apart when they thaw.  I made 20 of these with sausage, canadian bacon, cheese and eggs. Also made 10 with english muffins.  Thanks for another great recipe!!
Karen

These were great and so easy to make...cooking the eggs in the mug worked out super! I didn't freeze any, and I used American cheese, but these were a hit for breakfast! Thanks for the wonderful, yummy recipe! :)

What a fantastic idea, and a real time saver on a busy morning!
I made some of these with bacon, and some with mini Home-made Sausage Patties # 109125 and both were fantastic.
My 5 year old loves these and we usually eat these on School Mornings.
Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

Although I haven't tried one of these yet, my DH had one this morning and thought it was amazing! I love the method of cooking the egg - ingenius. :) I actually put these on homemade buns ("Fred's Favorite Rolls" on hillbilly housewife's website).  I put sausage on half, and Canadian bacon on the others.  I handed my DH a foiled sandwich in the morning, and he was able to warm it at work in the toaster oven.  Perfect! A great way to get him to eat breakfast (he usually skips it, sigh).
These were great.  We ended up having a few of them for dinner tonight with some french fries.  The only extra that I added was some smokey bbq sauce on the bagels.

You know, I did this again this weekend and this time, to save a bit of time, I pre-cooked my bacon, chopped it up and then added it to the eggs, which I broke into greased muffin tins. LOVED IT! My oldest son is always in a rush to get to school (he is 15) so these have been PERFECT for him. I took the suggestion of Swan Valley Tammi and made the eggs in the oven in muffin tins....PERFECT IDEA! This worked out so great. Thanks!

Dh is a college student (and I am a teacher), so we have to leave pretty early in the mornings.  He loves the bagel sandwiches at McDonalds, so I thought I would make him a batch of these. DH really likes these...he now actually eats breakfast everyday!  These were pretty easy to make...tried cooking the eggs in the muffin tin and for some reason it ruined my pan.  I will definitly be making these again but will try individually in mugs next time.

I can't ever eat first thing in the morning, but am always hungry by around 9:30.  Now, I grab one of these bagels and go!  It's really easy to heat them up and have something "real" for breakfast.

I make these all the time!  They are so good and so much cheaper than the pre-packaged store bought ones!   I use regular size bagels when I make them and here's another little trick. I made these for a bridal shower at work and they were a hit.  They are so simple to make.  Thanks for such a great recipe.  This one is a keeper!!!

These were great!  My kids love them.  I did toast the bagels first on my second batch because my oldest prefered them that way.  Thank for sharing!  I will be making them again!  Okay, I have been making these for over a year now and my family is still not sick of them.  I no longer toast or butter the bagels.  I spray a coffee mug with Pam, lightly scramble the egg and micro for 30 seconds, place the egg on the bagel,then cheese and bacon.  I make dozens of these at a time.

These were so easy to make. My son was in the kitchen while I was making them and asked me to add salsa to the egg mix before I baked them. He really likes them that way.
