And my chicken wasn't dry at all, it was very juicy!  I will certainly be making this again it was so darn yummy!
This was great!  Easy to make and everyone loved it.  Great the next day as well.  I left out the celery and used Italian seasoning instead of the thyme and oregano and it was still fantastic.

We have never had Jambalaya before, we were missing out! This was great, the only thing I changed was the sausage, I only could find polish...I think next time I will try harder to find andoille it would be better!  I also cut up the chicken just before baking. Thanks for broadening our horizons!
great recipe!!! I added jalapeno peppers and used kielbasa instead of andouille. The jambalaya was so good.
Wonderful - I used whole chicken pieces, bone-in (one chicken's worth) and followed the recipe otherwise, and it turned out beautifully.
Wonderful and super easy to make.  I did cut up the chicken and add it to the dish instead of leaving it on top other than that I followed the recipe exactly.  IT WAS SO GOOD!  Thank you!

This was good! I added chopped garlic in with the sauteeing veggies and did not add the extra salt (didn't think it needed it!). I sprinkled the chicken thighs with Cajun seasoning but next time I wouldn't use them at all- why get a pan dirty- and would just saute chicken breasts in with the veggies. I served this with Louisiana hot sauce and it was great!

Delicious, I am very pleased with the results. I omitted the cayenne and it was wonderful with the spice from the andouille and the chicken was very tender (marinated with creole spice before browning.) Amazing base recipe.

Pretty good. I think it's missing some flavor. I needed to add more liquid as well. I also would double the tomato. That would probably be enough extra liquid. My husband and I really like spicy stuff. It's a great recipe and very versatile. Thank you!
My husband and I love this recipe. Since he doesn't eat shrimp, I leave that out. It is still a wonderful recipe.
This recipe is fantastic.  I had a New Orleans themed dinner party and everyone just loved the jambalaya.  Thank you so much for sharing.  I will be making this again. Excellent flavor.

Delicious! The rice tasted awsome. I have made this three times in the last month! It is super simple also. Thanks for posting!
Absolutely amazing! I crave it ALL THE TIME now! My whole family loves it, even my super-picky 4 year old. Thanks!

I follow this recipe to a T with the exception of the Andouille. I use Evergood hot links and brown them off nicely before I add the onions.This for me deepens the flavor. I also add an aditional cup of stock to give it a moister outcome.Go with a 1/2 teaspoon of cayenne if you like spicy.Just excellent
Made this yesterday for DH. He just loved it said he could eat this once a week.  He ate it last night talked about eating it for breakfast and is going to eat it later .  Thanks for a great recipe.

Outstanding! This now one of our top three favorite recipes from this site. I made a few alterations, based upon excellent tips from other cooks here. For starters I used a one-pound bag of frozen shrimp and 4 chicken breasts. I also used a 12-oz package of Wellshire Farms Turkey Andouille Sausage from Whole Foods for its lower fat and sodium content. I used two sodium-free 14 oz. cans of diced tomatoes and a half a large can of crushed tomatoes. I used about 1-1/2 cups of low sodium chicken stock from Trader Joe's. And I tripled all the spices except for the salt, which I left out and replaced with Nu-Salt. My fiance said, "This is the best meal you've ever cooked." So yes, I'll be making this one again...Thanks a lot, Sue Lau!

I have made this a few times, with a couple of changes. I chop the chicken into bite sized pieces, as it's easier to eat, and I swap out the Andouille for Chorizo, as it's much easier to get. I also sometimes add some hot sauce to it when serving if I think it needs it. But I love this recipe!

I made this for Christmas Eve dinner for the family- wow! Although somewhat time consuming, it was a major hit! I used regular smoked sausage rather than andouille and added hamburger meat that I needed to use up.  This was my first time making jambalaya, but I am happy to say that it won't be my last--I'll definitely be making this again!
i added hot sauce and a several dashes of worcestershire sauce.  Otherwise, hubby loved it.
Delicious!

What a great dish! I did double the spices (except cayenne), and I cooked the chicken in cubes with the shrimp and mixed with the rice mixture instead of putting the chicken on top. It also took 15 more minutes than the recipe called for to completely cook the rice. My husband has requested that this become a regular in our meal rotation. Thank you!
Delicious and so easy to make.  Next time, I'd try making the rice separately.  I prefer fluffier rice.
Very good, we didn't have the chicken so I just made it without and it was wonderful. Will make again!
I used Louisiana hot links for the sausage - the spicy flavor from the sausage balances with the mild ingredients. Delicious and visually pleasing.

This was excellent! I followed other reviewer's advice and used frozen shrimp already peeled and deveined. And very satisfying to eat. This is a keeper...thanks for posting!
VERY GOOD!! Next time i will probably double up on the sausage and chicken, but thats just me. the spices are right on.

This was simply amazing!  I can't say enough how much we loved it!  Served it with some slighly sweet rolls similar to Hawaiian bread.  I skipped the chicken and just used andouille and shrimp since my chicken was still frozen but it was still really good.  Just the right level of spice and I probably did more than 1/4 tsp of cayenne.  We like things hot here in my house.  Thanks for sharing Sue Lau!!

This was very good, little hot for me, but I expected that, my husband loved it! I also used long grain brown rice, upped the shrimp to one lb, added another cup of stock. This works for a low carb meal!

I cut the recipe in half but still used the whole can of tomatoes. I used enough Minor's Chicken Base to make 1 cup of broth but only used 2 oz. of water since I was adding the whole can of tomatoes. Otherwise I followed the recipe and it was delicious. I'll make this again, maybe with some shrimp and andouille next time. Thanks for sharing.

Awesome recipe, tastes very close to restaurant quality.  The only issue I had was the rice was a bit over cooked by the time it was done.  Probably use a bit less liquid next time to try and remove some of the mushiness of the rice.  Still very tasty though.

My first Jambalaya and an instant favorite! Only one problem: I made enough for 8 people, but 5 hungry people finished all in one sitting! It was just that good.

Thanks Sue!

This is really a great recipe!!!  Loved and it freezes well.  The only thing I changed was instead of chicken thighs I used 2 cups of cooked chicken and left out the shrimp.  I also used turkey smoked sausage as we don't have andouille sausage in my rural area.
Yummy!  I didn't have any chicken broth, so I used water and it still turned out great!
5 stars, easy and delicious!  Everybody ate 2 plates, even my more picky 6 year old.  We will be making this again.
Excellent jumbalaya! I served this at a party and guests couldn't stop raving about it. I will use this recipe again. Thanks so much!

Mmmmm best I've made yet! As a former 'Nawlins gal, I can say this is good stuff. I did do one full green pepper though, as that would be truer to the trinity. Only things I changed with this recipe are that I left out the celery (didn't have it) and bumped up the spices a tad, as well as using brown rice. I'm used to another 10-15 minutes or so, but almost another hour was a serious issue for getting dinner on the table when I wanted it.  Still, flavor was good, ease was almost as easy as a slow cooker recipe, and a great meal for any kind of night!

Like a lot of others, I had to adjust the liquids the first time this came out of the oven, adding 2 more cans of tomatoes with juice and about a cup and a half of broth.  But the basic recipe is just exceptional!  Thanks so much for posting, Sue.

Fantastic!!!I followed the recipe exactly and we loved it--just the taste I was looking for. Thank you, Sue, for sharing this A#1 recipe.

Excellent and well received by family. I added some Old Bay seasoning; used leftover Thanksgiving turkey (cut into chunks, added after the oven cooking step) rather than chicken. Definitely worth making again.
A regular request at my house! A special ocassional recipe because of the cost of ingredients, but oh-so worth it! Making it for my son's college graduation party. He's psyched!
I left the cayenne out for my husband, but added it to my bowl. He said this is the best he's ever had, and I agree! Super easy for after work dinner if you have everything cut up the night before.

AH-MAH-ZING!!!!! Everyone enjoyed this and want me to make it again. THis is one that I will be making again and again! Thank you soooo much!

This is an awesome recipe.  A definate make again.  Personally we like a recipe that is packed with stuff. I also chopped the chicken to bite sized pieces and mixed with the rice mixture.

Great recipe, I put the full amount of cayenne in and it was slightly spicy but not overwhelming. Very easy to make, and my husband loved it! I used brown rice and had to cook it longer, so next time I'll use parboiled rice and it will probably be spot on for the time.
Tasty
Crazy good.  I made no changes because I like every ingredient.  Thanks for sharing, Sue.  This recipe is definitely a keeper!

Very tasty and pretty easy too.  Will be making this again.  It would be a great pot luck dish for a church dinner.
This was delicious!! I made a half recipe, and it turned out great :) I am going to have to make a full recipe for a family dinner one of these days.

I love this recipe!! 

Minor changes because we don't like spicy (just the hubby and he added hot sauce) I used smoked beef sausage and smoked paprika (no cayenne)

This was super easy to make and love that you can cook it all in one pot!

So simple, yet so delicious! The only thing I did differently than the recipe was not adding shrimp. I'm sure shrimp would have been delicious if fresh but all I can really get where I am is frozen. Highly recommend this recipe!

I have done this recipe exactly the way it was written. Tonight I omitted putting it in the casserole dish and just put my covered Dutch oven in the oven at the prescribed temp. Let's see how it works. ??

This was excellent.  I read the reviews of others and added bit more liquid (28oz of tomatoes) and used a full green and a full red pepper, but otherwise followed the instructions.  Easy to follow and very delicious!

EXCELLENT!! This recipe was to die for! It goes so well with yellow jasmine goya rice :) We had so much leftovers and ate it all for days. Yummy and delicious. This is one of my favorite dishes and really had a good taste. Super tasty !!! I sautéed my veggies and added a lil butter + fresh parsley !! Yum

Excellent recipe for one of my favorite dishes. Long live "Blind Betty" Caribbean hot sauce to make this Cajun favorite with a St. John Strong kick to it!

Tried this the other day and it was wonderful. I'm going to have to make it again this week. My Southern Kids thought it was so good they wanted to take the leftovers home with them. And there wasn't very much left over.

I LOVE THEM!!! I just made them exactly how you suggested and every one ate them up even the kids asked for more. I will be making again.

Delicious, light, lemony sauce.  A perfect weeknight dinner, goes together quickly.  I used frozen mixed veges in place of carrot and peas.

this is the best honey barbecue recipe ever!!!!
The whole family really enjoyed these--plenty of flavor, but no overwhelming heat for the kids. Easy to make, followed directions exactly. Will definitely make again--thank you for sharing!

AAAAAWWWWWEEEEESOOOOOMMMME!!! I made a big ol' family pack of wings, using this recipe. Let's just say these wings had no chance. Exactly what I was craving. Going to make it again tonight with chicken breast. Cooked on grill last time and again this time.  Double your chicken, it will go fast!!

I created an account just to talk about how awesome these wings are. My boyfriend and I have been looking for a great wings recipe and all the ones we've tried are pretty sub-par. This was the perfect soup to use up my 4lb butternut squash! DH tried it with nutmeg and I topped mine with sour cream and parmesan. WONDERFUL! CREAMY! DECADENT! Even our 1yo had a big bowl for dinner. Not very filling, so either eat a lot or have some crusty bread and a salad with it. Yum! I'm so glad I have leftovers.
This was the first butternut squash soup recipe I have made, the entire family LOVED it-including my picky husband!
Delicious and very easy to make. A perfect soup for a cold day.
This is a wonderful and easy soup to make.  My toddler loves it.  I freeze for easy dinners later.  I add red lentils to make it more of a meal and you can't tell they are in there.
made this for lunch, was REALLY good! YUM! My 18 month old devoured it! Served with greek yoghurt and croutons!
Made this soup a couple of times while i've been off work sick and it's so easy and tastes fantastic.  Hard to believe there is no cream in it, it is so creamy.  This website is fantastic.

Thank you for a great recipe.  I made this in my dearly beloved Vita-Mix, without any pre-cooking (the Vita-Mix does all the cooking).
Yes, I had to adapt it a little to the Vita-Mix, but it is still your recipe, and I couldn't have made it without you.  Very, very, nice.....
Thank you~
What a great soup!  I added a sprinkle of nutmeg and brown sugar and also 1/4 cream to give it more of a velvety texture. Really, really wonderful!

Wonderful fall recipe. My squash was larger than 1 1/2 lbs so I used a whole medium onion and thinned the soup with fat-free half & half. Served the soup with choice of toppings: Parmesan cheese, bacon pieces and fat-free sour cream. I'll just add my 'Thank-you' to those already posted!

Yum, yum, yum, yum, YUM! I've been looking for a way to make butternut squach b/c it's just so nutritious. I'm not thrilled about just baking up chunks of it and this soup looked good. It was SOO easy and DELISH! I left out the sage (personal preference) and parmesan and it's only 1 WW point per serving. I must admit, though, I had more than 1 serving. It's sooooooo good!

My first time making Butternut squash soup.  this recipe is very easy and versatile.  I love that it is low in fat too.  I highly recommend this recipe for the fall and holiday season.  I added some sour cream and hot sauce as a topping.  the spiciness is great against the sweet squash and the sour cream adds just enough creaminess.  If you use a blender make sure to vent the lid so the pressure is let out.  I used my blender and the soup came out very smooth. :)

I must say that I was slightly sceptical of this soup - it seemed too easy, and just doesn't have many ingredients!  But, I tried it because it had 5 stars after 75 reviews AND because I did have all the ingredients.  Per some of the other reviewers, I added 1/2 tsp of ginger, and the soup was delicious!  Am thinking of making this for a Thanksgiving starter.  Thank you for posting this recipe.
This is great!
Not a fan.
I have now made this soup twice, first following the recipe exactly then the second time adding a nutmeg and cinnamon.  Both ways were delicious will be making many more times

Delicious!  Like another reviewer, I added some ground ginger & nutmeg, plus about a tablespoon of cream.  I served it with salad and crusty bread, and my husband (who normally requires that meat be a part of every meal) actually loved it.

I'm on a detox and can't eat a lot of things right now. This is delicious! I don't feel deprived at all! I added a bit of cinnamon, a splash of almond milk and a drizzle of agave nectar to sweeten. Great recipe!

Very easy and simply delicious.  I took my cue from other reviewers and added a pinch of nutmeg and ginger.  The ginger, in particular, is a must.  I would keep all of the accompanying ingredients at a minimum, so as to not overpower the squash's taste.  Great recipe!

This is a wonderful, easy recipe.  I made it without the cheese.  Also, I pureed the squash completely smooth, and mixed in real maple syrup (to taste, I probably added 1/4 cup) and let the soup simmer another 20 minutes or so.  It added a really nice slight sweetness (don't add too much).

Silky & subtle, easy to prepare & quick to make.  I wouldn't hesitate in making this soup a starter for my fussiest company, or a quick cold day lunch.
The only change I made was not adding parmesan cheese, I garnished with a dollop of sour cream.
This will be going into my soup rotation.
Good soup, but I thought it a little bland. Had to jazz it up with more spices.
Love it!!! Read the reviews first and did and pinch of ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and about 2 Tblsp cream. Yummy Yummy. My 12 year old even loves it!

I had 2 cans of chicken broth and I added both (3.5c) not wanting to waste any- it was too much liquid. I think 2.5 c would have been better for a thicker consistency. I added nutmeg and cinnamon to mine as well- flavor was great!

Very nice soup.  I'm glad it wasn't too sweet.  I've had some butternut squash soup that was so sweet I couldn't eat it.  Found some nice prepared squash at Costco, used frozen chopped onions and frozen minced garlic  which made this fast and easy.  Thanks for sharing!
Very good.  I was a little worried when it was cooking, but thought it was okay when it was done.  BUT, I ate it for lunch the next two days and it was definitely better!

Fantastic!  This was super easy to make.  I peeled and cubed the squash ahead of time and put it in a baggie in the fridge.  Then it only took about 25 minutes to cook and puree.  I thought I had a spare carton of Swanson's chicken broth in the pantry but it turned out to vegetable broth!  So I ended up using 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth and 1 1/2 cups of vegetable broth.  The flavor was fabulous!  Even my picky husband liked it.  This is a wonderful, light and healthy treat.  I split the finished product into 4 bowls (rather than 6 servings) and calculated WW points to be 2 per serving which included the parmesan garnish!  Delicious, nutritious and easy to make.  Who could ask for anything more?

Holy WOW!  YUMMY YUMMY!! I made this soup for a family gathering and it was such a hit!  This soup is easy and very delicious.  The things I did a bit different were, I used 1 1/2 tbs of butter instead of 1 teaspoon of olive oil and vegetable broth instead of chicken broth.  I like to start soups like this with some yummy butter and we have a vegetarian in the family, so no chicken broth... :o)

Very yummy! This is the first soup recipe that has had the exactly perfect amount of salt. Instead of the parmesan garnish, I stir in a little half and half before serving. Also, the second time I made this I roasted the squash in the oven then scooped it right into the pot - it worked beautifully, and saved me the step of peeling and cubing (I made a triple batch, so it was definitely worth it)

Very easy to make and so simple with fantastic results.  It's got a mild flavor that is easy to spice up if you want.  First time making anything using butternut squash and was very happy with the results!

A hearty soup but not something I'll not make again.  I added seedless rye bread; helped bring out some of the flavor and was a welcome accompaniment.  Without that it needs too much else for this to be the recipe for success.  I agree with most posters this needs nutmeg and/or ginger.  Sounds like they took a yam/sweet potato soup and tried to change it up.

This was soooo easy and soo good.  I've avoided butternut squash because it's so dang hard to peel.  A friend told me to boil it first, and it worked!  This recipe was so easy, I had most of the ingredients on hand.  My son has made it as well, adding pureed carrots and cauliflower to it.  I tasted it with the parmesan cheese, but it's so good without it that I'd rather have it that way.

I was skeptical that such a soup could be ready in less than an hour, but it was great!! I'm used to soups needing to simmer for hours, and this soup is as creamy and flavorful like it took all day. I had an extra stalk or two of celery that I added to the mix. Turned out great, will make again.
so easy and yummy!  I love it!
This recipe was our family's first taste of butternut squash soup. It is amazing! Even our picky eater loved it!
So easy and delicious!  Very good on its own, but for a little extra kick I added some crumbled bacon & croutons to serve.  Perfect!

Very nice.  Made in about 30 min using frozen squash from the garden.  I followed directions as is, just adding still frozen squash to the broth mix, letting it simmer a good 20 min to soften.  I also added a pinch of dried giner like other reviewes.  Warm and comforting when coming down with a cold.  Don't skip on the cheese, a good grating of Romano cheese on top was the icing on the cake.  Served with toast points for dunking.  Absolutely will make again.
This soup was so simple to make and very tasty! I doubled it and froze half for later :) Sage and butternut squash is such a great combo, definitely do not omit the sage.

This soup was delicious!  It was quick after I peeled and cut up the squash, a process similar to peeling and cutting up a granite boulder.  Next time, I am going to bake the squash in the oven until it is partially cooked and then peel it and dice it to add to the broth.

Forgot to mention that I poked the whole squash with a few pricks and microwaved on high for 10 mins. until soft.  Cut it in half, scooped out seeds and added cooked squash to pot.  This saves lots of time peeling, etc.

This soup was very yummy!  I liIked it better than my hubby, but he only likes squash because we grew it so it's cheap!  :O)  I made it as posted except I microwaved the squash whole for 10 minutes, then peeled and cubed it.  Made it much easier!!  Also used veggie-chicken broth.  I forgot to try adding ginger, so will have to do that next time.  Thanks so much for sharing!!  :O)

I was skeptical about a thick, rich soup taking only 20 minutes to simmer but pleasantly surprised at the outcome.  I did nuke the squash in the microwave for 10 minutes first, as I don't have the patience to work with the tough butternut peels.  I also added a few dashes of ginger (as others here have recommended)  and some Lawry's pepper (my personal favorite - love a little extra pepper!).  Overall, this recipe was super easy and full of flavor.  I served with a few garlic/butter croutons and some shredded parmesan cheese.  It's a keeper!  :o)
Absolutely delicious! I added a pinch of curry powder to warm it up just a bit, and it took it over the edge to phenomenal. Now I am on the hunt for more butternut squash ....

I can't say enough how WONDERFUL this soup was!  I made it for a funeral reception today.  It was such a joy to hear such whispers as"did you try the soup" "I heard it was really good" "who made that soup"  "what was in that soup?"  EVERYONE who tried it LOVED it!  I gave the recipe out to 4 others and more still want copies!  I quadrupled the recipe and it worked out great!  I did have to make some changes b/c I didn't have chicken broth on hand, so I substituted it with a combination of beef broth, beef consume, and water to have enough liquid.  Then, at the end I added 1c cream per "recipe" (total 4c).  I must emphasize:  DO NOT OMIT THE SAGE!  That's the magic ingredient in my opinion!  It was utterly FANTASTIC!  This is definitely going into our winter repertoire!  Thanks so much!
Great base recipe.  I added a little five spice.  Thanks for posting.
Absolutely fantastic.

Not that this recipe needs another good review, but DH and I also thought this was a good soup--I forgot the parmesean (which probably would have made it great) and next time will remember!  I had to increase the salt (though I think my squash was larger than the recipe called for, so that would make sense).  I also added a dash of ginger, which added a nice warmth (as others have mentioned).  Such a creamy soup with no guilty cream!  Thank you for a keeper!
I could eat this soup everyday...seriously!  Wouldn't change a thing!
Very yummy.  Will definitely make again!
Sorry--I wasn't a fan.  It's kind of a lot of work dealing with the fresh butternut squash.  My husband did enjoy it though, and said that the Parmesan cheese made it.

My family and I LOVE this soup!!!  My husband, who is "anti-any kind of sqash" requests it regularly.  We buy a 2 pound container of peeled and cubed butternut squash at Costco for $5 and put the whole thing into the stockpot with 4 cups of chicken broth and TONS of dried sage from my mother's garden. After I use the stick blender, I always add a can of washed black beans.  It adds a little something and makes the soup stick to your ribs a bit more. ;-)  Quick, healthy and absolutely FABULOUS!!!!  Thanks for posting!!

Not great.  It was just so-so, rather bland and needed something more.  I added some oregano and a little more garlic and it helped, but I won't make it again as is.  I think if I had roasted the butternut first it would have been much better, because it needed some sort of depth of flavor which it was missing.

This was good, but I agree with some of the other posters that there is something missing as written. I used homemade chicken stock, roasted my butternut squash and used lots of fresh sage, but I couldn't quite put my finger on what was missing. I used another poster's advice to add some curry powder, and that made it much better!

great, easy soup!  I double it for freezing portions.  I find this recipe is a 5 star when a can of coconut milk is added (I use the lite version) and a teaspoon of nutmeg.  The flavor is enhanced if the squash is roasted too - I've used all kinds of squash with this recipe and it always comes out wonderfully.
I cut the recipe in half and and used frozen, diced squash.  I increased the garlic and added some rosemary.  Very quick and quite tasty.  Thanks for sharing!
YUM!!! I used extra onion & I was out of sage, so I threw in about two tea spoons of Mrs. Dash's Original. Turned out GREAT!

i wasn't nearly as happy with this as everyone else i'm afraid. my squash took about 45 min to cook and when i had blended it i found the soup watery and tasteless, even though i added an extra 2 cloves of garlic and subbed out half a cup of the water for the broth with white wine. i added 1/2 tsp dill, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, 1/3 tsp curry powder, 2 Tbs honey, another half a broth cube, lots of salt and pepper, 2 Tbs sour cream, a splash more wine, a bit more olive oil and almost a cup of powdered milk as well as topping with good grated parmesan. after all that it was fairly tasty but didn't taste like squash anymore. course it didn't start out tasting like squash either. i think if i make butternut squash soup again i'm going to start with roasting the whole thing for more flavor alongside plenty of garlic and adding some half and half to the base. and plenty more fresh sage and wine

This was very flavorful. I'm not sure what the other reviewers were complaining about. Based on their complaints, I did make a few minor adjustments. I subbed 1/2 cup of water for the broth (I used bullion   water for broth) with dry white wine. I also tossed in about 1/4 teaspoon each of thyme and rosemary with the sage. Next time, I will probably cut back on the salt a bit, as I found it a tad bit salty for my taste. My husband, on the other hand, thought the salt was just fine. Thanks for a solid recipe!

This was fantastic! I took the other reviewers' suggestions and microwaved the squash first to make it easier to deal with. Dinner was on the table in less than a 1/2 hour. I added a little fat free half and half and a dash of cayenne. Otherwise, made as directed. Very tasty!

Don't know if this add in was already mentioned, but had a wonderful butternut squash soup during a visit to PA recently that included some spicy Italian sausage. So we made this basic recipe but adding in a lot of the suggested spices and added a half pound of Italian sausage which we cooked and drained before adding. The PA soup also had some toasted walnuts added, but we left that out...was wonderful!
this was awesome! i too micro'd the squash first- then cut it up. as it is- flavors are very subtle. was a huge hit for TG dinner. Thanks!!

Very good and super easy. Used 2 lbs of diced, peeled organic butternut squash from Costco so this came together in no time. Fresh ground pepper makes a big difference in such a simple recipe. Added about a cup of chicken broth. Ate some right away and froze the rest in individual servings. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I made this recipe for a group of 5 girls over the weekend and everyone devoured it. I added one apple to the recipe for the slightest hint of sweet and a few table spoons of cream. I will definitely make again.

This was so easy to make but it didn't have a lot of flavor to it. This was the first time I have ever had squash soup and it wasn't all that bad but it's just something I would not make again for myself. I had frozen a lot of squash last summer and was glad to find a way to use it. I also added fresh shredded Parmesan cheese to my bowl. Made for 2012 Zaar Cookbook Tag.

Oh my goodness, is this soup delicious, and I love that it is healthy too.  It has a perfectly velvety smooth texture and gets a lot of flavor from the sauteed onion and garlic.  It's so easy to prepare!  Like other reviewers who didn't want to bother with peeling and chopping the squash, I chose to microwave mine (I pierced it all over using a knife, placed it on a plate, microwaved it for 5 minutes, turned it over and microwaved for another 5 minutes).  Thanks for sharing this recipe.  It's a keeper!

This did not work for me or my family - it was missing something.  Made as written and it tasted off so added some nutmeg and cream as suggested by other reviewers but still didn't help.  No one would eat it and it got thrown away.

This was absolutely delicious and quite easy to make!  My husband and I gobbled it up.  The prep time is not 10 minutes though... Peeling/chopping/de-seeding the butternut squash takes a while (at least it does for me), however; this simple recipe was totally worth it :-)  Can't wait to make this again!

I made this tonight as posted except I added 2 tsp grated fresh ginger and one large japanese pear (apple/pear) cubed. After I pureed all of the squash and pear I added a large dollop of sour cream because it looked a little watery. It was very good! And it was quick.

Good tasting soup...I roasted the squash, cut in half, put on foil on a tray after spraying with an aresol cooking oil spray, gives a rich product and makes peeling a breeze. This makes a thick soup and makes the possibility of adding at least 16 additional ounces of chicken broth a definite alternative without affecting the quality. Cheese toping prior to serving was an added bonus. Will make again.
Love this recipe! I add some red curry powder to give it  just a little more kick (personal taste).

Great recipe! It's a bit of a process, but the end result is worth it. I cut the squash in half, poked some holes in it and microwaved it ten minutes before peeling, etc. I also put it in the food processor prior to cooking it, and then again after the soup had cooled down. I put in a dash of cinnamon when I ate it, and it was delish! Thank you for this recipe!
Yumm!!! So simple!! Next time I'll go a little easier on the sage, but this was great and low calorie and Points!

I made this almost to the letter.  I used shallots instead of onions, I also added 1/2 t. of finely chopped fresh ginger and 1/4 cup of half and half. I pureed it to the point of no chunks. One of the best and easiest butternut soups ever.  This is a keeper.  Thanks.

This turned out so good! I did put the squash in the microwave 5 min each side before trying to peel or cut, made prep so much easier. I didn't have onions or sage so I used leeks and thyme. Turned out so delicious! Will definitely be making this again!
Used rosemary & added an apple cut up and seeded when I sautéed onion and garlic. Delicious. Freezes well too! Will try tip on microwaving briefly before peeling, really hope it makes peeling easier.

I have made this soup more than 10 times over the past 2 years. I can pick up big squash for 1.29 Each not per pound so this is old faithful when it comes to cooking. <br/><br/>Don't peel the squash, oven for about an hour cut in half length-wise or microwave(I don't poke the squash and have not had a problem YET) Wait for them to cool down before gleaning the meat. <br/>Add Cream or milk.<br/>Parmesan cheese take it or leave it.  <br/><br/>The recipe is better with chicken broth/stock so when my vegetarian sister-in-law not attending dinner I use it otherwise its good with vegetable stock.

This wasn't the recipe I was searching for today, but I tried and it and was pretty happy, although I made a few adjustments. Like one of the other reviewers, I thought it was a little watery and bland, so I added some canned pumpkin to thicken slightly, a few dashes of paprika and twice the amount of pepper called for, as well as 2 cups of heavy cream and some crumbled cooked bacon - my teenage daughter tried it before any additions when made exactly as the recipe stated, and said it needed "something" but was OK...then she tried it again after I made the additions and said it was delicious.<br/><br/>Also, I hate cooking with squash normally because it is such a pain to peel and cube, but I found at the local supermarket's fresh produce ready to use section a tub of peeled and cubed squash, so all I had to do was add it to the already cooking other ingredients. If I had to peel and cube it myself, I probably wouldn't bother.
In a word, Wonderful, thats all. YUM!

This was very good.  I used pre-prepped squash that I got from Walmart because I wasn't feeling well today.  It was a heavy soup that was filling and good for a sick day in our house.  I served it alongside Recipe #192896 for a well rounded meal.  Thank you erinBOberrin.

For calories & fat I would give it 5-stars but I just didn't care much for this. I even roasted the squash thinking it would add some extra flavor. I am glad that it has been a huge success for others though! Maybe I am just not a big fan of butternut squash?!

This was just as easy and delicious as the previous reviewers have said.  I had never heard of the microwaving the squash trick that was mentioned by other reviewers, but I tried it today and it works slick!  I microwaved a whole butternut squash for 5 minutes on one side and then 5 on the other on high.  It made it so much easier to peel and cube. The only thing I added was about a TB of butter.

Very nice recipe, and since squash is on sale a lot during this time of year, I took advantage.<br/>By the way the review by Good Cookie was very helpful in making this a quick go to fall or winter soup. so Kudo's to you both and Thank you!!
Family loved it!  I added some Cauliflower to it as well.

This was a hit!  Very easy...I followed suggestion to microwave the squash to soften for peeling and it worked great.  As I was making it, I found I didn't have any sage, so I substituted fresh tarragon.  It was delicious.  I will definitely make again.

You certainly don't need more 5-star reviews, but I need to be able to find this recipe again!  So delicious!  My butternut was closer to 1 lb. so I threw a chopped up zucchini in there with it.  Also, I subbed veggie broth for the chicken.  The soup turned out with a smoky-like flavor, almost like there was bacon in it!  I also stirred in a couple of spoonfuls of plain greek yogurt to help with the creaminess.  Thanks for a quick, healthy, delicious recipe!
Wonderfully easy and delicious!  I used  frozen butternut puree. So good!  Thanks for the recipe :)
Microwaved the squash. Added bone broth and added a delicious curry powder mix to sautéed onions and garlic in coconut oil. It was a huge family hit. Only problem is I wish I doubled the recipe.
Easy and delicious!

Very good. I did what some others recommended and added an apple, rosemary, and a dollop of sour cream mixed in. I bought a 20 oz container of butternut squash already cubed so this couldn't have been easier to prepare. Hubby liked it too.
This is a great recipe! I subbed 2 tbsp onion flakes for the fresh onion I needed. My husband and son loved it as much as I did!
I added more squash and puree , then added turmeric and ginger. Before serving 1 tbsp coconut cream delicious
I used a sharp white cheddar in place of parmesan and I prefer Acorn Squash - less sweet than butternut.
This was quick and tasty, but I found the tortillas a bit dry-maybe the brand I used was the problem. I would LOVE the filling in tacos with lettuce, cheese and sour dream on top. Yum.

We live in New Mexico and I can definitely say that these are restaurant quality chimichangas!  Everything turned out wonderful.  I added a roma tomato to the mixture as well as some garlic salt and pepper.   These are so good that we agreed to put them  on our weekly menu!

What a wonderful, healthy dish! Thumbs up, around the table. "Yummy little bundles," said my mother. "Chimichangas have to be fried," said my son before lunch, then "oh man, these are REALLY good!!!!" 
The only change I made was using olive oil instead of margarine to brush the shells in the oven. Came out crisp, just like fried!Thanks ever so much for giving me a new addition to my repetoire!
I can't describe how good these were. And so easy! I used a light brushing of olive oil instead of the butter, and it was great! We loved them... thanks!!!

I've never had chimichangas before so I can't compare to deep fried - but these were VERY GOOD!! To reduce the colesterol even further, I used low fat Cheddar & served with low fat sour cream on the side. Thanx Miss Annie!
I'm a beginning cook, but even I could make this without any trouble! It was absolutely delicious. Thank you!

These were very good. I used more chicken than called for, so my rolls were not too tight, and some of the filling oozed out into the baking dish, but it still tasted good. By the way, my children thought [4 and 10] thought the name was hilarious!

Oh Miss Annie, these were soooooo good!   The cumin and oregano really flavored the chicken and I loved your idea to add cheese to the filling mixture.  The outside was crispy and the inside was moist and juicy.  MMMMMMM!! We used sour cream and additional picante sauce as toppings.  MMMMM!!  We will be making these very often.  Thank you for posting!

Very good recipe.  We had this a couple days ago and had some left over.  It is very filling.  I mixed green chili sauce and cream of mushroom soup (had it left over from Taco Ritos)  this goes together very quickly and has great flavor.

Oh My Lord, these Chimies are first rate!  Really simple and quick to put together and bake ... We topped them with homemade green chili and extra cheese, with a dab of sour cream.  Served a scoop of refries and a scoop of spanish rice on the side! Extra-good, Mizz A! You've got yourself another 5* winner in this one! Laudee
what a winner!!! Made these with whole wheat tortillas and low fat cheese. Healthy and yumeeeee

Miss Annie these were just to die for! I made mine with salsa, and added just a little fresh chopped garlic in with the chicken mixture, and brushed them with melted butter instead of margarine, I don't use margarine in my house. they were just so yummy. I baked them in the morning, as it is very hot in the afternoon, so I have already gobbled down one, and am trying very hard not to eat another one LOL! I doubled the recipe for these, as DS and fiance will be over tonight, these will be gone in a flash...excellent recipe Miss Annie!, I will make these again and again! thanks so much for posting...Kittencal:)

Wonderful! I used Pace's Chunky Salsa, medium. Brushed top, bottom and sides with 3 tbls. melted butter.  Next time I will mix ingred. a day ahead. Marinade the flavors. However they were great as they were. Reheated nicely. We had them as a finger food. Thank you for posting. Peggy Martin at www.Awaken4u.com
Maybe I did something wrong, but this just wasn't that good.  My teenage boys didn't like it either.  I followed the directions exactly, used Pace picante sauce.

I was looking for something quick and easy to make with leftover chicken and this fit the bill.  Very good, and the kids really liked 'em too. I'll be making these again for sure.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

My hubby, 2 nephews (ages 13 and 15) and I loved these. I mixed up the filling in the morning and we all helped to roll them up for dinner that evening. Came out crispy and delicious. Served some guacamole, salsa rice & refried beans on the side. Doubled the recipe and they were all inhaled!  Great, easy recipe!
These where the best!!!  Will be making again and again!  So easy~  I made them and froze them then took them out as needed and baked them off for dinner.  Could not be better!

Awesome, Awesome, Awesome!!  This was the first time, in a long time, that everyone in my family LOVED dinner.  My husband wanted me to make sure to include this in my "usual" recipes so I wouldn't lose it or forget about it.  Both of my dd's ate until I thought that they might POP!  The only things that I did different is add some shredded monterey jack with the cheddar and basted with olive oil instead of butter.  Thanks for the great recipe that pleases the entire family.
Love these!! Almost as good as our favorite Mex Restaurant!
Absolutely delicious.  Like someone else that reviewed these, I brushed them with olive oil.  So delicious.  And really easy and quick.  Wonderful.

I used Tyson precooked diced chicken strips which made the prep time for this dish fast, fast, fast.  I also used the olive oil tip and they were pleasantly crunchy.  I did find the recipe stated it made 6, but listed 1/4 cup of the mixture on each tortilla??? I stuffed mine
 moderately full and got 5 servings.

My family really ejoyed these and I liked the fact that they aren't fried!  I used Canarygirl's Chicken Verde recipe for the chicken and followed your directions exactly.  It was delicious.  I topped them with sour cream and a little extra salsa along with Spanish rice.  I think guacamole and queso would be great as well.  Thanks Miss Annie!

Do you really need another 5 star review?! :D These were great! So easy to make...DH and I loved them. I only got 5 also, filling them pretty full, but that worked out fine. I really like the fact they are baked not fried! They turned out really cruncy and spicy! I used Pace hot picante sauce and served with sour cream and more picante sauce. We will definitely make again!

I must admit I was skeptical that the tortilla would act "fried" and not just blah and cardboard-like, but I was wrong. These were great! I used ground beef instead and prepared the beef as I would for tacos using a taco seasoning mix. Then I added all the other goodies and used the salsa as a dip. I can't wait to experiment with other fillings similar to the hot pockets frozen meals. Great for the lunchbox! Thanks for the idea!

These were awesome!  I poached chicken breasts in in water with chicken broth, garluic salt, onion powder, and some montreal chicken seasoning I found in the spice cupboard, and shredded the meat.  Added the roma tomato and used purple onion instead of green onion.  Brushed with Brummell and Brown spread, served with cheese, guac, sour cream and salsa, along with spanish rice and pinto beans.  Great meal, easy, just as good as (if not better than!) fried restaurant chimichangas.  Definitely will make again!  Thanks for the recipe!

These were really good. I loved the technique. I did think that there needed to be more spice to the chicken mixture. I used mild salsa and the spice amounts as listed. next time I will use more cumin, as I love that flavor, and some garlic powder, pepper, and chili powder, I think. Miss Annie these were "GREAT"!! Everyone loved them. I always have cooked chicken in the frig. Loved that I could bake them. Making them this weekend for the second time. Thanks!!

Thumbs up from my husband.:)I used a store bought roasted chicken. I also used extra chunky/mild salsa as I can't handle spicy foods very well. The recipe made 8 pieces for me.

This is a great OAMC recipe, and can be soooo versatile - I'm going to try brocolli and chicken, spinach artichoke, ham and mushroom.....the list goes on and on...

Absolutely fabulous. . .even with low fat cheese!!

excellent, in my oven only took 15 minutes.

Great recipe Annie. Quick and easy to prepare. Did not have any green onions so substituted with red onion, otherwise followed the recipe exactly. I will be making this often. Thanks Annie.

Wow! Great recipe, I added some red and green pepper along with some onion in mine...YUM!  My hubby and guest loved these.  I was especially delighted when the olive oil gave it that nice crisped texture. Thanks!

Wow!  These were great.  I wasn't sure what to expect, but was pleasantly surprised at how good these turned out for the low amount of effort involved. Like this needs another 5 star review! But here again it gets it. What a fantastic recipe...it has flavor, color, ease of preperation and did I say flavor? I did add some garlic and chopped cilantro the filling. I was amazed at how crispy they came out...this is a treat ALL the way around.

WARNING: "hot pocket" hot!  you'll want to taste more than the first bite.  this is definitely a keeper in my house.  i added  sauteed onions, green peppers, and chilis to the chicken and it turned out spectacular.  chimichangas are my favorite but i hate frying them so i never make them.  even with baking them, they are just as good.  thanks for the recipe!
Love these.

I have to tell you that, although I have never actually made this recipe, I took your idea and have used it over and over again, whenever I have leftover meat. Very tasty!  NOTE:  In order to make the tortillas pliable enough to roll, you must warm them up first. HINT: I used the spray butter that I had in the fridge to coat the tortillas after rolling them up -- worked just fine.  I think I might use some sour cream as a garnish next time (along with the previous suggestions).  I will definitely be making this again!

Oh my gosh, this was so good.  I knew my husband and son would love it but I am very picky and not sure if "I" would like it but I thought it was great.  My son and husband did love it and ate every single one, I am lucky I got to try the one I did.  Will make again, my son has already asked.  Thank you
Tried these and the whole family enjoyed them. Lots of flavor. Will definately do again.
Easy and very flavorful.  Came out nice and crispy, a keeper recipe.

My family was surprised that we were having Mexican food at home!  I bought cooked chicken breasts at the deli counter and shredded them for the filling - easy!  Next time I might add some cilantro and put a little sour cream on the side.  I served with refried beans and a salad.  Just like going out to eat.

Just Excellent! My 7 year old son said that it was so good he'd love to have one in his lunch box at school this year! Now THAT'S a compliment! My only changes were to use reduced fat Mexican cheese instead of cheddar, and instead of brushing with margarine, I sprayed the top with nonstick cooking spray...and I almost let them get TOO crunchy on the edges! I think we would like a little more salsa, and have them a little more wet. Truly delicious, healthy, easy meal that will absolutely be made again! Thanks so much!

These were very good.  Just what you would expect from the ingredients; I think you could play with the filling to make it just how you like.  The best part though is how by covering the rolled up tortilla with butter and baking it, it tastes and has a very similar texture to a true deep-fried chimichanga.
I made this recipe for dinner, and even my pickiest eaters loved it!  These really are the best chicken chimichangas ever.  I don't think it can even be improved upon!  Thanks, Miss Annie!

A great way to use up the leftover chicken I had in the fridge!  I love the fact that they are oven fried, but they still get nice and crispy... I sprayed my pan with some olive oil before placing the chimichangas in so they wouldn't stick and then sprayed the tops (instead of the margarine).   I served them up with lots of sour cream and salsa on the side...  Delicious and easy!  Thanks for sharing!!!
Perfecto

Loved the crispy tortilla.  I was generouse with the butter rubbed on it.  Wasn't totally satisfied with the inside mixture but it may have been the choice of picante sauce I used.  Served with rice and beans.  Nice way to use up chicken from the previous nites roasted chicken!

I am rating this on the cooking method alone - which was FANTASTIC.  I had left over chicken filling from enchiladas I made and so decided to use that filling with cheese to make chimichangas. My husband and I both just loved this!

These were awesome! A healthy meal for chimi's.I was in a time crunch, so I went to the store and bought rotissere chicken and just shredded the chicken. They were great as leftovers, heated up easy and tasted better than the night before! Thanks for an awesome recipe:) UPDATE: Made again using frozen chicken breast and cooked in the crock pot on low for about 3-4hrs w/ fresh squeezed lime juice. These are excellent. I've made these several time already and they turn out great. I usually double the recipe so that I can freeze some of them for a snack later on. Awesome!!!  My husband said that they looked and tasted like "restaurant quality" an that he'd order it every time!  When I went to roll the chimichangas up, they ended up looking more like square pouches, but still looked nice.  I had just made fresh salsa, so we used that to garnish the top, and it was excellent!!  Thanks so much for the fabulous recipe!!

I did love the way these are baked and I will use that part of the recipe again.  But I didnt like the oregano flavor in the chicken mixture.  It just doesnt taste like a chimichanga to me and I was born and raised in Texas...so I have had quite a few of them!!  
So I will use this technique again but add my own 'chicken mixture' next time.
These were very good and so easy to make.  I added fresh garlic when cooking the chicken in a skillet.  I will make these again!

I have a recipe at home much like this but I serve Chipotle Sour Cream and Jalapeno jelly on the side.  If I would have had the prepared sauces to go with these, I would have enjoyed them even more.  I like that you don't deep fry them, and they are crispy
Really, really good! The cumin needed to be cut back a bit but overall excellent.
Quick, good and pretty good for you. Filling could be good for enchiladas as well.
These were great!  Definitely something I would make again!
This was so good! My son and husband loved it. Only change I made was to use olive oil instead of margarine. I am glad to have found this recipe. Thanks again for posting.

I made it exactly as written and served it with sour cream, guacamole, salsa, chopped green onions and grated cheddar cheese on the side. Everyone thought it was very tasty. I served Restaurant Style Mexican Rice (#223518) with it. Great dinner!

Super easy and really flexible.  I used morningstar chicken strips in 1/3 and cooked chicken in 2/3.  The filling is easy to mix up  ahead,and when we were ready to eat, I just popped them in the oven.  This will be a recipe I make frequently!

WOW! I used left over London Broil taco mest (in a crock pot with taco seasoning YUM!) This was delicious and OH so easy! Oh my, these were incredible!  I want to try them with a sweet pork filling.  So tasty.  It felt so good not to be eating a grease-fried chimi.  However, you must serve them with sour cream as well. This is such an easy recipe, and I absolutely loved the results.  I used diced white onion in place of the green because I had none, and left out the oregano because I don't care for it. This was very easy to put together and the flavors combination was really good.  The only change I made was to use chili powder instead of the cumin. Oh yes! A new favorite! SO fast to make, leftovers are delicious heated up, and my husband, who never gets fired up about food, kept saying "Wow, really good!" "Yah, I like them" "You can make these any time".

Excellent.  We used ground beef instead of chicken (was all I had on hand) and I changed things slightly per our taste. Excellent and easy to make,even my picky eater liked it

Fantastic!  I used enchilada sauce instead of the picante, trying to match my favorite comfort food from a local Mexican restaurant, and this was spot-on!  We will definitely be making this again and again!  Great use for left-over chicken!

-little bit bland, would have wanted more kick.  Tasty and healthy but not an exciting memorable dis.h.
Really good  ,my family requests these alot now.

Wonderful! This was so easy and so good. I used canned chicken to make it even faster. The kids ate every bite. We will be having this again. So easy why didn't I think of that?! LOL  Served with Recipe #17126 and refried beans.  MMMMM

These were pretty good.  I used salsa instead of the picante and they turned out very yummy.  I would think you could do all kinds of variations with this.  Very good recipe.

Delicious! I used monterrey jack cheese instead of cheddar for the filling, and I also added about a cup of mexican rice to the filling, just like our favorite local mexican restaurant. These were devoured by my family!
These were fast and easy.Flavor is great. We will definitely make them again!

Amazing!!!  I read the reviews and thought "there is no way these can taste that good."  Well, they do!  I followed the recipe except for brushing with margarine (I used butter).  These are delicious!!!

Yummmo! I used ground beef instead of chicken and there was none left! I will definitely make this again.

I can't believe I just got around to trying this one.  It's going to become a staple dinner...thanks for posting!

I had a 14.54 pound bird, unstuffed. I did put a few clementines, washed and halfed, in it. We let it thaw for 72 hours in the fridge.

We were aiming for turkey on the table at 2PM, so we put it in at 9AM, to allow for 30 minutes of resting, and 30 minutes of "oops, it isn't done, keep it in there an extra 30 minutes," and about 15 minutes to carve.

Checked it at 3 hours, 30 minutes and it was done - I think over done. I'm glad I checked it 15 minutes earlier than the USDA chart recommended!

It ended up pretty dry, but I think that's because we left it resting for well over an hour instead of 30 minutes. I'll time it better next year, and probably check it around 2.5 hours or 3 hours. I also intended to get a thermometer with a cord, but forgot. I definitely will get one before I cook another turkey since I can't see inside my roaster without lifting the lid.

Absolutely the best way to cook a turkey! I followed the recipe and the turkey turned out fantastic. It was the most juicy turkey we have ever had. I cut up an apple and oion and put that inside. I then put bacon strips over the breast. It was fantastic. I know I will do the turkey the same way next time. Thank you for posting this recipe.
Best instructions for using a roaster oven! Thank you- our bird turned out fantastic.

Oh Em Gee - I will not cook another turkey in the big oven - from now on it's going in the roaster oven! I've cooked many a turkey in my 59 years and I have to say, this one was awesome. The ONLY thing it lacked was more crispy brown skin, but there was enough, on the parts closest to the oven walls, to keep me happy. The meat was so moist and tender and yet pulled right away from the bones.

I followed the instructions pretty much as given, putting one halved onion and one halved lemon in the cavity. I used olive oil, garlic salt, a little crushed dried thyme, and some coarsely ground black pepper for seasoning. Started it at 450* (as high as my roaster goes) and set a timer for 30 minutes, then turned down to 325* and set the timer for 3 hours and 30 minutes, for my unstuffed 18 pound bird.

Well I did check it after 3 hours and that sucka was DONE! Checked it in several spots with my instant-read thermometer and it was cooked through, and the meat pulling away from the leg bones. Since it was only 4 pm, I turned off the roaster, sucked out some of the wealth of luscious juice so the turkey wasn't sitting in it (it had risen very slightly above the rack) and let it sit til we were ready to eat about 5:15. I made the best gravy with that juice from the pan too.

DH who LOVES his turkey asked me to please come in here and give highest praise to Squirrel Gone Wild on this one! THANK YOU!

Perfect!!  I was nervous as well about cooking it on high and not putting any liquid in the pan.  I had my parents over for dinner and used this recipe. I never opened the roaster, not even to peek, and after 4 hours it was done perfectly.  I will use this recipe every single time!

I have done 3 turkeys this way and will not do another turkey in the oven!! Flavorful, moist and tender and keeps the house cooler!!! thanks for the recipe... I have had the roaster for 10 years and bought them for my girls now too!

This is by far the best recipe for roasting a turkey.  Easy to follow, and the turkey comes out very flavorful and moist.  The steps are very detailed and there is no way you can mess this up.  I now know how my future turkeys will be made.

Thank you thank you thank you!  This worked wonderfully!  And tasted great!  I even lost track of time and overcooked it and it was fab. So I'm a total beginner with Turkeys and ruined our thanksgiving bird tonight. It was without a doubt the best turkey I have ever made (I've been making Thanksgiving dinner for at least 40 years now).  The skin was brown and crisp.  The stuffing was oozing out perfectly and the meat was tender and juicy. Squirrel Gone Wild...thanks ever so much for posting and taking the time to share you great recipe.  BTW, I borrowed the roaster from a friend who swore by it...I almost chicken out (no pun intended) but say what the heck....I bought a ham in case the turkey was a bust.  The ham was a bonus...but the turkey was the star (5 Stars!)

WARNING--WATCH TIMING. I was excited to find this recipe for my Nesco roaster. With a targeted eating time of noon, I followed the directions to the letter.  Put my 18 pound turkey in at 7:30 am at 450 degrees for 30 minutes and then reduced the temp to 350.  I was using a remote meat thermometer that goes off when the breast hit 160. My husband and I both had a "deer in the headlights" moment when at 9:00 am the thermometer started beeping.  Assuming the thermometer wasn't working properly, I used my instant read thermometer at various locations. Sure enough--the turkey was done at 9am. Gulp.  I was concerned that the leg and things weren't done enough so I cut them from the bird and returned to roaster pan for an additional hour at 300 degrees. I wrapped the rest do the bird in foil to keep warm.  It actually worked out well.  The meat stayed warm and was easy to slice and not dried out. Will definitely will use the Nesco again but will adjust the timing.
I followed this recipe as written, used olive oil and it came out fantastic, thank you for sharing!!!!  I will always roast my turkey in my roaster oven!
I've had several unsuccessful attempts at making a moist and delicious turkey until trying this recipe

Love this recipe.  So easy and less clean up.  From now on, this is how I am making my turkeys!  Thank you!

Fabulous, thorough instructions!  This is my third time trying a turkey in the roaster and the ONLY time it didn't turn out dry.  And it kept my oven free.  This will be my go-to method from now on.  Thank you SO MUCH for taking the time to post this!

If this recipe hadn't been so good I wouldn't have gone through all the BS I had to in order to sign up and review it. I have an Oster 24 lb capacity electric roaster. Best $30 I ever spent on a kitchen "gadget"!   I spatchcocked my 16 lb turkey and it came out amazing!  Spatchcocking is basically using poultry shears to cut the backbone out of the turkey.  Flip the turkey over, push down until you break the breastbone so it lays flat.  <br/><br/>I brined the turkey with mustard seed, coriander, bay leaves, pepper corns, fennel, onion, garlic, coarse salt, liquid smoke and wine and 28 cups of water for 24 hours in a 5 gallon bucket.  Then I injected it with creol butter and basted it with the same thing.  450 degrees for 90 minutes.  Let it rest 20.  Don't lift that lid!  Fastest way to cook a turkey and you get all the skin crispy.

WONDERFUL!  I've used the roaster oven before...well, I tried but I was being supervised by family and being told how everyone else would do it.  This year, we're spending Thanksgiving at my parent's with my brother's family as well so I am off turkey duty.  The problem, of course, is my husband and I could happily live off the leftovers for a year and we won't have any.  So I did what any good wife would do...I bought two turkeys, one for July and the other for today. so I can have the meat in the freezer ready to be thawed for sandwiches.  <br/>Anyway, I had a small turkey (10.45 lbs) and followed the directions here to a tee, save one step.  I preheated at 450.  I covered my turkey in both olive oil and margarine, seasoned salt, pepper and poultry seasoning.  I took the neck and giblets and through them in the crockpot to simmer with carrots, onions, and celery to make stock and cook the giblets for stuffing.  I screwed up a little and preheated the roaster with the pan still in it.  Put the turkey on the rack and lowered it into the hot oven, covered it and left it on 450 for 1/2 hour.  I dropped it to 325 at that time and set the timer for 3 hrs and 15 mins.  I do not have a meat thermometer and the turkey didn't come with a popper, so I was using faith alone.  At 3hrs and 10 mins, I opened the lid.  The skin had come back from the legs so I knew it was done.  I turned it off and covered it and let it sit for 1/2 hour.<br/>I have used cooking bags, brined or 24 hours and basted to where my fingers were sore and this is one o the most tender, moist turkeys with crispy skin I have ever had/made!!  I was so surprised the skin got crispy!  I loved using the oven bags, but talk about no crispy skin.  This was just awesome!  Thank you!! (BTW, I didn't put any liquid in at all and due to using the rack, nothing was stuck on.  Clean up was a breeze)

I purchased an Oster 18-24# Roaster Oven for this Thanksgiving as I am always having trouble preparing whole meals when cooking meat/poultry that need longer cooking times. It worked great and the turkey was really moist. Loved having the extra room in my oven and it was really easy to do. The way you said to cook it worked great. I sent a picture earlier of our golden brown turkey.

This Thanksgiving was the first time I've cooked in a turkey in a long, long time.  My wife has always cooked the turkey in our roaster and she assured me it was real easy.  She said look on the internet find you a recipe and go from there. While cutting out coupons I found a recipe for brine using soy sauce.  I put the 16 lb turkey in the brine for 16 hours.  I followed the directions here as suggested.  I preheated the roaster on the highest setting,  Greased the bird down with olive oil.  Filled up the bird with stuffing and placed it in the roaster on the highest setting for 30 minutes.  Turned it down to 325 degrees as suggested.  Put it on the timer for 4 hours.  I didn't take the cover off once to check it.  Now I was reluctant and worried that the turkey wasn't going to be done or not cooked right.  I mean this was the first time cooking a turkey in quite some time.  OK folks the bird was PERFECT! The meat fell right off the bone.  The breast meat was flavorful, tender and juicy.  I was totally impressed how easy this was, (just as my wife said),  I highly recommend using this recipe.  I'd also suggest brine before cooking the bird.  You can't go wrong with this one.

Followed the instructions for this to a T, and it came out awesome!  The meat was perfectly tender.  The skin was roasted beautifully, and the flavor was incredible.  I was so blessed to find this, and read the previous reviews to see that it really does come out well; AND yes, it totally frees up the oven for all of the other casserole dishes that need to be baking at the same time. Next year I'll probably check it after 2:45.  I can't thank you enough for this recipe!  Oh, and I cut an apple and orange and lightly stuffed it with that.

Worked perfectly! Last year was my first time using the electric roasting pan. The turkey was amazing, but didn't have that that wonderful crispy skin. This year we followed the recipe found here. Searing the turkey for 30 mins first really made the difference. The turkey was golden brown on the outside and delicious! For a 13 lb turkey the timing was exactly right at 3 hours.

Used this recipe to make 2, 20.5 pound turkeys for my husband's crew for Thanksgiving. I followed it to the T, except I did add some Tony's injectable butter to each one and sprinkled with some extra seasonings. They both turned out AMAZING and not a bite was left. Thank you for making a really crummy Thanksgiving for our guys who had to work, a little bit better by filling their bellies with delicious food!

At 70 years old I've been around the block too many times as regards cooking Thanksgiving dinners for large and small crowds. This turkey was juicy, and very tender, and was enjoyed by all very much !  Thank you for turning a very old lady around with this method..........

Shocked at how good this Turkey came out!  I had a 24lb turkey in a 22 Quart Electric Roaster.  The first time using the roaster it had a burning smell and I ignored it and it was fine.  My 24lb Turkey was done in 4.5 hours (using this exact method).  It was a huge hit and very moist.  I wouldn't change a thing.  Nothing like keeping it simple!  Thank you for sharing.

Like everyone before me I was nervous because I have always had problems when I tried to cook a turkey in my electric roaster.  I followed the original recipe with the only exception being I had no seasoned salt so I made my own, very similar to others who have posted.  My turkey was over 18 1/2 pounds so I cooked it 4.5 hours and the white meat was dry.  Otherwise the process and the turkey were easy and perfect. I'm really grateful for this recipe as it was my first time cooking with an electric roaster. The instructions worked perfectly and the turkey came out so juicy and delicious. One star is off for two main reasons. 1 - the cooking times are definitely off. Perhaps electric roasters are manufactured differently now and cook even faster. In any event, it is best to have a thermometer - preferably a remote probe one to be sure. My 14 pound turkey was finished after 2.5 hours - and actually probably could have been turned off a half hour earlier. 2 - the turkey did not brown very much, especially on the breast. Wings and legs were pretty dark on the outside. I didn't experience crispy skin like others said they did. So instead I wrap areas that were browned with foil and stuck the turkey in a 450 degree oven for 15 minutes. Came out brown and perfect! I used Emeril's BAM! seasoning and Rosemary. Delish!

My oven went out this year (still had the stovetop) and could put the broiler on quickly to keep things warm in there. So instead of getting a new element I bought a turkey roaster (rival) $24.00 what a deal!  I have never been a good turkey maker and was also concerned because I needed to make it Gluten, Dairy and yeast free.  I found this recipe and bought a 16-20 pound GF butterball.  I turned it up to 450 and while it heated up, I olive oiled it, salt & peppered it like crazy.  Stuffed it with onion, celery, carrots, honey-crisp apples, lemons and a few leaves of sage.   It didn't have popper timer on it and I didn't have any string to tie the wings either.  Oh well, in it goes and the searing sound it made when that floppy bird went in there scared me to death!  So I hurried and put a little water in the bottom and closed the lid.  Then I thought I was going to steam it to death!  Yes, I was nervous.  Then I smell burning turkey.  It says to NOT lift the lid, but I didn't have a choice!  I lifted it and realized that it was the wings hanging and touching the edge of the roaster that was burning the skin, so I tucked some foil down the sides and put the lid back on.  About 30 minutes later, I'm sorry, I just couldn't resist to look because I was still smelling a little burning, so I lifted the lid and checked and it looked fine, the legs and half the turkey was browning nicely, so  I turned it down to 325 set the lid and figured I 'll just leave it and hope for the best.  I thought perhaps because I lifted the lid twice I would have to add on a little time.  Its 11:00AM.  Out at 2:00PM  Rest time and dinner at 3:00.    30 min for the 450 temp and 2 1/2 at 325.  total 3 hrs.  At 2:00 I looked and well, breast bone was sticking out!  The breasts where splitting away from each other!  It was a nice brown, not burnt, I am sure I overcooked it.  I put a meat thermo in that bird all over the place and it registered way to high.  Definitely dry turkey.  I pulled the bone right out, took my hands and just grabbled those breasts and pulled them off.  Cut it into slices and pulled the legs and rest of bird apart and put on a plate. OMG!!!!!!  That bird was THE BEST turkey I have EVER made in my life.  I am almost 50, have made a lot of birds in my years.  It wasn't overcooked at all, was juicy, tender, browned.  Monday after Thanksgiving. I figure definitely last day for eating turkey, mad a soup with the little leftovers we had.  STILL was tender NOT dry at all.  OMG!  Everyone complimented me on dinner.  TRY THIS, you won't regret it.  I will NEVER do a turkey in an oven again.  NEVER.  Besides it leaves the whole oven for other stuff.  :):)

I first started cooking my turkey in a roaster oven about 8 years ago. In this time, I've only had 1 (ONE) time it was a little on the dry time. When cooking with an electric roaster the cooking times are vastly different from roasting in a pan in the oven. While most calculators and the instructions that come with turkeys say a 21 lb bird needs 4.5 hours to cook, 5 turkeys in the past 3 years and the roaster oven instructions confirm that 2.5 hours total (30 min at 500 and 2 hrs at 325) are more than adequate. Obviously use a thermometer, but after 2.5 hours my bird was at 79° Celsius, 5° over the target temperature but still juicy and with crispy skin. If you allow for the longer roasting time be prepared to let the turkey rest, carve it, cover it, and heat it at 325 in the oven 30 minutes prior to serving.

I posted some of the following as a comment to someone else's review but I figure most people will not see it there. . I cooked a 20# bird in my new electric roaster yesterday. I initially set it at 450*F for 30 minutes and then 325*F for the rest of the time. I figured on 4-5 hours total time. I decided to give it a quick check with my instant read thermometer after 3 hours. The breast was already at 201*F! I checked it in 5-6 spots. That thing was probably done in 2 1/2 hours or less. I saved the meal by FTC (foil, towel, cooler) for 2 1/2 more hours until time to carve. It turned out well and very moist and flavorful and all the guests commented on how well it tasted. Wow, these roasters sure cook things fast. . My guess on the fast cook time is perhaps the marinade I injected it with added some steam to speed things up. Also, I added a can of chicken broth to the bottom of the pan, which probably added even more steam. I did not remove the lid prior to checking the temp at 3 hours. . I did rinse the turkey off with cold water before injecting it and putting it in the roaster. This is the only site I read where it said to not do that. 4-5 other sources said to rinse and pat dry. After thawing in the fridge for 5 days, a lot of red juices ran out when I unwrapped it in the sink and I didn't want any of that residue to be left in or on the turkey. . Maybe next time I'll change the cooking temp to 275 instead of 325. I plan on checking the accuracy of the roaster temp with a wired thermometer before then. I opted not to use it during the cooking because I didn't want the wire to leave a gap between the lid and roaster and let heat and moisture escape.

I love this recipe.  It easily feeds my family of three, and there are always leftovers.  Here are some alterations I made to enhance the flavor and keep it moist inside. I also use a 20 oz can of enchilada sauce as opposed to tomatoe sauce and water.  I either add a can of diced chiles, or better yet, buy some pablano chiles, blister the skin over an open flame ( I do it on the stove top, turning frequently) until charred all over, peel chop, and add to the mix.  I also soak the green onion in lime juice before topping the pie with them. I found a jalapeno corn bread mix that works great to kick it up.  Lastly, I think the recipe is just as simple and the crust gets a little more crisp if you  pour it all in to a 9x13 baking dish, top it with the bread mix (which is easiest to apply using a large ladel) and bake it according to the corn bread instructions ( I think at 425 for about 20 min uncovered).  Then top it with the cheese and onion, turn off the oven, pop it back in for five minutes for the cheese to melt and your good to go.  I also suggest serving with a bit of sour cream.  I know that sounds like a lot of extra flavor with more steps involved, but it really makes the dish a smash, and your only left with one extra dirty pan.  Have fun!  Thanks for the recipe!
