I made these last night to surprise my boyfriend with at work because it was his first night working alone.  The recipe seemed really easy and I had all of the ingredients on hand and he had mentioned cinnamon rolls earlier that day, so I decided to give it a shot.<br/><br/>First the good news: these came out amazingly well!  Unlike other reviewers, neither of us found these too sweet at all.  It's a really great balance between the biscuit like bread and the sugary awesome filling.  Sprinkling the bottom of the pan with filling is genius, as it gives the rolls a slight crunch that contrasts well with their softness.  Personally, I loved it, but I can see why some people aren't fans of it.<br/><br/>I did hit a couple of speed bumps while making these, though.  The first was completely my fault, as I thought that I had more brown sugar than I did, so for the filling I ended up having to use about half dark brown sugar, a third light brown sugar, and the remaining bit white sugar.  I don't know if this had too much an effect on the taste, but I think it did have an effect on the consistency of the filling, as it was kind of clumpy and hard to spread on both the bottom of the pan and on the dough.  The next bump I ran into was that 3/4 cup of milk was not enough to form a dough.  There was still loose flour and it just wasn't coming together.  Instead of an egg, like some reviewers have mentioned,   I just kept adding milk a splash at a time until the dough formed.  I had to add about 3 or 4 splashes.<br/><br/>I was afraid at first because once the dough formed it was pretty sticky.  I covered my rolling area with wax paper and a ton of flour so that I wouldn't make a huge mess while trying to roll.  The wax paper may have been unnecessary, but I definitely think that you have to use a lot of flour while rolling these out.  Other than that, though, I didn't have any trouble and rolling was pretty painless.  I don't think I made my rectangle wide enough, because I was only able to get about 9 good sized rolls out if it.  When I make this again (and I definitely will!) I think I won't roll it out as long and make it wider so that I get more out of it.<br/><br/>It might be my oven, but I also had to bake these for a lot longer than the recipe calls for.  They were in the oven for about 35 minutes or so before they became the nice golden color that I was looking for.<br/><br/>The glaze as written is pretty thin.  I had to keep adding powdered sugar to it to get it thick enough.<br/><br/>All in all, though, the problems that I ran into were pretty minor and easily overcome.  I don't think that they are huge enough to dock this a star, because when it comes to a recipe taste is the biggest factor in my mind, and these taste really, really good!  My boyfriend and I were both really pleased and he was really happy when I surprised him at work like the magical cinnamon roll fairy.  I think this will definitely be entering into my cooking rotation.

This way, everyone got the amount of frosting they desired, and reheating the leftover rolls was easier without topping to melt during reheating. <br/><br/>Also, I found rolling the dough out on a silicone mat useful, and I could flex the mat to roll the dough up after filling.I also used a silicone cake pan to bake the rolls in- no need to use anything to keep the rolls from sticking to the pan.

My hubby is just trying pork chops again (never liked the way his mom fixed them growing up), but he just gobbled this down.  Thanks for a great recipe, I will definitely be making these again!
Came out great!

SOOOO YUMMY! These scones were very easy to make and came out perfectly-soft and fluffy on the inside and with a nice sugary crunch on the outside. I reduced the sugar in the batter to 1/8 cup and used the raisin option, which gave them a wonderful fruity sweetness. I ended up not needing the full 1/2 cup of cream, so Id advise anyone who is making these to add the liquid little by little in order not to get a too sticky dough. I got 10 wedges out of the full recipe. Thanks so much for sharing this lovely recipe, which I will surely be making often again!
Made and reviewed for one of my "babies" in Spring PAC 2009.
These will be great with jam in the morning.

I made this with 6 forequarter chops, and they were quite big. I followed the recipe exactly, except I used water and chicken stock powder, instead of broth. It turned out mush more tasty then I expected, (thought I would add some plum sauce, but it doesnt need it)
I also found I needed to cook it an extra hour, maybe because the chops were big.
I would make this again, but if I used the bought stock powder, I would cut out the salt, I would also pour the gravy mix over the top of the chops, as it did stick to the bottom of the pot a little.
Thanks for sharing Buttercup :)

These were absolutely to die for pork chops!  I served them with mashed potatoes and green beans.  The gravy was yummy!  My pickiest eater gobbled these up without any coaching from me!  Thanks for a great recipe it is one that I will make over and over again!

Guess I am going to have to disagree with the previous reviews to this recipe...at least to a point. I followed the recipe exactly and although the chops were quite tasty and tender (but then again, any chops done in the slow cooker are tender)...I found the "gravy" to be very goopy and globby. I did not serve the "gravy" at all. Personally, I would not make this again.

Wonderful, buttercup!  This recipe is a cinch to pop into the crockpot and is ready in only a couple hours!  I used 4 -1" boneless pork loin chops and served this with Bergy's Penne with Broccoli and Garlic recipe #11647.  We all enjoyed our meal so much!  Thank you, buttercup!!

We loved this, I cooked it on low for 6 hours and it was wonderful and I normally don't do crockpot cooking, but something about this sounded delicious and it was.
Served with Mysterygirls Mile Hig Biscuits that I HIGHLY recommend, mashed potatoes, and steamed broccoli... an excellent meal. Thank you!
These were so tender my DH said he's never eaten a pork chop without a knife before.  I added some onion soup mix and a dash more garlic and they were very tasty.  It's a keeper.

I liked the fact that this recipe makes its own gravy without the addition of canned soup - not that I have anything against canned soup, but so many recipes lately seem to call for it.  I made it per recipe instructions - did add one cloved fresh minced garlic instead of the garlic powder.  My DH really liked this one - will make again.

Wow! This was a great recipe! The pork was tender and  flavorful. The gravy was excellent!
I have made this twice...once with Chicken Broth and once with Beef Broth! Both are excellent!!
Served it with mashed potatoes, green beans, and cheese biscuits! My DH said to keep this recipe handy! He expects it more often! Thank you for a great main dish!

I followed the directions for this recipe exactly, and my husband and I agreed that we would both give this recipe a 3. It is not a bad recipe and I did like the homemade taste of the gravy, but thought that overall the dish was somewhat bland. But, we all know that personal taste varies and I would still recommend this recipe to others so that they could develop their own opinion. It is quite possible that I had too high expectations-kinda like when people talk up a movie before you've seen it and then you're somewhat disppointed when you finally see it....
These were yummy.  The chops were fork tender and the gravy just right!  I served them with roasted potatoes.....my DD liked them so much she had the leftovers for supper again the next night!

First let me tell you that my boyfriend and I are both light eaters...I made this with Yukon Gold mashed potatoes and steamed broccoli. I have NEVER seen my boyfriend go back for second helpings at a meal...but he did on this one! We both loved it. It was tasty, easy and the gravy wasn't heavy. I'm sure I will be making this one many times in the future.

I have made this several times for years when I saw it in a cook book. I had to change mine around a little bit to get the fullest flavor I could and I use the "cheap" bone in assorted chops (family-gotta economize!) I double my ingredients too! but yes this is one of my favorite recipes!
My husband loved this. I liked it, but I'm not a big pork chop lover, but it was very good. I'll make it again, this time with lots of mashed potatoes for the delicious gravy. Thanks!!!

This recipe was very good, I used deer meat instead of pork, and I omitted the dry mustard. I added 1/4 tsp. black pepper, and I used beef broth instead of chicken. Everything else I left the same. This was very tender and tasty, I also made mashed potatoes for the very tasty gravy. Very good!

I made this yesterday for dinner exactly as the recipe states. Although the pork chops turned out wonderfully tender and tasty (used butterfly boneless), the gravy was thick and gloopy as previously stated and was a teeny bit bland as also previously stated.  Hubby said gravy could have been a little bit more gravy-ish.  Anyway I'm keeping this one, will do again with some added seasonings and tweekings. Overall, a pretty good recipe though because this is the best slow cooked pork chop I've had to date.
I don't what else to say that hasn't been said, except this was an EXCELLENT dinner. The chops came out fork tender and the sauce let the flavor of the chops shine through!!!! Thanks for posting!!!

I made this for supper tonight and it was really good. So easy too. I used pork cutlets that were already breaded and seasoned. That made it even easier. The gravy tasted great. I served it with mashed potatoes. I will certainly make this again. Thanks.

Nice, easy recipe for a busy day!  The most tender pork I have ever eaten!  I actually used bone-in chops, which I would not recommend because the meat gets sooooo tender and falls off the bone, so then you have to be careful about stray bones.  I also did not brown the chops at the beginning, so I am not sure how that would have affected the outcome, but it certainly works fine if you have to skip that step!
Served with mashed potatoes and peas.  A truly easy, tasty meal with that Southern-home-cookin' flavor. Thanks!
Absolutely wonderful!  Had time to get it in crockpot when I got home early from work and have it for supper tonght!  We ALL loved it!
This was so good and easy to prepare. I used breaded pork cutlets. They turned out so tender and the gravy was delicious. I served it with mashed potatoes. I will make this again. Thanks

I really liked these.  They needed some extra salt and pepper and I didn't add enough broth but this was a keeper.  I didn't have broth so I used a couple of boullion cubs and 1 1/4 c water for a substitution - next time I'll add a bit more water and they will be even better!

These are fabulous!  I have made them several times and am finally getting around to reviewing them.  This recipe makes the most tender pork chops I've ever tasted and it's so easy to make.  Thanks for the great recipe.

I am going to add to your reviews.... These were so tender and had an incredible flavor! I could not find condensed Chicken broth... so I used regular chicken broth and a bit of condensed cream of chicken. They were FABULOUS! I served them with Apple Sauce (#70097), Macaroni and Cheese (#52799), Buttery Yeast Rolls (#40983)and broccoli. Everyone loved them! My friend that I invited over could not believe that I slaved away all day - she would not believe me that I just popped them in the slow cooker! Thank you!

Great stuff! After 2 hours baking in the oven in a covered cast iron skillet, these were tender and tasty, and went well with the pasta and broccoli I served on the side. Seeing that other reviewers thought this a tad bland, I added 1 T prepared mustard and about 1/2 tsp dried rosemary to the cooking liquid.  I had just under a pound of pork, and found that 1/4 c flour was sufficient. After the chops were done, I added a cup of water to the pan drippings to create a gravy that I then thickened with a bit of cornstarch. Delicous meal-- thanks for posting!

MMMMM. I' don't know if it's just that I'm pregnant, but this was such a great comfort food. But I know it's not just me because my family felt the same way. We loved it. The meat literally just fell of the bone. I used tongs to get it out of the crockpot and all that was in the tongs was the bone when I went to pick it up. The gravy was delicious!!! I did change it a bit last minute because there wasn't enough gravy to cover the chops in the crockpot, so I added a can of chicken gravy. That made it the perfect amount of gravy. Thank you so much because we just couldn't find a good porkchop recipe. This will be used over and over again!!
Very easy to prepare. Everyone loved these but next time I might try using a low sodium broth. Thanks for the recipe.
This is AMAZING! The taste of the chops was really good and they were very tender. Served with mashed potatoes and you have the perfect meal. Highly recommend!

I liked the consistancy of the gravy. The pork chops turned out really tender which was great. I just felt the taste was a bit bland. I make a similar dish using round steaks, maybe I am just used to the beef flavor vs. the pork flavor. Overall a good meal :)

This is a really great recipe. I know I've tried versions of this before but for some reason this turned out much much better for me than the other recipes I have tried. The gravy had wonderful flavor, I ended up thickening with a little milk and flour. To those who feel it is bland just make sure you add enough salt.  I always directly salt my meat a little and stab it with a fork several times (unless it already has phosphates or salt in it). My chops were super thick about 1 1/4 inch thick. I cooked on low in my crock for 3 hours then kept on warm for 2 hours , was the perfect timing for my crock.
absolutely awesome

Great recipe.
Thank you!
Margie

I know I give a lot of recipes 5 stars, but this one truly deserves it for ease and taste!  It took less than 30 minutes to put together and the aroma of it cooking away in my crockpot drove me into the kitchen all afternoon anticipating.  the flavor was wonderful, the gravy was a great texture.  I served it with rice, but mashed potatoes or noodles would be good too.  Thanks, Buttercup

These chops and gravy are wonderful.  The meat is very moist and the gravy is plentiful.  I cut the recipe in half and served this over mashed potatoes.  I had 1 leftover so I shredded it and served it over bread for a quick lunch. Next time I'll try this with chicken breast.  Thanks for sharing.
This was such a fantastic recipe and sooo easy. Thanks for posting such a wonderful recipe.

Wonderful! Comfort food at it's best! :) 
This is great because it's a snap to put together , the crockpot does all the work , and it was really nice to eat a good meal in the heat of summer!
Delicious and will most definitely be made again!!!! Thanks for posting!!

Excellent super, super easy recipe! I cooked mine in crockpot 3 hours and they were very tender and falling apart! Gravy was very tasty and delicious with bread! Thanks alot for a great recipe! I too will definetly make this again and again!
The pork came out tender but still had to use knife to cut it.  Only cooked it for 2 1/2 hours on high.  Didn't like the sauce at all. It was mushy and didn't have much flavor.

My three boys ate all of this and getting three sometimes picky boys to all like the same thing means I'll definatly be making this again.  Personally, I loved the gravy.  However, I couldn't give five stars becuase the meat was not as tender as I had hoped, even after cooking all day. I'll be making this again, but will experiment with different cuts of pork.
Sorry to say but I was not fond of these at all and neither was my hubby. The sauce had no flavor at all. This recipe didn't really meet my expectations.

This was a fast easy recipe to fix.
The pork chops were very tender. I cooked it all day(8 hrs) in the crockpot. My family liked it. Thanks for sharing. Will fix it again.
Just excellent - had no dry mustard so I used a little orange flavored mustard from a jar. Everyone fought over the leftovers !!! This is a keeper - thanks for posting !
Everyone loved it. I had 8 or 10 pork chops so I almost doubled the flour mixture. Had no condensed stock - I used one cream of chicken and maybe 3/4 cup of regular stock. everyone loved it!

No wonder this recipe has so many great reviews.  My husband made it and I must say these were the most tender pork chops I have every eaten.  The gravy was super.  Loved the taste of this dish and will be making often.  We did add fresh garlic and I plan on adding fresh mushrooms next time.  Thanks buttercup0009 for such a wonderful recipe.
I'm in love with this recipe!! My husband was sceptical and ended up loving this. I used 2 cans regular chicken broth and 1 can(emtied by the broth) water. I also threw in a chicken boulion cube.

Excellent!!! I wish I would have doubled the gravy.  We were scrapping the bottom of the bowl for the very last drop of gravy. Next time I will double everything except pork. I found condensed chicken broth with the Campbells soup.  I also added fresh sliced mushrooms and used fresh garlic instead of powder.  Yum.....

These pork chops were absolutely delicious!!!  Hubby said a 4 rating...I told him no, a 5!!  I have never had pork chops this tender!  I did not have any chicken broth so used about 1/2 cup of beef broth (lower sodium and fat)and then added about 3/4 cups white wine...the finished dish was perfect!  Melt in your mouth pork that was so easy to prepare...I cooked for about 3 hours on high because hubby was delayed at work.  Served with mashed potatoes and roasted Asparagus....Buttercup, you have a real keeper here!!
We all liked it. Thank you.

Wow! The flavor is outstanding! I've even made this twice for other families and, believe me, none came back.  I've started doubling the spices and chicken broth to make more of that delicious gravy.  Super simple. Delicious!

If you are looking for a southern down home comfort food, this is where the buck stops. This recipe was so simple to throw together yet was bursting with slaved-all day-over flavor. 

I followed recipe to a T, but it came out rather pale, not rich and brown like the photo, but it was still presentable. I wonder if using beef broth would give it that richer hue.

Anyway, it was fantastic and my husband and kids went on and on how good it was to try something new for a change. Only now it will go into the menu rotation, so it won't be new for long.

GREAT RECIPE. Thanks for posting it.

I have to say I was a little skeptical about how this recipe would turn out. I thought there is no way that the gravy would thicken and I was worried that the flour coating would cook well and stay soft.  Boy, I was proven wrong. This recipe went into my top 20 crock pot recipes.  The flavor was fabulous.  I read one review about putting in beef broth to make it darker but I felt the color was consistent to what pork chops and gravy would look like not cooked in a crock pot. I suggest maybe adding a gravy enhancer like Kitchen Boutique.

This was wonderful.  Everyone loved it(even my picky 10 yr old).  The only thing I would do is add more garlic, salt, and some pepper.  We added it at the table but I am sure it would be better cooked into it.  I only cooked it for about 2 1/2 hours and the pork chops were not falling apart but very tender(just how we like them-I don't like the texture of pork chops cooked to almost nothing).  Much cheaper and better than the mushroom soup one I usually make.
WOW!! What a wonderful recipe. I too doubled the gravy ingredients. I seared mine in olive oil, and then whisked the rest of the flour mix into the chicken broth.

This was really good. Not quite enough gravy - guess I should've doubled it. And there was a bit much of a twang to it all. But the pork was so tender and falling apart. Made a good comfort dish for a Sunday afternoon. Thanks!

These were some great chops.  Tried many crock pot recipes this weekend, this was one of the keepers for sure.  I wilted an onion in the pan after removing chops, added a tiny bit of water to get all the good brown stuff also, and put this in the crock pot also.  Was great and sooooo moist.  It was nice to find a recipe that didn't require cream of something soup for the crock pot, husband hates that type of stuff.  Thank you for sharing this great chop recipe!!!
Easy and delicious!  Definitely a keeper.

Very, very tender, but not a huge amount of flavor.  Plus it seemed odd to brown flour on them and then soak them in gravy?  All the stuff came off the chops and became part of the gravy...good but not absolutely superb.

Comfort food at its best.  We really liked this.  I served it with mashed potatoes and buttered peas.  I will be using this recipe again as it was so simple.  
THank you.......Stephanie
This was great. It even impressed my mother-in-law and she is now going to make it for company. Very easy and very good.
I thought it was very good, although for some reason my gravy lumped horribly even though I stired the tar out of it.
Superb!!! I used 1/2 cup cornflour and it came out delicious. Deffinately a keeper. Thank you for sharing.

This was very tasty! I doubled the gravy ingredients as many suggested and it was perfect. I added 4 quartered potatoes to the crockpot before adding the browned chops. They remained firm but cooked in the end without being mushy. I used 2 cans of regular chicken broth instead of 2 cans condensed with no problems.I did add some chicken broth to the pan I used to brown the chops to deglaze and added that to the crockpot for extra flavor. The chops and potaotes were fork tender in about 3 hours on the high setting.

The flavor of this was amazing but the sauce didn't turn out as I had imagined it would.  It was very thick at the bottom (like paste) and watery at the top.  In the end I took it all and put it in the blender and then it was perfect.  I also cooked the pork for 2 1/2 hours and had a few pieces a bit undercooked.  Overall this was a wonderful recipe.  I will adjust the cooking time next round and I'm sure it will be great.

So delicious! My kids loved it. I used dream of chicken and some chicken broth wisked together. I then wisked the liquid with the dry and my gravy was perfect! I also thinly sliced a small sweet onion which also helped enhance the flavor. I have a really old crockpot so I cooked mine on high for 5 hours and they fall apart good. Served with mashed potatoes and applesauce. Thanks buttercup!

I just made this recipe for the first time.  My 13 yr old son came in from school and said "WOW something smells goooood!" lol.  My husband looked at and kinda grimaced. After tasting it he said "I really thought I wasn't going to like this but it awesome!!"  For sure a keeper.  Thanks for such a great and easy recipe....real comfort food. :)
this is great and the taste is wounderful put in on top of rice thank you

GREAT recipe. Very easy, doesn't require an overnight marinade or ingrediants that probably aren't in most kitchens already.  I did need to salt a little more before serving and also added a little crushed red pepper to add a little zing.  The meat comes out so tender and the gravy is wonderful.

Very Good!  My DH and kids ate this up with no problem whatsoever...they loved the gravy!  I thought it was pretty good - not a company meal perhaps, but a great weeknight dinner!  Easy to pop in the crockpot between events and have a nice meal to come home to!

The first time I made this, my family and I were not too impressed.  Like some other reviewers, we felt the dish was a little too bland.  Adding a bit of sage really helped.  I almost didn't bother trying this again, but I needed a quick and easy crockpot dish the other day--one that wouldn't require all day to cook, and so I gave this one another shot.  I made it exactly as the recipe call for (just as I did the first time--before I ended up adding the sage, that is), but for some reason, the dish turned out much more flavorful the second time around.  Maybe the quality or particular cut of the pork chops is the reason?  I don't know.  At any rate, this came together quickly and easily when I needed a crockpot meal to be ready in 3 hours, and it was so much better the second time I tried it that I'm sure I'll make it again.

Oh my gosh!  Such a wonderful meal with so little ingredients...I had some shoulder blade pork chops that didn't look too appetizing so I used them here.  Upped the garlic powder to at least one tsp, left out the salt but chopped a small amount of fresh onion and added that to the pot before topping with the chops.  My DH couldn't stop mopping up the gravy with bread!  The pork was falling off the bone and moist as can be...Delicious and I will be sure to make this again.  Thank you!
This was great!  I cut the amounts down as there are only two of us.  Served this with mashed taters as suggested.  I had leftover sauce which I have used with pasta...yummy!  Thanks buttercup!

I too-do not care for pork chops, but this was really good and very tender!!  Next time I think I will add some basil to the sauce just for something different, but you do not need to change ANYTHING!!  Thank you for posting.

This really wasn't a hit at my home.  I followed the recipe exactly.  We found the pork chops were quite bland and the gravy tasted like flour paste.  I was really disappointed because it had received so many good reviews.

yum!  i don't like pork, as a general rule, but i liked this recipe!  i would recommend that you make sure you get those chops really browned in the skillet...i think i took mine out too soon. 
i'll definitely make this again, DH loved it.

My family really enjoyed this recipe. I made it exactly as written other then I used pam in my pan and not oil to cook the chops. This was really good and easy to make. It made a GREAT gravy. I made this with stuffing and everyone enjoyed the gravy over the stuffing. Will be making this again! Thanks buttercup.

Sorry, but we didn't like this at all.  Only change I made was to add just a little bit of prepared mustard since I had no dry.  I used sort of thin boneless chops and at 2.5 hrs. on high they weren't close to fork tender.  The gravy tasted like flour, very bland, and was gloppy from the fried flour coating coming off the chops while in the liquid.  Honestly, we threw it away without eating it.
Really like this one! I've made it several times in the last few months. Gravy is great with mashed potatoes and peas on the side! Easy and quick-- my favorites :)
Big hit with the family.  Its a keeper.  The pork chops were tender and juicy.  The gravy was great.  Served with mashed potatoes and steamed veggies.

These pork chops were delicious!  However, after reading the reviews, I did make some alterations.  Fist of all, I seasoned my chops before browning.  Secondly, I did not have condensed chicken broth, so I used cream of chicken soup and chicken broth.  I doubled the amounts and used a 26 ounce can of cream of chicken and 1 1/2 small cans of chicken broth.  It made a lot of gravy, but it was well worth it!! I also added a little Kitchen Bouquet to give it a nice brown color.  The chops were so tasty and so tender. I cooked them on high for 3 hours and warm for 1 additional hour.  My husband and I had gone to a basketball game and had not planned on eating them that night, but they smelled so good that I cooked up some mashed potatoes and we performed a taste test.  My husband performed 2 1/2 taste tests!! They were delicious!

OH WOW!! Amazing!  These were so delicious and didn't really take that long to cook!  I wasn't too sure how the dry mustard was going to taste, but they are Absolutely fantastic.  This is definitely going to be a regular recipe in my house!  It made so much gravy, next time I will make biscuits too.
Thanks for a five star recipe Buttercup :)

These were great, fall apart, full of flavor pork chops.  I only had a can of regular chicken broth, so I added a bit more flour and it came out great.  There was plenty of gravy for my side of mashed potatoes.  This recipe is a keeper.  Thanks!
This was okay, Fairly tender due to the thickness and moist low cooking method. Nothing terribly special about the recipe and was a bit bland though better than tough dry chops.

These were okay, the basic taste was good, but not something I'd make again. I rate them 3 stars because I didn't have boneless pork chops, ours had bones in them, so possibly the boneless chops make a difference.

These were GREAT and very easy.  I didn't realize and mine had bones but I did everything the same and after 2 1/2 hours on high I turned down to low for another hour, til hubby got home... the meat just fell off the bone!  We all enjoyed this..even my dog!  The roasted greens beans were also a hit and complimented this recipe..
Taste was very good and liked the change from the usual way I make crockpot pork chops. Thanks for sharing.

My s/o claimed that this was the asbolute best thing I have ever made (now, I don't know how reasonable that is.... he says that with every outstanding dish I make.). But both of us could not stop raving, and I couldn't stop being thankful of how EASY it was... I had been running all day and got home late, but was able to have the pork chops ready in 2.5 hours on High... I added chopped onions to the gravy mix when adding into the crockpot, I also mixed a little bit of cornstarch and water to thicken it a teensy bit more after removing the chops. Served with mashed potatoes. And the gravy was delicious! This is def. going to be made again. Thanks for a very simple and delicious recipe!
Played with the seasoning a bit but loved the cooking technique.
This was ok. Too bland.

Just GREAT! I added a bit of curry powder to the flour mixture and thew in some minced onion. Cooked not in the crock pot but on the stove in a dutch oven for six hours on low heat...served with rice, sauteed mushroom and veggies...very nice! Thanks for posting it.
This was AMAZING.  My family said "Best Pork Chop Recipe EVER".  Super super easy.  I really thought there would be any flavor with so few ingredients but we LOVED it!!
The pork was very moist, but lacked any kind of flavor.  Next time, I will take the meat strait from the crockpot to the bbq and brown it up with some bbq sauce.  Should come out excellent.

I made this recipe yesterday for my parents, daughter and sister.  I knew that my sister probably wouldn't eat it as she doesn't like anything on her chops...  Just stick them in the pan and brown them.  I was surprised when she said that she liked them.  In fact, the entire family loved them.  The turned out really tender and juicy, and the gravy was simply amazing!!!  Delicious flavor!
I knew that we weren't going to be eating for a while, so instead of putting the chops and gravy in the crock pot on high for 2.5-5 hrs, I put them in for 5 hrs on low and they turned out perfect.

These were great pork chops.  Very tender and the gravy was great over mashed potatoes.  I did mine on high for 3 hours or so and then turned it to low for 2 or so more.  They were fantastic!  I will probably be making these again.  SO EASY! Thanks for the recipe!
Followed the direction exactly!  Delicious and easy.  Will make over and over.  DH  loved  it!
This is a keeper.  Easy and tastes great.  Next time I might double gravy, just cause we prefer more!!  Served over rice.  Thanks
Wonderful! So easy.  I will have to share this with my Mom.  It will be great to put in the slow cooker before church and come home to a delic, hot meal!

Great gravy and flavorful, tender pork chops.  Just what I was looking for---a recipe without fruit or spicy seasonings.  I did not have a can of condensed broth, so I mixed one and a quarter teaspoons of low-sodium chicken broth granules with the seasoned flour after dredging the chops, then added 10 oz of boiling water to make the broth and gravy base.  Freezing the leftovers and will definitely make again.

DH and I just finished eating this! AWESOME!! I didn't have any condensed chicken broth, so I used two boulion cubes in approx 11 oz of hot water. I increased the garlic powder a little and also added a little dried onion soup mix (like 1/4 package). Came out great- very flavorful and gravy was the pefect consistency!
Easy and so delicious!  We had this tonight with mashed potatoes and a tossed salad.  The pork chops were fork tender and the gravy was perfect.  Definitely a keeper!

I used country pork instead of chops. I followed the rest of the recipe as posted. This had to be the absolute best gravy that I have ever eaten ! The pork was sooo tender and delicious. I served it on top of white rice. A+ for the recipe.

This was so good. I used boneless pork chops and browned them with just a couple teaspoons of oil. It was so good we didn't leave any leftovers. I just spent an hour looking for this recipe because I forgot to review it when I made it a few weeks ago. I want to try it with pork loin that is on sale right now. I think I could brown the pork loin and then cook it on low for a few hours like I did with the chops.

These were sooo tender and moist!  I prepped them exactly as the recipe stated, doubling the amount of gravy since my husband is a big gravy fan.  Everyone went back for seconds on this wonderful dish.
I thought this recipe was wonderful.  I am not a big meat eater and I had seconds.  My husband and kids loved it too.  I will be making this often.  The pork just feel apart. Yummy

Yum!  I used a small pork roast.  I did not like the chops that were for sale that day.  This is very easy to prepare.  I also added some potatoes to the gravy mixture.  The pork roast is very tender and the gravy has a nice mild flavor.  Thanks buttercup.   "As You Wish"

Yummy chops!  This is a great crockpot recipe.  They were easy to prepare and tasted so good.  I used 3 really thick chops and added one sliced onion under them.  I omitted the salt and used my own chicken broth.  I cooked them on low for 5-6 hours.  I will make these again.  The gravy was very good with mashed potatoes.  I could have eaten that with a spoon by itself!  Thanks for the recipe.

My BF absolutely loved this recipe.  I really liked it too, but I prefer a little more flavor.  The 2nd time I made it I added a little white wine and it gave it just the kick I was looking for.  Thanks for posting, will make again and again!

This was great! The family loved it.
The kids liked and everyone knows kids are picky. I will make this again.
Thanks for sharing
Wonderful!

WONDERFUL!!!  We loved this meal!  I substituted white wine for some of the chicken broth and added half of a can of sliced mushrooms.  We had them with mashed potatoes and green beans.  We were actually sad when it was gone!
These were very good and we are not big pork chop fans.   The meat was very tender.  I served it with rice and cabbage.  I will definitely make this one again.  Thanks!

My husband is usually a "nice" guy when it comes to me trying new recipes. But THIS time? He was more than nice--- he ate a few bites and was like, "YUM! Definitely make this one again!" (UPDATE:  I made this in my oven the other night and I liked it WAYYY more... followed all the same steps except cooked it in a foil-covered 9x13 dish in a 350 degree oven for 2.5 hours...  the breading stuck a lot better b/c they weren't all stacked on top of each other and the gravy only covered the bottom half of each chop.  YUM!  this is a keeper!)  (my photo is of the Oven version, FYI)

Wow! This turned out awesome!  I needed a dinner where it could be done in a few hours without me sitting there watching it and this fit the bill!  I did not have any condensed chicken broth, so I used regular chicken broth.  I also ended up using double the amount of flour, mustard, salt and garlic powder to cover all of my chops which I cut off the bone since I had bone-in center cut chops. I ran out of flour mixture right in the middle of breading!  I would recommend making sure all the chops are covered in the gravy while they cook as those chops were the most tender.  I also used a whole container of chicken broth, (you know the broth that comes in the resealable containers).  I mixed in about 3/4 cups of flour and about another tsp of mustard, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp pepper and about a tablespoon of chicken buillion granules for the gravy.  My chops took 3 hours on high in my oval Rival crock pot and they were very tender.  I made sure to whisk the gravy really well to incorporate the breading that came off and adjust the gravy thickness after the chops were done and out of the crock pot.  If you need the gravy thicker, one cup cold water or broth mixed with one tablespoon of flour and bring to a boil in a saucepan or pour in the crock pot on high and let cook for 15 minutes or so until it thickens.  Use more or less flour/water mixture to get the thickness you desire.  These were moist and tender and this extra broth made enough gravy for all the mashed potatoes I made to go with these.  Very flavorful.  Very easy!  Took me ten minutes to prepare and throw in the crock pot and that was it!  I would definitely recommend.  I would also make sure to use boneless pork chops also, because in my past experience, the bone breaks down in the gravy and you get crunch bits in your gravy, yuck!  You can always cut the chop off the bone like I did and that worked great!  Just make sure you have lean chops or the dish will be too greasy! You gotta try this!  Thanks for posting buttercup!

These are the best pork chops I've ever had! I followed the recipe as is. The only thing I would do differently is use more chicken broth/flour to get a little more gravy in the pot when it's all done. Absolutely scumpcious!

I also had to add additional broth to cover the chops.  I would recommend these for people who love pork, and for those who hate them. I made this for dinner tonight with a few changes based on what I had on hand.  I had 1 lb of pork loin, I cut it into bite sized pieces and coated in 1/4 cup of flour, 1/2 ts of mustard powder, and a little salt, then browned it in a frying pan.  I removed the pork, added 2 tb of butter 1 clove of fresh garlic and scraped up the browned bits, added 2 Tb of flour and cooked it for a minute.  Then I added about 11 oz of reduced ham stock, and 1 ts of dry mustard to make a gravy.  I added the pork back in, covered it, and baked at 350 for 1 hour. I would have given this 4.5 if I could have. I am stingy with 5's :-). I made this mostly according to the recipe. I used boneless pork sirloin chops. I probably added proportionately slightly more dry mustard because I know I like that as a flavoring. I left out the salt, knowing it is easier to add later than to take out. I used Better Than Bouillon brand chicken bouillon (that is my go-to brand for all bouillons). I also added 3 red potatoes cut into 1 inch chunks. Aside from those minor changes, I followed the recipe pretty closely. After about 2 hours in the crock, I tasted the gravy, and thought it needed a bit more flavor, so I shook in some Nature's Seasoning blend and mixed it up a bit. After another 45 minutes, I couldn't wait any longer, so I cut off a third of one of the chops and pulled out a few potato chunks to have a little "before meal snack." It was very good! I did sprinkle a bit of pepper on it too, but that's all. And I am really the type to often "dress up" a recipe more than that. The pork was nice and moist. It wasn't yet "fall apart tender" but had a very nice texture. I put the lid back on and will let it cook another hour and then turn it off.

Very nice, easy, yummy dish :-)

P.S. Mine came out a light color like chicken gravy, not brown like in the picture, but I don't care about the color. It tasted very good.

Simple and delicious!  Reminds me of meals my mom used to make when I was growing up on the farm.  Served with mashed potatoes, corn and a cucumber salad.  Gravy was perfect, meat was so tender we could easily cut it with a fork.  Thanks for a keeper!

I made this last night for my family, they LOVED it! I did not have any trouble with clumping in the gravy and let it sit in the slow cooker on low for about 4 hours to insure the meat was extra tender. I served with mashed potatos and corn.
Amazing! I used the crock pot though. Turned out perfect! :)
We did not care for these at all. Followed the recipe exactly.

I actually made a recipe very similar to this tonight that I found on Pinterest: ( http://www.mydailymoment.com/recipes/slow-cooked_pork_chops.php ).This recipe called for condensed chicken and rice soup (which I thought was a little strange but was shockingly delicious!) and no addition of flour to the broth. My daughter said this was her favorite dish ever and "Don't lose this recipe, mom!"  It's a definite keeper... I'm thinking about experimenting with some different condensed soups for different flavors... maybe onion soup! Yum! Thanks for this easy go-to pork chop recipe... it's a winner! UPDATE: I made this recipe with condensed  french onion soup and it was pretty good but my daughter thinks it was better with the chicken and rice soup.

My family enjoys this, for me; it is easy to make on a busy day! It tastes great, my first try the pork chops were a little soft ( I wondered if I did not brown them long enough), we will see the results with what I am making tonight.

This is so easy and very tasty too!  Made as written and just added a little fresh cracked pepper to the finished product.  Served with brown rice, green beans and breadsticks.  Made for Name That Ingredient Tag.
I'm not a big pork person either but this was great.

A great recipe!  I was very thankful to find a recipe like this that did not use 'Cream Of..."  I read the reviews first and planned accordingly.  For my purposes I didn't need a crockpot.  I seasoned the chops and and browned them in an oven proof skillet.  Then I sauteed mushrooms, onions and garlic, added the stock and some flour mixed with dried mustard and water.  I was only making 3 x 1" thick chops but used the full amount of gravy ingredients.  It went in to the oven at 350 for 1 1/2 hours with a pan of brussel sprouts, carrots and cauliflower put in to roast for the last 40 minutes.  I found it very flavourful and suspect that those who didn't may not have used the concentrated broth.  It would make a huge difference substituting regular broth imo.  Anyway - it was a fabulous meal with lots of gravy left to pour over the mashed potatoes.  This will be a regular item here!

I'm amazed at how delicious and easy this recipe is -- the whole family loved it. I used homemade broth and make a couple of flavor additions -- replaced about 1/3 of the wheat flour with masa harina, and added an Italian herb blend (Penzey's Tuscan Sunset). Falling-apart done in less than 3 hours, and the gravy was smooth and delicious over rice.

This was good. I did a couple things differently - added some different spices to the flour mix, including some thyme and paprika. I also whisked the flour into the broth, in the same pan I fried the chops. That helped thicken things a little and I had no clumping.  As for the broth, I used the Knorr liquid chicken stock bubbles (no idea what their name is!)and instead of adding 3.5 cups of boiling water to it, I only added about 12oz water. Once it was bubbling in the crock pot, I thought perhaps there wasn't enough liquid and I added about a half bottle of beer. My husband LOVED this and there was a nice amount of gravy. I gave it 4 stars because it was a touch bland, but if I make it again, I will doctor it up more. I also cooked it on high for 2 hours, then switched it to low for 2 hours and it was fall off the bone tender. Thank you for this recipe!

This was a fantastic base recipe for pork chops and gravy that can be suited to your own tastes. As for me, I used 5 teaspoons of yellow mustard (didn't have dry) and increased flour to 3/4 cup. Also, I used a teaspoon of locally obtained seasoning mix that included salt paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, and black pepper. After browning chops, I made a roux w/ green onions and remainder of the flour, mustard, seasoning mixture. I used about 48 oz of chicken stock slowly mixed into the roux which was then poured over the chops in the crock pot. I cooked on high for two hours and all was done but not quite falling off the bone yet. Then cooked on low for another two hours. Also mixed in a tablespoon of cornstarch for thickening and added a cup of mushrooms. Finally, I tasted and re-adjust seasonings as needed before serving.

Read more at: http://www.food.com/recipe/slow-cook-down-home-pork-chops-and-gravy-45940?oc=linkback

I served these chops with brown rice and baby peas.  This was definitely a country-style, hearty meal.  :)  I can certainly understand why this recipe is so highly rated and has had so many reviews.  We will be enjoying this recipe many more times, I'm sure.  Thanks for sharing your recipe, Buttercup!

I was careful not to let it get too thick, since it thickens a bit more in the slow cooker.  This is the second time I'm making this, and it's a huge hit with mashed potatoes and fresh green beans.  Comfort food at its best!
Super cheap to make and extremely tasty to boot. I was pleasantly surprised at how good these turned out! My boyfriend loved them, as well. Will be making again!

Delish and all ready as soon as I walked in the door!
