I am always looking for things to stash in the freezer for breakfast and these were a big hit!  I can't wait to try chilies and tomatoes in them.  Thanks for sharing!

This made 48 regular sized muffins for me.  I probably used less than 2 lbs of sausage but I used HOT italian sausage and I think that the muffins turned out perfect.  I love that they are a freezer recipe.  I'm sure I will be making this again!

WOW!! These are really great... I just pulled some outta the oven and couldn't stand it anymore, they smelled so wonderful I had to taste and OMG, they are so good.. I made these with the corn muffin mix as suggested by one of the other raters and they are truly outstanding.. Im sure these will be a hit with the hubby and the kiddos 7 and 4... Thank you..
I loved these - however, my husband and son thought they tasted too much like cornbread...

These are SO GOOD!! I added a little onion to sausage while cooking(minced fine.. after reading ALL other reviews took hints and used jiffy corn muffin mix.. also read where some had problems with sticking to pans and paper liners..so I experimented..1 muffin I used paper liner 1 muffin I sprayed with pam the other 10 in this muffin tin I used Professional Baking Coating/Grease that I had made a few days ago painted it on with my 11/2" paint brush I uase for oiling stuff & they popped right out..so I'll be using THAT from now on!!! I got 42 really nice muffins in my regular old muffin tins next time (tomorrow I'm trying with bacon/onion this will be made over and over by me.. THANK YOU for sharing this great recipe

These turned out very nicely.  I had no problems with sticking in the muffin cups, I used a baking spray and ran a butterknife around the perimeter of each muffin before I pulled them out.  I used frozen turkey sausage and diced it up after I cooked it.  DH thought they were tasty, but I think I might add some herbs/spices next time.  UPDATE: I tried one of these myself for a reheat breakfast and these are soooo yummy!  No spice changes needed!

I made this recipe during my last OAMC session, and now it's going into my "OAMC Favorites" recipe book.  Hubby expecailly loves them.  Nex time I might see if I can get more "stuff" in them, and I might use more Bisquick and less cornmeal.

We loved these...finally, something BOTH my kids (2 & 3 year old) like!!!  They were so tasty! I cut the recipe in half (wanted to make sure they were going to eat it).  I used bulk breakfast sausage and mexican cheese blend, and I added a little extra cornmeal and a little less bisquick (i ran out!).  Very tasty, can't wait to freeze and see how they defrost!  Thanks!!  (PS:  Be careful not to OVERCOOK or I bet they would wind up dry...I took them out of the oven immediately when a toothpick stuck in the middle of one came out clean (about 13-14 minutes in my oven).  I got 16 with the half recipe.)

I think these would have been better for me if I had used regular sausage instead of chorizo, I really didn't like the smell or taste of it.  I will try it again, because I think it will be better!

Thanks!

These were really good. I halved the recipe and used regular breakfast sausage instead of chorizo. Half the recipe made 19 regular muffins for me. They stuck to the liners pretty bad, so next time I will skip the liners, or spray them with some cooking spray. This is a nice alternative to sugar cereals in the morning for the kids, who happen to like these too.

I made with Jimmy Dean sausage and mexican blend cheese and green chilis - they were lacking in flavor. I'm not sure I liked the cornmeal in them either - I think I'd prefer a more traditional biscuit instead.
I wanted to like these so much but they seemed so bland. I'm not very creative in cooking so maybe there is something I could have added to spice it up a bit.

These are really nice and versatile. I add green onions and red peppers  and took them to work for an early meeting and they were gone in minutes.  I really like the different texture the corn meal gave.  Thanks

I just finished making this wonderful recipe. The muffins turned out perfect. I did some in a regular large muffin pan (about a dozen) and the rest of the batter I used in a mini-muffin pan. I skipped the pan liners and added a can of drained Rotel diced tomates with chili peppers. They turned out GREAT!! We love them!! I put 2-3 mini-muffins in a snack-sized zip locked baggie they fit just right, then into the freezer.  Canâ€™t wait to pop them in the microwave in the mornings for breakfast on my way out the door! Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe!! I plan to try your recipe breakfast tacos next!

I love these!  I halved the recipe and it made 10 jumbo muffins.  I tweeked the recipe to make "stuffed breakfast muffins" that a local bakery makes.  I filled the muffin cups halfway, added the sausage and cooked eggs, then topped with more batter.  Took 15 minutes to bake the jumbo muffins.  I used less cheese and low fat sausage.  I added some onion powder,aleppo pepper, salt, pepper and a smidge of garlic powder to the batter.  These were great topped with white sausage gravy or with salsa.  This one is going in my permanent rotation!  Next time I will double this recipe!

Fantastic base with MANY variations possible! I made 1 1/2 of this recipe. I used crumbled link sausage and a mix of mozzarella and old cheddar cheeses. I also added green and red pepper, onion, garlic and oregano. Maybe because of all the "stuff" I added, it did take longer to bake, but SO worth it! I made minis and regular muffins and I have already eaten 3! *blush*
Great! I halved the recipe to try it and we love it! I will make more with the leftover bacon and green onions I have. THanks!

I made this exactly as stated except I cut it in half.  School is out and my boys really loved the fact that they can pull one out of the freezor and "nuke" it for their own breakfast.  Next time I think I will add some bacon to it.  Thanks for sharing.

These are tasty and just as good reheated in the micro.  To a half recipe I added half of a chopped red bell pepper and half of an onion and it made 24.  Will definitely make these again.  I skipped the cornbread mix that some reviewers suggested, cornmeal as the recipe calls for is just fine, I didn't find it grainy at all.

Yummy!  I can't eat chorizo as it gives me severe hickups....so I added hot italian sausage, and it was perfect for me. I added about 1/3 cup of finely chopped onion and once it was cooked up, I drained the fat off.  I made my own Bisquick, so next time, I would used a little bit more salt.  To make things easy, I sprayed a 1/4 measuring cup with Pam and scooped up the measured amount and placed it in muffin tins that I has used Kittencal's Pan Release, Better Than Pam Spray! (Professional Pan Coating) Recipe #78579.  I sprinkled a little bit of poppy seed over top for a nice touch.  I am thinking any type of sausage or cheese could be used in this mix....it is that flexable and forgiving!!  Nice contribution!

What a great recipe and so easy! I used the advice of others and used the jiffy mix and subsitued 1/2 milk and 1/2 buttermilk. Owens HOT sausage works really well if you're looking for that added kick!

I made these today for my son as a morning busride breakfast.  They taste wonderful!   I have to cook them nearly twenty minutes at 375 F. though unsure why...  for them to be firm and cooked through.  But wonderful and very filling for a teenagers morning commute to school every day!  Next time I will try adding some maple flavoring as my son commented it was the only flavor missing from a Mc griddle....
These are great! I froze most of them and take them to work. I heat them in the microwave and spoon salsa on top as I eat them. Tasty and filling meal!

I was very much looking forward to these, as they sounded so good and had so many great reviews.  I followed the recipe as outlined plus I added a small can of green chilis.  The result was much like a bland cornbread, even with the chilis added.  I will probably keep them in the freezer anyway and try to remember to serve them with a chili or stew dish.

Thanks for a great recipe! I made 1/2 the recipe, and used spicy sausage seasoned with a low-sodium taco seasoning to give them a bit more flavour. After tasting the first batch, I added a little salt - although I used Betty Crocker Bisquick, I found that a little salt was needed otherwise they tasted a little bland. These are great with a little salsa, or as a sandwich with avocado. Delicious!
I too ended up with a mouthful of bland muffin. Sorry but I won't be making again.

This was so yummy!  I split the recipe in half.  I used Johnsonville's maple flavored breakfast sausages cut into small pieces.  I added a little of garlic powder and some salt as well.  They freeze and reheat well.  Thank you!!
Love these!  Have made them many times.  Great with sausage, bacon, or anything else you can think of to throw in.  Great to microwave in the morning before I head off to class.

I had a hard time rating this one. I think it's a 5 star all the way but my 5yr old daughter did NOT like these and she likes sausage. My husband says 3 stars. He thought the first one was a little weird but he says they grow on you- he ate 4. I think they are both crazy! They were relatively quick & easy and I used silicone muffin cups so none of mine stuck at all even though I didn't grease them or spray them.  The flavor was great and the muffin part was tender and had a nice texture.  Mine took 18 minutes.

I'm giving this four stars - three for flavor (or the lack thereof, in my opinion), five for the awesomeness of having a quick portable breakfast prepared ahead and stashed in my freezer, that averages out to four.  I prepared the recipe almost exactly as written, using regular sausage - the only thing I did differently was to add some chopped onion and bell pepper.  The muffins are nice, but they need some more flavor.  I'd thought the sausage would be flavorful enough, but my husband and I both agree that this needs a kick.  Next time I might try the green chilies, or some chopped jalapenos, or a spicier sausage, or just adding a little cayenne pepper.  This is a good base, and I think with some tweaking of the seasonings and the addition of a little heat/spice, I'll be considering it a five-star recipe all the way.  Thanks for sharing!
Great recipe. Freezes well. Saves money by not buying fast food breakfasts. Makes a lot no need to double the recipe

I loved the idea but was very disappointed with the taste.  This is very bland!  Other reviewers mentioned this, but I thought it would be okay for my kids, but even they didn't like this.  I might try doing this again, using some spices or other additions, but in the meantime, I have a lot of muffins in my freezer that no one wants to eat.

Unfortunately my muffins were very bland. There was a little flavor from the sausage but not nearly enough. I even added salt and pepper before cooking them and it didn't help. I did think the recipe was a great idea, although it didn't taste great. They were easy to make and convenient to reheat, but I won't be making them again.

They taste super yummy straight out of the oven.  I haven't microwaved them yet, but I'm sure they'll be yummy.  I also used cornbread mix instead of cornmeal, and they turned out light and fluffy.  I think more sausage is needed (I used chorizo) to give the muffin more oompf.  My 7 year old daughter didn't think they tasted good on their own, but with some jam she loved them!
This a basic good recipe, to spice it up a little I used Jimmy Dean Hot sausage and sharp cheddar cheese and just a dash of garlic. Try it.

these are excellent! i used sausage, and left out the muffin liners due to sticking. 
also i should add i baked them for 20 to 25 minutes at 375 F and they came out golden brown and so much better than baking for 15 minutes.

This was a very versatile recipe.  I made it for a bake sale we had at work and everyone seemed to love them.  I am giving it 4 stars because when the first batch was bland I added a bunch of stuff to the mix...I used 1 pound of Jimmy Dean "hot" breakfast sausage and 1 pound of chorizo.   I also threw in some diced red pepper, onions and garlic into the sausage as it was cooking.  Instead of cornmeal I used 1 box of Jiffy Corn Muffin mix.  I added one can of diced green chilis and one can of Rotel tomatoes.  For spices I added chili powder and cilanto.  In the very last batch I added some black beans.  With all of these additions I give it 5 stars.  My 5 year old daughter loved them.  My coworkers thought it was like a breakfast burrito muffin.  Overall I think it is a good recipe that you can really play with to suit your own personal tastes.  I will be making these again to see what else I can come up with. Thanks!!!

These were very good! I used half Jimmy Dean sausage and half chorizo.  I also added some green chilies and some extra seasonings such as garlic powder, cumin, chili powder and salt since the other reviews mentioned it being bland.  Turned out very good, even the kids liked it!

I love the quick, easy, reasonably nutritious breakfast that this creats.  I made it strictly per the recipe the first time and they were really quite good.  However, I too now add some onion, bell pepper and garlic powder.  Also, we eat two each for the adults in the household, one for kids.

These are pretty tasty. I made the mistake of not reading the reviews before baking and so they stuck to the papers, and were a little bland. Next time I'll add some more spices, and probably forgo the papers in favor of Kittencal's non stick. I made a batch of these for a friend who just had a c-section, and she doesn't eat regular sausage so I used turkey sausage, they they turned out pretty tasty! Right now I've got a ton in my freezer, but I'd make these again, next time with the modifications.

Love, love,  loved these.  They are similar to a sausage cheese puff recipe I make, but with the added corn meal they make a great grab and go breakfast muffin.  I'm glad I had some when I did, my husband ate the rest in he mornings on his way to work.

Honestly, the convenience of OAMC is perfect for me as a single mom, and usually a recipe this highly rated is a sure win for my family. But as others who have rated this low have mentioned, these turn very bland for my family. My kids are pretty open minded eaters, but these were even too bland for them. They convinced our babysitter to let them drizzle syrup over them so there was some flavor, and that was the only way they got eaten. Now, as someone else mentioned, I have a couple dozen boring, bland muffins that aren't going to help me beat the morning craziness at our home.

The comment at the end of the recipe says, "if you like spicy foods, add green chilies." Well, my children don't tolerate spicy foods very well, so I decided to make the recipe "as is." "As is" my children will not eat them, and I only choked 2 down to try to encourage them. The texture isn't impressive, and there is no flavor. I hate to throw food away, but it's going to take a lot of syrup from my kids to choke these down.

I suppose if you added a good amount of garlic, pepper, possibly onion and salt, these might have a decent flavor. I had hoped I'd like the original flavor enough to work with alterations the next go round, but there is no way. I can't waste the time or the money.

They are convenient, if only edible.

I didn't have Bisquick, and prefer my own biscuit mix, so I cannot rate this with integrity. However, it is a neat idea, and they came out pretty good. I used aged cheddar, which I recommend for flavor. I also used a blander breakfast sausage, while next time I look forward to trying chorizo. I might also add green onions (which the kids won't like, ha ha) and a pinch of cayenne. I don't know if Bisquick is saltier than my usual biscuit mix, but I had to add salt to the batter that wasn't yet baked after I tasted the first batch. I also think I will try making a big one in my cast iron skillet, as I didn't like the way it stuck to the papers, or to the pans when I used baking spray. A good basic recipe to play with.

I made this recipe before I read the reviews and maybe I would have added more seasonings, because like everyones listed it is kind of bland. I split the recipe in half and used the chorizo. However, I dipped them in salsa while eating it or put salsa with a little cheese on top and it tasted very good. I like the idea of the recipe! Thanks for the recipe!

I made half a recipe and got 20 muffins.  I like the muffins that have lots of meat in them. I used Bob Evans hot sausage,4 oz. of chilis, Mexican hot sauce, pepper jack cheese and turned out very good,
Bland. The muffin itself was so blah that it took all the flavor out of the sausage. Also, it makes twice as many muffins as you probably want.

i made a 12 muffin version of this in a 6 jumbo muffin pan, using double the amount of vegetarian sausage and 2 eggs so only 3/4 cup milk. i also added about 1/4 cup of Gruy?re i had kicking around, about 1 tbs green tabasco, a tsp of dill and a tsp of garlic powder. i also topped each muffin with a bit of parmesan and i used old low fat cheddar. i was using a non-stick silicon pan and buttered it anyway. they didn't rise as much as i was expecting. had to bake for a good 20 min but that's because they were bigger then stated. still a little bit bland. i could have added at least another Tbs of tabasco and more spices but there weren't bad.
Love, love these muffins!  I take them to our Sunday school class all the time.  We just add some sage, nutmeg, clove, ground red pepper, onion salt and pepper and it makes the sausage flavor pop!

We really liked these.  I made them for breakfast on Saturday and the leftover got eaten each morning after before school.  they reheated nicely and the kids loved them.  I plan on making these again, using different types of sausage.  Thank you for sharing with us.

As others have said, good basic recipe.  I had to bake them for 20 minutes.  To make them a little more healthy, I used reduced fat Bisquick, reduced fat cheese, and ham instead of the sausage.  The first batch was a little bland, but I added salt, pepper, onion and garlic powders, and a dash of cayenne on the second batch.  Much better!  Quick and easy breakfast for a crowd.

Pretty good but needing a more flavor... maybe twice as much sausage would help. According to another reviewer's suggestion, I did add some green chilies and a little tobasco and found it wanting. But I would try again and double the chilies and tobasco. I also thought it would be good served together with a savory egg (doctored up a little). Thanks for a good, solid recipe with potential!
I tried adding some spices like sage, chili powder, garlic powder, and a little salt but still felt they were pretty bland. Maybe needed a lot more salt.
Really really really good!!!

Fabulous soup!  I'm so sorry that i didn't get a picture of this soup before it was all gone. I ended up multiplying by 4x. I didn't have any canellini beans on hand so used Great Northerns. I wanted a vegetarian offering, so used a roasted vegetable stock in stead of the chicken soup base. I might have increased the spices by more than 4x, but not much. i had 2 % milk instead of whole, but also used the 1/2 and 1/2. The addition of the potato flakes at the end is an inspired touch not to be skipped. It gave the soup a lovely full body without resorting to removing and pureeing any part of it. This soup smells wonderful, is very pretty to look at and tastes great. Thanks, Uncle Bill!

Very good, unique soup that smelled wonderful as it cooked!  I was hesitant to put the soy sauce in, feeling it did not go with the other spices and might detract from that flavor.  I used it in spite of my reluctance and it was delicious.  I did use skim milk and fat-free half and half and it still tasted rich.  The only change I might make next time would be to add another can of beans as we love them!  Thanks for sharing!

Wow Uncle Bill! I wish I had doubled this recipe when I made it. It smelled so good in my house and the taste was fabulous! I wondered about the soy sauce with the other ingredients, but it all came together well. I love the spiciness if the dish. Maybe when I make the next batch there will be time for a photo. I was too busy scarfing down this soup to even THINK of taking a picture. I had to make a substitution on the milk and half and half.  I used a can of evaporated milk. It was still delicious.
So yummy with 1.5 cups of m&ms and .5 cup shredded coconut!

Excellent recipe!!  I made this to go over pancakes (#66241) with Chambord spiked whipped cream!!  Awesome! My family of four devoured it.  I also added sliced almonds, almond extract,  and a few tabs of butter to the peaches.  I will definetly make again.
Made this just as a change from the strawberry sauces I usually make during the summer ~ Made a double batch, & we find it GREAT OVER ICE CREAM & POUND CAKE! Thanks for a great recipe
This is a great recipe.  Easy to do, just a few ingredients.  I ate it with caramelized onions, cheese, tomatoes and mustard.  Thanks ratherbeswimmin :)  Made for New Kids on the Block tag game
This was awesome!  Will definitely become a regular at my dinner table.
Excellent meal! I decreased the amount of chicken and increased the broccoli. I also added extra lemon juice and garlic powder. Great meal, thanks!
The sauce was not very liquid - mostly paste.

Very good dish.  The lemon juice gives a nice bite to the sauce.  I would recommend butterflying the chicken breasts so they cook through more quickly, or delay adding the broccoli (which is what I did).
My family didn't care for this recipe.  The sauce was strange for us.  But that's probably taste preference.

Great meal that's easy, too! This is one of those simple recipes that's as good as the quality of ingredients. Fresh lemon juice and homemade stock (sorry Kitchen Basics brand!) are required here. I would also suggest pounding the chicken breasts to uniform size so they cook evenly. Wasn't paying attention and threw the flour mixture in with the broccoli, so just added the rest and cooked away. It worked just fine. I used a little more stock since I freeze mine in 2 cup portions, and added a couple of cloves of garlic. Flour here is used as a thickening agent and when blended completely with the lemon juice and stock, should not be pasty at all. I agree with Leta, I would add the broccoli right before serving since it can loose that pretty bright green color if overcooked a bit. Great weeknight meal! Thanks for sharing!
This was not as good as I thought it would be but I used bottled lemon juice maybe that made a difference
I didn't have celery so I used 1 bell green pepper and 1 red.  Butter instead of margarine (always butter for me :p )  Very delicious and fast to do.
This was so delicious!  I used diced zucchini, carrot and red bell pepper in place of celery and green pepper.  It was a delicious addition to our chicken stir-fry.
Easy, easy, easy and very tasty. Accurate measures and times as well. God Bless you Amy.

The flavor of this was great. Very easy to put together, but the time needed to be adjusted for my microwave, so I ended up over cooking it.:( But that was my fault not the recipe's, I should have known better. I will make this again adjusting the time.

*Reviewed for Zaar World Tour 3*
Very easy to make and the directions were clear. The rice had a great flavour- reminded me of packeted "rice-a-riso". Makes 4 small serves
Easy!  Another one for a working mum who needs a quick and healthy dish for the kids (or adults!)
I love pilaf dishes, and this was no exception.  It was so simple to make.  Next time, I will reduce the bouillon to maybe 1 tsp. because it tasted a little too salty for me.
This is an outstanding recipe,very easy to make and very tasty. Try it, you will love it!
I have never had Chili's fajitas, but these are easy and wonderful. Will definately be making these again.

These didn't taste like the ones at Chili's.  But, they were still really good.  

I will definitely make these again.

I had some unseasoned chicken breast tenders I had pan cooked in my refrigerator. I sliced and put them in this marinade for 45 min or so. I then heated the chicken in the pan. They still had great flavor! My family just gobbled it up.
Excellent.  This worked perfectly in my rice cooker, DH loved it. I used gala apples, arborio rice, fat-free sweetened condensed milk, and reduced fat margarine.
Yummy!  Quick and easy! Wonderful on a cold and snowy day!
I found it a bit too sweet. I  would probably try it with more rice and water first then add the other ingredients. I will decrease the amount of butter. I will try it again though.
I found that 3 cups of water too much when using 1 cup of rice.  I would definitley make it again by increasing the amount of rice

Ours has turned out great every time!  It has become a family favorite.  Our changes: use arborio rice; leave the peels on the apples; no raisins.  Discovered that it is yummy to add Bailey's as a topping!  THANKS for the great recipe!

I loved the addition of apples to the rice pudding! This dish is delicious. The only thing I would have liked to be different is the sweetness. Even though I used about half the sweetened condensed milk called for I still found it to be too sweet for my tastes. Using a rice cooker to cook the pudding was so easy and convenient. The pudding was good both hot and fresh from the cooker and cold the next day. Made for Kittencalskitchen's Crock Pot and Rice Cooker Game.

I had to make this dairy free, so used coconut milk for the sweetened cond., which necessitated adding some sweetness (I figured out after I tasted it!)  I just added some liquid Stevia and it was just right.  I ran it through 3 cycles and it was still pretty creamy (some milk on top) so I might add a little bit more rice or less milk next time, but was still super tasty.

This was a nice holiday treat in between huge family meals. This makes a pretty big batch and since it's pretty heavy I'd recommend halving the recipe. Would I make it again? Probably only for the holidays with a large crowd who actively likes rice pudding. Otherwise it will mostly go to waste for me and my crowd. But it was good so at least give it a go.
This was awesome! No changes needed. I used real vanilla beans, which made it even more amazing.
Outstanding....I would not change a thing, I bought the rice cooker yesterday and have been trying a couple of different things...this one was great.

I can't even say how much we loved these!  I had some leftover grilled steak that had been frozen.  So I sliced it very thinly, and then marinated for about 3 1/2 hours. I also added 1 small red pepper for heat, but I could have used more. I sauteed it in olive oil just until heated through, then removed from the pan, and kept it warm.  I sauteed the onions and peppers in the same pan, till they were good and brown, poured the reserved liquid mixture over, then threw the meat back in the pan, and mixed well.  Served in flour tortillas with chopped tomatoes and cheese, rice on the side, and now I have to make these ALL THE TIME!  We're even going to grill some steaks to freeze so we can have these during the winter.(Too cold to grill around here.)Thanks for a great recipe!

Very Good! Instead of grilling (which would have been even better), I stir fried the strips of steak, added some sugar and extra soy sauce because of personal preference (tasted too much lime, probably because I marinated strips vs solid piece, and overnight). I skipped the red and yellow peppers, used the gr pepper and sweet onion, chopped avocado and picante sauce. My only complaint was the quality of tortillas, other than that, we loved the flavor of the beef. Thanks R.H.!
Really good recipe. I used chicken breasts in it. I will be making these again. Next time I will try them with steak.

The flavor of these is outstanding.  We went to dinner at the Outback one night and used our leftover prime rib from dinner in this.  Wonderful!  Thanks so much for posting - we'll be making these again - and again.

Yummy fajitas!  I poked holes in a flank steak, added it to a sealed bag with marinade and refrigerated for about 5 hours, turning 4 times.  I then broiled it and cut the meat into nice thin slivers with my electric knife.  I didn't use the yellow peppers, because I didn't have them.  Served with the usual fajita fixings.  I'd like to try this with chicken, as well.

These were so good, I can't imagine how wonderful they'd be if I had been able to let them marinate longer or cook on the grill!  I was only able to marinate for under 2 hrs., and had to pan-fry the chicken breasts.  The flavor was perfect, and I especially loved the faint zip that the cayenne gave to the meat!  This one goes in my permanent cookbook!
My son is a Chili's chicken fajita junkie.  I made these last night and he loved them.  I doubled everything except the garlic and used chicken.  Great recipe!

Not sure if it was just me... but don't marinade your BELL peppers, when it says "add peppers," it means black and cayenne peppers.  Other than that, would recommend marinading more than 2 hours.  Excellent!

Double the recipe using chicken - they were excellent.  As an added flavor we halved the onion,brushed with olive oil and threw on the grill with the chicken and the green pepper, then cooled chopped and did the carmelization thing.  Thanks - Making again for Mother's Day / B-day party on Sunday.

Really great recipe, I added about one tsp. of cumin to the marinade to emphasize the smoky flavor because we don't have a grill and that worked out great.  Marinated the beef overnight.  Perfect flavor, definitely a keeper.  Thank you Robbie!!
I made this with flank steak and it was delicious.  I'll make this again!
I made this for our company Christmas party. It was a huge hit! None were left over. Very good.

These were the best fajitas I've ever made. I always wondered why my fajitas were tough... now I know. The only thing was that the flavor was slightly too tart. Maybe I'll try less lime next time. Anyone have suggestions?
Delicious. Made with skirt steak.
Excellent!

I used hanger steak (from Balducci's here in McLean, VA). Very, very good.
I'm pretty sure Chili's uses skirt steak, but that could be a regional thing. 
Also, I think there should be more elaboration on cooking the onions and peppers. I sautee them. I cook on high heat in a cast iron skillet until browned, then reduce heat to low and cover the skillet and let sit for 30 to 45 minutes. 
As a time saver and alternate, if you live anywhere near a balducci's get the pre-marinated (in their chipotle lime marinade)skirt, hanger or flank steak. Delicous.

Fabulous recipe.  I added sliced fresh mushrooms and topped with Monterey Jack cheese.  Placed under the broiler to just melt the cheese and served with flour tortillas, sour cream, guacamole, salsa and lettuce.  Made a great lunch for work the next day as well.
I had some sirloin steak I wanted to use up so I picked this recipe...turned out great...grilled everything on the outside grill...will make again
Didnt taste like Chili's but they were ok. Used steak.
This was marvelous! We each enjoyed it very much. Absolutely as good as any I have ever eaten out. I know this will become a regular in our house. We used the steak this time. Yum, yum!!!
These were very good. I've never had the original from Chili's so I cannot compare the two. They went into our permanent recipe list nonetheless!
Turned out pretty yummy!  Will make again.  Not the same as Chili's in my opinion, but still good.

I have made this recipe with both the sirloin and the chicken and just love it. I adore Chili's fajitas and this copies them very well. If I marinate the meat and slice the veggies the night before or morning of, this goes together so quickly for dinner. You just don't need a seasoning  packet when you can produce such yummy results this way. I have also put the meat and the onion/pepper mixture on a heated cast iron skillet before serving as suggested by Todd Wilbur in his book and it made for a fun meal. You hear that sizzle and the smell wafts through the air seducing family and friends to the table. My husband is very happy just to have a steak grilled using this marinade all by itself. I've used the leftovers to make the Chili's Fajita Nachos the next day which is also one of my favorites. (I only get to eat at Chili's when I visit my parents four hours away)

This was so easy..........and my son and husband both said it equaled anything we have eaten in restaurants.........I couldn't believe I had really cooked this. Ha.  I was really apprehensive when I saw the sauce recipe........didn't sound like it would have enough flavor.....but guess what, less is more.......and it must be why the restaurant versions are so much better than mine. I wish there was a way to alert all viewers to try this.  I know this recipe was posted in 2001, but since there were not that many reviews, I wanted to add mine....This Is Great.  thanks so much........and will try it with beef too........

WOW! I followed this recipe exactly using chicken and it was the best Mexican meal I have made by far!  The meat was super tender and moist and the flavor was great! I will be making this again soon with sirloin.  Thanks!
Wonderful and full of flavor. The meat (steak) was very tender. This will become a standard in my house.
Yum -- this was great! Absolutely as good as Chili's! We made the chicken, and next time will try the steak. Delish!!

I can't believe it's taken me this long to review this...I've made this 3 times already!  Sorry!  I can't get over the flavor of the meat (I've used steak all 3 times).  I usually marinate overnight, but the first time it marinated only 4 hours and it was still so tender and flavorful!  I also thinly slice the meat, then marinade, and cook everything in a large skillet to save time/dishes.  I even made this for my B-I-L who is a soux chef and he LOVED it!  Thanks for the awesome recipe Robbie!!

I marinated top sirloin overnight but it just didn't pick up much flavour from the marinade, and was a bit tough coming off the grill. Maybe the bottled lime juice I used wasn't acidic enough to penetrate the meat? I'll try adding some extra white wine vinegar to the mix next time. It was a relatively healthy substitute for the tacos I was going to make and a nice way to get a dose of veggies. I topped them with Recipe #83371.

Very good! My friend hates bell peppers but he ate them anyway because he loved the taste of the marinade so much. I think the liquid smoke really seals the deal, I have an indoor grill but it really makes it taste like it's hot off the BBQ. Thanks!

I made this with chicken and only had time to marinade for one hour, but it still turned out delicious!  The liquid smoke does definately make the flavour.  I added the cayenne pepper, but also added 1/2 tsp of chipolte pepper as I like the heat. Definately a keeper and I will try steak next time as well

This was a great recipe, I used shrimp and beef.  I had one ribeye steak and about 12 small shrimp, for 2 people, and put it over salad,for a fajita salad.  It was really great!! I ended up marinating 2 days and it was still great. Charlotte
should be six stars!  I let it marinate for about 4 hours.  Thanks Robbie!

Yum!  We broiled the meat, as we were feeling a bit lazy that evening, but it still turned out great.  I added two fresh jalapenos from my garden to the veg...nice and spicy and perfectly seasoned.  Great recipe!

Yummy!  I've made this a couple times with steak and marinaded for different lengths and I would definitely marninade overnight.  It always turns out great but the longer marinade makes for a stronger flavor.  This is definitely a regular in our house.  I usually cut up half the peppers for the day of and then freeze the other half for the next time.  Thank you so good and so easy.

I cut up the chicken breasts before marinating and marinated for 24 hours.  Very good.  I also added a little chili powder.  I followed the recipe otherwise.  Robbie, I still use your delicious fried rice recipe.  I will add this to my recipes to make again.  Thank you for this wonderful recipe.

This was my first time making fajitas and I'm really glad I choose this recipe. It is so flavorful.  I doubled the recipe so I would have enough to serve 8.  I sliced the beef before putting it in the marinade and marinaded it for about 12 hours. The meat and pepper and onions were delicious.  Thank you.
Excellent! Almost like chili's--the closest I have ever had! I have only tried it with chicken so far, but next time I will try the steak. Thanks for the recipe :)
Love this!!!  Double the recipe because you'll be wanting more.
I tried it with chicken and it was great!  Can't wait to try it with steak (probably churrasco).  Very, Very yummy.

I used a sirloin and have to admit I became a bit skeptical but after grilling and serving, these ROCKED!  The vegetables had a great flavor and I think I may make some veggie fajitas for lunch, we will try chicken next time this is definitely in our top ten now!
fast, easy, and tastes great! it's also cheap, so it's ideal for this nightmare economy.

WONDERFUL! These fajitas are better than any I have ever had! We had guests over for dinner so I doubled the recipe. I marinated the chicken and steak for about 18 hrs. When the meat was done on the BBQ I turned the oven to warm and covered the meat and tortillas and let set until veggies were done. I cooked the veggies in a cast iron skillet and added mushrooms after the sauce was added. Meanwhile I took out meat and thinly sliced it. I would not combine meat in sauce I think it has better flavor left out. Served with Cafe Rio's Cilantro Lime Rice, a great combo!!! Thanks Robbie

These were just amazing! These are the best Fajitas I have ever had, let alone made. I used a pound of flank steak over sirlon. Wanted to use traditional fajita meat. Marinaded for about 6 hours and the taste was amazing. Did not grill the meat, but rather stir fried it. Just a small bit of remaining oil from browing the onions and peppers.
This is a great recipe...it's now the only one we use for fajitas!

Very good! I don't know why but my dish came out spicy and zesty! I marinaded the steak overnight.  I squeezed a little lemon in the steak since I didn't have any lime.  Otherwise I will make it again! I can say it was good.
I thought this was very close to Chili's!  Delicious!!!  We will be making these again

I haven't had fajitas at Chili's, so I can't comment on how close it is to theirs, but we were very happy with the recipe.  We had chicken fajitas and they were very flavorful, moist and just overall delicious.  We shared these with my parents who are Mexican food fanatics and they loved it as well.  I will be using this instead of the packaged fajitas flavorings for sure.
This was very easy and a hit for our backyard get-together!  I love fajitas and this sure beats the instant package of fajita seasoning! Thanks!

These were SO good! Used the steak, but we didn't have time to grill, so sauteed all on the stove top. Can't wait to try them on the grill. I marinated the meat for about 5 hours. Also, used only the red and yellow peppers. Next time I will add some shrooms to the mix. Served with shredded sharp cheddar cheese, sliced black olives, sour cream, chopped tomatoes, salsa and diced avocados. I put my tortillas in a glass dish, cover with a damp dish towel and microwave them for a minute or so. Then let everyone add their own toppings and enjoy! Delicious! Thanks for posting Robbie Rice.
Wow! What an amazing recipe! Thanks so much for sharing! I made these for my brother and his family as well as my own and they were a huge hit! I added more veggies, since we all love them!
These were amazing! They were easy to prepare and I was told that these fajitas rival any restaurant's...I agree!! This will definitely become a regular weeknight dinner!

Very good! I used chicken instead of steak to cut down on the fat.  The marinade was very good but I think it would have been better if I would have marinated it over night like some others suggested.  The only mistake I made was not making enough veggie sauce.  There didnt seem to be enough to cover all the meat and veggies so it was just a little dry.  I also like a little more kick to my fajitas so I think I will add just a pinch of red pepper next time.  Over all very great recipe!
This was sooo good!  I didn't have cayenne so I used half chili powder and half paprika and it was still wonderful.

I made this twice - once for my family, and once for my extended family (16 people!!)  Both times, I marinated for 12 hours.  This was AWESOME!  Great flavors, easy to make.  Everyone just loved it!  Thanks!
I live in Texas and I can say that I have eaten some of the best fajitas made. Both authentic and Tex-Mex. These fajitas are by far the best I have ever had and I will make these on a regular basis.
This was very good even though I only marinated it for about 30 minutes.  Next time will do at least two hours.  Was in a hurry!  Thanks!

The peppers were outstanding!  I sliced the chicken prior to marinating to pickup more flavor since I only had 2 hours.  I would definitely marinate longer next time and reduce or eliminate the water.  I have always shied away from liquid smoke - just sounds icky to me.  But I decided to be adventurous and try it - I'm so glad I did!  This recipe takes some prep work with all the slicing.  I could make an entire meal out of the peppers - I will definitely double the recipe for that portion next time!  Great Sunday night dinner - looking forward to trying steak next time.  Thanks for the great recipe!
This is a good recipe but a little to much lime for my taste.  The next I prepare this meal I will use no lime on the veggies
i was really worried that the lime would be a bit over whelming but it was very good! there what a nice hint of it without it being over powering. defiantly a hit with my family, thanks for posting!
My family loved this recipe. It has become an instant repeat for us. Didn't have to change much just added more garlic.

THESE WERE ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!!! we were short on time so we cut the meat up first and then marinated it for about a half an hour and it worked great.  I would like to have been able to marinate it for longer but it still tasted amazing! awesome recipe!!! we will definately make this again!
This was pretty good.  I was expecting more flavor though.
Awesome! I've made a few fajita recipes and this is the easiest & tastiest so far. Thanks!

Good - I didn;t follow all of the steps, though.  First I substituted chili powder instead of the cayenne, and also added the same amount of cumin.  Also, I cut my meat into small pieces before marinating, and then didn't marinate so long (I actually put it into my vacuum sealer for a few minutes after it marinaded for 1/2 to 1 hour).  I then dumped the meat and marinade into the pan and cooked till the meat was barely done, and then added the veggies right to that until they were barely done.  (The marinade was doubled, and I had lots of veggies :)  Oh, yes, an I used chicken.
Absolutely delicious!  Tastes very similar to Chili's.  The liquid smoke makes the world of difference.  Will be making these again soon!

This was so simple to prepare and we all loved them.  Our steak didn't take quite as long as called for maybe because it was a bit thinner then usual, but they turned out fabulous.  Thank you for sharing.

Tried this recipe. Love it. I am not a great cook but this was incredibly easy and turned out so delicious. Thank you so much.
I tripled it and it worked out great.

LOVED IT!!! Thanks for sharing. Followed the recipe exactly...almost. Didn't really measure the spices and used more than a 1/2 green pepper and veggies. Also added mushrooms to mine. My wife is a vegetarian, so I didn't combine the meat and veggies at the end. I marinated boneless skinless chicken breasts in the marinade for about 3 hours, grilled them and then sliced them into thin strips about 3 inches long. I then put them in a small fry pan on med-low just while the veggies got done. I then added a little bit of the veggie sauce to the chicken. Fried the veggies and added the veggie sauce to the veggies and kept them separate (for my wife ;)

We both love it. No need to go to the restaurant to order fajitas. This was better than at the restaurant. And it was made at home with fresh veggies.

Absolutely loved the flavor of the chicken. Will make this again...a lot as Mexican is our favorite dish.

Thanks

This was my 1st attempt at making fajitas & it exceeded my expectations!  I used shrimp & marinated it for 2 hours in the fridge.  I made the marinades exactly as directed except I left the salt out; I used reduced sodium soy sauce & that was enough salt for me.  Next time I will try with tofu.
I wound up marinating it for 3 nights (that's another story), so I don't know how flavorful it would have been had I not, but it was awesome. nom, nom.
My family really enjoyed! I followed the recipe exactly and my family didn't think it was spicy at all. Very good and easy. Thank you!

This is wonderful!  I marinated the chicken for at least 8 hours.  I used 2 green peppers.  When the peppers were almost done sauteing, I added about 1 T. butter for flavor.  My child enjoyed this too, and she is a picky eater.
Made this with Chicken and didn't change much except that I cut the chicken into strips before marinating and cooked in skillet. My whole family Loved it!
I almost didn't try because it's very different from the way I usually make fajita's.  I'm so glad I did!  I like this better, so did the rest of the family.  Thanks Robbie!

I LOVE this recipe!! I have made it many times n it's always gobbled up. My family n I have no complaints. This is our go to fajita recipe. This last time I made it I didn't have any limes so I just used lemons. I couldn't really tell too big of a difference. Thanks for a tasty n liked recipes

So good!  We aren't fortunate enough to have a Chili's nearby, so we only eat there about once a year when we are in Pittsburgh.  It is really nice to be able to recreate something that is a rare treat at home.  I think these tasted just like Chili's Fajitas.  I love the slightly American barbecue taste on these.  I used chicken that was marinated for a little over 24 hours and I served them with Recipe #37638.  Thank you for this great little recipe Robbie Rice!
Died and went to fajitas heaven.  Just give me a proper burial.
Much better than store bought packets and can be made with ingredients on hand.
These were delicious! Instead of grilling the meat I sliced it up & cooked it in my cast iron skillet with a little olive oil. Loved the browned edges on the chicken.

Seriously great. Best homemade I've ever had and better than some restaurants as well. I've made this for others too, who then requested the recipe. I've made the chicken in the crockpot (for ease) and on a frying pan (with some grill lines on it since we don't have a bbq grill). Frying pan is way better. I still liked the chicken in the crockpot, but it wasn't quite the same.
I made these the other night. I didn't have cayenne pepper so, I used a little bit of red pepper flake.

Absolutely delicious...i didn't use any meat..i used mushrooms instead...turned out great...my house had the aroma of Chili's which made me excited to taste the end result...my husband and I loved it... Thanks!
These were really good. I doubled the recipe, and added 1 t cumin and 1/2 t chili powder.

We liked these cookies.  A cakey cookie, nicely spiced with the pumpkin in the background. The only change I made was that I only have 14 oz tins of pumpkin and I'm too frugal (!) to waste 2 oz so I put in the whole can. Thanks Sue!

These are teriffic! I made the recipe as posted with no changes. They're soft, and the taste is very nice, spicy, pumpkiny (is that a word?) Anyway the taste is very good! And we liked the raisins. I will definitely make these again. Thanks Sue L!!

We don't care for raisins in stuff, so we omitted them.  Otherwise we followed the recipe to a tee and they turned out great.  I had a 13 year old and a 23 year old (not overly experienced cook) making them and they had no trouble.  They smell and taste like pumpkin pie.  Everyone was fighting over them when they came out of the oven.  Great snack to send to school with the kids!

Thanks for this great recipe! I decreased the sugar by 1/4 c., substituted 1c. of the flour with whole wheat flour and omitted the raisins. I used 1,5c. chopped hazelnuts. my husband and my grandma really loved it! this one's a keeper!
I liked the taste, but found them to be too cake like to be considered cookies.

Quite unique. While I love soft cookies, these are very cake-like, which took a little getting-used-to. The flavour was wonderful, and they also smell great when baking. As an experiment, I divided the dough in half before adding the additions, and added butterscotch chips to one half, instead of nuts and raisins, and used vanilla instead of lemon extract. I thought they would be to-die-for but, um, they weren't; they were merely okay and I prefer the original nuts and raisins version. The only other change I made was to use pumpkin pie spice instead of the ginger/nutmeg/cinnamon, which meant that a little allspice and mace were added to the mix.

I only made a couple changes. I only used 1 cup brown sugar. I didn't have any dark brown so had to make do with the light. I used 3 egg whites instead of 2 whole eggs. Less cholesterol that way. I also used the whole 14oz. can of pumpkin. I used 1 cup whole wheat flour and the rest white. I got 36 cookies and baked for 13 min. The came out nice and soft and we enjoyed them.
They were tasty but too cakelike for my taste. I used Craisins instead of raisins. I might use pumpkin pie spice mix next time.
Try substituting chocolate chips for the raisins.  They are great that way too!

I don't know if I did something wrong or if it's the recipe.  4 tsp baking powder is *a lot* for the amount of cookies this makes.  Mine came out like little chunks of rubber after 12 minutes, with very little flavour.  I added about a cup of oatmeal and another healthy dash of cinnamon, and they are passable, but still not very good.  The texture is bizarre.  I do really like the pumpkin-raisin flavour (used all raisins as I was out of nuts) but I think I'll have to look for another pumpkin cookie recipe, sorry.

I changed this a little by cutting the sugar in half and adding 2 tablespoons of molasses, then I cut the baking powder to 3 teaspoons and added a little cloves. It is still a little cakey but it tastes great! I will make it again and try one less teaspoon of baking powder next time.

I, too, changed the recipe a bit, creating a moist cake-like cookie that I had to refrigerate immediately (separating layers in a container using parchment paper). Instead of all the brown sugar, I used just 1 teaspoon, and added 1 cup applesauce.  I used just 1 and 1/2 teaspoons baking powder.  I grated the zest of two small lemons instead of the lemon extract.  I used just one cup of flour, but added 1 and 1/2 cups of whole wheat bran flour.  A very yummy treat!
libbie called these spicy pumpkin cookies from her little black book thank you for posting this recipe. dog gone stars

I am from the Philippines and currently going out with a hispanic man.  I don't know any hispanic recipes at all so I thought I try some recipes from the web and found this one. It was very good, delicious, tasty.  I felt so proud of myself seeing his whole family were eating the carnitas.  It was just a matter of minutes when they finished all 4 pound of my homemade carnitas.  Thank you very much.  I owe it all to you.

Rhea Tenorio

I used this recipe to serve 30 people at our family reunion.  I froze the cooked meat and  transported it the 7 hours to the reunion.  I reheated it in a pan and it was a hit.  A little was left over for lunch the next day.
Everyone gobbled it down!
Thanks for posting.

Wow!! The flavor of this roast was great!!  I followed your instructions exactly.  The meat just fell apart... it was so tender.  I served it with the flour tortilla, guacamole & salsa.  I also served up a plate of grilled onions with it.  Fabulous dish.  I highly recommend it!  Thanks so much for sharing.  :-)

This is a keeper.  I stayed on recipe through out. Obviously the guacamole and salsa are real important.  For whatever reason I felt compelled to put the guacamole down first, then the meat, and the salsa on top of it all. The only problem might be in presentation. I am not sure how Miss Anne serves her tortillas. I used them kind like a plate and they were hard to utilize in the meal. (Now our seven-year-old Sam will make anything into a burrito if he gets the chance, so he had no problem.) However, I think next time I will serve the tortillas rolled up on the side.

This recipe is great!! I used a pork roast, and followed the recipe exactly. Everyone loved it! I served it with tortillas, salsa and guacamole.  I shredded up the meat, and put it into the oven for a few minutes to "crisp it up". Thanks! This is a keeper!!

What can I say?  I loved this!!!  Other than using a pork roast and adding a bit of extra garlic and salt, I followed the recipe exactly.  However, when the meat was done, I put in a 400° oven for about 15-20 minutes to crisp up the meat.  I then covered a tortilla with some salsa, added a generous amount of carnitas and Mexican blend cheese on half the tortilla, folded it and grilled it on the trusty 'ol George Foreman grill, just enough to get the cheese all nice and gooey. I then dipped each and every yummy bite into some guacamole.  Reminded me of my favorite Mexican fast food joint, Super Taqueria's carnita quesadilla.  Mmm, mmm good!  This is one of my favorite recipes I've made on Zaar, I have to say.  Great flavor and extremely easy.  A definite keeper! Thanks so much for posting it!

Oh, Miss Annie, you did it again!  This was superb.  I did it in the crockpot on a busy day.  Served it with, rice, beans, tortillas, guacamole, sour cream and salsa.  I was encouraged to read that it freezes well - except that the over 4 pound roast was devoured by 5 people for dinner.  Nothing left to freeze!  I will be sure to do this one again!  Muchas gracias!
Delicious, tender meat.  Very accurate instructions - mine was done at exactly the 3 1/2 hour point.  Fork tender and juicy.  Great for stuffing tacos.
Excellent, no left overs!
This is a fantastic recipe!We all really enjoyed it.Thanks!

The flavor was wonderful.  Even my child who will usually not eat anything with green chilies, thought it was pretty good.  Next time i will not make the mistake of substituting a 7 bone chuck steak ... too much bone and grissle.

First of all let me say that this roast turns out absolutely "to die for" flavorful,  tender and juicy.  My roast was a little over 3 lbs and it took 3 1/2 hours exactly. No problem shredding this meat.  I served this with warmed flour tortillas and we had grilled onions, salsa verde and sour cream for condiments.  I served your recipe #12891 Green Rice Chile Bake as my side dish.  This made a wonderful Tex-Mex meal and I will definitely be making these  again.

This is a wonderful recipe. My family loves carnitas we usually buy them at the local import market and they are made with pork, so I did mine with pork. I htrew it in the crockpot for 10 hours and the meat fell apart. Served them in garlic-cilantro tortillas and Mexican rice. It made so much I have enough for 2 more meals in the freezer! Thanks for sharing Miss Annie!

This turned out wonderful!  I used a pork roast and used a potato masher to shred it.  It was so tender!  My husband was afraid of using all of the chili powder so we only used half.  Next time we will use all of it because it was not spicy at all.  We served it in warm tortillas with pico de gallo and homemade guacamole.  What a tasy meal!

This had a wonderful flavor!   I am so pleased with the taste.   We like to get the carnitas burritos at a local restaurant and these put them to shame.   Thanks for a recipe that I'll be making again and again.

I really wanted to like this.  It smelled so good when it was baking.  The meat was moist and shredded easily.  I mixed some of the juice with the shredded meat, but it lacked flavor.  I thought it needed some salt.  My DH liked it.  I doubt if I would make it again.  The only thing I changed was to use 1 can of chopped green chilies instead of two.

Wonderful, absolutely wonderful! I did this recipe in the crockpot and it turned out super! No one here is a guacamole fan so we just omitted that, used shredded lettuce, shredded cheddar, salsa and ranch dressing with whole wheat tortillas----WOW!  The small amount left over went into scrambled eggs for DH's breakfast this morning.  This recipe is gonna get alot of use here, believe me!  Thanks so much Miss Annie!!!!

Very easy and tasty. We made as directed ate some in burritos and froze some of the mix. It freezes and thaws very easily, you may want to taste and adjust seasonings once re-heated . Thank you for a simple mexican dish.

I made this from a pork roast because I had one in the freezer. I assembled burritos and added guacamole and onion to them. I froze them and brought them camping, I fried them but I think they would be good unfried too. They were a big hit! In the future I`ll also try them with beef

AWESOME recipe!  A very big hit with the family, even my 11-year-old - and *THAT* is saying something!

I made this with pork chops and rotel w/lime & cilantro (since I didn't have the roast or chiles on hand and didn't have time to go to the store) - very tasty!  Have tossed over rice, in black bean soup, on buns, in tortillas w/monterey jack cheese & sour cream... sigh... so tasty and *incredibly* easy.  I do believe I'll make some this weekend!

Thanks again for posting this recipe!

I combined this recipe with a few others from this site and the results were stupendous! after cooking the pork per thsi recipe, I lightly fried large pork pieces in hot oil. I then placed them in baking pan and returned them to the oven for approx. 8 minutes (for crispness). Chopped pork into 1/4 inch sized pieces and served in oil-softened corn tortillas. Garnished each plate with chopped onion, fresh chopped cilantro, avaocado slices, lime wedges and fresh homemade jalapeno salsa. FIT FOR A KING!
Made this in the crockpot and came out so tender and good flavor. I packaged this up in foodsaver bags for later use. Thanks.
I made this with a pork roast and just stuck it in a pot in the oven, no foil.  It was really tasty!  Thanks for a keeper!

I love this recipe!  I live with my boyfriend and made a roast a couple of weeks ago.  The flavor and tenderness of the meat was amazing!  Plus, it was so EASY!!  I froze what we couldn't eat and have made many different meals since.  It is so versatile.  I am planning on making another this weekend for a Cinco de Mayo party.  Thanks so much for sharing!

This was just wonderful ! Only thing i would change is using fresh roasted green chilies. I am going to make this again tonight for company, without a doubt it will be a hit yet again ! Thank you for posting !

Just wonderful! I used a pork roast and 2 big jalapeno peppers instead of the canned chiles. I made it spicier overall and I'm glad I did because even with the extra it was just pleasantly spicy for us. Thanks for sharing!

I made this for Superbowl supper. After wrapping in flour tortillas, I offered lot's of guac, salsa, sour cream to slather in it or on it. I also sauteed some onions in a little canola oil and drained well. We all enjoyed this, but most agreed that next time we will try it with pork instead of the beef. The cooking time was right on for a 3 1/2 pound roast, which is what I used. I served with Spanish rice, black beans and tortilla chips and of course Margaritas. Thanks for a fun, delicious new Mexican dish for me and my family to try.
I used a pork roast..Added 2 envelopes of sazon goya..Still was not as flavorful or spicy as we would of liked..But, I used leftovers in taco soup..Wonderful,way of using it up...

I made this as directed but with a pork shoulder roast.  It came out perfect.  I took the meat out of the tin foil, broke it into pieces/shredded it in a casserole dish, added in some of the drippings and then put it back in the oven for 10 minutes at 375 while I organized my â€œtaco station.â€�  I served these on corn tortillas with green onions, cilantro, guacamole and homemade salsa.

I'm sorry, Miss Annie, but this seemed like a run-of-the-mill pot roast to me.  And I could have done it more cheaply and with less mess in the crockpot. Although I was generous with the spices (more than stated in the recipe), it didn't result in any specific flavor, really. I guess a chuck roast is just a chuck roast...
This is very good!  I did up the garlic-------alot!   I served this with some cheesy baked rice.  My family loved it!  I'm making it again tonight.

Ms Annie...this is over the top!  I made it in the crockpot (low for 6 hours) and used you suggestion of New Mexico chili power.  There really is a difference in taste.  DH and I agreed these were the best carnitas ever.  Served with homemade flour tortillas, mexican rice and tomatoes, onions, avocado.  Will be making this often.  Thanks for sharing.

This was SO good.  I made exactly as directed but cranked the heat up to 400 and uncovered the meat to crisp it up during the last 15 minutes.  Served as a fajita filling, and hubby went nuts over it.  I will make this many more times.  Its worth mentioning that a generous amount of salt is needed (since no measurement is given).  Thanks for a keeper!

fantastic!!  i used a boneless pork loin instead of beef.  i doubled the garlic and drizzled the whole thing with fresh lime juice and olive oil.  i wrapped it up in foil and kept it in the fridge for a few days to marinate.  it was so simple to put together and it tasted so great!!  we had tasty pork carnitas!  thanks for the keeper!!
Wonderful flavor!  Thanks!
Made this recipe exactly as posted and it was delicious.  Served with homemade guacamole and salsa and I received rave reviews from my family.  Thanks for posting.
easy and tasty

I halved this recipe-throwing a 2 lb pork roast in the crockpot and splashing in some wine.  It was pretty good but I felt it definitely needed some more salt, seasoning and kick.  But a good starting point for sure!
Amazingly tender.  This was a delicious dish that I will make again and again!  Served it with fresh sliced avocado, lettuce, tomatoes, oives, salsa, cheese, and sour cream.  Thanks for posting!

This was wonderul and so quick and easy to put together.  My DH did think maybe next time we would "up," the chili powder, it was perfect for my taste. Had DH do this, and he must have overlooked that in making the sauce, 2 tsp of cornstarch should be placed in last,hence it became thick right away. lol  He also liked the chicken w/o the sauce so we set aside half of it to be mixed w/ sauce and the other half to be eaten as is. Thanks for a wonderful recipe, Anme!

Oh my godness. This was so good. I made a few changes though. I didn't have any honey so I put some extra brown sugar. And I added a dash of curry powder to the sauce. OUTSTANDING chicken! I made the recipe as is, but did double the sauce ingredients, 'cause I like it soaking-into-the-rice kind of thing! Oh YUM! This is so perfect! I love getting sesame chicken at chinese resteraunts, but it's not the same from place to place. Excellent recipe!  I love this dish, and usually have these ingredients on hand.  Thanks so much for posting!

I decided to make this recipe when I had some chicken breasts I wanted to cook up. We loved this recipe and will be making this dish often. I used 1 tablespoon sesame oil, other than that followed the recipe.  5 stars out to you Anne. Thanks for the great recipe.

It's a great recipe, my children enjoyed it! Thanks!
awesome recipe! so easy too! this was a huge hit w/ me and the kids. definately going into my favorites file.
Delicious!  Absolutely Deliscious!  It was so easy too.  I've made other Sesame Chicken recipes that were good but very time consuming.  This is quick, easy, and did I mention delicious!!!

Loved this recipe.  I used it when I had friends visit.  It was a big hit, I did not use five spice powder as I didn't have it on hand.  I added extra water to the sauch to ensure there was plent to pour on the rice.  I also added shredded broccoli and carrot.
This is so gooood!!!  I did double the sauce.  Otherwise, made as written.  Thanks for a great Sesame Chicken.

So quick and easy and so very good. I did have to make a few small changes for personal taste and it turned out fine. I decreased the ginger to 3/4 tsp. and the sesame oil to 1 tsp in the sauce. I will be making this one again. It would make a great quick meal for company. Thanks for sharing your recipe. Made for PRMR.

I really liked this recipe!  I made a mistake and did not read the directions properly and ended up marinating the chicken in what was supposed to be the sauce. I made as written except I subbed dissolved boullion instead of broth. DO NOT try this, as it makes the recipe too salty. My fault, but even so the recipe was great. My son wanted thirds of this (very unusual for the little man). Thanks! Can't wait to make again the right way!

This was really delicious, and the sauce was a thick dark brown the way you get it in a Chinese restaurant. Great for someone who wants to enjoy real-tasting Chinese food with no MSG!! :) I made mine with steamed spinach and stir fried Bok Choy.

This is delicious!  Better than most carry-out places.  I have used this sauce to glaze the chicken and bake it.  I have also used it for breaded and pan fried shrimp.  Very versatile (some weeks, I make it 2 or 3 times) and easy to make.

I made this recipe for a Christmas Party last month and it was GONE!!! I doubled the recipe too! I have since made it again for New Year's Eve and again, GONE! AWESOME!!!!!! This goes in my cookbook under favorites!!

This had great flavor! I did use the 5 spice but I used a little less than 1/2 tsp. I like the flavor of it but I feel it can take over a dish very easly. The sauce to this recipe is spot on.  Very good!!!

Great flavor to this recipe.  I did much of the prep work the day before. Made exactly as written - it turned out great.

This one got rave reviews!  Prepared as mostly directed, the only changes I made were to  double everything in the sauce except the Sesame Oil, I only used 2 Tablespoons total,  add several dashes of pepper flakes, and  several green onions.

I love anything Asian inspired, and this chicken came out so wonderful!  I loved the mix of flavors from all the ingredients, and this has been put in my "keeper" file for future use.  We loved it! Awesome!

Made as directed except omitted the 5 spice powder as I had none and I added fresh chopped chili in place of the flakes. This did taste like authentic chinese food but my sauce turned out very salty and not sweet at all.  I didn't use the sesame oil so maybe that would make a difference. It was a lot of trouble to make and very messy since I fried the chicken in 3 batches so maybe next time I would just use grilled chicken and add more sugar. Loved this! It took just a little longer to prepare, for me anyway, then stated. Definitely a keeper. :)

I made this tonight for dinner with white rice and some bok choy. The DH really liked it. I cut down on some time by making the sauce while I was cooking the chicken. I did have an issue with the chicken sticking to the pan so I'd suggest using a non-stick or cast iron. Also I skipped the green onion as I forgot it and the sesame seeds alone were a great garnish.

This recipe is definitely a keeper.  I never knew making Asian food could be so simple.  Like other posters I didn't fry the chicken but just cooked it in the pan with some vegetable oil and it came out wonderfully except the cornstarch seemed to cook off of it, I'll have to find a way to fix that next time.  Thank you for posting this!

I actually didn't do the chicken like the recipe called for, I just made the sauce. We liked the flavor and I loved that it made plenty of sauce. This was really good. So easy. I might make this with real ginger next time and a bit more pepper flakes, but otherwise it's a keeper!
Good, flavorful sauce and the chicken turned out very moist.  Next time I'd leave out the 5 Spice powder as it was a little overwhelming.
Very good! I enjoyed making what I have always enjoyed without the price tag..
Yummy recipe :) Definitely doubling the sauce next time

Restaurant Quality.  I doubled the sauce and recommend doing this. I used 1 1/2 teaspoons of ginger instead of the 2 teaspoons indicated after double the ingredients.  I will add 2 teaspoons next time.  I  used 2 tablespoons of sesame oil and increased the garlic. If you do not marinate your chicken you will lose some of the flavor but it will still be a good dish.  My DH said to make this again so that means MAKE IT:)

Sorry, but we really didn't care for this one.  I made as is except halving the recipe and leaving out the sesame seeds since we didn't have them.  The taste was nothing like restaurant sesame chicken.  Don't think I'll make again.  Sorry!

The kids and I thought this dish came out very good.  I made it as written except for omitting the sesame seeds (forgot them), pepper flakes (spice challenged daughter) and 5 spice powder (I just don't care for it). We really enjoyed this recipe.  I made half with chicken and half with tofu and both were very good.  I omitted the Chinese Five Spice powder as we do not like it, and served with brown rice.  It even got compliments from my picky eater!  Will be having this again.

Great dish. I made a minor adjustment. We don't like the five spice powder so we add powdered ginger and cinnamon to the sauce (2 of the 5). I'm really not sure frying the chicken is needed. I think it might be just as good with uncoated chicken. Great stuff, thanks.
This is my favorite sesame chicken recipe. I make it all the time. Delicious!

Overall this was a pretty good recipe. I didn't have time to marinate the chicken but I didn't feel like it was missing any flavor. Next time I'll either use low sodium soy sauce or cut the regular soy with water, thought it was a bit too salty for my taste. I will probably add a little more honey, we're used to a little bit more sweetness. Other than that, a great recipe!
Made this yesterday. Absolutely delicious. I didn't have the Chinese five spice so I used 1/2 tsp of ginger like someone else suggested...Thanks for sharing.

Delicious!  I made this for my family and we devoured it.  Its easy to prepare and it tastes just like our favorite restaurant.  I really liked the marinade for this dish, really makes it.  Thank you for taking the time to figure out the recipe.

This family favorite is restaurant quality for sure!  I followed to a tee but used extra garlic & sesame oil.  Paired it with brown rice infused w/garlic and chicken broth.  This will definitely be on my rotation.  Thank you anme for a wonderful 5 star dish!

I tried this a couple of weeks ago and just made it a second time per request.  My family loves it.  I advise using the Chinese 5 spice, and frying in a mix of peanut and canola oil - it really makes a difference.  I used 2 Tablespoons of brown sugar in the sauce because it wasn't sweet enough for us the first time, but my 4 boys like the chicken without any of the sauce as well.  I added blanched broccoli and fresh red bell peppers for color and texture just before serving.  It was every bit as good as what we eat at restaurants.

This is completely and utterly fantastic.  The sauce is exactly what you want when you want sesame chicken. I doubled the sauce and used fresh ginger, otherwise made as directed and served with fried rice.
Definitely need to double the sauce on this one. I added more honey and pepper flakes than called for. Really good, though!
YUMMY! I doubled the sauce but followed the recipe as written. Our kids got up and ate all the leftovers for breakfast, in our house that means it was a excellent :)

The five spice makes this dish delicious! I have been looking for that "missing Chinese flavor!" This tasted better than take-out!  I didn't have the suggested sherry wine so just added some red wine. It was divine! Thanks for a super recipe!

This was a hit at our house! I had to be away from the house for about 4 hours before supper, so I made it ahead and put it in my crock pot on the "keep warm" setting, and it was amazing! So tender and delicious! Served it with fresh steamed broccoli over rice noodles.

Great recipe anme, it certainly tasted restaurant worthy to us.  What a super recipe.  It was quick and easy to make with easy to follow instructions. I started preparations early to allow it to marinade for 8 hours.  So glad that I did, it had so much flavor.  The recipe was made exactly as written, but used a little less of the 5 spice powder (dh's personal preference only).  The chicken was perfect, moist and tender while the beautiful velvety sauce coated everything.  It truly tasted as good as it looked.  Thank you for sharing.

Very good, restaurant quality Sesame Chicken!  We successfully doubled.  Couple of minor changes: no cornstarch when we fried the chicken, and no five spice powder.  It turned out fabulously.  We will definitely make again :)

Followed directions and doubled sauce as suggested, over Jasmine Rice. YUMMY! Be sure to not thicken sauce too much before adding chicken for easier flow. We’ll be having this again. Thanks for posting!
This was delicious, I'd definitly make this again.

Yes, followed directions and doubled sauce recipe as others suggest. Steamed broccoli and tossed in extra sauce. But, only used about 1/2 amount of soy sauce. I also used drum sticks and baked them in the oven at 400 for 40 minutes after marinating them for a couple hours.

Made for DINING ON A DOLLAR, Feb.2013.  This recipe was a lovely surprise -- real homey, savoury, comfort food! I was very uncertain about the instruction to bake cabbage with the chicken for 45 minutes -- wayyy too long for cabbage, I thought. But this chef got it all right. I followed the recipe exactly as it was put down, using perhaps a little more veggies. The only very slight difference (which cannot make a difference to the outcome) was that I used a can of whole cherry tomatoes in their sauce (all I had). For seasoning, I used a local "Grill and Braai Seasoning", as McCormick is not available here. Adding ketchup to canned tomatoes is a great idea -- it intensifies the flavour. Taking into account that the contest list of ingredients was quite a challenge to work with, this simple dish was a great success with us. I was careful with the mozzarella topping, as mine was the common supermarket type, not the soft buffalo mozz. I added black pepper, and only left it in the oven to start melting, and then removed it. Thank you for a lovely home-style dish full of flavour and goodness! And good luck!

This was a good, wholesome one-dish meal! I made it with a bit more of the vegetables and half the meat (personal preference). I also prepared it with a bit less salt and next time would leave off the cheese, or perhaps use Parmesan.

As a lover of casseroles this one made a suitable supper for me with plenty left over for another time.  Chicken happens to be one of my favourite casserole foods but in this case I would have chicken breasts with a more suitable vegetable that makes up the majority of the meal.

Not sure how it turned out yet since its still in the oven lol I used potato instead of green peppers as I didn't have any. I also used garlic and curry to season with. I couldn't use the cheese because I didn't have that either! Lol it smells amazing tho and I can't wait to eat!!
The instructions are easy to follow and they turn out just like Starbucks.  The orange flavor comes through nicely, but I'm hooked because of the wonderful white chocolate morsels - yummmy!

uniquely GREAT!!!

-Delish..... made these 3 or 4 times. I bake them in a 12 X 18 X 1 cookie pan and only bake them about 20-23 minutes.This makes them thinner & more like starbucks. Easy to to follow recipe. Thanks for the great recipe.
I made this reciepe and it was so easy.I didnt have cranberries so I used cherry flavored crasins. I also added 4oz of cream cheese to the frosting instead 3 of I also added pecans. It was so amazing

This review is really just for the frosting and topping, which I used atop the easy version of these bars (I haven't tried these bars yet, but they look so good I *will* try them when I have a little time). Thank you for the recipe. Will make again.

I'm a huge fan of Starbucks' version of this so I was excited to try it.  For some reason mine were more cake like than the ones at the store. I cooked these in a 10 x 15 pan for 23 minutes, and all but the edges were a brownie-like consistency.  Thank you for a great recipe.

I used this recipe for work bake exchange and a family holiday gathering and got lots of compliments.  They are very rich.  I opted not to do the drizzle and they still tasted great.  Follow the recipe exactly to get them to be more of a bar consistency.  Let melted butter cool and blend sugars for 3-5 minutes.  It helps!

After having these from Starbucks I knew that I had to find a recipe to make them myself.  These are absolutely delicious and so easy.  I do not do the drizzle but chop up both the crasins and white chips and add them to the cream cheese as part of the frosing along with the orange zest.  Everybody just loves them and they are a new staple in my house!

If I could leave 10 stars I would. My daughter and I made them last night and they are wonderful. Oh, yes - we did share some and I'm waiting for the recipe request!

The Holidays begins for me the day that Starbucks put these out for the Christmas Season. I was very pleased by the taste. I cooked mine a little to long and they did not have the soft gooeyness that Starbucks has. Watch your time and next time I will actually take mine out about 5 minutes earlier.
