i used vanilla extract instead of orange. Since I used two tbsp of orange zest, so it still had the orange taste to it.  this dessert is very sweet, rich and yummy.  i'm anal and compared a lot of different recipes and am glad I chose this one.  Everyone liked them.
Not that close to Starbucks, I was a little dissapointed.  Baked for 20 minutes and they were dry, not the right consistency.

Oh, these are sooo good! I've never had the Starbucks bars, so can't compare. These were a bit  time-intensive, but so worth the impressive results. After cutting into triangles, I swirled pink-tinted icing over the tops for a lovely Valentine effect. The orange, ginger and cranberry flavors meld so wonderfully! Thanks for sharing this!
I made these 4 times in December.  They are wonderful.  I will be making them again for Valentines Day!  Can't wait to share them again.

These are seriously yum!  I haven't had the bars from Starbucks in many months so it's hard to say if they are exactly the same but they are wonderful for sure!!  I made them just as written but used a full size cookie sheet and only cooked them for about 16 min.  I will make these again and again!  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!!!

I just finished these to take to a potluck at work. I have to say that I'm a bit disappointed; they turned out very dry.  The flavor is all there if you can get past the dryness.  I went back over the recipe to see if I had missed anything.  I had followed it to a "T".  I might make again this year & cut down on baking time & temp.  I think they are worth a 2nd attempt due to the flavor.  If I don't get to it this year I'll try again next year for the holidays.

Exactly like Starbucks! They turned out beautifully, and tasted absolutely fabulous -- and so much cheaper to make than buying a tray of them at Starbucks. Everyone who tasted them asked for the recipe. My sister-in-law wants me to bring some to Christmas dinner. --Quite a compliment, since she's the best baker I know.

These are so good!  Taste just like Starbucks!  I made them twice and I think they taste the best if you let them chill in the fridge for a few hours to overnight.  I chopped the chips and berries that go in the dough the first time and the second time I left them whole and liked that texture better.  I left off the orange zest the second time and it tasted just as good.

What a disappointment!  Nothing like Starbucks Cranberry Bliss - while I had no problem with dryness and the texture was right on, I found the flavor dull and lacking.  I only made one change to the recipe - I softened and did not melt the butter, so it creamed nicely with the sugars, perhaps why the texture was good.  But so plain...not at all like the ones in the store.  Won't make again.

This is a GREAT recipe but for my family, it was way too sweet.

BARS
I cut the brown sugar from 1 cup --> to 3/4 cup
and 3/4 cup of white chocolate chips --> to 1/3 cup

FROSTING
I cut the 3 cups of confectioners sugar --> 1 cup

They tasted so much better with less sugar. I also don't plan on getting/giving diabetes anytime soon.

As for the texture, be careful as it will be dry if you don't cut the baking time in half! I baked mine at 350 for exactly 15 minutes and they turned out wonderful. Just as dense [although not as squishy] as the Starbucks version. If you want a clear sign, look for the brown at the edges, NOT the whole pan. I made this mistake the first time and they turned out a bit dry. I also creamed the butter instead of melting like one reviewer recommended.

Finally, do NOT skip out on the orange extract for the vanilla. Yes the vanilla is more common, but the orange, ginger, and cranberry flavor is what makes these bars so delish.

Overall this recipe is a 4.5, but since I had to make a few adjustments, I gave it a 4. Try it for yourself though!

Fabulous copycat! People may criticize the richness/sweetness, but it's no sweeter than the Starbuck's version. If you want a replica - this is it. If you want a low sugar dessert, you wouldn't be buying this at Starbucks anyhow.

I have had a craving for these for years, but after discovering my allergy to gluten, figured it was another thing I couldn't have. I weighed 1 c. all purpose flour and measured 135 grams. This is what I used to substitute my GF flours. I used brown rice flour (90 g), sweet rice flour(65g), tapioca flour (65g) & potato starch (50g)

Other than that change for my needs, I made one more. I added 1/2 tsp salt to the batter. I brought them to a party where there were a lot of gluten free eaters, as well as not. They were a hit with everyone. I do agree that using the orange extract yields better results.

I used an 11x17 baking sheet, sprayed it well with cooking spray and spread it out. I cut them into 2-3 bite triangles and it's just right.
Excellent recipe!  They taste just like the ones at Starbucks!  Good call on using parchment paper. It makes it easier to cut the bars and easy clean up.  I recommend this recipe to everyone!

These are so good and perfect for Christmas time, much better than the ones at Starbucks. I used 1 teaspoon each of orange zest and vanilla in the batter, and used a 1/2 teaspoon each of orange zest and vanilla in the frosting. The amount of sugar in the frosting seemed like to much so I used just half of the amount and they were perfectly sweet. Just make sure that when your melting the white chocolate, do it in 15 second intervals stirring after each one or it will burn. Thanks for the great recipe!

I made these tonight after having one of the "real bars" last week.  These are even better than the original bar and I will be adding them to my Christmas cookie list!  I used the 2/3 cup brown sugar as suggested and baked it in a 9 x 13 pan for the recommended time.  Thank you sooo much for this recipe!  Love it!!!

I have had this recipe on my To Do list for years.  Yesterday I finally got around to trying it for a casual dinner with friends.  I used my jelly roll pan, which I think is 10x15, half orange extract and half homemade vanilla in both the bar and frosting.  I cut the bars after they cooled, and then let my 6 year old and their 9 year old daughter frost them and sprinkle on the cranberries and orange zest.  I didn't do the drizzle; only because I forgot, but flavor-wise I didn't miss it. An absolute must-have, always works, go-to recipe!<br/><br/>A few tweaks--<br/><br/>Bars: go with 3/4 c brown sugar, then only 1 t orange extract in the bars + 1 t orange zest (about 1/2 of a  naval orange worth,) up the baking powder to 2 t<br/><br/>Frosting: only 1/3 t orange extract + 1 t orange zest<br/><br/>Topping: use any rind still remaining on the orange you've been zesting<br/><br/>This will allow all flavors to come through (the chocolate...cranberries...ginger) as well as the pop of orange.  Also, incorporating so much zest in the frosting helps it to be evenly distributed and kept moist (so the zest doesn't dry out and prevents the oils from escaping.)

This recipe is horrible and I wouldn't waste my time. At 500F with nothing to keep the chicken moist, you're going to dry out the breasts before they even cook through. You're going to burn the garlic (even the garlic in the picture is burnt) and probably even burn the sugar, too. If you're desperate for brown sugar and garlic flavored chicken, which sounds silly IMHO, coat the chicken in (uncooked   minced) garlic, olive oil, butter, and salt pepper. Don't heat it up, just mix together. Put breasts on a rack over a pan that contains onion, celery, and carrot. Put in an oven at 350F, cook until internal temperature is at 165. On a pan, make caramel out of brown sugar, and add a cup of chicken stock once the sugar is caramelized. Skim off fat, then deglaze pan with a touch of white wine, and put the fond into the pan with the stock and sugar. Add a tablespoon of butter to the pan. Boil and reduce until thick and creamy, then coat the chicken with the sauce. Now you have a chicken that has great caramelized brown sugar flavor, great garlic flavor, and the chicken isn't dry. One last thing: I didn't try this recipe. I've been cooking long enough to know what a bad recipe is just by looking at it, and I wouldn't waste my time and my money even trying this out.

Juicy, moist chicken, a sauce that is the best we've ever had! This fetuccini is the best ever!
Outstanding recipe!! This is the best alfredo sauce we've ever had. Loved it!! Thanks, we will make it a lot!
The best fettuccini ever! The chicken was so moist and tender, the sauce is sublime!! Thanks for a winner!

First rate! This is a really good recipe. It's very quick to make and was enjoyed by all.

I have to agree with everyone!  This was fantastic!!!

This easy and very good dish will be served at my house a lot! This is good!!

Excellent!  A great blend of flavors and very accurate instructions.  The chicken came out very flavorful and the sauce was rich and delicious. Absolutely wonderful!  The only change I made was to cut up the chicken and stir it in with the pasta.  Will definitely make this again and again!  And not only did I love it, but a family of VERY picky eaters loved it.

This was so delicious and the easy to follow directions made it so simple to prepare.  I will definitly make this again and again.

Excellent!  Inez, you've done it again!  I can always count on your recipes to be wonderful!  This has to be the best recipe I've found for fettuccini alfredo!  I'd give it more stars if I could!  I didn't change a thing... and wouldn't!  I served this with a salad and garlic bread.

What can I say after 40 reviews? We had this for dinner last night and it was glorious. I cut the chicken breasts into slices. The sauce was creamy but not heavy. I normally don't care for alfredo sauces at all.  I thought this was excellent, though I ended up adding a bit more cheese and a bit more dairy to stretch it for the enormous quantity of fetuccine I ended up making. Just wanted to add my 5 stars.  Great.

My entire family loved it!  My son says I should give it 10 stars.  Even my 'selective' eater begged for seconds.  The second time I made it I was out of cream and used half-and-half instead, but it still turned out fantastic. Thanks for posting it - it's going in our family favorites notebook.

Made this last night with spinach ravioli, my BF kept saying what a great dinner it was, with just the right amount of bam! Used fresh garlic, onion powder, and half & half.  Definitely a keeper recipe.

I wish I could give 10 stars for this recipe.  Its so wonderful you have to try it. the peppers are a great kick! made it for fathers day- it was a challange to make a big pot of it but it came out perfect.

Excellent, excellent dinner.  Followed recipe exactly as written.  Wish I had doubled the sauce.  The only thing I would do different is reduce the amount of garlic but that's just my personal taste, my family loved it with the garlic.

What perked this up to a 5 for me was the absolutely succulent chicken. I'm not a very experienced cook, so I was surprised that just salt, pepper, flour and butter could make me want more, more! I also cubed the chicken before adding to the pasta, since I only had 2 instead of 4. It's also hard for me to only put 1T of onion in a dish (esp. sauteed), so I used 1/2 onion, but next time a whole. I used tri-color pasta, which I think detracted from the alfredo flavor a bit.

I just made this dish and am giving it 5 stars, but mine turned out pretty poorly.  I'm giving it 5 stars because I must have done something wrong, plus I could tell that with some changes, next time it will be wonderful.

When a recipe calls for tsps or tbsps of minced onion or garlic, I assume they mean from a jar, not fresh, so that's what I used.  As we ate, the garlic was just overwhelming, and I think it's now oozing from my pores.. it was just too much.  Also, we felt there simply wasn't enough of the cream.  Even with the garlic, I could tell the sauce recipe was perfection, though.  I'll definitely make this again, but next time, I'll use more cream (double what the recipe calls for), less garlic (half of what the recipe calls for), and maybe more red pepper flakes (a couple of pinches more).

I made this just as directed.  It was so delicious and DH and I could not stop eating it.  I did add broccoli to mine, already steamed. Browning the chicken first in a little flour makes a big difference I believe.Thanx

This was great! The sauce was devine and the chicken was moist and tasty.  I really think the browning of the chicken after coated with flour makes this recipe stand out.  I did add alot more garlic to mine as we like lots of garlic!  Served with some crusty bread and white wine.  Thanks for posting.

I made this for supper tonight and it was sooooooo good!I did not use as much butter that it said to and it was still delicious. Fettucine Alfredo is not usually something my mom enjoys very much but she Loved this recipe! We were even talking about maybe adding shrimps and scallops instead of chicken next time!
What a great way to make chicken alredo!  This isn't dry at all.  It must be because of the flour step, it made the recipe a keeper!  Will surely make this again, thank you.
I made this for DH's birthday dinner and it was a huge hit. this dish was delicious. Thanks for posting it.
Wonderful recipe, and so easy! I halved the recipe and pureed the sauce for a smoother texture .. thanks!

Made only the sauce and put it over egg noodles, I didnt have fettuccini noodles. I loved the flavor of the sauce. However I did ammend it a bit. I used a pint of heavy whipping cream, added 1 tbsp of flour to it and added nutmeg. I think I over did on the nutmeg however. Next time I think I will just add garlic powder instead of fresh garlic, which is strange for me I am a garlic lover. Its just I thought the sauce had a raw garlic flavor, I think the powder would give it a more subtle flavor. I will definatly make this recipe again. Thanks for the recipe.
I make a couple of changes to this.  I use nutmeg instead of ginger.  So much better!!!  And, I normally use shrimp and also use fat free half/half to cut calories..

If I could give 100 stars I would!  Fettucine Alfredo is my all time FAVORITE meal and this was SO PERFECT!  The chicken was SO juicy and the sauce was absolutely incredible.  This is the ONLY alfredo I'll be making for a LONG time.  THANKS!
The flavor was very rich

This recipes was delicious!  The sauce was perfect and the chicken was very tasty.  I did not have 1 1/2 cup of light cream only 1 cup so I used 1/2 cup of half and half and put a little flour in it to thicken it and it tasted great! ill definently make this again!
Delicious! Not too hard to make and it tasted like it was right out of an Italian restaraunt. Personally, I add a little extra cheese, but other than that... fantastic!
Was a bit bland, needed something else.  Wouldn't make again
Easy and tasty.  I had to substitute marble cheese and whole milk for the cream.  (I added a bit of flour to the whole milk to thicken it up a bit.)  BF loved it and I enjoyed it too.

I think this pasta is just bland.  I added more salt and cayenne, but it still lacks taste... Remember to use a nonstick skillet to cook the floured chicken or else it'll stick in your pan very badly.

I really loved this pasta!  I used bow ties instead of fettuccine and it turned out wonderful.  I hope I'm not the only one when I say this...but what in the world is LIGHT CREAM?  (lol)  I looked it up online and I guess its a table cream with 18%-30% fat (for those that don't know).  I figured fat free half and half would work, but last minute I switched it up to whole milk.  AND WHAT A GOOD CALL!  For those of you using whole milk, don't forget to add 1-2 tablespoon of flour if the sauce isn't thick enough.  Also, if you really, really want the chicken to come out YUMMY, I would recommend using LAND O LAKES LOW FAT BUTTER.  I think my favorite part was the chicken :)  All in all, for those of you that want a quick and tasty, homemade alfredo recipe, TRY THIS ONE!

MizzNezz, you've done it again!  As my 16 yo daughter says: "You can't go wrong with a MizzNezz recipe."  I made this with Perdue pre-seasoned Italian style fresh chicken breasts, so I didn't use salt and pepper on the chicken.  They worked wonderfully in this dish.  The chicken already had some sort of Italian seasoning all over it, plus salt and pepper, so when I make this recipe again, I will use the same type of chicken or add some Italian seasoning to the flour.  A couple of changes I made out of necessity: I used linguine instead of fettuccine, I used skim milk instead of cream (I added two tbl. of flour to the butter, onion, garlic mixture) and I used a freshly grated 3 cheese Italian blend of Parmesan, Asiago and Romano instead of just Parmesan.  The ONLY thing I think this recipe needs is the addition of salt to the sauce and that is a personal preference.  Because some cheese is salty (especially the canned kind) and there is salt in the butter, it may be enough for some people, so taste before serving ;).  Thanks so much for posting this...this is definitely going into our bi-weekly dinner cookbook!
I am ashamed to say that I skipped instructions 1-9 and added a can of chicken in the end.  It was so awesome even when I cheated.  Thank you!
So yummy and so easy! I've made this several times and it has become one of my favorites!

This recipe was super easy and super tasty.  I used penne pasta, and added about 3/4 C peas, it looked fabulous! THe chicken was incredibly moist.  I served the chicken on the side, had no time to dice it up.   Next time i'm going to try shrimp for a summer pasta dish.  Thanks Mizz Nezz, as always, another great recipe!

loved this! we had it for lunch and it was delicious. did everything exactly except had no parmesan cheese and subsituted w/ pecorino romano...also only had heavy cream so had no choice but to use that. also a little less red pepper flakes just in case since my hubby can't stand even just the smallest amount of heat. great recipe! thank you for sharing another winner! =)

Had this for dinner las night. I was very good. My husbanc even liked it and he doesn;t like chicken. Will have again. I used reduced fat half and half and next tine will thicken it a little more, sauce was kind of thin. Real Good flavors.

What can i say? This is one of my personal favourites. i LOVE LOVE LOVEEE this recipe, i've made it so many times, with and without chicken. Perfect solution for a quick dinner. 5 Star Pasta MizzNezz Thanks!
My family didn't care for it.

This really does yield juicy chicken.  I followed the recipe to a tee (mostly), but chopped up the chicken and added it to the sauce, as well as adding steamed brocolli to the sauce.  To make up for the extra ingredient, I increased the light cream to 1 3/4 cups, and added a pinch of salt to the finished product.  Thanks for posting!
This was so easy and tasty and I will be making this again in the near future.
This was just wonderful. Added to my favorites!! Thanks!!
This dish was nice and easy! I added fresh mushroom slices and about two teaspoons of Italian spices to the sauce. It added a wonderfull flavor!

Simple, wonderful meal with lots of flavor! Only thing I will change next time is increasing sauce ingredients (perhaps by 2) because after coating the chicken there was barely enough left to coat the pasta. Even so, the family loved it!

NO CHICKEN in our house (veg-heads) but the alfredo alone was delicious. I'm a huge fan of alfredo but haven't made any this good for a long while. I also used a combo of whipping cream and half-n-half instead of light cream (Didn't have any)

I'll definitely make this again. Served with a caesar salad and everyone was happy!

Oh my word...this is the best chicken fettuccini alfredo I have ever made/had! My husband agrees with me as well. I made this for our valentine's meal, and it was perfect. We loved everything about this -- especially the chicken! This will be made again :)

Amazing!  Lovely easy recipe to follow with clear instructions.

thank you kindly for sharing a wonderful recipe.
Bravo 5 plus stars indeed!!

Very easy and so yummy. I grilled the chicken first. I used red onion instead of yellow and I sliced the chicken and added it into the sauce. So good and everyone loved it. This was my attempt at making alfredo sauce and it was so easy. Added a crisp green salad with garlic bread to complete the meal. A+!

Not sure what else can be added to the other reviews other then another 5 stars.  This dish was super easy to make and the whole family loved it.  I did skip parsley flakes as I didn't have any on hand but they only offer some visual interest therefore the dish didn't loose anything.  Also I increased the cream from 1 1/2 cup of cream to 2 cups and rather then using light cream I used heavy cream as that's what I had available.  Served it with some fresh garlic bread for completely fantastic dinner that was enjoyed by both children and adults equally.  Thank you for posting it here.  I have already added it to my cook book and will certainly be making it again.

This receipt was amazing! The only thing I did different was use heavy whipping cream instead of light cream. Great recipe. Everybody loved it. Thanks for sharing.
I love this recipe. Easy to make and my family loves it. I make it once a week. LOVE LOVE LOVE!!

This was good!  I cut up the chicken breasts into strips, but followed the recipe otherwise...will probably reserve this one for special occasions with the amount of cream and butter that is in it! When I poured the cream in, it came up eventually to flavor the sauce even more...

WONDERFUL! So delicious!  My husband LOVED the chicken and really liked the Alfredo sauce.
I used linguine pasta and added a little bit of cream cheese into the sauce.
FANTASTIC! Thank you!

Absolutely delicious and easy to make.  Perfect for a weeknight family meal, or for a dinner party. My only changes to the recipe were to use thin spaghetti, which I prefer over fettuccini...it worked beautifully in the dish. The red pepper flakes add that little kick that no one could quite place, but made the dish stand out.  This one is a keeper!
My man is a die hard alfredo fan and he loved this!

This was good. We like alot of sauce and this wasn't enough so next time I will adjust that part of the recipe. Also, I may try onion powder and garlic powder instead of minced to see which I like better. We will enjoy this again!

Really very good!  The seasoning on the chicken was perfect and the sauce came together very quickly, and tasted great!  Served as a type of Italian Noodle Bowl with chicken and broccoli on top of egg noodles with sauce poured over the top.  Everyone loved it, even my husband who claims not to be a fan of Alfredo.

Easy and tasty. I was attempting to feed 3 kids with a taste for the frozen ready-meal version, so I cubed the chicken, and then put it back into the sauce with the fettucine.  It was so good that no-one complained about the frozen broccoli I threw in near the end.

This dish receives the ultimate accolade - the eldest child will re-schedule her social life to eat it.
My step daughter is an alfredo "anything" fanatic.  This dinner was enjoyed by the whole family.  Definitely a must make again recipe
Was looking for a fast fettuccine alfredo recipe, made this with shrimp instead of chicken, left out the flour and parsley, came out fantastic.  It was devoured :) Thanks!
I made this tonight and it was AWESOME!  DH and DD loved it too (and DD is pretty pickey!)  Thanks so much for the recipe!
Made it last week and it was very good and easy to make.Thanks for the recipe!!

I made this into a vegetarian version by using the Quorn "chicken" breasts.  We cooked these in the oven for about 20 minutes, then sliced them up and put them on top of the pasta. We'll make this again for sure.

Let me preface this by saying, neither my husband nor I disliked this.  However, I found the sauce a tad bland except for its overabundance of garlic.  I really like garlic, but I thought that 2 tablespoons of minced garlic (I used fresh) was a bit much.  My husband didn't think it was too much.

The chicken was quite flavorful.  I used chicken tenders  so they were quite a bit smaller than full split breasts.  Just a tip for those who aren't used to cooking in pans that aren't non-stick, if you choose to use a pan that's not non-stick, once you put the chicken in DON'T MOVE IT.  Just let it cook and start to turn brown before you attempt to move the chicken around.  It will end up coming up by itself without sticking like crazy.

Overall, this was a nice meal, but not something that I would opt for often.  I hadn't realized how addicted I'd gotten to spicy foods.

I made this for our Valentines Day dinner.  I made as directed, except instead of the chicken I used shrimp.  This is a good sauce it just needed some salt and pepper.  I will make again using the chicken next time.  Thank you for posting.

This was good. I added real red pepper to it rather then flakes.
I also used milk rather than cream. I put in 2 tblsp of flour to the butter, garlic, onions after they were done cooking. That helped to thicken it since I used 1% milk. Anytime I hear "this is good mom" it makes it all worth while : )

Very good..my son had seconds.  I used a splash of chicken stock to deglaze the pan and then added the butter, onions, and garlic.  Thanks for the recipe!

I felt like the pepper really overpowered this dish.  I'd like to try it again with the red pepper omitted completely and perhaps with the addition of a bit of ginger.  I prepared this for 3 people, and all pretty much agreed the flavor was very distracted by the dominant heat from the pepper.

I made just the sauce for this recipe as my chicken smelled a little off so I was afraid to use it.  I made the recipe exactly as written except I did follow another reviewer's advice and added a bit of ginger and I used 1/3 cup of parmesan cheese.  It was very good and I'll definitely be making it again.  As good, if not better, than our local Italian restaurant!  Thanks for posting!

I just finished making this.  This is the creamiest, most flavorful alfredo I have ever had.  I did substitute melted butter and milk for the cream b/c I only had a little bit on hand. I also chunked my chicken, browned it, and added it to the sauce, but we loved this recipe. Simple, fast, and nice flavor. My husband is very picky and often calls food bland. He had no complaints and even went back for seconds.
This satisfied my craving for comfort food!  I Used shrimp and added mushrooms.  Thanks for a great recipe.

So yummy and so easy! I used a dry chicken rub instead of salt & pepper which gave a ton of extra flavor. Also, I chopped the chicken before adding it back to the sauce. My picky boyfriend loved it! Thanks for sharing!

Rich and delicious, we very much enjoyed this. I also cubed the chicken as we are not great meat eaters, in this was a little goes a lot further.   Quickly made, very nice for evenings when you want to spoil yourself a little.   Thank you MizzNezz!

I made this tonight and it was very good. I didn't see light cream in the store so I used 1 cup of heavy cream and 1/2 cup of 1% milk. Then, when it was time to add the minced onion and garlic I used a little less than called for. It was so good. I'm going to have to play around with the sauce because it didn't make nearly enough for us. I loved the addition of the red pepper flakes and my 1yr old and 2yr old cleaned their plates!
Really quick easy and yummy!
Terrific! Substituted half & half for the cream and it turned out no less creamy. Easy to make and very delicious!
a HUGE hit! thank you!

Let me start off by saying that I've never really liked alfredo sauce. Now let me tell you:  I LOVE THIS SAUCE!  This is the alfredo sauce that changed my mind. I was just a little disappointed with this. Maybe I was expecting it to taste a  bit like Olive Garden's version:) It was tasty, but I probably should have added a little more cream. Wonderful! I add spinach to the sauce to make it a complete meal. It was a hit!

This was a super easy sauce to make. I cut up some chicken tenders and baked them in Italian seasonings and garlic powder to give the chicken more of a taste. I also used more cream and cheese in the sauce. Added broccoli also. This sauce is the best Alfredo sauce i have ever had, and it taste better than any that I have ever bought.

This was fantastic!  I am not a big chicken fan but thought this had delicious flavor and very simple to make!  I used chicken breast tenders and after I browned them in the skillet I put them in the oven to finish baking.  I thought the sauce would be to thin because I used part regular milk too but it coated the noodles and chicken very well.
One of the easiest and tastiest Alfredo recipes I ever made. I added a little more Parmesan cheese. Thanks for posting it!
Good and quick to fix. Not a traditional Alfredo, but a nice creamy garlic sauce. Next time I'll increase the pasta and sauce since everyone wanted more. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Quick and easy, and it turned out delicious! Was fine with dried parsley.

This is so delicious! I used the bacon to wrap it, and the lemon juice. I baked one and froze one. I didn't use the cherry tomatoes but when I can get fresh from the garden I will. This would be very impressive for company. I'll definitely be making this again. Made for Please Review my Recipe. Thanks for a winning recipe FT!

Wow these are as every bit as good, as these reviewers have raved about! I only used 150g of cheese (the large one) for 4 breasts but it was still delicious.  Didn't need any salt for my family, and didn't have any lemmon on hand but will certainly add that next time.  I wouldn't usually think to serve tomatoes with something like this, but they are certainly meant to be together :D  Many thanks for a great recipe!
Gros bisou
This was fabulous.  I did use a lowfat spreadable cheese and it worked well.  My husband even it ate it in a sandwich the next day.

FT--You never disappoint!  This is one of the best chicken dishes I ever have had.  Of couse, how can one go wrong with bacon, chicken and Boursin? :-)  Delectable is exactly the right word.  I shall certainly make some for freezing and then will have an outstanding dinner party.  Thanks, Karen.

Divine! I can't descibe how good this was! I served with the tomatoes and croquette potatoes. I cooked the chicken for 1 hour and it was perfect. I made a sauce using the juices that came from the chicken whisked with left over boursin, white wine and some chicken gravy granules. It really made the dish come togather - thank you so much FT I will be making this very often as it is not only superb in taste but easy to make too! Tres Bien!

This dish is absolutely amazing, thanks for the suggestion to make the leftover juice to make a sauce. The only suggestion I could make is to turn the chicken 30 mins. in so the bacon on the other side turns golden
Fabulous!!  I increased to feed 7 people and it was perfection!!  The chicken is tender and moist and the flavors are just wonderful.  Thank you French Tart!!
Absolutly delicious and easy to prepare. Will make this again.
This deserves 10 stars, FT! LOVED it! Used Prosciutto for the wrap. Made for French Food and Foto Fun event.

This is hands-down the best chicken recipe I've ever had.  The flavor is incredible, and the bacon wrapping kept the chicken so moist and juicy.  I doubled the recipe and only needed 150 grams of cheese, and I used grape tomatoes rather than cherry.  It was outstanding.  Thanks so much for posting!!!

This recipe is fantastic!  It was recommended to me in the forums as a recipe that would impress and it did.  I used boursin cheese and a hickory smoked bacon (the thinner the better, I think). Don't be intimidated by the rolling and tucking. I got it on my first try. Easy prep for a wonderful meal.
