This gets 5 stars for being so easy to make, looking so impressive, and because it tastes so darn good!  This would be something to serve that would make it look like you slaved while it only took a few minutes.  Don't think it even took me the 15 minutes, more like 10.  I used some hickory smoked bacon but I bet the pancetta would be awesome.  Thanks for this one FT!

Made this last night after eye-balling it for a few weeks and it was awesome. Don't know why I waited so long!! Had to cook it a little longer to get the bacon to crisp up but the chicken was still moist. Added the tomatoes about 25 minutes into cooking and they were perfect. My only complaint was that I made only 4 for the 2 of us and today my husband and I are craving left overs. Just a tip, make more than you think because they are THAT good.

Oooh... where to start? Ok, I stuffed this with evelyn/athens recipe for Boursin # 80675, and omg what a wonderful meal this is! Skipped the tomatoes, and did use the lemon juice. This was incredibly easy to make, and certainly looks as though you've outdone yourself! I made sure I made extra for the freezer. What a classy presentation this makes! Thank you!

made this for dinner the other night and it was great! i would definetly recommend that you pop the bacon in the microwave for about a minute before so that it crisps up and you dont overcook the chicken
excellent! and simple to  make. i used lemon juice. served with organic quinoa and salad. thanks!

this was delicious and easy to make.  i rolled the chicken stuffed with boursin and wrapped in bacon and kept it in the fridge until i cooked it that evening.  i also suggest turning the chicken after 30 minutes.  my guests loved it.
This recipe had a very unique flavor but surprisingly delightful. I really liked it and will try it again.

I made this several weeks ago and my review evidently disappeared into the fourth dimension. (I think I've now learnt how to avoid that happening!) Because this recipe was such a delight to make and eat, that's NOT a problem as I remember it SO well. Check out the photographs if you haven't yet made this: it really is as delicious as it looks, and it's SO quick and easy to make. Wonderfully clear instructions, and I intend next time to make up more than I need and follow the instructions for freezing. I used pancetta and followed the advice of several earlier reviewers to add the tomatoes a little way into the cooking. As suggested, I spooned the excess Boursin and lemon juice sauce over the top of the chicken pieces and roasted cherry tomatoes. As others have said, a really top class chicken recipe, unbelievably easy to make - so great for week night meals and ideal for dinner guests Thank you, French Tart, for sharing this fabulous recipe!
I made this when I had some people over for dinner. It was very good and everyone loved it.

NEW VARIATION:
(First, let me say, OMG, this is good! But you already knew that, so let me share a variation I made tonight, instead.)
I left out the lemon juice and tomatoes, and instead soaked about 1/2 cup of dried apple slices and 1/4 cup of dried cranberries in enough apple cider to cover, while the chicken cooked for about 30 minutes. Then I scooped out the apples and cranberries, put them on top of the wrapped chicken breasts, and poured over about 1/2 cup of the cider they'd been soaking in. Back in the oven to finish. So very yum.

WOW....this was delicious and so easy! I cut 2 large, whole chicken breasts in half and used 1/4 of a package of Boursin for each 1/2. The pancetta wrap was perfect. I baked them for 45 minutes and they came out moist and wonderful.

Talk about a flavorful chicken dish!!!!  This is fabulous!!!  I bought chicken cutlets, so didn't need to pound it thinner and then used our local brand of garlic and herb cheese spread.  I then wrapped each chicken breast in two pieces bacon and left out the lemon juice.   Both DD and I give this 5 stars!!!  Will be making it often!!!  Thanks for sharing this FT.  Made for everyday is a holiday tag.

Delicious!!!  Soooo easy I almost felt guilty since they looked so nice and involved!  I used the lemon juice which really added a nice kick.  These were so good that the boyfriend cooked the frozen ones on his own (that's a big deal)
These were delicious and so impressive looking.  But the best thing is that they were easy, too - my 12yo made them!  This is a keeper!

This is great. I omitted the tomatoes and lemon juice.  I used the recipe for homemade boursin on here and loved it.  My company thought it was yummy too.  This is a keeper, now I always make a few extra and freeze them.

I have never written a review before but just had to for this great dish.  I am just no cook but needed to make something for a rather fussy dinner.  These tasted great and LOOKED like I really knew what I was doing!  I actually impressed people!

Tres Bon!  The flavors were wonderful and the presentation was lovely with the cherry tomatoes on the vine (my favorites). The aroma was wonderful as this cooked in the oven.   My family had this for Sunday dinner, but this would be perfect for company as well.  I will be sure to make extras next time to freeze.  Merci beaucoup for another fabulous recipe French Tart!

What an outstanding dish - beautiful AND tasty! I was dreading having to beat and wrap the chicken and feeling quite lazy so I compromised the recipe a tad. I used 4 thin cut chicken breasts and simply spread the cheese between the two slices then wrapped them in bacon and stuck in place with toothpicks. It turned out PERFECT!! None of the cheese melted out and everything stayed intact. I covered the bottom of the dish with frozen soybeans, 1/2 of a red onion, cherry tomatoes, sprinkled everything with black pepper and put it in the oven uncovered - stirring the veggies every 15 minutes or so to coat with the juices from the tomatoes and chicken and to prevent drying. Absolutely sinful!

This was wonderful dinner.  Thank you, French Tart!  Definetly a "make-again soon" recipe for our family.  They loved it.   Late this afternoon I had no idea what to do for dinner.  I searched recipezaar for "chicken, boursin cheese" recipes, and was thrilled when a French Tart recipe came up in the search.   This turned a "use what's in the fridge night" to a "Mom made something extra special" night.   The  changes I made were to omit the tomatoes, I didn't have any...and I wrapped each chicken with 2 "rashers", a British bacon instead of regular American bacon, because thats what I had on hand.  We all liked the rashers with it so well that we will use those again.   I spooned the juice in the pan over the chicken before serving.   Over the years, I've made several different bacon wrapped chicken dishes, and several chicken with cheese tucked inside dishes, but this is the best.  Unbelievably easy with "special dinner" results.

This was simple, and absolutely delish!  I had to make an adjustment, as I didn't have the boursin on hand, and wasn't going to brave the snow to go get it.  I mixed plain cream cheese with a teaspoon of my favorite herb blend, then let it sit for an hour or so before stuffing the chicken.  I wrapped with regular bacon, topped with salt, pepper, and lemon juice, and baked for 40 minutes.  I put it under the broiler for 5 minutes to crisp the bacon, which worked wonderfully.  I don't care for roasted tomatoes, so I left them out.  The smell from the oven while the chicken cooked was mouthwatering!  I could hardly wait to sit down to eat.  I'll definately make again, and likely for company as well as family.  The dish looks as good as it tastes, which is to say, amazing!  Thanks French Tart!
Husband and kids loved this. I used a cream cheese garlic herb mixture I found due to the boursin cheese being a bit out of my price range.Will make this again for sure.

Outstanding dish!  I used Court13's suggestion and cooked the bacon in the microwave for 45 seconds before hand.  I also turned the chicken half way through and it came out beautifully crisp.  Don't be afraid to use the lemon juice it blends so nicely with the cheese and drippings.  Served with roasted potato's, green beans and roasted cherry tomato.  Wonderful dinner and my dinner guests just loved it!
Wonderful weeknight or special dinner.  Good flavour, served with Skillet roast potatoes 171060

We're happy we tried this recipe that was recommendation by Chef #284180. It has lots of flavor, and it's very simple to make. We used stilton cheese with apricot bits, thick sliced tomatoes, and sprinkled a bit of thyme over top before baking. Thanks for sharing. :)

First time making a stuffed meat and this was easy and great. Thanks for posting, this is now my favorite way to eat chicken. My BF also stuffed the chicken with seasoned swiss chard (can also use spinach) and it turned out great.

I've made this several times (including tonight) and it's delicious!. I use fresh lemon juice and throw in a few grape tomatoes. Be sure to bake uncovered to crisp the bacon. My husband absolutely loves this chicken. Thanks for sharing!

I made this for our Sunday dinner last night and it was absolutely delicious.  I didn't have time to make the creme fraiche so I just used some sour cream and white wine and added some tarragon and parsley to the sauce.  It turned out very good.  Thanks for posting.

Thanks, FT, for a twist on an old fave. The addition of the boursin is fabulous! And what's not to love about bacon-wrapped chicken. I am glad to add this to my go-to list, for company, or just us! Thanks again, French Tart!
Great recipe!  I just prepared 24 of these for the freezer!  Now I don't have to worry about what to fix for company.  Thanks!

Out of this world recipe!  I made this for my family and they loved these little gems.  I can't wait to make this for my next dinner party.  The flavors all blend together so well.....yummy.  I served this with a rice dish and vegetables.  Thank  you for sharing this "oh so good" recipe.

This was so easy to make and turned out amazing!  My husband told me to add it to the regular rotation.  I made it with a homemade boursin cheese. and left out the tomatoes, lemon juice, creme fraiche and wine because I didn't have any - and we didn't even miss it.

Super easy prep for a great tasting & elegant looking chicken dish! The "15 min prep" is actually generous! My chicken didn't leak any boursin cheese to use in the optional sauce, however, there was some lovely bacon "juice" ;) with the roasted tomatoes (Next time I will add the tomatoes later into the cooking time as they became a bit overcooked too which could be my fault as I used the smaller grape tomatoes I had).  This is great without the sauce so you will not miss the sauce if you don't make it. I thought the sauce was a little disappointing compared to the chicken.  Since I am on a tight budget, I don't think the sauce was worth the value & will leave it out next time.  Since I cook for one, I froze the other prepared chix breast.  I'll come back & update the results!  I will definitely make more of these & keep them prepared in the freezer.  Thank you so much for sharing this super easy, yummy & OAMC-friendly(!) recipe with us! [Made & Reviewed for French Tart Appreciation Tag :)]

Great recipe! Very easy and a big hit with SO and his 14 yr old hard-to-please son. The cheese gave a great, intense flavor while the bacon kept the chicken moist! 5 stars for ease of prep! Thanks for posting!

A beautiful and delicious dish.  I used Pancetta rather than bacon, and could not find Cherry Tomatoes on the Vine, so just used Cherry Tomatoes.  This is a very rich dish -- delightfully sinful with the Boursin and Cream.  I served it with a roasted Potato, as suggested.  I was originally concerned that I did not offer another vegetable, but the Potato and the Cherry Tomatoes rounded out the plate well.  My only complaint is that it was salty.  I don't THINK I added any salt, but it is likely I did during one of the processes, merely out of habit.  My guests did not notice any saltiness.  I loved it.  Very rich, but a nice treat that is deceivingly easy to construct for the flavor and visual you get on the plate.  Bravo!

Ahhhhhhh! Relaxing in my recliner after finishing this superb dinner.  Each time I make a Zaar recipe I carefully read through all of the reviews & decide if I need to tweak the recipe.  The only change I made was to add the tomatoes ( some of the last ones of the season from my garden) during the last 30 min. of cooking time.  I did make the sauce although the chicken would have been absolutely fine without it.  I added in some extra tomatoes to the pan & mixed them up with some bow tie pasta & parmesan cheese to serve on the side.  "Wonderful"
This was delicious! The roasted tomatoes made a delicious sauce.

Just love it! I do not like to make them however,but the result it so worth it! Very good flavor,moist chicken,goes with almost everthing and looks lovely.I do use about 1/2 of the boursin called for and that works great for me.Also they are wonderfull cold with a salad and roasted sweet or regular potatoes.
Thank you for this wonderfull recipe,I will enjoy it alot!

This is a fabulous dish. I have been making this for several years now. You out did it with the sauce. (My hips are not thanking you.) The creme fraiche just throws it over the top. I have tried the wine before with just minimal success. I will be making this for years to come. Try Parma Proscuit instead of bacon. Also wonderful.

Simply delicious.  Even with some herb cream cheese (that's what I had) and turkey bacon it was good!!!  I used the left over cheese and some white wine to make a sauce which we drizzled over veggies.  Wonderful.

For me these were just ok.  I love Boursin, but I really couldn't taste the flavor of the cheese after the dish was cooked.  It was just like a plain chicken dish.  It was good, just didn't live up to my expectation.

This recipe is so simple and really is wonderful for the little amount of effort that is needed.  I didn't have boursin so I used a cheap tub of Garlic and Herb soft cheese from LIDL (69p) which worked great.  It was a 150g , so I used the lot which meant that some of the cheese was spilling out of the chicken when I rolled it, but it just created more sauce!  I didn't have cherry tomatoes so I used 3 large tomatoes quartered, which was lovely as the tomatoes and  juices cooked down into the sauce. I served it with slightly cajun flavoured potato wedges and mediteranean roasted vegetables!  Lush!!!!!!

Outstanding! It looks much more difficult to make than it really is. Ideal main course for a dinner party, but simple enough to serve on a weeknight. I was supposed take before and after pictures, but after taking it out of the oven we totally forgot. It looked soooo good, we just dug right in :) Thank you.
This made a great Valentines dinner.  It tasted elegant and the best part,it was easy to make.  I'll mark this as a company dinner.

When I saw the recipe I was thinking it could go either way - ie love it or hate it.  My husband dug into the dish first and said it is amazing!!  He loved the tomatoes.  They cooked up beautifully.  The only thing I did differently was instead of reducing the sauce with wine I used a little chicken stock.  It was absolutely amazing.  Thank you for a wonderful recipe.
Fantastic and easy.  Dinner party loved it - cleaned their plates!

The whole family loved this dish! Not an easy task in my household.  
I used garlic herb brie as the cheese, always seem to have that in frig.;)  Worked wonderfully.  I used San Marzano tomatoes cut in quarters to sub for the cherry tomatoes- boy were they delicious.  Donâ€™t get me wrong I loved the chicken but the tomatoes with the sauce were out of this world- I could have just eaten those and have a fabulous meal

This was very good, but I did take some liberties.  Used 'no name' garlic/herb soft cheese, which was excellent but might have been a tad too soft/melty.  And I subbed center-cut bacon -- the chicken was done before the bacon was crispy.  I will either broil briefly before serving, or  will try again with bacon the recipie calls for.  I used about 1-2 T. heavy whipping cream & a generous amount of white wine for sauce to get bits from pan, that was great.  Oh - one other item -- put 2x the cherry tomatoes you think you'll want in the pan, they go SUPER with this.  Thanks for sharing this recipie!

Made this and forgot to review!
Thanks to someone suggested in a thread, I can remember to do!
Delectable, restaurant quality dish made at home, seems like you did fuss, TRUE!
SO, simple, easy to do
Thanks!

Awesome, French Tart! I was feeling a lack of confidence in my cooking lately after a slew of mediocre dinners and needed to up the ante. I found this recipe and redeemed myself to my husband and toddler :) Thank you for that! I followed the recipe to a "T" and broiled it for 3 minutes at the end to crisp the bacon and pop some of the delicious cherry tomatoes. I didn't make reduce the sauce, but poured it over the chicken and side of risotto and spinach. A  From now on I'm going to you for truly excellent recipes!

Excellent.  I 1 1/2d the recipe for 3 of us and used 2 Tablespoons of heavy whipping cream that I had on hand with white wine for the sauce.  Delicious!  I can see why you make extra to freeze, that is what I intend to do next time.

Gorgeous! I found that the chicken needed a lot less cooking time, in my fan oven at 160 it took about 25 mins so maybe check your chicken before the end of the time specified here. I added some chopped baby leeks to the tray with the tomatoes and sprinkled oregano, salt and pepper over these, and some chopped thyme with olive oil on the chicken. I served the chicken and veg with a tomato risotto, a baby spinach and pine nut salad, and some garlic bread.  My guests loved it. Great recipe thank you!

This is an excellent recipe. I made it for a Mother's Day gathering of 8 and received rave reviews from everyone. I used the homemade boursin cheese substitute recipe that I also found on this website which worked out beautifully. I baked the chicken in a 400 degree oven for about 40 minutes and then turned the oven to broil for about 5 minutes to crisp the bacon. I didn't bother with the sauce and thought it was perfect as is.
The chicken was so tender and the flavors of the bacon and sauce were great.  I only had large tomatoes and can see the cherry ones would be better.
Followed the directions to a "T". The chicken was very tender and the flavor was great. I will definitely make this again. Very easy but tastes like you put in much more effort.

SOOO good and so easy!  I will definitely make this on a regular basis.  I used pancetta, and didn't  add any salt at all, and it was amazing.  I served it with rice and sopped up the sauce with foccacia and I STILL wanted to lick the plate.

great recipe! we loved the flavors.  i made it ahead and let my husband put it in the oven.  he put it in for the whole 45 minutes, so our chicken wasn't as tender as i would have liked.  next time, it will be cooked loooow and slooooow.

Words fail me. I made this today following the recipe completely, with the exception of the tomatoes since we have an allergy to them. I don't think I've ever tasted anything so comforting, so scrumptious, so rib-sticking, so delightful, so creamy, so heavenly... ever in my life. I'm food-drunk. I honestly can't thank you enough French Tart, and believe me when I say I will be following your every recipe. The only mistake I made was making a twice-baked potato, with shallots. The creme fraiche/white wine sauce on it was just too good. Can a person die from something being too delicious? I'm going to go lie down now as I'm in a food coma. This is the best possible way to go.

UPDATE: It's now been over a year or two since I first discovered this recipe. Still insanely delicious, easy, and my go-to for guests. Easily one of my favorite things to eat.

This is one of those recipes where I really want to be able to give half a star.  It was very good but  not one of my favorites.  When looking for a rolled/stuffed chicken recipe I'd probably just stick to a chicken cordon bleu instead, not because this recipe was bad but because we prefer it more.  I used prosciutto instead of regular bacon.

I love boursin cheese.  The dinner looked great and I was really looking forward to it after all the amazing reviews.  I made four breasts: two with prosciutto and two with bacon.  It was good but not great.  I would not go through the effort to make it again.
Made it tonight as a special dinner for my boyfriend's birthday. Delicious!!!  That is one dinner that is going to be added to the regular menu!

Absolutely FANTASTIC! This is probably one of the tastiest recipes I have rated on Food.com!<br/>I made mine with cream cheese mixed with fresh herbs from the garden (oregano, thyme and basil) and some black pepper.<br/>I was concerned that I hadn't 'tucked' the ends well enough but the chesse stayed put and the slices looked very elegant on the plates! Like others I broiled the last 10 mins to make sure the bacon was crispy!<br/>Easy enough for a weeknight but would be impressive to serve to company! <br/>Thank you for a true winner!

Absolutely devine! Was a huge with the fam and very simple to make. I used laughing cow garlic and herb wedges for the center (about a wedge per breast) mixed with some freshly chopped garlic for extra flavor. Used Applewood smoked bacon and cherry tomatoes and not only was the smell in the house while it was cooking enough to make our stomachs rumble and our mouths water but the flavor combination of  every thing was absolutely wonderful! Cooked it for 40 minutes with about 5-10 minutes broil time to cook the bacon further. Made a sauce with creme fraiche, chicken stock, and the remaining juices from the pan and it was all perfect served over fettuccine. Special enough for a dinner party, yet simple and quick enough to whip together after work on any week day.
This recipe is very good, but please NEVER thaw meats at room temperature or you risk food poisoning. Always thaw any meat dish in the refrigerator!

YUMMMEE I don't know why anyone would give the recipe anything less then 5 stars because if you cook well this recipe would be 10 at least. This recipe was our valentines dinner last night and it made me regret not finding last year. I should have added more tomatoes. I used home made cream fraiache and tripled the recipe thankfully because it wasn't that difficult to make yet we have enough for 2 more dinners and cannot wait. This recipe should be in every bodies house. Truly made our evening very very nice. I followed the recipe to a "T" I did sprinkle a a pinch of seasoning salt over the chicken. We loved this dish and it will be a staple.

This is a wonderful cake it not hard to make,and everytime someone eats it they taste one flavor more then the others.I had butter crisco on hand and that worked very well I thought that would make more buttery tasting but it didn't. I well be making this cake again.
This seems like the recipe that my aunt has made for years. It is also delicious without the glaze.

This is, without a doubt, the Queen of all pound cakes! The blend of flavors is superb. I used 6 flavors because that is what I had on hand (no pineapple). I increased the vanilla and almond to 1 1/2 tsp. because I wanted those flavors to stand out. I used real butter, pure vanilla and pure extracts if available. The glaze gives the crust a nice light crunch without adding too much extra sweetness. It actually soaks in so you don't even see it. Perfect texture--all in all the perfect pound cake, in my opinion! I also gave the recipe to a girl I work with and she made it before I did so I got to taste it before I made it. She loved it too, but she thought it was a little on the sweet side (I didn't think so, but it IS very rich). We both agreed that we will make it again. THANK YOU Sharlene--I will guard this recipe with my life!!
Another note: This made a large cake. I baked it in my stoneware fluted pan and it raised up and over the top of the tube. Next time I will bake it in my regular tube pan which has a taller tube.

Sharlene~W, I'm sorry you had to get this recipe at a funeral, but oh my goodness, I'm also glad you did. This is so good. I was a little confused by the first teaspoon of coconut, but on reading farther, figured you meant the extract rather than coconut. Also, this is a fail safe recipe. I didn't print the whole thing out so messed up in almost every way, but it still came out absolutely wonderful. This is a keeper by all means.
I have used this recipe for years it came from Watkins. Absolutely the best pound cake ever!

This was a very yummy cake! I didn't have any 'white sugar', so I added about a cup of powdered sugar (maybe more) to the mix so the topping was a little thicker. It still soaked into the cake, but it had a nice frosting on top. My family gobbled it up!! UPDATE: I used all 7 flavors (I got a lot of funny looks at the grocery store buying 6 of them at once, and nothing else), and it turned out wonderful!  I only had regular powdered sugar on hand, so I mixed a LOT of powdered sugar in the glaze mix and it made a great clear icing.  Everyone loved it!

Tried this recipe at BBQ party and it was a hit.  My husband even said it was a keeper.  I could not find butter flavour extract so I used orange extract and used real rum instead of extract as I had that on hand.
Thank you for your recipe, keep up the great baking.
Awesome recipe - didn't change a thing.  Pretty easy in spite of the list of ingredients.  Thanks for posting.

I couldn't wait till tomorrow to try.  Excellent!  I used 6 extracts I had on hand.  This is the best pound cake. It reminds me of that expensive frozen one.  Wonderful texture.  Nice crunchy edge.  Next time, I will use a loaf pan also to catch the almost overflow.  This is a keeper.  8-)

This is only the first night, and I imagine it will just be perfect by Christmas. I didn't have coconut or butter extracts, but used the rest of the flavourings, including almond, pineapple, and orange for good measure. I reduced the amount of sugar by half a cup, and by my recent samplings, it is just perfectly to my taste. I would never imagine that so many diverse flavours would work so well, but they seem to have melded quite nicely during the baking process. As mentioned, there seems to bake up a quite nice crunchy little crust on the outer rim of the cake. Next time I may add some chopped up toasted pecans to the exterior. This is really one of the best pound cakes I've ever tasted. Thanks!

When I made this cake and served a slice to my husband neither of us was impressed with the flavor. It seemed a bit 'off' and I made a note not to bake it again. I covered it and we didn't touch it again for two days. I was going to toss it but cut another slim slice for each of us. Both of us said the same thing...is this the same cake? It was so moist and tasty. The couple days of "ageing" had mellowed the flavors. The texture was improved and the cake turned into a "winner". We ate two more slices. It really was delicious! I will make this again, but be sure it is two or three days before I want to serve it!
I have a five flavor pound cake recipe but I decided to try this one, this tops my old recipe..Wonderful Cake.

This was a really rich and fragrant cake!!  I didn't have all the flavours that was required for this recipe, so I substituted some.  I didn't have coconut and lemon extract.  So what I added mango extract instead.  

I also doubled the mango and rum extracts for both the cake and glaze.  I wanted these two to stand out more.  

I tasted it on the first day, and i thought it was worth only 4 stars...BUT!  After 24 hours...my goodness!! All the flavours have come together, and it is a wonderful cake!!  5+ stars for sure!!!  

Do make this cake in advance, so that the flavours can come together.  You won't regret planning ahead.

This is a wonderful pound cake.  Very moist, very dense, very delicious.  I used almond extract instead of the coconut I couldn't find.  I used more butter instead of the shortening called for, otherwise followed it to a "t".  It's a great recipe!

I baked this pound cake this weekend and it was great!!  Pound cakes that I have made in the past usually came out dry but this one was very moist and tasty (I used the seven flavors).  My entire family loves this pound cake.  Will definitely make again and again.

This is my new favorite pound cake!! So moist and flavorful. Had it last week and just HAD to get the recipe. Was going to share here but then saw it was already posted. It doesn't surprise me because it is a wonderful cake. I know I'll be making it in the near future.

This cake is outstanding.  I served it today at my ladies' brunch, and it was funny how different ones of us could taste the different flavors.  I could taste the coconut over all the other extracts, but one lady tasted the rum and another the lemon.  Everyone loved it, and I'll make it again.  I made it this first time in my tube pan, and I'm glad I did because it would have been too much batter for my bundt pan to hold.  The syrup glaze that soaks into the cake puts this one over the top.  It keeps it moist and gives the cake added flavor.  Next time I think I'll substitute almond extract for the coconut (5 flavor) and see how it turns out.
This cake is wonderful!! I made it for our New Year's Eve party, and it was a hit. It will become one of my favorites going forward.
This pound cake has a wonderful flavor and is very moist and delicious.  I have made it several times and the compliments get better and better.  Thank you so much for a great easy to follow recipe.

This cake is so rich and moist.  My sister LOVED it and said it was the best thing she's ever tasted.  I, on the other hand, thought it had a slightly artificial taste to it despite using natural extracts when available and real butter.  The texture is velvety smooth and crumb is delicate.  Maybe if I use fewer flavorings, I can get a more natural taste.  Thanks for posting and I'll be sure to try it again w/ just vanilla, almond and lemon.

Definitely a cake that is to be made a day in advance. I cut it the same night and the flavorings were very strong.  The days after the cake got better and better.  A lovely cake to go with a cup of tea!  Thanks for sharing.

Delicious light flavored pound cake!  If I just had to say, I think I could taste the coconut over the other flavors.  The cake is moist and beautiful!  I actually shared it with my parents and my Dad said that I had to leave most of the leftover cake with him, which I did (I am a good daughter! LOL!)  It does make a lot of batter and it rose to the very top of my bundt cake pan, just barely not running out!  Next time, I will probably leave some batter out and make a few cupcakes or whatever, as one reviewer mentioned!  Thanks for a keeper Sharlene W!

I wouldn't have believed it if I hadn't tried it for myself. The extracts sound like they would be gross together, but they are really good! This is a rich, dense pound cake and the glaze really makes it moist. My only issue was that I sprayed my bundt pan with canola spray and the pound cake stuck to the pan. I think next time I will try the grease and flour method. Maybe my oven was a bit on the hot side or I cooked it too long. That is possible, too. BUT this recipe is so good that I will keep trying until I get it right. Thanks for a good recipe and GOD BLESS!

Very good pound cake, we enjoyed this very much. Very easy to make and then end result is a very light and moist pound cake. Well worth getting all the extracts. I will be making this cake again. Thanks Sharlene~W.

Some body needs to slap me, because I forgot to review this "OUTSTANDING" Pound Cake. How could I have forgotten after the first bite to run straight to the computer and give this at least "50" stars. Pound cake is probably our most favorite indulgence (sweet that is ) :-)
The hard part was to wait until the next day to try it! I have thrown out (pst) it is my sister-in law's recipe. Will never try another one. I made it as stated, used butter crisco for the shortening and also used Almond extract. (6 Flavors). I realy though it would all overpower, but others said it was sooo good, that I am glad I tried it, ...again...and again... one in the oven right now!! LOL Ingrid

VERY good pound cake! This was my first attempt at a pound cake and it turned out beautifully - except it did stick to the pan, but that is because it is an awful pan, nothing to do with the recipe. *Note: If you life in a high altitude like I do (3,500+), add 2 tablespoons of flour to the 3 cups of flour in the recipe. Worked perfectly! Thanks so much!! :)

What an interesting flavored pound cake.  I saw this months ago and couldn't wait to try it.  I made it a couple of days ago to use with Recipe #76627.  It made two full loaf pans of cake.  I used one for a dessert at home and saved the other for Saturday to use with the kabobs.  I trimmed the crust off the cake and cut it into cubes.  It was dense enough to hold its shape very well.  I would say the flavor to me was kind of tropical..I could taste the coconut and rum extracts in a dominant way.  The flavor went well with the margarita dip in the recipe I used.  Truly a great cake to use.  I'd love to experiment with other extracts in the future. Pam

This is a wonderful, moist dense poundcake.  The flavors are a bit overwhelming on the first day, so like most bake 1 day ahead if possible.  I think I taste a different extract with each bite--sometimes its the coconut, other times lemon, but no matter the flavor it is always delicious!
A lovely pound cake that makes the house smell wonderful
I really like the flavour but found it a bit too dense. I reduced the sugar by half and next time I will increase the baking powder. Other than that the flavour was surprisingly yummy!

Simple, but very flavorful. My husband took it to a potluck at work, and it was a hit. They had fun trying to guess all the flavors. The recipe makes a LOT of batter, so I also made six cupcakes. It definitely gets better with a little time.

This pound cake had the best texture and baked up nice and high. I substituted almond extract for the butter flavour extract. I found the glaze added too much extra flavour and created an unpleasant aftertaste so I will omit it next time. Thanks!

i baked this cake ,at first i did not like it,after a couple of days passed i loved it.i sliced some up and took it to work and one of my co-worker begged me for another slice,one told me that i did not bake it that i bought it.i was shocked myself how moist it came out i was expecting a heavy cake..it was perfect..i will be making it again..
This was really fantastic.  I made it dairy free using margarine instead of butter and soy milk instead of milk and it still tasted fantastic!  This has become my new pound cake to make

I was baking one evening before we turned on the heat. I was tired so I didn't make the glaze but I think it was really good without it. I cut it into large pieces and froze them, that worked out great. I will be making it again, probably for a potluck or something because it does make a large cake.

I have cooked this pound cake many times and the recipe was handled down to me by my mother.  She cooked one every week and it was known as her specialty!  She always added a small drop of yellow food coloring which made it look so rich.  The glaze is delicious, but the cake is also good without it.  Thanks for sharing this recipe to others.  It's a winner!!!

I did the 7 Flavor variation - twice this week. The cake is wonderful. It's been shared with many people who loved it. My only criticism is in preparing the pan. I used a Bundt pan with a nonstick coating. The first time I followed the recipe to the letter. Parts of the cake stuck to the pan, leaving a delicious cake, but an ugly presentation. The second time I greased and floured the pan and it came out perfectly. So, I srongly advise to grease AND FLOUR. I also agree with other reviews that the cake needs to be made at least a couple of days in advance to give the flavors time to blend and mellow before it is served. This cake is now one of my standards for potlucks and other group functions. It is great! Thanks Sharlene.
Update:  Today I used Kittencal's Pan Release (#78579) on my Bundt pan for this cake.  Got the best results yet.  The cake looks perfect and not a crumb was left in the pan.  Thanks again for this recipe.

This is a very good pound cake. It has the same ingredients as the 7up Pound Cake with the exception of all of the flavorings and milk instead of seven up. I made two cakes out of this batter. I made one medium bundt cake and one large loaf cake and there was plenty.

The idea of using this many extracts is very fun! I couldn't find the pineapple extract so I did the 6 flavor- I hope to find it someday! I made this for a Christmas party I am going to tonight & I baked it 2 nights ago so it should be perfect. I was one egg short after I started so I Googled what to swap out for an egg & it said 2 Tbs of Cornstarch or a Banana I ate all our bananas so I used cornstarch in place of 1 egg. Also I was nervous seeing all the comments about "using a larger bunt/tube pan the next time" so I poured some batter in a small loaf pan- I wish I hadn't because it could have used that extra batter, the cake was a little small to me & all would have fit fine in my Bunt pan -Oh well. I used the Crisco/flour method & it came out of the pan perfectly. I did put the glaze on it, I liked it both ways but I really liked the glaze on it!! I have a cute daisy cake pan w/ the flowers raised up I think I will put it in that next time since this cake doesn't use icing- Perfect! I cant wait! Thanks!!!

I've made this pound cake several times now and it is by far the best pound cake ever! I like watching people's faces when they taste it because they can't quite put a finger on the flavor. I've had nothing but rave reviews on this recipe. Thanks so much for sharing and allowing me to do what I love best and that's feeding family and friends with yummy food.

Amazing cake. The flavors meld to form a completely new taste. Instead of a glaze, I just used a sprinkling of powdered sugar. I had some Blue Mountain coffee saved for a special occasion, and it was heavenly with this scrumptious treat.
This was a wonderful dessert....went well with my oriental theme...

This was a HUGE hit with me and my girls.  I made the 6 flavor cake and I originally made it for a cake wheel at school, but while baking my girls caught a whiff and asked me to pleaseeee keep it at home.  I couldn't argue with them, it did smell good! lol  So mommy made another cake for the wheel and we kept this one! lol  This one will be made over and over, and I'm considering making one with fruit flavored extracts...like strawberry, banana, etc.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

WOW!!  I just took this cake out of the oven and it smells absolutely HEAVENLY!  The batter was awesome, so that means that the cake has to be as well!  Thanks for the recipe, and I'm 100% sure that I will be making this over and over again!

This cake was very easy to make and was enjoyed by all.  I changed the icing and made it with powdered sugar and warm water and added the 5 flavors as described.  Make sure you have a big enough bundt pan.  Mine was a little too small and it rose out of the pan but didn't leak over.  It baked perfectly in the recommended time.  I will definitely make this again.  Thanks!!

This is the most flavorful, tender pound cake I've had in years! I had put off making it due to the grocery list of ingredients, but I assure you it's worth every last one! I screwed up and forgot to pour the glaze over the cake while it was still in the pan, and but did it once it was out of the pan and cooling and it still came out perfect!  Thanks for posting.
This is my co-workers favorite cake! They always request it for their birthdays! It's absolutely easy and delicious!

I substituted buttermilk for the milk. Boy oh Boy, is this pound cake out of this world. It rose so high and the crumb is tender and moist at the same time...not dry like most poundcake. There is a light crust on the outside which I love. The combination of flavors is awesome. It is wonderful even without the glaze.  What else can I say except that this is the Perfect pound cake!!! Keeper for sure. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

I went to add this to the Zaar but found it already here with all the stars & glory it deserves.  5 stars for 5 flavors!!! Everyone that tries this loves it.  I think they at first think they'll be getting a slice of dried out ol' pound cake, but HAH! Out comes the flavor and moist texture of this truly divine, humble cake.
Wonderful flavor. Made glaze with the same flavors.  Took it to work and had excellent reviews
Great flavor in this pound cake.  I didn't have butter ext. so used almond and it was great.  I didn't make the glaze but served with fresh strawberries.

An okay flavor, but the consistency was not as nice as my best pound cake recipe that I have always used.  I will probably try this one more time if I make it just for me, but will not make it to take other places.

This brought back great memories as my mom used to make this when I was younger.  I made it yesterday for Mother's Day and took it to her house for our family meal.  Very delicious cake and so moist.  Bake time is right on too for a perfectly browned crust.  Thanks for sharing your recipe!

This was popular at work when I brought it in for a birthday.  I just loved the browned top that got nice little crunchy bits.  All the flavors worked great together, you wouldn't think so, but they certainly do.  I creamed the butter and sugar for 7 minutes, I think many times people cut that step too short.  I also poked small holes into the cake before pouring the glaze, that helped to really get it into the cake.  Last time I made a pound cake it was a flop, but this one was great.  I am hanging onto this one.

I have had this recipe for years, no summer barbeque is complete without a pound cake. I sometimes make this a 6 flavor pound cake by adding almond favoring. This is a family, holiday and cookout get together favorite.
Very good! This is an excellent recipe and is even better the next day.  Thanks for sharing!
My husband enjoyed this cake but I did not like it. It was too light and fluffy for my taste, more like a store bought pound cake. I like my pound cakes heavier. Won't make again.

Definately KING OF ALL POUND CAKES!  Ohhhh my!  I wanted to make the 7 flavor version, but could not find any pineapple extract at the store so only could make the 6 flavor version!  I was worried, when I first pulled out of the oven because . . .it was very brown on the outside.  I ended up not doing the full hour and half as suggested or it would have burnt.  Otherwise though, this cake was SUPER MOIST, and FLUFFFFFY!  Loved it, got lots of compliments at the family reunion - and will be making it again!   It's awesome!  Thanks for the great recipe!!!
www.seraphinos.com

This pound cake has the best texture, although it's a little too sweet for me (I already reduced sugar to 2.5 cups, with no glaze). I might try to reduce sugar a bit more next time. I also made some other changes: 6 eggs instead of 5, evaporated milk instead of normal milk, 1 tsp salt (could have added more), butter flavored shortening instead of the regular one.

The cake tastes better and better as days go by. the lemon flavor is more pronounce than the other four. Besides being a lil sweet, this cake is perfect!

Because my first attempt rose too much, this time I filled my pan 3/4 full and added the rest to what looks like a shallow slightly flattened bundt pan.  I took the short one out of the oven at about 30 minutes and baked the other for the full amount of time. . Both cakes were moist with a very nice crust. Delicious! The full size cake, I took to the office where it was promptly inhaled. Mahalo Nui Loa, Sharlene

I have made this cake several times. My mom decided to retire from making a pound cake after she taste it. I tried it in a bundt pan as well as a 10' pound cake pan. The bundt pan turned out drier than the regular pan. Other than that, the recipe is great!!!

I really don't know what can be said about this cake that hasn't already been said .....but wholly - hanna...this is unbelievable!!!!!!! I'm so thankful I took it to work or I would have eaten on it till it was gone.....And believe me my co-workers were glad too....Everyone I work with raved and of course wanted the recipe...So thanx so much for sharing

This is the best pound cake I have ever made or ate. The flavor is wonderful and it is so moist. It lasted 2 days here. My husband has asked for the chocolate version of this. I am going to make it for him today. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

I needed a  treat to take to neighbors as a "thank you" gift, and this cake was perfect. The recipe made 8 mini-loaves, which cooked for 56 minutes til done.  Next time, I will make 1-1/2 times the glaze recipe to cover all of the the sweet little loaves. I love the texture & flavor - will definitely be making this again and again.  Thanks for sharing!
I think the cake is great however when I made the icing it never got thick! It looked like tea. I also used whipping cream instead of milk and it turned out super good and fluffy.

I made this cake for the first time this past Thanksgiving and boy was it a hit!  I made it exactly as the recipe stated with the four flavors and they blended perfectly. The crust had a very nice light crunch and the glaze made the cake pop even more. This is by far the BEST pound cake I've ever tasted! The next time I bake it I'll double the glaze recipe and shave approximately 10 minutes off the baking time. Thus is a must try recipe!!!!!
4 stars only because Recipe #91644 is a better pound cake.
Wonderful recipe!!
I made this cake I ight using my cream cheese pound cake recipe I looksand smells delicious I can't wait to cut it

I would normally bring a cake to work once a week and this was the one i made the last time. Followed the recipe as written and everyone kept saying how flavorful and good it was. i immensely enjoyed mine with a cup of coffee.
This is a tasty meal - simple to prepare and nutritious, and allows for a lot of customization (i.e., trying different meats, vegetables, etc.).  Highly recommended!

What a produce saver.  I was already baking and realized I had some bananas that were about to be tossed and stumbled on this recipe.  I used 2 very ripe bananas and 2 Red Delicious apples, shredded with peels on.  I also added 1/2 t salt, 3/4 t cinnamon(habit, i guess) and baked in 4 disposable mini loaf pans for 50 min.  Excellent.
Very moist and fragrant.  Combinations of fruit are endless.  Thanks for the posting.

I prepared this recipe using 2 small Granny Smith apples and 2 medium bananas, and baked it in a bundt pan (bakes in about 45 minutes).  It turned out great and is very moist and flavorful! I will definitely use this recipe again.
This was a very good and 'banana-ey' bread.  The apples made it very moist... I followed Deborah's additional spice additions, and it came out fantastically.  Baked in 45 minutes in 4 mini-loaf pans.

I'm always looking for recipes that use up things like the last banana that no one seems to want. This fit the bill very nicely one day, I used more cinnamon than that since I am a cinnamon freak...

Thanks
This bread taste so good... I just made it and love it.A must try recipe:) Thanks!

I had 3 very very ripe bananas and two apples that were about ready to pitch.   I came across this recipe and it was a nice change from plain old banana bread.   
Thank-you,  a nice little surprise snack for my husbands coffee break!
What a great recipe! My husband made it a couple days ago and again today.  We also added an additional banana. We will be making this often and sharing the recipe.  Thanks!
OH MY!! This was soooo good.  My husband absolutely loves banana bread and this had just the right amount of banana flavor.  Thanks for posting.
this was sooooo good, even my husband who is pretty picky eater liked this. Will definitely make this again!
Definitely needs 1/2 tsp salt. I used 1 1/2 apples and it is alittle moist for my liking. Good taste, however. Carole in Orlando

This bread is great and so easy to make. I made some subsitutions because I was out of some of the ingredients. Instead of sour cream I used 1/4 cup of sour milk, instead of cinnamon I used 1/2 tsp of cardamom, and instead of walnuts (my ds doesn't eat nuts) I used raisins. Even with these changes the bread came out fantastic and we all loved it. I will definitely be making this delicious bread again.

I made this bread to take on an out of town trip to a football game where several other couples were joining us.  Everyone loved it.  It's moist and not too sweet.  I especially liked it in the morning with my coffee.
This is terrific bread. I would only add that after baking, one should let the bread cool in the pan for 5 to 10 minutes and then turn it onto a cooling rack.
This turned out really moist and favorful.  Quiet easy to make. I added chocolate chips. and sprinkled with icing sugar. Great for morning coffee break. Thanks.
With a sister in college in WA, I made this and sent it to her!  She left me a VM thanking me profusely - Thanks- it travels well!
A nice tasting banana bread, good for morning tea. Thanks

I agree that this bread is delicious! It's moist but light, and the cinnamon flavor is just enough to add interest but not overpower. I baked it in 4 mini pans which tested done in 48 minutes. I used 2 Royal Gala apples and 2 medium sized VERY ripe bananas. I think this would make a great dessert cake. The next time I make it I'll sprinkle 1/2 cup of chopped pecans in the bottom of a bundt pan (they'll bake into the top of the cake to make a nice topping), and I'll also add a praline glaze once the cake has cooled. (Glaze - Mix 1/2 cup of packed brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter in a saucepan over medium low heat. Cook, stirring, until the mixture starts to boil. Boil gently for 1 minute, stirring constantly, then remove from heat and continue to stir for about a minute until the glaze is smooth. Pour over the top of the cake and let it dribble down the sides.)
This bread was moist and delicious!  It smelled delicious while it was baking.  I added just a touch of nutmeg to it too.
I will make this again and again. My 3yo nephew pronounced it "dewicious" and we all agreed with him. I used egg and sugar subs. Next time I'll try FF sour cream. Thanks for a keeper.

I had three very ripe bananas and four very small apples, so I increased all the other ingredients (except the butter) by half, and baked the batter in a greased bundt pan and a loaf pan - not a very tall loaf because I made sure the bundt pan was full.  (Both baked in approx. 50 minutes.)  Excellent banana bread - the apple adds a little nice flavor and I think the sour cream helps as well.  I also added a bit of salt and nutmeg, and more cinnamon, and subbed one cup of whole wheat flour for unbleached flour.  I froze the loaf so I may edit this after I thaw it.  Please try this bread, especially with cream cheese!

I'm not generally a 5-star giver, and this came close!  It is a very forgiving recipe.  I used 2 Fuji apples instead of the regular baking apples, with peel on (you won't notice once baked) and chopped them randomly.  I also accidentally dropped about 3 TBS of cinnamon into it, omitted walnuts, used 4 egg yolks (b/c that's all I had on hand), baked it in a shaped bundt pan for about 55 minutes, and it still ended up OK.  I liked how idiot-proof it was and will make this again in the future.

Yummy!  I didn't have any apples, so I added an additional cup of flour and used 1 cup of cinnamon applesauce instead.  I also sprinkled a crumb topping on it before I baked it- so it was more of a coffee cake than a bread.

I baked these as muffins - made 18!.
Used 3 bananas and one grated apple - primarily because that is what I had. I think next time I'll experiment with crushed pineapple.  A versatile recipe.

I altered this recipe for my diet and replaced the brown sugar with Splenda's brown sugar, and the white sugar with the Splenda baking sugar, I used egg beaters for the eggs, and whole wheat flour for in place of the regular flour.  I did not have walnuts so I added some dried cranberries.  This recipe is a no-fail recipe!!  It is AWESOME!!!  You do have to watch the time. My loaf was done in 45 minutes.  Thanks Jen T for such a great, but simple recipe
Great recipe Jen T!! Wonderful texture that wasnt too much like a cake, and not too much like a loaf. I made this for the family and it has been devoured now :) Thanx for posting!!

This was baked in a ceramic loaf pan.  Equal amounts of sugar and Splenda were used.  The bread was done in about 50 minutes and while it was good warm it was even better after standing overnight.  The apples were a combination of gala and granny smith and pecans were used for the nuts.  Very good and moist.

This was so good.  I used a suggegstion from the comments & baked it in a bunt pan, added pecans to the bottom & then put a glaze over it....YUM!!  Thanks a lot for such a great recipie. Mine cooked in 45 minutes though.

Fantastic Stuff: I made this at my daughters house and we are both hooked.  My grandson who claims he is alergic to fruits & vegetables loves it. I added more cinnamon and graded orange peel.  I bring one into work once a week and it disappears in seconds. Thanks a bunch.

I made this with one large chopped Royal Gala apple, and 2 bananas. Baked in a 9" round pan (40 minutes) and a mini loaf pan (45 minutes), and both came out nicely done. Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe.
I had some overripe bananas one day and I made this! My whole family devoured it and asked me to make it for the holidays,(even my dad who's picky).Awesome recipe!!!

this bread is sooooo yummy!! 
i love it!

my whole family loves it too.
i will definetley be making this again.
my one complaint is that it crumbles when i cut it! idk why it does, maybe it was me, or maybe it was ther ecipe.
but besides that minor flaw this breaad has no complaints in my book! =]
Great - so moist. I used 1tbsp sour cream and 3 "eggs" of eggbeaters so it is lower calorie.
This was so moist, super easy to make, it was more of a dump cake when I made it because I was being lazy and it turned out perfectly.

I made this as muffins instead of bread and brought it into my classroom of kids.  There weren't any left by the end of the day so obviously it was well received!  I used one banana, two large red delicious apples and replaced the nuts with raisins.  I also subbed the sour cream with a small container of vanilla yogurt as I had some to use up.  I think it made about 15 muffins.   This was a nice change from your ordinary banana OR apple bread- a neat combo of the two.

I have several apple trees in the yard and I needed to find more recipes for apples so they didn't go to waste.  I had some over ripe bananas and decided to make banana bread...got on Zaar and ran across this recipe.  Boy!  This was awesome!  The apples, nuts and cinnamon gives it a Fall taste.  Some banana bread recipes I have tried were too "bread" like but this one is sweeter and more like a snacking cake.  I noticed there wasn't additional salt in the ingredients and contemplated adding a little...glad I didn't, it was just right without it!  This is one banana "bread" that I will keep!  Thanks, Jen!

A very, very good bread.  My only hesitation on giving it 5 stars was the flavor - it tasted very similar to other breads of this nature, nothing that knocked me out of the park.  However, it was extreamly moist and easy to prepare.  Made mine in a bundt with grated apple, and would do it again doubling the recipe to get the full height of the pan.  Definitely a solid recipe!

Loved this bread! The apples make it so moist. I used a glass loaf pan and the edges were pretty dark at an hour - though it did not have a burnt taste at all, I think I could have pulled it out 10 or 15 minutes earlier. Thanks!

I just made these! How delicious! I followed the recipe with a few exceptions, #1 I used my mini chopper to almost puree the apples, my kids won't eat things with "chunks". And #2 I made muffins instead of a bread, this way they can go to school in a lunchbox pretty easily. The recipe yielded 16 muffins, and I baked for 35 mins and they were perfect!
YUMMY!

This recipe made for a nice and light muffin. In the end, I used two ripe bananas and two grated pears.  I substitued the chopped apples for grated pears since I never really have apples in my house. I omitted the walnuts, as well, and the bread didn't seem to be missing anything. My picky two-year-old loved it.
got lots of compliments

This is a fantastic recipe!  It's easy and delicious.  I used a round tin to cook it in as well and found that the bread cooked very evenly.  The second time I tried it I used 1/2 cup of splenda instead of the white sugar and it worked out fine.  I also tried replacing 1/2 of the nuts (find they tend to dry out the bread) with chocolate chips just for fun- very yummy!

This is a very good banana bread recipe.  I am not really a fan of banana's thus not a big banana bread eater but this recipe rocks!  Followed the directions exact but used 3 banana's instead of 1 and it turned out moist and delicious.  The family loved it.  I will be making this recipe again and again and again.  Thanks for posting!
I followed the recipe as written and it was wonderful. Very moist and flavorful.
Lovely and moist! I'm sorry but you just gotta have butter and sugar sometimes! Baked it in a bundt pan  for 45 min. Will try the praline topping that someone else suggested. Yum!

Fabulous!  have made this 3 times in 2 weeks!  made as is the first time and thought it was great but the last 2 times added 3 apples and 2 bananas, with a pinch more of cinnamon, a pinch of nutmeg, ginger and salt... sooooo goooood! 
thanks so much for this delicious recipe :)

Awesome!  So tender and oh so delicious!  I did use Banana extract instead of the vanilla for a more banana flavor.  I also used sadielady's idea of the praline glaze, yum!  Thanks for a delicious recipe!
I mad it without the sour cream, added one banana and substituted 1/2 cup flour with granola mix. It cam out delicious! Thanks for sharing

This is the best bread I've ever made!!  I am making it as Christmas gifts for everyone this year because it is soo good!  I didn't have sour cream at home so I just changed it to milk.  I also added 2 bananas instead of 1 and a 1/2 tsp of nutmeg and dash of salt.  LOVED IT!!  Oh, baked it in a regular sized loaf pan and it took approx an hour.

I've had this recipe since March, 2000. This is a delicious bread! I doubled the recipe and made two 9x5 loaves, and the only change I made in the ingredients was to use pecans (which I had on hand) instead of walnuts. It is great for breakfast, lightly toasted with a little butter. Great for tea, gifts!

OMG!! This is so FREAKING GOOD!!! I just made this recipe for a quick breakfast tomorrow morning. I substituted the sour cream for vanilla yougart (I happened to have it on hand) and substituted the butter for canola oil. I also didn't have brown sugar so I mixed my organic sugar with a table spoon of Black Treacle (molasses). I baked these in HUGE muffin tins that I have and WOW! I can't wait to surprise my DW when she comes home. Good Job Jen T!
Delicious!!!  I was looking for a good recipe to use our orchard apples and some old bananas I had.  This was perfect.  Moist, dense and full of flavor.  YUM!
Moist and flavorful!  Thanks for sharing.
Very nice bread!  I made as directed except that I did use light sour cream and did not add nuts.  Made for Aussie Swap #36.

just made this bread, except I used Splenda, light butter, fat free sour cream, two bananas, fiji apples, whole wheat flour, and no nuts. My mom raved about it and I love it too. Thank you for the inspiration.

Excellent bread. I had 3 ripe
bananas so used all of them plus 
the two apples. This recipe is great!! Moist and delicious and
I definitely will make this one again. Thank You!!

This bread was really delicious, but perhaps a bit too sweet for my taste. I also added 1/2 tsp salt as per the other reviewer's recommendations. I think next time I will find a way to decrease the amount of added sugar, as my bananas and apples were pretty sweet to begin with. Made in mini loaf pans, and baked for 15-17 minutes.

LOVE it...moist but not wet, different with the addition of apples and just delicious.  I cut the sugar almost by half and used all regular (unbleached) sugar since I didn't have brown.  I doubled the bananas which added natural sweetness.  I doubled the recipe and cooked half in a loaf pan, half in a bundt pan.  I would check them before an hour if you do not like baked goods well done.  I happen to like them this way so it worked out for me.

Delicious!! I've made this twice, the first time following the recipe exactly and it was PERFECT. The bread was gone in a day and all my roommates begged for more! The second time I made it, I didn't have enough butter so I tried it with veg oil. Just pulled it out of the oven, and it didn't rise correctly (I'm just a beginner so I don't know why), but my boyfriend said it still tastes fine. I'll stick with butter from now on, but will be making this often!!

I made this using 1 apple and 2 bananas instead.  Also, didn't have walnuts, so I used pecans.  It was awesome and very moist.  I made the loaf this morning for "breakfast" and it was gone by 1 p.m.!!  (I shared with my husband, of course).  YUM!

love this. have made it over and over again as muffins usually with 2 bananas and one apple. i like to add a little extra cinnamon and a tbsp or 2 of honey. next time i'm going to try with wheat flour and a crumble top for the muffins.

totally wonderful! have made this twice now, (on request) made them into small loaves, using "throw-a-way alfoil trays. Took some to the hospital for Sam to munch. She "says" she hasnt got a sweet tooth, but told me not to lose this recipe!
It is a very sweet loaf, so the small slices were just right. The grand-girls (2 and 4) wanted theirs with butter.
2nd time around I chopped the apples smaller, and added a little more cinnamon. this is a true keeper for me, and Samantha, (I will make her rate it too )
made for Aussie swap july 2010
My first banana bread. It was very moist and tasty. Will make again.

Very good although I made a lot of changes. I added 1/2 tsp salt, used only 1/2 cup dark brown sugar and left out the granulated sugar completely. I also used 2 very ripe bananas and 3 very small apples. I subbed sour cream with heavy whipping cream (what I had at the time). I also added only 3 tbsp of macadamia nuts (didn't have walnut). The level of sweetness was just right for me. Next time I will add 1-2 tbsp more nuts. My baking time was about 50 mins.
Delicious & easy. First bread I've ever made & it turned out wonderful. The apples added a little extra to the traditional banana bread.

I subbed applesauce for the butter, used Gala apples, added cinnamon, nutmeg & cardamom; used Sucanat and cut the sugar in half, used 1/2 ww flour and 1/4 cup wheat germ. Made four small loaves. wish I had remembered to add some salt, but very tasty.

Love this recipe
I used Yogurt instead of sour cream
And skins almonds instead of Walnuts

I made this as written, but I cut the apples in large chunks (as it wasn't really specified in the recipe.)  It looked very pretty and was moist and very tasty.  I'll add a little salt the next time and  use "pumpkin pie spices" in addition to the cinnamon. As one of the other bakers did, I'll leave the peels on the apples, too. Thanks for posting.

Just tasted my bread and it's delicious!  I mixed in about 3/4 cup whole wheat flour, used two bananas, coarsely grated my apples, and replaced walnuts with pecans.  The mix was enough for two slightly less full loaf pans.  Cooked for 45 minutes, they came out so moist!  Will def make again.

I have made this sauce twice. The first time I used homemade meatballs (ground beef based) and pepperoni as the meats and deglazed the pan with about 1/4 cup Cabernet Sauvignon. I added 2tbsp brown sugar as I thought it was bit acidic with only 1tbsp. The sauce had a nice taste but I thought it was a bit thin. This time I browned 1lb of ground sirloin and some turkey pepperoni and deglazed the pan with water (only because I was out of red wine). I can't really tell a taste difference between the batch with wine and the batch with water, probably because I used such a small amount of wine. This time I only used 1 15oz can of tomato puree and used that 15oz can to add water, to keep the sauce very thick. I added the ground sirloin to the sauce and cut up 2 slices of the turkey pepperoni into the sauce (ate the rest! :) ). I minced 3 cloves of garlic into the pan drippings, and though I would like more (love garlic!), DH says that's a fine amount. I did not add the salt in the beginning, but added it to taste after the sauce simmered a while, as I had salted the cooking sirloin and DH doesn't like sauce "too salty." The sauce is very thick with a smooth taste. I actually prefer "spicier" sauce and my use of italian seasoning is a bit more liberal than 1tsp, but my family prefers smooth and mild and this sauce got compliments when I served it to company, who asked for the recipe. It is a good all-purpose meat sauce - I've used it to top spaghetti, to make lasagna, baked ziti, and when I made it without meat the first time I used it as a base sauce for a pizza casserole. I think it is better the second day and beyond, after it sits and the flavors have more time to "meld." I am not really a fan of pork italian sausage (due to the fat) but suspect that would give it more flavor than my version with beef due to the spices in italian sausage, so I may try turkey or chicken-based italian sausage next time I make this. Of the sauces I have tried from Zaar, my DH prefers this one.

Wow! Amazing brownies - I would only eat the Ghirardelli chocolate chunk brownies...until these! They are SO easy to make and don't dirty a bunch of measuring spoons to make either.

WOW! Not like you really need another review on here, but...these were fantastic! I added in chunks of Reese's PB cups and Hershey's Kisses. So rich! Next time I plan on doubling the recipe because one tiny pan just isn't enough!

This recipe is a little tricky with the baking time.  It will depend on what kind of "whatever" you put in.  I put in 1 3/4 c marshmallows and a 4 oz box of cookie dough bites candy.  I spread it out, but maybe not as carefully as I should.  Like a few of the other reviewers, I found it difficult to cook the brownie evenly.  My brownie has a small area in the middle that is underdone, but an area to the side of it is definitely baked to borderline overbaked.  So though it is common sense,  you should spread your "whatever" very evenly and depending on your oven, rotate the pan every so often.  I ended up cooking mine for double the stated baking time.  I also used aluminum foil at the bottom of my 8x8 pan, b/c I wanted to save on a few calories.  Haha, it was a little slow getting the foil off, since I did not grease anything.  Anyways, as far as brownies go, it's as good as any store bought mix and maybe even better.
