Great recipe!  We all enjoyed it, expecially my son.  I added a little paprika with the seasonings.
I mixed the spices in with the spinach and used minced garlic instead of powder ... WOW .. it was GREAT!  This recipe is a keeper, for sure!

Great recipe! Made it for my parents when they came over and it was a hit. Plus, if you have any extra chicken tenders from another recipe, you can follow the last two steps to make a quick snack for the office the next day. This is the first recipe going in my newly created cookbook.

Oh yum!!!  We loved this chicken.  I decided to bake these rather than fry them so I ended up dipping the stuffed chicken breasts first in one bowl containing a whisked egg and then in another bowl of the spices plus 1/3 cup bread crumbs mixed together.  Then I baked them for 45 minutes at 350.  WOW -- this is just a fabulous recipe!

I made this twice now.  The first time I used boneless thighs.  It was good but messy.  Tonight I made it with the boneless breast.
I added a little minced garlic to the spinach both times and some extra tomatoes tonight with a little mushroom.  It is just plain good.  BTW when I made with thighs I followed the instructions and then cooked about 15-20 min longer at 350 in oven  Thanks Dancer!  I am Diabetic with a goal of getting off the meds with diet and excercise. Finding yummy recipes like this help me stick with the goal!!
Sandra

Dancer, as usual a fabulous recipe!  
I can not believe I forgot to rate this and I even took a picture of it..  (though not the best quality pic.)  My hubby adored it and we recognize it as a weekday or weekend meal and a fantastic "company" dinner recipe... elegant, delicious and quick and easy, leaving time to    be able to enjoy your company. Loved it! 
Thank you for sharing. Aug 7/09  just an update I have made this many times and we still adore the flavor explosion!  thank you
This was good! We made as written and also had to cook an extra 10-15 minutes. Thanks for sharing.

So good!  It's messy to make, but it's worth it.  This chicken is filled with flavor, super-juicy, and looks great on the plate.  It's probably a good idea to cook the breast for longer though, because cooking chicken for that short amount of time can be a health hazard.  I doubled the cooking time, and the chicken was still moist and delicious.

Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe. Simply awesome. I followed the instructions as it is. I had cooked it in a small skillet one at a time. I cooked 4. Only change I made, at the end I put one tea spoon pesto & whipped cream, sprinkled chilly flakes. It was so juicy & succulent and super delicious. My children loved it. I shall make it again and again.

I agree with you- these are the best buns that I have made, too.  I used freshly grated nutmeg in place of the mace, and did the refrigerator-rise method.  Just heavenly- the tart cranberries are wonderful, here.  Thanks!

These were amazing! I hate when cinnamon rolls are just bread in the middle without much stuff. NOT a problem here! The filling was tasty and substantial and the topping worked into the rolls themselves. They were beautiful on top, very nutty and caramelized.  The cranberries added a nice change of pace.  They stayed moist for two days in a covered pan.  15 seconds in the micro to warm them up and they tasted almost out of the oven.

***** Wow. THE best sweet dough I have ever made. It's perfect. I got a new food processor that came with a dough blade. I had my doubts but gave it a try and, believe it or not, it worked beautifully. I may try to make the filling and topping more decadent (not that it's really needed)but this is definitely my future sticky bun recipe. Thanks, Mean Chef. Outstanding buns.

Utterly wonderful. I particularly enjoyed the fact that they aren't super-sweet.  Not sugary icky, but caramel.   Perfect for adults.  And kids.  The distinctive difference between these and many other sticky bun recipes is the dough.  The mace adds a whole new delicious dimension.  Anyone looking at this recipe--MAKE THEM. 
:-)

These were great.   I used orange zest instead of lemon simply because I love the flavor of oranges and cranberries.   I also used the cinnamon instead of the mace.   To reduce the sugars, I replaced the sugar in the filling with Splenda and used Splenda brown sugar for the topping.

This is a delicious sweet bun, with lots of good stuff!  I couldn't find fresh cranberries, as I made these the first week of May, and there are no fresh cranberries in the markets here now.  So instead I subbed dried tart cherries.  I used the lemon zest option.  I think I got confused with the topping/filling instructions, so I ended up just combining the nuts, dried cherries, lemon zest, cinnamon and nutmeg all together, and used it both for the topping and the filling.  It came out beautifully.  I will have to try this again in the fall when fresh cranberries are available, because that could only make this better.  I especially love the softly spiced sweet dough!
Thanks, kiwidutch!

I made this recipe for PAC Spring 2009. The chicken nuggets were so simple and quick to make and tasted awesome on their own and with the yummy chili sauce. The sauce was also simple to put together and had a great tangy taste that went perfectly with the chicken nuggets. Awesome recipe, I will definitely be making these again soon!!
Delicious, and very easy. I left out the water, and added about 1/3 cup of tomato sauce. Served with rice to soak of some of the delicious sauce.

This was quick and easy to prepare. I used butter and since I ran out of Tabasco I added a little Vietnamese Chili-Garlic sauce to make 1/4 cup. The sauce was tasty, and so was the chicken, but they didn't really want to stick together, because the sauce was too thin. I will be working on this to see how it can be thickened or made to stick better; it will be well worth the effort.

Really delicious.  I used not a hot sauce, but a thick hot wing sauce (I forget the name, but it's supposedly by the guy who invented buffalo wings). First of all, I wanted a lot of sauce, so I doubled the sauce amounts.  I added only half of the water called for, based on Jenny Sanders' comments (which were very helpful).  After putting it all together, I tasted it, and decided that we needed more heat, so I added several shakes of Tabasco.  I baked it exactly 25 minutes, and it was great - very tasty, and super easy.  I'll make this for the 2004 Super Bowl party.  The only other thing I'd do differently is to put in about half of the butter, and keep the extra water out.  Great flavor, and a recipe I'll definitely make again!

Made this for my husband who like hot wings and he loved this dish. I made it as is and removed the chicken from the sauce and broiled it to get a crispy skin. Poured some hot sauce on it after it came out and I was begged to make another batch!  Will be making this again!

This was very good. I followed B2B#2's suggestion and it worked very well.  I doubled the meat in the recipe and still had enough sauce.  The only thing that I might change is to marinate the thighs in the sauce before baking. Thanks for a great recipe!

I made it and it was good. Although I did adjusted it a little bit. I added some brown sugar and honey to make it a thicker sauce. But I like my sweet and spicy. Another thing you can add is a packet of Italian seasoning. It makes it hot too.

This received rave reviews from the two gents I served it to. I added a bit more hot sauce and only one tablespoon of water. I followed the other reviewer's advice and broiled this after. This was easy to make and was very tasty. It is also much healthier than the deep-fried variety. Thanks for a keeper!

Absolutely great! Made this tonight with Franks Red Hot sauce. I lined my baking dish with foil and sprayed it with cooking spray for easier clean-up. Next time I'll double the sauce. Thanks for posting such an easy, tasty recipe!
This is a really great recipe! My bf and I are addicted to wings and really appreciated this recipe! thanks!

I love that "buffalo-wing-taste"! It was nice to have that same flavor with the bonus of having more chicken meat with the boneless thighs. I used Frank's hot sauce, it is my favorite. Great recipe. Thanks!

These little gems were delicious.  I like buffalo wings, but don't care for the chicken skin on them, so these were perfect.  I used Frank's hot sauce, and the flavor was just right; a lttle bit of heat, but not overpowering.  Great dipped into blue cheese dressing.

Yummy!  I used bone-in skin thighs on as it was what I had in the freezer.  I browned them in canola oil and seasoned with a bit of garlic salt and pepper.  I cooked them in a foil pan on the BBQ since it was still 90 degrees on November 3 here in Southern California.  I covered the pan with foil and cooked for about 25 minutes, then removed the cover and basted every 5 minutes for about 15 minutes more.  Super yummy!!  I will totally make this again, and I may make a bit more sauce for the basting stage.  Served with a crispy romaine heart salad with chunks of celery, green onion and tomato that was dressed in a creamy and cool ranch dressing.  Outstanding recipe, that you for sharing!
This was amazing, everyone loved it. Served with blue cheese dip and butter mashed potatoes. Wonderful.

This is an excellent recipe for chicken thighs. I don't usually like cooking thighs, but this recipe has changed my mind and I will keep them on hand. The flavor of the sauce is pretty subtle, so this recipe is great for people who don't like spicy food. I used bone-in, skinless thighs that I seasoned before browning, only 2 T. of butter and 1 T. of water. I think next time, I won't add any water and maybe try just 1 T of butter, just to get a little more zing from the hot sauce. Thanks so much for posting, we loved this recipe and plan on making it often.

Great recipe. Quick and easy. But most importantly a family hit. The chicken was delicious and fell right off the bone.  I used Frank's buffalo sauce which was perfect for this recipe. Such a great dish. Highly recommended.
It was very Yummy!!
This is yummy. I used Frank's Hot Sauce. I followed the recipe exactly. I will be making this again. Thanks for sharing.

This was GREAT! I used bone-in, skin-on thighs, but next time I'll use boneless skinless because the skin was a little fatty and gummy. I preseasoned the chicken with garlic salt, Mccormick Rotisserie Chicken Seasoning, and Mrs. Dash Chicken Seasoning. My boyfriend said the seasoning really added something special. I also baked the thighs without browning them in the skillet, which worked fine. 350 for 30 minutes, then I added the sauce and turned the heat up to 450 for 15 minutes to get the skin golden. I used Frank's Buffalo Wing Sauce, and next time I'll leave out the butter and the water because all they really did was thin down the sauce. Delicious! The boyfriend told me I should definitely save this recipe for later. Will make again ,maybe for potlucks and parties !
Made it just as shown, delicious! Served with seasoned rice, celery sticks, and bleu.

I had bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, and I wanted them cooked faster, so I sprinkled with a little garlic salt and fried for closer to 7-8 minutes per side to crisp up the skin and speed up the cooking. Instead of hot sauce, I had Food Lion "buffalo style wing sauce" (super cheap and plenty tasty). Put the chicken on a cookie sheet, coating both sides of the chicken in just the sauce (no water or butter), roasted at 400 for about 10 minutes (used thermometer). My husband raved about these thighs! Will do again, paired with veggie pizza. No more Domino's! Some reviewers complained about the runniness of the sauce- no problem here. I omitted the water and butter and used the thicker sauce, and the thighs turned out nicely coated.

Great recipe. Only change I made was that I basted the chicken with the pan juices halfway through the baking time. I served it with fresh carrots, celery, blue cheese dressing, and roasted sunchokes. This is a tasty way to get that "wing" flavor without frying and with more meat.

I intentionally looked for a recipe that used boneless chicken thighs that would be baked. That being said, I was disappointed. I could've made some tweaks but that wasn't my intention. This would probably be ok for someone on a one of the new fangled diet but this wasn't what I wanted. I miss the extra crunch, the bolder flavor and a more appealing looking dish, ie there won't be a photo. ??

This worked great!  The soup mix, pepper and garlic powder were the perfect amount of seasoning.  I left the house to do some errands and forgot to turn the crock pot down to low, but the recipe is very forgiving.  Our turkey breast was ready a bit early -- but perfectly done!  Thanks for a great alternative to the oven.

Another great recipe from kittencal!  Can't go wrong here!  Thanks for the new spin on this yummy turkey!  It took 5 1/2 hours for a 6lb'er and they ate seconds and even thirds.  :D  (Shhh...I even snuck in some finely chopped mushrooms without my son noticing.  Hehe)

How easy can fixing turkey be? I had a frozen 6 pound turkey breast and I rubbed the canola oil over it and then rubbed it with Lipton's Herb and Garlic dry soup mix. I put it in my crockpot, covered it with foil as the top wouldn't fit snuggly and put it on high for one hour and low for 8 hours and it was heavenly! Had enough broth to make about 2 cups of gravy and a nice moist turkey breast that everyone loved. Thanks, Kittencal for another fabulous recipe (so easy it was sinful!) Carole in Orlando

Cooked a whole chix this way.  Came out nice and moist.  Next time I'll try a couple of whole chix breast.
Thanks!

I made this using a boneless turkey breast filet (the store calls it a Turkey London Broil).
I still marinated it for 24 hours (in a ziploc bag) and other than the cooking time itself and adding a small can of chicken broth to the crockpot when I started it I changed nothing else. I used the high setting on the crockpot for around two hours then reduced the temp to low for another two hours. I used Knorr Onion Soup Mix and my only extra touch was a little paprika and a tiny bit of fresh rosemary. It came out wonderfully. It was juicy and flavorful and I just thickened up the juices for the gravy. What a super recipe and a nice change from roasted or grilled turkey breast filet. Thank you for this versatile new recipe!!

Terrific!  I wasn't sure whether it mattered if I used a boneless or bone-in turkey breast.  I used a 6-pound bone-in breast that barely fit the crockpot.  The only problem I ran into was that it finished cooking MUCH sooner than I expected -- I had planned on it taking seven-plus hours, but it was done in five hours.  (Really done -- no joke.)  Delicious, moist turkey -- I just wish I had more leftovers!  Thanks for posting this.

This was excellent, and still is 4 days later.

My turkey did not fit in the crockpot, and I put foil over the top like a reviewer suggested and cooked it in there the first hour and a half.  I then wrote Kitten that that's what I was doing, and she was nice enough to hold my hand, and guide me thru roasting it the rest of the way in the oven instead (yes, I'm 60, and this was only my second try at fixing a turkey breast).

I was told it would probably take 2 1/2 hours in the oven, BUT remember it had started cooking in the crockpot.  I tested after about 1 1/2 hours or so, and it was done.  I put it back for just a few minutes to brown, but was afraid it would be too dry.

It was absolutely moist and delicious upon coming from the oven.  I let it cool slightly, and put it in the fridge, so I wouldn't forget it and let it totally ruin.  I warmed some pieces the next day, and it was delicious.

I can't wait to get a larger crockpot.  I want to try it exactly as written, BUT I can assure you if you put it in the oven, in a pan, and let it cook in there until it's done (like 2 1/2-3 1/2 hours for a 6 lb. turkey), it will be wonderful.

Thanks, Kitten, for all the help on this one.  I love(d) it.
This turkey breast turned out perfect! It was super easy and the result was moist and delicious. We will make this year-round. Thanks for posting!

This was good and easy to make. My turkey breast was only 3 1/2 pounds but I kept the other ingredients the same. I cooked it for 4 hours but it was a bit dry but I think I just cooked it too long. This had a wonderful flavor to it. I put red potatoes under the breasts and cooked everything together. Very nice. Thanks again Kit and get well soon!

I made this for both Thanksgiving and Christmas this past year.  And yes, I'm just now reviewing it (horrible, I know!).  Everything turned out wonderfully.  I used an almost 7 lb turkey breast, and cooked it about 7 hours.  It made those meals so much easier!  I was even able to go to the zoo on the day we did our Thanksgiving meal (2 days before the actual day).

The turkey was very tender and the prep/cooking was so easy, but as a cook who loves a lot of flavor in her food, I didn't find the turkey to be filled with flavor -- an addition of some herbs and spices might really add to this recipe.  I did this to a 7 1/2 lb. turkey breast, and it got done a whole lot earlier than I expected.  I came home to find that the pop-up timer had already popped after almost 6 hours of cooking on low (after the initial 1st hour on high).  I double checked the temp with my digital thermometer, and sure enough, it was done -- over 170 F when I took out the thermometer (I was gone for a while, so I don't know when it actually finished cooking).

I completely forgot to review this! I made this for dinner a couple of weeks ago and it was so delicious and easy! We forgot to rub on the seasonings the night before, but it still tasted fantastic. I'll have to try it again with the marinading time!

This is a terrific way to prepare a turkey breast.  We had a very busy Saturday with our kids sports and errands, plus we were having my mom over for dinner.  I threw the turkey in the crock pot before we left for the games and it was ready and waiting when we returned home.  The turkey was so moist and flavorful and it was nice to prepare such a healthy meal that didn't require any attention.    Thank you for posting!

I followed this recipe-- except I used butter instead of oil . I also poured some chicken broth -- about 3/4 cup-- over the breast.  WONDEFUL!!
 I will never make a turkey breast again  in the oven-the turkey was very moist and the gravy was delish! Thanks kittencal for another great recipe.

I thought this recipe was great....but my turkey breast (6 lb., bone in) cooked WAY faster than I expected!  We're talking 4 hours....I followed the cooking instructions of cook on high for one hour, then cook on low and it was done in only four hours!  MUCH too soon for dinner.  I ended up slicing up the turkey and serving hot turkey sandwiches for dinner instead of just plain breast.  Not sure why it cooked so fast.  I thought it might take longer because the inside was still a little frosty.  I also added a little organic chicken stock to the pot.  It tasted great!  Thank you for sharing.

This turkey was so moist and tender. It was a hit at my daughters birthday dinner. The broth made excellent gravy . 

Thanks Kittencal.

Bullwinkle

I made this for our Thanksgiving this year since there were only 4 us and I didn't want to go to the trouble of a whole turkey!  This was absolutely the easiest way to cook the turkey without worrying about it.  I used a 7lb bone-in turkey breast and 4 turkey legs.  Since I had extra meat, I added extra onions, a few pieces of celery and carrots.  This made a delicious gravy as well.  Thank you KITTEN for another wonderful recipe!!!!   Also, I did put it in the oven under the broiler to get that pretty browned look!  :)

Awesome recipe, but my bone-in 6 1/4 pounder was done (by temperature) in about 4.5 hours, and I couldn't move up dinner time, so it was a little dry.  Maybe my crock pot is a bit on the hot side?  The breast didn't want to sit upright in the crock, so I tossed in some carrots and celery which balaced it and added flavor to the juice which later made great gravy.  Timing seems to be the biggest challenge in cooking turkey!!

I couldn't believe you could actually cook a turkey in a crockpot but tried it anyway and it was the best turkey I ever made. I had an 8 1/2 lb. breast, I rubbed it with minced onion, parsely and lemon pepper seasoning, wrapped it and chilled it overnight then put it in the crockpot at 4:00 a.m. on high with no liquid. After an hour I turned it down to low just like the directions said and let it go. I had to make a tight seal with foil because the lid wouldn't fit but it worked fine. At around 8:30 a.m. I checked it and it was probably done, registering 155 on the thermometer but I didn't trust it so I left it for another hour. The meat was so juicy and tender and white and very easy to slice. I used the bag of gravy that came with the turkey breast along with a 1/4 cup of drippings and poured it over top of my sliced breast and OMG it was good. Try this, you will be amazed.

used basic concept of this and did 7 lb turkey brst in crockpot for time listed. used differnt opt. ingred..... I rubbed with garlic powder, salt and pepper, onion powder and a little soy sauce for color. stuffed with mom's favorite stuffing recipe ( put rest in another crockpot. once time done  I put in preheated oven 20 min to crisp outside a little and then let rest 10 min. (removed stuffing) served with kittencals easy no fail turkey gravy. thanks so much

Turkey was AMAZING!! I left it in crock pot for 6 hours, but the skin didn't get crispy enough for our liking, so I popped it inthe oven for 45 mins (with all juices from crock pot). Came out moist and awesome. Will make this again!! Thank u for posting!!
Turned out absolutely delicious! Not only that, but I had the beginning of stock for turkey chili later in the week!

Kittencal, this is a wonderful recipe. I put a 6.5 lb. turkey breast in the crockpot Wed. around 10 p.m. I followed your recipe and poured about 3/4 cup of chicken stock over the breast. I set the crock pot on high for an hour and then turned it on low until 6 a.m. Thurs. After letting it cool, I wrapped it in foil. About an hour and one half before dinner, I put it in the oven, temp at 325 degrees, took it out after one hour. We didn't eat until 4 p.m. and I was a little worried that it might dry out. But this is by far the BEST turkey I've ever made and eaten. The rest of the family thought so too. I strained the liquid and made about two cups of the best turkey gravy ever. I put some flour and water in a shaker and slowly poured it in the boiling liquid and cooked it a few min. Added a little pepper, it was already salty enough. Thanks for a wonderful recipe. This is a keeper!
UPDATE:  I made this again for Christmas dinner yesterday and it was again wonderful--moist and flavorful.  Gravy made from the liquid was also wonderful!!  The family ate almost all of this 6.5+ lb. turkey.  Thanks again for this fantastic recipe.
I have been only cooking turkey twice a year because it takes so much babysitting but not anymore!  I followed this recipe as stated and it was fantastic.
This is a NO FAIL recipe without question.  Deliciously moist!!!  *****Fatastic*****

I brined my 4 1/2 lb breast. Forgot to rinse it and so a bit salty. The turkey itself was perfect! Cut with a fork and non of the dryness associated with white breast meat. Cooked fast and do yourself a favor by investing in a probe thermometer. It told me exactly when it was done. Mine barely fit in the pot but I had a pyrex bowl that would have made a great dome lid! Just a tip!
Uber salty.  The breast meat did turn out very moist, but I think the onion soup mix took it over the top.

Since my family prefers the white meat and DH doesn't like turkey soup, I opted for a couple of bone-in breasts (totalling 5 lbs) paired with ham & scalloped potatoes for Easter dinner this year. I didn't have any garlic powder, used EVOO, white pepper & recipe #110331 Homemade Dry Onion Soup Mix. The breasts were cooked to perfection in a total of 5 hours, moist & delicious! The skin didn't crisp up but thats OK as we don't eat it any more. Thanks Carol for a great recipe that I'll use many times in the future!
Excellent flavor.  I followed your cooking time but it was too long for my crockpot...it must run hot.  I will make this again and watch it closer next time.
It had great flavor, was easy and made in the crockpot.

No stars for now... I couldn't use the crock pot I was running out of time... so I grabbed melted butter... garlic powder and the dry onion soup mix...  mixed it all together and basted the turkey with it.  OMG that was awesome...  thanks for the idea!!!!!!!!!!
Added:  I made this again... in the oven 325 and used Homemade Dry Onion Soup Mix
Recipe #110331.  This is just totally awesome...  Someday I may try it in the crock I don't know.  But for now I love this... juice turkey brest every time!!!
10/15/09
Today is the day that I am trying it in the crock pot!

My family was amazed that I could make such delicious turkey in the crock pot!  The turkey came out very flavorful, juicy, and tender.  This was so easy to make.  What a wonderful, easy way to cook turkey.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Seriously Kitten, I just love your recipes.  This was another great one.  The turkey was moist and delicious and super easy.  Thanks!

My entire family said it was GREAT! I did use a previously frozen boneless breast, but I had NO complaints! I cooked it on high for 1 hour and then on low for about 5 1/2 hours. I was skeptical, but now this will be the way I cook turkey breast from now on!

wow wow wow! Made this for my boyfriend for our first Christmas dinner. I eyeballed all the seasoning, but it came out great! My BF, isn't a fan of crockpot food, but he loved it!

Thanks
Kittencal
This was very flavorful and moist. I love the fact you fix it and forget it.
Oh My GOODNESS!  I cannot find the words to describe just how easy and wonderful this was!  I will never again cook my turkey breast in the oven!  THANK YOU!!!

We thought this was quite delicious and the prep was very easy. With our 100+ degree weather, it was a bonus to not have to use the oven. The meat was very moist and tender and we loved the oniony flavor. Cold left-overs made great turkey sandwiches. Thanks, will make this again.

This was great!  I love having turkey without having to heat up the kitchen in this weather.  I omitted the oil, and added about a cup or so of water in the bottom of the crockpot.  The 7 1/2 pound bone-in breast was done after 1 1/2 hours on high and 5 on low.  The drippings made a nice gravy, as well.  Served with mashed potatoes and Lemon Glazed Baby Carrots.  Looking forward to hot turkey sandwich leftovers, too.  Thanks for posting!
This was absolutely great - Moist and juicy with great flavor.        Another great recipe kittencal!

This is so delicious!  Very juicy and flavorful.  I added about 1/2 cup chicken stock and cooked for about 4 hours.  I was worried about the saltiness of the onion soup mix, but this wasn't a problem for me.

Very moist. I used turkey tenderloins instead of a whole breast. Hubby wasn't sure about the combination of onion soup mix and turkey but it worked. The flavor reminded me of pork instead of turkey too.
This worked for me.  I did this so I could have turkey for sandwiches for lunches and it was great. I am going to do it again soon for a turkey dinner for my sweetie.

Hey Kittencal - made this last week and it was so good, I am making it again today ! Even better than the turkey was the gravy recipe that goes with it ! That gravy tasted fabulous ~ I think it's the butter that makes the difference.
Needless to say, I will be making the gravy today as well.
THANK YOU for the first crockpot recipe that I like !

This one deserves 100 stars!!!  I can't believe I made this in the crock pot!  I made a 6 1/4 pound turkey (bone in) with skin on.  I used olive oil rather than vegetable oil and I increased the seasonings.  I was leery about the no-liquid thing and added 1/4 cup of water to the bottom of the crock.  I was also trying to figure out the appropriate timing since many people said this cooked way too fast and I have a pot that already cooks hot.  I cooked this for 4.5 hours and it was PERFECTLY cooked...fall apart moist and HEAVENLY in flavor!  For those of you who actually eat the turkey skin...you may not like the texture/appearance of this.  Something I'm sure could be rectified with a quick shot under the broiler.    Thank you for the most incredible way of making turkey!  A true winner here!

Wonderful! Won't cook turkey any other way. I never cook it because my husband found it a dry flavorless meat, unless done in the deep fryer. We don't use a deep fryer, and all the other cooking directions seemed too fussy and long for what you got in the long run, esp for just 2 or a small party. Am a HUGE crock pot fan, so I saw this and read the reviews and figured, why not. DH *LOVED* it!!! So it's a total keeper. I did a split breast bone in, added some red pepper to the soup mix and garlic, and some parsley, mixed with about 2 tbsps olive oil and rubbed breast top and below skin. 1 cup chicken stock, as other reviewers had mentioned. The cooking time was a little weird. I did an hour high and then 4 low, but still had to heat in oven to get pink out. I am trying a full turkey breast at 6.5 lbs tomorrow, and will leave the pop up timer in. I used a meat thermometer for the first one. But over all , easy, and a perfect way to do up the dreaded bird!
Love this recipe...back for the 4th year to fix this for Thanksgiving.  So easy and so juicy!
Used this recipe for THanksgiving, and it was perfect. Followed the recipe to the letter.

I'm sorry, but I do not get all of the 5 star ratings.  I consider myself (as do many of my friends) as a very good cook.  Since I'm having a full house of people for Thanksgiving next week, I plan on brining and roasting a turkey, but need to find a way for more meat as I don't have not enough space to roast 2 turkeys.  So 1 week Pre-Thanksgiving, I experimented by trying the quality/flavor of a Crock Pot cooked bone-in turkey breast to augment my 1 roasted turkey.  I followed this recipe exactly!  It was the driest, cardboard-iest piece of meat I have ever tasted/eaten. My wife took one bite and said, "you always surprise me with how good your food is, and this is the worst thing you have ever cooked"... and I agreed!  After choking down dinner I didn't want to dump it in the trash so I shredded the meat and added a ton of Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce to try to salvage the remaining meat for BBQ shredded turkey sandwiches.  We'll see.  One of the worst recipes I have encountered on the internet EVER!... and surprisingly I have never written a negative review of a recipe ever!  Sorry, but this was just plain awful!
Another Kittencal hit!  Our Thanksgiving turkey turned out great...thank you!

Wow, this was really really good!  I had a little 2 lb. breast for just the two of us. I reduced the oil to 1 tsp. but kept the spices the same. I put a couple ribs of celery and a big old carrot in the bottom to sit the breast on top.  I added a scant 1/4 broth as well. It was done after 4 hours on low and it was absolutely delicious! The drippings were great as well.
The best turkey breast I've ever cooked or tasted! A thousand thank yous!!! ; )

BEST TASTING Turkey I've ever made. This brine makes even the cheapest unknown named brand turkey very MOIST, I tested it when I had read it in a review and it's true. I brined it closer to 60 hrs, but have done it before @ 48hr. I put a turkey roasting bag in a 7.8 L huge tupperware bowl(the bowl is just to support the bag w/liquid). For the turkey I removed the cavity goodies, rinsed off the turkey and added it to the bag; then added the cooled brine to the bag, squeezed all the air out, tied the bag up and transferred the bowl & all to frig. After alloted hrs, take the turkey out of brine, rinsed it off, patted dry, separate the skin from the meat around the breasts. Cut up 1 stick of margarine into fingertip size squares & lightly dust squares w/Sage. Push your finger about an inch or further into the meat, then add one square of the margarine into the hole as far as you can push it. Make butter filled holes all over the top, sides and underside (up through the cavity) of the breasts about 1 inch apart, the more holes the better. Then I mixed sage, a little crushed rosemary, salt & pepper into the cavities, rubbed oil over all and roasted 1 hr at 400º (to brown beautifully) and then down to 350º for the remaining period until internal temp on breast read 170º. Let rest on counter 30 min or so before cutting. Before cutting I usually scrape and cut off the underside skin and fattyness (makes for less fatty/greasy mess and a beautiful presentation). This is a OUTSTANDING recipe - I will always brine my turkey and can't wait to try this on a brisket. Thanks you so much Di Neal.

At my house we go through SEVERAL pounds of chicken per week. My husband eats 6 times a day, but with his diet he eats a balance of chicken, sweet potatoes and some veggie for EVERY meal. Yes - EVERY.

I then divey them up into freezer bags and pour enough brine over them to cover the meat. I squeeze out all the air and leave 1 bag in the fridge and put the rest in the freezer. It's perfect! We NEVER have freezer burnt chicken [which I hate] and the chicken thaws in the brine and is good and ready when we cook it. We do rinse the meat for a few minutes and let it drain before we cook it. 

We also use chicken broth [especially the new flavors they have -Tuscan Chicken is THE BEST!] for half the liquid, and ice for the other half.

I would personally rate this a 5 star recipe but my husband (not a lover of curry) just found it okay.  I made a few adjustments to the spices though.  First, unlike some other reviewers I thought the curry might be overpowering (and I like curry, but still...)so I reduced the amount to 1 1/2 tbsp.  I reduced the cumin to 1/2 tbsp and replaced the cinnamon with a 1/2 tsp of garam marsala as another reviewer suggested.  This was my first time using that spice but it was a very good change to make.  I cooked my sweet potatoes in the microwave and then diced them and threw them in about the same time as the spinach as they were still a little bit hard.  I used the full amount of spinach (it looks like a lot but it reduces).  And as I don't like cilantro much, and it costs almost 3 bucks to buy fresh here I left it out.  I served it over steamed white rice.  I thought it was excellent with the changes I made and even my non-curry loving husband ate a whole plate full.  Some reviews suggested adding more spices to the dish or increased the amount of curry...I strongly suggest not doing that.  I like curry a lot but adding any more than 1 1/2 - 2 tbsp would be too much for most people and make it inedible for those who aren't keen on spicy or hot foods.

Really enjoyed this meal. It was so filling and flavorsome. I added some cumin seeds in when frying the onions and replaced the spinach with thinly sliced red pepper and green beans. I also added a few cashews on top as recommended in the comments and they really added to the flavor.
This was pretty good.  Spice lovers can definitely up the ante with chili powder or whatever.  I'm a spice wimp and I liked it as written; flavorful, but not very spicy.

Thanks for a delicious and healthy curry. I used 3 tbsp of curry powder, and doubled the cumin and cinnamon. Also, I used a 16 oz bag of frozen spinach instead of fresh, and omitted the cilantro. We served it over brown rice, and it will definitely be made again!

We really liked this.  I prepped everything a day in advance, which worked fine.  The potatoes turned just a little brown on the edges, so I wouldn't pret more than a day or two ahead though.  Served over brown rice, with sour cream (next time will use yougart but we're out right now).  Great mix of healthy ingredients.  Thanks

Good recipe.  I added an extra tablespoon of curry (yellow, mild curry),  a teaspoon of allspice, and about 1/4 teaspoon of ground cloves, as well as about a half-teaspoon of salt.  I also used stewed tomatoes.  All in all, a nice, warm dish with a lot of richness, especially to be such a quick dish.  It did need more flavor, hence the extra spices and salt.  I also added around 1/4 cup of half and half right after I took it off the heat, just to give it a little more depth.  Very good.  I will probably switch the chickpeas to a more tender white bean (or perhaps cooked and chopped cauliflower) next time, and may throw in some slivered almonds or chopped cashews next time, to add that chickpea "nutty" flavor, without distracting from the dish, as I thought the chickpeas didn't quite meld with the rest..

A disappointment, I was expecting a lot more from this curry.  This was my first time not using curry out of a jar, and I wish I had done! Don't get me wrong, it's edible, but it's also plain.  I doubled the spices in the recipe as when tasting I found it to be too bland.  Overall it's not a bad recipe but there is definitely something missing. I also added capsicums and mushrooms to the onions at the beginning, along with a clove of garlic - I tried everything to make it work!  If someone else can suggest what additional ingredients could be added I would be more than happy to try this again, perhaps as a substitute for cinnamon as this is a flavour I'm not too keen on as well.

This is great!!  I cooked (boiled) my sweet potatoes too long, so next time I will roast them.  I also added more curry and cumin, as suggested.  I also put in about 1/3 cup of light cream at the end as one person suggested, and I really like that addition.  Next time I might add 1/3 cup of coconut milk.  Thanks for the recipe!!!

Loved all of the ingredients in this dish.  I felt that the amount of curry powder and cumin was a bit overpowering as I could not easily taste the individual vegetables.  Next time I will decrease these two spices.  Overall, it was a great dish and I will definitely make it again.
I doubled the spices, but it still seems like there's something missing. Overall, it was pretty good, and went with na'an really well. Also, don't overcook the sweet potatoes like I did!

A good start to a great curry! I followed the directions with a few additions:

1) Prior to sauteing the onions I sauteed about a teaspoon of black mustard seeds in the vegetable oil--until they started crackling.
2) I added about a teaspoon a fresh grated ginger and one serrano pepper, minced, when sauteing the onion.
3) For the spice mixture I used: 1tbs mild curry powder, 1tbs garam masala, 1tbs cumin, 1tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp red pepper, 1/2 tsp salt.
4) I ended up adding a total of 1 1/4 cups water--kept evaporating.

Same basic recipe, but still could've used a little more kick. Anyhow, I'll certainly be making it again with the said changes. THANKS!
I found this to be good, but it needed a bit more......something. Maybe a bit more kick? I'm not sure.... it was good though. I would make it again but adjust the spices slightly.

Great recipe! My BF was skeptical when I told him what we were having, but when he tried it he liked it -- but of course he said to add chicken next time. I followed the recipe to a T....but declined to add any water, and am glad of that. I served over long grain and wild rice. I agree with other reviewers that it could use a tad more flavor, but it's good enough as is for 5 stars! (IMO) Will definitely use again!

Had for supper on Saturday night.   Not too complicated to put together, and great flavor.   We served with Jasmine rice which was very nice.   Does anyone have suggestions for how to get the rice grains separated (like in Indian restaurants, instead of sticky/fluffy?   My husband and I have really been enjoying Indian cuisine, and although we are not vegetarian, I prepare meatless dishes at least once a week, so this was wonderful.   I do not understand people who doubled the spices and still found bland.   We prepared as is and thought the dish to be very flavorful.
The ingredients say it all...

Delicious! We love sweet potatoes and never even considered using them in a curry. I followed the recipe as written, but I think I would add more spices, including some garlic and pepper flakes. the tomatoes were very tasty. Thank you!

I have to amend my review! We had this again last night and though I thought I had all the ingredients, I didn't, so had to improvise. I ended up using pinto beans instead of chick peas, and bulgur wheat instead of rice. It was a hit!
Delicious and nutritious.  In place of water, I add full-fat coconut milk.  I also add a little garlic, chili powder, and just a touch of sweetener.

This is very yummy and very fast to put together.  I microwave baked my sweet potatoes, everything else was as written.  DH liked it also.  I served it over Saffron rice made with brown basmati rice.  And since there are only two of us--looking forward to the left-overs.
This is such a delicious and easy recipe!  I added a little garlic and ginger ... and next time I'll probably add more onion.

I still found it was missing something and wanted to thicken it so I added half a jar of VH mango curry sauce, that made the whole difference.  Salt and hot pepper flakes when serving.

This was very good! DH loved it and so did I!  I did make a couple of additions and changes.  I added minced garlic, ginger and turmeric. The substitution of butternut squash was very delicious!  It still had that sweet taste that you would expect from a sweet potato.  I paired it with the basmati rice cooked with coconut milk. I will make again for my Meatless Monday rotation. Thank you!
Really delicious and simple to make

Delicious!  Was hesitant because of some reviews saying this was bland (we really like strong flavors!) - but made as directed with good quality spices and it was perfect. Very filling and tasty.  I would however, up the amount of diced tomato, as it would add some needed zip and more moisture.   Also needs salt.
It was Ok, the chickpeas were very good in it but I doubt I will ever make again. It was saerved with brown rice.
Great recipe! i love the combination of flavors.  Such a satisfying dish. i add a little cardamom, ginger, garlic, lemon and milk to mine and it's phenomenal.
Very nice, thanks! Only thing we changed was to add more of the spices at the end as it wasn't spicy enough for us at first.
I tried this the other night and really enjoyed it. It has a good level of spice and tastes great with the sweet potato.
Was really tasty and simple to cook.  Definitely one I will cook again.  Thanks!
Very easy to make, very few ingredients, and very delicious!

This turned our really good.  I did modify it slightly however.  I used fresh tomatoes, so I added another half cup of water.  I also added a bit of cayenne pepper because I thought it needed some kick.
Great quick dinner, Delicious! Next time I would add a tablespoon more of the curry and another teaspoon of cumin. I did use fresh tomatoes and added 1/2 cup extra water. Will make this often.

This was my first attempt at curry. I was a bit intimidated, but I had all the ingredients on hand so I gave it a try this afternoon. It was a very good curry. I also added a splash of cream at the end for a bit of added richness.  This is a delicious, flavorful, nutrition packed meal.  A welcome addition to my recipe box.
This was fabulous! Needed some extra moisture and a little less spinach to suit my tastes. It was a truly yummy meal!
I love curry, but never thought to use sweet potatoes.  We liked this a lot.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

This is pretty good! I did add mustard seeds as another reviewer suggested, and some cayenne. Also, salt, because I cooked the chickpeas myself rather than using canned. I found the spice level to be good, and I don't like bland.. I think maybe the age and quality of spices could be the problem when reviewers have mentioned it being bland. I'll make this again, for sure.
Very yummy and easy, put spinach in last so it was less wilty.
Very good, we will be making extra sauce next time as we felt it needed a little more. But over all it was really good.

loved this great blend of flavors and quick and easy to prepare. I had all ingredients in home and cooked it up in about 30 minutes. I also added shredded carrots to the pot and doubled up on cinnamon and curry.
Needs salt, other than that very good.it is a keeper .
I enjoyed this dish and my family thought it was pretty good. The mix of sweet potatoes and curry is yummy.
Absolutely yummy and easy. A bit dry for me so I added coconut milk.
Lovely, the only addition I made was Ginger. Will be making this again.

We loved this recipe! I made a few tweaks as I was going... I added a red bell pepper as I had one going spare, and frozen spinach. We really enjoyed this, thank you for posting!
spot on!
Have made this several times for my daughter. Her sister and brother enjoy it too. Tried some myself tonight so next time I make it, will tweak it slightly.
Amazing I added 2 crushed garlic cloves with the chopped onions, green beans with the other vegeatables and a bit of salt and pepper , it only too me 2 servings to eat rather than 6 without rice lol
Followed Dulcet Kitchen's recipe and it was nicely spiced.

Yummy! We made this tonight and it was like having a little bowl of cheesecake with strawberries. Fantastic! My kids and I loved it. Thanks for the  great recipe!

This was very good.  I used reduced fat cream cheese, 1/3 cup of Splenda for the sugar and increased the vanilla to 1 teaspoon.  I also used fat free half-and half.  Everyone enjoyed and had no idea it was reduced fat.

This was incredible!! Made this tonight for me and DH. We loved it. I should have blended the ingredients better before freezing it, though--I had chunks of cream cheese in the ice cream. EXCELLENT.  I just realized I probably used about 12 ounces of cream cheese, oops, and I used almond extract instead of vanilla, but mmmm-mmmmm, it was good!  Very creamy.. next time I will throw in some chunks of strawberry along with the strawberry puree.

This was my first attempt at using my new ice cream machine and the results were very successful ~ I am very pleased! Dee, I will be making this again!  Thanks so much for a wonderful and easy recipe!

Nice, creamy ice cream, just as all the other reviews have said. Something a little different than the standard strawberry ice cream. I microwaved the cream cheese for 15 seconds before mixing it in, to ensure that it would be soft and would blend smoothly. Thanks for posting this!

This was the first time I made ice cream. Very easy. Very good. Nice and creamy and very hard on the thighs. lol One I'll surely make again ;-)  fabulicious recipe.   Now.  For your "Lemon Cheesecake Ice Cream". I'm making that this weekend.

I used my new ice cream maker for the first time today, and I just had to try this recipe. It turned out great! It was smooth, sweet and creamy. I may never buy strawberry cheesecake ice cream again! This was a big hit in my home.
This was really good! Everyone who tried it wanted more, but I didn't have enough ingredients to make another batch.  Next time I try, I'll have to make at least 2 batches.  Thanks!

Mmmmm. Mmmmm, good. I didn't have lemon juice so I substituted 1/2 tablespoon lime juice and I increased the pureed strawberry to one cup. I used fat free cream cheese. No half and half so I used whipping cream. Used a bit more than called for in the recipe because the left over cream was going to be wasted.  The texture was smooth and creamy and both the strawberry and cheese cake flavours were discernable. Strawberry cheesecake was never one of my favourite ice-cream flavours but this recipe has changed that!

Yummo, delicious! There was the cheese cake and the strawberries, but where was the graham cracker bottom? Some graham cracker chunks crumbled into the ice cream could make a difference. I am not sure if the chunks would survive the ice cream maker without turning to bread crumbs, but I will try.

I finally broke down and purchased an electric ice cream maker. I've been eyeing them for so long and after watching all of the tasty photos pop on on Zaar of ice cream, I finally took the plunge. I am in cheesecake heaven... however i wanted graham crackers too.. so i did it two different way... got some graham crackers crumbs... the first time i scopped out a scoop & rolled it in the crumbs... the second time i spooned some as a topping... just what it needed.... it was gone in no time...
Very rich and creamy. And it actually does taste like cheescake. Thanks a lot!!!!!
Rich, creamy, and good!! Thanks!
We really liked this recipe. The Cream cheese was light, and not over powering, or to rich. I will make this again. I might even try different flavors like blueberry next time.
This was the first recipe I made in my new ice cream maker and we loved it.  I didn't change a thing.  Sublime.

This was awesome!  I love cheesecake and I love icecream.  When I saw this recipe, I thought, what could be better???  I just got an icecream maker for my bridal shower and used it for the first time last night with this recipe!  My family loved it!  My son said that it was the best day ever.  When I asked him why, he said it was because of the ice cream :) Thank you for making my son so happy :)  I'm making a mango sorbet tonight!  I'll post the recipe if it's good.

This is the best ice cream recipe ever.  I made a strawberry, raspberry, and blackberry cooly and swirled it in as the ice cream started to get firm.  We finished it off in two days.  Thanks for the recipe!
This was very good, a little too much cream cheese I think. If we do it again, we'll add sugar or use syrup packed berries. The kids put strawberry syrup on top with banana slices and loved it!

I loved this!  Very rich & creamy.  And so, so easy.  Thank you very much for a lovely recipe I will use again & again.  I will try other flavors too - berries, peaches.  The possibilities are endless.

this was the first recipe we've tried in our new ice cream maker and it was fantastic. Thanks for a great recipe to start our ice cream making adventure!

I have made this twice now - love it. The fresh stawberry flavor pops out and the cheesecake flavor is subtle and nice.

First time just like the recipe except I used fat free half & half and added some fresh slices of strawberry ( didn't care for the frozen strawberries in the ice cream).

Second time I made this with fat free half & half and fat free cream cheese - still very good but you lose the cheesecake flavor that is so good in the original recipe. 

Next time I am going to make this with some real half and half and regular cream cheese and put the soft ice cream from the machine into a cooked graham cracker crust and serve it like cheese cake with fresh strawberries and whipped cream on top.

This is a keeper!  I made it this afternoon, and was very happy that there was too much for the container I wanted to put it in, so I was "forced" to sample it.  So yummy!  I used reduced fat cream cheese and non-fat half-and-half, and added a bunch of cut-up strawberries at the end.  Delicious!  Thanks for posting this!

This ice cream was very good and rich.  It firmed up nicely in the ice cream maker.  We ate a big helping then froze the rest in the freezer. Super easy!  UPDATE:  A day later in the freezer, it gets hard and is sooo RICH and DELICIOUS.  Better than store bought!

Oh lordy, was this ever good!  I made it a few days ago and we have been munching out on it ever since.  The flavor is delicious!  Rich, creamy and full of strawberry flavor.  Perfect in every way, that's what it is!  if you like ice cream try this one.  It is sure to please your taste buds too!

Our favorite ice cream recipe yet. I made exactly as directed except doubled everything. I always use fresh squeezed lemon juice since I used bottle one time and it made my ice cream have an odd aftertaste. My husband adores cheesecake and I will definitely make again. Thanks.

This is fabulous!!!!!!!!!!! More like a  10  star in my book. I love it and did I mention how EASY this is to make...........this could be dangerous........not sure I want to share..........:)Thanks!!!
just made this today, though I havent had the frozen product the taste was great. I left out the suger and added 1/8 tsp of stevia. so simple. thanks for sharing: )

Nice combination. It was nice not having to add heavy whipping cream to get ice cream. This was very fruity, almost like a creamy sorbet in my opinion. I also used low-fat half and half and cream cheese. Thanks for posting!

Yummy! This is a super easy recipe, and the flavor is nice and creamy. It does taste like strawberry cheesecake, and I look forward to making a parfait later of layers of ice cream and crumbled graham crackers. Thanks for sharing this keeper recipe. :)
Best ice cream ever!!! I absolutely love this recipe. I was craving cheesecake when I was pregnant and this ice cream was the perfect solution.

Absolutey sinful, decadent, rich and wonderful!!  We are big time chocolate fans in our house and we were just trying to "use up" our strawberries. Delightful, easy, and very common ingredients to have on hand.  We'll be trying other flavors as well : )  Try this one and indulge!!
Great flavor! I did make the classic rookie mistake by not creaming sugar and cream cheese together first. Yummy stuff!

I made this for my Boss's birthday and froze it in a graham cracker crumb pie shell.  The cream cheese really gives it a zing.  I wanted to add mini white chocolate chips, but I couldn't find any at the store. Oh well.   Also, I used frozen non-sugared strawberries. I made this for an ice cream social...people loved it!  I used seedless blackberry puree.  I am looking forward to trying other fruit flavors as well.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Oh, yum! This is so good, and so easy! I'm going to try it with cherries to make a "cherry cheesecake" flavor! Thanks!
Yep, this one is a winner!  We had 4 types and this one was the favorite.  Easy to make and any fruit would work.

I made this for a church social and by the time I got to the end of the line it was all gone! Everyone told me it was the best ice cream out there! I'm going to try it again with blueberries- only this time I'm keeping it all to myself!

I made this last night and it was to-die-for. I don't like strawberry ice cream, but wanted to make this for my husband. As it turns out, I liked it more than him! It was awesome and so, so easy! Wow! This is really good stuff.  Have made it several times now and it is always a hit.  I have even sub'd low fat cream cheese, splenda and light half and half and it was still terrific.

Very good, but very rich for me.  I could only eat a few bites.  Maybe that's for the best!  It will last a while in the freezer too.
Used fresh strawberries from our garden. It wasn't really my cup of tea but my husband liked it. My oldest would eat it too but the other kids wouldn't. Isn't that always the way with kids?

We tried this recipe but used frozen cherries instead of strawberries.  But we followed the rest of the recipe as written.  Wonderful flavor and gorgeous color!  Everyone we shared it with loved it.  We will definitely make this again.
This came out beautifully. The only change I made was to fold in a crumbled graham cracker pie crust after churning, Everybody loved it.

WOW This is wonderful.  I only used 6 oz. of reduced fat cream cheese but the rest as written.  Will be making this many, many times.

This is fantastic!! I can't believe how much it tastes like cheesecake!!

Very Easy to make, we use fresh black berry and it come out great. Did have to put anything away since we finish the whole batch.

Absolutely delicious!!!! I just purchased the cuisineart ice cream maker and this recipe was my first choice!!!!!  It was the perfect choice for my first time trying to make ice cream!  My husband and daughters raved about it and wanted more.  If you like strawberry cheesecake and or want to impress your guests....definitely try this one!  After mixing and before chilling for the hour, I added extra mini chunks of the frozen strawberries!  Creamy, fruity and Yummy!!

Thanks so much for sharing this wonderful recipe, Dee514!
Awesome!  Very creamy & delicious!

I used whole, unsweetened, frozen strawberries (It's Jan, lol), Splenda for the sugar and 95% fat free cream cheese. It's freezing quality, after churning, would be better with real sugar but eaten in it's soft serve stage this is fabulous. I can't say that this is a cheesecake clone but it sure has a cheesecake accent that 's very good. Thanks for a lovely recipe :D

This is a delicious way to use up fresh strawberry puree when your family has picked too many berries at the U-pick!  I used fat free half and half as well as reduced fat cream cheese. I also decreased the cream cheese just a bit based on some of the previous reviews, but next time I will put the full 8 oz. in.

This is the recipe I used to break in my new ice cream maker -- delicious! The ice cream as-written is lovely, but it's extra yummy with some strawberry chunks and broken homemade cinnamon graham cracker crust folded in at the end. This is definitely going in the keepers file, thanks for posting!
I made this last night for a family BBQ. Everyone LOVED it! So rich and creamy. We added graham cracker crumbs at the end and also sprinkled some on top of our bowls. Awesome!!!

The perfect ice cream! The flavor of the strawberries really stands out. I love that it's not too sweet... store bought ice cream can be cloyingly sweet, but this is just sweet enough. I thought it would be too cheesy with a whole brick of cream cheese, and was tempted to halve it, but I'm glad I didn't. The flavors here are very well balanced. Thank you for posting this!

Absolutely devine!  I had some frozen cream cheese in the freezer, fresh strawberries...all I had to buy was the half and half.  I leave my ice cream canister in the freezer during the summer months for easy convenience!  I served this with my recipe Fresh Strawberry Marmalade (223183)  Kudos on posting a great find!
This was very good...creamy and an excellent flavor.  I was even out of sugar, so I used powered sugar with great success.  Will make again! :)

I am elated with this I've cream. I bought my machine about 3 months ago and have only made 5 or 6 batches of ice cream, but this recipe is my favorite. The texture is a bit off but the flavor is like eating a strawberry cheesecake. I followed the recipe exactly and the flavors were perfect. The balance of taste between the berries and cheese was great I am going to use this recipe as a base and put in assorted fruits because I love cheese cake but love variety. One combo I will try is the mixed berry frozen fruit you can buy in the stores. I'd give this recipe a 10 if I could. Eat ice cream!!!
There's nothing better than a bowl of Ed's Chicago Cocoa Chili and a bottle of your favorite beer!
This was the most wonderful chocolate chile I have ever tasted. It moved my taste buds to heights of orgasm!

I made this last night for an event.  It was a HUGE success.  Every bite was eaten.

Thank you!

WHOA!!!  THANKS ED! This is one of the best chili recipes I've have tasted. Well worth the effort to chop all the veggies.  Had a little trouble mashing the whole tomatoes into manageable bites.  I am not a big fan of cilantro and at first found it a little overpowering but after adding the OJ ect, it just added a nice kick. Had to use garlic from a jar as clove garlic is a little hard to find here but didnt seem to matter much.

AN EMBARRESING REVIEW! As the number served was a tiny amount for us, we added pasta to it to make enough for us,+added mushrooms instead of meat,BUT then it turned out GREAT-not a chili, but more like a great veggie mole'.  
Sure we have some exotic tastes, but this was not exotic, but an odd twist,+it turned out wonderful,my apologies to Ed, but it sure tasted great,thanks to Ed's great base recipe!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!5 STARS

It looked like an odd recipe, but it was fun to make with a multi-layered and yummy taste!  The flavors hit in waves, first sweet, then sweet/sour, then you get the heat.  More chocolatey than I imagined with a lovely color.

I minimized the garlic to 4 cloves and added them earlier because I was afraid the garlic would be too strong in left overs.  I also added a small can of tomato sauce because it looked a bit dry.  My family devoured it!  

I found enough time while frying the meat to prepare the veggies and enough time while cooking the veggies to get the spices measured out and together.  I thought I'd miss the beans but did not.  

It's actually an easier recipe than it reads and quite fun to make.  I suspect it's quite a versatile recipe, and it is my and my family's all time fav chili so far.  :)

Good job, Ed, and thanks!

My family makes me make this as often as possible. The spice mix can't be beat, and the various tastes compliment each other well. I did make some adaptions for our particular tastes, though the chili is great as is. In the spice mix, I only used about a tablespoon of sugar, and no cilantro, and I don't put the cocoa in with the spice mix, but add it by tablespoons until it tastes "right"---sometimes using more or less cocoa. I also left out the celery, jalepanos, and the sweet & sour mix---I use beer instead. I also added kidney  or black beans. I suppose ours is a "toned down" version, but it suits those with sensitive tastes. Thanks for the great recipe!
Can I just say "YUM"!!!!  My husband thought I was nuts when I said I was fixing chocolate chili...but after he tasted it, he ate his words.  He asks for it often.  Thanks for the post!
Made this for a party and everyone raved about it!  Cut the "hot" stuff by half and it still had a kick.  Thanks!

The THE KILLER COCOA CHILI SPICE MIX is fantastic!  This recipe makes awesome chili!  I made a few modifications minor modifiations - I used half ground sirloin, half ground turkey, subbed beer for the sweet and sour mix, and realized at the end I didn't have any chocolate.  This is SO good!  I got 10 servings out of this, and it's definately going in my regular rotation.  One caveat - as is this is very spicy.  I cut the heat with some sour cream.  Definately a wonderful recipe - thanks for sharing Ed!

Excellent! Knew as soon as I saw Chocolate Chili I said "Chicago"! I have put cocoa in my chili for many years, however, I love all the other stuff you put in as well. I am big on Hungarian Paprika, and other red peppers. Jalopenos really give it a nice kick. I was a little leery on the cocktail mix but I will try anything just to see and this was really very good. My favorite though was this cocoa chili spice mix which I would like to try on a few other things as well. Thanks a lot for sharing this wonderful recipe with all of us here!

I liked this chili, but I think I added too much chocolate as it was a bit on the sweet side for me. I halved the recipe and used beer instead of the sweet and sour mix. I also added an extra tsp of chili powder.  Next time I will try adding less chocolate and less brown sugar.  The spice mix was indeed killer!  Thanks for sharing.
Wow this was good. It even won me a prize at a chili cookoff. I found it to have a more complex taste the day I made it than it did the next day, but it was still good.

I made this for friends and it was a big hit. The tastes were complex and interesting. When it first started simmering the chocolate seemed a bit overpowering but that went away over time. It's important to get the right balance of salt. I didn't use the sweet and sour mix, I used beer. And I think it would have been a little better if I could have afforded better powdered cocoa. A little dab of peanut butter might give it an interesting flavor, too. I'll try it next time.

Oh my!  This was sooooo good!  I am a Texan and like a really meaty, satisfying chili and this fit the bill!  I did cut the cayenne alot because the kids won't eat it otherwise.  To keep the intensity I doubled the jalepenos.  Thanks for a real winner!

This is very good.  Even with the long list of ingredients it is quite easy to put together and well worth it.  I did not have the sweet and sour cocktail mix.  I did look this up on line and learned that it could be made with equal parts sugar, lime juice, lemon juice and water.  While the chili itself is quite decadent, you need to give this a try on top of macaroni and cheese--sinfully delicious.
This Chili was amazing and very addictive!! The combination of flavors was wonderful and kept me from getting bored even after my fifth bowl! LOL

Cooking this now for the first time. Slightly modified for personal tastes, but just the same, it smells great, looks great and tastes great. I just know everyone will love it. One modification that I would suggest is using Dagoba brand Xocolatl organic dark chocolate with chilies and cacao nibs as the chocolate bar. A bit pricey maybe - but only half will do for the chili and you can save the rest for a snack later!

I loved it!!!!!!!! Made it tonight for a little family get together. It's very different from the chili my brother & father made so they didn't care for it but everyone else loved it. I will definely make it again for company.

One word PHENOMONAL!!!This reciepe is so unusally good that I find my self making it many times.The cocoa mix is OUT OF THIS WORLD!I did find it time consuming to cut up all the veggies.And I felt the cocktail mix couldv'e been a little bit more clearer.Luquid or mix and add water... But other than that it was awesome!This is deffinetley a recipe that deserves to be added into your cookbook. Thanks Ed!

We enjoyed this. It was, dispite the long list of ingredients and directions, very easy to make and was good for a weeknight meal. I used 2 10oz cans of the rotel tomatoes with the jalapino peppers in them, drained, in place of one of the cans of crushed tomatoes and left out the bell pepper and jalapeno peppers. I also couldn't find swt & sour mix so i left it out. I made the spice mix almost exactly although I substituted some ingredients here and there. I also like beans in my chili so I added a can of kidney beans. This was a very good chili, served over fritos (DH's fave) with cheese on top and a dalop of sour cream and chopped green onion. I even have enough left over for another night which is always nice. I will be making this again and look forward to playing with the ingredients. Great post, thanks.
One of the best chili recipies I've ever seen. Delicious!

This is a rating on the Spice mix portion only! But it is EXCELLENT! I usually make chili using a combo of ground turkey and lean ground beef. I made chili using an old recipe but added Ed's spice mix in until I got the desired taste and it was wonderful! Makes quite a bit of mixture but it keeps well and great to have on hand. Will update review once I make the recipe in its entirety.

This was a really good chili. It has a very different taste and for those who don't know what's in it, they can't quite put their finger on what they are tasting. I have to say I had to add DARK RED KIDNEY BEANS to my chili. I am from Virginia and that is the only way I have ever eaten chili, otherwise, to me it is just a type of HAMBURGER HELPER. I used 1 lb. lean ground beef and 1 lb. ground chicken. I did not add the lemon or lime juice...just fogrot. For the dark chocolate I used a Hershey bar (yum-yum).  Anyway, I will be making this often. Thanks!
Excellent chili!  Though the list of spice ingredients is long, I had almost everything in my cabinet already.  Preparation is key and then the chili comes together easily.  Yummy!
Excellent chili.  Made it as directed.  Next time I think I will cut the sugar in half.  Thank you so much for posting!
I really liked this chili although the mix of all the tastes takes some getting used to.  I would probably put a little less sugar in next time as well!

Wow, what can I say..the kids LOVED it and they don't like anything!! The 5 yr old niece took home leftovers at her request!! I have to say the first go round..I wasn't sure and then I added some garlic hot sauce and it brought it home!! Yum...I think I might add more liquid next time..there was no sauce to it after a short time. It won't last around here that is for sure!! Great post Thanks from another Illinois Gal..

Not much to add that the other reviews haven't stated. LOVE this recipe. I changed it a bit to up the health factor - I used 1 lb ground turkey and 1 lb italian turkey sausage. Also, I left out the 1-2 ounces of dark chocolate. But aside from that I stuck to the recipe. It was great and I will use this for all future chili needs. I loved it, my DH loved and we will make sure our future kids love it.

Thanks Ed!

Used ground chicken and beer instead of the sweet and sour mix (of which i have never heard of and I doubt if it would be available outside of the US). The spice mix was great and it was fun to cook the chili. This was my first time to make something hearty with chocolate but it sure won't be the last. The spicyness was just right, good kick.
Thanks for posting.
I'm not sure what happened here!  This came out INCREDIBLY bitter.  Not sure if everyone else is using hot chocolate instead of cocoa powder, but this really didn't work for me.  Sorry!

This is just ridiculously good! The flavors are complex and interesting but so well-coordinated that it melds perfectly. As for the spice mix....well, let's just say that when I go, whip up a big ol' batch of it and stick me in there for eternity. Thanks!

This stuff is SO GOOD!! I substituted a chocolate stout beer for the sweet and sour mix, because I am going for that over-the-top chocolate quality. Also, like a previous reviewer, I used a bar of Dagoba Xocoltal (sp?) chocolate, which is 73% cocoa, and I used the whole bar (2 oz).

This is pretty spicy stuff, and I even seeded both jalapenos. If you want to reduce the heat you can cut the chili powder and/or cayenne pepper in half. 

I will definitely be making this again!

Ok, but borderline gross.  I made it exactly to the recipe.  It sounded weird to begin with, but when I read all the positive reviews I had to try it anyway.  I grew up in Oklahoma and I know "Real" chili.  This is not impressive.  Even my Yankee boyfriend didn't want seconds and he'll eat anything.  The recipe is too sweet and too chocolatey, yet burns all the way down.
This was wonderful! My picky boyfriend even loved it. And we have tons of leftovers! Great recipe Ed

Im a big fan of chili and was excited when I found this recipe.  I Followed the directions exactly and for all of the work thought it was average at best.  I didnt like the chocolate flavoring as much as I thought I would.
All the different flavors are amazing together. I have fixed this chili a couple of times and I find myself craving it constantly!
Very good. Lots of work. But tasted great.
We tried this recipe yesterday. As Ed said everyones taste is different. This touches four different senses as it passes over your tongue, OUTSTANDING!!!!! Play with it to your taste.

This recipe is terrific. I made it for a business chili cook-off held by our local Chamber of Commerce. I didn't win, however, it was a popularity vote so the business that had the most employees and friends there won. However, out of all the participants, we ran out because everyone came back for seconds! The fact that it was "Chocolate Chili" was a huge draw, everyone wanted to try it. Of course, I didn't follow the recipe exactly, I didn't have the sweet and sour mix, so used 7-up, also used V-8 juice. I also put in the beans to stretch it. This chili is awesome with corn chips. The sweetness of the chili hits you first and then you get this unexpected heat later. It is not an overly sweet chili, although you can easily adjust the heat and sweetness to your own taste. I was pleased, the professional chef that won, came over to taste my chil and was highly complimentary! Thanks for making me look good!

My husband loved this chili!  We just keep eating it (I did not expect to like the cocoa flavor- I was just making it for others- and I really liked it too).  I made a couple mistakes when making it, but they were not big enough to change the integrity of the flavor.  I made this for a large church function and won an award (hotness; cause I accidentally used a hotter pepper...) and I received many compliments.  If you are looking to try something different, this is a great recipe and well worth the effort.  I also did not find it very difficult to make.  Just make sure its not too late at night ;)

This was the best stuff when I tasted it immediately after combining everything.  I went through 5 spoons going back for another taste!

A warning though:  use the cooking method described in the recipe!  I always make chili in the crock pot, and for this occasion I had to let it cook overnight as it had to be at my daughter's daycare at 7am.  And then they kept it plugged in ALL day long.  By the 5pm chili supper, the complexity was gone and it tasted very bitter.

I think you can still use the crockpot, but mind the cooking times listed.  I'm giving it another go this weekend when I have the time to cook as directed.

I just asked my husband what he would rate this recipe and he said: "Very, very good!" The friends we hosted tonight concurred. What a wonderful blend of ... everything. Next time I will use the two jalapenos as directed (only used one this time for fear it would be too spicy) and keep everything else. Made my own sweet-and-sour mix with equal parts water, sugar, lime and lemon. Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful and I'm off for a second bowl!

Brought this to our neighbor's for 4th of July and it was a hit! I bought indidual Frito bags and had everyone laddle some chili right in the bag. Great way to have easy clean up. Can't wait to have it again!
With all the great reviews, I was really expecting something amazing and it just didn't fo it for me.
I love this recipe!  It is genius!!! My whole family has tried this and rated it a great!!!  Thank you!
I didn't love this.  There was just too much going on for my taste, I will probably take elements from the recipe, though, such as the sweet & sour mix and use them in a more basic chili recipe.

Very good! Definitely more of a mole than a chili, in my book but this doesn't bother me in the least. I love it. I didn't have any of the sweet and sour sauce, so I just skipped that. Otherwise followed the recipe exactly.

I make this often for football parties. It's always a hit! I leave out the sweet and sour sauce and I add chili beans (I like 'em, darn it!). My hubby has requested this for our New Years Eve party. What a great flavor to start the new year with. Thanks!

I've made this recipe for the past few years, and it is always a hit!  A lot of my friends don't like the chilis with beans and this is a great alternative.  I have made with the soy crumbles as well and the flavorful sauces transfers very well...but it's definitely better with the meat =)  A staple for my family - I even passed it along to a new bride (with all due credit!)
good stuff
chocolate is not just for dessert anymore! just made this and love it. made it with turkey for my granddauaghter who cannot eat red meat. its great
Very good chili!  We doubled the jalapenos and used urad dal and kidney beans instead of the ground beef.

I had a houseful for chili last night and made Ed's chili. Everybody raved about it and my wife who is not a chili person thought it was the best that she has had. I only made a few minor changes with the biggest one was adding a pound of chopped pork. I adjusted the spices to my taste and it came out perfect Thanks Ed!

This chili was...interesting. I was willing to try it as I recently had an enchilada sauce that had coco and chili powder in it and it turned out delicious. With all the rave reviews I was hopeful. But this actually upset our stomachs a bit. I made it exactly to the recipe's instructions, with only a few minor changes in the chili spice mix (a little less of this and that). I tasted it before we put the spice mix in and it was actually decent tasting, but the coco killed it. Even my chocoholic brother wasn't crazy about this.

I'm from Texas and have lived off of chili from the day I was born. Every great chili recipe has one or more of the following secret ingredients:cocoa, coffee and /or beer. Also, chili is very personal, which is why this recipe states to adjust spices to suit your own tastes. I LOVE THIS RECIPE!!! I made this recipe for the very first time this winter, for my two boys and husband. Knowing that they won't eat anything too spicy and I don't like my chili too sweet, I eliminated the jalape
Best Chili I've ever made or eaten!

I half a pablano pepper, since it was already spicy enough with cayenne and chili powder. I didn't add celery and carrots, but instead put in two cans of drained black beans. The recipe can take some time to make, mostly due to measuring out the ingredients for the "Killer Cocoa Chili Spice Mix," but the flavor makes it worth the effort. Three out of the four of us liked it and want to eat it again. The picky eater will just have to eat something else next time.
Dh made these.  We did not have vanilla extract so he used almond extract.  All I can say is delicious!

So good! I used ground beef instead of turkey sausage, because I had some on hand already browned. I didn't have any chevre cheese and I wish I had gone out and bought it-next time, I will. This tasted absolutely decadent, cheesy, flavorful, and wonderful. I served this as a one-dish meal, since it already had lots of veggies, and it made four big, hearty servings.

Every once in awhile I find a recipe that needs more than 5 stars.  This is one of them.  Absolutely delicious!  I have used spaghetti squash a few times in other dishes, but none as good as this!  I really liked the flavor of the chevre, and will use it in my next "real" lasagna also.  I did misread the ingredients and only bought 1 can of tomatoes but it still turned out so good!  Made for Fall 2007 PAC.
I made this last night and it was really good!  I used spoaghetti sauce in place of the tomatoes and I didn't have chevre so I used the feta I had on hand.  I will definately make this again.

I have made a lot of recipes on from this site and I have given a lot of them five stars.  However, my entire family (kids included) agreed this was the best recipe I have found here.  Absolutely delicious and satisfying....just amazing.  The only change I made was using fat free ricotta.  I wouldn't change anything else.
I thought that they were great and so did my family and my kids hardly ever eat sweets and well they ate these cookies right up
This recipe is pretty easy to make and the cookies look very nice.  They taste even better.  Everyone I've shared them with has loved them.

I halved this recipe and made it today. It was well enjoyed by all of us at home and I plan on making it again on 24th October this year, it being my mom and dad's 25th Wedding Anniversary!
