Today being the most 'SPECIAL' day of my life(as I met my BF on this day on ICQ on the internet for the very first time at 8pm on today's day, exactly 4 years back), I'd saved this recipe right from the moment you posted it just for TODAY! Thank You, Mirj! This is indeed what I'll give him to eat when he returns home back to tie the knot! This will be the 'perfect' shot at his stomach! This recipe indeed, IMHO, justifies the saying, "The way to every man's heart is through his stomach!".
Really great cookie and fairly easy to make.  Great Chocolate Flavor. Looks great on a cookie platter for the Holidays!  Thanks!
My mother's best friend was famous for these cookies when I was growing up.  They just make me smile.  It is such a soft, yummy cookie full of chocolate flavor.
Great cookie recipe!  Made these for an xmas cookie exchange.  They taste as good as they look.  Essential to let the dough chill for the 2 hours.  Thanks Mirj!
These are great.   I made a double batch and got 5 dozen cookies.  Nice chewy cookies with great flavor.
I loved the cookies. I made them for my work Christmas party and the Christmas party at my house and everyone just loved them.Thank you for a good recipe.

I guess I saved the best for last because I tried like 5 Chocolate Crinkle cookie recipes in the last 3 weeks.  I was looking for one that tasted like the ones I had at a church bake sale last year.  These came out Chewy, soft and DELICIOUS.  I did bake them about 11 minutes... but I guess it depends how big you make each cookie.  My first batch came out a little dough-y... but the rest... OH MY GOSH!!! THEY ARE THE BEST!!!!!!! Thanks! I might also add one more thing:  I chilled in the freezer for 45 minutes and had no problem rolling into balls and they weren't sticky like the other recipes I had tried!
Mmmmmm....a very nice addition to my cookie gift package! Beautiful! Thank you!

This is my son's favorite cookie recipe!  As for me, I can down a half dozen with a glass of milk easily!  These are so easy for the beginning baker, too, and look so pretty on a Christmas Cookie Tray.

Superb taste, but mine flattened, not as good as Sharon's picture.  I halved the recipe made 21 cookies.  I chilled the batter 3hrs before scooping them out into the powdered sugar.  But after i finish placing all the cookies, the first batch placed on the sheet flattened. And it went flatter as they bake.  But the taste and the chewniess is perfect. UPODATE: chilled the cookie dough overnight and it came out perfectly looking crinkles!

I made two types of this: as is and using sugar substitute. The latter came out perfect while the one with ordinary sugar came out flat. I chilled it again but it still came out the same.  I really wonder why.  Anyway, DH still liked it for the taste even if it came out flat.
Just like fudge brownies. Amazing!  I chilled the dough overnight and they came out as expected.

I hate to give out a bad review but I did everything as I was supposed to and they taste like vegetable oil.  I don't understand.  I kept thinking maybe I did something wrong but I did everything to the letter.  I will try again tomorrow morning.  
   I gave these a three because my husband is actually eating them (I made 2 dozen cookies and threw the rest of the batter in the garbage after trying to salvage them by adding even more vanilla extract- as an aside, I could still taste the oil).  I don't know whether he likes them or whether he's just eating them because I put them in front of him.  Hard to tell but I'll give the cookies the benefit of the doubt and say he doesn't taste the oil.
Made these for the company potluck and they were a huge hit. Chilling the dough is the key. They taste so good you can't stop eating them! Will make them part of our holiday tradition.
This was another recipe that I made for the students' Christmas party. They were okay, but not spectacular tasting and seemed a little dry.

These are easy to make even though I did everything by hand. I used sunflower oil. I then threw the bowl of dough into the freezer for a while and baked something else. Chilling the dough makes all of the difference - it is too sloppy if you try to make balls without doing so. And it is a good recipe that kids can help with. I baked these at 10 minutes in my small convection oven and then left them in there for a couple of minutes. These definitely made it into the Christmas cookie boxes and the kids were hanging out for any rejects. Perfect milk and cookie type cookies.
this is a great recipe...I have tried other ones but this is the way I used to make them too...One of my sons favorites....They turned out great..

Reportedly, these cookies were delicious! I can't say, as I - stupidly - halved the recipe and didn't get a single one: I gave some away in cookie baskets and the rest got gobbled up before I got back into the kitchen! I really enjoyed making them, though, and will certainly make these again - if for no other reason then to actually get to eat one this time!! Thanks Mirj, these were a big hit!

I made these for my Christmas cookie trays and they were a big hit.  My oldest son loved them.  They are easy and beautiful, made exactly as written except I added about 1/2c. of mini chocolate chips to the batter before baking can't have enough chocolate.  Thank you for the great recipe.

I had to significantly increase the cooking time as one batch came out sort of raw inside and later caused the other cookies to become too moist.  But the cookies are very delicious and very chocolately, next time I'd add some walnuts for some extra goodness

The cookies look and taste great, and I've been looking for a recipe like this for a long time. But, I made this exactly as the recipe described (except for cutting it in half), and 10 minutes was too long. All of my cookies ended up burnt, except for the last batch (only 3 cookies) which turned out fine at 10 minutes. Unfortunately, they looked perfect on the top, so I'm not sure how to fix this in the future. I couldn't tell they were burnt until I got them off the cookie sheet and they cooled a bit. Next time I would bake them for 8 minutes and then pull them out and check, adding one minute at a time if they were too goey on top. I'm still giving them a 4, because other than really watching the time, I think they would be fine. Oh, and a half batch got me 33 small cookies, not 48.

These are a family favorite too! *LOL* 
Very chocolatey cookie .. and they look cool too , because of the powdered sugar "cracking" on top. MMm! :)

FANTASTIC cookies! I chilled the dough in the freezer for one hour, since patience is not one of my virtues....I also made only 1/4 of the recipe, just to try them out, as I plan on selling them @ my school's bake sale, and needed to give away some samples. I think next time, Ill also try a different variation, without icing sugar, but instead, with luscious chocolate chunks in the batter. This makes a lovely cookie with a crispy exterior but wonderfully chewy and delicate interior. I will be making this again, and again and again. It's one of the best, if not THE BEST cookie recipe I've tried on Zaar to date.

These are awesome, and so worth the mess. (Maybe I'm just messy!) 

They do make 5 doz. The really spread out when baking.  my first batch are probably 3x the size they should be.  i cut all of my 2nd batch in half again and came out with perfect little cookies.  

These are so good.  I will definitely be making these again and again.
My grandma and I had a wonderful time baking these cookies, and the best part was that we were able to eat half of them and still have plenty for everyone else!

Well...made them AGAIN this year...brought them to work twice!!! they are a definite hit no matter where I take them...I really enjoy people's first reaction when they see them.
I didn't have any chocolate squares..so ...I used 12 tablespoons of cocoa and 3 tablespoons of oil which is the equivilant...(for those who don't know)...I think that is going to be my preferred way...the cocoa will not sit on my shelf forever and it is less expensive than the squares!  I don't know about any one else...but I needed way more powdered sugar than 3/4 cup...this is now one of MY "keeper" recipes!!!

This recipe will now replace my chocolate crinkles that I used for years. They are so moist, and this is DD's very favorite cookie, in this version.  My sister made our old recipe and side by side, these are so much darker and more chocolate looking. Taste wise, very chocolatey and decadent!! Thanks Mirj.

These were really pretty, and quite easy to make. my only complaint is that they taste a little too much like brownies. Good brownies, in cookie shape, and I was expecting/wanting more of a cookie-cookie, you know? but they are still very yummy, just it's best to know to expect them to be more like brownies. They do look really pretty though, and I'll likely make them again the next time I'm having a kind of brownie craving.
A delicious, easy to prepare recipe for chocolate crinkles. Using 1 inch sized balls I got about 60 cookies. They were so good they only lasted a day in a half! Thanks for a great recipe.

I absolutely LOVE these cookies!  I usually double the recipe and put them in my cookie-exchange boxes ^_^  I love the rich chocolate flavor of them.  Thank you for such a great recipe!  EDIT: These have become a staple in my home, and it's become tradition every Sunday for me to bake up a batch!  It makes my house smell like chocolate, and my BF is always waiting around to snag a cookie from the oven!

Changing from 4 to 5 stars. The longer and colder the batter is, the better the result.  Overnight in the fridge was perfect for me, three hours asn't enough, I got flat but tasty cookies with three hours chilling.  Overnight and mine look just like the picture from Karen67.
VERY economical recipe, would be great for gifts. If you have to sub cocoa plus oil for the chocolate sqares, I have done it both ways.
 Makes a lot, I thought I would never get the last batch in the oven. Very good, very basic ingredients that give a pretty and tasty finished product.
All I can say is WOW..Awesome cookies.. so simple to make and so fudgy, chewy and DELICIOUS, especially the second day..
The best cookie I have had in a long time. One daughter says it taste like little brownies. Very rich and sweet. This recipe is a new favorite.

Sooo good!!!
Thank you for sharing
We loved these cookies. They are so good. Thanks for sharing.

These were so good and so easy!  Tasted a lot like brownies...MMM!  The recipe only made about 5 dozen for me, though, but it might be that I made them bigger.  I'm going to double the recipe for Christmas gifts!  Excellent!
Great recipe! I made these for Christmas cookie trays and they turned out wonderful. I'll be making them again, thank you!
Traditional holiday recipe at my house that actually came from my dh's side. They are wonderfully decadent. Easier to make if you chill the dough overnight.

Fantastic cookies!  I love that they are soft and have a slightly crisp texture on the outside.  Instead of vanilla, I dissolved 1/4 teaspoon espresso powder in 1 TB of water to punch up the chocolate flavor...and added a few handfuls of semi-sweet chocolate chips (sorry, couldn't help myself!).  So yummy! Thank you for sharing.
My mom uses this same recipe, we love these cookies!!!!
Yummy!  I made these for Bible School at our church.  My husband kept eating them, though.  I had to make 2 batches so that he would have some extra.  These are great!

I was just going to add this 5-star recipe to Recipezaardom, but here it is! My recipe is exactly the same EXCEPT it uses 12 tablespoons of cocoa powder PLUS an extra 4 tablespoons of oil, instead of actual chocolate. Good to know it works either way! I'll add a photo of mine made with the cocoa. Delicious! (These also freeze exceptionally well.)

These cookies are delicious!  I made a couple of batches for my mother-in-law to take to a cookie exchange.  The only change I made was to follow the suggestions of previous reviewers' and chill the dough overnight before rolling into balls.  Bake time for my oven was 12 minutes.  I only got 5.5 dozen out of a batch given the size I made them, but that's still a lot of cookies!  They taste like brownies and are quite addictive.  I did end up using an unsweetened chocolate square substitution (recipe #188761) for the second batch I made because I didn't have quite enough actual squares; that substitution worked well and the ones made with the sub taste exactly the same as the ones with all squares.  Thanks so much for posting!  I'm definitely planning on making these again in the future.
I've used this exact same recipe for years...it's always a HUGE hit. Makes a great addition to gift baskets. I like to cook them til they are just done (don't overcook). :)

This was always a Christmas favorite in our house.  My Mom's been baking these for well over 50 years.  It's a keeper and I'm happy that it's on this site.  I've been making them with peppermint extract instead of vanilla.  Yum!
These are excellent!  I refrigerated the dough overnight and they turned out just like the photo!
My absolute favorite Christmas cookie!!  These were easy to make and came out perfectly. Thanks!!

I have been using the 3pack box for crackle cookies. very good product.  I press a Havilland thin mint  to the middle of each cookie
 right out of oven and when the chocolate looks a little melted I sprinkle them with 
crushed candy canes pieces. I get great compliments every time.

I just made these this morning. What a great cookie! I've never had these before, but came across the recipe when I was searching for holiday cookie recipes, and thought I'd give them a try. I refrigerated my dough overnight--only because when I was reading the recipe originally, I missed the part where it said to refrigerate for 2 hours. It was 9:30 pm at the time, and I wasn't about to start baking cookies 2 hours later, so it got left in overnight. From reading the other reviews, it sounds like that was a good thing. I also had to put the dough back in the fridge to stay chilled between batches. If the dough got the slightest bit warm, it was a little hard to work with. I will say, they are extremely messy to make, but no worries. That's half the fun at the holidays. I don't know if I made the cookies too large, but I got exactly 5 dozen cookies. not 8. Still plenty. My kids loved them and my daughter said they were "light as a feather". Mmmmm..so chewy and chocolately. Love them. I'll be putting these in my Christmas goody tins to distribute to neighbors and friends. :)

Delicious!  A co-worker said they tasted like brownies.  Slightly crunchy on the outside, moist and delicious on the inside.  However, they didn't seem to keep very well - after a few days in a covered cookie tin they started to taste stale.

I refrigerated the dough overnight, and still mine was very sticky.  Also, the recipe only yielded roughly 3-4 dozen cookies for me, but perhaps I made the cookies too large.

LOOOOOVED these cookies! Made them several times and they always come out great.  Love the tip of making them ahead of time and keep them fridge.  Gonna make a bunch and freeze for unexpected chocolate cravings!!!
Super Good! They were gone the night I made them. Not one person said they were any less than totally delicious.

Great flavor.  Slightly crisp on the outside and moist on the inside.  A little chewy %u2026 just a little. It was sticky to work with but the end result was worth it%u2026kept sticking it back in the frig to keep it cold.  I got about 4 dozen cookies.  I think next time I%u2019ll cut the sugar %u2026 personal taste. Everyone else loved it as is :) Thank you Mirj

We made these for our 2010 holiday tray for family and friends.  These were a great addition, everyone loved them.  DD took a tray to her french class and the kids thought they tasted like brownies, they were the first to go.  I thought they looked wonderful on our trays, thank you so much for sharing this recipe with us.
These looked really pretty and tasted just like a brownie! However, I wish they had been more chocolaty - a little mild tasting for me. Thanks for sharing!

These were delicious, and easy to make.  I made a half batch, and got about 2 1/2 dozen, so I guess ours were on the large side.  They did taste a lot like a brownie - very good.  We'll definitely make these again - Thanks for posting!
Super chocolatey.  Very sticky dough, but once you roll it in powdered sugared, it was easy to handle.  I scooped the dough in balls into the powdered sugar.  Came out great!

My family has also been making these cookies for a couple years, although they are affectionately dubbed "Reindeer Poop" because of the sugar coating. :-) My son absolutely looooooves these, and they go excellent with a last cup of coffee after dinner (or for a sweet morning treat!) I have always used the cocoa powder/oil combo due to price difference and have never had a problem. I will however try chilling it overnight to see if that helps with some of the mess. Usually not a problem, but I have told I will have helpers this year so they can secretely steal my holiday cookie recipes!
The BEST cookie on the planet in my recipe book. A yearly Christmas cookie tradition. :o)
A big hit with either the baking chocolate or the cocoa substitution.  And the variation of adding PEPPERMINT EXTRACT was even more popular.  Again, chilling overnight was crucial!

I wanted to try for a chocolate-cinnamon flavor. I added 1 tsp. cinnamon to the batter with dry ingredients. Then instead of rolling in powdered sugar, I rolled each ball in a mixture of 3 tsp. cinnamon and 3 Tbsp. granulated sugar. They are delicious- like a brownie in a cookie!!!
Update, 2nd time around: I made recipe exactly as written. Refrigerate overnight- dough is very soft and sticky. I used my small (1 1/4 inch) cookie scoop and got 6 dozen very small cookies.
Thank you for posting this classic recipe! We used sunflower oil, the cocoa substitution and ended up chilling them for 3 days.  They were wonderful.

We quadruple these and and freeze them after the rolling in powdered sugar. You get fresh baked crinkles all month long and none of the mess of the bowl of dough in your fridge for a week. Freeze on parchment on cookie sheet AFTER rolling in powdered sugar. When frozen solid an hour later, pour them into freezer bags. thaw on baking tray for a few minutes while you pre heat. Bake like normal..

These came out great, and while I hesitated to give it a full 5 stars because of how labor intensive it is with needing to refrigerate the dough between each batch, the finished product was perfect.  Not overly dense or too sweet, they maintained that perfect balance between a firm outside with a soft inside.

these are delicious and if you bake them exactly the right way the consistency is heavenly. However the size of the balls and even a minute can make or break this cookie!  Definitely worth it though!  Fun to rolll out the cookies with the kids
I have the recipe for mocha crinkles and they look like these, they're not overly sweet and it's low in calories

I have made these several Christmases in a row, but I think I will have to find another one for next year. I find them difficult and time consuming to make. Difficult because the "dough" is really a batter. Even cold it's very wet and sticky. I scoop the dough with a spoon into the sugar and they're manageable, but I always end up with them too big, and because the spread a lot, they run together into a huge chocolatey mass. Time consuming when rolling them the proper size, because then there's like 20 trays to bake off. They do pass the taste test, even if they're ugly! My family always eats all of the "cookies" that I call "chocolate crumble" since they look like a pile of broken cookies. I just want a prettier cookie, so I'm done with these.

I agree with the other reviewer who said this dish deserves more than five stars.  I made this last night and absolutely cannot stop eating it!  My husband loved it too, and he doesn't always go for my non-traditional recipes.  We didn't even miss the pasta.

Good stuff!  I had chevre, onion, zucchini, and yellow squash from my CSA box, so I decided to make a variation on this.  I used my summer squashes instead of spaghetti squash, slicing them and sauteing in a skillet until lightly browned.

I served it with rosemary batard grilled with garlic butter.

My husband joked that it needed noodles, but he went back for seconds, so I consider it a win.  ;)

Very good!  I used leftover spaghetti squash and roasted tomatoes and basil from the garden instead of using canned, but otherwise followed the recipe.  It was a love-hate thing for the family - 5 loved it, one hated it.

Wowwwwww this was amazing.  I'm a vegetarian so I used Boca meat crumbles and my carnivore DH said it was one of the best things I've ever made.  I also substituted fat free cottage cheese for the ricotta, and as a result I calculated only 330 calories per 1/8 of a 9x13 pan.  Naturally, then, we each had two and a half pieces.  Haha. :)

Wow! This was an incredible recipe that we all loved! This may be the "new" lasagna in our house! 
I made a few changes: used ground beef instead of sausage, omitted the goat cheese bcuz I didn't have any, and added mushrooms to the sauce. Used diced canned tomatoes, reduced the onion, used a combination of minced garlic and garlic powder, and butter instead of olive oil.
It was awesome, and I will definitely make this again! 
Thanks for Sharing!  :)

We grew Spaghetti Squash this year and I looked for recipes to add variety. This was superb! Nice and cheesy. I did cut it in half for just two of us and it was enough for two meals. We don't eat meat so I used Morning Star crumbles in place of the sausage and increased the garlic as we like the taste of it. It was just as good reheated for the second meal. I will be making this again.

I cannot stop talking about this recipe. It is the best recipe I have found on here. I even made it for my Italian husband's family and I have been asked to bring it to every family dinner!! I wish I could give more than 5 stars because this recipe deserves it!!

Excellent!  And pretty easy to throw together.  We were short on time, so we didn't cook the tomatoes and baked the dish only about 40 min.  Other than having quite a bit of juice from the squash and tomatoes, it was excellent!  We used about a 2 lb squash with corresponding changes in the amount of other ingredients.  That made a good size amount in a 9 x 13, so can't imagine how much a 4.5 lb squash would make!

I wasn't too sure how this one would turn out, but when my husband said, "This is awesome" with a full mouth of food, I knew it was a winner.  Delicious, hearty, and for those of us with a gluten problem, superb!

Absolutely delicious. My only complaint is that it took an afternoon to put together, but it was worth it at mealtime. Next time I'll probably include some olives as the salty would contrast nicely with the sweetness of the squash.

This was very good. I added tomato paste to the sauce, though not sure it needed it. Used Chicken sausage....our store doesn't carry turkey sausage, or goat cheese, for that matter! Probably a good thing for my family for the first time trying this, because the chevre might made it just too "different". As it was DH mostly just picked out all the sausage, which fortunately, I had doubled!
The flavor is delicious, and very much like lasagna. In general, I do not like squash of any kind, so that is pretty big!

I made this tonight for supper and thought it was good. I make my squash by cutting it in halve, clean out the seeds (keep the seeds for roasting by making Recipe #50958) place in dish cut side down, add 1-2 inches of water and micro for 10 min each half or until you can stick a fork through it easily. I only used the mozzarella and freshly grated Parmesan cheese. I did not use any meat and used spaghetti sauce instead of tomatoes. I only baked 30 min as the cheese on top was nice and brown. You couldn't even tell you were eating squash where the cheese was nice and thick. Makes a very good meatless lasagna and the squash is so healthy for you.

This is the first time I have made spaghetti squash and I was very pleased with the outcome.  This made a rich and satisfying meal that was really very hearty.  I made this exactly as posted and was rewarded with a fantastic meal!  Thanks for sharing.

This was very good.  I did not have the chevre cheese and shaved a few calories elsewhere along with the cheese.  It does make a lot so now I have lunches for most of the week.  We will make this again that is for sure.

So delicious! I made this about a month ago, & couldn't stop thinking about it! I omitted the chevre, & subbed fat free cottage cheese for the ricotta. Wasn't sure my husband would like it, but he did! I had it for lunch a couple of days, but also froze some. Had it a couple of weeks later; still terrific!

Awesome recipe! Had never cooked spaghetti squash before and this was a great recipe to try it with. I have several people already wanting the recipe. The only thing I did differently was use fresh basil instead of dried and add Oregano and didn't use the Chevre cheese because I couldn't find any. It was absolutely delicious and made enough to freeze for later. Thank you!

This was a hit last night when we had my family over to celebrate my father's birthday.  It is really decadently delicious.  Like other reviewers indicated, it is a bit labor intensive and takes a long time to make, but it was not that difficult and was worth the compliments.  The only changes we made were to substitute Field Roast (vegan) sausages for the turkey sausage and we didn't read the directions carefully to meld the sauce for several hours, so we cooked for about 1 hour with no lid.  This is a keeper that I will make on other special occasions.  Thanks!

OMG this was so awesome.  First of all I didn't read the recipe through completely.  I only had one can of tomatoes, so had to sub with an 8 oz can of tomato sauce and an 12 oz can of tomato paste.  Then I don't think my spaghetti squash was quite 4 pounds and I didn't read that the sauce was to cook for two hours.  But in spite of all my mistakes this was incredible.  I did add parsley to the ricotta cheese mixture and used Jimmy Dean's Hot sausage for the meat.  I will definitely make this again, but next time I think I'll add at least four lasagna noodles to soak up the extra sauce.  Thanks so much for sharing your recipe.  Last time I had spaghetti squash I ended up throwing it out.  Not this time - my problem is trying not to eat too much of it.

excellent recipe. As a vegetarian, I omitted the meat and substituted some eggplant slices and spinach I had in the freezer. It worked well putting it into the sauce. Recipe is flexible and forgiving.
Yummy yummy yummy!  Loved it!
Wow!  The family loved this, even my fussy Italian husband!  I didn't have ricotta, so I sub'd cream cheese & didn't use the chevre either.  I will definitely will be making this again!
The family loved it - even the one who questions "imposter food" Thank you for posting.

Yes, it was an excellent dish.  Didn't have the goat cheese so grated some hard provolone cheese.  Also being a vegetarian, instead of the turkey, I used white and portabella mushrooms with the onion in the sauce.  It was delicious.
This was beyond fantastic. Keep meaning to make it again but it hasn't happened because it is labor intensive but SO worth it.

These bread rolls went down a treat your right crusty on the outside fluffy in the middle and so tasty great with bowl of hot soup. And they tasted like a brought bread roll. Some home made bread rolls go hard the next day but these are still fresh.  I'll be making many more.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.

Bonnie Kiwi

Excellent tasting rolls!  The only downside was I did end up having to put almost 4 cups of flour in the pan due to stickiness of the dough.  They were still a little sticky when finished.  Other than that, the rolls were a great addition to my dinner.
This was a very nice roll.  I made them a bit larger (8 instead of 12) to use for sandwiches with Mean's Pulled Pork.  They were very easy to make & tasted good with a nice texture.

These buns were just fantastic! I made them in my Zojurushi home baker bread machine on the full dough cycle. I used regular dry yeast and proofed it in 1/4 cup warm water with 1/2 tsp sugar, then added it when the machine started kneading. I used 3-1/4 cups all purpose flour to create a very soft sticky dough. I shaped into 9 perfectly round balls, then proceeded to rise them for 30 minutes, then baked them in my air-convection oven for 22 minutes. I usually make dough on my Kitchen Aid stand mixer but it was being used for other things, I am very pleased with the end result of these buns, they are soft on the inside and crusty on the outside not overly salty or sweet, almost similar to a bake shop Italian roll. I will definately make these again on my bread machine, they are truly a winner. Thank you so much for sharing such a great recipe!...Kittencal:)

Very good rolls. I had to bake a little longer than suggested.. but they had a nice texture and flavor. I made crab cake sandwiches for lunch and used  Aroostook's Oven Baked Crab Cakes recipe. My family enjoyed them.

Love this recipe! DH just kept on telling me how good they were. LOL 
I had no problem at all with this recipe. Everything went as stated in recipe. I made the dough early this morning and made up the rolls and let rise. They were ready just like recipe said but I let mine sit on baking sheet til I got back from shopping. They still rose alittle while I was gone even. Great recipe! Thanks for posting!
Fabulous!  These are by far the best rolls I have ever had!  My family gobbled these up and were asking for more.  I used regular flour and saf instant yeast and they were great!  Thanks for posting!

These turned out wonderful!  I wanted to make some big Hogie style rolls for our French Dip Sandwiches for yesterday's dinner.  After a false start, I forgot to use the dough cycle and found baked bread when I returned home...grrr, I mixed up a second batch and hurried to get it done in time for dinner.  I made 8 large rolls and even though there are only 3 of us here...there is only 1 1/2 left this morning!  They were a big hit and this recipe is definitely a keeper!  Thanks for sharing!  Wonderful rolls which also make good bread, even accidently!

These turned out quite nice, with a beautiful crunchy crust and lovely soft texture inside.  I did have to bake them longer than suggested.  I sprinkled cornmeal on the pan before I put the rolls on it to rise for an added crunch.  Like the other review I did find the dough very sticky and so had to add another 1/2 to 3/4 cup of flour.  I served them for dinner with a nice pot of soup.  Thanks!
I made these today they were fantastic very easy to do,I had to bake them a little longer than suggested,I will be making this recipe often.

Great rolls, nice and crusty...They remind me of the ones made by my Grandma. Hard to find good country style rolls here in New York, so I will definitely be making these again. Thanks for a great recipe!

Excellent rolls and very easy to make!  I mixed the leftover egg yolk with one tsp water and brushed it over the rolls before baking, which made them lovely and glossy even more crunchy!  Awesome for brats, burgers, or sandwiches!!  Thanks Chris!

Have made them several times.  Tonight DH said they were perfection.  Put a pan of water in the oven when I preheated it and kept it there while baking the rolls above it.  Came out with a nice crust and very soft inside.  Great flavor too.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe.
Yum! Soft, sweet, quick and delicious. This will become a staple in my household.

This recipe was perfect for use as buns for BBQ pork sandwiches. The texture was very good inside and out. Will make next for hot dog buns.
Thanks for a great recipe!
Jean

I printed this recipe 3 months ago and have made them many times.  With this recpe I no longer buy rolls.  The ingredients are simple and they turn out great.  A definite 5 stars!  They are cooling out on the kitchen table as I write this.

I made these rolls to go along w/ DiB's French Dip (Crockpot) French Dip-Crock Pot Recipe... and they are PERFECT! I followed your recipe exactly and had no problems at all. The rolls are crusty on the outside and tender on the inside. I really like them! Thanks for sharing this recipe. I most definitely will be making these again!

Wonderful!!!!! Really a big hit and so easy to make.  Thanks
\Mystic_river
Very good rolls. Low fat, nice texture. I'll be trying them again.

These were fabulous!  I only got 6 rolls out of them, I put them in mini loaf pans that I had greased and dusted with coarse cornmeal and did the final rise in those.  These are the perfect rolls for a french dip sandwich or hoagie.  Will make again and again!

I made these yesterday to go with barbecued beef sandwiches-YUMMO!  I egg washed the tops (with the yolk and a little water} and sprinkled with sesame seeds.

Thanks for posting,
Di

These were great. I almost screwed up and forget about 1 cup of water.
I used Ms Dash instead of salt and used olive oil instead of oil.  DH said it was the best bread he's ever had.  Served with pork roast, but looking forward to having with soup tonight.
One of the best recipes fo rolls that I've ever tasted.

Excellent rolls! I don't own a bread machine so I made the dough in my KitchenAid stand mixer. I used only 1 1/8 cups water and included 3/4 cup whole wheat flour with the bread flour. The recipe made eight nice-sized hoagie rolls which I used with my Recipe #175640 recipe ~ Thanks so much!

Wahoo these were good!! OUTSTANDING rolls and so easy to make. I needed to add about 2/3 cup more flour in the dough cycle to make it the perfect pliability to divide and form into rolls. I too put a pan of water in the oven bottom when I pre-heated the oven and during cooking process and the rolls came out with a very nice crust and soft and delicious inside :-)  Thanks for a perfect recipe for hoagie buns! AAA+++

I used this recipe to make ham & swiss rolls for a road trip.  They turned out great, and this dough is better than the recipe i used to use.  Just make the dough in your bread machine, and when it is done, take it out, divide it into 16 pieces, flatten in your hand, put pieces of Swiss cheese and ham in them one at a time, pinch to seal in the contents, and put on a baking sheet in a 350* preheated oven for about 30 minutes.  They freeze well and travel well.  No mess!
These were great.  I, like Melanie, did add more flour to make a workable dough but the results were just great.  Thank you.

These turned out so well.  I just got a bread machine and this was my first experience making rolls.  The shape of the rolls wasn't pretty but boy did they taste great!  We didn't care what they looked like!  Thanks!

These are the best rolls I've ever made.They are tender inside,crispy outside and great tasting.I decided to try these after reading all the great reviews. From now on I will make sure I have a dozen of these in my freezer ready to serve when I need them.I included a couple of pictures.Thanks Chris for posting this winner.
Sage/Rita

For the longest time, I have tried making numerous recipes for rolls.  Some were okay, others quite good, but this is just the BEST!  I won't need the other recipes from now on!  They came out just like I like them, crisp outside and with a wonderful flavor.  No wonder they took first prize...They deserved it!  They tasted much better than most rolls from the store or bakery.  I think that next time I will try to use an egg wash and sprinkle them with either poppy or sesame seeds, but they really don't need an improvement.  Just to make them a little different from time to time.  I did make 12 rolls as suggested, but for sandwiches, I think I would like them a little larger - maybe make 8 rolls out of this recipe.  In my oven, it took more like 20 minutes, but ovens differ.  I ate two before they were completely cool!  DELICIOUS!  I sliced the rest in half and put most of them in the freezer for future use.  Thank you so much for posting this great recipe, Chris from Kansas!

Wow!  I am new at bread-making, and I don't have a bread machine, so I was nervous to try these despite the rave reviews and simple instructions.  I'm so glad I did, and thanks to the other reviewer who also used a Kitchenaid mixer!
I combined all the liquids and the yeast in the mixer, then gradually added the flour until it was the right consistency.  I also had to use closer to 3 1/2 cups, and I cut the water to 1 1/8 cups.  I let it rise for two hours, then made the rolls as written from #4 on.
YUM!  My 4yo son and I split one straight out of the oven, and I'll make these again and again.  I'm excited to try different variations, too.  These definitely increased my bread-making confidence...  Thanks so much, Chris from Kansas, for posting!
easy and delish- everyone loved them-thanksfor this great recipe
Best rolls we have ever made-we will use this a lot thanks so much

I am "new" to baking, but am trying more and more things since I got a breadmaker...  however, these didn't turn out for me at all.  I was left with a soupy mixture at the end of my dough cycle.  When I read the recipe I thought there was a little more water and yeast than other recipes I have tried and the same amount of flour...  maybe I need to play around with it some more to make it work for my machine...  I read where other reviewers had problems with sticky dough, so I was prepared for that, but my dough was so soupy I didn't want to waste flour trying to fix it...  Maybe it's just me since so many others loved it...  I will try it again soon.  Thanks for posting!!!

We did this by hand, as we don't make our bread in a machine.  This turned out really well.  These rolls were made for cheese steaks, which are notorious roll destroyers.  With a generous application of mayonaise on both sides of the roll, these guys held up very well, almost to the very end of the sandwich!
If you're throwing greasy stuff into your rolls, this is the way to go!  Great taste, great texture, and resistant to cheese stake toppings!

Made these today for Christmas dinner (in the freezer) I had the same problem mentioned here about the dough being too sticky, so expected to add more flour.  I added about 1/2 cup more (just felt it after adding a bit) and they came out wonderfully. I also put the water in the oven while I preheated it and it did the trick.  The tops were nice with just the right amount of "crusty" and tender inside.  My DH and I had to sample one to make sure we could serve them at Christmas, we can, everyone will love these.

Excellent! I made these into 8 big kaiser rolls. My family loved the taste and had seconds at supper tonight. I used a can of water also in the bottom of my oven, while they baked. Also I brushed the buns with egg yolk/water mixture, before placing in the oven. I didn't care for the smell of the egg yolk as they baked though. Kind of gross.But very tasty buns!
Excellent crust on these rolls. However I didn't think the flavor was that good. Thanks!

My first attempt at rolls and these came out awesome.  I did need to add additional flour as it was a humid day but I am used to that.  Took these to a potluck dinner and my friend's daughter declared these the best rolls she has ever eaten.  Thanks!
I'm a roll making queen thanks to this recipe.  Easy and tasty!  Thanks.  Tonight, I'm adding a little rosemary to it.  :-D

I made these rolls last night to have with some soup. These were a huge hit with my flatmates and boyfriend - the rolls had all disappeared before they had a chance to cool. I too found that I had to add close to a cup of flour to bring the dough to the correct consistency but other than that I followed all the directions. Delicious and great that there's not any butter too (makes me feel a little better after eating so many!)

With 41 5 star reviews you probably dont need another testimonial to how good these rolls are, but being a novice I just had to write to let those rookie bread machine users like me out there know that this recipe is great and that I had fanatstic results the fisrt time. They are indeed crunchy outside and soft inside. DH absolutly loves these!

These were great!  I made some in sub-bun shapes for last night's ham and cheese sandwiches.  The rest I made in the traditional round rolls.  They were great warm, out of the oven, with butter melted in the middle (am I drooling?).  Terrific recipe!  I will be making this simple recipe often.
Although these tasted very good, mine did not turn out crisp on the outside.  Next time I'll try baking a bit longer than indicated.

I've made bread, buns and cinnamon buns with this recipe, and gotten rave reviews everytime.  Great flavor, not overwhelming, fantastic cinnamon buns!  Has become a staple in my repertoire!  Will use often as it's very quick and easy!  Love it!
Very nice though mine didn't get a crusty top.  I think I will do as another reviewer suggested and brush the tops with egg wash before baking.
Pretty tasty.  Used this recipe for a more gourmet twist on a burger.  Thanks!
The best rolls I have ever made, I got lazy and added the whole egg,  I will be making this again and again.

I decided to try out this recipe as a possiblity for Christmas festivities. This lovely, soft dough made a delicious roll. I formed the recipe into 9 rolls making the perfect size for a leftover turkey sandwich! A few more batches and I will be set for the holiday season. Thank-you.

These are wonderful!! I will try 3 1/4 cups of flour next time, since the dough was very sticky and I had to dust generously to handle it.  But they came out beautifully, I made 6 small ones and 4 big ones from 1 batch.  I accidentally had the oven at 350, then boosted it to 400 at about 7 mins, they came out beautifully crusty.  I will try and do this again, next time on purpose. :)
I put the whole egg in and added ground chia and flax seeds. Also used 1/2 stoneground whole wheat flour and 1/2 white flour....so delicious!!!! I will make these again and again and again..... A

Excellent recipe!  I make two loaves of bread out of it as well.  The flavor is delicious and it is so easy to put together in my bread machine.  When making loaves, I just use the dough cycle and form into two loaves and rise, then bake in the oven.

Excellent rolls! I decided at 4:42pm that I wanted/needed/desired rolls with my chicken dinner. I set about trying to find a quick roll, that had a lot of taste, and pow! I found this. This is everything that I could of asked for. I don't have a bread machine, so I just dumped the whole bunch of ingredients into my KA (kitchen aid) and used the dough-hook to bring together (7 minutes) went and let rise for about 40 minutes, the put into a ball, and let rise another 20. Baked and presto, hot rolls right with the chicken. And GOOD too! Thx! My go to recipe for nice, crusty, hot rolls in a flash!

New to my bread machine, only have made a couple of loaves that turned out good, tried this first roll recipe and it turned out FANTASTIC.  Now I can make a couple dozen for Christmas Dinner and freeze them.  I uploaded a picture of my very first yeast rolls.  64 year old roll virgin baker ;D

Awesome rolls.  The crust coming out of the oven is lightly crunch. Once cool, it soften up and have a chew to it.  The inside is so soft and so tender...like cotton.  The flavor is so good...Love love these rolls. Thank you Chris.

This is a very nice recipe.  I prepared it all by hand because I don't have a bread machine, and it came together quickly.  The rolls weren't that crusty after baking, but I reheated/toasted some later and there was then a bit of crunch to the outside.  Thank you for sharing this.
Lovely! cooked half, froze half as dough, will cook in a couple of days. nice crust and colour. flavour good. 5 stars!
Everyone said my best rolls yet, very happy I found this, thanks for sharing
didn't much like them.  pretty sure I did everything right.  I think I wanted a buttery taste; should have known I wouldn't find it here.
this was super easy wld. recomend, rose super well.

I was very disappointed in these. They rose beautifully and cooked to a lovely golden brown. But the taste was nothing special. They weren't bad, just not delicious. I took them to a potluck and came home with 5 out of 21 that I took. That isn't normal for my rolls, so I'll go back to some other recipes I have made.
Absolutely delicious, best French bread I have ever tasted! I made into long sandwich rolls for French dips. So easy, and melt in your mouth good!
This recipe has great ingredients, butter and cinnamon.  I lightened up the recipe for the Make It Healthier tag game.

OMG these are good!!!  Used margarine for the butter and shortening and used about 1/2 cup sugar as I added some mini chocolate chips to the batter.  These muffins were moist and tasty - we LOVED them!!  Thanks Ms Sally! :)

These are so good! There's just something about the fragrance of cinnamon in the oven. I hardly ever bake things like this. My hubby always likes to have a slice of banana bread in the mornings with his coffee. He'll like the change! Thanks so much for posting and sharing!

WOW, I lightened these quite a lot and they are still scrumptious.
I used egg white instead of whole egg, Splenda for the sugar, skim milk, heart healthy margarine for the butter and unsweetened applesauce (with 1/2 tsp of butter extract mixed in) for the shortening. They tried to rise to the top of the oven and they're  moist, really fluffy, mildly flavored with sweet spice and utterly wonderful!

Oh my goodness, I was so surprised at these! Amazingly simple to make, and super tasty, almost like a little cinnamon doughnut.  Our  musical rehearsal loved them! The only important thing to note is that there is an additional cup of sugar, to mix with the cinnamon, which is not listed.  I'll definitely be demanded to make these again!

Yummy yummy in our tummies!  I lightened the recipe a bit by using applesauce in place of the shortening (I just don't use shortening) and I did not dip them in additional butter but instead sprinkled them with a Cinnamon Sugar spice blend before baking and they were perfect!  Nice and moist and love the cinnamony flavor throughout the muffin!  Thanks Ms. Sally for a great recipe to use over and over again!  Made for the Holiday Tag Game Dec. 08
I didn't like this recipe: too much nutmeg, brown sugar only on the top, and dipping your muffins in butter. But I will say they did look pretty.
They are fairly dry, but do look tasty. The muffin was too plain in my opinion.

Up-scale pastry shop recipe.  Just made it and was very satisfied. Although this was my first time baking something like this,(a couple of small errors) the next time I am sure it will be perfect.  Easy, superior taste and texture. If you want to push the envelope; drizzle with honey after taking it out of the oven.
Thanks for a delicious recipe.

I used jam inplace of egg white,
(apricot,raspberry or orange), I also added chopped dried fruit to the filling (plum, cherry or cranberry). I made this last Christmas and will make again this year, LOVE, LOVE them.

Yum Yum Yum!!  I made some of these this afternoon....they're almost all gone!  My DH has been eating them up...as have I!  Thankfully I have some more dough in the fridge, will make some more in the morning.  They are a little bit of work, but well worth it!

These have been my husband's favorite Christmas cookies so far this year and rank really highly on my list as well. They went over really well at my Christmas party at work too. They were delicious and reasonably easy to make.
I made these cookies for a party last weekend and they were a huge hit! The recipe is extremely easy to follow and the dough rolls out beautifully.  Thanks so much for this great recipe.

Oh, these are the neatest little cookies! I love the shape--they look like they are much harder to make than they are. And they taste divine! I filled mine with chopped walnuts, and, oh! they're nutty heaven! I made most of them for my grandpa, and he LOVED them. Thanks for the recipe!

My son dropped by when we were eating dinner and I told him he could try one.  He kept eating them and wanted some to take home.  My son is not a complimenter and he told me 3 times the Rugelach were very good.  Very easy recipe.  Next time, I'm trying the jam suggestion - good idea.

I screwed up my first batch of the butterhorns. I cut the dough (the already divided into 1/4 dough)into 4 quarters with a pizza cutter. Then I just rolled the big trianglar pieces and tried to make 4 big pieces of butterhorns. The result is surprisingly Good! I think the outside of the butterhorn was only half way done (but I guess since I used jam instead of egg white, it is okay that it is not fully cooked)I told my husband," it is not quite done yet and it tastes like apple pie". My husband tried and he said, "it tastes much better than an apple pie, it is delicious!". Thanks Karen for the great recipe. How do you pronounce this in Hungarian?
These were awesome! They didn't take all that long and very easy to make. Taste delicious! Simple yet elegant. What a treat!! This recipe a keeper. Thank you for sharing.
I made two batches of these for a cookie exchange it made over 9 dozen mini schnecken.  Plus, how awesome is Schnecken to say?  :)  They are very good and pretty darn easy too!

I had an old recipe for Rugelach that I misplaced, and when I saw this recipe, I was hoping that it would be the same one. That didn't work out, but they were good, tho not what I expected. It was always hard for me to roll a circle with dough, but the filling seemed a bit dry and lots of it fell off the dough, even tho I followed exactly as written. They do look a lot harder to make, than they really are, but my expectations were higher. Sorry that I couldn't give it a higher rating, but they still are a worthy cookie to make and serve to company. I will try them again, and try and figure some way to moisten the filling so that it doesn't fall off. I also think (not sure) that my old recipe called for cream cheese in the dough, which may be the reason why it tasted different from what I expected. Thank you, Karen, for sharing this recipe.  ADDED NOTE:  I was informed by Karen that the reason that some of the filling fell out, was because I did not press it into the dough; something that I will do next time, after librally brushing it with the egg white glaze.  Also, I regretfully neglected to add the cream cheese (major oversight).  I somehow missed that important ingredient, and therefore, the rating.  As soon as I bake these again, I will re-rate this recipe, and make the proper adjustment.  My apologies to Karen!

I made these today as part of my jump-start on Christmas baking.  The dough was very easy to work with and the directions were simple to follow.  Although the first couple of trays I made didn't look as pretty, once I got the hang of rolling and glazing I found the process to go very quickly.  The taste was exactly what I was looking for.  For some reason mine turned out too small for the optional "curving shape".  Thank you so much for posting this recipe.  These are a keeper and I'm glad I decided to try them!
I don't think anyone should write a review if they don't follow the recipe as it appears.  Especially if they leave out a crutial ingredient.
This was so easy to make! My 9 yr old son helped and was so proud of himself, lol. They were delish.
I was hoping that these would have a flakier pastry.  They tasted fine, but maybe since it was the first time I ever ate them I was expecting them to be different.

This is great!  I am making this recipe tonight to take to the lounge room at the funeral home tomorrow where my family will be all day for my Aunt who passed away.  I wanted something sweet, and easy to eat - finger food but not necessarily chocolate.  Lets face it, EVERYONE brings chocolate - I like to be different. ;)  This recipe was SO EASY!  They TASTE GREAT!  Major bonus points for this being so easy to follow that I was able to prep the dough and throw it in the fridge in the morning before work and then come home after a long day and not start filling and rolling until 10:00 p.m. AND THEY STILL TURNED OUT!  My brain is fried right now from work, stress and exhaustion and I still managed to make these, and they taste good.  It doesn't get better than that!

I've had rugelach tons of times growing up, and they never did anything for me. However, today I needed to make something for my in-laws, and I had a huge block of cream cheese from costco in the fridge, so I decided to make these. After they finished one, I tried it just to make sure it was edible, and... it was soooo good! I couldn't believe it! Maybe I DO like rugelach, and just never had had good ones! They were easy and gorgeous. Only substitution was hazelnuts for walnuts.

I fell in love with all kinds of Austrian pastries while traveling in Austria and dining at Vienna's Demel. I made these cookies as one of my Christmas gifts for my dad last year. Since my dad has a nut allergy, I substituted toasted sesame seeds for the walnuts or pecans. The dough bakes to be light and flaky while the cinnamon, brown sugar filling melts and caramelizes developing a surprisingly deep, delicious taste. My father actually mistook the filling for date spread or fig jam because of its intensely fragrant flavor. Thank you, Karen=^..^=, for this beautiful Eastern European delight!
I would give this more stars if there were any. Very good dressing. Thank you for sharing it.
Wonderful dressing, Great photo.  Thank you for sharing.  Lolly

Super dressing!  I made as is except left out the poppy seeds this time.  I used it as the dressing for Warm Mushroom & Spinach Salad #179514 and it was great.  You did really well with your tweaking Sharon Anne!

I really enjoyed this dressing!  It was just perfect with baby greens, strawberries, mandarin oranges and toasted almonds. I was concerned that it might be a little sweet and will leave out the sugar next time I make it.
Love this!!  Used it on green salads with nuts and fruits.  Also tastes good with a bit of feta.  Thanks.

This is my new favourite dressing...kudos to the chef!  I reduced the mustard to 2 teaspoons (personal preference), and used a whisk to combine ingredients because my immersion blender made the dressing very thick, but otherwise I think the balance of ingredients is perfect. Thank you for submitting.

I had a strawberry salad with a raspberry vinaigrette that was to die for a few months ago. It was a creation of one of the top caterers in Atlanta, so of course the recipe was a secret. This recipe is the closest I have found to it. I use a few more raspberries than what the recipe calls for, but it is awesome! Thanks!

I just finished making this for a dinner party that's due to start in 30 minutes -- but I didn't want to wait to tell you how good it is!  Just the right sweet/sour combination, lots of flavor -- this is a definite keeper!
Delicious.  Served on a spinach, strawberry, & toasted pecan salad.  I did scale this way down, but it was easily done.  Will use again.

Awesome recipe!  I didn't use sugar (sweet enough), or frozen raspberries (I forgot to get them), didn't need them either.  I used raspberry balsamic.  I made a salad with spring mix lettuce, pecans, dried currants, and feta.  It rocked!  Thanks for posting!

Fantastic rich dressing!  We had a spinach salad this weekend at one of our favorite restaurants and they used Raspberry dressing, bacon, hard boiled eggs and red onion.  I wanted to recreate this because I thought the Raspberry dressing really gave this salad great flavor.  This dressing comes very close.  Thanks for a great recipe!
I didn't follow the recipe exactly, but my 4yo asked for seconds on salad, so it must have been good! Thanks for a great idea.

Incredible! Really delicious over a spinach salad made with bacon, hard-boiled egg, purple onion, and fresh raspberries. I also used on a salad of mixed greens with grilled chicken and fresh raspberries. Will definitely make this one again. Thanks for sharing!
Very good. I've played with omitting one or two ingredients (sugar, dijon, poppy seeds) and made as written. Great with any variation. Lots of compliments from others too.
Loved it! I didn't have the raspberry vinegarette on hand so I added more raspberries and rice wine vinegar. Delicious with grilled chicken!

I am typically not a fan of raspberry vinaigrette dressing because they're always so sweet (I cut down on the sugar a little).  I needed one though for my pomegranate raspberry salad I'm serving on Christmas Eve.  I just tested this recipe now and WOW, what fantastic flavor without being overly sweet.  The poppy seeds are a great addition as well.  I used the emulsion blender, but it didn't blend it as well as I would have liked, so will use my mini prep food processor next time. Thank you so much for this recipe that I will make over and over again.

Very good!  The flavor of this dressing is as good as store bought!  I loved knowing exactly what was in my dressing and loved that there were no preservatives in it.  I did not realize until recently that there were preservatives in the popular store brands.  I could not find any without...the reason I started looking here for recipes.<br/>  I was a little short on oil, so dressing was a bit potent, but I like a bit more vinegar taste anyhow. <br/> Also, I did not have poppy seeds on hand. I am sure they would have enhanced the appearance, but I am not sure if they contribute to flavor. ???  <br/>It was a little thick for my preference.  Next time I may use the emulsion blender to blend the raspberries and vinegar first and then add the remaining ingredients and just shake to blend.  That may allow for a thinner dressing.
Made to use on Recipe #231575.  Great flavor and added to the salad with candied almonds.  Emulsified beautifully with a hand blender.

This was very good! Although I didn't have any raspberry vinegar or raspberry jam I just used about 2/3 c of raspberries and balsamic vinegar and only a teaspoon of sugar. I don't care for poppy seeds so I didn't add any.
Tastes delicious!

This came out delicious! I added a few more raspberries to make up for lack of raspberry vinegar and added rice vinegar instead. It was very thick and creamy. I omitted the poppy seeds because I coudn't find mine.

This is nice. I did use homemade stock instead of bouillon cubes, because I am being careful of salt content. I also used fresh garlic and parsley. My bacon wasn't sliced, so I chopped it fine. My only question about this recipe is the 20 to 25 minutes simmering time. I did simmer my soup for 20 minutes on the lowest setting of my range, but quite a lot of liquid evaporated and I had to add more water. Thank you for an interesting recipe. I'll be using it again.

This was really good and quite simple to make.  Baked the squash and sausage in the morning and put them together in the afternoon for lunch.  Topped with smoked cheddar cheese and zapped them in the microwave.  Great make ahead dish that can make weeknight meals a snap.

I would have never thought to put these ingredients together, but I am mad about it! The sweetness of the squah with the zestiness of the sausage, earthiness of the mushrooms and creaminess of the sour cream work spectacularly together! I did add a very generous dash of garlic powder to the sausage mixture will browning it, and with the sour cream I stirred in about 1/2 c. freshly shredded parmesan and some chopped parsley. I was in heaven while eating it. Just so incredibly good!
Very well done, Lainey.  Not a thing to complain about here.  All the flavors combined well.  Only thing I added was a sprinkle of paprika for added color.  Will have this again.

Such a surprisingly good dish - agree that the combination of ingredients is not something I would normally think to use, but so glad I tried this recipe!  I pre-cooked the acorn squash in the crockpot (whole) as I hate cutting squashes -- they are so hard!  My husband, who will never try squash, actually hate half a squash, because the sausage was included.  A keeper! (Both my husband, AND the recipe!)
Great concept!  I ended up using ground turkey, sweet onions, and red bell peppers with low fat sour cream (that's all I had on hand) and it came out fantastic.  Thanks for such a wonderful idea!

I've made this a couple times and I just love it. I love winter squash without all the sweet stuff added. One of the times I made it I didn't have mushrooms so I substituted shredded carrots and celery. It was very good, though I prefer the mushrooms. Thanks!

I can say that the filling is very good even though there is no cheese in it.  I used fat-free sour cream.  It's great mixed with the sausages (I used spicy), mushrooms and onion.  The only thing I didn't like is the acorn squash.  It was my first time tasting it and I won't buy it.  I think it's too sweet for my taste.  Thanks Lainey :)  Made for Photo tag.  I would do the filling to use with spaghetti squash.  It would be delish :D
This was easy to put together and tasted good. My husband wanted butter on the squash, but otherwise I wouldn't change anything (I didn't think it needed it...) I used mild bulk pork sausage.

Absolutely love the stuffing! The sour cream really makes it. I used spicy sausage and I love the contrast with the sweetness of the squash.

I was afraid like another reviewer that I would need to add a little butter to the squash, but the stuffing has so much flavor I didn't find I needed it.

I may try making it with lowfat ingredients next time because I bet that will be great too.

A great savory dish just in time for Autumn. I made this with hot Italian pork sausage, onion, mushrooms, and celery plus salt, pepper, garlic powder, and parsley. The sour cream is a must and I can see how cream cheese would be a good option as well. The stuffing is amazing! Didn't season the squash because we mixed it up with the stuffing in the skin while it cooled down.

Two of us were eating - one of us does not like squash, both of us thought this was great.<br/>I followed the recipe as written, but halved it since there was only one lonely squash in the bowl.<br/>The recipe was so easy to prepare, I'm sure I will be making it again.<br/>Thank you for this!

I only used one squash because there was only two of us for dinner tonight.  We thought it could use a little seasoning, which could be solved by using a spicier sausage.  We just added a little garlic salt, onion salt and pepper. That did the trick! We both enjoyed it.
This was really good. We will make this again. I made the recipe as written but added a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese on top.

This was easy to work with and tasted really good.  My son used this for a high school Government project.  He made the Berlin wall, two soldiers and a base.  I think we probably rolled it a little thick, because I don't think we would have gotten 3 houses out of it if that was what we were going for, but it worked for us.  We will be using this recipe at Christmas to make Gingerbread houses.  Thanks for posting!
this is amazing! i haven't had gingerbread this good in a long time. great recipe, i'll be using it at christmas time. thanks.

I chose this because it said, "This dough is very easy to work with."  It was and it makes delicious cookies as well.  So many times I have tried to make cut out cookies with my kids and been disappointed with the either the process or the end result.  This was so good.  First of all, watching the dought foam up was really cool and kind of gave the project a science angle.  Second, the dough didn't have to be refrigerated.  This is great, because kids have a hard time waiting.  Third, it was so easy to roll out.  I sprinkled sugar on the surface just in case and had no problems.  My 8 year old daughter did most of the work rolling and cutting.  We iced the cookies using the recipe that came in the box with the icing bags and tips.  We had a great time during the whole process.  The end result is beautiful.  Thank you Luv2Bake for a recipe that will now be passed around among my friends and family and will become a Christmas classic in my house.

My thanks to you for this recipe.  It made the most delicious gingerbread cookies that I decorated with various colored sprinkles.  They look so festive and will definitely fit in nicely with the other Christmas treats on my holiday tray.  And another great recipe has found a place in my special occasion cookbook!!!

Hate to be a grinch but I found this dough to be aych-eeey-double-hockey sticks to work with. Too sticky, but somehow at the same time it was way too dry, and I didn't even use all the flour it called for. To compensate I added water and kneaded until I got the right consistency. THEN I had to use lots of flour when rolling it out to keep it from sticking. Very sticky. At 1/4" thickness I barely got 1 house out of it, average size house. Then it cracked lots and badly when rolling it out. To top it all off it bubbled in the oven instead of coming out flat. Very frustrated with this recipe. Kudos to those who could make it work, cuz I sure couldn't!

Delicious!  This dough was very easy to work with.  I got 1 small house, and a dozen 4" cookies out of 1 batch.  I checked my cookies after 6 minutes and to my surprise they were done.  I wanted to take a picture of the house, but it tasted so good we already ate it :-)

Wonderful recipe for when you need to make cookies fast, and don't have time (or don't want) to wait for the dough to chill!

I think the recipe is a bit finicky. The first time I made it, it turned out exactly as expected. The second time, the dough was awfully crumbly, and I had to add a bunch of water and some oil, but the end result was fine. I used brown sugar the first time and white the second, and we'd had a dy spell for several days before the second time, so the flour had been more dry than normal.

I also added an extra quarter teaspoon or so of ginger.

FUN!!!  Making this dough was a lot of fun - especially when it bubbled up.  Made enough for one gingerbread house with 5x5 walls and roof.  Tastes great too!!  I also would cut out a window and before baking would add crushed candies such as jolly ranchers and then bake - came out as stained glass windows!!  Thanks!

Thanks so much for this recipe!!!  I tried this out this afternoon and it turned out perfect.  I have the gingerbread mold from Pamper Chef and use this recipe on this mold. I found the recipe that came with the mold way too dry and not very tasty.  This worked really good and tasted great.  I just baked it for 17 minutes and it was fantastic, can't rave enough!!!  Thanks again.
we made this with cookies and after when anyone tried it they liked it and after we made them they stayed soft i loved them!!

This recipe really is fantastic! The only thing I did differently was to use shortening instead of margarine. The dough is extremely easy to work with and tasty, as well. I was able to roll and re-roll it and it held up. Thank you for the recipe!

I'm so glad I found this recipie again- somehow I forgot to review it last year at this time.  This really does make an easy to work with dough that is delicious!  I made cookies for the whole family last year and they disappeared stealthily in no time!  Heating the spices made my whole apartment smell warm and wonderful too.  Thanks for posting this unique recipie!

Wow!  We have made gingerbread houses 3 days this week and have had a ball!  This is the easiest dough I have ever worked with.  I think adding the flour to the warm mixture cooks the flour somewhat and makes a dough the consistency of play dough.  I lightly floured the surface to roll the dough out, but only enough to keep it from sticking.  I loved this recipe and am already sharing it with all my friends!  This will be a new tradition for us!  Thank you for the GREAT recipe!

This dough was a pleasure to work with! The recipe yielded two small houses and a dozen cookies that we used as ornaments by poking a small hole through the top edge of the cookies with a straw before baking. I will definitely be using this recipe yearly from now on. It is truly unique, easy, and delicious!
This was a great recipe. Thank you!

It was easy to work with as promised -- made a very gingery dough. I like that it didn't need refrigerating too. Made them for a cookie party and the kids ate them up. ONE CAVEAT!: When you add the baking soda, it REALLY foams up! I had selected a sauce pan that proved to be too small -- when it started foaming over the top, I had to grab another bigger pan to pour it in. I baked the cookies for 11 minutes and they turned out fine.

Very nice recipe.  Made this with my four yr old daughter.  We followed the recipe except subbed organic whole wheat white flour and organic butter for the margerine and for the sugar we did half turbinado and half brown to make the half cup.  The directions couldnt have been simpler and this being my first time making gingerbread from scratch I was not sure if I could do it.  The dough came out perfectly and we made a little house, some trees and people/angels to go with it.  My daughter was thrilled and gave the taste and texture two thumbs up as well.  Taste was just like what we get at wholefoods; not too gingery but rather just right, and the texture was great; not cakey, but not too hard either.  Terrific and thanks for sharing!  This helped make a nice Christmas memory for my daughter and myself.

This cookie is sooo... yummy.  It doesn't need any icing to be enjoyed and is not too.. hard to eat.  I highly recommend this cookie.  I must confess I was a little worried when I first started to roll it out as it seemed very crumbly, but a little pat of butter and the dough held up fine.  Thank-you for making this first time gingerbread cookie maker a lover of this cookie.  My kids will love decorating these delights as well as eating them.  Happy holidays to you.

We really enjoyed this gingerbread.  The dough was a little fiddly in the beginning, but once you work it and get it warmed a little it's great to work with.  I did half the dough one day and half the next - the second batch was far better, since the spices had time to work their way through all of the dough.  I think I might add a little salt next time to really bring out the flavour.  Great with a lemony glaze!
Everyone at the office raved about these!  I iced 1/3 of them with the corn syrup/powdered sugar recipe and it was wonderful.  Thanks again, maybe next year I wll try to build the house :)
The recipe was so super simple and tastes fantastic! I used it to make gingerbread trees for xmas and found it a breeze! The cookies looked fantastic and the mixture was easy to work with!
it was delicious, but burnt eaisly :S
We'll be making this our gingerbread house recipe. :o)
Was great to work with however I don't think it would have yielded 3 houses.
Great dough for gingerbread. I used it for the first time this year in a set of house molds and it came out just fine. It's definitely going to be my gingerbread house recipe from now on.

Wonderful recipe! I had to make a castle for social studies with it. Me and my mom have no complaints whatsoever. At first it seemed very dry but with a little more elbow grease, we got it to a firm dough perfect for a large gingerbread castle.
Thank-you

First let me say that I truly enjoyed these cookies but the experience I had making these outshined the actual cookies.  I made these with my twin 2-year old granddaughters and did we ever have a blast.  We used every cookie cutter I had in the drawer as well as every confection/sprinkles/decorations.  It was a great experience all the way around.  Also, my 2 dogs enjoyed the cookies since they each got one decorated with doggies treats on top!
Thank you for sharing this recipe, the cookies were truly scrumptious and I'll be making these for the xmas season as well.  (Made for ZWT4)
Great recipe! Thanks! My men came out perfect!

This gingerbread turned out awesome!  It looked exactly like the  stuff you buy in the store for 10 bucks a pop.  It was really sturdy (my kids didn't even break it).  I will be using this recipe for all our holiday gingerbread houses from now on.  Honestly, this is the recipe you are looking for.  Thanks tons!
what a GREAT recipe! I just saw it an hour ago, and my 2 sons and I just baked enough walls for 3 houses (4x4), and they made some extra ginger bread men. VERY yummy & easy!!!!thanks SO much!!!!!!!!

Heh, it was pretty funny because my problem was oppisite to many. My dough was too sticky! But I just floured it alot and it worked out perfectly fine. The taste itself was wonderful. The gingerbread were soft and spicy, and so irresistable with icing on top. I will definetly make these again.

Very sticky dough, I did have to add quite a bit of flour, and had trouble rolling out.  Taste was awesome, and talk about sturdy.  I made a large gingerbread house (first timer), walls 8x11 and roof approx.  cookies were crispy and yet not rock hard.  perfect if you ask me.  I'll deal with the stickyness if it gets me results like this.  I love it, thanks.

I'm so glad I chose this recipe, the flavor is wonderful, not too spicy, and the texture for building a house is perfect. My 9 yr. old and I had a lovely time using all of my neat gadgets to cut out windows and doors. We used the blue Jolly Ranchers for the windows. Now we need to build it with icing. Thanks!

Great tasting, fairly staight forward in a complicated way, haha. I like mine a bit softer so I've shortened the bake time to 9 min, they're kinda fragile but deliciously fluffy. I didn't have time to finish baking my other half, so I stuck it in the refrigerator, and warning to future bakers, this is NOT A GOOD IDEA. I was able to salvage it by crumbling into pieces and adding some water and kneeding it back together, but the refrigerator really made it very dry and hard(literally) to work with. Aside from that, this recipe is fabulous. Absolutely wonderful texture. Thank you! [MLP]

This is a great recipe for gingerbread!! The dough came together wonderfully! This is the first time I have ever made gingerbread and it was really cool to watch it puff up in the saucepan!! It's a real science experiment!! I learned while baking that the best method is to bake your cookies or pieces on foil so that you don't have to try to remove them from a baking sheet but just transfer the foil and pieces to a cooling rack!! This keeps your pieces from the risk of breaking. I used the recipe for recipe#19250 by Miss Annie and it held my house together and the pieces in place well. Had a great time and used this to enter the Zaar 2008 Gingerbread House contest. Thanks for the recipe!!!
Fantastic recipe, great tasting gingerbread. I made about 4 dozen cookies, next time I might try a house.

Let me start by saying that I trust this sight so much that I made a tripple batch right off the bat since I had to make 6 gingerbread houses!  It was a bit of a mistake, I pulled a Cramer!  not realizing how much it would bubble up, I ended up transfering it to a larger bowl and then a larger bowl again!  By the time I got it all mixed up my arms were tired and I had a dishwasher full of dishes.  Having said all that, it rolled out and baked beautifully.  I will use this again and again, I'll just start with a larger pot and bowl!  This was so much easier and faster than using my mould.  Thanks!

This is a wonderful recipe!  I found my grandmother's cookie cutters and wanted to do something special for some friends.  I've never baked Gingerbread cookies before  and this was great fun!  The kneading provided excellent hand therapy as well.  Thanks Luv for a great baking experience!
Wonderful recipe.  My son and I made a double batch and got a huge house and dozens of large gingerbread men.  Very fun to make and tasty cookie.

Amazing ^ ^
I had never tried heating the molasses like that, but the cookies came out better than my grandma makes. I've been blabbering about this recipe since I tried it, and I'm positively sure I'm going to try it again. Thankyou, Luv! Now my xmas season has been started the right way. :D
This dough is so easy to work with, and the coolies taste great too.  My fussy 8 and 4 year old loved them.

An excellent recipe.  I used this to make my very first Gingerbread House and the rest of the dough was made into Gingerbreadmen.  Easy to follow recipe and the dough was great to handle.  I subbed butter for the margarine.  My house didn't turn out as pretty as the ones posted but I'm very chuffed with it!  Thanks for a great recipe!!  Oh, I got the templates for the house by googling "gingerbread house templates free".

Every Christmas, I Google a recipe for gingerbread, but I've never found one that was actually worth keeping. This recipe, however, is THE recipe! The cookies are not too spicy (great for kids!), they turn out a beautiful color and texture, and--overall--taste absolutely wonderful. I'm making more tomorrow!
The best recipe ever! I made santa's sleigh and deers :)

I'm basing the review of this recipe not on taste, but on ease to use for making a gingerbread house.  I actually used this recipe twice, the first time was a disaster as it came out WAY to dry to work with.  However, It's winter in MN, so a dry environment is natural and given all of the great reviews I had to try again!  Today I did a double batch and used only 5 cups of flour, turned out GREAT!  The dough was a little soft to begin with, but I just kneaded flour into it as needed while rolling out the house pieces.  As time went on though it didn't need nearly as much flour added and the double batch was enough to make 1 really large gingerbread house.  I'll use this recipe again, but with less flour to start out!

We used this recipe last year and forgot to leave a review. So, here we are again this year and I madly searched for this recipe to create these perfect gingerbread cookies and house. UNBELIEVABLY delicious! Chewy by 10mins and perfect for the house by 15mins. 
We also cut out windows and put the pieces of crushed Jolly Ranchers in them to create stained glass windows. I believe I learned that from a review on here last year. What a fanastic site. 
I've found if I don't follow the recipe exactly, it's not as easy to roll out so take my word for it... follow LUv 2 Bake's EXACT instructions and you'll have moist, easy to roll out dough!

Thank you so very much for this recipe once again!

this was great for our gingerbread houses.  i made 2 decent sized houses and a small one.  i did roll the dough pretty thin, but it had no problems at all as far as strength when putting together.  i used burnt sugar to put it together so it was pretty quick and wasn't going to move at all.  i will use this recipe again next year.
I made two good sized houses and a couple dozen gingerbread men out of a double recipe.  It tastes great, was easy to work with and the houses turned out fabulous!!  Thanks so much!!
