My 5 yo wanted to make "real" gingerbread men. I tried this one bcz it required no sitting or chilling. We loved kneading it and had no trouble with cracking or stickiness. It was PERFECT! The only time it started to crack was after the 2nd time or two re-rolling the scraps. No big deal. I only had 1/8 C molasses so I also used dark corn syrup. Great taste. The 5 yo kept eating the small scraps! Baked for 14 minutes and came out just right. It made over 4 trays of cookie shapes. Will save and give recipe to friends! Thanks Luv.  I put this into my book#234006.

I love this gingerbread dough! I made gingerbread men and various cut-outs and we did not have even one broken cookie while frosting - they are very sturdy cookies. I chilled the dough overnight (I ran out of time to finish) and wouldn't do that again as the dough was tough to roll out.  I loved the taste of these cookies too and plan to make them year after year!!

Our gingerbread house is about 10 days old now and its still standing strong and making the house smell wonderful!  We built a monstrosity, and made this recipe over and over again and every batch came out fabulous.  Tip:  If the dough seems too stiff to roll out, add 1 tsp water at a time, working the dough thoroughly in between to make sure you aren't adding too much.  Conversely, if the dough is too gooey, sprinkle flour generously as you flatten and roll out.  I recommend a silicone sheet for rolling, then you cut away what you don't want and transfer the silicone sheet with the dough on it directly to your cookie sheet and bake!  Use the sheet again to remove the baked piece to a cooling table.  This will save HUGE amounts of frustration, I promise!

Sturdy AND tasty!  I have made up this recipe twice and am now printing it out so dd can make her own gingy-house.  I made a house which is so pathetic I'm not going to upload pics, but it's strong as anything - any shortcomings are due to my impatience and lack of artistry.  I melted sugar to hold pieces together and it worked great.  This recipe doesn't compromise flavour for strength, as the gingerbread hearts I cut out of the extras have proven.  Also great for gingerbread men, a great project to do with kids.  HOWEVER, be warned that some kids may not enjoy the flavour of gingerbread, period.  My dd says it tastes "mediciney," which is probably due to the molasses.  Maybe it's an acquired taste!

I made gingerbread cookies for the first time for an winter orientation event at my university.  A double batch yielded 41 5-inch cookies.  They were very sturdy and have really good flavor! However the statement "the dough is very easy to work with" I found was a false hope.  I found it very difficult to incorporate the last 2 cups of flour into the dough and in the future will only use 3 cups of flour per batch.
Thanks for the recipe!

I made this at Christmastime, for houses and cookies.  I made the first 2 batches with molasses as stated.  It was PERFECT!  It was very easy to work with, as the recipe states. It was perfect.  When I went to make batch 3, I didn't have enough molasses and used dark brown corn syrup (I found the substitution online)  THAT batch was horrible, it was sticky and not nearly as tasty.  I threw that stuff out and went back and made 2 more  batches exactly as the recipe states, with molasses, and those two batches were perfect like the first two!  This has become my favorite recipe. The smell and taste were wonderful and the dough was soft and fun to work with, that warm dough in your hands is almost therapeutic! (Just don't substitute anything, follow the recipe as written!)

i subbed 4 1/2 tsp of pumpkin pie spice instead of the other spices. i also added in a little bit of black pepper. 

definitely use a medium sized pot, i used a small one and it almost overflowed once i added the baking soda. i really liked how the mixture became very mousse like afterwards though, and melting in the margarine was a breeze, much easier than letting it sit till room temp and mixing it in while solid. 

this dough was so easy to work with, didn't need any refrigeration at all, just very minimal dusting of flour and it rolled out and cut so nicely.

i baked at 350 for 10 minutes since i was baking something else at that temp concurrently. they came out fine.

next time, i will add more spice and more black pepper though for more flavor, i may also use butter instead.
Turned out beautifully, and will be great fun for my kids to decorate.  Thanks.
This dough is wonderful to work with and very easy to make. I made two batches for a gingerbread victorian mansion. I would definately make these again when I find my gingerbread man cutters.
This is a really good recipe. I loved that you didn't have to refrigerate it. It was quick and easy, and it made really good cookies!

WOW!!!  This is the ONLY gingerbread recipie I'll ever need!!!  I made 5 batches (yup, 5) today for a 'house' party I'm having.  No substitutions needed, easy dough to work with (great for 4 yr olds), great flavor and texture!  I did cut windows and used crushed butterscotch candies for that 'glow from within' look.  I'll send pics of the finished masterpieces...thanks SO much for sharing!
Will not use this one again.
This recipe is amazing for a gingerbread house.  The dough is very easy to make, and rolls out perfectly.  Cooking time of 12min is perfect for gingerbread houses.

This was pretty good but initially the dough was really dry and wouldn't stick together.  I added more butter, (melted) and some water.  Once it was fixed up it worked great.  I had exactly enough for my gingerbread house.  I'm making it again today!

very easy to make and work with! i couldnt believe how pliable the dough was but very tough it could be handled over and over. we used it to make a GB house but it tasted good too. and fun to make with the foaming. thanks i will keep this if i ever make a GB house again!
nice to find a gingerbread recipe that did require several extra hours to let the dough sit.

I tried this last night and accidentally use Gluten free flour in place of regular flour.  I did not realize that Ihad the wrong flour until I wondered why the ginger bread was breaking apart. If I had realized that I use the wrong flour I could have added some xantham gum and they would have been perfect! They had good flavor.
easy, quick and tasty - loved the fact that the dough didn't have to chill

I have tried so many recipes for gingerbread houses, this one is by far the best!  The dough is truly easy to work with and is foolproof!  Thank you so much for making an old tradition so much less stress free.
this came out great! So easy to make, roll, cut and bake!

I liked this recipe for a few reasons. First, because I was able to roll it out pretty thin and it still held up to what seemed like lbs and lbs of icing/candy. Second, because of it's ease. Third, and maybe most importantly, it was delicious. I'm not one for crunchy style cookies but this proved to be very tasty. Especially with coffee. We let some guests demolish our leftover gingerbread houses during a party and they were raving at how good it tasted. Thanks for the keeper!

I made two DOUBLE batches of this because I was trying to make enough pieces for 6 houses, and I came up short (My fault - I kept eating the dough; it was so yummie!).  The first batch was tougher to roll - it was a dry day, and I think I had added too much flour.  The second batch I ran out of molassas and had to add corn syrup - that batch came out stickier (it was also raining), and it fluffed up the cookies a little bit more.  The cookies SMELL great, and the pieces I've nibbled on (from the sixth piece, which we didn't use) are very good - not as tasty as they smell, but still very good!!
It's great! Best texture to work with-- so smooth. The cookies look lovely and taste good too.

Tripled this recipe - rolled out every scrap of dough perfectly! Loved not having to dust the countertop with flour.  Baked 13 sets of 'gingerbread nativity sets'........now for the fun of icing and decorating.  Couldn't have chosen a better recipe for my first attempt at baking with gingerbread!!
I found this dough very hard to work with, but the cookies tasted good :)

I loved the baking soda part, its so fun to watch foam up. I found the first batch wasnt sweet enouph for my taste so i added in an extra half cup of sugar without any problem. I am making a ginger bread house and will continue using this recipe for years to come for houses because its fun, the dough rolls out like play dough, and the rectangular shapes keep thier form very well! Very wonderful recipe, thank-you for sharing:)
Worked well.  I chilled the dough I wasn't using (the weather was warm) and added more ginger than called for.  We made three small houses and at least a dozen cookies.

This dough was easy to make and amazing to work with...no sticking, very sturdy even when rolled thinner than the recipe calls for.  There was more than enough dough for a medium sized gingerbread castle with four towers...

Scrumptious.  The flavor and texture is exactly what I had in mind when I wanted to make gingerbread cookies.  I've now made this several times.  The dough is very easy to work with.  I agree with another reviewer that the dough seemed to dry and crumbly but it actually works extremely well.  It broke up and crumbled upon first rolling but I just shoved it together and rolled more and it was great.
Tough enough to make a sturdy gingerbread house, yet snappy and delicious. Made one large gingerbread house and about 12 cookies. This is going in the permanent Christmas file!
This is the best gingerbread recipe ever! So easy, so fast. Like pp said it's not a sweet cookie, which is a good excuse to load it with icing and candy :o) I used this recipe to make 5 mini houses.

My 4th year using this fantastic recipe!  It's so hard to find molasses where I am so quite often I have subbed honey.  Not as wonderful as the molasses (flavour and colour) but still very VERY good gingerbread!  Last year I decorated our whole Christmas tree with gingerbread cookies (and lights of course) and it turned out awesome :)

I am cut-out cookie-phobic, but now that I have little ones it's my duty, right?!  Well, I've tried a few recipes over the past few holidays and gotta say this is the easiest and least temperamental!  It is not as sugary as most recipes, so if you're not frosting you'll need to take that into consideration.  One of the reviewers stated that it's almost therapeutic because you knead it while it's still warm and I have to agree.  My only change after reading other reviews is to not add all the flour at the beginning.  It's really dry here in SoCal so didn't want crumbly dough.  I added about 2 1/2 cups of the flour to start and then kneaded in another 1/2 cup on my board and then used about another 1/4 cup as bench flour.  I've already shared with many friends and will use again next year.  Thanks for a great recipe!
This was a totally frustrating dough to work with; very crumbly and dry. It only started to work ok with the addition of a couple tablespoons of water. Even then, super fiddly.

Really really good recipe. I copied the recipe exactly as written. The flavour of these guys is a big seller for me. I rolled the dough out as thin as dared on parchment paper, (pretty thin.) pealed them off and transferred to the baking sheet lined with parchment paper. I baked for 9 minutes at 325. They reminded our family of gingersnaps and everyone loved them. I got a mix of Large snowmen, med. gingerbread men and med. stars.. Total cookies about 48. Thanks for the awesome recipe

This is the most fantastic gingerbread recipe I have ever tasted!  I thought it was strange at first that you boil the ingredients and mix it together in the pot, but it made the process so easy and the clean-up was quick.  The dough is great to work with, I did not need any extra flour at all to roll it out, and I loved that I could use it right away and not refrigerate it.  I tripled the ingredients and made 3 large gingerbread houses from it, with not a scrap of dough left over.  This is now my go to recipe for gingerbread, I will never use another recipe again!

I used this dough to make a gingerbread house and a few gingerbread cut-out trees to decorate. The dough was great to work with right after being made, but (as another reviewer mentioned) DO NOT put the dough in the refrigerator to use another time. I only had enough time to bake half of the dough the day I made it, so I put the rest away to use the next day. I could barely even roll it out without it crumbling into pieces and making a horrible mess everywhere. I tasted a cookie on the first day that I made and baked them and, unfortunately, I wasn't particularly happy with the taste. They smelled absolutely fantastic but tasted super plain and just not that good. I followed the recipe exactly, but maybe I still did something wrong. I will still use this recipe to make houses with (since mine are only display and the texture and smell matter most in that capacity anyway) but I won't use this recipe for cookies that I plan to eat.

Made one batch last night and another one already today.  Made 3 houses and tons of various cookies.  I used only about 3 cups of flour per batch.  This is my first attempt at a homemade gingerbread house, and I see no need to look for another recipe.  This is perfect.  Now, time to decorate!

I just slid these out of the oven and I am thrilled! After reading other posts, I only put in 3 cups of flour and saved the rest for kneading and rolling. It was perfect. I rolled the dough on parchment paper, used my cut outs and peeled away the excess so I could make the dough thinner. Mine was closer to 1/8 inch than 1/4 inch and I reduced bake time to 9 minutes. My last set of pieces were even thinner so I could get a full second house out of it. They smell great and I really don't plan to eat them, only decorate them for centerpieces. As another post said, I google recipes every year but this is THE ONE. I can use this in years to come with grandkids (and I don't have any yet-that's how long I plan to use this recipe).

This recipe calls for far too much flour... or way too little everything else. Our dough was very dry; we had a hard time even rolling out the dough without it cracking. Because the dough was dry, we shortened the baking time to 7 minutes, which was plenty for cookies. When we finally had cookies to eat, we were disappointed at the lack of flavor--they tasted mainly like flour (which shouldn't have been a big surprise, given the quantity!). Look elsewhere for a gingerbread recipe if you're actually hoping to enjoy eating these.

This is such a great recipe! I was taken in by the ease of it. Then the flavor did me in. Yum! It is very delicious and crazy simple to make! I had two four year olds helping me and we all agreed that this is well worth 5 stars!

This is the least complicated gingerbread dough recipe I've found!! The directions are easy to follow, and while it took a little time, it was not nearly as bad as I feared it would be. My children were able to help! Also, I had rolling out dough, but this was easy. It handles well and tastes great!! The whole house smells amazing! I'm using this to make my very first gingerbread house. I'm not sure how well the template I used will work, but I know that if it doesn't stay together it's not because of the dough!!!

Stacey

PS- I did use butter instead of margarine.
Very good recipe! Thank you! :)

I made one batch of this recipe (I didn't have allspice or cloves so I bumped up the ginger and cinnamon a bit) and it made one large gingerbread house (the roof pieces were 10" by 4", the walls were 9" by 6" and the end pieces were 9" by 4.5"). I had enough dough left over to make a couple snowmen and Christmas trees to decorate with. I LOVED that this was a one pot recipe and that the dough didn't have to chill. I was afraid that it wouldn't all come together, but when I kneaded it on the counter the dough did finally come together smoothly. Next year I'll be doubling the batch to make two houses and we'll have a friendly competition over who can decorate theirs the best! I did roll out half the dough on the baking pan (and cut away the parts I didn't need) and half of it on the counter. Rolling on the pan was really worth it to me because those pieces were much less wonky once they were baked than the ones I transfered.

I made these cookies back at Christmas time, and forgot to rate the recipe.  The dough worked up to a great texture, and was easy to roll and bake.  I made gingerbread men and Christmas trees and decorated them with squeeze bottle icing (I know, that's cheating).  Not only was the dough easy to work with, the cookies tasted great, and my entire family liked them a lot.

Easiest gingerbread recipe I've ever encountered. Made according to directions but leaving out 3/4 cup flour for kneadjng on the counter. Only required 1/2 cup due to humidity. Dough rolled out thinly and evenky without sticking to the counter (no flour required) and releasef from cutters perfectly. These baked with a slight puff but otherwise maintained their sharp edges which I love. No mlre fat and wide gingerbread men or houses. Was able to get 33 mini gingerbread houses and a dozen mini men from this recipe doubled. Absolutely no scraps! Will use it every year.
Delicious and easy. I used sorghum instead of molasses (I honestly don't know the difference
This was a great recipe to make a gingerbread house!  Worked wonderful!

We made four 4"x5" houses and one batch of dough would probably have been sufficient if they were made pretty thin....We went ahead and doubled it though and had enough for lots of gingerbread men as well.  We crush candies to put in the windows (bake these pieces over a piece of foil).  Great recipe!  Thanks for sharing!
This is the first time I ever tried to make gingerbread from scratch, and it came out beautifully!  Thanks for such a stellar recipe.

This is the best recipe I have come across, easy to follow and I love that you don't have to chill the dough. I had to add a little water, but this brought it altogether nicely and I love how it isn't at all sticky and easy to roll with minimum flour needed while rolling. The biscuits came out lovely and fluffy and kept their shape, I baked a few for longer so they were thin and crispy and a few that were a little thicker and baked for less time. I added a salted caramel topping and sprayed a few with edible gold and silver spray. Gorgeous!!! Thank You so much for sharing :)
Love this recipe. Super easy!

This is a great foundation recipe but the changes I made were too significant to warrant 5 stars for tasty gingerbread cookies. After reading several reviews and making two batches here are the final changes I made to the recipe: 1) used butter, not margarine (but only because I had butter); 2) 2 teaspoons ground ginger 3) 1.5 teaspoons ground cinnamon 4) 1.25 teaspoons ground cloves 5) about 3 cups total flour (2.5 cups to make initial dough, and 0.5 cups for the kneading and rolling of dough). 6) baked 11 minutes This resulted in dark, flavorful, ever-so-slightly soft in the middle gingerbread cookies my 4-year old son said he liked and would eat everyday (if I let him). They're not particularly sweet which is perfect for icing. I'm pretty sure if I rolled the dough more thinly (just under 1/4 inch) the cookies would be crispy. I also think using all of the flour would help create stronger cookies for a gingerbread house (3 cups for the initial dough, 0.5 cups for kneading and rolling). I made the first batch by following the recipe except I used butter (because that's what I had), and the reduced flour but while the raw cookie dough tasted great, the baked cookies were bland. If I were making a gingerbread house with no intention of eating it I probably wouldn't mind but if you're making something to eat then it can't just look good, it has to taste good. But, I still think it's a great recipe because it's so easy and quick. Definitely worth trying.

Great if you're looking to throw away baking supplies. Ruined two German pots from molasses stains and made gingerbread that looks like the cracked Arizona ground. Also the addition of baking soda caused an eruption comparable to Mt. Vesuvius. Was not anticipating that level of spillage! Giada would not be proud of this failed recipe. Cheers

Excellent! This was a great dough & required minimal effort with perfect results. I only use real butter when baking,it's imperative. I substituted 1c whole wheat flour for the AP flour. Glazed with a lemon glaze (1/4 c. Softened butter, 1/4 c. Lemon juice & 1 1/4 c. Powdered sugar) & frosted cookies warm from the oven. Thanks, we're using this one going forward!

I just made this recipe today, the flavor is amazing! I doubled the recipe to make a gingerbread house and some cookies. It yielded one medium house and 2-3 dozen cookies. I would suggest increasing the baking time of larger gingerbread pieces by about 5-10 minutes depending on how large it is. Another tip: make sure to use a large saucepan, as the baking soda makes the mixture poof up a LOT. I would not change a thing about this recipe, and I will definitely be using it for christmas!
Great recipe! I've tried other gingerbread recipes and this was the best. I made a house and ornaments.

For a 1st time gingerbread house/cookie maker. This was a very tough "dough" to work with. Think my first proble with not using a large enough sauce pan. Make sure your using a larger then you think you need pot. After that it was just really tough to "stir" with a fork 7cups of flour (I doubled) baked perfect and smells like they taste great so only took off 1 star for the toughness. ;-) Merry Christmas

I absolutely love this recipe.. nothing i bake ever comes out right but surprisingly this one came out perfect.. i made 4 houses and 8 gingerbread men... going to surprise my daughter with them tomorrow so we can decorate ... only thing is i added about half of a teaspoon more of ginger ... cookies are not too sweet by themselves but i bought loads of candy and icing so i imagine that it wouldnt be a problem.. I LOVE THIS RECIPE.. I will be using this often.. p.s. for the comment that says the molasses scortched her pan or something .. make sure you take the molasses off of the heat AS SOON AS it hits a boil.. DO NOT continue to boil it while adding the sugar and spices. :)
This is tasty dough. The easiest to work with ever. It was super dry, but after kneading as instructed it was perfect. No sticking, great texture. We will use this recipe forever!
I mixed this like the recipe calls for but its dry like rice, what went wrong?

Wonderful recipe! For one batch use a 3 quart saucepan and double batch use a 6 quart. If you stir your flour first, the measurement will always be closer to what the recipe calls for...but it all depends on how stiff you want your dough, altitude and humidity. When you cook the molasses longer and bake longer, they get darker. I followed exactly but used a little less flour and baked 10 minutes for a softer cookie. I made four 3 inch houses with 3 batches. Very spicy/molasses which I love!

12/13/15 - rated five stars no comments. 12/28/16 - Still five stars, but I want to say this dough was easy to work with, and smelled wonderful for days. There was a little spread while baking, so next time I will reduce or omit the baking soda. Since last year we decided to make creating a gingerbread house an annual tradition for my family, so there will definitely be a next time!

I made this recipe exactly as directed with the exception of using my kitchen aid dough hook, it came together beautifully, rolled easily and the cut cookies held their shape nicely while transfering. They had very minimal spread after baking and they taste absolutely phenomenal! I am going to make a second batch for a gingerbread house but will likely pop the trays into the freezer for a few minutes before baking to try to prevent spreading. I might try adding a little more spice but that is my personal preference. I bake for a living and can definitely say this is a keeper!

I am a long time baker, but haven’t done much work with gingerbread. This recipe appealed to me as it was different than the usual “cream butter and sugar..” and needed no chillling time. We loved the light sweetness of the dough so that when the frosting and candy is added, it’s not nauseating. Mild tweaks I made: I used dark brown sugar instead of white, and butter instead of margarine. Next time I think I would increase ginger to 2 tsp too. Great consistency, easy to work with. When working with children, I think the baking soda foam part is just fun too!! Thank you!
I am looking forward to making this as the reviews are great. However I have no idea how much is in a cup! Eek! I will have to Google it. ?? I cannot give more than 3 ?? until I have tried it.

The dough was super easy to work with. It made two large gingerbread houses. I used the remaining dough to make a few cookies. The mix isn't very sweet, not that gingerbread is typically super sweet, but in the future I'd use a different recipe if I were only making cookies.

Cannot believe the results of this recipe! Spent 10+ hours constructing a large and detailed gingerbread house to watch it collapse in on itself the next day due to the extreme softness of the baked dough. Heartbroken and disappointed- very surprised given the number of positive reviews but don’t be misled, this is not construction grade dough!

Substitution WORKS!! I halved the recipe just for a test to see how it would turn out. I didn't have molasses so I used honey. And yes, it worked out perfectly fine. I have to admit though, the dough was quite tough and dry, but once it's out from the oven, it'll be-depending on your thickness, soft or crumbly. Heads up, do not make it too thin unless you like crispy cookies. Next time I'll try to substitute brown sugar(melted in saucepan) instead of molasses, to see the difference. Still planning on practicing how to decorate with royal icing. :) Otherwise, it was a really simple recipe(and make sure you don't overcook it).

Love this recipe! My partner and I pumped out 4 batches easily; each batch making 1 gingerbread house plus 30 mini gingerbread men/ladies. We used 1 cup of brown sugar in place of molasses, added 1/3 cup honey, 1 tsp vanilla and increased the ginger to 2 1/2 teaspoons. We used nutmeg instead of allspice too. Love the method with melting everything on the stove and the fizzle from the baking soda is so cool, looks like caramel toffee before the flour is mixed through! If you dont have ground glove, putting a whole clove in the pot and allowing it to cook through the sugar & spice mix works fine (remove before mixing in the flour) Cheers for the recipe!

Love,love, love this recipe! I didnt have allspice so I changed it out with pumpkin pie spice. My house smells wonderful- the gingerbread houses look awesome! Definitely will continue to use this for the holidays!

Wonderful dough! I made 4x the recipe as we needed four houses. I made this recipe using 3/4 molasses and 1/4 honey, and half white sugar and half brown sugar to sweeten it a bit. The baking soda really foams up, so be sure you make the dough in a deep pan. Also as I added the flour, it became hard to stir as the dough is thick, so I added half the flour while in the pan then transferred to my mixer with the dough beater for the remaining mixing. Kneaded and rolling the dough was a breeze. The dough dries out, so wrap any you are not rolling and cutting. Also add a few drops of water if it too dry or cracking. For ginger bread houses, unless you want very thick pieces, roll to 1/4 thick.

I tried making this and the “dough” that resulted was a dry, crumbly mess. This was not my first rodeo...In other words, I know my way around a kitchen and cookie dough. No amount of kneading would turn this into a workable dough. I added exactly 3.5 cups of flour. If I could go back and do it again I would cut out one whole cup of flour. Instead I made a different recipe that was much easier and turned out great.

Highest rated recipe I could find. Tastes great and can be cooked hard for houses or soft for cookies. It’s a good go-to recipe. As far as adding the egg to a hot liquid, it worked fine because the butter (margarine)cools it down. Be careful about the heating. Boiling the sugar too long may get close to candy if not stirring and adding the butter pretty quick, The flour quantity is fine but you have to add it slowly and mix it in all the way each time. I rollled it really thin less than 1/8 inch for tea biscuits and 1/4 inch for house walls 1 foot long. It cooks best on stoneware. Especially the thin ones as they tend to overlook on the edges. Parchment paper helps but I noticed that on long pieces it causes ripples on the underside from the contraction of the cookie. Not much of issue if it is an inside wall of the house. If you want a really smooth back, flour it well and bake it right on the pan. That will also ensure even cooking. Take them out when puffy and before they look done. They will firm up when cooling. The dough is really easy to work with, my 4 yr old could smash, roll and cut her own cookies. Just keep adding flour to the work area. I personally think they could spicier but they taste good. Just don’t overcook, the 12 minutes in the instructions should only be for large thick house walls. Cookies were done in half that time. Remember thin dark pans cook faster. Stoneware is best.
