I made this using 6 boneless skinless chicken thighs from Trader Joe’s, in an oval covered glass Pyrex baking dish. I accidentally forgot to set the timer when I first put them in, so I just estimated the first 30 minutes and then cooked them uncovered until the largest thigh reached an internal temperature of 165°, and then I let them sit for five minutes. They were delicious, and although I was concerned about cook time because the chicken thighs were all different sizes, every piece came out just fine and that Sauce is WOW delicious - and so easy to throw together from pantry staples. I substituted roasted garlic powder and Chinese white pepper because that’s what I had on hand. I will definitely be making this again! It was so easy and I think my kids will love it.

Excellent!!! I have made this a few times now and the whole family loves it! It is also good with added grated fresh ginger. I sometimes add pineapple chunks at the end of cooking.....also double the sauce recipe, as it is delicious served over rice! A fast, easy, delicious ‘go to’ recipe!
Can this recipe be made with boneless skinless chicken breasts?
I like to use the low sodium soy sauce and I even dilute that with water. I have been making this for years. It is a good one.
This recipe was good! I doubled the sauce but not the garlic. I had to cook an extra 15 minutes so that chicken was cooked completely.

This recipe sounded so good. I made the recipe with only 4 chicken thighs but the full recipe for the sauce. I really needed 2-3 times as much sauce, as had not nearly enough to cover chicken when basting. Disappointing.
anybody try this in a crock pot??

This is an awesome dish.. I use a little more cheese than called for, and I sprinkle a little on the top before I put it into the oven, and it's delicious.. works when you want something crispy crunchy and cheesy but not super fattening =)

I was just about to post this recipe and searched to be sure it wasn't already in here...  Great taste and makes you feel like you are cheating when you are not.  Good way to stick beef/turkey in the rotation for the husband who gets sick of chicken all the time!

Delicious, the tortilla comes out nice and crisp without the added calories from deep frying.  I served this on a bed of shredded lettuce topped with guacamole and salsa.  The meat mixture was made a day in advance and then reheated when needed.  The tortillas were microwaved for about 20 to 30 seconds in the microwave.  The timing was excellent.

My friends loved this.  I also got it from the cookbook.  I use whole grain tortillas, which are heavier and more calories, but healthier.  Soften these in the microwave before folding, or they crack.  I serve this with jazzed up fat-free refried beans for even more fiber.

These were delicious and very easy to make!! They definitely didn't taste low fat or reduced by any means! Thanks for sharing...these are a wonderful way to get a "mexican" fix without all the fat and calories! We will definitely be having these again...soon!

OMG - This was excellent.  My boyfriend is vegetarian, so I replaced the turkey breast with a can of Navy Beans, and added a can of mushrooms.  EVERYONE (even the picky eater) loved them.  Best part, even after the substitutions the total calories were only like 260 each!  Has already been requested again for in a few weeks.  I am guessing that it is a new family favorite.  Thanks!

My family and I are ADDICTED to these chimichangas. We find ourselves making them weekly now. The hubby and I love the "skinny" factor and the kids don't even know or care that they are healthier for them. We may never eat mexican food out again. Thanks!
Fantastic!!!!  I serve with mashed avocados and fat free sour crem.  I also add 1/4 cup of salsa to the mixture to spice it up a little.  Thanks for sharing!

Wow!  These are really good.  I made it with ground beef due to personal preference.  I did notice an little bit of an odd aftertaste, I wasn't sure if it was the spices or the type of nonstick spray I used.
These are great! We served them with extra low fat cheese, salsa and low fat sour cream. Delish. Thanks for sharing this keeper!
So Yummy!  I was so excited to try it that I burnt my tongue.  :D  I used 1/4 cup of chunky salsa in place of the  chilies.  It was a family hit and we'll be making this again.
This was so good! Love that it's baked and not fried. Added some salsa and rice mixture I had in the fridge. Will definitely keep in the cookbook and make again.

5 Stars, DH & I both loved it!  It was mildly spiced which is kinder to our digestive systems, and it is easy enough to make often; anyone wishing it to be stronger could make with chopped jalapenos instead of mild green chiles, or use spicy salsa instead of tomato sauce, as others have done.  Makes about 2 3/4 cups of filling, so DH can make 2 small chimichangas (burritos) with smaller tortillas tomorrow. Made for Please Review My Recipe.

Fantastic!  Thank you for sharing your delicious recipe.  I used ground chicken and whole wheat tortillas.  It is what I had on had.  All of the flavors blend really well in this easy meal.  This is definately company worthy, and the company won't know this is healthy.

Other than using some shredded (then chopped) turkey breast, I followed the list of ingredients & had A GREAT MEAL, one well worth at least 5 stars! Thanks for a keeper of a recipe! [Tagged, made & reviewed in Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup Game]

I really liked these and thought they cooked up quickly and easily. My husband thought they lacked much spice, so if you are looking for something with a little more flavor, you may need to doctor up the spices a bit. For myself, I thought it was fine--just mildly spiced.  Thanks for sharing.

We really liked these...we opted to use jar salsa rather than all the different spices for simplicity - and to add extra moisture, veggies and flavor; it was tremendous.  Make leftovers for lunch the next day.  Your dieting co-workers will be jealous!
Another keeper. The DH proclaimed these to be the best, and would never ask for a taco again!  Thanks for the tasty recipe!

What a great recipe..and guilt free too!! I prepared my turkey mixture in advance and just reheated it,and then added the cheese,when I was ready to serve.A really simple and easy dish to prepare.The tortillas crisped up beautifully,and the whole thing just tasted great.My DH,who can eat happily eat chimichangas all day long,gave it a thumbs up.
Another winner from you Teresa,thanks x.
Scrumptious!  Easy and relatively fast for a weeknight dinner.  Thanks for posting!
Another winning recipe for Teresa. I cut the chili powder in half, and added a little more cheese. These made for a GREAT dinner last night, and defineately will make again.

Yummy! I guess you must be my chef of the week because this is the 3rd recipe of yours I have tried...(I just changed my name, it was Mama Soule :) Anywho...this was soooo good. It's things like this that makes weight watchers easy!! I opted for the extra points and had it with the sour cream. Thanx alot for posting :)
Loved the flavor and how easy these were to put together. I wish they would have been a little more crispy though, but for lowfat, these were good.  Thanks!

These are a perfect weeknight meal because they are super quick to put together.  We all liked them a lot but thought the filling was just a little bit bland.  I like CPolenchek's idea of using salsa instead of tomato sauce and will try that next time.  I also had trouble getting my tortillas to cooperate.  They kept splitting.  This may be one of the drawbacks to fat free, or it could be because I was lazy and warmed them in the microwave instead of the foil/oven method that the recipe calls for.  It didn't matter taste wise, the tortilla really did crisp up in the oven and were really tasty.  I served this a guacamole salad.  4 cup of chopped lettuce with one tomato.  The guacamole was just 1 avacodo mashed and mixed with some garlic powder, lime juice, cumin, salt and pepper.  One chimichanga and 1/4 of the salad came out to be a grand total of 370 calories and was surprisingly filling.  A bit high in fat because of the avacado, but it's healthy fat!  Definitely will add this to my rotation. Thanks!

Really loved it and so did my boyfriend who is still getting used to the whole "diet food" thing.  

I was shocked that it really tasted like a chimichanga and I love Mexican food so I was pleasantly surprised.

Made this with 1/2 turkey, 1/2 beef as that is what I had (doubled the recipe).  Instead of tomato sauce (which I didn't have and it was honestly -50Â° out)  I used salsa so that meant no green chilies either.  Kids and DH loved them--all left overs were gone the next day.  I topped with a little enchilada sauce after  baking and a little cheese.  I love sour cream so served on lettuce with that.  Delicious!
Great as is.  No changes

Fantastic recipe! Thank you so much for sharing it with us. I read some of the other reviews and took the suggestion to use salsa instead of tomato sauce since I wanted more heat. Even though I used a "hot" flavored salsa, it still came out with a sweetness to it. Maybe next time I'll throw in a bit of chopped jalapenos. Either way, it's a great and filling dish that doesn't taste diet at all.

A chimichanga that is low in fat?! Based on a recommendation from KateL, I decided to give these a try. I'm so glad that I did! These chimis may be lacking the fat but they do not lack in flavor. I thought it was a perfect combination of spices and sauce. We couldn't even tell it was ground turkey breast because of the other flavors blended in. I wouldn't change a single thing to this recipe (unless you like things hot - then you could use jalapenos, etc...).Terrific low-fat addition to our rotation. Thank you!!

We added extra spices to the meat and it was still fairly bland. If I were to make it again I think I would cook the meat with a packet of taco seasoning. My husband didn't really like this, though, so I don't think I will be making it again.

This is the first time I have used ground turkey breast in anything and it was great.  I can't rate the recipe because when I went to make the dish, I was unable to get online and follow the recipe, so I just winged it.  I added some cumin, crushed red pepper flakes, oregano, and garlic salt but the meat was still pretty bland so I ended up using taco seasoning in the turkey (1 lb of turkey), then threw in a half can of Rotel tomatoes and half a can of black beans. Used low carb tortillas and after baking, I topped them with a spicy queso and lettuce.  I think my chimichangas turned out a bit higher in calories and fat (cheese sauce) but overall still pretty healthy, very yummy and filling.

I really liked these! I thought they were pretty good and actually got much better the next day, after the flavors got to "mingle" a bit. DH thought they were good, but would like to try them with lean ground beef instead of turkey. I think next time I'll also leave out the green chiles and add tabasco sauce instead. Thanks for sharing!
We all thought these were really good and lots of flavor.  I used shredded chicken and make extra.... wrapped individually, froze and I have been having them for my lunches.

These were really good!! I'm not a big fan of ground meat of any kind so I used a can of 99%FF chicken chunks. I crumbled and squished them so they were shredded in consistency. A 12.5oz can of chicken weighed out to be 8oz without the water. Next time I will make extra and freeze for quick lunches. Thanks for this recipe!!

These were great.  I made just a couple of changes:  I doubled the recipe and used 10" tortillas; it was the right amount of filling for 6 of them.  I don't use cooking spray, so I very lightly brushed the tops with vegetable oil - probably used about a teaspoon total for the 6 large burritos, so it added very little fat.  They browned really well and my family wants me to make this again!
I use to have this cookbook and lost it, so thanks for posting this. Made it again (after 4+ years) and it was still good. Leftovers are great for lunch. Used whole wheat tortillas.

Yummy!  These were really easy to put together.  Instead of a whole onion I used a whole red bell pepper and 1/4th onion.  I also added 1/2 finely diced jalapeno.  The taste was good, we really liked the combo of spices, but I think there was just too much tomato sauce because there was a lot of sauce and it made the bottom of the chimichangas a little soggy, when we would have liked for them to be a little more firm.  I will make these again for sure, so easy, just with less tomato sauce.  Oh, we also didn't add any cheese, and didn't miss it!
These were a yummy treat for lunch yesterday.  I made exactly as stated, except used whole wheat tortillas.  I love that they are tasty and diet friendly at the same time.

These were fantastic!  Even my daughters loved them and they are picky.  I used lean ground meat instead of turkey and I let the meat simmer about an hour to really thicken.  I used quite a bit less onion but it still tates great.

Well we could tell these were "light", but they still were quite yummy and we had leftovers for lunch the next day as well.  Do serve with some salsa or similar on top, as they will be a bit dry otherwise.  
Thanks for posting.
these were really good! Thanks!

Super good chimichangas! I doubled the recipe so I could use the whole pound of ground turkey that I had. I doubled everything except the chili powder, and I also used a large onion (instead of two). For the tomato sauce and the mild green chilies, I substituted medium picante sauce, and I added a bit of Recipe #178827 into the chimichangas before I added the meat mixture. I had 8" tortillas, but I am apparently fold-deficient, so they were like open-sided chimichangas. I could've easily gotten 10 or so, but only 8 fit, because I baked them in a 9x13 glass pan (on the 2nd to top rack-my oven has 4 rack positions). The baking time and temperature were perfect, and my husband looked up while he was eating and said, "Mmmmm!" (It was so cute. :) ) I think that says I'll be keeping this one in my permanent file. I served this with the leftover Recipe #178827, and I also made Recipe #17126. We had a bit of light sour cream on top of them. Thanks so much for posting it!
Yummy! Made the recipe exactly as stated. Next time might throw in some bell peppers to the mix. Thanks for sharing a delicious, easy recipe!

I've made baked chimichangas using a different zarr recipie & this one is just as good, if not better!

I added chicken instead of turkey and used green onions instead of a reg. onion. Also, I put in some cilantro & about 1 tsp of garlic salt. For the cheese, I used reduced-fat cheddar & monterrey jack.

Normally, I would make my own salsa/pico de gallo and add that to them, but this time I stuck to what was listed (green chilies) to try it out. The hubs and I thought it was uber delicious and yummy! 

Thanks!

I started making these just as the recipe called for. I then noticed that I didn't have the flour tortillas I thought I had, so I had to used corn tortillas. I toasted them in the oven for 5 mins before I topped them with the meat mixture, then cooked them for another 5 mins to toast the cheese. We served them warm, topped with salsa. This is a tasty recipe that will satisfy your craving for mexican food without blowing your daily points. The seasoning on the meat is good, it doesn't taste like packaged taco seasoning, so it's good when you want a little something different. Thanks for sharing this recipe, next time I plan to make it exactly as called for (just got to make sure I have flour tortillas).

These were excellent! Hubby and I loved them...although the teenager didn't like the fact that they had turkey in them... Made just as stated except I doubled recipe to make 8 instead of 4 so there would be leftovers for hubby and I to take to work.  They were just as good the next day and one is filling enough.  Made with pintos and cheese. Thanks for this keeper

I doubled the recipe and didn't have any onion so I used 2 tsp of onion powder instead. I made my chimis a little big so it ended up making 7. I served it with refried beans and a dollop of sour cream. 
We all loved it! Even my two picky little boys gobbled it up! 
Thank you for sharing this great healthy recipe!

I made this a while ago and forgot to review it. It's a very tasty and easy meal.  One of my first meals on ww and so glad I found it. My bf loves it too! Thanks so much for posting. This is a recipe I'll definitely make again.
So Yummy!!! My husband really loved them. This is now one of our favorites.

Sorry but this just didn't do it for me. I was excited to try this recipe given all the rave reviews. I didn't care at all for the spices that the recipe called for they tasted like something I made up myself and not something form an atual recipe.  I gave it 3 stars because dh loved it.
These were good, I used hot salsa because I forgot to buy tomoato sauce, I did think they were better the next day as leftovers.  Dh didn't like them but he is not to big on turkey.  Thanks!!

I changed this a tiny bit. I could not find fat free tortillas or cheese (went to a different store then usual), and instead of green chili's I used a couple small pieces of jarred jalapeno's. I didn't care for how they tasted, they weren't bad, but not something I'd make again this way.. I got 6 out of this and ate 2. I didn't try eating the rest yet. But I didn't really care for them. I think if I were to add some refried beans or kidney beans and some salsa I would have enjoyed them more, but not as is. I think I might give these another try but with different ingredients now that I know the basics
Just ok. Not my favorite. Needs something extra to make it work, maybe something crunchy.

Yum!  This was a pretty good recipe.  Very easy to make as well.  I made exactly as directed, except I doubled it so I would have leftovers for a lazy Saturday!  My tortilla shells kept breaking as I rolled them...I had even warmed them up first.  Other than that though they were still a yummy supper.  Thanks for posting!  Made for Zaar Staars tag game.

Made this tonight subbing reduced fat ground pork for the turkey. I also subbed salsa for the tomato sauce, onions, and chiles. We really enjoyed this. I doubled the recipe, and had enough filling for 10 tortillas. Made for Healthy Choice ABC game. Thanks for sharing!

This was a great technique and I liked the filling as well. The ground turkey was well disguised so no worries there for those who aren't keen on it. I used the turkey this time but more often have beef on hand so will try that in the future. Like others I used salsa (home canned) in place of  the sauce and green chiles. We can't have cheese and I didn't have a replacement on hand so I blended some pinto beans and added between 1/4 to 1/2 cup to the mix. It did the trick! I also made my own tortillas out of Recipe #377353. There was enough filling for 5 chimis. Going forward I will double the recipe and freeze the extra.

I was not a big fan of these. They just didn't have a very good taste to them. I'm not sure what would help with the flavor, though. I would highly consider eating them with salsa...at the very least.
These are really healthy.  Unless you're on a special diet, you'd need to add salt in order for this to have a lot of flavor.

I love salmon, and this easy recipe is delicious. I didn't add the 'extra' butter as I found there was enough still in the pan. Will make this again.
Served with Dorothy Parks Lemon Roast Potatoes. mmmm.

Salmon...is one of those rare ingredients that can stand alone and be delicious. Dill, lemon and a touch of cream enhances the flavour of the salmon to perfection. However, what I did do was cut back on the butter in the sauce..but this is personal preferrence. This will be a family favourite. Thank you for posting this recipe. :-) UPDATE: I had this recipe again tonight. It is a wonderful Salmon recipe which is complimented by Dorothy Parks' Lemon Roast Potatoes!!!! As Evie says, "Mmmmm".
This is so easy and soooo good!  Salmon turns out creamy moist and so tasty.  Love your recipes, Inez.
DELICIOUS, YUMMY, MOIST, a great way to do Salmon, I also made it with Dorothy Parks Lemon Roast Potatoes, a great combination. Am looking forward to making this again soon.

My husband loved this recipe!  I thought it was quite good too.  It was very easy to make for a first time salmon cooker.  I did end up using the second part of the butter, but that's probably because I cooked the salmon a little longer than probably necessary.
excellent!

This was quite good.  A little greasy for my taste, so I think I will halve the butter next time.  Other than that, no complaints!  I also prepared this with the Lemon Roast Potatoes, and they complimented the dish very well.  Thanks!

Sooo delicious, Inez. Salmon is one of my favorites. I am like some of the others and only used 3 tablespoons of butter. There was enought left over in the pan to make the cream sauce. The lemon-dill and cream sauce were just the right accent to the fillets. Thanks a bunch.

This recipe was very delicious!  Made it last night for my employer and Mrs B said, wow, that was really good, where did you get the recipe?  I said "Recipezaar of course!"  Thanks MizzNezz for a really good recipe!

Okay, toast up some hawaiian rolls, make a nice salad, bake a sweet potato(top w/butter & brown sugar) and you have an instant hit.  My family inhaled this meal, and I have an eight year old picky eater.  Thanks for making me look good.
"SOOOO GOOOD" is right!!!  The whole family loved it!  Served this with baked potatoes and salad!  A delicious (and easy!) meal!  Thanks for sharing, MizzNezz! :)

Wow! I'd give this 10 or 15 stars if I could. We deemed this restaurant quality - definitely suitable for company. Like some of the other reviews - I think I'll leave out the 2nd addition of butter - it was just a little too rich and decadent (but not much!)

This was a tasty, easy recipe!! I am usually nervous of cooking salmon because it was never something that my family ate when I grew up... but this recipe was easy enough to take my fears away! I liked the cream sauce so much that I went back and made more... plus I was compelled to add extra dill!! I used "It's a Dilly" seasoning by McCormick, which is not pure dill, which might explain why I needed more. When scaled down to a single serving, this recipe was quick enough to prepare for a small meal for myself, which is something I have been looking for. I had this for lunch and am going to make more tonight to test it on my husband, who doesn't usually care for salmon. As others have suggested, I will try the Lemon Roast Potatoes as well, along with a few fried shrimp just in case my husband doesn't care for the salmon!! But I think he will... it had a great flavor. Even if he doesn't, it will go on my easy lunch recipe list! Thanks!
I really enjoyed this meal.  I would have preferred more sauce on the salmon but I would recommend this recipe to any Salmon lover.
good and easy like they all say. i added some diced tomatoes to mine, thrown up just before the cream was added. served with sauted veggies, it was filling, light and healthy.

Awsome,simple and fast way to serve salmon.  I used about a 1/2 cup of heaavy cream though - 3 tsp not near enough. I also added white wine when cooking the fish, and some dill and diced tomatoes to the cream sauce - MMMMM good!
Very good & super easy.  I agree that half the butter is plenty; more is maybe a little too much for our taste.  Otherwise perfect and couldn't be simpler.
Delicious....everyone loved this recipe..I did add a little white wine and chopped tomatoes as one person suggested..excellent and very simple to make. will make a regular at my table.
We loved this!!  It was rich, but we served it with an Australian Grenache Shiraz and it was heavenly!!!

Quick to make, and gone twice as quickly. the only thing said was, "hmm, you should have made more!" 
excellent recipe, thanks for sharing! the suggestions about the tomatoes and potatoes sound great... :)

(I also cut down the butter)
Perfect, basic way to cook salmon that really shows off the fish.  I omitted the cream, which would have made it even tastier, because I had none, and it was still delicious and lemony.  Thanks.

WOW!! This is delicious. My husband is a man of few words and can't quit commenting on how good this recipe is . I didn't have cream so used half and half. But don't put it right into the hot pan. I didn't even think about it, it curdled. I also cut back on the butter/marg.I had to double the sauce recipe because it was just enough for one filet. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe. Definitely a keeper in my family!! UPDATE: Have also tried it with sauteed baby bella mushrooms or English peas which makes it a very pretty looking dish. Again, thank you for such a fantastic recipe!!

Yum yum. This was so simple and tasty. I couldn't find any dill at the store so I used fresh parsley and milk instead of cream. Can't wait till I can find dill. Good for people with little "fish" experience. Thanks again.
Superb and super easy!

I needed a skillet recipe for salmon, as I usually grill it, and I was out of propane.  This was perfect!!! I always serve my salmon with butter, lemon, garlic and dill - so I just added 3 cloves of garlic to the butter - and I used more lemon.  I added artichokes and tomatoes to the "sauce" and served over pasta!  My husband LOVED it!! Thanks so much - another winner - as usual!!!

I'm 16 and not a good cook so when i tried this for lunch I was amazed at how simple and delicious it was. It's perfect for a change from the boring everyday salmon recipe, i didnt have cream so i just used Vitamin D milk it was still really good. If i can make it then so can any one.
This was very, very good. I didn't have any cream, so I just used sour cream and it came out excellent. This is a definite keeper.
This is an excellent recipe-one of the best salmon dishes we have ever had.  I used half-and-half instead of cream.
Great recipe!  It was quick and easy to make, and everyone in my family loved it, even those who normally don't like fish.

My salmon took a lot longer to cook than the 10 minutes on LOW.  I did the 10 minutes on low, turned my stove up to medium and did another 6 minutes or so and then got completely impatient and put the salmon in the microwave for 2 minutes.  The sauce was truly sublime... I thought I had dill in my spices but I didn't so I used tarragon.  I can't wait to try this with the dill!

I'm giving this recipe five stars based on potential :).  I thought I had all of the ingredients on hand, but no dill!  I used rosemary instead out of desperation.  The result was good but lacking.  I am nearly positive, however, that the dill would give this dish the kick I was missing and cut the richness enough to be most enjoyable.  I look forward to following the recipe more closely next time.  Thank you for a wonderful salmon recipe that doesn't overwhelm the fish.
Very easy and quick way to cook & serve Salmon. Simple flavor. My family enjoyed it!

I was looking for a quick salmon solution that didn't involve heating up my house with the oven.  This recipe was just perfect!  I wanted more of a cream sauce, but I don't keep cream on hand, and all I ever have is powdered milk.  So I sauted some sliced onions and minced garlic in the skillet the salmon came out of, seasoned with s&p, then made a roux with a bit of flour.  I deglazed with a small amount of white wine and then used 1/2 cup of milk (I made 2 servings, not 4) to make the sauce.  Added some dill to the sauce to mirror the flavors in the salmon.  I know I deviated quite a bit, but this recipe was an excellent base on which to build.  Next time I may try capers in it, too.  Thanks for posting!

really nice!  made it for my date and it was a big hit!  I try not to use butter or margarine in cooking but tried it here. very nice!  As others have suggested it went really well with the lemon roasted potatoes also here on the zaar!   This will be  my new favorite way to serve salmon!
SOOOO easy as well as good. I made this tonight, using sour cream in place of the cream, and it was done in no time, no muss, no fuss. And yes, it was also SOOOO good!

WOW!  The entire family loved the fish.  My 3 year old said she wanted to eat it every day!  This was delicious, and even better it took less than 20 minutes.  I only exchanged the cream for the half and half.  This will be one of my favorite salmon recipes.

This was very easy and it tasted delicious.  Very creamy!  I used sour cream as one person mentioned.  I also added some minced garlic, in with the lemon juice and dill.  Great recipe!  Thanks for sharing.

Made this for dinner last night and it was delicious. Unfortunately (somehow) I didn't have any lemons or cream, so I ended up using lemon pepper seasoning salt and some powdered milk (we had no milk either btw). It was still fantastic. A lovely new way to cook salmon =) DH loved it as well. Thanks a bunch!

This is what I was looking for! Thanks, MizzNezz. I think I'll add more cream too. And I also ended up having to turn my burner up to medium. Probably just depends on your range. But I agree it did turn out nicer cooking slower on a lower heat. Thanks again!
This was a nice, mild salmon that can be put together quickly and still look good.  I did not add any salt and I used about half the butter called for and it was still wonderful.  Thanks for sharing!
Very good salmon recipe.  I loved the simplicity of the ingredients and the method.  Will be making this often!
Excellent!

Wundabar! Simple and delicious.  I did manage to complicate it a bit.  With the pan juices and butter, I added a teaspoon of flour and made a medium dark roux.  Thinned it out with a touch of lemon juice then added milk and a touch of salt to build a light gravy.  Wow and, Thanks!
by recipie, not enough sauce and too much work, taste not great.  I am a west coaster and doesn't do anything for fresh salmon.
This was so good. The only thing I did differently was use 1/2 and 1/2 instead of cream. Followed everything else exactly. I will be using this quite often.  Thank you
Very good!
I used FF half and half instead of the cream but otherwise followed the recipe and the result was an excellent dish that my DH and I enjoyed thoroughly!  Thanks for sharing MizzNezz!
This was very easy to make and the family liked it a lot. Thanks for sharing.

Mmm mmm. I cant imagine fish tasting much better than that! It would also be delish without the cream but the cream sauce is sooo good. This was my first time making fish on the stovetop and 10 minutes was perfect. Thank you so much MizzNezz, we will be having this often.
We loved the technique and flavor of this dish. I added a little flour to thicken it up and also doubled the sauce. It was so good! Made for Zaar Alphabet Soup tag.
Simple and Delicious!  Used Wild Salmon, light butter and half and half.  Perfect with a side of asparagus.
Hubby was staring and I had already thaws out salmon so I tried this quick and easy recipe that turned out so delicious. I used about 2T less butter and it still came out wonderful. Thanks very much!

This was pretty good.  I had defrosted salmon fillets and forgot I couldn't use the oven and it was raining - so the grill was out too.  I didn't have lemon juice so I substituted lemon pepper and some garlic.  I also cut back on the butter.  Not bad at all, and very quick.  We served it with brown rice and green beans.
This was OK.  I thought it was a little bland.  I might try adding some more lemon juice with the cream and capers with a little bit of white wine.

Amazing recipe!  I may have used more than 1 tsp lemon juice, just squeezed half a lemon and poured in cream till it looked right.  Cooked 3 minutes each side but we don't like our salmon cooked well done.  This will be saved for used again & again.
Really liked this sauce! I'll make sure to double it next time.

Excellent! This was my first time making salmon, and I was more than a little bit wary, as my mother has never had salmon that she liked before and I was making dinner for the two of us.
I used wild caught fillets and cooked them for about 6-8 minutes, as I am usually fond of fish on the undercooked side. I added a little lemon and salt to the cream sauce for flavor, and corn starch to thicken it a bit more. I served it over fried rice and it was excellent!!
The whole thing was much easier than I'd expected and took very little time.
And the best part--my mother loved it! The woman who'd never found salmon to be digestible before was absolutely raving about how good it was.
Thank you for posting!!!!

I've been on the hunt for a salmon recipe that wasn't flavorful on the outside and dull on the inside and I think I've found it!  Very easy recipe.  Next time I'll use thinner pieces of salmon so that I can cook it better.
I've made this a few times now exactly as written and everyone loves it.  Today I mistakenly shook some of emeril's original and it made the sauce outstanding!  Great recipe!
It turned out wonderful! Thanks for sharing such an easy and delicious recipe.
Excellent salmon recipe. The ingredients were very well balanced. The salmon was the star, and the sauce complimented it perfectly. Thanks.
A yummy slaw with the added apples! I enjoyed the dressing too, although I did add just a touch of sugar.Thanks!

I doubled the recipe.  I omitted the green pepper.  And I forgot to add the apple.  I used dried dill and I added a big tablespoon of zucchini relish to have a little bit of sweet.  It's delicious.  Thanks Dreamer :)  Made for Market tag.

Busy days and finding that lunch is a frazzled rush with just a sandwich.  Realizing that left me short on veggies I stumbled on this tasty dish and decided it would be a great solution.  Decided to adapt it to the WW Core program using non-fat mayo and yogurt and it worked great.  The salad was popping with flavor and much to my surprise the dill and apple worked well together.  Like the other reviewers, I felt it needed a wee bit of sweetness and added a teaspoon of Splenda.  Next time I think I will make a little extra dressing as the slaw was a bit dry for me, but this was minor and a matter of taste.  Thanks for posting!  Made for *Potluck Tag*.

Delicious slaw! I did the fine shred - love coleslaw with carrots, green pepper, green onions and apple. Used fresh dill and like I do to most dressings -  a touch of sugar. ( a personal preferance) Great slaw, have added it to my coleslaw collection.

I thought this was great! I usually don't put apple in my coleslaw/waldorf salad anymore so the bits of sweetness from the apple was a welcomed change. The dressing fit great, and would have been even better if I had some fresh dill instead of dried. :)Thanks! Reviewed during ZWT 4.

Between tagging this recipe - I was drawn to the inclusion of apples - in Zaar Stars Tag and making it, dim memories started surfacing of a coleslaw with apples that I used to make several decades ago. Recipe long since lost! Enthusiasm for making this recipe grew! I'm sure my ancient recipe did not have the delicious dressing that Dreamer's recipe has: great blend of flavours. Just loved the dill and lemon flavouring. I made my coleslaw with Savoy cabbage, a couple of baby carrots (which have a great natural sweetness), 1/2 red pepper (I find them more flavoursome than green peppers) and a Fuji apple (love them). My coleslaw would have been slightly higher in fat because I used Greek yoghurt (the only yoghurt for me) but I did use light mayonnaise. Never knew coleslaw could be SO delicious. I made this out of season - it's winter here right now - and loved it, so come summer, I'll be making this a lot as a really healthy (even with my decadent Greek yoghurt) take-to-work-lunch. Thanks so much, Dreamer in Ontario, for sharing this wonderful recipe.
Loved it.  I added extra apple, used lemon pepper in place of the regular pepper, and added some sesame seeds.  Instead of the dill, I used fresh chives. Fabulous side dish.  Made for Veg*n Swap 3.

This is very good.  The dressing was just right for us without the dill and no added sugar.  Liked the crunchiness and sweet of the apple.  Kind of a cross between waldorf and coleslaw!  Was great with the baby-back ribs we had.
This is a very good Coleslaw recipe.  Lightens it up nicely and you don't really give up taste.  I liked all the different tastes and textures, too.  Home run!

I chose this for kittencalskitchen forum tag game, it's a wonderful coleslaw that improves in flavor after chilling, I used Greek yogurt add in some garlic powder and seasoned it with season salt, thank you Dorit, this will be enjoyed all week!

As we were eating this I realized I forgot to add the lemon juice so I quickly stirred some in. Served with portabello mushroom burgers, fresh plums for a yummy but easy Saturday dinner. I used both red onion and scallions and wish I had some red cabbage on hand to add but didn't. Most of the ingredients were from our CSA box, too. Thanks for posting. Reviewed for Veg Tag/July.

This was a great change of pace that I was happy to serve for a friend who hates mayo-based slaw. I made it with a red cabbage from my CSA box, which made it absolutely gorgeous to look at! I think I may have oversalted it at first, because just before serving I felt I needed to add a few spoons of sugar to balance the flavor. Turned out great! Made for Veg Swap 36.
I made a batch of these today. My family ate all 12...so this evening I'm making a double batch! They are so good...moist...hearty...fruity...just great. :o)

Awesome!  These are absolutely delicious and so simple to make.  I made some in full size muffin tins, then tried a batch of mini's.  I like the mini better - 1 bite!!  The only difference was with the mini tin, I baked them for 13 minutes and they were perfect!  Thanks!

Like another reviewer I also liked the mini's better. The larger muffins were a bit bland. I added more spices to the mix and made the rest minis. The kids really liked them and I just thought they were ok. But a great way to use up canned plums- used them for the puree

This is very tasty! I brought it to a family gathering, and even though some of them were mumbling, "Cous-what??", they still came back for seconds. The balsamic vinegar gives this a great flavor. I only used 3 tomatoes because it looked like plenty, and it was the perfect amount for me. This one's a keeper.
This is just wonderful.  Took all of 10 minutes to make and just simply bursting with flavor.  Thanks for the great recipe.
This was very good...I needed to add more olive oil because it seemed a bit dry to me, but that's just me. Other than that, it was wonderful.
This was delicious!! I highly recommend and I did not change a thing.
nice flavor.  I halved the recipe at it tasted great.  I didn't have any tomatoes, so I left them out.  Thanks!
This was easy to make and absolutely delicious! I'll definitely be making it again.

I liked it as a cold salad, but it wasn't really a very intresting dish. The flavors, however, were nicely balanced; though I watered down a can of chicken broth to make the two cups, and so it maybe needed some bullion added for an 'oomph' of flavor.

This was so easy to make, i did like i always do, put the couscous in a bowl, with all the ingredients, mix, cover and on the fridge for 30 minutes, then mix again, and wait until diner =)
Thank you very much! i used some fresh mint. Next time i'll use some fresh lemon juice too.

This was bursting with flavour!  Next time I'd add extra tomatoes. One recommendation is that I would never add water to compensate for the broth as I think the broth is an essential ingredient.  This is a great recipe for first time couscous eaters...enjoy!
This is simply divine. I don't have words... just beautiful flavor.
I love healthy food that tastes good and this fits the bill!  I used Roma tomatoes and added just a little bit of green onion. Thanks for sharing this great recipe!
Very good side dish.  I used a 14oz can of diced tomatoes (drained) but besides that followed exactly as written.
I made this exactly to the recipe and we loved it. Will certainly make it again. Yummy. Thanks for the recipe.

This was not only easy to make but very tastey too.  I took it to work for lunch and ate it cold, and was asked by two co workers for the recipe.

Thanks so much.

Excellent flavor! It was fast and easy to make. I'll definately make this again. I made it with whole wheat couscous, 1 can of diced tomatos, drained with the liquid used to make up some of the coooking liquid. I also tossed in some sliced polish sausage and topped with sprouts to make a complete meal.

Very nice. I made this recipe with a couple of small additions First, I used 1/2 tsp of fresh thyme in addition to the basil (to marry the dish with the particular main course I was making). Then before heating the broth, I added 1 tsp of olive oil to the pan and sauteed the garlic, herbs and 1/4 tsp of salt for just a few seconds to 'bloom' their flavors. Then I added the broth and proceeded with the rest of the recipe as written.
This was a very nice, very light side-dish.  The perfect accompaniment (sp?) to a highly-spiced chicken dish. Very good.  Will make again.

Very tangy and light side dish.  Perfect with grilled chicken.  I didn't have any fresh tomatoes so I used some fire roasted canned ones I had in the pantry.  It turned out extremely well.  I might cut back on some of the balsamic vinegar next time since it was quite tangy for my BF, but delicious all in all!  Thanks for sharing...
I cooked the tomateoes in oil and salt and pepper then added the balsamic to reduce it (making it less tangey and more sweet).  Great recipe!

Mmmm--LOVED it!  I was looking for a recipe to use up some leftover plain couscous, and this worked great.  I just mixed the garlic and basil in with the tomatoes and threw in a little extra sauteed onion from the main dish I was making.  Then I just added everything to the reheated couscous.

I just love how simple and easy this is, and how tasty.

Anyway, I'll be making this again very soon.  In fact, as good as this is as a side, I can see eating it by itself as a light main dish.  Thank you so much for posting!
Very easy to make and just a little different using all the ingredients I had on hand.  Into my keepers file it goes :)
I have been making this for a year and never rated... sorry! This is really awesome. Everything eats it and says this is totaly different! thats exactly what I was looking for. Thank you.

I've been wanting to try this one for a while.  Other than realizing I had no pepper whatsoever, I followed this recipe to a T.  It certainly didn't disappoint!  This is tangy and cheerful - can't wait to impress others with it!  I had this with a piece of baked flounder.

Thanks so much!

To us, it was MUCH better cold.  The flavors were, although subtle, more pronounced and perfect.   I used chicken stock for a little extra flavor, otherwise, wouln't change a thing.  Nice, healthy, lowfat!  THANKS!

Delicious! AND SOOOO FAST to make!! As my husband said, fancy food that's easy to make should get bonus stars.  Fresh tomatoes are a must here-ours came from a local farm.  Can't wait to use tomatoes from the garden to make this.  Awesome!

Oh, my. This is a winner. So delicious, so filling, so healthy (especially with whole wheat couscous) and also very easy. I made this as a side to Recipe #116150, and it was just perfect. I'll be keeping this one anytime I need a great side dish that's a little different. Thank you so much for sharing this.

Ok...I couldn't get to the computer fast enough to give this a 5 star rating.  SUPERB!!!!!!!!!  I love couscous...I love balsamic vinegar...I LOVE tomatoes.  You couldn't have asked for a more perfect combination.  The flavors and ease of this dish were unbelievable.  I might even go so far as to say this might be my favorite recipe of all time off this site...and I've tried tons of them.  If you like the ingredients...you will DIE over this dish!  I didn't change much other than to use chicken stock and to increase both the garlic and the tomatoes.  Next time I will also use fresh basil rather than dried.  Just fabulous.  Thank you so much for this one.  I adore it!
wow ...that is some good couscous my friend ... thanks alot

Very easy to make and very tasty.  I made 2/3 of the recipe with all the basil and garlic.  I had some whole wheat couscous that I used up.  I could see how some might find this overly tangy, but we like it that way.  Also, I had some extra feta cheese that I sprinkled over it, so that offset the tangy taste a bit.  Tried it both warm and cold.  Thanks!  Will post a picture soon...

We enjoyed this very much.  I had fresh basil in the garden, so substituted for the dried, and since I didn't have any garlic, I used  garlic powder.  I used a box of pine nut couscous, and that amount equaled a half recipe, which was all I wanted to make. I used the spice pack in the box.  Fresh garden tomatoes were available, and it was a delicious side dish with our roasted chicken dinner.

This was my first taste of couscous, and it was good. My son loved it! Reminded me of bruschetta. We decided we prefer it cold but it's still pretty good warm. Used dice tomatoes instead of fresh but other than that followed the recipe exactly. Served with recipe #172387 for the traditional burger and cold salad with a twist.

We like couscous (DH and I) and I needed a tasty side dish.  I cooked the garlic in the olive oil then added the balsamic vinegar, basil and pepper as suggested by another review.  this was very good and DH says it needs to be repeated.
Very yummy! Will definitely make often to keep in the fridge to snack on. Thanks! (-:
Love this recipe, I added feta cheese. This is a keeper, thanks for sharing
Very tasty with fresh basil, too!
Used 1 can petite diced tomatoes instead of the fresh - very good!
This was really good. Next time I'll add some feta to it. I think that would compliment the taste nicely. Thanks for this healthy and easy recipe!

I thought this couscous was really good, Hannan (DH) didn't think it was anything amazing. He would have given it a 3. I liked the flavors. I did without the tomatoes as I don't care for them and used 2 T. of Balsamic vinegar instead of 3 as some others said it was a bit much. I thought it was great! I would definitely make it again, super easy, super fast, and super tasty!
This is very good!  Both of my kids (5 and 2) ate it up fast!  This is nice a quick, light lunch time meal or even snack.
Tasty, quick, easy and cheap.  Another good Ladypit recipe!  I had everything to make it in the house. I think I'll add grilled shrimp to the leftovers for a different salad.

This was probably the easiest and quickest dish I've ever prepared, and while it lacks an impressive kick of its own, it is a great side, or a great meal if you're just in one of those moods for something light. A sprinkling of mozzarella or Parmesan would go nicely atop it.
Fantastic. I added some cucumbers at the end. Thanks.

Finally, a couscous dish with some flavor!  I made this tonight for the first time and really enjoyed it.  I made as written with home made chicken broth and added both fresh basil and thyme.  I liked the idea of adding the garlic to the boiling broth so the garlic flavor isn't too fierce.  We were pleased with the results.  Goes great with chicken.  Thanks for posting.
Just made this tonight for dinner to have with grilled chicken and salad.  This was GREAT!  I made it exactly as the recipe called for and it was perfect.  I will definitely be making this again.
Very nice recipe.  We are not hugh fans of couscous cause it can turn out dry sometimes.  This recipe has just the right balance of flavour & moistness, thanks for sharing.

Made 1/2 recipe and used Israeli couscous -- so simmered according to package directions.  We have an abundance of Roma tomatoes, so chopped 4 and added to oil and balsamic, and allowed to simmer a few minutes with couscous before serving.  DH proclaimed "This is GOOD !" -- hence 5 stars !  Served with gas-grilled pork tenderloin and garden Swiss chard (with lemon and feta).  Thanks for posting, ladypit.
Fantastic! Perfect seasoning, we loved this. Thanks!

So good! And it's sooo simple! I have made other couscous recipes and haven't had much luck. Well this one was just delicious, i'll definately make it again! I use whole wheat couscous and used cherry tomatoes cut in half. I added extra basil to the finished couscous and it was SO good with that extra basil! Thanks
An easy tasty dish.  Next time I'm gunna try using sun dried tomatoes and make this during a camping trip.
This is a very good side that doesn't take away from your main dish. I've used a VERY drained can of tomatoes also. Made this a few times now and it's simple and easy to do.
Quick and tasty side dish, and great way to use couscous. Yummy!

This was very good!  I cut the recipe in half and it still made a lot!  I added some sliced green onion and about 1/2 tsp garlic salt.  It might also be good with some chopped black olives added.  Thanks for posting this.  I'll definitely be making this again!
This was very good!  The balsamic vinegar adds a nice flavor.
Very Good!!! I made the recipe as written but added some onions and cucumbers for a cold salad.  Again, Very Good!!!!
Yum! This was my first time trying couscous and this recipe made it a winner for me!
The kids usually don't like couscous but they loved this.  Will keep this around to serve w/ grilled meat.

Wonderful flavor!  I LOVE couscous and am always looking for a new way to make it.  This was quick, easy and a hit with my family- even my two year old!  You could easily add chopped cucumbers to this or small cubes of mozerella and a few basil leaves for a 'Couscous Caprice' kind of feel!
I made this first for a mother's day picnic and it was so easy and delicious. I've made it a few times since and personally like it much better cold/room temp than hot. Good any way though!
I added cut up cucumber to this and left out the dried basil and garlic. I also added some chopped onion. It was delicious! Made for I Recommend Zaar Tag Game 2010.

This turned out pretty good. The flavors were subtle, or at least they were to us. I ended up adding some cilantro. If I try it a again, I think I might add a little more vinegar and some cucumber as other reviewers had done. We thought it ws best at room temp. Thanks for posting.

Yummmmmm.  I made this to go with some moraccon chicken and we loved it.  I cut back a bit on the vinegar but otherwise followed the recipe.  We loved it.  I will make again with all kinds of meats.  Thankyou  for sharing this with us, its a great recipe.

I have never tried couscous before and have always heard bad things about it, but this was really delicious! The vinegar gave my sad looking tomatoes such a nice zip, and it went together so quickly by boiling the broth in the microwave first, and then following the other directions. My husband even said he likes couscous now! Thanks for posting!
Great!  I added more garlic though.

I tried this as written and it was pretty good, but then I tried it with the suggestions from other members and it was great! I accidentally used quinoa instead of couscous (a senior moment) and I made some changes that other reviewers mentioned! I added cucumber, onions and grated mozzarella, to make this more of a caprese salad. I also added salt for more flavor! I liked it better served cold! I'll make this often!
This is one of my favourite recipes and so versatile. Sometimes I make it exactly as written, other times I'll add spinach, feta or whatever else takes me fancy, it's always glorious!
This is one of the best things I have made in a long time!
Delicious!  I did not have cilantro so substituted basil and a few mint leaves, worked beautifully.  Thank you so much for a great meal!
Easy and tasty, but I'm hoping it is more flavorful cold as a salad. Made for Cooking Tag Mania 2013.

I haven't even put the tomatoes in yet and WOW! The flavor is amazing! Even my super picky husband liked it! I used a couscous, millet, lentil, quinoa mixture. SO good. Will definitely make again. In fact, I made a second batch for my party tomorrow because I couldn't keep my fingers out of it.

The first day, this was OK. Leftovers the second were ABSOLUTELY UNBELIEVABLY EXCELLENT!!!! I used the Israeli Pearl (large) couscous and a low acid orange tomato. Craving more as I write this......thank you for posting, Ladypit!!!

Didnt actually like the sound of this but had all the ingredients in the cupboard and though..hell why not?!?! Turned out superb, flavourful.. could probably do with a little less balsamic vinegar as its very vinegary i would suggest 2tbps.. but overall a good 5/5.. kids and hubby loved it.. had it with barbeque pork chops...YUMMY
Would someone please check the Nutrition Facts of this recipe.

Made these for Sunday brunch and they went down a treat. Easy to make, did the 2nd proving in the fridge over night then poured over the coconut milk and popped in the oven the next morning. Served with Nutella spread. Will be making these again! Thanks for posting.

I have a great story to go with these buns! I made the dough on sunday night, let it rise twice, shaped it into buns and put them in the fridge overnight. I was going to make the sauce and bake them off on Monday morning, but I ended up in labor at 2am monday so my mom had to finish them up on tuesday. Anyway, they turned out great despite all the excitment! I would recommend making a little extra of the sauce if you don't plan on eating them right after baking, they really soak it up overnight!
I followed coastys suggestion and served with nutella.. really yummy! will make agian

I totally love these. I used iceburg lettuce, smoky turkey bacon, mild cheddar cheese, and mayo. The only addition is some thinly sliced onion with the tomato then in with the rest of the ingredients, wrapped up finer then a man in his Sunday best and devoured. Great, great, bravo, bravo, absolutely love these! Thanks, I'm Pat!

I eat "mostly" low carb and am always looking for new recipes. I made this for lunch and followed the recipe as written. These were good and easy enough to make. Next time I make BLT's for my family, I will make this for myself.

This was a great idea!  I really enjoyed this.  Next time I am going to leave out the cheese for a more authentic BLT taste!  Enjoyed for breakfast this morning.  I made this for Everyday is a Holiday tag!

What a truly wonderful breakfast - or any time of day - treat. I sauteed 1/2 an onion and some garlic, both minced in a mini processor, while panfrying the bacon and I omitted the cheese, not because I don't like cheese - I love it - but there was enough flavour here without it. Thank you so much for sharing this fabulous recipe, Pat. It's so quick and easy and so delicious that I'll be making this often. Made for PRMR.

I just made these now for brunch. I liked them, but don't know that I would enjoy mayo for an earlier breakfast. I would love these for lunch and can see how they would be a perfect treat for someone avoiding carbs. I used an iceberg lettuce and vintage cheddar cheese. Thanks for posting Pat.
WOW!  A sandwich without bread...I smashed a little avacado into the mayo mixture with good results.  Now if I could just give up the sweets!!!  Made for Everyday is a Holiday

Who doesn't like a BLT? My romaine (Cos) was very fresh and crunchy, so it didn't wrap easily. I'm not a big fan of mayonnaise; I would have preferred a fat-free ranch dressing or salad dressing spritzes instead. Four tablespoons of cheese is a bit much for 1 person. Ultimately this says "Lunch" or "Salad" to me, and I would rather eat it as a salad with a fork. It was fun to try. Made for Karen Elizabeth's  Wrap it Up Party in Potluck Tag.

Best part of the sandwich is the filling and this is the best because it is all filling. Made as written using fat free cheddar. Got three wraps due to the fact that I was down to the smaller inter leaves of the romaine. Makes a great lunch. Thanks so much for the post.

This was really good, filling and messy to eat!!  I used green leaf lettuce so it was a little hard to wrap since the leaves were wavy and thin.  I did add in 1/2 a diced avocado that was going to go bad.  This will be made again!  Made forEveryday Holiday.

This was a nice treat to try something different and healthy. I used bacon medallions to cut the fat and left out the cheese as I was looking for a true BLT flavour without the fat. I used iceberg lettuce and it was easy to roll and not as messy as I expected. Thanks for a lovely new healthy treat!

Yummy!  I made these for my DD and myself for lunch and they were gone in no time.  I did add some avocado and a little sliced onion but otherwise followed the instructions.  I used iceberg lettuce for the wraps (that is what I had).  Made for the Recipe Swap#62 March 2012 Aus/NZ .
Great breakfast when you realize you're out of eggs ;-) Thank you.
These were great! I skipped the mayo and used butter leaf lettuce so it wasn't messy at all. Also good with egg and avocado, and you can skip the cheese to make it paleo.

This was really good. I added some garlic powered to the butter and a little sesame oil. No peas for me! Other than that cooked as directed. I think cooling the rice really made a differance...I never knew about that so thanks for teaching me something new!

This was a nice quick dish to put together. I omitted the eggs altogether. I used just 1 tbsp. of soy sauce which my mom felt is a bit more, so next time, I'll use about 1/2 tbsp. only. This one's a keeper!
This rice was ok. I needed to add a lot more soy sauce and butter because when I taste tested it, it seemed very bland. I did, however, love the peas in it! Not quite benihana's, but decent!

This is really delicious...have made it twice already.  In place of the grated carrots, I just used frozen carrots & peas.  Passed it along to my daughter and my grandson, who is two, loved it also.  Makes a great kid lunch...veggies, grain, protein.  Can't miss with this one.

I'm rating this so high because of how simple yet first-rate this dish is.  Lots of flavor, yet unassuming enough to serve along side any main dish.  I used brown basmati rice for more substance and served it along side Japanese Mum's Chicken recipe #68955 (you really should try!!!)
My first attempt at making fried rice. Easy ad delicious.
This was a GOOD fried rice recipe.  Thank you for a nice simple dish.  Easy with good flavor.
We absolutely LOVED this recipe.  We felt the soy sauce had enough sodium, so we didn't add the salt.  Devine!!!
I slightly overcooked the rice, but this was excellent and I'll definitely make it again.

I thought this would be too salty with soy sauce and salt, but a little salt was needed (I did use low sodium soy sauce).  I used a 10 oz box of frozen peas and carrots and didn't measure, but it seemed close to the amts given.  I also made the rice a day ahead to speed the after work dinner prep.  I am sure it was much healthier than "take-out." We loved it, and cannot wait to eat it again.
The very best!!!  We omit the salt because with the soy sauce it's plenty salty, but otherwise- fantastic!

Great, great, great! It was also very simple to put together.  It makes prep a snap since the rice can be made in the microwave and cooled until you're ready to use it. I didn't change anything and it came out perfect.  My family wants me to try adding cooked meat (beef, chicken maybe even shrimp) to make it a meal.  This will be a regular in our home.  Thanks!
Great recipe!  So easy to follow, my 10 year old son cooked the entire dish by himself!  It was delicious!  Thank you!
My DH and I enjoyed this dish very much. For the left overs I added some chopped shrimp..  Thanks for posting!

Love it, love it, love it!!! I have never had Benihana's rice but this is absolutely delicious. I am Thai and make lots of Thai fried rice for my BF, which is very tasty... but when I want a very mild flavored fried rice to serve with some stir fry, I always turn to this recipe.  My BF refuses to eat 'plain, white rice' (steamed Jasmine rice) so this rice is great for him.  I also love how beautifully it fries up in the wok.  Make sure to let your rice cool after you cook or otherwise you will end up with a big sticky mess intead of beautifully soft separate grains of rice.

ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS !!  I made this last night with  Roasted Resemary Chicken with Lemon/Soy sauce (recipe # 60201). It was great together.  I followed the recipe exactly but switched the carrots for waterchestnuts ..(out of carrots).  My DH inhaled the rice and I'm glad I didn't double it as I considered, because he would have eaten it all..and he's trying to diet  Thanks for posting this....and by the way, I'm going to make it again tonight to have with our leftover chicken for tacos.  Donna
I thought this recipe was delicious!  I added a little more carrot, but other than that it was perfect!  I never thought it would be so easy to make fried rice.

I found the other benihana recipe and kept thinking "this doesn't look like the one I made earlier"  I kept searching and was so happy to have found this one again since I made it a month ago and everyone especially my really picky son loved it. This one has the genius of being really simple the proportions are perfect and it is beyond delicious. A nice change from complicated flavors.
I finely diced the carrot, only used 1/2 cup of peas, and probably 4 tbs. soy sauce--very good, thanks for the post!

Great recipe!  I don't know if it is like Benihana's rice because I haven't been in a long time but it was delicious and pretty easy to do. I didn't use carrots because we didn't have any around and I already had all the other ingredients so I chopped some red bell pepper up in put that in instead to give it a bit of colour.  We had it with teriyaki salmon, soup and a salad with ginger dressing.
This recipe is so wonderful and has become a staple meal in our home!  Thanks for sharing.

Loved this; my idea of excellent comfort food. Because I served this with recipe #147175 which already has plenty of soy sauce, I decided to flavor this with oyster sauce. Wonderful way to enjoy brown basmati, Andy.
This is so easy and good. It is a great light and fresh side dish that can easily pair with almost anything. I served it with pork chops. Yummy.
This came out great! I also made a batch of recipe #23753 to drizzle over our fried rice, that's what we like to do in the Japanese restaurants.. Loved it..
I never realized how easy fried rice was! We omitted the peas and replaced them with mushrooms to suite our taste better. Delicious, thanks Andy.

I turned it into a meal.... :) doubled everything... added a pound of shrimp and YUMMMM.  Oh and about a teaspoon of garlic (because I just love it). Thanks so much for sharing this recipe. Never knew it could be so easy!!!!

I just wanted to add an update - if you like Japanese Steak houses and the 'white sauce' served with the seafood  -  check your produce section (in the chilled dressings area) for Makoto's Vegetable Sauce - its so close to the real thing and great with your fried rice and shrimp!

Just fabulous! Everyone (including the picky kids) loved this. So easy too! I didn't put the egg in (I hate eggs lol) but no one said a word ;) We'll be making this a lot around here. (I did cheat a bit and found a box of rice with peas/carrots and some seasoning) and just added some more rice, onion and the sauces. Of course, topped the 'grown-ups' portions with green onion. Just perfect! Thanks!

This was recently used at a Girls' Night In I hosted, thank you so much for posting this recipe! This was fantastic! My FI and I both loved it. Like other posters next time I will probably only use one ranch dressing pack. I also might add some more mushrooms and maybe more chicken. Overall though I throughly enjoyed! Thanks for a great easy recipe!

The flavors were good, but it was SO soupy and my chicken tasted overcooked...I was disappointed.  If I make it again, I won't add a whole can of chicken broth (maybe a 1/4 cup or 1/4 cup white wine)...And I think I'd take one of the ranch dressing packets out and I'd remove the chicken after 5 hours and then add the cream cheese/garlic/soup mixture (pre-heated) to the other liquids and whisk them real good to combine.  Maybe its just me...everyone else thought it was terrific.  Sorry...

I used only one packet of ranch dressing and one can of mushroom soup, but was still too salty for us.  Also, the chicken seemed a bit overcooked, and the sauce was watery.  I will try to make it again with some adjustments. Perhaps I will leave out the chicken broth.

Manda, I think you should call this "Absolutely Fabulous Crockpot Chicken" It was wonderful. My four year old and DH ate it up! I will make this again! I did add a lil cornstarch to thicken but didn't change anything...love it! :)

We absolutely loved the way this turned out!  I pre-mixed the cream cheese and mushroom soup before adding and it thickened the sauce nicely.  Served over whole wheat noodles so we loved having a lot of sauce.  Thanks Manda!

The chicken in this recipe is tender, moist and has an excellent flavor. The gravy left behind was too salty for my taste (it also made A LOT and I didn't add the 2nd can of mushroom soup). If I did it again, I would cut the ranch dressing in half (I think that's where the over salt flavor came from... and maybe not adding the 2nd can of soup) and I would halve the other ingredients except the chicken. If you halved that then maybe a 1/2 a package of ranch dressing mix overall? It might work. I had to whisk the cream cheese into the sauce at the end, it hadn't broken up when it was ready to eat. We had it over baked potatoes and it was enjoyed. 5 stars for the chicken, 3 for the gravy.
Haven't used my crockpot in years. I came across this recipe and now I'm sure I'll be keeping the crockpot close at hand. What a delicious recipe! Thanks for posting it!

I love this dish. Absolutely delicious! I used 1 can of soup, 1 package ranch dressing mix and about 3/4 can of roasted garlic chicken broth. I used 2-3 oz cans of mushrooms. Everything else I used as called for. I served over egg noodles. A real hit with the entire family. Thanks for the great recipe.

This was a very easy and delicious dish.  I only used one packet of ranch dressing as I was afraid it would be too salty.  I also added a tablespoon of cornstarch the last hour.  Served over brown and wild rice for me and over mashed potatoes for my husband.  Good meal on a busy day!

Using Ranch Dressing mix in this recipe caught my eye and interest. This was a very easy,very tasty crockpot dinner. I served it over brown rice. This was a big hit and will make again and again. Thanks Manda!!

Oh my goodness!  This was awesome! My daughter was hurt at school and needed stitches, it was so nice to have dinner waiting when I got home.  I was a little worried as I wasn't sure of the smell, but I couldn't believe it when I tasted it.  I made it pretty close to the directions. I used whole chicken breasts, which I don't recommend unless you plan to take the chicken off the bone part way through the cooking process.  I had little bones everywhere.  I thickened the sauce and put it over mashed potatoes.  I have tons of it left and plan to serve it over egg noodles for the next meal! Thanks for the WONDERFUL recipe!!  I will be using this one ALOT!!
Good and so easy.  We thought it was alittle on the bland side, but the kids loved it.

Wonderful dish!  My mom even raved about how wonderful it smelled only halfway through the cooking time.  I printed out the recipe & gave it to a few friends who also just love it.  I decrease the chicken broth to just one cup (one cup of boiling water with one chicken boullion), and only one can of soup.  The first time I made it just as directed & found it was a little to runny.  Decreasing the amount of liquid also makes the flavor a little zippier.  This is wonderful over pasta, rice, or even potatoes.  This recipe has remained a staple on my menu for the past year!!  Yummy!

This was rather tasty!  Cut recipe in half.  I only had ranch dip mix...so used that. Didn't add mushrooms...hubby doesn't like.  Used boullion instead of broth and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder instead of garlic.  It is alittle "rich" for me but was good.  Will make again someday.

Yummy and easy to make.  I will definately keep this recipe on hand.  I will say that next time I make it I will also cut back on the liquid.  I will also add the mushrooms about 2-3 hours before serving.  They seemed to be a little chewy.  I think it would add some nice flavor to saute the mushrooms with some onions and garlic and then add it all to the crockpot.

very good, easy to make. I only used one pack of the ranch dressing and used veg. broth instead. I found this recipe to be very salty?? Not sure what did it. I only added a pinch of salt. I will try this again, but maybe a half of a pack of ranch and no salt, I also wanted to cube the chicken and pour the sauce and chicken over egg noodles. I had it with the egg noodles and loved it. I was nice and creamy, rich though. The garlic was yummy!

DELICIOUS!  Loved by all!  I'm not usually a 'condensed soup' recipe person, but I loved this!  I did make a few alterations though.  First off I only added 1 packet of ranch mix, used fat free soups, lowfat cream cheese, and low-sodium chicken broth.  I omitted the butter.  Then, a half hour before serving I whisked 2 tablespoons corntarch and 2 tablespoons water together, then mixed it into the crockpot which thickened it very nicely.  Even my stepson, who claims to hate mushrooms, ate everything and didn't even notice!  Thanks for the great recipe!

I'm sorry to say I was also disappointed with this recipe.  The only change I made was I had to use bone-in chicken breasts.  After reading some reviews I decided to ladle out some of the chicken broth so my gravy would be thicker.  I also combined the soups with the cream cheese on my stove top before adding to the crockpot.  This made my gravy creamy.  The chicken came out very moist but overall I found this dish to be bland.  I was a tad underwhelmed after all the great reviews.  :(

With all the good reviews I was really looking forward to this. Was really disappointed though.  There really wasn't a lot of flavor.  I put in extra mushrooms and garlic and even that didn't help.  I cooked it on low for 7 hours, 5-6 on high seemed like it would be dry.  I did give it 3 stars because my husband said he liked it.

OMG...this recipe is AMAZING! All of the flavors come together to create one super flavor.I can't stress how much we loved this.The only thing that I did different was to add a whole stick of butter because I had to go to the store for chicken broth(I bought some with garlic added)and I didn't want it to burn.The sauce for this was so good that when I was cleaning up I ate what little sauce was left and burnt the inside of my mouth...it was TOTALLY worth it.Thank you so much for my "new" very favorite chicken recipe!
Delicious! Used 1 packet of ranch seasonings and extra shrooms of course! It's a keeper!

I've got a smaller crockpot so I used 3 breasts, and a can of "soup at hand" (creamy chicken) instead of the two condensed cream of mushroom.  I added 2 hours on low tothe begining since I started with frozen chicken. It was still a little runny so I kept the lid off for the last half hour or so.  It turned out really well tho!

This chicken was wonderful! For two of us, I split the chicken breast in half & use 4 halves.  Used fresh sliced mushrooms, 1 pkg. Ranch dressing mix, 1 can soup, 1/2 can chicken broth, 1/2 broth can of white wine and 4 ozs. of
cream cheese. The sauce was just right.  Will make this many times. Thanks Manda for posting. Any more good crockpot recipes?
This was very easy and so good.  I served it over rice.  The chicken was so tender and I now have new crockpot recipe.  Love my crockpot.
This was very good, served it over noodles, and did thicken it with cornstarch for a nice gravy effect.
Excellent recipe---made it exactly as written, except omitted the butter, and it wasn't even missed.  Will definitely make again!

I really liked this a lot.  Next time, though, I will add only 1 pkg of dry ranch mix.  Was really overpowering with 2 and extremely salty - and I love salt!  Will definitely make again with 1 packet.
we loved this recipe, I only had ranch dip mix and only 1 pack, also cooked it on low for 8 hours and added the soup and cc 3 hours before done. Will definately make again.  Thanks

One word, WOW.

Oft times, after the first try, I will change a recipe to suit our tastes.  Not so this one, it stays just as it is written. Easy to make, smells so good while cooking and tastes great.

I served over basmati rice which seemed just perfect.   Thanks Manda for sharing.

This was very good!  Both my DH and little boy loved the taste of this chicken.  Next time I might thicken the mushroom "gravy" with cornstarch... otherwise I will cut the liquid ingredients in half.  Thanks a lot for this super easy recipe! :)

We loved this...I did not add mushrooms because the kids would not eat it if I did.  Definately salty.  At first I was worried just tasting it but when I put it over the egg noodles and ate it together it was really good.  Kids gave it a 5 and hubby(very picky) gave it a 4.5.  He said it needed more color.  Maybe next time I will add some peas.
This recipe was easy and called for ingredients I always have on hand. However,we found the taste a little bland and the dish was colorless. Don't think I'll make it again.
This chicken was very good. It does make a lot of sauce. I served it over rice with a veggie. Very good and easy. Thanks.

This is a good recipe to be tossed in with the hassle-free meals during the week.  I wouldn't serve it to company, but my family ate it and enjoyed it.  It was a very moist.  I found it to be too bland for my tastes so I might experiment with additional flavors (like fresh herbs) next time.  I served it with wild rice and green beans. I also had way too much sauce left over so I'll reduce it by maybe 1/4 next time as well.

I really have enjoyed this twice.  Each time I followed Mizz Nezz and halved the recipe.  I have not mastered a smooth sauce and have had cream cheese lumps.  The flavor is still terrific but before I show this off for company I need to get mine to look like the picture! :)

What an amazingly easy and comforting dish. I followed the recipe for the half version. I added 2 TBSP of Fairbanks sherry to the finished produc (WOW! What a flavor enhancer!) I also used Baby Bella's and wished for more mushrooms also. I used an 8oz container with 3 chicken breasts. Like another person wrote, I also used a tsp of cornstartch with a little water to thicken. I shredded the 3 chicken breasts, and to my amazement, this created a very large amount of food, enough for 7 full servings! With only 3 chicken breast. This is a great money saver - and next time I will use the 6 chicken breast and freeze half! It would be so nice to just thaw also - even though the slow cooker makes it just as easy if not easier! Thank you for this recipe and we love it! Served this over rice with lemon brocoli.
YUM!! This was so good and easy!

even with all my goofs, this was still great! I accidentally put the cr of mush in at the beginning, and forgot to add the cream cheese and garlic at the end.  Still completely delicious!  I imagine it would be even better the "right" way!

Nice & Easy, smells wonderful while it's cooking!  I followed the recipe exactly, it makes a lot of sauce, I used a 7 oz box of rotini and had to cook another box after dinner for the leftovers, there is only 3 of us so next time I might consider halving the recipe. Great crockpot recipe with lots of flavor!

A very versatile, easy-to-modify meal. We served it over noodles and since I only had 3 thigh quarters in the freezer, I added about 8oz of sliced kielbasa. I didn't have the ranch dressing mix, either, so I subbed a cup of ranch dressing. Great stuff!

This was wonderful! I followed the recipe as written other then I started with frozen chicken tenderloins. I cooked the chicken with broth and butter for six hours on Low. I ate some at that point and it was very good. I did add the rest of the ingredients and cooked on warm for about a half an hour. I didn't add the garlic as I forgot and I didn't think it needed salt or pepper so I didn't add that either. I would think if you cooked this on high and for as long as the recipe calls for it would be very dry. With cooking it on low, putting the chicken in frozen- I thought this came out perfect. Will be making again.

I love the fact that this recipe reminds me of chicken stroganoff.... It is VERY rich and creamy- but I must confess that the chicken turned out dry, dry, dry.  I agree that LOW setting is best for this dish- my crock pot was cooking on high for about 2 1/2 hours before adding the last of the ingredients and.... well, dry chicken was the result. My 3 year old, who I swore would LOVE this, did not want more than three or four bites- of the noodles with the sauce- and then asked for more peas. Go figure. I did add a touch of sherry to the sauce (nope, that wasn't the prob. for her, she gobbles it up in other dishes) and only used one packed of ranch dressing mix. It was salty(ish) even using low-sodium cream o' mushroom soup- even for this salt fanatic. I served over egg noodles along side of sauteed fresh spinach. I did really like it- creamyness and all and will probably attempt this again, tweaking the ingredients a bit more... perhaps using only one can of soup and 1/2  pkg. of cream cheese.... hmmm, the possibilities! Thanks  for sharing!
This was good.  I cooked it on low, chicken was no dry.

I totally loved this! It's a great stick-to-your-tummy easy meal that DH and I both enjoyed. I did use fresh mushrooms (and lots of em!) and added some chopped onion and fresh parsely in the first round of cooking. I used lf/ff ingredients and served mine over low carb noodles. Tasty!

This was definitely interesting. It looked horrible when everything was put together and didn't smell so great while it was cooking. But I was pleasantly surprised when I finally tasted it. Served over egg noodles with some crusty bread. I added some canned corn at the last minute for a little color. Really filling!

Due to the high sodium and fat in this recipe I was really hoping that it wouldn't taste good (my butt doesn't need it. LoL!) - But to my butts dismay, it was wonderful :) This would be fantastic with leftover shredded beef - a little twist on stroganoff!
very good!

I enjoyed this.  The chicken fell to pieces when I stirred in the cream cheese which was a time saver for me since I was planning on shredding it.   Despite other comments to the contrary, my meal had lots of gravy but it was nice and thick and creamy.  The only reason I gave this recipe 4 stars instead of 5 was because it was a bit salty to my taste.

We'll definitely be having this again.
