Since there are just two of us at home now, I did change the recipe slightly by using only 4 chicken breasts and 1 can of soup.  All other ingredients were used in the quantities listed.  That said, it still made a lot of broth, so about 15 minutes after I added the cream cheese I added about 8 oz of egg noodles to the crock pot and let continue to cook on high for another 45 minutes.  The noodles thickened up the broth just right.  We thought this was definitely a keeper.
My family really liked this...I thought it was too much flavor.  Because my kids ate it all, this will be a recipe I use often.  Thanks for sharing.  :)

This was wonderful! I used can mushrooms because I forgot to buy fresh, but still wonderful! Husband loved it and he hasn't really liked anything I have made in the crockpot. I took leftovers to work and everyone wanted some of my lunch. I think I will double the sauce next time to serve over rice. So great! Thanks again!!

This was a very easy and delicious meal.  We don't eat mushrooms, so I omitted them.  In the last hour, after mixing all ingredients well, I added another can of chicken broth and 2 1/2 c of uncooked egg noodles, and reduced heat to low.  Everyone loved it, and I will put it in our regular rotation.  Thanks for a great recipe.

I only had 1 can of soup and 1 ranch mix so I halved the recipe. I used a whole chicken (economically cheaper) and skinned it. When it was soft enough I removed the bones and put the meat back in the pot and then continued with step 3. I then added some thickener towards the end.  I have to say that even though I halved the recipe it was still a lot of sauce.  DH wasn't sure if I served him a chunky soup or not.  Even still, the flavor was excellent.  I will be making this again.

This was easy and yummy!  After reading the reviews, I used only 1 envelope of ranch dressing mix and decreased the broth to 3/4 cup. I put my chicken breasts in frozen solid and cooked for an hour on high then reduced to low for the remaining cooking time. I used a combination of canned button and fresh crimini mushrooms because that's what I had in the house.  I also used healthy versions of cream soup - 1 can of mushroom and 1 can of celery, reduced fat cream cheese and upped the garlic to 3 big cloves.  The chicken was juicy and tender and the sauce was thick and creamy.  Served it over wide egg noodles with steamed green beans.

Despite my mistakes, this was GOOOOOD - a lot ike a chicken stroganoff! I cut the recipe in 1/2 (1 can soup, 1 pkt ranch, 4 oz cream cheese) and accidently mixed in everything at the beginning, except the cream cheese.  It looked wierd cooking, but I added some cornstarch/water to thicken toward the end and threw in some Whole Wheat egg noodles for about 20 minutes and it turned out to be saucy goodness.  Served with steamed broccoli!

I'm sorry, this just wasn't our thing.  The ranch overwhelmed the sauce (which I needed to thicken with cornstarch, as it was very watery) and overall the sauce was overpowering and too rich to enjoy. :(

Loved this exactly as written!  Served over egg noodles which really soaked up the sauce.  I'm thinking this would be really good with some peas added in the last hour as well.  Will make again; Thanks!
This had so much flavor. It was delicious!

This was VERY good, DH loved it and he's usually picky when it comes to trying new recipes. I used low sodium mushroom soup, reduced sodium broth, and didn't add any salt, but it was still delicious. Will definitely be making this again.

This was wonderful! Made it for company and served it over egg noodles... 
We threw everything but the cream cheese into the crock pot at the beginning and added the cream cheese the last hour... so simple and oh so good! 
Thank you so very much!!

Delicious! I used one can garlic cream of mushroom soup, and one regular can. I also used only one envelope of ranch and some minced garlic out of a jar as I didn't have any fresh cloves. I served over a bed of mashed potatoes. Extremely tasty, even better the next day after my boyfriend heated up the "sauce" on the stove top and whisked it smooth. Thanks!

This dinner was a hit with my picky eaters! it reminded me of Beef Stroganoff but with Chicken rather than beef. I made a few substitutions, I didnt add any mushrooms other than the mushroom soup,  I used actual ranch dressing from the bottle,used an herb flavored cream cheese and at the end (because we're going on vacation tomorrow) tossed in some sour cream and whipping cream because I had them in the fridge.

My family loved this dinner! I cook for a smaller crowd, so I made 3 servings instead of 6 and since I was out of mushroom soup (drat!) I increased the chicken broth and thickened it with a little cornstarch dissolved in water. Regardless, it was well worth the effort. The second time I made it, I cubed the chicken breasts and cooked it on top of the stove, also with great success. Thank you for this wonderful flavor combination!
We don't like the taste of ranch. I have easier recipe: 4-6 chicken breasts and 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup. Dump into crockpot and cook on low for 6-8 hours.

My DH and I loved this recipe. It was very easy to make and smelled good while it was cooking, it was hard to set it and forget it! Since it's only 2 of us, I "halved" the recipe using 4 chicken breasts, 8 oz of chicken broth, a packet and a half of ranch seasoning (we like ranch), one can of cream of mushroom (98% fat free), 5 oz of cream cheese (low fat), garlic and butter. I added a little pepper at the end, but no salt was needed. Also, I have a crock pot that's too big for 2 people, so halving the recipe didn't allow the juices to completely cover the chicken. After about 3 hours, I turned the chicken over so both sides were able to absorb the juices. Then I turned it over again when I added the cream cheese mixture. We served it over rice. I'd definitely make this again only next time I think I'd shred the chicken at the same time I add the cream cheese mixture. It's already so tender by this point, it seems right to do so.

This is a fantastic dish. I made it for a potluck at work (doubled, of course), and the guys were coming back for THIRDS! Very flavorful. After reading the reviews, I did cut back slightly on the ranch dressing. Other than that, no revisions. This is a no fail dish and definitely a keeper. Highly recommended!

I made this yesterday for dinner and we are having the leftovers for tonight!  A nice thick creamy sauce with fall apart tender chicken; delicious!!! It also smelled wonderful cooking all day long!  It's a keeper!!!

This was absolutely delicious! I was a little concerned about cooking the chicken breasts on high for so long, but they turned out tender and moist. My husband is not fond of cream of mushroom soup (or anything with mushrooms in it for that matter) and he also thought this was delicious. Thanks for the recipe!

Hubby really liked it. I made it almost a pantry recipe with some minor adjustments, but it was pretty close to what you had.

Used a pint of home-canned chicken and the broth, a can of mushrooms and the liquid. Did not add a can of broth. Everything else was as written. Served over rice and peas.

Easy to throw together. Thanks.

This recipe is SOOOO good!!  I made it last fall and have been searching for the recipe ever since.  It is now bookmarked!  I served this over home made mashed potatoes and it was delish!  A little heavy so I am going to try with egg noodles.  Thanks for posting this recipe!!

Probably more like 4.5 stars!

I forgot the cream cheese (and it was great).

I only had about 3/4 of one package of ranch dressing mix (and it was still great).

I threw 6 FROZEN breasts in and put it on low for about 10 hours while I was at work. Great flavor. Served over egg noodles. Too easy and too good not to make it again.

This was a fantastic dish!  All my kids loved it, including the big kid-DH!  lol  I didn't have the need to thicken my sauce.  It came out just right.  I served this with egg noddles.  Used an entire tube of fresh mushrooms, sliced-because, well, I LOVE mushrooms.  I did use a 3 lb. bag of frozen chicken breasts without any problems. Oh, and I used one can cream of mushroom and one can cream of chicken. All I had on hand.  Next time, I think I'll throw in some spinach leaves with the mushrooms and chicken.  YUMMO!  Will be making this again.

This is reallly good!  I made this and it is so comforting.  The chicken was so tender and the mixture of ingredients was divine.  I served this on white rice and we loved it.  Thank you for sharing this with us.  delicious.

So surprised. After the great 5 star reviews I thought this was going to be a hands down winner. This was ok.  Everyone ate it but no one wanted seconds. I had issues some of the other posters have noted. The "sauce" was runny like soup and not creamy. Next time I would have to omit some liquid. The cream cheese didn't dissolve in the last hour properly. I think I will warm it with the soups then add it in if I made it again. Not as easy as this states but would be creamier. The color was plain and the flavor was a tad bland. I would need to find a seasoning mix of herbs to jazz it up. The plus of the recipe was the chicken was falling apart and not dried out. It was easy and fast. Definitely add more mushrooms. This was made as written. We served it atop a choice of egg noodles or rice. Thanks for posting. Enjoy! ChefDLH

This was very good.  My chicken was so tender after 4 hours it fell apart as I tried to take it out of the crockpot so I shredded it and added it back to the broth.  I heated the soups and cream cheese on the stovetop then added it to the chicken.  I also added a little milk.  This was great over noodles.  Thanks for the recipe!

February 12, 2013 - Update - Made this for supper tonight.  The whole family loved it.  I would however, cut back a little on the the dry ranch as we thought it was a little salty and I would also half the recipe...there is alot of sauce.  We will definitely be making this again.  Thanks for sharing!

Awesome recipe!  The only changes I made to the recipe was to add a couple cans of greens in the bottom of the crockpot and I quartered a few red potatoes and added them to the crockpot as well.  Otherwise, I made the recipe exactly as written and it was fantastic!  I will definitely be making this one again!

I was excited by all the great reviews but was disappointed by the dish. Like others have said, the cream cheese didn't really melt in the crockpot. The chicken was ok but when we ate the sauce over noodles it was way to rich and taste mostly of cream cheese. I will not be making this again. I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 because the chicken was ok

I made this last night for dinner and ate it for dinner this evening. The family just loved it :) and so did I! But I did modify the recipe by using 1 can of cream of broccoli (as that was all I had, and I only used 1 can), 8 oz neufatel cheese (low fat), only 1 (8 oz) dry ranch dressing mix, 16 oz of mushrooms (purchased 1 carton of baby bella mushrooms & 1 carton of white button mushrooms) and minced garlic (3 or 4 cloves). I omitted the broth and butter that the recipe called for and still did end up with a liquidy sauce (since crock pots do add added moisture to your dish) so I just added a mixture of cornstarch and water to thicken the sauce. The chicken and sauce was just perfect over a bed of rice. <br/><br/>I would love to make this dish again and try other "cream of" soups in my pantry (I currently have cream of celery and cream of potato... wondering if it would still come out just as yummy).
Cut the recipe in half, but otherwise followed the directions. Served with mashed potatoes and green beans. It was really good!!! We're looking forward to the leftovers.
I made these with my lasagna tonight and my family loved them. I will definitely make again.Thanks much!

Lvs2cook

tried this recipe. Found it was excellent.  Except I found that I had to bake this recipe for 25 minutes at 375.  Next time I will do it at 400 for 15 or 20 min.

Thanks It is EXCELLENT.  My wife is raving about the taste and texture.  I have been making my own bread and rolls for quite a few years.

Chef 235524

These are delicious, nice and soft inside with a buttery garlic/parmesan crust. I set my timer for 15 minutes and forgot to check at 10 and they were almost too browned (but the inside was perfect). Very yummy, thanks Lvs2Cook.

These rolls were just absolutely awesome.  The texture was sooooo soft.  The flavor was  undescribely good.  My DH won't let me make anything else now.  He couldn't stop eating them.  Thanks for such a wonderful recipe.
Really simple, really good! A very nice change from plain old garlic bread. Great recipe--light, fluffy, buttery, with just the right amount of garlic & cheese.

this was really a very good yeast roll. i only made half of the recipe since there was only two of us,because i knew that they all would have been eaten in one day if i didn't :).it took about 15 minutes longer to rise than the recipe stated,but that was o.k.and i baked them at 375º and they took about 25 minutes to get to the desired color.as i said these were really good.as lots of possibilties to add different herbs to go with lots of main dishes.thanks for posting.
Oh My!  What wonderful rolls!  I'd give them 10 stars if I could.  I baked them for about 20 minutes and the parmasean toasted up nicely.  I will definitely make these again.  Thanks for posting!
I've made these twice now and the result is consistent -- absolutely fabulous.  My 22-year-old son said they're the best ever, and I agree.  Thanks Lvs2Cook.
These rolls were great tasting and so quick and easy to fix. Thanks Lvs2Cook....

I just made these to go with dinner, and if I could give them 10 stars I would!  They turned out lovely, and the entire family said to please make again , not to lose this recipe and that we could try different toppings.  I said "NO" they are perfect just the way they are, why bother?  I  made by hand and baked at 350 (375 seemed to high for my oven) for about 20 minutes.  They were light, golden and simply delcious.  Thank-you for sharing this recipe.
Another "keeper" recipe. These are delicious!  I didn't have nonfat dry milk powder so substituted dry non-dairy creamer with good results.
So yummy! Def will make again.
These were great, will make again. Thanks!

The rolls turned out as I imagined them.  They were soft and the garlic, butter, cheese combination was perfect.  However, there was one drawback:  My husband commented that the rolls made him think of 'holiday cookies'.  When prompted to explain what he meant, he said that they were 'a little sweet' in an uncritical, questioning tone:-)  I knew he was right after my very first bite, though I tried to ignore it.  So, knowing that baking is a science and a change of ingredients can have a big impact, I cannot suggest reducing the sugar; but the dough is a bit over-sweet.
Great recipe.  My partner loved these rolls.  They turned out lovely and light. Next time I am making them a bit bigger to use them as lunch rolls.
These were quite good...served with White Sauce Chicken Lasagna.

I use to make this same recipe that I got from a betty crocker cookbook years ago but I lost the book when I moved. I have been searching for it for a while and now I have finally found it again. We absolutely loved this bread. thanks lvs2cook

Really really tasty rolls.  They were soft and fluffy and the toasty parmesan was the perfect accompaniment.  We had these with Gypsy Soup, and the warm buns and hot soup were the perfect thing for this snowy November day.
I'll definitely make these again - Great easy bread machine recipe, thanks!
These are excellent.  Made them twice this week.  Thanks for a very good recipe!
These were wonderful, my whole family enjoyed them.  Thank you for a simple but tasty recipe.
Great easy recipe...Followed the recipe exactly, made these for a small dinner party of 5, only cut into 16 large rolls, everyone raved and I took home an empty dish. Thanks for sharing! Angela

Very Good! Rave reviews from all 6 members of the household. Will definitely make these again and keep in regular rotation. Thank you for a wonderful tasty garlic cheese roll recipe :) I made these exactly as written. We only achieved  12 rolls though but not a big deal as we had plenty.
YUMMY! It took longer than 15 minutes to cook, but worth waiting for!

Delicious, easy to make.  I was in a hurry, so none of my rolls were the same size, so only got about 18 rolls (which was plenty!).  They were light, browned well and tasted delicious with our pork loin tonight! Man I love the breadmaker!
I'm the best mom in the whole world when I make these. My kids love them!  Thanks!

Easy and VERY tasty!  I've made these 3 times now and every time the rolls just disappear.  I don't roll and stretch the dough, I just pull at it from the machine and roll it into balls that I drop onto a greased 9x13 glass pan.  Giving them time to rise is the key to light and fluffy rolls.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe that is a keeper in our house.
Mmmm! I added a tsp of garlic powder to the flour so that the garlic flavor would be pronounced.  These rolls have excellent texture.

These were the best rolls i have ever made!!!! hubby says 10 stars!!
the only thing i did different was to bake them first then brushed with melted butter mixed with a little garlic powder, then sprinkled with parm cheese. put back in the oven for a couple min, i am embarassed to say hubby and i had 3 each!!

will make again for sure

I am not going to give this recipe stars because I am not sure if it is my fault or the recipe since so many people like it and gave it 5 stars.  Anyway,  my dough didn't rise after 3 hours.  Also,  I think 3 cups of flour were too much because the dough was too dry.  If I get a chance,  I will make this again with 2 1/2 cup of flour.  Also,  the rolls were on the sweet side so I am going to reduce the sugar.

We really liked this. My husband and kids gobbled them up. As per some other reviews I decided to use only 1 tbls. of sugar as I didn't want them to sweet and  used more garlic cloves. Also I have used frozen store bought dough that I defrosted with great results when I don't have the time to make the dough.Thanks for posting, it's a keeper.

WOW!!! I can't post what was said about this because it was rather explicit in a good way ;) I will say that I'm very new to bread making and still getting acquainted with my machine. This is the first recipe besides pizza dough that came out perfect!!!! I followed the recipe exactly and IT IS SO DELICIOUS!!!! I planned on having a lot left over since there are only two of us...I won't tell you have many I actually have left, it's embarrassing, lol. We are stuffed! I can't wait to make these for company next week. We give this recipe all the stars in the sky!

These are the best garlic rolls I have ever had! My DH is Italian so we eat a lot of bread around here and this is made often. I do add some garlic powder to the dough for extra garlic taste and put shreddred cheese on top before baking as both DH and DS love cheese. They turn out great.

I made these to go with recipe 167669 and they were AMAZING!! Best garlic rolls I've ever had- all the rolls disappeared I& my guests (and family) raved about them. I didn't even have any parmesan cheese to add to the top this time either. I took another reviewers tip and added some garlic powder to the dough.

I followed the recipe, but when the dough cycle was finished, I rolled the dough and made bread sticks.  I rolled the dough into a rectangle, added the butter, cheese, etc. and then let it rise a bit.  The result was large puffy breadsticks that everyone enjoyed.  Thanks

SO YUMMY!! Looks just like the pictures shows. Very pleased hubby and I both were. I cut the recipe in half because I didn't need to make so many cause I didn't need to eat so many haha. They were very flavorful soft fluffy. DELICIOUS!!
I cut the recipe in half because of the size of my bread machine.  They were delicious.   Our boys ate every single one at dinner.  I cooked them for 15 minutes - might do two minutes more next time.

I made exactly as written and the rolls turned out beautifully. The family was crowding around the kitchen while they were baking and a bunch of rolls were gone in no time. So soft and fluffy! I baked for 21 min. We will definitely make these again - and again! Thanks for sharing this recipe!

We LOVED these rolls! I loved how easy they were, too. I baked mine at 375 for 18 minutes and they came out perfect! These smell so delicious while baking, too.  These rolls don't need any extra butter on them, either; as they taste so yummy with the topping and the melted butter that ended up on the bottom as well. I made these to go with Lasagna and with our Meatball Pasta Soup. I will be making these often for Italian dishes. Thanks for sharing.

Wow these were great! Sooo easy and turned out perfectly! My first attempt at home made rolls and what a great recipe to choose :) I used buttermilk powder instead of milk powder, and I accidently put the garlic in with the bread which was not a bad thing at all, so i mixed garlic powder with the butter to pour on the top and it was perfect that way for me. Served this with italian manicoti and salad. Thank you so much for posting this! :)
These are so good. I make them as bread sticks. My son takes a baggie of them in his lunch bag every day. They freeze very well.

Oh MY Lord!!! These are awesome.  I used garlic powder instead of fresh garlic just for ease. I also sprinkled both fresh & grated Parmesan cheese. My husband wont be home for another half hour & I'm using self control to not go eat them all!  I can't wait to make these again and again and again...
These were pretty good, but not exactly the taste I was looking for.
These are awesome! I topped half with shredded cheddar cheese. The whole family loved it. Gonna make these very often.

So delicious!  I used half all-purpose and half whole wheat flour, and topped with grated garlic (I used my microplane) rather than crushed, a sprinkle of salt and grated cheddar instead of parmesan.  I loved the flavor and my husband couldn't stop telling me how much he loved them.  I will absolutely make these again, thanks!
These were really good!  I added cheddar cheese to the top too!  Thanks for the recipe!!!

Yummy! I cut the sugar down to 2 tbsp and they turned out perfect. I also used olive oil instead of butter (personal preference). Next time I would probably put a little more garlic on them and some garlic in the dough as well.
I cut the recipe in half to make 12 rolls.  I had to add quite a bit of extra water to get the correct consistency.  All in all, a very good tasting roll that I would consider making again.
Totally awesome and simple to make. 5 stars!

Delicious! I keep minced garlic and Italian seasoning in olive oil in the fridge so that the flavors blend. That is what I used to make these and it came out delicious. Also, I mixed this by hand with a wooden spoon because I don't have a bread machine. Still very easy to make. Thank you for the wonderful recipe!

Yummy!  Pretty quick and easy to put together, made the recipe as is with no changes except extra garlic in the butter drizzled on top, not overly sweet to my taste.  Done in 15 minutes perfectly.  Had some for dinner with tortellini tonight, froze the rest to keep me from completely stuffing myself!  Great recipe, thanks for posting!

I made this recipe this past weekend and the family loved them.  I had to make 2 batches because the first one did not survive the cooling period.  The second batch I did add additional amounts of butter and garlic to put on top.  This was a request of the kids and hubby.  I would definitely make this one often.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

My dough rose very well at the end of the dough cycle but when it was turned onto a floured surface the dough collapsed completely ! The dough was also very sticky and I managed to get only 12 balls from these. The baked rolls were not fluffy at all but still edible, rather chewy. Didn't like the cheesy taste on the rolls.

So delicious! For some reason I only got 12 rolls from this recipe, but that's OK. I used plenty of garlic as we are garlic fans in this household. My rolls came out looking nothing like the pictures (they were kinda sad looking), but who cares as the results were soft, fluffy, and tasty. I served these with chicken parmagian. Can't wait to make these again...thanks for posting!
Unbelievably good. Added two cloves of pressed garlic and cheddar to the dough. Cant make enough of these as family and friends eat them so fast!

My goodness....these rolls are absolutely amazing and a beautiful compliment to any meal. They are soft, airy, moist, and delish! They also keep well. Very fun and easy to make. I did substitute the powdered milk for two tablespoons of fresh whole milk. Yummy!!!!

Made this just as instructed except used frozen clean devained shrimp as it was what I had on hand. My family loves it! The recipe is fast and very easy.  Should have doubled the sauce and rice as everyone raved...two familiy memebers went home and made it the next day.
Absolutely wonderful with the shrimp eaters at this house. I love the herbs that give it a wonderful flavor. That little bit of beer rounds out the herbs nicely. Very good.
Good work, EdsGirl!  Had to substitute Smart Balance for the butter because dairy products trigger my colitis.  It was still great!  Next time, I think I will add a bit more garlic.  Yums!

We LOVED this dish!  I had to cut way back on the cayenne and peppers because of kids but other than that this dish rocks.  I served it over basmati rice along with baked tomatoes and zuchinni. Can't wait to eat this dinner again. YUM!

Ay-yiyiyiyi!  Made this last night, exactly as directed, but doubled the sauce ingredients, as others had suggested.  Well, both DH and I LOVE spicy food, but next time I double this, I'll double the beer and leave the spices as is.  Boy-oh-boy did this "light us up".  We totally enjoyed it, but my DH asked me if I'd added "Dave's Insanity Sauce" - it was that hot, to us, when I doubled the spices.  Even with the spice heat, we loved the taste, and the ease of this recipe - very similar to a dish from one of our favorite local restaurants.  Totally delicious, EdsGirl - we'll make this often, I'm sure.
I made this for my dd who is a shrimp fan-a-tic.  I myself am not but must say I really enjoyed this dish.  Loved the spicey taste.  Will definitely make this again. Thanks!

Excellent recipe.  Incredibly fast and easy to make (and not much washing up!).  Didn't have the dried herbs specified so used dried 'mixed herbs' instead. I also toned down the heat considerably by leaving out the cayenne and using only 1/4 teaspoon crushed chilli (from a bottle).  This gave it enough zing for our taste. Also doubled the sauce.  Despite these changes we LOVED the taste and will make this again ... and again .... and again.  Thanks.

WOW!!! What a great dish.  I too doubled the sauce.  In half I put shrimp the other half cubed chicken.  I also thickened the sauce a little w/ flour and butter. Thank you so much for the great recipe.  We will have this again.

I made this for the first time this Valentines Day and being a guy and in college this was so, so easy. I've never cooked shrimp before and even I could pull it off. Both me and my date love, loved it. Thanks!!!!!

I made this the other night exactly as directed served with linguine.  It was pretty good BUT...it is extremely hot!!! Way too hot for me, I couldn't eat more then about 4 mouthfuls.  Hubby ate his entire plate but he was panting and sucking back cold beers the whole time. I might make this again, it was very simple, easy clean up and quite fast for a weeknight but I won't be adding any of the cayenne next time.  This rates about a 8 alarm for heat prepared as directed.

i followed the other reviewers and doubled the sauce ingredients and served over rice.  HE loved the spicey taste and I kept gasping for air cause I am a wimp when it comes to hot but I really enjoyed the flavor once I could breathe again.  will make it again to prove I am not a baby!
we missed with this one - not sure why - made for special Valentine's dinner - did not care for spice combination

I did not enjoy this as much as I thought.  I loved the smell of the herbs and the shrimp as they were cookiing, it lost it when I added the beer.  I would make it again without the beer. It just didn't add anything for me. I gave the recipe to my mom who didn't add the beer and tossed with pasta, and toned down the heat, and she is still raving about it.

I made this recipe twice. The first time I followed the recipe and it was so hot we couldn't eat it. The second time I cut the cayanne & crushed peppers in half and we enjoyed it very much. I will add this recipe to my favorites list and will prepare again.

What a popular recipe!  I made this for my family last night and it was way too spicy for the kids!  However, for hubby and I it was wonderful.  I'm using the leftover shrimp in enchiladas tonight.  Thanks for sharing this superb recipe!!!

Wow!  Awesome shrimp dish!  The only think I did differently was omit the salt, double the butter, and reduce the amount of beer to about 1/4 cup (because I'm not too fond of beer).  It was spicy hot, but I loved it that way!  If I were to prepare it for guests, I'd probably cut back on the heat just a bit.  I served this over wheat pasta along with a fresh tossed salad.  This is a keeper!

I'm sorry this really didn't work for me. This sounded like something I would really like too. I've made it twice, just in case I messed it up the first time. The second time I used fresh herbs and still didn't like it.
LOVED this recipe!  The dressing was perfect...not overpowering.  I used white wine vinegar instead of regular vinegar and it was great!  Will use this one again!

This was a miss for me too.  I thought by the sounds of it that we would love it, but no one in my family cared for it.  The beer just seemed to overpower everything else.  It could be that we drink "darker" beer with a little more flavor than your typical lite beer.

I loved this in the pan before I added the beer, but then it lost some of its appeal. I typically love recipes with beer, so I'm not sure what the problem is. I would have liked more depth to the flavors...we ended up adding a little Worcestershire and lemon juice. It was very good and really easy...I'll make this again, the spices are dead on...very spicy and buttery, just how we like it. I may experiment with wine or some other liquid than the beer. DH liked the sauce better than I did, he thinks sometimes the Worcestershire sauces get *too* heavy. Really interesting recipe, thanks for posting!
We thought this was pretty good and followed our carb plan.  Nice flavor.  Used frozen deveined shrimp.  Super fast recipe.

My husband and I love spicy things and thought this was just right.  I doubled the sauce as suggested by others but substituted 1/2 c. pinot grigio and 1/2 c. chicken broth for the beer.  I also dusted the shrimp with flour to help thicken the sauce.  The sauce was so good we ate an ungodly amount of french bread that night!
I saw a review of this last week and knew local boats were bringing in very nice shrimp. Excellent recipe to serve with garlic bread! Didn't change a thing.

Delicious!  I toned down the cayenne and red pepper a bit; it still had a little zing but nothing overpowering.  I'm on a low carb diet so I used low carb beer and ate these alone with a side of veggies and some slaw.  Great recipe!

I served this over rice for dinner along with a salad.  This makes a wonderful meal.  I cut back on the cayenne pepper and the red pepper flakes and it turned out perfect for us.  This recipe will also go in my Appetizer Folder.  Can't wait to serve it to guests. This is a great new way to prepare shrimp.  Thanks for sharing, EdsGirlAngie.
Oh so good!   I cut back on the peppers as well, as we don't like it too spicy.   We truly enjoyed this, and can't wait to make it for a party!

I came across this recipe sort of by accident; was looking for a use for some precooked prawns in the freezer.  This was the perfect recipe for those little critters!  Between two of us we used almost a whole loaf of french bread for the sopping.  Can't wait to make it again!

I made this to go along with our easter steak this year. I halved the ampount of shrimp and hot stuff so we would have plenty of sauce for the 2 of use to "sop" up. It was warm, but I was happy I cut the cayenne and peppers in half as I like to taste the shrimp not hot. I served the leftovers over basmati rice. I was surprised that it got saltier overnight, not hotter. But fantastic either way. It will be repeated here often.

I can't believe I actually forgot to review this recipe. I've probably made it half a dozen times! It's one of my husband's favorites and we love to have it with lots of bread and a caesar salad. Low on effort, high on flavor. Wonderful stuff!
I loved this recipe, served with warm crusty bread to absorb the delicious sauce, thanks for a great recipe.

Very good, but oooh, so hot!  I used half the cayenne pepper called for, and it was still too hot for my husband and I.  But our guests, who love spicy food, gladly took the leftovers home with them.  I used frozen, cleaned deveined shrimp, and doubled the sauce, and served it over a wild rice medley, with fresh corn on the cob and a salad.
Perfect!  I would not change a thing with this recipe.  Some toasty bread, fresh sliced tomatoes and cucumbers, and dinner is done in about 15 minutes.  DH was impressed.

This was wonderful.  I took the advice of other reviewers and halved the cayenne & red pepper flakes and it was just right for us.  Served with Boconcini salad for the coolness of the cheese and tomatoes to contrast with the heat from the prawns and crusty bread to clean up the extra sauce.  This made for a light delicious dinner!

Now I love hot food, but I anticipated this dish would be too spicy as written, so I cut both the cayenne and red peppper flakes down to 1/4t. It was still very, very hot. But it was pretty, and very easy. I'd make it again, but I'll omit the cayenne and use only the red pepper flakes.
Very good.  Loved the spiceness of this dish.  Served over rice.  Next time I will thicken the sauce with a little bit of corn starch.  Will have it again soon.

I made this last night for a Mardi Gras party.  I don't think a single person at the party didn't like it.  They all wanted the recipe.  But I think next time I'll use the suggestions of putting flour or cornstarch in it to thicken the sauce a little bit.  But even without it, it was a HUGE hit.
I loved this shrimp! I don't do many shrimp recipes, but I will now. I wasn't sure about the spices-oregano, basil and thyme-at first, but I've learned not to doubt zaar chefs-this was awesome!

This was soooo fast & Yummy. We had it with rice & the sauce was FANTASTIC!!!! 
Definatly a great appetizer!!!!
Delicious. I served over plain white rice for an easy yet very impressive late meal. Thanks.

Holy cow, thanks for such a great recipe!  I made these for a party and served with store-bought remoulade.  They were delicious, popular and could not have been easier! These are great for parties because I discovered that they taste great hot, room-temperature or cold!  I made this as written and wouldn't change a thing.  This will be a keeper.

I have made A LOT of shrimp recipes from this site, and many were very good....this is without a doubt the BEST shrimp recipe I have ever tried PERIOD. I made this exactly as directed, and served with a crusty bread and a bottle of Chardonney. Perfect kick from the peppers and I loved the mixture of the herbs. We LOVED this. Couldn't have possibly been in better. I can't wait to make this one again.
Wow-wee.  Served this on jasmine rice.  I halved the cayenne pepper and the crushed red pepper flakes and I was glad for it after a few bites.  I also added a little cornstarch to thicken the sauce.

Fast, Easy, and Delicious: What more could you ask for?  I had to scale back the heat a little bit for the kids (not too much, they like a little kick) but other than that I made it exactly as posted.  Everybody loved it, and I will definitely be making this again.
This was easy enough to prepare, however it was a bit spicy for my kids. My husband and I enjoyed it very much!

this was very, very good.  I tripled the sauce, using 1 1/2 sticks butter, and 1 1/2 cup beer, and 3X spices, except for pepper which I basically halved, with the substitution of Hot Paprika for some of the cayenne. I used cooked, ready to eat shrimp, 1 lb. pasta shells, and added flour to thicken, and 1 T lemon juice.  Also added 1/3 more garlic. Served over pasta.  I think next time I will use 1/2 beer or white wine and  1/2 chicken broth, as there was a slightly bitter aftertaste with the beer, although that may be due to good rich beer. Also, I think I want to try it with french bread or rice... the flavor i think would work better than with pasta.  it made for a slightly strange pasta dish, but the flavor and spice heat were so good it didn't really matter.  I am eager to try the leftovers! Thanks Angie, for a great versatile dish!

This was FANTASTIC!!! And yes it was spicy, a little too spicy for my fiance, so next time I might leave out the cayenne pepper and go with a little less red pepper flakes. I doubled the sauce but I used half the butter and threw in some extra virgin olive oil. Instead of adding beer, I added white cooking wine. Divine smell when cooking. Served tossed with linguine. I will absolutely make again!! Thanks for posting.
Good flavor and easy to make.

This was pretty good.  It was easy enough for anyone to make and the flavor was good, just wasn't my favorite way to make shrimp.  I served this on top on recipe #91685 (avocado tequila linguine) and the combination was really good.

Made this for a group dinner(lots of other entrees), doubled the recipe and then redoubled the sauce------GONE, totally disappeared, vanished, dish wiped clean, empty in a matter of minutes!  Every one loved it!  Had to go to the host's computer and print off several copies of the recipe--Immediately!  
Why did I wait so long to try this recipe?  Thank you so much for posting this!
Love it!  Yummo!  But it is spicy.  I could have used it a little less spicy but DH loved and said leave it as it is. Thanks for this great recipe.

Made this for dinner tonight and it was really good.  I left out the crushed red pepper - DH and DD don't care for too much spice. I think I could have added a dash and it would have been OK.  My DD was standing over the skillet test tasting as I was cooking and decided it needed something extra, so I added salt and juice of one lemon and I think that was just what it needed.  Next time I'll try thickening the sauce up a bit.  Thanks!

Angie, this was great!  I went back for more than seconds, I tell ya'!

Made it just as published and only wish that I had listened to your advice regarding the crusty French bread!  I will have bread on hand next time!

Thanks for a great recipe.

Simple and awe-inspiringly delicious. We LOVED this dish. I served it over whole-wheat couscous. The only change I made was to use 1.5 lbs of shrimp. I just thought we'd like the extra sauce, and ahem, we really did! Thank you soooo much for sharing. I can't wait to make it again. PS: a super easy weeknight meal.

I made this with 2 lbs. of large shrimp and doubled the sauce mixture.  I did double the butter, beer, garlic, oregano, basil and thyme but only did approx. 1/2 tsp. on cayenne and 1/8 tsp. red pepper flakes.  Also, used two to three grinds of fresh pepper.  It was plenty hot but not to where you couldn't enjoy it!  Served with french bread.  Great recipe!  It was very easy to make!

Scrumptious!!!!!  Super simple to make, super tasty too boot!  If you need dinner on the table in a jiff, this is a fantastic dish for that!  We used our favorite Texas beer, and the dish just turned out wonderful.  Thanks so much for posting this little darling :)

I cut down on the cayenne--a little goes a LONG way!  Excellent flavors, I'll be making this again! I used about 12 oz of shrimp so I cut the sauce ingredients in half (eyeballing it) and it was still great!

Amazing! Made these for a birthday party.  The men were licking thier bowls. I dont even like beer, and loved these shrimp.  I did not have have red pepper flakes, so used a couple dashes cayenne instead.  I also doubled the sauce, and was glad I did.
We just ate as is, but would be great over pasta.
I too enjoyed this. I cut the recipe in half for the two of us.Cooked it outside on the BBQ burner.  Went great with bread and a good glass or two of white wine.  Thanks for the post EdsGirlAngie.

I did not eat this myself as I am not a seafood fan but my fiancee and daughter loved it! I was worried that it might taste like beer as thats how it smelled but they said you couldn't even taste it. My fiancees brother in law owns a restaurant that serves a similiar shrimp dish and he said this one beat the pants off of his!
WOW!!! This was fantastic!  I too doubled the sauce and had plenty of French bread for sauce-dipping.  The shrimp, the bread, and a salad - that was all we needed!  Simple to make and delicious!

This is YUMMY! Made it exactly as written. My son is allergic to shrimp so in a seperate pan I made him a smaller portion using chicken breast tenderloins and he LOVED IT! I think next time I am going to try reducing the beer a bit and serving this over a nice juicy grilled flat iron steak!
EDIT: I have made this so many times now it is not even funny. I LOVE this! Like some other reviewers I have floured my shrimp to thicken the sauce. I always make double the sauce because it is SO good over rice, or over steak, or over chicken or over...well, you get the picture! Also, Ihave found that I like to use a nice dark beer. I prefer Killians. It gives it such a nice flavor. Thanks EdsGirlAngie for such a wonderful recipe that has turned into a staple at our house!

WOW! Was this ever good! I doubled the entire recipe and four of us scarfed it down in record time. I served it over white rice which I cooked with chicken broth and the same spices (light) that are in the shrimp.  Awesome.  I probably could've eaten more!  I will add this to my repeats for sure.

I made this the other day for dinner and it was a hit with my DH.  It was a little spicy for me so next time I will just tone down the cayenne and red pepper flakes.  I did double the sauce.  It was super easy to make and even easier to eat.  I served with rice and a good sourdough.  This would be a wonderful appetizer for a party.  Thanks for posting a keeper!

I made these shrimp for an appetizer at a Labor Day barbeque and they were a hit!  I asked DH to taste test them and he said that we need to make these sometime just for us at home.  Then he stared at them until I finally relented and let him test one more!  At the picnic, I had several people comment on the incredible shrimp, despite all the tasty food their!  I will be making this again and again.  I used 1.5 lbs of frozen shrimp, thawed.  Doubled the amount of sauce and reserved half to heat up and top the dish with right before serving.  Perfect heat, very garlicky and not overpowering from the beer.  I need a batch of these babies and a loaf of french bread stat!

Thank you for sharing, as I like the general idea for this recipe. The flavor before adding the beer was amazing. As recommended by others, I dusted the shrimp in flour and it really thickened up the sauce nicely. The beer, unfortunately, gave it a rather bitter taste that overwhelmed the dish. I used Heineken. I *do* plan on making this dish again. Next time I will use Riesling or Pinot Grigio wine instead of beer. I believe the sweetness of these wines will pair well with the spicy herbs.

Gato made it and said, "I love fast meals", so that says it all (he is a good cook but doesn't do it often) for me. It was WONDERFUL flavor, too. I loved the whole spicy, but Gato will tone it back next time despite his love of spicy. He says it's "missing something" but I'm not sure I agree. It was so very good over white rice. Next time there'll be crusty bread and Chardonnay, too! Thanks, EdsGirl!
Edit: We used Dos XX Lager - Perfect!

This was wonderful.  I had a shrimp fanatic here tonight, daughter of my best friend and she ate a pound on her own.

Terrific dish, next time i will cut down on the heat bc i did not use cayenne, just crushed red pepper and it was HOT.  worth every firey bite :)

Started to make this when i realized i was out of dried oregano but i did have ground oregano. So i substituted that but i added less of it. I thickened the sauce as some other reviewers had suggested. It was delicious but i felt like it needed something so i added a can of tomatoe sauce and it was perfect! Thanks sooooo much

These were good.  I felt a little too much thyme and beer really made it soupy.  Next time will reduce thyme and omit beer.  They seemed a great consistency before I added the beer.  Thanks for posting.
i can't really comment on this because i put too much cayenne that they were inedible, will try again sometime though because they sound awesome!
I made this a long time ago and forgot to rate it. Luckily I came across it again!! I served it over rice and it was soooo good!! Now that I found it again i'm going to be making this quite often!

Great recipe!  I found this today while looking for finger foods and I couldn't wait to try it.  It reminds me of a BBQ shrimp recipe I tried years ago minus the huge amount of butter.  I'll try dusting the shrimp to thicken the sauce since I love dipping the bread in the sauce.  Thanks for posting this one.  It's a keeper.

Every once in awhile I find a recipe that makes me believe for just a moment that I am capable of great things in the kitchen, and this was one of those. This was hands down, by far and without question the *best* shrimp dish I have *ever* eaten *anywhere* in my life, and I've made it a point to eat more than my fair share of shrimp. I made this exactly as written except that I just made it as a half recipe (silly, silly me - should have quintupled it) thinking that as a side dish two pounds would be too much for the two of us. Wrong. Both of us couldn't help commenting with every bite that it was just perfect. Just one more pinch of cayenne pepper or pepper flakes would have been too spicy, just one more tablespoon of beer would have been too powerful, but as is, the spiciness lingered for a bit but wasn't too much, and the hint of beer flavor just added a nice earthiness to the whole dish.

Next time, this will *not* be a side dish but the main dish with the French bread suggested and also a nice bottle of Chardonnay. And a much, much larger batch. I can't wait!!

my b/f told me not to make this, sounds bad.  i snuck it in a few nights ago, didn't tell him which recipe it was.  served the shrimp with steak.  he couldn't get enough!  - it'll have to be our secret ;) thanks!
I love recipes like this. Packed with flavor and super easy to put together. Thanks for posting this! I didn't change a thing.
great recipe!!! definitely a keeper... thanks a lot for this :)
Made this for hubby, he loved it. He said next time to use less  cayenne, it was a little too spicy.

This was really good!  There are just two of us, so I used only one pound of shrimp.  Wound up with plenty of the delicious sauce.  I cut back the cayenne to 1/4 tsp.  It was fiery enough for us, because of the red pepper flakes. I removed the shrimp when it was cooked and reduced the sauce to the thickness I wanted, then poured it over the shrimp and tossed.  Yum!  Will make this again.

Woohoo! A big hit (okay, I would have only given it four stars.. but..)My boyfriend LOVED IT (and i love him). So this will definitely stay in the rotation, as others had suggested, I cut the cayenne in half and it was the perfect amount of spice.  I also added a slurry of 1 tsp corn starch and 1/4 c cold water at the end to thicken the sauce. It turned out great!
Served with crusty bread and salad. mmmmm. quick, easy and delicious!

It was great. I didn't have any thyme, so skipped that and used chicken broth for the liquid then followed  everything else except for the salt and pepper did that to taste. We had lots of sause for our bread-yummy.
Then made the same sauce for some fish (rock fish) cooked the fish in the sauce and it was the best fish I have had in years...was perfect. On the fish I only used one T of butter and 1/3 of the seasoning, didn't want to over power the fish. Everyone loved it and finished all of it. We had both the at the same meal. We had planned on grilling the fish, but when the shrimp came out so good we tried it on the fish. ...Plan on trying it on salmon this weekend with the full amount of spices!! and no kids at the meal.

This has the potential to be very good. I used chicken since we are not big shrimp eaters.I doubled the sauce.I would cut down on the cayenne next time since it was a little too hot. Also, didn't care for the beer taste. Next time, I will use wine & chicken stock like some have done. I will make it again with these changes.
YUMMY!!  A keeper n will make again.  Thanks Angie!!!!

Fabulous!  I also used white wine and chicken broth.  Served with Kittencal's Famous Greek Salad and the whole family loved it.  Thanks for a really yummy recipe!  (P.S. I left out the cayenne so my 6-year-old would be able to eat it.)
Yummy!!
Spicy and delicious! Served with rice and french bread. I used olive oil instead of butter. Turned out perfect. Thanks for an awesome recipe!
This is some goooooood stuff!  The only change I made was to add a little cornstarch to the sauce to make it thicker.
It was ok. I felt it lacked depth of flavor. I think I'll stick to my Shrimpin Dippin Broth recipe from Bubba Gump Co. Thanks!
This was great and easy. I made a few minor changes...I added fresh mushrooms and did 1 tablespoon of butter and one of olive oil and I doubled the sauce! The sauce over rice..yummy

So I've had this tucked in a cookbook for who knows how long and now I'm wondering why, why didn't we try this sooner!!!  As others suggested I doubled and thickened the sauce but halved the cayenne/red pepper flakes.  We got a lovely spicy kick - we do like it hot so I might turn up the heat a tiny bit next time - oh yes there will be a next time!

Amazing.  We are sodium-conscious because of my bf's kidney disorder, so I omitted the extra salt.  
This dish was great, exactly the spice I was looking for.  So easy.  I woke up about midnight craving spice... I was going to make shrimp cocktail but threw this together instead in no time.  Thanks a ton - can't wait to share this one!

KC_Cooker this recipe is AWESOME! I can't believe I didn't review it yet. It is full of flavor and easy to boot!  We love the kick of the peppers. MMMMM! I have made it several times. The first time I followed your directions but doubled the sauce. Since then I use it as a base and add scallions, lemon zest and juice, capers, asparagus, and cherry tomatoes. I usually serve over abed of rice. DH and DS always give this one 5 stars!

Yum!  Fast fast fast--great for a weeknight.  Very spicy and delicious--I stirred in some grape tomatoes and day old rice and served it w/ parmesan roasted asparagus and garlic cheese bread--a hit!  Thank you for a great recipe
Made for DH - I don't eat shrimp, but loved the sauce! Really quick to make, and great flavor; maybe I'll adapt for chicken. Thanks for sharing - going to weeknight 'keepers' file!

This is the first time I've ever cooked shrimp in a pan at home (not counting fried, or bacon wrapped - but those aren't in a pan) that I have actually liked the outcome. I didn't have the green spices listed but I did have Italian seasoning, so I doubled the butter, the beer, used 4 tsp. Italian Seasoning, 1 tsp. salt, and half the amounts of the red pepper ingredients (1 tsp. cayenne, 1/2 tsp. red pepper). At the end I thought it was a little bit watery maybe I used a tad too much beer so I added some extra virigin olive oil and IT ROCKED! Loved it! Thanks!  UPDATE: August, 20 - Made this again today with prawns but without the basil and I loved it even more.  I wish I could give you a hundred stars.
Made this as is except used 1/2 tsp. of cayenne. Dipped Olive bread in the sauce. Had Broccoli Salad with Avocado on the side.Very good! We love the Shrimp and sauce.

I made this wine cooking wine instead of beer. I had the beer poured ready to go in and I backed out at the last minute. I had a pale ale on hand and after a long day just didn't want to take a chance when I knew wine would be perfect.  We really enjoyed this.  Added double wine and double butter to serve over pasta. Excellent!

This was good, but I have other shrimp recipes that my family likes better that are just as easy to make, so I'll probably stick with those.  It made for a good supper, but I don't think I'll make it again.  It was nice to try for something different, though.

Really delicious dish! I doubled the sauce as suggested by others and also left out the thyme because we don't like it. I had some extra bacon in the frige so I chopped that up and fried it before I followed the other directions. My 2-year old twin granddaughters dipped tortilla chips in the broth and LOVED it even though I thought it might be too spicy for them but it was nbot. This is so easy too that we will have it often. Next time I will serve this over pasta.

I'll try this one again sometime but the first time I made it was waaay too spicy for myself.  The BF loved it though.  I had cut down the cayenne and doubled the sauce like others suggested, but perhaps for us weenies I'll just add a dash of cayenne.

Very spicy but I loved it!  I served it over leftover brown rice.  I doubled the sauce, use light margarine, and omitted the salt.  If you cook the shrimp until pink and done and then simmer for an additional minute, the shrimp will be overcooked and rubbery.  So, my shrimp was just becoming pink when I added the beer, covered the simmered for a minute.  The shrimp was perfect!  A definite keeper.

It was fast, easy and delicious!  Got rave reviews from my boyfriend.  We used cooked and peeled shrimp from the freezer and just let them heat up in the beer.  Great flavor in under 15 minutes.  We're going to try it next time with white wine instead of the beer.
I think this had really great flavor.. The overall concensus of last nite's recipients was to leave out the crushed red pepper flakes.. Other than that, it was awesome.

This was a super-quick and easy dish to make, I loved it! I substituted paprika for the cayenne peppers because my family can't take spicy foods, but it was still great and the sauce was amazing to dip french bread in! Thanks!

Made this AGAIN last night and the ratings are right, it was fantastic. (My only regret was no doubling the sauce-first review). Made it again tonight and tripled everything but the shrimp.  Also we are spoiled with just right cooked shrimp.  So before adding the beer or broth, remove the shrimp and cover to keep warm. Pour in beer or broth and reduce a little to thicken.  But make lots, you will want to soak up every drop of the sauce!
These were fantastic!  My family doesn't like a lot of spice, so we left out some of the cayenne, and garlic, and they still had lots of flavor.
Very good. Will make again.
love this!! I make it for dinner when I get home late. family loves it too! I add in alot more butter ( unhealthy i know) but it tends to absorb too quickly

This was very good. I have a recipe for a similar dish. The shrimp is cooked in the shell which gives it a great flavor, but boy is it messy. This you could serve for guests without having to provide finger bowls. (and I don't have any) A keeper!
Super!! Added more butter!

Excellent! We're not big fans of spicy dishes, so I reduced the crushed red pepper and took out the cayenne. Doubled the sauce and have been eating the leftovers for the last 4 days! The sauce is amazing on garlic bread. It also goes well with egg noodles.

My brother and I made this on one of our cooking Wednesday and we really liked it.  I took the advice of many others and doubled the sauce, although I did not double the red pepper, and left out the cayenne altogether - it was just a good amount of heat I thought.  We served it with brown rice (and egg noodles to make the picky children happy) and bread.  Both kids even asked for seconds although one thought it was kind of spicy.

Thank you! We really enjoyed this recipe. I doubled the sauce ingredients per other comments, and I don't think we would have had enough if I hadn't. I did not double the beer (more out of mistake), and actually thought it may not even need the beer at all. I didn't have any cayenne so I left that out as well. Still really, really good!! Def making this again!!

This was really good, and spicy!  I thought the sauce was yummy, but I wanted it a little thicker so I used 2t cornstarch in a slurry with a little chicken broth.  The shrimp were really flavorful and it all comes together quick, easy, and impressive.

This recipe was amazing!  The shrimp had alot of flavor and the whole dish came together rather quickly..  It does have alittle kick to it as far as spice goes but my 8 yr.old handled it just fine.  Thankyou!!

It was very good.  I used half of the red pepper flakes, cayenne pepper and black pepper.  It was still plenty hot enough.  Next time I will use only half of the thyme.  It seemed to overpower.  I used Killian's Red and tossed the shrimp with flour first.

this recipe wasn't bad, but i didn't find it to be great either. the first couple shrimp were pretty tasty, but it just ended up being way too overpowering for our tastes. i think the concentrated mixture of so many dried herbs in the shrimp (which are already naturally salty) was too much. thanks for the recipe, but we probably won't be making it again...

A LOVELY dish! Quite spicy, even when served over rice, but I found it incredible. My future DH wasn't able to finish his portion due to the heat of the herbs, but that only meant more for me! If you enjoy foods with a bit of temperature, you're sure to appreciate this recipe.

This was so good, and easy to make! Since I wasn't too concerned at the time with being healthy, after all when you're going to enjoy something you should do it right, I used 7 TBSP of butter! Also, at the end after reducing the sauce with the beer, I added a little half&half to make it creamy (bf likes creamy foods). We ate it with garlic bread and salad! Thanks again!!
Great tasting shrimp!  They are very spicy.  I did decrease the cayenne and red pepper flakes by half.  Thanks for posting this recipe.

The neighbors gathered for "Shrimp Night" and I brought this.  I cooked it at home and brought it in the crockpot.  It never made it to dinnertime because everyone dug into it early.  I followed the recipe except for decreasing the cayenne and red pepper for personal tastes.  Good one, EdsGirlAngie.

I thought I liked spicy things but WOW.  I doubled the recipe but should not have doubled the cayenne.  Otherwise it would've been excellent.  I might've gone heavier on garlic too, in place of the hot spices. Will try it again!

Yum! My husband loves shrimp and this recipe delivers on flavor. We cut back (1/2) on the cayenne and used 3 large cloves of fresh crushed garlic and still thought it had just enough spice, but not overpowering.

This recipe is similar to one of my favorite shrimp recipes (Recipe #391721). Except my recipe has slightly different ingredients, using white wine instead of beer. I had to try this beer recipe and it was great. I can now use beer when I am out of white wine in my recipe because this Butter-Beer Sauce is just as good.
Super easy to prepare.  I will say it is really hot... so hot that you loose the flavor of the other spices, so I am definately going to cut the cayenne to 1/2 teaspoon at the most.

This gets 5 stars for two reasons - one is its simplicity and two is the flavor. I actually added a smidge more cayenne and red pepper flakes because we love HOT HOT HOT, nose running hot. :-) It was great for a fast meal on a Wednesday evening. I served over rice for my husband, but smashed cauliflower for me, as I'm low-carbing.
This is so good.  I'm a huge shrimp fan and this recipe is fantastic.  I served this with rice pilaf and steamed broccoli.  Thank you for sharing this recipe with us.

Awesome! I loved this! It reminded me of a spiced shrimp I've had on the coast of North Carolina. Wonderfully delicious and easy too!  I served it with Jasmine rice and some stir fried zucchini. Note: I dusted the raw shrimp with some cornstarch to thicken the sauce a bit. I have to modify the heat for my household.

Disappointed with the heat of the recipe...if you do not like too much heat, then halve the red pepper flakes...we left out the cayenne pepper and it was so hot, we could not finish the meal.  It is easier to add than to take away...that is why we only gave it a 3 stars...the flavor is delightful!  Wish we could have finished it, but we were too busy using our handkerchiefs during the whole meal.  My suggestion is to use a whole bottle of beer when you dredge the shrimp in flour...otherwise, it will be extremely thick.

I really enjoyed this recipe. I had to cut back on the cayenne pepper by half when i made it for the first time because I knew it would be a bit much.  Made this with pasta and broccoli... Very Yum!! Will definitely make again.

Awesome recipe.  I think I will hold back just a tad of the red pepper flakes next time I make it.  But I am not complaining at all.  Just prefer a little less heat.  This was so easy it should not have tasted this good.  I am sending the reciepe to my son in college.  I have introduced him to this web site and he loves it. My husband told me he wished he discovered this receipe first so he could brag.  Great recipe.
For my DH it was 5 stars!  He loved it!  For the family...it was too spicy!  I will have to tone it down next time!  I loved it also!!!  Thanks for a great shrimp recipe!
Just made for my mom and I for dinner.  We both enjoyed it.  I added some stirfry vegetables and we had it over angel hair pasta.  This goes in our keeper pile!  Thanks!!

I doubled the sauce recipe like some suggested and it was too much on the herbs. It was almost like chewing on weeds. Plus I left out the cayenne but used the pepper flakes since I am cooking for toddlers. I am not rating cause I didn't follow the recipe but I don't think I will try this again either way.

Delicious! I added broccoli & whole wheat linguine and omitted the cayenne and used 1/4 c. beer.  A restaurant quality dish! Some flour or cornstarch to thicken the sauce would have made it even better.

This was a very good. I doubled the broth components, as suggested by another member and left out the cayenne because I have small children. I'll be making this the next time I need an appetizer. The flavor was fantastic.

Quote from my husband, "I would eat this again, anytime--this was excellent!".  We added very thinly sliced bell pepper and some diced fresh roma tomatoes for the veggie factor--served over noodles.  Really good--spicier than I thought it would be but we like spice.

Very good. As advised, I doubled the sauce and served over whole wheat angel hair with chopped steamed asparagus then topped with parmesan cheese.  Add a salad and you've got yourself a healthy meal that tastes awesome.  Thanks for the recipe

We love this! I don't like my food as hot, so I lightened up on the cayenne pepper. As someone recommended we did it tossed in Alfredo over linguine noodles. This is one of our favorites and I wonder sometimes if my BF isn't with me just for this sometimes : )

I read some reviews first and followed some advice- double the sauce, but I didn't double the cayenne. OMG! We will be adding this to our regular rounds of dinner. So good- everyone loved it and it was seriously delish! I served it over pasta with some ceasar salad and crusty bread and we all wished there was more when we finished. Seriously good and considering how fast it came together and how easy it was- this is a huge winner in my books! THanks for a great recipe!

Neither one of us really liked this. Other than omitting the cayenne pepper, I made just as posted. I couldn't put my finger on what was wrong, but my son said he thought there were too many herbs and spices competing with each other and nobody was winning that contest.  I ended up rinsing off my shrimp to finish dinner.

I hesitated to make this as some of the reviews indicated that the taste wasn't quite right, and with the variety of herbs and spices, this made some sense to me.  But other reviews raved, so I figured I'd give it a shot.  I am so glad I did.  This was a big hit at dinner tonight!  The only thing I changed was to omit the crushed red pepper and give people the option of adding it at the table.  The flavor was just right and nobody used any of the red pepper I'd set out.  It was quick and unique and I will definitely make this again!  Thanks for sharing!
This has been a hit every time I've made it.  It goes well at pot lucks and parties.  It's very easy to make.
Disappointing to say the least.  The cayenne overpowered the flavor of the shrimp.  This won't be made again.

This recipe is delicious, I have made this 5 times now.
The amount of cayenne pepper in the recipe does make it quite hot so the last time I made this I substituted cajun instead of cayenne and it was perfect.
I also cut down the time of making this recipe by using 1 &1/2 teaspoons of garlic powder instead of chopping garlic, I found no difference.
Tossed with linguini noodles is the best!
I also double the recipe as the original does not make much.
Made this recipe for my family>>>>they love it!!!!! everybody came for seconds and some for thirds>>>>> Also try the bullalo Shrimp they were killer as well.
This was good just served with French bread to mop up the sauce, but I have a feeling it would be very good served over pasta or rice.    Super simple to make.

I made half the recipe.  I used 2 garlic cloves.  I omitted the cayenne pepper, salt and pepper.  But used the spices mentionned.  The spices were perfect with the shrimps.  And we used bread to dip in the liquid.  It was like having garlic butter bread.  Thanks Eds :)  Made for Holiday tag game
The recipe was excellent! I doubled the sauce. However, I only gave it 4 stars because it is SO hot! Next time I make it I will halve the cayenne pepper. Otherwise it was great.

So GOOD!!!! I cut back the cayenne pepper to 1/4 tsp. and it was perfect for us. We really enjoyed this. This recipe will be used often when I make shrimp. We try to have it once a month. And, I will make sure I have the french bread for dipping next time. Thanks EdsGirlAngie for this great recipe.
quick, easy, tasty!
very good but, for me, too spicy with the full suggested dose of cayenne.  Cleared the sinuses nicely.  very quick and easy to make, will do again (will a bit less kick!)

Immediately after finishing his dinner my husband said "I'm excited to have this again for dinner sometime."  So you can bet we'll be having this again!  LOL.  We like spicy food but 1 tsp seemed a little insane to me; I reduced it to 1/2 tsp and it was the perfect amount of heat for us.  (I kept the crushed red pepper at 1/2 tsp.)  I used unsalted butter and 1/2 tsp kosher salt and it was PLENTY salty; if I only had regular butter on hand, I'd reduce the amount of extra salt.  My husband said it reminded him of a dish they served at a restaurant where he used to work.  I served with plain, steamed broccoli (I put it on the same plate so it got some flavor by the sauce) and one loaf of French bread.  Quick, easy, and delish!
Reduced Cayenne to 1/4 tsp and red pepper to 1/2 tsp and it was still pretty spicy, but very good.

Dear sweet lord this was incredible. Followed advice and doubled the butter beer sauce and we finished off 2 whole loaves of bread sopping it up. I used peeled and pre-cooked shrimp for simplicity but the ended up overcooked since, duh, they were cooked already and I threw them in hot butter sauce for awhile. Plus the sauce tastes best warm so I'd really suggest using raw shrimp for this.

Could eat this every day! Even the neighbor's kid comes a-runnin lol!!!!!!!!!!!!

I do double the sauce and go easy on the cayenne for kids, serve with lots of French bread to sop up that delish sauce and salad :)
I only added a dash of cayenne and omitted the crushed red pepper, I just personal preference.  Very good flavor, nice blend of spices.
Made half a recipe for the two of us and was great.  A little spicy but great.  Left out the cayenne and added cajun, no beer so used white wine.  Served with sourdough bread and roasted garlic.
Great spice combo!  Reminds me of New Orleans.  I served it over angel hair pasta.... perfecto!  Thanks for the great recipe~
This dish was prepared by our daughter for New Years Dinner and I believe she followed the recipe as is and it was spectacular.  Will be making again for sure
Made this for dinner last night, my boyfriend loved it! We doubled the 'sauce' componant since he's crazy about sauce. It was great.

A very nice and easy recipe. I cut way down on the cayenne, just used the pepper flakes. I admit to adding some cream to the sauce, to increase it (I should have read the reviews first), and also to cut down on the heat (find for me but not for DH!). I should also add that fresh prawns/shrimps seldom get peeled here in the southern parts of Africa -- we prefer it shell on. Thanks!

I made this last night served over brown rice.  By following others, I doubled the sauce recipe, and should have served it over pasta.  I added extra garlic, as we like to actually be able to taste the garlic, especially in a butter sauce with shrimp!<br/><br/>I have to agree with others here, it was smelling AWESOME until the beer.  I removed the shrimp while trying to simmer for "another minute" after adding the beer.  I was quite worried they would over cook and become rubbery.  I'm glad I did, because the 'sauce' was way too thin, and I had to thicken it with just a bit of cornstarch.  <br/><br/>Overall, a great tasting dish, with my additions.....

We really liked this but I did make some changes. With reading the other reviews I did double the sauce but wasn't sure if I really needed too. I used Italian seasoning instead of oregano, basil and thyme as that is all I had. I also used old bay instead of the cayenne and red pepper flakes. I forgot to double the salt and pepper. I ate some on brown rice but everyone else ate them plain. We all really enjoyed these with the changes made.

Loved this!   Made exactly as written except I did cut down on both the cayenne and the crushed red pepper.  I used 3/4 lb of shrimp because there were only 2 of us but kept the rest the same so we'd have lots of that delicious juice.  Dumped it over bowtie noodles with steamed broccoli as the veg.   Quick, easy and delicious.

Delicious, favorite part was the sauce!!! I cut back a little on the heat and served it over egg noodles. Hubby was not a fan of the dried herbs so, I will make it with ground herbs next time. And I agree, make extra sauce, you will be so glad you did!

To start with, I do not eat shrimp. So why make this recipe? Well, when I read the ingredients for the sauce DH said that it would be nice to try with codfish. OK, tried that and it was a hit. Made just as stated (with the codfish instead of shrimp) with the exception of, as another reviewer suggested, decreasing the cayenne pepper to just 1/4 teaspoon and it was plenty. Next time I will also decrease the thyme to 3/4 teaspoon as it was a little overpowering. We had enough sauce to save for the next day when we tossed it with spaghetti. Delicious! Thanks for posting.
Love the shrimp. So good. I made it with a creamy tomato pasta. My hubby loved it. But be careful can get really spicy.

This is really tasty and really easy to make. I doubled the sauce but kept all ingredients as stated.  I did not find it too spicy nor did my kids.  Will definitely make again when splurging on a buttery recipe.
Forgot to add the 5 stars!!
So good!  I didn't have cayenne pepper so I substituted red pepper - I was still delicious.
I like hot food but this was really hot and I only used half a teaspoon of cayenne.  Next time I would omit the cayenne entirely and let the red pepper flakes alone provide the heat.

I love this recipe. It has become a staple whenever we have company at the holidays. I sometimes adjust the amount of hot sauce depending upon who will be eating it. Thank you so much for posting this recipe for others to enjoy

I have made this twice now (made a video of the second) and the family likes it. Little spicy the first time, cut back on the hot stuff for the kids. We our ours over spaghetti for a different style shrimp pasta.
Linda, this is an excellent way to make roast.  I've been doing it for years, at my friend Sarah's suggestion, and it is a guaranteed winner.  Thanks for posting it for everyone.

Oh my goodness!!! This is the best way to cook a roast. We used an english roast. It tasted just like prime rib. My husband would not shut up about how good it was. Simple recipe!!! Rave reviews from ages 2 to 41, in my house.

I made a Roast Beef dinner for my family on Sunday, and used this amazing recipe.  Linda, you certainly DO know HOW to cook a roast with this recipe!  I never had such a devine roast in my life.  Done perfectly at 14 minutes, as we like it rare.  Worked out perfectly for all of us, as the ends were cooked enough for my DH.  He gave the roast 8 fingers and 2 thumbs up, and with a huge smile on his face!  I will never cook roast any other way from now on.  This is a foolproof recipe, and will work for anyone.  Much thanks goes out to Linda's Busy Kitchen, for showing me how to get my roast from the oven to the table in a timely fashion, with great flavor, and cooked PERFECTLY!  Kudos to you girl!

Perfect! This is an outstanding recipe! It came out just the way we like it.  I am thrilled to finally be able to make our roast perfectly medium rare all the way through.  The directions were easy to read, and if followed, you can't fail with this one. Merci Linda!

This recipe is absolutely PERFECT!!! For all the years I have been cooking making the perfect med. rare roast beef has been a challenge, no more!
Thank you for sharing your mothers recipe, my husband and I enjoyed the roast I made today very much.
Can't say enough about how good our Sunday dinner was.
Thank you again Linda's Busy Kitchen!

AWESOME! We had a 2.75 lb roast - wasn't sure what to do with the timing. I roasted at 500 for 15 minutes, turned the oven off and roasted for another 34 minutes - deciding it was better to be too rare than too done.  It was a little rare for dh - perfect for me. Thank you!

I made this for the main dish for our Christmas dinner, and it was perfect!  I cooked my roast 15 mins. per lb. and it came out tender and full of flavor! The only thing I did different was to insert cloves of garlic into the roast before baking.   Excellent recipe Linda, and one I will be using often in the future! Thanks so much! Jenn

Simple and easy, just like I like it.  AWESOME recipe and one that will be my choice from now on.  Doesn't get any better than this.  Great new way to cook my roast. Loved it!  Thanks so much to Linda for sharing it with us.

This roast beef was the bomb.  We used bottom round which is the same as rump roast.  It tasted wonderful.  Cooked just like she said to.  One comment is there a suggestion how we can get some of the meat just a little more done. This is for people who like rare to medium rare roast beef, but it is perfect. The taste is excellent with a little horseradish, Aujus or with out. super easy to make.

i have no idea what i did wrong but i had a 2 1/2 pound roast and cooked it for 18 minutes at 500 shut the oven off and cooked it for 38 minutes and it was very rare so much so that nobody wanted to eat it i had to put pieces in the microwave to finish cooking. I am very dissapointed! EDIT: I needed to edit this review because I think my boyfriend overreacted about the doneness of the roast. My brother thought it was perfect and when I tasted it I did too!! I think maybe my boyfriend likes his meat cooked a little more but when he tried a piece of the roast he liked it too..so sorry about that bad review, I should have waited. It was the perfect roast afterall!!

This was just perfect.  This is the only cut of meat that we like well done.  Mine turned out exactly how I wanted it.  Served this with your recipe #52267 gravy and carrots.  Just such comfort food.  Thanks Linda
I omitted the onion but we put onion flakes on the roast beef and garlic powder.  It's delicious and we had it medium.  Thanks Linda :)  Made for Zaar Star Game.

This was cooked to perfection, but I was very disapointed when I bit into my flavorful, cooked to perfection roast beef and it was as tough as shoe leather.  This was not the recipes fault by any means but I got a lousy roast.  I can't wait to try this again with a better cut of meat....

I will not review this recipe this time as I think my cut of meat, an eye of round was maybe to big or thick but it came out too rare, really almost raw.  I cooked it at 500 for 18 minutes and left it in the oven for 45 min. on off.  I think next time, I will leave it in at 500 for about 25-30 minutes and then leave it in the oven for 1 hour.  I want to try this again as the outside looked great and the onions were very crispy and yummy. Thanks for the recipe I will try it again with some adjustments and then review again.

We had company this weekend and I made this roast.  It was a 5 lb. roast.  I baked it at 500  for 15 minutes then turned it off and let sit for 1 hr 15 minutes.  It came out perfectly med-rare.  I let it sit out on the counter until it was room temperature, and I think this is the key to this roast coming out perfectly.  If I hadn't done that, I think it would have been very rare.  Thanks so much for adding that "Key" information into the recipe Linda!  Everyone really loved this roast and it made a splendid gravy!  This is how I am going to do my roasts from now on!  Perfect recipe!  Alexa
I have been cooking for over 20 years and could never make a good eye round roast. OMG!!! Thank you soooo much!!!!! Perfect all the way through.

I have made this at least 10 times now and just have to say this roast comes out perfect every time.  Just follow the directions and it will be perfect for you too!  Excellent way to fix a roast.  We all love it here Linda. Makes a luscious gravy too! I'm not going to waste my time looking for more recipes when this simple recipe works so well.  Thanks Linda ~  Ann

I have made this roast several times now and each time it has come out GREAT!  Make sure you use a pan without high sides, so the roast gets nice and brown all over.
