Easy and delicious, but not as crispy as hoped...maybe I was impatient and didn't preheat long enough. I substituted smoked paprika for the cayenne and it was delish, plus gave the bird a lovely color. Will be trying again, maybe with rosemary in the cavity as well as lemon
DELICIOUS!  One of my families' favorites.  I use olive oil instead of butter.  Been cooking this recipe for 5 yrs now!
My family loved it.  I put carrots and potatoes in the pan and stuffed the cavity with an onion.  Super moist.

Tonight was my 1st roasted chicken...it REALLY turned out just like the photos, and WAS as delicious as the previous ratings here claim! I read many, gleaned some tips and would like to add some of my own because all together, they worked GREAT! <br/>I used room temperature/softened butter and added all the other ingredients (except the whole onion), then whisked it all into a creamy "seasoning paste" which in one step I rubbed inside/outside & under the skin. I stuffed a big onion inside, added about 1 cup water to my favorite oven-safe pan (didn't add a rack, either), baked uncovered at 475 for 15 min, flipped the bird and did 15 more minutes at 475, then reduced the heat to 400 and just cooked it till the meat temp registered 165. I thick cut potatoes and carrots a little late to cook with the bird so while the bird was removed/rested for the 15 minutes, the vegetables were added and roasted at 400 in the same pan along with the drippings. By the time the chicken was ready to serve, so were the vegetables. My son wolfed his down (white meat and all!) while I savored every bite without first adding a mandatory thick layer of BBQ sauce-both unheard of at our house before this recipe! I sure recommend trying it, IT IS absolutely delicious!

This chicken was pretty fantastic, moist and juicy. Delicious! Easy to make and fast. No need to slow roast for 5 hours to get a juicy rotisserie style chicken. Wasn't sure about the whole lemon in the cavity of the chicken, but totally worth it, it adds great lemony flavor. Added 10 minutes to each section as my chicken was 4 1/2 pounds total, was just right.
Must try. Delicious and easy.
This was the most amazing roasted chicken EVER!!  It was so moist and flavorful!!  I don't think I'll be able to roast a chicken any other way again.  Two words... "No Leftovers!"
Tasty.  Easy and SO much more flavor that grocery store rotisserie chicken.  Thanks and You!

I don't know where you get all these good recipes, however, if you have one that is what I am looking for it's the one to use!  I enjoy cooking and have been doing it for a long time now. <br/>This recipe is no exception.  Thank you so much for sharing with all of us.

This is a great recipe. I switch up the spices to suit our mood. Just made a 4 lb bird. I like to season the bird and let it sit at room temp for 3-4 hours before cooking. This most recent time, rinsed and patted dry, seasoned the interior with Emeril Essence (Google the recipe, we go through a bottle a month of this DIY all purpose seasoning). I zested a lemon, and chopped some fresh thyme, rosemary, and sage, mixed with olive oil and more Emeril Essence, Then brushed that mixture on the outside of the bird. I tied a small bundle of rosemary, thyme, and sage and inserted into the body cavity, then inserted a few peeled cloves of garlic and a halved lemon with the ends trimmed off. I lined the bottom of the roasting pan with cubed carrots, parsnips, sweet onions, diced celery, and diced rutabaga (under the bird, over the baking rack so the veggies don't soak up too much oil. Did the 20 minutes/450 degrees - 40minutes/400degrees roast method. While the bird rested, we made pan gravy with the drippings. Delicious!

Very good! will definitely be eating this again,next time I'm not going to cook it so long ,my chicken was small and the breast started to get dry.I did the 20 mins on 450 ,lowered it and cooked for 40 mins on 400.used 1 tsp salt,1 tsp paprika,1 tsp garlic powder and the pepper.Instead of lemon because I didn't have any, I used 1 Tbsp Balsamic vinegar ,cut the whole chicken in half and laid it flat.The skin was tasty and crispy.My husband enjoyed it also  I served it with pasta salad.
I don't use any other recipe for whole chicken.  I've been using this recipe for years with the help of Kittencal.  She is a lifesaver and I've never had a bad dish using her expert cooking advice.
Thank you Kittencalskitchen! I enjoyed making this recipe for my husband and son, easy to make and moist.
This was SO easy and amazing.  The seasoning is JUST right and my family loved, loved, loved it.  Thank you so much!
Love this recipe.  So easy!  This is the only way I do whole chicken.  Great for soup too.
This was the best roasted chicken I have ever made , my daughter loved it. Will use over and over again. I followed the directions just as written, came out perfect, was easy to make.

I just realized I haven't rated this yet.  I've made it several times and it has never failed.  I use the carcass to make Kittencal's Best Chicken Stock Broth.  Cook a 5 pound chicken in under 2 hours.

I make a lot of chicken, but looked up recipes this afternoon, always looking for new things or ways to improve.  I tried out this recipe tonight.  Oh my holy heavens, it was superbly wonderful (no joke).  It's the high heat technique.  I did not use lemon, but otherwise followed the formula.  Fantastic.  Couldn't be easier or tastier.  Thank you for posting this recipe, and upping my chicken game. :)
This was incredible! And a huge hit with my 4-year old
Simple but excellent. High temp really does make crisp and tender. I did brine a couple of hours, probably helped, certainly didn't hurt. Had to cover with foil last 20 min to prevent burnt skin..

Incredibly tasty and unbelievably easy! Was making dinner for my mother and she almost forbid me from buying a whole chicken at the grocery store because she was so sure that I would mess it up. Luckily I insisted and had this incredible recipe on my side. Chicken was moist, flavorful, and delicious. Can't wait to make it for the boyfriend!

Put an orange and a lemon (after using the lemon juice in the marinate) in the cavity. My chicken was 6.5 lbs. I basted after 30 mins and added potatoes and carrots for the last hour. Also put tarragon in the cavity with the fruit. My oven doesn't get hotter than 450 so I cooked the large bird a bit longer.
Best whole chicken recipe ever! Fast too! No changes to the recipe, I've made several times and am always pleased.
The skin was so good.
Didn't have lemons, but this is going to happen again and again. Yum!This little $5.00 chicken was juicy inside, crispy outside. Hubby was impressed!

What a fantastic chicken! I just ate nearly half the 3.35 lb. bird all by myself. (Oink.) I used a meyer lemon and when I got to the breast meat near the cavity of the chicken, the cooked lemon rind took on a flavor that was so unexpectedly delicious in the meat! Thanks so very much for the recipe, Kitten! It's going to join the rest of my favorites and will be passed along for others to enjoy!

I doubled this recipe.  It was so yummy!  I did not use the fresh parsley, as I do not like it. Such an easy, delicious side dish.  I served this with steamed asparagus and mustard-garlic glazed salmon.  It all went together really well.   The two people I made this for thought it was fabulous!!! And it really was.  I will definately be making this all the time.

I wish I could give this TEN stars! It was outrageously good. I hope my picture does them justice, because my family went wild over them.  We will be making these often since they are so easy and delicious! I added a little sprinkling of Herbs de Provence and it is an understatement that these were TO DIE FOR! Thank you for this recipe. :)

I must agree with the others,these were SO yummy... and talk about easy to throw together! I was a little leary about the dijon mustard but it was wonderful! I didn't have any fresh parsley so I used a little dried, other than that followed the recipe exactly. My husband loved them and proclaimed them the best part of the meal! Thanks Kittencal these will be made over and over again!
Wonderful, different way to prepare roasted potatoes. The onions in them were especially delicious. Thanks!
My family and I thought these potatoes were some of the best we have ever had. Totally loved the mustard sauce. Will be a regular at my house. Thanks.

Easy and delicious!  Especially the onions.  Although I greased the pan before throwing the mixture in, it did stick a bit but that was okay, it wasn't for company!  Potatoes browned nicely...I stirred them a couple of times so they would brown evenly.  Thanks for a new potato dish, Kittencal!
M&Mers
"Out of this world"

Not the "prettiest" side-dish but it sure is tasty! Its also good for a weeknight since you can basically forget about it while you prepare your protein dish. The recipe didn't indicate peeling the potatoes so I opted to leave the skins on; I stirred them several times while baking. Thanx Carol!
woohoo! Served these with baked beans. DH mixed them together.  This recipe is now on the regular menu rotation.  Thanks!

These potatoes were quite honestly some of the best I have tasted.  Easy to put together with excellent results. They browned beautifully and had a wonderful flavour.  I will make these again, often!  Thanks!

I opted not to grease the pan after reading some of the reviews about the them sticking and frequent turning was required. Instead I used non-stick foil, so I didn't have the browning that others did, but if I cared too I could have popped them under the broiler. My eldest DS was bummed, he had 2 helpings and wanted a 3rd serving, but I wanted to bring some leftovers to my MIL..
Thanks a bunch again Carol!

We loved these potatoes! I halved the recipe and used parchment paper (my new best friend). They browned up beautifully! As others have said, I agree it is one of the best potato recipes I have tried......a definite keeper!
Thanks Kittencal!
These were very good! Five stars - I'll be making them again! I only had about 1/8 cup of olive oil, but that didn't seem to cause any problems and these cooked perfectly!
Another great recipe by Kittencal!  These made a wonderful side dish to go with our steak tonight. I love the dijon and honey flavors together.  Yummy!

These were delicous!! The flavor was wonderful and my family wolfed these right down!!
The only change I made was to add a little extra honey and onion. They were perfectly browned, didn't stick and just plain good! This recipe is  going right into my favorites cookbook. Thanks kittencal!!

What a wonderful flavor. It took a few bits for it to really grow on you. I took the advice of another reviewer and added Herbs de Provence. Came out excellent. Will be making this again. Thanks for posting Kittencal.
I cut these potatoes into slices,and just for the record used two russet potatoes and half an onion.  Otherwise, everything exactly as stated.  Turned out great, will definitely make again.

Perfect ! easy and yummy :D
i only used 1/8 olive oil,oh! now that i'm reading, i realize that i forgot the parsley ... grr.
I used real dijon mustard and "moutarde a l'ancienne" with mustard seeds =)

Totally awesome !!! These have become our favorite potatoes.  Very easy to make.  Followed recipe exactly and they are to die for.  Also tried them with Sweet Potatoes (not yams)for a healthier substitute to regular potatoes along with a pinch of cayenne pepper instead of the black pepper.  Also sprinkled a bit of ground flaxmeal for that healthy touch and they were very good too, however I myself prefer the regular potatoes. Thanks for the yummy keeper recipe.
Great side dish - easy to make, uses staple items, and the family loved it - who could ask for more??

I gave this 4 stars. My 4 yrs old newphew and I had this for dinner tonight. He didn't like it but I thought it was good. I ran out of dijon mustard so I had to use 3 tbl. yellow mustard. I forgot to add the parsley. Mine took 40 minutes to bake. I think next time I'll try the grainy mustard and some more seasonings. Thanks for posting a good recipe! Christine (internetnut)
Thanks for posting another great way to roast potatoes -- we liked this and it was especially good with whole grain mustard.  Thanks.

Made this tonight and served it with ham.  It was very good.  I doubled the recipe and baked it in a 15x10 Pyrex baking dish sprayed with PAM. Stirred the potatoes twice while baking. Potatoes were tender in about 45 minutes.
Nice and tangy!  Easy!  Even better reheated!  thanks!
I loved these!  Unfortunately, they weren't a big hit with my family---a little too much mustard for them.  I'll probably make it again in the hope that it will grow on them!
Thanks to you Kittencal, I'm a hero! Everyone at our birthday bash gobbled up these spuds in a flash.I did not adjust a thing and... perfecto.
This recipe was okay, I think something is missing, but I am not sure what!
Another winner from Kitten. My fussy hubby took one bite, moaned in delight and said 5 stars. Nuff said.

These were delicious. As far as flavor goes this is a definite five star. The only reason why I'm not giving it the full five stars is because the onions did not cook at the same rate as the potatoes so they still were kind of crunchy instead of nice and soft the way they are when I fry them up over a low flame for a good long time. Next time (there will be a next time for sure) I will fry the onions first and then add them to the potatoes. Yummy!

I really liked these - I thought it tasted like warm potato salad.  Maybe I will add bacon next time.  I think all of your recipes are delightful.  Hubby said they were "different", but what do men know?

This was a big hit. I was able to adapt it for my diabetic family by leaving out the honey and using honey mustard instead of dijon.  We also used a big sweet onion instead of a small one. I used Idaho potaoes since red or white wasn't specified. So yummy!
These had a nice flavor, but I don't think I quite added enough salt to them.  When I make these again, I'm planning to add in a bit of garlic and top with bacon as another reviewer suggested.

Considering my husband isn't a fan of the potato, and he had SECONDS of this, I'd consider this recipe a keeper!  I doubled the sauce and made a little extra potato.  Next time I might add a little extra salt and maybe a little garlic. Thanks!
NIce potato recipe. I doubled the sauce and it cooked nicely. I might try adding garlic next time. My dh really enjoyed it. Thanks for posting.

Ok, what I need to do is stay away from potato recipes that have Kittencal as the contributor, because it seems I cannot stop eating the potato recipes of yours that I have tried.  I made this recipe earlier in the day to serve at room temp later in the day, and bad news for everyone else because I am sure there will not be that many left.  Delicious, easy and man does my house smell fantastic!  Thanks for another winner of a recipe!
Goo-ood!  Smelled great baking too.  I cut WAY back on the olive oil (I maybe put a tablespoon in there) and it was great.  Served with a pork tenderloin.  Good stuff!

These were great. Wish there was a bit more flavor to it- we used stone ground mustard instead of Dijon. I will likely make this again, maybe adding a bit of heat to it or a splash of soy sauce or balsamic vinegar. Yum.

I loved the flavor of these.  However, my DH said he thought they were just O.K. and would have been better without the onions.  I loved them just the way they were.  I sliced the onions nice and thin and cooked it for about 40 - 45 minutes or until the onions had started to carmelize a little.  That was my favorite part!  Thanks Kitten for another great recipe!
I made this dish as an alternative to potato kugel - what a nice & refreshing change with the added bonus of being half the work!  Thanks - will definitely make this again real soon!!

I was a bit worried about the onion because I don't like onions with any sort of 'rawness' to them.  I sliced them really thin and when it came time to taste the final dish I actually really enjoyed the onions mixed with the honey Dijon sauce.  So, for me to actually pick out onions as something I particularly liked about a dish is a victory alone because I am the one usually picking them out of a dish.  The recipe as a whole was very easy to put together and as somebody that only cooks for two it was so nice to have this recipe be for two so I didn't have to scale down a recipe for a change.  I served this with some pork chops and it was a great pairing.  Made for Cookbook Tag.
Hubby said these were the best potatoes I've made, which is saying alot because I've tried MANY potatoe recipes.  These were my 2nd or 3rd favourite:)

I really enjoyed these, Kittencal! The only thing I'll do differently next time is to add more mustard as the Dijon flavor really mellows out as the potatoes roast--I prefer a sharper flavor. Had no onions but a sprinkling of onion powder made this recipe a treat to eat. Thanks for posting!

These have a good taste and are very easy to make! I used regular yellow mustard instead of the Dijon mustard. I will try it the next time with the Dijon to see if it makes a big difference in the finished taste! I used 4 tablespoons of honey instead of 2! I added 4 drops of hot sauce at the beginning of cooking, I did these on the stove top rather than in the oven, it took the same amount of time, either way it will work.

This was good, but I wasn't a huge fan of the onions. Next time I'd probably use a full TBSP of honey, and cut down on the salt (I used about a tsp, too much!). But overall it was super easy to make and pretty tasty. Thanks Kitten!

I didn't enjoy these at all.  I was very disappointed since I have enjoyed most of Kittencal's recipes.  These had no zest that I thought the mustard would bring & the flavor of the potato disappeared.  I really don't know what I would have done different, but I think the sauce may have been better on a salad.  Sorry Kittencal.

Mmmm....Mmmmm....Mmmmm... Made your recipe on Friday evening to go along with supper after seeing the photo and reading the ingredients on Zaar the same day. I never changed or added anything extra and the potatoes turned out perfect and absolutely delicious. Gee, they're even good cold!!! As I am watching my fat intake and calories hubby got to eat most of them, while I just had a sampling. There was enough left over for him to have this morning along with scrambled eggs. Will definitely be adding this one to my "all time favorites" cookbook. Thanks for sharing.

This recipe was waaaay too sweet for my taste. I added salt and garlic powder, but it was still too sweet. Then I put some ketchup on top to see if it tasted better that way, and it was good in small amounts (1/4 cup or so at a time). Sorry Kittencal. I am hoping that your garlic buns are better.

I liked these potatoes very much - they went great with brats on the grill. I made the sauce a few hours before dinner since I knew I'd be short on prep time. I love how the dijon turns the potatoes sweet and the everything was done just right after 45 minutes. DH hates mustard, but he enjoys these potatoes anyway.

I had a bit of difficulty with this because I doubled the recipe and then tried to use a pan that was too small. I ended up moving the potatoes to a half-sheet and cooking them again (I think for the full amount of time) after the rest of dinner was done. Oops. I thought the flavor was really good, though, and I will certainly make them again. I also neglected to add any parsley because by the time they were cooked I was the only one still interested anyway. I served these with Recipe #335534 and Pan-Roasted Broccoli With Lemon Browned Butter.
Really good.  I'll definitely make this again.  I used red potatoes and left the skin on and they turned out pretty and flavorful.

I thought this recipe was great! Very simple and very tasty. I thought the amount of mustard might be overpowering but it really mellowed. The onions were nice and creamy and it all tasted great! This is the second recipe I have tried and LOVED from you. Thanks!

So simple and delicious!  I used 3 lbs. of potatoes to serve 6-8, but just doubled the sauce ingredients and it came out great.
Thanks for sharing the recipe.
Easy and very good!
Yum!  These are so good and so easy.  I let mine cook for about 40 minutes without stirring them.  Next time I would stir them halfway through.  Even slightly black on the bottom they were fabulous!

Wow!  Not sure I can add much that hasn't already been said, wonderful flavor....I think I have a new favorite roasted potatoes recipe :)  I doubled the recipe and added 1/2 tsp garlic powder to the mix.  I also stirring halfway through and didn't have any trouble with them sticking.  Thanks for sharing!

These were average.  I thought they were a little bland and needed something else.  I even used garlic powder.  I didn't use enough onions which would have helped, I think.  I was a little concerned about them having too strong of a mustard taste, since my kids don't like mustard, but they didn't at all.  The kids liked them with ketchup.  I'm not sure I will make these again as I have another roasted potato recipe I use all the time.  I was out of some of those ingredients, so that is why I tried this one.  This is not bad by any means, but nothing that screams "make me often."  Thanks for your many wonderful recipes.
I agree...these were just average.

I don't know if it was the recipe, my potatoes, or my oven but I had to bake the dish for over an hour. I followed the directions exactly and the dijon taste was too strong so I added more honey. It was good but it wasn't the "greatest".
Good at dinner with a side of beef and veggies or breakfast with turkey bacon and eggs.
Very tasty!  The cooking time worked great for my oven, too.  Next time I may cut the amount of oil a bit, since they potatoes seemed overly oily.  Thanks!
The family was concerned because they weren't the normal potato dish but they turned out great!  We added a bit of garlic and topped with mozzarella cheese.

Kitt another wonderful side dish that we enjoyed! I used yukon gold potatoes and doubled them so we would have leftovers. The honey mustard sauce is very good and tastes great on the potatoes. I added the potatoes to a zippered plastic bag then added the other ingredients. Tossed them around a bit in the bag then placed on a cookie sheet and baked for about 45 minutes. If you like honey mustard you will enjoy these a lot. Made and reviewed for KC's Grilling Tag Game.

What a great side.  I made these last night to go with some tuna patties and we loved these little gems.  The honey mustard is wonderful wit these potatoes (I would have never thought) and the thinly sliced onions is a bonus gem.  We loved them and will continue to make, Thank you so much for this lovely side.

We really liked these potatoes!  I made them last Sunday and had leftovers during the week.  I couldn't even imagine what they would taste like when I put them in the oven, but they turned out delicious!  Thanks for posting another winner Kittencal!

I am not surprised...another great recipe from Kittencalskitchen!  I liked these, they were definitely different.  I made these as a side dish to steak (used Kittencalskitchen recipe for marinade and tenderizer for pork or beef).  Between the honey in these potatoes and the honey in the marinade, I may have been on honey overload.  But, that has nothing to do with the recipe, again, both recipes from Kittencalskitchen were a hit with me.

These are amazing potatoes! My only issue was I used too many potatoes but forgot to increase the sauce. The 2nd time I made them I made sure to increase the sauce, because it's the best part! Really good with pork dishes.
Loved these and want them again already!

This was so yummy and easy! DH and I ate almost the whole casserole. I used a can of chopped chiles as suggested in the description.  I spread the chopped chiles on the bottom of the casserole and laid thick slices of monterey jack cheese on top of the chiles.  I then followed the recipe as instructed, pouring the egg mixture over top and sprinkled with mild cheddar cheese.  It cooked to a beautiful golden color and when spooned into, the monterey jack cheese oozed out, making your mouth water!  This has a quiche like texture and the chile flavor is mild, not overpowering.  I think it would make a great brunch idea! I will definitely repeat this and want to use whole chiles as in the recipe! Thanks Pvt Amys Mom!

This one is a keeper. I used fresh roasted poblano chiles, instead of canned chiles. So quick and easy not to mention tasty. I recommend serving them with black beans and mexican rice topped with cilantro...Wonderful.
this is a good dish for lent and its very warm and comforting thanks for posting dee

This is an excellent recipe.  I was suprised that the flavor of the chiles permeated the entire dish.  I stuffed the peppers with Chihuahua cheese and topped with a Mexican cheese blend.  Will definitely make this again and again.

I love this recipe and will definitely make it again.  The casserole puffed up beautifully!  We used 3 fresh poblano chiles, which I roasted just prior to putting the in dish.  I put a gravy boat of ranchero red (enchilada) sauce on the table, to be used instead of marinara, and I served oven-warmed flour tortillas and butter, and freshly made guacamole with the casserole.  Awesome meal!  Thanks!
Easy to make. We added seasoned groud beef for more flavor.

These were awsome!!  I used 6 fresh roasted pablano chilis and oaxaca cheese.  I upped the egg mixture by 1/2 and baked in a 9x12 dish and topped with a cheddar/jack combo.  I took the dish to our Easter BBQ along with some Mexican rice, where we served with carne asada and chicken.  The rellanos were the hit of the meal!  My BIL "volunteered" me to bring them next weekend to his daughter's BD party!  They were so easy, that I gladly agreed!  I have to say that I like these better than the traditional fried version!  Thank you so much for a recipe that I will be using over and over!!

These were super tasty!  I roasted 7 fresh hatch green chiles over the gas stovetop and I also used oaxaca cheese.  Left the batter measurments as-is and the cooking time was perfect!  These are better than the chile rellenos I make at home and waaay less work!  Topped with mexican blend shredded cheese.  Leftovers today for lunch- I can't wait- YUM!

I made this tonight for dinner and it was pretty good. The can of chilies only had 3 large ones, so I added a small can of diced chilies to the dish too. I didn't measure the cheese, I just eyeballed it. Next time I'll buy 2 cans of whole chilies. My guy and I typically don't eat a lot, but I found this made only 4 servings instead of 6. I'll be making this again and sharing my photo soon. Thanks!

So first, this was exactly the type of recipe I was looking for. I absolutely HATE, HATE, HATE to fry anything! And seeing how Relleno's are one of our most favorite Mexican foods, well you can see the conflict. I  was slightly off my game yesterday, so when I made this I totally spaced that I had 5 big poblano chilies. After following the recipe, there wasn't enough "batter" to cover my chilies. I made another 1/2 recipe, probably not really enough either. But in the oven they went. They stuck to my pan like a son of a gun. However, the flavor and texture was there! After thinking about this recipe I realized it is very similar to a breakfast item called a Dutch Baby. A crepe batter that is poured into a very hot pan with melted butter and baked until puffy and brown. A much wetter batter. So for me this recipe is a keeper. I love that you can have leftovers as my husband takes a lunch every day. I will be making quite often as I can now have a non-fried Relleno, hooorayyy!!!

I made chile rellenos from scratch in a tiny apartment kitchen in 1964. It seemed to take forever and I vowed "Never again" but I've been wanting to try one of these chile relleno casseroles. I chose this one, but used a 27 ounce can of whole chiles. Split them and took out the ribs and seeds, laid them in a 9x13 Pyrex buttered pan, put the jack cheese slices on and then another layer of the split chiles, then the batter and cheddar. I mixed the batter with a whisk as I didn't feel like getting out my electric mixer and that worked fine. Next time I will leave out the cheddar as the dish was a bit cheese intensive for me, and I might try separating the eggs and beating the whites to make a lighter, more traditional batter. These are really good with a little Tabasco Chipotle sauce on top. I made Spanish rice to go with it. Thanks for the recipe! It's so much easier than making them from scratch.

Excellent! But then we are cheeseheads.  LOL!    And so easy.  I beat my eggs while doing rest of recipe.  Mine was not runny.  There are only 3 whole chiles in pan so think there are more like 3 servings. Served ours with cornbread and a bit of Spanish rice.  Muchas  gracias for sharing.

I was going to make the regular  type rellenos but didnt want to use all that oil(most of which is either GMO or made from soemthing that isnt supposed to be used as cooking oil(either, or and)so I made these based on the amount of flour used in recipe as opposed to othewrs.I did add soem thin slices of tomato on top and threw in soem chopped red onions,I also used 8oz nuefatchel cheeseand mozzarella becuase thats what i had.and i didnt use as much as recipe called forI found this to be an excellent dish and am making it again 4 days later. I also used fresh poblano chiles roasted on the gas burners(5 large ones)so tell your motherr thasnk you it is muy bueno.

Love Grandmas who are good cooks!  This was savory comfort food.  I used a 2 pound chuck roast but kept all the other ingredients and the cooking time the same.  I didn't have any trouble with drying out.  The roast was fork tender and ooooooh, that onion gravy.  Soooo good.
This such a tender roast. And since I love onions, the gravy is the best!

The gravy with this roast is awesome.  However, it didn't seem to thicken as much as I would have liked.  After the roast was done, I poured the gravy into a saucepan and thickened with a bit of cornstarch.  This was a great comfort food for a dreary Sunday night.  The house smelled wonderful as it roasted.

This was quite good. The meat was a bit "beefy", and  the gravy had to be thickened on the stove. Still it's the first time I was able to cook a "cross-rib CHUCK roast" and have it edible. Hubby loved it as well. Next time I might cut the water a bit.
This was delicious! The gravy needed a bit more salt and next time I think I will cut the onion into chunks to get it to cook and be more tender. Will make this again, thanks!
This was the best ever...change nothing
This was an excellent recipe! Tasty, Tender,easy to fix. That is what it is all about.My compliments to the Grandma Chef. Michigan Shutterbug
I didn't care for the brown sugar in this. I couldn't taste that beefy flavor I'm used to in my gravies. I will try this again without the brown sugar.

I made this last evening and it was moist and very tender. I did not follow the recipe exactly but used 3/4 cup of Wondra in place of ap flour. My wife chopped the onion in the food processor when the meat was done and we put the gravy in a sauce pan and added 3 small cans of mushrooms heated it until the mushrooms were hot.

We love this recipe!!  I have made it several times and it comes out great each time.  My husband raves everytime I fix it.  Whats for dinner tonight? You guessed it! "Country Chuck Roast with onion Gravy".   I have passed this along to several friends and family.

MAJOR 5 STARS! But using my 'Southern girl' know how when it comes to working with flour I used all the ingredients while including my own method.. I had a 2 LB chuck roast that I rubbed down with the salt, pepper & brown sugar mixture and let sit for a half hour on the counter while I pre heated my oven to 300'. When my oven got a steady 300' I took out my dutch oven and on the stove top over medium heat added about 2 tablespoons olive oil in there till it got hot then browned my rubbed down chuck roast both sides.. & I mean BROWNED it.. crusted it... let the bits crust up in the bottom of the dutch oven without really burning it. Removed the roast... added the thickly sliced onion & reduced the heat slightly so the onion cooked down a bit without letting the onion burn. Added the half cup of flour to the onion and let the flour get hot though out while not letting it burn.I simmered up the 5 cups of water in a seperate sauce pan with one cube of beef bouillon. Once onion looked slightly softened I added the roast back into the dutch oven then added the 5 cups water simmered with the beef buillion. Added 2 cloves garlic chopped and a good splash soy sauce into the whole mix. Put the lid on the dutch oven, put the whole thing in the preheated 300' oven and let it cook for 3 hours.. perfect meat.. perfect gravy. Serve this with mashed potatoes.. or rice.. a crisp salad.. and some bread.. anything you would like to dip in gravy.. cause you'll have a good bit of it and the gravy is wonderful!

I baked mine in mini-muffin cups for about 18 minutes, could have probably taken them out a few minutes earlier.  Took them to a party, lots of rave reviews!

Wow! The recipe didn't look too exciting and I kind of laughed at the three tablespoons of chocolate chips, but I followed the recipe exactly, and these were FANTASTIC!  I read a review or two where sticking to the papers were a problem, but I used foil baking cups and sprayed them with a baking/flour spray and didn't have an issue at all.  Thank you for posting this!

Very good!! I even made them more healthy! I used sugar substitute for both the brown sugar and the regular sugar. I also used whole wheat flour. I did cheat a little and add some extra chocolate chips. I figured out with my changes each muffin only has about 100 calories! They are now a permanent addition to my diet snacks-so much better than those 100 calorie packs.

I have discovered my new favorite muffin! These are fantastic! Made them up last night and after tasting my first one...popped some in the freezer so I wouldn't finish off the entire batch in one sitting! Thanks for posting these tasty treats!!

These are tremendous muffins.  I wanted to do some commando baking (a large amount) so I used all my frozen bananas and quadrupled the recipe.  Easy to do.  I used part fat free vanilla yogurt and part skim milk to sub. in for the buttermilk.  I use a white/wheat flour combo, and I was liberal with the mini chips.  Otherwise I stayed the same.  Love how moist these are even without added fat.  The only issue I had, and it is because of my oven and my attempt to make this in such quantity, is that you really have to check and see if they are done.  They start browning and I would think they were done, but when I took them out there were still underdone.  I usually like my muffins to not get brown (because often in low fat muffins that means they will be dry) but these need a good brown color to be fully cooked.  Something I'll make again.  Thanks!
Fantasic! I may or may not have added a few more tablespoons of chocolate chips. Well worth the extra time at the gym, if you ask me.
Very good for what it is.  Mine roase very strangly and were a bit overcooked with the time given but still good.
This are delicious!  30 min is a little too long. I would start with 25min and then see if they need more time.  I also used 1/2cup of chocolate chips, to die for!

By far one of the best recipes for muffins.  Although very tempted to add butter in the beginning.. Added blue berries.  Saved the butter for after the baking process ;>) ! 

Very good... Thank you...
AMAZING! I followed the recipe exactly as written and it was a HUGE HIT with the kids and DH(who doesn't care for low fat type recipes). We'll be making this often!

I guess I'm in the minority but these were just OK for me. They were moist but in a rather too dense, heavy sort of way. The texture was just "wrong" somehow. It was also soggy in parts. Also, 30min might have been a bit too long. Even though I checked early, they still got too dry on the outside, so much so that we had to remove the dry "shell" to get to the softer part inside. Only change I made was to reduce the sugar to 3/4cup and I used all brown sugar.
WONDERFUL, I followed the recipe other than the salt, I only used a few shakes. These were great, I made 1 dozen bite sized and 6 regular. Will make again!

Great!!!  Add the 1/2 C. chips as suggested by others, you won't be sorry!  Very moist muffins, yummy!  Just don't over mix the batter.  The recipe says, "combine well" I think it would be better to say, "mix just until moist."  I baked these for 26 minutes. Thanks Manda!!!!

VERY nice. I made 2/3 of the recipe, only used 1/4 cup each of brown and white sugar, and added vanilla, cinnamon and cardamom to these, and i got 23 perfect little mini-muffins. even my little sister said they were good, and she's probably the pickiest eater I know! (i also omitted the chocolate and nuts). Thanks!

Terrific!  I made 'em as mini-muffins, which made them the perfect size.  I also added 1/2 cup chocolate chips, and was shocked to discover that even though I'm a complete chocoholic, I thought that was too much.  Next time I'll add 1/4 - 1/3 cup.  I had trouble believing these were as low in fat as they were -- they were quite moist and delicious.  A definite keeper -- thanks for posting this!
it was a great hit tonight when we had company over for supper! I didnt add the walnuts but added extra chocolate! yum!

You would never ever know these were low fat.  I was amazed at how moist these are, considering there is not a drop of oil in them.  I followed the recipe exactly, and included the walnuts. I love the texture they give.  I'll never throw away my black bananas again!  Thanks for such a simple and delicious recipe!

These were really yummy and very simple.  I don't like nuts, so I used additional chips in place of them.  I had too much to fill my cups, although after baking I saw that I could have filled them up more, because they didn't rise much.  I set my timer for 25 minutes to check on them, and they were past done and overbrowned.  As a result, they were a touch dry, but definitely still tasty, and I'll just have to check on them soooner next time.  I could have been the oven, too.  We get a new one in 3 weeks!

Yummmmmmyyy!!! These were soo delicious!I just made them today and i am trying soo hard to stay away from the rest so i can take them to work!! It really is amazing that there's no butter or anything in them and they are still soo moist and delicious. I did think that they are a bit sweet so i might just use only brown sugar next time. Thanks!

These were awesome.  I made mine in a mini muffin pan and they turned out great.  These were perfect in my sons' lunch boxes.  They liked that it was a "sweet" and I liked that it was healthy.  These are now on the frequent request list! Thank you so much for sharing!

These are great muffins. They are sweeter then I thought they would be and were done a little bit before the time stated (both definite bonuses!).  I used the mini chocolate chips and made them for our 5 year olds lunch box! He loves them! Thank you!

I baked these for a church bake sale for a youth fundraiser.  They were a hit!  My friends asked for these yummy, moist, best tasting banana muffins I have ever made.  I will make them again and again.
Came out super fragrant, moist and yummy. I used egg white and subbed milk for vanilla soy milk. As well as some high altitude modifications. Came out great.

Excellant!  These turned out better than I expected!  I am a Diabetic, so, for half of the muffins I put 1 tsp. uncooked oatmeal in the bottom of each muffin paper, filled it 3/4 full of batter then sprinkled walnuts on top.  I also used Splenda in place of the granulated sugar.  It pleased my grandkids, as well as me-- to not feel guilty about eating something so yummy!

O-M-G! These were fantastic. I gotta admit I am usually not one to alter recipes (not sure why) but I did use Splenda baking sugar instead of the regular sugar and used half flour and half wheat flour for the (1.5 c of flour). I added a few more chips than suggested and MAN these were still fantastic!  I couldn't believe how scrumptious they were. I knew they would be good but they were out of this world! Thanks Manda!

I loved this recipe. But I did have some problems! My bananas were quite large and I had to add another 1/2 cup of flour. I also added 1 tsp of baking powder and another 1/2 tsp of soda. I got 12 regular sized muffins and 1 small loaf. Great low-cal recipe only I ended up eating 5!

Absolutely fantastic!  I think next time, I might use a few more chocolate chips...but I'm a diehard chocoholic.  My only complaint is that they came out pretty gooey on top, and I'm not sure why.  I'll definitely be making them again, though.
very tasty that i could barely imagine it is low-fat! :) thanks for posting.

What can I say?  These were amazing.  These taste so decadent to be low fat!  I took a batch to work and they were gone in a flash.  I'm a huge chocolate fan, so I will play with adding cocoa powder to the batter.  These are going in the keeper file!
WOW!  Like the others, I was suprised at how delicious and fluffy these muffins are!  I will be making these all the time.  Thanks!

These really are AMAZING. Im not watching my weight, but these are better than full fat varieties. I always use 100% whole wheat flour in baking, and these remain moist and flavorful. I used 1/2 cup chocolate chips. I like chocolate. Yum, and thankyou so much for posting this keeper.

Awesome. I can't believe there's no butter in these! The bananas do the trick of making these moist and rich...and the chocolate chips don't hurt either :) We substituted whole wheat flour and made them as mini-muffins (about 15-17 min baking time). Just took these out of the oven and my husband, who is not a snacker, tried one, then had another because "it looked lonely"...must be really good for him to be sneeking a second one! 
Thanks for posting this, Manda!
These muffins were great! They have just the right amount of chocolate chips and nuts in them. I will definitely be making these again.
A lovely moist muffin that no one could resist.  The best thing to make with those over ripe bananas.  Thanks for posting.

These were awesome!  I didn't add the walnuts and forgot the chocolate chips and I didn't miss them.  I used an egg substitute and added a 1/2 cup of applesauce and flax seed (not as low fat, but a great way to get my DH to get flax)  I ended up with 15 or 16 and froze them so we can have them in the am.  Thank you for sharing.  I will be making these again and again.
Good muffins and my BF's favorite. I omitted the walnuts and added mini chocolate chips(5 Tblsp.) Will make these again soon. Thanks!

I made this today and was very satisfied.  I was looking for something guilt free and this was it.  I used 4 bananas because that is what i needed to get rid of.  I also substituted 1/4 c egg beaters for the egg, I used whole wheat pastry flour instead of the all purpose flour, 1/2 cup splenda for the sugar and added in 1/2 cup of applesauce.  The flavor was great.  Just enough sweetness and a hint of chocolate.  I will definitely be making these again.  Thanks!

The recipe that is MY no-fail banana muffin recipe is identical to this, only it calls for 1/3 cup oil in place of the 1/3 cup buttermilk. I can't wait to give it a try with the milk and see if the difference of taste is worth it for the difference in fat content.  UPDATE:  So I tried these with the buttermilk and thought they were really good...only thing I may add next time is vanilla!

amazing!!!  i bit into one of these and they taste like a delicious regular muffin, not lowfat at all!  the bananas i used were just ripe, they had spots all over them but when peeled were still rather firm but i think this helped set the muffin better.  I used skim milk and vinegar to sub in as buttermilk, and i used ALL wholewheat flour, i was a little nervous using all wholewheat but they came out GREAT, i will definitely use this again and again.  I cannot believe there is no oil or butter in there, i even halved the amount of sugar!  I still cant believe that when im eating one of those muffins that they are made from all whole wheat flour, skim milk and very little added sugar.

I tried it and this was AWESOME!  I began to make it and realized I didn't have either of the milks the recipe called for so I substituted canned evaporated milk.  I was nervous!  I didn't add the white sugar. I used four overly ripe bananas and didn't put in the chocolate chips but instead I added a dash or two of nutmeg and cinnamon and I was very generous with the chopped walnuts.  The result? Extremely yummy and light muffins.  I baked them for about 20 mins. and that was too long.  Next time I will bake them for about 17 mins.  These are so good and I will definitely be making them again and again.  Thanks so much for posting!

Really great recipe for delicious muffins that are a snap to put together.  Lots of sugar though, I'm not sure I would call this a super "healthy" muffin, even if it is low-fat.  I used whole wheat flour, soy milk instead of regular, and added a couple tablespoons of flax seeds.  They were yummy, but 30 minutes to bake was way too long for mine (maybe because of the flax seeds and soy?).  Anyways, they were a little bit too chewy and hard, so I would reduce the bake time to 25 minutes.  Other than the texture though, they were great!
Delicious! I wasn't even looking for a low-fat muffin, but these are really good. I cooked mine for 24 minutes instead of 30.

This is a great base for a lower fat banana muffin.  I did however have to make a few substitutions.

I thought the sugar content was too high, so I cut back to 1/2 cup each of the granulated & brown sugar, but even still they were pretty sweet.  The sugar can still be cut back even more.  I also cut out half of the salt.  Since I added the walnuts and they were salted, I knew I wouldn't need a full tsp of salt.

I also cut back the flour to 1 1/4 cups.

I added 1 tsp of vanilla extract and 1/4 tsp of ground cinnamon.

The 12 muffins were done in 20 minutes, 30 minutes would have burned them.

Otherwise, I followed everything as is.  I really enjoyed them and will be making this recipe again for sure.  It's amazing how the butter and/or oil is NOT missing in the recipe.  

I enjoyed these for dessert and as a quick breakfast on the go.

Thanks Manda for posting this great recipe.
These came out great.  I used another reviewer's suggestion and added 1/2 cup of applesauce and 1/2 cup of rolled oats.  I used 50%cocoa dark chocolate chips.  No nuts for me.  Great recipe!

My husband loves banana bread with chocolate chips, and I have been searching for the perfect recipe. Thank goodness! Here it is! These were moist and delicious. And, as the family health nut, I love that these are low fat. Will make again for sure...and again...and again! Thank you!!!! <><
These were a little "heavy" for my taste and DH and son agree.  Maybe my bananas were too big. (?)

Awesome muffins!! Easy to make with great success !! I added 1 tsp of vanilla (doubled the recipe) as well as extra chocolate chips as recommended by another chef. Mmmmmm good!
Thanks Recipe Zaar, always just a tap away !!
Diane (Ontario, Canada)

These were good, but we didn't feel they were anything special.  Still good, though, but I think I'll be sticking with my usual banana muffin recipe... sorry to give a less than stellar review after all the ones raving about this recipe! :s

I'm a shamed to say I got this recipe from recipezaar a long time ago and haven't rated it until now.  This is my go-to ripe banana recipe and can be adjusted so easily to taste.  Thank you,  Manda,  this IS something special!!
These were awesome and a huge hit here.  I followed some suggestions and added applesauce and oatmeal and they were just delicious.  We'll definitely make them again.

WOW is right!  I just made these and ate one piping hot out of the oven.  Delicious. Great taste and texture.  Excellent muffin.  I probably added too many chocolate chips because for me it was all about the chocolate but these muffins are really really good.  I am going to have to freeze some now so I don't eat the all!!!!
i love this muffin! it's not really a muffin, more of a gooey, banana-ish sweet snack. very more-ish! i substituted the sugar for Equal and made them in little muffin cups. YUM!

Delicious! So very easy to make with  wonderful flavour and so very moist.  I did need to bake them for 30 minutes which could have been a result of larger bananas or my oven temperature. Great way to use up those last ripe bananas. Thanks for sharing this great recipe.

Although I have come across other muffin recipes that taste better, these are remarkably moist and delicious for a low-fat muffin. I usually make half as posted and half with extra walnuts sprinkled on top instead of chocolate chips. These are now making a regular appearance in my kitchen ;)

This has become a regular recipe in our house. I don't buy premade snacks for the childrens lunches, so this has come in handy. I make them at least twice a week, they are very quick. Even when I am in a rush I can make these before school . I replace the white flour with whole wheat, and also add ground flax seed and wheat germ, and replace the sugar with splenda.

These were YUMMY!  I used frozen ripe bananas (I unwrapped and microwaved 30 seconds until thawed enough to mash).  Forgot the salt but I dont think it mattered  (my little one was covered in flour from helping me, so I was a bit distracted LOL!)  I did notice that they were a bit dense but that might of been from me forgetting the salt.  Flavor & texture were great, nice and moist.  My 3 kids DEVOURED them.  I love that they are low-fat!   Made 24 mini muffins.  Thanks for a keeper!
Delicious, moist and tasty.  I used 4 bananas.  I didn't use muffin tin liners, but they came out of the pan just fine.
Awesome recipe < best Ive ever made!
I make these delicious muffins any time we have ripe bananas. I fill up my 2 mini muffin tins first and then put the rest of the batter into regular sized muffin tins.

I really enjoyed this one. Like some other reviewer, I added almost 1/2 cup chocolate chips (2 Tbsp? -what?) but took out 1/4 of sugar so it would not be too sweet. Then, I used my muffin top pan to make 6 tops and the rest of the batter fit in my mini muffin tin (for 12). My room mate loved them too!
Very moist for a lowfat muffin.  Freeze well if they stay in the freezer.  Thanks!
Made these banana muffins just used dark chocolate chips and added half cup applesauce they turned out great loved them ??

These came out of the oven about 5 minutes ago and 2 are already mysteriously gone! These are moist and delicious and it is really hard to believe that they don't have fat. I didn't make them for me but for my kids because I don't typically like baked goods. But these? I like!

My first time making and trying banana muffins. Yummy! Turned out really good. I followed the instructions to the letter except I had chocolate chunks and I added a few more then called for. 
Definitely a keeper! Thanks for sharing.

Wow, these were yummy! I cut back a bit on the sugar, used a 1/2 cup ww flour, added much more chocolate chips, i cut the nuts (didn't have any), I made a flax and water egg substitute, and i used skim milk and lemon juice. These were good! Definetly could use more chocolate chips, and next time i would probably add a smidgen more sugar. thanks!
great muffins, kids really love them. I didnt have mini chocolate chips so I just chopped up the regular ones a bit. Baked for 25 minutes and were done.  Thanks!!
yum yum, great muffins! I used 1/3 cup fat free half and half instead of the milk, and 1/4 cup mini choc. chips. They turned out wonderful . Thanks Manda for sharing this recipe.

Thank you for sharing that recipe. They were delicious. I used 1/2 cup of chocolate chips, and i 3 1/2 bananas total the 1/2 i cut into small pieces and folded in with the chocolate chips so there were little chunks of banana in the muffins.  I will definately be making them again probably next week. Thanks again.

Yummy! These are great muffins and I love that they have no oil or butter in them but they are still full of flavor and moist. They tasted best the first and second day. I used about 1/3 cup mini chocolate chips. Thank you for the recipe, I'll be making these again!
I thought these banana muffins were good. I was impressed that there was no oil or any kind of fat. Easy to make as well.

These were very good! Following some of the suggestions of the other reviewers, I subbed whole wheat flour for white flour and Splenda Granulated for white sugar, to reduce the calorie count and increase the fiber. I made a double batch, half regular muffins (done in about 22 minutes) and half minis (done in about 12 minutes). Spraying the foil liners was great, they come unwrapped extremely easily. For the minis, I just sprayed the pan and spooned the batter straight in, and that worked well too. I used the amount of chips called for, but because I used mini chips it was enough. (I didn't want them to be overly chocolatey anyway, for first thing in the morning.) And yes, they freeze great. I like to toast them after defrosting to crisp up the top a bit. Will definitely make these again!

Wonderful recipe! I omitted both the chocolate chips and walnuts so as to keep the fat and calorie level down as low as possible. Both kids, the ex and myself all loved these muffins. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe!

Delicious and moist! This is a very easy, very tasty recipe! I had 4 very ripe bananas on hand so I used all 4. To compensate for the extra moisture I added about 2 tablespoons more flour. I also added 1/2 tsp. each of cinnamon and nutmeg plus about 1 tsp. of vanilla. The addition of the spices gave these a really nice flavour! I got 12 regular size PLUS 12 minis out of the 4 banana batch. Cook the minis for about 15 mins. and maybe only 25 mins for the regular size, at 30 mins mine were a touch dark...but still moist and very delicious! Thanks Manda for posting!! :O)

This is a trick...they can not be low in fat. Very tasty and moist muffins. I slipped and some extra walnuts and chocolate chips fell in...oops. I used butter milk and added a little applesauce. I will make again for sure .
One word, YUUUUUUUUUUMMMMMYYYY!!! These are so awesome. So fluffy, so moist, so YUMMMM!!!!

This is a great recipe!  Very moist and tasty.  I made some modifications to it: instead of 1 1/2 cups flour, I used 3/4 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup flour and 1/4 cup wheat germ.  I reduced the white sugar to 1/4 cup and added more chocolate chips and some pecans instead walnuts.  I will definitely make these again!
SO yummy! To make them even more healthy, I used whole wheat flower and used skim milk.  So yummy and so easy! Will totally make them again:) Thank you!
I used half whole wheat flour and 1 more tblspn of choco chips, and these were really moist!  Thank you Manda for a simple, delicious, low fat recipe

Wow!  Excellent!  We have a favorite pumpkin muffin recipe, so, I added some of the items from that to try to get some more fiber for my 2.5 year old.  I only had 2 bananas and it turned out great.  I added the 1/2 cup of applesauce and used 3/4 of  whole wheat flower and 3/4 of regular flour.  I completely forgot about trying to at oats, but, will next time.  I also added 1 tsp of cinnamon, 1 tsp of vanilla, and 2 tbs of ground flaxseed to the mashed bananas.  Oh, and of course, upped the choco chips! I baked them for 22 minutes and they came out perfect!  It's a keeper!
Well it isn't low fat when I get through adding choc. chips and walnuts, but I don't care. These are great!
My hubby and I love these!  I added a little more than the 2-3 T. chocolate chips, plus the walnuts, and they turned out awesome.
They sure don't taste low-fat!!! Used two large bananas and used regular butter. Also added about 1/4 cups of mini chocolate chip muffins. Thanks Manda! :)

Perfect! I used 3 very ripe bananas and 1/3 cup milk (no butter) and instead of choco chips i used dark chocolate which i divided into small pieces. Cooked for 30 min. Came out great! Super moist, yummy! Thanks for the recipe..

I made these muffins for my family this weekend and they loved them.  I had three bananas that had gotten too ripe for us and this recipe was perfect.  I loved the addition of chocolate chips, not too many, just right.  Thank you for a nice muffin to serve my family.

This is a really good recipe to take care of those over ripe bananas.  I have tried several recipes for banana muffins and this is the best so far.  I think the brown sugar really makes a difference.  Also, substituted in 1/2 cup whole wheat flour.   Very good recipe.

These are awesome!  I have a daycare and the kids LOVED them and I did too!  I love that they don't have any butter or oil.  I got 16 good sized muffins instead of 12.  Put this in my "will make again" file!

I doubled this recipe so I could freeze some.  I made it exactly as written except I added a few more chocolate chips.  They were very good and I like that there is no oil in them.  But 30 minutes is definitely too long of a baking time.  My mini muffins were done after 15 minutes and the larger were done after 20.

Excellent!!!  I subbed 2/3 C. agave nectar for the white and brown sugars.  Thus, I knocked the baking temp down to 325 (baked for 33 minutes) and only used a scant 1/3 C. milk.  Next time, I might use even less milk.  I also used about 1/4 C. chocolate chips since I needed to use up the rest of the bag I had.  Yummy recipe!
Excellent. Only used two bananas, no probs. Loaded on the chocolate chips...delish!!! Love that there is no oil or butter! Thanks for a keeper!

Used lowfat buttermilk and a LOT more chocolate chips and no nuts.  Also added about a tablespoon of flavored agave nectar.  Replaced the white sugar with Splenda.  These were yummy and cooked a little quicker than indicated.  Look, ma, no butter!  Thanks for sharing.
These were fine, though I probably won't make them again since I like my muffins to be a bit more healthy.  The chocolate chips are definitely a nice touch! I used 3 Tbsp. minature chocolate chips.

Fantastic! I had a craving the other night for banana chocolate chip muffins, and I knew recipezaar would the place to find a great recipe. These are amazing! I used 1 C wheat flour and 1/2 C wheat germ, egg white instead of egg, and realized that I was out of baking soda so used baking powder instead. Like other reviewers, I added more chocolate chips (I used minis) and decided to throw in some walnuts for good measure. These muffins turned out absolutely perfectly! My husband and I have already finished almost the whole dozen and I can't wait to make another batch! Thanks for a can't-miss recipe!

Boy oh boy these turned out fabulous....I did use splenda for baking instead of real sugar and added a tsp. of baking powder to give them a little more lift...they turned out perfect...oh i did double the recipe as I had quite a few bananas to use up...

Very easy and good way to use up 3 'rotten' banana's! Fill muffin liners full. I sprinkled choco chips on tops and then swirled them into batter with a knife--they came out perfect. I don't like choco chips 'sinking' to the bottom in muffins! This recipe is a sure keeper!

Delicious! By far the best banana bread/muffin recipe I've ever tried. It's good that these are low fat, because I could eat a dozen! I just made these last night, and my husband already asked me to make more. The only thing I did differently is I baked them for 27 minutes instead of 30. YUMMY!

Used 1/4 cup milk chocolate chips and no nuts. Substituted splenda for sugar and added 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce and 1/2 cup old fashioned quaker oats. With these changes, it made 18 muffins and when I put it through the WW recipe builder it came to TWO POINTS per muffin. These are delicious and "point-friendly" for a filling, good-sized muffin. I will be using all my ripe bananas for these!!
Super moist and yummy! Made only half the recipe but used a whole egg - turned out great!

Great recipe-very moist with a mild bananna flavour.  I used 4 banannas, Splenda instead of granulated sugar, egg white instead of a whole egg, added 1/2 c of quick oats (as suggested by other reviewers) and some additional mini chocolate chips.  I baked it in a loaf pan for about 60 minutes, and even with all these changes it still came out wonderfully.  Thanks for posting!
Loved these muffins. I did get 1 and 1/2 dozen muffins out of the batter and I only cooked them 20 minutes. Thanks for the great recipe!
these were amazing! We didnt really notice the walnuts so I may leave them out next time and skip the extra calories they add.

Excellent low-fat muffins. They are dense and moist, and not at all rubbery like some get when you substitue apple sauce for butter. I used 1/2 whole wheat flour and 1/2 white, increased the walnuts to 1/3 cup and cut out the chocolate chips. I would include the chocolate next time (DH isn't keen on chocolate, which is why I left it out this time).
These were really flavorless and bland...I suppose for a "diet" food they were good, but just to eat they weren't that appealing.  My hubby liked them, but I don't think I'll be making them again.
This is good but Recipe #43509 is so much better.

SOOOO good.  I will admit that I added a lot more chocolate chips than the recipe asked for but other than that I did everything the same.  This is a very moist flavor full muffin.  They taste the best the first day but they really do not last longer than that at our house.
Easy and tasty.  The batter was almost runny, but the muffins rose to a beautiful texture.  Sweetened dried cranberries work nicely, too.

Well I started making these thinking I had chocolate chips, but ended up not having ANY. So instead I added some cinnamon, a little vanilla and some toasted coconut flakes, made them delicous! Very moist cupcake! I will be making these again, next I'll make sure I've got chocolate chips on hand!>
These were really great for being low fat and super easy.  Making again to make a  big batch and freeze.

It's hard to believe these are low fat they are so delicious.  I left out the nuts (husband doesn't like them) and did add a bit more mini chocolate chips....about 1/2 C. total.  I ate one, my husband ate the rest.  I'll definitely make these again, the next time I have overripe bananas.

These are excellent! I added an extra egg and about 1/3 C cocoa to the mixture and used mini chocolate chips. They were excellent, chewy and flavorful. I only needed to bake for 18 min. Will be making these again very soon!
These are amazing!  I also added the applesauce and rolled oats and they are definitely moist, which is a problem I've found with a lot of other low-fat muffin options.  Highly recommended recipe!

I am giving these a five for flavour, ease of making and healthiness.  I made these with my two boys 3 and 2 years old and we had a blast.  I added applesauce and oatmeal as well.  They will make a great breakfast from the freezer.  I used peanut butter chips as I had a bag to use up.  We decided to eat them for luch with some yougurt. The only complaint we have is that they stick to our paper cups.  I sprayed them and everything.  My two year ate most of his cup in his haste.  I will try them without the cup next time.  Thanks for a healthly delicious muffin.  These are a keeper.

I love these; especially considering their nutrition facts! I added 1/2 cup oats, 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce, and a heaping tsp. of cinnamon as well. I think I actually added too many chips for my liking (which was well over the 2-3 tbsp. called for), so I will decrease that next time, as I think they somewhat overpowered the banana. I sprayed my liners and had only very mild problems with sticking. I left them in the oven for 25 minutes, perfect! My boyfriend stole HALF the batch to take home!

I preheated to 180 deg celcius and then cooked at 150 deg celcius for 40 min, but left for another 10 min as I got sidetracked so was probably drier than was intended, then squeezed a generous amount of orange juice over the top and put back in the oven for approx 10 min as the oven was cooling down . I did not mix by hand- I combined dry ingredients in a bowl and put it aside, then starting with the bananas, I used a standing mixer, added all wet ingredients then added the dry ingredients 2 cups at a time until all was well combined. I did crush my own walnuts so the pieces were a little chunky which I didn't like so next time I will buy crushed walnuts. This recipe made me 2 mini loaves and 12 muffins. So if you're not making for a lot of people be prepared to freeze some or cut the recipe in half. Perfection!! Oh, and do not over cook it as it will lose its moistness.

WOW!! Very good!! I also simmered a hambone with the veggies for about hour. I  added  1/2 c. of sliced carrots just because I like them in soup and they added some color. I made this a few weeks back and did it as directed. It was AWESOME! thanks for a great meal

5 stars  from me with no extra additions. 5 Stars all the way.

Just made this for dinner.. omitted the extra salt.  Rich tasting and flavorful, definitely going into my winter rotation.

OMG!  That is amazing!  I made it tonight since it is sooooo chilly here, and we ate it with some crusty rolls....the kids even loved it! Thanks!

WOW this was easy and so great on a cold night. BF loves ham and I don't so I made it as a treat for him. Both of us loved it!!! Only problem is now he says the guys at work want to try it. Thank you for the comfort soup.

YUM! This didn't last long at my house everyone loved it!

Enjoyed the soup, good with crusty bread to dip in it.  Will make again to use up left over ham next Easter.

Good but not spectacular.  Was expecting a lot more flavor.  Was a nice compliment to blackened spicy snapper.

Wonderful! Loved the flavors and the ease of preparation. The rice turned out perfectly. Thanks for sharing.
Incredibly easy, tasty, goes with anything. What more could you want?
Pretty good. Not to spicy, not too bland. Gonna add this to the list of 'yummy things'. :3
Great recipe! Definitely making this again. Thanks!
Delicious! I add a can of chopped chili's and shredded chicken sometimes. But they are delicious just as you have it here. Thanks!

Excellent! I halved the recipe and boy are these things FILLING! I served them with sour cream and salsa on the side. I added a couple of chopped jalapeÃ±os for some heat. I had to bake mine for at least 1/2 hour to get them heated through.

Very yummy!  I used a kobacha squash instead of sweet potatoes because I prefer the flavor.  I also added a bit of fresh cilantro for flavor and subbed low fat pepper jack cheese.  I also put a bit of spicy salsa for a bit more spice.  Review for PAC Spring 2008.
This is really good!  Such a strange mix of ingredients but a delicious result.  I've made it as described and with cans of refried beans.  Both ways end up with good results.

Delicious!  Better than I could have hoped.  The sweetness of the yams goes perfectly with the chili powder in the beans. I had a sweet potato hanging around for a while and was looking for something to do with it.  I actually found this recipe on Allrecipe web site but wanted to rate it so I came here.

I left the bean/onion mixture a bit rough as I like the texture of the beans.  Oh, and I forgot to add the water to the bean mixture but I don't think it took anything away from the recipe.
Loved it and so easy to make. Wouldn't change a thing!
I'm as guilty as a homemade sin...ate more than my fair share.  Made for PRMR.

I just loved this-the chicken marinade is so delicious....a perfect blend of flavour.
We really enjoyed this,and look forward to making it again.
Made for 123 Hits.

This is incredible stuff!  (And if you haven't visited www.thepioneerwoman.com, you definitely should.)  I served this on homemade sub rolls for a great, messy sandwich. This was so good!!  I used b/s chicken thighs and a grainy mustard, and left out the red pepper flakes.  I let it marinade for 3 1/2 hours and the flavor was perfect!  Will have to try grilling this when it warms up, loved the marinade!  Made for AUS/NZ Recipe Swap #47.

I thought this was just okay. The marinade was really good (I let it soak for 3 1/2 hours) but after I fried it in the bacon grease, it lost a lot of that flavor. But anything topped with bacon and cheese is good. It was worth a shot but I think it's more calories than it's worth eating. Sorry!
Pretty yummy stuff! My husband LOVED it, and my son & I thought it was pretty good. :) Can't go wrong with Pioneer Woman. I used Recipe #392356  to cook the bacon.

The other 1/2 was perfect for lunch after I wrapped it in a paper towel and microwaved for 30 sec. Thanks for posting!

This is a hit with my husband and kids.  The marinade is wonderful.  I do agree with another poster that frying it in bacon grease takes away a lot of the flavor of the marinade.  I have made it with using the bacon grease and without, and without is by far a favorite here.
Super easy, super moist. Next time I may add rasins. I think that would be good too.
I don't know if mine turned out right..they were super mushy, even after 30-35 minutes! still tasted awesome..almost the same texture as pumpkin pie, creamy.  these are awesome!

Simply delicious! I did not make muffins but a 13x9 cake instead - I  watched it and inserted a toothpick for doneness.  Baking time was roughly 25 minutes, and it's nice and moist. It came out great!  Thanks for sharing.
I am not on a diet but these were wonderful... I changed nothing and they came out super moist and full of flavor..

I thought these were wonderful & my husband loved them too.

Since some reviewers said that the muffins didn't bake as well, I added an egg.

Thanks for sharing a great recipe!

These were very good.  Especially considering they have only a few calories.  Since I'm not on weight watchers, but I am concious of calorie intake, I added a little bit of frosting to them. You can use any cake mix with this recipie. If you add an egg it is more cake-like. Very Yummy!

These were really quick and easy to make.  I think next time I will take previous reviewers advice and up the spices a bit.  They would be awesome with a little cream cheese icing (kinda defeats the two points but yum).  I am going to print an extra copy for my mom. Thanks for a great snack.
This recipe is fantastic!  I followed the recipe below that used 1 egg, skim milk, and water and I added Fat Free Cool Whip as frosting!  Everyone at our house LOVED it!!!!!!

These were fine.  They need something extra, though.  I think diced apples would go nicely in the mix or maybe topping them with cream cheese icing would do the trick.  I probably won't make these again.

They are over the top with a bit of cream cheese frosting!

I followed this recipe to a T and it worked perfectly.  I have been eating them constantly since I made them, and for four points I can have two muffins and a pretty filling breakfast.  These are really really soft and yummy too, just like pumpkin bread!

These are awesome!! They are moist and taste great.  It is hard to believe that just 3 ingredients can make such wonderfully delicous  muffins.  I added just a few chocolate chips to them because I love the mixture of pumpkin and chocolate.  Who knew that low fat would taste so sinfully good. I will be making these again and again!! Thanks so much.

For a diet muffin they were very good. They were moist and flavorful. Thery were very quick and easy to prepare. Went well with our morning coffee. 

Thanks Nad Smith. 

Bullwinkle

Thanks!

I loved these muffins.  First time i made them exactly like the recipe.  I loved them.  Next time I used 1/2 cup water (instead of 1 cup) and added two egg whites so they would be light and fluffy.  Loved them both ways.  Thanks for the great recipe.
I left out the water and these turned out great.  A dollop of fat free cool whip makes these even better!  Thanks for the post.
Absolutely wonderful.  A little dollip of cool whip on top and wha-la.  Delicious.

I've made these a couple of times once with a spice cake and once with a carrot cake.  Always delicious.  They never stay around here very long:)
Thanks for posting!

They do have that low-fat kind of texture like you would expect from a muffin made without oil and they aren't crumbly-tender like a high-fat muffin, but still very tender and moist.  Although I don't usually use cake mixes, this is a recipe I'd make again.

Loved these! So easy and very moist. It's not like a bakery muffin but it's equally good in in its own way. I'll take it over a high fat muffin any day. I'm still experimenting with cooking and baking and don't force my food on anyone but I immediately brought these in for co-workers the next day. Might try some walnuts or chocolate chips on my next batch as others have suggested!

I made these for my family this week, and they were a HUGE hit! I reduced the water to 3/4 cup and added 1/4 cup lite splenda sweetened applesauce. I also added 2 egg whites to help the texture. This recipe is delicious, simple, family pleasing, and light...a combination I didn't even know was possible from a cake mix! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!
Delicious! I don't see why anyone bothers to add oil and egg? I love the springy texture and they're good with or without frosting.

These were wonderful. I added some pumpin spice to the batter. I will be making a batch today to bring with me tonight to give to the staff that work at my vets office.

Instant pumkin pie? Thanks nad smith for posting a very delicious recipe.

thanks for an easy, decently healthy snack!!

very good!

Yummy! I love these easy and tasty muffins.

Love it! OH they are SOOOO good. I will be making these around the fall time for sure, so I can replace my usual pumpkin pie and pumpkin roll (maybe ice them with a little cream cheese icing). These are so tasty and easy. Thanks for the great recipe!

this recipe made great muffins very moist and falvorfull

These were excellent. The only thing I did different was to use a carrot cake mix yum yum thanks

Great muffin recipe for WW.  I added the egg and reduced the water.  Also used cupcake tins and wrappers.  Love the pumpkin flavor.  Will make it with another flavor next time.  This is a keeper for sure.

Love this recipe!  I have made as the recipe says and i've also reduced the water to 1/2 cup and used 1 egg to make fluffier if i take them somewhere as they are more like your traditional cake texture. I didn't have spice cake mix on hand so I used a yellow cake mix and did the following tweaks:

1 egg
1 cup oatmeal
1 1/2 tsp cinnamon
1/2 tsp nutmeg
1/4 tsp ground cloves
1/4 tsp ginger powder
reduced water to 2/3 cup

I found the oatmeal reduced the excess moistness leaving a balanced muffin (moist still but not too moist). I also reduced the water to 1/2 cup because I added an egg to the recipe. The whole house smells like fall when these are being baked! Next time I might add nuts or craisins for extra flavor.
2 points per serving (24 cup cakes)!
Quick, easy and very good...thanks for sharing.
I always make these with no water.  Just pumpkin and spice cake mix.  It's a wonderful muffin!

These are amazing!  I did decrease water to 1/4 c and added 1 egg.  Hard to believe these are weight watchers!  I have a second batch cooking using chocolate cake batter since I didn't have another spice batter.
