Excellent and very easy to make.  I also reduced the amount of brown sugar for a slightly less sweet sauce, and ate it over brown rice.  Wonderful, savory dish.
Awesome recipe, tasted just like it did when I was a kid!!! Easy to make and no odd ingredients! Thanks for posting it.

This was fantastic! My husband said to give it more than 5 stars if possible.  He really enjoyed it!
I did make a few changes...
I used two bags of frozen veggies, one broccoli and one sugar snap pea stir fry mix, slightly defrosted, added one more small onion and I didn't add the water to the cornstarch/garlic powder mixture before tossing the beef in it. Other than those changes everything was as posted. Delicious!
Very easy, and I too like the simple ingredients.

Excellent and soooo easy!  I used a bag of stir fry veggies (broccoli, carrot strips, celery, red peppers & water chestnuts), a can of cut baby corn and an extra can of water chestnuts.  It was awesome!!!
Awesome. I doubled it and it turned out perfectly. I think next time I will use the less salty soya as it was a bit to salty for my taste. I think button mushrooms might be a nice touch also.

This is reaaaaally good. I added a touch more ginger and garlic, then lightened up a little on the soy sauce/brown sugar mix. I have a hard time sticking to recipes, but didn't stray far with this one. I will say that the results were fantastic. I'll be making this again and again.
Really good recipe, just the way it is!
Excellent! I followed the advice of others and left out the water in step 1. I also used frozen broccoli. So easy! And so yummy!
Very easy and tasty.  Tastes is surprisingly very similar to regular beef and broccoli.  Thanks for the recipe.
Very tasty. Think I will also leave out the water next time as it seemed a little watered down . I used frozen broccoli also and it turned out just fine
Super Easy. Didn't have ginger, but still tasted great. I added carrots. Family fav!

Awesome recipe! This was my first time making beef and broccoli and this is the only recipe I will use. It was a bit hard to cut the meat thin but that is my fault. This recipe has been requested several times since making it. Thank you!
It tasted really good and it was similar to the restaurant taste but not exactly it. Still good though but still in search to replicate the Chinese restaurant taste...

Loved this easy recipe.  I added sesame oil, ginger and sriracha to the marinate for flank steak and red pepper, mushrooms to the veggies.   
Served with Recipe #72124 and rice.

this has to be the easiest beef and broccoli recipe i came acroos. i did sub the meat w/ chicken instead but followed everything else to the T. was a big hit w/ the whole fam and there's none left over except onions. ha. next time tho i will use low sodium soy and a bit more brown sugar since i like my beef & broccoli a tad sweeter. great recipe tho thanks for sharing!

This was so easy and super quick to make.  I made the recipe exactly the way it was printed and personally I wouldn't change a thing.  Everything worked very well and was very tasty!  This is the first time I have ever prepared anything asian and thought that it came out well.  I will totally be making this again!  Thanks so much for posting!
This was a total success!  I must admit I marinated my meat before hand and added mushrooms and peppers.  I doubled the sauce and it was great!  A real winner!

This was really good and so simple to make! I used a frozen bag of broccoli florets, which saved me some time. I did feel that flavor-wise it was lacking something, but I can't put my finger on it... MSG the flavor enhancer? lol  Definitely good enough to make again!

Quick and easy, i made this for 2 it turned out a little salty but that was on my behalf i think because i replaced the water with more soy sauce cause i was just throwing it together for lunch. I will make this again TY chris

Easy and delicious. I added julienned carrots, red peppers, and zucchini. Next time I would also add in some snow peas. I liked it so much, I made a veggie version the next day. I thought it had a little too much soy sauce, but my husband liked it as is. Oh, and I added 3 garlic cloves, instead of garlic powder, on the second round and I preferred the cloves.
Delicious ! I tripled the recipe and added carrots, next time I will add some pepper flakes and less ginger.
great tasting and easy thanks

The sauce had a great taste, I did double the sauce, we like it juicy and I also had added baby corn, water chestnuts, mushrooms and pea pods.  It was delicious. This was very good. Also gets lots of stars for being nutritious and quick. I only had half the soy sauce but it was still great. Looking forward to trying it again with fresh ginger. This is a keeper and is going in my "Working Woman" cookbook on recipezaar.

Easy and yummy, one that I will make again. I substituted 1 tsp fresh grated ginger for the ground ginger in the recipe. FYI, this recipe took me 55 minutes from start to plating - a little longer than the recipe states. Definitely worth the effort though!

Very good Recipe indeed! I made a few changes used chicken breast, added Mrs. Dash extra spicy seasoning with cornstarch and garlic powder for just a little zing and omitted water with the mix. This was a perfect weeknight dinner.  It was so easy and delicious!  Having teenagers, I doubled the recipe and they gobbled it up!  This will DEFINITELY be part of our rotation.  The only change I would make is to use low sodium soy sauce next time.  Thanks for a great recipe!
Did anyone find this cut of meat to be extremely tough and bland?  The flavor was good, but i'll definitely use a different cut of beef next time.

Great recipe, my husband and kids loved it. I added more veggies, button mushrooms, sweet mayan onions, sliced red and yellow bell peppers and topped with 1/4 cup of fresh spinach. Sprinkled with red pepper flakes. Delish

Excellent!!  I doubled the sauce, added fresh ginger, extra garlic, spinach, carrots and scallions...  yummmmmmmm....
Thanks so very much!

This is a really good base but is very flexible if you want to change it to suite your tastes.  I made a few additions. I added fresh water chestnuts, carrots, mushrooms, and bean sprouts because i think every dish can use more veggie. Also used fresh garlic (3 cloves total). I added just a dash of red pepper flakes and a little sesame oil, and like many others suggested I tossed the cornstarch with the beef minus the water. My roommates said it tasted like it had come from a restaurant.

This was fantastic!  It tasted just like a restaurant.  I've been looking for good Chinese recipes because my daughter has a nut allergy so we can't go out for Chinese anymore.  I'm a novice cook, but this was easy and delicious.  I did have to use more oil than was called for, but I didn't change anything else!
The only change I made was use fresh garlic and fresh ginger. This is super easy to make and tastes fantastic! I used frozen broccoli that I first defrosted. Thanks so much for posting this.

This recipe is so simple and yummy! My hubby and I have had it several times and we both really like it. So simple and easy. I really like that is uses most ingredients you have on hand. I made it tonight (again!) and added red pepper this time...can't wait to try it! Highly recommend this one!!
What an easy and tasty meal!  I used fresh garlic and ginger, but made everything else as directed.  I felt this needed some spice, so I will add some cayenne next time.  Thanks!

Very easy meal to throw together.  Husband thought the meat could have been more flavorful - maybe it was the beef I bought or the cornstarch technique (I made a recipe in the past using cornstarch like that and he didn't like that either).  I added water chestnuts and served with fried rice (had white rice last night).  He ate all the veggies and left a plate of beef :(  Oh well at least he got some veggies in!!  
In the future I will either add more spices to the cornstarch or skip the meat all together!  Thanks for a great sauce!!

This was great; however, I feel that it was because of an addition I made, after reading other reviews. Otherwise, I followed the recipe, as written, and my son asked me how much of it he could gobble up! Rave reviews, from him, too!
Outstanding, thank you for the recipe! Tastes like restaurant quality!

Awesome recipe!  I made it exactly as written, except doubled it and added about 1/4 cup of teriyaki marinade in with the soy sauce.  Served with fried rice and even 3 year old DD had seconds!  :)  Oh, next time I will add some water chestnuts and mushrooms as well.
wonderful! easy! tasted great!  i used vension steaks since we have so much on hand and you couldn't even tell!!!  i added a can of mushrooms and waterchestnuts as well.  will make again soon!

Great recipe. Easy to adjust for individual tastes. As suggested by other cooks I used fresh ginger and went half and half with the soy and teriyaki sauce. Made this recipe for my family last night and we all gobbled it up, even my picky 3 year old.  I added 1/3 cup of beef broth to help mellow out the soy sauce.  Other than that, I followed the recipe exact.
A keeper ... made as directed except for adding water chestnuts (sliced), carrots (cut in diagonal rounds), and green pepper (sliced). THANK YOU!

This was SOOOO good!  Huge hit with our family...not a fan of asian, but loved this!  Used tri-tip for the beef and added thinly sliced red peppers to the broc/onion mix.  Following a previous review, added about 3/4 cup beef broth...and topped it all off with chopped green onions.  A keeper!
Tasty! Very salty and kind of bland as is. I added some hot sauce and that made it delicious!
Very good recipe.  I agree with others that the sauce could be doubled and will try this next time.
This was the best broccoli beef recipe I've tried.  Great flavor, easy to prepare, and thank goodness, no odd ingredients!  Thanks for sharing!
This was very good.  I doubled the sauce so it was a little salty so I think next time I will use half water and half soy sauce.

this was good, but not authentic-tasting. maybe the meat should be marinaded?  i did omit a little of the soy sauce and added a touch of beef broth as other posts recommended, but don't feel it affected the taste much. dh liked it, but it just didn't hit the spot for me... sorry.

sauce was sooo good!

I tried this too. But I added some veggie medley. It was really good.  My hsband loved it but, the next time im going to put more salt in the rice or just use a seasoned brown rice
Very good.  Needs a few modifications.  The cornstarch coating on the meat left it a little gummy.  Would cut down on that.  The sauce was good.  Will make again.
This was a great, great tasting recipe.  Had good flavor, I stuck to the recipe and didn't change anything.  So good!!!

I feel a little silly rating this because I don't actually include the beef.  I make this for my vegetarian daughter who loves broccoli.  The sauce is a total winner, and she asks me to fix it at least once a week and then takes leftovers with rice for her school lunch.
Great recipe! Easy to make and great flavor. We loved the sauce. Thanks for sharing!

Great stuff!  I substituted the broccoli with red peppers, carrot shreds and green onions since I'm not a huge fan of broccoli.  The sauce was thick and sweet and delicious. Very good!  I made just a couple small changes, to suit my family's taste.  I increased the garlic powder to 1 teaspoon (one can never have too much garlic!) Thank you for posting this here.
My family loves this recipe.  I sometimes make it with chicken and add other veggies.  You can hide some really healthy veggies like kale in it easily.

This is definitely a keeper.  I made it with sirlion tips and added red pepper.  Doubled the sauce as another reviewer had said and it was fantastic.  Served over white rice and along side a salad.  Thanks for posting.

This recipe easily rivals the beef & broccoli found at ANY local Chinese restaurant. My family really liked this recipe
Great recipe the whole family loved!! We will definately be making this one again only next time more of it so I might have some leftovers.
This came out great. Realized I had run out of rice, so I cooked up some linguine and tossed it in w/the beef mixture. Ended up with a beef lo mein-type dish. Everyone loved it!
really just perfect!  I used real garlic and real ginger--scrumptious!
this was exactly what it said it would be! EASy and amazing. iwas wary of ingredients but when it was done, my husband thought i put Take out in a bowl!!!

This is the kind of recipe I have been lookng for. As other reviews, next time I make this I will double the sauce.  Thank you very much :)

You dont need another 5 star but you are going to get it. this was wonderful. My husband sliced the meat very thin. I used some fresh grated ginger and 1 clove of grated garlic as well. really good!

My youngest thought I bought it from a Chinese restaurant and reheated it.

This was so good! Wow better than the one I buy at the restaurant. Now I can make it at home.

I LOVE this recipe! It was soooo yummy!

Thank you Chris!
Very good! I used less meat & added red pepper & fresh garlic. Nice to have ethnic recipes that use kitchen staples.
This is a keeper, for sure.  I'm not one to usually say this, but it could use just a little kick...maybe 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes?  Very very good though as is!!

This is very good. Like a previous reviewer I also added 2 minced garlic cloves and minced fresh ginger and a little sesame oil.  I also wanted a little kick so I added a couple of pinches of red crushed pepper. I will definitely be making this again.
Boring. My family normally loves Beef Broccoli Stir-fry but this lacked flavor. We thought it tasted like a brown gravy sauce.

A great $10 family meal worth five stars for both ease and taste. This is the first time I made it, and I scaled it up for six servings. It was absolutely delicious, but I would add a bit more water next time because the family likes more "juice".

This is the best ever!! I can't wait to make this again and again!

This is the first time I've ever made a dish like this and I Love it!! Next time I will add a little heat to it.

this was a pretty solid recipe, i followed exactly but at the last minute added some red pepper flakes to the soy sauce mixture..good move!

This was better than the Chinese restaurant!  I used leftover rare eye round roast and marinated in the soy, water, and 2 cloves of garlic.   I added a little heat with crushed red pepper and it was DELICIOUS!

pretty good. i followed the recipe, but ended up making more gravy for it. i used fresh slices of ginger (used a potato peeler to make 15 thin slices) which was great, and then sliced up a red pepper, roasted it in the oven for 15 and added that in with some chive.

Easy and my family loved it!
Wow!  This recipe really works. Tastes authentic - My husband said it was better than restaurant Chinese and no MSG!  No leftovers either!

We love this!! So easy and quick. It's my husband's favorite and I love being able to make it fresh for him. I usually double the sauce and use a lower sodium soy sauce. This is a great recipe! I will make again, maybe with chicken next time. Yum!!!
I really liked this as well.  I would add a little heat with fresh chili paste next time.

Excellent...finally a recipe for beef and broccoli that is great!!! Only thing I did differently was skip the dredging of the beef in cornstarch/water/garlic powder. Outstanding recipe, thanks for sharing....still saying "yummy"!

This doesn't need another review but it was that good. I've tried other recipes that said they were as good as a restaurant and found them to be lacking. This one was. My husband, whom does not like chinese food raved. Thank you for really having a restaurant quality recipe and sharing it with all of us! Outstanding. Probably one of the best recipes I've pulled off 'zaar.
Very easy and delicious. My husband said this taste better than the chinese restaurants around here in AK.
This was great!! Sooo simple soooo yummy!! Thank you!!

This was the flavor of Chinese "beef and broccoli" that I was looking for. If you are looking for authentic beef and broccoli, try this recipe. Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly. Will definitely make again.

Simple and delicious, thanks! Also easy to adapt to more challenging diets. Something hot like chilli powder or seeds is really recommended!

While adding this to one of my upcoming menu's I noticed I've never rewiewed this.  It's become one our favorite stir fries and is made often.  Super easy and super delicious!

The timing on this one is perfect and the onions and broccoli come out with just the right texture. I like to use peanut or sesame oil when making this dish to add just another little layer of flavor.
Very good! Enjoyed this dish very much. I used frozen broccoli and it still came out delish.
I just made this for dinner made only two changes, first I used chicken instead of beef and ginger freshly grated. YUMMY!! can we give it 6 or more stars :9

This recipe is absolutely delicious!!!!  I only changed it a little due to personal preferences. I added colored peppers just because I love them in stir fry's. They add a lot flavor and color. I will be making this quite often, and this will be my beef stir fry recipe from now on!!!

ok well as i wright this review i am so enjoying this meal, i did make a different meat selection i choose thinly cut flank stakes and still turned out great and i took the oil out and used sesame oil

Well, after making this dish, I wondered why I even bothered.  Wait, don't get me wrong...I NEVER order or eat beef and broccoli stir fry at Chinese restaurants. This was the best Beef and Broccoli ever!!  Easy to make and delicious!
The whole family loved it, very easy.  I used flank steak.

After I made this dish, my husband emphatically told me I should work in an Asian restaurant :) He LOVED it, and I'll be trying it with chicken next time. I don't typically like beef, but even I enjoyed this dish! Wonderful.

This recipe is just as good as the local chinese place!  I thought this had very good flavor, but the sauce was a little too thick for my taste.  Next time I will decrease the cornstarch in the sauce.  My toddler loved it!

AMAZING!! I will be honest, I have never made this recipe with the beef that it calls for, I use ground turkey. I am usually a little wary of any recipe stating that it's "the best" but, honestly...this really is pretty dang awesome! Like other people have done, I used the powder garlic for the beef mixture as well adding 3 minced garlic cloves when cooking the onions. This was FANTASTIC !!  I did skip the water at the beginning and added some fresh garlic to the oil and sauteed for a bit before adding the beef. I also added some sliced carrots and zucchini to bulk up the veggies.  Rave reviews from everyone once again.  Thanks! :)
This was amazing. My husband wouldn't stop eating it and kept telling me that I needed to make it for him again. I will be making this again soon!

This was honestly really good!! Beef and Broccoli is a family favorite in our house!! Kid friendly and delicious!! My husband loved this sauce.  I think next time I will add some carrots and cauliflower.  Was so easy and quick.  A Keeper.

I really don't think you need to double the recipe to get more sauce...I just added more water and the sauce cooked up to the consistency I needed. (but then, I don't like my food swimming in sauces!)  Served over a mix of wild and brown rice....I would do this one again!!

This is the first stir fry I've ever made and the first I've ever tried. It was amazing. I used 20oz of frozen broccoli florets, less onion and eye of round steak. We served over rice. It was soooo good! I can't wait to have it tomorrow for lunch!
This was awesome.  I even made it with pork and it came out good.  I always find myself adding a tiny bit more soy sauce then called for.  Delicious though!

I made this for dinner tonight and I thought it was great! I made a few changes based on my tastes and what I had on hand. I used 1 and a half cups of left over shredded turkey, added 1 large carrot cut into matchsticks, added 1 ts of crushed red pepper, doubled the sauce and tossed it with 1/2 a lb of linguini. Start to finish dinner was done in less than 1/2 an hour which is always great! The only thing I think I'd do differently is use a little less ginger next time. Over all it was really good!
Thanks so much for posting!
Yummy and quick. Substituted fresh garlic and ginger for the ground. Added carrots. Super delicious and easy. A definite keeper, thanks for posting.
Soo good, if your looking for something new to do with round steak, this is it!! Will cook this again and again! Added some carrots also like others have, i do recommend it :)

Great recipe. The only change I made was choice of steak. We used ribeye because they looked really fresh at the meat counter! Other than that, made as posted and just as good as any restaurant. Thanks for sharing!

I enjoyed this (as leftovers after derby scrimmage) when my daughter finished cooking it for me. I had finished step 2 when I had to leave. All of us agreed that the sauce was a little too thick. I realize, however, that she might not have understood exactly how much cornstarch and water she still needed to add. I think I would make this again as written before trying to change it. The balance of flavors was good.
Delicious and easy!  Actually thought it tasted better than some of the restaurants' beef & broccoli.  The sugar was a nice touch.  Gave it a little different flavor but wasn't overly sweet.

I loved this.  I pretty much tailored it to what I had which was beef cut for a stew and some frozen broccoli.  I didn't have cornstarch so I subbed with double the amount of flour and more water.  I'll probably skip or use less next time.  I also used minced garlic and added red pepper flakes.  Got to use my trusty wok and added Worcestershire sauce to the soy that I only had a 1/4 cup of and perhaps too much ginger since it was powder, but I love it.  To sweeten and add more spice I used Tijuana flats Georgia peach and Vidalia onion sauce and some honey since I had no brown sugar.  All in all it was easy and delicious and will be made again.
Very easy to make.  Great taste.

Cooking this recipe was my first time ever attempting stir-fry. It turned out great!

I would use a low sodium soy sauce next time because it tasted a bit salty. I would also add more vegetables such as carrots, peppers, bean sprouts, etc. These are personal preferences though. The recipe by itself was still great.

This recipe has cured me of my curse with Chinese dishes. This was easy, precise and delicious. I followed the recipe exactly, except for using fresh garlic. Next time I will marinate the meat as suggested by another reviewer. Absolutely wonderful.
I think this was great. I added yellow pepper, water chestnuts, and carrots made this even better!!!
Good, easy, meal, but definitely needs a bit more garlic and ginger than in the recipe.  Next time I'll use minced garlic and at least double the ginger.

Not that this recipe needs to be reviewed, but I made it last night and WHOA! So yummy!  I am not a huge fan of Asian cuisine, but I had everything in my kitchen to make this and it turned out awesome!  I added some chopped carrots and sliced mushrooms to the mix.  Thank you for sharing this recipe!
LOVE IT! Made this with noodles, so so yummy! :)

Simply wonderful. I did add some sesame oil to the sauce at the end, but it was just great. We'll add some pepper flakes next time to up the heat, just for preference. We will also be adding two more cups of broccoli, again for preference.

OMG this is so good.  As the reviewers before me, I used the sauce to marinate the london broil steak I used for several hours and then made another batch of sauce for the cooking.  I used fresh ginger grated but next time I will use more then I added, didn't measure but I could have used more, I am a little afraid of ginger as it can be overpowering if too much is used.  I added scallions at the very end of cooking and everything was just delicious.  My husband could not get over how tender the meat was, as well as flavorful.  I want to thank all the previous reviewers for their hints and opinions, they were very helpful.  I want to try with chicken and shrimp in the future.  Try this recipe, you won't be disappointed.

Yummy, what a great dish, so easy and delish. I made the sauce and used it for a marinade (omitting the starch) and used a couple garlic cloves, red pepper flakes and a smidge extra ginger. I did however make another batch of sauce for the the end but instead of more soy sauce I used beef broth, so it wasn't too salty and it was great, little extra water helped as well. I will make this again and again, trying different meats and playing with it a bit. So Simple and So Good!!

Delicious, fresh, and simple, yet still satisfying if you have a craving for takeout. Five stars (from me and the husband) for the dish. We used a cast iron skillet and ended up de-glazing the pan with red wine because we do that every chance we get and it usually never hurts the dish. :) Also used fresh ginger and garlic and marinated the beef strips for a little while, as mentioned in other reviews. This is a recipe we'll definitely make again.

First time cooking this and it was a great hit with the whole family!  I'm not a great cook either however it was easy to put together, fast, and it was very inexpesive to make!!  Thank you for sharing, deffinately going to make this again.

My family loved this recipe.  Next time, I will take the advice of the other chefs and use london broil (marinated), light dredging of the meat and fresh garlic along with some additional fresh veges.  I think it's a wonderful go-to meal for the family!
i didn't enjoy it, but maybe i over-cooked the beef.  recipe was simple to make.

This is delicious~~I would give it more stars with the exception of the fact that the nutrition values do not match up with MyFoodDiary.com. Great with chicken breast too!  I used toasted sesame oil and that was the only change.  otherwise, it's great.
This was really tasty.  My family loved it and it is worth making again and again.  So easy, too!

It really satisfied my craving for Asian food!  Chris, thank you for sharing your recipe!  It's a keeper!!!

wow....i've been trying to avoid using pre-packaged sauces/mixes and processed foods these days.  wanted to try to make my own broccoli beef without that usual packaged spice/sauce mix that probably is loaded with MSG......i found this.  WONDERFUL.  i followed some of the suggestions and marinated the beef first.  and since money is so tight these days, i actually used leftover beef (rare) from a roast i had fixed previously. (cant wait to try this with a nice fresh piece of kansas beef!)  i then attempted to "dredge" the wet marinated beef in the garlic, cornstarch and water mixture (it was a little weird lol, but it worked).  this is an easy dish, excellent flavor.  the ONLY thing i changed is i added a few drops of sesame oil to the vegetable oil when i stir fried for a bit more flavor.  excellent.  thank you chris from kansas!!!!
great recipe. worked well for me thanks. :o)

I am not a very good cook. Baking, I'm super comfortable with but cooking? Not so much. So when I was determined to make my boyfriend (who is an excellent cook) dinner for him when he came home from work, I knew I needed to find a good recipe. This is it!!

I marinated the beef like a lot of people before me did and cooked up a bunch of pasta noodles instead of rice but it turned out SO amazing! My boyfriend not only had seconds but ate it for lunch at work the next day! This recipe gave me the courage to try cooking more. Thank you so much for this recipe!!
My husband and I LOVE this recipe. Since the first time I made this, I have also made it with other vegetables and also with chicken instead of beef.

This was a fantastic meal!  For the beef, I used some thin rib-eyes steaks so it would be super tender and would not have to be marinated. I served  the stir fry over buttered noodles garnished with chives. This was very delicious! I'll be making this again.
OMG!! Made this one tonight. Tasted great!! This one is a keeper!! Made it with fresh onions and fresh bell peppers and fresh ginger. Used low sodium soy sauce. Everything else was the same.

Excellent, I doubled the sauce, added apple juice and garlic and marinated the meat for a day-wonderful, next time im going to try to add noodles, bean sprouts, water chestnuts and whatnot. Thanks for the post!
Fantastic recipe..  I'm not usually a review writer but this was truly simple yet delicious.  This will work w/ any protein substitute i.e. chicken, shrimp.
OMG! Thank you It was delicious.  It was quick and  easy to make.

By far, the best beef and broccoli recipe that I have found on the internet (including those from "celebrity" chefs)! This recipe is very tasty with an excellent blend of flavors. I highly recommend this recipe for even the most avid Asian food enthusiast.
Fabulous! The beef marinade actually tenderized the meat. Perfect recipe, easy to make and has become the new favorite.
This was pretty good.  I made exactly as directed.  I had trouble with the steak being tough but probably because I bought a cheaper cut of meat.
This was too bland for me :(
Loved this recipe.  I didn't have beef so I used some left over boneless pork loin chops that I had chopped up and frozen.  It was absolutely delicious.

Wow! This was really good! I don't think you really needed another review however, it was sooo delish...I just had too! Thanks for posting such an easy recipe...also...tried it with chicken...that was really good too!
This recipe was beyond EASY!!! I love it. I used shrimp instead of beef but all in all it even taste great!!!
Loved it! I'm an asian food lover and this made the grade for sure!!

This recipe surprised me even with all the accolades.   I had quite a bit of leftover london broil as well as broccoli, and wanted an easy recipe.  I followed the recipe exactly.  Dried garlic and dried ginger?  It was delicious.  The only change I would make next time would be to use less or no cornstarch for the initial marinade.  Thank you Chris!
it was great! the whole family praised me for it! swapped out broccoli for pepers and onions this time... still amazing!

I have been on a kind of Asian homemade take-out freak out and this has come the closest to what I'd expect at a restaurant.  Really, super easy too!  I've actually made this twice now (both times turned out great) and once used sesame oil - not drastic but a bit more take-out-y.  Thanks!

Great recipe!!! Super easy & quick & DELICIOUS!!! My family loved it!!!
LOVE this recipe! Made it for my wife and she loved it! Simple and easy. Very cheap to make for people on a tight budget! Thank you!
Very good! Easy to make.  Just a little too salty. Will use low sodium soy sauce next time.

The change I would make is either add more water to have leftover sauce OR use a reduced sodium soy sauce as it was just too salty.  Otherwise, the flavor notes are spot on of an authentic beef & broccoli.

I gave this 2 stars because the way the beef was cooked was delicious (the 2 stars)  HOWEVER, the sauce was WAY WAY WAY too salty! Almost threw this whole meal in the trash until I remembered a little trick - I spun the sauce off it in my salad spinner! I then basically started over with the sauce adding some water and wine vinegar. Salvaged the meal barely. Next time I will cook the beef this way and make my own sauce.

Give this recipe a try - you will not regret it!!!

"Awesome" (per my dinner guests) and I have to agree whole heartedly!! It definitely had an authentic taste to it. Super easy recipe that exemplifies that keeping it simple really works!

Although, like many reviewers, I did make a few changes as well:
sweet brown rice flour rather than cornstarch, minced garlic rather than powder, grated fresh ginger root rather than powder, olive oil rather than vegetable oil, organic cane sugar rather than brown sugar, organic reduced sodium soy sauce, and I added a teaspoon of Better than Boulloin Beef base.

I think that with quality beef there is no need to marinade the beef. Dredging as instructed is the way to go to ensure a good base for the sauce. It also seals in the moistness to prevent chewy beef -thereby ensuring tender beef!

I paired it with Jasmine tea spiked with Japanese Cherry wine ... which was a huge hit as well. The kiddos had Japanese sodas ; )

I didn't think this tasted the same as the restaurants here but this was very good.  I made it as is with the exception of reducing the ground ginger to about 1/3-1/2 tsp. which was perfect. One tsp. would have been overwhelming.  I also added some minced garlic when I stir fried the broccoli.  Need to definitely marinate or season the beef which I didn't do.  Having more flavor in the beef would have made this a 5 star recipe.  10/18/12 UPDATE:  Instead of doing Step 1, I mixed 3 Tbs. cornstarch, 3 Tbs. soy sauce, 1 Tbs. brown sugar and 1/2 tsp garlic powder and marinated the beef in this mixture for one hour.  I followed the rest of recipe except added 3 minced garlic to the broccoli and onions during the last 2 minutes and reduced the ground ginger to 1/3 - 1/2 tsp.  Yummy!  My husband liked this better than the Chinese restaurants.  Thank you, Chris, for posting this recipe.
Simple, tasty, and filling.  Excellent.

This Recipe was very quick, easy and delicious, I made just a few changes, I added a jar of green giant mushrooms and used beef stock instead of water.  It turned out greattttttt!  Made the Hubby very happy. 8-)  Thanks for sharing.
Add some big chunks of bell pepper and it's perfect.

MmmmMmmm....This hit the spot! This is a very different recipe than what I usually use for beef stir fry. I usually add sherry and sesame oil,leaving out the brown sugar. This was a nice mild sauce that glazed the meat to perfection. Chuck steak was just the right cut of meat, it was soooo tender. This meal was simple to put together and delicious. I'll be making this again. Thanks for posting the recipe.

I have made beef and broccoli numerous times using a tried and true recipe, but I decided to try this as a new recipe since it seems like a lot of people really like this recipe.  But my family is not among them.  I followed the recipe with the exception of using fresh garlic and ginger in place of powdered.  The end result is what I would call too sweet and mostly tasteless.  The recipe that I have used many times that I think is much better calls for more fresh ginger and garlic, beef broth in place of water, and oyster sauce in addition to some soy sauce and no sugar.
I love this recipe, Its amazing and delicious. Good substitutes or partner with medium cook liver. So juicy. I also love the sweetness and crunchiness of broccoli.
Good eye Chris from Kansas.....this is awesome.....I'm a rookie chef and this was quick, easy and delicious!!

Really good and easy recipe. The only thing I did different was to add 1-2 tbsp soy sauce to the garlic, water, cornstarch mixture and then let the meat marinade in the mixture for a couple hours. Otherwise I followed it exactly. I would highly recommend using Kikkomen soya sauce. To me it had more of a restaurant quality taste.
Excellent flavor with simple  ingredients! Versatile, too -can add mushrooms, matchstick carrots, if you want.

This recipe is quick and easy and tastes good.  I was looking for something to make in my new wok without having to buy a lot of ingredients and for this all I had to buy was cornstarch.  I didn't dredge the beef and I parboiled the broccoli before stir frying but otherwise I followed the recipe.  It turned out well and was tasty.  I wouldn't say it's the best, for the time and effort its a great meal, and an easily modifiable recipe.  I worked with a Chinese family for a long time so I'm comparing this to authentic Chinese dishes and I wasn't wowed, but I'll almost definitely make it again.
Great!!! I didn't have the ginger, and it still turned out. I also marinated my beef in teriyaki for an hour before cutting it and dragging it in the cornstarch/garlic mix. Tasted amazing!!

My 15 year old daughter said "You know, I'm not  a big fan of stir-fry but this is really good!" It was a hit! I used 4 cups of broccoli and then 2 cuts of additional veggies (matchstick carrots, snow peas, etc.)
Omg!!! The best recipe ever!!! I made this tonight for Mr and my mom and it was so good we had to make another batch!!!! Thanks for the recipe! :)

First time round so I cooked it exactly to the recipe,I found it to be very easy and so tasty will become a regular in my house.  Thanks to the reviews posted will be trying to substitute chicken & seaseme oil, add capsicum etc.   Cheers for sharing.

So simple and so delish!  My only preference/twist is to use ground beef and skip the dredging in cornstarch.  Just cook the beef and garlic and drain fat. Also serve over spaghetti noodles.  More filling and fun to eat w/chopsticks:)
Made this tonight, it was awesome. Doubled the recipe and it was a hit. Thanks!
My teenage boys really enjoy making--and eating--this one.  It's quick and easy.
Absolutely wonderful! Glad I found the recipe.
This was such a simple and delicious recipe...will be adding to my personal cookbook

Tried this tonight, and it was awesome!  Added a few flakes of dried red pepper for zest as others had recommended and omitted onion (hubby hates).  Really is delicious,  Will make again - this will replace my old "La Choy" recipe for Beef & Broccoli!

This is a delicious recipe, but I did make a couple of changes.  We love garlic, so I marinated the beef in the soy sauce & garlic & meat tenderizor (my round steak seemed tough) for about an hour.  We also like more sauce, so I used 1 1/2 cup water with a couple of beef bouillion cubes dissolved & increased the cornstarch to thicken.  Also added about 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes. I will definately make this again & again!!

This is very good. I felt that you didn't need to marinade like others said because the beef in the gravy has enough flavor already. I made sure that the meat was browned to give it a nicer texture and flavor.  I doubled the gravy (except for the ginger) and added 1/3 cup of chicken broth to tone down the strong flavor of the soy sauce (lite soy sauce was fine) and added cornstarch to thicken to a nice gravy.
Outstanding. I grated fresh ginger and garlic, otherwise followed recipe exactly. This is so tasty and satisfying. No MSG and Gluten Free. LOVE IT!

I was looking for something to use some leftover grilled teriyaki flank steak strips and this handled it just great with wonderful results. I found this recipe very easy to make. I added more garlic though as we are garlic lover's! Will make again!
Tried this today, it is amazing!!!!  Been looking for a good recipe for b&b for a while now and am very happy I tried this one!!  I will def make again.
This recipe was awesome! I doubled the amount of sauce and marinated the meat in half of it for a few hours. Very glad I did!

I agree with others about this being better than any local Chinese restaurant. This was the best my fiancee and I ever had. I used a London Briol that I marinated in soy sauce over night. I also left out the ginger but everything else I did according to the recipe. This will be a dish I will serve for guests for a long time. Thank you to the original chef!!!

This was amazing. Absolutely delicious, and everyone in the office commented on how good it smelled. I didn't use round steak as I thought it would be too tough. I used strip loin and cut it into thin strips, discarding the fat. I halved the recipe but I kept the amount of soy sauce mixture the same, as I like my dishes saucy, especially over rice. Delicious!!

Really good! Even my kids liked it!<br/><br/>I did spice it up and add a bit more garlic (that's how we roll...)<br/><br/>Here are my notes:<br/>I put the beef in a bag and added the cornstarch and garlic powder to coat - then added 2 tbsp rice vinegar with water. Marinated for 30 minutes. I used many of the suggestions from the reviews and this came out excellent except when using oyster sauce, I should have cut the soy sauce amount in half.  I used all fresh ingredients, no spices. I also used beef stock for the sauce and added fresh ginger, fresh garlic, and oyster and Sriracha Hot Chilli sauce. Pretty good! I followed the recipe as is with two modifications -- 1. I used chicken breast instead of beef and 2. I used fresh garlic. Overall, it tasted good, but I have another recipe (that I couldn't find!) that tastes better to me. Until I find the other one, I will use this though.
This is a really good weeknight recipe that everyone enjoys, including the picky eaters in my family. I add carrots for colour and double the sauce.
I made this last night, followed the recipe exactly and it was really delicious. I will definitely make this again.

This recipe gets 5 stars for ease, but I found it lacking in overall appeal.  It was missing some heat for sure...and although it may have been chef's error, the meat was too tough. I made this recipe as is. My husband loved this dish at our favorite restaurant- we miss you Oriental Table! I made it last night and we both were so happy our favorite Chinese comfort food was back in our lives.

Closest to restaurant flavor that I've found!  I used less oil than it called for and it was still very good.  The meat should be tenderized first or marinated as others have suggested. Would not cook the veggies in oil but maybe add a little water to let them steam as the oil with the meat is more than enough.  Very kid friendly!

Absolutely delish! I did what others suggested and marinated the beef in the sauce (minus the cornstarch) and added fresh garlic and ginger. I was running short on time so only marinated for an hour. The beef was so tender and flavorful. I would agree just as good or better than any take out!

this is surprisingly good for what seemed such a simple recipe , it really could pass for chinese take out.  I added mushrooms and also added minced garlic and fresh minced ginger and sesame oil to the sauce.

this is the most amazing recipe my kids ate all of it so I had to make more

easy and good. It made the whole house smell yummy and everyone in the family liked it!

This recipe was definitely the bomb....Best beef broccoli I've ever eaten or prepared for that matter. The kids are saying that daddy (me) should cook more often lol.  No offense to the rest of the guys but it pays to listen to women sometimes...

Easy and fast, good go-to weeknight recipe.

Sure helps when we have a craving for Chinese and don't feel like going to the city.

This is the best recipe ever!  I made it tonight for my daughter and son-in-law, who had flown on business all day, and for my 9-and 10-year-old grandchildren who were a bit skeptical. Really is a wonderful recipe!  Very easy to make and my family of 6 ALL enjoyed it.  Made my night when my lovely wife told me over dishes "Well, we need to add that one to the recipe book."  Awesome!!!

This is the BEST beef broccoli! The sauce taste delicious!

Hubby said its better than take out. More meat less broccoli ;) I took the advice of others and marinated beef before, used minced garlic, added some sesame oil and doubled up on the sauce. Very good, will def make again!

Stir fried this up this twice before I decided to post a review.  Made it exactly as recipe posted.  Second time I made it, I was convinced it beat any other recipe I have tried in the past! My VERY FIRST attempt at cooking Chinese and I was not disappointed! It was delicious. Next time I will double the recipe for leftovers.

excellent, easy, fast!  3 of my favorite things for weeknight dinners!  i too marinated meat and drained before i put the meat in with the cornstarch water mixture.  also added fresh garlic which i think added some more authenticity.  really good, will definitely make again!
Exactly as the title describes, BEST and EASY!!  Made several times and always good. I added mushrooms and some sesame oil, and think I'll add fresh garlic next time as well.

So good! Followed recipe as written except for subbing fresh minced garlic/grated ginger and adding a little onion powder to the meat and sesame oil to the sauce. Next time I might double the sauce as a preference.
This taste amazing. I'm a beginner to Asian style meals, and this was easy for me to make, and came out really delicious.

Added about 1/2 a teaspoon of crushed red pepper as well which gave it a nice spice and at the end of cooking, I tossed in about 1/4 cup of scallions. All in all it was a hit. Thank you for the recipe... I'll be making it again with the few adjustments.

I NEVER use vegetable oil, canola oil or a number of the other 'oils' sold on the shelf. Research how they are made and find out how many are only a step away from plastic (that's why there's a difficult coating left on your pans/casserole dishes/skillets), and you shouldn't use them either.  Research is the key! So, needless to say, I did change the 'oil' in this recipe as well. Be sure to check the temps that the oils are best to cook with, too. EVOO is not one to use with this dish. I used Sesame oil, that I happened to have. I'll be researching it after this review though, too. WE'VE got to take back OUR health. Not rely on others to do it for us.

Flavor, texture and taste are FIVE stars. However, the way this is written out as a recipe is unfinished. I am a firm believer of not blaming a chef if I screw up their recipe as it would usually be my fault. But when it comes to baking and you have to, for example, cook a custard, a recipe worth its weight in salt tells you the EXACT size of saucepan you need (if it's too big, your sugar will stick to the bottom and burn no matter how much you stir it, or the ingredients will evaporate) , some sort of guideline as to HOW thick the mixture should be (coats the spoon, leaves a space at the bottom of the pan when you swirl the spoon, etc), approximation of how many minutes the mixture takes to thicken, and this recipe had none of that. I threw out my first mixture and just started over. I used what I figured to be the right size pans (my spaghetti pot for the mixture was WAY too big) kept stirring and just hoped. And I got lucky. My recommendations are to reduce the milk by half a cup and increase the flour by adding a tablespoon at a time, whisking quickly while it's on the stove. My final tip is to strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve when it's done cooking, this will catch any stubborn lumps of flour.

I haven't tried this recipe yet, but I wanted to point out that the nutrition facts clearly state that the splenda blend was not taken into account for the carb count. If you are looking for a good no carb sugar substitute use xylitol. It is the best sugar substitute for baking.

While it is stated that the Splenda Blend is included (it's in the fine print), there really is no excuse not to provide an accurate calculation. Serious LCers care about the counts, and the counts do matter. That said, with all due respect, anyone who blindly accepted the information as it was provided can't have put more that 2 seconds worth of thought into it. Splenda Blend is Splenda (sucralose) mixed with regular sugar (sucrose). Anyone really serious about an LC lifestyle probably wouldn't touch this product with a ten foot pole! But, if an LCer decided to try it out anyway, I would think s/he would be VERY careful to calculate accurately.

For the record, 1/2 cup of Splenda Sugar Blend has 96g of carbs, so 3/4 cup has 144g of carbs! That's for the whole pie, but that's very high (and doesn't include the 20g carbs from the rest of the ingredients). For the total pie (and I'm assuming that the rest of the counts are, in fact, accurate) there are 164g of total carbs, or 161.6g net carbs (after subtracting fiber). Each serving, then, is 20.2 net carbs.

I would ignore the author, and use regular Splenda (although be sure to count the carbs if you use the granular--from the malodextrin used as a filler). Liquid sucralose, which is hard to find in stores (but is available online) has zero carbs.

For those complaining of a bitter taste, try combining at least two different sweeteners (e.g., sucralose and stevia, or sucralose and one of the sugar alcohols like xylitol or erythritol). Combining the sweeteners tends to help reduce the "chemical" taste. It's worth noting that erythritol has the lowest impact on blood sugar of the sugar alcohols, and causes less "problems" than the others.

I hope this helps someone.

Excellent recipe. I've made it two years in a row now. For all the naysayers freaking out about the carb count, maybe you should stop eating substitute foods and either resort yourselves to whole foods only on your strict diet or simply indulge in the real thing. I used stevia instead of splenda and coconut milk instead of cream, and it came out well.  Thanks for the recipe.

I agree with the reader that was upset about the amount of carbs.  Fortunately...I realised this BEFORE I made it.  I used all Splenda, and added a tsp. of maple flavoring to the ingredients. It worked out very well.  Delicious dessert. I'll be making it again. OFTEN!

Seriously have no idea why there are so many complaints about the carbs in this. I for one love this recipe and thank you for going to the trouble of posting this. I'm sorry you had to read the few negative reviews as in my opinion they were not warranted. Thank goodness the majority of people loved this as you can see by the five stars that consistently remain!! Such a fast a delicious recipe!!! *The only tweak was two teaspoons of pumpkin spice instead of the cloves, and baked it 45 minutes.

I had some serious concerns about this.I have recently been on the Atkins diet and this was the first holiday cooking for others with my diet in mind. I was so excited that I had a recipe that did not have an aftertaste. I will make this every Thanksgiving to come and maybe Christmas too!
We liked it!  I used all purpose flour,and left it in the machine for the whole cycle but other than that made it as posted. Thank you.

I also left it in the bread machine for the whole cycle.  It turned out wonderful and was delicious.  My husband's comment was, "You better make another loaf tomorrow because I'm going to eat all of this one."
I have made this in the bread machine and out of it.  Great both ways.  I used bread machine flour for the 3 cups and whole wheat flour for the 1/4 cup and it was still light and delicious!

This bread came out with a velvet-like texture and a wonderful homey flavor.  I did the whole thing in the bread machine on the 1.5 lb. setting and it worked out great.  Served with home-made chicken noodle soup and the whole family loved it.  Made toast with it this morning and that was pretty good, too.  Thanks for sharing!

Wow - this bread is wonderful! I had to add a bit more milk but I think it is because it is a very dry day here. I followed the recipe exactly except for the addition of extra milk and am so pleased with the results! My only concern was that my loaf rose very high in the oven, but it turned out perfect. Delicious, chewy bread. This was a very easy recipe to make. I'll be making it time and time again!

Excellent bread!  I made it to serve with soup and we loved it!  I made the recipe exactly as posted except I left it in the machine and let it bake in there since I was busy.  It rose beautifully and baked up in the machine wonderfully.  This will become a favorite around here!  Thank you for posting the recipe!

Delicious bread - great flavor along with great texture. I baked it in the bread machine and it turned out very nice. It didn't rise much until the very end...I thought it was going to be a flop, but towards the end of the cycle it rose nice and high and baked up wonderfully.

This was delicious bread!!  We made it in the bread machine as some others did here... but the first time it did not rise enough using the machine's defaults.  We made it again, and added 15 minutes to the final rise time, and it came out absolutely perfect.  We have made it again since then, and it has become a favorite!  Thanks so much Iva for this delicious bread recipe!  Dianne

First of all I didn't have the bread machine to mix it and then I found out I didn't have bread flour so used self-rising flour instead and made it and kept my fingers crossed!  Well it was DEVOURED!  Between DH and my three DS, there is none left.  I had one slice and it is so good.  I will definitely be making this bread again.

This will definitely be my bread of choice from now on. The texture is perfect. I love the slightly sweet taste of the honey. I subbed 1 cup of whole wheat for the bread flour. I did everything else as the recipe stated. This deserves 10 stars. I am going to try this with 2 cups of wheat flour the next time as it had a very light texture with the 1 cup of whole wheat that I added.  Thanks Iva Day.
This is wonderfull bread !!  My kids loved it!  It made a HUGE loaf!

I love homemade bread, but dont make it quite enough.  But after finding this bread recipe, and the ease of it, I will be making a loaf of it everyday.  My family loves it, and I love it.  I had a slice this morning toasted with butter and it was divine!  Thanks so much for this wonderful recipe that will be used over and over again in my home.
I forgot to mention my subsitutions -- 1 cup SOY MILK (regular), 3-1/4 cups WHITE FLOUR, 4 TB MILK FREE MARGARINE.
An excellent recipe! I used it to make rolls .. My husband loved it as well .. I chose this recipe because of the cute title, and I am glad I did, thanks!

I didn't have a bread machine so I just did it the traditional way.  It was very delicious and the bread was nice and fluffy.   One day I might experiment and add more honey and see if that makes it sweeter, although it's perfectly fine the way it is now.  Thanks!
Great recipe!  I've made this bread at least 4 times now and has come out perfect each time.  If you want the bread more sweet add another teaspoon of honey.

Great bread! I used 1 1/4 cups of whole wheat flour and 2 cups of all purpose. Using the comments of other reviewers, I used my bread machine for the whole process, choosing the 1.5 lb. 'grain' setting. The bread has wonderful, sweet flavor and the additional of the whole wheat flour gave it a chewy and delicious crust. I will definately make this again.

This was the first recipe I tried in our new bread machine and it turned out great. I used 1 1/2 cups of wheat flour and 1 3/4 cups all purpose flour and just left it in the bread machine the whole time. Just delicious and couldn't have been easier.

I wish I could give them credit too! I made this in my bread machine using the sweet setting and out came a perfect loaf! I used margarine and 1 cup of whole wheat flour. Just finished a sandwich made with this and it was just a nice as yesterday, not dry at all. Thank you Iva Day for sharing this delicious recipe!
Wonderful flavor.  I would have liked it to be a little lighter.  Will make again!

A wonderful loaf of bread. I has a distinct butter smell when baking, and a slight sweet flavor of honey after. Thank you for sharing. I let this go all the way through in my bread machine on the basic cycle on light crust.

This bread is delicious!!  I made the recipe exactly as written and it turned out perfect.  I used my bread machine on the "dough" cycle and after the first raise, I removed the dough and let it raise again in the bread pan.  The loaf was baked in a cast iron loaf pan and the crust was beautiful.  I will definitely be making this bread frequently.  Thank you so much for sharing this fantastic recipe!!

Oh my goodness!!  This bread is absolutely amazing.  It is the best bread I have ever produced using my breadmaker.  I used the breadmaker to bake it instead of the oven.  It was so deliciously soft and perfect!  My DH couldn't stop eating it.  I plan on making a second loaf tonight already :)  Thanks so much for a fabulous recipe that I will use over and over.  I substitute about 3/4 cup whole wheat flour and it still turned out so light and tasty.
This has to be one of the best bread recipes I've used.  It's great for bread, rolls and especially good for cinnamon rolls!!!  Wouldn't change a thing!!! Thanks.

This is excellent bread.  Love the taste and texture.  I ate 2 slices right out of the machine with my apple butter (#93886).   MMMMMmmmmm...comfort food on a chilly day.  I know I will be making this many times.  Thanks for a great recipe.
This wasn't as good as I expected.  For the name of the recipe, I was looking for a sweeter honey taste, and this just tasted like white bread.

Lovely white bread recipe. I ran out of milk, so I used about 3/4 c of buttermilk instead. Also, I used just 1 tsp yeast as that's all I had on hand. Beatiful soft texture. There's about a third of the loaf left, which I'll use for french toast in the morning. Thanks for posting!

Fabulous! I don't have a bread machine so I prepared the recipe by heating milk, letting the active dry yeast rise for 10 min. Added everything but flour and mixed, added flour by half cups (I needed extra)Let mixer run for 6 minutes. Let dough rise for 60 minutes and then followed the recipe directions from there. I followed the advice of other reviewers and added more honey. Smell: amazing. Taste: just like mom used to make. I even used it to make nutella and strawberry panini.

Sooooo good!!  I added 1/3c honey, a little more flour than called for, and mixed it w/the KitchenAid.  It's so soft and fluffy.  DH said, "This bread is amazing."  Thanks so much for sharing!  I'm going to be making this on a weekly basis!

This bread is soooooo good! i decided to make it this morning just to try it! Oh it was a good thing i did! it is so soft and warm and good :) i dont have a bread machine so i just did it by hand and i had no problems. i also didnt have instant yeast or bread flour. so i used all purpose flour, and i used regular yeast( put in a bowl with 1/2 a cup of hot water and a sprinkel of sugar for 10 minutes ). it was so good. thanks for the recipe!

Wow - this bread is wonderful! I used 3 cups bread flour with 1/4 cup whole wheat flour and it was still light and tender and delicious! This could not have been easier. I did the whole thing in the bread machine and it worked out great. A definate keeper. Thanks for sharing!

I don't think I did anything wrong... I did increase the yeast to a full packet and added a bit more honey, and had wanted a honey herb bread so I added a teaspoon of herbs. This loaf's shape and color are pretty; its subtle honey taste is also very nice! I baked mine using 25-30% whole wheat flour and stopping at just over 3 cups. And I used soured milk, only three tablespoons margarine, and one teaspoon salt. Thanks for sharing an excellent bread recipe!

I'll just have to chime in even though there are tons of other glowing reviews--it is FABULOUS bread.  I too used part whole wheat and my daughter didn't even notice ;)I also made it completely in the bread machine and it was fine.  Thank you for sharing this great recipe with us all!!!
Very nice bread! Was just perfect coming out of the oven. Rose real good too! Wonderful texture and mighty tasty :)  Thanks for sharing the recipe!
This was wonderful! Next time I will try using some wheat flour as I don't think that would compromise the heavenly flavor. Thanks!

Everyone loved this bread!  My mother thought she was eating a piece of cake, even though it really isn't that sweet.  Perfect & so easy with the bread machine.  Wish I had some now as it's been a while since I made it.

This bread is amazing!  I have been using another bread recipe but this is so much better.  It is soft and velvety, just wonderful.  I'm going to start using this as my regular recipe. It smelled so good while cooking too! Thanks so much!

this bread is wonderful.  Instead of doing it in bread pans we did the whole thing in the bread machine.  It turned out so moist and full of flavor.  I also used regular flour instead of bread flour and it still turned out perfect.  I will be making this many more times in the future.

This will be a good one to make for my picky MIL. Thanks so much for sharing!
WOW! I was very impressed with the results of this loaf. The texture was so soft. Woo-Hoo!! I will be making it alot more! Thanks so much for posting, I followed recipe as stated! Highly recommended!

Made as directed.  It took another 20-30 minutes to raise enough in my turned-off machine, but it baked into a very large beautifully shaped loaf in the oven.  Thanks for posting.

This bread was wonderful!  I did use 1 cup of whole wheat flour and I think that you could even add a little more without changing the texture.  My husband has requested this maybe once a week instead of buying bread.  Using the bread machine made it very easy.  Thanks for our new bread recipe.

I've been trying lots of different recipes since purchasing a bread machine. I've been looking for a recipe that turns out a soft crust suitable for sandwiches.  Most I have tried failed in that regard but this was fabulous!

Positively the best bread that I have made so far! Your bread recipe is amazing. The only problem that I have is that the dough has to rise a lot longer than the recipe states, at least where I live anyway. Wonderful recipe nonetheless. Thank you so much for sharing this!!
this bread is great for grilled sandwiches! A+++++
WOW I love this bread it is just FANTASTIC!!! my DH loved it. I made a loaf and it was gone by the end of the day , thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe!!
This was really yummy - and I'm not even a fan of white bread. Thanks for sharing Iva :)
This was a really good, dense bread.  My kids even loved it. Thanks you for sharing it. They are requesting it toasted with peanut butter for breakfast.
Excellent!  I hate the crust on ABM, this crust is fantastic and the bread is delish!! Thanks for sharing.
Perfect bread! Thanks for the keeper Iva!

Yummy bread. Made it in my bread machine with on the basic/light setting. Used non-bread flour and 1 cup wheat, had to use 2/3 honey and the rest a honey syrup and it was still amazing. Will definitely be making this again.
Very tasty and turned out great.  It also lasted a few days longer than some other recipes.  Will be making again!

This recipe is wonderful. I did have to add about another 1/2 cup of flour. I also added some italian spice to it. I will definitely use this recipe as my main pasta recipe.
SO quick and easy, tasted delicious. We just ate it with some butter. Tastes so much better than store bought. I had no idea I could do this so simply at home. Thanks!
Excellent !  Tastes great and rolls out nicely with the kitchenaid pata rollers

My first attempt at homemade pasta and it was very well received by my teens & hubby.  Will be trying this again soon!
Done with Semolina.  Tasted good but could use something to bring in the zing!  However, everyone enjoyed, easy to work with and make.  Made lasagna noodles and tagliatelle.
This dough was delicious tasting but to work with it was too sticky so after adding another 1/2 cup of flour the problem was fixed! It was very easy to make.

Quite honestly I did not believe that canned green beans could be any good at all but since my daughter had opened one by mistake and was going to toss it I decided to give your recipe a try and OH my I am so glad I did. Threw these together tonight as a side dish to go with Roasted Kielbasa & Potatoes. They tasted pretty good. No changes necessary. Thanks for sharing!
I thought these were very tasty green beans. My kids liked them too. I used fresh green beans and minced garlic (not thyme). I will definitely be making these again.

Excellent! Hard to believe I can say that about canned beans but it's true. Super easy and quick! I'm SO glad that I made this tonight! Made with ingredients I always have on hand. This was very good.  Don't know why I never thought of adding anything other than the regular butter, salt and pepper.  I usually stay away from 'canned' vegetables, especially beans, simply because I find them watery and tasteless.  This adds a whole new level of possibilities to canned veggies.  Thanks so much for giving me a much needed boot in the ol' butt.

A great taste from the norm. The taste of thyme was barely noticeable.

YUMMY  with a capital YUM!  And quick prep ... company's coming taste with a quick week-night dinner prep. I happened to use Pecorino Romano cheese because that is what I had on hand. Thanks Mama's Kitchen!

Exact words from my BF were 'These beans are bangin'!'  I wished had had made 2 cans! Excellent flavor.  Made as is including thyme.  Thyme is not necessary but gave it another flavor. Thanks for a great keeper!!

I've never really liked green beans but love these!  My huband has been eating them every day.  Haven't been using the thyme and they are just as good in my opinion.  Thanks!

Who woulda thought?  These are awesome!  Economical!  These make green beans from a can (which I don't mind in the first place) to something I really really like.  I'm already planning to have them again tomorrow.  Thanks!!!
I am an intensive Needs teacher and I am always looking for easy recipes the kids can make.  This was a real winner!  Bravo!  thanks you!

Yum! What a simple but tasty side dish. We really enjoyed the thyme and Parmesan in these. Thanks for another great keeper mama. Made for I Recommend tag.

I saw this recipe and made it 1 min later and loved it. My boyfriend wanted to eat all of it but he had to share. Thanks.
Makes a can of bland green beans edible.

Oh mama, I made these for lunch for me and oh man talk about yummy and cheesy. The only thing different I did was cook the butter with the beans and then tossed them with the cheese. I gave this recipe 3 stars. I got mixed reviews on this recipe. My future hubby and my 6 yr old newphew didn't like this recipe. I on the other hand really liked this recipe. This was very good and a great change from the regular green beans.  I added extra parmesan since I am a huge fan.  I will be making my green beans this way from now on.  Thank you so much!

This stuff is so good! I made this for my MD, DDS, JD, BFF and my LOL! ;) Ha! But seriously I love it and my wife does too. I've been making this recipe regularly for about 2 yrs now. To make it easy on myself, I open my cans of tomatoes and put the juice only in the blender, to that I add a 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup Lime Juice.  I just toss in about half an onion (the blender will chop it), 1/4 of a bunch of Cilantro (stems and all), a clove or two of garlic.  For heat I use a fresh jalapeno, but the secret here is to fry it in a pan with a little oil. Keep turning until the skin becomes bubbly all over.  The heat will release the capsicum.  Usually you will only need half of the jalapeno.  Blend it all up with out the tomatoes.  Taste it, it is very strong at this point, make any adjustments to taste, I usually add more salt.  Toss in the tomatoes and a couple of pulses...You're done. The flavors really come together after a day in the fridge.

This is a great salsa recipe for those, like myself, who don't like chunky salsa. I have made quite a few "upgrades" to the recipe but feel like I have now perfected my recipe. First I should say, as much as I try, I can't get this to taste the same with fresh tomatoes, most people I had try both batches actually preferred the canned tomato version versus the fresh tomato version. As for my alterations, I use a can of Del Monte Diced Tomatoes with Zesty Jalepenos instead of using a can with diced green chilies, I typically use  one full fresh jalepeno (depending on how big they are) sliced but not de-seeded and 2 cloves of garlic instead of the garlic salt. I then just throw the onion half (cut up into two or three pieces) in my Vitamix, followed but the garlic and jalepeno, whole tomatoes and then the diced tomatoes on top and, lastly, the cumin, salt and sugar on top. I then just turn on the Vitamix, turn the dial between 3-6 sometimes higher when the onion doesn't seem to want to chop up. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours (THIS COULDN'T BE MORE IMPORTANT!) and it's ready to eat. Every time I bring this with me to work I have to bring in separate containers for certain people to take home because they love it so much. I'm going to try my hand at canning the salsa just the way it is and see if it work.

This is an old wives tale.  The best way to keep eggs from cracking when they boil is to temper them in hot water first to avoid thermal shock.  Cover the eggs in the pan with hot tap water and let them sit for 3-4 minutes.  Pour that water off and do it again.  Now the eggs are slightly warm and ready to boil - gently (turbulence can crack eggs too) - either the way described here, or boil them gently for exactly 12 minutes, then cool them immediately in ice water and peel under running tap water.  If you want your eggs to peel easier, use old eggs.  That's right - OLD eggs.  if you plan to boil a bunch for Easter, buy them two weeks ahead of time, then store them in their carton flipped over on its side (read on).  The albumen (white) in new/fresher eggs has a lower PH which causes it to adhere to the inner shell membrane.  The PH is higher in older eggs, which makes them easier to peel.  DON'T USE VINEGAR - it lowers the PH, and that's the exact opposite of what's needed.  One-half teaspoon baking soda per quart of water will make it alkaline and could help a little to raise the PH on fresh eggs, but it can also intensify the sulfur flavor, so just stick with boiling older eggs for best results.  You can increase the odds of centered yolks by storing them in the refrigerator inside their carton that's SET SIDEWAYS so the long axis of the eggs face east and west, instead of north and south.  Not completely reliable, but increases the odds of centered yolks.

I boil 4 dozen or more eggs each week for our church's Sunday morning service. They peel perfectly every time. Age of the egg doesn't matter. Start with the eggs and water at room temperature. Bring to a soft rolling boil for 12 minutes and immediately immerse in an ice bath to stop the cooking. Bathe for a minimum of five minutes. Start the crack at the blunt end of the egg to get a grasp of the membrane. Some will be stubborn, if so; throw them back in the ice bath while you peel the rest. This allows the water to get under the membrane.

Close, but not quite. While Madras style curries are known to be very fragrant with sweet spices, this sweetness is always balanced with pungent and earthy spices. This recipe has waaaaaaaaay too much cinnamon and other spices, namely ginger and cardamon. The recipe is also missing Fenugreek, which is a must for Madras style curry. Here are my suggestions to correct the above:
1. Reduce the cinnamon to 2 Tbsp
2. Increase Cumin Seeds to 8 Tbsp
3. Add Fenugreek Seeds - 2 Tbsp
4. Instead of powdered Cardamom, use 2 Tbsp of whole cardamom. This will reduce the overall amount once it is ground, and drastically improve flavor.
5. Reduce ground ginger to 1 Tbsp. Since most curries contain fresh ginger, this reduction is essential. Also, fresh ginger is far superior.

This will yield a spice mixture that will not only be more balanced and authentic, but it will certainly liven up any dish that you may but on to stew. ENJOY!

I have been doing my veggie stock this way for a few months & figured I'd give a review! I LOVE to do this for a few reasons. One, it's cheap. Actually, it's free since all you use for this stock you usually just toss. Two, it's more natural, nutritional (I imagine), pure, and flavorful. There are no preservatives or things you can't pronounce in there. Super low sodium, too! Three, you can really modify the stock. Have an over abundance of tomatoes in your garden? Make a stock - it'd go great to cook with rice, etc. Since I like a stronger onion flavor I just add an extra "layer" or two off my onions when I peel them. Four, you can use veggies and scraps that were previously WASTED. Got some veggies in the fridge that are about to go bad? Toss them in the stock freezer bag! I NEVER EVER waste veggies now simply b/c I didn't use them in time. 
I put all my scraps in this, including ones I wouldn't necessarily eat. For example, I toss the onion skins but still add that tough outer layer of the onion to this; normall it'd just get trashed/wasted. I add the middles of peppers when I gut them - seeds and all. I've even tossed a few fruit items in there - don't be scared to try it (just don't get carried away)!! I usually cook it all in the crockpot overnight, line my strainer with paper towels, and drain. This prevents the seeds and parts from falling through. Depending on what I have in that batch, sometimes I don't use paper towels but rather strain then blend. I've never actually seen this recipe posted but it's SUCH an easy method that one should really try it rather than buying stock. Plus, you always have so much on hand you'll find yourself adding your stock to things you normally wouldn't. Adds flavor and nutrients! Thanks for sharing!!

What a great idea! I have always made my own chicken stock. I make a whole chicken in the crockpot and use the juice that it develops and any leftover bones, skin, etc. Then I add water, salt/pepper, garlic, maybe onions, etc. I will save all my scraps from now on. I just started making this and added in some cabbage, Swiss chard stocks, ends of leeks, 2 carrots, stems from broccoli. I'll bet this will be even more awesome than usual! Like the idea to save trimmings from beef, although I don't usu. buy beef anymore, only occasionally. Then I can make my own beef stock.  Edited to add: This made it into my Top Fav's of 2008 book.
Wow - I don't know why I never thought of this before.  This is so easy to do and smelled so nice while simmering.  Thanks for sharing!

Wow!  Thanks so much Karen.  I made this today and it made so much.  I now have 21 1/2 cups of vegetable/chicken stock ready to freeze.  This with only a few days of adding to the freezer stock bag.  I make celery, carrot & apple juice every morning so I had a lot of celery leaves and stalks to add to it.  It is wonderful.  I make risotto often so I am always buying 4cup containers of liquid stock, but not any more, this recipe is wonderful and I am so happy that I found it here. By the way I used the carcass of a roast chicken to add to the vegies in the stockpot.  I also used more water because I did have a heap of vegetable peeling etc, that's why I got so much stock from it.  What a wonderful idea Karen, thanks so much.

The ONLY downside to this (outside of your friends thinking you are bonkers for freezing your garbage) is it will never be the same - and that really isn't a down side is it?  The ingredients will most always vary in selection, but amount also changes too.  What is a given though is the wonderful flavor from such a simple recipe.  I've enjoyed what I've made and really can't wait for the summer veggies to come calling (always hated throwing out the corn cob, seemed like there was just too much goodness left).  You are only limited to your imagination on this one.  THANK YOU!!
this is great.  i cook on low in the crock pot for 20-24 hours or until the chicken bones break easily.  thanks so much for posting!
Fantastic idea and super easy!  I have been using all of the spices and onion skins, carrots, celery, leeks, parsnips, garlic and mushrooms.  Thanks for sharing.
Awesome idea!!!!  I use every bit of my veggies now, no waste..  What a great money saver and I never have to worry about not having stock on hand.  And it's fun to make.. :)  Thanks so much.

I have tried this twice now, and both times my broth came out quite bitter. My mom says it's the celery leaves. Any idea what I'm doing wrong? I put in scraps from onions, tomatoes, carrots, broccoli, garlic, leeks, zucchini, and probably a few other veggies too. I really love this idea but my results are just not worth the effort yet. I am somewhat of a beginner cook so please tell me if there is something obvious that I'm doing wrong! Thanks.

I have been using this method for awhile now and am just realizing that I never rated it.  I was looking for it to give to a friend.  Everyone should do this for so many reasons.  I just threw two bags full of veggie scraps in a huge pot with the turkey carcass.  It always turns out to be the most delicious homemade stock.  I love not wasting all the parts of the veggies that we don't eat and also any veggies that are about to go bad.  My favorite way to store the stock is by freezing it in my muffin tin, one batch at a time and then once frozen putting them in big zip lock freezer bags.  Each one is 1/4 cup size.  These thaw quickly and that way, I can pull them out when I need them rather than having to plan ahead and put a larger container in the fridge to defrost ahead of time.  To everyone reading this method for the first time- once you try it you will wonder what took you so long!  I could never go back to canned stock/broth again.

Loved it - the last time I had this was when I was a toddler! On our second try we got it by just putting the yolk in the hole, and then adding a little more white, not enough to quite fill it. I fried the extra white and am going to have a couple healthy "hole sandwiches" for breakfast tomorrow. Thanks!

My Dad used to make this for me as a kid.  "Egg In Bread"  was my favourite weekend brekkie!  I now make it for my own children :)

Spot On!!! It doesn't get any easier or YUMMIER!!! Love it! Thanx for sharing!!!

Excellent cookie!  We love cookies and this cookie will now be one of our faves!  I just made to take to a party today and I have all ready eaten 3 and this is just right after breakfast.  My cookies baked in 13 1/2 minutes and I used an ice cream scoop.  Taks Jollymae for this great recipe!

Yummy cookies! Not sure why they're called Election Day cookies, but no matter (my boss asked if the toffee chips were supposed to be the independents lol). Great rub! Used this on country style ribs.I definately will use this in the future.Highly recommend it!

Great rub!  We used it on ribs for our 4th of July bbq.  It was a big hit.  Great flavor with little effort.  It goes on the list of recipes to be used often, especially since the ingredients are usually on hand anyway.  Thanks for posting!

this was very good. i cut the ribs in half added the rub and wrapped them in foil for about 6 hours.then cooked them on the grill with the foil still on turning them every 8 minutes for 1 hour. i took off the foil and added the barbecue sauce and cooked them 2 minutes more on each side. they were so good and moist i couldn't stop eating them. this is a keeper for sure, thanks

Hubby took a pork tenderloin out of the freezer by mistake, but we used this rub on it anyway, it was fab! Thanks, I will try this rub on many cuts of meat, the flavour is great, and I don't like sloppy sauces!

great rub only i steam mine in beer for an hour before baking.
