GREAT! Used this on pork chops and baked in oven for about 30 minutes. Excellent flavor.

OH YUM! We have used this twice now. The first time we used on 20lbs of ribs that we smoked in our propane smoker. Excellent and our guests loved them too. This will be the only dry rub we use from now on! **UPDATE**Rubbed a substantial amount of this on a 6lb beef brisket last Weds and smoked it in our propane smoker on Saturday!  IT WAS TO DIE FOR!

We loved this!  Used it on ribs, smoked in our grill with indirect heat and they turned out amazing.  Made some more rub to go on chicken legs for dinner tonight...YUM  Thanks so much for posting this!

This is EXCELLENT!!!  We love it! Next time I may add a bit more cayenne for a little extra kick.  I used the rub on pork ribs that I cooked in the crockpot.  They were mouthwatering!! Thank you for posting!
What a great rub.  Used it on some babyback ribs and they were wonderfully flavorful.   Thank you Luvmybge for sharing the recipe.
Awesome rub.  For those of you who know me, you know I don't eat much pork so I tried it out on turkey legs.  So good.  Grilled them up just like ribs.  Give it a try you wont be disapointed.

Truly excellent!  Spicy and so very flavorful.  With only 1 rack to cook, I halved the recipe, expecting to have a little rub left over.  Instead, I ended up using it all, and it was the perfect amount for 2 lbs. of baby backs.  
Next time, I'm going to go much lighter on the BBQ sauce, brushing on just a thin film so the taste of this wonderful rub can really take center stage.

I have tried quite a few rubs and this one takes the blue ribbon. I will become my standard.  It has a nice spice to it and not too much sweetness.  It caramelizes beautifully on the grill.  The Old Bay was a great addition.  I was skeptical of that, but boy does it work.  I agree with other reviewers, go light on the sauce, it does not need it!  I have made this recipe twice including last night, and I am already craving it again.  Nice post!  Thanks!!
I used this AWESOME Rub for my Mom's Bday dinner ribs and it was a big hit. Thanks!
These were great. Thanks for the recipe. I did as others suggested...used Sweet Baby Ray BBQ sauce and cooked at 250 for +3 hours. We will be having these again for sure.

This is the best dry rub I have ever used on my ribs!  Everyone oowed and ahhed as they dug into them!  I used my old standby Sweet Baby Rays for the bbq sauce, as it never disappoints!  This is one of my favorite rib rubs and will be used many times over!

oh how yummy. I loved it. I used bone-in country ribs. I decreased the amount of salt, seemed like a lot. I cooked the ribs in my Showtime Rotisserie for about 1 1/2 hrs. There was some juice that accumulated in the pan during marinating so I brushed that on the first 1/2 hr then the last 1 hr I brushed 3 times with some diluted orange juice concentrate. No need for bbq sauce at all. I marinated from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m and they were very flavorful. When it's not 30 degrees and snowing in MN I will try them on the grill like the directions say.
Update: I finally tried these on the grill w/ spare ribs & they are outstanding. I did some w/ bbq sauce & some without. Both were equally delicious.

this recipe is AMAZING! i followed the recipe to a T except for the onion powder, i didnt have any and just used some thin sliced onions on top. i let the rub sit on the ribs for about 3 hours before cooking, on 325 for 2 1/2 hours. i used 3lbs of beef ribs, and i must say they turned out spectacular!they are soooo moist, and juicy. the flavor is wonderful! not to over powering, but enough flavor to make them taste great! they smell wonderful cooking too!  i was orginially going to put some bbq sauce on, but im glad i tasted them before i did! i dont want to ruin the great flavor of these ribs with bbq sauce! this is going to be a recipe we use many times in the future. i couldnt be more pleased with how these turned out! the recipe was spot on, and so were the cooking times! thanks!

Wonderful recipe. I added smoked paprika, and more garlic.
I used on chicken yesterday and today I marinated ribs overnight and used another great recipe for the bbq sauce. I cannot wait to see how this will taste. Thaks for such a great recipe.
The only way I will make ribs from now on and it is so easy!  A keeper for sure!

This makes awesome ribs! Made many times now and the reviews get better and better.  This is the first rib recipe I ever tried, so I had to learn a few tricks.  First, I now make 1.5 times the rub. I rub some in for the overnight marinading, and then sprinkle some more on just before cooking. If you don't the ribs seem rather bland or maybe I just didn't rub the rub in good enough?  I dunno.  I got the tenderest batch at 250 for 3 hours. However, after work one day I was pressed for time and only did 1.5-2 hours at 280 or so. Then DH finished them on the grill and that smoky taste was awesome too. I leave out the chili powder and cayenne. I'm a wimp when it comes to spicy food! I also reduce the brown sugar to 7 TB (or 10.5 TB when i'm doing 1.5 x the recipe). I didn't notice a drop in flavor and I feel a little healthier. :)

These were some of the best ribs I have ever made and even tasted.  If restaurants used this recipe they could become known for their ribs.  I agree that you don't really need the bbq sauce but my family used it as they just need wet on their ribs.  I will definitely make these again just as they are listed.  I made no change at all.  Mine marinated for 3 hours so next time I will do the overnight thing.  Thank you so much for sharing this with us.

Now there's no excuse to buy store bought rub when you have a great rub like this that's so simple to make.  Rubbed this on my baby backs and the taste was tremendous.  Cooked at 225 for 21/2 hours and snow did not permit outdoor grilling.  Still perfect.  The ribs were too fatty but that's not your fault!  This one's a keeper for sure
i love this rub! its good on ribs but honestly its great on pretty much every thing you can think of so don't be afraid to try it on other things as well. great recipe!

Wow -- how good is this rub?  So good that although I had the sauce ready, I decided to skip it!!!  I followed the recipe except rather than 8 tablespoons of brown sugar I used 4 Tablespoons of Splenda's 50/50 brown sugar/splenda mix (I try to save my intake of sugar for chocolate!!)  I rubbed my beef ribs and let them sit for about 15 minutes or so, and then popped them into my crock pot on low for 6 hours. I poured off the liquid in the crockpot and was ready to pour on the sauce and let it simmer on low for another hour, but decided to taste.  The ribs were so good that sauce wasn't necessary.  Thanks for posting (and please thank Barb for me too!)

This rub is fantastic. The meat was so tender and so tasty. We're definitely a ribs-with-sauce kind of family, so I did one rack with sauce and one without, and they were both equally tasty! Great rub, and anything with Old Bay is a definite bonus! Thanks!

This was a nice rub.  Other than doubling the Old Bay (as someone who grew up in MD must), I followed the rub recipe exactly.  Cooked the ribs in the crockpot, using Recipe#16705 - they were outstanding.  Thanks for posting!

A winner for sure.  I applied the rub approximately 18 to 20 hours before cooking the ribs.  I cooked them 'slow and low' for about 5 hours.  Like another reviewer I also left some ribs dry when I grilled them and they were outstanding as well.  I would be proud to serve these ribs either way.  Thanks for contributing to our successful Father's Day 2010 BBQ.
Loved this.  Did not have any thyme but do not think it mattered.  Thanks for posting.
This was fabulous!!  I used it on salmon-everyone loved it!!!

EXCELLENT! I've been making ribs for years, but the family all said this was the best one I've ever made. I doubled the recipe and cooked it 'lower and slower'... at about 250 for 4hrs. Fell off the bone and SO tasty. Thanx!

This is an incredible rub mixture and will be what I use going forward. Had all the ingredients on hand. I doubled the recipe and used it on 2 slabs of baby backs. Rubbed them the night before a party and let them "marinate" wrapped in the fridge overnight. Then cooked them for 5 hours at 200*. Kept them covered in foil for the first 4, then removed the foil for the last hour to get them crispy. Didn't bother broiling/applying BBQ since we prefer just a dry rub.

BEST RIBS EVER. Only thing I do differently is that once I've got them good and rubbed, I drizzle honey on the ribs before closing up in foil. We serve a little more BBQ sauce at the table after brushing on the ribs while they are on the grill. These are my GO TO ribs for summer and everyone FREAKS OUT when I make them.  Thanks so much for posting!
Great rub. Used this rub with the ribs my way recipe. Perfect.

I have made these ribs 4 times in the last month since finding this rub!  The only different thing I have done is drizzle the ribs with a little honey before baking off in a 200 oven all day.  Oh, and I never seem to have the Old Bay on hand (and keep forgetting to buy it) and the rub is still fantastic!

Very, Very good. Cook in several competitions yearly in Texas. Brisket, beans, chicken, and RIBS. Tried this rub and got second. (feel like I owe her some money lol) She got mostly 5 star ratings except for a few, and those I did not understand totally. One lady gave her a 4 star because her ribs were falling apart because the cooking time was too long. The recipe states to cook for 2 1/2 to 3 hours OR UNTIL DONE. You would think people would check on this as they cook. Just a tutorial not a given. Everybody's source of cooking is different and unique depending on what they use. Thanks again for the win. Will use it very often.

My first time making ribs! I made as directed, but did use one tip from another recipe- removing the tough membrane on the bone side before rubbing with spices. This has great flavor that my husband said was better than the local restaurant! Next time I might decrease the sugar; I prefer for the other flavors not to be overpowered by sweetness. But I could be wrong...

This is the best rub I've ever used.  I was smoking some ribs and planned on using a dry rub that I had bought.  I decided to make this due to the reviews.  I did a taste comparison and threw the store bought rub away.  Worked great for ribs.

Wow This is all I can say. Great rub recipe my first to try out. And like other reviewers I felt there was no need for bbq sauce. My family had put some on there's but that was just a personal preference.
Thanks for sharing this, didn't use old bay as I didn't have any but this dry rub was Delish!!!! Thanks
I'm not even a fan of dry rub ribs but this is amazing. I will definitely make it again.

This an all-around great recipe.  Simple, easy, and delicious!  My guests for Christmas dinner raved.  I served the shrimp on beds of garlic-sauteed spinach.

Thanks for a great recipe!

Oh!! My!! God!!!
This was out of this world. I could chow down on this recipe every day.  Perfect flavor, perfect taste.  Any one who makes it will fall in love.
This has got to be one of our favourite recipes.  I made this exactally as written using king prawns and served with a salad.  Thank you marie for a fantastic recipe.  We will use this alot.

Wouldn't change a thing! Absolutely fabulous!

Omigosh, marie, these are soooo fine!!!

I had a small problem with the cooking time, but it wasn't the fault of the recipe.  The only seriously big shrimp my market had today was the size they classify as "colossal".  (1.02 lbs., and I only got 8 shrimp.)

Another 5 star review.  I didn't change a thing, and everyone loved them.  When you combine simplicity and outstanding flavor you have a winner - and this is it.

Definitely worth the 5 stars!  So easy and so tasty.  I used panko (Japanese) breadcrumbs and the shrimp came out nice and crisp.  We had these with french fries and cole slaw for a great dinner!  Thanks marie for a great recipe.

Definitely one of the best shrimp recipes of all times. My husband wanted me to make it again the following night! So easy and really delicious. I made exactly as stated and served with roasted asparagus and a cauliflower gratin and a salad. Thanks for posting.
Butter, Garlic, & Shrimp...how can you go wrong?  Make it quick and easy like this and it's a keeper!  (Just wish shrimp was in the budget every week!)  Thanks!
Yep, another 5 star review.  The shrimp are excellent and the preparation easy.
Great!!!!!  Like the other reviewers stated, it is so easy yet so delicious.  Will make this again and again.

Stop it already!  I can't afford to do this two days in a row! So delicious, so easy, so perfect.  I did wonder one thing when I made it the first time, should I use fresh grated parmesan or the "green can stuff"?  I'm sure its good either way.  BTW I used the Kraft!
Made these shrimp for an office party using medium shrimp and doubled the recipe.  Needless to say, they were all gone in a flash.

Wow,this honestly deserves 10 stars! It's  a wonderful, wonderful recipe!  Shrimp is my favorite food to eat at a restaurant and I think this surpasses any shrimp dish I have ordered out!  I used Pecorino Romano cheese and Panko breadcrumbs and an extra clove of garlic!  Thank you for sharing such a delicious recipe!
i did these for my dinner party last night and everybody raved about them. they are very easy and i used king size prawns instead of tiger prawns. excellent
Thank you Marie for a awesome recipe.  I paired your Jumbo Shrimp Parmensan with David Ball's Buttered Egg Noodles #11107 and it made for a great marriage.

This was an outstanding meal. Did it as an anniversary present for my girlfriend.  Goes really well with Asparagus, Lipton 'Butter and Herb' packaged noodles. Just bake the shrimp and serve on top the noodles. Simply outstanding.
OUTSTANDING!!!!!  My family LOVED this recipe!
I made these for dinner last night and thought they were probably the best shrimp I have ever had!!  They were easy to make and got 5 stars from my fiance too!!

Outstanding shrimp! This was so simple to make and the flavor is delicious. I added more garlic, but other than that, didn't change a thing and can't see any reason to do so. We really enjoyed this and will make often. Thanks for posting!
Awesome shrimp!  I love shrimp and with the garlic it was heavenly!  Definite keeper here marie, thanks

Excellent! ABSOLUTELY THE BEST SHRIMP I'VE EVER HAD! I've made this several times and the only changes I've made were to use 30 count shrimp and Key Limes. Both are merely personal preferences. Thanx for posting this great recipe. Pierre
Delicious and easy to make! My husband and son loved it! Thank you for the great recipe!

I got a few shimp all battered up to see how they would compare, and since we drizzle butter on them, it makes them too soggy, and the cooking time increases. I noticed that cooking the shrimp long enough to get the bread crumbs really golden makes a big difference in flavor. Yumm! ooops..I forgot to give this one the 5 stars it deserves!!  Great dish!
Killer!

Ok.. another review..   I know it doesn't need it but I made these last week and they were delicious. I didn't have unseasoned bread crumbs so I used Italian Style crumbs and the shrimp were very good.
i made these for labor day weekend as we had company, and i had to give them the recipe...it was a huge hit and looked like it took me all day to make...fantastic
Yum!  I used 2 lbs 51-60 shrimp and instead of drizzling with melted butter I sprayed with spray margarine, 5 minutes in the oven.  The whole family loved them! Thanks for a great recipe.

Excellent! I made the recipe as directed using 1 1/2 pounds of U10-12 shrimp and  marinated for 1 hour. The shrimp came out perfectly cooked with a lovely garlic-Parmesan flavor. Great recipe Marie, goes into my "book of special tricks" !

Excellent!  Followed the recipe exactly and wouldn't change a thing.  My husband loved these, thanks!
Delicious! I even omitted the butter & used spray margarine, added a tsp of Old Bay seasoning and it was melt in your mouth good.  Thanks!

We're not the Rockefellers, so I had to settle for 26/30 count shrimp.  But I did them the same way, and oh, boy, were they good!  I added about a half-teaspoon of Thai chile sauce to the marinade, because we like things spicy.  Other than that, I'd halve the 'breading' because I wound up throwing WAY too much away, and that's just not thrifty!

Very tasty. Made this to go along with So Easy Fish #7913 and sort of combined the breadcrumb mixture for both recipes (breadcrumbs, parm cheese, lemon pepper and garlic powder) and used it for both the shrimp and the fish.  Very tasty. Thanks for the recipe!

Well here I go!!!!!!  Jumping on the "OH MY GOD" band wagon.  This was hands down the best shrimp I have ever made and I have made some awesome shrimp.  I hid some for my lunch tomorrow. Thanks Marie.  Laura Lee
A little bland.  I tried this with the So Easy Fish (#7913).  The fish turned out very good, but next time I'll try broiling or BBQing the shrimp.

SOOOOOO delicious!  I had gone out to eat and ordered shrimp parmesan and when I found this recipe I knew it would be great.  I served it with the classic baked spaghetti #32731 and the shrimp dissapeared...will be making very very often.  Thanks marie!
Delicious! The best shrimp ever.
Wonderful shrimp.  Most of us never had shrimp made with Parmesan before and let me tell you these were gone in minutes!  Thanks for sharing, Marie!!!

My daughter requested this for her 10th birthday dinner. It was simple enough that she was actually able to do it almost completely on her own, yet tasted like something much more complicated. Everyone loved it, young and old alike. We served it with other seafood and a rice pilaf. I think the only change I would make next time is to line the pan with tin foil to make clean-up easier. Thanks! :o)

I used fresh tiger prawns and scallops for this recipe. Turned out pretty good. My only complaint is that the coating is not crispy at all. They turned out slightly soggy, but the taste is great. The scallops needed an extra 10mins to cook. Simple and quick dish. Thanks!

These were extremely easy to make and very tasty!  Only change I made was using italian seasoned bread crumbs because that's all I had on hand.  Also, to get these crispy may I suggest broiling them on LOW for approximately 10 minutes and make sure you flip them at least once.  The breading on ours turned out nice and crunchy, so if you are looking for a crispy version of this recipe, try the broiler.  Thanks Marie for a great recipe and these would also work great as an appetizer!

Excellent!! No "jumbo" shrimp available, so I used large shrimp (16-20 ct.), italian bread crumbs, and a little extra garlic. Left them in the oven an extra 2 minutes to get a little crisping, and they turned out superb! Thanks for a great Valentine's dinner, Marie!

Delicious!  I got home late from work and was really tired, so I didn't allow the shrimp to refrigerate for 30 minutes.  I let them soak for about 5 minutes at room temperature, then proceeded to step 7.  Served with a baked potato and a fresh tossed salad.  Thanks Marie for another great recipe!

Very Good!!! Used 1lb 41/50 ct shrimp. Omitted butter, doesn't need. Cooked 12 min on lg bar pan. Next time will broil for a few min. to get crispier. Great for company!!!  Can't wait to try with large shrimp.  This is a real winner!!!!
Everyone loved this, including me, the chef!  I used jumbo prawns and followed the recipie as directed.  Easy, delish and impressive to guests!

Wow...I'd give this 10 stars if I could!  This is one of the best thing I've ever eaten.  Tastes like something you'd get at a fancy restaurant.  I didn't have any plain breadcrumbs, and used seasoned Italian breadcrumbs instead.  AWESOME, thanks!

Really great shrimp recipe.  Simple to make,and just a few basic ingredients. I used Panko breadcrumbs, and a combination of Parm and Asiago cheeses. Simply wonderful, and wonderfully simple. I will make this one again for sure.

This was very good and so easy that my nine year old enjoyed helping.  Prep time is mostly the marinating time for the shrimp.  It really only took about five minutes total prep time for this dish.  I served mine with Pasta and garlic alfredo sauce and brussel sprouts.  I drizzled the butter on the shrimp with a teaspoon, but a medicine dropper would be good to use too, because they do  not need but a few drops on top of each shrimp for them to turn out nice and golden/crispy. Very good and thank you for posting.
The shrimp turned out crispy and flavorful.  I served with with steak and it went over well.
Wow What was not to like! =) Simple, easy to prepare and delicious!! The seasonings are just right.  They add a nice bit of zap and still let the flavor of the shrimp shine through.  Excellent!

Another high five from a shrimp lover!  The combination of shrimp, garlic, and parmesan was a winner in this house.  All these ingredients mingled perfectly.  This recipe will be reached for again and again!  Thank you!

I too used large frozen shrimp.  About 45 to a pound.  I let them unthaw before I marinated them and cooked them for about 5-6 minutes.
I didn't have large shrimp, so I used smaller with excellent results. They cooked in about half the time. I look forward to eating this again and again!
We have made this probably a dozen times and the only thing we have started doing lately is squeezing lemon and lime on the shrimp before eating.  Wow!

This was a very easy and delicious recipe. The only thing i changed was down sizing the jumbo shrimp to regular sized shrimp. I made atleast 2 dozen. I'm going to continue to make this for years to come.

From now on, this is the only way I will prepare jumbo shrimp. Wonderful recipe, Marie!  I have made it twice and was more than pleased with the results.  I used panko crumbs and they were nice and crispy.  Squeezing on the lemon was just the right touch.  I wouldn't change a thing.  Thanks so much!

These were without a doubt as good as any restaurant recipe, if not better!! My husband couldn't stop raving about them. They were simple to make as well, which is nice for our very busy family. We also squeezed on the lemon juice, and it made the flavors pop!

I'll add my 5 stars to this one.  I did add the juice of a half of lemon to the olive oil, garlic mixture, but other than that made as directed.  Absolutely wonderful.  Thanks so much for a great recipe.

I prepared this for my DH as I don't eat shrimp.  I used 12 41-60 count shrimp amd marinated them in 1 Tblsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp lemon juice, 1 fresh clove minced garlic and some fresh ground black pepper for about 2-3 hours.  I used about 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (Quick bread crumbs for Casseroles recipe #57875 which I had in the freezer - great recipe!) and 1/4 cup parmesan cheese.  I baked them 10 minutes.  My DH loved them.  Said the flavor was outstanding!  They were pretty easy to prepare, especially since I did the first part of the prep earlier in the day.  Thanks for sharing your recipe Marie!
This was fabulous.  I used Kasseri cheese and added ~1/2 tsp. italian seasoning to the oil/garlic marinade.  Taste was fantastic.  I will definitely make this again.

ooh lala! i used large shrimp and had fantastic results. prepared the shrimp with all the same ingredients, but made adjustments where necessary to get them nice and covered in the marinade. i loooooove garlic so i added 4 cloves, and the flavor was perfect. this one deserves more than 5 stars! even my picky BF thinks so-- thank you marie!

I made this recipe for part of Father's day dinner. I used frozen cooked shrimp and doubled the ingredients. It was easy and delicious and it tastes like you worked much harder than you did! It deserves more than 5 stars. Thanks for sharing.
Oh my goodness these are so darned good!  The two of us ate every single one while I was still in the kitchen!  Next time I'm going to sit down and savor every bite.  And not share!  Thank you!

Where did those prawns go???
I only had smaller 31 count in the freezer, but they were still wonderful!  Easy, easy, easy & they made a great appy with champagne.  I made them up ahead & when company arrived I put them in the oven.
I will be making these again. thanks

I cannot even begin to describe how wonderful this is...it deserves 100 stars.  It is soo easy and unbelievably good.  It was devoured.  I did put the oven on broil for a few minutes at the end so it would brown up a little. WONDERFUL!!!If you have'nt tried this you MUST!!!

I cooked them in a stoneware dish sprayed w/Pam and they cooked to perfection. The only thing I will do differently next time is double the recipe!

This dish was yery easy to put a great meal on the table. The shrimp were perfectly done and had a great flavor with the cheese and garlic. I loved adding the splash of lemon at the end, thanks for posting.

My kids love to go shrimping at night, so ive been trying new shrimp recipes... well i have found my new favorite.  This was simply divine...so easy and so so good! Thank you Marie, and everyones comments made it a must try!
Absolutely fantastic...followed the recipe exactly. I also used panko. Will be making this again soon! Thanks!
I made the recipe exactly as written and it is perfect.  I wouldn't change a thing!  We loved it and will make it again.  Thanks for the great recipe.

Delicous! I made these with panko and everyone loved them I will definatly make them again!

DH loved this recipe! We used it for our traditional Xmas eve seafood extravaganza. He liked it much better than fried shrimp. We used regular sized shrimp. DH recommends pulling the tails off before baking for easier eating.

I got rave reviews all around for this one!  My sister held up 2 hands - - 10!  Absolutely delicious. If you BWB can this salsa, these are the current directions for salsa making from the NCHFP: 
Wear plastic or rubber gloves and do not touch your face while handling or cutting hot peppers. If you do not wear gloves, wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before touching your face or eyes. 

Peel and prepare chili peppers. 
Wash tomatoes and dip in boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds or until skins split. 
Dip in cold water, slip off skins, and remove cores. 
Coarsely chop tomatoes and combine chopped peppers, onions, and remaining ingredients in a large saucepan. 
Heat to boil, and simmer 10 minutes. 
Fill hot, sterilized jars; wipe rims and place lids. 
Screw on bands finger tight. 
Process pint jars in boiling water bath for 15 minutes up to 1000 feet elevation; 20 minutes at 1001 - 6000 feet elevation; 25 minutes at higher elevations.

These were amazing!!! I made them for an end-of-semester party, doubling the batch so I would have more than one for everyone. They were devoured. My professor (with a soft spot for chocolate) was very pleased, and so was I!! These are great with coffee.

Have made these twice...Absolutely delicious! Mad ethese for wife's valentines day surprise breakfast..outstanding..used the weight watcher's recipe provided by Matt&Averies Mommy..and they turned out perfect..but then blew it by covering with chocolate ganache..LOL..oh well I'll never tell....she just loved them..Thanks

Very very good!! These were so chocolatey and moist. Very good recipe. Thanks for posting. I am keeping this one!

I can't believe I didn't review these!  Fantastic is all I can say.  Great flavour, nice consistency... Have to admit I replaced the flour with SR flour and omitted the raising agents.  Will definitely make again!

5 min out already had 2 of them,i had some quite time while my wife&kids were enjoying this treat. i used whole wheat flour and3/4 cup brown sugar,they turned out so light&moist . i had to give some away or i would have finished them up  thanks for the chocolate fix
These were great. I loved how easy it was to make. I did not used the miniature chips, but the regular sized one. They turned out fabulous.

My guy is a chocoholic, so even though I don't make these exactly to the recipe, I've been using this recipe as a base and they've turned out great every time.  I usually use 1/2 whole wheat and 1/2 white flour.  I also add some ground flax seeds, molasses, spiced applesauce and/or blueberries.  I also cut the sugar down and remove the oil.  I guess that changes it quite a bit, but I wanted to thank you for a great recipe.

This is a very easy muffin to make and all the flavours go well together.  Little Miss (DD) really enjoy mixing it up. Direction are well written and simple to follow.  Thank you Charishma Ramchandani
Made these for Zaar's Muffin Day! They were moist and delicious! I will be making them more. Thanks Charishma Ramchandani!

Really great muffins. I got 14 muffins from the batter. I was going to make them jumbo but I made standard muffins instead and I'm glad I did because they're very rich and chocolatey. (But that's a good thing ;) ) They are a little sweet though so I think next time I'd cut back on the sugar. The bananas and chocolate go so well together. They turned out nice and moist and they're wounderful fresh from the oven. I'd make these again. Thank's for sharing!

This was a great recipe!
I made a change to it that I think was quite tasty - I substituted the banana for pureed prunes. Now, I know that sounds a bit weird, but they were still really chocolaty and VERY moist.

These are absolutely amazing!  I've made them at least three times already and can't get enough!  :)  I have played around with the recipe a little to make them more healthy... white whole wheat flour for the all purpose flour, 1/2 c. honey for the sugar... Thanks for a great recipe that we love even more than banana bread! (Oh, I have also make mini loaves and just baked them a tad longer...)

These are fantastic!  I used about 2 cups of banana (that's how much I had, and I didn't want to waste any!) and it was just fine. I can't fathom ever making a banana muffin from a box again!

These were good muffins, I liked how easy it was to put all the ingredients together. I would like to try this without the cocoa though the next time I make these, I have never really liked banana and chocolate in a cake, brownie or muffin.

Really good! These are the first muffins I have made that had rounded top. I halved the recipe and got 5 muffins. I used Splenda, omitted the chocolate chips, a little bit more of banana because I didn't want to use oil. I was a little bit scared of that but they rose up beautifully in my toaster oven and were really moist ^^

I've used this recipe a few times and abbled around with quantities and ingredients according to what I have around. It never fails me and is a huge hit served warm with vanilla ice cream. Also good put in the lunch box straight from the freezer and they keep lunch cool and are ready to eat by lunchtime.

Get a tall glass of milk ready!  These are wonderfully decadent breakfast muffins! Thank you for taking the time to post this recipe!
Very good. I used 1 c flour 1/2 cup whole wheat and 1/2 c sugar 1/2 c splenda. I thought it was really good and not too sweet.

Absolutely loved these muffins!
Moist & a wonderful banana chocolate flavor.   I have made a few batches already & these have been a big hit. 
Thank you so much for posting this recipe.
Katherine in Alberta

Made over the weekend but realized I didn't have any cocoa powder, so these ended up being Banana Chocolate Chip muffins!  Used slightly less amount of sugar and regular size choc chips. Super yum!  I made exactly as you suggested - wonderful.  Moist, chocolatey over a background of banana.  These are aweesome.  Thanks!

Scrumptious !!!  Easy to put together, delicious, moist, just what I was craving..a combination of my two favorites, chocolate and banana.  I used 4 smallish bananas (may have been more than the 1 1/3 cup, plus I added a splash of vanilla extract.  Yummmm

i was craving for something with chocolate... i have tried many others chocolate muffins recipes but there's NO OTHER that tastes like this. these muffins are the best chocolate muffins i've ever tried (and i can't wait to add the chocolate chips since i didn't have any the first time). i'm so excited that this recipe turned out this good... finally i've found the perfect chocolate muffins recipe. thanks a bunch!

this was okay, not bad, but not amazing, then again im not too big on chocolate all the time, or it might be bc i just tried a diff recipe for banana muffins that was healthy AND good, so im a little biased.  but it is an interesting combo, i like the bananas with the chocolate

Perfect!! I just had one of these hot out of the oven and they are scrumpdeliumptious! I'm trying to refrain from having a second and I don't think I'm going to able to last much longer. Yummy! Yummy! Yummy! I got 16 muffins and baked mine for 20 minutes.

Bananalicious! This recipe is a perfect alternative to banana bread when you are trying to use all your ripe bananas. I probably could have gotten 14 muffins out of the batter. Good for breakfast or dessert, just make sure you have a big glass of milk on hand!

As many have stated before me, these are absolutely delicious. You can taste the banana and yet they are so chocolately. I have not found a single person who does not like these muffins. They vanished so quickly that I learned to make double and triple batches, and whatever is left, after my family has its way with them, freezes welll.
These are awsome!!  I used 1/2 cup regular sized chocolate chips and 1/2 cup peanut butter chips and they were amazing!!  Chocolate, bananna and peanut butter....what could be better?

I made these quite a long time ago and cant believe I forgot to rate them. These were the first banana muffins that DH gave 5 stars to, so that makes them great in my book. Nice chocolatey flavour. Thanks!

Fantastic -- our new favorite!  I used regular sized chips and substituted 1/2 cup of the flour for whole wheat flour (a bit better for us) and they were perfect...next time I might try 1/2 cup splenda.  I found that 2 medium ripe bananas worked great.
Perfection - moist and chocolately!  I got eight large muffins from this recipe.  I used 3 medium sized bananas and substituted applesauce for 4 Tablespoons of the oil.  A new favorite!

These were so fantastic. I was a little low on bananas so I added a touch of oil to make up the difference. I baked them in my heart shaped pans and they were a great treat for us all.

Thanks so much!!!  THis is a great recipe.  I have made it many times and the kids love it everytime!!  I replace oil with applesaucs to make it healthier.
We really like these!   Nice and yummy.   My kids really like them too.   We'll make this again soon!

Awesome, rich & fudgey muffins!  Very moist!  I loved using the mini chocolate chips - it gave you an extra burst of chocolate in every bite!

Really good made 18  out of this recipe and about 6 ripe bannanas

These are awesome, wonderful muffins!  I have made muffins every week for friends for the last 3 years.  We loved these.  Just the right amount of chocolate & they rose beautifully. This are incredible!  Moist, full of flavor.  I used mini bananas so since they are so sweet, used about 1/4 cup less sugar.  Wonderful recipe!

thanks, loved!!!!!!!!!!

Awesome!  I used flax instead of egg, and subbed honey for the sugar. Some I topped with dark chocolate chips and some with cocoa nibs. :-)  They turned out very well.

Really good! I had some extra banana stuff I needed to use up and they came out so nice! I even cut out 1/2 the sugar (personal preference) and used some WW flour. Will definitely make again.
I used tigernut flour & lakanto monkfruit powdered sugar with a little stevia glycerine and oh my!! Wonderful

I love making homemade nut butters but this is the first time I've tried walnuts. Made as directed and after tasting I added 1/8 tsp of kosher salt and that tiny bit lifted the flavor nicely. I think that I'll try using a tad less oil next time. Currently it's fresh out of the food pro and fairly liquid but that could change to a better spreading consistency after some standing time. Thanks for sharing Jen :D

I added about 1 teaspoon of raw sugar. This was decadent! I loved it. Proud<br/>to add this recipe to my Best of 2013 Cookbook! This is my first time making walnut butter.<br/>I've made many kinds of nuts and seed butter including flour and meal but never with walnuts. <br/>Can't wait to experiment more with this butter. Tested with: Recipe #461568 and also delicious on slices of Granny Smith apples as well as spoonfuls of it right out of the storage container. Much better results and luck for me to dry roast the nuts in a cast iron skillet instead of in the oven. fyi Made for Veg Tag/July.

Tried this and it was delicious, Also made a variation; Flaxseed Butter, 1 cup of flaxseeds roasted for 10 minutes I upped the amount of Flaxseed oil to 9 teaspoons for it to congeal And 1/2 teaspoon of salt A omega 3 packed butter tastes like popcorn
So good and easy to make!

It's quick & easy. Roasting the walnuts gives it a more "peanut butter" taste vs. raw walnuts. To make it less a "peanut butter" I ground it less, added more salt, a touch of cinnamon and 2 tablespoons of honey and 1 more teaspoon of oil. I use olive oil.
just imagine a walnut chocolate bar yummm

Yes, we Southerners do like wilted lettuce.  This is a great salad to serve.  I used red leaf and green leaf lettuce.  The red leaf added a pretty color.  Be sure and serve this dish immediately.  Thanks for sharing, Sharon!

Oh boy! I haven't had this in 30 years!  Fond childhood memories of wilted lettuce dressing- sometimes with a touch of sugar for a heavenly sweet/sour taste.  Best on leaf lettuce.  Thanks for posting and reviving memories.
Wilted lettuce is one of my favorites, only we fried out fatback(salt pork) and used grease instead of butter.

This was a old southern dish that I never really cared for until recently. This recipe is delicious. I did add alittle sugar in with the mixture you pour over the lettuce. 
Thanks so much for sharing this old southern favorite!
This was our traditional family salad, from my Dad's side of the family in Kentucky. Goes well with any meal, tangy, I use splenda.

Simple and tasty.  I did add a little sugar (not quite 1 tsp) and I loved the tangy flavor.  I sprinkled just a tad of red pepper flakes over the salad.  This is a perfect side dish for a complex main dish.  Thanx for sharing!
Very Good!!! I did 2 things diff. I added tosted almons and used baby spinch. Thanks for the keeper!!!

A real winner! I always order Spinach Salad in restaurants, but now that I have this recipe I will not have to! The dressing is amazing! I brought this for a  Bar-b-que and it went over very well! I added extra mushrooms because I love mushrooms but everything else I kept the same. I am so glad that I have this recipe! It is a definite keeper--Thanks for sharing it!

This is a great salad. I followed the recipe exactly and I thought it was a nice combination. Next time I might use a different kind of white cheese like mozzerela or even monterey jack. I also might add cold peas. Great recipe. Thanks!
Great!  Dressing is wonderful!

Absolutely superb!  Really, I only made the dressing to add to my spinach salad.  I put it on my salad cold.  My husband was reluctant to try because he loves the hot bacon dressing, but he heated this dressing and loved it.  He now says that this dressing is his new favorite.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!

Loved this recipe.  Made it for a Christmas gathering and
everyone enjoyed it.  I am
definitely making this again on a more regular basis.  This
was simple and delicious.  Thank you for your help!

This is the best spinach salad ever.  Then again I would be hard pressed to find a recipe of Hey Jude that I didnt like.  I eliminated the tomato cause i dont like tomato in spinach salad and I increased the bacon, green onions, and used 3 hard boiled eggs.  Kept the sliced mushrooms on the side cause DD hates mushrooms but we love them.  Try baby portabella they are fantastic with this recipe.  Thanks again Judy for another great one.  The dressing is kick az

I made this for my MIL's birthday. It was delicious! This will arouse your taste buds! I announced that I didn't want any leftovers and everyone enthusiastically volunteered to have seconds. I will be making this again but next time I will try using baby portabellas like BoxO'wine recommended and I meant to top each salad with more of the freshly grated cheese but I forgot. I had soup before the salad and my MIL commented that this could be the meal and she'd be satisfied! Thank you, Hey Jude, for submitting this recipe!

This salad is just scrumptious.  Turns into a great cold marinated spinach "casserole" the next day too!  I used 3 eggs as BoxO' Wine (interesting name!) suggested and it was a good amount.  I used Extra Virgin Olive Oil and raw, unfiltered apple cider vinegar.  Thanks for posting.

We were entertaining and I needed a fast dressing for my spinach salad.The dressing was one of the easiest I've ever made, since it didn't require any onion or garlic. I did make the dressing about an hour in advance to develop the flavors. I think this help tone down the honey flavor.  I used white wine vinegar, ready cooked bacon microwaved slightly with chopped portabellos,horseradish mustard,avocado,  mixture of mostly spinach and some spring mix. I assembled it at the last minute and didn't have time to taste it and was delighted with my first bite and received compliments from my guests. I highly recommend my add-ins for the salad. They were a perfect match with the honey dressing. This is going to be a favorite recipe of mine!

Roxygirl in Colo.

I've made this salad twice now and both time to rave reviews from my diners.  BIL actually requested it the last time he visited.  I made it exactly as directed except that I keep forgetting the hard boiled egg.  But apparently it's not missed that much.  This is a fav at our house and will be made numerous times throughout the summer months. Thanks for sharing it.
Delicious!  Will make again!Thanks!
YUMMY!! This salad is awesome.  I could have eaten the entire thing all by myself.  Very easy to prepare and oh so good!  Thank you for this recipe, I will be using it many more times to come.
Made this today to go with our Christmas prime rib, it was awesome!  We will definitely make this one again...and again!

I made a few ommissions... I left out the egg and the parmesean due to personal preference, and this salad was awesome! I took it to a dinner party last night and everyone raved about it! Thanks for sharing such a tasty recipe!

A KEEPER! I left out the egg and tomato- preference- and used turkey bacon- mixed the dressing in the warm pan that was used to cook the bacon and drizzled over salad while it was wamr- om goodness- it was delish! LOVED the honey instead of sugar- fab touch! Thanks for a great recipe!
Yummy and different salad. We opted to leave off the egg, but did everything else the same. You could really taste the honey in the dressing! Thanks Hey Jude!
My family really loved this salad and the dressing was great.  I used sugar free honey and white wine vinegar and it tasted wonderful.
Fantastic! I make this when I have guests for dinner, and it is always a huge hit. Thank you for sharing the recipe.

Very delicious. Had my parents for dinner. I always make salad for my mom & I but even my dad had a serving of this salad and enjoyed it! The dressing is just perfect in my opinion. Thanks a bunch, will be my staple SS recipe.
This was incredible! I love the honey bacon dressing and am thinking about making more just to keep in the fridge. Thanks so much for posting--we will definately be making this again and again!

Fantastic salad! Dressing is a perfect balance of sweet and tangy, just right for a spinach salad. Just realized I forgot the parmesan, but it was still one of the best salads I've ever made. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I like the salad but it did not get rave reviews with my crowd, everyone voted mediocre.  Next time I might try a flavored vinegar with it and see if that makes a difference.  I did notice that I only needed to use 1/2 of the dressing, as it pooled at the bottom of the salad bowl.
Totally awesome spinach salad!  We've been making it for a while and finally decided to comment.  Made this for company several times and keep getting more and more compliments.  Really great salad!
I used apple cider vinegar, and we both liked the salad!  Next time I'll use a little more spinach.

Fantastic flavor! I omitted the tomato (personal preference), added some chopped spanish onion, and used three eggs. But the secret of this salad lies in the dressing. It's delicious. There wasn't a bite left. Thank you for posting, Hey Jude.
Excellent.  I love spinach salad but am not fond of the traditional warm dressing.  This was a very nice alternative.  My mother-in-law said "this dressing is a keeper."  Enough said.
This dressing is the best!

I served this at a dinner party I had this weekend and everyone loved it. I served the dressing on the side as I personally don't like it slathered in so much dressing ( I'm a 'put it on the side' kinda' gal). Thank you Hey Jude for a nice recipe to add to my repertoire!
The dressing is fantastic! The salad is great too. I will likely use this dressing for other salads also. A definite keeper. The whole family loved it. Thanks, Hey Jude, for the recipe!!
Very good dressing and salad.  I tried it out while entertaining and it didn't fail me.  Super easy to make with great results.
Awesome salad! I will definitely be making this one a LOT! I used turkey bacon in place of the regular and it came out wonderfully! Thank you!

Thanks, Jude, for a lovely and delicious salad.  Served with grilled chicken breast, and nothing was left over.  Can hardly wait until next summer, when I can prepare this with the special spinach grown by one of our farmer's market vendors.  Until then, I will continue to make it with the spinach available at our store.  Thanks again, Jude, for posting a winner.

Oh My goodness this was simply delicious and super easy! I didn't add hard boiled egg, and it didn't matter. I will be making this all the time! Thanks,
Anne
Really enjoyed it!  Will make again.

This is the BEST spinach salad I have ever eaten.  I added sliced avocado, 2 eggs, and left out the tomato (poor selection at the store).  I used regular spinach and was a bit worried I wouldn't like it as much as baby spinach.  I'm glad I did though, the tougher texture was truly wonderful with the creamy and crunchy toppings.  And the dressing is divine!  I will make this salad again and again.  So simple for such flavor!

Hey Jude!  What a delicious salad! I scaled it down to 4 servings and made it for my DH who is wild about spinach any way I serve it to him. Yes, he ate the whole thing...he's 6'3" and needs a BIG salad.  Made a Cobb salad for me as I was craving one, but managed to get DH to give me a bite so I could submit a review. We both give it 5 stars!  I followed your recipe except for one step. In order to make it similar to the spinach salad served at one of our favorite Italian steakhouses, I warmed the dressing, poured it over the salad, and served immediately.  It was as good as the restaurant!  I thank you and DH gives you a BIG thank-you!
Easy & very good. My family loved it. Thank you for sharing.

This was delicious. I did not put the egg in (personal preference)
For the dressing, I did half Balsamic Vinegar and half reg Vinegar and put in Dijon mustard instead of the yellow one. I, also, added a 1/4 tsp of salt and a pinch of pepper.

This was a good salad, although washing the spinach was a pain.  I like spinach and the other ingredients mixed with it well.  I was serving a crowd of vegetarians and non-vegetarians, so I cooked the bacon and left it on the side.  I think the dressing would be better with the bacon mixed in (more flavor).

Yum, yum, yum!  I served this with a veggie pesto pasta, and it was GREAT!   We added feta, craisins, and sunflower seeds, and it was soooo good!  To the earlier reviewer who tried to make it vegetarian, it makes me wonder about using bacon bits instead of bacon.  I didn't realize until recently, but most bacon bits are soy based.  I'd be curious to hear from anyone who tried that with this recipe!  :)

Oh my!  Our spinach is ready in the garden so I was looking for something different then what we usually make.  This is great. I love the dressing and the mushrooms with the spinach are fantastic.  I will use this recipe often as we all liked this salad very much.  Thank you for posting....Stephanie
An easy salad to make and absolutely delicious!  I adapted it for a diabetic by leaving out the honey and substituting a little Splenda, but that was the only change.  This one's a keeper!
Terrific - classic spinach salad.  A must-keep for your cookbook.

This surpassed my expectations. I expected a salad that would make me dutifully eat my greens. What I found was a salad I couldn't stop eating. I only used a half recipe of the dressing, and that was plenty for my large bowl of spinach. The youngest kids didn't care for the dressing. I omitted the mushrooms because they are fungi (I don't like them!).
I ahve used this recipe a couple of times and love it each time.

Made a great addition to my German dinner.. Guests loved it!
I did take the dressing and give it a few minutes in the pan the bacon cooked in.. picked up a few bacon bits and toned down the vinegar a tad.
I used just the salad dressing part on lettuce and tomatoes using bacon bits instead of crumbled bacon. Delicious!
Pretty good salad, but a lot of work.  I suggest using red onion to add a bit more flavor.
Wonderful!! Took to boyfriend's grandmothers b-day and had very little left over.  Couldn't stop eating it.  Added more bacon. yummy
Delicious. I had all on hand and I did cut the recipe back a bit to make enough for 3 people. :)

This salad was amazing. I am not very found of all spinach salads, but this one made me a believer. I loved the dressing. Due to my anemia, my doctor is always encouraging me to eat more spinach. Now there is a way I can do it that is delectable!! Thank you so much for this tasty recipe!!!
I must admit, I just made the dressing and poured it over spinach. I used microwave bacon. Despite my laziness and short cuts, this was excellent and I will definitely make it again! Thanks!

Not sure why but I didn't like this very much, and neither did my family.  I suspect it was something that I did given all the 5 star ratings so I won't rate it until I've tried it again.  I suspect that I didn't have enough spinach for all the dressing.  It was overpowering, and not particularly pleasant.  I think maybe I needed to use a flavoured vinegar instead of just white.  Any suggestions?

I forgot the cheese, left out the tomato and mushrooms and only had two slices of bacon, but it was scrumptious anyway. I also threw in a handful of dried cranberries. I followed another reviewer's suggestion to use white wine vinegar and halved the dressing recipe because I didn't think I had 8-10 servings worth of spinach and I still had lots of dressing left over. Guess I'll have to get some more spinach tomorrow!

Fantastic! I made half of the dressing which another user suggested and it was more than enough dressing. Other changes I made was to use white wine vinegar, whole grain prepared mustard and extra virgin olive oil. This is a great recipe and so easy to make! I received many compliments at dinner. I will definitely make again but I will omit the green onion but that is a personal preference. Thanks for posting the recipe!

WONDERFUL!  Let me start by saying this is not even the type of salad I would ever choose to buy/make/eat.  I had guests staying at my house and wanted to make a salad with dinner but realized I only had fresh spinach.  I came here in search of a spinach salad that incorporated all ingredients I had in the house...this was the only one that fit that bill.  I had to improvise and use fresh bacon bits (no bacon in the house) but followed this to the "T" (cutting the dressing in half per other reviewers recommendations).  PERFECT!  Delicious!  I'd say everyone at dinner ate 3 helpings of this a piece.  That says a lot!  Even I enjoyed it despite the fact that this is not the type of salad I would gravitate toward.  DELISH!

excellent recipe, we really enjoyed it. I pretty much halved everything, lightly pan fried the mushrooms (no oil), and used 1 tomato and 1 egg per person, and less parmesan. I also added in 2 boiled potatoes to make it a full meal. I also sprinkled with a handful of toasted pine nuts. The dressing is fab, thanks for sharing.
Dressing is delightful!  Thanks!
Very nice dressing! I got lots of compliments and will make it again, for sure!
This has make me again all over it!  I made for a light dinner, and served some Baked Swordfish with it.  This salad is loaded with lots of flavors that I truly enjoyed!  Thank you!  Dave

I really enjoyed this!  I only included the things that I had on hand, so a couple salad parts were left out.  I loved the dressing!  My boyfriend didn't care for it much, he found it too vinegar-y, but he usually doesn't care for my homemade dressings.  I'm using the leftover dressing today on another salad.  Thanks!

What a great salad! This may be the first time the bf was more interested in the salad than the main dish! The honey in the dressing was a bit much for us though- had to tone it down with lots of mustard. In the future- I will use less honey right off the bat. Thanks for a great salad!

Not that this needs another review but DANG THIS WAS GOOOOOOD!! I must admit I totally cheated and used Hormel REAL Bacon Bits to save on time.. (1 tb bits= 1 slice bacon) and I used White Wine Vinegar.. It was perfect for a light Sunday meal, and I WILL be making this again... YUM! Thank You very much..
This salad was a rave around the table!!  We ended up only using half the dressing for the amount of ingredients, but it was awesome!!  Now we have enough for another salad!  Woohoo!

Just delicious!!! Made it a few minutes ago and scoffed the lot. I cut the bacon up using scissors, put all the bits in a frying pan, chopped my onion popped that in too, along with slices of mushrooms. When ready i put the warmy goodness ontop on the spinach. Topped off with sliced cherry tomatoes and the lovely dressing YumYum
Very nice.  Thank you for a wonderful salad.
My DH is trying to watch his calorie intake and he had this for lunch and he loved it! I sauteed the fresh mushrooms in olive oil and garlic, YUM!!! thanks!
My DH loved it.  He wants to give it 10 stars.  I give it five firm.  I halved the recipe, and it turned out perfectly.  Will be making this many times.  Thanks for this keeper.  :)
This was delicious even my kids loved it I used apple cider vinegar instead of white vinegar we prefer this.
We really enjoyed this!  I used the cider vinegar, as suggested by another rater, and left out the (despised) mushrooms, and halved the recipe.  Yum!  Thanks!

OMG  Was this fabulous or not. I had friends over for dinnner and it was a huge hit. My friends husband who is not a Spinach fan thought it was one of the best salads ever expecially the dressing. I made exactly as directed other than using Canola oil in place of Vegetable oil . This is a definite keeper . The pastqa i served with it was Fab too and I willhave to post that

This is a terrific salad!  It is as good (or better) than any restaurant spinach salad I've eaten.  The only change I made was to add an extra egg and decrease the amount of dressing used (I like my salads lightly dressed).  This will be my "go to" recipe for spinach salad from now on.  Thanks for posting Jude!

Very tasty. I scaled this down to serve just me for lunch, using 2 slices of bacon and a half a hard boiled egg, and cutting the dressing ingredients in half - used maybe 2 TBSP to dress the salad and had plenty leftover.  Also red onions in place of the green as I didn't have any. Forgot the parmesan, which would have been a nice addition.  I heated the honey in the micro for about 30 seconds, which made it more pourable and gave me a warm dressing.  Very nice lunch, will make again,  Thanks for posting!

My husband gives this 5 stars.  He really enjoyed it.  I cut the recipe in half since I don't care for spinach all that much.  Didn't have fresh mushrooms so I put in some canned that I had patted dry.  Definately a keeper and a great way to help use up my garden spinach.  Thanks for posting!
Spicey Brown mustard really makes this salad POP, I brought this to my Ladies Night dinner party and it was thoroughly enjoyed, everyone loved it. Great post!
I love yellow mustard, so that's what I used for my salad dressing.  Excellent flavors in this salad and I really love it and have it often!
I made this for lunch and added some pre-cooked fajita flavored chicken strips. Nice recipe!
This had GREAT flavor but the dressing was VERY soupy.  If I can make it the consistency of regular salad dressing I would rate this 5 stars!

I thought the recipe was really good. I noticed that it has more dressing then it needed so instead of adding it all at once just add until coated. I'm going to stick with my own spinach salad recipe because it suits my tastes better because I use sugar or splenda instead of honey.  Taste is subjective.

Took Jencathen's comment and did not add the dressing.  I served it on the side - I'm glad I did or else it would have drowned the salad.  I also took Slick Rick's advice and added some slivered toasted almonds.  I used cherry tomatoes and doubled the egg.  When the bacon was almost done and put honey on it and let it soak.  It was a wonderful salad.  Thanks for the recipe and thanks to the reviewers for the comments - the Zaar is an awesome experience!!

Very nice.  I really liked the dressing flavors.  I used red onion and skipped the tomotoes and mushrooms and we really enjoyed the combination.  Would like to try this during the summer with fresh homegrown tomatoes.  Thanks for sharing.
very good!  I added chopped pecans and finely chopped red onions instead of the green,and back bacon. My teenagers love this thanks!

Delicious salad for a dinner party.  I omitted the tomato and added sliced strawberries for the salad and for the dressing used 1/2 Balsamic Vinegar and 1/2 white vinegar and everyone seemed to really like it.  Will definitely make this again.
I really enjoyed this as well. I added avocado and cucumber just for more vegetables. The only thing is that the dressing was a little bit strong for me. Other than that, great recipe!
Loved the dressing on this salad.  Will be having this one a lot.

Love the dressing for this salad! A good, sweet vinegrette!! My mom used to make it all the time! We used to use it on a salad with lettuce, spinach, cubed chicken, bacon bits, nuts, and mandrin oranges! The oranges sound a little strange, but it is SOOO yummy!! So easy to make your own!
This was one of the tastiest spinach salads that we have had.  All the ingredients were right on.  Thanks for posting this magnificent spinach salad.  We will use it a lot I'm sure.
This salad had a good blend of flavors but the dressing was way too sweet for us. I have made this before with a hot dressing that suited our tastes a little better. Thank you.

While I was nursing my son, I had to cut out dairy.  This was one recipe I turned to for lunches and I found it very tasty!  It's been too long since I've eaten it, but I think I left out the tomato (and I know I left out the cheese) and I may have added pecans or some sort of nut.  I will need to resurrect it--with cheese this time. Yummy!

I was anxious to try a variation of my standard spinach salad and this one hit the spot!  Loved the sweet and sour flavor of the dressing.  I sprinkled a little pepper on the salad and Ooh La La the salad was brought to life!

Probably one of the best Spinach Salad recipes ever!! I made this exactly as stated with the exception of using grated parmesan instead and cut the measurement in half for it. The dressing is soooooo yummy!! Thanks for a keeper!
Absolutely amazing salad! I normally don't care for raw spinach, but this recipe makes it taste wonderful!

I made this recipe for a group Christmas dinner and it was a hit, I couldn't believe how many raved and requested the recipe during dinner.  In fact, I'm making it for Christmas day dinner!  I am allergic to spinach so I substituted Arugula and it's peppery flavor went just as well with the recipe!

Very good!  My wife said it's the best thing I've ever made for her.  I used half sesame oil and half vegetable.  I also added some toasted rice noodles by La Choy that added a bit of crunch to it.  I might add some dried cherries next time I make it.

I absolutely love spinach salad, and this one is amazing...even my picky teenagers, who refuse to eat any salad "with stems", loved it!  The dressing is absolutely perfect - as good as any restaurant version I've had.  I omitted the cheese, and don't think it was missed. Thank you for sharing, I will be making this on a regular basis.
Not the best bacon salad dressing = but salad was good
This was pretty good but definitely not the best spinach salad I've made or had.

The dressing is what really makes this for me. I took off from the actual salad ingredients and used what I had - spinach, eggs, mushrooms, pomegranate seeds, and crispy thin chow mein noodles for a bit of crunch along with the bacon.

How many times do I need to review this before reviewing?  This is my go to recipe for spinach salad.  Very tasty as a main dish salad.  The last couple of days I have made it has a main dish wish a cup of soup on the side.  If there is extra dressing just refrigerate for later.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.
One of my favorite salads!  You can even warm up the dressing and make it a warm spinach salad too!

Great recipe! I halved it and added red onion sauteed in the bacon grease. I think red wine vinegar  works best for our tastes. Added salmon and avocado to make it a dinner salad. Thanks for the keeper!

Very good salad. I used shallots instead of green onions and shredded pepperjack cheese. I also added some sugared nuts. The dressing tastes very light and tangy. I used red wine vinegar.  Thanks for posting!

Whole family really enjoyed this!  Only thing I'll say is it makes waaaay too much dressing.  You can easily cut it in half.  Otherwise, pretty much perfect.  Thanks for the great recipe Hey Jude.....

This has to be the best salad I've ever made/had! I'm not the biggest salad lover, but this was phenomenal! So much flavour! I wanted soft boiled eggs, but apart from that I made it exactly as the recipe stated. That dressing is to die for!
This salad was great! The mushrooms added some heartiness. The only thing I did different was to double the dark mustard for extra tang, because otherwise the dressing is quite sweet.
This spinach salad recipe is the best that I try.??????thank you.

This was good. My only criticism is regarding the dressing. If the dressing is made with the listed ingredients it makes more than a cup. That's a whole lot of dressing even for 8 cups of spinach. I halved the whole recipe to make four servings and made only 1/4 the amount of dressing and still thought it was way too much. Guess there are folks who like their salad swimming in dressing.
I didn't have poultry seasoning so I added some soy sauce.  Quick to make if you have some cooked chicken.
This came out awesome! I didn't change a thing.

The finished chops were tender but NOT succulent like a broiled chop would be. The seasoning sounded better to me than it was in reality. I LOVE lamb and lamb chops, having them at least once a week. This was a disappointment. :(

I do think that the seasoning and then broiling the chops might be worth trying.

The weather outside was frightful and I wanted some comfort food - to me that usually means crockpot.  Well this recipe filled the bill.I love my lamb chops pink but I knew crockpot chops wouldn't be pink  so instead of Loin chops I used shoulder chops. I cut the recipe in half and still cooked it for 6 hours on low.  I added a potaoe and used 2 small onions (the onions were my second veggie).Wonderful flavor Thanks again Dancer

I'm a recent owner of a slow cooker and really have been amazed how lovely meat tastes after being cooked in one. It is so tender and the flavours I've tried have been great.
For this recipe I used 6 hogget leg chops, the garlic/herb rub is perfect with the lamb.
Thanks for a wonderful recipe.  =)

I am a fairly new slow-cooker user. These chops turned out so well. The rub was supreme. The onion and garlic flavor a definite plus. The meat was so tender and falling off the bone. I cooked on low for 4 hours. Thanks for posting this.

My husband is a lamb chop lover. I actually have never had them until now. They turned out great. Very tender and juicy. The mixture of herbs and spices was a great compliment to the flavor of the lamb. This was so easy that even a beginner cook like me could do it. Thanks Nurse Di.

We used pork chops with this recipe, and felt that preparing them as the recipe states, made them turn out too dry.  I would recommend modifying it and adding a liquid, possibly a broth.  This meal is what I would consider a mid-western, farmer type of meal, that is what most would consider a "confort" food.  It is easy on the stomach, but lacks "interest" for me.  I would recommend changing up the spices, kicking things up a notch!  May consider using again..?

These turned out great for us--and like Michael Stok I consider these "comfort food" which I love. I had to make a minor change in the recipe because I was out of garlic, so instead of garlic powder and salt, I used 1/2 tsp garlic salt and sprinkled 1/4 tsp garlic powder over all. They came out scrumptious. We had the lamb  chops with salad and baked potatoes with brownies (from a mix) for a perfect weekend meal. Thanks NurseDi for posting another keeper.

I made this using a boneless leg of lamb rather than chops.  I doubled the herb mix (just stuck to one onion, though, since mine seemed very strong) and the only thing I did differently was I put a little olive oil in the bottom of the pot and also drizzled some over the lamb.  This was going to be in the pot for 12 hours so I was a little worried about it drying out.  It was needless to worry since it really produced so much juice (I made a good amount a gravy and I still had a lot of juice leftover) and the lamb was very tender.  I think DH gave 5 "mmmm"s as he ate it, so I think that deserves 5 stars.  :)  Thank you!

These were wonderful.  I sauted the onions in a small amount of olive oil before adding to the crockpot and then browned the chops in same pan.  Deglazed the pan with about 1/4 cup of water, scraping up all the tidbits that stuck to the pan.  Poured this over chops in crockpot and cooked for 5 hours.  Very tender and moist.
These smelled wonderful cooking in the crockpot all afternoon. I was worried they'd be dry without any extra liquid, but they were deliciously moist. Two thumbs up from the whole family.

I'm in shock.  I chose this recipe in desperation...from lack of time, chops that needed to be cooked today, and a scorcher of a day...with no expectations of it turning out very well.  I couldn't imagine my favorite lamb chops being very good cooked in a crockpot.  Boy was I wrong...they turned out to be fabulous, tender and flavorful.  I love this recipe! I don't usually review things, but i thought i would post my cautionary tale for a laugh.

So a friend gave me about 5 lbs of chilies of various heats from his garden and i decided i wanted to make a jam.  I'm travelling for work, so i thought this could be a good project for my solitary evening in the hotel room.  The hotel stovetop was not heating very well, so i covered the pot and walked away for a couple of minutes.  I caught it just as the pot was boiling over, but was not in time to save the carmelized peppery boil over from burning.  I opened all the windows as soon as i could, but was too late.  The smoke alarm went off.  The front desk called to tell me not to open the door or else the hallway alarms would go off.  I listened, choking on fiery pepper seed smoke the whole time.  I got a call five minutes later saying that the fire department will be at my room in a minute.  Five firemen and a policeman couldn't stand the spice in the air!  Needless to say, it was a spectacle - all the hotel alarms going off, me and the firemen gathered around a huge fan with 20 or so spectators in the hallways, most of whom were wearing earplugs from the screech of the alarms.  Please watch your pot when you make this one!

After all was said and done, nothing was burned and the jam turned out great!  I made it just as the recipe says and can't wait to enjoy every bite!  :)

Ended up blowing bubbles in the sink to put it out. But the jelly was worth the pain. Even used the pepper pulp mixture for flavoring a roasting chicken.

I have baked a lot of bread but this recipe is by far the best bread recipe I have ever tried. I suggest the following to make it truly fail proof for those of you who did not have good results: Use bread flour and weigh the flour. If you don't have a kitchen scale, get one. Set it to grams. Then, weigh the measuring cup and then add 120 grams of flour for each cup. The final 1/2 cup of flour will be 60 grams of flour plus the weight of the cup). Then, I used 1-1/4 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 teaspoon sugar. I also used 2 teaspoons of active dry yeast (do not use instant yeast!). I ended up adding 1 teaspoon of additional flour to the bread maker since the dough seemed to want to stick just a tiny bit in the first kneading cycle. Then, because I used a dark cookie sheet (or nonstick pan), I reduced the oven temperature to 425 degrees. I baked the bread for 20 minutes. I checked the internal temperature of the bread with an instant thermometer and it was 200 degrees. I then cooled it on a wire rack. Perfect. Thank you for the best bread recipe ever.

I either roast eggplant on grill or in oven, depending on Canadian weather.  I use garlic, minced, and mostly do a combo of tomato paste/home made salsa instead of the tomato sauce.
