This has really good flavor, but we felt the recipe was a little underdeveloped.  Next time we will roll this mixture up in tortillas, maybe with a little rice.  Overall, very delicious!  Thanks!

I love eggplant and Mexican food...so I knew I had to try this dish, and what a great combo it is! It was easy to make and so delicious! I added minced garlic instead of garlic powder, and also added black beans. Definitely a keeper!

This was wonderful! Even hubby who doesn't like eggplant liked it (don't know if he even realized it was eggplant - never told him what was in it). I used half as much cheese - part lowfat, part fat free & a couple slices of processed American cheese.

This was really easy and really good.  The only modifications made were that my cheddar was not fat-free and DH doubled the cumin and garlic powder.  Perfect.  DH and I ate the whole dish.  DH also indicated he would have this again.  A real compliment!  He is interested in adding beans the next time we make it to see how it compared.  Thanks for posting!

Excellent recipe and easy on my budget. I love the simple ingredients and delicious flavor. Also love that you can add different things to this recipe and have a new meal each time.
I added kidney beans.
Super easy and so yummy!!  The second time I made it I used a whole jar of tomato sauce (Classico Spicy Red Pepper) 24 oz.  It was perfect!
Scrumptious!  Filling, healthful and satisfying.  I used 2% sharp cheddar.  Couldn't find non-fat cheese.  I recommend highly!

This was yummy. I used 2 small eggplants that yielded 17 slices. I baked first and added a little salt, pepper, and cumin to the roasting eggplant to make sure that there was a lot of flavor. I doubled the cumin, added corn and kidney beans, and to the sauce I added 2 tbs of my own, homemade enchilada sauce. I only added cheese to the top and I added 2 layers of tortillas...which my husband said really made the recipe! I will make this again because it was good, but it probably won't go into my weekly routine b/c I wasn't super excited about the consistency of the eggplant. Maybe grilling will help firm it up some.
Very good! I made the recipe as directed except for using full fat cheese. I will make this again.

I have made this several times now, and have varied the recipe slightly each time.  Made without olives, used onion instead of green onion, etc.  I decided that next time I am going to "beef" it up with the addition of zucchini squash.  Great recipe every time!
This was a really hearty satisfying meal without feeling too heavy. I used full fat cheese, and roasted jalapenos and anaheim chiles, Easy, quick, healthy and tasty. Thanks for posting the recipe.

This is so good! I usually avoid eggplant, but this is worth the weird vegetable! It really tastes yummy! I substituted refried beans for the green chilies to add some substance- mixed about 1/3 of a can with half a can tomato sauce. (only used 1 large eggplant, and it served 2 of us.) Thanks for posting this great recipe!<br/>*Made it again; the flavor of the sauce really makes the dish, I found that adding a bit of chili powder kicks it up. We also like to add just 1 or 2 tortillas in strips.

Yummy! And SO easy. I sliced and cooked 2 eggplants (good sized), but only used about 1.5. Based on some of the reviews, I doubled the cumin and garlic powder, and I added a tsp of chili powder. I used a low-fat Mexican blend cheese, the package was 2 cups.  I omitted the olives because I don't care for them.  The eggplant came out nice and soft (but not mushy), and the flavors were so good.  I love eggplant, I think I'm going to try this same approach as a "parm" - all the taste, but not all the work. Updated:  I tried this as more of a parm version.  I coated the slices with a breadcrumb and cheese mixture, then used more Italian spices with the tomato sauce, and mozzarella for the cheese.  I wish I could say it came out as good as the Mexican version, but it didn't.  Guess I'll stick to regular eggplant parm, and use this recipe for Mexican eggplant.
We didn't like it, but I think it was mostly an aversion to the eggplant.
Can this be made without an oven? In a microwave? If yes, how?
Great recipe! Thanks

I gave this 5 starts because it is easy and flavorful. I love eggplant and was looking for a different way to make them. I made a few minor changes because I didn't have certain ingredients in the house. I substituted regular onions for the green onions, and some chili powder for the chilis. Will make again. Thanks.

This dish was amazing! Thank you so much. I had a last minute get-together and some eggplant I wanted to use. We were doing a Mexican theme so this was a no-brainer. I've never had it this way. I LOVE eggplant anyway, but this is my new favorite! So delicious and EVERYONE loved it. I had no leftovers at all, so I made it again today ;) Thanks again!
Was wonderful my husband had thirds. I made this but made some alterations. My husband and I like medium hot spicy Mexican foods.
With the tweaks me made (thanks Gayle H.) this was delicious, we do like spice :) . We also think this would work with pork mince as an addition for a non-vegetarian option.
Wow! This was great!! Made it exactly like recipe! So good!
Simple, very rich - I used store-bought gnocchi so it was a ten-minute meal.

This was a pretty good dish. I did use premade gnocchi though to save time. I also decided to add some steamed asparagus ti it. The only real complaint I had with it is that melted gorgonzola is a very unaatreactive grayish-green color. I will probably make it again.
I don't mind the colour of this delicious sauce one little bit!  I used purchased potato gnocchi.  Loved it.

Exceptional, perfect balance.  It is worth it to purchase creamy gorgonzola for this dish, which is excellent for a special occasion!  This was a great copy of my favourite gnocchi dish from a Melbourne Italian restaurant.  I didn't make the gnocchi but I will as soon as my potato ricer arrives!

I like making gnocchi, but it's generally a messy process for me,  however, these were absolutely beautiful and so fuss free!!  I don't have a ricer, so I grated the potatoes.  I also had a couple of small sweet potatoes in the veg bin, I used them and that accounted for about 100 gr of my total potato weight.
So, my gnocchi were a great suceess and I will use this recipe to make them again!
The sauce was made as directed, except, I added a good pinch of nutmeg.   Incredibly rich and creamy, to die for.   For DH, it was too rich, he felt that a handful of fresh chopped herbs might have provided a bit of 'taste freshening', however, for me, this was heaven on a plate!!!

Loved this, Leslie, thanks so very much, made for Aus/NZ Swap#34

Fabulous Leslie! I cut back on the recipe and made the gnocchi with 1 lb of spuds, there are only the two of us! I also subbed the heavy cream for creme fraiche as I do not use cream often, and always have creme fraiche in the fridge.........the combination of the cheeses and creme fraiche was fabulous! I LOVE all blue cheese, and so I did use gorgonzola, and left a few chunks whole to sprinkle on top of the finished dish with the parmesan. I sprinkled some freshly chopped parsley over for colour before serving for a delightful lunch today! Made for the Aus/NZ recipe swap and a keeper for us darlink! FT :-)

I have always wanted to make gnocchi and now I can say that I did and I'm good at it! This was so easy to make and the little dumplings were light and fluffy. We aren't real blue cheese people so I mixed it with parmesan, cheddar and mozzarella. There was a ton of cheese, but everyone really liked it! We enjoyed this very much with Recipe #316270. Made for ZWT7 for our tour guide. Thanks Leslie! :)

Made this on Friday, I used grouper since I didn't have any shark steaks (already ate them) and it was very good.  The only other thing I did differently was to chop up a couple portabello mushrooms and a tomato into the bottom of my pan and put fish and marinade ontop.  Will try this soon with shark on the barbie!

This was my first time eating shark; I bought it on sale and had no idea what to do with it then I searched and found this easy recipe. I made this for me and my mom, both of us doing low-carb dieting.  She loved it; I didn't care for the shark taste itself, the marinade was fine.  I will try this marinade recipe on other fish though.  Thanks for posting!
The flavor was very good.  My husband likes things with sauce, so he was not to sold on it.

I bought some shark on sale & had no idea how to cook it...this recipe sounded easy & flavorful.  It WAS easy, although my shark didn't absorb as much of the marinade flavor as I hoped, even though I let it sit 4 hours.  Maybe that's just the nature of shark.  I grilled it on a Foreman indoor grill and it came out with a nice dark/grilled appearance and pretty tasty, almost like chicken in texture but more tender.  I'd make it again for sure!

Here on the coast of Maine we get very fresh fish.  Last week I got a shark steak right off the boat - and prepared it just as written.  PERFECT!  - I am having this again tonight.  My DH loved it and this time he stopped to get a fresh shark steak.  Maybe it's because it is so fresh - but it's great.

I didn't grow up eating fish or any sea food so each week my husband and i try a new creature of the sea ;) and i must say there have been quite a few i didn't care for  however this is not one of them A   awesome

We recently moved to south FL.  Black-tip sharks abound here - not endangered, or threatened, and we obey bag limits. :)  We learned from the locals the strict cleaning process...and we soaked the meat in fresh water overnight, then in milk for 6-8 hours.  After that, however, I really had no idea how to go about cooking shark.  (And, we were out of propane for the grill!)  So, I found myself staring at this recipe last night...and it was a huge success!!  Everyone - kids and hubby - loved it!  I doubled everything, just because we had so much meat.  Our "steaks" were also more like slender fillets...maybe that helped them absorb the flavor.  Either way, this was terrific and it is going in the "Save" file!!  Thanks!

This is absolutely delicious!! Son's boss blessed him with 10 lbs. of thresher shark steaks.  We've eaten shark prepared by others, but never having cooked it myself, I searched for recipes.  Found this one, tried it several times, and the results have been perfect each time.  I thoroughly pierced each piece with a sharp fork and marinated for the full hour.  Tender and tasty!! Thank you!!  Will try this with other fish as well!

great recipe - I first inspected the fish and cut out any dark areas - then soaked the fish in lemon water for several hours in the refrigerator.  Removed and dried the fish and marinated as directed. Followed the recipe and got raves from all my quests. Loved it
I made the  gnocchi and used my red sauce (family recipe).These brought back memories of my aunt Lina. Very very good.

These turned out great, easy to work with, light and fluffy when cooked.  Only cooked 25 of them and made half the sauce but less blue cheese.  Great flavor to the sauce.  I froze the other 80 I got from the recipe so will see how they cook up.  Served with Italian bread and a salad.

This is an absolute winner! The combination of potatoes, curry and chickpeas cannot be beaten, especially when you are in need of some guilt-free comfort food! I'd cook it with some additional chopped chilli, and serve it with some VERY lightly steamed spinach for a feast for body and soul...

Great recipe, Dancer^. My husband and I both thought it was very tasty. I increased jalapeno to 1 t. and that was perfect for our tastes. Potatoes and chickpeas go well together and we are carb lovers so the comfort level was high. The curry, onion, and tomato flavors were well balanced. Thanks for another good one.

Absolutely delicious and so easy to make.  Better than the ones I buy at the Indian restaurant.  My husband, who is very fussy, loved it.  We will have it tonight with rice.  Thanks.  Love you Recipezaar.

I just made this for lunch this afternoon. I doubled this recipe! ;)

I did not use potatoes in this because I'm trying to cut on starchy food these days. I used fresh chickpeas which I soaked overnight, boiled this morning and then added to this recipe while cooking it. I did not use tomato juice. I used about 6-8 small fresh tomatoes(peeled and chopped).I found this on the spicy side, it's the curry that is so flavourful! I loved this with rice and yoghurt; delish absolutely, Auntie Janette! Thanks so much for posting! Miss hearing from you...Hope your good!
yum! This was so simple to make, and the flavor was so rich and delicious, and very filling dish too! I normally hate tomato juice, and was pleasantly surprised by how good it could taste.
Very tasty! Easy to put together and makes lots. Lovely colour. Nice aroma.
This was very good, economical and tasty.  I ate it with the hot peppers, but I think it would be also good without.
I have made this dish several times and it gets better each time!!  Very easy to make and little prep time.  I make it without the jalapenos, but add red pepper.

I loved this recipe. It was easy to prep and then just let cook. The flavors were lovely. I should note that my family didn't like it as much as I did...they found it too mushy. I disagree, but I probably could sautÃ© the onions less, keeping them crisper, and reduce overall cooking time so the potatoes and chickpeas would be more firm. I also think serving it over lightly steamed spinach would give it more crunch. But regardless, those silly meat-eaters don't know what they're talking about anyway. This was wonderful!

OMG I just want to say that I loved this recipe. My daughter (25 yrs old)& I love to try new recipes. We both love curry. The combination of the curry and potatoes was just amazing. Thank you for post such a great recipe. This is now 1 of our fav's :)

I have made this recipe several times, and I and my partner just love it! It's quick to prepare, healthy, and the flavors blend just beautifully. I have served it on rice and on thin spaghetti, and both are good. I'm planning to make it again this week!

This is an amazing dish!!!! Very easy to follow. When you have that can of chick peas and dont know what to do with them here is your answer. I some time add a little fresh spinach to it for color. Thanks for posting.
My family really likes this dish!  I used a can of diced tomatoes instead of the tomato juice and it turned out great.  Thanks!
I made this for dinner last night.  We enjoyed it, but we were not blown away by it.  It seemed to lack a bit of flavor.  Followed recipe exactly including the addition of jalapeno.
Very nice! Simple, healthy and super filling. Thanks for sharing the recipe.
There isn't a kid in the world that doesn't love these. My grandmother made these for us when we were little. Thanks for sharing your recipe with us at 'zaar.

I had never heard of Apple Schmarren before I found this recipe.  If you have never tried it, I suggest you do for a real breakfast treat!  I prepared this without the raisins only because I had none in the house. I used the only non-stick pan in my kitchen, which happened to be a crepe pan, which worked perfectly for this amount of batter. If you will look at the photo posted above you will see that I prepared this as one piece instead of allowing it to break into pieces.  I used two very flexible spatulas to flip, and it worked out well. The sweetness of the apples gives this recipe a wonderful flavor.  I loved the cinnamon-sugar topping, but I also think a bit of real maple syrup may work well also!  This recipe will serve two very hungry people easily!  Love this recipe, Montana Roux!  Thanks for sharing it with Zaar!

Excellent!  I learned how to make Schmarrn while living in Germany, as this version tastes very authentic.  I usually make mine with lemon flavor, but this was really yummy with apples & cinnamon too.  I omitted the the raisins.  Delicious and super easy to prepare.  In Germany,the kids get to chop up the pancake at the end of the cooking process with two forks.

I didn't get the hang of flipping the schmarren in 1 or 2 pieces, so my schmarren was more like scrambled scharren.  But it was good!  I used all of the cinnamon sugar.  Besides the 2 tsp. of sugar, it's really the only sweetener in the recipe and it coats the apples so nicely.  This would be a very nice brunch recipe.

This is good! I made this for breakfast today, and followed the directions except that instead of breaking it apart in the pan, I let it cook until nice and browned on the bottom, and then put it under the grill until browned on top .. I used an oven safe skillet .. this is good and easy, thank you for posting!
So easy, so palatable, so original.  In other words, PERFECT!  Thank you for sharing this recipe!  I will definitely make this often.

I think this was fabulous. Thanks Debby for this wonderful treat. I added 2 1/2 tsps of sugar and topped only with the cinnamon(which I love). I used Bev's technique with good effect and used a non-stick pancake pan. Next time I will try the oven top browning technique. I used the raisins and they also contributed to the sweetness. SO it was perfect! :) Fay

Excellent breakfast!! This looked like a big, fat, stuffed pancake cooking. But it had a very light taste and texture when eating - more like a souffle has. I used both the apples and raisins, and when I flipped it, using two spatulas it only broke in half - perfect for my DH and self. A definate keeper in my book!

Fantastic!! Loved it!! When I flipped it, it broke into two pieces, which was ok, because each piece was a portion size, so when I put it on our plates, it looked so pretty. We thought the sweetness of this was just perfect, it wasn't overly sweet, but yet you could adjust the sweet taste by adding more cinnamon/sugar topping. It was a delicious breakfast treat which was so simple to make. Thanks Charmed, this is a WINNER.
This was a very good breakfast.  I've not had schmarren before, and it was very tasty.

I made this for breakfast this weekend, wanting to do something different, but having limited supplies on hand.  This had good flavor, but the apples were a little too crisp for my taste, even though I sliced them thin. I wonder if grating them would work....  Anyway, DH and DS both liked this too, which I served along with some beef sausage. (I omitted the raisins too, due to preference.) And I was able to get it flipped in one piece!  Thanks for the recipe! I'll make this again!
Yummy breakfast. I used whole wheat flour, one egg and an egg white. We loved the flavor and I even got it flipped in one piece. Thanks for a great recipe!
It is a great recipe and I ate it a lot as a child. Raisins are a must for me. I like the picture.It is a good idea to serve it in one piece.

We didn't like this too much. I made it for breakfast yesterday and it just tasted too eggy to me. And I didn't like that combination of apples and eggs. I mean it was okay with the nice sweet topping but definately not something I'll try again.
This was such an eggy mess I could not eat it. It tasted too much like an omlette (which is not what I wanted for breakfast), and the apples were too crunchy. The birds are getting this one!

I can't believe I have never rated this before.  I have made this many times with vanilla soy milk and 2 egg whites and one egg yolk.  I think people need to remember that it IS an eggy recipe, but that is what makes it so great!  Mine never looks good like Bev's photo, but that's okay.
Today, I sauteed the apples while I mixed up the egg mixture.  The apples were still firm, but I like it that way. I drizzled it with a bit of maple syrup.  YUM!
This has been in my Best of Zaar so Far cookbook for several years now.
KCShell

This is very reminicent of an apple pancake, but soft and eggy.  It was good with syrup, and great with vanilla yogurt (my pancake topping of choice). I think I'll try sauteeing the apples next time and only doing a half batch.  My kids didn't like it much, but that just means I don't have to share now!

The pancake was wonderful, quick and easy to make. This light and tender pancake tasted delicious, it was satisfying without being heavy. It was soft and eggy with apples, spices and raisins.  The apple cinnamon topping was the perfect touch. Thank you for sharing your recipe, which we enjoyed very much and which I will make again.  Made for Whats on the Menu Tag Game.
This cake is really tasty and I've enjoyed serving it to little kids at my home in Muscat, Oman. Always makes them happy and ask for more:)
This recipe is a favorite wherever I take it!  Kids and kids at heart will love this easy chocolate treat.

My family loved this cake!!! Tastes just like Ho Ho's and soooo easy to make! I took the cake out of the pan, sliced it in half and put the filling on the bottom half, put the top layer of cake back on and topped it with the icing. Very very good! Thanks, this is our new favorite cake!!

was wonderful, made it for a funeral potluck and there were only crumbs left. Thank you for the great recipe. Had a hard time getting the filling to pull together, but found if you beat for 10 min and let it rest for about 5 min. and beat again that you have better luck with it.

Excellent recipe! Tastes just like a "Ho Ho". I made it for my husband's birthday. the whole family raved and my mother requested that I make it for her birthday. Thanks for the recipe-fun way make chocolate cake a little more interesting.
I have never given a 1 star before but this was horrible. No one in my family would even finish their first piece. I had to throw it away. Im sorry but I will not be making this again.

My sister-in-law makes this all the time.  She lives in another town, and I was really hungry for this, so I searched here on the Zaar and found this one that is most like hers.  I thought it was great.  I like the frosting idea on this one as compared to the other recipes that call for melting chocolate chips, margarine and adding raw egg.  The raw egg kinda bothered me.   This is excellent.

I prefer the bar version made in the jelly roll pan, but the timing needs to be adjusted to 17 minute bake time.  The cake mix could also be divided into two 9X13 pans and then double the filling and icing to make two pans.  Also, the only way to frost these is with homemade frosting as follows.  Melt 3 oz choc with 3 T butter, then mix in 3 c powdered sugar w/1 tsp vanilla.  It will be very crumbly.  Then mix in about 6 T boiling water until it reaches a pouring consistancy.  Pour over top and refridgerate.
Dear....this is definitely comfort food...just like Mum used to make...we LOVED the flavours and it made such a gorgeous gravy!
This was absolutely fabulous!!!  Very tender and flavorful!!
This was soooooo good. The house smelled heavenly while it was cooking. And it lived up to all it promised. I used a cheapo 7 bone roast. It was great!
made this for dinner last night and it was so comforting! i did not have any horseradish but will make sure i pick some up at the store next time-i'm sure it's even better!
Mmm, this was so good!  Different from the regular recipe we use, and everyone enjoyed it.  I especially loved the flavor from the horseradish, and served more alongside.  Thanks for posting!

I've tried at least 20 different ways to make chuck roast. NONE of which I ever wanted to eat a second time. This is the first one that I know I'm going to crave a lot. I had a smaller roast, but used the rest of ingredients as prescribed. Do not be fooled at 180 minutes! (4 flips at 45 minutes). My DH thought it was "done" and turned off the oven. I came in and decided to go ahead and cook that final hour with the veggies. It was a very wise decision. I pulled out half the meat before adding the veggies, just in case I was wrong. OHBOY! What a difference in that last hour. The meat actually absorbed all that yummy mustardy oniony goopy goodness. Mine was super flavored since my roast was only about 2lbs. The gravy needed zero touch-up. In fact, I would like to have had a bit more. Not too salty or too rick, and it flavored those taters and carrots to perfection.

I'm picky. I've tried some nasty recipes off this site that I was so disapointed at that I couldn't even rate them. This one is absolute perfection and tasted like nothing I've ever had.
Just wish I'd had enough tangy pure horsradish left over (I used last of my jar) to eat along with the meat....
BLESS you for FINALLY giving me a chuck roast recipe that has a definitive flavor and still tastes like someone's grandma made it

I used a smaller roast (2.88 lbs) and used less mustard and horesradish. I felt as I was spreading that it was too much for the size of beef so I decreased the amount (next time I might use the regular amount despite the smaller roast size). The house did smell great as this was cooking! I think I might have needed a shallower pan since my broth ended up quite deep and probably boiled (instead of roasting) my vegetables and I think dilluted some of the mustard/horseradish sauce.I made the day before and the meat sliced nicely (for a pot roast) and I reheated the sliced meat with the gravy in a latge skillet, and served over mashed potatoes, with the other vegetables on the side. My gravy turned out nicely and it went great with mashed potatoes. I liked that it didn't get overly thick upon refrigeration. I found the directions to be exact and that was helpful. I will make this again for sure. My whole family liked it a lot. It was a comfort meal. Thanks Kelly!
Roxygirl

Wow Kelly! This is a definate keeper! The end result doesn't taste like horseraddish and mustard.. it's one of those flavors that if you ate it out somewhere, you wouldn't be able to put your finger on the seasonings. I used a 3lb tip roast. I like the fact that while it was very tender, it doesn't fall apart when you slice it. The gravy was excellent also.. I've never used that technique for gravy before, I may have to use it with my turkey juices on Thanksgiving.  This is a wonderful recipe! I also noticed that you have a LOT of great sounding recipes to your credit. Thanks so much for submitting! I will be making potroast this way from now on!
Very, very good!  I am not a fan of horseradish or mustard, but this was delicious.  I will definitely make this again.
This roast was a very pleasant surprise!  Will use it again.  The horseradish & mustard in this recipe is mild after cooking and makes all the difference!

My husband tried this the other night, he said it was the best potroast he had ever had. My inexpensive roast came out tender, and we loved the horseradish/mustard flavors. A welcome update to potroasting.

This was wonderful and the aroma while it was cooking had all our tummies rumbling!! I used an almost 3 lb. boneless beef chuck roast,a few more carrots,Zaterains Creole Mustard, and added 1/2 t. of Kitchen Bouquet to darken the gravy a little. The pot roast sliced neatly and the flavor of the horseradish and mustard were nicely tempered after the long cooking time.Thanks, Kelly, for a definite keeper!

Excellent!  I'm still swooning. I loved the sauce that the broth and mustard and horseradish made.  It was so good smothered on everything.  I added parsnips with the vegetables and, oh, were they good in there, too!

I may as well join the 5 star list because this recipe is that good.  i also used a tip roast and was very very pleased with the results.  we made ours in a crock pot.  lots of gravy left... i added more carrots and potatoes than listed but next time i will add even more!  the flavor is just outstanding- will be making this again, Thank You!

I agree with other reviewers about great taste & wonderful aroma, but 3 1/2 hours seemed excessive, and while the end product was flavorful, it was also more dry (well done) than I would have liked.  Use your own judgement on that one.

I just finished devoring this lucious roast. It was exactly what I was looking for!Potatoes and carrots were not overly mushy. I made a roux and add the broth from the finished product to make gravy. It was absolutely out of this world. I will be making this very often through the colder months! Thanks for sharing
This is better than my grandmother's pot roast! I don't know what else to say, and anyone who has grandmothers understands! Absolutely mouth-watering delicious.

We loved this!  It was very easy to make and made 3 full meals for us two on a 3.5lb roast (the gravy is wonderful on hot roast beef sandwiches later).  I used a creole-style mustard and didn't use the onion because the DH doesn't like them.

This smelled so good and homey while it cooked, and my DH and DS both loved it. DH says 5 stars,  and DS (age 2) kept pestering me for some while it cooked. I used 2 medium-large onions, and didn't have quite enough horseradish. DH said he couldn't really taste either; probably since I was short on the horseradish and only had Dijon mustard (I think stone-ground would be more flavorful). I might add some garlic in future. The recipe made a lot, too--plenty of leftovers for lunches. Definitely a keeper!

This really was wonderful.  We like LOTS of gravy, so I used a 32 oz container of beef broth.  With so much liquid, I did not want to dilute the mustard and horseradish, so I doubled the amount and I am glad I did.  While you could definitely taste it, it was very mellow and subtle.  If I had stuck with the original amount, it would have been lost in all the broth.  The only other change I made was to thicken it with flour rather than cornstarch.  I prefer gravies thickened with flour....personal preference.  I served this with Beer Bread, recipe #73440, and they went together perfectly.  Thanks!

Oh My God, oh so good....Next time the only thing I would change would be use a little less Dijon Mustard. The flavor was outstanding, we just kept on commenting on how good our meal was.  We added fresh mushrooms and had homemade french bread.  Delicious!!!
Yummy!!! Wonderful comfort food.  The only thing I changed was that I didn't have red skinned potatoes, so used white potatoes which I peeled.  Thanks for a great recipe!!!

Excellent! I had a little smaller roast but used all of the horseradish and some country style dijon mustard. Glad I did. This was wonderful and the house smelled great. I made a lot of gravy so DH was one happy camper! Thanks Kelly!

My husband went out and got me a new crockpot; it was a more than subtle message that he wanted me to make him some pot roast!  I picked your recipe because he likes horseradish, whole grain mustard and everything else listed!  The only thing I changed was to add a little bit of celery at my husband's request.  Well, I don't really even like pot roast but I found myself more than picking at this one, Kelly!  My hubby must have liked it because it's gone and he bought another chuck roast last night when he went to the store!

I made this roast over the weekend, and it was so tasty!  Everyone loved it.  The name should be "Extrodinarily Delicious" Pot Roast" :D  Kelly, thank you for posting your recipe here for us all to enjoy!

Well I gave it 5 stars and haven't even tried it yet! I have a roast in the fridge now and I'm headed back to the store to get the other few ingredients I need to make this roast, my mouth is watering as I type,lol! I will update sometime this week when I get a chance to make it. (I'm so impressed with all the 5 stars ratings, and very lenghty reviews)!

I made this last weekend and it was good but it was the smell that really made this.  My husband commented about how good the house smelled to his folks 3 days later. I am always baking cookies, etc and he has never said anything about those smells (those have been pretty good if I can say so myself). I used a 3.5 lb bottom round roast.  I had to cook the carrots and potatoes about 30 mins longer to make them soft enough so that is one thing that I would change about this recipe.  The gravy made a lot and was tasty-I added some salt and ground pepper for more flavor.  Overall a great recipe!

This pot roast is really incredible, Wildflour! I made as directed using Dijon mustard, red onion and baby carrots. The roast was fall apart tender and also the vegetables were perfect!  I added more than the required amount of horseradish and mustard, but the flavors all combine so well, I could hardly detect the flavor on its own.  This recipe will be made again!  Thanks so much, Wildflour!
I made this last night exactly to your recipe...It was delicious...we had a 4lb chuck roast...and sad but true...no leftovers!!  Thanks for such a great recipe!!

This was excellent.  Just the cooking time - I needed temperature at 300 for 90 minutes and then check.  It was quite over-done.  The broth also dried up on me.  Everything was still great and next time I will make these adjustments.
Really good stuff here!  I was unsure going in, but boy oh boy...this is a keeper.  Thanks for sharing.
Wonderfull. Needs good sharp horseradish and a tangy mustard for full effect.
Wonderful!  Great flavor, meat and veggies were super tender.  I put the veggies in after the last flip (at 1 1/2hrs) and let it go another 1 hour 45 minutes.  Wonderful!
Soooo good, Kelly! The mustard/horseradish mixture really pops this recipe. Delicious! Made for Comfort Foods in Cooking Photos.

I was looking for a "cold remedy" for my DH who has brocchial pneumonia, and I have a "little cold" I caught from him... Not sure if this "remedy" is for cold weather or under the weather but it works either way.  This was flavorfull and delicious.  My DH who can't taste anything, loved this wonderful dish, the first thing he's liked all week. If I was making this without the "colds", I would cut the salt in half, since we've weaned ourselves down on the salt and this would have been too salty for us if we were our normal selves.  Other than that it was great !!! I will be making this again, hopefully under better circumstances.  Thank you Wildflour

This was wonderful.  Everyone enjoyed the flavor and couldn't stop raving about this roast.  Will make again.  Made as directed and wouldn't change a thing.  Thanks for posting this recipe.

Raylene

You are not kidding! The smell is so heavenly while this roast is cooking It's hard not to salivate! I was cooking this with windows open in my condo and i had a few extra visitors! My mom told me she could smell it from outside. I had never tried whole stone ground mustard before this recipe. So i tried a spoonful before adding it to the roast. Wow! it's so good that i added extra on the roast and in the sauce. I used a 3.3 lb roast and it was gone in seconds. Really...I cooked the roast with Yukon gold potatoes, Parsnips, Carrots, Onions and Celery. The roasted vegetables also seemed to disappear quickly. The sauce is very, very good. If i didn't find the idea of drinking gravy replusive i'd drink this sauce/gravy. yeah, It's that good. I'm making this again, and again, and again. No complaints from me. Thanks very, very, very much for sharing this.
My family loved this recipe. I used hot horseradish and honey mustard. The onions were out of this world. This is almost too easy to prepare with great results. Thanks for the recipe

This was very tasty and easy. I made pretty much exactly as stated only I used a 3 lb elk roast, spicy brown mustard, and was a teeny bit short on the horseradish. Even DH who usually hates pot roast loved this. Thanks. We'll make this one again.
Update: Made this again using beef but the elk was way better. Used Dijon mustard and was also out of real horseradish and thought I'd give it a try with the cream added kind which really didn't work; I'll only make this recipe with the spicy mustard and the real horseradish from now on because it really didn't have much flavor without them.

Nice, flavorful roast. I used dijon mustard but will definitely use a whole grain next time,  I think it will be even better. I browned the roast then cooked it with the vegetables in the crock pot on low for 8 hours. Tender, moist and delicious. Made Hye Rollers with the leftovers!

This is the only way that I make pot roast now.  Except I make it in the crock pot...so I skip the whole browning step and just salt and pepper the roast, smear it with mustard and horseradish, cover it with the onion slices and throw it in the crockpot with the broth and potatoes and carrots for 8-10 hours on low.  Oh my goodness.  It's the best pot roast in the entire world.  And it's so easy!!!
Yep. This is the best. I know I'll be serving this one for a long time. It is cheap, easy to throw together, and the flavor it spot on. Just like I grew up with in my midwest town!!

Excellent!!  We used a 2 lb roast, 24 ounces of broth and did 1 1/2 half times the mustard and horseradish.  Wish we would have doubled it!!  Wonderful recipe, just so fantastic.  Thanks!!  Highly recommend this one!

I love horseradish and never thought of adding it to my roast recipe, until now. This was very good! I used my new Kitchenaid warming oven which is also a slow cooker and cooked this on low for 9 hours. The roast was very tasty and not HOT becuase as you said, the horseradish mellows in the cooking process. Very good recipe. My DH came back for seconds and thirds!

This really is a good roast.  The horseradish & brown mustard gave it a German flavor influence which we enjoyed.  It isn't "spicy hot" at all so no one should worry about that.  I followed all of your instructions except  after searing I cooked this on low in my crock pot.  It cooked beautifully. I had tender roast, tasty veggies, and a tasty gravy- all no fuss & easy.   Thank you for sharing this recipe!  I will use it again.

From all of the reviews, I was truly looking forward to this one.  I love mustard and horseradish, and everone was saying it had a wonderful flavor.

Sadly, it turned out to be the blandest roast I've made in recent memory.  The smell while cooking was great, but the taste of the mustard and horseradish nearly completely disappeared while cooking - and I used my own freshly prepared horseradish, not anything storebought - so it was VERY sharp and fresh.   Only a hit was left in the carrots.  Unanimous in this house was that it was all very, very bland. 

However, I think this recipe has some potential, so I'm going to play around with it, and hopefully I can find a way to make it more to our tastebud likings.

SIMPLY AMAZING! I'm not sure why the previous poster thought it was bland because this dish is BURSTING with the most incredible flavors! I only had one very small onion, but I had 3 shallots, so I sliced those up with the onion. Probably did add depth to the wonderful flavor, so maybe try this if you're concerned with blandness (which you really shouldn't be). My hubby LOVED it! I did make the gravy but didn't like it at all- just use 32 oz box of broth instead to have extra loveliness. Thank you!
This was good, but I'm not sure if I'm a huge fan of the horseradish.  I think just a personal preference issue.  DH loved it and definitly wanted me to make it again.
I used horseradish mustard instead of horseradish and mustard. It was fantastic! Easy, great flavor. I will definitely make this again.
This is FABULOUS.  I've made it again and again.  Thanks for a keeper!

This is great!  I used a 2.88lb chuck eye roast and added more mustard and horseradish to it after tasting the "gravy".  I used a crock pot, skipped the browning in the skillet and just salt and peppered the roast and spread the horseradish/mustard mixture on both sides.  I layered the onions, potatoes and carrots and added the beef broth, I didn't feel a need to add butter.  Next time I think I'll actually use less broth.  The final result after letting it cook for 10 hours on low was VERY tender meat and delious "gravy".  My husband rated this a 9.5, which means he really liked it as he has never rated anything a 10.....yet!
This is our favorite!  It's what we make every year.  Thanks for posting :)

Another five star review!  I loved telling my mustard and horseradish hating family the secret... after the raved about the pot roast!  "HORSERADISH?!?!?"  :)  The flavor was very mellow and almost sweet.

My whole family loved it; however it  was much better the second day. I served it sliced with gravy, and the vegetables on the side the first night. DH gave it 3-1/2 stars and the kids and myself 4 stars. But on the second day I cut it into chunks and mixed it and the vegetables with the broth and the leftover gravy; it was soooo good! The chunks of meat were so tender and my kids even enjoyed the cooked carrots and onions, whereas normally I'm the only one who likes these. As previous reviewers said, the horseradish and mustard (spicy brown) complemented the flavors wonderfully; they were not overpowering. Thanks for a great recipe!

It is amazing how tastes differ.  Even my vegetarian wife said how great this roast smelled while it was cooking.  I expected to bite into the most savory meat I ever tasted.  Instead it was so bland I couldn't believe it.  I had to review the recipe to make sure I hadn't left anything out.   At a minimum it needs a little more salt.  Still, with an aroma like that it has potential.  I will make it again and work on getting more flavor into the meat.

I was getting really hungry just waiting for this roast to be done.  I was not disappointed, either.  I made a few changes to the recipe, to suit my tastes and to cut the fat.  I didn't use any oil or butter at all.  I seared the meat in a dry cast iron Dutch oven.  I think I was able to do it dry because the meat was still frozen.  I did get a nice crust all around.  I added 3 cloves of garlic, 2 celery stalks, cut the carrots down to 4 and omitted the potatoes (I don't like carrots or potatoes cooked with pot roast for some reason).  I put the vegetables in the bottom of the Dutch oven as a rack and used chicken stock instead of beef as I had no beef stock on hand.  Because my roast was still frozen, I left it in the oven at 300 for 4 hours, and it turned out very well.  But, the piece de resistance (so to speak) was the "gravy" I made using the vegetables and some of the liquid in the bottom of the pan.  I pureed most of the vegetables and half the liquid in the blender, added a little salt, pepper and an additional tablespoon of mustard.  YUM!  I think those who find the recipe bland would certainly appreciate this use of some of the vegetables and sauce.  We very much enjoyed this recipe and will be using it again.  Thank you, Wildflour!

One of my favorite recipes! The house smells wonderful while it is cooking. After searing the meat, I put everything in the crockpot and the house will smell amazing all day! I also like to de-glaze the pan with a little beef broth after I sear the meat to get all the good flavor from the there and I add it to the pot.

Thank you so much for an excellent recipe! The reviews were very helpful and I read them AFTER I put it in the oven! I was salivating as I seared the meat and spread the horseradish mustard sauce over what was soon to be the bottom of the roast! My husband enjoyed the gravy more than most gravy I have cooked! The only tweak I did was to rub it with Spade L seasoning instead of salt and pepper. This made excellent enchiladas the next day. I had a rather large roast and was concerned about it drying out, but I used a roasting pan in the oven and actually had to discard some of the broth. It was not dry like the other reviews I read. I WILL be using this again!

I used this recipe with a sirloin tip roast and added rutabagas with the carrots and potatoes. Also, I made a gravy from the drippings. I mixed the horseradish with spicy brown mustard. My meat was really flavorful but the vegetables was a little bland. I think I will have to make this recipe a couple of times to perfect it. Thanks for another great recipe!

Hands down the best roast I ever made and the house smelled amazing.  I followed the recipe exactly except forgot to turn it once or twice - it was still very moist.  I am not a huge roast lover but I can definitely see myself craving this one - YUM!
Awesome!!!

Excellent recipe!  I was expecting a much greater "kick" from the horseradish and mustard, but this was a very mild pot roast.  I halved the recipe but left the cooking time the same, and the result was a wonderfully tender roast.  I am going to experiment with this recipe, increasing the horseradish/mustard mix to see what happens.  As posted, this is absolutely delicious, and I'm so happy I made it.  Anytime I'm home for an extended period of time I love to make something that makes my house smell wonderful, and this recipe certainly had everyone clamoring for dinner.  Thanks for sharing!

OMG This was so perfect. I have been looking and looking for a pot roast with a rich dark gravy. The only thing I changed was I mashed potatoes instead of putting the potatoes in . A true winner. I wish I could give it more than 5 stars, because it more than deserves it. Leftovers freeze really well too.

We REALLY enjoyed this meal!  This will be a bi-weekly meal at our house.  The whole family loved it.  We love the leftovers too!  
It was simple, classic and clean.  The meat was very tender and had just the right flavor.  I thought I would taste more of the mustard and horseradish, but in the end I didn't.  It was flavorful and yummy.
i use this in chinese resteruants in glad to make it home .dee

I love this oil. I always order it with Chicken and Broccoli at my favorite Chinese Take Out. Sometimes they forget, and now I have my own! Thanks for posting this recipe.

Nick's Mom
Wonderful!  So versatile.  I love that I can make this at home!

Very good!  I'm so happy to have the Panda Restaurant's secret now for making our dishes "extra spicy!"  This is it!  So easy to make....And now I can add a little to any food I make!  Thanks for sharing this -- I'm so glad that I chose to make this for ZWTII!  :)

Funny how often Zaar can make me a star!  DH often eats lunch at an oriental restaurant & raves about this chili oil they served.  We had an Asian inspired meal last night & I whipped out this oil before he could even whine!  I added LOTS of crushed peppers & a couple of whole, dried ones.  Considering his ears smoked when he ate it, I think I got it about right. Thanks so much for posting this!

I split the batch into two smaller jars...one for us and one for my DSIL! They called yesterday to say WOW it was very good and very hot....just the way they like it. I haven't had a chance to use mine yet, but I will soon!!  Thank you for a GREAT recipe I can make and use as gifts for my "Chili Head Friends"!!

Soooo easy!!!  Soooo spicy!!! :))
I will never buy another bottle of 'hot and spicy' oil!!
Thank you!!

A very good, easy to make cake that tastes really special. I used Meyer's Dark Rum and a dark chocolate cake mix. I left out the chocolate chips because DH doesn't care for them. It turned out just lovely, very deeply flavored and moist. Thanks!!

I loved the ease of preparation.  However, it didn't turn out all that well for me.  I think it must have been the ingredient choices I made.  Do not use Duncan Hines,  large chocolate chips or Puerto Rican golden rum (versus dark rum).  With these things, it wasn't sweet enough, the large chips made it difficult to test doneness, and the rum tasted raw.
This has been a go to recipe for me for a few Christmases by popular demand. I use butter instead of canola oil and it comes out that much more decadent.

Thank you for this wonderful technique. I have often made my own chili oil waiting weeks before the cold oil absorbed the chili flavor this cuts the whole process a day or so.  Quite fun wathcing the chilis sizzle.

easy and perfect. i used some dried chili peppers i had, with a lil toasted sesame oil in the food processor. then used canola for the heated oil. also put a garlic clove and a piece of star anise in for a lil extra something. i'll never have to beg the local chinese takeout place again.
so easy to do and very spicy.  Thanks currybunny :)  Made for All you can cook buffet

We actually gave this a 4 1/2 star. The ones in the voting that kept it from being a full five star just don't like cilantro.  There are some strong flavours in this recipe but they come together perfectly - not too mild nor overpowering.  I wouldn't change a thing.  We served over couscous exactly as the recipe says.  Do put a spoonful or two of the dressing over the chicken.  This dish presents very nicely and tastes like you prepped all day but it's easy enough for weeknight meals. I'll definitely be serving it to company too.
This is an excellent salad.  I did make it with rice, however, being gluten-intolerant.  Could make it without couscous or rice.  It just tastes very good.

wow!! any chance i get to use cumin other than in chilli, i will try! BF made this and it was sooo yummy. used only 1t of dried cilantro as neither of us care for it.  used red bell pepper instead of yellow also used no tomatoes as we were all out.  doubled the onions.  verrry great taste!!

Very simple to make and tasty.  I used a HOT Hyngarian sausage delicious. I thought that 1/4 cup water would be too little but stuck to the recipe- I kept my eye on the pot - it was perfect.  I held off adding the Peppers until 5 minutes before serving so they held their color and were still crisp.If there are any left overs they are perfect as pan fried taters  Thanks smiley_face for a keeper

I close my eyes and I'm in Greece while I eat this delicious risotto. I used the Arborio rice for this dish and was thrilled to discover that I could make a risotto without standing for a half hour of more, stirring and adding broth to my rice.  It came out exactly right...creamy.  I add the feta, and think it added a wonderful dimension, but my husband doesn't care for it and left it out. I'm keeping this recipe to make some other risotto variations using the same proportions, since it turned out so well.

Great and easy, really tastefull. I used lime juice (that's what I can get here in razil), jasmine rice and sardo cheese, it turned out a little too acidic, but great. Next time I'll cut the lime juice.

I made this for last night's dinner, and am having the leftovers for breakfast this morning - - it's that good.  The proportions are perfect, everything simply blends together to create something fabulous.  I used converted rice, and added feta at the table.  Wonderful!  Thanks for sharing this!
This was a great side to our london broil! Simple and Tasty - a great combination! The olives and the feta really give this the flavor it needs - dont skip them. Thanks Ev!

Love this . . . went very well with our roast pork loin.   Because there are only two of us I cut the recipe in half.  Did not have fresh lemon juice so substituted white wine and it was great!  Thanks for sharing.
This was a wonderfully delicious and easy to prepare meal. Nothing else is needed except for some rolls or garlic toast. TERRIFIC!

Will definitely make this recipe again and again! I prepared the spanakorizo using risotto and on another occasion, I used brown rice. The dish is excellent with either rice! I used my pressure cooker which sped up the cooking time. Brought in this dish to my Greek friends at work and I received MANY compliments! This dish is now a frequent request from my children (ages 15, 14 and 9)! Yummy!
One of my favorite vegetarian meals. I made it last night but I also used fresh tomato and one teaspoon tomato paste and added the lemon just before serving!

I've made this 3 times in the last 3 weeks! I can't believe I forgot to review it. I love Evelyn's recipes so much that I will make anything with her name on it. I know it will be straight-forward to prepare, at least fairly healthy and that it will have wonderful flavor! We have another staple, Efharisto!
Wonderful new way to make risotto. This combines two of my favorites into one great dish.  I made it just as described and it turned out delicious.

I really liked the combination of lemon juice and dill in this, as it gave it a distinctive taste.  We served it with feta cheese. Kalamata olives would have been good too but we didn't have any.  My only comment would be to add the spinach a little later in the cooking process because I felt it came out a bit slimy.  Also, we thought the amount of olive oil was excessive so we reduced it substantially.:)  Thanks evelyn!
Reminds me of home. Very good recipe and much close to the real thing. I would add a little extra tomato paste. Adding a little more fresh olive oil, lemon and feta on your serving plate is a MUST.

Just made it earlier today, delicious! I also added 2 garlic cloves with the onion at the beginning to add to the flavour, and a bit of sweetcorn for the last 2 minutes for added crumchiness. Lovely dish, I recommend addind a bit of feta, too!
This recipe was just right for me. I did cut the recipe in half. I ate every bit of it. I used some garlic pepper just for some added flavor. I did not need anything else to put with it. Thank You

Very good and very easy! I addded shredded cabbage that needed to be used up and sprinkled some Lawry's Seasoned Salt and pepper on all of it and within 25 minutes we had a great lunch. I served it with sliced tomatoes and we will have this again. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

This is so good that I was going to post it until I found smiley face’s recipe. 

We have cooked it on the stove and it is good that way, but we prefer to cook it on the grill when the weather’s nice enough.  We add more peppers, onions, omit the water, and add our favorite seasonings to taste to cook it on the grill.   We slice or cube the potatoes in smaller pieces so that they get cooked though, line the bottom of the grill with foil, and put a “tent” of foil on top of it to keep the moisture in and to make it cook quicker. It does need stirred occasionally to make sure everything cooks evenly.

This is one recipe that tastes as good as the  picture of it, and the aroma coming from the grill is heavenly.  

This also nukes wonderfully if you have any leftovers, which we sometimes intentionally make extra for a quick easy lunch. 
 
For ease, simplicity, presentation and taste this is a definite 5 star recipe.

I started making this about 5 years ago, coming up with the combination on my own. And all this time I thought I was being original! Oh well. I did start preparing this a bit differently, tho, after a few too often complaints of "crunchy potatoes" from my DH. It seemed that there were always a few potatoes that were not quite "all the way done" inside. So I started parboiling the potatoes first. Then I drain them and add the rest of the ingredients and continue till everything's done. And of course, I have to make sure we have ketchup for this - my kids seem to think ketchup is it's own food group. Protein group, dairy group, grains group, veggie group, ketchup group. And they do their best to meet or exceed the Recommended Daily Allowance!

This dish is so easy, yet incredibly delicious! I did not have a bell pepper, so I used a half head of shredded cabbage instead. Increased water to 1/2cup and added 2 tsp beef bullion granules. Also salt and pepper to taste. This is how good this is: my two young girls ate it without complaining. Before, they always complained when I made them eat their cooked cabbage. They loved it. Will make this one often!!! Thanks for posting.
This is so good.  We had this for dinner a couple of nights back.  It's quick and easy to prepare and very tasty.  I will use this recipe often.

Country style is exactly what this one-dish meal is.  I made this last night and my family loved it.  I cut my onion in eighths and the bell pepper in large slivers.  I used venison sausage with quite a lot of seasoning in it so I only added salt and ground black pepper to this recipe. The 1/4 cup water seemed sufficient but I stirred this pretty often so the potatoes would be sure to get done.   I served this with a hot pan of cornbread.  This recipe is definitely a keeper.  It is very easy to make and uses ingredients we usually have on hand.
This is a wonderful one-pot dinner that taste even better the next day.  Although, the first time I made it there wasn't anything left.  :-)

Wonderful!  I wondered if I would need more water but I didn't.  In fact I drained it when I was done.  I would add the peppers a little later but other than that it was perfect!

The nice thing was I'm used to frying the sausage and then boiling the potatoes separately.  So the meat has more grease that way and we would normally put butter on the potatoes.  With boiling it we didn't need all the extra fat.  

Thanks again!

This dish went over very well with my family.  I liked it because it wasn't nearly as greasy as the old-fashioned tators, onions, and peppers, I learned to make using bacon grease.  Mine cooked a lot quicker than I expected so was a bit mushy but that's easy to adjust the next time I make this.

Thank you for sharing this recipe with us!

So easy and so delicious with things I had on hand. Didn't have a bell pepper, but had a package of coleslaw  mix and threw the whole package in. I also had a package of refrigerated red potato wedges and used those. Sprinkled everything with Old Bay seasoning, let it come up to a boil, reduced to medium low, covered and let it go for 35 minutes. Yum!

YUM!  Absolutely delicious and couldn't be easier.  I read the other reviews and noticed a couple people questioned the "1/4 cup" water, as I did, but because the reviewers said that amount worked, I used it. Just perfect! It didn't need a drop more water. I'm polishing off my second bowlful and it's so good!  This recipe is definitely a keeper and satisfies all requirements for "good aroma, quick, comforting, filling, and delicious!"  Thank you, smiley-face.

This was excellent just as the recipe is written.  When I make it again (and I surely will) I think I will add a little spice. Maybe just one small jalapeno for spice and a bit of garlic. My house guest thought it was perfect as is.
I make something much like this in the oven.  I have added chopped cabbage and carrots and even corn (not all at the same time).  This is a very good meal!

This was really great.  So simple to make- and love that I only used one dish.  Took someones advice and boiled the potatoes for 10 minutes while I chopped up everything.  Only other change I made was to add 2 cloves of garlic.  Thanks for sharing!   We loved it!

Sooo good and oh so easy! I was a little skeptical about this recipe but it was amazing! I used a red pepper which set off the flavour of the sausage. The amount of water was perfect as well. Only addition wad c1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
This recipe is so yummy and quick. I think is a very comforting dish. My DH enjoyed his with mustard and beer.Thanks so much for posting.

This is a recipe I will use again and again--so tasty and easy after working all day.  I cooked the cubed potatoes in the 1/4 cup water while I cut up everything else.  Seasoned with Lawry's seasoning.  Thanks!!

Good easy recipe. I barely covered with water then when the liquid cooked off, I let it brown abit to intensify the flavors. Hubby went back for seconds and asked for the leftovers for his lunch at work.

Very easy and quick meal.  I used smoked turkey sausage/  I sauted my potatoes, peppers and onion in a little olive oil first and then added the water and covered to finish off.  Only took about 15 minutes and the potatoes were done.  The thing I like about this recipe is that I used much less oil than when I cook the whole meal by frying....trying to get the potatoes done that way can be tough.  This way, the water takes care of it.  Thanks for posting.
Quick, easy, and delicious!  And the leftovers are wonderful for an omelet or breakfast skillet the next day!

This is a good one pot meal. I followed the directions exactly, using a "light" smoked sausage and did end up adding an additional 1/4 cup water. Next time I will also add some seasoned salt and pepper. I love these quick and easy meals. Thanks!
Great recipe- thanks!
Best tasting and easiest meal I've made all year! We did add salt and pepper because it seemed too easy, but it was amazing!
Very easy and delicious go to dish. I started by sauteing some chopped garlic in a small amount of olive oil. I also used Lawry's seasoned salt, pepper, and paprika for some added flavor.

I couldn't believe how good this was for such a simple recipe!  I buy a lot of smoked sausage (it's always buy one get two free at the grocery store), so I have been looking for a good new recipe.  I had to omit the onions :( because DH won't eat them, but I added the peppers and just had him pick them out of his bowl :).  The water amount is just right, don't change it.  I love this recipe!

This is soooo good!!  I found your recipe a few years ago and it is a favorite winter meal.  I made it again last night and it was perfect since I hadn't planned anything for dinner and it was bitterly cold.  The way I make it is to start the smoked sausage and potatoes first with the water.  When the water's almost gone and the potatoes have softened some I add more water and then throw a medium onion that I've wedged on top.  I don't mix it in so it sort of steams the onion.  Since I usually have frozen peppers, I throw that in at the last minute.  I love red and yellow peppers in this.  When it's all done I have a little bit of a "sauce" from the extra water and the onion and peppers are still somewhat firm.  Put it on a plate and shake on some black pepper and I am good to go!  I think this would be an easy recipe to stretch for unexpected company.  And another potatoe or two, extra onion and slice the sausage really thin and you could probably feed 6.  I plan on making this when we go camping this summer.  Thank you for a simple wonderful recipe.
So so good!! We ate it up!! The best part is it is so cheap to make and most of the stuff we had around anyways. Thanks.
I didn't think my kids would go for this, but they loved it - even the picky eater.

Sometimes you read a recipe and think "what the heck, we like all the ingredients but it doesn't look like anything special" That was my initial response to this recipe - I was wrong - the total tastes so much better than the ingredients would lead you to believe!  I used 1/3 less fat Hillshire farm sausage.  It was a wonderful, easy, stressfree dinner for a Sunday night!  Thanks for posting!
This was an easy meal to make and my family enjoyed it! The only thing I did differently was to parboil the potatoes like a previous poster suggested. Thanks for posting this!

This was SUCH a great weeknight supper! Prep time was minimal, and dinner was on the table in less than an hour. My family thanks you! Served w/ applesauce, this was a delicious dinner. I cut down on the peppers, as my little ones aren't big fans...We'll definitely make this again!

Thanks for sharing!

This was so good and comforting..... I have prepared it twice and couldn't believe I didn't review it the first time..... My family loves it.... Thanks so much for sharing this quick and easy wonderful tasting meal....

5/2/08
yum yum yum! a poor man's meal fit for a king. I didn't have a bell pepper, so I used celery instead, which tasted really good (like a soup without the soup!) I also added sliced jalapeno pepper, bay seasoning, salt and pepper (as suggested in previous comments). Thank you! 5/15/08 I forgot to mention that I boiled the potatoes for a little bit beforehand.
This looks amazingly simple and it is... but the taste is as amazing as it is simple to make. We love this. Even my kids who normally don't like onions and peppers loved this.
This looks wonderful and as soon as I'm done typing I'm going to go make it!!

5-star recipe!  I started out by sauteeing 2 cloves garlic along w/the onion.  Then I added the potato (sliced pretty thin), hot chipotle beef sausage, & the pepper. Thanks for such a great, easy recipe. I followed the recipe pretty closely only adding a couple of small tomatoes cut up and some garlic/pepper season salt (after checking the saltiness of the sausage). It was soooo good. This is so great. Made it just as directed.
This is surprisingly tasty in spite of its simplicity! We do love kielbasa, which is what gives the whole dish its flavor.
This was quick and easy as well as delicious. Thanks for sharing.

what a great recipe to double or triple for large groups.  I made this at our Family Reunion & it was a big hit.
an awesome go-to to have on hand.  thanks smiley
Definitely a keeper - but seasoning is a must.  I took other reviewer's advice and added Lawry's Seasoning Salt while cooking.

I agree with No Gluten 100%.  Did the same, made it with Turkey Smoked Sausage and was amazed at how good these few items were together.  Also great the next day with eggs and/or white sausage gravy and/or cheese.  It's permanently added to my recipe tin.  Thanks Smiley!
I used Prodohmes blackening steak magic on it, and swapped brocolli for green beans.  It was superb!  Thanks for a new meal for my family.

This is really one of the easiest meals to make and has great flavor. Usually my green pepper and onion end up over done so I add them after 10 minutes. Also like to make sure whichever kielbasa I get isn't too greasy.

So I thought I had a bell pepper when I started this... but alas, it went missing... so I added 2 jalapeno and 2 carrots instead... I also used chicken broth instead of water for a bit more flavor... and

This was good, not great though. I sauteed with a bit of olive oil and only seasoned with salt and pepper.
It satisfied us though, and while not in a regular rotation will probably be repeated in a, quick I need something for dinner.
Good dish-quick and easy! Definitely needs seasoning. I think next time I will make some country gravy to go on top!

MY family loved these potatoes.  I did not measure the sausage, I just kept adding until the amount looked about right for us. I did add a Knorr beef cube and some black pepper. This was an easy dish to prepare with great results. Thanks for the recipe.

Very good recipe!!! I have made this twice this week, once with bratwurst and once with chorizo; both are tasty and delicious. I also added some corn on the cob to the chorizo and it fit in perfectly. Thanks for a delicious meal that I'm adding to my regular rotation.
Dang tasty!

I thought this was ok. I added some beef bullion and black pepper like another reviewer suggested as well as some cajun seasoning. I also added a can of diced tomatoes. Absolutely delicious as is.  I did have to add just a bit more water only because the pan that I used doesn't have a snug fitting lid.  Had this with cornbread.  Thanks for posting.
Taste good. Used chicken broth and seasoning. Will make again.

This recipe is a keeper for me!  I put just enough water to barely cover the potatoes, which was over double the amount called for. My family loved it and only wished I'd made more.

A very easy (yet tasty) one pot meal. Made as posted and its delicious. Equally as delicious with a sliced jalapeno added. Thanks for a fun and easy recipie, Smiley_Face !
I followed the recipe and did not alter it as other did. It was edible but that's about all I could say about it. I promised my kids I wouldn't make it again.

So I must admit, I didn't think my wife would like this dish since she is not a fan of smoked sausage. Made as directed except I added a sliced jalapena. Wow, everyone liked it!! And there was no leftovers. We will be having this again.
My hubby and I love this. We are not fans of smoked sausage so I substitute mild Italian. We ake this at least once a month. it's quick and easy.
So quick, so easy and sooo good.

Gussy it up with your favorite seasonings. I made in a large cast iron skillet. I added cracked red pepper and, of course, salt and black pepper. Some dried parsley. Sure you can add celery and other veggies of your choice. Definitely used broth instead of water. Although we are not huge smoked sausage fans, this is a nice comfort food meal on a chilly night. Goes great with skillet cornbread or buttermilk biscuits.

This was surprisingly very good, given how simple the recipe is. I didn't add any extra seasonings, but the sausage flavored everything very nicely. I used both red and green bell peppers and kielbasa.

Very light tasting and easy to make.  My family enjoyed this and I will make it again. Thank 
you for sharing with us.

Delicious recipe!  My family loved it and so easy to make!  Great for St. Patrick's day dessert!

I was so glad to find this recipe, Pixie!  I had it years ago but have misplaced it and of course they never print it on the cake mix box anymore.  This is so cool and refreshing to have for dessert, especially in the summer!  I have tried it using many different cake/Jello/pudding combinations and it's always a hit!  Thank you again.  =)

3 jalapenos!!? I used ONE, and I was overwhelmed in heat!! This has a good flavor... but seriously I don't see how anyone could ever use 3 jalapenos... unless they were TINY, and ALL the seeds were removed. Also I used Lime juice rather than lemon.

Great.  We used all the jalapenos, but cut the garlic clove in half.  No mayo for us, just the oil and a bit of lime juice.  We seeded and deveined the pepper, but it was not overwhelmingly spicy.  Thank you for posting.
This sauce is divine!!  The only thing I gave a miss to was the celery, otheriwse made to recipe.  This is definitely the recipe I will use from here on out.  Thanks!

This is wonderful!  I'm really making an effort to prepare more foods from scratch and eat less processed foods (and less take-out), and this pizza sauce was wonderful with my home-made dough.  The only change I made was leaving out the fennel seeds since we don't like them, but everything else was as written.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

I have made many pizza sauces that are very delicious, but they lack the "Pizzaria" flavor.  This has it!  It is the fennel seeds!  This is not just a delicious sauce, but really tastes authentic.  This is my standby now!

This sauce was just fantastic, and I do believe that the fennel seeds adds what is missing from alot of the "homemade" sauces!  I doubled this recipe, and froze it for another pizza which should not be too long in the making.  Thank you so much for my new pizza sauce recipe. :)

Oh my gosh what can I say about this recipe, except your title says it all, ULTIMATE PIZZA SAUCE! This is the best pizza sauce I've ever tasted, way better then even pizza places. This sauce is awesome. I put all the spices into my mini chopper to grind them fine, mostly because I was a bit worried about biting into whole fennel seeds. (DH is picky!). 10 stars!  I doubled the recipe and was glad I did.  This comes close to the pasta sauce at a local restaurant that I wanted the recipe for.  I plan to use this for more than just pizza. Fantastic and so easy to make!

Fantastic taste! We doubled it and had plenty for two medium pizzas with more than half left over for next week. Thank you for sharing this!

Wonderful sauce...I did not use the fennel seeds because I did not have them.  I added extra garlic and used tomato puree for some of the tomato paste.  Still turned out great.  Used on pizza dough Recipe #172304  which was great too.

Very delicious, made this for our homemade pizza tonight and got lots of compliments on the sauce. The only change I made was to whirl the veggies and the fennel in the blender with the tomato sauce to hide them from the kids! This was a great sauce and it was enjoyed by all, thanks!

DELICIOUS!!
The only difference I did was that I blended the fennel seeds, onions, the minced garlic clove, and the tomato sauce while the oil and butter were melting. Than I just did as the instructions said. Simply outstanding!  Thick and rich and verrrry spicy (which we love).    The only change I made was to omit the fennel since my family isn't very fond of it.  I doubled the recipe, and it reached the perfect consistency after about 30 minutes of simmering.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe, SC.  This one gets filed under "Favorites"!
We loved this recipe so much that now I make a big pot of it to freeze for later!  Wonderful!

Kudos on this Pizza base sauce, its absolutely marvellous. The texture, the taste - magnifique!  The celery adds a great taste.

Excellent sauce. I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out fantastic.

(((( Yummm! ))))

Left out the fennel and added crushed red pepper flakes instead. Fabulous thick pizza sauce!

Oh my. This is astoundingly good! I replaced the fennel with crushed red pepper, replaced the fresh celery with some celery seed, and cut back to just one tablespoon of olive oil. Thank you soooooo very much for this recipe!! I will absolutely make it again, and make more in order to freeze it.
Hubby loved this sauce better than all the others. Thanks for sharing.
excellent sauce. flavorful and tasty!  didn't even add fennel seeds or bay leaf, and it was really good on the pizzas we made. thanks!

Excellent sauce. Thank you for the recipe. My husband's only complaint as that I didn't use enough.

The most unbelievably good pizza sauce!  I've always been partial to "Pastarelli's Pizza Sauce," found in most grocery stores.

I can't thank you enough for this recipe. I love the sauce. It taste just like my favorite pizzeria which I don't often because of the 20-25 dollar price tag. This recipe essentially will save me some money. Thanks again, Highly recommended.

Thank you so much for this recipe! This sauce was truly a keeper for all time! I used the Eazy Peezy pizza dough recipe from this site along with this sauce and it rocked! My family loved it! We may never eat pizza in a pizzeria again!

We love this recipe and use it every week.
This was the best pizza sauce! My grandkids loved it and I made plenty to put in the freezer. Thanks!

Magnificent!!!!  SUPER flavorful!!  Truly authentic tasting!!! I'm from Chicago and take my pizza VERY seriously and this is a contender to some of my favorite pizza joints.  EXCELLENT!

We have tried several different recipes looking for just the right pizza sauce. Our search is now over. The flavor of this sauce was just perfect. Thanks so much!!
The end of the search, like someone else said. Pizza doesn't get much better.

I've never been a big fan of pizza.  I know I'm weird.  After finding this recipe we make pizza at least twice a month.  I do not puree or crush anything, just saute until soft. I haven't bought a pizza in about a year.  Thank you for a family staple.  I think it will be passed on for generations.

My DH has been craving a pizza. We live 20 miles from a good pizzaerri..I decided to make my own..This recipe is wonderful. And sooooo thick...I made my own crust #70165,,Took care of our cravings..I will definitely be making this again..Thank U....

I will admit, when this was simmering on the stove, I tasted it and it tasted too much like pasta sauce to me..but when it was on the pizza, OMG the best sauce I ever had!This was my first time making sauce and now I'm never going back to store-bought! Thank you!

This is a fantastic recipe.  I've made this several times now (1st time exactly as listed) and would like to share what I've learned. While we like the depth fennel adds we also don't like to bite into a strongly flavored seed.  We have since skipped it.  (Perhaps it would work well if ground or in a spice bag?)  I've also cut the celery and increased the onion to 3/4 cup (only because we don't generally have cellery around).  We also like slightly sweet/spicy so we've upped to suger (I use brown) to about two teaspoons and have added crushed red pepper for some great heat.  Finally, we have taken to adding red wine (about 1/8 to 1/4 cup) and then simmer for about 1/2 hour or until there is no longer an alcohal smell.  It adds a great level of flavor!  Thanks SAMS_Club, this is our new favorite!
Very good pizza sauce.  I used it in calzones, with a little on the side for dipping.  Definitely a keeper.
This was a great sauce-I followed directions, which I rarely do, and it turned out great!  Very tasty on a grilled pizza.

This sauce is fantastic!!!
Great recipe.  I make a double batch and keep it in jars.  It doesnt last more then a week in my house.

Great sauce, very easy to make with all the ingredients on hand!  Made this to combine with Tofu pizza grilled on the BBQ and had great success with that.  I froze the left overs.

This is heavenly!!! Used fresh basil (about a tablespoon.) Didn't have fennel, bay leaf or Parmesan. Outstanding sauce!  I loved the thick zestiness of it, it worked perfectly on our pizzas tonight.  I used celery seed in place of actual celery, and followed everything else.  Thanks for the great recipe!

Delicious sauce! My husband kept raving about it and was licking the spoon/pan clean as he cleaned up after dinner tonight. I didn't have any fennel seed, so I left that out but otherwise made it exactly as written. This is now my go-to recipe for pizza sauce. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

Even at the lowest setting on my stove, despite using a non-stick circulon pan. I was surprised that no one had experienced this problem  in the reviews. Adding sugar or salt increases the boiling point of any liquid making it easy for a thick liquid to scorch or burn, even at low heat. To avoid this problem there are two solutions.  Either make the recipe 'as is'  whilst stirring continually.  Or leave out the salt and sugar until the end and add it in the final minute or two. Even then you may need to watch the pan and check on it from time to time.

Especially food recipes that I can always count on to be the same quality every time I make them. I came across this recipe for pizza sauce and like all the others, it claimed to be the best.
