I don't like to go through the bother of making rolled biscuits, but plain old drop biscuits tastes...well, plain and old. I didn't get to add the butter and garlic on top when I made them the first time, and even though they were delicious without I'm definitely doing it from now on because I think that will make them a knockout.

Mmmmm!!  10+ stars for this one!  We made just as directed, except we used butter instead of shortening and 1/2 C cheese (1/2 cheddar and 1/2 colby/jack because we ran out of cheddar).  We also didn't put the melted butter on the top, and it was fine without.  Thanks Marg - this one's a keeper!

These biscuits are great! I am a garlic lover so I put 1/4 tsp of garlic in, I thought it was a good amount of garlic. I had some family over who are not real big garlic eaters so they prefered less garlic. They would have liked only 1/8 maybe and maybe no garlic butter on top..... But I loved them!!! So did my kids.
Soft and moist. Excellent texture! I won't change anything except doubling the cheese (or using sharp cheddar instead of medium cheddar) and maybe adding minced garlic to the batter next time.

Excellent texture and taste, simple and very quick.  I added a little bit more of the cheese.  I have made the equivalent with bisquick (copycat recipe) and these do not have that odd "bisquick taste."   The texture and taste beats the other recipes hands down!  These took me less than 20 minutes from start to finish (taking out of oven!).  Thanks!

I can't believe how easy these are, yet they are soft & delicious! I cut the recipe in half, used skim milk & low fat mexican cheese. Like others I used much less Splenda (for the sugar). I had no cream of tartar but good thing it worked out still! I had to use butter for the shortening, which also worked fine. Served these to hubby w/ his lasagna. Thank u for sharing!

No bread in the house this morning for our Sunday breakfast feast.

Whipped these up and everyone thought it was a super treat.

Thanks!

These are so awesome!  Kids and adults all loved them!  I used a clove of grated garlic instead of the powder.  I mixed it into the milk .  These will definitely be in the rotation since they take about 5 minutes to throw together!

I tried this using white whole wheat flour and soymilk and it was a bit disappointing.  Not as cheesy and garlicy as I had hoped.  It was hard to make 10 biscuits with this recipe, it made more like 5-6 for us.  Easy recipe though.  I would recommend sticking to the recipe without the above substitutions.

You are right. These are better than the ones made with Bisquick. I wanted to make garlic cheese biscuits and noticed I was out of Bisquick. That is when I logged on to Recipezaar and found this recipe. The sugar really makes the flavors blend nice. I did use more cheese and a wee bit more garlic. Thanks
These were good and super quick!  Baked up nicely.  I will add more garlic next time as we are garlic lovers, but wouldn't change anything else.  Thanks so much.

We loved these! I was looking for a cheddar biscuit recipe that didn't use Bisquick and this was it! Fantastic. Made them twice and added a bit more garlic the second time b/c we really like garlic. Thanks Marg!

Heaven!  So light and fluffy!  They came out exactly as described and made 10 perfect piles of deliciousness.  I thought that it didn't seem like there was much cheese in them as I was mixing, but they came out perfect.  I used 1/8 teaspoon of garlic powder in the biscuits themselves.  The 1/8 that you mix in the melted butter and brush on at the end adds enough "extra" garlic flavor!  These are tops on my list of easy, quick dinner sides!  Thanks!
Fantastic! Ultra-fluffy and flavorful. Going into my 'definite keepers' folder for sure.

Fabulous!  These were very delicious!  I don't use shortening, so I just substituted the same amount of butter for the shortening.  They turned out very soft, moist, and perfect!  My family of 5 devoured them.  Thank you!

I wish I could give these 10 stars!  They were so good and I hate to admit it, but I ate three!  They were super easy to mix up and bake.  When the came out of the oven they were soft and light and very moist!  I will never buy the packaged mix again!  I did not have any cream of tartar so I did as another reviewer suggested and added an extra teaspoon of baking powder and a half teaspoon of baking soda.  I read many reviews before I made them and lots of reviewers stated that they should have made a double batch, so I did!  Which I am so glad I did!!  Now we have extra to eat tonight!!  Yum-yum!!  Thanks for such an awesome recipe!!

There are so many rave reviews that it makes me think I did something wrong. I'm a decent cook though. Maybe it's just a matter of taste. I love Red Lobster's biscuits. I didn't care much for these. I had 3 other people try them and everyone thought they were okay, but not spectacular. I ended up throwing some away that no one ate.

I had a serious hankering for biscuits one morning, but I didn't feel like doing all of the work.  So, once again, Recipezaar to the rescue!  This was breakfast time so I left out the garlic powder and cheese.  I didn't have cream of tartar I did as suggested and added more baking powder and soda.  Less than half an hour later I was enjoying biscuits with butter and warm jam.  Yum!

I was in charge of making breakfast this morning and craved a bread product. Biscuits seemed to be the easiest options and found this on Recipezaar. Followed recipe to a T, except I used a full tsp of garlic powder, a few dashes of dill weed, between 1/4-1/2 of shredded cheddar cheese, 1/2 cup of almond milk, and left out Step 6. The end result were moist biscuits with a slightly crunchy exterior. This recipe yielded only 5 large biscuits for me... the next time I make this recipe I will definitely double the ingredients. Overall, a quick and easy recipe for flavorful biscuits that you can experiment with!
Thanks Marg!  Just got home from a trip and wanted something that I could throw together. These were great. I made as directed, except the cheese was a finely grated italian blend. Will make again.
Awesome biscuits to go with just about any savory meal. Thank you so much for posting a recipe that didn't start with Bisquick!!!

Nice biscuits but if I make them again, I'll omit the sugar. They were just too sweet and whilst I like sweet/savoury things on occasion, these were really sweet to me. They didn't get gobbled up either which is unusual in my house. They turned out to be sort of a cross between a biscuit and a scone. (I am aware of the slightly different terminology between the US and Australia in terms of biscuits, scones, cookies etc.) I'm not wild about the half-biscuit and half-scone texture. I think I prefer normal cheese scones or cheese biscuits rather than a mishmash.
I've never used Bisquick and don't know if we even have it in Australia but honestly, who would bother trying to take a shortcut with Bisquick because these are really easy and quick to make.

Perfectly delicious! I omitted the sugar, doubled the garlic powder, and used butter instead of shortening. (I did not do step 6.) Baked at 400 for 10 minutes, they were light and fluffy! Yum! And such a quick recipe!
Very, very yummy and took no time at all.  I think 25 minutes tops was the bake and prep time!
Incredible recipe! I made these and wrapped them around the little morning brakfast sausages and then baked! They were sooo good. Thank you for sharing. This recipe is a definite keeper.
Excellent!  Light, fluffy and delish, thanks for sharing.  Like another reviewer, I also skipped step 6 and baked at 400 for 10 minutes.  Yum!

Wow!  I thought I had a great recipe for buscuits...but mine doesn't compare!  Thanks for sharing the recipe to these scrumptious morsels.  My kids couldn't get enough of them and my DH was very impressed!  Note that I changed out the shortening for butter as I'm not a fan of shortening.  As well the bake time seemed a bit off, perhaps its my oven but they seemed to have need a bit more time perhaps closer to 15 minutes.

Wow!  These are amazing I made 50 biscuits.  I am giving some to friends and family.  I will definitely be making these again.  I added a cup of chopped ham.  It really was a great addition.  Marg, another great recipe!  Thank you so much.

I have a feeling this recipe failed because of a mistake on my part or bad ingredients....
I am sad to say that these biscuits, although super easy and quick, turned out HORRIBLE. They looked delicious and I followed the recipe exactly (apart from using a pastry blender to blend shortening). At first bite, they had good flavor, but after a few seconds of chewing a terrible taste took over. I can't even describe it really. My best guess is one of my ingredients was off. I was really looking forward to trying this recipe out, and will try it again, especially since so many others got rave results! I won't give up!
I only got 8 small biscuits out of this recipe. I thought they could use more salt and more garlic powder. Other than that they were light and fluffy.

"Yummy, excellent!" raves 8 year old Joel.  He can eat 3 or 4 of these dreamy biscuits in one sitting, which leaves just enough for the rest of us.  Little Danielle (not quite 2) already has a taste for them too.  Easy to make, and way, way worth the effort.  We double the cheddar cheese, and also dump in a good amount of Parmesan.  I'm beginning to salivate as I write this.  You get the idea.

These turned out pretty good. I have never bought a box of Bisquick and never plan to. I want to make them again, when I do I think I'll substitute real butter for the shortening as I think it was missing the buttery flavor. Likewise, I'll double the garlic as my DH stated he couldn't taste it at all and missed it. The prep, texture and baking times were right on, I ended up with 9 medium sized biscuits, just enough to go with our Chicken Pot Pie tonight for dinner. Thanks for sharing.

Delicious. A very light, fluffy biscuit with a rich cheese and garlic taste. I doubled the batch and they were still eaten in 2 sittings. I used minced garlic in place of the powder since I LOVE garlic. Easy to put together and ready in a snap. Will use this recipe again for sure.

These are pretty good, but 1/2 cup milk is way too much. Dough wouldn't come together until I added more flour. Once baked, they turned out ok. I would make them again, maybe with some herbs for additional flavor.

Nice & simple! I'm trading out my old drop biscuit recipe for this one. I didn't follow the last step & instead put a lil shredded cheese on top of the biscuits before baking. I also used margarine when I cut it into the dry ingredients, because I didn't have any shortening on hand. I also added some parsley flakes to the mix. I appreciate the fact that this recipe doesn't call for Bisquick like many of the cheddar biscuit recipes. Thanks a bunch for a great recipe!
Best biscuit recipe I've ever made!!!

Very delicious! Made these at the last minute for dinner. I usually make one that calls for Bisquick, of which I had none, so I decided to see if I could find a scratch recipe. Yours was the first one to pop up on the search, so I went with it. The only changes were to increase the salt to 1/2 tsp. and the cheese to 1/2 cup. I also added a pinch of dried parsley, crushed between my fingers, to the butter that gets brushed on at the finish--it just looks pretty! They turned out perfect and delicious. Dough consistency was just right, baking time was accurate for the recipe yeild. The only things I might change next time would be to eliminate or reduce the sugar because while it wasn't bad, I could detect a bit of a sweet taste that seemed odd for a savory biscuit and I would increase the amount of the butter that gets brushed on after baking to 3 Tbsp. because it was hardly enough. Thanks for a great recipe!
I was glad to find this recipe that did not use Bisquick, since I never have it on hand.  Very good, next time I will double or triple the recipe to freeze and have on hand :)

I made these as a side to go with our pasta dinner tonight.  The biscuit itself was great.  They were very light and fluffy, not heavy at all like some other biscuits we've tried.  However, my family didn't think the garlic or cheese flavors were very noticeable.  For that reason, they only rated the recipe as written, 3 stars.  Next time I will increase both the garlic and cheese and see how it effects their rating.
These were absolutely delicious!! Marg, thank you so much for the recipe, I'll be making this one often!
what would be the equivalent if you used minced garlic vs g. powder?
Can I sub butter for the shortening and still have fluffy, moist biscuits that rise high?
These had a good flavor, but they did not turn out as soft as we like them to be.  They also did not carmelize as I was hoping they would.

ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!!! I would rate this with 10 stars if I could. I have an e-mail list with over 1800 addresses & I am sending this recipe out to everyone, but I won't say that it is my recipe. I will give you credit for the recipe, as you deserve it. Thanks for posting it.

These were pretty darn good!  My Dh just loved them. I would of liked them to be alittle more cruncher though. I let them bake a little longer than called for in hopes they would get cruncher. Still the flavor was very good. I will be trying these again.  Thanks for sharing!
These were easy and turned out really well. I only had 1 lb. of carrots left, but the cooking time was still perfect.

Nothing brings out the natural sweetness of vegetables like roasting.  These are so easy to do and wonderful.  I added some pepper after cooking but other than that didn't change a thing.  For easy cleanup, I did line the pan with foil.  Delicious!

This lovely photo by Paula inspired me to make these carrots. I started roasting at 400 degrees for half and hour and decreased to 375 for about 15 minutes, since I was short on time. I used the bagged baby carrots which I normally find to be tough(but convenient). 
The butter and the roasting really mellowed the carrots and I noticed everyone cleaned their plates. Served with chicken fingers and pasta with peanut sauce.
Roxygirl
The wonderful thing about this recipe is how the natural sugar in the carrots caramelizes and glazes them. Thank you for a recipe that is so simple and yet so absolutely delicious!

What glorious flavor these carrots pack! They are so wonderfully easy to prepare if you use the baby carrots as well. Mine never carmelised at all even though I left them in about 20 minutes longer to see if they would. I will make these time and time again!

EXCELLENT! We all loved the flavor and they were so easy to fix! I decided to try this recipe, rather than steam the carrots like I usually do, because I was making a casserole so the oven would be on anyway. I'm so glad I did! We all agreed we like them better than steamed so I'll be fixing this dish again. It did take mine about 10 more minutes to cook than called for, but that wasn't a big problem. One tip, we all preferred them after they had sat about 10 minutes too. The flavor seemed more intense. I was pleasantly surprised at how sweet the carrots were without any sugar or honey added. A definite winner! Thanks!
This was too easy but it tasted great! I used baby carrots too...perfect!
I only made 1 lb and used baby carrots. They turned out sweet and crunchy. Very good and extremely easy!

So simple, yet perfect. Easy to make, with outstanding results. I used organic carrotes. They were cooked perfectly and tasted  sweet and tender. I will be making carrotes this way from now on. Thanks so much for sharing Cookin-jo, this dish rocks.
Now how easy is this!! It really tastes so good---the little bit left for me to taste! I did add some black pepper and a pinch of Kosher salt. I will make it again soon. Thank you for this recipe.
Simplicity has its rewards and this is one of them!! Thanks for sharing this with us.

WOW! I never would have guessed such a simple recipe would have packed such a natural sweet tasting carrot without sugar being added. My youngest DS had 2 helpings!!
Thank You-
No sugar added, simple (stupid simple), and a delight for the taste buds! Thank you!
These were a real winner in my house i dont usually roast carrots but i will be from now on...yum!!  Thanks :)

I really debated on rating these a "like it" or a "love it" and I went with a "love it" because of the simplicity and how much my kids ate.  They were super easy, but I prefer a little more sweetness than these had.  They just tasted like your typical roasted carrot to me, nothing fancy, but definitely super easy.  Thanks!

Absolutely wonderful carrots!  I used just, about, 2/3 lb. of carrots...put them in an 8x8 non-stick pan, added about 1 T. of 'Buttery Sticks' (vegan butter, no fat), and they were done in about 45 minutes.  They were soft, carmelized, somewhat sticky and very sweet and delicious.  This is a keeper recipe and will be made again.  Thanks cookin-jo :)
Easy and delicious! I was surprised how good the carrots were without sugar or other seasonings. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

Wonderful!  These carrots were so flavorful - I'll not be steaming or boiling them again either. So simple, it kind of makes me slap my head and say "Why didn't I think of that?!?"  DH went back for seconds - unheard of with veggies of any kind!  Thanks for posting.
Buttery yummy good

I loved how soft and sweet these turned out.  Just like steaming them but so much better! Excellent recipe, thank you for posting this.  By the way I sprinkled some cinamon on there, simply because I love the way it smells and it gave it a little kick. (Not that it needed it)

This was the first time I've ever roasted carrots in the oven by themselves in butter.  I do throw them in my pot roast, but sometimes, I just want a plain ole carrot.  It took me several years to like them and when I finally tried them (in the hospital, no less) I fell in love.  I always keep raw baby carrots on hand and canned for other quick meals.  I did cut the recipe in half because it's just me eatin, but when I do have company, these will for-sure be something I will serve up.  YUMMY...thanks for the idea!
Loved these carrots! I can't anything better that hasn't already been said about them....
Most simple recipe ever, but the only one I will use for carrots from now on.
These were delicious!!!! I used real butter and sprinkled them with salt and pepper. I baked mine at 375 for one hour and they were perfect. I will definitely be making these often!
Fantastic and so easy. My kids loved them.
Delicious! Next time I might add some fresh thyme - they're so good with carrots - but, truthfully, these are scrumptious as is!!

I have prepared carrots with brown sugar, honey,-  several different ways, these were the best.  I will now only prepare them this way.  They were delicious and company quality. Thank you for a great recipe.
These are the best ever!  I will never use the pressure cooker again for carrots.  Sometimes simple is just better.
Simple but wonderful.  Easy to make and the flavor is something else.  We'll be using this for the Holidays.  Thanks for sharing.
It's crazy how simple and delicious this is.  We have these about twice a week now.  Sometimes we cut down on the butter and sometimes we don't.  Either way is awesome.

I'm not going to rate this as I realized I messed up.  The carrots came out a little drier than I had expected, and I wondered why, so I checked the recipe.  It turns out that I forgot to stir!  I'm going to try this again soon, stirring as instructed, and will report back.  Until then, everybody make sure you stir.  :)
I make a lot of carrots this way. Then I freeze them. I do not cook as long in the oven. Thanks for posting. When reheating I add margarine and a little chicken broth.
Yes, simpler is amazingly better. This is now the only way I will make carrots. Absolutely just lets the delicious, natural flavor of the carrots shine through. Thank you!
I have been making carrots like this for years and we love them. I even cook them on the grill like this.

Fantastic!!  Made these twice.  First time I cut them in about 1/4" strips and used fresh carrots out of the garden.  They were fantastic.  Second time used bagged baby carrots from the produce and cut in half lengthwise.  They took a lot longer to cook and were not near as sweet, they really had no flavor.  Fresh is the only way to go.  We'll be eating carrots this way from now on.  Thanks.

These were great! So sweet tasting. The whole family loved them. I even ate them cold the next morning for breakfast and they were good that way too. I did add a little garlic salt and pepper to them before roasting. Served these with crockpot roast as I do not like to put carrots in with it. A definite make again!
These were absolutely fantastically sweet!  I browned them a little because we like them that way and they were just great.  Simple and perfect.  Thanks!

The texture of the carrots was great, but they didn't seem too flavorful, so I sautated them with a little more butter and some honey for a few minutes after I removed them from the oven.  I also added chopped parsley for color.  Thanks for sharing.
Perfect.....easy,tasty....delish. The carrots made there own glaze with the butter....mmmmm.   This will be my only way to cook carrots from now on.....thank you   Stephanie
Couldn't be easier to make.  Think I'll try light butter next time.  Thanks for posting.

I'm not going to rate this because I am not sure what went wrong.  I followed the directions exactly, with half the ingredients.  Mine came out shrivelled and terribly ugly on the outside while not cooked on the inside.  With so many positive reviews, I wonder what went wrong with mine?
This the fastest to make, best tasting carrot recipe.  There are never any leftovers.

These made perfect carrots!  It is the most simple recipe ever and you really do not need to use a large amount of butter to give them a lot of flavor.  Cooking them for an hour really releases sweetness from the carrots.  This is the perfect sidedish.

Who knew carrots had a sweeter side?  No one would believe me when I told them I had not added sugar to this dish. I served this as part of a roast game hen dinner for my card group and there was great discussion on the carrots! I used full, stemmed carrots and left them whole rather than chopping them up - simply for appearance reasons. There were fantastic!
Delicious and soooo easy.  Used baby carrots and it couldn't have been simpler if it had been delivered.  Thanks for a new favorite!
excellent. very good carrots - crisp tender and not overly sweet.
very good.No need to boil these vegetables.This method is so much better.I add sliced parsnips to the carrots for color and flavor.

How easy! I made this to go with recipe #67742 and mashed potatoes. And because they were in the fridge, I added pea pods and chopped walnuts to the carrots. The pea pods came out kinda strange (crispy), but the carrots were especially delicious--and I'm not a fan of carrots.

Had these last night with Kittencal's Beef or Pork Marinade and tenderizer (did London Broil on the grill, Oh my!!! mmmmm).  These carrots were fantastic!  Loved the flavor - very very simple way to cook them and what they add to a meal - makes me hate to call them a "side dish".  They held there own in taste as well as compliments from the "eaters"..they were perfect with the London Broil and I don't believe I'll ever be guilty of boiling another poor carrot again.  Thanks so much!
Simple, easy and delicious. A definite keeper of a recipe. The only way to do carrots from now on.
Simple and delicious! No need to steam up your kitchen when you can make these delicious carrots right along side your roast. Thanks for sharing!

Sorry, but this was a waste of time. I love carrots no matter what, but the hour spent did not at all add any flavor or excitement to the dish. May as well steam and add butter, not much different and much less time consuming.

It was a bit flavorless and lacking in something special.  Before serving I tasted the carrots which were very bland.  I added a tablespoon of brown sugar and a good dose of salt and pepper and then they were perfect for my taste.
I use baby carrots and added a tablespoon of brown sugar,a bit of garlic The flavor seemed more intense.I will be butter Roasted more.thank you!! Grpa!

I made these and I am not sure if I did it right or not. Some of the other reviewers mentioned that their carrots carmelized. Mine did not. Since they were cooked with a lid they were just steamed. They were good but not exactly what I expected. Was I supposed to remove the lid at some point? The word "roasted" would indicate so.  I will make them again because they were good and it is just sooo easy to put them in the oven if you are baking other parts of the meal. Thanks for the recipe. I will probably mess with it next time and see if I can find the elusive carmelization!

Not wanting our carrots taste steamed, I cooked them for the first twenty minutes without any lid.  During the last forty minutes, I added a loosly fitting piece of aluminum foil that would let steam out.  I did stir the carrots as mentioned.  They turned out to be delicious!  We'll be cooking carrots this way again often!  Thank you!
Did I do something wrong?? These just didn't do it for me. I followed the recipe exactly but the results weren't only so-so.

This was a nice easy recipe. I only kept my carrots in for 40 minutes since we like them to be a bit crunchy. These weren't, like, some new extremely flavorful way to make carrots but they were easy, tasty and a nice change from the same old glazed carrots. We'll definitely be making these again. Thanks.
I really liked it. It's a perfect side dish that you throw in the oven while you get the rest of the meal ready. No hustle yet great flavor. Thank you.

Yum, who doesn't love butter roasted carrots? I loved these incredible, tasty, carrots SO much! Followed exactly, but only used a quarter pound of carrots, so I only let roast for 30 minutes. It was just perfect in everyway. Thanks for posting!
I am not a fan of cooked carrots and have tried to like them many different ways. These carrots are simple and delicious! I added some salt at the end, as I add salt to everything. :)

Not sure where I went wrong here but my carrots did not caramelize or have a roasted flavor.  I followed all the directions, but they definitely did not cook all the way through.  I had to cook them longer just to get them crisp-tender and they tasted like regular steamed carrots.  However....I am going to try this again, possibly without covering.  I don't want to drag the rating down on a recipe that is obviously beloved by so many other cooks.  I am giving this a 4 star rating because it is a very easy side when you have other parts of the meal that require more time/energy.  Thanks for the recipe.
Very easy & tasty. I roasted the carrots with some potatoes. While they didn't look real pretty (they got pretty shriveled), they tasted great. I added a little salt and garlic to the mix.
Made these for Easter. Super easy and delicious! Cut carrots in half lengthwise, then thirds. Cooked at 375 for 40 min. Perfect!

I made these very similar to what Vermonter said, and they were GREAT. I cut 2 lbs of carrots in half lengthwise and then into thirds. But then I actually melted the 2 Tbl of butter in the microwave and then drizzled it all over the carrots and tossed them in the hot butter, salt, pepper and some dried before cooking them at 375 for 45 min and then uncovered for 10 mins more and they were delicious - no one could believe I hadn't addded sugar!
This was ok for us. There was WAY to much olive oil. The chicken was drowning in it. If you like oregano, this one's for you. Made for Fall PAC 2011.
Kit thank you very much for guiding me through this recipe, and for all you help you are the best! thanks to you we had the best Christmas dinner ever, you are a true friend, thank you.

I'm sure this is the perfect turkey recipe,but it was too juicy for my family's taste. We've been brought up on dry, overcooked turkey, so this was new for us. The taste was great, but since I forgot to buy a meat thermometer, nobody was convinced that it was cooked all the way, and we were scared to eat it. We ate the outer meat for dinner, and later I threw the leftovers back in the oven to dry it out a little, so I will defenitely try this again, just with the thermometer.

I knew where to go for my Thanksgiving turkey recipe.  Carol, my boyfriend said this was the best, most juicy turkey ever.  I really appreciated having a recipe that I knew would work and I did not hesitate or look around for any other recipe.  I used this in conjunction with your turkey brine recipe.  Thank you (and my guests thank you) for a wonderful Thanksgiving turkey.

This was perfect! I knew I could trust Kitten! This is similar to what I usually do, but I had never tried the chicken broth in the bottom of the pan, and I always put it in uncovered first, then covered it later if it started getting too brown. This works better! It was moist, and VERY flavorful! Thanks Kitt! You rock!

The BEST Turkey I have cooked...I even WOWED my husband!  This is the first year I had to make the turkey by myself and I was very nervous but I turned the unstuffed turkey on the breast and put a cheesecloth on top, then lots of Chicken Stock and basted it often.  It was very moise and very flavorful.  I also added onion and garlic to the turkey and saffaron on top.  It was so good I would like to have another oppotunity for a turkey meal besides Thanksgiving!

i have always used the reynolds plastic bags for my turkeys.this year I tried this method.The difference was amazing !!!! Thanks you very much.My family could not believe how moist the turkey was even for sandwiches the next day !!! thanks again
I've always cooked my turkeys in cooking bags also and decided to try this out.  It was great!  I highly recommend using a meat thermometer to make sure you don't overcook or undercook.

This was the moisted turkey I have ever eaten. Even my own Mother could not believe how moist it was. Best part was the following day, still nice and moist, not dryed out. I cooked a 15 lb bird, unstuffed, with 5 cups of chicken broth didn't need to add more. Thanks Kitten for yet another outstanding recipe!
I made this for Thanksgiving this year and it was very good with a lot of flavor.  Will definately make again.  Thank you for sharing!

Delicious & Succulent mmmm, it got me thu Thanks Giving with raves. Everyone liked it. The recipe was easy to follow, thanks for the roasting chart. It was a great help as I was wondering how long to roast the 24 pounder. Thanks for sharing
I made this trukey for our christmas dinner and it turned out soooo good. I cooked the turkey breast down for about 2 1/2 hours and then turned it around for browning and it was extremely moist!!!!
The absolute best turkey I have ever eaten!  Cooked exactly as instructed, and it was moist and flavorful.  Amazingly delicious and the family loved it.  Made for my Christmas Eve Dinner.

We trusted Kittencal for our Thanksgiving holiday dinner centerpiece, and this did not disappoint! We stuffed ours and roasted it breast side up. It took rather longer than we expected, but the final result is tender, savory and moist. Our turkey had a tender timer but we also used a meat thermometer. Thanks! Edited to Add: We did this again two days after Christmas and it came out even more beautiful!

My first roasted whole turkey turned out beautiful.  I did not stuff mine at it was only 8.35lbs so it cooked in 2 1/2 hours exactly.  The broth turned into great gravy.  The only problem I had was the broth never fully evaporated so the under side of my turkey (where the breasts were) never truly browned, but it was nice and tender.

Fantastic!!  We cooked this recipe last night and followed the directions exactly.  Everyone raved about the tender, flavorful meat.  We roasted it breast-down and added some apple slices to the carcass and cooked the stuffing separately.  Take your time seasoning the bird before cooking and you will be pleased with this easy and delicious recipe.

This turkey turned out fantastic AGAIN but this time on my Kamado Kooker charcoal grill.  It is the be the best one I've ever grilled.  Here's what I did as my personal variation:<br/>Start with an 17 lb. fresh, natural turkey.  Rinse it well, then brine it for 12-14 hours.<br/>Rinse it well after brining, rub with the recipe plus add a tbs. dry rub to the mix.  Add a couple of sprigs of fresh rosemary to the bird cavity.<br/>Place into a large, disposable aluminum roasting pan, breast side down.  Tie the wings tight to the side of the bird.  Add the liquid, cover with foil tent.  Maintain a 325 temperature.<br/>  Make sure to baste every 40-50 mins.  Rotate the bird 90 degrees after about 3 hours.  This helps even out the cooking.<br/>Defiantly use an electric meat thermometer to get the thigh meat up to 160.<br/>Keeping the temperature constant was the biggest challenge, as it usually is on any grill.  But the result was well worth the effort. The meat turns out packed with flavor, juicy and succulent.

I used 10 cups of water and it was quite soupy so I left the lid off the pot and it thickened up very nicely towards the end of the 1 1/2 hours cook time.  I'll certainly be making this again, thanks so much for posting this recipe Uncle Bill!

Very, very good!  And, easy to boot.  Followed the recipe to a "T", however, I took the other reviewer's advice and only used 8 - 10 cups water.  Pureed 1/2 of the soup, leaving chunks.  Served with homemade rolls.

What a dinner!!  Thanks Uncle Bill.

This is a wonderful soup and I found the texture to be perfect as is.  I did omit the bouillon and salt, as I felt the amount of sodium from the hambone I had would be more than enough and it was.  Thank you Uncle Bill for sharing this marvelous recipe.

Simply the best!  I followed the recipe exactly, except I used 8 cups of water because I like a thicker pea soup.  There was no need to puree it, as the peas dissolved into a lovely thick creamy soup. It was absolutely delicious.  I can't think of any possible improvement.

WOW this was good soup. I had a ham bone in the freezer left over from Easter which still had a lot of meat on it. I used yellow split peas and instead of beef cubes I used ham cubes. I will definitely be making this again. Thanks Uncle Bill for a great recipe.

FANTASTIC!!!! I had a huge ham bone sitting in my freezer, and I wanted to make your recipe, I was just waiting for a cooler day, and today was it! I used 5 cups of chicken broth and 5 cups water in place of all 12 cups water, and only used 1 beef cube... wonderful smokey taste that thickened up to just the right consistancy. I let it simmer slowley for about 2 hours, we really enjoyed this with homemade crusty buns...Uncle Bill has done it again! thanks for another winner!...Kitten:)

What a great soup!  I used only 8 cups of water and had a nice, thick soup.  As I was somewhat pressed for time, I simmered the peas for 20 minutes (rather than letting them sit for an hour in boiling water).  Added 2 small bay leaves, but otherwise followed the recipe.  Thanks for sharing!

Best Pea Soup ever. I am not a big fan of pea soup but I had a large ham bone left over from a party. My husband asked me to make soup. He and I finished the pot in 2 days. I followed your recipe exactly and it turned out great!
Thanks for this wonderful recipe.
Excellent soup!!   Followed the recipe and it turned out perfect. The  beef bouillon gave it the extra flavor. In my keepers file this recipe will go. Thanks Uncle Bill.
this is how i make it  too its really good .dee

Excellent soup.  I usually can't make a good soup to save my soul... I got this one right though!  That says something about the recipe writer.  I will make this again next year to use up my Easter ham bone!  Thanks for posting!

Uncle Bill we loved this. It's getting cooler is Qld, Aust now and this was perfect. I grated my carrot and used bacon hocks which my butcher cut up into smaller pieces for me.  I also used the full 12 cups of water and I'm glad I did. It ended up simmering on the stove all afternoon which meant that I didn't need to puree as the split peas and veggies were so very soft - yum. I took the lid off and turned it up slightly higher allowing the soup to reduce down. Both my 2 and 4 year olds loved this. Served with Kittencals Delicious Cheesy Parmesan Garlic Bread Recipe #105726. Thanks for sharing a wonderful recipe :)
We all loved this soup. It came out great. thanks for a good "that hit the spot" recipe!

Loved this soup, Uncle Bill. So easy to make and very satisfying. Perfect with a chunk of crusty bread for dinner on a chilly, rainy evening!  I added 1 tsp thyme and 2 bay leaves. Also, I used about 1/2 c salt pork rather than the ham bone. Sauteed it up with the onions, carrots, and celery (and 2 cloves of garlic) prior to simmering it all with beef stock and split peas. Excellent flavors-- my husband went for seconds and said it's really good. Looking forward to leftovers for lunch. Thanks for posting!

OMG I could have sworn I rated this weeks ago. I loved this, my whole family did. I have never eaten this before, the green color turned me off, and I am not a fan of peas. Wow what have I been missing? Just one of the best most econimcal soups you can imagine. I did not have a ham bone, so I used a ham steak, cut into small peices and even put the bone in, can't wait till I have a real ham bone!!!!!!!!! This was unbelievably good, even if it is green!!!!!ha

This was the best pea soup I have had in ages! My boyfriend and daughter both loved it. I did only use 10 cups of water like suggested by other reviewers. This will be a favorite in my house. Can't wait for the cold weather to have an excuse to make more!

This really hit the spot!  Very full of flavor!  I did use about 8 cups of chicken broth instead of the water & bullion cubes, simply a preference.  Next time I will use less liquid (6 cups?)or more split peas (3 cups?) as it was a little thin for us.  Thanks for a delicious recipe!

DH requested Split Pea Soup and I decided to give this recipe a try.  I didn't have any ham bones in the freezer so I bought 2 smoked ham hocks and used a ham steak for the chunked meat (hocks gross me out so I used for flavor only.) Following the advice of others I used 5 cups of water and 5 cups chicken stock and upped the thyme to 1/4 tsp. After the 1st step of having the beans sit for 1 hour, I simmered for 2 hours and the texture was perfect the soup was thick but not globby, no blending needed and there was still chunks of carrot.  Next time I make I will make sure to use low sodium broth and possibly lose the additional salt. It was a bit on the salty side the way I made it but easily fixed.  Great soup - the family loved it!  Thanks for posting Uncle Bill.
Perfect!  I followed the directions exactly and ended up with the best pea soup I've ever eaten.  Thanks Uncle Bill for this delicious and easy recipe.

This was the best pea soup I ever had!  The only thing different I did was add fresh thyme, 3 beef cubes and 1/2 tsp. salt. My husband and I keep eating it!!! Great for a cold night. Thanks Uncle Bill.
Just changed to 5 stars--this was even better cooled down a bit.  Don't eat it really hot.  Good, healthy, long, but easy to make.  A winner.  My French husband said it was better than his mother's.

These is a very good soup recipe.  I made it with pork neck bones rather than a ham bone, and I added a little more salt and pepper at the end.  Also, I couldn't fit all the water in my pot, so I only used about 8 cups.  I used the hand-held blender to smooth it all out.  Thank you Uncle Bill.  UPDATE:  On day two, this soup is incredible.  I had to come back and up it from four stars to five!

This was very good!  The only other split pea soup that I had was very thick but I liked it much better this way (even though I did add 1/2 cup of extra split peas-and glad that I did).  I added a lot of black pepper and some crused red pepper because we like most things spicy.  Even my little picky eaters enjoyed this!  The only other change I made was in the end I thickened it up a little with instant potato flakes.

This is a wonderful soup. I did cut the recipe in half for just the two of us and as a result had a nice meaty soup that we enjoyed for thee meals. The seasonings are just perfect. Adding the thyme and bay leaf gave it a wonderful tang.

Excellent!  I had a  large, frozen ham bone in my freezer since Thanksgiving and used it up on this soup.  I omitted the salt and used a 1 1/2 cubes of ham boullion instead of the beef.  After I removed the ham bone, I pureed the soup then added the remaining meat off the bone.  Thanks for posting; it's delicious!

Delicious! I made this Sunday night, using a ham hock, because I had already used my ham bone I had. I did have to cook it a little longer for the ham hock to get tender. But for the rest, I followed the recipe to the letter. I did take your advice and puree about four medium size bowls of the soup, since I like a thicker pea soup. This is wonderful on a cold day! I shared it with an elderly man next door and a new mom and dad that brought their baby home Sunday. Served it with corn bread and biscuits and banana pudding for dessert. Great dinner. We all loved it. Thanks Uncle Bill!

Fantastic soup! I used my Easter ham bone I had frozen and followed the recipe exactly, it was so flavorful, I used my immersion blender to puree it and boy was it good with crusty fresh french bread, it makes a lot too.

I tossed everything in a crock pot and cooked on low over night.  I woke up to the smell of a good split pea soup.  I did add more split peas in the morning and cooked for an additional couple of hours(I like a thicker soup).  Great recipe!
This is a very yummy soup. It's easy to follow and has an excellent taste. Had it for lunch today!!! Will definitely make again. Thanks, Uncle Bill, for a keeper!!!

I didn't have any beef bouillon cubes, but it was still really good!   This made a lot of food and was a great way to use up a ham bone instead of throwing it away.  Glad I found this recipe before I trashed it.  Thanks a lot!

I recently had surgery and wanted to make a few dishes that I could eat the week I was recovering. I'm so glad I chose this one! The flavors of this dish seemed to develop over a few days and the soup's taste really kept getting better. Wonderful, wonderful soup.

This is so delicious.  I always make this a day or two after making ham following recipe #57765.  I have made it exactly as directed everytime and it never feeds as many people as you'd think - we just keep gobbling it down till near-explosion!

This was very good. I did adjust the recipe a bit. Omitted the celery (not a big fan) and subbed 4 cups of chicken stock for 4 cups of water. Also, I used a combo of split peas, lentils and small white beans. I did add an additional 1/2 cup of both peas and lentils. For a total of 3 cups dried peas/beans. I also pureed about 1/2 the soup to make it smoother. It was the perfect consistency. Very delicious! I will for sure be making this again. Thanks Uncle Bill!

Wow. I love split pea soup, but this is just the best--with some minor tweaks. I used only ten cups of liquid-half water, half chicken stock and it was still a little bit much. Also, I used just a pinch of salt, since the stock had some. My husband just finished his third bowl and can't stop raving about it. (And I thought my previous recipe was pretty good--this is GREAT!) I am going to go out tomorrow and buy more of everything to make another huge pot to freeze for the winter! UPDATED:  our first pot for this winter- I've found (over the last winter and many pots!) that 3 rounded cups of split peas make the perfect thickness for us, and we add three crushed garlic cloves.  I can't wait for my first bowl of the season!!! (OK, technically it's still summer, but there's a HINT of autumn in the air here!)

Just like my mom makes! I cut the water back to 9 cups. I also had to use smoked turkey necks in place of the ham bone. ... but to make up for it during the last half hour of simmering I added 8 ounces of finely chopped ham steak.  Very delicious. Thanks for another good recipe Uncle Bill! By the way... I'm still using your method for cooking steaks and it has NEVER FAILED me.
great soup! made this with just a few changes.  added fresh garlic and used fresh tyme.  didn't have ham so i used smoked turkey and chicken stock instead of water.  loved it!

Who knew something so full of vitamins could be so good?  I halved the recipe, and at first glance the 6 cups of water/broth looked like too much; it wasn't.  I'll make this one again, and I won't change a thing.  Thanks, Uncle Bill!

First time I made Split Pea Soup and this is an awesome recipe! I used the bone from the Thanksgiving Ham. Used 8 cups of water instead of 12. Puree'd using a blender for a smooth and thicker consistency. Delicious! Thank you very much!

This soup is delicious !!! I made a double batch so I could freeze some. I used two pork hocks and added a extra bay leaf. When it was almost done I added 2 smoked ham steaks cut up into bite size pieces. Thank You Uncle Bill !!!!

I have never made Pea Soup before and found this recipe.  I read the reviews and I reduced the water to 11 cups and added more chunks of ham and found that next time I made this I will add more peas.  Everyone loved it =) THX 4 sharing

Made 12 cups of water and a lb of split peas (about 2 cups).  Great flavor, the split peas were mostly broken down by the end of the cooking time and the consistency was thin with a split pea remnants on the bottom of the pot.  I like my soup a little thicker so I raised the pot up to a rolling boil for about 10 minutes and stirred with a metal spoon most of the time.  This caused the split peas to disintegrate and stay in suspension, giving me a soup with the consistency of a cream of mushroom type soup.  More to my likening.

I will definitely be making this again.  Thanx Uncle Bill
Wonderful, just made it for the 2nd time today- compliments all around!

My husband said, "When you said we were having pea soup for dinner I curled my nose.  I'm sorry I did.  This is soooo good!"  This coming from the fussiest guy in the universe!  GREAT soup with a great use of the old leftover ham bone.  I can't wait to try the leftovers! I served it with nothing but garlic bread and it was hearty enough to be a complete meal.

According to my daughter, this was AWESOME! And I must say I agree! I did follow the suggestions of cutting back on the liquid and used 10 cups of water, next time I think I'll sub in some broth. Thanks for a super easy and delicious recipe!

Fantastic soup!  I had not had Split Pea Soup in years because my husband and kids turned their nose up every time I offered it.  This time, I gave them no choice and prepared it while I was the only one home.  Well, the neighbors were commenting on the wonderful aromas coming from my house.  The soup itself?  Perfect!  Exactly what I had been longing for.  Other than omitting the salt, I followed the directions to the letter.  What a wonderful way to use that leftover holiday ham bone!  Thank you so much for this culinary walk down memory lane!
Yummy and easy if you think about early enough in the day.  Perfect lazy Sunday fare.  The thyme adds a depth of flavor other recipes don't.  Thanks Uncle Bill.

Thanks for the great recipe.  I pureed the carrots, onions, celery and some garlic and sweated these in olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients (I keep  bags of this pureed mixture in my freezer to use as a soup base - it's easier to do a bunch at a time than in small batches every time I make soup).  And I used some Brazilian bouillon cubes for traditional black beans (feijoada) instead of beef cubes (because they've got ham flavoring).

Cut the recipe in half and used chicken boullion instead of beef.  Chopped up some canadian bacon instead of using hambone.  Wow. Good stuff and a nice change from the milk or tomato based soups.  Thanks.

This was great!  I used a ham bone, and also two smoked pork necks (they were on sale).  Instead of boullion, I used some frozen turkey stock I had.  I used less water overall than called for.  I, too, burned my lip fairly badly trying to taste it out of the pot, so be careful!
Very good soup! I made it exactly as directed. I will definitely make this again! Thank you for sharing your recipe.

This was by far one of the best Split Pea soups I have had.  I added 1/4 tsp liquid smoke and it was enjoyed by all.  I served it with Sweet Hawaiian Yeast Bread http://www.recipezaar.com/94674 and I got rave reviews.  Thanks Uncle Bill.

My husband LOVES this recipe. This is only my second attempt at making split pea soup and the first one was a disaster. This one is great! I made a few changes: I dropped the water down to 8 cups and didn't have a bay leave so I left it out. We had a ham bone left over from dinner last night as well as a ton of ham. This was super easy and flavorful. I cannot wait to have some more tomorrow, provided my husband doesn't polish it off tonight.

My husband has always told me that he loves Split Pea soup, and I always bought the store bought canned versions. Well Never Again. I used 2 ham hocks and did blend at the end to thicken it up just a bit. Would suggest to blend before adding meat back to soup. Thanks Uncle Bill for another tried and true recipe.

Soooo good!! I made a batch of this with my leftover hambone from Easter and I am so glad I did! My DH said this is the best he has ever had and I agree. I did add an extra cup of split peas as others had recommended I also used half chicken stock and half water but I thought the 12 cups was perfect. I did need to leave it on the stove for about an hour longer to get it to thicken up good! I will make this again for sure! Thanks Uncle Bill!
This is the best split pea soup I have ever made.  Perfect for any day!!!

Oh, Uncle Bill, this was just perfect for the cold weather we've been having.  My partner rated it better than her mother's split pea soup, and  she doesn't say that very often at all.  
As usual, wonderfully clear instructions and this came together so well.  
A couple of changes were made - subbed bacon bones for the ham bone, and I used 2 cups of beef stock and 10 cups of water in place of the bouillon cubes since we find they add too much salt for our taste.  
Thank you so much for recommending this recipe - it was exactly what we were looking for and we''ll be making this often.

A good recipe and definitely worth a try if anyone has any doubts.  However, cooked as directed, either the amount of water was too much or the amount of split peas was too little, because I wound up with a watery soup and had to double the cooking time (uncovered) to achieve the right thickness.  I would also edit the recipe and include more specific direction for the amount of ham to be added, instead of suggesting the ham bone scraps.  Each ham bone can be different, so without specifics, each pot of soup can also be different, making it difficult to get the desired result from each person using this recipe.

This soup is fantastic! And for all those who thought that there was too much water, I would have loved to have been there the next day when they went to reheat it for another serving - it thickens up so much you can hold the pot upside down and it would stay - LOL.. I always, always make pea soup the day before I want to serve it, exactly for that reason. This recipe was about the same as the one I've always used, but the addition of thyme and bay were new to me and added so much more flavor.. this is the one I will always use from now on. I used smoked hocks this time, for I generally only have a ham bone like once a year.. anyhow, thanks for posting this!
Great tasting soup but a little too watery.  Next time I'll make it with 8 cups and add some more peas. Everything else was great!

Made this soup on Sunday. Had it for lunch on Monday. But I will agree it is a bit liquidy. I put in smoked ham hocks cause I had no ham bone but followed the recipe as directed. I used my immersion blender to blend it a bit. The flavour was great though. The next time I make it I will add more peas in it. After reading all the reviews I don't know why some have it liquidy and some have it thick. But a good soup nontheless. Thanks for the posting Uncle Bill

After reading some of the reviews, I cut down the water some and just cooked it until it was the consistency I like. Wonderful flavor! I served with homemade bread and apple slices. A simple yet hearty dinner. Thank you for sharing.

I used a ham steak rather than a ham bone.  I thought this was very good.  I am used to a thicker soup though, so I would decrease to maybe 10 c instead of 12 c.  Or start with 8 c for the soak and then add 2 more c when you add the rest of the ingredients.  I actually added 1/2 c. dry peas hoping to make it thicker and it was still thin.

This is a great recipie. I can't imagine using 12 cups of liquid though. I only used 8 cups and it's still a little to watery for my liking. I agree with those who suggested using two bags of beans. I intend to add a second bag of beans to this batch then i'm sure it will be perfect. I used a ham bone but it was pretty clean so I cut up part of a ham steak as well. I also added garlic to this and only used chicken stock for the liquid. It's a great recipie. Perfect amount of veggies and seasoning. Thanks so much.

I have to say this gets better each day.  We had leftovers for lunch and my 3 year old asked for seconds.  I changed my vote from 4 to 5 and i'd go higher if I could.
Excellent! :) I doubled the peas for my large family and it turned out great! Thanks.

Outstanding! I think this beats Pea Soup Anderson. I followed the recipe, but used 3 small smoked ham hocks. I pureed the whole thing and the thickness was perfect. I used the 8 cups water. Not sure why some people are talking about 12 cups water...I don't see that in the recipe.
At any rate, this will be in my repetoire to cook ahead of time to take on camping trips. Thank you Uncle Bill!!!

I've never made pea soup before and this turned out just like I remember my grandmothers.  My husband said that he never like pea soup until now. I left the celery out due to personal taste but followed everything else exactly... thank you!

This was my first time making/eating split pea soup and it was fantastic! I wanted to make something with my left over hambone and this was perfect. After 1 1/2 hours I actually ended up putting in two extra cups of water because I was letting it simmer for even another hour while I waited on family. We served this over rice and I am positive everyone went back for at least second helpings! Thank you so much fo ra great recipe! I will definitely be making this again!
This was really good.  I added bacon which made it too salty.  I'll remember that for next time.  It was really thick, so I did add some extra water.  Very good leftover too.

This year I have decided to try and leave nothing unused that is useable. Looking around on Zaar I found this recipe, the name Uncle Bill Popped out at me because about a week I tried your wonderful method for cooking Turkey. I made this as the recipe as states just with less onion and vegetable bullion.  This soup is so yummy, I thought that for sure that I would hear can I make roman or have a bowl of cereal, but even my finicky 12 year old daughter loved it!  She ate two big bowls and believe me that is saying a lot. It is so nice when all you hear at dinner is mmmms and the clanking of spoons hitting the bottom of the bowl. Thanks for another wonderful recipe.
my family loves this soup! we make it whenever we have a ham bone available.
Excellent Split Pea Soup. I will make this recipe EVERY time I have leftover ham-bone! Thank you Uncle Bill!

Absolutley fantastic!! first time making a ham bone split pea soup. Tastes awsome!! Thank you for the recipe. Now I can eat good for a week!! I didn't puree anything and the peas seemed to puree themselves after a day of setting. GREAT RECIPE!!!
It's a keeper
This recipe is fantastic.  I've made it several times and comes out great every time.  Thank you for a great recipe.

Uncle Bill I love your soup.  This is great.  My two year old, and my husband both thought this was yummy.  I didn't have a ham bone so I used 1/2 a bag of diced ham, doubled the celery, skipped the bay leaf because I didn't have it, added an extra handful of chana dal (for of yellow pea) and used 2 tsp. all natural ham base from Orrington Farms, I also cut back a bit on the salt....we all had seconds.  Thank you.

What a wonderful split pea soup recipe!  I removed the ham shank and used an immersion blender to blend the soup after it was fully cooked.  I didn't make it very smooth.  We chopped up some of the ham, put it back into the soup, and again used the immersion blender to chop it into finer pieces.  It was a real treat on a snowy day.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe that will be made again and again.
Very delicious and filling. Will make again soon. I added the remnants of a bag of lentils (about 3/4 cup), tasted great.

WOW!!!  Superb!!  I can't believe how flavorful this is and how low in fat!!!!!  My husband is one of those guys that "thinks" he hates something even though he hasn't tried it in 20 years.  He scoffed at my making this..and I was making it for myself...took one taste and went crazy for this!  I wish I would have doubled the recipe now!  I bought pork hocks from the grocery store since I buy boneless hams...I followed the rest of the recipe just as stated and it was THE BEST!!!!!!  I didn't puree anything because I love the large bits of pea.  The consistency was perfect with the stated 8 cups of water and I diced up some cooked ham I'd made the night before to add.  Froze most of it and will thaw to eat daily for lunch.  Just LOVED it!  Thanks Uncle Bill!

I omitted the beef bouillon to restrict the salt a little, but otherwise made following the recipe.  I had lots of ham on the bones, to make it nice and meaty and was this soup ever delicious!  Brings back memories of my grandma making this for me as a child.  Good memories too!

As far as taste and value this recipe wins hands down. So easy to make - smoked ham hocks are super cheap as well as the rest of the ingredients. I served this for dinner along with some crusty rolls and everyone loved it. If you are tempted to add more meat, don't - I added some chopped hamsteak and it was a little too much. But that's my fault.
Thanks for sharing!

I've made this recipe several times now so I felt I owed a review.  I love this soup.  I've made it using water and I've made it substituting chicken broth and I feel the chicken broth is better.  Other than that, I cook some potatoes in a separate pot of salted water and add just before serving.  There are never any leftovers.  Thanks Uncle Bill!

So far this is turning out pretty good.  It still has a little bit more to go on the stove.  There is a little story behind this.  When I was a little girl I had a baby sitter that would always feed us "Split Pea" soup, but it  was like just mashed up peas, and when I was little I could not stand peas.  Growing up, I never wanted any part of the yuckie green soup that I remembered from my child hood.  Well, when I was on my luch break one of my co-workers was eating a soup that looked great, and sure enough it was Split Pea soup, not like I remembered though.  She let me try some and it was delicious, who would of thunk.  So, I decided that I wanted to try and make it, and here I am making it.  Thank you for helping come over one of my fears of PEAS!! Mt only down fall with this is that I am not sure how it is sopose to taste, so far its pretty yummy.

Mmmmm.....I did everything as directed, except I didn't have an hour to let the peas soak, so I simmered them for 20 minutes covered and then followed the directions.  I also took the lid off the last 30 minutes or so to thicken it up.  This was delicious!  My husband loved it!  Thank you for sharing!  :)
Made this again yesterday. THE best recipe I've ever used for split pea soup!
Very tasty, just like grandmas. Very hearty. I added some meat that was still on the bone. This is even better the next day.

Sorry, Uncle Bill, This recipe just was not for us.  The flavor being "off" somehow and It was much too thin.  It did thicken up on the second day and I thought it was better, but my husband wouldn't eat it and he will eat almost anything.
Amazing!  Tastes like a cream soup but it's just good ol' healthy peas!  Will never use another recipe.  You rock, Uncle Bill!
Uncle Bill this is a great soup.  Even my mom who strongly dislikes split pea soup thought this was good.  I used 3 ham hocks and a dash of liquid smoke.  Perfect!

Bill I just wanted you to know that when I got a hankering to make some split pea soup, I knew to look in your postings first.  But this went even above my already high expectations.  Like your delicious mung bean curry, I prepared this in my pressure cooker.  For my cooker (Presto 6-quart) I brought it to steam, cooked for 10 minutes with the stopper rocking gently, then ran the pot under cold water to reduce the pressure before opening.  I removed the smoked ham hocks and hit it with the stick blender- beautiful!  The flavor is just incredible.  Thanks again!
My family very much enjoyed this recipe. I did use a ham hock instead of ham bone though.
I have used this recipe twice and have loved it both times. I wouldn't chsnge a thing!

here are my 5 stars! i used a lb of dried peas and 8 cups water - perfect! finished with my stick blender. even my family (who are not soup people) really enjoyed this. thanks Uncle Bill! btw - i omitted salt and bouillon cuz it was salted enough and the flavor was excellent as is.

Bill Im sorry I forgot to rate this recipe becuase I use it all the time and we love it.  The only thing I do different is add a little cayenne (DH likes cayenne in almost everything.)  Last time I made it I canned it and thats what Im doing again.  We travel in an RV a lot and it is a wonderful way to have home made soup on the road.  Thanks for the recipe.  Gloria

SOOO GOOOOOOD! This is such comfort food, especially when you're sick!! I like the added beef bouillon, it added more depth. I used a really nice smoked ham shank. Pureed till smooth and added the meat at the end. I also used 10 cups of water and it was the perfect consistency ~ I don't like it too thick. It was the best pea soup we'd ever had. Thank you, Uncle Bill!! (Hi Emi!)
Wow, this soup sounds very good!  I just happened to buy some ham hocks and dried split peas last week, perfect timing!  I can't wait to try it!  (Hi KAY!)

I have tried four of Uncle Bill's soup recipes so far.  Each has been outstanding, including this one.  Didn't change a thing, other than use Bill's suggestions of chicken broth and liquid hickory smoke.  What a flavorful soup--I can hardly wait to try others (and he has lots of soup recipes) from this amazing chef.

This soup is amazing!!  Just like my Mom makes!  I used 8 cups of chicken broth and for the beef bouillon, I used two teaspoons instead of cubes, but really followed it to the letter!  My kids loved it!  They said it looked like something Shrek would eat, but they thought it was sooo good! I'm going to search out Uncle Bill's other soup recipes.  Great job!  Thanks for the recipe!

This soup was terrific!  My very picky 16 year old step-daughter hates pea soup but when she saw this one she said it looked different than her grandmothers and surprisingly gave it a try.  She loved it and had seconds.  Husband and I also loved it.  the only thing I would change is next time leave out the salt.  We had a lot of ham on the bone so it was a bit too salty but we still ate it all.
This was my first attempt at making split pea soup, and it was a HUGE hit!  My father-in-law actually liked it more than my mother-in-laws recipe!  Thanks uncle Bill!
Delicious.  I just put everything together in a pot and bring to a boil, simmer for 1.5 hour.  Yummy.  Couldn't be easier.  8 Cups of water was perfect.
Very good.  Split pea soup is my favorite, and this was probably the best I ever had.  I used a smoked ham shank for the hambone.  Sorry, Uncle Bill, this is MY recipe now!!

Wonderful soup! I love RecipeZaar :) I used 8 cups of water as written and then added a little more (probably about 2 cups) so that the ham bone was covered. I also added more ham to the soup after it was finished and let it simmer for a few minutes to warm through. I think the sugary coating of the ham adds a nice subtle sweetness to this soup. A+!

I was really impressed by how good this was! I dump the peas that have been sorted for rocks and rinsed right into the slowcooker with whatever liquid you prefer, water, broth, etc along with onion and garlic and seasonings. Super easy and the liner makes clean up a breeze!

I'm a Pastry Chef and a Culinary School Grad. I'd just like to point out that I was taught that there is a different in a 'frosting' and an 'icing'. The former is much thicker and has many ingredients, where as the latter is very light and has only 2 or 3 ingredients. Also, I'd love to send my very best frosting recipe. I learned how to make it in CA, and now that I'm in The Thousand Islands, no one in northern New York knows how to make it. It's not a buttercream. It's called a mock whip, and it's very fragrant, not ickky sweet, soft and fluffy. When I'm setting up a wedding cake at Best Western, the front lobby folks can smell them from the Banquet Room. Before I know it, their GM is running down to take any frosting left, from setting up the cake, to take home. She even washes out my mixing bowl in the kitchen for me. When I came here, I only baked as a hobby. Every place I took a cake, or wedding cake, (restaurant, resort, army base, etd.) would call me in a few days and say they were going to refer all their clients to me exclusively for cakes. I developed an over night business that required hiring 5 employees, to keep up with. I did have my dream come true when I graduated from the local Culinary College, at the age of 40, and have taught some of their classes. My website is www.BestCakes.biz if you'd like to learn more about cake flavors, fillings, and frostings.

I sprayed the pan with Pam, melted 1T butter and mixed that with the left over bread crumbs and poured it over the chicken. It certainly was tender. Will I make it again? Probably not, although I am glad to have tried it.

What a great chicken dish, hubby and I loved it. Like most of the others, I cut the butter in half, and will use even less next time. I used seasoned bread crumbs instead of the crackers, and cooked it almost an hour. Will certainly make it again! We liked the leftovers the next day for lunch. A keeper!

Outstanding recipe.  I made the following changes: I used less than one half the butter and decided to use Progresso Italian Bread Crumbs.
Since I was using flavored breadcrumbs I didn't use additional spices.  However, I used Locatelli Cheese which is a type of Romano/Parmesan Cheese. Also, I didn't cut the Chicken Breasts.  Baked at 350 for 1 hour.  Excellent taste, flavor, easy to prepare.  I definitely would make this recipe again and I might even try the Ritz Crackers next time. 

Another thought, you could add Provolone Cheese on top of the Chicken when it's almost done add a little Marina Sauce and you have Chicken Parmesan with a side of Angle Hair Pasta, Antipasto Salad, nice Red Wine.  Great Gourmet Dinner!

Easy and versatile, I didn't have parmesan, so used shredded romano, and used only one tablespoon of tarragon and a dash of sage, have made this two or three times and changed it a bit each time, it is always wonderful.  I also have used pam in the pan to cut down on the amount of butter used. For those of us who should be counting calories.
Yum yum yum yum yum.  Yum.

I made this without the butter and used no-fat sour cream. This probably reduced the yumminess factor, but the chicken was very moist and delicious. I used my own bread crumbs, and added cayenne, garlic salt, and pepper to the sour cream. It was not as crispy as it would have been with the butter, but overall. Very tasty.

We absolutely LOVED this recipe!!  I added 1 tablespoon of lemon juice to the yogurt and marinated the chicken strips overnight. Also, I used 1/2 cup of butter instead of 1 cup (as per the suggestions from the others).  Since I didn't have enough parmesan cheese on hand, I added some romano cheese. I used fresh tarragon from my herb garden. Can't wait to make this for friends.  Thank you, Steve, for a wonderful recipe.

I used frozen chicken breast in a bag type and left them whole.  Had 10-11 pieces though, and I cleaned out the cupboard of all the left over crackers, Ritz, Chicken in a Biscuit, Town House and a few saltines, and used garlic powder.  Sprayed pan with Pam and used half the butter.  Was good meal but not to die for.  Will it become a staple, probably not but I will make it again as we all did  enjoy it!
It was good, but it wasn't what I expected.  For all the calories and high fat content I thought there would be more flavor.  I will not probably not try this one again.

I'm sorry to say that I didn't like this recipe.  Sorry, Steven.  I followed the recipe exactly and it came out bland and greasy.  The chicken was moist but you can achieve moist chicken in many other ways that taste better and are a lot healthier for you.  This isn't one I'll be making again.
This is a great recipe! With the fall fast approaching I will be making it even more. Thanks for sharing. Gail(Maureen)

Can't add anything more than what has already been said.  This dish is fabulous!!  Instead of breading each individual piece of chicken, I arranged the chicken in the baking dish and then simply sprinkled the cracker crumbs completely over the top.  I then drizzeled the butter over the cracker crumbs.  Why?  I'm lazy.

This is the ABSOLUTE BEST chicken recipe I have!! I make this recipe about once a week, and the entire family loves it!!!  I have brought this dish to several gatherings and everyone has demanded the recipe!! Easy to make, I reduced the amount of butter by half and it is just as tasty.

This is a great recipe.  I followed your instructions exactly except I cut the butter in half.  It worked out perfectly for us.  I used the tarregon instread of the oregano.   I will make this dish again.  Thanks.
The recipe was easy tasteful and a keeper.  The ritz and sourcream tasted great and next time I will try it with less butter to see if it tastes the same
I used 1/2c butter instead of 1c, however...I just didn't care for the flavor of the chicken.  Too bland. Needs more seasoning IMO.
EXCELLENT!  I modified slightly with less butter and low-fat sour cream also, less Ritz.  Also tried with saltines which was delicious.  Thanks!

I'm sorry this took two years for me to write. I thought I wrote a review for it!
I looooooooooooooooooooove this recipe. It's one of my family's all time favorites.
I always make it with Chicken In A Biscuit crackers, I like the taste much better then with Ritz. I usualy serve it with peas and mashed potatoes or roast some veggies covered in thyme butter. Yum! Heck think I'll make this next week!
Excellent recipe.  Made it for supper today. Thanks for sharing.
Great comfort food, simple & tasty.

Wow! This recipe had so many reviews, I had to see what all the fuss was about. Oh my! Now I know. Recipe was made as directed (using marjoram). The chicken came out so moist and tender and flavorful, it was incredible. It's very rich, though, so you can't eat much of it without getting that "ugh" feeling. Or maybe I just ate too much?  :)  Excellent chicken; I'm sure I'll be getting requests from "the boys" for this one often.

Ok...I read ALL the reviews...here's what I did: I used 6 chicken tenderloins, didn't scrape off any sour cream when I dredged them, my crumb mixture was: 1 1/2 sleeves of ritz crackers,1/2 cup parm,1 tsp tarragon,three pinches of white pepper. I melted 1 stick of margarine, used about 4 tbls on the bottom of the dish, then the dredged chick, sprinkled the rest of the bread crumbs on top, followed by almost all of the rest of the melted butter,( I used the leftover melted butter for my green beans, no potato, so I wasn't "over saturated fatting us"...you don't miss it with the bread crumb mixture!)... then spinkled garlic powder over that, baked for 50 mins...OH MY GOD!!! this was simply awesome!! Who knew that chicken could cut like butter???? The flavor was just perfect!!!..my kids (11 & 16yrs) want to know why there isn't more??? gotta go, makin' another batch and printing this out for all my friends to try!!!
This was ok - dh liked it but 11 yr old thought it tasted "sour" - it could have been from the plain yogurt though...

Absolutely delish!  After I served this, I heard something I've never heard before:  "When's leftover night?"  This dish is so rich that half of it served my family of 4 big-eating adults.  A note: I used only 2 rolls of crackers and there was plenty.  I also decreased the butter to 3/4 cup.

I did not make the recipe as it was posted due to the reviews so it's hard to rate it correctly. I payed attention to the reviews and make adjustments accordingly and it came out really really good. My DH didn't even use ketchup or hot sauce like he does on everything because he said he didn't want to ruin the flavor. I read complaints about the fat content, so I marinated it in fatfree yogurt instead of sourcream, and I greased the pan with a little bit of oil instead of all that butter, then I only drizzled about 1/4 cup butter over the chicken instead of 1/2. I also read reviews that the crackers were too sweet, so I used half Ritz crackers, half bread crumbs. As for the spices, I replaced the 2 TBS terragon with Garlic Salt and Italian Seasoning/ Oregano, salt/pepper, and a touch of Cayenne pepper. I think we should use the herbs we like here. It Was Really Great. Thank you Steven for the recipe and thank you everyone for the reviews.  This is how you perfect a recipe for yourself!

Read all the reviews, used part Ritz, part saltines, and left them a bit chunky.  Used half the total butter, dredged individual strips that I had marinated in fat free yogurt- no sour cream here. Hate tarragon, used combo of garlic, herbes de provence, salt and pepper, cooked a bit longer.  Good, still very rich, even with the changes.  DH loved it.  I thought it was good, but falls short of great for me.  Was fast and super easy though.  I would make it again, with more garlic next time.

Sorry but Ritz crackers aren't available here in The Netherlands so " 1 Box Ritz crackers, 3 roll size " was a pretty useless measurement for me and I had to completely and totally guess the quantity of breadcrumbs. (I used approx 1.5 cups in the end)I read all the reviews, used 125g butter in total, halved the tarragon and upped the cooking time so that it became crispy and asked the 6 people at dinner to rate it... generally it was liked becuase indeed it wasn't dry and was tasty, but they agreed that it lacked the total "wow" we expected to get given the title of the recipe...  therefore I would have given it 3 stars, but DH who isn't a huge fan of chicken actually asked for it to go into my cookbook and for me to make it again, and that alone was worth the increase in rating to 4 stars.
Summary: nice enough,easy to make, would make again, everyone liked it but it wasn't nearly exceptional enough to rate a "5". Thanks for sharing it Steven :)

Totally TDF!  Couldn't believe I didn't rate this as I've been cooking this for a few years now.  It's a family favorite around here and my relatives often ask that I bring to potlucks & parties.  Yummy yummy yummy!

This recipe is definately a favorite of mine! This time I made it I didn't realize I was out of Tarragon & Marjoram until I was in the process of seasoning. So I used Mrs. Dash seasoning and a little bit more parmesan cheese instead. It turned out pretty good anyway. Great recipe for church dinner. Thanks for sharing!

Steve-  As the recipe stands my family would give your famous chicken 3 stars.  They felt it was too buttery so we would cut it back to 1/2 cup and half of the cracker crumbs.  We liked the flavor a lot but there was just too much butter floating in the dish.  They do want me to try it again making the adjustments though.  Thanks for the recipe. Paddles

This is definately to "die for".  It even tastes good the day after...cold!  I ate the leftovers for breakfast because I woke up craving them!  Cut back on the butter, and used different spices, but OMG it was good!

Followed recipe to a "T" - was awesome!!! Hubby told me rate it 6 STARS. Used Sour Cream, Chicken in a Biscuit & Marjoram, and would not change a thing about it.  Regarding butter, I didn't notice any greasiness or such. Was really a perfect recipe & weeknight meal. Easy & tasty. Thanks for posting!

This dish was excellent!  I will absolutely make this again.  I only used 2 rolls of crackers and I still had a bunch left over.  I just sprinkled the remainder over the top.  Also, I forgot the tarragon or marjoram, but I don't think it mattered much!
Very good. A little on the rich tasting side for me. But my family loved it, so I am giving it a higher star rating than I would just for myself. Thanks for the recipe!
I tried this out on a table full of guests and it was wonderful.  I doubled all the ingredients except the butter and only used 1/2 cup total butter.  Very impressive recipe with little effort!

This is OK.  It lacked flavor, unless you consider "fat" as a flavor.  It was a tad boring, I thought.  My husband liked it better than I did.  I followed other's advice and cut down the butter to 1/4 total and I can NOT imagine having more.  If you have picky eaters, this is a good choice.

This was very good!!  I used 1/2 cup of butter, Chicken in a bisquit crackers, marjoram, garlic
and plain yogurt.  Everyone loved this.  I will make again and perhaps season the chicken just a bit more. Thanks for posting!!!!

I haven't tried this exact recipe, but I make something close to it. In the sour cream you need to add worcestershire sauce, enough to turn it a beige color, maybe 2 tble. spoons, and some lemon juice, about 1 tbl. You will first dip breast into butter, coating well, then dip it into sour cream mixture, then roll in ritz crumbs or bread crumbs, pour remaining butter over each breast, it shouldn't be much.
No need for the parmesan cheese nor the tarragon. 
The breast are so moist. I have found that the frozen boneless skinless breast are the most tender.
yummy & easy.  this stayed nice and moist.  kids loved i-i too used only 1/2 cup butter total and it was good. thanks for the yummy recipe.

I didn't really care for this recipe I thought the Chicken was a little bland, I tried it again this time I use a mixture of sea salt and a very little course sugar and it was better, Maybe I'll try it with Chicken in a biscuit next time.

We loved this chicken....wow!!
