I made one addition and added some garlic to the crumbs and boy, was it ever a big hit.
I'll be making this one again!
Thanks for posting!

Maybe not 'to die for', but very tasty. I used 1 cup crushed chicken-in-a-biscuit crackers mixed with 1 cup Italian breadcrumbs for the breading. I wasn't entirely sure if this recipe was calling for fresh or dried herbs and I noticed that some people said the flavor was too strong so I went with 2 tablespoons of fresh chopped marjoram (thinking they used dried and it came out stronger). I did cut the butter down to 1/2 cup and it was still too much. It kept the breading a little soggy. At any rate, it was easy; the chicken was moist and tender and the overall flavor was good. Thanks.
â€” Update -
Tried this again with ritz and tarragon instead of chicken-in-a-biscuit and marjoram and added 1 1/2 tsp garlic salt, 1/2 tsp each cayenne pepper and thyme to the mix as well. Definately liked the marjoram better, no real preference on the crackers. I used turkey this time which worked fine and cut the butter down to 2 tbsp which made it still soggy on the bottom, but crisper on top.
Loved the tarragon flavor! I followed the advise of some reviewers and sprayed my pan with cooking spray and cut the amount of butter in half.

This is outstanding! Don't leave the parmesan out - it gives it quite a flavor. I made this for the first time and everyone LOVED it. This is definitely a keeper. It is to die for - you become addicted to the flavor and want more and more.

DH and I had this for dinner tonight. Nice! We have a similar recipe that calls for Dijon mustard mixed in with the sour cream. Next time, I'll add some cayenne or mustard to spice it up a bit. All in all, though, this is a keeper. Thanks for sharing.
We didn't care for the flavoring of the Ritz crackers and the tarragon.  The chicken was very moist though.

I made this last night for dinner and boy is it good.  I doubled the recipe and used marjoram instead of the tarragon.( I was out)  We really liked this recipe.  I agree with the other reviewers about it being rich, but if only made in moderation....lol.  I will definately make this again, so simple yet so good.  Thank you.....Stephanie

My whole family loved this recipe and I have made it several times. The chicken turns our super moist and I love the flavor of the Chicken in A Biscuit crackers! My only complaint is that the bottom of the chicken turns out soggy. I have altered the amount of butter and with only 4 tbs. it tastes the same but less soggy. So I melt 4 tbs. and drizzle it over the top of the chicken before baking it. I don't put any butter into the bottom of the dish- this helps keep the coating crunchy!

We really liked this recipe.  Since we are on a lower calorie diet, we substituted the regular sour cream for low fat sour cream and sweet butter for "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" and since we did not have tarragon or marjoram we used paprika.  Even with these substitutions, it was really delicious.  We will be making this many times to come.

I finally got around to making this dish.  I loved it, as written. Baked it a wee bit more for crispness and subbed "Smart Balance" for the butter. 
I like a mild dish and this fit the bill. Tarragon is a must.

I'm sorry to say that for my family this was not to die for.  I used the chicken in a biscuit crackers and cut down the amount of butter just to keep the bottom from being mushy and it was just bland.  Of course we have probably had our taste buds burned off by all the hot sauce we eat.  Will not try again.  T

My husband & I loved this recipe! I used plain yoghurt and wholemeal salada biscuits as i didn't have the other crackers. Also used mixed dried italian herbs and for a split second I thought i was eating a healthier version of KFC. This inspired me to search the KFC 'secret spices', and next time I make this I will substitute the cheese & herbs with the KFC secret spices!
Good. I added garlic. Served with rice and steamed broccoli. Thanks.

You have to give 5 stars to a recipe that you really go astray on and it still is super!  I thought I had gotten chicken out, instead I had thick pork chops.  Being short on time I thought, heck with it.  This should work on those too.  It did and it was darn good.  Juicy!!  I just pasted on the sour cream let em sit for an hour.  I used Ritz crackers the vegetable kind.  Did them in the oven for about the same amount of time turning them half way through.  Turned out great.  The coating was not real real crispy but browned nicely.  Thanks Steven, add pork chops to die for!

Just used 2 tbsp of butter and mixed cheddar cheese with parmesan.Put the chicken in a dish added the yoghurt and then tipped in the rest of the ingredients-it came out fab the top was crunchy and the sauce was lovely.
I made this yesterday and the name is right on.I used only 1/2 cup butter.

The whole family loved this juicy & tender dish!  I let 3 lbs. of chicken tenderloins & sour cream marinate in a ziploc bag for an hour.  I only had 2 rolls of the Ritz crackers...I crushed those & added some Italian seasoned bread crumbs & grilled chicken seasoning.  I didn't have Parmesan cheese, so I used mozzarella.  To cut down on prep time, I layered the bottom with 1/2 cup of butter and a few crumbs.  I then layed the chicken on top of that, followed by the mozzarella, bread crumbs & butter.  I cooked this for 45 minutes and it came out perfect!

the meat was really nice and the taste was OK on the top, although I would add some salt - but there was way too much butter and it made the cracker really soggy on the bottom of the chicken. so next time I will try to reduce the sour cream and be very careful with the amount of butter I use...
I have made this dish twice now. I let the chicken marinate overnight in the sour cream. I also added just a little bit of seasoning to the Ritz crackers. All in all, excellent
HIGH fat content. Tender but the fat content was out of control-mild flavored but good

I'm not leaving stars since I switched it up a bit, using only enough butter to coat the bottom of the pan. This recipe was VERY tasty, giving the chicken a nice tang. Also, didn't marinate the chicken (no time), but plan on doing so next time. Yum, yum!

I switched this around a little bit to use what I had on hand.  I took some individually frozen chicken breasts and cut them into strips, cooked them on the stove top until almost done.  Then I added the leftover ranch dip we had (ranch salad dressing and sour cream) and poured it on top, combined some crushed Townhouse crackers with some parsley and parm cheese and 3 Tbs melted butter.  I stuck the whole thing in the oven for 10 minutes, then broiled it for about 4 minutes to really crisp up the crackers.  
This was fantastic- I ended up making the recipe the way it is written  about a week later, and Dh preferred the ranch flavor, so I will be doing that from now on.  Thanks so much for posting!
i made this dinner for some friends everyone loved it even my honey

I read all the reviews before attempting this dish. I added tobasco sauce to the sour cream, marinated it for two hours, sprinkled it with garlic salt before rolling in Ritz and I used the roasted vegetable flavor Ritz. Also, I cut the amount of butter in half and it was plenty. 
That said, this recipe was rated a "keeper" by DH, my 9 year old DD said it was great(and she came back and ate it cold for snack) my 8 year old Ds said it was good, and my 7 year old DD said she didn't like the taste. I thought it was good but next time I will spice it up a bit more and maybe try the Chicken in a biscuit crackers.
All in all, we will be making this recipe again.

Excellent!  I cut the butter to about 4 TBS and used 4 large chicken breasts sliced into strips.  used reduced fat parm. cheese and FF sour cream.  I also substituted 2 TBS Italian seasoning for the tarragon.  We really enjoyed it with green beans and potato rolls.  Thanks!
Good.

I give this recipe ten stars for taste and maybe 3 for texture of breading. The chicken was amazingly tender and moist ( I used tenders which always dry out) but the underside of the breading was soggy. I halved the butter and even though I drained the pan twice, there was still to much. Take my advice, grease your pan well and use maybe a 1/2 of stick total butter. I don't favor the spices used so I left those out and in place added a teaspoon of garlic powder to my crumbs along with a good dose of pepper. I will definitely make this again with less butter, Thanks!

We loved this recipe!  I adjusted a few things.  I halved the butter, used bread crumbs instead of Ritz, used garlic powder for seasoning and used cream of mushroom soup with chili powder mixed in instead of sour cream.  So I guess I kind of made it my own recipe, but it was based on this one.  My husband loved it and I will definitely be making it again.
Huge hit with my family.  Even my 2-year-old loved it!!!!!

Made this for the family I worked for and they requested it again tonight!!  It's super easy. They didn't have sour cream or yogurt so I used ranch dressing instead w/ a lil garlic powder added and it was SO GOOD!! Used breadcrumbs for the coating and served w/ steamed veg and alfredo noodles - delish! Thanks for sharing!

This was really good.  However, I did cut the butter down like everyone suggested.  I also felt like it was lacking a bit of kick.  I used thyme, paprika, garlic, freshly ground black pepper flakes and salt insted of tarragon, because I was out.  I also used bread crumbs, since I didn't have any ritz on hand.  I think next time I will use the ritz cracker.  I bet the buttery taste helps kick it up.  I will also use the tarragon next time I make it.  It turned out pretty good though.

This was good although the fat content is rather scary.  I tried to cut down on some of the fat content.  I only used 1/4 cup of butter, 1/8 for the bottom and 1/8  for the top and think that if I ever made this again I would forgo it completely as it isn't necessary to the dish.  I also used low fat sour cream.  I added garlic powder, pepper and onion powder to the ritz cracker mix as well as I thought it may be bland otherwise.  As I said, I would make this again with even more modifications and perhaps try with a thicker yogurt next time.  It is a promising base that makes the chicken super moist.  Thanks for posting.

This is a great quick & easy recipe! I didn't have time to marinate as long as suggested and used less crackers and butter than it called for, but everything still turned out perfectly moist and flavorful.

Prepared 2 large breasts, sliced in half length-wise.  Marinated in sour cream for about 2 hours, then  dredged in plain breadcrumbs with some Panko, parmesan, garlic powder, onion flakes and tarragon (as suggested by other reviewers).  I did not melt butter in the bottom of the casserole -- just sprayed heavily with Pam Butter, and topped with 2 TBSP melted butter. This was tender, flavorful, and moist.  Thanks, Steve , for posting a tasty chicken dish !

Oh, this was definitely worth it!  I used chicken thighs, as that was what we had on hand.  I also added poultry seasoning, salt and pepper to the tarragon.  I also used only about half of a stick of butter.  It was moist and delicious but not soggy.
very good

This was good and very moist, but the chicken needed seasoning like onion powder or something.  Next time I'll season the chicken before marinating.  I'll also add a can of fried onion rings to the cracker crumbs.  Also, I had a ton of cracker crumbs left over, so I'll only use 2 tubes.  I reduced the butter to only 2 tb and drizzled it over the top of the crumbs and I used low fat sour cream.  Thanks!
Well, we REALLY enjoyed this chicken.  It was moist and yummy.  We had leftovers which were great cold in a salad.  Will add this to my dinner rotation.  Thanks for a great recipe!

My DH loved this recipe and told me I could make it for him "anytime".  I used a mix of breast and thigh, since he likes only dark meat.  I cut back on the crackers and the butter, but I think I could cut back on the butter even more.  I used marjoram for the seasoning, but I think I would prefer oregano and maybe some garlic or onion powder.  I certainly will make this again.  My husband thinks the recipe should be a six- or seven-star!  Thanks for a great recipe!

This was good, but just had too much of a sweet flavor to me. It was very crunchy, but I cringed using all that butter, so if I make it again I will cut back on the butter and maybe not use sweet butter, or add some garlic or ranch seasonoing to the crackers instead.  Overall a good recipe, but we will tweek it to our tastes. Thanks!

This was just ok for us.  I was expecting/hoping for a WOW.  It was good, but not great.  Made as directed.  It's always fun to try new recipes even if they don't work out for me, so thanks for sharing.
A++! We used whole chicken breasts and it was fantastic. Tasted so great. It's a keeper!

I would give this a 10 if I could.  I had to improvise a bit.  I only had 1 package wheat ritz and 1 package of saltines.  I crushed them all together and used oregano in place of the tarragon.   I did the rest the same.  My husband came very close to giving this a 10 - which he very, very rarely does!  Thanks for the keeper!

I made this dish for the first time and it was fabulous!! I used whole wheat crackers, low fat sour cream. and used the whole chicken breast instead of cutting it into strips. Very, Very moist chicken!! I made extra and heated it up the next day and it was still very most and alot of flavor. My teenage son and his friend couldn't get enough of it and didn't believe the coating was Ritz crackers! A definite KEEPER!!

Very tasty, and easy. The chicken pieces were moist, the coating was flavorful, with the tarragon giving a unique exotic touch. The one cup of butter almost made me pass this by, but I'm glad I didn't - DH & DS make this a keeper. As another reviewer suggested, I only used 2T butter, nonfat s. cream, & whole wheat Ritz - these worked out great. One thing - I used less than half of the crumb mixture & of course had to toss it since it had come in contact with raw meat. One and a half rolls (5-6 oz.) would have been plenty. But then you may want to reduce the parm. cheese & tarragon to reflect this change.

great recipe!  i read the reviews and here's what i did decided to do differently:  i cut the chicken into thin strips, i used the chicken in a biscuit crackers that i highly seasoned with pepper, garlic powder, chicken boullion granules, cayenne and tarragon, instead of using 1/2 the butter on the bottom of the dish i just sprayed with pam, i did use the 1/2 cup of melted butter to pour on the cracker crust, but i think next time i might use the whole cup of butter on top (terrible, i know)!!  i did need to broil a few minutes to brown up the crust.  i think next time i will spread the strips out on 2 baking sheets instead of have everything all crammed in a casserole dish, i think it made it a little soggy.  however, everyone loved this dish.  even the leftovers were delish reheated in the oven the next day!  i really loved the flavors of the cracker and tarragon crust with the sour cream.  thanks steven!!

I am re-rating! This can be modified in so many ways--sometimes I use wheat thins, chicken-in-biskit, or whatever crackers I have on hand.  I do recommend still cutting back on the butter.  Choose your own favorite herbs to add, or go with a more flavored cracker.

We loved it made just the way it was posted.  I wouldn't change a thing in this recipe!  We had it with baked potatoes and coleslaw for a very enjoyable meal!  I love the rich buttery taste from the Ritz crackers and the cheese adds so much flavor.  This is a winner!
Wow, this was awesome! I'm pleasantly surprised!
Awesome chicken!
Delicious!  The chicken was so moist and flavorful!  Thanks
Its ok. I used italian bread crumbs. Sprayed the bottom of the pan with Pam. It's not one of my favorites.

Loved this, although I did make it following MizzNezz's suggestions: reduce butter to 1/2 cup, reduce tarragon to 1 T, reduce crackers to 1 1/2 sleeves, add 1 t salt, 1/2 t pepper, 1/2 t cayenne pepper, 1/2 t thyme.  This is very moist chicken & flavorful.

I doubled the recipe to feed my guests and then followed Mizz Nezz's reductions and doubled them.  I used tarragon instead of marjoram and I have to tell you it was a hit all over the place!!  My company raved about it all through dinner.  Served with Garlic Whipped Mashed Potatoes and Corn in Butter Sauce it was MMmm Good!

Steven~Fantastic recipe the chicken came out beautifully crunchy on the outside and so moist inside
thankyou for posting this great recipe

I used light sour cream, a different combo of spices (smoked paprika, thyme, salt, & pepper), and only about 1/2 cup butter. It still came out a little greasy - I think you could cut back the butter even more. I'm a veggie so I didn't try it myself, but the BF thought it was great, even better when he added some more fresh-ground pepper. Hint for easy dredging: Crush the Ritz crackers, spices, and parmesan in a ZIploc bag, then just throw the chicken in there and shake the bag, two or three pieces at a time. Less mess!

Really disappointed with this recipe- hoped it would be better. Only used half the butter- but still very greasy & heavy. Chicken wasn't even crispy after 45 minutes. But the flavor was good albeit soggy. Sorry.

WOW>>>WOW>>>WOW! Thanks so much for posting this! It is incredible. One reviewer said this was bad???? NO way Iv'e eaten and made chicken a million was and this is now my all time favorite! I will make this forever! thank you SOOOOOOOOO much for a keeper!

I read the other comments after I made and ate this. I used the Chicken in a Biscuit crackers and made it as written except I knew that 2 tablespoons of Taragon was too much for my tastes and eyeballed what I put in. We all agreed that this recipe is a keeper with minor adjustments. Next cut the butter to 4 tablespoons or so and just pour on the top. For the bottom of the pan I will use PAM. I intend to keep tinkering with this recipe until I get it right to our liking. The taste was fantastasic and the chicken was so moist.
6/8/10 I remade this recipe last night.  I made the changes above.  I think I am going to cut the butter all together next time.

I found this recipe on this site years ago and make it for company and special occasions. It always receives raves, and although it does contain a good amount of butter, I have always prepared it without modifying it in any way, usually using Marjoram. I believe the crackers add to the distnict flavor of this recipe and the fact that it isn't crispy doesn't matter, it's delcious as well as very easy to prepare.

World famous, to die for?  C,mon Steven, this recipe was tasty, but not all that.  Too many reviewers modified by spraying the bottom of the pan and slightly drizzling the chicken with butter.  I did too, and am glad it was suggested.  On the plus side, this is easy to make, the chicken turns out tender and probably most cooks have all ingredients on hand.  I am looking forward to trying some of Steven's other recipes--they sound interesting.
I didn't have time to marinate the chicken for an hour so I dipped it in the sour cream and laid it in the bowl with the broken crackers & butter on top. Came out delicious!
I made this using bread crumbs and basil sooooooo good! I added some seasonings though to both the sour cream and crumbs mixture.

We really enjoyed this chicken dish. I did cut the amount of butter in half and used poultry seasoning ( not fans of taragon in the house). I knew going in that this was going to be a really rich dish. Since we generally eat healthy, a once in a while splurge is okay. To the reviewer who commented that this is a heart attack waiting to happen, if you are so concerned with it being unhealthy, why did you make it? My main gripe is the comment that "the only one who enjoyed it lives outside and eats out of a bowl" is really nasty. It does not make you cleaver, just snarky. Shame on you. This site does not need nasty!!!

Don't make this recipe if you're dieting or want a low-fat meal - it's definitely not THAT!  But, it was one of the best "not good for you" chicken recipes I've ever made.  I cut the butter in half, increased the cooking time to 50 minutes and turned the chicken over half way through to brown both sides.  My hubby went back for seconds.  I'm using the left overs for chicken taco's tonight - hate to waste them!

I had to post a review because this was so good.  I just made an account to do so.  My husband hates sour cream so I did not tell him what was in the recipe until after he raved about how good it was.  I just had random boxes of crackers in the cupboard that I mixed together.  I think next time I am going to use goldfish crackers.
These were really good...had such a delicious taste!  I will for sure make again!  I did only use 1 cube of butter and it was quite sufficient.
My family LOVED this! It was easy and delicious! Thanks for sharing

Yum!!! This chicken is terrific! I made it last night and got rave reviews from everybody. I served it with buttered noodles and fresh green beans. It will definately be a regular on my table. You know, when I see 5 star reviews and then a one star review, I wonder how this is possible. Maybe the one star reviewer left out a crucial ingredient? Like the chicken?

Ah yes! Great on bread and I use vlokken and hagelslag for baking too. Gestampte muizen is only for bread, at least, I have never found another use for it. 
Through the years here in The Netherlands I have become so brave that I nowadays eat it on an open sandwich. 
All these products should be available in every country! You don't know what you're missing!
Thanks for posting.
I grew up with "sprinkle" sandwiches. My children now love them too. They love their sandwich with peanut butter and milk chocolate hagekskaag.
yum - but i love my sprinkles on beschuit (Holland Rusk for the U.S. market) - makes a good anytime snack - it's not just for breakfast anymore :-)
Oh my gosh a sprinkle sandwich?!  It's like I died and went to heaven.  This was so odd to me, but really great... I used two slices of bread. maybe someday I'll "graduate" to one!

Yummy and so much fun! We watched a program about Netherlands last week and I was so amazed the traditional breakfast was chocolate sprinkles. Netherlands is now on our list of places to visit because of the show and this recipe. Little Miss (DD) would love to have chocolate sprinkles everyday. Thank you for posting the recipe kiwidutch - *Made for Zaar World Tour 4*

I must agree with Chef floWer, my Little Man is really ready to come for a visit now that he has tried this treat- and this is a typical breakfast?  YUMMY!!  I don't know if he could keep the smile off his face long enough to get the food into his mouth!!LOL...Great, easy tasty recipe - made for ZWT4.

I made this with my class for ZWT 4! We had just spent a week reading a story that takes place in Holland and this was a fun treat for them. They thought it sounded strange at first, but 22 out of 24 kids give it 2 thumbs up! (The other two were unsure what to make of it!)
Wow, this is sure a kid pleaser! Very simple to make, my daughter enjoyed this treat so much. Made for ZWT 4! :)

How fun!  I ate a slice of this with my 6yo this morning, and loved watching her eyes light up as she realized she was being given chocolate for breakfast! :)  I had some qualms at first, but then I realized that this was much better (nutritionally speaking) than donuts and some of the other stuff kids eat for breakfast.  And you can't beat the speed of this recipe! :) Made for ZWT4.

Tasty and a bit naughty which is always a fun combination.  I first had this a few years back when I was introduced to it by a Dutch friend and this as good as it was then.  I don't think it is any worse than a sugary Danish or a donut for breakfast if done in moderation.  Made for ZWT4.

We had some chocolate sprinkles left in the cabinet after making Brigadeiro for Girl Scout International Thinking so we gave this a spin. My dd was tickled by the recipe and acted as chef and taste tester. She buttered a piece of whole grain bread and sprinkled away. She declared it good and thought that a repeat performance for breakfast in the future will be in order. Thanks for posting this simple but fun recipe.   Made for my Babes for ZWT4.

I grew up eating this.  Sometime I would take it to school for lunch.  The kids teased me about it but after trying a bite they liked it also.  My daughter just loves this.  Every year I order Hagelslaag for her for a Christmas gift.  Looking forward to giving it to my grandson to learn to like it also.

It was always a good day when I had this! With relatives in the Netherlands, we'd never be short on hagelslaag. I'd have it both with untoasted and toasted bread. Untoasted was definitely my favourite. Nice soft bread with the chocolate bits in every bite.. MMM! Toasted on occasion was a nice treat as well since you end up with *melted* chocolate bits instead. Yummm! Darn, now I want more right now! Thanks! ;)
For an interesting taste twist, layer some thinly sliced Gouda cheese over the top of the hagel on buttered wheat bread.  Sounds strange, but the taste combination is outstanding.

I LOVE that you put this on here! I haven't had this in a long time but seeing it brings back many a fond memory. I'm half Dutch, so I like mine lightly toasted, and then you need to put on enough butter (yes, BUTTER lol) to soften it a little bit, and the hagleslaag stays in place when there's enough. You should do this quickly so the chocolate melts at least a little bit, and open-faced is the way to go. Thanks for bringing back memories!

Mmmm! Thank you, kiwidutch, for reminding me of this wonderful treat! Made this with nice, soft, white bread, lots of butter, and De Ruijter brand chocoladehagel melk (milk chocolate "hail"). Luckily, we have a Vietnamese grocery a few blocks from home, which stocks a lot of Dutch goods--like these lovely chocolate sprinkles. I used to enjoy this often, but somehow fell out of the habit; now, thanks to you, I've introduced my young son to it. He seems to love it as much as I do...but honestly, what is not to love? Thanks for posting, kiwi! Made for Holiday Tag game.

Kiwidutch, what a fun breakfast, I loved it!  On a side note, I was feeling a little decadent about how many sprinkles I used until I looked at everyone else's pictures...now I don't feel bad at all :lol:  Edited to say that OF THE 350 RECIPES I REVIEWED IN 2008, THIS HAS GONE INTO MY TOP 20 FAVORITES COOKBOOK.
Wow! So simple, but super delicious!!!

I've made these b4 for my daughter's birthday party. I cut the bread with cookie cutters and used muli-color sprinkles on some, chocolate on others and colored sugar on others. I remember my mom loved them. I'll have to send her this. I've made them for afternoon snacks, tea parties, and midnight snacks but I've never thought about making them for breakfast, but why not? A very simple idea that is cheap, easy and will hit the spot with good home made bread. Thanks for posting, the family is getting these for breakfast 2morrow :)
I felt very Dutch as I ate breakfast this morning! LOL I used softened butter and Tijgervlokken (milk chocolate and vanilla shards), which had been sent to me from the Netherlands ;) Thanks KD :D
Excellent choice to make for my party!
These are wonderful and the smell in the kitchen was awesome.  Couldn't wait for them to cool down.  I will definitely be making more of these.

Absolutely delicious, made these today to include on our nibbles table for Christmas. 
And the smell while in the oven was divine.
awesome recipe, easy to make.  I couldnt stop eating.---Yum

WOW!  These are so easy and soooo tasty!  I made them for my sister's bridal shower, and I'm fighting the hands off--hoping there'll still be some left for the party!!  The cayenne pepper is very subtle, and a little sneaky (you don't feel it until after a few nuts).  I would recommend baking them on parchment paper, because I did have a little trouble getting them off the cookie sheet after cooling, but maybe I didn't grease the pan well enough.  Thanks for a super recipe Lennie!  I am planning to make lots of these for gifts this year.
Made these this morning and they were great.  The flavor really has a kick and yet they were sweet.  Loved them.
Delicious and a hit with the hubby!!

Made these last night for Christmas gifts and they are totally awesome. I cooked them a little longer than suggested and used the new Reynolds non stick aluminum foil and it worked pretty well. Nice crunch and flavor....will definitely make many times!!

This made a great addition to the Christmas cookie trays this year.  It was sooo easy and quick to make.  I used all pecans.  The nuts were so flavorful.  No one noticed the "kick" to the nuts until they were on the next mouthful.  ;)  Everyone loved them!  For the people that don't like spicy or hot foods I omitted the cayenne and the results were just as good.  I ended up making 4 batches.  Word of warning... I forgot to butter the pan once and had a heck of a time trying to get the nuts off of the aluminum foil.  Thank you for sharing!!this recipe!
Just a note to everyone: if you spray your baking sheet well with nonstick spray like Pam, you won't have any "sticky" problems!

So wonderful. I have made 2 batches so far this week with requests to make more for New Years. Wonderful sweet-spice flavor and a delayed little "gottcha" with the cayenne. Thanks Lennie, from the Daniel family.
Made these last night.  The smell in the kitchen was sooooooooo good!  I'm not sure which I like better, the smell or the taste!  They are wonderful!!!!!
Excellent - sweet, yet spicy. Really, Really good!

These nuts are really special!  They were so easy to make, but the kick from the cayenne was on the cutting edge.  It is a surprise to be eating about 3 nuts and then the cayenne kicks in.  Truly a wonderful treat.  Thanks for sharing this recipe. 
:-)

I made this for my sister's surprise party and they were a HUGE hit! To my chagrin, I realized I didn't have cayenne half way through the recipe- so I crunched up some red pepper flakes and paprika in the old morter and it worked like a charm! If you have the good fortune of owning a silpat, I recommend lining your cookie sheet with it for this recipe to avoid serious stickiness. Thanks Lennie, everyone was asking me where I bought these nuts (hee hee).
Can't wait to serve these again at the holidays.
I just took these out of the oven, and have sampled a couple.  The "bite" does sneak up on you!  I used parchment paper and cooked them for about 15 minutes at 325.  They are perfect!!!

These are so addictive. They're very simple to make and taste wonderful! I used parchment paper and had no problems with sticking. They were a huge hit!! This recipe's a keeper, thanks so much for posting it Lennie.

I tripled this recipe because I knew that it was going to be tasty from these reviews!!  I will probably add just a "tad" more cayenne pepper next time.  Everyone's right, you don't taste the "bite" till the next mouthfull!!  I will be making these again, thanks!!

Very, very nice.  I made these for a dinner party and they were much enjoyed with drinks.  I think the cayenne could easily be upped to 3/4 tsp for a bit more heat - these were just mildly spicy.  Thank you.
Very nice and easy. Made it twice. Second time, I really kicked up the cayenne and added some cumin. The second batch was the favorite! I gave it away as a Christmas gift.

Quite tasty! I personally would prefer much more spice, but my guests loved them as written---2 batches disappeared quickly. I admit, I kept munching on them while they were cooling. You know, to get rid of the broken nuts;) I used parchment paper so clean-up was a breeze. Thanks for posting!
I had these out pre T-Day dinner. They were well liked and so easy to make. I will make these again.
Good recipe.  I We really enjoyed these...they're addictive!
Thought these were outstanding! Was a little nervous about the cayenne, but boy, it really makes it! Can't wait to take these to our family Christmas party. Thanks a bunch!

These nuts are really great!  I have to admit that I was a little afraid of the cayenne pepper so only used 1/4 tsp.  They were not spicy at all though so next time I will use the full amount.  I also used all pecans because that's what I had in, but I'm sure it would be even better with the combo of nuts.  Thanks for a great recipe.  I posted a picture too.

Just wanted you to know that these nuts were the best.  I have given this recipe to numerous people.  They all loved it.   I did decrease the cayenne pepper to 1/4 tsp. and added a little bit more of the nuts than was called for.   LindaJim

I rated these a while ago but only gave 4 stars...heaven knows why they are fab!! I've made these over and over again to rave reviews. So decided to place a new review giving it the 5 stars it deserves.Make sure you place them on parchment paper though as it makes for an easy clean up.
These nuts are delicious!  They were a huge hit at the party I attended last night.  The spice mix was perfect.  Thanks!
Great recipe! Seems like we like it hot, since I would double the cayenne, and the salt as well, next time.
These are terrific!  Just perfect for the holidays.  I followed the recipe to the t.  It is a great balance of spice and sweet.  Thank you.

Yummy! I really enjoyed making (and eating) this wonderful treat. The recipe was great and needed no special tweaks on our part. I'm planning to make several batches of these as a snack to set out during our homemade rehearsal dinner - I think the guests will really enjoy them as much as we did. Thanks so much!

Holy addiction, Batman !!  We can't put these down !  They're fantastic.  I made just a few changes:  I whipped up 2 eggs whites because we really like the crunch that they add to the nuts and I also doubled the cinnamon and cayenne and substituted peanuts for almonds, which I loathe.  I used regular salted nuts and they were perfect !
These were great! easy to make and quite the taste sensation... Thank you for posting it.

I was looking for something to make as a small Christmas gift. I found this..decided to try them...WOW!! They are not only quick and easy ..but absolutely delicious! I'll put them in a nice container and have a very nice gift! Thanks Lennie. Will be making these again...this time for me! I forgot to mention that I lined the baking sheet with parchment paper..worked wonderfully..NO CLEAN UP!
These were so good that they didn't even make it to their destination! I will definitely be making these again.

I've never made spiced nuts before and I thought they would be a good snack to bring to a holiday party. I'm so glad I chose this recipe! I did it exactly as written, and they were really easy. I was afraid they were going to be too spicy for a crowd, but everyone enjoyed them - even the most sensitive palates! Thank you for posting!
These are so yummy. My family loves these. I'll be making these often.

I made as written with all pecans. They are still a little hot from the oven, but man they taste good. Sweet at first, but then the heat kicks in by the 2nd or 3rd one. I cooked 21 minutes total- stirring at 8-16-21 minutes. I put foil on the pan and sprayed the foil, so clean up will be a breeze. I honestly believe that I could have used 3 cups of nuts and still had enough coverage from the listed ingredients.
Thanks!!

The taste was good, but I found that the temperature or baking time was just too high for the pecans and they turned a little too dark.  I switched to a similar recipe that called for a lower heat (225 for 45 min and then 275 for 15 min) and that worked much better for me.
Wonderful.  Enjoyed by children and adults.  Thanks for the recipe.
These were easy and tasty! I love the cayenne kick at the end. I used brown sugar instead of white, it was great
These didn't go over very well. They tasted ok but nothing special. Made as per the recipe.

I had an egg white that I wanted to use.This is the perfect recipe to use it in.I used 1/2 cup each of peanuts,walnuts,pecans and almonds.I never had cayenne so I used a little bit of chili powder.The hardest thing about this recipe is not eating them as they cool down!

So GOOD. But the yield is way off. I doubled the recipe. But ended up with about the amount of a single batch. Everything seemed fine when I took them out of the oven to cool, I left them cooling while I did other chores. When I returned, about half had "evaporated" (according to my husband and his buds - who were mysteriously milling about my Kitchen).
My recommendation either quadruple the recipe or wait till hubby's out of the house!
I used unsalted mixed nuts with very good results. Looking forward to making these over the winter holidays.

When making this recipe I used milk with 2% fat along with 1 1/2 cups of frozen berries as well as the rest of the indicated ingredients & had a very, very tasty smoothie! Another time I might leave out the honey, but other than that . . . Thanks for sharing this great recipe! [Made & reviewed in Zaar Cookbook recipe tag]

Yes, this is a very pretty shade of purple, and it's really tasty too!  I used regular 1% milk and followed the recipe exactly.  This made a nice breakfast smoothie for me and I will definitely be making this again.  Made for PRMR Tag Game.

Great smoothie (and I am not a fan of mixed berries!)!!  I had some strawberries, raspberries and blueberries from the summer in the freezer that I used along with 1% milk.  Mixed this in a regular blender and my 6yr DS and I had a cool, healthy afternoon snack!  Made for PRMR.
This was ok but for me, something was missing. I would also prefer more broccoli in the soup.

I don't eat cheese but I made this today for my fiance and he said it was pretty good, just couldn't taste very much cheese in it. I will make again but probably with a sharper cheese. Thanks for putting this recipe up :)

Woweee!!!! This was SO, SO, SO good!!!! I have been wanting a good recipe for this soup and my search is over! Sue, I never heard of steaming the broccoli first but it sure did preserve the BRIGHT green of the broccoli and made it look so much more appetizing than the gray-green color it fades to after extended cooking. I followed the recipe exactly except for the addition of about 1/4 c. of diced ham that I needed to use up. Next time I will double the recipe!

Yum! I Did not see a specification for the amount of celery, so I used 1/4 cup, finely chopped.  I also added some cubed ham when I added the broccoli.  Served it with a loaf of french bread.  Wonderful! [Editor's Note: recipe was edited as a result of this comment 12/17/02]

Ick!  We did not like this soup at all. I followed the directions exactly and did not have good results.   It did not have good flavor and it was not smooth like I had anticipated.  The soup was thick and pastey...not a big hit with my family. I will continue my search for the "perfect broccoli soup"recipe.

Wonderful! A top 10 for comfort food.This recipe is simple and easy to follow. I doubled it,added 2T of worcestershire(at the end)& used SHARP wisconsin cheddar and served the soup in crusty bread bowls...my kids ate it up!
A tasty soup that is quick easy and delicious. Followed the recipe exactly and it was just right!! Thanks so much for posting.

I made this soup for dinner on Valentines day along with Crab legs. This was sooooo good.  I had a hard time finding a Broccoli and Cheese soup that didn't have processed cheese in it.  I was so glad to find this one. It was fast, easy to make and everyone liked it!  I put the steamed broccoli in the food proccessor before putting it in the soup because I wanted a fairly smooth soup. I didn't have white pepper, so just put in a dash of regular pepper in it. It turned out great!
This recipe was very east to put together. I really didn't measure the ingredients, I just eye balled everything, leaning toward the heavy side. We really liked it and will make it again.
This recipe results in yummy, creamy goodness. I added sharp cheddar and swiss cheese to it. Didn't have any celery but it was still perfect.
This soup was o.k. I've tasted better (usually without cheese). But it was a nice change. I did not cook the broccoli separately though. Why waste a pan for color? May use this recipe again.
Excellent soup and so easy and fast to make.  Served with grilled ham and cheese sandwiches.  Very good dinner.

This soup was really great... my daughter was very impressed that i made it and excited cause that means i can make it again and she won't have to beg me to buy it. it was easy and came out nice and creamy, not overly cheesy or too thick.. very nice. thanks
Really good!  Excellent taste and easy to put together with my leftover broccoli.  Thanks for a great recipe

This soup is really good.  I love broccoli cheese soup!  Too bad my DH hates broccoli! I think I used a little too much cheese this time (used some velveeta and some mild cheddar).  Oops! I always add rice as well (2 cups cooked rice).  All in all, it dirties a few pans, but it's worth it! Thanks!
We really liked this soup. One of my husbands favorites.
Wow this just hit the spot. I know I will be making this again.
This soup is really good. Nice thick and creamy with a rich cheddar flavor. Yummy! :) Thanks for the recipe.

I used the ingredients I had on hand, which meant substituting soy milk for milk and buckwheat flour for regular flour - then I tripled everything to use up my broccoli - and guess what, it still turned out delicious (although of course it looks brown instead of that lovely yellow in the picture (so I wouldn't make it this way for company).  Oh yes - I added worcestershire sauce to give it a little kick.  Very good - I'll no doubt make this again.  Thank you for posting.

This was the first time I ever made my own soup, and it worked out great. I followed the directions exactly, and I loved it. I had this with some nice garlic toast, and it was a nice meal for a cold day.
Wonderful! Wonderful! I'm glad I double this recipe and so is my family. Tasted just like I imagined.Great on the snowy night we had last night here in West Virginia.Thanks so much for sharing.
My first attempt at soup from scratch. Very easy and very good. I used shredded carrots instead of celery and added a clove of garlic when sauteing. Will definitely make this again.
This soup was really good!  I did add a small minced clove of garlic.  My 11yo son said, "make this again, Mom."  Even the baby liked it!  Thanks!

Just what I was looking for! I doubled the recipe, used turket stock from Thanksgiving, carrots instead of celery and frozen broccoli flowerets that I chopped fine. Yum-m-m! This is a great comfort soup and so flavorful. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

Very good soup. I used carrots instead of celery, and used water instead of chicken stock. I added a little salt and turmeric to make up for the missing stock (I was out). We'll definitely make this one again.

I've made this now about 5 times!  My friends and a couple coworkers that I share it with love it too.  

My adjustments are that I have to add the broth before I thicken because I use corn starch and I almost always leave celery out of my cooking.  Also, I used frozen broccoli and microwaved it.

Thanks!

I had a few issues with the soup. It didnt thicken up as much as I thought so I needed to add cornstarch/water mix to try to get it to thicken more. I really didnt find it  cheesy or brocc. flavour. If I ever made it again, I would use the water I pre boiled the brocc in instead of stock. It was edible and good, Just not WOW!

I just got finished making this soup.  I too had issues getting it to thicken however, I'm hoping it will thicken after a day of sitting.  Some changes that I made, as I doubled the recipe:  I used skim milk so I didnt use as much since it would thin down the soup.  I also threw in some shredded carrots for some color.  Instead of shredded cheese I added velveeta.  I used 16 oz of velveeta for the doubled recipe and it melted really easy and gave it a creamy cheese flavor.  I also used frozen broccoli and just microwaved it.  I used 6 cups frozen.  The soup has a wonderful flavor--I just need to figure out how to thicken it better.  I might try cornstarch next time.

Just how I like broccoli soup..... cheesey and thick, but not too thick.   The little bit of celery does a lot for the flavor.  I used extra onions and opted for the greater amount of cheese listed.  This is a keeper.  Thanx for sharing!

not only DELISHIUS but easy as well!
this was just what i was looking for! thanks!
Wonderful.  I added extra cheese and took a hint from the fan who added some ham that needed to be used.  I made crispy fried bacon to sprinkle on top.  Big hit at our house!

Very easy. I was looking for something to make that wouldn't require me to run to the store. This was perfect and fast. I think next time I might add a bit more seasoning but it was still very good. Thank you.

I think the reason I didn't like this was because I used too much broccoli and I don't think I cooked it right before adding it to the soup.  I will make it again using frozen broccoli and chop it up in my food processor as another reviewer suggested. The soup didn't thicken up too much, but it was an okay consistency for me.

DEEEEElicious!!!  I am very happy to find a recipe for this soup that doesn't require processed cheese and buying special items like whipping cream, and being able to use ingredients I have at home (milk, cheddar cheese, etc.).  It tastes wonderful, and I will definitely make this again (and again, and again!)  Thank you!

LOVE THIS! I got the broccoli in a microwavable steaming bag and that made it super easy. Taste great, easy to make and one of the best broccoli cheese soups I have ever had. That is quite an accomplishment because I am a a broccoli cheese soup addict! 5 stars. Give this one a shot!

This soup was absolutely wonderful!  We loved loved loved it!  I made a pot for 2 of us last weekend and we ate the whole thing for lunch.  I think I'll make some more this weekend, lol.  I followed the recipe exactly except that I pureed about half of it for a thicker consistency.  Yum!  Thanks for posting!

OMG! I know this is really kind of a fat bomb, but who cares when it tastes this good. My 7-year-old loved it and found out that by dipping her chicken into it, it made a whole new taste sensation. Gotta love that! I used the full 2 cups of cheese (we live in California, where the best cheese comes from!). I would not change this recipe at all.

This was great! I made it for lunch guests and served it with homemade crusty bread rolls and quiche and it went well! I only had colby cheese so that's what I used. I also added a cup of cooked chicken. Thanks heaps Sue!

WOW!  I just got done snarfing this down, and I ate way way too much.  This is a wonderful soup, altho I did make some minor changes based on what I was craving and what I had in the cabinets...  I was out of onion and celery, so I used onion powder and celery seed.  After the butter was melted I added shredded carrot and sauteed that with the flour.  I used frozen broccoli that I nuked for a couple minutes so I could chop it.  I also added 4 oz cream cheese before I added about 2 cups colby/jack.  I did cook this a bit longer to make sure the carrots were tender.  The 18 mo ate it as well.  Thank you for a fantastic recipe I'll be making again as soon as it gets chilly!

I thought that it was a little rich for me, but the rest of the family enjoyed the soup.  I did use a can of evaporated milk and topped the rest off with non fat milk and used a 6 year old aged cheddar for the cheese component.  Thanks for posting an extremely quick soup to make.

Just made this tonight, and it was a big hit in our little family!  I love broccoli & cheese soup, but even my "anti-trees" husband finished his bowl.  I reduced the milk and upped the stock, in order to cut a few calories and up the flavor.  I had leftover ham, so added that and floated sea salt croutons on top.  Mmmmm.  There's enough left for a couple of tasty lunches!

I altered this slightly to make it in the crock-pot.  I followed the first two steps of the recipe, then I put all the ingredients except the cheese in the crock-pot and added extra broth.  I let it cook for 4 or 5 hours on low.  I used evaporated milk instead of regular and frozen broccoli.  About an hour before serving I pureed some of the broccoli chunks in the blender to make it smoother, then I added the cheese.   My husband, who is not big on soup requested that I make this again.  Thanks Sue!
Definitely the best Broccoli Soup recipe soup I've come across.  Wonderfully rich, creamy, and tasty.  Adding this to my regular meal rotation.  Thank you!
This is so yummy and way better than what I have had in restaurants.  Very thick and creamy.
My husband really liked this but it was missing something. I can't put my finger on it. I most likely won't make this again.

Pretty good! I shopped for the ingredients before I found a recipe, so I substituted heavy cream for some of the milk, didn't add onions because my husband hates them, and used sharp cheddar. Thanks for providing a recipe without "cream of... soup" or Velveeta, I chose this recipe specifically for its true scratch ingredients. It was really quick to put together. I steamed the broccoli & ran most of it through the food processor before adding it. Everyone loved it and had seconds.

Loved this... very tasty.  For the broccoli, I used Green Giant steamers chopped broccoli (the whole bag) which was perfect and fast.  I used 2 cups of sharp cheddar.  It was very cheesy, which is how I like it!  Totally delicious the next day too.  Oh, also, my daughter is a vegetarian so I subbed organic vegetable broth for the chicken broth.  Divine!  Thanks for a new family favorite!
Very good!! Quick and easy and my kids love it! I make it exactly as written. I prefer this recipe because i dont like the velveta cheese. I dont like the texture it give the soup.
Very easy to make and very good.  Tastes clean and fresh.  I basically doubled the broccoli, onion and celery.  Perfect consistency.

DS and I had this for lunch today.  I had some broccoli in fridge that needed to be used and we chose this.  Its very good.  I did use a potato masher to break up the broccoli a bit but otherwise followed recipe.  We loved it.  Thank you for sharing this with us.
Awesome!! so simple! rich and creamy----the fiance loved it! thanks so much for sharing! :D

Straightforward, simple and tasty.  I doubled the ingredients.  Following some other reviews, I substituted a little shaved carrot for the celery and used half 2% milk and half light cream.  I also pureed the thickened mixture before adding the broccoli.

This is absolutely delicious! I had two huge bowls as soon as I finished making it (I'm pregnant). I omitted the celery because I don't like it and instead added a whole large onion chopped up. My husband isn't really into carrots, so I decided to that was a bette route. I also used a really nice, white cheddar cheese (so worth it to go for a quality cheese vs. something like Velveeta) and went for the full 2 cups. A perfect,cozy, cool weather dinner!

Good taste, strange consistency. I followed the directions as written except for the omission of the celery. Not sure if I made a mistake along the way or if it just the way this soup tastes but it was gritty. I will probably try the recipe again and use less flour??

i didn't have any celery but i added two big garlic cloves to the onions. used only 2 cups of 1% milk and that was plenty. the broth became a cup of water and a broth cube. added a bit of dill too. i found this only made 2 meal-sized bowls. would have made 4 side-dish-sized cups. this was very easy and wonderful comfort food. will certainly make again.

I was so happy to find a cheesy soup recipe that didn't call for Velveeta!  This was a delicious soup.  My whole family loved it! Like others, I ommited the celery and substituted shredded carrot instead.  The only other change I made was in the cheese.  I didn't have cheddar so I had to use a mexican blend instead.  I turned out wonderfully!  Comfort food at it's finest.

I absolutely love this soup!!!  I've been making it for about 4 months now and cannot believe that I have not review it yet!  The flavor is awesome.....and it is easy to double!!  Sometimes I will use heavy cream for some of the milk!!  Thanks!

YUMMY! You think the Broccoli and Cheedar soup in a can is delicious but when you make this... It blows the canned kind out of the water!! This is absolutely delicious and we didn't alter anything in the recipe; Definitely a recipe to add to the cookbook :)
Very yummy simple recipe that didnt include Velveeta for once!  I cant wait to make it again and try adding things to it :) Thanks!
Delicious

Love it. Tastes as good, if not better then restaurants. I like to add shredded carrots (and sometimes shredded cabbage) as well. I also use 1/2 the salt and double the pepper using black. I use fresh broccoli and find that it retains its bright green color after 1hr of cooking/cooling. If i lack time, steaming first while the rest cooks will be my go-to method. Using 2 cups of broth and 1 1/2 cups of milk still give it a great rich flavor and thickness, while cutting out a little of the fat.

This was a great recipe!  I boiled the broccoli before I added it to the soup, but not for very long.  The color remained a bright green as well.  Next time I try this, I will have to add more things like maybe some shredded carrot or ham!

Thank you for this recipe Sue.  I love it. I particularly like that is does not include canned soup or velveeta.  I used fresh broccoli, chopped, then steamed in the microwave.  I also added carrots to the celery and onion.   It is a wonderful recipe.
A great soup! Stayed mostly true to the recipe but added some real bacon bits and more cheese. Plus I used old cheddar. Will make it again!
This soup is great and a keeper for me. Thanks!
I think I have found a great basic cream of whatever recipe!  Thanks so much for sharing.

This was quite tasty and super easy to make.  We have some very sick peoples in this house so a warm bowl of soup is what I made.  I did use my hand blender to cut up the onions, carrots (I added it), and celery.  The soup was very creamy and hearty.

Very good!  This was exactly what I was looking for and was surprisingly filling.  I followed the recipe exactly, including the steaming and cooling of the broccoli.  Flavors blended very well without the gritty texture of other broccoli and cheese soups.  Thanks for a delicious, comfort soup Sue Lau!!!

Was looking for a good recipe to make broccoli and cheese soup for the first time, this is it!! It was easy to make but more importantly tasted amazing. I added an extra cup of chicken broth and found the consistency perfect. Thanks for the great recipe!

I made this for the first time today. All I can say is "delicious".  I followed the directions exactly. The prep work was easy using my Kitchen Aid food processor. Didn't t not find it hard to do at all. This will definitely be the recipe I go to every time I want some broccoli and cheese soup. No need to look anywhere else.

Really yummy. Used 2 C of skim and 1/2 C of whip cream. Didn't have celery on hand so just doubled the onion to 1/2 C. Used homemade chicken stock which always makes a difference. Was ever so slightly salty probably from the rotisserie bones in the stock so I will wait and add the salt at the very end to taste. Made exactly 4 servings for us with none left over, will make sure to save this and use it again when I have some cheese that needs to get used, thanks!
This recipe is delicious and very easy to make. Love it. It says it serves six but that would have to be six very tiny people. It really serves two to three people.
Sue, thanks for a great recipe!

New to the OAMC.  My family really enjoyed this recipe.  I used chicken breast.  Very tasty and moist.
Thanks

Amazing, the family loves this. Thank you Trish, it's such a welcome change from the regular baked chicken. I served it with cornbread and cooked carrots as a veggie (carrots were all I had on hand at the time) and a green salad. It all came together beautifully!! Will use this again.
Very easy and tasty!  It worked as advertised & was a hit.  Served it over white rice (the sauce was very nice mixed in with the rice) and green salad.

This was really good! My family (myself, hubby and 5 year old) really like it.  I have to say I was skeptical at first, I mean, taco sauce and apricot jam??  But the flavor in the end was fantastic!  I served this with rice and it was a hit.  Awesome easy meal.  Thanks for posting this!

Yummy! we loved the flavour of this and it could not be easier. I used a jar of eveln/athen's apricot jam from the last RSC contest recipe#116457 and my own taco seasoning recipe#4292  and threw everything in a ziploc bag into the freezer. One morning I dumped the entire bag into my crockpot and let it cook all day. I came home to a delicious meal and my house smelled terrific. I used chicken leg quarters this time but I plan to try breasts or thighs in the future. Thanks for sharing :)
This soup is outstanding.  I leave out the vineger, and serve with diced fresh tomatoes.

EXCELLENT!!  My DH rated this in this way.  It is great with a little heat, when you first tasted it you can really taste the apricot jam, and then the taco seasoning comes and kicks it in the a@%! 

I made this with homemade taco seasoning mix, and homemade salsa and sugar free apricot jam.  Very good it is definately a keeper!  Thanks for sharing.
I made it w/ frozen chicken & cooked as directed for 2 hours, stiring twice.Was very moist & tasty.I was afraid there wouldn't be enough sauce, it didn't look like a lot but the was plenty.TFS

Delicious and SOO easy.  Even my son who hates salsa liked this.  I added a little extra jam because my salsa was very strong.  Also, the sauce makes quite enough for a 3.5 lb chicken, or even more.  We poured the extra sauce from the bottom of the pan over mashed potatoes--yum!

This was really good, the flavor went throughout the entire piece of chicken, not just the skin.  I dumped the bag into my crockpot and cooked on high for about 3 1/2 hours or so - it was just perfect.  May I suggest throwing in some rice the last half hour of cooking to go with all that delicous sauce?  Thanks for a great OAMC-to-crockpot recipe, Tish!

I am totally impressed with this recipe, because it is incredibly easy and deeee licious.  I used the crock pot--threw all ingredients in, stirred, and cooked on high for 3 1/2 hours.  This will become an old standby.  I served with corn recipe # 161110, and it was a great combination.
Great for OAMC!! I used Bonless Skinless chicken breasts and it turned out GREAT!  I used a chunky salsa and I think I will use a smoother one next time, but thats just my family's preference.

We really love this chicken and will make it often.  I used about 2 1/2 pounds of chicken thighs and made it in my crockpot.  Excellent blend of flavors.  the sauce is so good I am trying to turn it into a dip for tortilla chips.

My husband and I truly loved this recipe.  I was a bit skeptical, but I thought I would give it a try.  I loved the marinade so much that I saved the rest of it after it was cooked and poured it over some steak I had left over.  Thank you for the wonderfully, easy recipe.

tender,juicy,yummy!
uhmm used italian seasoning instead (that's the one available) and still, it was great!  Made this 2x.  That's how good it is! Thanks for sharing this recipe.
This is wonderful and so easy. I have made it twice now for 2 different sets of friends and it was a hit with everyone. Thanks Tish!

This was very tasty and the chicken was very tender.  I made this with 3 chicken breasts and the full amount of sauce, so I had plenty of extra sauce.  I froze this early in the week and then packed it in the ice chest on Friday to take out to the weekend place.  I baked this for 30 minutes.

We really enjoyed this recipe ~ the flavor was great!  I dumped this into an aluminum pan and baked in my roaster oven and it worked like a charm.  I served with recipe #16465.  Today, I took the leftovers and shredded the chicken, spooned the leftover sauce over, heated in the microwave and served in tortillas.  These were yummy, too!  Thanks so much for posting!!!
Excellent recipe!  We all really enjoyed this.  The sweet slightly spicy flavor is a winner.  Easy to make for the freezer and easy to prepare and serve.  Thanks Tish!

This was good....really, really good!!!  I couldn't believe how easy this recipe was!  I took the suggestion of cooking the chicken in the crock pot and it came out moist and tender.  I would highly recommend this wonderful, easy recipe
So very easy for such a great tasting dish. Many good tips here for using more of that wonderful sauce.  Thank-you Tish for the recipe -

I am a new fan of dump recipes.  This is very good.  Next time to spice it up I will had some crushed chillis and garlic.  I did everything in the crockpot and it turned out nicely.  Thank you Tish and keep those dumps coming.

My husband likes spicy, I like sweet, so this was the perfect recipe for us!  We altered the proportions of ingredients to suit our taste:  1 cup of salsa, 1/2 cup apricot jam and 1 tbsp of taco seasoning.  This made plenty of sauce for 4 chicken thighs, with enough to top our rice and chowmein on the side.  Delicious!

This was really good!  I think next time I'll try it w/o the taco seasoning mix- it's definitely flavorful enough and I bet it doesn't need it.
Super easy and yummy!  Thanks Tish! :)

I couldn't believe how easy this was. Definitely converted me to include more OAMC recipes in my line up. My BF said it was great chicken and that I should add it to 'the list' because my chicken never has this much flavor! LOL Next time I'm going to make it with some corn on the cob!
I have never come across a recipe like this before Zaar.  I liked this so much I am planning several of the other "Dump" versions.  The kids even used the extra sauce to put on top of their rice.

Very good chicken! I cooked it in the crockpot for 3 and a half hours on high and it was still nice and moist, I stabbed the chicken with a knife a few times before cooking it so it had tons of flavor. I served it with tiny acini de pepi pasta, it is tiny little pasta balls, and steamed baby artichoke, great meal.
Very yummy! I knew I wouldn't like too much sweetness so I halved the jam, I was right, but it was wonderful with only half. It froze perfectly too!

Good recipe- easy to do, and came in handy on a summer Sunday evening when I don't want to do much of anything....It's not at all bad, definitely tasty. But I don't think we'd make it again. It was just underwhelming.

Tried this last night at the recommendation of a Cyber-friend. As it was baking, I thought it would be very spicy because of the aroma - but the boneless chicken breasts were fabulously tender (I had pounded them with a mallet before cooking)and had a very even flavor thanks to the apricot jam.  I'd cut down on the amount of salsa next time, as alot of it went to waste.  My picky eaters loved this recipe!
good...easy and kids ate it..Im happy!

This was a big hit at my household.  I used pineappple/apricot jam and added the whole jar.  Threw it in the crockpot.  The first time we ate it with lettuce, rice, tomatoes and cheese with ranch dressing as a salad type meal.  The second time I made this the kids ate it directly out of the crock pot.  It is a keeper.  Thanks.

OMG! This is so good! I was a little skeptical at first but decided to try it and  I was not disappointed.  I did use only about 10 oz of salsa and it was plenty juicy.  Be daring and try this delicious chicken!!!!  I did not freeze it--I just made it up in the morning and let it marinate in fridge all day.

This is an incredibly easy chicken to prepare and how delicious and moist it was to eat.  I marinaded the chicken for a few hours and then put it in the crock pot for 4 1/2 hours on low.  If I had more time, I would have made rice to soak up the wonderful sauce.  This is going in my favorites...especially for the ease.
Excellent recipe!  Since my family is picky I switched the jar of salsa to a 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes.  Absolutely delicious!  A keeper for this family.

Thank you Tish. This is a keeper in my OAMC. Very easy to do and cooks up well. I made this 2 week ago and I cooked it in the crock pot for 5 hours on low. It was soooo nice to walk into the house and smell this. We had it with steam rice. All plate clean and happy faces all round.

I have just started OAMC and using the opportunity to try tastes I don't normally think of myself.  I like taco seasoning and salsa but usually in small doses so I wasn't sure if the sweet would even be very noticeable but it was a perfect blend and I came back for a second 'dose'.

Wonderful make-ahead dish! The apricot and salsa flavours are a great combination. I froze 4 large bone-in chicken breasts with the "sauce" a month ago and pulled it out early in the morning to thaw. Then dumped it all into a large casserole dish, covered, and baked for almost an hour. The chicken was juicy and tender and very flavourful. I really appreciated this on a busy day. Thank you, Tish!

I read so many great reviews and I was SO excited for this chicken...but it was just 'so so' in my opinion. I dunno...the flavors didn't really do it for me. Very strong flavors. The only redeeming quality about this chicken is that it definitely got better after a couple days. The leftovers were actually pretty good!

This is a great OAMC meal! We made it with chicken thighs and the meat was so juicy and tender, with lots of flavor. Not too sweet or spicy, just perfect. I put this in the crockpot FROZEN on low for about 6 hours and it was perfect.

I was very excited about the ease of the recipe, but it did not meet my expectations. I'll admit the chicken was very tender from cooking in the juices but the taste was ok. Maybe reducing the amount of salsa and adding a little cream would help. Thank you
I was disappointed by the flavor of this.  The chicken was tender, but maybe would be better using a fruity-type salsa.
We found the flavors delightful.  I used chicken tenders and plan to make this again.  And it was sooo good the second time around.

This was the first dump chicken recipe I'd ever even heard of and I'm so glad I gave it a try - this was incredible! It's so basic and simple and was a huge hit with my family. The combination of spicy and sweet is fantastic. I'll be making this regularly and I've added several other dump recipes to my cookbook to try. Thanks so much!
Super easy and fantastic. I'm usually stingy with my stars, but I would give this one 6 stars. I served with french fries to scoop up the sauce, and the whole family liked it.

Great make ahead dish.  I put the oven on delay start and headed off to soccer practice.  Dinner was almost ready when we got home.  We served this sliced in tortillas with some lettuce.  A nice twist on the taco.  The sweetness is a nice change but not at all overwhelming.  Thanks, Tish!!
I used this tonight for fajitas.... delicious!

We loved this!  Chicken turned out moist and flavorful.  Loved the sweetness, but not overly sweet.  A hit with all of us including the 3 year old.  We used 3 leg quarters and it still gave us plenty of yummy sauce to spoon over rice.  It was easy, economical and a good addition to our OAMC rotation.

Thanks for posting this winner!
I wasn't sure my family would eat this because of the chunks of "red & green stuff" from the salsa, but they ate the chicken and they loved it!
This was incredible!  I used pineapple apricot preserves and mango salsa.  I took this dish to a potluck and we fought for seconds.  This will definitely go into my favorites list for OAMC recipes.

This is great. I used peach jam and only have 3/4 of the taco seasoning packet. Also served with rice. Next time I am going to try adding a cup or two of rice in with the mixture so the rice cooks in all of the yummy salsa-sweetness.

This was so good!  The chicken was so moist and every bite had a wonderful spicy/sweet flavor.  My husband is a picky eater and does not like sweet things, but the combination of the two were just perfect for him and he even asked me to make this for him again. :-)  Thanks for a yummy new recipe that I will use again.

New family favorite! I used boneless chicken breasts, peach jam, and didn't have taco seasoning but had fajita seasoning, so I used it and add a touch extra cumin. I froze first, then just dumped partially thawed into a slow cooker on high for 1 hour, then low for about 6 hours. I added rice the last hour, but I won't do that next time, because it wasn't minute rice and it never really got soft, but stayed a little crunchy. The flavor was infused in every bite of chicken, and the sauce was delicious, not too sweet at all. I will make it again and thicken the sauce to serve over the chicken, or cook the rice separately to put the sauce over. Thanks so much for posting!

Ok, so I love that this recipe can be made in advance- I was so excited to make, freeze, eat and rate this one- it sounded soooo delish. So, here goes.... I love the combo of the flavors, however, I think that the taco seasoning was a bit much. Perhaps just a quarter of the packet would suffice next time? I served with rice and braised broccolini and bok choy- which sounds odd, but it turned out to be a great mild pairing with the super flavorful chicken. I eneded up squeezing the juice from 1/2 a lemon over the entire meal to sort of mellow out the flavors. Overall- good, just may need a bit of tweeking for our family's taste. Thanks, Tish- for a great idea and a fun recipe to play with!
This was pretty good.  DH liked it quite a lot; I was slightly less impressed.  BUT it was easy, we made it ahead of time, so it was a quick dinner fix.  THanks.

I loved how easy this dish was.  I just dumped it all straight into the crock pot and let to go!  It was good, but was slightly too sweet for our tastes.  Maybe next time I will use a hotter salsa and less jam.  I will give it another shot though.

This was a great meal, and even better leftovers.  We made quesadillas with our leftovers and fantastic wraps with our leftover leftovers.  This recipe will be making the OAMC rounds at our house again and again.  Can't wait till the next time it's on the calendar.     Thanks for the keeper!
quick and easy.
Gosh this was tasty.. and easy too. The only change I made was to use a low sugar orange marmalade instead of apricot jam because I had a jar in the fridge. I used boneless skinless breasts

This was very easy to make, as expected.  Unfortunately my husband found it average, and my children didn't like the sauce.  I loved it, but I also like the taste of fruit salsas.  There's an awful lot of sauce leftover, so I think you could get away with less sauce especially if you cook it in a smaller pan (I used a 9x13).  I'd be tempted to use a 7x11.
My favorite OAMC meal so far!
This is so simple yet so delicious. I love to bake or grill the chicken then mix with sautÃ©ed bell peppers and onions  and wrap in a tortilla for quick fijitas
So easy and OMG so good. You can switch up the salsa to hot, extra hot, add in more hot/jalapeno's etc.....this was great. Thanks Tish!

This is a pretty of a salsa based recipe, so if you're not a huge salsa fan, you probably won't care for it as much. We really enjoy salsa though, eat it almost every day on something or other, I think...yeah, we're weird! And we like spicy salsa, but the beauty of this is that you can have it what ever spiciness you like. The other really AWESOME thing about this one is it is basically a dump and cook recipe, which really rocks!!! I love easy to make recipes that have great flavors. Best of all, you can make it and throw it in the freezer for whenever you need a quick and easy meal. The instructions show two ways you can make the recipe. One that allows you to make it right away, and the other so you can throw it in the freezer for later. 
 
There's a couple different ways you can do this recipe. As is, which sounds great, or with rice. I read a review where a woman put hers in a crock pot on high for 3.5 hrs and added rice during the last 30 minutes or so, so the rice would soak up all that nummy sauce. Sounded like a great idea to me. I baked mine in the oven, but it still turned out. I had to cook it longer than the suggested time, but it was worth it. We were able to play with the kids while supper was cooking. It's basically a cook in one pot sort of recipe! Even though I used chicken breasts, I had to cook mine for closer to an hour, but I used an 8x8 pan and am not sure how big a deal that was being deeper liquid. I had to guess-timate the amount of rice, so I kind of did the regular ratio of water to rice. I figured if the recipe called for 1.5 cups of salsa, I'd put in 3/4 c. of rice in. I don't use minute rice, so I am not sure how that would work. I covered it up and threw it in the oven. I stirred it a couple of times, just because I didn't know how long it was going to take to cook, so I took it out periodically to check on it. I'm not sure you would have to stir it. You could really smell it when it was ready to come out of the oven.
Sweet and tangy, this recipe was a hit with my kids. So easy and really delicious. Thanks!!

This is so good! I made this into a freezer kit for my parents the first time I made it. They both work long hours and are too tired to cook when they get home, so I let them try it first. I used thighs and put it in the zip top bag. I also made rice in my rice cooker, so they could heat it and serve the chicken over the rice. Well, my dad ended up putting the rice in the bottom of the baking dish and dumping the chicken over it and cooking it that way. He and my mom raved about that chicken for days. We make it that way too and the rice is so yummy. It's so easy to package the rice in a smaller zip bag and then put both into another larger bag. Then just thaw, throw the rice and chicken in the dish and bake it. Comes in handy when your really busy. Even the boys (16 and 4) love this. Thanks Tish! This is a real winner!

This is SO quick and easy.  And it tastes great.  For those two reasons it goes in the "family favorites" cookbook.  DH said, "Yeah, you'll be making this often."  All you have to do is dump (hencee the recipe name) three ingredients and your chicken in a pan and throw it in the oven.  Love it!  Thank you!

I must admit I was a little skeptical.  But this was really good, and we all liked it.  I used bits of various jams and jellies to equal 8 ounces, so "fruity" would describe it.  I used mild salsa, and boneless, skinless breasts.  The sauce resulted in almost candied peppers, onions and tomatoes, which were yummy.  My oven is programmable for delayed start, so I put frozen chicken with sauce in the oven in the morning (it is insulated, after all), and programmed it for 35 minutes total (to include heating time).  Came out perfect, moist, and very aromatic.  Will make again, and will try apricot.

This was delicious!  I made 2 batches and froze them.  When I baked them up a few weeks later, oh my... the chicken was melt in your mouth tender.  My whole family loved this chicken.  It took me only minutes to prepare in throw in the freezer for future easy meals.  This is definitely a keeper and one I will add to my OAMC recipes.  Thank you!
Wonderful recipe.  I used chicken breasts and cooked them on the stove top.  It tasted a bit like sweet and sour chicken with a mexican flair.  Thank you.
It was very easy to prepare and the flavor was good.  Not an amazing recipe, but good enough to make once a month for family.
Quick, easy and my boys loved it.  I serve with cheese baked rice and cut up veggies

I made this while my sister was visiting. Her and all the kids loved it. The only thing i didn't like too much was the taco packet was a bit over powering. I will make this again, but use only half packet mix. Thanks for a great alternative chicken recipe.
Excellent. I don't usually like sweet meats but the spiciness of the taco seasonings and salsa balanced the sweetness of the jam nicely.

Wonderful!  We made this a few nights ago and loved it.  The only changes we made were to decrease the taco seasoning by half and then thickened the sauce prior to serving over rice.  Big hit with my husband!  We will definitely try making this again but will maybe add some corn to the actual dish when cooking.
Very good and the chicken was so tender.
Very good. The sauce is delish, and I wish I would have made mashed potatoes to go with it. It was sweet, but we like that. I think it would also be good with orange marmalade.

This was quite good. VERY tender chicken. Kids liked it although it was a little spicy for their taste due to the taco seasoning. Hubby and I really liked the sweet/salty mix of it. Definitely a good base for a lot of different variations.
This was so easy and so good.  I served it over rice as the sauce was teriffic!!!   This is definately a keeper recipe.  Thanks.

So good!  So fast!  So easy!!!
Thanks for another terrific recipe Tish!!  I served it with rice & it was a big hit!
