Tasty soup, loved the flavour of the broth, herbs used gave a nice flavour. Thanks for sharing.

Cheap and easy, can't ask for more than that.  Thanks, Toni.  I added a splash of white wine, I might add more next time, as well as more garlic, but that's just me.  Hubby liked it as is.  I served with a peice of garlic toast.
Hearty, satisfying and easy to make.

Toni, this was a perfect dinner for our first full snowy day of "Canadian living"! I used safflower oil instead of vegetable, subbed in some oregano because I don't have any marjoram and went with green lentils. Also added a touch of arrowroot because the consistency was a bit watery- but I think that has more to with the bouillon powder I used than with your recipe. I served this with a crusty baguette, and even my lentil-indifferent boyfriend loved it. Got some in the fridge for tomorrow, can't wait!

wow this is easy and really tasty. ive already made it three times for guests...i never use celery because i always forget to buy it...and i usually double or triple the recipe...i dont top it with yogurt. 

i find that it sometimes turns into stew so i have to add more water...

the best tip i have is squeezing a bit of lemon and good extra virgin olive oil into the bowl for a more complex treat. the olive oil is optional, but the lemon juice really takes it to the next level.

Deeelicious!!!!  Fabulously yummy!  I accidently put 1 teaspoon of dried marjoram instead of a 1/4 as directed and it came out wonderful.  I didn't have any yogurt on hand...and really its not needed at all! Love this soup! Thanks Toni!!

This is my ideal recipe, nutritious, easy to make, economical and my very picky toddler gobbled it up and said mmmm the whole time! I added about 10 slices of chopped bacon (to a doubled recipe) and sautÃ©ed with the veggies until cooked but still soft. I didn't serve with yogurt but stirred in vinegar instead. This will be made often in my home.
This recipe is outstanding, I also used 1 tsp marjoram and chicken broth instead of vegetable stock. It is one of the very few really healthy recipes that I just love and make over and over.

This is one of the best lentil recipes I've tried! I was also happy to find a use for the barley that's been waiting in my pantry. I made a few changes to the recipe based on what I had at home. I used canola oil in place of vegetable, celery salt in place of a celery stalk, chicken broth in place of vegetable stock, and I omitted the carrot and the parsley. I also added about 1/4 cup white wine.  I tried it with a spoonful of sour cream (at the suggestion of another reviewer) but decided in the end that I like it just the way it is without any topping. Thanks again Toni!
I added some yellow potatoes with the water, and tomatoes at the very end. Very easy, fast, and good.
A nice basic soup that I will probably "jazz up" a little next time. Very healthy and simple. DH said it didn't look like much, but it tasted better than it looked :wink:

I just about double the veggies, and added a can of diced tomatoes along with the stock and water. I did not use the optional topping. Really delicious and satisfying. I like that it is a healthy vegetarian option, but still very filling. It's perfect for fall lunches. Thanks!

Yum!! I was looking for something along the lines of Amy's Organics Lentil soup. The flavors in this soup really aren't the same, but I didn't care because it was so good. It was super easy to make. It was perfect for a fall day and I'm looking forward to the left overs. I made the following changes: 1 Tbs dried minced onion for the fresh, double the carrots, no celery, upped the pearl barley to 1/2 cup, added 1 Tbs of apple cider vinegar, 1 Tbs vegan Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 can diced tomatoes undrained, no topping. Next time I may thicken up the broth a bit as a personal preference and cut the Worcestershire sauce down to 1/2 Tbs since that flavor was a little too strong.

An A+ soup that was warming and hearty on a chilly day. I did skip the sauteing and added the veggies directly to the soup. Aside from that everything was "By The Book" and the amounts were just right for me. I chose to pass on the yogurt this time and didn't have fresh parsley but I couldn't have been happier with the finished soup. Thanks toni for another winner that hit the spot perfectly.

Very good soup! Easy to make, all ingredients on hand except the marjoram. Used a little more thyme, some sea salt and added the juice of half a small organic lemon and that woke the flavours right up! Thanks for a delish and nutrish recipe!

I am a big fan of barley soups and this was a very good one indeed.  I used cooking spray rather than the oil to take off a few fat grams and I threw in a few mushrooms but other than that I sticked to the recipe.  My partner asked if there was more left and then grunted sadly when I said there wasn't.  So, you can take that has his approval too.  Made for PAC Spring 2008.

Very tasty soup.  I had some leftover lentils and barley from previous winter soups in my pantry, and this was the perfect way to use them up.  In order to make it even heartier, however, I added some sliced linguica sausage that I had in the fridge.

I liked the texture very much but found the flavor really bland. I think  it was my homemade vegetable stock (spinach,  broccoli) that contributed to this. I doctored it up with garlic powder and  lemon juice and that helped.
Roxygirl

Wow, I was really surprised at how good this was.  Usually I find lentil soups pretty unimpressive, but this was great!  I served this with sour dough bread, and I think the only thing I'll change next time is that I'll add a little bit of pepper.

I've been looking for healthier meals and this one hit the spot. Do you want to know how good this was? Mr. Picky Picky (my oldest son) ate seconds!!! Everyone enjoyed it and I will definitely be making this again. 
p.s. I didn't add the marjoram because I didn't have any and I did add pepper.

This was so good!  Even my husband liked it, and he thinks soup doesn't qualify as food unless it's served with a pizza.  I was a little worried about it being bland with a  vegetable stock instead of a beef stock, but by the time it had simmered and I'd added the fresh parsley, it was delicious!  This is definitely a keeper.

An excellent combination, barley and lentils. I didn't have any marjoram, so used sage instead. Also, i only had red lentils, which i believe tend to get mushier than brown or green. This may have made my version of this soup thicker. Everyone loved it. I plan to try it with the original ingredients as soon as i get a chance.

This soup is amazing.  Beautiful.  Fantastic.  And really easy.  I used pearl barley and it got a little bit too mushy, but even that I grew to enjoy.  I ate this soup ALL WEEK for lunch.  I prefer thicker soups and though this was just-about-right for me, it was even better as it continued to thicken gradually in the fridge over the week.  I am counting the days left on my meal plan so I can make this again soon.

Who thought healthy could taste this good?!?  When I first looked at this recipe, I thought "Are there enough spices in this?"  Just in case you're wondering the same thing...Yes, there are!  This is a very flavorful, hearty soup. (Not to mention it's so inexpensive to make!)  Thanks so much for sharing, Toni!  This will be a frequent flyer at my house!

Very good soup.  I've tried some other lentil soups that turned out rather bland but this came out quite good.  I ate it for the next two days and it held over for that entire time and was still good.  I didn't bother with the garnish or with the final touch of parsley at the end of cooking, since I didn't have fresh parsley on hand.  Regardless of my omissions though it was quite delicious.  Thank you.

A nice change from the usual lentil soup. The barley added a little bit more substance and fiber which is always good. I liked the fresh parsley added at serving time. It really boosted the flavor. Thanks for posting.

I fixed this for lunch and it was very nice. I would like a little more seasoning, however. Next time I will add some Italian sausage, I think. I liked the barley mixed with the lentils and it is a terrific Weight Watchers soup at 3 points. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

Hearty but not heavy, this soup is so good! I was looking for a recipe after having a great lentil soup in a restaurant recently.  This one was even better!  I added a 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes and used homemade chicken stock instead of vegetable stock.  Also I added a lot of fresh thyme - I just threw in several big sprigs from the garden, the leaves fell off in the soup, no chopping necessary.  Next time I will garnish it with crumbled bacon, that's the way it was served at the restaurant.  This recipe is definitely a keeper!

This soup is AMAZING!  I love it!  I did change some things.  I doubled the recipe, added 1/2 cup white wine, used pearl barley, 2 tsp Cumin, lemon juice, 1 Tbs worshire sauce, 1 Tbs apple cider vinegar, used split peas and lentils.  I also crumbled Queso Fresco (white mexican cheese) on top before serving.  That adds a lot.  Thank you!! It is so good!  I am also going to try putting fresh basil in today's batch.

A very nice soup. A little bland for my taste. I loved that there was no meat or potatoes, but I just didn't find enough flavor. After making the recipe in half (your version) and mine. I made the following changes.

I added a bit more garlic, more celery, and a can of diced tomatoes. I also used all fresh herbs (more of the fresh of course) which I think gave it a brighter flavor. I used all vegetable stock (no water, that just "watered" it down for me), more pepper, but salt I do to taste.  I think the fresh herbs and the tomatoes did it for me. That was all it needed.

I did use the topping and mix a bit of lemon juice and zest in with the parsley and sour cream.  It was a nice topping to the soup. Served with with a nice baguette that I grilled with some melted havarti. A nice complement to the soup.

I was excited about making this healthy soup but ended up disappointed in the lack of flavor. I followed the recipe but also added extra carrots and celery to it. After trying it when it was done I tried adding additional seasonings other than just the thyme, marjoram, salt and pepper, but I still thought it lacked something.
Reading through some of the other reviews now I see that a lot of people have added everything from lemon juice, cider vinegar, worcestershire sauce, tomatoes to white wine. I'll try the recipe again sometime but make some changes to the seasonings.

This is a reeally basic recipe to begin some really awesome soup.  I saw the reviews and I definitely opted for the plain yogurt mixed with lemon zest and juice to add to the top.  It made it worlds better!  I also chopped some celery leaves on top which was really good.  As for the seasoning, I had to add a lot.  I added some curry powder, garlic salt (I used low sodium vegetable broth), extra garlic, a little cumin and a little Sriracha.  I also added extra pearl barley.  This recipe turned out really great with lots of help from other reviews!!
Pretty easy, a nice tasting hearty soup.  Didn't have thyme and marjoram, just added italian seasoning instead. Used chicken stock.  We'll be making this again.

So good. I added parmesan and red pepper flakes on mine for a bit more flavor. My kids loved it as is. My kids who cannot agree on anything to eat were both going back for seconds. Thanks for the recipe!

This soup is a great basic soup, but it definitely benefits from a few extra additions. I did not use marjoram but I did add some oregano and basil. I also added some pepper flakes and hot Italian sausage. The sausage was a great addition and actually added some extra sweetness to the soup. I loved the different flavours and the textures from the barley and lentils. Bowls kept getting refilled tonight! Thanks so much!
I didn't have vegetable broth, so I used chicken broth and also added a package of Knorr's vegetable soup mix.  Incredibly flavourful! Will make this again.
Needs a bit more spice but good and basic recipe. Eaten with Greek yoghurt.

This has always been one of my comfort foods! It is even better with mushrooms and bay leaves. My mom would always make this soup in the winter or when we were sick. This soup always brings me warm, happy, memories. :)
Veery easy to prepare. I followed the recipe but added about 5 large white mushrooms to the saute. Served with greek yogurt. A nice vegetarian soup.

Tried this yesterday for breakfast.  The only thing that didn't turn out was the bisquik in it.  After 35 minutes, I checked it and it was cooked, so I took it out and served it up.  The eggs, cheese and bacon were fantastic (I used turkey bacon), but the bisquick was like mushy dough.  We just ate around it.  I think without the bisquick it would have been great.  Will try it without next time!
If you haven't tried this recipe then you should! I loved the flavors together and will definitely be making this again and again.
Great recipe!
Very fancy! In the end I added a drizzle of balsamico. I think garlic would go well here, too.

This is now my favorite sloppy joe recipe.  It is not runny and has a nice chunky texture..(I chopped the red pepper and onion in a medium dice).  Sloppy joes should be slightly sweet in my opinion & this fills the bill.  I put some grated cheddar on top and place under the broiler for a bit.  I used Famous Daves Steak & Fajita seasoning.  Terrific!!!
this is the ONLY way my family will eat sloppy joes.  much better then that canned stuff
Delicious!!! Very easy also. I used a green bell pepper instead of red. I also added some garlic. This will be a keeper for me!
This was as simple to make as sloppy joes from a mix and yet tastes far better. I don't think I will ever make it any other way after trying this recipe.  It was great!

Super recipe. My thanks to you and Rachael Ray.  Quick, easy, tasty.  I used a 15 oz. can of tomato sauce; it worked fine. I've been looking for a no-ketchup recipe for sloppy joes for a long time.  This is it!

AWESOME RECIPE!!! I made this for my boyfriend and his buddies on a camping trip and they ate it all before I could eat some (good thing I tasted it in the pot before I went :)  They loved the red peppers in it! Thank you for a great cooking success!

"Super Scrumptious" is right!  I made these today and it turned out great. I forgot to get the brown sugar at the supermarkey, so rather than using white sugar, I used cane syrup for the molasses flavor. It made it a little runny but otherwise it was delicious.  I will definitely make it again.
This is the best sloppy joe recipe! The ingredients are perfect and go together so well! Thanks for posting it.
Fabulous!!! I can't cook and this came out GREAT!! My husband thought it was a little too sweet (thats why its 4stars instead of 5). I definately will make again. Maybe add a little less b.sugar.

Definately one of the best recipes for Sloppy Joes yet, according to my DS! I reduced the brown sugar to about 2 tablespoons and added in fresh garlic and a small chopped onion to the ground beef mixture. Glad I picked this recipe to make, it's wonderful! thanks NDP...Kittencal:)

Yummy stuff!  Made for dinner on 12/9 and then left in the crockpot on "warm" when we went out for some errands.  Came home and enjoyed this mixture on some yummy sesame rolls.  The sweetness was a hit here, and I enjoyed some crunchy dill pickles on the side.

I omitted the red pepper, but added some red pepper flakes with the steak seasoning for a bit more kick.  In the future, I would reduce the amount of brown sugar just a bit, as it was a little sweet for our tastes.  I served this on toasted buns with pickles and a side of Easiest Veggie Salad (recipe 88312) for a quick weeknight dinner.

These are fantastic sloppy joes!  They are sweet, but that's just how we like them.  Except for using ground turkey instead of beef, I followed the recipe exactly (including using McCormick brand spicy steak seasoning).  It was a little more runny than we like so I let it simmer for about 45 minutes and it thickened up just right.

I made this tonite and enjoyed it very much. I followed your ingredient list as written but kept the grapes aside until the squash had baked for thirty minutes. The reason for this was because I have baked with whole grapes before and I was afraid they would get too soggy. The dish was really very tasty and company-worthy.

I've made this several times now, and everyone who has tried it has loved it.  I even sent the recipe to my neighbor last year when she wanted something different to serve at her huge Thanksgiving dinner, and she liked it so well she plans to repeat it this year.  It's a nice combination of flavors and textures; quite unexpected, which makes it even better when offering to company.  Thanks for sharing.

This is positively AMAZING! I could not stop eating it. What an amazing layer of individual flavors. Next time I will add more sage. It's beautiful and delicious! I will be adding this to our Thanksgiving menu. I'm on board with Zeldaz, add the grapes and allow then to roast with all the other ingredients. Watch your timing. It may not take 50 minutes. I wish I have made more!  I forgot to add the pine nuts before the taking the photo, but I did roast and add them before serving. Do not leave them out! YUM!  Thanks Geema!
Loved it!  This was a great combination of flavors and so easy to do. I just drizzled on some oil, (no butter), and put everything in a 9x13 pan. Baked it for about an hour. Perfect!

You can not go wrong with this yummy side. The sage and grapes bring a whole new wonderful level to your everyday roasted squash. Made as written using globe grapes. Will make again. Thanks for the post.

What a wonderful combination of flavors!  Made exactly as posted-and wouldn't change a thing.  All my favorites plus an easy oven recipe.  Am going to add this to my 425 oven collection.  Thank you for sharing Geema.

YES! This is the first five-star rating I have EVER given! I roast a lot of veggies, including butternut squash, but I never would have thought of using the grapes. It's a wonderful combination with the onions and squash, and visually attractive, too. I'm afraid I disagree with Happy Harry #2 about the grapes, they are really good all caramelized and sweet and soft, not soggy, after the full roasting time. They'd be good even roasted by themselves. The pine nuts add a firm, crunchy texture that complements the softer grapes and squash. Pecans or walnuts would probably work too. Oh, I did use all oil instead of butter, but I'd use the butter for a special meal, like Thanksgiving.

Added 12/20/10: Out of sage? Try rosemary! It's a nice variation. If you have neither, thyme is goo, too.

Delicious. I wasn't sure how the whole roasting grapes thing was going to go, but they really made this dish stand out. The pine nuts were a nice touch, but those suckers were pricey so I would probably skip them next time. I didn't really measure the oil and butter and I think I put too much in, so I'll watch that more closely next time. I've always eaten steamed or boiled butternut squash, but now that just seems silly since roasting is clearly the yummier way to go :)
Delicious!!   I loved the combination of flavors and the smell while it's baking is amazing!!   This would be a great side dish to almost anything.  Will be making again - thanks for sharing!

These were good. They were a little plain or bland at first.. so I pulled out a different crock pot sloppy joe recipe I had and added dry mustard, garlic powder, chili powder and some other stuff.. after spicing them up they were every good!

This side dish is so easy, so good, and so Fall!  Prep is reduced by buying pre-diced squash.  I loved the addition of pine nuts and the savory taste of the sage.  I actually served as a side to falafel sandwiches because I was looking to use up ingredients, but this recipe would pair well many different main dishes.  I already saved this into my keeper file.   Thanks!
This is sooo good!

I made this recipe which was posted in response to my "what should I make with 1 lb. of ground beef" thread in RR and I picked a winner!  I browned the burger with the veggies and then drained the grease and added the sugar, spices and some garlic.  We loved the flavor and it was super simple to make.  Thanks for posting a keeper!
Great recipe.  definitely a keeper.
Very good!  I used a leaner ground turkey and it still tastes great.  I added a bit more of the steak seasoning, but that might be a personal preference.
This is my favorite sloppy joe recipe.  I make it as directed, with the exception of replacing the ground sirloin with ground turkey breast.  Great stuff.

add another 5 to the ratings. This is definitely a grown ups sloppy joes. I followed the recipe except for using 1 1/2 pounds of meat and I added about 1/2t. chopped garlic to the blend. I enjoyed the unique technique of browning the meat with the brown sugar and seasoning blend. I did simmer it for about 30 minutes after all the ingredients were added as DH was late getting home, but even with the additional simmer time and meat it was still nice and saucy. We got 5 sandwiches with enough leftover to make at least 4 more. It isn't the sloppy joe I grew up with, but it sure is a lovely change! A definite repeat at our home.
Very good! I made exactly as directed (except a green pepper instead of red) and it was wonderful. Will never turn to the can again. Thank you for sharing.

You should have heard the debate around the table about these sloppy joes!  Everyone ate them, everyone liked them, but some felt they were slightly too sweet, other felt they were slightly too hot (the pepper from the 2t of steak seasoning).  I used only 1lb. of ground sirloin & just one can of tomato sauce & the entire can of tomato paste w/a little water (so as not to waste any open cans).

I made this recipe last year for my youngest daughter's birthday party.  Everyone loved these Sloppy Joes!  Many said they were the best they've ever had!  I'm glad this was posted, so I can now add it to my cookbook.  I'd almost forgotten about it.  Great recipe!!

This was very good! I didn't have tomato sauce so I used pureed tomatoes instead. I cut down on the sugar and we thought it was a great balance of sweet and spicy. I toasted French bread and served them open faced. What an easy, delicious meal!

I followed this recipe exactly (this is hard for me, I always think I need to change things!) My husband & I both really liked this & my daughter had the leftovers when she showed up for a visit. She asked for the recipe so she liked it too. I am not a big sloppy joes fan, but this was great!

We liked these. They are quick and good. I have tried several sloppy Joe recipes but every time at least one in our family didn't like something-but this recipe pleased everyone. No one was rolling on the floor because they just couldn't believe the goodness but everyone found them good enough to qualify as my go to sloppy joe.
I made this and everyone one love it they couldn't believe that I made it home made and not out of a can

This was a pretty excellent recipe! You're right, the sugar content would have been too much if it were higher than 1/4 cup. I would reduce it to a little lower than that, even.

I added juice of half a lemon while the beef was cooking to cut down on the beefy smell in the kitchen -- a trick I use with fish, as well. You can't really taste it in the final product, but I reduced the amount of red wine vinegar to account for the acidity of the lemons.

Even with stale buns, this was very good, and as a plus, I had everything in my pantry.

I didn't have steak seasoning, but I used Jane's Krazy Mixed-Up Salt, and a dash of cayenne pepper and thyme to give it a kick.

Great sloppy joes. I grew up eating Manwich sloppy joes and still love them. This version is more adult with a nice chunky texture. I used the full amount of brown sugar and the sweetness was just right for my taste. I also threw in a couple of garlic cloves when the meat was browning. This comes together very easily and can be done on a busy week night. Thanks, newspapergal, for posting a great recipe.

Really good! This will be my new sloppy joe recipe. I too added less sugar,and more pepper. I also used a green pepper instead of the red because I like them more than red. Really quick and easy to throw together too.
Thanks!

I thought I would love these, but I thought it tasted more like Italian meat sauce.  I like mine sweeter, but about half of this went at my step-son's birthday party.  I added more brown sugar and some catsup the next day and liked them better.  Thanks
Very tasty! Reminded my of when I was young!  Of coarse I had to had a ton of chili flakes, hot sauce and garlic to mine though!

I have been making this version of Rachael Ray's sloppy joes for about a year, so I thought I'd add my review. This is my family's absolute favorite and I won't be making it any other way again! We loveeeeeeeee the flavor and the consistency is perfect. I have used Splenda brown sugar before and it still turned out great. The only other substitution I make is: I swap out the red pepper and replace it with chopped celery - just my family's preference. 
We LOVE this recipe! Thanks for posting. :-)
This recipe was really good!  Very quick and had great flavor!  We toasted hamburger rolls and served open face sandwiches...next time might try adding some cheese!  But these were very good!

I am going to give this four stars because I think it is very good, but not outstanding. I would make it again. I did add extra brown sugar and winged the spices since I didn't have a steak mix. I don't think you need the olive oil unless you have incredibly lean meat. I am NOT a big sloppy joe person at all, but I did like this in small amounts. My hubster loved it, so it must be good.
This was by far THE best!!!  I used garlic red wine vinegar and we loved it!  I have made it several times and we love it more each time.  Thanks so much!!!

These were pretty good, although not enough to warrant fives stars (at least for our family). I don't ever remember my mom's (or any other recipe) sloppy joes being sweet. I thought the this recipe was a bit different with the brown sugar and wanted to try it. We thought they were TOO sweet and I even used about a 1.30 lbs. of ground beef instead of the 1 lb. so it would have been even sweeter. I had a jar of the McCormick steak seasoning, although it wasn't Montreal. I had never even opened it (don't remember why I bought it!). I didn't really have a clue as to what the ingredients were in it either...didn't know there was hot peper in it! We like hot pepper in certain things, but not in sloppy joes! It was *okay*, but I probably wouldn't add it next time. I think with a little tweaking, I might make these again.
I have this in a 30 minute meal cookbook from RR and it replaced the way I used to make sloppy joes.  Super tasty and a big hit with my family!
Love it love it love it! This is so good, you won't believe it! I love the different spices that come together in your mouth!

I love this recipe with a few changes...I had used this before out of the Rachel Ray coookbook and I made the following changes:
Left out bell pepper, used the whole can of tomato paste, 1 can of tomato sauce and 1 cup of water, use 3 T vinegar, onion powder, garlic powder, chili powder, salt, pepper, smokey paprika, and cumin to taste. And finally I used about 2 1/2 lbs of ground beef.  Makes wonderful leftovers!!
I like my sloppy joes to be alittle sweeter so I added quite a bit of BBQ sauce.

This is a good sloppy joe recipe.  My kids love sloppy joes and I've made alot of different recipes and this one rates right up there with the best.  I made this in the camper on vacation and they were very easy to put together, which is a plus in my books.  Thank you for posting.
Yummy recipe-thanks for posting!

Perfect recipe.
I add extra seasoning.
A keeper in my house.
Made this for my clients this week and almost ate the entire thing myself.

Well this is my now go to Sloppy Joe recipe. SO much better then from a package. The last few "from scratch" sloppy Joe Recipes I tried were way too sweet. This was just perfect. I made no adjustments beyond using green instead of red peppers.

This is one of the best sloppy joes I made.  DH really liked this one.  :)  We had it with monterey jack cheese, mustard, relish, hot peppers in a jar.  Really good.  Thanks newspapergal :)  Made for I Recommend tag game
Mmm-mmm, very good!  Spicier than other sloppy joe recipes I've tried--I did add about 3 tsp. of the Montreal Steak Seasoning.  I will definitely make these again.  Thanks!
This was a really easy recipe to prepare and the taste was very good. I will make it again for sure.  Thanks for the recipe.

I made this one day when I was craving sloppy joe's and couldn't find the packet of seasoning like my mother used to use.
We loved this so much, I'll never use the packet again!
I made this exactly as the recipe stated. Very good. I wouldn't change anything.

Hubby asked that I leave this feedback - "keep this in your "go to" for sloppy joes! Best I've ever had". I served on onion rolls with a slice of mild cheddar on top...didn't toast them (too big for toaster) but did butter the bottom (which caused a raised eye brow on hubby but he understood when I told him "that's what Rachel says to do" :) He enjoyed them so much that it's to stay out for a little while so he can have another in an hour or so. TY RR!
Very good and very easy evening meal.
Fantastic recipe!! I've made this vegetarian with veggie "beef" crumbles and even the meat eaters loved it!!
My sister is a vegetable lover supreme.  She thought this was wonderful.  The only thing I did different was to marinate the vegetables for a couple of hours and then grill.

I made this last night, and I was not dissapointed.  I did substitute a grated medium onion for the green onions (didn't have green onions on hand).  I also used non-fat sour cream, non-fat cream cheese, and I used light cheese.  I had a wonderful taste.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.
I made this recipe as is and it was wonderful and rich! Thanks for a great recipe!

Scrumptious! I love the richness and the spark of flavor from the green onions.  I made it for two, so I halved the recipe and I also low-carb'd it (I used 2.5 cups of finely shredded cabbage instead of noodles).  Thanks Bekah for posting this wonderful comfort food recipe!
Sounded weird but yum yum!  Great stuff!
Wow!!  I didn't really know what to expect with this one, but it was wonderful.  TRY THIS RECIPE!!!  You won't regret it!
You must try this recipe!!!!!  It is sooo good.
This was so good.  I made it exactly as directed and was liked by all.  It was so filling and it made so much we had another full meal.  It is good the next day too.  Thanks.
Absolutely wonderful.  A must try casserole and coming from someone who is not crazy about any casserole.  Thanks
Wow, This was great, comfort food at its best!! I did use regular onions as thats all I had on hand, this ones a winner!!
I found the recipe easy to make. I followed the recipe and have decided the next time I fix this dish, I will use 1/2 cup of sour cream and 3 oz. of cream cheese.

Bekah, this is a great casserole! I honestly had my doubts because there didn't seem to be enough spice in it for me. I was wrong! I took a spoon and had a bite of the creamy mixture with the sauce and was really surprised at how good the combo was. Now, I did have one issue with this - and this isn't a deal breaker, but I didn't cover the pan and wish I had because my noodles got a little crunchy on top. The next time, I would cover with foil and remove the foil while the cheese is melting. Oh! I also added a little more cheese since we are cheese freaks. My family loved this and the green onion in the cheese/sour cream mixture is so good! I served this up with some garlic bread and a glass of wine and the guys both had two huge servings. This will be another regular, thanks for sharing!

Very yummy!  I had to make some modifications because I am watching what I eat.  I used 97% ground beef, reduced fat (not "no fat") sour cream, Neufchatel cheese (low fat cream cheese... VERY good if you haven't tried it), No yoke egg noodles.  This turned out very good.  Husband loved it, but asked next time I make it to use a higher amount of tomato sauce.  This might be my fault because I used Rotel and 8 oz of tomato sauce.  Next time I will use the 16 oz of tomato sauce AND the Rotel... Thank you for sharing!

This was tasty - and I agree it is great economical comfort food! I made this recipe exactly as directed, but there was too much of the sour cream mixture and not enough of the tomato mixture for my families taste. We also will increase the amount of noodles next time as well.  Thank you for sharing this interesting and satisfying casserole.

I wouldn't change a thing w/this recipe!  We loved it as is ... It's even better the next night!
I did use reg. onions ...  didn't hurt it at all.
Tis filling, tasty, economical, and just plain good stuff!
Thanks Bekah...This'll be a regular at my house!
Laudee

This made a nice casserole. Followed the recipe exactly other than adding the salt (I used seasoned salt) and pepper to the ground beef when I browned it and I sauteed a diced onion before adding to the cream cheese/sour cream. Very easy recipe with a unique taste. If I made this again, I think I would add some extra tomato sauce as some others suggested. Thanks.

I am sorry to say this was not what I was hoping for, I don't know exactly why it was not a hit here but nobody really cared for it, I think it may have been just to much of the cream cheese sour cream combo, sorry Bekah :(

Since we eat very little red meat, I used ground turkey instead.  I also used regular onions because it was all I had. I was sure I wouldn't like it because of the cream cheese/sour cream combination.  But was I wrong!  This is delicious!  My husband wants it on our menu on a regular basis.  Thanks, Bekah, for a truly filling and tasty meal!
This casserole was delicious. I used light cream cheese and fat free sour cream. Nice and cheesy. I did add some extra tomato sauce. Thanks Bekah
This was pretty good - my son loved it.  I thought it needed more tomato sauce and spices.  I think I'll add Italian seasonings like Basil and Oregano next time.
Loved it and so did my family.  I also used low fat sour cream and neufchatel cheese.  The idea to ad a can of Rotel was a good one and I think I'll try that.
So FREAKIN good !!!!! followed directions to a tee!!!!!! Added parsley to the sour cream but that was it.......  SOOOOOOOOOOO good!!!

Hubby liked this dish while I didn't care for it that much.  It was easy to make but I thought it had too much sour cream/cream cheese.  It reminded me of a stroganoff.  I might try this again but just cut back on the sour cream/cream cheese mixture and maybe add a little more tomato sauce.

I thought this was very good.  My DH really liked it and asked what was in the middle.  I did use only 4oz of cream cheese and an extra 1/2 can of tomato sauce.  I will defintaly be making this again.  It's different from any other cassarole I've had before.
Thanks!  Dad actually did make this easy recipe and it turned out fabulous.  Very tasty and filling.  We are adding this to our "regular favorites" category of recipes.

This was a wonderful recipe, could not be any simpler.  I did take everyone else's advice and used the full amount of tomatoe sauce and a can of rotel and I also added extra cheese on top of the sour cream.  This has a great taste one you would not expect and it feeds a lot.  I cannot wait to make it during the winter I think it will defintely be a great comfort meal.

I see no need for any changes here!  What a great casserole!  I had no egg noodles in the cupboard so I used rotini pasta, which gave the casserole an interesting "twist" ; )  Delightful combination of flavors.  I was tempted to add some parsley or Italian seasoning, but really this recipe didn't need it.  I did however double the cheddar on top simply because we love it : ) I will use the rotini again.  Thanks for a great recipe, ~Bekah~.  We enjoyed it so much!
Great comfort food!  It was delicious and my large family loved it.  Thanks for posting!

Wow!  I don't think I can addd much more to all the wonderful reviews, but this was delicious and so easy to make!  I used fat free sour cream and light cream cheese, and followed the recipe as stated.   Since there's only two of us here, we've got lots of leftovers for tomorrow!  Thanks for sharing this great recipe, ~Bekah~!
This is a really good alternative to your everyday casserole. The cream cheese/sour cream mixture really makes this casserole unique. I will be making this one again!

Wow!  I couldn't believe the explosion of flavors in my mouth when I took the first bite!  This is a favorite with everyone who tried it and I am sure I will make this again.  Didn't change the recipe at all.
Great recipe.  Easy to make, very fast.  I added the can of Rotel, so it was somewhat spicy.  Yum!
I have made this a couple of times already.  My family loves it!  It is so easy to make, and a real comfort food.
This was great, thank you so much for such an easy, wonderful and tasty dinner.  This is a definite keeper.

I made this recipe lastnight and it was fantastic! I am a college student, so I am always looking for something easy, and this was that. I didn't use as much cream cheese (just because I didn't have a lot) and added more shredded cheese. Also I thought there was too much tomato sauce, but once it came out of the oven, it was a firm casserole, not runny at all. Thank you for sharing this recipe with all of us!!!!!

This was good, but I think it had too much sour cream for my taste.  It also reminded my DH too much of Hamburger Helper--he's so hard to please!  Made for pretty good leftovers, although I was the only one eating them.

Great casserole and easy to make.  The kids didn't care for the cream cheese and sour cream mixture, so I will cut back on it the next time.  I  didn't have green onions on hand so used a white onion.   Thanks for posting it Bekah.

DH & I loved this. I halved the sour cream/cream cheese mixture (and added a bit of milk to thin it a little) and threw in a can of Ro-tel, and it was wonderful. I also covered the casserole with aluminum foil while baking to keep the noodles from getting crunchy (thanks Denise!), and then I took the foil off during the last 5 - 10 minutes of baking to let the cheese finish melting. This is easy and quick to make, and I like that it has basic ingredients that I always have on hand. The green onions really make the flavor of this dish, in my opinion. Thanks!
Usually when I ask dh to help me rate a recipe he chimes in with 4.3, 2.6 or something like that. Not today,though. Without hesitation he said 5 stars. You know this must be a very special recipe!

Bekah very easy meal.  Loved the creamy and cheesy sauce. Green onions a must also.  I didn't have enough tomato sauce so I cut up some tomatoes into it.  Also DH liked mozzarella cheese on the top.  Put in a 13x9 pan and family ate it all up. Will definately be making again.
WoW!! Wish I could give this one more *'s!! My husband LOVED it (as did I).  Truly a comfort food.  Super easy to make, and a winner for all.  I will be adding this to our faves!!

Thanks to everyone's advice, we used a whole large jar of spaghetti sauce and a whole bag of egg noodles.
We had leftovers for days, and that's a good thing!  We will be keeping this recipe in heavy rotation.
Thanks, Bekah!

DH said to give this 5 *'s and I agree! Very easy and yummy! I didn't have green onions so I sauteed a small yellow onion with the ground beef and garlic, and I did cover with foil while baking. I took the foil off and covered with 2 cups of  cheese as we both LOVE cheese! The sour cream/cream cheese mixture makes this so rich it's just heavenly! There's tons for leftovers...I brought some in to work to share and they all agreed...this is some kinda wonderful!

Sorry we did not enjoy this one at all.  Had to throw it out, sadly.  The cream cheese was strong and clumpy and there just wasn't much flavor to it.  I did substitute canned tomatoes for the tomato sauce and omitted the green onion.  So that could have been part of the problem.

I had heard several people rave about this recipe, but hadn't taken the time to look at it.  Today, I saw it mentioned again and decided to take a peek.  What do you know?!?  It is the same recipe that I have been using for years, but called "Hamburger Noodle Hotdish".  LOL  I found this recipe in a cookbook that I received as a gift at my wedding shower.  Hubby loves this.  I consider it a stand-by recipe.  It is easy and tasty.  The leftovers re-warm well, too.  Thanks for posting, and sorry that it took me so long to check out this recipe.LOL
Ok but not something I will make again. This is very hamburger helperish. If you like that...you'll like this.

By reading the recipe i could tell it had more dairy in it than our family would like, so i cut back the cheeses and sour cream quite a lot. Even so we still found it to be too rich. It is a nice quick and easy family-comfort-food recipe though, so I might try it again, cutting the sour cream/cheese down to half (or less) of what the recipe suggests.
I liked this dish but it was too much cream cheese for us.  I would use more shredded cheese and a whole lot less cream cheese.
Comfort food to the max! Very good Bekah! The only change I made was using crushed tomatoes instead of tomatoe sauce, but it was still great. Weall loved it!
everyones fav, people ask me to share it. Way to go on making a best seller :)

This was so good!  And so very, very rich from the cream cheese...this will definitely be a keeper around here!  I had no problems with my noodles getting crunch on top as a previous reviewer did.  I just made sure the sauce covered the second layer of noodles completely.
Hubby liked it but kids did not like the cream cheese layer (I don't no what is wrong with them??). I made the recipe as written. Great with salad and garlic bread.
Excellent. Even better as leftovers.Thanks for a great recipe.
This has got to be one of the best recipes I've ever come across!  I've made it every month since I've found it! Excellence at it's best!

Loved this. I also would reduce some of the sour cream/and cream cheese, and I am glad that I went with a large jar of marinara sauce. There's no way I think of hamburger helper while eating this. Very tasty and economical. Thank you.
Really good. This is one of our new favourites. Only chllenge was to use the metric system, it came out a little dry. But will only add some minor adjustments next time

I was preoccupied and before I realized what I was doing I had added the tomato sauce to the hamburger (oops) so I ended up adding all the ingredients together, rather than layering than topped it with cheese. I would cut back the cream cheese amt. next time, this was very good-but too rich for us.
Thanks Bekah-
Total comfort food!  I did not add the sugar, other than that I followed the recipe exactly.  My husband kept saying TASTEY!  I will definitely make this again and again.
This was ok.  I only used 1/2 the cream cheese and it still tasted like too much.  Maybe substitute the cream cheese with ricotta?  Also, next time I would mix the whole thing together and then bake.

This was really good and simple for a cold winters night.  I used a whole jar of garlic and herb spag sauce, and seasoned the meat with salt, pepper, and italian herb. Next time I will start with some spag sauce as my first layer under the noodles, and my husband and I both agree that some jalapenos would give it a nice kick.

This was really good. I used ground turkey instead of beef and seasoned it with garlic powder, salt, oregano, and some roast beef seasoning. I added 2 tablespoons of sugar (misread the ingredients) and used light sour cream and light cream cheese. I also used 2 cups of cheese, because we just love cheese. Turned out great! Thanks for the recipe.

This was good, but I probably won't make it again.  I felt that it needed more tomato sauce and a little less of the cream cheese mixture.  The cream cheese/sour cream mixture really seemed to overwhelm the other flavors in my opinion and I would definitely cut back on that the next time I made it.  I would also add just a little more tomato sauce.  Thanks for sharing!

I love this dish.  I made it for my parents when they came home from a long trip and they devoured it.  i use extra sauce when i make mine...'cause i like my dishes gooey.  this dish is so good.  don't skim on the green onions...they are pivitol to the final taste.  this is one of my favourite dishes.  SO VERY GOOD!!!

I was true to the recipe (I did double it however) and I do not think I would change a thing! I did bake it covered and I think it helped keep it nice and moist. Simple to make. It is a wonderful comfort food with a great combination of flavors!

I made a double batch of this and it was almost polished off by the end of our meal.  But then how can you go wrong with pasta and cream cheese...lol.  I will be making this often.  It was so simple to put together and had a fantastic flavor...thank you.....Stephanie
this had a nice flavor but it did not blend well maybe next time i will just mix it all together i think for my tastes it would be better thank for the recipe
This recipe was easy to make, and my son loved it, but I didn't paticularly care for it.  I think it might have been better if I used tomato soup instead of the sauce.  Thanks for the recipe though.
yummy. I only had white onions, and I cute the cream cheese in response to the feedback. but it was great. thanks!

Another 5 stars.  I did follow the suggestions and only used 1/2 cup sour cream and 4 ounces of cream cheese.  It was really good.  The green onions gave it a suprising flavor.  It was really good!!!  I also used low fat cream cheese and low fat sour cream and you couldn't tell :) !!!  Also, I double batched it and put the other half in a ziplock freezer bag to eat later on down the road.  Hopefully that will be equally good!!!

This was very good, I made it pretty much as directed, ecxept I used a heartier pasta, because I was afraid the egg noodles wouldn't hold up to the heavier sauces. The only other change I think I will make next time, is I think I will saute the green onions before adding them. I don't like a crunchy onion in a dish like this, and it also mellows the flavors a bit. But it was a very easy and tasty dinner, Thanks for Posting Bekah!
This was a great dish!!!  It was really good.  Next time I will try it with some mushrooms and extra cheese.

I made this recipe last night and everyone "loved" it. I did make some alterations to suit my taste. I didnt have fresh garlic so I used minced garlic. I also used 1 1/2lbs. of lean groundbeef and 24 oz. of Prego sauce because it has a delicious mix of flavor and spices which balanced the cream sauce. One more thing, I added mushrooms that cooked for 4 minutes and added it with the cheese topping. I can't believe how wonderful it turned out. Great for sneaking in veggies for the kids. Thanks for the great recipe.
This recipe seems to have an identity crisis...it doesn't know if it is stroganoff or spaghetti.  I really didn't care for the combo and won't make it again.  My husband thought it was ok.

Threw this together for dh to have for dinner tonight.  He really enjoyed it!  From the taste I had, I loved it as well.  Looking forward to my helping for lunch tomorrow.  Thanks for sharing Bekah.  I am not sure why someone would think this has an identity crisis- to me this is good, old fashioned comfort food.  Yum!
bad too much sour cream and cream cheese yuck
This was pretty good. I will add a little more seasonings next time but I will be making this again. Thanks!
Since I didn't have any sour cream on hand, I just took a whole 8 ounce block of cream cheese and melted it into the sauce.  It came out delicious!  I also mixed in some mozzarella with the cheddar.
This is DELICIOUS!  I make it about twice a month and it is gone within a day.  I often omit ground beef and it is very good this way also!

The kids loved this dish!  I am impressed with it's versatility.  Depending on the spices, it can be either Italian or Mexican.  For a Tex-Mex version, I plan to add chili powder, maybe some cumin, oregano, and a little cocoa to the tomato sauce/rotel tomato mixture.  For an Italian flair, I plan to add Ricotta cheese to the cream cheese (no sour cream) mixture.  I will use spaghetti sauce in place of the tomato sauce and top with mozzarella cheese.  Thanks for a great recipe Beka!

We liked it, the kids ate it well. It's not really to our normal dinner tastes, but it WAS good. It's very similar to a pasta dish with Gouda cheese that I have so in a lot of ways it tasted, to me, like I forgot the best part of my dish!

Thanks for sharing!  I made a couple of adjustments because I didnt want to run out to the store and it was still great!  I used Garlic powder instead of cloves and I cooked a half of sweet onion with the hamburger instead of green onions.  For my family tastes I will only use half of the cream cheese and sour cream mixture next time.  We thought it was too rich with all of it.  Will make it again!
This recipe wasn't too bad, but it waasn't too great either for my husband and I. It was just okay, I think I'll try other casserole recipes before I come back to this one.
I have to give it only 3 stars as I was the only one in the family that liked it.
Yum, yum and yum!  I didn't have tomato sauce so I used a can of petite diced tomatoes cooked down.  It turned out delicious!

This is really great comfort food. I read other reviews about the cream cheese being too strong but I decided to cook the recipe "as is" and it turned out great.  DH loved it and so did my picky 6 yr. old son. A half cup more tomato sauce added to the recipe will balance out the richness of the cheese/sour cream mixture for those that think this is too rich tasting.

Very good flavor and easy to fix.  Although I just skimmed the instructions and put the cream cheese on top instead of in between the layers of noodles and meat.  It was still delish.  My husband, too, said it reminded him of Hamburger Helper, only much much better.

Mixed reviews in the family. Hubby really, really liked it (unusual), eldest son didn't like it at all, I thought it was ok & my youngest ate it ok.  I'm giving it a 4 star rating because of my husband- it's not often he tells me he really likes something without me even asking.

Easy to put together for a weeknight meal!  My family also had mixed reviews.  The biggest complaint was too much sour cream.  I will definitely make it again and just cut back on the sour cream and cream cheese mixture. Will also throw in some black olives too!
A  definite "man pleaser", and easy too. It's now in the "tried and true" keeper list.

This is fabulous. Both my husband and my three kids loved it. This was so easy to make and pretty basic ingriedients. I was excpecting a lasagna flavor but it was really different. I didn't have any tomato sausce so I used 1 small can of tomato paste and 1 lg can of diced tomatoes that were pre seasoned with oregno and basil. It gave it a good hearty feel.
I am adding more stars!!! This is my husbands absolute favorite meal of all time!!! Thank you, Thank you thank you!!!

Very good meal.  Made this at the last minute after I decided I didn't want leftovers and it came together so fast.  I used a 9x9 square dish and it worked great.  Definitely a different flavor than I was expecting.  My DH loved it!  I have a feeling this would freeze really well too.  I'm looking forward to having it for lunch tomorrow.  It is a little rich, but with a side salad it is a great homecooked dinner.

I am always looking for new recipes for ground beef, and this one blew me away, I loved it! Even my fussy 7 year old daughter loved it so much. I had no green onions so I added regular instead, and it was fabulous! Thank you for sharing!!!

ALERT, ALERT casserole snobs - this recipe is real Southern comfort food.  Yum!  Easy to prepare, easy on the budget and should be served at anyone's table. I used ground turkey, added a little more garlic and was short on quantity of sour crm and crm cheese, so I supplemented Queso Fresca, heated red and white mixtures together, stirred in noodles and topped w/ cheddar. Baked for 20 mins. Thank you for sharing :D

This casserole sure was delicious!  Very easy and fast to whip up.  It made great leftovers as well!  I didnt have enough egg noodles, so I used penne pasta.  I did think the tomato mixture needed more seasonings during cooking.  So I added in some garlic and onion powder, italian seasoning, a little more sugar, and basil.  Also I thought the hamburger mix was a little dry so I added in a thing of diced tomatoes to give it more sauce and texture.  Put all together and baked, this was great!  I cant wait to make again and have some crusty garlic bread with this.  How much easier can this be!  Thanks for the recipe!

This was so simple, tasty and filling.   (And cheap!)  Next time I make it, I will experiment with decreasing the cream cheese/sour cream mixture and increasing the amount of tomato sauce, as it was a bit rich for our family.  But it was delicious!  And great for kids.
Waaaayyyy too much sour cream and cream cheese!  It is all you taste... Yuck!

I tried this recipe to use up some egg noodles I had.  I loved this and think it would be great with the addition of a can of corn.  I did not use all the cream cheese to try and cut down on the richness other reviewers had mentioned.  My hubby and kids did not like it at all but then again they are not fans of egg noodles.

I have to agree with others. Making the recipe exactly as written my family thought there was WAY too much sour cream/cream cheese.  I might try it again and 1/2 the mixture and see if I can up my rating.

I have been making this recipe for a while now.  I cut the recipe in half but use the full amount of ground beef and tomato sauce.  I only use 2 oz. cream cheese, and 1/4 cup sour cream.  I mix the noodles with the tomato sauce mixture, put layer of noodle mixture on bottom, spread with cream cheese mixture, add layer of cheddar cheese, more noodle mixture and top with cheddar cheese.  Sometimes I add yellow onion to ground beef instead of the green onion.  I bake covered for 20 minutes and then uncover and bake for 10 more minutes.  Serve with garlic bread.
This recipe is a favorite of mine, but the first time I made it there was a bit too much sour cream/cream cheese so now I just cut that part in half and it's perfect! It makes a great family meal!

This was very good! My husband loved it! I read the comments about people halving the cream cheese and sour cream but went for the full amount instead of halving it and it was great for us. The only thing i think i would changes was use spagetti instead...the egg noodles are a little thin for the sauce. Other than that it was great. Thanks for the recipe!
We thought the sour cream/cream cheese combo was a lil too powerful. Not for everyone....
Wow this was good. Have had it before with cottage cheese for the cream cheese but I think this way is even better. Excellent- thanks!
For minimal ingredients this tasted great.
These potatoes were really great tasting. Thanks *That Girl*....

I had a recipe similar to this at a bridal luncheon I recently attended and really wanted the recipe but was told it was a family secret. So I found this recipe on Zaar and I think it's almost, if not, the same thing. I halved the recipe for my husband and I and added a little garlic. I'll probably make this for holiday events this year since it can be made ahead and reheated. Thanks for sharing a  great recipe!
The potatoes were dry and uninteresting. It was not difficult to make and it was nice not to have to mash potatoes at the last minute.
Came out dry and nothing special.

These were great and saved my behind on Christmas, when I tried to make as much as I could the day before.  I used a bit more butter than the recipe did, just based on personal taste.  They were great and GONE at the end of the meal.  I will definately make these again.
These potatoes are great.  I used 8 oz. cream cheese.  It's nice to be able to make these ahead, especially during the holidays.
I used 8 oz. cream cheese also, other than that followed the directions exactly & they couldn't have been better. Chives & cheeder on top would make a nice addition, but not really needed.
Made these for Thanksgiving.  Made one change. I mashed the potatoes with some milk (not in the recipe).  I did everythinge else as written. They were wonderful and I will always make them this way.

Simple potatoes with wonderful flavor.  I whipped these in my Kitchenaide for the creamest potatoes ever.  I added the butter with the cream cheese and sour cream, but didn't add more when reheating.  I did keep covered until dinner was almost ready to serve and removed the casserole lid only for the last 5-10 minutes.

I made these for thanksgiving this year the night before to help save time the day of.  I enjoyed them, but dh didn't.  He said that they had an "odd" taste.  I think that next time I will use a little less cream cheese & that might help.  Thanks so much for sharing!
Mmm... these potatoes are so good.
This was an excellent recipe- made it for Thanksgiving this year (2 days ahead) and everyone loved it.  Thanks for posting!

These potatoes were great!  I only made 3 pounds of potatoes.  I used 4 oz of cream cheese and halved the rest of the ingredients.  I also used a clove of garlic when cooking the potatoes and then stirred in 1 cup of cheese crumbles right before putting the potatoes in the casserole dish.  I topped with crumbled bacon.  This recipe is a life saver when putting together a meal for company!
Easy to make and delicous! What a great time saver on Thanksgiving day!
Man, were these ever good!  Creamy and flavorful- Yum!
I made this recipe after searching for a good alternative to plain mashed potatoes. Loved it! It was even good before it had been baked. Thanks for sharing such a wonderful recipe!

add 1cup shredded chedder, 1 bunch green onions chopped,3/4tbs basil, 1tbs garlic 1tbs smoked paprika, 10 slices crisp bacon,1/2tsp red pepper flakes, 1tsp cajun seasoning, and you have some really killer spuds, i have people offering to pay me to make them for them

These are very good. I used onion and chive cream cheese(that's what I had).  They turned out great.  Everyone loved them.  With the left overs, I topped them w/cheddar and parm. cheese and baked again. Very yummy!
Thought these potatoes were great!! It was wonderful making them ahead of time...less stress the day of the meal.

We really enjoyed these.Mine were a little lumpy so I'll add a little hot milk to get my cheap beaters to work or use my kitchen aid. They were still really good. Next time I will add a couple of garlic cloves to the water just to change it up a bit.

OH MY WORD!!  These were great.  I halfed the recipe. I used onion powder instead of onion salt (what I had in the cabinet).  I also added some dried minced onion and a very small amount of skim milk to account for the dried onions.  I also used red potatoes and cooked them whole and used my potatoe ricer.  These is an awesome recipe, I can see it being used many times to come.
I am new to this site and tried this as my first recipe. We were having a church potluck and I wanted to take something great. These truly are GREAT. So creamy and good. Thanks!!!
This is a truly great recipe!  The family just love these potatoes.  Will definitely be making them again.  Thanks for sharing.

I made this yesterday and we all really enjoyed it.  Even my 17 year old son who is very picky when it comes to potatoes (is there any other kind than french fries??).  The only thing I changed was adding a little milk to mash them with and I sprinkled a little cheddar cheese on top.
Very convenient and something we will  have again.
Yummy and easy.  Makes a nice dense serving of mashed potatoes.  I only made a couple of hours ahead, but it was nice to get them out of the way.  Thanks!

I made these potatoes for our early Thanksgiving dinner, and it was a big hit! I prepared them about three days in advance, and the taste was wonderful! I used fat free cream cheese and sour cream. I omitted the regular salt, just using the onion salt, and it was fine. So nice not to have to be peeling and cooking potatoes while everyone else is having fun! Thanks again..Hazeleyes
These can be made several days ahead of time.  Put them in a crock pot and cook them on low for 5 hours.  My variation omits the onion salt but includes 1/4 cup crisp bacon, crumbled.

Made this for a family get together and everyone said how much they liked the potatoes fixed this way. I really liked that they could be prepared ahead of time. It's a keeper. 

Thanks "That Girl"

Bullwinkle.
I have been making these for years every Christmas and Thanksgiving.  What an excellent time-saver/stress free side dish for a crowd!

These tasted very good.  The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars was that they kind of solidified and I had to fluff them up prior to serving.  But, I'll definitely be using this recipe again and again! Thanks!

This is another recipe I have been making up for years.  I got it out of the Best of Bridge series.  I like the fact that this dish can be made up ahead of time....freeing up last minute prep work.  They turn out light and fluffy...perfect for Christmas/Thanksgiving

Wow!!!!  These were wonderful.  I normally make my mom's recipe which is very plain but yummy.  Everyone gave me a fit when I said that I was trying a new recipe but were very happy when they tasted them.  They said that I can make these sometimes but still like the other way too.
These are wonderful! Thank you for posting! :)

I usually cook 10 lbs of potatoes for our big Sunday dinner. I doubled this recipe and made it the day before.  It was fabulous and made clean up so much easier.  I served it with prime rib and yorkshires and rich gravy. It really simplified preparation before dinner and clean up afterward.

I make these potatoes a lot -- and they always come out great.  It's so nice not to have to worry about cooking and mashing potatoes at the last minute.  I've also put them in the crockpot -- place the crock in the fridge and then popped it in the warming unit about 3 hours before they are to be served.  I was going to post the recipe -- but found out it was already here -- and getting great reviews!!!!
This is the BEST mashed potatoes I have ever had! I used garlic and chive cream cheese- YUM! Thanks!
worked great.  usd a crockpot to reheat and keep them warm.  i did omit the onion salt as i had none.  first time at making mashed potatoes.  thanks for sharing.

These were fantastic.  I thought they might be too heavy with the cream cheese and sour cream (because to me, standard mashed potatoes are heavy enough when the rest of the meal is rich) but I needed a reliable do-ahead for Thanksgiving.  Since I had never made these before, "reliable" was trusting the comments and ratings, and I'm glad I did. I ran out of room in the oven to heat these up before the meal and ended up microwaving. They still tasted like freshly mashed potatoes, not too overpowering, and everyone loved them.  I will make these again next year.  Thank you That Girl, and all the commenters too!

This is a rich but very good recipe!  P.S. ... I don't really like when people take a very good recipe like this (37 reviews and nearly 5 star average) and then tell everyone how they changed the recipe to make it their way.  And then sometimes they don't even rate the recipe.  Very strange.
I just loved these potatoes...made them for 21 people for Thanksgiving and this recipe was perfect...will make every year.

I made these to go along with steaks in mushroom sauce.  This was well liked and gobbled up in no time.  I like the fact that these can be made up ahead of time and wait until needed.  Fabulous idea, I plan on using this recipe for Easter dinner.  Thank you for posting.
Absolutely excellent!  Everyone keeps asking for it!
Delish! Simple and easy and wonderful that they can be made ahead. Thanks *That Girl* for a new keeper. Made for Cookbook Tag.
These are so creamy and delicious - I will definitely keep for Christmas

These are the most awesome and delicious potatoes ever.  I've been making these for years.  It's such a help at holiday time to make them the day before (or even 2 days ahead).  Creamy, delicious!  I've also added an egg white before baking on occasion for extra creaminess.  I've also heated them in the crockpot to save oven space on holidays. Thanks for posting - seems like every time I make them I have to check the cream cheese - sour cream ratio.

Thank you for a great dish! Took this as my contribution to our family's get together and it went over well. Made it Thanksgiving morning since it was all I had to cook. Put it in my crock pot ceramic dish in the oven for 30 minutes before we left and while at their house I kept the crock pot plugged in to stay warm. I had to omit the onion salt since I didn't have any but will buy some specifically for this dish next time. Thought about adding garlic salt but decided against it. I am sure garlic would be good with this but some people might not like garlic so I played it safe. Turned out a winner!  Oh, I had to add a lot of milk to get it mixed nice and creamy.  I've never made mashed potatoes with russets before and they seemed way too dry without the milk.  Will start making mashed potatoes with russets from now on though.
A real hit!  This is slight different from what I've made in the past. I made enough for 16 but should have made even more as they were just scarfed down. A true winner!

I made these last year for Thanksgiving and forgot to leave my rave review!  Made it again this year with just as much success.  These are fantastic . . . . I think the onion salt gives them the perfect zing.  An outstanding recipe that saves me so much time in the kitchen on the big day.
Like the 47 reviewers before me, I thought these were great.  They are loved by everyone and the convenience factor makes this recipe a keeper for those big holiday meals.

These make-ahead mashed potatoes were AWESOME!!!! I made them a day ahead and served them for Christmas Eve. My Guests LOVED them! What a great blend of flavor with the cream cheese, sour cream and onion salt. Very easy to make.  Would recommend recipe to all! Guests were still talking about them the next day at Christmas!

I made this twice, once with russets and once with gold yukons, and it is definitely better with the russets.  I made it the night before, stored it in the crockpot insert in the fridge. I cannot believe that I haven't rated this yet. I made it a few times and we all LUV it. I just made it again for thanksgiving and what a life saver it was to precook it. I make it exactly as stated, only change is use 1/2 cup sour cream, and will do that every time. Thank you for a wonderful easy recipe.

This dish is just simply delicious.  I love the fact that I can make this the day before and just pop it in the oven the next day.  The flavors come together so much.  What a great time saver for Thanksgiving day.  Thanks for this wonderful recipe.
Just made this for Turkey day - I have to travel 4 hours with all turkey dinner and this is the Bomb it is yummmm and can't wait to serve it - made 10 lbs thanks for the post

OK - I wanted to make mashed potatoes ahead for Thanksgiving, so tried these a few weeks ago. Delicious.  I also froze some to try them out.  Reheated in the microwave, stirred well, and could not believe how good.  So....I cooked 30 POUNDS of potatoes, mixed in several batches, and froze them in Ziploc bags. Sure enough, on Thanksgiving, my son said, "These are the best mashed potatoes you have ever made", so I handed him a couple of bags to take home to enjoy! A Thanksgiving regular recipe in my house now. Thanks for sharing.

Excellent.  I make something every similar during the Holidays.  I liked the addition of the sour cream.  Something you can't enjoy very often, but is always a crowd pleaser.  I made 1/2 the recipe for the 2 of us with left-overs for my son to take home tomorrow.  Thanks for sharing.  :)

This recipe is an old standard at our house; made as everyday fare or fancy company dinners.  It's an easy travelling potato dish and make-ahead recipe, enjoyed by everyone who tastes its complementary flavors.  I sprinkle a bit of paprika on top for added color.
Very yummy potatoes.  Will make these more often.  Thanks for posting.
Both easy and fantastic.  A great recipe anytime you entertain.

I have made this previously but evidentally I did not review. This is a GREAT recipe. The finished product is delicious and if made ahead it saves a ton of stress the day of the dinner. I will certainly be using this again at Thanksgiving. I made the recipe exactly as written. I do prefer to make it a day or two ahead, put it in the crockpot then turn on low about 4 to 6 hours prior to dinner. This time I re-heated in the over for 45 minutes which was not long enough. I had to microwave in two batches to get it to the serving temperature. Thanks for posting.

I made these potatoes last year at christmas. At first my husband was a little worried about messing with the potatoes. After trying these he said those were the best potatoes ever and he even requested them this year!

Made for the Football Pool 2012 game.  We loved this dish!  It is really good for people who don't like a lot of tomatoes.  I added some diced onions with the peppers and ground beef to our dish.  Thanks for posting!

This was a real treat. The health numbers aren't horrible as written but I'm forever trying to keep them as low as possible. It all came out YUM!. Made as a bonus in Photo Tag.

This is very hearty and I loved the bacon flavor.  Made the entire recipe of sauce and only half of the pasta along with half of the sauce.  The other half of the sauce made it's way to the freezer for a quick meal on a busy night.  Thanks for posting this loof.  Made for 1~2~3 Hits.

This recipe is amazing.  The sauce is great.  I loved the smell of the bacon and the taste.  So addictive.  I used red bell pepper.  A little bit more tomato sauce to not waste and added a little more water.  I used fresh mushrooms (8 ounces), omitted the salt.  Thanks Loof :)  Made for PRMR tag game

With the bacon, garlic, and green pepper, this is very reminiscent of the stuffed bell peppers we've enjoyed for years. It's not your standard Italian spaghetti sauce! We did bake it as instructed, but I think it would have been good if the sauce had been simply served over the spaghetti, too.  Made as a prize in Top Favorites of 2009.

The bacon and mushrooms add so much to the flavor!  I used shell pasta and fresh mushrooms.  I also left out the salt, because the bacon and cheese added enough saltiness.  A delicious, hearty casserole.  Made for Please Review My Recipe Tag.

This was delicious!!
The smell while it was cooking was quite delectable...and it was all I could do to stop myself loading up a spoon there and then and indulging in all of that smoky,meaty yumminess.
I also used fresh mushrooms,and subbed mozzarella for the provolone.
We really enjoyed this,and I am led to believe that the leftovers were good too...the non pasta loving DH snaffled them for his lunch!!
Thanks loof...this is a keeper!

Adding the bacon really changed our regular spaghetti.I used fresh mushroom and garlic. The kithen didn't smell like I was cooking spaghetti.so it's a great dish to fool the family.Thanks for sharing.

Wonderful!  DS just loved this...I had to leave out the green pepper, and only added mushroom to half because of DS, but it was wonderful just as I made it!  I did use fresh minced garlic instead of garlic powder.  We really loved this!  DS is taking the recipe back to college with him to try and impress his roommates!  Thanks for sharing.

FANTASTIC!!!  Though I left out the green pappers, and used whole wheat pasta, this is full of flavors.  The bacon and mushrooms really increased the flavor to this.  Loved the sauce too. An all around a  recipe .  Made for PRMR tag.

What a hearty spaghetti dish!!!  I made this using fresh mushrooms and some minced onion which I cooked along with the ground beef.  I left out the green pepper, family preference.  I loved the addition of the bacon, what isn't better with bacon, lol!!!  For the cheese, I used a combination of provolone and mozzarella cheeses for a great dinner!!!  Thanks Loof!!  Made for Stars Tag Game.
Was thinking about wrapping myself all up in slippery spaghetti.  Please don't jump to judging another's mania too quickly.  Try the recipe.  Made for #48 A-NZ Recipe Tag.

Lovely smokey, comfort food! I had my doubts - i thought the bacon would make the whole thing too rich, that there wasn't enough sauce for the amount of noodles, yada, yada, yada, Silly me, it all balanced out just right. DH loved that the dish tasted smokey but not obvious that it was from bacon. This isn't an over saucy dish but that keeps it from being overwhelming . YUM! This is so good! I made as posted with the exception of cutting the recipe in half and using fresh mushrooms. We loved the cheese combination. This very well may be the only way I make spaghetti in the future. (except for the quick jar/spaghetti for emergencies). Loved it! Can;t wait for the leftovers. Thanks for posting. :)

Have made this a couple of times now as we were getting bored of bolognese in our house. It does make a generous amount, but is a really tasty and simple to prepare meal. I left out the mushrooms as I am the only one in the house that eats them. This will be a regular on our midweek meal planner now, thanks for posting.

"GREAT COMFORT FOOD INDEED" A great new way for an all time favorite dish. I forgot to cover while baking but it didn't affect the out come. Next time I will use spaghetti, this is a keeper and will go into my "Best of 2012 Cookbook" and made often. Thanks!
Super fast and easy to put together.  I left out the green peppers but otherwise made as written. The bacon gave it a nice salty flavor.  Made for Zaar Stars.

Made for your Football Pool win & I love this pasta dish too. *Made for 2012 Football Pool*
Very good! I skipped the mushrooms but otherwise made as directed. Wonderful dinner! Thanks for sharing!

This had such a wonderful flavor with the added bacon.  However, I did use tomato sauce with basil and garlic which added a lot of flavor I think that otherwise would have been missed.  I made half the recipe for the two of us with plenty of leftovers for the weekend. I wish I had doubled the bacon since I added double the sauce.  The flavors were so good and DH loved it.  I'll be making this again   Thanks loof.
Excellent easy recipe that is quite filling. I used thai basil, homemade ricotta and a green bell pepper but it still looked pretty good. Tastes delicious too.
These were good. Kinda time-consuming and messy though.

Talk about chili dogs with the works. This is the best as far as my husband and I are concerned. I put everything in the crockpot in the afternoon. It was ready right on time for dinner. The chili cheese sauce is to die for. We used all the toppings. I especially liked the corn chips. Great all-American food. Thanks.
These were great!  My family loved the crunch of the corn chips with the soft gooey chili dogs.  It was so simple to make - my five year old helped and was so proud of himself.  A definate winner!
These were great!!!  So simple to just mix everything together and toss into the crockpot, and the results were fabulous!

The men in my family love chili dogs. This recipe was so easy and delicious, that I am now also a fan. I liked just adding the ingredients to the crock-pot and walking away. Definitely easy, which is a plus, but, I thought they pretty much tasted like chili dogs.  My family liked them, but I think I was expecting something maybe a little cheesier.  Maybe 2 cans of cheese soup?  Don't get me wrong, everyone had a great time eating these and piled on the chili and toppings.  They were really good, just not exactly what I expected.

We had our first cool evening last night and for some reason, it made me crave chili dogs. From now on, this is the ONLY way I will make them. The method was  easy and the flavor was as good as it gets. The chips were a good idea. Thanks Nurse Di.

As far as chili dogs go, these were pretty tasty and filled the craving I had for them on a chilly night. Mine were more than ready to eat in 4 hours in my 5 quart crockpot. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

These were very good and a nice change from the usual crockpot meals. We served the chips seperately and skipped the onions but topped the hot dogs with the shredded cheese. Delicious! Thanks for sharing!

Very tasty chili dogs. But what I loved most was the convenience. Put everything in the crockpot and then get on about your business. Got the family's approval, too. When you want a good chili dog, this is the way to go, imho. Thanks.
Nice change from ordinary hotdogs. Only had 1 can chili so used some coney sauce I had in the freezer. More than enough sauce for 1 pkg wieners - next time will throw in another pkg.

Thanks, Di, for a great crockpot family meal!

Yum--will probably never make chili dogs any other way-DH loved them! Made the full recipe of sauce, but only 1/2 pack of hots for 2 of us.  Put some of the sauce on fried potatoes, also great.  Saving the rest for burgers later in the week.

Best chili dogs yet!

So easy and the kids didn't even complain!  What more could a mother ask for!  Thanks Di for the quick and easy dinner for a busy mom.  Can't wait to try another of your amazing recipes!
Very good recipe.  One that would please just about anyone.  I think the canned cheese just made it.    Thanks for posting this recipe.

This was so easy and tasted great, i love using my crockpot every chance i get, i bought my oldest son a crockpot to take to college, so i'll be sending him this recipe, i always send him recipes that taste great and are quick and easy. Thanks NurseDi.

Yummo!  Everyone enjoyed these.  Made exactly as written.  I think next time, I'll skip the slow cooker because it watered down my chili sauce a bit.

Easy recipe! i thru everything in before i left for the day and my bf had chilli dogs waiting for him

How yummy and easy - not to mention it happens to be cheap! We don't eat meat, so I used smeat dogs and meatless chili. I actually cut the hot dogs up and just poured this over toast with cheese on top - would make a good fork sandwich!
Very tasty chili dog! Quick, easy and the sauce tastes great on a burger (topped with american cheese and grilled onion). Thanks for posting!

Great recipe, my husband kept saying, you have to make these again.
