The only way i do broccoli now! Good without pine nuts, too.  Even the most picky carnivores LOVE this! Will make for years to come THX!
Excellent. I beiieve all has been said about this great dish.  Won't want to eat plain steamed Broccoli  after tasting this dish. A repeat is in order for this recipe.

Very nice and tasty broccoli dish!  The pine nuts and lemon made a really nice addition to this dish.  I paired this tonight with recipe #334683 and recipe #65469.  Was a great combination.  Will definitely make this again.
This is delicious!!  Yummy!!  I made this with recipe #95376 and red skin mashed potatoes.  It was such a simple and easy meal to prepare, but really great flavor and textures.  Thanks!!

Add me to the list of fans! My broccoli florets were a little big, so I'd probably roast them a couple more minutes.  I melted the butter in a wok pan, so it made tossing easy and kept the broccoli warm while other dishes were served.
This was a great side with Recipe #238069 and garlic mashed potatoes.  I loved the lemon, which gave it a really refreshing taste.The kids even liked it, which is a miracle!
Fabulous!  This is a definite keeper.  I used toasted almond slices instead of pine nuts and it was divine!
Great broccoli.  I served it with Recipe #123947 and Recipe #159894.  Great combination of flavors.

This was a nice side to a lime baked Tilapia dish that I made.  I used a combination of broccoli floret and broccoli rabe.  I parboiled the broccoli rabe (not the florets) first for 6 minutes to remove the bitterness before roasting.  I ended up liking the rabe prepared this way even a little more than the florets!  This tasted great.  We used 1.5 Tb of lemon, but would probably scale it back to 1 Tb next time.  I added a little more garlic and used salted butter.  I thought the pine nuts gave the dish an especially nice touch.  I will definitely make this recipe again.  Thanks for posting!
So So good and EASY to make -didn't change anything at all and will definatly make this again

I served this for the first time for my parents for Sunday dinner.  The whole family enjoyed it.  The broccoli stays crunchy while the pine nuts, lemon, and garlic add a nice flavor.  This was also very simple to make and easy to add to the oven while other food was cooking.  Very nice recipe!
Love it!!!  Used oil instead of butter and it was awesome!
I tried this recipe when MeanChef was still on the site. I suppose I never rated it, but this broccoli is awesome! I have made this sooooo many times and love it every time.
I've made this recipe LOTS...even those who don't like broccoli love it! My family asks for it when we all get together for dinner.
Yummy!  I made this for Christmas dinner.  I used walnuts because I didn't have any pine nuts.  We all loved it!  I'll definitely make this again and again.
This was very tasty.  I used almonds instead of pine nuts and it turned out great.  Thank you!

Fantastic recipe, an interesting and flavorful way to cook broccoli! I didn't have the pine nuts so I left those out, and used bottled lemon juice instead of fresh, but it still turned out delicious. I will be making this again.
We really enjoyed this recipe.  Loved how easy it was to make.  A KEEPER FOR SURE!!
Lovely way to make broccoli. I tasted it before adding the lemon juice and I liked it better without.
This a a great broccoli recipe.  The lemon gives it a lovely flavor.  I will be making this again.

I made this for a family gathering a few nights ago and everyone loved it!!  I have to say that it was fantastic even before I added the lemon sauce and to be perfectly honest next time I make it ill toss the broccoli with the oil and then sprinkle with salt, pepper, and garlic like i did before and then bake and eat it, it was fantastic just doing that.. although it was also amazing with the lemon sauce on it paired with the shrinp scampi we were also having, I would only be omiting the lemon butter sauce to save the calories..

Made this last week and I thought it was the best broccoli ever!  I served this over a bed of rigatoni.  I MUCH prefer it without the lemon garlic sauce (no pine nuts, allergy).  I served the sauce on the side as I have picky eaters in the house.  My husband had no idea that sauce was for the broccoli and instead used it over his pork chops.  He said it was to die for, and told me to make it for pork chops from now on.  LOL. Bought a bunch of broccoli and will be making it again tonight for the family.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I liked the texture of the broccoli very much as same of the combination with pinenuts.
I did not know that was possible to prepare broccoli directly in the oven and I tried out roast the pinenuts together at the same time. Come out perfect and I would do it again!
Thanks a lot for this yummy recipe and teachint!
Very quick and easy - and tasty. Roasted broccoli was such a great change of pace from the usual. I didn't add any nuts at the end, just out of personal preference. Thank you!
So delicious! I highly recommend this.
Excellent - the family loved this, teens included :)
Made and ate it without the lemon butter sauce...just roasted with olive oil, salt and pepper. What a great snack, side dish!  Loved both by kids and adults alike!

Good but lemon is not that great on broccoli for us. | used frozen organic broccoli florets, light tasting extra virgin olive oil, sea salt, no butter to be dairy free just additional olive oil, organic garlic clove, good quality (fresh tasting) walnuts I toasted in a dry frying pan instead of pine nuts as that is what I had on hand (loved them), plus the rest of the ingredients, although possibly no pepper as I may not have had it when I made this recipe and the problem with this site is my reviews were not showing so I didn't write this immediately afterwards. Made for Healthy Choices Tag Game 2013.

Great broccoli!!  I made as directed and it came out perfect.  I like the flavor of lemon and broccoli, but not a ton of lemon flavoring.  Will definitely be making this again!  Made for Name that Ingredient Tag.

I was very happy to come across this recipe since I was really getting tired of my standard broccoli preparation. The flavors and textures in this dish work so well together. I'm not sure I can ever go back to plain, blanched broccoli again. Thanks for sharing this! I featured it on my blog as well - http://danasfoodblog.com/?p=1626.

Great side dish. We love broccoli roasted, it is so much better than steamed. And lemon is broccoli's perfect match. I used a lot less butter and more of the nuts. We love our veggies, so this feeds two to three for us.

And I quote my DH, "This may be the best broccoli I have ever eaten!" I'll be interested to see what my DS who prefers his broccoli steamed thinks of it.  Thanks for sharing. Made for Best of 2013 tag.
Wonderful dish. So full of flavours, I absolutely loved it! I edited the recipe a bit and roasted broccoli, cauliflower, and brussel sprouts. So delicious and healthy!
Even better, roast the broccoli as described, make a hollandaise sauce and add a tablespoon of ranch dressing to the hollandaise before pouring it over broccoli.

Years ago,we had a small grocery that made the best sausage.I did know that they added buttermilk to the mix.This recipe tastes just like that wonderful sausage if you add some red pepper flakes.You can grind your own pork in the food processor.

These are sooooo good and so simple I'm amazed. I only altered a couple of tiny things-I used a clove of real garlic and added a pinch of fennel. The fennel (one of my favourite spices) was excellent in these. I only made 6 and they took about 10 minutes a side, but they were extremely juicy.
What a great flavour.  Very easy to make too and the cheese melts beautifully.  I served with Recipe #203770 and they matched perfectly together.
Great recipe thanks, added a pinch of fennel and smoked paprika.  Terrific for breakfast with eggs, tomatoes and cottage cheese.      Thanks again.

I was the happy recipient of some wild pig and was debating various recipes.  This was so simple and far superior to the pre-packaged type.  There's no excuse to use any other sausage patty.  Whip them up and freeze them if you must!

WOW, the flavor of the sage dominates everything else.  Overall, I liked it but would like to have used less sage.  This recipe is truly for sage lovers.  All in all, it beats the options I have here for breakfast patties.  Thanks.

Tasty, low-fat curry!  I think with additional spices this could be a real winner, as it's a bit bland in its current state.  This recipe made 6+ servings.  Quick and healthy dinner!  Thanks ontariomamaof7!  Made for PAC Fall 2008.

Fantastic! This was so tasty and delicious, Even my picky eaters enjoyed this. Didn't change anything in the recipe. Thank-you so much for posting this. The onions were so soft, it was a culinary explosion on my taste buds.
Very nice way to serve chicken.  Made exactly as stated except I didn't have any black olives!  Served over rice.  Will do again.
These were really good. Although I did add some chicken along with the sausage and then sauteed red onion in the pan in place of green onion.
Delicious! I am proud of the baked wontons, versus the original recipes' deep fried ones! Saves on some calories for sure. Great recipe!

These were great!  We had these for a snack tonight for family movie night and everyone loved them.  The wonton chips were wonderful. I made this recipe as described with the exception of no green onion.  Thanks for posting!

We made these last night and LOVED them!  I actually liked them BETTER than the ones at Johnny Carino's, if that's possible!  They were so good, and made a beautiful presentation on the platter, with the red of the tomato and green of the onion on a white background of melted cheese.  We will make these often, especially when we have company.

I made these for a small dinner party!  They were easy to make and everybody enjoyed them.  I've never worked with wonton wrappers before, but they were so much fun to work with!!  I can't wait to experiment more with them.
Very good! I made this using an alfredo sauce I got from this website.  I also added chicken to the recipe and it was a hit with the family.  Thanks for sharing!!

This was great! I need a starter for a big italian dinner i will be making and this is perffect. I messed around with it a bit and the o nly thing i did different was I sprayed the wrappers with olive oil cooking spray then brushed with egg, sprinkled the italian seasoning then I sprinkled a little grated parmasean cheese. I will be making this again, thank you.
Wow this was so good! The alfredo sauce was strange... and SO GOOD!

Thank you so much for posting this! I had these at Johnny's while on a shopping trip, but unfortunately live in a place that doesn't have any Carrino's. I made these once, and am going to make them again for Christmas Eve!

My family LOVED this, the only thing I would change is the nachos.  I actually looked up at one of my favorite resturants and found they use pizza dough (fried) for the nachos, we tried it and it was great..just cut into triangle pieces and fry! Yum!!
~T
My wife loves the Italian Nachos from JC's.  I just made them for her and let's just say we won't be going there as much.
These were really good. I must say though not quite anything like JC's. I'm not sure what I did wrong with the chips but I had to make them twice because the first batch burned.

Wow! I fried the wontons just because I was Leary of baking them. Now that I know these are "spot on" per DH I will try baking next time. Delicious and sure to save on our weekly trip to Carinos just for my fix. Just think! We can explore new restaurants in town. Woohoo!

While looking for a great Alfredo sauce recipe, I came across this one, and it brought back a lot of memories. Me and my wife loved these from Johnny carino's. Probably one of our favs. This recipe is pretty close to the way that they are actually made but not all the way. Baking the wontons may be healthier, but frying them will achieve the same taste that u are looking for. Unless u go there and order the nachos and add onions... Then 86 them, they do not belong. Dice toms, blk olives, sliced pepper rings, and slice jalape

We have never had Italian Nachos before, so we can't compare them to any restaurant. But, everyone in our family really enjoyed them.  I did make a few slight changes. We have both vegetarians and meat eaters in our house. So for the Italian sausage I used a vegetarian version of it that we all like.  I used the Italian seasoning option and left off the optional pepper flakes.  I also used a light Alfredo sauce. I would suggest that you keep an eye on the wonton wrappers while they are cooking, luckily I checked on mine. They were perfectly browned at 4 1/2 minutes. These made a yummy, quick and easy meal.

Love this recipe.  I made it for our Super Bowl snack and used  Recipe #52892 for the sauce.  I did bake the wontons and turned out they needed to be baked longer but just a minute, two was too much on the first batch.
Quick and tasty--a great way to have tilapia

WOW!WOW!WOW!!!  This was quite possibly the best fish recipe I've ever had.  EVER!  Even our friend who hates fish liked it and ate every bite, and our other friend who hates fish and usually refuses to take even a bite tried it and said it "wasn't bad."  We did marinate it for several hours, so it was kind of spicy, but we though it was perfect!!!

I would eat this fish dish for breakfast, lunch, and dinner if I could!  It is so simple to prepare, and tastes so unbelievably good!!!  I marinated for about 1 1/2 hours cuz dh was delayed getting home, but the fish stood up to the longer time.  The cooking time was perfect for my 6 oz fillets.  After dinner I went to bed and spent the night dreaming about my dinner! Thanks SkinnyMinnie!

This dish was great! I'd never cooked with tilapia before and this was a yummy introduction. The only reason I gave it a 4 instead of a 5 was that it was too salty by far.  I will definitely make it again, as I loved the flavor combination of the lime and garlic and red pepper but will probably substitute half of the soy sauce with rice wine or sherry.  With frozen tilapia fillets and ingredients found in the cupboard, the dish came together in a matter of 10 minutes --a valuable addition to the "what am I going to cook for dinner in the next 15 minutes so we don't have to order out" category. Thanks SkinnieMinnie

I've made this twice since I first tried it.  We just love it, quick, easy and super tasty!!  The only substitution I made was honey instead of sugar.  I think I'd like to try this on shrimp or salmon.  Yummy!!
Great.  I used low sodium soy sauce and it was perfect.

My family is usually not a fan of ginger so I usually leave it out.  I'm glad I didn't this time.  This was terrific!!  I used mahi mahi instead of tilapia with great results.  Thanks for sharing a good recipe.

Excellent!  I actually did this on the grill in foil.  Our grill took about 12 minutes with 2- 6 oz fillets.  I also used Splenda in place of the sugar.  I servedi this with Recipe #178976.  Delicious!

I loved the marinade for this fish.  I cooked it in a pan on the stovetop, skipped the broiler.  The sauce thickened nicely in the pan.  Unfortunately the fish I used (flounder) was overly fish, perhaps freezer burned :(   I will make this again though!

Fantastic!! I had never tried tilapia before, but I loved it with this marinade and now it's found it's way into my regular rotation. Super easy to put together fast. I put it in a foil 8x8 pan and throw it on the bbq.

I adored this recipe! ;) I usually hate soy sauce, but this recipe was very nice tasting. Next time, I might add a little sesame seed oil just to give it some taste.

I will be making this again. Thank you!

WOW! I have to agree with chef #351614 this is the best fish DH and I have ever had. He really doesn't care to much for fish but I'm the cook and he eats what I make. This one he said to make sure and fix again. Very yummy and quick to fix. I served it with a great noodle dish recipe #230831. They complimented each other wonderfully. Thanks SkinnyMinnie for posting.

My new favorite fish recipe!  I broiled it for 5 minutes then turned the oven off, shut the door, and served when the rest of dinner was ready.  I served it with Fried Plantations and steamed broccoli.  YUM!

When a recipe is this fabulous, one simply does not tinker with it. I cooked it on a skillet as it was easier that way. Only complaint my daughters have was that there was not enough sauce.. it only goes to show how yummy this dish was. Thank you for posting.

The sauce was wonderful.  The only changes I made were that I doubled the sauce amounts and added a heaping tablespoon of crunchy peanut butter then served it over pad thai noodles.  I reduced the sauce to make it somewhat thicker to stick to the noodles a little better.  My daughter and girlfriend loved it.  I grilled them rather than broiled.

Loved this amazing Tilapia recipe.  The combination was perfect for us.  Loved the heat that the red pepper flakes added.  I still trying to get used to my broiler, so instead of risking ruining this dish, I choice to cook it in a skillet on the stovetop.  Perfection.  Thanks so much.

Loved it! Didn't have fresh ginger so used powder, and omitted the pepper flakes as hubby doesn't always like spice. But it turned out sooo good! The sauce was fantastic over the rice and I served it with Glazed Carrots from this site (sorry don't know how to link). Will be making this often!

Delicious, easy to prepare dish that is tangy, flavorful, and very healthy! My fiance and I both loved this. I followed the directions almost exactly, only I used brown sugar, and 4 Tbs lime juice. I served the fish over brown rice pilaf, and it went together perfectly. I would definitely try serving this over plain white rice as well, since there was plenty of extra sauce. This is going into my regular rotation--thanks!

this definitely gets 5 stars from me, i followed the recipe exactly with the exception of doubling it and using chicken breast instead of tilapia. it was fantastic, i butterflied the breast and put under the broiler, it was so moist and flavorful. i served it with orange glazed broccoli and plain chinese fried rice. the sauce this makes taste perfect over the rice. thanks for sharing!! now you know the recipe is versatile ;-)
This was delicious!  I had dressed tilapia and not much time, so I made the marinade, put it inside the fish, and let it sit for about a half hour.  Everyone raved!  Thank you for the recipe.
This fish was soooo good!  I used orange roughy and cooked it on the grill.  The fish was so moist and the glaze was perfect.
This recipe was excellent.  I too doubled the sauce.  I also added green onions.

This was very good and just the right amount of spice.  I used cayenne powder as I didn't have red pepper flakes.  Our fillets were a little on the thin side I think, as after 10 min under the broiler they were slightly over done.  I doubled the sauce, but had leftovers, so next time I will stick to the recipe amounts.

Everyone loved this recipe and I was happy to find a new way to cook tilapia. We try to incorporate fish into our diet at least twice a week and tilapia is a fillet that we can all agree on. I doubled the sauce also, tossed some julienned squash and diced red bell peppers into the reserve, stir fried them while the fish was cooking and placed them on top of the rice and fish. It was excellent! Thank you for this recipe, it is so easy and quick!

I had such high hopes for this one as I love Tilapia.  I think I would have liked this better had I not marinated it. Seemed to me the fish was overpowered by the soy mixture. Next time, I'll just baste the fish while cooking to see if I like that better.  I would also recommend using a thicker cut filet if you plan to marinade for the 20 mins.  Sorry I couldn't give it a higher review. I'll try again, and let you know if it goes any better.

This was tasty and easy to throw together.  I make a second batch of the sauce and poured it over a bunch of veggies which I then stir-fried and served with the fish over rice.  The pan I broiled in, however, came out incredibly burnt and it took hours of soaking, scrubbing, washing, and repeating for it to finally come clean.  I may try grilling or pan frying the fish next time.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!  Its a great way to add variety to my fish dishes.
Really Light, really good!

We liked this a LOT.  I also doubled the marinade and used half on my stir-fry veggies that I served with it.  I added it when the veg were almost done, so as not to overcook any of the marinade ingredients.  Served it with brown rice.  Yum!
Went very well with a side of Curried Tuna Couscous (recipe #303872).
Just what I was looking for!  Delicious and the sweet, salty, hot flavors melded together so well for the fish!

This recipe is SO GOOD! I'd never had or made Tilapia before but couldn't wait to try it; settled on this recipe. Unfortunately I didn't have time to marinate it, but it still turned out amazing. I too ended up adding some peanut satay to the sauce which I and the family found to be a great addition. Also cooked it on the stovetop rather than baked it in the oven. DELICIOUS! Received rave reviews from everyone else, as well. Thanks, SkinnyMinnie!
Love this recipe!  I always add honey instead of sugar and a bit more red pepper flakes just because we love spice.  Thank you!!

This was incredible!! Like other reviewers I doubled the sauce and then reduced it on the stove after the Tilapia was done, adding about a tbs of flour and a tsp of honey. We served it with brown rice and broccoli. My boys (5 & 3) loved it and my 5 yo had 3rds!
I will eat this many times. Added extra crushed red peppers and 1 Tablespoon of crunchy natural peanut butter.

I was looking for a new recipe for tilapia when this one caught my eye. I've been trying to get my family to eat tilapia, without much success. It would either come out dry, or flavorless. We all love Asian flavors, and this certainly fit the bill. I tweaked it a bit for us - used low sodium soy sauce, substituted splenda for the sugar, used 2 Tbsp of rice wine vinegar instead of the lime juice, added about a tsp of sesame oil, and doubled the crushed pepper. The fish was very moist and delicious. NO LEFTOVERS!!! Thank you for posting the recipe!
Quite delicious!  Used the marinade, and grilled the fish for about 4 minutes each side.  VERY VERY light, and full of flavor!

Oh My, this was excellent! I cooked this for dinner tonight and wished I had cooked more. I used the exact recipe and grilled it on the charcoal grill. I reduced/cooked the marinade in the microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through. I served it with my own recipe for Lemon Rice Pilaf (I have it posted) and an Asian salad with dried cranberries, won ton strips and sesame-orange salad dressing. I will be cooking this again! Thank you for posting. Jan

I wanted a new way to cook Tilapia and I found a keeper! I followed the recipe with 1 exception, I use lemon juice in place of lime. The whole family enjoyed it. I suggest if you are reading my review go ahead and try this recipe.
I like spicy food but for me the marinade was a bit strong for the mild fish.

I absolutely loved this! I didn't have the pepper flakes so I changed out some of the garlic for garlic chili sauce.  I used the countertop grill rather than the oven.  It was so tasty, moist and easy. I could eat this every night for dinner.
This is a very good recipe.  Adds lots of flavor to the fish.

Made this tonight and it convinced me to finally make an account on this website!
It turned out amazing and I paired it with brown rice!
I didn't include the lime juice and I used very little pepper flakes. I also subbed the garlic and ginger for their powder equivalents. i thought that it was kind of garlic heavy. Next time I make this I'll use 1/2Tbs garlic powder!
Thank you soooooo much for the reviews.  Made tonight and got rave reviews.  So amazingly simple, and tastes so good!!!!!!!  You HAVE to try it!!

Horrible! I followed the recipe religiously and ended up with fish that was horribly over-salty due to the soy sauce-based mixture (20-minute marinade, right!?!), and burned in the time that was recommended for broiling. My wife refused to eat it, based on it's blackened appearance and overwhelming saltiness.This recipe ends up in the garbage can!
used honey in lieu of sugar & it was excellent!

This was super yummy! It was just for me, so I made the full recipe with one piece of fish. After marinating, I baked the fish in the oven. I reduced the sauce with a couple of teaspoons of flour and a tsp of honey. I didn't add the full amount of crushed red pepper since i'm not a big spicy fan and i microplaned the garlic in and used dried ginger.  I served it with Sesame snow peas #190896 and brown rice with the sauce over it. Easy and quick, will make again!
Our kids love it.

My husband loved, loved, loved this dish.  I used swia fillets, and I cooked them on the stovetop.  I brushed the sauce ( which I doubled )  on the fish instead of marinating.  I served it with Korean Pasta salad, which was also delish, you can find that recipe, on this site.  DH loved it so much, he asked to have the leftovers, the next night and, he is not one to do leftovers.  This is a KEEPER!  Thanks for sharing!

Wow....LOVED this. And I'm lukewarm on Asian food and tilapia. Like many recipes, I doubled (approx) the sauce. Used half to marinate and half I added approx 1 heaping tsp of coconut flour and reduced into a sauce in a separate pan. I was low on tilapia and had a guest so I also added a piece of mahi and it was delicious as well. I served with steamed broccoli and an Asian cabbage salad mix from Costco and this meal was a huge hit. Every plate clean and moaning about no seconds. Will make again SOON.

We LOVE this recipe! I've been using it now for about 4 years or so, we love it with Coconut ginger rice and broccoli.  I use the full recipe of sauce although I don't usually use a full pound of tilapia. I also marinade the fish for longer than 20 minutes if at all possible because it tastes SO good!
It was AMAZING!!!!!!

What a great comfort food!! I will be good on a cold snowy day or anytime you just want to feel warm inside!! I did add some salt and pepper to it, I may even try a little red pepper when I want a kick to it.
Hearty, thick and quick for a busy evening. A great, filling meal with lots of flavor and few ingredients. I made no changes to the recipe and it was fantastic.

This soup was so perfect for us tonight.  I needed something fast and hearty and had all these ingredients on hand, plus a handful of mushrooms that I threw in.  It was really cold here today and my husband works outside, this was the perfect meal to warm him from the inside out.  I made this as written, adding a bit extra water...I think my potatoes were sucking it up.  Thanks so much Laurie, this was devoured and asked for again :)

How can something so simple be so good???  I was looking for something quick to make with ingredients on hand.  My only substitition was a can of baked beans with bacon as I did not have any bean with bacon soup - delicious.  A real comfort food that will become a regular at my house.  Thanks for sharing.

This soup not only tasted great but it was so simple to make.  I doubled the recipe and added salt and pepper to taste and a dash of garlic powder.  This soups flavor really comes out the next day.  Thank you for such a simple and quick yet delicious meal.
This soup was very easy to make and tasted fantastic.  The only thing different I did was add a little apple cider vinegar to my bowl after serving to perk up the taste a little.  Excellent!
Yummy comfort food for cold days....definitely needs salt and pepper.

EXCELLENT! 5 star all the way! Everyone loved it (the sister suggested adding a bit of shredded cabbage next time) and the housemate actually asked for the recipe! I took Tony's advice and added a little apple cider vinegar to my bowl (about a tsp.) - very nice. Will be making this a lot! Thanks so much for posting this keeper.

DELICIOUS!!! I love this soup! It's comforting, tasty, and so quick and easy. I browned the kielbasa first and took it out of the pot. I cooked the onion, carrots, and celery for few minutes and I used chicken stock instead of water. The  bean with bacon soup adds a great flavor and makes this soup nice and creamy. I let it simmer for 20 minutes, mashed it with potato masher a little, and had a huge bowl of it for lunch. I can only imagine it will be even better the next day. This is definitely going into my Favorite recipes cookbook. Thank you Laurie!
This hits the spot!!!! Quick and easy.  I also sauteed the veggies a little and added chicken stock.  Yummy!

This is definitely a keeper!  I made some variations, however it would be great just as is.  I added extra veggies, especially onions, since we absolutely love 'em... and cooked them in chicken broth.  I added the uncooked slices of kielbasa after about 10 minutes of simmering time, added a 12 oz can of v8 juice and a can of drained rotella tomatoes with chiles.  It was excellent at this point, even.  After adding the bean soup and tasting it, that definitely was a souuuperb finishing touch.  Thank you sooo much for this recipe!

Very quick and easy with great flavor.  The soup was simmering when Hubby came home for dinner and after sampling it, he commented that it was a great version of Bean and Bacon that he ate as a kid.  I had to fess up that it did have canned soup in it, but before that, he thought I was a genius. LOL
Very hearty and filling. During the winter we have "soup night" once a week.  This definitely will go in my favorites file!

Made this for a friend that is fighting cancer.  I had some left over and shared with some co workers.  I followed the recipe exactly, and I got 1 quart and 7 12 oz servings.  Very easy and I did use a store brand bean with bacon soup.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.  I also used Healthy Choice Kielbasa.
This is a flavorful, quick and easy recipe.  I have made it twice, and it was better using chicken broth rather than water.  I added italian seasoning, salt and pepper too.
Excellent soup!  I used turkey sausage and also used chicken broth instead of water.  I added a pinch of Mrs.Dash and salt and pepper to the end.  Very hearty, warm and delicious!  Thank you Laurie!
Easy to make.  A great cold day meal.  Even my 3 picky little boys liked it.
AMAZING SOUP!!!  I've been using cream of mushroom soup instead of the bean with bacon, and no matter what it always comes out amazing!!!!

I loved the mixture of vegies with the bean w/bacon soup. In an effort to cut back on fat and calories, I substituted Jenny-O turkey kielbasa for the regular kielbasa. This is a great hearty soup for winter!

I just love the simplicity and flavor of this soup.  I did not have the bean with bacon soup but substituted 1 can cream of mushroom and 1 can cream of celery.  The cream of celery really added a nice flavor.  We will be making this soup again and again!  Thanks for posting!
Quick, easy to make and very tasty!!! Thank you for a wonderful recipe.
This soup is quick to make and has great flavor. My children 7 and 9 loved it.

Both hubby and I really enjoyed this soup.  I think it would be wise to make the soup, refrigerate it overnight, then re-heat and serve.  The left-overs were even better than the fresh served.  I think the overnight sit made the flavors blend a bit more rather than being distinct separate flavors.  Also, the kielbasa had time to give off more flavor. I really enjoyed this soup but I won't give this any stars as I made so many changes I don't think it would be fair. I had some left-over kielbasa in the fridge and needed to use it up. This recipe was perfect! After reading some of the reviews, I used chicken broth in place of the water and subbed cream of mushroom soup for the bean with bacon.  I sauteed (sweated out) the onions, carrots and celery in a little butter/olive oil before adding the chicken broth. I think that adds a little richness to the soup. I also added a little more broth than called for as I had some of that left over as well.  I also added a can of water with the cream of mushroom soup. I added chopped garlic and chopped celery leaves to the broth with the potatoes and let it all simmer about 15 minutes.  I cut the kielbasa in bite sized pieces (quartered length-wise, then sliced thin) and added it along with an undrained can of cannellini beans. When finished, I tasted it and added some fresh ground pepper.  Since I also had about 1 1/2 cups of left over mixed veggies, I threw that in the pot as well.  All in all, it is a very good tasting and satisfying soup. Not bad for using up left-overs!

We usually make two rings of sausage so that my wife can add the extra to the bag soups the next day. My turn to use the leftover and this recipe was easy enough. Great taste! Will make again - will try to remember the celery next time!

And the prep method also works for grape pie.  For the pie, use a tablespoon of granulated tapioca for each cup of grape filling, simmer 5 minutes, then cool before filling the crust.

these did not work out well for me, I was really dissappointed!
this is now my pb cook recipe...i add choc chips to it and they are GREAT!!
These taste pretty good, but they spread and flattened out way to much.  I think I will stick with my pb cookie recipe.

Very good cookie.  I did add a whole cup more of flour.  And baked them at 375 for 9-10 min. I might try adding a little more peanut butter to give it more peanut butter taste. It stayed soft and chewy even after it cooled the next day, which is the true test.  I will be replacing my old recipe with this one.
Yum! These turned out really good. Not flat like another reviewer said. Soft and chewey. I think next time I'll add peanut butter chips for a more peanut buttery flavor.

OMG.. GREAT COOKIE.Im not a big peanut butter lover but these were outstanding.. I dont know what some of you were doing wrong but mine came out perfect, i did use 2 1/2 cups of flour, a whole 16 oz jar of crunchy peanut butter and a half teaspoon of baking powder. They baked for 18 minutes exact. I got almost 5 dozen out of the recipe and they were very chewy and thick. the family loved em. I will never make another peanut butter cookie recipe, This is my go to recipe.
This is my new go-to recipe for peanut butter cookies!  Delicious!!

This is a really good, chewy cookie recipe.  The 18 minutes baking time was perfect for my oven too!  I made these one night, then sandwiched some homemade ice cream between two cookies, wrapped in plastic wrap and refroze.  Delicious!  Can't wait to have another.  Thanks for a great recipe!
I have made plenty of cookies in my days and these by far rock any Peanut butter cookie recipe out there!

* be careful on step #2 when it says mix dry ingreds it means ONLY the flour, b.soda & salt --- not the sugars.

Directions are right to say fork should be wet when making the crisscross pattern. Don't use sugar on fork (as other pnut butter cookie recipes recommend); it won't work w/ this batter.
They spread. And didn't stay all that soft.

My husband wanted peanut butter cookies.... I found a recipe and made them .  They were horrible.  To redeem myself I made these!  He was so happy and declared it the best he has ever had,,,!  I listened to reviewers.....I add 2.5 cups flour, 2cups peanut butter and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda.  Perfect texture, flavor and bite, little crispy/chewy on the out and very soft and yummy inside.  This is a keeper!!!!

I have NEVER tasted a peanut butter cookie this AWESOME!!  To the spreading comments, look at how thick they are in the picture. They are not thick and yes they do spread but fabulous flavor and phenomenally chewy texture.  Our new favorite!
These cookies are AWESOME! Highly recommend this recipe....I listened to the reviews and added 1/2 cup of flour and 1 tsp baking powder and they turned out perfect!

I tried this recipe, and while it was very moist and chewy while it was warm, it became extremely hard and dry when it cooled.  It didn't seem to have much of a peanut butter flavor, either...some, but more as if the peanut butter was barely there.  I'm sorry to say, I won't be making these cookies again.  I was, and am, very disappointed with this recipe.

I altered the recipe, but they are fabulous none-the-less!  I turned up my oven to 325 degrees, used 2 cups of PB (16 oz total), added an extra 1/2 cup flour (2.5 total), 1/4 tsp baking powder and a bag of Candy Corn M&Ms.  I also refrigerated my dough for 15 minutes before scooping and in-between batches in the oven.  Crisp on the outside and chewy inside...just like Mrs Fields!  Will definitely be making again!
Flat as a pancake and tasteless.  Won't try again.

My husband and I made this recipe and gave it a five star. This recipe makes the best peanut butter cookies. We did take the reviewers comments and used 2 1/2 cups of flour, 1/2 teaspoon of baking soda and a full jar (16 oz) of creamy peanut butter. I did leave dough in fridge overnight because it was too sticky. Next morning nice and firm.

Amazingly delicious and crispy-chewy :) We got 5.50 dozen cookies using a cookies scoop. They still are crispy on the edges and nice and chewy in the inside. We stored them in an airtight container and also placed a layer of plastic wrap on top of the cookies. I will never look for another PB recipe again. Thank you and this is a keeper!

Something tells me that this is not the actual name brand Mrs. Fields cookies.. I made these tonight-- made the additions that many others suggested and yet they were still on the thin side.. yes delicious but ive never had such a thin peanut butter cookie.. i dont even want to imagine using this recipe without the added flower and baking powder and peanut butter... please adjust this recipe:) Thanks

I have been on the hunt for the best, chewiest pb cookie!  They are my husbands favorite!  They are different because its a very soft dough, which I think helps them stay chewy!  The only thing I would do is add more peanut butter....thats it!  As for the people who dont like how flat the cookie is...add a bit more baking soda.  That is what makes the cookie rise.
Great cookie will add more flour next time.

These were perfect. I did have to substitute margarine for butter. I added approximately 1/2 c of extra flour because of this. I did not soften the margarine. I had bought crunchy PB by mistake, but we ended up loving the little peanut bits throughout the cookies. My cookie dough was a little less stiff, so that made for wider, flatter cookies. They baked for 22mins and came out with nice chewy middles and perfectly crispy edges. We like flatter, chewy cookies so I always do a trick my great-grandma used to do- the minute they come out of the oven I smack the cookie sheet down on the countertop :) Thanks!
Just the recipe I was looking for. I will always use this when I make Peanut Butter Cookies. The BEST recipe!
Great cookie! I followed directions, except for adding double the amount of peanut butter. I also put chocolate chips in the second batch which turned out great. Thanks for sharing.
Chewy and delicious. Added a dollop of Nutella to a few just for fun.
I live in high altitude I went by the recipe exactly baked for 17 minutes and they turned out perfect!

Excellent!  I used a grahm cracker crust and it was divine.   I used only 2 Tbls of butter in the crust, 12 ounces of fat free cream cheese and 12 ounces of low fat cream cheese, used splenda sugar, and kept everything else the same.  Making these adjustments cut the fat, without loosing taste.  I will be making this again!  HINT:  the layers are very thin using a 9 inch, maybe next time I\'ll experiment with an 8 inch to make \

This is my recipe, I make it all the time with some different versions.  It is an all time favorite of anyone who tastes it, it is a little piece of sin, taste like a piece of truffle!  Oh, and never use margarine for anything.

I made this cheesecake for my husbands work party and some of his fellow employees wanted to know if I had gone to culinary school. It's that good. I used the entire leftover package of semisweet chocolate, melted and poured it over the top like a ganache. It looked gorgeous decorated with sugared cranberries.
This was fantastic! It makes a great presentation too. I agree with Erin that the layers are a bit thin so I will try using a smaller pan as well. Otherwise, just perfect :)Thanks!
Great recipe!! I made this for my mom's boyfriend's birthday, and it turned out beautifully. I wasn't at the party to taste it myself, but he thanked me for the delicious surprise.:)

Excellent! The recipe turned out perfect and the end result looked like it came from a bakery. I used semi-sweet chocolate chips and used the leftover chocolate to make chocolate covered strawberries. I will make this again.
I made this as a gift for one of my employers and one for my family. It was truly  delicious. I would prefer a smaller pan for a thicker cheesecake other than that AMAZIN'........
Simply said, this is absolutely amazing.

this was pretty good. The chocolate topping was rather hard to cut through with a fork. It was like a candy bar sitting on top. Flavor was good. For some reason, mine didn't look as tall as in the pictures.

This cheesecake is a real winner! I mixed the layers seperately and came up a bit thin with the chocolate and white chocolate layers, but wow did it taste amazing! Great recipe, well worth it, Thanks!!

For the semisweet chocolate and strawberry layer one word describes them: delicious. However I did not care for the white chocolate layer - I'm not quite sure why.
I managed to pour the white chocolate layer over the semi-sweet easily - my mum poured the strawberry on top and I'm not quite sure what she did but she made white come through, so mine looked nothing like the picture.
 I was a bit anxious that the mixture was going to overflow however, it did not rise much. I used a digestive crust, and also found the chocolate topping hard to cut though. Maybe next time I'll use a pureed strawberry topping.  What I like about this recipe is you can do soo many things with it e.g triple the amount of strawberries for a just strawberry cheesecake. Or just use two flavors and marble them together.  I did find this recipe created quite a lot of washing up but it was definitely worth it.
Nice Cake, Mine didn't turn out as high as the one in the picutre but the flavor was very nice. Thanks
I added all of the chocolates into the mixture and added a drop of red food coloring to give it more color.

Delicious!  Soft dough handles well after chilling (Step7-8) - I refrigerated dough overnight.   Step 6 make them very easy to roll to 1/4-inch thickenss after dough was chilled.  I used a 3-inch gingerbread man-shaped cookie cutter, and recipe made 48 gingerbread, and about 20 (1-1/2") smaller men I cut from the scraps.  I cooked them a little longer than stated, as we like gingerbread men crunchy. Next time I'll add more ginger, etc. to suit out taste (guess I was thinking gingersnaps).    I froze cookes and will ice them just before placing in clear decorated bags to include in gift baskets. (Thus I can't comment on icing yet.) Mean, thanks for a delicious recipe that works well, even for a novice.

Awesome! I love gingerbread cookies and this one was a real winner! I think the best tip was cooling the dough AFTER it was rolled out, it made the dough easy to work with and easy to ransfer the cut outs to the baking sheet. I rolled out the scraps and cooled it again before cutting out the shapes. I made these for a Christmas bake exchange and they were a real hit. I didn't use the icing suggested, I used melted white chocolate instead. This recipe made 15 dozen tiny gingerbread men ( approx. 1 inch tall) thanks for this great recipe!

Great recipe, I did everything except I did not have unsulphured molasses on hand, but the regular molasses worked just as well.  These cookies are soft and yummy, and the icing is perfect.  Great recipe.

This is a wonderful recipe!!  I made giant (8 inch) gingerbread men for my daughter's 2nd grade class. The have a great flavor that was not too spicy for the kids. I did not try the icing but used Wilton's royal icing instead.
The cookies were a big hit.  I'm sure they will become a yearly tradition.  Thanks for the recipe!

These are great! I made only half a batch today to test the taste of these before christmas, and I'll definitely be making a few more. I did, however, have to bake them for about 3 minutes longer to cook all the way through.

This was my first time making gingerbread cookies, but it won't be my last! I really liked how easy the dough was to work with, using this technique, and the color is so much more fun than plain sugar cookies. My 3 yr old and 1 yr old were quite a sight with their paintbrushes and cookies; thankfully this recipe granted me plenty of cookies for giving away too. We made a variety of sizes and shapes. We used less icing than the recipe called for but had enough.
zummy and the dough was so easy to work with...  this will be our chritmas gingerbread recipe for now on.. thanks!

I made these for my family while I was home visiting over the break. They were very impressed--my mom called them the richest gingerbread cookie she's ever tasted and also raved about the royal icing. (I ended up making sugar cookies, too, and my mom asked me to make more of this icing....and then to make even more of it to drizzle over her homemade breakfast breads for friends.) These were soft and had just the right amount of chewiness. Duly impressed again, mean chef.

This was my first attempt to make Gingerbread cookies and this was a really simple recipe!  My 4 year old daughter has been begging for Gingerbread (don't ask me why since she's never had it) cookies all week.  The whole family was most impressed with these little men!  Definately a keeper!  Great job Mean Chef!
They are the best I've ever made.  I added some finely chopped candied ginger to the mix.  Nice!

This is a great gingerbread cookie. I skipped from step 6 on and used a gingerbread mold pan instead. This made several gingerbread "cakes". My children and I enjoyed the flavor enough without frosting, so I left it at that. The taste is great and the recipe is easy. Thanks Mean Chef for posting this keeper!
Excellent cookies!  I didn't use the frosting, instead I used cinnamon candies for the eyes and buttons.  A must have recipe!

Finally, a soft gingerbread man cookie!  This cookie has a mild flavor that teams up well with red hots for buttons and raisins for eyes.  The icing sets nicely and tastes great.  Step six is very important, and not to be skipped. I've made this recipe twice so far this holiday season, and I've given several slabs of chilled dough (between the two layers of plastic wrap), as gifts to friends so they too can have fun cutting out cookies.  The dough's been a big hit!

These are wonderful, and the flavor gets better a day or two after they're made.  They stay nice and soft, too!  I formed the dough into logs and froze it.  After it thawed, I sliced it and baked it that way, rather than rolling the dough out.  I didn't make the icing - instead I made a simple powdered sugar and milk glaze, flavored with a bit of Kahlua.  I dipped one end of the cookies in this and topped them with red and green sprinkles.  I don't think I've made gingerbread cookies before but I have eaten enough of them to know this is a great recipe.  Thank you!

A very NICE recipe from MEAN CHEF :)  These cookies were wonderful!  I prepared the dough for my 9-year-old daughter and her friend to make Chirstmas cookies.  The results were excellent; the dough is easy to handle and the technique of rolling the dough between wax paper sheets was critical.  I rolled it a little too thin on the first pass, and when I pulled the paper away, there were a few wrinkles on the back, causing the dough to break.  But no problem; I just dusted with flour, rolled gently and it was fine.  A very forgiving recipe - I recommend it highly, especially for making with children!  (Also good with cream cheese frosting, made into sandwich cookies late at night.)

This is an excellent recipe and I wish I could give it ten stars. Easy to make, easy to roll, fabulous flavour and everyone wanted more. I halved the recipe and made 12 large gingerbread men. Thank you very much Mean Chef, we miss you.

I used this gingerbread recipe last night. I was expecting the cookies to taste ho-hum generic. It seems gingerbread men tend to be more for looks than taste. They're usually bland and hard as rocks. I have been humbled! Just right with moistness, and very flavorful. Mmmm...the cookies were out of this world. Finally, gingerbread that tastes as good as it looks! I didn't even feel bad when I bit off the gingerbread man's pretty little head. Thanks for the recipe :)

I hate to be the minority here but I was not very impressed with these cookies.  I thought they were chewy and a bit bland.  The two stars are for the fantasticly detailed instructions...I will never have trouble making cut outs again...and the dough was easy to work with.  They smell devine, it's too bad their taste doesn't match.

I had some trouble rolling the dough out (due to my inexperience) until I added enough flour to the pin and surface area.  Then VOILA!  The cookies were fabulous, moist and soft, and truely delicious.  A great recipe.

thanks for such an awesome recipe. the cookies taste great. they have just the right amount of spices to give them an authentic gingerbread taste. i'll definitely be making these every year from now on. thanks again and merry christmas
Very easy directions,but the cookie flavor is bland,and not very sweet at all.I usually look to reviews as a deciding factor when choosing a new recipe,but this time I was let down.
yum! so tender
These were really good and soft!  A lengthy process, but worth it.  My husband liked them and he never eats cookies!

This was a great recipe, although I found it difficult to mix evenly. I don't like cloves, so I left them out and doubled the nutmeg. I used salted butter and regular molasses, and didn't notice a difference. The cookies were lovely - chewy and soft. Yummy! Very reminiscent of spice cookies. I don't like regular gingerbread, but these were so good they didn't even need icing.

I bake a lot, but never made gingerbread cookies. My daughter requested some this Christmas and I thought I will give this recipe a try, and I am very happy I did.
Recipe was easy to follow, cookies are soft. I only ended up with too much icing, but that's ok. This one is a keeper, and I am making another batch. Thanks so much for sharing!

These are excellent.  So easy to make (if you have the molasses in the house, silly me).  They are easy to roll out, I had left them overnight in the fridge and I let them sit on the counter for 15 minutes.  I made teddy bears for the dayhome kids to decorate and the parents loved them.  Thanks this will be a keeper.
Cookies came out great.  Easy to work with and flavor-wise one of the best I've had.  The icing is GREAT as a glue to add candies and such.

I used this recipe for the first gingerbread contest here on Zaar and I made 2 cottage style houses and loads of gingerbread men, they ended up at the end of year school parties

The recipe is very easy to work with and the biscuits are soft and yummy, everyone loved them, many told me they were the best they had ever tried!!! I made the recipe about 4 times in total and will keep this as my favorite one now. 
The only thing I did different from the recipe is that I used golden syrup instead of molasses.

Thanks for a great recipe Kim D.

EXCELLENT recipe for softer type gingerbread cookies.  We used larger cutters and baked 8 minutes.  The icing is the key, as without they are not as sweet.  It hardened perfectly after allowing for ample dry time.  We had so much fun decorating these...forget the house that never gets eaten, we are adding these to our  holiday must-make list because they were fun to make, eaten and enjoyed by everyone.  TY for posting!

This recipe is now our family's new ginger bread men recipe.
All of the children are involved in making and eating. We all loved the flavor and texture. Thanks

These were excellent gingerbread cookies! I make them at least once a month! The refridgeration step is definately required. Since I don't like icing and the cookies aren't sweet enough to eat plain, I topped my cookies with red hots and they were just right.
These are great. I love that they are soft and not the super crunchy hard that a lot of gingerbread cookies turn out to be.

Every Christmas I get bullied into making these cookies by my family. ;) Everyone loves them! You really, really need to set aside time for these to chill though, as the dough warms up it gets too sticky to work with. Thanks for sharing!

I made half a recipe and got about a trillion cookies out of it. Granted, I make "kid sized" cookies (about the size of a thumb print) because my little siblings always drop food on the ground or leave half a cookie in a pocket or whatever; this way they don't waste a gigantic cookie.

I didn't chill them at all, I just rolled them into balls and pressed them on the cookie sheet with a fork.

These were excellent. I did add some cayenne pepper just to give it an extra kick. Thanks for posting!

Ciao,
Bella

Love these cookies, I followed your recipe exactly and it made 25 - 5" Gingerbread men. I had gingerbread after a friend of mine had shared one out of a gift basket she had gotten. I have been craving it ever since. These hit the spot! They are so good after spending the night in the refrigerater, I like them thick, firm and cold. These were perfect! Thank you for sharing this recipe, I will be making them again.

One of the best. Soft enough to enjoy oh so much, but still has the solid feeling of a great gingerbread cookie. They worked beautifully for little Gingerbread men. They chilled and rolled out wonderfully and the flavor is a mild spice, you really feel like you're eating a gingerbread cookie, which I loved instead of only tasting spice while biting through a very solid hard cookie. Great Cookie, thanks!
I used with Recipe #19250

These are excellent.  The flavor is perfect, nice and spicy.  Fantastic texture...crispy but not hard.  Sturdy enough for decorating and light enough for eating.  The dough was very easy to make, only took minutes, and easy to work with.  A keeper for me!

These were very good. I've only tasted them undecorated so far, but they were just exactly the right spiciness. They filled the house with a marvelous, spicy aroma as they cooked. Instead of pressing out several pieces and chilling, I pressed out all the dough at once between two large pieces of plastic wrap (commercial-size roll) and then cut pieces off with my bench knife. I kept the dough chilled, re-wrapping scraps and placing in the freezer to chill again before rolling out again. I got 35 cookies, some larger gingerbread boys and some small gingerbread boys and girls. The only complaint I have is that while the texture is fairly good (firm, but not hard), they do seem just a little on the dry and crumbly side. However, I may have overcooked them a wee bit, so I'm not faulting the recipe. If after adjusting the baking time next time they still seem dry, I'll add a little more molasses. Thanks for posting, Kim D.--my search for the perfect gingerbread cookie recipe is finally over!
This is a great recipe for gingerbread cookies! I accidentally used 2 tablespoons of ground ginger and the spice was twice as nice!

The first time I have ever made gbread and they received rave reviews! I brought them to work and they disappeared quickly which is a good sign during the holiday season considering all the competing treats & goodies there are around.

I even made a few reckless substitutions:
baking powder instead of soda and ww flour for 1/2 the all purpose flour.

I used packaged icing to decorate them.
What a wonderful, easy to make recipe. I made these for a gingerbread decorating party. The cookies were softer than others I've tried, which was great. I wouldn't change a thing!

i didnt really like these, but my family did. 
so, 3 stars!
these were EXCELLENT, so soft and yummy and delicious! best gingerbread ccokies I've ever had.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed these yet! I've been making them for about 2 years now, and they are wonderful! My husband and I don't like crunchy cookies, and these are nice and soft. I make them every Christmas for my family, and everyone loves them. Thanks for posting!

Just lovely Kim....I've never had homemade gingerbread cookies and normally struggle with cutouts, but this dough really is a dream to work with- just chill it in between batches.  As a gingerbread newbie, I thought I'd share a few tidbits: I've found that I like my gingerbread a bit sweeter, so next time I might up the sugar just a bit (or add lots of frosting!) and I realized just had bad molasses smells in the jar!  Thanks Kim for posting this excellent recipe which will be a holiday tradition in my home.
This recipe made beautiful cookies.

Great cookies and great dough to work with! I used regular molasses and regular flour with good results. I skipped the cloves because I didn't have any and it didn't affect the finished product one bit. Thanks!

It's a good base recipe. However does not spread. I made the forming easier by rolling the dough into a tight cylinder before chilling, making it easier to form by slicing after an hour.I also baked it an extra two minutes, attaining the uniform golden brown.

Great flavor, I didn't have a problem with sticking, I did refrigerate as directed and added about 1/4 t. of ground cayenne (red) pepper to punch up the flavor a bit more (my favorite Gingersnaps, Stauffer's list that as an ingredient in their cookies).
If you like them soft, don't roll them quite as thin, if you like them crisper, I would suggest leaving in a bit longer, any thinner rolling might make it difficult to transfer from surface to pan.
We decorated with our own lemon glaze (3/4 c. powdered sugar, 1 T melted butter, 1 T. milk, 1/2 t. vanilla extract, 1/2 t.lemon juice & food coloring). Very tasty. Thanks for sharing!
This recipe is Nick Malgieri's from How to Bake page 246. His recipes are always spot on.

A wonderful dough to work with, not crispy and dry like the gingerbread cookies we made when I was a kid.  They taste good, too.  I may try them with a little freshly grated ginger and some blackstrap molasses next time (I like them really spicy!)  My son had a great time helping me cut out the "gingermen" and little Christmas trees.

This recipe was wonderful!  The dough was easy to work with as long as it was cold.  I made about 4 dozen cookies with this recipe so it was a good yield too.  I used all fresh spices and felt at first that it wasn't enough.  By the next morning though, the flavor seemed to intesify, and they were spot on!  The cookies were thick and yet still tender, with a slight crunch but still softer than a gingersnap!  I only gave it 4 stars because I wanted an icing without raw eggs so I found another on here that definitely added to the flavor.  Thanks for sharing!

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this recipe until now. *smacks self in forehead* I've been using this recipe since I first joined RecipeZaar. I have it printed out in my favorites notebook on my shelf, but I needed to share it with my daughter who is now all grown up and on her own and needed the recipe for herself. This is the recipe my 5 kids have grown up eating. We all love it and I still make recipes from Mean Chef's postings all the time. This makes a great tasting dough for cutouts or houses. Thanks Mean Chef for posting it all those years ago, and thanks to Kim D. for adopting it. :)

This recipe was easy to follow and simple to make. The results were AMAZING. They were an enormous hit where I took them. I had to use honey as I was unable to get my hands on the treacle but they were still amazing and I'm looking forward to trying again. I bought some marzipan and put a small ball that I flattened out on each cookie and then put a chocolate coated coffee bean on top of that and they were delicious. Thanks for sharing.

I found this dough to be terribly sticky...so sticky that it couldn't be manipulated, even after several hours of refrigeration. I followed the recipe exactly. My butter was soft (room temp), maybe that was the problem? The taste of the cookie was soft, and good. Great gingerbread cookie, not so much as a gingerbread man!

This was my first time trying to make Gingerbread Cookies and they came out wonderful. The coloring, flavor and texture were perfect. I followed you instructions completely except I used the plastic wrap when I was rolling out the dough before cutting. That prevents any sticky to the rolling pin. Of course you have to work fast, as you stated or it just gets soft and sticky to cut. Thank you! I hope my child’s class enjoys them.
I felt that these crepes were not as thin as they should be. The mixture was too thick and produced large, flat american style pancakes. More milk? Less Eggs?
Very easy very tasty recipe and one that I think is probably better with butter than margarine or oil.  Nothing complicated in this at all.
Based on Latchy's advice, I used butter - quick, easy & delicious! I used as a topping on your Hamburgers (#68644). THanx Kitten!
Delicious and so easy too! The directions were clear. Thanks so much for a recipe I will use often.

Thanks Syd!

Scrumptous!  It had been a while since I was on Zaar.  Holidays were here and I wanted to make something new. OUTSTANDING!! Mike, this is a winner.  Made the recipe as called with no changes.  This will definately hit your taste buds.  Probably going to make another batch, and store them.  Made for 1-2-3 hit wonders.
Made for hubby & Carly who love butterscotch who both gave it a thumbs up.  Thanks Mike, this made them both happy.  Made for PRMR, a tag game.
These are wonderful! Love cashews so I  knew these couldn't disappoint. Made just as stated. Thanks for sharing! Made for Gimme 5 tag.

Fabulously rich and so absolutely sinful.  Who wouldn't like the taste of salty sweet and especially if the salty is cashews.  What a great find:-)

Delicious!  My cashews weren't salted, but I'd like to try them with salted cashews as well, to see what CB is talking about.  These were super easy and quick, too!  I sprinkled the top with icing sugar, which was a pretty touch.  Thanks for posting, Syd!

Wonderful!  I would say the onions cook down by 2/3rds.  I was tempted to take them off the heat when the onions were tender but then I cooked them for another 10 - 15 minutes and they really got carmelized.  Don't rush the process. It's worth the wait.

What more can I say Kitz.  These are excellent.  I made these for Dave's hamburger tonight and he loved them.  I made myself a different hamburger, but I did try a smaple.  Just amazing flavor.  Thanks

Fantastic! And you should smell my house! Every year when the Walla Wallas and Vidalias come in I caramelize a ton of them, vacume pack and freeze them to use during the fall and winter.
