This is the first time I have ever made carmelized onions and I am so happy I picked this recipe. These were so easy to make and were perfect with our grilled steaks today. Thanks for a great recipe.
Yum. The sugar is just that added umph that is needed for caramelized onions. I will definitely make this again. I used red onions this time around.

I have been wanting to make caramelized onions now for awhile. So glad I chose this one!! very easy, and fast to make. After the sugar step, I too, left it for about another 10-15 mins. sooo good, thanks for another winner, definately be my standard onions from now on.

This is the first time I've tried carmelized onions. This recipe is easy to follow and the onions smelled and tasted great. I used one very large vidallia onion and it made enough to freeze some for another meal. We all enjoyed it very much, thanks.
Excellent.  Made these with a roast pork recipe also from the Zaar.  Nice side dish.  A welcome change from the same old same old.
I always make my onions this way.  I didn't know that they would freeze well.  I will have to try that.

I made these to top recipe#208583. DH said they were the best onions he's ever had. I will make these again and again, to top beef, pork, use in fajitas, wraps, on cheesesteaks, any recipe I want perfect onions for! My only brown sugar was Splenda blend, so I opted for the white sugar. They turned out perfect. Thanks again Kitten!!!!!

These were delicious, I served them with Thorsten's Crispy Beer Flat Bread and everyone loved them at the New Years Party we attended. Made almost as written except I cooked them in my crockpot on high for about 5 hours and about 20 minutes before we were to go to the party I took them out and drained the liquid and sauteed them in a heated and buttered fry pan for about 10 minutes to give them a little more color.  Thank you for the great and tastey recipe I will definately be making these again.

Kit, these are great! Cooking solo, I had never bothered to prepare these for myself before but decided to make them ahead for dinner guests I'm having tomorrow. I sampled them right out of the pan and these will be a great addition! I was a little surprised to see how much they reduced after all that crying and slicing but the taste is certainly worth it! I used 4 large onions and was still able to put some aside to freeze for me to use later! Thanks for a great method/recipe which has inspired this somewhat reluctant cook!

This recipe is delicious!!!!  I tried it last nite with some marinated mesquite steak and baked mushrooms and is was delicious.  I didn't think that I could cook anything that delicious.  The onions do make your eyes tear a lot, so look up n a few methods online on how to stop your eyes from tearing.  I will use this recipe on a regular basis now, I am still amazed how delicious it was and it was a snap to make.  I added a little bit more sugar(I used white this time), about a tablespoon more.  I am exiced to try brown sugar next time, just need to make a trip to the store.  I would strongly recommend this recipe to anyone wanting an easy quick way to spice up the usual steak dinner!!!  You don't even have to be an experienced chef which is the best part.  Enjoy!!
Yummy. I made these all the time and add it in with all kinds of recipes!! I love it on pizza
So Amazing, they made me cry! Luckily I hadnt done my makeup yet. Thanks, I will be using these with a lot of my recipes.

Caramelising onions is something I've always improvised, so making these to a recipe - and one of KITTENCAL's recipes! - was something I really looked forward to when I tagged this recipe for Zaar Stars Tag all of about twelve hours ago.  Guess I just couldn't wait to try it!  I took KITTENCAL's advice about this recipe freezing well - just loved the idea of having these readily available in the freezer - and doubled the recipe.  These were just SO delicious and they smelled divine while they were cooking!  Obviously just the right balance of butter and oil and sugar (I used brown sugar), a smidgeon of salt and a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper.  We enjoyed these with ellie_'s Mushroom Burgers (Ww) 317385 which were really low in fat, so that allowed the indulgence of a generous portion of these yummy caramelised onions.  Thanks, KITTENCAl, for sharing this wonderful recipe! This is another must-make-regularly-recipe for me.

I cut the recipe in half and used brown sugar twin in place of the brown sugar.  I then added in about 3 T. garlic and about 1/4 c. juice from the jar. Over med. heat I let the liquid evaporate (a couple of minutes), then added a little olive oil and some cooked whole wheat spaghetti to the onions and garlic.  Stirred around, and then let sit for a few minutes to absorb flavors.  The onions were great and made my noodles taste so good!  I will use these more often now that I have this recipe!  I never knew you were supposed to add sugar.   I always just sauteed them until they were very soft and used those before finding this recipe.  Another fantastic recipe from Kitten!  Thank you for sharing it with us!

Wonderful onions!!!!!
I made these last week to top our steaks - there were leftovers so I tossed them in with mashed potatoes a day or so later.  DH asked if we could have them again this weekend but I was tired of the slicing and tearing involved.  He has just arrived home from work with a 'present' for me.  A beautiful professional quality mandolin that will take a year to learn how to manipulate.  Hugs and omg's and then he says he has the second part of the present in the car. FOUR 3 lb bags of onions!!!!  Not sure if I should kiss or kill him :)  I'll be making these again tonight it seems.  Thanks so much for the recipe Kittencal...I think ;)

Thank you, KC, for another great recipe.  I use these onions on top of my homemade pizzas.  Everyone raves.  Next I was thinking that I would dice the onions, make them according to your recipe and serve them over a log of chevre for an easy appetizer.  Thanks!
Love this recipe!  I chose to make this for Recipe #77393.  Lucky me I chose to make more to freeze.  Came out great for the burger had.  Will be making a batch for future meals.
This was delicious.  I threw in a can of drained green beans with this and up'd the seasoning accordingly.  Loved it!
This recipe is simple to make yet the results are wonderful. Will be using again and again. Many thanks.

Perfect is the word. My brother asked at the last minute for caramelized onions with our brats tonight. I scaled the recipe down for one onion and it came out great. I know we'll be making the full recipe again soon. Thank you for posting!

I used two large yellow onions and 2 tsps brown sugar, ran out of white sugar.  I served them over steaks and hamburgers.  They tasted good the day off, but even better the after. Thank you for a simple but delicious recipe.
YUmm!! I cooked these, cooked them and cooled for a yummy goat cheese and green salad.
I stuffed my burgers with a little blue cheese and these yummy onions :) Delish!!!   Thank you so much for posting :)

This is the first time I have been able to carmelize onions to my liking, even though I think I put in a bit too much oil. They were great. Will do these from noe on. Served them with "Recipe#374280" for Photo Tag.
Perfect. There is nothing more to say- just PERFECT. :)
These were great! so perfect for what I was looking for. Thanks for posting!

Absolutely delicious!  I've made them twice now and served them on New York Strip steaks the first time and with Italian sausage and peppers last night.  We love vidalia onions and this is a great way to have them, even out of season, as I plan to make another couple of batches and freeze them.  Thanks Kitten!
Once again another winner for my Recipezaar cookbook - thank you for the simple yet yummy recipe.
Soooooo yummy!  Thanks Kitten for all your wonderful recipes.
Very good! Kitten Cal, I LOVE your recipes.

These are over the top GOOD!!  Here's what I did, flour tortilla, smeared some avocado on it, grilled flat iron steak that had marinated in some spices, caramelized onions and a dollop of sour cream. YUMMO!  These onions are to die for. I can see me doing these often. Thanks again for a superb recipe, as always!! Merry Christmas!!

I only recently had the pleasure of tasting caramelized onions. Oh my, how good they were. I decided to try this recipe and oh my, how good these are! I like that these are so easy to whip up and the fact that I can make a big batch and freeze. Yum Yum. I made this and mixed it in with mashed potatoes, wonderful! can't wait to try it with/in other dishes. Patience is definitely the key. Thank you for sharing.

Excellent!  Prepared this dish to serve on a vegetarian sandwich.  I did not use sweet onions and did add the brown sugar.  Made with two onions and cut back on the butter and oil, this came together nicely in a non-stick skillet.  Mine came out browner than the other pictures.  Who doesn't love caramelized onions anyway?
Thanks! Worked perfectly in this recipe Recipe #307396 although I skipped the salt and pepper for obvious reasons. cg ;)
so so easy! i could have been making this for years had I known it was so simple!! i used splenda to be a bit healthier and it came out perfect!!

Excellent! Kittencal does it again! I make these as directed and use them on panini sandwiches but last night I did something different.

I used 4 large onions, 1/2 cup butter (will use less next time), no oil,  brown sugar, salt and pepper and put all ingredients in the crock pot overnight until they were nicely carmelized. THEN I MADE THEM INTO SOUP! I added 4 cups veggie broth, 2 veg-chicken bouillon cubes, 1/4 cup sherry, few dashes or Worcestershire, 1-2 tsp minced garlic, big pinch of thyme and a bay leaf - cooked on low for 1 more hour and served. Everyone LOVED the soup!!! I will make this again and again, with less butter of course! Toasted half a multi=grain sandwich thin with a piece of havarti cheese on top, slapped it in my bowl of soup and VOWALAH!!!
I only used one big onion, but we ate so many straight from the pan, there was hardly enough for our hamburgers!  Delicious!!
looking good - going to serve them up on some pulled pork (I saw restaurant sign up tonight after work and I already had some leftover pulled pork iin the fridge so voila!!

Fantastic! Another winner! My first attempt at making these gems. I made a batch ahead of time to take to a Burger Bash BBQ later this afternoon. This recipe couldn't be simpler. Thanks a bunch Kitten!

I don't know how I forgot to review these onions- I make them several times a month! The Gold Standard is using Vidalias, but they aren't available year-round. So any sweet onion will turn out yummy... This is a winner, Kitten!

Oh these are so good.  We had steaks tonight and I made these to go along with them.  The little bit of brown sugar makes them so good.  We all loved them and I can't wait for the leftovers with our omelets in the morning.  Thank you for sharing yet another fantastic recipe from your collection.

Great go-to recipe! I always make the mistake of trying to not follow this when making carmalized onions and slowly but surely over a few months my onions become less and less perfect. I always end up coming back to this recipe and am appaled that I hadn't been following it the whole time! No fail!
Another home run from Kittencal! Made this to put inside an omelet. We were having breakfast for dinner so made omelets with caramelized onions, mushrooms, ham and cheese. Thanks again!
This recipe is AMAZING! Used it over pan-fried kielbasa slices, a bit of mustard with it on a sub roll and it was sandwich HEAVEN.
Perfect! Perfect! Perfect!
These onions turned out great! I made them for chicken patty melts tonight and my whole family loved them. They were so easy and good. Thanks for posting!
Wonderful!  Mine took about an hour to get them caramelized but let them cook on 3 until they were at the color I wanted.  Used them in a pasta dish.

Fantastic onions!....We recently had appetizers at some friends' house and when we entered the house there was this marvelous smell of onions being caramelized.  They added them to a simple packaged onion dip, and it took it to a whole new level of deliciousness.  Everyone loved it.. Thanks for teaching me how to caramelize my own onions, Kitten!  I will be looking for more ideas of how to use them because they're just so good!

Wow, this was great! I did four medium-to-large yellow onions in my large stockpot, and replaced the sugar with agave syrup (for those of you who want to try this, use about 1/2 the amount called for, because my agave came out slightly too sweet... and don't worry... you can put the agave in at the time that the sugar is called for in the recipe). I also cut down on the salt.

Fantastic! I will use this again and again. Thank you for posting.
What a great recipe!! Even my son who will not eat onions ate them!!

I had four cups of frozen sliced Vidalias from the past summer's bounty (the local market's, not my own crop)---and tried this recipe today.  I could have happily eaten the entire skillet!  The soup idea from LilMsBritches below is inspired. I'm trying that next, and expect great things!
Tremendous caramelized onions.  Highly recommend
These onions are a great addition to sandwiches for an extra sweet crunch, they also work great added to cooked rice.

This salad has become our family's favorite! The first time I made this, I served it with PCrocker's Homemade Pizza #98671. I didn't have the balsamic vinegar, so I substituted red wine vinegar, and the results were delicious! Thanks Chris!

Wonderful salad! The simple dressing is absolutely wonderful. I love the combination of ingredients, especially balsamic vinegar with sweet cranberries and almonds. I could have easily eaten the whole bowl myself. Thanks, Chris, for another great recipe!
I prepared this recipe for a picnic, and it was a huge favorite. Every bite was gone. I didn't use all the dressing, probably 2/3 of it.

It was good! My friends loved it.  I used walnuts instead of almonds, since that's what I had, and red wine vinegar instead of balsamic, so next time I'll try the others.  Perhaps because of the red wine vinegar or because my dressing proportions weren't exact, I thought the dressing was a little strong, but otherwise it was yummy.

I don't know what to say other than we enjoyed this very much. It's the perfect combination of flavors, bright and crisp. The sugared almonds were a special treat, too! This salad would work perfectly for Thanksgiving and it's easy to prepare. Thank you for sharing the recipe with us.
Oh my gosh - this was an amazing recipe - doubled the recipe for a potluck and everyone loved it - even forgot the parmesian cheese and it was still fabulous!  Thanks for a keeper!
very tasty! not terribly unique, but i served it at a dinner party and got multiple recipe requests
I really liked this salad.  I was afraid the dressing would be too strong, but it was lovely - everything worked well together.  Thanks for posting!
This was a truely tasty salad. Everyone enjoyed it so much that the bowl was completely empty!  The flavors were delightful.  Thanks for the recipe.  Will be making it again soon!

I made this salad on both Christmas Eve and New Years Eve (for different groups) and both times it was fabulous. I didn't change a thing
The dressing is enough for two salads.
Made today for an after church lunch.  I think it was a big hit because it was gone in a flash!  Thanks, I'm sure I'll make again.

This salad was extra special with basic ingredients. I used a good balsamic and did not add any S&P to the dressing, it didn't need it. I used a large box of Spring Mix salad and did everything else "as is". I served this at a dinner party and everyone raved - one friend had to eat every last bite of what little there was left! I'm going to make this one often. Simple flavors that mixed together really shine. (As noted by another reviewer, you could get 2 big salads out of one recipe of the dressing.)
I made this show off Pork Roast and Make Ahead Mashed potatoes for company. Everyone enjoyed this salad.

Wonderful, wonderful!!!!
Worth more than 5 stars.
Great recipe Chris-Thanks.

This salad is DELICIOUS!  I've made it three times and keep getting cravings for it, so I'm making it again for dinner tonight.  The dressing makes it 5 stars- it's simple yet fabulous!  I use Splenda and it comes out great.  (Cut back on the Splenda if you don't like sweet dressing, it comes out veeeery sweet, which I love!)

This is a very yummy recipe!  I started with 1/4 cup of sugar for the dressing, but I didn't think it was sweet enough, ended up using just under a 1/2 cup.  The dressing has a strong flavor with the balsamic vinegar and a little goes a long way IMO.  It also makes a lot, I probably have enough for a whole second salad and then some.  Thanks for posting this, I made it for dinner guests and everyone enjoyed it!

This is a great salad! I just used a mixture of greens that I had growning in my garden. I used craisins and we did not even use the cheese. The dressing was simple and very tasty. With all of the salad that we have growing in the garden we will use this often.  We love the dressing and have used it for other salad combinations.  I did use a raspberry balsamic vinegar and have used a splenda blend instead of sugar.

Great combination of ingredients, but far too much sugar for my liking. I think the cranberries (I used a mix of cranberries and raisins) give the salad enough sweetness and simply toasting the almonds would work better than glazing them in sugar.. unless you want to serve an unusual dessert of course :) Saying this, I guess if you use unsweetened (naturally sour) cranberries then adding a little extra sweetness might work well. Very difficult to find unsweetened cranberries around here though. I also found that I didn't even need half the dressing I made following the recipe.. so need to make some more salad tomorrow to use it up!!

I didn't use the brand name drink mix suggested for this, I just used 12 ounces of premade liquid nonalcoholic pina colada drink mix, and I added in some toasted coconut, topped it with whipped cream and more toasted coconut... this pie is absolute heaven and light as a cloud...so easy to make also. thank you mariposa!...Kitten:)

I like the sauce, so well-balanced and really enhanced the flavor of the grilled Salmon. This recipe made plenty of sauce. The second time I made this, I brushed the fillets with the sauce instead of using salt and pepper, and it was even better. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
I never liked Salmon until I tried this at Applebee's.  I made the honey pepper sauce with low sodium soy sauce and it was even better than Applebee's.  Thank you for this yummy recipe.

I have always looked forward to going to Applebee's for this dish, but I finally decided to try it at home.  I followed the recipe exactly as written, and it turned out delicious and tasting the same as at the restaurant!  I think I may have boiled the sauce a minute or two too long, but otherwise, this is exactly the kind of stuff I love; easy and flavorful!  Thanks for posting this!  It is a definite repeat!

This was one of my favorite things to get at Applebee's, and now they don't have it there anymore! That is okay though, because now I can make it at home with this wonderful and easy recipe! It is my favorite way to prepare salmon! Thanks!

I love the sauce. I was out of pineapple juice so I had to sub with orange juice.  I cooked the sauce and boiled it down then drizzled it over the baked salmon fillets and broiled it for 1 - 2 minutes, just until it browns.  This was flavouful enough without having to serve the sauce on the side.  I will try this sauce on ribs the next time.  Thanks for posting.

I don't know what to add to this other than it is wonderful! Thank you for posting it. I did cut back the cayenne to 1/4 t. as my husband doesn't like too spicy food and it was just right. Try this one, you won't be sorry.
My family didn't care for this one.  I liked it but they didn't.
this is Great!!!!! we love it at our house. my fiance is a very picky eater but he loves this!! you have to try it!!! it was easy to make and tastes great!

Excellent!  We absolutely loved this!  The flavor of the sauce perfectly complements the salmon.  So very easy to prepare on the grill.  The spices were just right for our taste.  I followed the recipe exactly for superb results : )  Thank you kindly, DonnaR for posting this to share! I will hold this one close to be sure to prepare again.......soon!
my son and i loved this salmon! i can't wait to make it again. i left out the olive oil and it didn't seem to make a difference. i also halved the recipe to make 16 oz. salmon. thanks.

This made a delicious salmon dish, and that's coming from a person who normally doesn't care for salmon.  Sweet and spicy, the sauce was the perfect complement - in fact I liked it so much I used it on the wild rice I served with the salmon as well.  Thanks for giving me a reason to eat more of this healthy fish :)

I tried this and it turned out fantastic.  I've made it about half a dozen times or so now.  The first time I make it I tasted the sauce by itself and was a bit worried because it was an odd taste to me, but it's a great compliment to the salmon.

YUMMY!  My son and I poured this over our grilled salmon last night and I swear we both about licked the plate it was so good.  I am going to try this with chicken next.  I would give this more stars if I could.
very Good ! DH inhaled it and went back for seconds.Thanks for posting
This was so simple to do and man was it worth every second!! I made this for my very picky mother and she is still raving about it.  i am going to try this on a grilled pork tenderloin as well!!!

We loved this recipe!!  I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out great.  I will definitely be making this one again!!  I used the leftover sauce (very thick, but reheated in the microwave) as a dip for fried okra the next evening.  The flavor in this sauce will go with just about anything.
Thank you!!

This recipe is sooooo good and easy that my kids were begging me to make this again. Only thing is, my leftover sauce from last Friday did not taste as good today ( 4 days later ), so I would not suggest keeping it for use at a later date. Other than that, absolutely delicious recipe. Thank you so much for sharing.
Delish!  I use Chef Prudhomme salmon seasoning then top with this.  Don't fear the cayenne.  It's just a great note in the background.
Great recipe! I didn't have any pineapple juice, so I used sherry instead and it turned out wonderful! Thanks!

This was my first time cooking salmon, so I was a little nervous, but this seemed like a good recipe to start with. The BF loved love loved it but it was a touch too zippy for me. The BF liked it so much, he used it as gravy on his potatoes. Thanks for sharing.

Perfect!  I made this for a dinner party and recieved rave reveiws!  Before puting on the sauce, I rubbed the salmon with olive oil and sprinkled on some Old Bay.  Other than that I stuck to the recipe!  Fantastic!
Thanx DonnaR

YUM!!!!!  I placed this in a glass baking dish and basted both sides with the sauce. I then reduced the sauce till it was quite thick (I did use fresh pinapple juice as well) we drizzled it over the top.  Delish!
Was so thrilled to find the recipe for my favorite thing at Applebee's that I had to try it right away.  Now I am so excited to be able to eat salmon my favorite way anytime I want.  Love it!!!

I've had this recipe for 4 years from TSR, and just finally got around to making it! The sauce is very unique and flavourful. The only change I made was to use rice vinegar. Served it with Applebee's Almond Rice Pilaf. Thanks for posting Donna.
This was just like the name says..Applebee's all the way..we enjoy Applebee's all the time and now can do it at home..Thanks

The sauce is great! I used 1/2 lb salmon (for just me!) and cut the sauce into a quarter. I used OJ instead of pineapple juice, Splenda brown sugar & low sodium soy sauce. I also used a little less vinegar. The sauce simmered well, and I baked this at 375 for 20 min. After coating the sauce on both sides, I poured the rest of the sauce over it. As it baked, I spooned up the sauce from around the salmon to keep the flavor going. This wasn't terribly spicy but there was a slight "kick" which is what I was hoping for!

Awesome! I think I'd eat most ANYTHING if it was covered in with this sauce! I baked the salmon, as others suggested, and added the sauce after cooking. Just wonferful flavor! I might try adding sauce before baking next time, and see how that works. Yummy!!
This turned out JUST LIKE APPLEBEES!! This sauce made a lot...next time I'm going to cut the recipe in half. OUTSTANDING...now I don't have to eat out to enjoy this wonderful salmon!
This dish is beyond yummy! It's delicious!

My husband is not fond of salmon but after eating it with this sauce he told me I could make it again...so that's saying something!  I love the sauce and have used it on chicken as well.  Just fantastic!! Thank you for posting this.
So delicious!  Made exactly as directed and served with recipe #75113.  Will make this over and over!  Thanks, DonnaR!!

I really don't like salmon that much usually because of how fishy a flavor it has, but this sauce was like a holy grail of flavor!  I will definitely be adding this to my permanent pile of recipes.  I got heavy compliments on it, but I was too busy eating it to notice!

Awesome Flavor!!! The flavor is in the sauce. This is so EASY and DELICIOUS and FAST. My daughter who won't touch salmon went back for seconds after tasting it with the sauce (would not share any with her father either). This one is a keeper. Thanks so much.

UPDATE: I had a lot of the sauce leftover and I cooked a ham and basted it with the sauce the last 30 minutes and it was awesome.!!!

WOW!  This is a bit of heaven on earth!  Delicious hardly describes it.  Our grill was out of gas, so I used the Foreman grill (grilled a 1 lb. salmon steak for 10 mins.) and sprinkled on some extra paprika and cayenne for color...perfection! Very good sauce. I made 1/4 of the recipe for 2 fillets and it was enough for the steaks but not enough for my husband. He was almost licking his plate. Also, like some reviewers, i drizzled it onto the fish and broiled and kept basting the fish with the sauce. Sweet and tangy at the same time. THanks for sharing.

Awesome sauce.  My husband also does not care too much for salmon, but he definitely told me this recipe is a keeper.  He ate it all up, and wanted more!  I agree with others this sauce would be great on other meats as well.

This recipe was really good...the sauce is amazing! I only used it a couple of times on the salmon, but I find it is also an amazing marinade for pork tenderloin. I reserve some of the sauce to drizzle over after...mmmm

I prepared the sauce as directed, then put it in a gallon ziploc with my split hens and let them marinate for about 30 min before tossing it all into a roasting pan with a rack on the bottom. I basted the hens about every 10 min with the sauce and then let them cook undisturbed for the last 15 min. I also threw in some baby carrots around the hens as they cooked to make an easy side dish. It was a small dinner party of 4 and everyone commented on the wonderful flavor of the glaze. The hens had a nice sticky crisp on the outside and were absolutely tender on the inside. Thanks for sharing this versatile recipe! Definitely a keeper!

How can this be possible? A recipe SO delicious, yet extremely easy. It's just a matter of combining the ingredients and topping the baked good. It takes no time, and for once, I really had no need to make alterations with the ingredients listed. The only change I made was baking the salmon and drizzling the sauce directly on the salmon.

We love this recipe! I've made it several times and forgot to review it. This recipe makes it to our grocery menu at least once a month. The only thing I do differently is use half the cayenne pepper so it's no quite so spicy. Thanks for a great recipe!
This is great!  Next time I will cut back on the pepper so it is not too spicy for the kids.  Otherwise, perfect.
This had a really good spicy flavor.  It went well with the salmon, and the french fries I had the next day!
simple, yet amazing. I made this with salmon, the used the left over sauce with chicken the next day. I did cut back on the cayenne pepper and paprika by 1/2 (my hubby doesn't like spicy food).

Fantastic!  Outstanding!  This was just amazing!  I've never had the Applebee's Version, but honestly who needs it???!!!  This was super quick, and so delicous.  My DH loved it and he's not a fish fan, especially salmon.  This will be made again and again for sure!

Will definitely make this many times again, toying around with a good potato accompaniment.   We eat Asian food several times a week so we want a change from rice.

Superb tasting sauce that the whole family enjoyed (most who don't like salmon!). Served it with peas, rice, which were great with the sauce spooned on top. I baked the salmon at 450. Thanks Donna, for posting.

Wonderful sauce! I added more soy to it and used it with a shrimp and vegetable stir fry. Yummy!

My DS and his wife said to give this 10 stars, so there ya go.  Thanks Donna!  Milt

I LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE this recipe. I like salmon anyways but this was out of this freaking world. My husband said it was the best fish he'd ever had. Ever. My dinner guests thought it was incredible, so I guess that's all I need to say! 5+ stars for this one!

No doubt...this is the best sauce I have ever made at home.  We are already planning other things to use it with.  I made the sauce exactly as written then baked my salmon fillets in the sauce finishing them off with a bit of broiling.  We served small bowls of the sauce with the salmon.  I can't wait to try this with chicken and pork.
The sauce is absolutely amazing and it goes with just about everything including seafood, fish, meat and poultry.  Thank you so much for sharing.

This was super yummy.  I really enjoyed this.  Thank you for the recipe.

This is quite awesome.  The sauce is super good and it was easier than I thought it would be.  The only (very minor) complaint I have is that it is kind of expensive but in the end totally worth it.  You have to try this one!  Thanks DonnaR....

I rarely cook salmon well. I don't know what it is about this type of fish that eludes me, but I've learned to steer clear of salmon because, although I love it, I botch salmon recipes time and again. The fish market had a sale on wild-caught salmon, so I picked up a fillet. I don't like baking salmon because of the way it makes the house smell, so I looked up a grilled salmon recipe on good ol' Food.com/ex-Recipezaar.com and found this recipe. It was so, so simple to grill this salmon this way and make it taste delicious. I started by patting the salmon dry with paper towels. I don't know if this removes some of the "fishiness" that cooked salmon tends to end up with, but it has made salmon less fishy-tasting for us in the past. I coated the fillet with olive oil on either side, added salt and pepper to taste, and then grilled for 6 minutes per side over medium-high heat for an average-sized salmon fillet. That's all I did and the salmon tasted great before I even added this wonderful sauce. 

The sauce is involved, with many ingredients, but utterly worth it. This sauce made the salmon taste even better. I will say that I used orange juice instead of pineapple, a dash of red pepper flakes instead of the cayenne, and I used half the amount of sugar listed in the recipe. The sauce was sweet enough and would've been too sweet if I had used the full amount of sugar, and too spicy had I used the cayenne pepper. I made double the amount of sauce and have frozen it in batches to use on future fish or chicken dishes. Thanks for making me less scared of cooking salmon! Be well.
