The sauce was excellent.  I don't usually cook with soy sauce so I put a lot less and added chicken broth to make up the liquid.  Instead of chicken wings, I made chicken parts and browned them on top of stove then put them in the oven with this sauce.  Thank you for such a great idea

These are excellent and so different from hot wings, very flavorful.  They are more of an Asian type of wing.  I bought a package of fresh chicken wingettes which was 1 1/2 lbs.  I made 3/4 lb of the wings and 1/4 of the sauce and that worked out to serve two for us, as I served it with a small bacon wrapped potato for lunch.  The only thing I didn't like about this recipe is that your house really smells after cooking these wings,  but it is worth it, lol!!  Made for 123 Tag Game.

I followed instructions as listed with excellent results. I like that these are baked instead of fried and that they do not turn out "rubbery" or fatty. The flavour is very nice and not overly salty. This recipe was just enough for DD and I, but then again we are both big eaters;) DD was so impressed she printed out the recipe to bring home with her.

These were good, my whole family really enjoyed them. They were fall-off-the-bone tender and the flavor of the sauce was excellent. I cooked them for the full hour, plus turned my oven up another 50 degrees and cooked them for an additional 5-6 minutes. My only complaint is that the sauce doesn't get as thick as I want it -- I thought they could stand to be stickier and more glazed. Perhaps this could be solved with cranking the oven up higher for another few minutes, but I didn't want to risk drying them out. Overall a great recipe and definitely one I'll use again.

These were great.  Made no adjustments to this except I did cook them an extra 15 minutes.  Great recipe if you dont want them too plain or spicy.  A great dinner that could be enjoyed for anybody.  Definately a repeat recipe.   Made for Recipe Swap #46.

We just loved these delicious sweet wing though I did cut the honey back by half for dietery reasons and baked at 170C fan forced oven for the hour for fall of the bone tender chicken wings.  Thank you AZPARZYCH, made for ZAAR Stars.

Liked my fingers once, liked my fingers twice and then snatched one away from DH. I made as written cutting down to serve just two and it worked out fine. We both really enjoyed these sweet sticky little wings, thanks for the post.

I reserved some of the marinade and cooked with a slurry of cornstarch to baste in the final minutes.  After being cooked, they were gone within minutes.  Seems my best trick is making food and margaritas disappear.  Made for A-NZ Recipe Tag.
The sauce is absolutely delicious, but when the chicken was done the sauce was not caramalized. (I followed the recipe exactly as written.)

This recipe is so easy to make and turns out absolutely fantastic. Everyone are licking their fingers and craving for more of this delicious dish. Next time I will do 6 lbs chicken wings.  I was very careful not to overcook; the first time I made them I overcooked the sauce and it was inedible! Made properly, this sauce would be great over many different types of foods.<br/>I like to play with my food and I did here too. Okay...all of you wanting to do the skinless boneless chicken and want the sauce to be thicker...here's how: 3/4 cup katsup 3/4 honey 1/2 soy 3-4 cloves garlic 1/2 teaspoon tabasco cook the mixture on the stove top until boiling and reduce heat. Pour on top of chicken and bake at 350*F. for 35-40 minutes...it makes the thick sauce we have been looking for in this recipe...I made this for REVIEW MY RECIPE SEPT-OCT 2013..... Thank you!!! Grpa
Perfect. I will tweek and add to most any recipe.  This one does not need a thing...except I used Veg. Broth...lol.  Thank you for a wonderful recipe.

WOW!! This has the same consistency and taste as the restaurants do.  I've been looking for it for years.  It's wonderful, but I added an extra teaspoon of salt to help bring out the flavor.  Thank you!

This was AMAZING!!!!! I didn't realize that I needed a dutch oven to make it, so I started out in my regular large stock pot (non oven proof) and when it came time to put it in the oven, I transferred it to a large baking dish and covered it with a sheet pan.
The only thing I changed was I added some salt at the end, to taste.
Thanks so much for this recipe!!!!

Proper. I used this recipe for the first time and it was a hit. Even after I left out the garlic and tomato paste because I was in such a rush, everyone was none the wiser but it was gone at the end of the night. Coked in a Lodge porcelain lined dutch oven.

I don't know what I did wrong, but the rice turned out as a tasteful, yet globby mess which resembled cornmeal. The rice dissolved into nothing. Made a second batch my usual way nd it was fine. Loved the flavor though. Any ideas? My normal rice is fluffy, but not quite the way a restaurant does it. Sorry for the bad review but the consistency was the worst. Don't let this stop you from trying. All the other reviews raved about it. Interested to see if anyone else had this issue.
This is the closest restaurant style rice I have found! My favorite so far!

I have been trying different recipes to come up with one my husband thinks compares to restaurants. I think this deserves 5 stars, but my husband gives it 4 stars. He thinks it still needs something else added, maybe garlic. Thanks for the recipe.

Update: We had the leftovers of this recipe by making fried rice, adding 2 scrambled eggs, one heaping teaspoon minced garlic and sprinkling of soy sauce. I also added some zucchini and chopped cabbage that I fried in butter before adding the rice. We did enjoy this as we often have fried rice for breakfast or supper. Again, thanks for the recipe.

This are so sticky licking finger good...we just loved them...I cut the recipe in half and cooked them in a 7X11 pan...which I covered in foil for easy clean up...I did need to cook mine for an extra 30 mins to get them to caramelize...but it was worth the wait because the meat just fell off the bone while eating them...they were so tender...thanks for posting it...=)

i made this for football yesterday. I did cut the honey down to 3/4 c because it sounded too sweet. Next time I will probably only use 1/2 c of honey. They baked up nicely, so I was happy not to have to deep fry or grill anything. I think I would maybe "brown" them in a small amount of oil before placing in the baking dish to crisp them a bit. No matter... the flavor was delicious. I will definitely make these again. Thank you for your recipe. (Made for Football tag 2013)

This is actually a recipe from 365 ways to cook chicken and it is missing a very important ingredient.  Before you pour the sauce over the wings you need to sprinkle the wings liberally with black pepper...the mixture of the sweet with the pepper is amazing.

I thought I'd just try one of the most popular recipes for chicken wings, expecting to be slightly disappointed, but they were simply awesome. As close to an orgasm as the taste of chicken wings can get.

Thai is great easy :)
I don't have soy sauce at home, I used oyster sauce yummmyy
I had no ketchup so I instead I added 1 tbsp. fig jam and 1 tbsp. laksa paste. Not sure really why I chose those but YUMMM! A slight oriental touch.

Very good tecipe, but for the folks wanting a thicker sauce - please do not add cornstarch to it. It will scorch and is not necessary. Simply cook down the sauce in a small saucepot until it thickens to the consistency of barbecue sauce before brushing it onto the uncooked chicken. Then baste as you would barbecued chix. Crank the heat to 375° in the last 8-10 minutes. This way the meat does not steam, it actually caramelizes, and you won't ruin the sauce with cornstarch.
Very good, but why two tablespoon of olive oil?

We have to give credit where credit is due. I have made this rice about 5 times. Today will be 6th. I am making it for a monthly "cook-off" my family has. This is absolutely phenomenal rice! My wife and I agree: this is the best Mexican rice we ever had!!
Update: The rice was a hit at the Mexican "cook-off"!!
This recipe is fantastic!! I love Mexican rice, but I've never been able to get the right flavor or consistency at home. This recipe
Good flavor but did not turn out dry and fluffy like the restaurant.

Followed this recipe perfectly other than cutting down on the amount of olive oil.  I rinsed my rice 4 or 5 minutes until it ran clear.  I cooked it in my dutch oven as directed, but it turned out very mushy. The general flavor was just okay and the taste of tomatoes was much stronger than I've ever had in Mexican rice.  For my taste it isn't worth tweeking, I'm tossing it out.  I'm so happy that I tried it out the day before I was planning on bringing it to a Mexican potluck.

Very soft and buttery flavor. My kids dug in within seconds of pulling first batch out of oven. Smelled really good while in oven too. One great tasting cookie. I put sugar and cinnamon in a sprinkle jar. I then sprinkled a tiny bit right once I pulled them out of oven. I also made a bit bigger cookies and baked for 10 min. Thank you for sharing this recipe was a hit here :)
GREAT! I love these! even after they get out of the oven and have been in a container for a couple days these cookies are still chewy and yummy! :D

I love these cookies! Im only 11 right now and I love to bake! This was an easy recipe that tasted exceptional! They stay chewy for a very long time and thats one of the things that makes them great! 
Thanks Again! :)

Great snickerdoodle recipe.  Easy to make (and I know because I had "help"!) and taste great.  Santa's favorite cookies are snickerdoodles you know, so these will be making a repeat performance in my house!
These are really good, but they spread alot.  I also cooked my longer but I think that was because my cookies were huge!
These didn't last long.  Easy to make, especially when you chill the dough a while, and very good.

Great cookie! Fun to make and the kids love them. I did a couple of things slightly different. Chilled the dough for about 1/2 hour to make it eaiser to work with. I always roll mine in the cinnamon and sugar mixture instead of sprinkling. Minor tweaks...
excellent!

Snickerdoodles are my favorite cookie and this is now my favorite snickerdoodle recipe!  They are just how I like them - a little crunchy on the outside and soft in the middle.  The only change that I made was to roll the balls of dough in the sugar and cinnamon mixture because my daughter was helping me and that's her favorite part of making snickerdoodles.

I made these to bring to a local fireworks festival.  I made them small (one inch dough ball gizmo).  They were engulfed by many hungry children and were pronounced delicious.  Thanks for a great recipe!

Very good. I used spreadable butter and actually had to replace some of the flour with wholemeal because I ran out of plain. But they were still great. I halved the recipe with no problems and made 16 big cookies, so had to cook them for about 15 minutes. Oddly, mine didn't have that cracked appearance, might be my fan forced oven or my Anolon cookie sheets ... hmmm ...
5 stars all the way! i have tried many snickerdoodle recipes over the years but none that were as good as these! baked up beautifully, nice and soft on the inside. LOVE LOVE LOVE THESE COOKIES!!!
We love this recipe.  Everyone loves the cookies, they are delicious.  We are now making another batch of them because we liked them so well last week.  Thanks for a great recipe!!

Brought these to school for a little party in class. Wow..they were gone so quickly! I even saw one guy take 5 cookies at once with him to his seat! Lol! The cookies were delicious, crisp edges, chewy middle (just how I like 'em!) Thank you for sharing this recipe, I'll be using it again. :)

Oh my god! I'm so glad I went with this recipe. Out of habit I chilled the dough for 2 hours. At first I was skeptical because the dough was ooey-gooey and very sticky. I always lick the cookie dough off the bowel *guilty* and it wasn't the best cookie dough until I baked it. 8 minutes was the perfect time to cook them and they were so good. The perfect snicker doodle, where the outside it crispy and the inside is nice and soft. Mine made 77 cookies, and after baking half of them were gone from me and my family. Killer cookies. I always watch my diet, but these are my calorie killers. Every time I walk by I have to have one

I'm currently making these cookies for my Dad to take to work, some for the house, and some for my own coworkers and boy, are they delicious! Definitely a keeper recipe! The cookies are soft and fluffy. My oven cooks weird, they had to cook for 10-12 minutes instead of 8. I also rolled the cookies in cinnamon and sugar instead of sprinkling it on top. I didn't flatten my first batch, forgot to, and they turned out more puffy, equally good.
These cookies are outstanding - best snickerdoodles we've ever hard. Very addictive.
It's already been said - delicious.  I used parchment paper instead of greasing the cookie sheet.

The dough seems very gooey, refridgerating it for at least an hour before baking helps. I make balls and roll them in the cinnamon sugar and I don't flatten them, just how I've always made snickerdoodles. I also don't grease the baking sheet, just use foil or parchment paper for easy clean up. These come out puffy and perfect even with those deviations from the recipe. They are too soft to eat straight from the oven, I let them cool on a cooling rack. They are soft and delicious and stay soft even when stored in a container for a few days (not that they last more than a day usually when I make them)

Loved these cookies. I refrigerated dough as it was easier to work with. I flattened slightly with the bottom of a class dipped in the sugar mixture and sprinkled more of the mixture over top. Baked on parchment paper covered sheet just a minute or so longer than recipe states.

Yummy salmon patties, tasty and moist. I made them as stated, the mayonnaise really makes a difference. Served them with a Wasabi mayonnaise. Thank you Dari, for posting this recipe for others to enjoy.
Easy to make, nice and moist. Made the recipe as stated. Served with a nice salad and lemon juice.

These are the best salmon patties that I have made.  Instead of chopping the onion, I grated it and added about 3Tbs. of green bell pepper and about 1 Tsp. of dill weed and of course salt and pepper to taste with a dash of garlic powder.  The flavor was so wonderful and I love the fact that you add flour and corn meal instead of bread crumbs like all the other recipes that I have.  I ended up frying my patties in a little bit of olive oil and butter...this is a wonderful recipe...this is my only recipe from now on for salmon patties!!!!
We had some leftover grilled salmon fillets so I shredded it and followed your recipe with great results. Served with tartar sauce.
Yummy and easy. I'll remember to keep this recipe in mind. The patties went great with BLT salad and savory sweet potatoes.

Had these for dinner tonight. Very good recipe. will make again.
Jim

Loved the fact that this recipe is so easy to mix.
I made it as written but think next time I will make a few additions like JeanetteG.  Served this with a tossed green salad & home made oven baked fries.  A keeper for me :)
A very yummy recipe. I wouldn't change a thing. It is very easy to prepare. It is a keeper. Thanks for posting.
Love this reipe.  I am planning to make these tonight.  You seem to have great reviews so thats enough for me.
I turned these into tuna patties and it worked marvelously. They have a terrific, smooth texture and hold their burger shape perfectly. We enjoyed them with wasabi  mustard.

I thought my salmon patties recipe was good until I tried this. This was great. I served it with creamed peas, and macaroni and cheese. Thought I would have left overs for lunch the next day. My mistake. Thank you for posting this recipe.

OMG!!!! i wish i could give this recipe more than 5 '*'s. my SO said that these tasted just like his mother's.the only thing i added to this was a little salt and pepper.i really enjoyed the little zing that the mayonnaise gave the salmon was just great.as i was forming them, i used a 1/4 cup measuring cup,and i ended up with five patties.this will be made often in our home.thank you so much for posting.
These were different from what I'm used to so I didn't like them very much.  All I could taste was onions!  I will omit the onions next time and see if they turn out better.

These are the best salmon patties I have ever tasted! I had been making them a different way for years and decided to try something different. Am I ever glad I did!! These are WAY better than my old way! Followed recipe except added a little bit of cayenne pepper for a bit of a kick! Served with fried potatoes and creamed corn. Thanks for the great recipe!

Quick and easy to put together, I liked the added mayonnaise. I needed to use up 3 green onions and they gave the patties a lovely light onion flavour.
Thanks for sharing.

This is the best salmon croquette recipe I have ever made.  This will be the way I make them from now on.  My husband and I both loved it.  I made a dill sauce to go with it, but they would be just as good without.  Thank you!!!

these were very easy, great texture. I cooked two for mum, and tasted it, too bland for me, but fine for her.
I added 1/2 cup corn and a tablespoon of chili sauce for us, and served them with caramised onions, great meal that I will make again.
Because of the high flour content, dont cook them too quickly, or they will be doughy inside.

I'm giving this five stars because these are the first salmon patties I've made (and I've made lots) that are not so full of fillers that the salmon flavor is overwhelmed.  These are delicious -- and so easily and quickly put together.  Keep a can of salmon on the shelf and you can whip these up in no time.  Thanks so much for postng!

I eat A LOT of canned salmon, so I'm always looking for new recipes that use it. I have about 3 salmon patties recipes, but when I made this my husband said this was the winner. They had a wonderful texture and flavor and cooked easily. Thanks Dari.
WINNER recipe.  I kicked it up a notch by breading the patties in crushed sour cream and onion potato chips.  Fried patties in oil and garlic butter.
I'm going to have to add to the accolades here. wonderful recipe. I used leftover salmon and my picky boy ate 2 big patties. We like ours with lemon and shoyu, or maybe a tongatsu sauce. Good stuff!
I am not fond of salmon, but my husband loved these. Thanks for sharing.
THIS is THE recipe for Salmon patties.  I will be throwing all my others out.
These were delish! I followed the directions precisely, and was delighted they were so good! Thank you for posting from a fist-timer!

WOW!!!!! The best ever. I just got through making them. The only thing different is I used 2 Tbs spicy mayo and one tb regular. And I added some red pepper flakes as well! This is a keeper!!!!! Thanks so much! Oh by the way there was no left overs!!!!
Great!  They really do stay wonderfully moist under the crispy, crunchy crust.  I might add some salt and garlic powder to the mix next time.  Thank you, Dari! :)

These were easy and delicious.  Because I did not have regular cornmeal I used 1/2 cup of buttermilk cornbread mix since it has probably 50% flour already.  I also took a clue from some of the other comments and added a little black and ground red pepper.  The saltiness is perfect as it is.
Thanks for sharing!

Really yummy! Delicious way to add healthy salmon to our diet. It's a very easy recipe but it's quite a departure from my usual menu. My first time making salmon patties and they turned out fantastic. I added some salt and pepper to the mix. We had them with herb and butter flavored rice. My hubby had two patties for lunch the next day and he said they reheated very well and tasted great. I will be making them a lot.
Thank you Dari for this keeper!

Quite tasty, although I thought they needed more salt. A breeze to make and the texture and flavor are wonderful. I found it best to brown well on the first side before flipping as they held together much better that way.

These were fantastic! I have been eating salmon burgers since I was a little girl and these were by far the best ones I've ever eaten. My husband was very skeptical but even he asked if I would make them all the time. I used 3 small cans of skinless and boneless salmon instead of one big can.

Wow! Moist and tasty.
I added a little salt & pepper plus a sprinkle of Old Bay Seasoning.  I served them with a drizzle of Sweet Thai Chili Sauce and stir-fried red, green & yellow peppers. 
I will pass this recipe on!!

I loved the idea of not using mashed potatoes.  This was tasty and easy.  I served with a side sause of mayo & lemon with dill.  I also served it on top of a spinach salad with Paul Newmans's Soy & Ginger Dressing.  This recipe will be made again and again.

What a great recipe.  I've never tried anything like this on my family but they loved it.  Both sons loved it and begged for more.  I prepared it exactly as written.  My dh is from MD and is used to crabcakes and was very pleased with these.

Shhh...don't tell my Grandma, but these are better than her recipe I've always used. Who'd have thought that the addition of Mayo would've made these so much better. I also threw in about a 1/2 teaspoon dried dill weed.
Oh...and I always eat mine with mustard on them. I know, us Okies are a strange bunch! :) Thanks Dari!
We've had these twice and love them! They are quick, easy, and very tasty.  Thanks for sharing!

Very good! I just made these for breakfast thinking there would be a few patties left for lunch tomorrow. Nope - all gone! Simply delicious. I made as directed. Instead of chopping the onion I grated it on the large holes of the box grater and added the onion juice to the salmon mixture. This is a keeper! Thanks Dari!

Wow, these are tasty!
I have never had salmon patties before, but was looking for a way to get more salmon in my diet- and to use up those cans of salmon in the pantry.   These cooked up beautifully, and tasted great! I had them for lunch with some garden-fresh tomatoes, and again for dinner with some sauteed zucchini, onions, garlic, and tomatoes.  I used 2 6 oz cans of salmon and 2 tbs fat-free miracle whip and 1 tbs mayo, and ended up with 6 evenly sized patties.  This recipe will definitely be used again. Thanks for posting!
I made these a few weeks ago and forgot to rate them!  They were easy and delicious.  I halved the recipe, as I am the only one in my home who likes salmon patties. Will definately make again.

Very good and very easy to make. I didn't have quite enough salmon so I mixed it with some tuna, which worked fine. I got way more than four servings from this recipe, though. I got about seven good-sized patties. They cooked up nicely in a few tablespoons of oil.

YUMMMMOOOO! I too halved the recipe, as I had a half can of leftover salmon from last night. Had these for lunch today, and they are SOOO good and crunchy. I put canned salmon or tuna into my diet a couple of times a week. These are very crunchy, very tasty, and very easy.....not to mention nutritious. A new staple in my diet. Good job! Thanks, Dari!
Very good.  I subbed green onions for white.  I used left over grilled salmon and these turned out wonderfully.  Thanks for sharing.
Great recipe, kids loved them.  I used sour cream as I had run out of mayo and I also coated the patties with corneal prior to cooking.  Thanks for sharing,

Awesome recipe! It was the first time my DH and I had ever had salmon patties and we were both very pleased with the result. My only complaint would be about the canned salmon I used. It smelled very fishy and had a fishy taste akin to tuna. But even so it was a great eat =D I will simply try left over salmon (HAH! When is there ever any left over salmon?!) or a different brand of canned. If all else fails, I will simply to add apple to take care of the fishyness. Either way, thanks for the easy dinner!
This is my first salmon-patty-making experience, and they were delicious! Browned up so nice and crispy on the outside, but had a rich, wonderful taste inside. Beautiful, perfect patties! DELISH!
Excellent! I used leftover grilled salmon. Thanks, Dari.

Best salmon patties i have ever cooked. The mayo makes 'em! I also added a dash of Old Bay Seasoning to mine. We loved this recipe better than any other salmon recipe I've ever tried. DELICIOUS!Vicki in Moultrie, Ga.

These were really good.. I am not sure I will use cornmeal again, will probably  just crush up saltines.. I did add 1 stalk of celery (sliced) into the mix, it gives nice crunch to the patties.. My daughter likes these alot! Thanks for the recipe!

We loved these, the cornmeal was a perfect addition and wasn't too much in my opinion. I even lightly coated the outside with cornmeal after forming the patties then fried them. The mayo kept them moist and can't even tell it is in them. Will definately make these again!
Delicious!  I doubled the recipe for my family & served w/fried okra.  This will definately be in my list of faves.

These are good.  I had to get used to the onion in the patties (as I've always made them without before) but I liked them.  I made them exactly as the recipe states and they seemed a bit soft, but very good!
These are OK as is, but great when topped with a touch of honey teriyaki sauce.  Nutritious, too!

I also grated my onion and added grated green peppers, and about an 1/8 tsp of garlic powder. I used seasoned salt and black pepper.  Another substitution I made was, instead of regular conmeal, I used 1/3 cup Jiffy cornbread mix.  This is my new recipe for salmon patties.( I went back for seconds, only to have my feelings hurts. And I made about 8 using this recipe. They are excellent.)Very easy to make. hint hint teach that non-cooking person this one people!
I just made these tonight, followed the recipe exactly but added a few shakes of Old Bay Seasoning. They were perfectly delicious and I will make them again.

Love It! Love It! Love It! I had never tried making salmon patties before for fear of not being "as good as mom's". Glad I picked this one to try! Wonderful Recipe! Easy to prepare! Have made it several times. Only thing I changed afer making them the first time- I use the pouch salmon (don't have to worry about bones & cleaning). This recipe stays close at hand! Thanks Dari!

When I saw this Salmon Patty recipe had cornmeal in it, I was a bit skeptical.  Some of the best Salmon patties also have cracker crumbs in them or they are coated with crumbs.  This recipe looked a bit bland to me, but hey I'm an open minded person.  I gave it a try.  I only made 2 changes - a little more salt and a dash of dill weed.  I was particularly impressed with how well the patties held together, how nicely they browned and with the final taste and texture of the prepared dish.  Yummy!  This is a keeper recipe!  Thanks Dari for sharing.

these are so delicious! and moist! and flavorful! and easy! trying to make them as healthy as possible, i used smart balance mayo, egg beaters, and baked them at 350 for 20 minutes instead of frying them. i wish i had a sauce to go on them (so much for saving calories!) but they are just delicious alone, too.

This is one of my husband's favorite foods and he gave this recipe a 5!!! My mother in law's "recipe" didn't use mayo or flour and it was hard to get the patties to hold together and they could dry out. These patties held together beautifully and stayed moist. Thanks!
I've made this twice now, once fried and the other baked. They came out great both ways. I did add a little bit of Old Bay for flavoring and it added just the kick we were looking for.
Made as directed. Loved it. Great recipe, thank you.

We love these. These are similar to the ones my grandmother and mother always made, but the cornmeal is a new addition that added a little extra crunch! I think this method much better than using breadcrumbs. For added goodness, fry a little chopped bacon (I like to use leftover breakfast bacon), add minced onion and green pepper, saute, drain, cool, and add to mix before frying. Using the same skillet adds flaver. It's also nice to add shredded cheddar before frying in olive oil. Yum! In our family, we have these with macaroni and diced tomatoes for a simple, delicious meal. Glad to see this recipe online!

Great recipe!  My husband like them and he had never had salmon patties before.  Note:  After I had started making these patties, I found that I was out of eggs.  I added just a little more mayo and continued to cook as normal.  The patties came out perfectly!  They did not fall apart or dry out.  I was pleased to find that the egg can be considered optional!
Delicious!  DH says let's make these every week!  Thanks for a great recipe, Dari!

I am giving this recipe FIVE stars because I ate a WHOLE patty. I remember my mom making these as a kid and they grossed me out. My husband and I wanted to try to get some fish into our diet and I thought I would revisit salmon. First, I had to get past the bones in the can. OMG!! I was appalled. I then made up the recipe only to find my hubby was going to be late coming home. I just covered it with plastic wrap and left overnight in the fridge. I think it helped to meld the flavors. I just fried them up nice and brown and dang if they are not tasty. This recipe is for keeps! Thanks.

These are good, and easy to make, but a little doughy for us.  The second time I made them, I cut the flour and cornmeal in half, and they still stuck together well and tasted more salmon-y. The next time I will also add a little Old Bay seasoning.  The leftover patties make great salmon burgers!

I read all of the reviews of this and knew that the original recipe was a great one with the mayonnaise being a key ingredient.  However for my taste I added the Old Bay Seasoning, finely minced green pepper, smoked paprika, dill, cayenne pepper and salt and pepper.  They were crisipy, moist and delicious.  Will definitely make these again.

Added Tony Chachere's Creole seasoning for added zip, and cut the cornmeal and flour a little, so they would be nice and salmony.  They coated up fine, and they tasted so good.  Make sure you don't keep flipping them in the pan, as they tend to fall apart if handled too much.  We had with fried green tomatoes and creamy mashed potatoes.  Couldn't have been better!

These are wonderful.  I like the texture and the way they hold together.  I too added some Old Bay seasoning, a required seasoning for seafood in our house.  Having the mayo in the main ingredients just really makes sense.
TY for posting.

Yummy! These were DELISH!! They were even good the next day...COLD! Easy to put together, had all items in my pantry, whipped up quickly ~~ brought me back to when my mom used to make them when I was a kid. This is a definite keeper!
What more can I say that hasn't been said already?  The texture was perfect and I liked the crunch from the cornmeal.  Thanks.

I made these for my kids one evening and they weren't sure about it but when they tasted it that loved them.  DH isn't a fan of salmon so I prepared these on a night when he was out of town and we now have a new "daddys out of town meal".  They enjoyed them as much as I have always loved salmon patties.  Thank you for posting.

This is a nice recipe.  I have only had maybe 2 other salmon pattie recipes in my life prior to this one, and I do think this was the best.  I only had miracle whip on hand, so I used that.  I grated the onion and used about 3 T of it plus the liquid.  Also used white cornmeal, only kind I had on hand.  Added a generous dash of hot sauce, some shakes of dill, garlic powder and onion powder as well as salt and pepper.  They had very nice flavor.  Coated them in additional cornmeal on each side of pan and fried on medium heat for maybe a total of 15 minutes on medium.  There was a nice outer crunch and a somewhat creamy interior.  They were definitely not dry at all, and there were no issues with them holding together...in fact, they were amazingly "sturdy"!  Next time, I'm going to try without that outer coating, I think I might like it even better as originally written.   We topped ours with miracle whip with added fresh lemon juice stirred in, and it was a good, simple sauce.  I fried in a combo of olive oil and butter.  
Finally, I served these to my husband and daughter who had never had salmon patties.  I thought my daughter was going to turn up her nose, but she ate an add'l 1/2 of one and my husband grabbed another whole one.   We had a total of 5 good sized patties.  Thank you!
